On Wednesday, Indonesia's mines minister announced the cancellation of parliamentary approval for Bre-X Minerals Ltd's application for contracts related to the Busang gold deposit.
Bre-X requested a halt in trading of its stock on the Toronto Stock Exchange to address the news.
Trading of Bre-X was also halted on Nasdaq.
Bre-X had not released a statement by late Wednesday's trading session.
Gold analyst Catherine Gignac expressed uncertainty about the implications of the minister's statements for Bre-X's future.
Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana stated that Bre-X's contract of work would be processed from the beginning.
Umar Said, the secretary-general of the ministry, mentioned that the government was investigating representations made by Bre-X to North American regulatory authorities.
Vince Borg, a spokesman for Barrick Gold Corp, indicated that they were seeking clarification on the impact of the parliamentary committee on their negotiations with Bre-X.
Barrick Gold Corp was negotiating with Bre-X to form a joint venture to operate Busang.
Barrick's stock price fell on both the Toronto Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange on Wednesday.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. and Barrick Gold Corp. are negotiating an alliance to mine the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
Bre-X Chief Executive Officer David Walsh stated that negotiations with Barrick are progressing slowly.
David Walsh mentioned that legal issues are hindering a full agreement with Barrick.
The Indonesian government advised Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick to operate Busang.
The Indonesian government requested a 10 percent stake in the joint venture and set a Dec. 4 deadline for negotiations.
After the Dec. 4 deadline, Bre-X and Barrick announced that several issues remained unresolved.
The Indonesian government has expressed doubts about Bre-X's rights to the Busang deposit, which is estimated to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.
Umar Said, Indonesia's secretary-general of mines, stated that Bre-X's previous application for contracts of work has been cancelled.
Umar Said indicated that Bre-X and Barrick must submit new applications for work on the Busang deposit.
David Walsh claimed that Bre-X's permits and applications for the gold property are in good standing.

Falconbridge Ltd is a Canadian nickel company focused on expansion through acquisition and exploration.
Oyvind Hushovd is the new chief executive officer of Falconbridge, having replaced Frank Pickard.
Frank Pickard died suddenly at the age of 63 during a business trip in Chile in September.
Oyvind Hushovd has worked for Falconbridge for over 22 years and was previously the executive vice-president.
Falconbridge plans to double its annual nickel production to 200,000 tonnes and triple its copper production to about 500,000 tonnes within 15 years.
Falconbridge lost a bid to take over the Voisey's Bay nickel, copper, and cobalt deposit in Labrador.
Falconbridge is involved in ongoing work in New Caledonia, Ivory Coast, and Zambia.
Falconbridge plans to start producing nickel at the Raglan project in Quebec by the end of next year.
Falconbridge plans to produce copper at the Collahuasi joint venture project in Chile by 1998.
Falconbridge joined a consortium in Zambia to develop the Konkola Deep copper mine.

The world's gold producers are likely to suffer due to a decline in bullion prices and uncertainty in the gold market.
If the weakness in bullion prices continues, gold miners may experience lower profits, money-losing operations, closed mines, reduced exploration budgets, and falling share prices.
Analysts predict that smaller gold companies will be more vulnerable to takeovers as industry conditions worsen.
Michael Fowler, a gold analyst at Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion in Toronto, stated that earnings for gold producers are expected to be poor.
Gold was fixed at $358.55 an ounce in London on a recent Friday and has lost more than $13 since the beginning of the year.
The decline in gold prices has negatively impacted Canadian gold stocks, causing the Toronto Stock Exchange's gold index to drop over nine percent since December 30.
At least two gold companies have announced the shutdown of marginal mines recently.
TVX Gold Inc. announced it would close its Casa Berardi gold mine in Quebec.
Placer Dome Inc. stated it would sell two small mines in Quebec and cease operations at its high-cost Paymaster mine in Northern Ontario.
Analysts expect the effects of low bullion prices to be reflected in fourth-quarter earnings and in the first quarter of 1997.

Czech National Bank (CNB) Governor Josef Tosovsky stated that the central bank is committed to keeping the crown strong.
Tosovsky made these comments after a meeting with Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and top business executives.
The central bank aims to keep the crown within a specific band against a mark/dollar basket.
Tosovsky indicated that the central bank would try to maintain the rate within a plus/minus 7.5 percent band.
He dismissed speculation about moving the crown outside this band.
Analysts have debated the need for a devaluation of the crown to boost exports and address a current account deficit.
The current account deficit is projected to approach six percent of gross domestic product this year.
Tosovsky claimed that a stable crown has helped regulate inflation and that a stronger crown could enhance the competitiveness of Czech industry.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated that the government would provide more funds to export promotion agencies.
Klaus emphasized the need to lower expectations of higher inflation to avoid it becoming a self-fulfilling prophecy.

Bitter infighting occurred among Czech Social Democrats on a Friday before elections.
The opposition party hopes to defeat conservative Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
Party chairman Milos Zeman denied any split in the party.
The Social Democrats are competing closely with Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) before Senate elections.
Zeman threatened to resign next spring unless a party deputy chairman who voted with the Klaus government resigned first.
A Social Democrat deputy threatened to leave the parliamentary party due to a conflict with an ex-communist colleague.
Klaus's three-party coalition lost its parliamentary majority in lower house elections earlier this year.
Opinion polls show the Social Democrats are level or slightly ahead of the ODS.
Jozef Wagner led a revolt by four Social Democrat deputies that allowed the 1997 state budget to pass its first reading.
Zeman downplayed Wagner's threat and stated there is no real split in the party.

Komercni Banka a.s. reported a 10 percent decline in profits for the first nine months of the year due to accounting changes.
The bank's net profit under international accounting standards decreased from 5.44 billion crowns to 4.88 billion crowns.
Shares of Komercni Banka rose on the Prague Stock Exchange following the profit announcement.
Kamil Ziegler, the bank's finance division director, stated that the accounting method was revised to exclude unpaid late fees and commissions.
The revised accounting method only includes fees that have been paid, whereas previously outstanding receivables were included.
The amount of late fees that would have been included under the previous accounting method was 1.2 billion crowns.
Komercni Banka posted a net profit of 5.11 billion crowns for the entire year of 1995.
The bank's total assets increased to 432.04 billion crowns at the end of the third quarter from 336.21 billion crowns year-on-year.
The net interest margin decreased to 4.07 percent from 5.40 percent, but increased from 3.93 percent at the end of the first half.
Under Czech accounting standards, Komercni's gross profit for the period was 3.87 billion crowns, down from 6.83 billion crowns year-on-year.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced a state commission to address bureaucracy.
The commission is named the 'Commission for the Removal of Bureaucratic Burden'.
The commission will have a steering committee, a chairman, two vice-chairmen, two sections, six sub-commissions, and more members than Klaus's cabinet.
Klaus stated that the only bureaucrat at the commission would be a secretary.
The commission's staff will number around 20 and will work part time.
Klaus's cabinet consists of 16 members.
The Czech bureaucracy has historical roots in the Austro-Hungarian empire and was further developed under communism.
Applications for documents such as company registrations, licenses, and work permits can take weeks or months to process.
Citizens often have to queue for hours to be attended to by bureaucrats.
Knocking on office doors for attention is prohibited.

Czech President Vaclav Havel called opposition Social Democrat leader Milos Zeman 'extremely irresponsible'.
Havel's remarks were made during a bitter campaign for Senate elections.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus accused Zeman of lying about the BIS intelligence agency.
Zeman alleged that the BIS tried to extract compromising material from his elderly mother.
The conflict between Havel and Zeman escalated after BIS director Stanislav Devaty resigned.
Devaty resigned over allegations of spying on a deputy premier and a subsequent coverup.
Klaus criticized Zeman's comments about the BIS, suggesting they were inappropriate for a constitutional official.
Zeman accused Klaus of playing dirty in the Senate elections.
Zeman claimed that an operational group within the BIS was responsible for shadowing Social Democrat politicians.
Havel stated that Zeman should have brought his charges to a parliamentary commission before making them public.

Czech President Vaclav Havel voted in Senate elections on Friday.
Havel called on citizens to participate in the elections despite apathy towards the upper house.
Havel voted in a Prague suburb and showed his identity card to election officials.
The Senate elections are the first electoral test for Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus since losing his lower house majority in June.
Opinion polls indicate that many Czechs may not vote due to a lack of understanding of the Senate's role.
The Senate was established in the Czech Republic's constitution, which came into force in 1993.
The Senate elections are occurring now after delays in the electoral process.
Havel encouraged citizens to vote in both rounds of the elections, which take place over two weekends.
Turnout for the lower house elections in June was 76.4 percent, but lower turnout is expected for the Senate elections.
A survey indicated that only 57 percent planned to vote in the first round of the Senate elections.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's party, the Civic Democratic Party (ODS), led in Senate elections.
Voter turnout in the Senate elections was 35 percent.
The ODS topped voting in 66 of the 71 declared constituencies.
Most candidates will face a second round run-off on November 22-23.
The Central Election Commission reported a turnout of 34.27 percent in 53 of the 81 constituencies.
The turnout was significantly lower than the 76.4 percent in the lower house elections held in June.
Klaus downplayed voter apathy and emphasized the ODS's performance.
The Social Democrats, led by Milos Zeman, did not win in any constituency.
Zeman attributed the poor results to low voter turnout.
Miroslav Sladek, leader of the far-right Republicans, criticized the Senate without participating in the elections.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) announced a change in its methodology for calculating industrial production.
The new methodology aims to align with western standards.
CSU Chairman Edvard Outrata stated that the change will take effect in January 1997.
The new methodology will exclude multiple calculations of semi-finished products, resources, and other materials.
The new index will measure output changes by units, weight, or other measurements for 1,304 products from 879 product groups.
Output indices for product groups will be categorized into sectors based on their weight in the respective industrial sector.
The overall index will be calculated from weighted changes in the sectoral indices.
Outrata mentioned that the old system of measuring gross production was suitable for a planned economy.
Construction output data will be adjusted to the new methodology at the beginning of 1998.
Preliminary monthly data will be released on the 40th day after the end of the month being examined.

Czech Ceska Rafinerska a.s. closed a cracking unit at its Litvinov refinery on Monday after a fire occurred.
The fire at the Litvinov refinery was the second in eight days.
Company spokesman Ales Soukup stated that the restoration of crude processing would continue despite the fire.
A fire broke out on Sunday night in a furnace of a cracking unit as crude flow resumed after an eight-day stoppage.
Oil flow had been halted since a blaze began on November 23 and lasted for more than two days.
The latest fire was extinguished several hours after it started.
Soukup indicated that production at the refinery would continue as crude is diverted around the cracker.
The shutdown of the cracker would limit the content of processed crude.
The extent of damage at the refinery has not yet been determined.
Soukup stated that reopening the cracker would take more than just hours or days.

The Czech government approved a declaration on post-World War Two reconciliation with Germany.
The declaration includes mutual expressions of regret for the Nazi occupation from 1938 to 1945 and for the brutality during the post-war expulsion of ethnic Germans from Sudetenland.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated he was authorized to sign the text without changes.
Klaus indicated that the government sees no reason to make changes to the declaration.
The foreign ministers of the Czech Republic and Germany are scheduled to initial the text in Prague on Friday.
Signature by the two presidents and confirmation by the parliaments are expected early next year.
Klaus claimed the declaration aims to close negative chapters of history and improve future relations.
Groups representing families of Sudeten Germans expressed anger over the declaration for not compensating lost property.
Germany's Christian Social Union (CSU) has given qualified support to the declaration but made demands regarding participation in a planned fund.
The Czech parliament's mainstream parties support the declaration, while the extreme-right Republican Party and far-left Communists oppose it.

Volkswagen AG Czech unit Skoda Auto a.s. announced that its new mid-sized Octavia sedan will have a base price of 335,700 crowns ($12,800) in its home market.
Skoda plans to produce 64,000 Octavias in the next year and increase production to 90,000 in 1998.
The Octavia is built on a common VW platform designed for the 1998 Audi A3 and upgraded Golf.
The Octavia will be available with three petrol and two diesel engines, with the top SLX automatic model priced at 497,900 crowns.
The Octavia will be showcased at the Paris International Auto Show in October and is expected to be delivered to Czech dealers in November.
Skoda was taken over by Volkswagen in 1992 as part of a government privatization plan.
Skoda built a new factory specifically for Octavia production.
The Octavia features modern but conservative design lines, positioned between a Ford Mondeo and Audi's A-line.
The cheapest Octavia model includes a 1.6 litre, 55 Kw engine, ignition immobiliser, driver-side airbag, adjustable driver's seat, and steering wheel.
Skoda Chairman Ludvik Kalma expects about 20,000 units of the Octavia to be sold.

The Czech government approved rules for a tender to sell a 34 percent stake in Aero Vodochody a.s.
The tender is open to both domestic and foreign investors.
The winner of the tender will be announced on April 2.
Chemapol Group a.s., Boeing Co in alliance with Ceske Aerolinie a.s., and CIMEX Holding a.s. have shown interest in Aero Vodochody.
Aero Vodochody is developing the L-159, a light training subsonic fighter.
The Czech army has signed a contract to buy 72 L-159s.
The Czech government approved a financial package of 3.26 billion crowns to help Aero Vodochody.
Aero Vodochody's basic capital was reduced from 962 million crowns to one million crowns.
The chosen investor must pay most of the share price from their own assets.
The state will retain at least a 34 percent stake in Aero Vodochody.

Tibet's toilets have views that some consider spectacular.
Many tourists in Tibet are focused on the beauty of the Himalayan plateau.
The altitude in Lhasa is 3,680 metres (12,000 feet).
Visitors often do not notice the odors from public toilets due to the scenery.
Mary Beth Cooper, a U.S. tourist from Cleveland, Ohio, described Tibet as vast, overwhelming, awesome, beautiful, and interesting.
Tourists are impressed by the beauty of Tibet's Himalayas and the warmth of its people.
Tibet's tourism is a growing sector and a major source of foreign exchange.
Tibet earned $22 million in tourist dollars last year and aims for $30 million this year.
Tibet hopes to increase tourism earnings by 8-10 percent annually.
The Tibet Tourism Bureau opened Tibet to foreign tourism in 1980.

Tibet offers tax breaks, tax holidays, loans, clean air, and scenic beauty to attract foreign investors.
Investors in Tibet face high transport costs, frequent power outages, and unreliable telephone lines.
Beijing has implemented policies to attract foreign investment in Tibet.
Wang Yaju, vice director of the Department of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation of the Tibet Autonomous Region, reported improvements in investment conditions due to new policies.
Fourteen new foreign investment projects were approved in Tibet this year.
From 1988 to 1995, only 61 joint ventures were established in Tibet.
A planned $48 million venture between Taiwan's Kwang Yang Motors and Tibet's Summit Motor aims to produce motorcycle engines in Sichuan province.
The Tibet Plateau Cashmere Co. was established by John McKay, a U.S. company, and a private Tibetan partner to process cashmere.
The joint venture by Tibet Plateau Cashmere Co. is exempt from income tax for the first five years after making a profit.
Investors in Tibet have noted that navigating Chinese bureaucracy for permits can be frustrating and time-consuming.

China's private sector has become an important source of jobs for workers laid off by loss-making state enterprises.
In 1995, the private sector hired 1.5 million workers made redundant from state- and collectively owned enterprises.
The type of staff being employed by private enterprises has shifted as China's fastest growing sector expands and modernizes.
The number of workers employed after leaving state enterprises has increased in the last two years.
High wages are the main reason workers are attracted to private enterprises from state firms.
At the end of 1995, China's private companies and self-employed accounted for a total of 56 million jobs, or six percent of China's employed workers.
China had 654,500 private companies and 25.28 million self-employed workers at the end of 1995.
Shenyang found jobs for 800,000 laid-off workers in the last two years.
In Shanghai, more than 85,000 redundant state workers created their own businesses or found jobs in private firms.
Private enterprise in China averaged growth of 50 percent to 60 percent a year over the past three years, expected to slow to about 30 percent in the coming years.

China's Communist Party issued a document warning against Western ideas such as parliamentary democracy and capitalism.
The document, consisting of 15,000 characters, was adopted at the annual secret plenum of the ruling party elite.
Party chief Jiang Zemin aims to combat corruption, pornography, and the worship of money while promoting nationalism and hardline communist ideology.
The document expresses a strong opposition to the West, particularly the United States, which China perceives as pursuing a policy of containment.
Jiang Zemin seeks to appease leftwing party hardliners who believe that profit-based economic reforms have eroded puritan communist values.
The document states that the standard of moral conduct has declined and that worship of money, pleasure-seeking, and individualism have increased.
It warns senior party officials against the temptations of power, profit, and sex, labeling corruption as a virus that could threaten the party's stability.
The document emphasizes the importance of patriotism and urges self-sufficiency in the face of pressure from Western countries.
It contains 14 mentions of Deng Xiaoping, compared to three for Jiang Zemin and four for Mao Zedong.
The document warns that socialism has faced serious setbacks globally and that pressure from developed capitalist countries will persist.

Winston Lord is the U.S. government's top Asian official.
Winston Lord left China on Thursday after a visit focused on human rights and issues on the Korean peninsula.
The meetings during Lord's visit were described as frank and cordial.
Lord raised concerns about China's treatment of dissidents during his visit.
Lord is the Assistant Secretary of State for East Asian and Pacific Affairs.
Lord arrived in Beijing on Tuesday for a previously unannounced visit.
Lord held discussions with Deputy Foreign Minister Liu Huaqiu and had a brief meeting with Foreign Minister Qian Qichen.
The discussions included a focus on the Korean peninsula, but there was little sign of concrete progress.
South Korea and the United States called for four-nation peace talks with North Korea and China in April.
China has not taken a clear stance on the proposed four-way talks.

China aims to launch manned space flights early next century.
China plans to land a spacecraft on the moon in the 21st century.
Xinhua news agency reported on China's ambitious space program.
Senior Chinese space officials seek to enhance the country's competitive edge in international space development.
China is focused on expanding its role in the commercial satellite business.
Manned space flights are a top priority in China's space program.
China is developing a heavy solar satellite in partnership with Germany.
China aims to create a new generation of lightweight spacecraft for satellite deployment.
Wang Liheng stated that a breakthrough in manned space technology is expected at the beginning of the next century.
Li Jianzhong indicated that China is working to improve launch vehicle technology in the 21st century.

China is unlikely to concede on its demand to enter the World Trade Organisation as a developing country.
Pei Changhong is the head of the department of Foreign Economy and Trade under the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Pei Changhong stated that China will only enter the WTO as a developing country.
The United States insists that the size of China's economy ranks it as a developed country.
China was disappointed when its application to join the WTO as a founding member failed two years ago.
Talks regarding China's accession to the WTO have proceeded slowly in Geneva.
Pei Changhong expects little progress during the upcoming WTO ministerial meeting in Singapore.
China will attend the WTO meeting in Singapore under observer status.
Pei Changhong mentioned that China would explain its position in side meetings at the WTO.
Pei Changhong noted that China's economy is already open compared to some neighboring countries.

Intense haggling among trade ministers aimed to create a deal to free the global information technology market.
The United States and the European Union reported progress toward a global pact to eliminate tariffs on a $600 billion market for information technology.
Discussions on monopolistic business practices were ongoing.
Differences on labour standards appeared to narrow between developed and developing countries.
WTO officials aimed for a final declaration at the first ministerial meeting by Friday.
The EU, United States, Canada, and Japan were working towards consensus on an Information Technology Agreement.
EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan stated that significant progress was being made.
Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefksy agreed with Brittan's assessment but did not provide further details.
Negotiators aimed for a quick agreement to encourage Asian trading partners to sign on by the end of the meeting.
Japan's Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda expressed hope for a significant agreement in trade liberalization.

Harrison Ford and Brad Pitt are on a blacklist of 50 people barred from visiting Tibet.
The blacklist was confirmed by Chinese officials on a Friday.
The blacklist was created by the Tibet Tourism Bureau.
Brad Pitt, Harrison Ford, Melissa Mathison Ford, Martin Scorsese, and Jean-Jaques Annaud are included on the blacklist.
The Tibet state security office verbally informed that these individuals should not be granted entry permits to Tibet.
Formal documents regarding the blacklist were received at the end of April or early May.
The official stated that the individuals on the blacklist are banned from visiting Tibet for any reason.
None of the individuals on the blacklist have applied to visit Tibet.
Brad Pitt stars in the film 'Seven Years in Tibet,' directed by Jean-Jaques Annaud.
China has not formally objected to the film 'Seven Years in Tibet.'

China sentenced Ngawang Choephel to 18 years in prison for espionage.
Ngawang Choephel was a Tibetan music expert touring the Himalayan region on a U.S. scholarship.
He was detained in Tibet in August 1995 while producing a documentary about traditional music and dance.
The Intermediate People's Court of Xigaze Prefecture issued the sentence under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.
Ngawang Choephel was deprived of his political rights for four years.
U.S. officials did not comment on the case immediately.
China has been known to crack down on signs of anti-Chinese unrest in the Himalayan region.
Robbie Barnett from the Tibet Information Network described the length of the sentence as extraordinary.
Ngawang Choephel's sentence was the most severe in a political case since 1989.
China has shown confidence in using counter-espionage laws against perceived foreign threats.

China's Premier Li Peng visited Russia for 43 hours.
China described the visit as politically and economically significant.
Diplomats stated that the warming ties between China and Russia are not likely to lead to a major strategic alliance.
China's rhetoric regarding the visit was intended to signal to the West that it has allies other than the United States.
The People's Daily reported that the visit resulted in fruitful achievements.
An agreement was made for the prime ministers of China and Russia to meet twice a year.
Chinese President Jiang Zemin is scheduled to visit Moscow in April for discussions.
Several deals were signed during the visit, including the supply of Russian Sukhoi Su-27 warplanes.
The deal for the Sukhoi Su-27 involved the sale of a complete production line to be built in northeast China.
The People's Daily emphasized the political significance of the visit and the importance of Sino-Russian partnership.

China has launched a manhunt in Tibet following a bomb explosion in Lhasa.
The government has tightened airport security in Tibet.
A reward of one million yuan ($120,000) has been offered for information leading to the arrest of those responsible for the bomb.
The bomb exploded outside city government offices in Lhasa on Christmas Day.
No arrests have been made in connection with the bombing.
The reward notice was published in the Lhasa Evening News on December 27.
The bomb caused widespread damage but resulted in no casualties.
Officials believe the blast was politically motivated and linked to followers of the Dalai Lama.
Police have established a special task force to search for the culprits.
The bomb was identified as a home-made device made from ammonium nitrate.

China exercised its veto at the United Nations for the first time in nearly 25 years.
The veto killed a U.N. plan to monitor disarmament and a ceasefire in Guatemala.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang stated that Guatemala must be wholly responsible for the situation.
China has no objection to the dispatch of U.N. peacekeepers to oversee a peace agreement in Guatemala.
Shen accused Guatemala of forcing China to exercise its veto due to its ties with Taiwan.
All Security Council members except China voted in favor of a resolution to send 155 peacekeepers to Guatemala.
The resolution was based on a U.N.-brokered peace accord signed on December 29 between the Guatemalan government and leftist rebels.
Shen criticized Guatemala for recognizing Taiwan and for sponsoring a General Assembly resolution for U.N. membership for Taiwan since 1993.
Shen condemned Guatemala's invitation to Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang to a peace signing ceremony.
China's veto meant that the resolution failed, as announced by Council President Hisashi Owada of Japan.

Air Macau expects to carry between 20 and 30 percent more belly cargo with the delivery of two Airbus A321 aircraft.
Air Macau plans to serve three new routes into China next year.
Simon Tang is the cargo supervisor for sales and marketing at Air Macau.
Air Macau has achieved 60 percent load factors on current available capacity.
Air Macau carried 3091 tonnes of air cargo in the first nine months of operations.
No cargo was carried during the first two months of Air Macau's operations.
Air Macau's cargo figures show an increase from 161 tonnes in January to 489 tonnes in August.
Air Macau's Airbus A321 aircraft will be on seven-year leases.
Air Macau currently serves six destinations with 63 frequencies per week.
Air Macau aims to fly to 22 destinations in the next three years.

Freight forwarders in Hong Kong have been warned of a 20 percent increase in transpacific air cargo rates starting September 1.
The increase is expected to occur during the peak season leading up to Christmas.
Anthony Lau is the vice-chairman of the Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents Ltd (HAFFA).
Lau stated that the 20 percent increase is not surprising and is in line with expectations.
The rate increase will apply to cargo destined for both the U.S. east and west coasts.
Warning notices have been received from major transpacific carriers including Northwest Airlines, China Airlines, Japan Airlines, United Airlines, Evergreen International Airlines, and Polar Air Cargo.

Evergreen International Airlines Inc has increased the number of flights from Hong Kong.
The increase is due to high trans-Pacific demand.
Evergreen now operates six weekly Boeing 747 freighter flights instead of four.
Evergreen stated it cannot keep up with current demand.
All flights are fully booked according to Evergreen's vice-president Kersti Krepp.
Evergreen would be able to fill additional flights into Hong Kong.
The additional flights on Mondays are to Columbus, Ohio, New York, and Los Angeles.

Hong Kong civil aviation department statistics indicate that cargo handled in August increased by 6.7 percent compared to August of the previous year.
Air cargo imports for scheduled and non-scheduled flights in August totaled 59,910 tonnes.
Air cargo exports for scheduled and non-scheduled flights in August totaled 71,675 tonnes.
In August 1996, the unloaded cargo from Africa was 195 tonnes and loaded cargo was 241 tonnes, showing a 20.0 percent change from August 1995.
In August 1996, the unloaded cargo from Asia - others was 4,013 tonnes and loaded cargo was 4,824 tonnes, showing a 12.0 percent change from August 1995.
In August 1996, the unloaded cargo from Australasia was 2,996 tonnes and loaded cargo was 2,676 tonnes, showing a -6.1 percent change from August 1995.
In August 1996, the unloaded cargo from Continental Europe was 8,850 tonnes and loaded cargo was 9,449 tonnes, showing a 1.6 percent change from August 1995.
In August 1996, the unloaded cargo from Japan was 5,570 tonnes and loaded cargo was 12,197 tonnes, showing a 2.4 percent change from August 1995.
In August 1996, the unloaded cargo from Mainland China was 1,841 tonnes and loaded cargo was 2,896 tonnes, showing a 9.5 percent change from August 1995.
In August 1996, the unloaded cargo from the Middle East was 700 tonnes and loaded cargo was 1,291 tonnes, showing a 2.7 percent change from August 1995.

John Findlay is the general secretary of the Hong Kong Aircrew Officers' Association.
The Hong Kong Aircrew Officers' Association has 700 members.
The association is providing each member with an e-mail address.
Members can stay in touch regardless of their flying locations.
Members currently access the association's bulletin board using a telephone modem.
The association has 300 members based outside Hong Kong.
Committee members who are airline pilots can stay in touch with union business via laptop computers.
The bulletin board has been in use for two and a half years and is updated daily.
The bulletin board includes a newsletter, a leisure forum, and a 'for sale' site.
The association aims to create a website page specifically for Hong Kong pilots.

Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals Limited (HACTL) may keep its facilities at Kai Tak as a depot after the new airport at Chek Lap Kok opens.
HACTL's managing director is Anthony Charter.
Air freight forwarders in Hong Kong are pressuring the Government to keep Kai Tak's twin terminals open.
Charter stated that HACTL has approached the Government regarding the future of Kai Tak's facilities.
A final decision on the future of the land occupied by Kai Tak is expected next year after a report from planning consultants.
HACTL's private franchise at Kai Tak will expire when the new airport opens in April 1998.
HACTL plans to move to a new one billion HK dollar Super Terminal at Chek Lap Kok.
The new terminal at Chek Lap Kok is claimed to be the world's largest air freight complex under one roof.
The Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents (HAFFA) reported that some freight forwarders are concerned about the costs of moving to the new airport.
HAFFA has supported the retention of Kai Tak's cargo facilities and first proposed the idea over five years ago.

All three airlines flying directly between Hong Kong and London can start using a new shortcut to Europe across China from October 27.
The new routing allows for more cargo and less fuel to be carried and reduces passenger journey times by up to an hour.
Cathay Pacific Airways, British Airways, and Virgin Atlantic will utilize the new northern route over China instead of the traditional southern route over Thailand and India.
The shortcut was agreed upon during recent talks between the British and Chinese governments.
A Cathay Pacific spokesman stated that up to an hour can be cut off flying time for its Boeing 747-400 aircraft on some European routes, allowing an additional four tonnes of cargo.
British Airways can carry an extra 70 tonnes of air cargo a week if its twice weekly 747-400 aircraft utilize the new routing.
Virgin Atlantic's new routing will enable its Airbus A340 aircraft to carry an extra six tonnes of freight westbound and two tonnes eastbound, saving around 50,000 pounds of fuel.
Aviation analysts indicate that the new routing offers significant cost-saving advantages and allows airlines to carry full cargo loads year-round.
Peter Negline, Vice President and senior research analyst at Salomon Brothers Hong Kong Limited, stated that Cathay Pacific cannot utilize the new routes on all flights due to not being granted a full quota.
Curfews at Heathrow and Kai Tak airports will cause scheduling difficulties until Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok opens in 18 months.

Work will start on October 30 on Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd's new HK$1.6 billion headquarters at Chek Lap Kok.
The main contractor for the project is Dragages et Travaux Publics (HK) Ltd.
The project includes a 10-storey office building, a 333 room staff complex, a three-storey workshop and stores building, and a three-storey leisure centre.
The total floor area of the new building is 102,630 square metres.
The new building is scheduled to be completed in stages from January 1998.
The overall construction period is 22 months.
The new airport at Chek Lap Kok is due to open in April 1998.
Dragages is also building the new base maintenance facility for Hong Kong Aircraft Engineering Company Limited (HAECO).
Dragages is constructing Cathay Pacific's new flight kitchen at Chek Lap Kok.

El Al is Israel's flag carrier.
El Al will start using a Boeing 747 on its weekly Tel Aviv to Hong Kong service.
The Boeing 747 will replace a smaller Boeing 767 that flies via Tashkent.
The 747 will be a direct flight from Israel to Hong Kong with a refueling stop in Bombay on the return leg.
El Al claims to be the only airline offering a direct link to the Middle East.
The larger aircraft will increase cargo capacity from 10 to 24 tonnes.
The larger aircraft will also increase passenger comfort.
El Al is conducting seminars with travel agents to attract more tourists from Hong Kong.
Current passenger levels to Tel Aviv are between five and six thousand a year.
El Al believes there is significant market potential for travelers from Hong Kong.

A labour shortage is threatening to delay the completion of Hong Kong's new airport.
Clinton Leeks is the director of corporate development for the Airport Authority Hong Kong.
The Airport Authority Hong Kong oversees the completion and operation of the HK$49.8 billion airport at Chek Lap Kok.
An additional two to three thousand construction workers are needed to meet the opening target of April 1998.
Trade unions in Hong Kong are expected to resist attempts to import more workers from overseas.
The Confederation of Trade Unions has stated that contractors should prioritize local tradesmen.
Clinton Leeks mentioned that without the additional workers, certain aspects of the project are at risk.
There is a specific skills shortage of electrical and mechanical workers in Hong Kong's construction industry.
The Hong Kong government is aware of the labour shortage through regular meetings to discuss progress.
The Hong Kong Government stated that 5,000 or 18 percent of the new airport's total labour force is imported.

Polar Air Cargo will start new services to New Delhi, Dubai, Bangkok, Kansai in Japan, and Manila within the next four months.
Jack Kane is the executive vice president of Polar Air Cargo.
Polar's first Boeing 747-200 and 14th 747 freighter was recently handed over to the company.
The new Boeing 747-200 acquisition from Air Hong Kong will provide longer ranges, higher weights, and reduced fuel consumption.
Polar is awaiting final U.S. Department of Transportation approval to begin flying to Kansai.
Polar has received permission to fly to Bangkok and expects to start services to Manila in the first quarter of 1997.
With approval for Kansai and new services to London and Amsterdam, Polar plans to begin a round-the-world service early next year.
When the Kansai operation begins, Polar expects to offer four cargo flights a week from Hong Kong to the U.S. west coast and five or six to the east coast via Anchorage.
The Boeing 747-200 allows Polar to avoid stopping in Khabarovsk, Russia, for refueling.
Polar does not have rights to operate in China but is in discussions with Chinese airlines for a possible joint venture.

Cathay Pacific chairman Peter Sutch initiated the construction of the airline's new corporate headquarters in Hong Kong.
The new headquarters will cost US$448 million or HK$3.5 billion.
The headquarters will be located at Chek Lap Kok airport.
The new building will accommodate almost all of Cathay Pacific's staff under one roof for the first time.
Sutch stated that the new headquarters represents a commitment to Hong Kong.
The new headquarters is described as an important stage in Cathay's 50-year history.
The complex will provide a 'home from home' for more than 4,000 employees.
The headquarters is expected to create new commercial, business, and marketing opportunities.
Hank Townsend, CEO of the Hong Kong Airport Authority, attended the ceremony.
The complex will cover one million square feet and include a 10-storey office block and a 23-storey staff hotel with 350 rooms.

The UK government ruled out tax credits on share buybacks and some special dividends.
Analysts believe that British utilities will find share buybacks and takeovers more costly due to this ruling.
Michael Cohen, a utilities analyst at Salomon Brothers, stated that companies should still proceed with buybacks or special dividends if justified.
Chancellor Kenneth Clarke announced that shareholders can no longer claim tax credits on share buybacks or special dividends related to share consolidations or takeovers.
This government move aims to provide the UK Treasury with more room for a cut in income tax in the November budget.
Shares in the utility sector initially declined following the announcement but later showed some recovery.
Kevin Lapwood, a utilities analyst at Merrill Lynch, described the initial market reaction as a knee-jerk reaction that was slightly overdone.
Shares in Anglian Water fell to a low of 525 pence before recovering to 544-1/2 pence.
Yorkshire Water shares decreased to a low of 613 pence and were down 17-1/2 pence at 622-1/2 pence.
London Electric shares dropped to a low of 598 pence before recovering to 608-1/2 pence.

Ofwat announced it would review water company price limits in 1999, five years ahead of schedule.
Commentators noted that the decision was not unexpected and may have political implications.
The opposition Labour party welcomed the review, calling it 'long overdue'.
Ofwat set the current price limits in 1994 for a 10-year period with an option for a five-year review.
Ofwat director general Ian Byatt stated that a ten-year gap between reviews is too long.
Janet Langdon, director of the Water Services Association, said the review decision was not surprising.
Labour environment spokesman Frank Dobson claimed the review indicated that Labour was correct in arguing that water companies overcharged customers since privatisation.
Byatt announced the review to eliminate speculation and regulatory uncertainty and to allow time for consultation.
Water company shares fell following the announcement, with Anglian Water, Severn Trent, and Thames Water all experiencing declines.
Byatt indicated that the review would focus on balancing supply and demand and improving leakage control.

Shares in media group Pearson rose sharply on Monday due to takeover speculation.
A report claimed that broadcaster BSkyB might be planning a bid for Pearson, which was later denied.
Pearson shares increased by 25 pence to 721-1/2 pence by 1115 GMT after reaching a peak of 745 pence.
The Independent newspaper reported that BSkyB, with a 40 percent stake from Rupert Murdoch's News Corp, was planning a bid worth over four billion pounds.
BSkyB's chief executive, Sam Chisholm, stated there were no talks about a bid for Pearson.
Pearson owns the Financial Times newspaper, Penguin Books, and several television production companies.
Analysts believe any potential bid for Pearson is likely to occur before new management takes control next year.
Pearson appointed Marjorie Scardino as chief executive and Dennis Stevenson as chairman.
Analysts noted that Pearson shares are nearing the top end of their price target range for full valuation.
Speculation about a bid for Pearson last surfaced in August with rumors about Reed-Elsevier as a potential buyer.

British utility South West Water could face bids worth 950 million pounds ($1.51 billion).
The government may allow Severn Trent and Wessex Water to proceed with firm offers.
The official approval for any bids is likely to be linked to a deal offering price cuts for customers.
Philip Hollobone, an analyst at Williams de Broe, stated that the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) may decide that the bids are against the public interest unless there are price cuts.
The DTI could announce its decision as early as Friday, four weeks after a report on the bids was submitted by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).
Wessex Water announced its intention to bid for South West Water on March 7.
Severn Trent expressed its intention to bid on March 21.
Both intended bids were passed on to the MMC under government regulations.
South West Water shares were trading at 705.5 pence, up 4.5 pence.
Analysts suggested that offers might be around 750 pence per share, valuing the company at over 950 million pounds ($1.52 billion).

J. Sainsbury Plc expects its new banking venture to turn in profits in a relatively short period of time.
Kevin McCarten is the marketing director of J. Sainsbury Plc.
Sainsbury has applied for authorisation from the Bank of England to set up Sainsbury's Bank.
Sainsbury will own 55 percent of Sainsbury's Bank, while Bank of Scotland will own 45 percent.
The banking service will offer products at better value than currently available.
Sainsbury will use its customer database from the Reward loyalty card for direct marketing of banking facilities.
Sainsbury is not planning to limit access to banking services to Reward loyalty card customers.
Sainsbury currently has about five stores in Scotland.
The new bank will have its own identity and will not carry the Bank of Scotland logo.
There will not initially be banking counters in Sainsbury stores.

CalEnergy Co. launched a $1.2 billion takeover bid for Northern Electric Plc.
Northern Electric Plc rejected the unsolicited takeover offer from CalEnergy Co.
This bid is the second for Northern Electric in just over a year.
CalEnergy's bid includes an offer of 630 British pence for each common share and 103 pence for each preferred share of Northern Electric.
The total value of the deal is approximately $1.23 billion.
CalEnergy's CE Electric unit is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy and 30 percent owned by Peter Kiewit Sons.
Northern Electric previously fended off a hostile bid from Trafalgar House last year.
CalEnergy Chairman David Sokol stated the company's strategy is to become a leading global provider of energy services.
CalEnergy has invested in geothermal and other energy projects in the U.S., Indonesia, and the Philippines.
Northern Electric is based in northeastern England and is described as the smallest regional electricity company.

Thames Water reported a rise in profits and dividend on Tuesday.
Thames Water's first half pre-tax profits rose to 176 million pounds from 165.4 million pounds in the same period last year.
Profits before exceptional items increased by 15 percent to 188 million pounds.
Thames Water's one-off items included a 12.2 million pound cost for repurchasing convertible bonds.
Thames Water increased its dividend by 22 percent to 11.2 pence.
David Campbell of broker Greig Middleton commented that the figures are reassuring and the dividend is a major feature.
Thames managing director Bill Alexander stated he expects to maintain the dividend at the current level.
Thames shares rose by four pence to 549 pence.
Thames Water announced an additional investment of 150 million pounds in services aimed at reducing water leakage.
Thames Water reported a 10 percent decrease in leakage from year-ago levels.

Allied Domecq reported a fall in annual profits.
Allied Domecq ruled out a demerger of its spirits business.
Allied chairman Sir Christopher Hogg stated that improving operating performance is the company's overriding objective.
Chief executive Tony Hales said that the costs of a demerger would be very expensive.
Hales mentioned that a demerger would distract management for at least 12 months.
Allied Domecq's full-year pretax profits to August were 575 million pounds.
The company's exceptional losses for the year totaled 311 million pounds.
Allied Domecq paid out a total dividend of 23.59 pence a share.
Allied's shares fell to 453 pence after touching a low of 451 pence.
The company aims to improve performance in its spirits and wines business through various strategies.

Political pressures may delay government approval of recent takeover bids for British regional electricity companies.
Gordon Culfeather, a utilities analyst at Greig Middleton, stated that a referral to competition authorities is a possibility.
Seven of the original twelve regional electricity companies have been sold since March after the government's protective golden share expired.
Three of the sold regional electricity companies were acquired by U.S. utilities seeking to expand into the UK market.
The latest bid is from Dominion Resources, which agreed to pay 1.3 billion pounds for East Midlands Electricity.
Northern Electric is facing a hostile bid from CE Electric, a unit of U.S.-based CalEnergy, which has acquired 29 percent of Northern Electric.
Trade Secretary Ian Lang has blocked two bids for regional electricity companies earlier this year.
Hanson acquired Eastern Electricity and plans to spin it off as part of its demerger plans.
Scottish Power acquired Manweb, another regional electricity company.
Dominion and East Midlands Electricity believe their deal should not be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.

South West Water is a British water and sewerage company.
South West Water's pretax profits for the six months ending September 30 rose to 72.9 million pounds.
The profits increased by 35 percent compared to the previous year.
The company's profits were ahead of expectations, which ranged from 57 to 68 million pounds.
South West Water announced a 20 percent increase in its dividend.
The company promised real dividend increases of eight percent in the coming years.
South West Water plans to pay out an interim dividend of 11.8 pence.
The company will pay a rebate of 15 pounds each to customers due to blocked bids.
South West Water's non-regulated businesses contributed 6.6 million pounds to profits in the first half.
A financing deal involving standby letters of credit contributed 5.7 million pounds to first half profits.

London Electricity is a British regional electricity company.
Entergy is a U.S. firm considering a bid for London Electricity valued at 1.2 billion pounds.
London Electricity declined to comment on a Wall Street Journal Europe report regarding Entergy's interest.
The Wall Street Journal Europe reported that Entergy was seeking 1.1 billion pounds to acquire a British electricity firm with a financial profile similar to London Electricity.
Entergy stated that discussions with another party were too early to be meaningful.
Entergy's spokesman, Patrick Sweeney, did not deny the Wall Street Journal Europe article.
Shares in London Electricity reached a high of 671 pence and closed at 667 pence, an increase of 30-1/2 pence.
The Wall Street Journal Europe article mentioned that Entergy used the code name 'Atlantic' for the target company.
The bid mentioned in the documents was assumed to be around 700 pence per share.
Entergy expressed interest in the British market and indicated that this could lead to an acquisition.

National Power Plc reported a decline in half-year profits due to exceptional charges from an aborted takeover.
The company's pretax profits for the half year before exceptional items were 57 million pounds, down from 254 million pounds previously.
National Power's output for the year could be down by 20 percent.
The company paid a dividend of six pence per share, an increase from 5.4 pence, but at the lower end of forecasts.
Shares of National Power fell by 12.5 pence to 440.5 pence.
National Power's dividend increase of 11 percent was lower than PowerGen's 20 percent increase.
Exceptional charges included an unrealised loss on its investment in Southern Electric and costs from an aborted acquisition.
The bid for Southern Electric was blocked by UK authorities in April.
National Power's market share decreased to 27 percent from 30 percent a year ago.
The company is changing its structure to become a leading global power company and expects overseas activities to contribute 70 million pounds in post-tax income.

National Grid is a British electricity transmission business.
National Grid is expected to report a rise in half year profits on November 26.
Analysts predict National Grid's first half profits will range from 279 to 304 million stg.
A dividend payout of 4.45 to 4.9 pence per share is forecast for National Grid.
National Grid accepted revised transmission pricing proposed by industry watchdog Offer.
The revised pricing includes a one-off reduction of 20 percent starting April 1, 1997.
For the following three years, price increases will be capped at four points below inflation.
National Grid previously described Offer's original proposals as 'contrived, illogical and inconsistent.'
National Grid's chief executive expressed confidence in maintaining a 'progressive' dividend policy.
Energis, a service of National Grid, expects to break even in 1999/2000 after an operating loss of 72.8 million stg last year.

Eurotunnel announced a deal giving creditor banks 45.5 percent of the company in exchange for eliminating one billion pounds of debt.
The restructuring ends months of negotiations between Eurotunnel and 225 banks to which it owes nearly nine billion pounds.
Shareholders will own 54.5 percent of the company after the restructuring.
Eurotunnel co-chairman Alastair Morton stated that the restructuring plan provides medium-term financial stability.
Eurotunnel is currently making a profit before interest.
The company has taken around half of the cross-Channel market from European ferry companies.
Eurotunnel indicated that a strong operating performance could allow it to pay its first dividend within the next 10 years.
French co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle described the debt restructuring plan as an acceptable compromise for shareholders.
The details of the restructuring plan need to be finalized and agreed upon before submission to shareholders and the bank syndicate for approval.
The debt-for-equity swap will be at 130 pence per share, reducing outstanding debt by one billion pounds.

Mercury Asset Management Plc is expected to report a rise in pre-tax profits for the first half.
MAM shares were priced at 11.32 stg on Friday, near their year highs.
Analysts expect pre-tax profits of around 80 million stg, an increase from 63.6 million stg from the previous period.
The market anticipates a higher interim dividend compared to six pence last year.
Analysts believe Mercury has demonstrated its ability to operate independently after separating from S.G. Warburg.
Speculation about a takeover of Mercury has diminished, although there is still interest in potential acquisitions by the company.
UBS analyst Martin Cross stated that any bid premium on MAM's share price is unjustified.
Cross noted that MAM has significant capital, which it may use for expansion in U.S. markets.
BZW analyst Phillip Gibbs expects MAM to continue making small strategic acquisitions.
Gibbs mentioned that the FTSE index increased from 3,700 to 3,954 during the relevant six-month period.

Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) has not contacted London-based securities houses regarding a French investigation into Eurotunnel SA/Plc share dealings.
The SFO was asked to assist in an investigation by French authorities into alleged market manipulation of Eurotunnel's shares.
The SFO stated it would help in the French investigation but has no grounds to launch its own investigation into the dealings.
Securities firms contacted by Reuters reported they had not been approached by the SFO and did not expect to be.
The securities firms indicated they would cooperate fully if approached by the SFO.
The investigation is part of a history of corporate issues involving Eurotunnel, including previous investigations into insider trading.
Salomon Brothers and Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) were cleared of insider trading earlier this year related to a Eurotunnel rights issue in 1994.
The underwriting group for the Eurotunnel rights issue included several banks, such as Banque Indosuez, Morgan Grenfell, and Credit Lyonnais.
Approximately two-thirds of Eurotunnel shares are held in France, with more trading occurring in Paris than in London.
The SFO typically issues notices for interviews or document submissions but can also apply for search warrants.

NatWest Markets is the investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank.
Peter Hall has been named the chief operating officer of NatWest Markets.
Peter Hall currently runs NatWest's American operations.
Hall will report to chief executive Martin Owen.
NatWest Markets will consolidate its origination and distribution functions into one Global Financial Markets division.
NatWest stated that no job losses would result from the consolidation.
NatWest has recently acquired several companies, including J O Hambro Magan, Greenwich Capital, Gartmore, and Gleacher.
Analysts have expressed concerns about NatWest's ability to integrate its recent acquisitions.
Investment banks are currently benefiting from low inflation and steady growth in major economies.
Owen believes that operational management should be separated from strategy and client development.

British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke announced the phasing out of tax relief on profit related pay (PRP) schemes.
Analysts were surprised that new PRP schemes could still be registered as tax relief is reduced.
The upper limit of pay free of income tax will remain at 4,000 stg for profit periods beginning before January 1, 1998.
The ceiling for tax relief will be reduced to 2,000 stg in 1998 and to 1,000 stg in 1999.
No tax relief will be provided for profit periods starting on or after January 1, 2000.
Bob Rothenburg from Blick Rothenberg stated that the gradual reduction of relief would prevent pressure on employers to compensate employees.
Douglas Fairbairn from Ernst and Young expressed relief that the Chancellor's proposals did not include immediate abolition of the relief.
The Inland Revenue confirmed that new PRP schemes would be allowed at the lower rates of relief.
The Inland Revenue expects the proposal to yield 100 million stg in 1997/98, 700 million stg in 1998/99, 1.7 billion stg in 1999/2000, and 3.1 billion stg in 2000/2001.
There are currently around 14,000 PRP schemes covering 3.7 million employees.

Ernst & Young reported a profit of 75.2 million pounds ($125.4 million) in Britain.
The profit represented a 21 percent increase for the year ending June 30.
Ernst & Young's gross fee income was 456 million pounds.
The average profit per partner increased by 17 percent to 200,000 pounds.
Nick Land confirmed that Ernst & Young plans to become a limited liability partnership registered in Jersey.
Ernst & Young's worldwide revenue for the year to September is expected to rise by 13 percent to $7.8 billion.
Ernst & Young is the world's largest tax accountancy practice and the second largest management consultancy after Arthur Andersen.
Ernst & Young was formed in 1989 from the merger of Ernst & Whinney and Arthur Young.
The firm's move to limited liability is a response to industry-wide changes regarding liability status.
Ernst & Young's management consultancy saw a 40 percent increase in gross fees to 77.4 million pounds.

The British government published proposed new laws governing home lenders on Wednesday.
The new legislation reduced the immunity of building societies from takeover if they converted into banks.
Some home lenders responded coolly to the new legislation.
A leading player indicated that its plans for conversion might have differed if it had known the government's intentions.
Under the new draft law, a building society loses its five-year immunity from takeover after converting to bank status if it acquires another financial institution.
The Woolwich, with assets of just under 30 billion pounds, expressed disappointment regarding the government's timing of the draft.
The Woolwich stated that its board might have chosen a different conversion approach if aware of the potential legal changes.
The Treasury acknowledged that the new Building Societies Bill might not be enacted before the next election due to limited parliamentary time.
The Alliance & Leicester expressed disappointment and noted that some concerns had not been fully resolved.
Northern Rock welcomed the changes and described them as a reasonable compromise.

Morgan Grenfell Asset Management is the fund management arm of Deutsche Bank AG.
Trading in three European funds will resume on Thursday after being suspended earlier this week.
The three suspended funds are the MG European Growth Trust, MG Europa, and MG European Capital Growth.
The suspension was pending an investigation into possible irregularities related to unquoted securities.
Britain's Investment Management Regulatory Organisation is investigating the management of the funds in conjunction with MGAM.
IMRO is working with MGAM to resolve the situation for investors affected by the suspension.
The investigation focuses on the level and valuation of unquoted securities in the funds.
Deutsche Bank has purchased some securities from the funds to protect investors' interests.
Industry sources estimate that Deutsche Bank may have spent around 150 million pounds on these securities.
Peter Young, the manager of two of the funds, has been suspended and replaced by Stuart Mitchell.

Halifax Building Society is Britain's largest mortgage lender.
Halifax announced its planned stock market flotation could be worth up to 12 billion pounds.
Halifax's chief executive is Mike Blackburn.
Halifax has assets exceeding 100 billion pounds.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is the flotation adviser for Halifax.
The estimated share price for the flotation is between 390 and 450 pence per share.
Analysts expect the market worth to be between 10.4 and 12 billion pounds.
Halifax has 6.7 million investing members and two million borrowing members.
Each qualifying member will receive a basic allocation of 200 shares.
The total number of shares in the flotation is 2.675 billion.

BZW is the investment banking arm of Barclays Plc.
BZW plans to use defence technology to manage risk in financial markets.
BZW has formed the Financial Laboratory Club to develop new risk management solutions.
The Defence Evaluation and Research Agency of the British Ministry of Defence is involved in the project.
The project has funding of 1.8 million pounds for the first two years.
Silicon Graphics, Royal Sun Alliance, the London Stock Exchange, City University and Business School, and Z/Yen are also involved in the project.
The British government is providing a grant of 750,000 pounds for the project.
BZW is contributing 500,000 pounds over two years.
Martin Dooney is the global head of money markets at BZW.
Dooney believes there are similarities between trading rooms and battlefields.

Northern Rock Building Society reported pretax profits of 167.5 million pounds for 1996, an increase of 14 percent from 147 million pounds the previous year.
Northern Rock plans to publish its transfer document detailing the flotation and preliminary valuation in the first week of March.
Members of Northern Rock will vote on plans to convert the institution into a bank in April.
Northern Rock's profit figures exclude a non-recurring cost of 10.3 million pounds related to the conversion to bank status.
Northern Rock will create a foundation to which it will covenant five percent of its annual pre-tax profits after flotation.
Predictions for the value in shares each member would receive from the flotation range between 750 and 1,000 pounds.
Northern Rock's cost to income ratio decreased to 33.1 percent at the end of 1996 from 33.5 percent at the end of 1995.
Net lending for Northern Rock rose 44 percent to 1.9 billion pounds in 1996 from 1.3 billion pounds in 1995.
Northern Rock's share in Britain's net mortgage lending market increased to 10 percent from eight percent.
Assets of Northern Rock grew 19 percent to 13.7 billion pounds in 1996 from 11.6 billion pounds in 1995.

Elizabeth Forsyth, a former aide of Polly Peck head Asil Nadir, was released from court after her appeal against a five-year sentence for handling stolen money was allowed by three judges.
Forsyth is 60 years old and is also appealing against her money-laundering conviction.
Forsyth described her 10 months in prison as an experience and thanked the court for its understanding.
The appeal judges stated that Forsyth would not return to Holloway prison, indicating that her sentence was disproportionate.
Lord Justice Beldam stated that Forsyth should not serve any longer considering the time she has already served.
Forsyth's lawyer, Geoffrey Robertson QC, made a bail application for her release pending the outcome of the rest of the appeal.
Forsyth has been in prison since March 1996 after receiving a severe sentence from Justice Sir Richard Tucker.
Forsyth was chairman of South Audley Management, a firm established by Asil Nadir for his family interests.
During her trial, the jury accepted that Forsyth helped launder money stolen from Polly Peck by Nadir.
Asil Nadir fled to northern Cyprus in 1993, skipping bail of 3.5 million pounds.

Czech leaders are discussing a surge in the trade deficit.
Analysts suggest a mix of macro and micro-economic fixes for the trade deficit.
Most analysts advise against devaluing the crown.
Some analysts believe the trade deficit is a necessary result of economic reform.
Imports increased by 15.2 percent and exports by 6.4 percent from January to August year-on-year.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus called a meeting to address the trade deficit, which was postponed.
The trade deficit reached a record 100 billion crowns ($3.68 billion) from January to August.
Forecasts indicate the current account deficit will grow to around six percent of GDP in 1996.
Analysts suggest that capital inflows could finance the deficit in the short term.
Vladimir Kreidl, an economist, recommends that the government aim for a budget surplus next year.

The Czech National Bank (CNB) has proposed merging Ceska Sporitelna with Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. (CSOB).
The new megabank resulting from the merger would be the largest in post-Communist Eastern Europe.
CNB spokesman Martin Svehla stated that the proposal is part of a plan to privatise major stakes in the 'Big Four' Czech banks.
The aim of the privatisation is to increase the competitiveness of banks and prepare them for foreign competition.
The CNB proposed delaying the privatisation of the new combined bank for three to five years to analyze the merger's effects.
The new bank would have combined assets of approximately 540 billion crowns ($20 billion), making it the largest bank in Eastern Europe.
The cabinet's schedule for debating the CNB proposals is unclear, but it may be discussed at the next government meeting.
Jack Schrantz, an equities analyst at Creditanstalt Prague, indicated that the merger would lead to staffing cuts due to overlap in departments.
The CNB plan includes quick privatisation of the state's 31.5 percent stake in Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB).
Nomura and Dutch ING NV are considered potential partners for IPB, but officials have not commented on their interest.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) cut its forecast for 1996 real gross domestic product (GDP) growth to 4.8 percent.
The CSU's revised GDP projection for 1996 is the same as the real result for 1995.
The CSU's previous GDP forecast for 1996 was 5.1 percent.
Czech GDP grew a real 4.3 percent in the first half of 1996.
The CSU expects full year 1997 real GDP growth to be between 5.1 to 5.6 percent.
The CSU revised its forecast for the full-year 1996 current account deficit to 6.9 percent of GDP.
The current account deficit is expected to grow to between 6.8 to 7.4 percent of GDP in 1997.
The merchandise trade deficit is projected to grow to 163.3 billion crowns by the end of 1996.
Export growth is expected to accelerate in 1997 to between 10.0 to 11.4 percent.
Import growth is projected to be between 14 to 16.2 percent in 1997.

The Czech government's tourism office forecasted record income from foreign visits in 1996.
Income from foreign visitors in the Czech Republic could exceed $3.5 billion in 1996.
This forecast is an increase from the record $2.87 billion in 1995.
Jiri Cech is the director of the Economics Ministry's tourism division.
The Czech National Bank will release balance of payment figures for the first half of the year in September.
The tourism component of the first quarter balance of payments showed a net inflow of $261 million.
Total tourism receipts in the first quarter were $581 million.
Analysts forecasted first half total tourism revenues at about $1.6 billion.
The overall current account posted a $505 million deficit in the first quarter.
The merchandise trade deficit contributed to the current account deficit.

Volkswagen AG's Czech unit, Skoda Auto a.s., launched sales of the new sedan, the Octavia.
Skoda Auto aims to improve its reputation regarding quality and achieve profitability with the Octavia.
The Octavia is built on a common VW platform designed for the 1998 Audi A3 and upgraded Golf.
The new model is Skoda's first post-Communist mid-sized car and will be available in showrooms worldwide.
Skoda's strategic markets include central and eastern Europe, western Europe, and some Asian markets.
Skoda expects to sell Octavias in all of its 66 markets.
The Octavia was well-received at showrooms in Prague, with crowds attending its launch.
The car will be available with three petrol and two diesel engines, with prices ranging from 335,700 crowns to 497,900 crowns.
Skoda plans to produce 64,000 Octavias in 1997 and increase production to 90,000 in 1998.
Skoda Chairman Ludvik Kalma expects 20,000 Octavias to be sold annually in the Czech market, with the remainder exported.

Czech analysts stated that the domination of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's party in the first-round Senate elections would have a neutral to mildly positive effect on local financial markets.
Analysts noted that thin voter turnout made it difficult for Klaus and his coalition to conclude that the electorate had returned to their favor after losing their majority in June.
Radek Maly, an economist at Citibank Prague, commented that the total voter turnout was insignificant for drawing conclusions.
Maly predicted a mild strengthening of the crown but did not expect any major movement in the currency.
The currency has recently traded around 26.9 to the dollar and 17.8 to the mark, approximately 2.5 percent above parity with the central bank's mark/dollar basket.
Maly emphasized that the market was more focused on macroeconomic fundamentals than on political influences.
Klaus's rightwing ODS party won 36.47 percent of the vote in the Senate elections, while the second place CSSD received 20.47 percent.
The ODS won three Senate seats outright in the first round by securing over 50 percent of the vote and placed 73 candidates in the runoff election.
Only 35 percent of the electorate voted in the Senate elections, a significant drop from over 70 percent in the June general elections.
Miroslav Nosal, an equities analyst at Patria Finance, stated that a premature general election was unlikely and that the stock market had concerns beyond party politics.

The Czech crown firmed from the central bank fixing on Thursday.
The strengthening of the crown followed a strong showing of the senior coalition party in Senate elections last weekend.
Analysts expect Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) to take a majority of the 81 seats in the newly-created Senate after runoff elections this weekend.
The crown was trading at 26.661 to the dollar and 17.757 to the mark on Thursday afternoon.
The crown was 3.05 percent above the Czech National Bank's dollar/mark basket.
Citibank economist Radek Maly stated that the ODS winning a majority in the Senate is fairly likely.
The ODS won three seats outright last Saturday and has 76 candidates in the runoff elections.
Despite a ballooning trade deficit, the crown has remained well above parity with the basket.
Maly predicted the currency would stay close to Thursday's levels and possibly strengthen further on Monday.
Petr Korous, a dealer at Ceskovslovenska Obchodni Banka, noted that the market was firming due to the ODS showing despite low voter turnout.

Czech pundits viewed the mid-November Senate elections as a potential solution to the political uncertainty following the June lower house elections.
The recent two-round Senate vote revealed that many Czechs are indifferent to the Senate.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and his centre-right coalition claimed that their victory, winning 52 of 81 Senate seats, provided a strong mandate for the minority cabinet.
Klaus criticized a headline in Mlada Fronta Dnes that described the election results as a political 'draw'.
Klaus's Civic Democratic Party won 32 Senate seats, despite having the potential to win 79 seats.
The coalition maintained control of the Senate due to a better-than-expected performance by its two junior partners.
The opposition Social Democrats, led by Milos Zeman, secured only 25 Senate seats after previously performing well in the June elections.
Voter turnout for the Senate elections was 30 percent, indicating limited public engagement.
Political analyst Jiri Pehe stated that the election results do not suggest a move toward early lower house elections.
Klaus asserted that the election results indicated the need for a functioning government rather than new elections.

In May 1945, seven-year-old Madlenka Korbelova listened to the radio in London with her father, an exiled Czech diplomat.
Madlenka and her father cheered when General George Patton's army liberated the brewery town of Pilsen from Nazi soldiers.
Madlenka and her father expressed frustration when Patton had to hold back his troops and allow the Red Army to take Prague.
Madlenka Korbelova is now known as Madeleine Albright.
Madeleine Albright was nominated as U.S. secretary of state, becoming the first woman to hold the position.
Albright returned to Prague after the Nazi occupation but left again after a Communist coup.
President Bill Clinton chose Albright to be the highest-ranking woman in the U.S. government.
Albright's father, Josef Korbel, was a close aide to Czechoslovak Foreign Minister Jan Masaryk during World War Two.
Josef Korbel served as post-war ambassador to Belgrade and later as a delegate to the United Nations.
After the Communist takeover in 1948, Josef Korbel sent a cable indicating he was leaving with his family on vacation.

Germany and the Czech Republic announced that a declaration on post-World War Two reconciliation would be initialled this week.
Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec and Germany's Klaus Kinkel are scheduled to sign the document in Prague on Friday.
The declaration expresses regret for Nazi atrocities during the war and the expulsion of ethnic Germans from former Czechoslovakia.
The declaration must be signed by the presidents of both countries and confirmed by their parliaments.
Germany's Christian Social Union (CSU) stated that its support for the text is not guaranteed.
CSU chairman Theo Waigel indicated that last-minute changes to the text could occur.
Final approval from the CSU depends on assurances regarding the involvement of Sudeten Germans in dialogue between Prague and Bonn.
The mainstream parties in the Czech parliament support the declaration, while the extreme-right Republican Party and far-left Communists oppose it.
Members of the Social Democrats expressed concerns about compensation for victims of Nazi aggression.
The Czech foreign ministry stated that Zieleniec and Kinkel would sign a protocol on the completion of negotiations of the Czech-German Declaration.

Volkswagen AG's Czech unit Skoda Automobilova a.s. launched the 'Octavia' sedan on Sunday.
The launch event took place in Prague's Old Town Square.
The Octavia is built on a common VW platform designed for the 1998 Audi A3 and upgraded Golf.
The Octavia will be tested internationally at the Paris International Auto Show in October.
Deliveries to Czech dealers are expected in November, followed by launches in European and other foreign markets.
Skoda aims to build on the success of its Felicia economy five-door hatchback with the Octavia.
The Octavia measures 4.51 metres in length, 1.73 metres in width, and 1.43 metres in height.
The design of the Octavia features modern but conservative lines.
Skoda's general director Ludvik Kalma stated that a price tag of 350,000 Czech crowns for the basic model would be 'too expensive'.
Skoda plans to produce approximately 5,000 Octavias before the end of this year and between 70,000 and 80,000 in 1997.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated that his ruling Civic Democratic Party (ODS) would end the governing coalition if partners supported opposition plans to lower the pension age and increase farm subsidies.
Klaus warned that adopting these plans could lead to a collapse of Czech post-Communist reforms.
Klaus claimed that the approval of certain laws would be interpreted as a basic threat to the post-Communist economic transformation.
Klaus indicated that if the Social Democrat plans were approved, ODS would have to leave the government.
ODS objected to a plan by the Social Democrats to increase state intervention in agriculture.
Klaus's party has been credited with fiscal prudence and currency stability, contributing to high investment ratings in post-Communist Europe.
Klaus described the current political situation in the country as very serious and unprecedented.
Klaus warned that passing the proposed laws would create an imbalance and burden for the budget, which would be unbearable for taxpayers.
Governments led by Klaus approved five consecutive balanced budgets before falling two seats short of a majority in the lower house of parliament.
KDU-CSL chairman Josef Lux stated that the ODS statement did not reflect reality and rejected the threats, but did not see it as a signal to end the coalition.

Czech President Vaclav Havel has been moved out of intensive care three weeks after surgery to remove a malignant tumour from his lung.
Havel will spend Christmas in the hospital according to doctors.
Dr. Pavel Pafko, head of Havel's medical team, stated that Havel has been moved to a standard-care room.
Havel's health is improving and there are no further complications.
Havel had surgery that removed half of his right lung and was previously fighting complications.
Havel was taken off a respirator late last week and has been able to speak occasionally.
Doctors reported that Havel's cancer was caught at an early stage and there is no sign of the disease spreading.
Pneumonia developed in Havel's other lung after surgery, but both the pneumonia and a high fever have subsided.
Havel entered the hospital on November 25 after his office announced he was fighting pneumonia.
Presidential spokesman Ladislav Spacek stated that Havel would write a shorter New Year's address than in previous years.

SkyePharma Plc is a fast-growing drug company in Britain.
SkyePharma's chairman and CEO is Ian Gowrie-Smith.
Ian Gowrie-Smith stated that 1998 would be a significant year for the company.
SkyePharma announced a reduction in pretax losses to 6.0 million stg in the six months to July.
The company was formed from the former tent hire company Black & Edgington.
SkyePharma's growth is based on acquisitions of Krypton Ltd and Jago Holdings AG.
Krypton Ltd holds a portfolio of generic drugs for the U.S. market.
