Jago Holdings AG specializes in controlled-release drug delivery.
The U.S. generic drug market is expected to grow rapidly.
SkyePharma has two drugs in Phase III trials and plans to start clinical trials on a non-CFC asthma inhaler next year.

Shares in Zeneca Group Plc increased on Thursday, reaching a record price of 17.25 pounds.
The rise in Zeneca's stock was attributed to speculation regarding Roche Holding AG's intentions.
Roche Holding AG named Franz Humer as its chief operating officer.
There is speculation that Humer wants Roche to not be subordinate to Glaxo Wellcome.
Traders noted that few people are willing to sell Zeneca stock due to potential takeover interest.
The potential takeover of Zeneca could be valued at $30 billion.
Peter Laing, an analyst at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull, stated that Zeneca shares have gained 37 percent this year.
SGST believes a hostile bid for Zeneca is unlikely at current valuations.
Some analysts believe Roche may be more interested in acquiring Schering-Plough Corp than Zeneca.
Schering-Plough Corp has a similar market capitalization to Zeneca.

New evidence about British Biotech Plc's anti-cancer treatment Marimastat will be presented next week.
British Biotech is making five presentations at the European Society of Medical Oncologists meeting in Vienna.
The presentations will include Marimastat's effects on ovarian, colo-rectal, pancreatic, and gastric cancer.
British Biotech will issue a general update on Monday morning.
The company is based in Oxford and is considered a bellwether for the U.K. biotech field.
Investor sentiment towards Marimastat significantly impacts the biotech sector.
Forecasts for Marimastat's annual sales range from a few hundred million dollars to up to $4 billion.
The data presented on Monday will come from patients who continued using Marimastat beyond Phase II clinical trials.
Yamaichi International analyst Erling Refsum hopes to see evidence of increased patient survival due to Marimastat.
Lehman Brothers analyst Ian Smith believes indications of Marimastat's effect on patient survival may be gleaned from the trials.

British Petroleum Co Plc (BP) reported its best-ever third quarter earnings.
Third-quarter net earnings for BP increased by 22 percent to 650 million pounds ($1.07 billion).
In the first nine months of the year, BP's net earnings rose by 28 percent to a record 1.93 billion pounds.
Strong oil prices, around $22 a barrel, boosted BP's earnings by between $400 million and $500 million in the third quarter.
Weaker profit margins in refining, marketing, and chemicals offset the earnings gains, accounting for about 27 percent of group net earnings.
Group chief executive John Browne stated that BP's profit increases were due to cost-cutting and efficiency drives adding $150 million to profit each quarter.
BP shares closed at 640.5 pence after adding two pence, following a high of 647 pence.
Trading in BP shares on the options market was active, with speculation of a sharp rise in BP shares.
BP's results contrasted with disappointing third-quarter figures from rival Royal Dutch/Shell Group, where profits fell due to low refining margins.
BP maintained a long-term view that oil prices would settle back into a range of $16 to $18 a barrel.

Dominion Resources Inc. announced it might bid for East Midlands Electricity Plc.
The potential bid for East Midlands Electricity Plc. could be worth about $2 billion.
Dominion Resources Inc. is based in Richmond, Virginia.
Dominion Resources Inc. owns the electric utility Virginia Power.
Dominion stated it would not offer a price much in excess of East Midlands' closing price.
East Midlands' share price increased by 70.5 British pence to close at 608 pence.
The value of East Midlands Electricity Plc. exceeded 1.2 billion pounds.
Dominion stock rose by 75 cents to $39.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
East Midlands has reportedly cut costs significantly and needs investment to grow.
Dominion Resources has a market capitalization of around $6.6 billion and annual sales of around $4.7 billion.

Analysts advised caution regarding rumors that Roche Holding is interested in acquiring SmithKline Beecham Plc.
Shares in SmithKline Beecham Plc increased by 30.5 pence to close at 788 pence.
Shares in Roche dropped by 140 Swiss francs to 9,830 francs.
Rumors suggested that Roche was attempting to assemble a funding package of up to 50 billion Swiss francs.
An unnamed analyst noted that Roche has frequently been mentioned as a potential suitor for Zeneca Group Plc.
Both Roche and SmithKline declined to comment on the acquisition speculation.
SmithKline had a market capitalization of approximately 21.3 billion stg at the close of trading.
Analysts indicated that a hostile bid for SmithKline would likely require a premium of 30 to 40 percent.
Roche has a market value of 95.1 billion Swiss francs and possesses around six billion Swiss francs in cash.
Paul Diggle from Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull stated that a merger between Roche and SmithKline is more feasible than a takeover.

Investors in the British biotechnology sector can expect volatility in 1997.
There are potential profits for investors who select their stocks carefully.
The biotechnology sector has experienced significant declines since its peak in May.
Analysts predict that 1997 will see companies publish data proving the effectiveness of their drugs.
British Biotech Plc is currently viewed positively due to its cancer treatment Marimastat.
Companies such as Biocompatibles International Plc, Celltech Group Plc, Chiroscience Group Plc, Cortecs International Ltd, and Scotia Holdings Plc are expected to succeed in 1997.
Other countries, particularly France and Germany, may begin to compete with Britain's biotechnology industry.
Britain has more biotechnology companies than the rest of Europe combined.
Lehman Brothers reported a 40 percent drop in biotech stock prices since May.
Despite the decline, biotech stocks have an overall gain of around 150 percent since February 1995.

Smith & Nephew Plc is expected to report a solid performance for 1996.
The company will announce full-year results on March 4.
Smith & Nephew reported that operating conditions and price pressures in the U.S. market remained difficult.
The company reported a 7.4 percent rise in first-half sales to 540 million stg.
Analysts expect full-year sales to increase by six to seven percent from 1.03 billion stg in 1995.
Sales in the U.S. market improved by two percent in the second half of the year.
Prices for Smith & Nephew's products in the U.S. are being pressured down by health providers.
Shares in Smith & Nephew rose 4 3/4 pence to 182 3/4 in early afternoon trading.
The stock reached record highs of 217 1/2 pence in June.
Analysts noted that the full picture on the Dermagraft product will not be available until April.

Britain's chemical industry is expected to experience steady growth in 1997.
The growth is supported by improvements in European economic prospects and lower stock levels.
Elliot Finer is the director-general of the Chemical Industries Association (CIA).
Finer stated that chemical stocks are currently low, which contributes to growth prospects.
Finer believes that the economic situation in Europe is better than previously anticipated.
The rest of Europe accounts for more than a quarter of British chemical output and half of all exports.
Finer noted that the disruption from German reunification is easing.
Finer expressed concern about the recent rise in the value of sterling, describing it as 'unpalatable.'
Britain's chemical industry is the third largest in Europe, with annual sales of 40 billion stg.
British chemical companies spend around three percent of turnover on research and development.

Budgens Plc expects to open 10 new wholly-owned stores in 1997.
Budgens Plc plans to increase its presence on petrol station forecourts.
Budgens Plc announced an 18 percent rise in first-half pretax profit to 5.04 million stg.
John von Spreckelsen is the chief executive of Budgens Plc.
Budgens Plc's sales rose by 8.1 percent to 183.0 million stg in the 28 weeks to November.
On a like-for-like basis, Budgens Plc's sales climbed 4.5 percent.
Sales growth for Budgens Plc slowed down in the run-up to Christmas.
Sales for Budgens Plc picked up again in January.
Shares in Budgens Plc were trading just 1/4 pence higher at 46 1/2 in early dealing on Monday.

Milumil babymilk powder was withdrawn from British stores and clinics due to a Salmonella poisoning scare.
Around 25,000 mothers in Britain and Ireland use Milumil babymilk powder.
Milupa, part of Nutricia NV, announced the withdrawal of Milumil milk powder due to an unconfirmed link with 12 cases of Salmonella.
Dennis Segal is the managing director of Milupa UK.
The company is in talks with the Irish government regarding the situation, although no incidents have been reported in Ireland.
The Department of Health identified 12 cases of Salmonella anatum infection in children under 12 months old linked to the consumption of Milumil.
Only two of the affected children were admitted to the hospital, and all have since recovered.
Parents and caregivers were advised to stop using Milumil immediately, and all stocks were ordered to be withdrawn.
Nutricia's shares were suspended for about an hour in Amsterdam after a sharp decline but later recovered some losses.
Sales of Milumil milk powder amount to between six and seven million pounds a year, with a market share of around five percent.

Britain's Imperial Tobacco Group Plc acquired Rizla International BV for 168 million pounds and assumed 17 million pounds of Rizla's debt.
Rizla International BV is based in the Netherlands and is the world's largest maker of handrolling tobacco papers.
Rizla employs more than 700 people in France, Belgium, and Wales.
Imperial Tobacco's chief executive is Gareth Davis.
Rizla has a large market share in seven or eight European countries.
Imperial Tobacco's shares rose by 9.5 pence to 394 following the acquisition announcement.
Rizla has approximately 66 percent of the world market share in branded handrolling papers.
Rizla was founded in 1796 and is active in more than 60 countries.
No job losses are anticipated as a result of the acquisition of Rizla by Imperial Tobacco.
Rizla will continue to operate as a separate division under its existing management.

The Ministry of Mines and Energy will investigate alleged involvement of drug kingpins in Colombia's oil industry.
A spokeswoman announced the investigation on Thursday.
Ecopetrol and a foreign multinational awarded multimillion-dollar service contracts to a company thought to be headed by Pastor Perafan.
The contracts awarded by Ecopetrol and the multinational date back to 1991 and were put out to bidding.
Margarita Mena, a former minister of Mines and Energy, stated that the Medellin drug cartel attempted to invest in Colombia's oil industry in the late 1980s.
Mena did not specify which companies were involved in the cartel's attempts.
The Ministry of Mines and Energy plans to form a special commission for the investigation.
Rodrigo Villamizar, the current Mines and Energy minister, is expected to formally launch the inquiry on October 22.
Villamizar was surprised by Mena's remarks during a congressional debate.
Cromos magazine reported on business ties between Ecopetrol, Occidental, and Inversismica, a company linked to Pastor Perafan.

Senator Luis Guillermo Giraldo stated that Colombia would remain a paradise for drug traffickers unless Congress overturned a 5-year-old ban on extradition.
Giraldo is a member of the ruling Liberal party and an opponent of President Ernesto Samper.
Giraldo proposed legislation to reactivate a 1979 extradition treaty with the United States.
The legislation faces a vote in a 12-member constitutional committee in the Senate.
Graffiti in Cali threatens those who support extradition.
Some legislators are influenced by the United States' argument that extradition is essential in the drug war.
Political analysts believe Colombia may not regain U.S. certification as an ally in the drug fight without reintroducing extradition.
President Ernesto Samper criticized Giraldo's bill as poorly timed and suggested focusing on tougher penalties for drug crimes.
Justice Minister Carlos Medellin supports renewing extradition.
Alfonso Valdivieso, chief prosecutor, has called for retroactive extradition, which may upset drug traffickers who surrendered for leniency.

Colombian truckers resumed work on Friday after a deal was signed with the government to end an 11-day strike.
The Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC) head is Javier Suarez.
The agreement includes a 16 percent increase in cargo freight rates and a promise of another inflation-linked increase next year.
The original demand from the truckers was for a 30 percent increase in freight rates.
The agreement was reached after Interior Minister Horacio Serpa threatened to use police and military to end the strike.
Suarez stated that the deal is a partial solution and will prevent truckers from operating at a loss.
A joint committee will be established to address future transport policies.
Key sectors of the economy criticized the transport paralysis but expressed relief at the agreement.
The coffee sector has been significantly affected, with 250,000 sacks of coffee delayed due to the strike.
Private coffee exporters indicated that many would default on delivery contracts even if the strike ended soon.

Colombia is moving closer to lifting its five-year ban on extradition.
A senator fled abroad to escape death threats from drug traffickers.
The Senate approved a draft law to overturn the constitutional ban on extradition.
Proposals for stiffer anti-drug laws in Congress have stagnated.
The Colombian government may bypass Congress to implement anti-drug measures by decree.
Colombia may be on the verge of a new terror campaign similar to that of Pablo Escobar.
A bomb was defused outside a chemical plant owned by relatives of Senator Claudia Blum in Cali.
A small bomb exploded outside government offices in Bogota.
Senator Claudia Blum has received regular death threats since mid-October.
Blum requested a leave of absence and left for the United States due to the threats.

British Petroleum Co Plc received a lukewarm reception to a Colombian proposal regarding the Piedemonte field.
The proposal was outlined by Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar.
The Piedemonte field is estimated to contain between 600 million and one billion barrels of crude oil and condensates.
BP has identified three hydrocarbon formations in the Piedemonte field: Volcanera, Pauto, and Florena.
These formations account for about 15 percent of the total area of the Piedemonte field.
The proposal would require BP to return rights to 85 percent of the Piedemonte field that is still unexplored.
Ecopetrol would re-award BP half of that area under improved contract terms if the proposal is accepted.
BP's Colombian subsidiary stated that the proposal would mean losing access to a large portion of the Piedemonte field.
Under the existing Piedemonte association contract, profits are divided equally between BP and Ecopetrol while production is below 60 million barrels.
Ecopetrol's share of profits increases as production rises, reaching 76 percent at 150 million barrels.

At least 23 people were murdered in attacks in central and northern Colombia.
An entire family was hacked to death with machetes in San Miguel de Sema, Boyaca province.
Three children, their mother, and grandparents were killed by unidentified assailants.
Police chief Col. Humberto Prieto stated that the killings may be related to the death of two relatives several years ago.
Prieto suggested that the murders were likely a revenge attack.
Boyaca province is known as a stronghold of right-wing paramilitary groups.
Prieto indicated that San Miguel was not affected by political violence.
In northern Sucre province, the bodies of 17 peasants were found in four isolated areas near Tolu Viejo.
Benjamin Irragori, regional head of the state security service DAS, reported that two fronts of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) were active in Sucre.
Sucre has experienced a recent increase in attacks by right-wing paramilitary death squads.

Colombian lawmakers met on Thursday to discuss a bill aimed at seizing drug barons' fortunes.
An 11-member conference committee is debating whether to override the lower house of Congress.
The House of Representatives voted 59-57 to reject a 20-year time limit for seizing criminal assets.
The Senate had previously approved the 20-year time limit for asset seizure.
The conference committee was convened under pressure from President Ernesto Samper and senior ministers.
They criticized the lower house's decision as a 'virtual amnesty' and warned of potential U.S. economic sanctions.
The committee is expected to support the government and recommend reinstating the 20-year time limit.
Colombia's business community has called for Congress to approve an asset forfeiture law with a 20-year clause.
The United States decertified Colombia as an ally in the drug war in March.
The U.S. withdrew President Samper's entry visa due to allegations of drug cartel financing in his election campaign.

At least four people were killed and many others were injured in Monteria, Colombia, due to a bomb explosion.
The explosion occurred at 3:15 p.m. at the headquarters of the Fondo Ganadero.
Police are unaware of the motive behind the attack in Monteria.
The blast in Monteria followed a car bomb explosion in Medellin that killed one woman and injured 48 people.
Authorities attributed the Medellin attack to drug traffickers working with leftist guerrillas.
Provincial governor Carlos Buelvas stated that it is too early to determine responsibility for the Monteria attack.
An emergency meeting of the provincial security council will be convened to assess the situation.
The Monteria blast was the second in the town in two months.
An earlier bomb explosion in Monteria on October 21 injured 10 people and was blamed on the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).
It is unclear if the recent bomb in Monteria is connected to a statement from a group called the Special Anti-paramilitary Commando.

John Naranjo is the commercial manager of Colombia's national Coffee Growers' Federation.
Naranjo stated that no decision would be made on the ACPC export retention plan until an emergency meeting in Brazil in January.
Brazilian traders have reacted coolly to the suggestion of expanding the ACPC export retention plan.
A Brazilian exporter suggested that Colombia's proposal may be a bluff, indicating doubts about Colombia's coffee supply.
The ACPC members agreed in May to limit green coffee exports to 53.5 million 60-kg sacks until June 1997.
Ivory Coast Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauza and Abel Rwendeire of Uganda called for an additional cut of 2.5 million 60-kg sacks in the first half of next year.
Colombia supported the call for an additional cut in coffee exports.
Colombia is forecast to export 11.5 million 60-kg sacks in the 1996-97 coffee year.
The impact of an increase in the ACPC export retention plan on Colombia's exports in the first half of 1997 is unclear.
Armando Montenegro, head of the National Association of Financial Institutions (ANIF), predicted 1997 would be a year of transition in Colombia's coffee sector.

Rescuers are recovering bodies from a bus wreck in the Colombian Andes.
The bus crash resulted in the deaths of 37 people, all from a single extended family.
Three passengers survived the crash, including a nine-month-old baby.
The bus fell into a 1,500-foot chasm in Narino province on Friday morning.
More than 50 volunteers participated in the rescue efforts.
Rescue operations were complicated by extreme mountain conditions, thick fog, and intermittent rain.
It takes at least two hours to recover each body from the ravine.
Red Cross spokesman Mario Arias stated that it could take three more days to recover all victims.
The bus was traveling from Cali to Tumaco when it swerved off the road to avoid fallen rocks.
The deceased worked in a small, family-run shoe factory.

Icy relations between Colombia and Washington are improving.
Colombia aims to change its status as an international drug pariah by spring.
Colombia was decertified by the U.S. due to lax anti-narcotics laws and alleged ties of President Ernesto Samper with drug lords.
The decertification led to a reduction in U.S. aid to Colombia.
U.S. Ambassador Myles Frechette praised the Colombian government for its teamwork in anti-drug efforts.
Frechette's comments were made at a funeral for a U.S. pilot killed on an anti-drug mission in Colombia.
Colombian authorities hope that the appointment of Juan Carlos Esguerra as ambassador to Washington will help regain U.S. certification.
Colombia has implemented a drug crop eradication program and a new law targeting cocaine kingpins' assets.
Col. Leonardo Gallego stated that Colombia is committed to combating narco-trafficking.
Former Justice Minister Enrique Parejo expressed skepticism about Colombia's commitment to fighting drug cartels.

Gilberto Rodriguez Orejuela was sentenced to 21 years in prison.
Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela was sentenced to 18 years in prison.
The sentences were halved due to the brothers pleading guilty.
Gilberto Rodriguez was fined $8 million.
Miguel Rodriguez was fined $4.4 million.
The Rodriguez brothers are eligible for additional sentence reductions for working and studying in prison.
U.S. Ambassador Myles Frechette called the sentences 'totally unacceptable.'
The public prosecutor's office in Colombia plans to appeal the sentences.
Gilberto Rodriguez led the Cali drug cartel until his capture in June 1995.
The Rodriguez brothers supplied an estimated 80 percent of the world's cocaine.

Colombia will announce cuts in coffee exports next week under a retention plan agreed by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).
Jorge Cardenas is the head of the National Coffee Growers' Federation.
Colombia's internal coffee price will be raised due to recent gains in international markets.
The specific timing and percentage of the internal price hike have not been disclosed.
Coffee growers in Colombia are concerned about potential crop damage from recent heavy rainfall.
Rainfall levels have increased by up to 160 percent compared to the seasonal average.
The ACPC deal established a reduction of total exports by 1.3 million bags in the first half of 1997.
The original export target was set at 26.28 million bags in May.
Robusta-producing countries will cut one million bags, while Colombia will reduce exports by 300,000 bags.
Cardenas did not specify the proportion of the cut that would apply to Colombia.

Blenheim is a British-based exhibitions group.
Analysts believe Blenheim is a good fit for United News & Media.
Reed Elsevier is considered a rival to United News & Media for Blenheim.
Industry sources suggest Reed Elsevier is no longer in the running to acquire Blenheim.
Blenheim has a strong presence in Europe, particularly in France.
The exhibitions business is performing well at this stage in the cycle.
Dutch publisher VNU acquired a 15 percent stake in Blenheim for 500 pence per share.
VNU stated its 15 percent stake in Blenheim is a strategic long-term investment.
Clive Hollick, chief executive of United News, is reportedly considering a bid of up to 520 pence per share for Blenheim.
Blenheim shares closed at 477.5 pence on Monday.

United News & Media made an agreed offer valuing Blenheim at 592.5 million pounds ($935 million).
The deal will create the world's largest trade exhibition group with a turnover of more than 500 million pounds based on 1995 figures.
United News & Media secured acceptances for 51 percent of Blenheim after offering five pounds per share.
United chief executive Clive Hollick stated that the acquisition will be earnings-enhancing in the first full year.
United News shares increased by 30 pence to 683-1/2 pence after the announcement.
Blenheim shares gained 23 pence to 496-1/2 pence after the announcement.
Dutch publisher VNU, which acquired a 15 percent stake in Blenheim, will not make a counter bid and is likely to sell its stake.
Anglo-Dutch media group Reed-Elsevier dropped out of the running for Blenheim.
French utilities group Compagnie Generale des Eaux plans to sell its 15 percent stake in Blenheim following United's offer.
Blenheim operates more than 170 exhibitions worldwide but does not have a significant publishing portfolio.

Shares in Pearson Plc decreased on Thursday following the appointment of Marjorie Scardino as chief executive.
Marjorie Scardino is currently the chief executive of The Economist Group, which is half owned by Pearson.
Scardino will succeed Frank Barlow as chief executive at the end of the year.
Dennis Stevenson is a non-executive director and will become deputy chairman and then chairman at Pearson's annual meeting next May.
The appointment of Scardino concludes a period of uncertainty regarding Barlow's succession.
Market players expressed skepticism about Scardino's appointment due to her relative obscurity.
Pearson's shares fell to a low of 668 pence before recovering to 678 pence, resulting in a loss of 10 pence.
A report indicated that Pearson had resolved tax concerns related to selling its stake in BSkyB but faced challenges in separating holdings.
Pearson's indirect stake in BSkyB is valued at approximately 440 million pounds at the current share price.
Pearson has a market capitalization of nearly four billion pounds and operates in various media and leisure sectors.

Analysts believe that Merchant banking and Madame Tussaud's may no longer be necessary for Pearson Plc.
Pearson Plc is transitioning from an industrial conglomerate to a focused media enterprise.
Marjorie Scardino will become the chief executive of Pearson in January.
Analysts state that Pearson's overall profit performance is inadequate.
Mark Beilby of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell commented on the imprecise definition of Pearson's three core business areas: Information, Education, and Entertainment.
Analysts suggest that Pearson may need to sell high-value assets to concentrate on specific areas.
Reed Elsevier is cited as a successful example of a media company that has identified key market areas.
Pearson's market capitalization is approximately four billion stg.
Pearson's 50 percent stake in Lazard Brothers is considered a candidate for disposal.
Louise Barton of Henderson Crosthwaite indicated that selling Lazards could help Pearson become a more genuine media company.

BSkyB is considering further investment in Germany.
BSkyB will broadcast its second pay-per-view sports event in Britain on November 9.
BSkyB reported a pre-tax profit increase of 31 percent to 66 million pounds for the three months ending September 30.
BSkyB had a total of 5.65 million paying subscribers as of September 30, with a net increase of 146,000 for the quarter.
BSkyB's operating revenues for the three months to September 30 increased to 266 million pounds, a rise of 24 percent from the previous year.
Earnings per share for BSkyB were 3.9 pence, which is a 30 percent increase.
BSkyB shares rose by 4 pence to 582.5 pence.
BSkyB announced plans to take a stake of up to 49 percent in DF1, a German digital television venture.
BSkyB plans to introduce digital satellite broadcasting in Britain late next year.
BSkyB launched two niche channels, Sky Scottish and The Computer Channel, bringing the total number of channels on Sky Television to over forty.

British Telecom and MCI Communications Corp. are in talks for a $22 billion merger.
The merger would create the world's second largest telecoms group.
BT scheduled a news conference for 8 a.m. EST on Sunday at its Central London headquarters.
Executives from BT and MCI were in separate board meetings on Saturday.
MCI is the second largest long-distance phone company in the U.S.
BT has a 20 percent stake in MCI and operates a joint venture called Concert.
Analysts speculate the price for MCI could be $40 a share, valuing the company at $28 billion.
BT would pay approximately $22.1 billion for the remaining 80 percent of MCI.
The deal would be the second largest involving a U.S. company.
BT and MCI have stated there are no guarantees that an agreement will be reached.

The Office of Fair Trading (OFT) launched a probe into how travel companies sell foreign package holidays to British consumers.
John Bridgeman is the director-general of the OFT.
The probe includes an inquiry into ownership links between tour operators Thomson and Airtours and retail travel agents.
The Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) will investigate discount practices among travel agents related to specific travel insurance purchases.
Shares in Airtours fell almost 10 percent in London, losing 69p to 644p.
Bridgeman expressed concern that practices of vertically-integrated companies like Thomson and Airtours could distort competition.
Thomson owns the Lunn Poly travel agency, and Airtours owns the Going Places travel agency.
Thomson and Airtours together operate around 40 percent of British travel agents.
Thomson and Airtours supply approximately 45 percent of over 10 million foreign packages sold to British consumers.
Paul Brett, chairman and chief executive of Thomson Travel, stated that Thomson is confident it will be vindicated from allegations of anti-competitive practices.

Camelot LOTT.CN reported lower interim profits due to a decline in scratchcard sales by over 450 million pounds.
Camelot's chief executive is Tim Holley.
A second weekly National Lottery draw is scheduled to launch on February 5 and will occur every Wednesday thereafter.
Camelot reported pre-tax profits of 31.5 million pounds on sales of 2.1 billion pounds for the 24 weeks ending September 14.
This is a decrease from the previous year's pre-tax profit of 36.2 million pounds and sales of 2.51 billion pounds.
Camelot's five shareholding companies shared a total dividend payout of 10 million pounds, an increase from 9.5 million pounds.
Sales for the weekly National Lottery game increased by two percent to 1.68 billion pounds.
Two thirds of the adult population in Britain regularly purchase tickets for the Saturday draw.
Sales of Camelot's 'Instants' scratchcards decreased from 871 million pounds last year to 419 million pounds this year.
Camelot stated that over one billion pounds, or 50 percent of turnover, was distributed in prize money in the first half of the year.

Britain's Ladbroke Group and the U.S. Hilton Hotels Corp (HHC) announced an alliance to reunite the Hilton hotel brand globally.
The reunion of the Hilton brand is the first since 1964.
Steve Bollenbach is the chief executive officer of HHC.
Bollenbach stated that the alliance will eliminate customer confusion and benefit millions of customers worldwide.
HHC owns the Hilton name in the United States, while Ladbroke holds the rights elsewhere through its Hilton International (HIC) subsidiary.
The two companies signed an outline agreement to unify the Hilton brand, which was separated in 1964.
Ladbroke acquired HIC in 1987.
The alliance includes 400 hotels in 49 countries, and HHC and HIC plan to cooperate on sales, marketing, loyalty programs, and hotel development starting next year.
Ladbroke reported first half pre-tax profits of 72.8 million pounds, a 29 percent increase from the previous year.
HHC intends to acquire a five percent stake in Ladbroke once the final agreement is signed.

EMAP Plc ended a boardroom dispute by ousting two non-executive directors.
Shareholders voted to remove Ken Simmonds and Joe Cooke at an extraordinary general meeting.
More than 109.2 million votes were cast in favor of the resolutions to remove the directors.
Chairman Sir John Hoskyns stated that the board would be united after the resolutions passed.
Simmonds had been a non-executive director of EMAP for 15 years.
Simmonds expressed a conciliatory tone after the dispute, stating that EMAP would continue to be great.
EMAP shares increased by 5p to 735p after the resolution vote.
The dispute involved changes to the company's articles regarding non-executive directors and board majority rules.
EMAP reported a pre-tax profit of 50.6 million pounds in the first half of its current financial year.
Hoskyns denied reports that he supported Robin Miller as his successor.

Carlton Communications Plc reported a 20 percent annual profit rise.
Carlton plans to expand into pay television as a content provider and operator.
Carlton aims to build on its broadcasting strengths in a multi-channel future.
Chairman Michael Green stated that free television and pay channels are complementary businesses.
Carlton's pre-tax profit rose to 295 million pounds for the year ending September 30.
Carlton increased its dividend by 17.5 percent to 11.1 pence per share.
Carlton agreed to pay 85 million pounds for Westcountry Television.
Carlton operates ITV licenses for the English Midlands and London weekday television.
Carlton broadcasts to 22 million people.
Carlton is considering investing in digital terrestrial television, expected to launch in Britain in 1998.

Pearson is a British media and leisure firm.
Pearson is awaiting the arrival of a new chief executive.
Pearson shares gained 25p to 714 1/2p by 1300 GMT after a trading statement.
Analysts stated that the trading statement contained no unpleasant surprises.
Marjorie Scardino will become Pearson's chief executive in January.
Scardino will be the first woman to head one of Britain's top 100 companies.
Scardino is moving from the 50-percent Pearson-owned Economist Group.
Many share analysts believe Pearson has not completed its transition to a focused media company.
Analysts expect Scardino may sell off Pearson's merchant banking interests and Tussauds Group.
Pearson has a 50 percent stake in London merchant bank Lazard Brothers.

Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc launched Caverject, an anti-impotence drug.
Pharmacia & Upjohn initiated a marketing program that included contacting Time magazine, Newsweek, Smithsonian, New Yorker, and over 50 other national publications and radio stations.
These publications and stations are participating in a consumer awareness campaign about impotence funded by Pharmacia & Upjohn.
U.S. consumers are receiving numerous advertisements for health problems and prescription drugs.
Advertising spending on prescription drugs in U.S. media reached $323 million in the first six months of 1996.
This spending was compared to $356.8 million for the entire year of 1995, according to Competitive Media Reporting.
Robert Pondiscio, a spokesman for Time Warner, stated that prescription drug advertising is a growing category for Time magazine and news magazines.
Time magazine published a 90-page special issue titled 'Frontiers of Medicine' that was largely funded by Glaxo Wellcome Plc.
The spread of direct-to-consumer prescription drug advertising is seen as a victory for drug companies.
The American Medical Association opposes direct-to-consumer prescription drug advertising.

Outboard Marine Corp chief executive Harry Bowman spoke with Alfred Kingsley and Gary Duberstein of Greenway Partners.
Greenway Partners purchased an 8.5-percent stake in Outboard Marine Corp for nearly $30 million.
Stan Main is the spokesman for Outboard Marine Corp.
Greenway Partners specializes in buying shares in struggling companies and pressuring management for changes.
Greenway has a history of seeking significant changes in companies they invest in.
Kingsley confirmed that he had a conversation with Outboard Marine Corp about the company and its operations.
Kingsley expressed interest in Outboard Marine Corp's new FICHT fuel injection technology.
Kingsley indicated that Outboard Marine Corp is likely not satisfied with its financial performance.
Outboard Marine Corp has acknowledged its financial difficulties and is developing a plan to address them.
Outboard Marine Corp reported a loss of $0.18 per share in its third quarter ended June 30.

Guidant Corp shares closed down 2-7/8 to 46-1/2 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Guidant chief executive Ronald Dollens stated that lower than expected third quarter sales growth may explain the decline in share price.
Sales increased by 11 percent in the third quarter compared to the same period last year.
Last quarter, Guidant's sales were up 18 percent.
Dollens indicated that sales would have increased by 13 percent without the negative impact of exchange rate translations.
Approximately 39 percent of Guidant's sales are in non-U.S. markets.
Unfavorable exchange rates had the most significant impact in Japan during the third quarter.
Guidant reported earnings of $41.2 million, or $0.57 per share, on sales of $260.1 million.
A year prior, Guidant's earnings were $28 million, or $0.39 per share, on sales of $234.1 million.
Earnings increased by 47 percent and were above analysts' expectations.

U.S. hospital management and nursing home companies are expected to post mixed results in the third quarter.
Big hospital companies are outperforming non-profits and achieving high profit margins despite cost and competitive pressures.
The average gain expected from the top five hospital firms is 17.6 percent, according to First Call estimates.
Analyst Joel Ray from Wheat First stated that margins in these companies have not deteriorated due to market share gains, cost control, and efficiency.
The proposed merger of Tenet HealthCare and OrNda HealthCorp is valued at $1.8 billion and will create the second-largest hospital company in the U.S.
Integrated Health Services Inc acquired First American Health Care of Georgia, the largest privately held home healthcare company in the U.S.
The nursing home and post-acute care market is less concentrated than the hospital business, leading to a mixed profit outlook for the third quarter.
Analyst Jean Swenson from Alex. Brown & Sons indicated that profit results will vary widely.
Vencor and Genesis Health Ventures are expected to report significant profit gains, while Beverly Enterprises and Horizon/CMS Healthcare are forecasted to have weak results.
Challenges for the hospital and nursing home sectors include upward wage pressure due to low unemployment and ongoing debates over Medicare reimbursement rates.

St. Jude Medical Inc. agreed to make four strategic transactions to enhance its position in the medical device business.
The total value of the transactions is $665 million.
St. Jude's stock fell $1.25 to $37.375 after the announcement of the transactions.
St. Jude agreed to buy Ventritex Inc. in a stock swap valued at $505 million.
Ventritex is the smallest of three companies in the implantable defibrillator market.
The implantable defibrillator market is valued at $500 million.
St. Jude is making three smaller deals to resolve legal actions and cross-licensing restrictions related to Ventritex.
St. Jude agreed to buy assets from Telectronics Pacing Systems, acquire Medtel, and buy intellectual property rights from SulzerMedica's Intermedics unit.
St. Jude is the world's largest maker of heart valves.
St. Jude's chief executive Ronald Matricaria previously acquired Pacesetter Inc. for $500 million in 1994.

Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co, also known as 3M, is based in St. Paul, Minnesota.
3M reported strong third quarter sales and earnings growth compared to the previous year.
3M's shares increased by 2-1/8 to 73-3/8 following an earnings report that exceeded analysts' estimates.
Analyst John Franck from PNC Institutional Investment Services noted that it had been a long time since 3M beat any estimate.
3M's third-quarter sales increased by 7.5 percent and profits increased by 17.4 percent.
Douglas Christopher, an analyst at Crowell Weedon, stated that the spinoff of Imation has allowed 3M to meet investor expectations.
Imation Corp began operations as an independent company on July 1, 3M's data storage and imaging businesses were spun off.
3M reported third-quarter profits of $398 million, or $0.95 per share, on sales of $3.62 billion.
3M expects solid growth in the fourth quarter following its recent performance.
More than half of 3M's business is conducted outside the United States.

U.S. consumers are showing little interest in the latest home computers.
Home PC sales in the U.S. were weak in October, according to major electronics retailers.
Analysts believe there are few signs of recovery in PC sales without lower prices or a technology breakthrough.
Terrence McEvoy, an analyst at Janney Montgomery Scott, noted that PC purchases have suddenly decreased.
Mail-order computer vendors and sellers of computers to businesses are thriving despite the overall market decline.
Edward Lee, an analyst at Robertson Stephens, stated that the market is shifting from first-time buyers to repeat customers.
The pool of entry-level buyers in the PC industry is contracting.
Veteran buyers are looking for vendors that offer many peripherals.
Best Buy reported a 15 percent decline in same-store sales in October compared to the previous year.
Circuit City experienced a nine percent decline in same-store sales in October.

Monsanto Co. announced it will spin off its chemicals business.
The spin-off will allow Monsanto to focus on its agriculture, food, and healthcare units.
The transaction will result in the elimination of between 1,500 and 2,500 jobs.
Monsanto expects to take a fourth-quarter charge against earnings of $400 million to $600 million due to the spin-off.
Monsanto's annual sales are approximately $8.9 billion.
Monsanto's products include Roundup weed killer, NutraSweet sweetener, carpet fibers, and drugs for treating arthritis and insomnia.
Monsanto Chairman Robert Shapiro will lead the company after the spin-off.
Executive Vice President Robert Potter will run the new chemicals company.
Monsanto employs 28,500 people worldwide.
The anticipated job cuts will reduce the workforce by 5 percent to 9 percent.

In 1997, U.S. medical device manufacturers will face pressure from customers to reduce prices.
The largest firms in the medical device sector are expected to show healthy growth in 1997.
David Kessler recently resigned as U.S. Food and Drug Administration Commissioner.
The White House has not yet named a successor to David Kessler.
The approval of new medical products may be affected by the appointment of Kessler's replacement.
Current Congressional and White House sentiment on healthcare reform is lukewarm.
Health maintenance organizations and hospitals are pressuring medical device manufacturers for lower prices.
This pressure has negatively impacted profits and limited growth potential for some medical device companies.
Many medical device companies are seeking growth opportunities overseas.
Companies with global reach, such as Medtronic Inc, Boston Scientific Corp, and Guidant Corp, are expected to perform well in 1997.

Major retailers reported mixed results for the holiday sales season.
Stocks of major retailers dropped on Wall Street following the reports.
Morgan Stanley retailing analyst Bruce Missett stated that the holiday season showed moderate growth.
UBS Securities retailing analyst Annie Erner noted nervousness about retailer reports affecting stock prices.
J.C. Penney reported total sales of $3.6 billion for the four weeks ended Dec. 28, a 23.2 percent increase from the previous year.
Same-store sales at J.C. Penney increased 6.2 percent over the previous year.
J.C. Penney expected fourth-quarter earnings to fall short of Wall Street expectations.
Dayton Hudson reported a 4.2 percent increase in same-store sales across its department stores, Target, and Mervyn's.
Dayton Hudson's department store sales increased 0.3 percent, Mervyn's sales decreased 4.1 percent, and Target sales rose 7.1 percent.
Carson Pirie reported a 12.8 percent increase in sales to $194.1 million for the four-week period.

General Instrument Corp. plans to split into three companies through a tax-free spin-off to shareholders.
The move is intended to boost the company's stock market value.
Wall Street welcomed the spin-off as a way to unlock the value of General Instrument's core high-tech communications business.
NextLevel Systems Inc. will be created from General Instrument's cable television, satellite, and telephone business.
CommScope Inc. will be formed from General Instrument's coaxial cable manufacturing business.
General Semiconductor Inc. will be established from General Instrument's units that make electronic components.
General Instrument will incur an after-tax charge against earnings of $55 million to $65 million for the fourth quarter due to the breakup.
The fourth-quarter charges will mainly consist of costs related to the transition to digital products and restructuring costs.
General Instrument expects fourth-quarter earnings to be in the range of 28 cents to 32 cents a share, excluding the charges.
Last year, General Instrument reported net earnings of $53.5 million, or 43 cents per share, in its fiscal fourth quarter.

Ford Motor Co is considering selling its interests in Budget Rent a Car.
Budget Rent a Car is the sixth-largest rental car agency in the United States.
If Ford sells Budget, it would be the fifth major rental agency to change ownership since 1994.
WEFA Group automotive consultant George Magliano stated that the car rental business is not profitable.
Jon LeSage, editor of Auto Rental News, noted that there is new interest in the car rental business from investors.
Ford has not confirmed a report about selling Budget to Team Rental Group Inc for $350 million.
Budget spokeswoman Kimberly Mulcahy stated that Ford does not own Budget outright but controls it through an option to purchase shares.
Ford announced plans to exercise its option to buy Budget's common shares last year.
Analysts believe that the deal for Ford to sell Budget may be uncertain due to a U.S. Federal Trade Commission antitrust review.
Ford began investing in Hertz in 1987 and purchased all of Hertz in 1994.

Shareholders are pushing for change at WMX Technologies Inc.
A major investor is proposing that WMX hire investment bankers to examine further sales of non-core assets.
Lens Inc has hired an executive recruiter to assemble an alternate slate of nominees for four WMX board seats.
The board seats include WMX chairman Dean Buntrock's seat.
WMX is the largest U.S. garbage hauler with $10 billion in annual revenues.
WMX has been under investor pressure for several months.
Shareholders demanding changes include Lens, headed by Robert Monks, and billionaire George Soros.
WMX has responded to shareholder pressure by repurchasing shares and selling parts of its business.
The sales have raised about $1 billion in cash.
WMX's stock price has not significantly changed despite these actions.

Australian oil and gas companies are being acquired by foreign companies seeking undervalued stocks.
Analysts predict a positive outlook for the sector due to higher oil prices and a deregulated gas market.
In 1996, approximately A$2.5 billion worth of takeovers were announced in Australia's oil and gas sector.
An additional A$600 million worth of asset sales occurred as some non-oil and gas companies exited the local market.
Local oil companies with low share prices and overseas assets are attracting foreign interest.
Timothy Savage, an analyst at Hartley Poynton, stated that overseas investors recognize the value of oil and gas assets, especially in Southeast Asia.
Mobil Corp made a A$1.78 billion bid for Ampolex Ltd in February, marking the largest bid in the sector for that year.
Clyde Petroleum Plc acquired Crusader Ltd, and Premier Oil Plc and Cairn Energy Plc made bids for Discovery Petroleum NL and Command Petroleum Ltd, respectively.
Stuart Baker, an analyst with BT Securities, noted that companies with offshore oil assets have been the primary targets for takeovers.
Baker indicated that the rise in oil prices was not the primary driver of corporate activity in the sector.

Rupert Murdoch intends to use sports broadcasting rights to dominate pay television markets in Asia and globally.
Murdoch believes that purchasing sports broadcasting rights will allow him to enter the world's sporting establishment.
Murdoch stated that sports are more influential than film and other entertainment genres.
News Corp has acquired long-term rights to major sporting events in most countries.
News Corp has invested significantly in sports programming rights over the last five years.
News Corp formed a worldwide sports programming joint venture with Tele-Communications Inc and Liberty Media in January.
News Corp established an Asian sports programming joint venture with ESPN.
Murdoch emphasized the importance of sports and plans to invest in long-term rights.
Murdoch stated that football is the most important sport.
News Corp has purchased rights for the NFL in the U.S. and Premier League soccer in the UK.

Rupert Murdoch is an Australian-born mogul who transformed his father's newspaper business into a global media empire.
Murdoch is preparing the next generation to succeed him in his business.
Murdoch's eldest son Lachlan and daughter Elisabeth will focus on digital technology and multi-channel television satellites.
Murdoch believes that television will drive the next stage of growth for News Corporation Ltd.
The television business generates the most revenue among News Corp's five main operations, which include newspapers, magazines, films, and book publishing.
News Corp recorded total revenues of A$13.0 billion (US$10.27 billion) for the year ending June 30, 1996.
Elisabeth previously owned and operated two TV stations in California before joining British Sky Broadcasting Plc (BSkyB).
Murdoch's other son James and daughter Prudence are not involved in the family business.
Murdoch's wife Anna is on the board of News, which is approximately 32-percent owned by the Murdoch family.
Elisabeth was appointed head of programming at BSkyB in October.

Optus Communications is Australia's second largest telephone carrier.
Optus reported its first annual profit of A$60.3 million for the year ending June 30, 1996.
In the previous year, Optus had a loss of A$17.0 million.
Telecommunications analysts expected Optus to deliver a profit between A$55 million and A$65 million.
Optus experienced a revenue growth of 36 percent to A$1.94 billion in 1995/96.
Optus is 24.5 percent owned by U.S. BellSouth Corp and Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc.
Optus plans to achieve A$2.0 billion in revenue for 1995/96.
Optus is expected to make its sharemarket debut by the end of 1996.
The float is expected to raise around A$1.5 billion.
The Australian government plans to raise A$8.0 billion from the sale of one-third of Telstra in 1997/98.

Boral Ltd reported a poor start to the 1996/97 year due to weakness in the Australian housing market.
Chairman Peter Cottrell stated that Boral's operating profit in the first four months of 1996/97 was in line with budget but 20 percent below the previous year.
Cottrell indicated that first half earnings for 1996/97 would be above the second half of 1995/96.
Boral's net profit for 1995/96 fell by 30 percent to A$205.69 million.
Sales for Boral decreased to A$4.69 billion in the year ending June 30, 1996, down from A$4.94 billion the previous year.
Cottrell announced a dividend payment of 7.5 cents per share for the six months ended December 31, 1996.
Boral reduced its second half dividend for 1995/96 to 7.5 cents per share from 10.5 cents per share.
Boral's total dividend for 1995/96 decreased to 18 cents per share from 21 cents the previous year.
Cottrell expressed optimism about a recovery in demand for home building materials in the second half of 1996/97.

Westpac Banking Group is Australia's second largest bank.
Westpac renewed its interest in Asia through an alliance with Standard Chartered Bank.
Westpac had previously sold several of its Asian units 3-1/2 years prior to this alliance.
The alliance indicates Westpac's intention to expand in Asia after a period of withdrawal.
Westpac and Standard Chartered will share banking services for medium-to-large scale corporate customers.
The primary markets for the alliance are Australia, New Zealand, and Asia.
Westpac's chief executive Bob Joss stated that the initiative is important for Westpac's future growth.
Standard Chartered's group chief executive Malcolm Williamson expressed commitment to the new relationship.
The venture will initially focus on Singapore, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Thailand, and Malaysia.
The banks expect the alliance to generate a rapidly growing revenue stream.

Placer Dome Inc is pursuing takeover bids for Placer Pacific Ltd and Highlands Gold Ltd.
Analysts believe the takeover bids are likely to be successful.
A successful takeover would give Placer Dome control of the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea.
David Kauler, a gold mining analyst at ANZ Securities, expressed confidence in the success of the bids.
Placer Dome acquired a 33 percent stake in Highlands before launching a bid of 75 cents per share.
Placer Dome is offering one of its shares for every 15 shares of Placer Pacific.
The offer for Highlands represents a 36 percent premium over the share price on November 26.
The offer for the 24.6 percent of Placer Pacific not owned by Placer Dome represents a 50 percent premium over the November 26 price.
Shares of Placer Pacific and Highlands increased in value after the takeover offers were announced.
Analysts do not expect Placer Dome to raise its bid prices for either company.

The Australian dollar has recently surged.
Higher jet fuel prices are expected to negatively impact exporters of fresh food.
Brian Lovell is the chief executive of the Australian Federation of International Forwarders (AFIF).
Lovell stated that perishables will be the hardest hit among exporters.
Fresh food exports from Australia primarily go to Asian countries.
Exporters with contracts signed before the recent freight rate hike may struggle to meet obligations.
Some exporters may find themselves unable to fulfill binding contracts due to increased costs.
Many AFIF members were surprised by the freight rate increases from local air carriers.
Qantas Airways Ltd has raised its jet fuel surcharge, while Ansett Airlines Ltd has not changed its freight rates.
The Australian dollar has increased by four percent to US$0.8000 over the past five months.

Federal Airports Corp (FAC) is an Australian government-owned airport operator.
Barry Murphy is the chief executive officer of FAC.
FAC plans to privatise its 22 airports.
Murphy stated that FAC would cease to exist if all 22 airports are sold to other owners.
FAC is developing a service group called FAC Airport Consultancy.
FAC Airport Consultancy aims to have 20 to 30 specialists in aviation and property management.
FAC Airport Consultancy intends to sell services to remaining airports and new airport owners.
The Australian government has shortlisted 10 consortiums for bidding in the first sale phase.
The first sale phase includes 50-year leases for Melbourne, Brisbane, and Perth airports, expected to be sold in early 1997.
The sale of the Adelaide lease was delayed for an upgrade.

United Parcel Service (UPS) could start flying its own planes to Australia if growth in the Australian market continues at the current rate.
UPS started serving Australia in 1991.
UPS currently uses commercial airlines to carry packages in and out of Australia.
UPS general manager Australia Terry Hales stated that the realization of flying its own planes to Australia is possible within the next five years.
UPS does not currently use its own planes to fly to Australia due to insufficient export business from the country.
Australia imports four times as much air freight as it exports.
UPS projects a 34 percent growth in revenue for calendar year 1997 from Australia.
The import business is expected to grow at a rate of seven to eight percent.
UPS uses Australia as a service center rather than a hub for the Asia Pacific.
UPS is spending US$400 million on its Asia Pacific hub terminal in Taiwan.

The Australian Stock Exchange's transport sector is expected to see modest gains over the next year.
The transport index rose about 30 percent during 1996.
The broader market increased six percent in 1996.
Paul Xavier is a transport analyst at BNP Equities.
Brambles Industries Ltd and Mayne Nickless Ltd make up more than half of the transport sector.
Andrew Mullholland is a transport analyst at Pru-Bache Securities.
The transport sector has significantly outperformed in the last 12 months.
TNT Ltd was taken over by Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV through a friendly A$2 billion bid.
Mayne Nickless plans to sell its 25 percent stake in Optus Communications in 1997.
Qantas Airways Ltd's share price has underperformed compared to the transport sector.

Placer Dome Inc agreed to a deal with Highlands Gold Ltd regarding the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea.
The deal gives Placer Dome control of the Porgera gold mine and resolves a dispute between the two companies.
Highlands Gold Ltd will remain a listed company and can continue developing projects in Papua New Guinea.
Placer Dome will pay Highlands A$316.1 million to acquire Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera mine.
The Porgera mine produced an estimated 850,000 ounces of gold in calendar 1996.
Placer Dome previously offered A$276.8 million for the same stake in the Porgera mine.
Highlands managing director Ian Goddard expressed satisfaction with the deal.
The restructuring plan involves cancelling all shares in Highlands except those held by Placer Dome.
Shareholders of Highlands will receive a capital return of 65 cents cash per share and one share in Highlands Pacific.
Highlands will create a new company, Highlands Pacific Ltd, which will hold various projects in Papua New Guinea and Indonesia.

Analysts expect UK electronic business information company M.A.I.D Plc to launch new screen-based products.
M.A.I.D Plc declined to comment on a report about new online products that would undercut Reuters Holdings Plc and Bloomberg LP.
M.A.I.D executives are on a roadshow in the U.S. for about a week.
A company spokesman stated that M.A.I.D does not comment on market speculation regarding product development.
The Sunday Times reported that M.A.I.D is poised to unveil a screen-based real-time news service at lower prices than Reuters or Bloomberg.
Other potential products from M.A.I.D could include transmitting financial data to hand-held devices using mobile-telephone technology.
Analysts have heard of a potential deal between M.A.I.D and Finnish group Nokia for a mobile share price service.
Experts expect a similar deal between M.A.I.D and Psion Plc.
Keith Woolcock, an analyst at Merrill Lynch, stated that M.A.I.D and Reuters will compete more in the future.
Reuters Business Briefing currently offers mainly online business news and share price data, while about 70 percent of M.A.I.D's data is market research information.

British Telecom (BT) announced a $20 billion merger with MCI Communications.
The merger is named Concert Plc and positions BT as a leader in the telecoms market.
BT holds a 20 percent stake in MCI prior to the merger.
The merger is part of BT's strategy to expand internationally as global markets liberalize.
BT has six joint ventures in the top six European markets valued at $135 billion.
The merger aims to enhance BT's access to the corporate market for long-distance calls, data, and mobile services.
BT will distribute a special dividend of 2.2 billion pounds ($3.6 billion) to its 2.4 million shareholders.
The U.S. telecoms market is valued at $200 billion, which BT aims to penetrate.
Concert is projected to have annual revenues exceeding 25 billion pounds.
MCI has a 20-22 percent share of the U.S. long-distance telephone market and operates the largest Internet backbone in the U.S.

British Telecom announced a $20 billion merger with MCI Corp.
The merger positions British Telecom as the second largest company in the international telecoms market.
The new entity formed from the merger will be called Concert Plc.
Concert Plc will serve 43 million customers in 70 countries.
MCI is the second largest long-distance phone company in the U.S. after AT&T Corp.
The merger is pending regulatory approval in both the U.S. and the U.K.
MCI shareholders will receive up to 2.3 billion pounds in cash and new Concert American Depositary Shares.
For each MCI share, investors will receive 5.4 new BT shares and $6.0 in cash.
BT will distribute a special dividend of 2.2 billion pounds to its shareholders.
BT already owns 20 percent of MCI.

Shares in Cable and Wireless, Britain's second biggest telecoms group, lost value on Tuesday.
Analysts stated that the creation of Anglo-U.S. Concert Plc posed a significant challenge to Cable and Wireless.
Cable and Wireless relies on its Hong Kong subsidiary, Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, for about 75 percent of its attributable profits.
The Hong Kong unit's net profits increased by 12.1 percent to HK$5.39 billion, which was below some analysts' expectations.
Cable and Wireless' shares ended five pence lower at 470.5p.
Executives of Cable and Wireless' Hong Kong unit claimed they were unconcerned by the merger between British Telecommunications and MCI Communications.
Analysts indicated that the merger created a $54 billion company and posed a substantial threat to telecom rivals.
Cable and Wireless' U.S. operation generates annual revenues of about 0.5 billion pounds.
British Telecommunications' annual revenue is now approximately $18 billion.
Analysts believe that Cable and Wireless is difficult to value due to its Hong Kong stake.

British Telecommunications Plc reported second quarter profits that exceeded analyst forecasts.
BT's profits before tax rose 7.4 percent in the second quarter and 5.2 percent in the first half.
After accounting for a 235 million pound redundancy charge and a 60 million pound charge for bond repurchase, half year pretax profits were 1.6 billion pounds.
BT's second quarter pretax profits were 730 million pounds, which was slightly below the figures for the same periods in 1995.
Chairman Sir Iain Vallance stated that there was sustained high growth in demand for telephony services.
BT's shares increased by 8.5 pence to 369 pence during heavy trading.
BT maintained its 20.5 million residential customer lines over the past year despite competition predictions.
Inland calls, BT's largest business segment, grew one percent to over seven percent in the quarter on a 12 month moving average basis.
Finance director Robert Brace reported a 4.5 percent increase in turnover to 7.37 billion pounds over six months.
BT has formed six joint ventures worth $135 billion to access European markets.

Vodafone Group is Britain's biggest mobile phones firm.
Vodafone posted a 21 percent rise in first half profits.
Vodafone expects the mobile market to maintain a growth rate of 20-25 percent next year.
Vodafone announced it is buying The People's Phone Company for about 77 million pounds.
Vodafone is licensed to serve over 250 million people in 13 countries.
Vodafone has five wholly-owned service providers and investments in another four.
Vodafone's pretax profits in the first half of the year rose to 252 million pounds.
Vodafone's sales in the first half of the year were 771.5 million pounds, a 16 percent increase.
Vodafone's dividend increased by 20 percent to 2.36p per share.
Vodafone had 2,654,000 subscribers in its core British market at the end of September 1996.

Airtours reported record pretax profits of 86.8 million pounds for the year ending in September, a 46.1 percent increase from the previous year.
The company's earnings per share increased by 39 percent to 45.63 pence.
Airtours raised its dividends for the year by 14.3 percent to 16 pence.
Bookings for Airtours rose by 57.2 percent compared to the previous year.
Winter bookings increased by 12.6 percent in Britain, 92 percent in Scandinavia, and 58.9 percent in Canada.
David Crossland, chairman and chief executive of Airtours, predicted a positive outlook for the company's major markets.
Airtours's shares increased by nine pence to 712 pence despite a weak market trend.
The company plans to spend between 200 and 250 million pounds on acquisitions.
Airtours has a balance sheet with about 425 million pounds in cash and its dividends are covered more than three times by earnings.
The company's record profits were attributed to strong results from its Scandinavian operations and careful pricing strategies in Britain.

Institutional investors in Northern Electric indicated they would likely sell their shares if instructed by the company.
Northern Electric operates in northeast England.
Northern Electric was expected to announce its decision regarding CE Electric's bid of 782 million pounds ($1.3 billion) within 72 hours.
CE Electric declared its bid unconditional after securing a 50.3 percent majority of acceptances.
A fund manager from an institution stated that the offered price was too low and they were awaiting Northern's judgment.
Another institutional investor expressed doubt about retaining its stake and indicated that selling would be their normal procedure.
Northern Electric previously fought off a hostile bid last year, becoming the only one of the 12 regional electricity companies to do so.
The Prudential Corp attempted to defeat the takeover by persuading investors to sell their shares to them instead of accepting CE Electric's offer.
CE Electric aims to acquire at least 90 percent of the shares to conduct a compulsory purchase of the remaining shares.
A CalEnergy spokesman commented on the implications of shareholders deciding not to accept the offer.

British Telecommunications (BT) downplayed talks with Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT).
Analysts speculated that BT and NTT might be negotiating a deal.
BT has been courting NTT with its American partner MCI Communications.
A BT spokesman stated that the meeting with NTT was not significant and that regular contacts would continue.
Some analysts believe BT is interested in entering Asian telecom markets through NTT.
John Tysoe, a telecoms analyst, suggested that a deal between BT and NTT might be close.
Another analyst made a bet that a deal would be signed or announced before the end of February.
Chris McFadden, an analyst at Merrill Lynch, expected something to happen within the next 12-18 months.
Analysts dismissed NTT's statement about preferring to expand independently as a 'courtship ritual'.
Analysts believe NTT will want to control any deal and may prefer multiple global alliances.

Angry British businesses expressed dismay after news of another overhaul of telephone prefixes.
Telecommunications watchdog Oftel announced plans to create billions of new phone numbers.
Britain has barely recovered from 'PhONEday' in April 1995, when the last batch of new numbers was created.
Simon Sperryn, chief executive of the London Chamber of Commerce & Industry, stated that the changes mean more disruption and cost to businesses.
PhONEday cost British Telecommunications 100 million pounds.
Companies have to pay thousands of pounds to notify business contacts and change stationery and logos when numbers change.
London dialing codes will be lengthened by a uniform 020 prefix in the year 2000.
The current London codes of 0171 and 0181 will be shortened to 7 and 8, respectively.
Northern Ireland, Cardiff, and southern English coastal cities will each get a new prefix starting with 02.
Prefixes of 03 to 06 are being kept for future generations.

Misys is a software supplier based in Britain with a valuation of 950 million pounds ($1.5 billion).
Misys posted record half-year results and is considering up to five international acquisition targets worth up to $30 million each.
Chairman Kevin Lomax stated that Misys is interested in businesses operating within a strong international financial services market.
Misys supplies software to 12,000 banks with 4,000 separate installations.
Misys has 18.7 million pounds in cash and low debt levels, providing room for further acquisitions.
Misys announced a planned $60 million acquisition of Summit Systems, a New York company specializing in financial derivatives trading software.
The group raised pretax profits by 23 percent to 23.7 million pounds on revenues of 129.5 million pounds, which is 10 percent higher than the previous half year.
Misys's shares have more than doubled in the last 12 months, increasing from 567 pence to 1140 pence.
Lomax believes that acquiring regional software companies could create significant shareholder value.
In international banking, Misys is three to five times larger than its competitors.

Schroders Plc reported a first-half pretax profit of 115.9 million pounds ($181.5 million) compared to 85.6 million pounds in 1995.
Schroders Plc warned that conditions for its businesses may become more uncertain due to imminent elections in the U.S. and UK.
The bank lifted its half-year dividend by 33 percent to 6.0 pence.
Analysts expected Schroders to report pretax profits between 106-125 million pounds.
Schroders' shares fell 57.5 pence to 13.90 pounds following the cautious outlook announcement.
Profits at Schroders' investment banking arm rose to 50.7 million pounds from 41.7 million pounds.
Earnings from Schroders' securities businesses in North America and Europe grew satisfactorily.
Activity in Schroders' Asia/Pacific operations was more subdued.
Total funds under management at Schroders rose 13 percent to 83.4 billion pounds.
Pretax profit in Schroders' asset management division increased to 65.2 million pounds from 43.9 million pounds in the same period last year.

Shareholders in Anglo-American conglomerate Hanson approved the final plank of its four-way demerger.
About 98 percent of shareholders voted for the motion to spin off the Energy Group division.
Hanson announced its decision to demerge into separate companies in January due to stock market mistrust of conglomerates.
Energy Group's chairman Derek Bonham expressed satisfaction with the outcome of the shareholder vote.
Energy Group plans to be listed in London and New York and is considering acquisitions in Britain and North America.
The potential acquisitions could be worth up to 1.4 billion pounds ($2.3 billion).
The Energy Group is expected to start with a market value of around 2.8 billion pounds and will have 1.4 billion pounds of debt.
Energy is expected to rank among Britain's FTSE 100 companies and America's Fortune 500.
Bonham stated that there would not be a further sub-demerger of Peabody Coal and Eastern Group.
Energy executives aim for the company to be viewed as a growth stock rather than a utility.

Most U.S. software publishers are expected to report modest increases in their third-quarter earnings.
The modest increases are attributed to a seasonal slowdown and a lack of new products this quarter.
Marshall Senk is an analyst at Robertson Stephens & Co in San Francisco.
Senk stated that business is still good for major companies like Microsoft Corp and Oracle Corp.
Summer is identified as the slow buying season for most of the software industry.
Analysts expect Microsoft to report substantially higher earnings for its first quarter of fiscal 1997.
Microsoft's expected earnings are supported by strong sales of its networking software and business programs.
Microsoft is scheduled to report its results on October 21.
Better-than-expected sales of personal computers will contribute to Microsoft's revenue.
Microsoft makes about a quarter of its revenue from the sale of its Windows family of operating systems.

Apple Computer Inc. reported a $25 million profit for the last three months of its fiscal year.
Analysts had expected Apple to report a loss of 30 cents a share.
Apple posted a profit of 20 cents a share, its first quarterly profit this year.
In the same quarter a year ago, Apple had a net income of $60 million, or 12 cents a share.
The most recent quarter's operating results included a gain of $17 million.
Fourth-quarter revenue for fiscal 1996 declined 23 percent to $2.32 billion from $3 billion.
Apple's shares increased by as much as $4.25 to $30 a share in after-hours trading.
The profit was attributed to aggressive cost cutting, a larger-than-expected employee exodus, and lower prices for key components.
Fred Anderson, Apple's chief financial officer, expects costs to increase only slightly in the December quarter.
Apple reported huge losses in the past three quarters due to declining Macintosh sales and competition from Windows PCs.

Vantive Corp.'s stock dropped by 24 percent on Friday.
The decline was due to the company's expectation of slowing revenue growth in the next two quarters because of a shortage of sales staff.
This warning was issued one day after Vantive reported better than expected third-quarter earnings.
Vantive, located in Santa Clara, Calif., closed at $31.50 on Nasdaq trading with a loss of $9.25.
4.5 million shares of Vantive were traded on that day.
Vantive develops software that assists large companies like Hewlett-Packard Co. and Motorola Inc. in managing customer relationships.
Vantive's revenue has more than doubled in recent quarters due to increased demand for its customer-service products.
In the third quarter ending September 30, Vantive's income increased to $3.17 million, or 12 cents a share, from $632,000, or 3 cents, a year earlier.
Third-quarter revenue rose to $11.1 million from $4.29 million, driven by strong software sales and service contracts.
Vantive executives indicated that revenue in the next two quarters will be flat to slightly higher compared to the third quarter.

Microsoft Corp. will unveil a set of software technologies on Monday that facilitates software creation for sharing information through networks.
Microsoft executives, including Chairman Bill Gates, will discuss development plans for the Windows family of operating systems at an event in Los Angeles.
Microsoft will encourage programmers to write commercial software based on its standards at the Professional Developers Conference.
Oracle Corp. is holding a conference in San Francisco the same week to promote its approach to writing programs for information sharing through networks.
Both Microsoft and Oracle have been updating their key applications and networking software to function on the Internet and intranets.
The technology Microsoft will unveil will reduce the need for programmers to understand complex programming techniques related to Windows operating systems.
Analysts believe Microsoft's new technology will encourage developers to create more commercial products based on Windows NT networking operating system.
Oracle will also unveil tools for writing intranet software that accesses information stored in Oracle databases on the same day.
Corporate programmers have developed extensive libraries of software using Oracle's products.
Oracle's new programming tools will allow programmers to convert existing libraries to work on the Web.

Apple Computer Inc executives showcased products and technology for business computer users.
Apple reaffirmed its commitment to corporate markets.
Apple Chief Operating Officer Marco Landi spoke at a software trade show.
Apple plans to allocate resources to improve compatibility of Macintosh with rival systems from Microsoft Corp, Sun Microsystems Inc, and International Business Machines Corp.
Apple has faced challenges in selling its machines to large corporations.
Large corporations prefer machines with Intel Corp computer chips running Microsoft software.
Apple will release software and computers that can access information from large corporate databases.
Landi assured programmers that their investment in Apple technology is secure.
Apple executives demonstrated network servers for data storage and distribution using Oracle database management software.
Apple demonstrated HotSauce technology, which aims to simplify database searches for average users.

Intuit Inc is a financial software company.
Intuit has been the subject of buyout speculation since May 1995.
Microsoft Corp abandoned its plans to acquire Intuit in 1995.
Intuit shares recently increased due to speculation about an offer from American Express Co.
Many industry analysts believe Intuit's future does not include a merger.
David Farina, an analyst at William Blair, believes Intuit can maximize its value independently.
Intuit's key product is Quicken, which helps users manage personal finances.
Intuit relies on partnerships with banks and brokerages for online banking services.
Scott Cook, Intuit's chairman, stated that the company would not become dependent on a single financial institution.
Analysts question whether Intuit can compete with Microsoft in the long term.

At this year's Comdex computer trade show, corporate computer buyers are the most sought-after individuals.
Personal computer makers and software vendors are relying on corporate customers to compensate for disappointing consumer sales.
Many consumers are delaying computer purchases until early 1997 when new gadgets are expected to be released.
Corporate customers are purchasing new machines that can run the latest business software from Microsoft.
Michael Winkler, senior vice president at Compaq Computer Corp., stated that a major upgrade cycle is occurring.
Winkler predicted that the fourth quarter would be excellent for business.
The release of Microsoft's Windows NT operating system and Office 97 is driving corporate sales.
Domestic PC shipments in the fourth quarter are expected to rise 20 percent to 8 million units, according to International Data Corp.
Jim McDonnell, a group marketing manager of PCs at Hewlett-Packard Co., expressed a strong outlook for 1997.
Stocks of most PC makers have increased recently, including Compaq, IBM, Intel, and Sun Microsystems.

Apple Computer Inc. agreed to acquire NeXT Software Inc. for $400 million.
The acquisition reunites Apple with its co-founder, Steven Jobs.
The acquisition will provide Apple with software technology to improve the Macintosh personal computer.
Apple's Macintosh has lost technological appeal compared to PCs running Microsoft software.
Apple Chief Financial Officer Fred Anderson stated the company will pay $350 million in cash and stock for NeXT.
Apple will also pay off NeXT's $50 million debt.
Steven Jobs will return to Apple part-time to lead software development for the Macintosh.
Jobs will report to Apple Chairman Gilbert Amelio.
Apple plans to base its next-generation operating system on NeXT's technology.
NeXT's technology is expected to attract more software developers to create titles for the Macintosh.

CompUSA Inc. warned about weak Christmas sales on Thursday.
CompUSA expects a small rise in sales in the fourth quarter due to weak PC sales.
CompUSA is based in Dallas and is traditionally a healthy PC retailer.
CompUSA is the third major PC retailer to report a weak outlook in two weeks.
Scott Miller, an analyst at Dataquest Inc., stated that the situation is not a good sign.
Stock in Compaq Computer Corp. fell to $72.375.
Dell Computer Corp. stock decreased to $51.25.
Intel Corp. stock declined to $130.375.
Analysts reported that PC companies focused on home users had a disappointing year.
There were no compelling new technologies in 1996 to drive consumer sales.

Apple Computer Inc. Chairman Gilbert Amelio stated that the company's three-year turnaround plan is still on track.
