Apple announced it will report a first-quarter operating loss of up to $150 million.
Amelio spoke at the MacWorld trade show to Macintosh computer enthusiasts.
Amelio called on several computer industry executives to support the Macintosh.
Amelio assured Mac customers of a smooth transition as Apple improves its finances and software.
Apple has been struggling to stop financial losses, develop new software, and increase revenues.
Apple's three-year plan aims to stop financial losses in 1996, develop new products in 1997, and increase revenues in 1998.
Amelio has implemented cost-cutting measures since becoming chairman a year ago.
Apple agreed to buy NeXT Software Inc. for $400 million to assist in software revamping.
Apple plans to provide regular upgrades to its current operating system while developing a new operating system called 'Rhapsody.'

Apple Computer Inc. reported a $120 million loss in the first quarter of fiscal 1997.
Apple does not expect to return to profitability until September 1997.
The loss was attributed to slow sales of Performa desktop computers during the Christmas quarter.
The loss of $120 million equaled 96 cents a share, compared to a loss of $69 million, or 56 cents a share, in the previous year.
Sales for the first fiscal quarter ended on December 27 fell to $2.13 billion from $3.15 billion.
Apple plans to develop additional restructuring programs during the second quarter.
The goal of the restructuring programs is to reduce the break-even point to $8 billion in annual revenues.
Apple expects to return to profitability by the fourth fiscal quarter, which ends on September 26, 1997.
Apple exited the quarter with $1.8 billion in cash.
There was a 15 percent sequential increase in high-end Power Macintosh sales.

Synopsys Inc. agreed to buy Epic Design Technology Inc. for about $428.1 million in stock.
The acquisition aims to gain expertise in semiconductor design.
Synopsys will issue 0.7485 of its shares for each of Epic's 13.7 million shares outstanding.
Based on Synopsys's closing stock price of $41.75, the payment for each Epic share is about $31.25.
Shares of Epic fell 87.5 cents to $31 in late Nasdaq trading.
Shares of Synopsys remained unchanged at $41.75 on Nasdaq.
Synopsys specializes in software for designing the overall framework of microchips.
Epic specializes in software for designing individual microscopic circuits.
The acquisition is expected to give Synopsys an edge in the design automation industry.
Epic will become a unit of Synopsys, with Sang Wang as the head of the unit.

Toronto stocks ended firmer on Friday, adding 10 points to the week's gains of 90 points.
The Toronto Stock Exchange key 300 Composite Index rose 10.9 points to end at 5193.0 points on Friday.
The TSE 300 has recovered from its lows in July and is climbing towards its all-time high of 5248.37 points.
MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie stated that the market is ignoring bad news.
Canada's central bank cut short-term interest rates by 25 basis points, easing the key bank rate to 4.25 percent.
Analysts believe the interest rate cut will help maintain interest in Toronto's bank issues.
Investors picked up heavily weighted gold stocks as gold prices approached US$400 on New York's COMEX.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indices rose, led by golds, forestry products, base metals, and transports.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declining ones 481 to 371, while 310 stocks traded flat.
Meridian Gold Inc. rose C0.30 to C$6.20 on more than two million shares, topping Toronto's most actives list.

Canadian consumers are expected to spend similarly to last year during the holiday season.
Frank Anderson is a partner at Arthur Andersen and heads the firm's consumer products division.
In 1995, Canadian retailers experienced one of their worst holiday seasons in recent years.
An unseasonably cool spring in 1996 negatively impacted sales for Canadian retailers.
58 percent of survey respondents indicated they would spend the same amount as last year.
28 percent of respondents forecast lower spending for the holiday season.
14 percent of respondents said they would spend more than last year.
The survey conducted by Arthur Andersen and Le Groupe Mallette Maheu polled 1,220 Canadians in October.
The survey results were similar to last year's poll regarding spending expectations.
Canadians are prioritizing paying down debt over increased spending due to concerns about job security.

Investors helped drive the Toronto Stock Exchange to its 50th record close this year.
Michael Metz is the chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co Inc in New York.
Toronto's key 300 Composite Index set its 50th record high close last Thursday.
The previous record for annual record closes was 45 in 1987.
The 300 index has risen almost 19 percent this year.

A survey indicates that 3 percent of Canadians with Internet access plan to buy holiday gifts online.
Augustin Manchon is a retail and consumer business consultant who commented on the survey results.

Metz believes the Toronto Stock Exchange is in the middle of a bull market.

China is not expected to be in the international market for sugar before mid-1997 due to high stocks and recovering domestic prices.
A lack of cash among state-run sugar processors could affect farmers' willingness to grow sugar cane.
China had up to two million tonnes of processed sugar in reserve after imports in 1995.
The actual figure of China's sugar reserves is considered a state secret.
China's sugar demand has not significantly increased over recent years.
China's economy in 1996 has not been strong, affecting sugar consumption.
Sugar is not considered an essential item in China.
The bulk of the Chinese sugar market is industrial.
Central authorities are expected to maintain tight control over the sugar industry.
A crackdown on smuggling has helped bring control back to the sugar industry.

China has banned imports of some U.S. chicken meat due to concerns about a fowl plague.
U.S. officials stated that their chickens do not have highly pathogenic avian influenza.
A U.S. quarantine official confirmed that there is no record of highly pathogenic avian influenza in domestic poultry.
Highly pathogenic avian influenza was eradicated in the U.S. after an outbreak in the 1980s.
The U.S. Agriculture attache in Beijing confirmed that China blocked imports of chicken meat from 10 U.S. states.
U.S. sources in Beijing reported that no written notification about the ban was received from China's Administration of Animal and Plant Quarantine (CAPQ).
A senior diplomatic source described the ban as unexpected.
Embassy officials planned to meet with Ministry of Agriculture officials regarding the ban.
A quarantine official in Beijing confirmed the ban on chicken imports but did not provide details.
The ban could significantly impact U.S. poultry exports to China, which were valued at US$445 million in 1995.

China has banned imports of poultry from 10 U.S. states due to concerns about a fowl plague.
The ban affects an export market valued at approximately $500 million annually.
The affected U.S. states are Arkansas, Florida, Maryland, Utah, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Texas, and Wisconsin.
Chinese authorities are concerned that the poultry products may carry highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI).
HPAI has not been found in the U.S. since 1984, according to a U.S. embassy official.
There is confusion among Chinese quarantine officials regarding the distinction between HPAI and avian influenza (AI).
The AI virus can be found worldwide, especially in wild fowl, but has not been isolated from commercial poultry flocks in the U.S.
China is the second-largest market for U.S. poultry products, following Russia.
China is the only market for U.S. chicken feet.
In 1995, U.S. poultry exports to China totaled 330,000 tons, worth $445 million.

Chinese buyers of soybeans and soybean meal are defaulting or canceling contracts due to falling international prices.
A trader in Hong Kong stated that they have stopped doing business with Chinese buyers for now.
Traders in Hong Kong, Singapore, and China reported that Chinese soymeal buyers are delaying finance arrangements to negotiate lower prices.
Chinese buyers have defaulted on three to four cargoes of soymeal, each weighing 50,000 tonnes, since international prices began to fall.
Chinese buyers are delaying the opening of letters of credit in hopes of reducing prices by two or three dollars.
Traders indicated that physical soymeal for prompt delivery is in tight supply and commands a premium.
Chinese traders have developed a reputation for dubious payment practices since entering international trading.
Some Chinese buyers default on or cancel orders if prices fall after the order is placed.
Traders reported that maximum Chinese orders of U.S. soybean meal in the past two weeks were 300,000 tonnes.
The price of soybean meal on the Chicago Board of Trade has fluctuated significantly since late September.

Chile is the world's biggest copper exporter.
China is the world's biggest copper importer.
Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Mariano Fernandez stated that Chile hopes to establish close trade and technical support ties with China.
Fernandez mentioned that there is Chinese interest in participating in mining projects in Chile.
Chile has an interest in participating in service and technology in copper mining in China.
In 1995, Chile's total mining exports were worth US$7.85 billion, with $280 million earned from copper sales to China.
Chile produced 2.512 million tonnes of copper in 1995.
Chile holds 25 percent of the world's copper reserves.
Copper accounted for 36.4 percent of Chile's total exports in 1995, which were valued at $16.5 billion.
China's demand for copper in 1996 was officially estimated at one million tonnes.

Wheat is unlikely to be affected by the tensions between Beijing and Washington over U.S. arms sales to Taiwan.
Higher grain production in China is reducing the need for wheat imports.
A U.S. trader stated that there may be no business with China for the rest of the year.
China's domestic wheat crop for 1996/97 is expected to reach a record 107 million tonnes, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture revised China's total wheat imports downward to eight million tonnes.
Beijing opposes the sale of weapons to Taiwan, which it considers a renegade province.
China has demanded that the United States cancel its arms sales plans to Taiwan.
China has canceled approximately 1.4 million tonnes of wheat orders from the United States since early June.
China is expected to maintain its traditional level of wheat imports from Canada at around five million tonnes per year.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman expressed optimism that China will continue to buy U.S. wheat.

China has approved corn exports but set a minimum selling price of US$170 per tonne.
The world price for corn is currently around $140-150 per tonne.
Traders report that the high minimum price is preventing sales of Chinese corn.
COFCO executives indicated that the government has agreed in principle to export two million tonnes of corn.
There is no written confirmation of the export agreement from the government.
U.S. corn is arriving at Asian ports at $145 per tonne, including cargo and freight.
Traders believe it would have been more beneficial to issue export licenses earlier when Chinese corn prices were lower.
Farmers in China are complaining about a lack of funds to purchase fertilizer due to the export restrictions.
Traders expect corn prices to continue falling due to a large anticipated U.S. harvest.
China is projected to have a record corn crop of 115-120 million tonnes and has around 30 million tonnes in storage.

Wheat is unlikely to be affected by the tensions between Beijing and Washington over U.S. arms sales to Taiwan.
Higher grain production in China is reducing the need for wheat imports.
A U.S. trader stated that there may be no business with China for the rest of the year.
China's domestic wheat crop is expected to be good, leading to cancellations of many orders.
China's wheat production for the 1996/97 season is expected to reach a record 107 million tonnes, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture revised China's total wheat imports downward by one million tonnes to eight million tonnes.
Beijing opposes the sale of weapons to Taiwan and has demanded the U.S. cancel its arms sales plans.
Sino-U.S. relations have fluctuated due to various disputes, including human rights and nuclear proliferation.
China has canceled approximately 1.4 million tonnes of wheat orders from the U.S. since early June.
China is expected to maintain its traditional wheat imports from Canada at around five million tonnes per year.

Some Chinese traders are selling copper to take advantage of rising world copper prices.
A rise in copper stocks in London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouses in Singapore is partly attributed to Chinese selling.
Stocks in Singapore rose by 5,000 to 6,000 tonnes late last week.
Chinese buyers sold copper material recently taken from LME warehouses elsewhere.
China is reportedly adding up to 300,000 tonnes to its central stockpile.
A third of the copper stockpile is currently passing through customs in Shanghai.
Three-month LME copper prices have increased almost 20 percent in recent weeks.
Three-month LME copper hit a five-month high of $2,232 a tonne on Tuesday.
LME copper stocks are below 100,000 tonnes for the first time since 1990.
Traders in the Far East believe the current supply/demand situation will keep prices buoyed in the short term.

Protectionist policies in Heilongjiang are keeping soybean prices artificially high in China.
Heilongjiang will not allow soybeans to leave the province except in value-added form.
This policy has been enforced for three years.
Heilongjiang produces one-third of China's annual soybean crop.
Domestic soybean prices have not fallen despite a recent crop of 10 to 12 million tonnes.
Officials confirmed that the policy of appropriate control would remain in place.
The policy aims to meet demand from local crushing mills.
Crushers in regions outside Heilongjiang are paying inflated prices for soybeans.
Grade three beans in Heilongjiang are priced at 2,840 yuan per tonne.
Beans in other provinces are priced up to 3,320 yuan per tonne.

China has banned poultry imports from Oklahoma and Missouri.
The ban is aimed at preventing the spread of a deadly poultry epidemic.
The ban went into effect on Monday, as stated by China's Ministry of Agriculture and the State Bureau of Animal Plant and Quarantine.
Five cases of viscerotropic velogenic Newcastle disease (VVND) were discovered in the U.S. between July and September.
VVND is described as an extremely harmful contagious epidemic disease by China's Xinhua news agency.
Phillip Holloway, a representative for the Oklahoma state agriculture department, stated that VVND is the most feared of poultry diseases.
Holloway noted that he had not heard of any recent cases of VVND in Oklahoma.
The U.S. embassy in Beijing confirmed the Chinese ban but did not provide further details.
Oklahoma and Missouri account for less than five percent of U.S. poultry exports to China, according to Holloway.
The United States exports approximately US$500 million of poultry and poultry products annually to China.

Demand is expected to drive China's metals markets in 1997.
Analysts and traders anticipate a modest flow of money to maintain consumption of base metals like aluminium and copper.
A South American industry executive stated that consumption is more important than commonly perceived.
The executive claimed that the fundamentals indicate a higher price for copper.
Some firms believe an increase in worldwide copper production capacity could lead to a supply glut after the first quarter of 1997.
The Chilean source disagreed, asserting that global demand would keep copper prices above US$1 per pound for much of the year.
Chinese consumption is expected to constitute a significant portion of total copper demand.
A senior metal trader in Shanghai noted that the city's metal futures exchange is becoming more aligned with real market fundamentals.
The trader indicated that if traders do not see a need for copper imports, futures prices will remain low.
The Shanghai Metal Exchange reportedly has enough copper stocks to meet end-user needs until Chinese New Year in February.

Russia is expected to have its second consecutive bad grain harvest.
Russia will need to import grain despite Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's prediction of sufficient output.
Andrei Sizov of SovEcon Ltd. stated that the volume of grain produced in Russia may meet demand, but the quality will not.
Chernomyrdin forecasted a grain output of 77-78 million tonnes for 1996, which is higher than the previous year's 63.4 million tonnes.
Chernomyrdin claimed this output would provide bread and bread products until the 1997 harvest.
Georgy Zelinsky from Khleboproduktprogress indicated a shortage of first-class wheat in Russia.
Sizov predicted that Russian imports of grain and flour would rise to 5.0-6.0 million tonnes in the 1996/1997 crop year.
Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun mentioned that Russia may import up to 4.5 million tonnes of maize and soymeal and 500,000 tonnes of food wheat from the U.S., Canada, and/or Australia.
Zelinsky noted that there is a shortage of domestic feed maize, but maize for human consumption is available.
Industry sources indicated that Russia would likely make small, piecemeal purchases from Western markets.

Aluminium industry sources expressed doubt about Kontsern Alyuminiy's ability to contain output to support world prices.
A Western trade source in Moscow stated, 'I don't believe they'll do it.'
Representatives from the Krasnoyarsk smelter and the Bratsk plant reported having no information on plans to contain output.
Andrei Toropovsky from the Bratsk plant's foreign economic relations department said he had no information on the strategic question of output containment.
Igor Prokopov, chief executive of Kontsern Alyuminiy, stated that Russian smelters agreed to maintain aluminium output at current levels.
Prokopov mentioned that smelters would not exploit at least 80,000-100,000 tonnes of idle annual capacity.
Vladimir Kalchenko, first deputy chief executive of Kontsern Alyuminiy, referred to weak world prices and unprofitable domestic smelters.
Sources indicated that Kontsern Alyuminiy had little leverage and was unlikely to influence producers.
London Metal Exchange benchmark aluminium prices remained around $1,330 per tonne, showing little change.
A European metals source stated that smelters tend to act independently and that Kontsern Alyuminiy's statements do not affect their business.

Russia is changing its approach to foreign investment in its oil sector.
New domestic companies will be prioritized over Western majors in future energy deals.
Vladimir Tumarkin is the chief spokesman for Rosneft, the state oil holding company.
Tumarkin stated that foreign oil firms will no longer win majority stakes in Russian reserves.
He referred to past deals with Western and Japanese oil investors as mistakes.
Amoco Corp, Exxon, Texaco, Total SA, and Norsk Hydro ASA are recent bidders for oil development in Timan-Pechora.
Bidders will be required to form a consortium and give at least a 50 percent stake to Russian companies.
Russia's oil output has declined by 46 percent since the mid-1980s.
Some Russian oil companies are struggling with non-payments and corporate taxes.
Oil analyst James Bunch expressed doubt about the financing capabilities of Russian companies.

Russia's grain crop is one of its lowest in three decades.
The nearly complete 1996 harvest is 74.6 million tonnes.
There is little high-quality bread wheat and virtually no stocks from last year's output.
Last year's grain output was officially 63.4 million tonnes.
The Federal Food Corporation may return to the international market for imports.
The Federal Food Corporation has bought 450,000 tonnes of domestic grain out of a planned 4.5 million tonnes this year.
Russian farmers have declined to sell to state reserves due to recent high prices.
Benchmark Chicago contracts for grain are at $3.75 per bushel.
Forecasts suggest Russia's total grain imports for the 1996/97 crop marketing year could be five to seven million tonnes.

Russia is the world's third-largest oil producer.
Crude oil output in Russia is ending a decade of decline.
Vitaly Kamenev of the Economy Ministry's fuel department stated that output could stabilize at 1996's level.
A real pick-up in oil output is not expected until at least 1998.
Russian oil output decreased by two percent year-on-year to 146 million tonnes in the first half of 1996.
The State Statistics Committee reported a three percent decline in the first half of 1994.
The decline in output primarily came from companies producing over 10 million tonnes a year.
A Fuel and Energy Ministry source predicted a further decline of two or three percent next year.
Russia's 1995 oil output was 305 million tonnes, which is stabilizing at just over half of the 1987 peak of 570 million tonnes.
Tamara Okhundova, an energy analyst, stated that output will be flat next year.

Russia's Bratsk plant is the world's biggest aluminium smelter.
Bratsk opposes output-cutting schemes and aims to boost production.
Yuri Shlaifshtein is a board member of Bratsk and is based in London.
Bratsk supports market-economy principles and opposes anti-monopoly law violations.
AOOT Bratsky Aluminievy Zavod (BrAZ) is located in southern Siberia.
Bratsk has increased its output of A7 higher-grade material to 69 percent of total production.
Bratsk produced 62,800 tonnes of primary aluminium in October 2023.
Bratsk's production costs are an average of $1,250 per tonne.
Bratsk aims to streamline costs further and improve competitiveness.
Bratsk does not support cutting output to boost world prices.

Russia is uncertain about its export curbs for heavy fuel oil this winter.
Traders expect an export duty of up to 80,000 roubles per tonne of mazut.
Moscow is delaying the announcement of the timing and size of a possible tariff.
Yevgeny Lukashov stated that the cabinet might debate the issue on Tuesday.
Moscow has previously raised mazut export tariffs or banned deliveries abroad in winter.
Some industry sources are questioning the delay in decision-making regarding export curbs.
Sarah Anderson stated that waiting too long to implement curbs defeats the purpose of ensuring fuel supplies.
Matthew Sagers described the decision-making process in Moscow as haphazard and inefficient.
Russia is oversupplied with mazut in winter, so any curbs would not significantly affect export levels.
The lack of transparency makes it difficult for traders to estimate Russia's winter mazut needs.

Russian and foreign oil companies signed a $2 billion deal to build a pipeline from Kazakhstan to Western markets.
The signing ceremony involved last-minute negotiations and left some questions unresolved.
The Caspian Pipeline Consortium split into two entities for tax reasons during the signing.
Russia's oil pipeline monopoly, Transneft, may take a stake in the pipeline project.
The role of Transneft has been a contentious issue among CPC members.
Chevron senior Vice-President Jeet Bindra expressed satisfaction with the commercial structure of the project.
Chevron aims to move the project to the next stage and hopes for a share acquisition by February 1997.
Officials from various companies and governments attended the signing, including LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov and Kazakh Oil and Gas Minister Nurlan Balgimbayev.
Chevron will own 15 percent of the CPC, while LUKoil will own 12.5 percent.
The remaining ownership includes Mobil and Rosneft at 7.5 percent each, British Gas Plc and Agip SpA at 2 percent each, and Oryx Energy Company and Munaigaz at 1.75 percent each.

Western oil firms are frustrated by Moscow's delays on foreign investment laws.
A study was presented to convince conservative officials that Russia will benefit significantly from oil deals.
The study outlines benefits from six production-sharing contracts requiring $129 billion in expenditure.
Foreign oil firms have invested only a small fraction of the required total due to high taxes and a flawed production-sharing law.
A top Western oil executive stated that no investments will occur until there is a firm legal base.
The Petroleum Advisory Forum and Russian academics prepared the study.
The study claims that six major international projects requiring $102 billion in Western funding would generate $591 billion in total benefits.
According to the study, Russia would receive 87 percent of the total benefits from these projects.
The projects would create 550,000 jobs and raise real gross domestic product by $450 billion.
State revenues would increase by $257 billion and Russian private sector revenues by $258 billion.

Khozhakhmed Yarikhanov is the president of the Southern Oil Company in Chechnya.
Yarikhanov stated that Chechnya would guarantee the safety of a major oil pipeline across its land.
He demanded a cut in foreign deals that will use the oil pipeline.
The pipeline is part of an $8 billion multinational consortium that plans to export oil in 1997.
Yarikhanov claimed that the pipeline was safe but acknowledged potential risks such as sabotage and technical errors.
The northern link can carry 17 million tonnes of oil a year.
The pipeline connects the Azeri capital Baku to Russia's Black Sea oil export outlet of Novorossiisk.
The Azerbaijan International Operating Company plans to reverse the flow of the pipeline to ship up to 100,000 barrels per day from August 1997.
The consortium is led by British Petroleum Plc and Norway's Statoil.
The Chechen conflict has caused instability and concern among oil firms regarding their investments.

Russia's oil industry earned higher export revenues in 1996 due to increased world prices.
Energy analysts expressed concerns about the slow recovery of domestic demand for oil in 1997.
International oil prices rose about 30 percent in 1996, reaching their highest level in six years.
Domestic producers exported large quantities of crude oil in 1996, taking advantage of high international prices.
Analysts indicated that higher domestic demand for Russian oil was not expected in the near future.
Eugene Khartukov stated that 1997 could either show a recovery in oil output or a further decline.
Russian crude oil output in 1997 could increase to 6.3 million barrels per day from 6.1 million barrels per day in 1996.
Russia's oil output has nearly halved since its peak of 11.5 million barrels per day in 1987.
The Fuel and Energy Ministry reported a two percent decline in crude oil and gas condensate output from January to November 1996.
Exports of Russian oil increased by 4.7 percent year-on-year to 92.8 million tonnes during the same period.

Norilsk Nickel is a key supplier to world markets.
Viktor Feldman is the deputy economics director at Norilsk Nickel.
Norilsk Nickel is experiencing a financial crisis.
Feldman stated that the high cost of maintaining social services is a major issue.
Norilsk Nickel's flagship plant is the Norilsk combine.
In 1996, Norilsk Nickel produced 100,000 tonnes of nickel.
Norilsk Nickel is the world's second largest producer of refined nickel.
Norilsk Nickel accounts for about 45 percent of world platinum and palladium production.
First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin mentioned that the plant might need to issue stock to pay off debts.
Norilsk Nickel's debts are reported to be 1.7 trillion roubles, equivalent to $300 million.

Russian cocoa importers expect an increase in business this year.
Increasing competition from Western chocolate bars is affecting the market.
Yuri Granilin, supplies director at Babayevsky confectionery plant, stated that there is a general tendency for growth in cocoa purchases.
Domestic producers face competition from Western ready-made chocolates.
The State Statistics Committee reported cocoa imports from outside the Commonwealth of Independent States increased to 47,700 tonnes in the first eleven months of 1996.
The International Cocoa Organisation reported Russian grindings for 1995/96 remained flat at 75,000 tonnes.
A Nestle source predicted a 15-20 percent growth in Russia's ready-made chocolate products market this year.
Alexander Pavlov from the Agriculture Ministry stated that Russia's cocoa imports and derivatives decreased by eight percent year-on-year in 1996.
Pavlov estimated that cocoa imports would total 130,000 tonnes, including about 75,000 tonnes of beans.
Imported ready-made chocolate products are estimated to comprise 10-15 percent of the domestic market.

The French electronics group Thomson SA may be sold to either Alcatel-Alsthom or Lagardere Groupe.
The government is expected to announce its decision on the sale of Thomson SA on Monday or Wednesday after a cabinet meeting.
The announcement timing may be affected by a planned journalists strike on Tuesday over tax increases.
The decision regarding Thomson SA has implications for France's defense industry and consumer electronics sector.
Alcatel-Alsthom is led by former arms engineer Serge Tchuruk.
Thomson SA is 76 percent owned by the state and 20 percent owned by France Telecom.
Thomson SA owns Thomson Multimedia, a leading television set company, and has a 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF, a top defense electronics company.
Thomson SA reported a loss of 1.379 billion francs in 1995 and has debts of approximately 25 billion francs.
Thomson-CSF made a profit of 1.01 billion francs in 1995 and has a 20 percent stake in SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV.
Lagardere Groupe is led by Jean-Luc Lagardere and has interests in media and defense.

Air Liberte is a French regional airline with 1,400 staff that is under bankruptcy protection.
The staff of Air Liberte published a full-page advert in the Journal du Dimanche demanding to see the takeover bids made to the administrators.
Air Liberte went into administration on September 26 with debts of about 1.5 billion francs.
Offers for Air Liberte have been made by British Airways Plc, Virgin Express, a consortium led by Jacques Maillot, and commercial pilot Fernand Denan.
The commercial court of Creteil is expected to decide which takeover option will be pursued early this week.
The staff of Air Liberte blamed the French authorities for the company's difficulties, citing obstacles to development.
The staff also criticized certain shareholders for abandoning the company before a recapitalization.
British Airways plans to pay 25 million francs for Air Liberte and aims to merge it with its French TAT unit.
British Airways intends to invest 440 million francs to return Air Liberte to profitability within three years.
Air Liberte owns about a quarter of the landing and take-off slots at Orly.

The chairman of Daewoo Electronics is Bae Soon-hoon.
Bae Soon-hoon made job and investment promises to French critics regarding the acquisition of Thomson Multimedia.
Bae Soon-hoon stated that a counter-bid for Thomson Multimedia was 'not realistic'.
Bae Soon-hoon did not discuss financial details of the proposed takeover until the government's decision is final.
The French Privatisation Commission and the European Commission must approve the acquisition deal.
The French government selected Lagardere Groupe to buy state-owned Thomson SA for one franc.
Lagardere plans to merge its Matra Defence Espace unit with Thomson-CSF and sell Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo for one franc.
Thomson Multimedia reportedly made a three billion franc loss in the first half and has debts of at least 14 billion francs.
Bae Soon-hoon promised to create 5,000 jobs in France at Thomson Multimedia over five years.
Bae Soon-hoon stated that the partnership would enable a 13 billion franc investment plan and create 6,600 jobs in final assembly and 2,500 jobs in component production.

Air France is a state-owned airline in France.
British Airways Plc (BA) plans to enter the French domestic market.
BA's TAT French unit announced a joint bid of 780 million francs with French private bank Rivaud for domestic carrier Air Liberte.
The bid will increase BA's share of takeoff and landing slots at Paris' Orly airport to 20 percent.
An Air France spokeswoman acknowledged that BA's increased presence in French aviation would have an impact.
BA will manage its French assets from a distance initially.
TAT and Air Liberte will operate separately until at least 1999.
The Creteil commercial court will review the BA/Rivaud offer.
A creditors meeting for Air Liberte is scheduled to take place within a month.
Virgin Express plans to raise its bid for Air Liberte, which has been in administration since September 26.

Air France is a French state-owned airline.
Air France stated it is prepared to face increased competition from British Airways Plc in the domestic market.
British Airways' TAT French unit announced a joint bid of 780 million francs for domestic carrier Air Liberte.
The joint bid will increase British Airways' share of takeoff and landing slots at Paris Orly airport to 20 percent.
An Air France spokeswoman acknowledged that British Airways' increased presence would have consequences for Air France.
Air France plans to improve its product and service while reducing costs and prices.
British Airways is set to acquire a 70 percent stake in Air Liberte after approval from the Creteil commercial court.
Air France Europe holds an 80 percent market stake on its operated routes and 60 percent of the total French market.
European liberalization of the airline industry will open French airspace to competition starting in April 1997.
British Airways acquired a 49.9 percent stake in TAT in 1993 and the remaining shares in July 2022.

Analysts had mixed opinions on Rhone-Poulenc SA's third quarter results.
Some analysts indicated they might raise full-year forecasts, while others kept their forecasts unchanged.
Guy Phillips, an analyst at BZW in London, stated that the figures were better than his forecast.
Phillips mentioned that the operating profit at life sciences and pharmaceuticals was particularly pleasing.
Phillips is considering raising his profit per share forecast from eight francs to 8.5 francs.
Brokers Leven in Paris stated there was no reason to adjust estimates.
Shaw Bridges at Merrill Lynch noted that health care earnings exceeded expectations, but fibres and chemicals performed weaker.
Bridges maintained his forecast for 1996 net attributable profit at 2.7 billion francs, compared to 2.134 billion in 1995.
Bridges kept his 'hold' rating for Rhone-Poulenc shares, stating they were fairly valued.
Liliane Gauffre at BNP Du Bouzet said the results confirmed that Rhone-Poulenc was driven by its pharmaceuticals and agro divisions.

French Prime Minister Alain Juppe stated he wanted a public debate on the planned privatisation of Thomson SA.
Juppe announced the intention for a public debate after an outcry over a previous government decision.
The government announced on October 16 its intention to sell Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe instead of Alcatel Alsthom.
The planned sale of Thomson was for a symbolic franc after an 11 billion franc capital increase.
Lagardere plans to merge Thomson's defence electronics group with its own Matra Defence Espace.
Juppe claimed his decision to favor Lagardere was in the best interests of the country's defence industry and job market.
The Privatisation Commission is studying both offers for Thomson and will determine if they reflect the true value of the company.
The decision from the Privatisation Commission is expected in early December.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis announced the government's preference to prevent insider trading.
Thomson Multimedia's labour unions expressed dissatisfaction with Juppe's comments about the company's value.

Daewoo Electronics launched a charm campaign in France with newspaper advertisements.
The campaign was in response to criticism regarding Daewoo's plans to acquire Thomson Multimedia.
The advertisements featured the slogan 'Do you know the dwarf Daewoo?, the 34th biggest world company'.
The French Privatisation Commission will announce its decision on the sale of Thomson SA in early December.
Thomson SA is being sold to Lagardere Groupe for one franc after an 11 billion franc capital injection.
Lagardere will sell Thomson Multimedia, a producer of televisions and video recorders, to Daewoo.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe stated there would be a parliamentary debate on the deal, but no vote will follow.
Daewoo claimed its electronics division had sales figures comparable to Thomson Multimedia, around 40 billion francs, but with higher profits.
Daewoo stated that its global sales network would enhance market access for Thomson's new products.
The Communist Party is organizing a seminar on the privatisation of Thomson on November 13.

French carmakers Renault SA and Peugeot PSA are in talks with the government on a long-term plan to rejuvenate their workforce.
Renault SA and Peugeot PSA did not confirm a report about seeking approval for a five-year plan to cut 40,000 jobs in exchange for hiring 14,000 young people.
The newspaper Les Echos reported that the cost of the proposed operations could be 30 billion francs ($6 billion).
Renault's chairman Louis Schweitzer and Peugeot's chairman Jacques Calvet wrote a letter to Prime Minister Alain Juppe in July with a proposal.
The Renault spokeswoman stated that discussions have occurred since the letter was sent, but the government has not yet replied.
Peugeot officials declined to comment on the existence of the letter but acknowledged the need to rejuvenate the workforce.
The average age of a car worker in France is 42 to 43 years, while competitors, especially Asian manufacturers, have an average age below 30 years.
The Peugeot spokesman stated that older workers present a competitive handicap as markets are increasingly being opened up.
Renault's average worker age is 45 years, and the oldest factory is at Flins, which dates from the war.
Renault had a worldwide staff of 139,950 people at the end of 1995, with 72,163 involved in car production in France.

Cie Generale des Eaux launched its bid to compete with France Telecom by starting a fixed telephone network in Nice.
Philippe Glotin is the managing director of Generale's telecoms unit Cegetel.
Cegetel aims to achieve a market share in 2003 that would yield 40 billion francs in annual sales.
More than half of Cegetel's projected sales in 2003 would come from mobile communications.
Cegetel competes with France Telecom in mobile telecommunications through its SFR unit.
Cegetel is allied with British Telecom Plc and MCI for business services.
The local residential market in France is expected to grow to 55 billion francs in 2003.
Cegetel aims to gain a 40 percent share in mobile telecommunications, 20 percent in long-distance, and 10 percent in local loops.
Cegetel has received permission from French authorities for a telecoms experiment in Nice and will offer residential telecoms services starting in 1997.
Cegetel plans to invest three billion francs in Nice and central France to prepare for market liberalization in 1998.

Cie des Machines Bull sold five percent of its shares held by the government.
Thierry Breton is the managing director of Bull.
Bull plans to participate in the restructuring of the European computer industry.
Bull may engage in market operations, mergers, or acquisitions as part of its strategy.
Jean-Marie Descarpentries is the chairman of Bull and was a former McKinsey consultant.
Bull aims for the state to sell 20 percent to a fourth industrial partner and financial investors.
Bull returned to profit in 1995 after losses of 22 billion francs since 1990.
The French government plans to privatize Bull before the end of 1997.
The state share sale will occur after a capital increase of several hundreds of millions of francs.
Motorola, NEC, and France Telecom each hold a 17 percent stake in Bull and are expected to participate in the capital increase.

The French Industry Minister is Franck Borotra.
Franck Borotra reminded the chairman of Britain's General Electric Co Plc of his conditions for an Anglo-French nuclear merger.
The merger plan involves GEC Alsthom and state-controlled Framatome.
Borotra stated that French interests must maintain a majority in the merged entity.
GEC chairman Lord Weinstock expressed a desire for at least 50 percent ownership in the merger.
Framatome shareholders are set to appoint Dominique Vignon as chairman and chief executive.
Dominique Vignon will replace Jean-Claude Leny, who criticized the merger plan.
The Industry Ministry outlined five non-negotiable conditions for the merger.
The conditions include state control over strategic nuclear decisions and preservation of Framatome's identity.
Framatome has a technical alliance with Siemens for developing a future European nuclear power station.

National Mutual Holdings Ltd is an Australian life office.
National Mutual Holdings Ltd is expected to debut on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchanges on Tuesday.
The institutional offer for National Mutual Holdings Ltd was six times oversubscribed.
The final price of National Mutual shares was A$1.60 each.
National Mutual Holdings Ltd has a market capitalisation of A$2.7 billion (US$2 billion) upon listing.
National Mutual is Australia's first listed life office.
At A$1.60 per share, National Mutual will rank among the market's top 30 firms.
Institutional bidders received on average only about 15 percent of the shares they sought.
National Mutual's listing marks its transition from a mutual company to a listed group.
Axa SA owns 51 percent of National Mutual upon listing and cannot sell its stake for six months.

Foster's Brewing Group Ltd. is seeking expansion through possible joint ventures in India and Vietnam.
Foster's executives stated that the company is well positioned for growth opportunities despite challenges in Canada and China.
Chief Executive Officer Ted Kunkel emphasized the priority of seeking new direct investment opportunities after addressing current cash needs.
Chairman John Ralph mentioned that the group is considering joint venture breweries in Vietnam and India, as well as other investment options.
Ralph indicated that the Vietnamese opportunity involves an existing plant.
Foster's has breweries in Shanghai, Tianjin, and Guangdong in China.
Foster's China reported a loss of A$17 million before interest and tax in the latest year.
Molson Breweries, which is 40 percent owned by Foster's, performed poorly but is undergoing restructuring to build market share.
Kunkel forecasted higher operating profits from Carlton and United Breweries in Australia over the medium term.
Kunkel identified Asia as the most attractive region for investment, with beer volumes expected to rise significantly.

Crown Ltd is Australia's most profitable casino operator.
Crown Ltd plans to focus on Asia for its long-term ambitions.
Crown's new casino and hotel complex in Melbourne is nearing completion and cost A$1.6 billion.
Crown chairman Lloyd Williams stated that success in Melbourne could lead to success in Asia.
Crown plans to open three additional marketing offices in China, Taiwan, and Malaysia.
Crown currently has offices in Bangkok, Singapore, Jakarta, and Hong Kong.
Crown derived about 30 percent of its gaming revenue of A$490 million in the year to June 30.
Crown's net profit after abnormals rose by 76 percent to A$58 million.
Lloyd Williams expressed interest in major casino licenses in Asia, specifically mentioning Malaysia.
Williams indicated that Crown would bid for a casino license in Thailand if one were awarded.

Tabcorp Holdings Ltd is an Australian gambling group.
Tabcorp is hoping for increased betting activity during the Melbourne Cup next Tuesday.
Ross Wilson is the managing director of Tabcorp.
Tabcorp's total turnover rose 17 percent in the first quarter ending September.
The increase in total turnover was due to a 27 percent rise in turnover from 12,000 slot machines.
Tabcorp's wagering division had a poor start to the current fiscal year ending June 30, 1997.

Amcor Ltd is an Australian paper and packaging group.
Amcor Ltd is expected to report a significant decline in annual profit due to lower paper prices and weak demand in Australia.
Analysts predict that Amcor's pre-abnormal net earnings will fall by around eight percent.
Stock analysts forecast an average pre-abnormal profit of A$372 million for Amcor in 1995/96.
Amcor's profit in 1994/95 was A$359.7 million, a 40 percent increase from the previous year.
Amcor relies on white paper sales for 45 percent of its turnover.
Paper prices have decreased by approximately 30 percent since late 1995.
Spicers Paper Ltd, in which Amcor has a 46 percent ownership, reported a 35 percent decline in annual net profit to A$16.02 million.
Analysts expect Amcor's sales to exceed A$6.6 billion, but margins are expected to remain tight.
Analysts predict that Amcor's pre-abnormal net profit may stabilize at around A$400 million in 1996/97.

The Broken Hill Pty Co (BHP) reported a 9.8-percent decline in first-half profits.
BHP's net profit for the six months to November 30 was A$790 million, down from A$867 million for the same period last year.
BHP's share price initially rose to A$17.59 after the profit announcement but later settled at around A$17.20.
BHP's pre-abnormal net profit was A$683 million, which is a 15.8 percent decrease compared to the corresponding 1995/96 period.
BHP's petroleum division was the largest earner for the quarter, generating A$253 million, which included an abnormal gain of A$107 million.
BHP's minerals division doubled its profit contribution in the second quarter to A$154 million.
BHP's managing director John Prescott stated that there is an accelerating improvement in performance.
Analysts had expected a first-half group pre-abnormal result of around A$760 million.
BHP's steel division reported flat earnings in the latest three months compared to the previous quarter.
BHP's North American copper operations returned to profitability.

BHP has agreed to pay its domestic steel workers a 10 percent pay rise over two years.
The Australian Workers Union represents about 80 percent of BHP Steel's 15,000 unionised steel workers.
The wage deal was endorsed by the workforce just before Christmas.
The annual wage rises are effective from New Year's Day, with five percent in 1997 and five percent in 1998.
The wage increases will be paid as three percent instalments in January and two percent in July.
The wage rises include site-specific productivity offsets and adjustments for inflation.
The wage deal does not affect existing performance-related payments for workers.
AWU negotiator Mick Eagles described the wage deal as a good outcome given low inflation prospects.
BHP's spokesman stated that the agreement involves new employment arrangements that provide business benefits.
The deal aligns with a recommendation from Australia's Industrial Relations Commission.

Pacific BBA Ltd reported that trading conditions in the second half of calendar 1996 were softer than expected.
Pacific BBA Ltd expects 1996 profits to be around the same level as 1995.
Barry Jackson is the managing director of Pacific BBA Ltd.
Barry Jackson stated that the 1996 profit would be similar to the 1995 net profit of A$15.9 million.
Jackson cited the flat Australian economy, weak automotive sales worldwide, and the cost of developing new projects as constraints on profit growth.
Jackson believes the domestic economy should improve in 1997.
Pacific BBA Ltd has a goal of 15 to 20 percent annual growth in sales and earnings before interest and tax.
Pacific BBA Ltd has budgeted to spend around A$60 million in capital expenditure in 1996.
The group is exploring expansion opportunities in Asia and North America, requiring annual capital investments between A$5 million and A$200 million.
Barry Jackson expressed concern about the need to expand cautiously to avoid over-stretching the company.

Coles Myer Ltd reported a 5.4 percent rise in sales revenue to A$9.9 billion for the six months to January 26.
Coles attributed its sales revenue increase to good management rather than an economic pick-up.
Coles chief executive Dennis Eck stated that significant work was done to achieve the sales results.
David Jones Ltd reassessed its profit outlook, indicating a less severe decline than previously forecasted.
David Jones had initially feared a 50 percent fall in interim profit but later revised this outlook.
David Jones reported overall sales of A$783 million for the first half year ending January 25, which is one percent lower than the previous year.
Retail analyst Simon Shakesheff stated that consumer spending may have reached its lowest point but does not expect a dramatic turnaround.
Australian retail sales are at their lowest level in 35 years and have fallen in trend terms for the past five months.
Australia's jobless rate is currently at 8.6 percent.
Coles confirmed that trading conditions remain challenging, particularly in clothing and fashion.

Foster's Brewing Group Ltd reported a 2.4 percent increase in interim net profit to A$169.4 million.
The increase in net profit was affected by a A$5.6 million abnormal loss.
The abnormal loss was primarily due to restructuring costs at Molson Breweries, which Foster's owns 40 percent of.
Foster's reported a 10 percent rise in pre-abnormal net earnings to A$168 million.
Ted Kunkel, the chief executive of Foster's, attributed the rise in pre-abnormal earnings to strong performance from Carlton and United Breweries (CUB).
CUB experienced a four percent increase in the volume of beer sold.
The overall beer market in Australia only rose by 0.6 percent during the same period.
CUB contributed A$187.4 million in earnings before interest and tax, an increase of 11.5 percent compared to the first half of 1995/96.
Foster's group result was slightly below the average forecast for first-half profit of around A$170 million.
Foster's shares were trading at A$2.60, down five cents from the previous close.

Brian Quinn was a former chief executive of Coles Myer Ltd.
Quinn spent millions of dollars of the company's money to renovate his home.
A court heard that this case involved greed and excess from the 1980s.
Quinn is 60 years old and rose from a junior store assistant to run Coles Myer Ltd.
Quinn went on trial in the Victoria Supreme Court on a charge of conspiracy to defraud.
Quinn has pleaded not guilty and claims he was set up.
The prosecution alleges that Quinn conspired to spend around A$4 million on renovations to his Melbourne home from 1982 to 1988.
The renovations included expanding the home, building a tennis court, spa, and pergola.
Prosecutor Paul Coghlan accused Quinn of excessive spending and work on the renovations.
Coghlan stated that one room was painted 10 times and the house was extended by 70 square metres.

Comalco Ltd is Australia's biggest aluminium producer.
Comalco announced a loss of A$16.8 million in calendar 1996.
In 1995, Comalco reported a net profit after abnormals of A$232.3 million.
Before abnormals, Comalco's earnings in 1996 were A$32.9 million.
Comalco's share price fell eight cents following the loss announcement but rebounded to A$6.88.
Comalco is 67 percent owned by global mining group RTZ-CRA.
The London Metal Exchange aluminium price averaged 70 U.S. cents a pound in 1996.
The Australian dollar averaged 78 U.S. cents in 1996.
Comalco's earnings were negatively impacted by lower aluminium prices and a strong local currency.
Comalco expects an increase in aluminium production and a stronger aluminium price in 1997.

RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd is the world's biggest mining house.
RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd is expected to report a sharp fall in annual profit this week.
The expected fall in net profit before exceptional items is 26 percent to US$1.067 billion for calendar 1996.
RTZ-CRA made US$1.441 billion in profit in 1995.
Australian analysts' forecasts for RTZ-CRA's profit range between US$1.04 billion and US$1.097 billion.
The decline in profit is attributed to a drop in copper prices, a weak aluminium price, and issues with the Bingham Canyon copper smelter.
Copper and aluminium accounted for almost 41 percent of RTZ-CRA's total revenue in 1995.
The copper price fell below 90 U.S. cents a pound after the Sumitomo trading scandal in June.
Yasuo Hamanaka admitted to charges of fraud and forgery related to the Sumitomo trading scandal.
RTZ-CRA's iron ore business experienced a six percent drop in sales despite an increase in annual output.

Microsoft Corp. executives believe that the Internet will be the next mass medium.
Microsoft unveiled a new version of the MSN online service with a focus on entertainment programming.
The new MSN programs are organized into six core channels aimed at specific demographic groups.
MSN has become the No. 3 online service with 1.6 million subscribers in just over a year.
Microsoft executives expect to double the number of subscribers by mid-1997.
The company plans to take market share from America Online Inc. through a $100 million marketing campaign.
Microsoft acknowledges that America Online has a broader selection of content.
The company plans to target new online customers under 30 rather than trying to convert existing AOL customers.
Laura Jennings, a Microsoft vice president, criticized the previous MSN service for its ease of use.
The new advertising campaign will include billboards, print ads, and television commercials starting in early November.

Microsoft Corp is expected to report a slowdown in earnings growth due to a sales surge last year from the launch of Windows 95.
Industry analysts expect Microsoft to post earnings of $0.90 a share for its fiscal first quarter, up 15 percent from last year's $0.78.
Chris Galvin of Hambrecht and Quist stated that the September quarter last year was strong due to the initial release of Windows 95.
Analysts noted that Microsoft's business is expanding steadily, benefiting from rising sales of personal computers and the penetration of Windows 95 and Windows NT.
Microsoft's profit margins are rising as the company sells more software preloaded on new computers or through licenses to large customers.
Analysts expect Microsoft's business to gain momentum through the fiscal year as Windows NT gains acceptance and a new version of Office is rolled out in December.
For the fiscal year ending June 30, 1997, analysts expect earnings of $4.07 a share, up 19 percent from last year's $3.43.
Scott McAdams of Ragen MacKenzie believes Windows NT will significantly drive earnings in the December quarter and early 1997.
The arrival of 'thin client' products, such as the Network Computer, could pose a challenge for Microsoft.
Sun Microsystems Inc is expected to launch products based on Java, which may be positioned as an alternative to Microsoft's operating systems.

Boeing Co defense and space group President Gerald King believes the company has a better than 50-50 chance of surviving to the next round of the military's Joint Strike Fighter program.
King expressed that he is not as optimistic about Boeing's chances of surviving into the next round of competition for the Evolved Expendable Launch Vehicle contract for the U.S. Air Force.
Boeing is competing with McDonnell Douglas Corp and Lockheed Martin Corp for a contract to build approximately 3,000 jets for the U.S. Air Force, Navy, Marine Corps, and the British Royal Navy.
The Pentagon will eliminate one of the bidding companies in a downselect next month.
King stated that Boeing has put significant effort into developing what they believe is the right solution for the Joint Strike Fighter program.
King believes Boeing's design has a high degree of commonality, which should allow for a lower price for the modular aircraft with three configurations.
King thinks Boeing's chances of advancing to the next phase are better than 50-50 due to their innovative solution.
King expressed concern that the Pentagon might favor other bidders, particularly McDonnell Douglas, to maintain a broad national industrial base.
King argued that maintaining an industrial base does not make sense because the U.S. already has excess capacity to build commercial and military aircraft.
If Boeing is eliminated, the company would be available to partner with the surviving contractors.

Microsoft Corp. plans to announce a new initiative for inexpensive, easy-to-use personal computers.
Microsoft is collaborating with Intel Corp., Hewlett-Packard Co., and Compaq Computer Corp. on this initiative.
The announcement is scheduled for a conference on Monday.
The announcement will occur one day before the unveiling of an $800 device from Sun Microsystems Inc.
Sun Microsystems Inc. is introducing a network computer positioned as an Internet-friendly alternative to traditional PCs.
Microsoft executives, including Chairman Bill Gates, have previously downplayed the threat from network computers.
Rob Enderle, an industry analyst, stated that the threat from network computers is very real, particularly for corporate users.
Dataquest forecasted that personal computer penetration in U.S. homes would reach 38 percent by 1999, up from 29 percent the previous year.
Microsoft has been increasing efforts to simplify personal computers for consumers.
In April, Bill Gates introduced technologies for the 'Simply Interactive PC' to make PCs easier to use.

Federal officials confirmed 29 cases of bacterial poisoning linked to fresh apple juice.
The cases were associated with Odwalla Inc. fruit juice consumed in California, Washington, Colorado, and the Vancouver area of British Columbia.
Bob Howard of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control stated that the infections were caused by a potentially fatal strain of the E. coli bacterium.
At least 36 additional cases are suspected or under investigation according to state, county, and provincial officials.
State and federal officials tested Odwalla juice samples but found no evidence of contamination.
Arthur Whitmore of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration indicated that results from the samples would take a few days.
Odwalla, based in Half Moon Bay, California, provided samples from production runs from two weeks prior to the first reported cases.
At least four children remained hospitalized due to complications from the E. coli O57:H7 bacterium.
The bacterium can cause severe illness, including stomach cramps, bloody diarrhea, and kidney failure.
Health officials speculated that contamination may have occurred from apples that had fallen to the ground, although Odwalla claims to wash all produce thoroughly.

Nordstrom Inc. reported a 16 percent increase in earnings for its third quarter.
For the fiscal third quarter ending Oct. 31, Nordstrom's sales were $984 million, up 9 percent from last year's $907 million.
Net income for Nordstrom rose to $34 million, or 42 cents a share, compared to $29 million, or 36 cents a share, last year.
When excluding certain one-time gains and costs, Nordstrom earned about 38 cents a share, exceeding the Wall Street consensus forecast of 36 cents.
Piper Jaffray analyst Saul Yaari indicated that analysts expected to raise their estimates for Nordstrom.
Jennifer Black Groves of Black & Co. stated that Nordstrom had a difficult summer due to an over-reliance on unpopular body-hugging fashions.
Nordstrom experienced heavy markdowns in July and August that negatively impacted earnings.
Nordstrom executives indicated that the deepest markdowns appear to be behind them.
Comparable-store sales for Nordstrom fell 0.3 percent in the latest quarter but were up 1.5 percent for the year to date.
Nordstrom plans to open three new department stores and several smaller stores next year, adding about 719,000 square feet of store space.

Sierra Semiconductor Corp's stock increased by 23 percent on Thursday.
The increase in stock price was due to expectations of the company becoming more profitable after exiting the computer modem business.
Sierra Semiconductor Corp is based in San Jose, California.
The company announced its exit from the modem-chip business on Wednesday.
Sierra Semiconductor Corp plans to focus on the market for computer networking equipment.
Analyst Elias Moosa stated that the company will be smaller but more profitable after the exit.
Sierra Semiconductor Corp may cut up to 150 jobs from its current workforce of 500 people.
The company plans to take a charge against earnings of $50 million to $80 million for asset write-downs and severance payments.
Scott Randall of Soundview Financial Group indicated that selling the modem-chip business may be difficult.
The market for networking chips is attracting larger competitors like International Business Machines Corp.

Boeing Co plans to acquire McDonnell Douglas Corp for $13 billion.
The acquisition will enhance Boeing's position as a military contractor.
Boeing is already the world leader in commercial aviation.
Airbus Industrie may face competitive pressure due to Boeing's increased resources.
Analysts believe the primary benefits of the acquisition will be in Boeing's military business.
Historically, Boeing's military business was not a major player in the industry.
The combined company could derive nearly 50 percent of its revenues from government contracts.
Boeing's historical revenue from government contracts was 25 to 30 percent.
The acquisition follows Boeing's $3.2 billion purchase of Rockwell International Corp's defense and space business.
McDonnell Douglas was recently eliminated from consideration for the military's joint strike fighter plane.

Phil Condit is the chief executive officer of Boeing Co.
Condit was elected chairman of Boeing's board of directors on December 9.
Condit began negotiations for a $13.3 billion deal to acquire McDonnell Douglas Corp. the day after his election.
Condit will serve as chairman and chief executive of the merged company if the deal is approved by shareholders and federal regulators.
Condit began his career with Boeing in 1965 and was promoted to chief executive in April after serving as president for over three years.
Condit's promotion to chairman will take effect on February 1 after Frank Shrontz's retirement.
Condit is known for changing from a business suit to a sweater and slacks for meetings with workers.
Condit has a drive to cut costs and create a stronger aerospace company.
Boeing's workforce was reduced by about one-third over five years ending in 1995.
Boeing experienced a 10-week strike by its 32,000 unionized Machinists last year.

Airbus Industrie's preliminary restructuring agreement may improve efficiency.
The restructuring poses no near-term threat to Boeing Co's market dominance.
Details of the Airbus agreement were not revealed.
The agreement represents progress from last July's announcement about transforming the consortium into a single corporate entity by 1999.
Wolfgang Demisch of BT Securities stated that the agreement is a step in the right direction.
Airbus faces increased pressure to act following Boeing's plan to acquire McDonnell Douglas Corp.
Analysts believe Airbus needs to streamline its management structure to compete with Boeing.
Boeing controls about 60 percent of the worldwide market for commercial jets, while Airbus controls about 35 percent.
Boeing officials welcomed the news of Airbus's reorganization.
The Airbus consortium includes Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz AG's aerospace unit, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA.

Microsoft Corp expects desktop applications led by its Office suite to generate about $5 billion in revenues in the current fiscal year ending June 30.
Richard Fade is the vice president in charge of the desktop applications division at Microsoft.
Fade expects 35 to 45 percent of users to upgrade to the new Office 97 version.
Office has an installed base of approximately 24 million customers.
About 30 million users utilize component applications such as Word and Excel, which are also being upgraded.
Analysts estimate Microsoft will post overall revenues of slightly more than $10 billion this year, an increase from $8.7 billion in fiscal 1996.
The productivity applications could account for $3 billion in sales driven by Office 97.
Fade stated that Office 97 is a significant release for Microsoft, comparable to the introduction of Office 95 and Windows 95.
The development of Office 97 involved hundreds of person-years and has been in progress since late 1994.
The entire Office division, nearly 1,000 people, has been working on Office 97 since August 1995.

Microsoft Corp. reported second-quarter profits of $741 million or 57 cents a share for fiscal 1997.
This represents a 29 percent increase over the $575 million or 45 cents a share reported in the same quarter the previous year.
Revenues for the quarter rose 22 percent to $2.68 billion from $2.2 billion a year earlier.
Microsoft's earnings exceeded analysts' highest forecasts, leading to a rise in shares to $89 in after-hours trading.
The stock later fell to $85.50 due to warnings about slower earnings growth.
In regular Nasdaq trading, Microsoft shares gained $1.125 to $87.125.
Analysts had expected Microsoft to report earnings of 51 cents a share, with estimates ranging from 47 to 55 cents.
Strong sales in Windows operating systems, BackOffice server software, and Office applications drove Microsoft's earnings.
OEM sales through computer manufacturers rose 29 percent to $866 million.
Revenues from countries outside the United States, Canada, and Europe rose 32 percent to $424 million, with Japan performing particularly well.

Revisions to Ivory Coast's coffee and cocoa auction system have been finalized.
The revisions are in line with donor loan conditions and require government approval to take effect.
An exporter stated that the government could implement the changes within 12 hours if desired.
Talks with the World Bank and the Caistab cocoa and coffee marketing board concluded in September.
The new system will allocate contracts among the highest bidders in proportion to their bids.
The Caistab launched an electronic screen auction system in May to meet World Bank loan conditions.
The electronic auction system has been under review since July due to complaints.
Final approval from the government is needed before $45 million of a $150 million World Bank loan can be disbursed.
Changes in management rules will occur when Yves-Marie Koissy becomes president of Caistab.
The Caistab will award export contracts based on the price and quantity bid by the five highest bidders.

Cocoa arrivals in Ivory Coast at the start of the 1996/97 season are slower than normal.
Exporters are awaiting financing and warehouses are filling up at the main port, Abidjan.
Rene Ekra, head of the exporters' trade body GEPEX, stated that there is a problem of finding space in the port.
Delays in issuing export licences and freight rates have blocked shipments of cocoa.
Large consignments of cotton are taking up port space.
Exporters are unable to secure bank finance without export licences and contracts.
Ivory Coast opened its 1996/97 cocoa marketing season on October 24 with a farmgate price of 320 CFA per bagged kilo.
The cocoa export tax was reduced by 10 CFA to 150.
31 exporters were given licences last year, but 1996/97 applicants are still waiting for government approval.
Yves-Marie Koissy, head of the Caistab cocoa marketing agency, is expected to return from the United States in early November.

SIFCA is one of Ivory Coast's largest cocoa and coffee exporters.
SIFCA will appoint a liquidator for its subsidiary SOGEPAG, which is losing money.
Exporters and buyers claim that port arrivals will not be affected by SOGEPAG's liquidation.
Pierre-Dominique Blind is the spokesman for SIFCA and managing director of UCEPAG.
SOGEPAG's warehouses may be empty for the rest of the season after a liquidator is appointed.
Liquidation of SOGEPAG is expected to take at least three months.
DAFCI is a minority 33 percent shareholder in SOGEPAG and was not available for comment.
UCEPAG reported cocoa purchases of 46,000 tonnes and coffee purchases of 9,741 tonnes in 1995/96.
SOGEPAG was established in 1991 to guarantee farmers fixed farmgate prices when world prices dipped.
SOGEPAG increased its number of sites from four to 17 since its inception.

Ivory Coast's 1996/97 coffee crop is expected to reach 250,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Coffee output in 1995/96 was approximately 180,000 tonnes.
Experts believe the increase in coffee output is part of a cycle that affects the sector.
A San Pedro exporter stated that the crop is very good but has some quality problems.
A large buyer in coffee-rich areas predicted the crop would be at least 250,000 tonnes.
Exporters are currently not buying coffee due to low world prices.
Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan announced that the crop would exceed 200,000 tonnes due to a rehabilitation plan and better maintenance.
Ivory Coast reduced its 1996/97 farmgate price for unhulled green coffee cherries from 700 CFA to 500 CFA.
The new coffee marketing season opened on November 14, delayed from early October.
Coffee marketing is expected to begin in mid-December after cocoa harvests.

Ivorian cocoa arrivals for the 1996/97 season were reported at 330,000 to 350,000 tonnes by early December.
The December 7 figures were lower than the estimated 410,000 tonnes reported by December 3 the previous year.
Analysts suggested adding 50,000 tonnes to this year's figures for comparison due to a late season start.
Ivory Coast opened its 1996/97 marketing season on October 24, three weeks later than usual.
The initial total crop expectation for Ivory Coast was around 950,000 tonnes.
From October 24 to the end of November 1996, about 285,000 tonnes of cocoa had arrived.
San Pedro, Ivory Coast's second port, had received 100,000 tonnes so far this season.
Cocoa arrivals typically decrease during the Christmas and New Year holiday periods.
Weather analysts noted rain in early December, which is usually a dry month.
Cocoa inspectors reported good quality with humidity levels of 8-10 percent and average bean sizes of 90 per 100 grammes.

Port dues at Ivory Coast's main port of Abidjan will rise by up to 6.4 percent from January 1.
The increase in port dues is intended to fund expansion projects.
Rates will increase by 6.3 percent for ships, 6.4 percent for container gantry cranes, 5.8 percent for containers, and 2.5 percent for cargo and other items.
The charges were agreed upon by Abidjan Port Authority in September and awaited government approval.
The cabinet has approved the new rates.
Shipping companies stated that the costs would probably have little impact but were awaiting more details from the Port Authority.
Some shipping managers indicated that if the increase is a port charge rather than a direct handling charge, it would be passed on to consumers.
Competition on West Africa-European routes may lead some companies to absorb costs to attract business.
More ships have been deployed in the West Africa region due to higher freight rates compared to Far Eastern routes.
International donors have been advocating for efficiency measures instead of infrastructure investment to enhance cargo handling capacity.

Chad is holding parliamentary elections on Sunday.
Voters in Chad hope that democratic reforms and oil development will end ethnic rivalry.
Approximately 300,000 nomads began voting on Thursday.
The total number of voters in Chad is 3.5 million.
There are 658 candidates from 49 parties competing for 125 seats in the new national assembly.
The new national assembly will convene on March 31.
President Idriss Deby won a presidential election in July against Wadal Abdelkader Kamougue.
Deby's Patriotic Salvation Movement is favored to win the upcoming election.
Election officials expect vote counting to conclude by Wednesday.
Provisional results are expected a week after the election, with final results by January 25.

Security forces in Chad have executed many people since a November decree allowed instant justice for criminals caught in the act.
Victims of public executions include a pregnant woman, street children, and suspected thieves.
Human rights groups believe many other killings have occurred secretly.
A charity worker named Marie-Odile reported that the execution policy has been in effect since November.
Officials confirmed the shoot-at-sight decree but did not provide specific numbers of those killed.
President Idriss Deby stated that organized gangs are a significant problem in N'Djamena.
Chad has faced internal conflict or war with Libya for over two decades until 1990.
A Western resident described crime as a major issue, with the army and bandits controlling the area.
Chad borders Sudan and the Central African Republic, and is seeking a strategy against cross-border banditry.
The Chadian Human Rights League reported that a docker was executed for breaking into an empty container, causing a pregnant woman to miscarry.

Ivorian cocoa arrivals for the 1996/97 season reached 640,000-650,000 tonnes by January 13.
The cocoa arrivals figure for January 13, 1996/97 is lower than the 730,000 tonnes recorded on the same date the previous year.
The 1996/97 cocoa arrivals include 50,000 tonnes from the first three weeks of October.
An exporter stated that there is too much cocoa in the port, leading to slowed buying in San Pedro due to lack of storage space.
Sources close to the Caisse de Stabilisation marketing board reported a higher arrivals total of 707,000 tonnes by December 27, excluding the pre-season 50,000 tonnes.
Some exporters estimated total arrivals at 555,000 tonnes by the end of December.
Cocoa arrivals were reported at about 60,000 tonnes per week.
Bean sizes averaged 95-97 beans per 100 grams, and humidity levels were around 9-10 percent.
National weather data indicated no rains at eight out of ten monitoring stations in the first ten days of January.
Up-country buyers reported that bush tracks had dried out and collection rates were normal.

Light rains in Ivory Coast after a dry start to January will help mid-crop cocoa crop development.
A crop analyst stated that more rain in January and February would be beneficial for cocoa crops.
Rain distribution was patchy, with most rainfall occurring in central and northern cocoa and coffee areas.
Key areas that received rainfall include Man, Daloa, Yamoussoukro, and Gagnoa.
Little rainfall was recorded in coastal areas around San Pedro and Abidjan.
A weather analyst noted that central areas have seen a surplus of rain while southern areas are in deficit.
One crop analyst reported good light showers in most cocoa areas after an up-country tour.
Dry harmattan conditions from the Sahara have retreated northwards and did not reach southern Ivory Coast as expected.
Cocoa humidity levels remained around 8-10 percent, which is above the exportable quality of eight percent.
Coffee farmers faced drying problems, and export activity remained low with shipments at 10,492 tonnes for October to December.

Ivory Coast's 1996/97 coffee output is expected to exceed last season's figures.
Rising coffee volumes are causing quality issues, according to regional buyers and exporters' agents.
Coffee marketing is currently sluggish but is expected to improve in February.
One buyer in the Man region reported that there is a lot of coffee available, but its quality is poor.
Exporters have purchased little coffee so far and have made significant quality adjustments.
Port forwarding agents have not reported major quality problems with coffee received for export.
One quality inspector estimated that as little as 150,000 tonnes of coffee could be shipped this season.
Ivory Coast opened its 1996/97 coffee season on November 14 amid falling prices.
The forecast output for this season is 230,000 tonnes, compared to 180,000 tonnes last year.
Farmgate prices for coffee were reduced by 200 CFA to 500 CFA per kilo.

Ivory Coast opened three days of cocoa sector reform talks on Wednesday.
The talks aim to fine-tune donor-sponsored liberalisation policies.
Bean quality is a key topic on the agenda of the talks.
Philippe Mian is the president of Ivory Coast's Consultative Committee, which is hosting the talks.
Louis Bensdorp is the president of the Dutch Cocoa Association.
The Consultative Committee was established in October under the World Bank Agricultural Sector Adjustment Credit (ASAC).
Ivory Coast has liberalised internal and some external cocoa marketing functions since 1990.
There are concerns regarding cocoa quality and the functioning of a new commodities auction system in place since May 1996.
Guy-Alain Gauze is Ivory Coast's commodities minister.
The auction system allows 85 percent of Ivorian cocoa export rights to be auctioned to local exporters, with 15 percent reserved for direct sale to traders abroad.

African robusta producers will meet to discuss export limit quotas on February 26-27.
The meeting follows a January world agreement in Rio de Janeiro to support prices.
Ivory Coast's Commodities Minister, Gauze, is also the chairman of the Interafrican Coffee Organisation.
Gauze did not provide details about the meeting venue.
The meeting will focus on how to divide export limits among African producers.
Gauze called off talks in Bali with Asian robusta producers on February 5.
The world Association of Coffee Producing Countries decided on January 23 to cut robusta exports by one million bags.
The export limitation is expected to be shared between African and Asian producers.
Gauze stated that Africa's export limitation share is 850,000 bags.
Indonesia has decided to reduce its exports by 150,000 bags from January to June 1997.

Debt reduction is the central task of top managers at Time Warner Inc after the $7.5 billion Turner deal.
Time Warner took control of Turner Broadcasting System Inc last week.
Time Warner is in discussions to restructure its cable-television partnership with U S West Media Group.
A Time Warner executive indicated that talks with U S West could yield a deal within months.
Ted Turner, founder of Turner Broadcasting and vice chairman of the combined company, wants Time Warner's $17.5 billion debt halved.
Time Warner and U S West have been partners since 1992.
U S West bought 25 percent of most of Time Warner's cable systems, film studios, and HBO pay-TV service in 1992.
Time Warner completed its takeover of Turner last week, a deal opposed in court by U S West.
U S West is expected to close its $5.3 billion acquisition of Continental Cablevision next month.
Time Warner now sees itself primarily as a programming group after acquiring Turner.

Silver King Communications Inc. agreed to buy the Home Shopping Network (HSN) for about $1.3 billion in stock.
Barry Diller is the chairman of both Silver King and Home Shopping.
The acquisition may position Diller's companies to compete with ABC, NBC, CBS, and Fox.
Silver King owns 12 TV stations that were spun off by HSN in 1992.
Diller plans to drop HSN programming from Silver King's stations and replace it with locally oriented news and sports.
Diller stated that cash generated by HSN would help Silver King pay for programming and other costs.
Details of Silver King's programming will be unveiled in November or December.
