Richard Branson's Virgin Group has secured the CrossCountry passenger rail franchise.
Virgin Group plans to invest an additional 250 million pounds on new trains and increased services.
CrossCountry operates over 100 stations and is based in Birmingham, UK.
CrossCountry is one of the last passenger rail franchises awarded under Britain's rail privatisation programme.
CrossCountry has 842 staff and reported passenger revenues of 108 million pounds for the year ending March 30.
Will Whitehorn, director of Virgin Rail, stated that the company plans to purchase a new fleet as part of the franchise bid.
Train orders for the new fleet will be placed next year, with deliveries expected in 2002.
Virgin Rail will receive a subsidy of 115 million pounds in the first year of the 15-year franchise.
The subsidy amount is 12 million pounds less than the subsidy received in 1996/97.
Virgin Rail will refurbish existing HST 125 diesel trains and increase train miles by 14 percent.

LucasVarity announced a corporate shake-up involving 13 non-core disposals and a plan to cut 3,000 jobs worldwide over two years.
LucasVarity was formed by the merger of Britain's Lucas Industries and Varity Corp of the U.S.
The company expects to achieve operating savings of 120 million pounds, which is double the anticipated amount after the merger.
LucasVarity's shares initially rose to a 12-month high of 263 pence following the announcement.
Comments about the auto industry during a conference call caused the stock to drop by 16.5 pence to close at 234 pence.
LucasVarity expects to incur an additional one-off charge of 130 million pounds, mainly in non-cash items.
The company plans to cut its worldwide headcount by 3,000 as part of its restructuring efforts.
Thirteen companies have been identified for sale following a three-month review after the merger.
Victor Rice, the chief executive, stated that the company is in active negotiations regarding the sale of some of the 13 businesses.
The eight named businesses for sale include small niche firms in Britain, Argentina, and South Africa, with combined sales of 270 million pounds.

SaveSmart Inc. is a start-up company based in Mountain View, Calif.
SaveSmart plans to unveil a credit card-based scheme for consumers to find bargains from various merchants.
Consumers can qualify for automated discounts on items such as groceries, dining, movies, clothing, furniture, and auto repairs.
SaveSmart's special credit card aims to eliminate the inconvenience of paper-based promotional coupons.
Only about 2 percent of paper coupons are redeemed, according to industry figures.
SaveSmart claims its service enhances sales promotions and is cost-effective for merchants.
Bernard David is the executive vice president of business development at SaveSmart.
The interactive promotion service could significantly impact the $120 billion industry, according to advertising analysts.
Mary Doyle is a Web marketing analyst for IDC/Link Resources.
SaveSmart's website offers an online database of personalized merchant promotions.

Computer Associates International Inc. issued its quarterly financial results.
The company's financial results exceeded Wall Street's consensus forecast.
The stock price fell sharply after executives announced plans to accelerate investments in personal computer-based corporate software products.
The company plans to de-emphasize mainframe software sales.
International sales for the company fell about 5 percent in the latest quarter compared to the previous year.
Computer Associates shares lost more than $4 in early trading.
The stock regained some ground later in the day after analysts reaffirmed 'buy' ratings and raised future earnings projections.
The stock closed at $62.875, down $2.75 on the day, on the New York Stock Exchange.
President Sanjay Kumar confirmed plans to increase investments in the PC-related mid-range software business.
Mid-range software accounted for about 31 percent of overall revenue in the latest quarter.

Computer Associates International Inc is set to announce deals to extend its systems management software onto new computer platforms.
The deals are expected to strengthen ties with Microsoft Corp's Windows NT.
Analysts expect CA to announce that its software will run on Novell and Tandem computer systems.
Computer Associates has scheduled press conferences with Microsoft, Intel Corp, and Tandem Computers Inc.
The announcements are expected to be made at the CA World conference starting Sunday in New Orleans.
Chet Geschickter from Hurwitz Consulting Group expects CA and Microsoft to announce tighter integration of CA's Unicenter with Microsoft's BackOffice suite.
CA and Microsoft have a co-marketing pact for CA/Unicenter for Windows NT that was announced in 1995.
Morgan Stanley analyst Chuck Philips speculated that CA and Tandem have agreed to a partnership for CA to port its software to Tandem's transaction computers.
An analyst predicted that CA and Intel would announce a deal for CA to market Intel's LANdesk Novell network management software.
Computer Associates is the world's top mainframe software supplier and the second largest independent software firm after Microsoft.

AT&T Corp named John Walter as heir to Chairman and Chief Executive Robert Allen.
AT&T believes it must take a gamble to prepare for increased competition.
John Walter was previously the chief executive of R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co.
Walter will replace Allen as CEO and chairman in 18 months.
Robert Miles, a corporate turnaround consultant, compared AT&T's challenges to those faced by IBM.
Analysts credited Walter with successfully guiding Donnelley through expansion into marketing services.
Walter has a reputation for understanding business operations and profitability.
At Donnelley, Walter closed underperforming businesses.
Donnelley spun off Metromail Corp and plans to spin off Donnelley Enterprise Solutions Inc.
Financial analysts are skeptical about Walter's ability to manage AT&T's larger scale.

Microsoft Corp. and Fore Systems Inc. plan to announce a deal on Tuesday.
Microsoft will license Fore's high-speed networking technology for future versions of its Windows operating system software.
Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) is an emerging technology for higher speed networks that can handle voice, video, and data simultaneously.
The deal will integrate Fore's ATM emulation software into the Windows operating system.
This integration will allow desktop office computers to use ATM technology without changing existing software.
The deal could open a potential market of millions of PC users to adopt ATM network technology.
The integration will ensure compatibility with older network technologies.
Industry analysts believe Microsoft's support of ATM will increase its legitimacy with corporate network administrators.
Mary Petrosky, a network analyst, stated that connecting PCs to ATM networks will be easier with the new deal.
Existing technologies like Ethernet and Token Ring remain dominant in corporate office networks.

AT&T Corp. is facing competition in its long-distance phone business.
AT&T needs to enter new markets and is undergoing a management transition.
British Telecommunications Plc announced plans to acquire the remaining 80 percent of MCI Communications Inc. that it does not already own.
The acquisition values MCI at more than $20 billion.
AT&T called on U.S. and European regulators to condition approval of the merger on increased competition in the UK market.
British Telecom claims it operates in one of the world's most open markets.
The merger will combine MCI's marketing skills with British Telecom's financial resources to form a new entity called Concert.
Analysts believe the merger will enhance British Telecom's and MCI's global resource pooling and strategy coordination.
AT&T's share of the U.S. long-distance market has decreased from 60 percent to under 55 percent in two years.
MCI is expected to increase its efforts in the local U.S. phone market with British Telecom's financial support.

Leading data networking stocks experienced profit-taking on Tuesday.
Securities analysts reported that profit-taking followed strong price gains in recent weeks.
Cisco Systems Inc opened at a 52-week high of 67.
Cisco Systems Inc's stock retreated to 65-1/8 during the day.
Cabletron Systems Inc began to decline immediately after Tuesday's opening.
Cabletron Systems Inc lost 1-1/8 to 67-3/4 by mid-afternoon.
3Com Corp's stock also fell after the opening.
3Com Corp was down 2 to 70-1/8 by mid-afternoon.

CompuServe Corp investors' fears were allayed by H&R Block Inc's decision to postpone plans to spin off the remaining 80 percent interest in CompuServe.
Analysts noted that the potential market inundation by the 74.2 million CompuServe shares held by H&R Block had negatively impacted the stock's prospects.
Analyst Peter Krasilovsky of Arlen Communications expressed relief at H&R Block's decision.
CompuServe faces challenges including declining online membership counts and the failure of its new WOW! consumer service.
Other analysts praised H&R Block's decision to postpone a shareholder vote on the spin-off but expressed concerns about the implications for stocks like CompuServe and America Online Inc.
An unnamed analyst stated that the online market is at a crossroads and appears unstable.
CompuServe's issues have negatively affected America Online's stock price.
Analysts indicated that while competition from Internet access providers may have contributed to the slowdown of established online service providers, most of CompuServe's problems are unique.
On Wednesday, CompuServe stock rose to 13-1/2, while H&R Block stock fell to 26-1/4.
America Online stock increased to 31-5/8 by mid-afternoon.

Semiconductor equipment stocks surged on Friday.
Investors reacted positively to signs that the downturn in the chip industry has hit bottom.
Applied Materials Inc. reported lower earnings but indicated that profit margins would remain higher than in prior downturns.
Analysts raised Applied Materials' rating from 'hold' to 'buy' following its report.
Applied Materials stock increased by $6.625 to $38.625 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.
KLA Instruments Corp. stock rose by $5 to $38.25.
Tencor Instruments stock increased by $5.50 to $26.75.
Lam Research Corp. stock went up by $4.625 to $34.125.
Intel Corp. stock rose by $3.125 to $122.
Sales of personal computers are expected to increase demand for chip-making equipment.

Texas Instruments Inc. established a licensing agreement with Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. that will generate over $1 billion in royalty payments over 10 years.
Both companies agreed to drop pending patent infringement lawsuits against each other as part of the agreement.
The new agreement replaces a previous five-year deal that expired at the end of 1995.
Merrill Lynch analyst Thomas Kurlak stated that the terms of the new agreement appear to be less generous than the previous agreement with Samsung in 1995.
Kurlak assessed that the new agreement's royalty formula is at roughly 40 to 50 percent of the rate of the old agreement.
The new license covers a broad base of patents from both companies, including semiconductors, personal computers, consumer products, and telecommunications equipment.
Texas Instruments expects to receive about $105 million from Samsung in the fourth quarter for catch-up royalties covering the first nine months of 1996.
Analysts indicated that the catch-up payments should significantly boost earnings for the quarter ending in December.
Kurlak estimated that Texas Instruments will see $35 million in additional quarterly royalties from the Samsung deal going forward.
Texas Instruments has nearly completed its 1995 round of patent cross-license agreements with major semiconductor makers.

Flextronics International Inc Chief Executive Michael Marks expects revenues of around $1 billion during fiscal 1998.
This revenue expectation is more than double the $500 million expected in fiscal 1997.
Flextronics' stock price declined by 12-1/4 to 25 after the company announced a restructuring plan.
The restructuring plan is likely to dampen near-term profits.
Marks stated that Flextronics' restructuring is designed to allow the company to gain market share.
Marks anticipates annual earnings growth of 35-40 percent through the year 2000.
Marks claims that Flextronics will be third in the market by revenues next year, rising from its current fourth place position.
Only SCI Systems Inc and Solectron Corp are larger than Flextronics in the market.
Marks attributed the stock price decline to the volatility of the Nasdaq market and the departure of momentum investors.
Flextronics announced that its restructuring would include charges of $5 to $7 million over the December and March quarters.

Technology stocks rose on Wednesday due to increased belief that price-cutting has boosted holiday personal computer sales.
Money managers purchased stocks to enhance their portfolios at year-end.
The rally was influenced by positive comments from Soundview analyst Mark Specker regarding Compaq Computer Corp.
Fears of poor holiday sales for PC manufacturers diminished.
Mark Specker upgraded his short-term rating on Compaq to buy from hold and recommended buying the stock for long-term gains.
Specker's recommendations on technology stocks are influential among institutional investors.
Other PC makers like Dell Computer Corp. also benefited from the rally.
Compaq's stock rose by $6.375 to $78.625 on Nasdaq.
International Business Machines Corp. added $6.75 to $158.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Intel Corp. was the most active stock on Nasdaq, gaining $5.75 to $135.75.

Foreign investors have shown strong interest in a new share offering by Sakura Bank Ltd.
Sakura Bank Ltd. is Japan's fourth-biggest bank.
The bank issued preferred shares last month despite its weak financial strength rating.
Demand for Sakura's preferred shares reached nearly two trillion yen ($18 billion) for an offering of 150 billion yen ($1.35 billion).
Kazuya Johno is the assistant general manager at Sakura Bank's Planning Division.
Sakura issued 75 million shares of preferred stock at 2,000 yen ($18) each.
Sakura Bank is the fourth major Japanese bank to launch a convertible offering in the past year.
Holders of preferred shares do not receive voting rights but generally receive higher dividends than common shares.
Foreign investors are more positive about Japan's big banks compared to domestic investors.
Sakura's preferred stock was repackaged through an overseas trust for selling abroad.

Nippon Life Insurance Co plans to set up a joint venture in the Philippines.
Nippon Life will be the first Japanese company to sell life insurance policies abroad.
Nippon Life and the Yuchengco group will sign a contract by the year-end to establish the joint venture by next March.
Nippon Life will own 50 percent of the joint venture, which will be based in Manila.
Great Pacific Life Assurance Corp will own 30 percent of the joint venture.
Rizal Commercial Banking Corp will own 20 percent of the joint venture.
Nippon Life is expected to send several executives to the new company.
Nippon Life aims to sell policies to people in the medium to high income bracket and target Japanese firms in the Philippines.
Nippon Life is looking to expand into other lucrative markets in Asia.
Only an estimated five to 10 percent of people in Southeast Asia have life insurance policies.

Investors in Asian countries are increasingly interested in Tokyo's property market.
Richard Mandel is the managing director of the Japanese unit of Kennedy-Wilson Inc.
Kennedy-Wilson Inc. aims to attract foreign investors to Japan's real estate market.
Japan's real estate market has been in decline for five years.
The decline in Japan's real estate market is linked to bad loans from failed mortgage firms.
Asian investors view Tokyo as a significant global business center.
Real estate prices in Tokyo have decreased by 75 percent since the early 1990s.
Kennedy-Wilson has not finalized any deals in Tokyo since starting operations in 1995.
Negotiations are ongoing with Asian investors for commercial and apartment buildings in central Tokyo.
Japanese property prices are lower than those in Hong Kong and Singapore.

Japan's financial industry is recovering from the effects of bad debts from the economic bubble years.
Smaller banks and loan institutions continue to experience difficulties due to bad loans.
Analysts believe the worst of the bad loan situation has passed due to government and major bank efforts.
Further serious damage to the financial system is considered unlikely by analysts.
Small financial institutions are struggling with soured loans from the late 1980s lending boom.
Restoring confidence in the banking sector is expected to take years due to ongoing issues.
The collapse of Nichiei Finance Co Ltd and losses at a regional bank have unsettled financial markets.
Biwako Bank reported losses due to suspected misappropriation but stated it remains in sound health.
Tobishima Corp's new restructuring program raised concerns about additional burdens on banks.
Katsuhito Sasajima from Nikko Research Center stated that banks are addressing bad loans in stages.

A loan-collecting body is seeking the involuntary bankruptcy of Sueno Kosan, a major real estate firm.
If declared bankrupt, Sueno Kosan would be one of the largest business failures in Japan's history.
Sueno Kosan has estimated total liabilities of 670 billion yen, equivalent to $5.87 billion.
The bankruptcy request was made to the Osaka District Court by the Housing Loan Administration Corp (HLAC).
Sueno Kosan is a major borrower from the 'jusen' mortgage firms, which collapsed during the 1980s bubble economy.
Finance Minister Wataru Kubo stated that the Sueno Kosan issue could affect financial firms that lent it money.
The price of Japanese government bonds rose to record levels due to concerns about the banking industry.
Kohei Nakabo, president of HLAC, indicated that the bankruptcy filing was somewhat expected.
Sueno Kosan chief Kenichi Sueno pleaded guilty to charges of hiding assets from creditors.
Noboru Matsuda, governor of the Deposit Insurance Corp of Japan, stated that bankruptcy action would be necessary for some borrowers like Sueno Kosan.

Japan's Finance Ministry has decided to relax its regulations on the corporate pension system.
Industry sources claim the Finance Ministry's proposals do not adequately address the needs of Japan's aging society and the financial issues of pension funds.
An official from an overseas-based investment advisory company stated that Japan needs a drastic overhaul of its corporate pension system.
The total amount held by Japanese corporate pension funds has grown to approximately 60 trillion yen ($540 billion).
Yoshihiko Miyauchi, a member of an advisory panel to the prime minister, reported that the Finance Ministry plans to abolish restrictions on investment locations for employee pension funds managed by trust banks.
Current rules require trust banks to invest at least half of the funds in fixed-income assets and limit investments in Japanese stocks, foreign currency-denominated shares and bonds, and real estate.
Japan's corporate pension system includes employee pension funds supervised by the Welfare Ministry and Tax-Qualified Retirement Pension plans (TQPs) supervised by the Finance Ministry.
The Finance Ministry is considering allowing investment advisory firms to manage TQPs and is studying the possibility of variable yields and flexible benefits.
The Welfare Ministry has lifted restrictions on employee pension fund management and allowed investment advisory firms to manage these funds.
Employers in the corporate pension system must maintain specified yields of 5.5 percent per year, while the actual return on investments is about three percent.

Japan's 20 biggest banks reported half-year results indicating they have returned to profitability despite significant write-offs of problem loans.
Analysts noted that all of Japan's major banks continued to actively write off problem loans linked to the collapse of the 1980s real estate bubble.
The 10 largest commercial banks announced their interim earnings and loan write-off statistics on a Friday.
The combined write-offs by the 20 largest banks totaled approximately 2.4 trillion yen ($21.4 billion) for the six months ending September 30.
In the previous fiscal year, the 20 largest banks disposed of nearly 11 trillion yen ($98.2 billion) worth of problem loans.
As of the end of March, the Finance Ministry reported that the 20 banks had around 25 trillion yen ($223 billion) in problem loans.
Problem loans include loans made to bankrupt companies and those with interest payments overdue by six months or more.
Analyst Katsuhito Sasajima predicted that the 20 banks might dispose of at least five trillion yen ($44.6 billion) in problem loans during the current fiscal year.
Analysts indicated that many large banks are recovering from issues related to problem loans, but some financially weak banks will continue to face challenges.
Three long-term credit banks reported parent current profits for the first half of the year after experiencing losses in 1995-1996.

A bill to lift a 50-year-old ban on holding companies is expected to be submitted to Japan's next parliament.
Economists believe the passage of the bill is almost assured due to the government's deregulation plans.
The financial industry is expected to benefit first from the lifting of the ban.
Political delays have postponed a decision on the holding companies ban for almost a year.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto plans to liberalize financial markets by 2001.
The proposed breakup of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) is part of the plan to lift the ban.
A holding company controls one or more companies but does not engage in a specific business.
Big business has pressured the government to lift the ban to streamline and compete with overseas rivals.
The Fair Trade Commission (FTC) plans to submit a bill to end the ban in January.
The FTC previously sought to revise the Anti-Monopoly Law to remove the ban but faced opposition.

A tentative deal was reached between the United States and Japan to open Japan's insurance market.
The deal is expected to create disruptions in the insurance industry but is seen as a step towards financial sector deregulation.
The agreement was reached on a Saturday, ending a dispute identified by U.S. President Bill Clinton as a significant trade barrier.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher contacted his Japanese counterpart to apply pressure before the deadline.
Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto expressed relief that the agreement was finalized.
Insurance trade groups criticized the agreement for not addressing consumer needs and limiting access to growing market segments.
The agreement allows Japanese companies to gradually enter the 'third sector' of insurance, which includes cancer and healthcare coverage.
Foreign firms are anticipated to benefit from deregulation of rates in the non-life insurance sector by the end of 1998.
Analysts believe that changes in the insurance market were already underway as part of Hashimoto's efforts to revitalize Japan's financial sector.
Income from auto insurance policies constitutes 40 percent to 50 percent of revenue for non-life insurance companies.

More Japanese finance firms are preparing for court-protected liquidation.
Analysts state that Japan's banking sector faces a long recovery from bad loans.
The banking sector is struggling to eliminate troubled finance firms and regain credibility.
Concerns exist about potential unexpected bad news affecting the banking sector.
Japan's stock market decline could hinder recovery efforts.
All Corp has debts of 274.5 billion yen ($2.36 billion).
Sanwa Tatemono Sogo Finance Co has debts of 66.4 billion yen ($572 million).
CS Sogo Service has debts of 71.3 billion yen ($614 million).
Ubumi Sagara, president of All Corp, announced a shareholders' meeting to seek approval for liquidation.
All Corp's cumulative debt exceeded its assets by 195.4 billion yen ($1.68 billion) as of September 1996.

Japan's major securities houses believe that deregulating commissions on stock transactions is essential to retain major customers.
Many Japanese brokers oppose the liberalisation of commissions.
An increase in Japanese individuals buying stocks through overseas brokers has been noted to avoid higher domestic commissions.
Deregulation of commissions should be implemented gradually to protect small brokerages that rely on commissions for revenue.
The Big Four brokers in Japan are Nomura Securities, Daiwa Securities, Nikko Securities, and Yamaichi Securities.
The Big Four are preparing for the liberalisation of broking fees due to concerns about losing customers.
Japanese brokers charge 535,000 yen for buying or selling a contract worth 500 million yen, while overseas fees are less than half that amount.
The Big Four relied on commissions for about 30 percent of their revenue in the fiscal year ending March 31, 1995.
Commissions accounted for over 70 percent of revenues for many of Japan's 230 smaller brokerages.
The Pension Welfare Service Public Corp commissioned investment advisory companies to manage its funds, which led to trading in London to save on fees.

Investor confidence in Japan's banking sector is currently low.
Bank shares declined following rumors about Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) holding an emergency news conference.
Masaaki Higashida, a strategist at Nomura Securities, stated that the negative trend in the banking sector has not ended.
Analysts believe that it is difficult to predict the extent of the decline in bank shares.
There are no quick solutions to restore confidence in the banking sector aside from improving asset quality.
Katsuhito Sasajima, an analyst at Nikko Research Centre, indicated that the banking sector may remain under pressure until Japan completes its Big Bang financial reforms.
Yoshinobu Yamada, an analyst at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc, noted that land prices under pressure could further erode the market's view of banks' financial health.
Financially weak banks need to reduce non-performing loans and less-profitable assets to regain investor confidence.
Some opposition politicians in parliament are advocating for the use of public money to address problem loans.
Moody's Investor Service downgraded the ratings outlook for NCB and three other Japanese banks to negative due to serious asset quality problems.

Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and its allies agreed to lift a ban on holding companies.
The ban was put in place by U.S. Occupation forces shortly after World War Two.
Party members stated that lifting the ban will help Japanese firms restructure and boost their international competitiveness.
Taku Yamasaki, chairman of LDP's policy-setting committee, said diversified corporate management is necessary for international competition.
The anti-monopoly law had contributed to Japan's economic development over the past 50 years.
Changes to the anti-monopoly law are needed for economic and financial reform.
The agreement involves the LDP, the Social Democratic Party (SDP), and the Sakigake party.
The government plans to submit changes to the anti-monopoly law to parliament in March.
Yamasaki indicated that the revised law could take effect within a year, possibly next January.
Lifting the ban is necessary for restructuring Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) into several companies.

China's efforts to push domestic investors out of foreign currency B shares on its stock markets have not succeeded.
B share trading volumes have significantly decreased since the announcement of the ban on local investors buying B shares.
On September 21, official media announced a ban on local investors purchasing B shares listed on the Shenzhen and Shanghai stock exchanges.
Domestic investors have accounted for more than 50 percent of B share trading on both of China's stock exchanges in recent months.
Traders and analysts report that local investors continue to support B share prices despite the ban.
The ban on local investors buying B shares has not been strictly enforced, allowing some to continue purchasing them.
B share trading volumes have dropped significantly since the ban was announced, raising concerns about a potential market collapse.
Foreign investors sold their shares and exited the market during a surge in domestic B share buying earlier this year.
Beijing authorities are concerned about a potential outflow of foreign exchange if foreign investors are allowed to sell B shares to local investors.
A Shenzhen stock analyst predicts that the B share market in Shenzhen will gradually open up to domestic investors after the return of Hong Kong to China in mid-1997.

Many Internet users in China commonly complain about not being able to access the Playboy website.
China controls information more strictly than most countries.
China is gradually increasing Internet access despite challenges associated with free information dissemination.
Security filters were implemented on main Internet access servers in Beijing and Shanghai in the middle of the year.
Restrictions on ordinary people opening Internet accounts have been removed after a testing period.
The filters block access to politically sensitive sites and sexually explicit sites like Playboy.
Internet usage in China is rapidly increasing, leading to overloaded phonelines.
The growth of Internet usage is outpacing infrastructure investment, causing technical problems.
There are no longer restrictions on Chinese people signing up for Internet access, according to Zhang Weihua from Shanghai's Post and Telecommunications Bureau.
As of the end of August, there were 3,200 registered Internet accounts on the Shanghai server, with an increase of several hundred accounts per month.

Shanghai's foreign currency B share market has been hitting historic lows over the past two weeks.
Analysts predict little prospect of recovery for the B share market until at least the middle of next year.
Foreign investors have largely sold their holdings in the B share market and left it to local investors.
Disappointing company results and the failure to add new, sizeable companies have diminished foreign investor confidence.
The B share index closed down 0.809 points or 1.77 percent to a record low of 44.867 points on Monday.
The B share market has hit all-time lows on five separate days over the past two weeks.
The performance of companies in the B share market for the full year of 1996 is unlikely to improve.
The local A share market continues to attract significant investment and is setting two-year highs.
National growth in China is expected to reach at least nine percent this year.
Many B share firms were formerly state-run enterprises, and their management practices have not significantly changed.

China unveiled its first major shipping exchange on Tuesday.
The Shanghai Shipping Exchange aims to consolidate and standardize ship chartering and cargo fixing in East China.
All shipping and freight companies in the East China region have been instructed to move their business to the Shanghai Shipping Exchange.
The Shanghai Shipping Exchange will allow ship owners and charterers to arrange deals and fix prices for carrying cargoes.
The exchange has the direct support of the Beijing authorities and has been under preparation for two years.
The founding members of the exchange include 116 companies, mostly shipping firms from Shanghai and the adjacent provinces of Zhejiang and Jiangsu.
Zhang Jinxiang, an official with COSCO, stated that the exchange demonstrates the government's determination to make Shanghai an international shipping center.
Zhu Yongguang, a senior Ministry of Communications official, mentioned that the Shanghai exchange is one of several planned shipping exchanges in China.
The exchange will handle international cargo-fixing, but most initial business is expected to be domestic.
The establishment of the exchange was welcomed by an official from Shanghai Haixing Shipping Co.

Shanghai city is in the process of renting out the former Hongkong & Shanghai Bank building on the riverside Bund to an unnamed bank.
The senior official Zhou Jinbao stated that final negotiations are ongoing with two or three contenders for the building.
The building was constructed in 1925 and symbolizes the financial power of the British Empire.
Zhou Jinbao is the general manager of the Bund Buildings Transformation Corp.
Zhou Jinbao confirmed that the Hongkong & Shanghai Bank will not be the tenant.
The Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd, a unit of HSBC Holdings Plc, had discussions with Shanghai city officials for over two years but decided not to proceed with the proposal.
The Hongkong Bank proposed to demolish several buildings behind the main structure to build a modern office tower.
Zhou Jinbao stated that the proposal from the Hongkong Bank would impact wider development plans for the area, which are not yet finalized.
The main building has 24,000 square meters of space, and the expected rental price is around three U.S. dollars per square meter per day.
The lease term can be for any period up to 30 or 40 years.

China's B shares surged on Tuesday with Shanghai's index gaining 11.63 percent.
The Shenzhen index increased by 4.7 percent.
Trading volume on the Shanghai B share market reached a 15-month high of 63.595.
The Shanghai B share index ended up 6.525 points at 62.639 points.
Market sentiment was boosted by the strong performance of the Shenzhen B share market.
The Shenzhen B share index rose 7.42 points to end at 165.10.
Foreign investors are showing increased interest in Shanghai B shares.
ING Barings activated its seats on the Shanghai Stock Exchange for the first time due to heavy trading volume.
Shanghai Dajiang surged 34.37 percent to $0.516 on a volume of 1.1 million shares.
Shanghai Jintai increased by 28.78 percent to $0.170 on a volume of 712,000 shares.

China is expected to maintain its tight credit policy at the end of the year.
Local fixed asset investment is threatening economic over-heating in China.
Analysts noted that a surge in fixed asset projects since July influenced Beijing's decision to keep austerity measures.
Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji stated the need to control new fixed asset investment projects.
Zhu Rongji emphasized the importance of curbing inflation and controlling new industrial projects during a visit to Fujian.
The People's Daily criticized provinces for rushing to invest in high-profile industries, highlighting 22 provinces focusing on car production.
A Beijing-based official from the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China warned of inflation resurgence and economic over-heating due to rising fixed asset investment.
Retail price inflation growth is expected to slow to six percent year on year in 1996.
Local governments have approved 700 new fixed asset investments since July.
China's State Planning Commission estimates fixed asset investment will reach 2.3 trillion yuan in 1996.

China's Shanghai Pudong Development Bank will rent the former headquarters of the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp.
The building is located on the city's waterfront Bund.
A signing ceremony for the lease will be held on Thursday.
The building was opened in 1925 and symbolizes the financial might of the British Empire.
The Pudong Development Bank is a state-owned Chinese bank based in the Pudong Development Zone.
The Shanghai city government is the majority owner of the Pudong Development Bank.
The lease duration agreed upon is 30 years.
The building has a total floorspace of 24,000 square metres.
The property was believed to be worth at least $3 per square metre.
The Hongkong Bank had discussions with Shanghai city officials for over two years regarding control of the building.

The former Hongkong & Shanghai Bank headquarters on the Bund in Shanghai became a bank again on Thursday.
The Shanghai Pudong Development Bank signed a 30-year lease for the building.
The building was first opened in 1925.
The city of Shanghai failed to find a foreign bank to rent or buy the building.
The city spent two years discussing terms with Hongkong Bank but did not reach an agreement.
Hongkong Bank, owned by HSBC Holdings Plc, announced it would not take back the building.
Bankers stated that the city asked for an unrealistically high price for the building.
The building was the Shanghai headquarters of the Chinese Communist Party from 1949 until last year.
The chairman of the Pudong bank, Zhuang Xiaotan, stated that the bank would pay an annual rent of 145 million yuan.
The Pudong Development Bank plans to build its own headquarters in Pudong, which will be ready around the year 2000.

China's stock market crackdown is driven by fears of social instability due to market volatility.
The crackdown aims to prevent disruption from foreign and domestic speculators before the Hong Kong handover in mid-1997.
Analysts state that social stability is the primary concern of the Chinese leadership during the transitional period of Deng Xiaoping's political exit.
A Shenzhen-based broker reported rumors that surges in the Shenzhen market were supported by overseas funds from Hong Kong and Macau.
The People's Daily criticized the stock markets for overheating due to speculation and warned against government intervention in case of a crash.
In response to the commentary, stock exchanges implemented a 10 percent limit on price movements for individual shares.
Most shares on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges reached the 10 percent limit-down level on Monday and Tuesday.
Since April, share prices on the two markets have increased by over 100 percent on average.
A political analyst noted that the central government acted at an appropriate time before the Hong Kong takeover.
A spokesman for the China Securities Regulatory Commission stated that the crackdown aims to protect retail investors and develop the markets.

China's young stock markets have experienced significant losses in share values.
Analysts have highlighted widespread irregularities and a lack of regulatory structure in China's stock markets.
A warning from Beijing regarding speculation preceded a week of losses on the exchanges.
The situation reflects a historical boom-and-bust cycle in China's markets.
An economist stated that widespread irregularities are partly a legacy of the old planned economy.
Some firms resort to irregularities to survive due to the influence of administrative edicts on the markets.
Beijing's announcement aimed to reduce speculative trading but may have the opposite effect, according to analysts.
A trader noted that policy changes are a key speculative topic in China's stock markets.
Market sources indicated that using market means instead of administrative edicts could have led to less volatile market responses.
Shanghai's A share index fell 20.07 percent to 922.34 points at the close of Friday's trading.

Chen Yifei is China's top-selling modern artist.
Chen Yifei is currently in Shanghai.
Chen Yifei is planning to shift his subject matter to illustrate China's Generation X.
Chen Yifei opened his first retrospective exhibition on Saturday in the new Shanghai Museum.
The exhibition will run until January 19 before touring other cities.
The exhibition features more than 40 works from public and private sources.
The works include drawings from Chen's youth during the 1960s Cultural Revolution and his latest paintings of Tibetan peasants.
Chen Yifei aims to capture the feel of Chinese urban youth in the mid-1990s in his future works.
Chen holds the record for the highest price paid at auction for a modern Chinese painting, which is 2.86 million yuan ($344,000).
Chen Yifei emigrated to the United States in 1980 and is the first mainland Chinese artist to do so in modern times.

Production at the nickel deposit at Voisey's Bay in Labrador is not expected to begin for several years.
Environmental concerns and pressure from aboriginal groups may delay production at Voisey's Bay.
Inco Ltd is a Toronto-based company that gained control of the Voisey's Bay nickel deposit after a bidding war.
Inco Ltd planned to start open pit production at Voisey's Bay by 1998.
Inco Ltd planned to begin full-scale underground mining at Voisey's Bay by 2000.

Poor metal prices negatively impacted earnings at Canadian base metal miners in the third quarter.
Inco Ltd. reported a third-quarter profit of $29 million, down from $44 million a year earlier.
Falconbridge Ltd. earned $30.1 million in the third quarter, a decrease from $84.5 million the previous year.
Cominco Ltd. reported earnings of C$5.2 million in the third quarter, down from C$22 million last year.
All three companies cited copper prices as a significant factor in their earnings decline.
The average copper price on the London Metal Exchange in the third quarter was 90 cents a pound, down from $1.37 a year earlier.
The average nickel price for the quarter fell to $3.26 a pound from $3.92 at the same time last year.
Inco's stock rose C$1.15 to C$41.90 in Toronto trading.
Falconbridge's stock increased by 75 cents to C$29 in Toronto.
Cominco's stock gained C45 cents to C$30.65 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

Major mining companies may reconsider partnerships with Bre-X Minerals Ltd due to its new strategic alliance.
Bre-X announced an alliance with PT Panutan Duta, an Indonesian company controlled by Sigit Harjojudanto.
The alliance includes a support services company that will be owned 60 percent by Bre-X and 40 percent by Panutan.
The support services company will provide utilities, petroleum products, and limestone for the Busang gold discovery.
Analyst Doug Leishman stated that the new company could control significant parts of operating and capital costs.
Leishman warned that if services are not priced at normal market rates, it could lead to increased costs.
Any major mining company considering a bid for Bre-X must consider potential extra costs and loss of supply control.
Bre-X is seeking a major mining company to partner with for the development of the Busang discovery.
Barrick Gold Corp and Placer Dome Inc stated they need more details about the supply company before making a decision.
Bre-X's stock initially rose after the alliance announcement but later declined as investors recognized ongoing issues.

Royal Oak Mines Inc is focusing on low-cost gold deposits in the Timmins area and British Columbia.
Peggy Witte is the president of Royal Oak Mines Inc.
Royal Oak Mines Inc will close its mine in Hope Brook, Newfoundland.
Royal Oak Mines Inc will write down the reserves at its Colomac mine in the Northwest Territories.
Royal Oak expects to incur C$37.4 million in charges due to the decisions regarding Hope Brook and Colomac.
The after-tax charges will decrease net income by about C$27 million or C$0.19 per share in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Royal Oak plans to move most mining and mill assets from Hope Brook to its Matachewan project in northern Ontario.
Hope Brook is scheduled to shut down in the third quarter of 1997.
Matachewan is expected to start production in the second half of 1998.
Royal Oak recently increased its gold reserves at its Timmins and Matachewan properties.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. has not communicated publicly since announcing a partnership with Sigit Harjojudanto, the son of Indonesian ruler Suharto.
The announcement of the partnership has caused concern among shareholders and prompted regulators to seek additional information.
Bre-X has not spoken to the press for several weeks and only responds to a select group of analysts.
Gold analyst Rick Cohen from Goepel Shields stated that he has not received any returned calls from Bre-X.
Bre-X announced its alliance with Sigit Harjojudanto on October 28.
The partnership is significant due to Sigit's extensive business influence in Indonesia.
Bre-X has chosen to release selected press materials instead of directly addressing questions about its business in Indonesia.
The company faxed a story from the Far Eastern Economic Review to media, analysts, and shareholders, which discussed its links with Sigit.
The article mentioned Sigit's potential connections with the Indonesian army and claimed that Barrick Gold Corp. attempted to pressure Bre-X into an unfavorable deal.
Bre-X has not confirmed or denied the claims made in the article and has not responded to inquiries about it.

The world potash market is experiencing significant changes.
Potash Corp of Saskatchewan Inc is the largest potash producer in the world.
Potash Corp is in discussions to acquire a controlling stake in Kali und Salz AG from BASF AG.
If successful, Potash Corp would control 25 percent of Germany's potash market.
Analysts estimate that the acquisition would increase Potash Corp's share of world production capacity from 35 percent to about 50 percent.
Asia Pacific Resources Ltd has made a significant potash discovery in Thailand.
Asia Pacific Resources claims that at least one mine in Thailand is economically viable.
Asia Pacific president Gerry Wright believes the property could produce about two million tonnes of potash by the year 2000.
Wright anticipates production could increase to between four and six million tonnes by 2005.
Asia Pacific has signed confidentiality agreements with eight companies to find a partner for mine development.

Barrick Gold Corp is negotiating to acquire a majority share in Indonesia's Busang gold discovery.
The Busang deposit contains at least 47 million ounces of gold.
The Indonesian government requested Bre-X Minerals Ltd to transfer 75 percent of its Busang stake to Barrick.
If the deal is completed, Barrick Gold Corp would become the world's leading gold producer.
Barrick Gold Corp's board includes former U.S. President George Bush and former Canadian Prime Minister Brian Mulroney.
Barrick Gold Corp produced about 3.1 million ounces of gold per year as of the time of the passage.
Barrick Gold Corp started with no gold production in 1983 and grew through acquisitions and exploration.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd acquired the Busang properties in 1993 and discovered gold there in 1995.
Bre-X's stock price increased significantly after the gold discovery, reaching over C$200 before a stock split.
Bre-X faced legal disputes and delays in obtaining mining permits due to ownership issues.

Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd has a December 4 deadline to make a deal with Barrick Gold Corp.
The Busang gold deposit in Indonesia is estimated to contain more than 57 million ounces of gold.
The cost to mine the gold at Busang is estimated at US$96 an ounce.
The Indonesian government has mandated that Bre-X must share its stake in Busang, with Barrick receiving 75 percent and Bre-X receiving 25 percent.
The Indonesian government, led by President Suharto, has expressed a desire for a 10 percent stake in Busang.
Some figures in the gold mining industry are protesting the deal between Bre-X and Barrick as unprecedented and unfair.
John Willson, CEO of Placer Dome Inc, stated that Bre-X should have a say in choosing its partner.
Placer Dome, Newmont Mining Corp, and Teck Corp have been negotiating for a stake in Busang.
These three companies were excluded from the process when Indonesia directed Bre-X to partner with Barrick.
Analysts suggest Barrick may have influenced the Indonesian government through political connections.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. and Barrick Gold Corp. are negotiating a deal regarding Indonesia's Busang gold deposit.
As of Wednesday, no final deal had been reached between Bre-X and Barrick.
Bre-X and Barrick are addressing several unresolved issues in their negotiations.
Bre-X's Chief Executive David Walsh stated that the main issues are regulatory in nature.
Walsh mentioned that he could not disclose details due to a confidentiality agreement.
The Indonesian government has instructed Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick by December 4.
Under the proposed joint venture, Barrick would receive 75 percent of Bre-X's stake in the gold discovery.
Bre-X would retain 25 percent of its stake in the joint venture.
The Indonesian government may receive 10 percent of the gold discovery from the companies.
Bre-X stated that no new deadline had been set by the Indonesian Mines Ministry.

North America's major gold companies are competing to become the world's biggest gold producer.
Hugh Leggatt is a spokesman for Vancouver-based gold firm Placer Dome Inc.
Placer Dome has made a $600 million bid for Highlands Gold Ltd. and the 25 percent of Placer Pacific Ltd. it does not already own.
Placer Dome plans to raise $300 million through a preferred share issue and sell off some small Canadian mine properties.
Placer Dome is interested in Bre-X Minerals Ltd., which discovered the Busang deposit in Indonesia.
Barrick Gold Corp. is based in Toronto and is currently the world's most profitable gold company.
Barrick Gold Corp. aims to surpass Anglo American Corp. and Gold Fields to become the world's largest gold company.
Jakarta has requested Barrick and Bre-X to form a joint venture to develop the Busang deposit, with Barrick controlling 75 percent.
Newmont Mining Corp. was interested in Bre-X but shifted focus to Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp. after Barrick gained an advantage.
Homestake Mining Co. has made a $2.3 billion bid for Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp.

The Indonesian government regained control over the Busang gold deposit on Monday.
Barrick Gold Corp. and Bre-X Minerals Ltd. submitted a joint development proposal for the Busang deposit.
The Busang deposit contains at least 57 million ounces of gold.
Bre-X CEO David Walsh stated that the proposal requires guidance from the government on certain concerns.
The Indonesian government instructed Barrick and Bre-X to form a joint venture, with Barrick holding 75 percent and Bre-X holding 25 percent.
The joint venture agreement includes a 10 percent cut for the Indonesian government.
Barrick spokesman Vince Borg confirmed that the joint submission aligns with government parameters.
The Indonesian government has extended the deadline for the companies twice, with the latest extension until the end of December.
Bre-X shareholders have expressed anger over the government's statements, which have negatively impacted the company's stock.
A group of Bre-X shareholders has hired Texas lawyers to ensure a fair deal for shareholders.

Falconbridge Ltd is a Canadian nickel company focused on expansion through acquisition and exploration.
Oyvind Hushovd is the new chief executive officer of Falconbridge, having replaced Frank Pickard.
Frank Pickard died at the age of 63 during a business trip in Chile in September.
Oyvind Hushovd has worked for Falconbridge for over 22 years.
Hushovd previously held the position of executive vice-president and was involved in creating a strategic plan for Falconbridge.
Falconbridge aims to double its annual nickel production to 200,000 tonnes and triple its copper production to about 500,000 tonnes within 15 years.
Falconbridge lost a bid to take over the Voisey's Bay nickel, copper, and cobalt deposit in Labrador.
Falconbridge is involved in ongoing projects in New Caledonia, Ivory Coast, and Zambia.
Falconbridge plans to start producing nickel at the Raglan project in Quebec by the end of next year.
Falconbridge is part of a consortium developing the Konkola Deep copper mine in Zambia.

The world's gold producers are likely to suffer due to a decline in bullion prices and uncertainty in the gold market.
If the weakness in bullion prices continues, gold miners may experience lower profits, money-losing operations, closed mines, reduced exploration budgets, and falling share prices.
Analysts predict that smaller gold companies will be more vulnerable to takeovers as industry conditions worsen.
Gold analyst Michael Fowler from Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion in Toronto stated that earnings for gold producers are expected to be poor.
Gold was fixed at $358.55 an ounce in London on a recent Friday and has lost over $13 since the beginning of the year.
The decline in gold prices has negatively impacted Canadian gold stocks, causing the Toronto Stock Exchange's gold index to drop more than nine percent since December 30.
At least two gold companies have recently announced the shutdown of marginal mines.
TVX Gold Inc. announced it would close its Casa Berardi gold mine in Quebec.
Placer Dome Inc. stated it would sell two small mines in Quebec and cease operations at its high-cost Paymaster mine in Northern Ontario.
Analysts expect the effects of low bullion prices to be reflected in fourth-quarter earnings and in the first quarter of 1997.

Oskar Lafontaine is the chairman of Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD).
Lafontaine communicated with Czech President Vaclav Havel about a post-war reconciliation pact.
Havel's spokesman, Ladislav Spacek, reported that Havel thanked the SPD for their interest in improving relations between Germany and the Czech Republic.
Lafontaine expressed the SPD's desire for an early debate on the reconciliation declaration.
Lafontaine stated that the SPD aims for the declaration to be approved within the year.
The declaration addresses historical issues related to the Nazi occupation and the expulsion of Sudetens.
The Czech Republic has not yet reconciled with Germany regarding these historical issues.
Negotiations on the declaration have been ongoing for over a year and have faced political challenges.
The Czech government claims the text of the declaration is complete, but approval is delayed by demands from the Sudeten German community.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl expressed hope that the declaration could be signed by the end of the year.

The Czech cabinet is expected to decide soon on the further privatisation of Ceska Sporitelna a.s.
Jaroslav Svoboda, deputy general director of Sporitelna, stated that there is no need to rush the privatisation.
Svoboda believes the state should retain a 10 to 15 percent stake in the bank after the sale.
Svoboda mentioned that deciding on the privatisation is important to calm the situation for foreign investors.
The central bank recently suggested merging Sporitelna with Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka (CSOB).
The state currently holds a 45 percent stake in Sporitelna through the National Property Fund (NPF).
Svoboda indicated that 30 to 35 percent of Sporitelna should be sold to one or two long-term investors.
Svoboda expressed concerns about domestic investors' ability to finance the purchase compared to foreign investors.
The Czech National Bank's proposal includes merging Sporitelna with CSOB to create the largest banking institution in Eastern Europe.
The CNB proposed delaying the privatisation of the new combined entity for three to five years to analyze the merger's effects.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated that the large Czech foreign trade deficit is due to a temporary investment wave.
Klaus forecasted a perpetual, but smaller trade gap for the Czech Republic.
Klaus described the record 110.7 billion crown trade deficit in the first nine months of the year as 'not tragic'.
Klaus emphasized the importance of discussing the current account and the whole payment balance, not just the trade balance.
Klaus predicted that the Czech Republic would likely never have a positive trade balance in the long term.
Klaus attributed the current trade deficit to a temporary above-average rate of investment.
Klaus noted that the investment boom would ease, leading to a narrowing in the differential with savings.
Klaus mentioned that a lack of natural resources, the structure of the Czech economy, and its geographical position would perpetuate a trade deficit.
In the first nine months of the year, imports rose by 15.2 percent to 551.2 billion crowns, while exports increased by 5.9 percent to 440.5 billion crowns.
The Czech Statistical Bureau forecasted that the foreign trade deficit would reach 163.3 billion crowns for the whole of 1996.

Czech National Bank (CNB) Governor Josef Tosovsky stated that there is no need to hurry the sale of the state's stake in Komercni Banka a.s.
Tosovsky indicated that when the time comes to sell the stake of approximately 49 percent, it could be offered to several investors.
He mentioned that a strategic partner is not necessary for the privatisation of Komercni Banka.
The CNB does not currently have a strong consensus on what to do with the stake in Komercni Banka.
Tosovsky noted that it is possible to sell the stake to both domestic and foreign investors.
The CNB has submitted a plan to privatise shares in the 'Big Four' banks, which includes a merger of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. with Ceska Sporitelna a.s.
Tosovsky stated that the CNB prefers to wait several years before privatising state shares after the merger is established to analyze its effects.
He mentioned that CSOB is ready for a fast privatisation, but the CNB believes that a merger with Ceska Sporitelna would be more suitable.
The Czech cabinet must approve any privatisation of shares in the Big Four banks.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus requested details from the CNB regarding a quick sale of the state's 31.5 percent stake in Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus accused opposition Social Democrat leader Milos Zeman of lying and losing his nerve.
The accusations occurred during campaigning for weekend Senate elections.
Zeman alleged that the BIS intelligence agency tried to extract compromising material from his elderly mother.
The conflict between Klaus and Zeman intensified after BIS director Stanislav Devaty resigned over allegations of spying.
Klaus stated that Zeman's comments indicated a loss of nerve before the elections.
Zeman accused Klaus of playing dirty in the Senate elections.
Zeman claimed that an operational group within the BIS had been responsible for shadowing several Social Democrat politicians.
Devaty resigned after Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux accused the BIS of spying on him.
Klaus clarified that the BIS agent was spying on a former adviser, not on Lux.
Allegations of politically-inspired spying have been common in the Czech Republic since the fall of communism in 1989.

Czech power producer CEZ a.s. reported a nine-month net profit of 8.4 billion crowns ($312.6 million), an increase from 7.4 billion crowns for the same period last year.
The increase in profit was attributed to a surge in household electricity demand.
CEZ's gross profit for the period remained flat at 13.1 billion crowns.
Under Czech accounting standards, CEZ's profit for the first nine months was 7.04 billion crowns, up from 6.7 billion crowns last year.
CEZ maintained its profit forecast under Czech standards for the whole year at 8.1 billion crowns, the same as last year.
CEZ wrote off 4.1 billion crowns in the first nine months, compared to 3.4 billion crowns in the same period of 1995.
CEZ paid 4.7 billion crowns in income tax, down from 5.7 billion crowns last year.
Overall electricity demand rose by 5.5 percent during the period and is expected to reach a record high of 55.3 terawatt-hours for the whole of 1996.
Household electricity consumption increased by 10.5 percent, while demand from large clients rose by almost two percent.
CEZ's short-term indebtedness increased due to unpaid debts from regional distributors, totaling 3.2 billion crowns as of September 30.

Czech opposition Social Democrats blame party chairman Milos Zeman for their poor performance in recent Senate elections.
Zeman's pre-election claims about harassment by intelligence agents are suggested to have negatively impacted the party's support.
The Social Democrats received 20.3 percent of the vote in the first round of voting.
The ruling Civic Democratic Party (ODS) received 36.5 percent of the vote in the same election.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus leads the ODS.
Social Democrats experienced internal conflict after the election results.
Vasil Biben, a Social Democrat candidate, criticized Zeman for harming the party's appeal to centre-left voters.
Zeman alleged that secret agents attempted to extract compromising information from his mother before the elections.
Zeman accused the state intelligence agency BIS of spying on him but did not provide evidence to a parliamentary watchdog.
Low voter turnout of 34 percent affected the Social Democrats' performance in the Senate elections.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) announced a change in its methodology for calculating industrial production.
The new methodology aims to align with western standards.
CSU Chairman Edvard Outrata stated that the change will take effect in January 1997.
The new methodology excludes multiple calculations of semi-finished products, resources, and other materials.
The new index will measure output changes by units, weight, or other measurements of 1,304 products from 879 product groups.
Output indices will be categorized into sectors using weighting based on their significance in the respective industrial sector.
The overall index will be calculated from weighted changes in the sectoral indices.
Outrata mentioned that the old system was suitable for a planned economy and allowed for total production measurement against state plans.
Construction output data will be adjusted to the new methodology at the beginning of 1998.
Preliminary monthly data will be released on the 40th day after the end of the month being examined.

Czech surgeons began exploratory surgery on President Vaclav Havel on Monday to remove a spot from his lung.
Vaclav Havel stated that his health was not in serious danger.
Havel's office announced a news briefing would be held on Monday afternoon after the operation.
An official stated it was impossible to determine how long the surgery would last.
Havel has been ill for several weeks and is a heavy smoker.
In a weekly radio address, Havel expressed optimism about the operation.
Havel described the spot on his lungs as small and in a favorable location.
Havel was admitted to the hospital last Monday after suffering from pneumonia.
Surgeons described the planned surgery as medium serious.
A sample of the spot will be sent for immediate analysis during the operation.

The Czech government approved a declaration on post-World War Two reconciliation with Germany.
The declaration includes mutual expressions of regret for the Nazi occupation from 1938 to 1945 and for the brutality during the post-war expulsion of ethnic Germans from Sudetenland.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated he was authorized to sign the text, which took two years to negotiate, without changes.
Klaus indicated that the government sees no reason to make changes to the text and considers the negotiation closed.
The foreign ministers of the Czech Republic and Germany are scheduled to initial the text in Prague on Friday.
Signature by the two presidents and confirmation by the parliaments are expected early next year.
The declaration aims to close negative chapters of history and improve future relations between the two countries.
The declaration has faced criticism from groups representing Sudeten Germans for not addressing property compensation.
Germany's Christian Social Union (CSU) has not guaranteed support for the text without assurances for Sudeten involvement in dialogue.
The Czech parliament's mainstream parties support the declaration, while the extreme-right Republican Party and far-left Communists oppose it.

Volkswagen AG Czech unit Skoda Auto a.s. announced that its new mid-sized 'Octavia' sedan will have a base price of 335,700 crowns in its home market.
Skoda plans to produce 64,000 Octavias next year and increase production to 90,000 in 1998.
The Octavia is built on a common VW platform designed for the 1998 Audi A3 and upgraded Golf.
The Octavia will be available with three petrol and two diesel engines in three lines, with the top model priced at 497,900 crowns.
The Octavia will be showcased at the Paris International Auto Show in October and is expected to be delivered to Czech dealers in November.
Skoda was taken over by Volkswagen in 1992 as part of a government privatization plan.
Skoda built a new factory specifically for Octavia production.
The Octavia features modern but conservative design elements, positioned between a Ford Mondeo and Audi's A-line.
The cheapest Octavia model includes a 1.6 litre, 55 Kw engine, ignition immobiliser, driver-side airbag, adjustable driver's seat, and steering wheel.
Skoda Chairman Ludvik Kalma expressed expectations for increased production, aiming for 350,000 units next year and 400,000 at the turn of the century.

Ceska Rafinerska a.s. plans to reopen the hydrocracking unit at its Litvinov refinery by the end of January.
The hydrocracking unit was damaged by a fire on December 2.
Ales Soukup is the company spokesman for Ceska Rafinerska.
The fire on December 2 and another fire on November 23 will affect the company's 1996 earnings, but the extent is unclear.
The Litvinov refinery is currently processing crude at normal levels, but the quality of processing is lower due to the absence of the hydrocracking unit.
Ceska Rafinerska is insured, which will cover some of the damages from the fires.
Final results for Ceska Rafinerska's earnings for the previous year are expected by the end of the first quarter.
The fire affecting the hydrocracking unit occurred just as crude flow resumed after an eight-day stoppage.
The IOC consortium, which includes DuPont Co unit Conoco, Royal Dutch/Shell, and Agip SpA, owns a 49 percent stake in Ceska Rafinerska.
The state holds a 51 percent stake in Ceska Rafinerska through Unipetrol a.s.

Chinese police detained Liu Xiaobo on Tuesday after searching his home.
Police confiscated documents, books, and photographs during the search.
The search occurred at Liu's home in Beijing at about 8:00 a.m.
Police did not provide a reason for Liu's detention.
Liu Xiaobo is a renowned literary critic and dissident.
He gained fame during the 1989 student-led pro-democracy movement.
Liu has recently sent open letters to the government demanding press freedom.
On September 30, Liu and Wang Xizhe urged the Chinese authorities to honor a 1945 promise for religious freedom and political rights.
Wang Xizhe was still at liberty in Guangzhou on the day of Liu's detention.
Liu was previously detained in 1995 for more than seven months without formal charges.

Liu Xiaobo has been ordered to serve three years in a labour camp after being detained by police in a raid on his Beijing home.
Liu Xiaobo's wife, Liu Xia, reported that police notified her of the administrative sentence without providing a reason.
Liu Xia expressed anger over the punishment and stated that her husband has not done anything illegal.
Liu Xia mentioned that citizens have freedom of speech to write articles and express opinions.
The administrative punishment against Liu Xiaobo was issued after he was taken from his home by police who confiscated books, papers, and photographs.
Liu Xia stated that re-education through labour is a power of the public security bureau and does not require judicial oversight.
Liu Xiaobo may be sent to a labour camp near his hometown of Dalian.
The administrative punishment of re-education through labour has been increasingly used against dissidents in recent months.
Liu Xiaobo is a renowned literary critic who gained fame as a dissident during the 1989 pro-democracy movement.
Liu Xiaobo has recently sent open letters to the government urging for freedom of the press and political rights.

Time in Tibet is two hours behind Beijing.
The economy in Tibet is largely based on yaks, goats, and Buddhism.
Beijing has invested more than 35 billion yuan (US$4.2 billion) in Tibet.
Economic growth in Tibet reached 10.6 percent in 1995.
Rural per capita incomes in Tibet were about 600 yuan ($72) a year in 1995.
Urban incomes in Tibet neared 2,000 yuan ($240) a year in 1995.
The Tibet Investment and Trust Corporation set up a stocks trading center in Lhasa in 1994.
Beijing offers preferential policies such as income tax holidays and easy loans to businesses in Tibet.
Numerous entrepreneurs from elsewhere in China are attracted to Tibet due to favorable policies.
Lhasa has streets that specialize in selling Tibetan furniture and other goods.

Wang Dan is a detained Chinese dissident and former student leader.
Wang Dan's family stated that he could stand trial this week for plotting to overthrow the government.
The family claims the charge against Wang Dan is unfounded.
Wang Lingyun, Wang Dan's mother, stated that the indictment does not break the law.
Wang Dan has been charged with plotting to subvert the government based on critical writings and accepting foreign funds.
Wang Lingyun claims her son is unjustly accused and has always advocated for peace and non-violence.
The family has not been notified of the trial date but believes it could occur this week.
A lawyer has been found to defend Wang Dan, and legal formalities have begun.
The Beijing People's Intermediate Court informed Wang Lingyun that she had one day to find a lawyer for her son.
Wang Dan was detained in May 1995 but was not formally arrested or charged until last week.

China is exploring the freedoms of Hong Kong.
Analysts believe that Beijing's recent statements on freedom of expression may be causing hesitation.
China's communist rulers are used to exercising unchecked power.
China attempted to clarify a warning made by Foreign Minister Qian Qichen regarding freedom of expression in Hong Kong.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang stated that Hong Kong people will have full freedom of expression within legal limits.
Qian's interview suggested that Hong Kong may not be able to commemorate the anniversary of the June 4, 1989, crackdown.
Qian's comments led to public outcry in Hong Kong.
China has promised a high degree of political freedoms in Hong Kong for 50 years after the handover on July 1, 1997.
Western diplomats expressed concern over Qian's remarks and their potential impact on Hong Kong.
Chinese officials noted that Qian was interested in the reaction to his comments from Hong Kong.

Wang Dan's name cards describe him as 'Free Man' and 'World Citizen'.
Wang Dan was imprisoned for 11 years after being sentenced for plotting to subvert the government.
The Beijing Number One Intermediate People's Court convicted Wang Dan in less than four hours.
The sentencing of Wang Dan left only a few dissidents free in China.
A prominent dissident commented that the government does not believe a young person like Wang Dan poses a threat.
The dissident suggested that Wang Dan's imprisonment serves as a hostage for potential human rights gestures to the West.
Most dissidents in China are either imprisoned, in labor camps, in exile, or living under the threat of arrest.
The dissident stated that Wang Dan's imprisonment is a warning to the United States.
A U.S. State Department official described China's current leadership as the most difficult for Washington to deal with in 25 years.
Historian Bao Zunxin lives quietly in Beijing after participating in the 1989 pro-democracy demonstrations.

China is unlikely to concede on its demand to enter the World Trade Organisation as a developing country.
Pei Changhong is the head of the department of Foreign Economy and Trade under the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Pei Changhong stated that China will only enter the WTO as a developing country.
The United States insists that the size of China's economy ranks it as a developed country.
China was disappointed when its application to join the WTO as a founding member failed two years ago.
Talks in Geneva regarding China's WTO membership have proceeded slowly.
Pei Changhong expects little progress during the upcoming WTO ministerial meeting in Singapore.
China will attend the WTO meeting in Singapore under observer status.
Pei Changhong mentioned that China would explain its stance in meetings on the sidelines of the WTO meeting.
Pei Changhong noted that China's economy is already remarkably open compared to Japan and South Korea.

Ministers engaged in intense talks on global trade liberalization.
The issue of labor rights complicated the final agreement.
World Trade Organisation (WTO) Director-General Renato Ruggiero expressed optimism about the negotiations.
Ruggiero stated that there was a clear sense of achievement at the Ministerial Conference.
Negotiations focused on the Information Technology Agreement (ITA) and contentious clauses in a final declaration.
The final document aims to consolidate agreements from the 1986-93 Uruguay Round of trade talks.
The document will guide future discussions on topics not fully covered by the WTO.
There is a significant debate over including core labor standards in the document.
Some Asian countries oppose the inclusion of labor rights in the WTO agenda.
International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz stated that Malaysia would not allow a WTO study on labor rights.

China will accelerate listings of new firms on its two stock markets next year.
A senior securities official made this statement to meet demand and curb speculation.
An official statement warned investors against excessive speculation, leading to a sell-off on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission official stated that tighter regulation is needed due to insider trading and excessive speculation.
The Shanghai domestic A share index fell 20.07 percent to 922.34 points last Friday.
The foreign currency B index decreased 3.84 percent to 63.743 points after a week of trading.
Zhang Dongsheng, a deputy director of the Finance and Banking Department, indicated that China would list additional firms to balance supply and demand.
China announced a share quota of 10 billion yuan for 1996, nearly double the previous year's quota.
Analysts believe the decision to increase new issues aims to absorb excess funds fueling speculation.
The number of trading accounts opened by Chinese investors rose to 21 million, up from 12 million at the start of the year.

Draft amendments to China's criminal law are currently under debate by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.
The Workers Daily reported that the debate among lawmakers has been fierce regarding specific clauses of the draft amendments.
One major topic of controversy is the scope of the death penalty and whether corrupt state managers should face execution.
The criminal law amendments and a new anti-corruption law are key items on the agenda of a week-long meeting of the standing committee.
The Workers Daily noted that there is a debate about whether there are too many death penalties in China.
Some opinions suggest that the number of capital crimes in the current criminal law, which exceeds 30, should be reduced.
Amnesty International recorded 3,612 death sentences and 2,535 executions in China in 1995.
China will introduce lethal injection as a method of capital punishment starting January 1, when a new criminal procedures law takes effect.
Another perspective argues that the death penalty should remain as it serves as a deterrent and meets public demand for harsher punishments.
The amendments to combat corruption include over 60 clauses defining graft and increasing the types of officials subject to the law from seven to 32.

China has launched a manhunt in Tibet following a bomb explosion in Lhasa.
The government has tightened airport security in Tibet.
A reward of one million yuan ($120,000) has been offered for information leading to the arrest of those responsible for the bomb blast.
The bomb exploded outside city government offices in Lhasa on Christmas Day.
No arrests have been made in connection with the bomb blast.
The reward notice was published in the Lhasa Evening News on December 27.
The bomb blast caused widespread damage but resulted in no casualties.
Officials believe the blast was politically motivated and linked to followers of the Dalai Lama.
The bomb was identified as a home-made device made mainly from ammonium nitrate.
Police are focusing their search on Tibetan exiles returning from abroad with political connections.

Deng Xiaoping is currently living as a recluse.
Analysts believe that power-hungry individuals are using Deng's name to strengthen their positions.
A 12-hour documentary on Deng's life was launched on New Year's Day.
The documentary portrays Deng in a positive light.
A Western diplomat stated that those around Deng are benefiting from enhancing his image.
The pro-Deng camp appears to have the upper hand according to the diplomat.
Jiang Zemin is identified as Deng's anointed heir-apparent.
Jiang Zemin would benefit if Deng remains alive for another year and a half.
Deng Xiaoping has not been seen in public for nearly three years due to his health and desire for privacy.
There are rumors regarding Deng's health, including recent hospital admission and fading lucidity.

Officials in Chongren county, Jiangxi province, China issued an action plan to eliminate worship by the underground Catholic church loyal to Rome.
The Cardinal Kung Foundation, a U.S.-based church group, reported on the Communist Party document detailing the action plan.
The document warns against infiltration by overseas religious forces and threats to political stability.
The action plan is titled 'Procedures to Legally Implement the Eradication of Illegal Activities of the Underground Catholic Church' and outlines measures from November 25, 1996, to March 31, 1997.
Measures in the plan include public relations efforts, registration of religious believers, and forcing underground Catholics to deny their faith and join the official church.
The document attributes the increase in illegal religious believers to overseas religious infiltration and the influence of underground religious activities.
It claims that underground believers use religion to commit criminal activities, disturbing social order and affecting political stability.
Local authorities are urged to use resolute and organized measures to eliminate the underground church.
China permits Catholics to worship under the state-sponsored Patriotic Association but prohibits allegiance to Rome or the Pope.
The document aims to destroy the organization of underground Catholic forces and their illegal assembly places.

Virgin Atlantic Cargo will begin a new, shorter route on its Hong Kong to London service later this month.
The new route will cut an hour off the journey time.
The new route will enable an extra six tonnes of freight to be carried westbound and two tonnes eastbound.
China granted permission for the shortcut after negotiations with the British government.
The new northerly route will be via Beijing and then over Russia and Germany, starting on October 27.
The current southerly track used is over Thailand, Bangladesh, Tashkent, and Turkey.
Brinkley Chan is the assistant manager for Virgin Atlantic Cargo in Hong Kong.
Virgin's Airbus A340 aircraft will require 50,000 pounds less fuel on the new route.
The new routing will allow eight tonnes of cargo to be carried with a full passenger load from Hong Kong.
Virgin has been able to carry only two tonnes of belly cargo during winter months and four tonnes during summer months from Hong Kong.

U-Freight Holdings Limited is a freight forwarding company based in Hong Kong.
U-Freight is considering opening an office in Guangzhou.
Anthony Fong is the managing director of U-Freight.
U-Freight's operations in China have been concentrated in Beijing, Dalian, and Shanghai.
