U-Freight has a new warehouse near Shanghai airport that is scheduled for completion in December.
U-Freight was established in Hong Kong 28 years ago.
China Southern Airlines has invested in a new fleet of Boeing 777 aircraft.
China Southern Airlines is starting a Guangzhou-Beijing-Amsterdam service next month.
U-Freight is among many freight forwarders interested in the new market in Guangzhou.
The licensing procedure for freight forwarders in China can take a significant amount of time.

Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd has retired its last Lockheed TriStar airliner.
Cathay Pacific operated 19 TriStar airliners since 1975.
The TriStar airliners logged over 487,000 flight hours.
At its peak, the TriStar fleet logged 609,000 kilometres weekly.
Captain John Bent described the TriStar as having character and being a thoroughbred.
The TriStar airliners were phased out over the past two years.
The replacement fleet includes Airbus A330-300 and Boeing 777-200 airliners.
The fleet replacement program cost US$9 billion.
The Airbus A330 can carry up to 32 LD-2 cargo containers weighing up to 22 tons.
The TriStar could carry around eight tons of cargo.

This is Reuters' 2nd ex-Hong Kong air cargo market report.
The report will be published regularly until a new version is released.
Current average ex-Hong Kong air cargo market rates are provided in Hong Kong dollars per kg for a 100kg shipment with a volume-to-weight ratio of six to one.
As of October 17, the average rates for various routes are: EUROPE HK-LHR 22.25, HK-FRA 22.40; USA HK-JFK 20.70, HK-LAX 21.05; MIDDLE EAST HK-DXB 15.80; ASIA PACIFIC HK-SIN 9.10, HK-TAIPEI 4.10, HK-TOKYO 30.70.
The rates were obtained by Reuters journalists from airlines, large forwarders, and smaller cargo agents on a confidential basis.
All prices are quoted in Hong Kong dollars.
The tariffs represent averages calculated from a range of prices and indicate current market activity.
Demand for cargo space has eased slightly as a backlog is cleared, but key ex-Hong Kong rates have continued to rise.
Airlines and freight forwarders report brisk business as the peak season approaches, allowing airlines on European routes to raise rates for the second time within three weeks.
Sam Chung, chairman of the Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents, stated that the market is strong, especially for shipments to the United States.

Chris Humphrey is the head of British Airways World Cargo (BAWC) in Hong Kong.
Chris Humphrey expressed confidence in a dramatic improvement in freight handling service standards at London's Gatwick and Heathrow airports.
A leading Hong Kong air freight forwarder expressed being appalled at BAWC's handling of ex-Hong Kong cargo in London.
One consignment took three and a half days to clear Gatwick according to the forwarder.
The forwarder stated he tries to avoid Heathrow due to its indefensible service standards.
British Airways recently had its ISO service standard award revoked at its main Heathrow cargo hub.
Chris Humphrey acknowledged the problems and assured customers that improvements are underway.
Major changes to working practices at Gatwick have caused a short-term downturn in service standards.
BAWC's newly opened dedicated centre for freight from the Pacific region began handling Hong Kong cargo earlier this month.
Chris Humphrey stated that improvements in service standards are expected despite challenges with an old building.

DHL Worldwide Express is investigating the establishment of a new operations centre in Hong Kong near the new airport.
Andy Tseng is the Hong Kong and China area manager for DHL.
The proposed operations centre would complement the express freight centre currently under construction at Chek Lap Kok, where DHL has an equity stake.
DHL has an existing town centre base near Tai Tak airport and several satellite depots across Hong Kong.
DHL recently invested HK$15 million in an automatic handling system at its existing airport base, which can process 4,000 items per hour.
Andy Tseng stated that the decision regarding the new operations centre is vital for DHL's future and involves significant consideration of customer needs.
DHL has been approached by four real estate developers offering sites for the new operations centre in west Kowloon.
West Kowloon is primarily an industrial area near the new bridge and motorway link to the new airport on Lantau island.
Other air cargo companies are also considering off-airport sites due to concerns about high building rents and staff relocation issues at the new airport.
A viability study conducted by a task force for DHL is expected to be completed by the end of the year.

Japan Airlines (JAL) is expanding its express cargo service called 'J Speed' to meet rising demand for rapid deliveries throughout Asia.
The J Speed system guarantees delivery for shippers facing urgent deadlines on high volume cargo routes.
J Speed offers late acceptance at the departure airport and early delivery.
A proposed service from Bangkok to Tokyo is next on the J Speed network, with plans for gradual expansion over JAL's entire international network.
Kazuto Yamamoto, JAL's assistant vice president for freight and mail, expressed high hopes for the new service to boost high-yield cargo sales on key Asian routes.
The Tokyo Narita - Manila sector was chosen for the J Speed launch due to a 50 percent average annual growth in the Japan-Philippines market over the past three years.
JAL stated there is usually a two-hour deadline before departure from Japan for regular cargo, while J Speed cargo is accepted up to an hour before takeoff.
J Speed cargo is cleared through customs before the flight arrives in Manila because the air waybill is faxed.
Customers are willing to pay a premium price for the J Speed service on busy routes.
JAL plans to extend the service from Japan to Jakarta, Kuala Lumpur, and Bangkok, and is studying a service to Singapore.

Anthony Lau is the chairman of Hong Kong freight forwarding company Baltrans Ltd.
Baltrans Ltd acquired a majority stake in Fond Group, a Los Angeles competitor, this summer.
The acquisition was for a 67.4 percent stake and cost HK$32.2 million.
Baltrans expects to achieve synergy and economies of scale from the acquisition.
Currently, Baltrans and Fond Group are operating independently.
Baltrans is positioned in Asia, while Fond Group is positioned on the US west coast.
The acquisition aims to increase the overall profitability of Baltrans in trans-Pacific segments.
Fond Group specializes in shipping cargo from Hong Kong to the west coast of America.
The Fond Group includes Fondair Express (HK), Fondocean Express (HK), and Fondexpress (USA).
The combined turnover of the Fond Group is around HK$300 million.

Air China is planning to restart flights to Los Angeles next year.
Zhang Jinming is the general director of Air China's advertising division.
The Beijing and Shanghai service to Los Angeles will operate at least twice weekly.
Air China will use a Boeing 747-400 or Boeing 747 Combi aircraft for the Los Angeles service.
Los Angeles was previously part of Air China's network but was discontinued.
Air China's service to Los Angeles will be its third service to the USA, following San Francisco and New York.
Zhang made these statements at China's first official air show in Zhuhai.
China Southern Airlines confirmed plans to start a Los Angeles service in March of next year.
Air China is expected to announce a new service from Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou to Sydney and Melbourne.
A report from the New China News Agency indicated that Air China planned to open US west coast and Australian routes last month.

Asiana Airlines will take delivery of a third Boeing 747-400 freighter next month.
The new freighter will replace a wet leased DC-10 cargo aircraft on the Seoul to New York route.
T.S. Kang is the cargo marketing and sales director for Asiana Airlines.
Asiana Airlines currently operates two DC-10 freighters wet leased from Gemini Air Cargo and World Airways for six flights per week to New York.
The World Airways freighter will be returned, while the Gemini freighter will be retained until the end of next year.
The Gemini freighter will continue to operate three times a week to New York.
The new Boeing 747-400 will operate the other three flights to New York.
The 747-400 has a cargo carrying capacity of over 100 tonnes, compared to around 65 tonnes for the DC-10.
Asiana Airlines currently has two 747-400 freighters and one 767 freighter.
Asiana Airlines plans to expand its cargo aircraft fleet to 10 by 2005.

The Hong Kong Shippers' Council is urging the government to inform airlines that a fuel surcharge on air cargo rates is illegal.
Clement Yeung is the executive director of the Hong Kong Shippers' Council.
Cargo managers from major airlines operating to Europe met in Hong Kong on October 31.
Some airlines agreed to raise ex-Hong Kong cargo rates by HK80 cents per kilo starting November 4.
The Hong Kong Shippers' Council has written to the Civil Aviation Department to outlaw the surcharge.
Clement Yeung stated that airlines should obtain approval for rate increases and support their cases with facts and figures.
Yeung noted that only a few airlines have decided to impose the surcharge, while others have not.
The Hong Kong Shippers' Council represents 15 leading trade associations, including the Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce and the Chinese Manufacturers' Association.
The Federation of Asia Pacific Air Cargo Agents (FAPAA) is opposing the fuel surcharge.
Bernard Angeles, chairman of FAPAA, stated that the airlines' surcharge bid might fail due to lack of approval from Hong Kong's Civil Aviation Department.

Engineers are investigating the cause of an engine failure aboard a Cathay Pacific Airways Limited airliner on November 11.
The airliner was forced to return to Ho Chi Minh City on one engine.
The Airbus A330-300 had 132 passengers and reached 37,000 feet after take-off when one of its two Rolls Royce 700 engines suffered a suspected gearbox failure.
The pilots could not restart the engine and decided to return to Ho Chi Minh City.
The engine was removed and flown back to Hong Kong for a detailed inspection.
The suspect gearbox part has been returned to the U.K. for detailed analysis.
Cathay Pacific has a fleet of nine Airbus A330s that seat around 320 passengers and carry up to 17 tonnes of belly cargo on inter-Asian routes.
Hong Kong Dragon Airlines, in which Cathay holds a minority stake, operates 4 Rolls Royce powered A330s.
Rolls Royce has been a long-term supplier to Cathay since the Trent 700 engine entered service in February 1995.
This incident marks the second recorded inflight shutdown of a Trent 700 engine with Cathay.

British Energy Plc announced job cuts and cost savings on October 9.
Opposition politicians criticized the job cuts announced by British Energy.
Labour's energy and industry spokesman John Battle stated that British Energy has not performed as promised.
A spokesman for British Energy confirmed the announcement would cover job cuts and cost savings but did not provide further details.
Analysts expect British Energy to cut about 20 percent of its workforce of over 6,500 by the year 2000.
Newspaper reports indicated that British Energy could cut between 1,300 and 1,500 posts to achieve cost savings of around 100 million pounds.
John Battle called for British Energy to confirm its dividend policy as outlined in the company's privatisation prospectus.
At privatisation, British Energy stated its initial interim dividend would be 4.6 pence per share and forecasted a final dividend of 9.1 pence for 1996/97.
Battle expressed concern that job cuts could damage British Energy's performance and hinder reaching targets.
British Energy operates eight nuclear power stations in England and Scotland and was unpopular among the ruling Conservative party's privatisations.

Britain is taking legal action to ban Resale Price Maintenance (RPM) on non-prescription medicines.
Analysts believe this decision is likely to boost competition and benefit some stores in terms of market share.
John Bridgeman, head of the Office of Fair Trading, stated that he would seek to remove RPM from over-the-counter (OTC) medicines.
RPM allows manufacturers to set minimum sale prices for certain over-the-counter medicines.
The Community Pharmacy Action Group stated that the removal of RPM could lead to the closure of one in four local pharmacies.
The Office of Fair Trading's request will go to the Restrictive Practices Court, which is unlikely to consider the issue before late 1997.
Retailers are not expected to start an immediate round of price cuts.
Boots expressed disappointment at the decision and believes RPM operates in the public interest.
UniChem stated that the removal of RPM would be immaterial to its profitability.
Superdrug welcomed the move to remove RPM but ruled out immediate price cuts.

Cable & Wireless Communications is a new British cable operator formed from a group led by Cable & Wireless Plc.
Analysts believe Cable & Wireless Communications has the potential to be competitive in the cable market.
John Tysoe, an analyst at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull, stated that the advantages of scope and size for the new company are clear.
Cable & Wireless, NYNEX Corp, and Bell Canada International announced a merger of their British subsidiaries.
The merger will culminate in a float of 15 percent of the new company.
Tysoe indicated that the merger creates an integrated competitor that will challenge British Telecommunications (BT).
Shares in Cable & Wireless closed at 466.5 pence, up 25.5 pence, after reaching a high of 476.5 pence.
NYNEX Cable Communications shares increased by 23.5 pence to 119.5 pence.
Chris McFadden of Merrill Lynch stated that the merger should result in significant cost savings.
The new company will compete with BT in the franchises it operates.

Britain's J. Sainsbury Plc announced plans to launch banking services in partnership with Bank of Scotland.
Analysts believe the banking venture may be profitable if executed correctly.
Marketing director Kevin McCarten stated that the banking services are expected to generate profits in a relatively short time.
Sainsbury applied to the Bank of England for authorization to establish a new bank owned 55 percent by Sainsbury and 45 percent by Bank of Scotland.
The new bank will be called Sainsbury's Bank and will offer telebanking services to 12 million customers.
Sainsbury's Bank will launch in 1997 with Classic and Gold Visa cards and account-based services.
Sainsbury's Bank aims to provide better value products than currently available options.
Sainsbury's shares increased by 10.5 pence to close at 360.5 pence following the announcement.
Tesco's shares rose by 2.5 pence to close at 324 pence after the announcement.
Sainsbury chairman David Sainsbury indicated that Sainsbury's Bank would enhance the company's market position.

Britain's J. Sainsbury Plc launched banking services in partnership with Bank of Scotland.
Sainsbury is the first supermarket to offer banking services.
Sainsbury applied to the Bank of England for authorization to establish a new bank.
The new bank will be owned 55 percent by Sainsbury and 45 percent by Bank of Scotland.
The venture will be called Sainsbury's Bank and will offer telebanking services.
Sainsbury's Bank will provide deposit, lending, and cash management services to 12 million customers.
The launch of Sainsbury's Bank is scheduled for 1997, along with Classic and Gold Visa cards.
Sainsbury's shares increased by 10.5 pence to close at 360.5 pence following the announcement.
Sainsbury chairman David Sainsbury stated that the bank would provide customers with a trusted name and banking expertise.
Analysts noted that Sainsbury's Bank must offer attractive deals to attract customers.

CalEnergy Co. launched a $1.2 billion takeover bid for Northern Electric Plc.
Northern Electric Plc rejected the unsolicited takeover offer from CalEnergy Co.
This was the second takeover bid for Northern Electric in just over a year.
CalEnergy's offer valued Northern Electric at about $1.23 billion.
CalEnergy's CE Electric unit, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy, made the offer.
CalEnergy proposed to pay 630 British pence for each common share and 103 pence for each preferred share of Northern Electric.
Peter Kiewit Sons owns the remaining 30 percent of CE Electric.
Northern Electric previously fended off a hostile bid from Trafalgar House last year.
CalEnergy Chairman David Sokol stated that the company's strategy is to become a leading global provider of energy services.
Sokol mentioned that Northern Electric's distribution and supply know-how would complement CalEnergy's production capacity.

Shares in J. Sainsbury Plc rose on Wednesday despite a fall in half year profits and sluggish sales.
Half year pre-tax profits for J. Sainsbury Plc fell to 393 million pounds from 456 million pounds in the same period last year.
J. Sainsbury Plc announced a dividend of 3.5 pence per share, up from 3.4 pence.
J. Sainsbury Plc reported its first fall in full year profits in 22 years in May.
Pre-tax earnings before exceptional items for the business year to March 9, 1996, fell 5.5 percent to 764 million pounds.
Several analysts cut forecasts for J. Sainsbury Plc's current full year profits to 710-725 million pounds.
Shares of J. Sainsbury Plc closed up 8.5 pence to 363.5 pence.
Current sales from comparable stores at J. Sainsbury Plc are rising in line with inflation of around three percent.
The Reward card is accounting for much of the increase in sales at J. Sainsbury Plc.
Dino Adriano will take over as chief executive of J. Sainsbury Plc's supermarket business on March 8.

Allied Domecq reported a fall in annual profits.
Allied Domecq ruled out a demerger as a solution to its problems.
Allied chairman Sir Christopher Hogg stated that improving operating performance is the company's overriding objective.
Full-year pretax profits to August were 575 million pounds, down from 645 million pounds.
Allied Domecq's exceptional losses for the year totaled 311 million pounds.
The largest part of the exceptional losses was from the sale of its 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley to Bass for 205 million pounds.
Allied paid out a total dividend of 23.59 pence a share, unchanged from the previous year.
Allied's shares eased 10 pence to 458 pence by 1040 GMT.
Allied's corporate restructuring was largely completed with the sale of its stake in Carlsberg-Tetley and smaller food companies.
The cost of tackling overstocking of U.S. spirits contributed to a 14 percent fall in year trading profits in the spirits and wines business.

Dominion Resources Inc. is based in Virginia.
Dominion Resources Inc. agreed to acquire East Midlands Electricity Plc for approximately 1.3 billion pounds ($2.15 billion).
Dominion offered 6.7 pounds ($11.07) per share for East Midlands Electricity Plc.
East Midlands Electricity Plc's shares were trading below the offer price due to concerns about potential obstacles from British competition authorities.
The Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) is expected to closely examine the deal.
East Midlands Electricity Plc rejected an earlier bid from Dominion, stating it undervalued the company.
East Midlands Chairman Sir Nigel Rudd recommended the latest offer as fair value for the business.
Seven of Britain's original 12 regional electricity companies have been acquired since March when the government's protective golden share expired.
Dominion's Chief Financial Officer Linwood Robertson stated the company intends to run East Midlands as a stand-alone business.
Dominion's stock increased by 37.5 cents to $40.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Shares in British utility Northern Electric rose on Friday after a report that U.S. group CalEnergy was set to raise its takeover offer.
CalEnergy's current offer is 630 pence per share.
The London Evening Standard reported that CalEnergy might increase its bid to 660 pence to gain a recommendation from Northern Electric.
CalEnergy has a 70 percent stake in CE Electric.
Northern Electric shares reached an intraday high of 618 pence before closing at 608 pence, up seven pence.
Other stocks in the utility sector also gained due to increased bid activity.
East Midlands accepted a bid of 1.3 billion pounds at 670 pence per share from Dominion Resources.
CalEnergy has acquired more than 29 percent of Northern Electric's shares.
Northern Electric claims that CalEnergy's offer undervalues the company and that a price of 700 pence was discussed prior to the bid.
Concerns exist that the bids may be referred to British competition authorities due to political pressure.

London Electricity is a British regional electricity company.
Entergy, a U.S. firm, is reportedly considering a bid of 1.2 billion pounds for London Electricity.
London Electricity declined to comment on a Wall Street Journal Europe report regarding Entergy's interest.
The Wall Street Journal Europe reported that Entergy was seeking 1.1 billion pounds to acquire a British electricity firm with a financial profile similar to London Electricity.
Entergy stated that discussions with another party were too early to be meaningful.
Entergy's spokesman, Patrick Sweeney, did not deny the Wall Street Journal Europe article.
Shares in London Electricity reached a high of 671 pence and closed at 667 pence, an increase of 30.5 pence.
The Wall Street Journal article mentioned that Entergy's confidential documents referred to the target company as 'Atlantic'.
The bid mentioned in the documents was assumed to be around 700 pence per share.
Entergy expressed interest in the British market and indicated that this could lead to an acquisition.

The British opposition Labour party plans to implement a one-off 'windfall' tax on utility companies.
Analysts believe that the uncertainty surrounding the Labour party's tax plans may cause more damage to the stock market than the tax itself.
Labour intends to use the tax revenue to fund welfare reform if it wins the next general election.
The next general election is expected to occur within six months.
Analysts suggest that the market dislikes uncertainty and may assume the worst-case scenario regarding the tax.
Philip Hollobone, an analyst at Williams de Broe, stated that Labour has not provided specific details about the tax, which is causing damage to utility shares.
Labour has not specified which companies will be targeted, the amounts to be taxed, or the timeline for implementation.
Reports indicate that the tax could raise between five billion pounds and ten billion pounds.
Speculation suggests that up to 30 companies, including British Telecom, British Gas, and BAA Plc, may be targeted by the tax.
The water and electricity sectors, which were privatised by the Conservatives, have faced criticism due to high executive pay, large dividends, and significant takeover deals.

Tax changes on long-term assets were made in the British budget.
Utility sector stocks fell on Wednesday following the tax changes.
Analysts believe the concerns about the tax changes may be overdone and expect the sector to recover.
Finance minister Kenneth Clarke proposed the changes in the budget on Tuesday.
The changes cut capital allowances on assets with a working life of over 25 years from 25 percent to six percent.
The Treasury aims to raise around 1 billion pounds from the tax changes over three years.
Shares in utilities fell, with Anglian Water down five pence, Yorkshire Water down seven pence, and Severn Trent down nine pence.
PowerGen and Yorkshire Electricity also saw declines in their share prices.
The tax changes will affect companies spending over 100,000 pounds a year on long-term fixed assets, with exceptions for shipping, rail businesses, and office buildings.
Analysts noted that utilities could be vulnerable due to their large infrastructure and future investment needs.

Barclays Plc is in talks with Morgan Stanley regarding its global custody business.
The global custody business unit of Barclays is confirmed to be up for sale.
Barclays and Morgan Stanley stated they are exploring potential future cooperation.
Barclays' custody business employs 350 to 400 staff worldwide.
Barclays' custody business has been considered not part of the bank's core operations.
The custody unit manages securities worth approximately 150 billion pounds.
In August, Barclays categorized custody under 'Businesses in Transition' in its interim results.
The 'Businesses in Transition' category reported a profit of 23 million pounds for the half-year ending June 30.
Analysts believe the sale will contribute to the consolidation of the global custody market.
Analysts expect Morgan Stanley to pay less than 100 million pounds for Barclays' custody business.

Mercury Asset Management reported a 29 percent increase in first half pretax profits to 81.8 million pounds.
The company's pretax profits were up from 63.6 million pounds in the first half of the previous year.
Mercury Asset Management's cash reserves rose to 261.6 million pounds from 189.9 million pounds at the end of March.
MAM chairman Hugh Stevenson stated that the company would consider acquisitions if they increased shareholder value.
Stevenson emphasized that the U.S. market is important but the main aim is to provide value for shareholders.
Stevenson mentioned that the company prefers a conservative balance sheet and has seen a significant increase in cash over the last six months.
Mercury Asset Management raised its interim dividend to 10 pence per share from six pence per share.
Funds under management increased to 85.9 billion pounds at the end of September from 70.9 billion pounds a year earlier.
The increase in funds under management included two billion pounds of net new business.
Mercury shares were reported at 11.19 pounds, down 23.5 pence, following profit-taking after reaching a year's high.

Sir Chippendale 'Chips' Keswick will take over the chair of Hambros in July next year.
Hambros is one of the few remaining British independent investment banks.
The firm has been dominated by the Hambro family.
Keswick has over 30 years of experience at Hambros Bank.
This will be the first time in the bank's history that a Hambro has not occupied the chair.
Hambros Bank has a history dating back to 1839 in London and has Danish origins.
Keswick is a member of the family that controls the Jardine group of companies in the Far East.
Keswick was born in Shanghai in 1940 and attended Eton College.
He joined Hambros Bank in 1965 and became chairman in 1986.
Keswick is a non-executive director of the Bank of England, De Beers Consolidated Mines, Anglo American, and Persimmon.

The world's major banks are competing to establish a dominant position in the private banking market.
Private banking focuses on high net-worth individuals with liquid assets of at least $500,000.
A survey by Price Waterhouse estimates the global market for high net-worth individuals at between $17 and $20 trillion.
It is estimated that between $4 and $6 trillion of this market is located in Europe.
Ian Woodhouse, head of Price Waterhouse's private banking practice, predicts the emergence of a private banking super-league of 25 to 30 banks.
These banks will manage at least $75 billion, with many exceeding $100 billion.
Notable banks in this super-league include Chase/Chemical, Citicorp, Swiss Bank Corp, Credit Suisse, Union Bank of Switzerland, ABN AMRO, Deutsche Bank, and HSBC.
Coutts Group, owned by National Westminster, manages around £20 billion ($33.6 billion), categorizing it as medium-sized.
The survey indicates that the private banking environment is becoming increasingly competitive.
Clients are becoming more demanding and less loyal, often using multiple banks before making a decision.

Three of Britain's largest building societies are Woolwich, Alliance & Leicester, and Northern Rock.
These societies plan stock market flotations in 1997.
The societies have combined assets of around 70 billion pounds ($117 billion).
The draft legislation related to protection from takeovers has caused the societies to reconsider their flotation plans.
The societies plan to convert to bank status next year.
A change in the draft of the new Building Societies Act has created confusion regarding their plans.
The draft proposes that societies lose their immunity from takeover if they merge with another financial institution after flotation.
Adam Applegarth, director of Northern Rock, expressed concerns about the loss of five-year protection from takeovers.
The Treasury is considering representations to retain immunity in the case of friendly mergers.
The societies are concerned about a proposed clause that would allow shareholders to waive the five-year protection.

Creditors of the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) will receive a payment of $2.65 billion, equal to 24.5 percent of their claims.
BCCI was founded in 1972 and was closed by central banks in 1991.
BCCI collapsed with debts of more than $12 billion due to evidence of massive fraud and money laundering.
At the time of its collapse, BCCI had assets of $24 billion and operations in 71 countries.
Liquidator Deloitte and Touche stated that a further payment of 10 percent of the admitted claims, totaling approximately $10.5 billion, should be made in the next 12 to 16 months.
The gross fund of amounts recovered by the liquidators is around $4.0 billion, which includes $1.5 billion paid by BCCI's majority shareholder, the government of Abu Dhabi.
The government of Abu Dhabi will pay an additional $250 million following a settlement reached earlier this year.
US authorities recovered more than $500 million from the United States, contributing to the first dividend payment.
Sheikh Khalid bin Mahfouz paid $245 million as part of a settlement related to the BCCI scandal.
The liquidators have outstanding claims against the Bank of England, the Institut Monetaire Luxembourgeois, and the auditors of the bank, Price Waterhouse and Ernst & Whinney.

The British government published new draft legislation on home lending institutions on Wednesday.
The Building Societies Bill would remove a society's five-year immunity from takeover once it converts to bank status if it takes over another financial institution.
The bill may not be enacted before a general election due to a lack of parliamentary time.
The draft received mixed reactions from four societies planning to convert to banks.
A Treasury spokeswoman stated there is currently no slot for the bill in the Parliamentary agenda.
Treasury Minister Angela Knight stated that societies converting to banks will proceed if their members want it.
The Woolwich expressed disappointment over the government's handling of the draft legislation.
The Woolwich board may revisit its conversion plans if the bill is enacted.
Northern Rock welcomed the changes in the draft legislation.
The Building Societies Association supported the revised Bill and encouraged its early introduction to Parliament.

Lloyds Bank was fined 325,000 pounds ($550,000) by the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO).
Lloyds Bank is expected to pay millions of pounds in compensation to disadvantaged customers.
IMRO fined Lloyds for breaches of rules related to its pensions transfer business between April 1988 and June 1993.
Lloyds Bank merged with TSB last year to form Lloyds TSB Group Plc.
Lloyds agreed to a settlement of disciplinary proceedings with IMRO, marking the fifth such settlement for mis-selling pensions products.
IMRO stated that Lloyds did not obtain all relevant facts about customers' personal and financial circumstances for proper pension transfer advice.
IMRO indicated that Lloyds failed to provide certain customers with necessary information for informed pension transfer decisions.
Lloyds must pay IMRO's investigation costs of 63,000 pounds and contribute to its disciplinary costs.
Lloyds has offered redress to some customers and is reviewing approximately 2,600 transfer cases, expected to be completed by December 31, 1997.
Lloyds TSB has made provisions totaling 165 million pounds for possible compensation related to the mis-selling of pension products.

The flotation price of the Halifax Building Society is expected to be at the high end of an estimate prepared by the Society's bankers.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell set a price range for the June float of the Halifax Building Society between 390 and 450 pence.
The expected market capitalisation of the Halifax Building Society is between 10.4 billion and 12 billion stg.
Peter Toeman, a banking analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, stated that a valuation of 12 billion stg aligns with expectations.
Some analysts expect the price on flotation day to be higher than the initial estimates.
John Leonard, a banking analyst at Salomon Brothers, suggested that a share price of around 475 pence or 490 pence would be reasonable based on earnings per share figures.
Analysts often compare the Halifax Building Society with Abbey National Plc for their calculations.
Abbey National Plc converted to a bank in 1989 and generates 65 percent of its income from core mortgage and deposit activities.
The Halifax Building Society generates about 80 percent of its income from core activities and plans to expand into life and general insurance, long-term savings, and funds management.
The Woolwich, Alliance & Leicester, and Northern Rock are also expected to float later this year.

Nicola Horlick is a former fund manager at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
Horlick stated that her chances of being reinstated at MGAM are slim.
Horlick is seeking reinstatement or compensation from MGAM after resigning.
MGAM and its parent company Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) have not responded to Horlick's requests.
Horlick met with her lawyer John Farr from Herbert Smith to discuss her situation.
Horlick's advisers indicated that legal action against DMG has not been ruled out.
An internal inquiry into the situation at MGAM is ongoing.
DMG suspended Horlick for soliciting staff to join a rival firm shortly after her promotion to managing director.
ABN AMRO has denied trying to poach Horlick and her team but expressed interest in acquiring a large British fund manager.
Deutsche Bank does not expect to go to court with Horlick.

Northern Rock Building Society will publish detailed proposals for its stock market flotation in the first week of March.
The proposals will include a preliminary valuation of the company.
A special meeting of members will be held in April to vote on the approval of the flotation.
Adam Applegarth declined to speculate on the value in shares each member would receive from the flotation.
The predicted value in shares is between 750 and 1,000 stg.
Northern Rock announced a pre-tax profit of 167.5 million stg in 1996, a 14 percent increase from 145 million stg in 1995.
The 1996 profit figure excludes 10.3 million stg of non-recurring costs related to the flotation.
The cost to income ratio for Northern Rock was 33.1 percent at the end of 1996, down from 33.5 percent at the end of 1995.
Net lending for Northern Rock increased by 44 percent to 1.9 billion stg, capturing around 10 percent of the UK net mortgage market.
Adam Applegarth stated that market conditions are improving and that any rise in British interest rates should happen gradually.

A British High Court judge rejected a $1.8 billion claim by the liquidators of Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) against Ernst & Whinney.
BCCI was closed by central banks in 1991 and collapsed with debts of more than $12 billion due to fraud and money laundering.
Judge Hugh Laddie stated that the claim by Deloitte & Touche, representing BCCI liquidators, was based on assertion and lacked relevant facts.
The original claim against Ernst & Whinney was for $10 billion but was reduced to $3.5 billion in June 1995.
The principal claim against Ernst & Whinney now stands at around $1.7 billion related to the firm's audits of BCCI Holdings SA and BCCI SA in 1985 and 1986.
A similar claim remains against Price Waterhouse, which became the auditor for BCCI in 1987 after Ernst & Whinney resigned.
Ernst & Young senior partner Nick Land stated that 85 percent of the claims against Ernst & Whinney have been struck out or withdrawn.
Land criticized the liquidators for pursuing speculative claims instead of providing funds to BCCI's creditors.
BCCI creditors began receiving payments last month after a five-year struggle.
Deloitte & Touche announced a payment of $2.65 billion to creditors, which is 24.5 percent of their claims.

CKD Holding a.s. won two contracts worth approximately $200 million to supply trams to Manila, Philippines.
The contracts were awarded by Manila's MRTC for a new mass transit project.
The trams will be produced at the CKD Tatra plant in Prague.
The contracts include the supply of more than 70 large-capacity tram units.
One contract is valued at $104 million, with assembly starting in the second half of 1997 and supply scheduled for 1998.
The second contract is a joint 10-year agreement for maintenance and technical assistance for the trams.
The maintenance contract is worth $95 million to CKD.
The contracts were signed with MRTC, the owner of the Manila project.
The Czech Foreign Ministry stated that the contracts could help Czech suppliers enter other Asian markets.
Indonesia and the People's Republic of China are identified as potential markets for CKD trams.

Czech President Vaclav Havel expressed deep disturbance over a Chinese court's 11-year prison sentence on dissident Wang Dan.
Wang Dan was accused of plotting to overthrow the government.
Havel described Wang's sentence as 'unacceptable' following a similar 14-year sentence given to Wei Jingsheng.
Wang was sentenced to 11 years in prison after a brief hearing.
Wei Jingsheng was sentenced to 14 years in jail last December on a similar charge.
Havel stated that Wang's sentence exemplified an unacceptable understanding of the citizen's position in society.
Havel expressed deep dissatisfaction over the decision regarding Wang's sentence.
Havel considers it his obligation to express solidarity with those advocating for justice and human rights non-violently.
The Czech foreign ministry protested the conduct of Wang's trial and judgment.
Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Shen Guofang stated that Wang's jailing was an ordinary legal matter, not a human rights issue.

Italy seeks a larger role in integrating former East Bloc countries into NATO.
A senior Italian diplomat stated that it is better to integrate fringe candidates like Slovakia and Romania.
Undersecretary for Foreign Affairs Piero Fassino made these statements during an official visit to Prague.
Fassino identified Hungary, the Czech Republic, Poland, and Slovenia as primary candidates for NATO's expansion.
Fassino mentioned that Slovakia and Romania could also potentially belong to NATO.
Fassino emphasized the importance of Slovakia and Romania implementing agreements with Hungary to protect the rights of ethnic Hungarians.
Fassino stated that it is necessary to determine if Slovakia and Romania meet NATO's standards of democracy before rejecting them.
Fassino argued that integrating countries allows for the enforcement of NATO standards, while isolation does not permit such demands.
Both the EU and the United States have criticized Slovakia's government for slow democratic reforms and laws threatening political opponents and ethnic minorities.
Fassino believes it is more useful to integrate countries like Slovakia to apply more pressure for democratic reforms.

Dr. Richard Salzmann is the president of Komercni Banka, the largest bank in the Czech Republic.
Salzmann believes the Czech banking system is fundamentally sound and improving despite some recent failures among smaller banks.
He advocates for increased fairness and transparency in the Czech economy to combat secrecy in banking.
Salzmann is running for a seat in the newly-established Czech Senate in the upcoming November elections.
He aims to restore good practices in the banking industry and improve the reputation of the Czech finance sector.
Salzmann states that better risk management is essential for the banking industry.
Komercni Banka and three other large banks account for about 80 percent of all Czech banking activity.
These banks have increased their reserves to meet Western banking standards and improved their risk management techniques.
Salzmann noted that there is a high proportion of risky loans in the portfolios of Czech banks, partly due to past practices.
He attributed the recent failure of Kreditni Banka a.s. to greed and naivete among the founders of the banks.

Czech National Bank (CNB) Governor Josef Tosovsky stated that it is too early to dismiss the central bank's plan to create the largest bank in post-Communist Europe.
Tosovsky expects the full cabinet to consider the CNB's plan in a few weeks.
The CNB's plan includes a proposed merger of Ceska Sporitelna a.s. with Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. (CSOB).
Tosovsky mentioned that only some preliminary opinions from a few officials have been expressed regarding the proposal.
Most members of the cabinet have not seen the CNB's proposal, according to Tosovsky.
The central bank has submitted a plan to fully privatise state holdings in the four largest banks.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus indicated that the cabinet requires more concrete details about the plan.
The merger of Sporitelna and CSOB is projected to create a bank with over $20 billion in assets.
Klaus compared the merger plan to merging Prague's top two soccer teams, which many Czechs find unthinkable.
The merger plan has faced criticism from Klaus's adviser Martin Kocourek and officials at both banks who wish to maintain their distinct identities.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party won 36 percent of the nationwide vote in the first round of Senate elections.
The centre-left opposition Social Democrats received 20 percent of the vote.
Only 35 percent of the electorate participated in the elections.
The Civic Democrats won three Senate seats outright and 73 candidates advanced to the runoff.
The Civic Democrats received less than 30 percent of the vote in June's general elections, resulting in a loss of majority in the lower house.
Analysts predict a mild positive impact on local financial markets due to the Civic Democrats' performance.
Radek Maly, an economist at Citibank Prague, stated that the low turnout makes it difficult to draw conclusions about voter sentiment.
The Czech crown has traded around 26.9 to the dollar and 17.8 to the mark.
Miroslav Nosal, an equities analyst at Patria Finance, indicated that a premature general election is unlikely.
Nosal noted that market concerns are more focused on macroeconomic fundamentals than on political influences.

The Czech crown firmed from the central bank fixing on Thursday.
The strengthening of the crown followed a strong showing by the senior coalition party in Senate elections last weekend.
Analysts expect Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) to take a majority of the 81 seats in the newly-created Senate after runoff elections this weekend.
The crown was trading at 26.661 to the dollar and 17.757 to the mark on Thursday.
The crown was 3.05 percent above the Czech National Bank's dollar/mark basket.
Citibank economist Radek Maly stated that the ODS winning a majority in the Senate is fairly likely.
The ODS won three seats outright in the first round of elections and has 76 candidates in the runoff.
The crown has remained well above parity with the basket despite a ballooning trade deficit.
Maly predicted the currency would stay close to Thursday's levels and might strengthen further on Monday.
Petr Korous, a dealer at Ceskovslovenska Obchodni Banka, noted that the market was firming due to the ODS showing despite low voter turnout.

Czech President Vaclav Havel will undergo exploratory surgery on his lungs next week.
Havel's spokesman, Ladislav Spacek, stated that the president would have a necessary operative procedure on his lungs.
A surgeon described the procedure as medium-serious.
Havel, aged 60, was admitted to the hospital after suffering from pneumonia.
Havel canceled his official commitments for the rest of November and early December due to his illness.
X-ray findings cannot be specified until a diagnostic operative measure is carried out, according to Spacek.
The symptoms or extent of Havel's illness have not been fully disclosed.
Havel is known to be a heavy smoker, but his illness has not been officially linked to smoking.
Havel canceled a planned two-day state visit to Ukraine and a summit of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.
Spacek stated that Havel was in good physical and psychological condition and was in constant contact with his office.

In May 1945, seven-year-old Madlenka Korbelova listened to the radio in London with her father, an exiled Czech diplomat.
Madlenka and her father cheered when General George Patton's army liberated Pilsen from Nazi soldiers.
They were upset when General Patton had to hold back his troops and allow the Red Army to take Prague.
Madlenka Albright recalled her childhood experiences during the Nazi occupation and the Cold War in a speech to American and Czech veterans in Pilsen.
Madeleine Albright was nominated by President Bill Clinton to be the first woman U.S. Secretary of State, pending Senate confirmation.
Czech ambassador to Washington, Michael Zantovsky, stated that Albright has a deep connection to her native country.
Josef Korbel, Madlenka's father, was a close aide to Czechoslovak Foreign Minister Jan Masaryk during World War Two.
After the communist takeover in Czechoslovakia in 1948, Korbel sent a cable indicating he was leaving with his family on vacation.
Josef Korbel and his family received asylum in America and settled in Colorado.
Josef Korbel became a professor of European history and politics and later a dean at the University of Denver.

Germany and the Czech Republic will initial a declaration on post-World War Two reconciliation on Friday in Prague.
The Czech foreign ministry announced the ceremony will conclude two years of negotiations.
Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec and Germany's Klaus Kinkel will participate in the ceremony.
The declaration includes mutual expressions of regret for the Nazi occupation from 1938 to 1945 and for the brutality during the post-war expulsion of ethnic Germans.
Groups representing expelled Germans, known as Sudeten Germans, expressed anger over the lack of compensation for lost property.
The Christian Social Union (CSU) indicated it would no longer oppose the agreed text of the declaration.
CSU chairman Theo Waigel described the progress made by Prague in apologizing for the expulsions as a 'great success.'
Mainstream parties in the Czech parliament support the declaration, while the extreme-right Republican Party and far-left Communists oppose it.
Members of the Social Democrats expressed concerns about compensation for victims of Nazi aggression.
The declaration establishes a Czech-German Future Fund with Germany contributing 140 million marks ($90 million).

The Czech coalition government is recovering from the resignation of Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda.
Jan Kalvoda admitted to using a phoney academic title.
Kalvoda resigned his cabinet and parliament seat on Tuesday.
Kalvoda is the leader of the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), a junior coalition partner.
Kalvoda's resignation speech surprised members of the government.
Four other members of parliament also admitted to using false academic titles.
The ODA party has four seats in the 16-member government.
Leaders of the ODA were scheduled to meet on Wednesday evening to discuss Kalvoda's replacement.
Political analysts stated that Kalvoda's confession was damaging to the government.
The stability of the government could be threatened if the coalition agreement is reopened.

The Czech National Bank (CNB) may make a modest interest rate cut early next year due to slower-than-expected third quarter economic growth.
The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) reported that third quarter gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 3.6 percent year-on-year.
GDP for the first three quarters of 1996 is 4.0 percent higher than the same period in 1995.
A Reuter survey predicted GDP growth for the first three quarters of 1996 to be about 4.2 percent.
The official GDP growth for the first six months of 1996 was 4.3 percent, and 4.8 percent for the whole of 1995.
Analysts indicated that the CNB's mid-year tightening may have been too aggressive.
Economist Radek Maly from Citibank Prague expects a slight cut in rates early next year.
Inflation in 1996 has been above nine percent until recent months, slowing to 8.6 percent by November year-on-year.
Maly suggested that the government should consider lifting controls on energy and rents to stabilize inflation.
The key measure of money supply growth, M2, slowed to 13.8 percent year-on-year by the end of September.

Harvard Capital & Consulting (HC&C) paid a one million crown fine for illegal trading practices from 1993 to 1995.
The fine amounted to approximately $36,500.
Viktor Kozeny, the founder of HC&C, confirmed that the fine was paid in June from his home in the Bahamas.
HC&C stated that deficiencies from 1993 to 1995 have mostly been removed and they are working on correcting the others.
The Finance Ministry levied the maximum fine allowed by Czech law on HC&C.
HC&C was cited for several violations of the law on investment companies and funds.
Marie Jezkova, head of the ministry's department of fund supervision, stated that HC&C was primarily cited for manipulating assets of the Harvard Guarantee & Multiple Fund.
Jezkova indicated that the violations included unprofessional care in dealing with the fund's assets.
Vostry mentioned that one reason for the fine was exceeding the maximum limits for purchasing shares in individual companies.
At the time, funds were limited to holding a maximum 20 percent stake in any one company.

General Motors Corp invested 300 million stg in its U.K. operations.
The investment reflects confidence in Vauxhall Motors and the Astra model's international prospects.
The three-year investment will modernise the Ellesmere Port plant in north-west England.
The Ellesmere Port plant produces Astra cars and vans.
The investment guarantees the livelihoods of 4,200 employees at the plant and will create at least 200 new jobs.
Nick Reilly, chairman and managing director of Vauxhall Motors, stated that increasing shifts at the plant could create hundreds more jobs.
The Astra model has been one of the top five sellers in Britain and Europe since its launch five years ago.
Reilly noted that the 300 million stg investment was won against competition within GM.
Reilly forecasted strong growth for the Astra in Latin America and Asia Pacific.
Vauxhall aimed to maintain a market share of around 14.5 percent in 1996.

Reckitt & Colman Plc announced a special Foreign Income Dividend (FID) of 35.65 pence per share.
The company plans to take one in every 20 of its shares out of circulation.
The FID is funded from earnings made outside Britain.
Reckitt shares increased by 18.5 pence to 735 by midmorning following the announcement.
Reckitt aims to clean up its balance sheet due to sharp falls in its debt.
The company spent $1 billion in 1994 to acquire the U.S. household products group L&F.
Sales of non-core businesses, including Colman's mustard, have generated over 430 million pounds.
Chief executive Vernon Sankey stated that the company has no major takeover target currently in sight.
Reckitt is focused on acquiring smaller businesses that fit its product range and extend its global reach.
The company generates around 150 million pounds a year in cash.

British Biotech Plc published evidence on Monday that its cancer drug Marimastat worked.
Analysts stated that there is still a long way to go before Marimastat's potential can be confirmed.
British Biotech's shares ended the day 19 pence lower at 210 after the announcement.
Some analysts predicted that Marimastat could one day have sales of $4 billion a year.
Presentations on Marimastat's effectiveness at a science conference in Vienna were similar to previously published data.
Finance director James Noble expressed caution in the company's statement to avoid raising patients' hopes.
Noble stated that there is significant evidence that Marimastat increases survival chances in cancer patients.
The studies involved 381 cancer patients who continued taking Marimastat after the required 28-day Phase II trial period.
Patients who continued taking Marimastat for more than 28 days lived significantly longer than those who stopped.
British Biotech confirmed that Marimastat caused joint pain in around 30 percent of patients after three to five months.

British Petroleum Co Plc (BP) reported its best-ever third quarter earnings.
Third-quarter net earnings for BP increased by 22 percent to 650 million pounds ($1.07 billion).
In the first nine months of the year, BP's net earnings rose by 28 percent to a record 1.93 billion pounds.
Strong oil prices, recently at around $22 a barrel, boosted BP's earnings by between $400 million and $500 million in the third quarter.
Weaker profit margins in refining, marketing, and chemicals offset the gains, accounting for about 27 percent of group net earnings.
Group chief executive John Browne stated that BP's profit was aided by cost-cutting and efficiency drives adding $150 million to profit every quarter.
BP shares closed at 640.5 pence after touching a high of 647 pence.
Trading in BP shares on the options market was active, with speculation of a sharp rise in BP shares.
BP's results contrasted with disappointing third-quarter figures from rival Royal Dutch/Shell Group, where profits fell due to low refining margins.
BP maintained a long-term view that oil prices would settle back into a range of $16 to $18 a barrel.

BOC Group Plc reported its best-ever full-year profits of 444.9 million pounds ($745 million).
Profits increased by 11 percent despite challenges from a stronger pound and a decline in the health-care business.
Sales rose by seven percent to just over 4.0 billion pounds.
The profit outcome was at the top-end of analysts' forecasts.
Shares in BOC Group Plc increased by 29 pence to 865 pence in early afternoon trading.
Operating profits in the industrial gases sector rose by nine percent to 408.3 million pounds.
Sales in the industrial gases sector increased by 6.8 percent to 2.8 billion pounds.
Chief executive Danny Rosenkranz expects profit margins in gases to improve by about two percentage points over the next three to four years.
The Ohmeda health division experienced an 11 percent decline in operating profits to 53.1 million pounds.
Edwards Vacuum Products posted a 28 percent gain in performance despite expectations of a poor outcome.

A revolution in the treatment of HIV and AIDS is benefiting both patients and drug companies.
Drug companies have invested millions of pounds in fighting the HIV and AIDS epidemic.
Cocktails of new and old drugs are improving quality of life and life expectancy for patients.
Some patient groups forecast that death rates from AIDS in Europe could fall by 50 percent next year.
Drug companies like Glaxo Wellcome Plc expect significant increases in sales of AIDS and HIV products.
Global turnover of AIDS and HIV products is forecast to treble by the end of the century.
Analysts at Lehman Brothers predict sales of AIDS drugs at Glaxo Wellcome will rise to around $2 billion by the end of the century from $300 million in 1995.
Keith Alcorn stated that this year has been exceptional for AIDS treatment, with tangible effects on patients' lives.
Advances in treatment have revived the fortunes of Glaxo Wellcome's Retrovir, also known as AZT.
Doctors have found that combining Retrovir with other treatments can significantly reduce HIV levels in the blood.

The UK government is selling AEA Technology Plc as part of its last privatisation venture.
The sale is expected to generate around 200 million pounds ($312.7 million) for the Treasury.
Ian Lang is the Trade and Industry Secretary overseeing the sale.
AEA Technology is a spin-off from the Atomic Energy Authority and is based in Oxfordshire.
The government plans to retain a 'golden share' in AEA Technology for three years to veto takeover attempts.
The opposition Labour Party has raised concerns about security implications related to AEA Technology's role in monitoring UK nuclear submarine safety.
Peter Watson is the chief executive of AEA Technology.
AEA Technology's sales for the year to March were 253.3 million pounds.
The company has diversified its interests beyond the nuclear industry, including work on battery life extension and safety expertise at Chernobyl.
AEA Technology aims to increase foreign sales from just over one-fifth to one-third of total sales.

Blue Circle Industries Plc reported tentative signs of a turnaround in its European heating operations.
The company promised a ten-fold increase in heating profits over the next three years.
Blue Circle blamed low infrastructure spending for a decline in British cement sales.
The company's interim pretax profit increased by 11.7 percent to 116.3 million pounds.
The interim dividend rose by 6 percent to 4.25 pence.
Blue Circle shares closed down 5 pence at 372 pence.
The heating operations posted operating profits of nine million pounds in the six months to June.
Blue Circle expects 1996 sales in the British cement market to be down four percent from 1995.
Ian McKenzie, chief executive of Blue Circle Cement, cited poor housing starts and low government spending as issues.
Keith Orrell-Jones stated the company aims for annual cost savings of 25 million pounds in the heating division.

BTP Plc expects profit margins in its adhesive and textile coatings business to recover fully over the next 18 months.
Raw material price rises and intense competition pushed margins as low as three percent in the year to March.
Divisional operating profit for the adhesive and textile coatings business slumped 37 percent to 3.8 million stg.
Finance director Rob Martin stated that margins could be restored to six or seven percent within 12 to 18 months.
BTP's group pretax profit rose just 0.7 percent to 37.5 million stg due to weakness in the adhesives and textile coatings and performance chemicals divisions.
BTP is restructuring its adhesives manufacturing operations in France and Germany.
Martin noted that all group operations are performing well.
Continental Europe is facing tougher markets, but there are signs of improvement.
Sluggishness in France and Germany, which account for around 15 percent of group sales, remains a challenge.
BTP is a major supplier of agrochemical intermediates in the U.S., which accounts for about 30 percent of group sales.

Celltech Group Plc expects to post a pre-tax loss of around 10 million stg in the year to September 1997.
Finance director Peter Allen stated that a further 10 million stg receipt from the 1996 sale of the Biologics business to Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG would lead to profit the following year.
Analysts indicated that around half of the payment from the Biologics sale would contribute to Celltech's bottom line.
Celltech is developing a septic shock treatment with Bayer AG and a leukaemia drug with American Home Products Corp.
Peter Allen predicted that Celltech would post an operating profit in 1999 if both products launch as expected.
Celltech's cash reserves exceeded 46 million stg at the end of September 1997, eliminating the need for fresh funding for day-to-day operations.
Allen stated that cash burn for the current year would be just under 10 million stg, with research and development spending rising to 21 million stg.
Allen predicted milestone payments would total between 5.5 to 6.0 million stg.
Peter Fellner, the chief executive, mentioned that Celltech is committed to collaborating with major drug companies but may take more products through later stages of development.
Celltech's psoriasis drug, currently in Phase II trials, is a candidate for later stage development by the company.

Shares in Britain's pharmaceutical industry rose sharply on Thursday.
The increase was attributed to the weakness of sterling, takeover speculation, positive broker comments, and news from Medeva Plc.
Shares of Glaxo Wellcome Plc rose by 3.3 percent to 955 pence.
Shares of SmithKline Beecham Plc increased by 4.4 percent to 880.5 pence.
Shares of Zeneca Group rose by 3.0 percent to 1,723 pence.
Traders noted that the decline of sterling on foreign exchanges contributed to the gains.
Earlier in the month, shares in major pharmaceutical companies fell after NatWest Securities reduced 1997 earnings estimates due to currency impact.
Analyst Robin Gilbert from Panmure Gordon stated that currency is very important to the sector.
Speculation about Roche Holding AG potentially announcing a merger or takeover may have positively influenced Zeneca and SmithKline Beecham.
Shares in Medeva rose by 8.5 pence to 288 pence following positive trial data for its hepatitis B vaccine Hepagene.

Zeneca Group Plc announced that its 1996 performance is expected to meet market expectations.
Analysts predict a pre-tax profit increase for Zeneca to around 1.0 billion pounds in 1996, up from 619 million pounds in 1995.
Zeneca will unveil its results on March 11.
Zeneca stock decreased by four pence to 1689-1/2 pence in early trading.
Sales volumes for Zeneca in 1996 are expected to rise by approximately 14 percent year-on-year.
Sales of the cardiovascular drug Zestril are projected to grow at a rate similar to 1995's 12 percent growth.
Sales of the prostate cancer treatment Zoladex continued to grow strongly.
Sales of the breast cancer product Nolvadex experienced a slowdown in decline.
Sales of the prostate treatment Casodex and the backup drug Arimidex exceeded expectations.
The launch of the asthma drug Accolate in the U.S. was reported to have gone well.

Ricardo Gomez is a novice torero from Bogota, Colombia.
Gomez is 22 years old and weighs 120 pounds (54 kg).
He is 5 feet 5 inches (1.7 meters) tall.
Gomez's training in bullfighting began at the age of 16.
He has been a novice bullfighter for four seasons.
Gomez's performances have received positive reviews from audiences and the press.
The Santamaria bullring in Bogota has a capacity of 15,000.
Bullfighting in Colombia is often associated with wealth and elite status.
Gomez aims to become a top professional matador.
Cesar Rincon is Gomez's idol in the bullfighting world.

Colombia's main oil workers' union is called USO.
USO has merged with a smaller labor organization to create an industry-wide front.
The new grouping will target workers not currently represented by any union.
The merger vote took place in Barrancabermeja.
USO has about 5,700 workers and has primarily recruited within Ecopetrol.
The merger with ASOPETROL could lead to a 'super-union' of 40,000 members.
The new union may cover production, refinery workers, contractors, and transport and distribution operations.
SINTRAOXY, representing Occidental Petroleum's workers, is expected to join the new union.
USO has accused foreign multinationals of undermining national sovereignty and exploiting Colombian workers.
Some multinationals believe USO has ties with Colombia's leftist guerrilla movements.

Colombia's Foreign Relations Ministry stated it would give full attention to accusations linking British Petroleum to political killings.
The ministry denied that any official investigation into the allegations was underway.
The ministry claimed that without judicial investigations, it is irresponsible to credit the allegations against BP.
Colombian government attempts to clear BP of the allegations led to new controversy.
The chief prosecutor's office and the attorney general's office opened inquiries into human rights abuses in Casanare and Arauca.
A 1995 multi-agency report documented human rights abuses and blamed military and paramilitary groups for murders in Casanare and Arauca.
The report indicated that oil companies contributed to social upheaval in the region.
BP stated it paid a 'war tax' to the government for the army's counterinsurgency campaign against guerrillas.
BP denied any links to irregular or paramilitary forces.
Recent allegations in British newspapers claimed BP was involved in killings by right-wing death squads in Casanare.

Two Germans were arrested in northwest Colombia while attempting to smuggle a kidnap victim out of the country.
The arrest occurred at Rionegro international airport near Medellin at 1 am local time.
The Germans were trying to transport Brigitte Schoene, the wife of a former BASF Chemicals director, onto a charter plane.
A list of 83 international guerrilla organizations and several false passports were found in the detainees' bags.
Gen. Alfredo Salgado, head of the anti-kidnap police in northwest Antioquia province, suggested the Germans were linked to the National Liberation Army (ELN).
The ELN is identified as Colombia's second largest rebel group, known for attacks on oil infrastructure and multinational companies.
The two Germans claimed they were mediating the release of Schoene, who was kidnapped from her home along with her son and chauffeur.
Schoene's son and chauffeur were released hours after the kidnapping.
The German Embassy in Bogota declined to comment on the arrests.
The man had forged ID papers with the names Norbert Schroder and Jurgen Seidel, while the woman was identified as Silvia Schroder and Isabel Seidel.

Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Bogota on Sunday to call for an end to the crime wave in Colombia.
Colombia is referred to as the kidnap capital of the world.
At least 1,100 people have been abducted in Colombia this year, with more than half taken by warring factions.
National Police chief Rosso Jose Serrano participated in the march and viewed it as a challenge to leftist guerrillas.
Francisco Santos, founder of Pais Libre, stated that abduction strips victims of their soul.
Santos was kidnapped six years ago by the Medellin cartel.
An estimated 15,000 to 20,000 people participated in the march, with organizers claiming the number was twice that.
Norberto Garcia's 14-year-old daughter Andrea disappeared almost a year ago.
Seven-year-old Victor Alvarez was kidnapped and murdered in southwest Colombia last Wednesday.
Conservative estimates suggest that there are three abductions per day in Colombia.

Colombia's largest guerrilla army, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), will not free 60 captive government troops unless a large area of southern jungle is demilitarized.
President Ernesto Samper stated he would honor his pledge to clear 5,400 square miles (14,000 sq km) of Caqueta province.
Samper rejected FARC's demands to clear three military bases in the zone.
Samper urged the rebels to release their prisoners before Christmas under terms he set the previous week.
The FARC's decision was communicated from Mexico City and complicates the process of securing the release of the soldiers captured three months ago.
The FARC's Aug. 30 attack on a base in Putumayo province resulted in the deaths of 27 soldiers and the capture of others.
Military analysts noted that army commanders were reluctant to allow FARC to dictate terms for the troop handover.
Samper pressured military leaders to agree to clear a 5,400-square-mile (14,000 sq km) area of Caqueta for 10 days starting on Friday.
The president and military officials stated they would not withdraw troops from barracks in Montanitas, Cartagena del Chaira, and Remolinos del Caguan due to concerns over drug trafficking.
FARC claimed that the towns mentioned are on strategic routes into and out of the proposed demilitarized zone.

Colombian lawmakers responded to government pressure by revising a bill to seize assets from drug barons.
The asset forfeiture bill must survive a congressional plenary vote to be enacted.
The United States has threatened economic sanctions on Colombia for not adequately addressing drug trafficking.
A conference committee reversed a previous decision by the House of Representatives that weakened the asset forfeiture law.
The House of Representatives voted to limit the law's retroactive application to 1991, leaving significant assets from the Cali Cartel untouched.
Justice Minister Carlos Medellin expressed optimism about the bill's approval in the plenary session.
Colombia's business community supported the 20-year time limit for asset seizure to avoid U.S. sanctions.
Key export sectors in Colombia may be adversely affected if U.S. sanctions are imposed.
Political analysts believe Colombia is unlikely to regain its status as a U.S. ally in the drug war.
Other anti-drug legislation demanded by the United States has faced challenges in Congress.

A car bomb exploded in a residential district of Medellin, killing one woman and injuring at least 48 others.
The bomb contained about 120 pounds (50 kg) of dynamite and was packed into a minibus.
The explosion occurred outside the home of Juan Gomez Martinez, a regional newspaper editor and former provincial governor.
The Colombian government suspects drug cartels were responsible for the explosion.
President Ernesto Samper stated that the government would not succumb to terrorist violence from drug traffickers.
Five unidentified gunmen opened fire on private security guards near Gomez's home before the bomb detonated.
Three houses were virtually destroyed and 15 others were seriously damaged by the explosion.
The deceased woman was identified as Lucia Cevallos de Bernal, aged 60.
Gomez was not at home during the attack, but one of his sons was injured.
Authorities offered a $150,000 reward for information leading to the capture of those responsible for the attack.

The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) is Latin America's oldest and largest guerrilla army.
Marco Leon Calarca is the international spokesman for FARC and is based in Mexico City.
FARC defended the actions of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) regarding their attack on the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
The MRTA launched the raid on the ambassador's residence on Tuesday night.
Colombian authorities estimate that FARC has about 12,000 fighters, while independent analysts suggest it has more than 18,000.
The MRTA is believed to have no more than about 2,000 insurgents.
Calarca stated that the MRTA attack was well-planned and suggests it has popular support.
Calarca claimed that people must defend themselves against the aggression of neoliberalism and that the oligarchy will not voluntarily relinquish rights.
Members of the MRTA traveled to Colombia in the mid-1980s to join the America Battalion.
The America Battalion included Colombia's M-19 rebel group and Ecuador's Alfaro Vive Carajo! and attempted to create rebel liberated zones in Colombia.

The Colombian authorities referred to U.S. pilot Robert Martin as a hero in the fight against narco-trafficking.
Robert Martin, 35, from Lubbock, Texas, died when his Turbo Thrush T-65 crop dusting plane crashed in Guaviare province.
Martin was fumigating illicit coca leaf plantations at the time of the crash.
Colombian Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra, police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano, and U.S. ambassador Myles Frechette attended a religious service in Bogota to honor Martin.
A bugler played the 'Last Post' and the U.S. flag was draped over Martin's coffin during the service.
Serrano stated that they were there to say goodbye to a hero who fought against narco-trafficking.
Martin was one of six U.S. civilian pilots working in Colombia under contract with the U.S. State Department.
Frechette noted that Martin was the first U.S. aviator to die on such a mission.
Frechette assured that Martin's death would not affect U.S.-Colombian cooperation in the drug war.
Police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano indicated that there was a heavy rebel presence in the area but no evidence that the aircraft had come under fire.

Colombia's President Ernesto Samper announced plans to boost revenues by broadening the tax base.
The 1997 budget would be cut by over a trillion pesos, exceeding the 900 billion pesos previously approved by Congress.
The measures are part of an emergency plan to address the fiscal deficit.
Samper stated that overall income tax rates and the 14 percent value added tax would not be raised.
Samper pledged to expand the tax base and combat tax evasion.
Public sector workers will receive below-inflation wage rises as part of an austerity law.
The merger or closure of inefficient government offices will help reduce public spending.
Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo indicated that everyone would be affected by the proposed measures.
An economic emergency has been declared for an initial period of 20 days, allowing the president to rule by decree.
The fiscal deficit rose to 4 percent of GDP in 1996 from 0.2 percent in 1995.

Mexican Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria criticized the United States for its policy of rewarding or punishing countries based on their measures to fight drug trafficking.
Gurria stated that the certification process is a barrier to cooperation in the war on drugs.
Gurria called for the scrapping of the certification system, claiming decisions are often based on ulterior motives.
Gurria mentioned that the certification process inhibits cooperation and places countries under scrutiny.
Gurria expressed that there are better ways to promote cooperation in the fight against drug trafficking.
Last year, Colombia was removed from the United States' list of allies in the drug war.
Mexico received certification from the United States and avoided sanctions despite severe criticism.
Mexico established a ministerial contact group to address drug trafficking issues with Washington, leading to improved relations.
Colombia has faced heavy criticism from the United States for not sufficiently addressing drug trafficking.
The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration estimates that 80 percent of the world's cocaine is supplied by Colombia, and over half of the cocaine in U.S. cities has been transported through Mexico.

Plans are being drawn up for new peace talks between the Colombian government and leftist rebels.
The spokesman for Colombia's Conciliation Commission is Diego Vargas Uribe.
The Conciliation Commission has consulted all sides in the four-decade-old conflict about the basis for a negotiated peace.
Diego Vargas Uribe stated that details of the peace talks would be released in a few weeks.
Political analysts warn that the prospect of peace is slight.
The Colombian armed forces announced they would increase their counterinsurgency campaign.
Marxist rebels have escalated their attacks in the current year.
FARC leader Manuel Marulanda expressed the group's desire for a political solution to the conflict in their magazine Resistencia.
Manuel Marulanda stated that any peace deal must address political, social, and economic inequalities.
The National Liberation Army (ELN) began tentative moves toward peace talks with President Ernesto Samper's administration last year.

Manchester United's share price increased by over 10 percent for the second consecutive session.
The increase in share price was influenced by a report that Mark McCormack's IMG marketing agency was considering a bid for the club.
An official at IMG stated that they do not comment on unsubstantiated press stories but expressed interest in increasing involvement in football.
IMG previously lost a bid for control of Olympique Marseille to Adidas.
The report indicated that a credible bid for Manchester United would need to be between 650-700 pence per share, valuing the club at approximately 430 million pounds.
On Monday, Manchester United shares rose by 54.5p to 568p, valuing the club at around 350 million pounds.
The share price has nearly tripled since the beginning of the year and increased by almost 25 percent in the last two sessions.
Chief executive Martin Edwards stated that Manchester United's status as Britain's most profitable soccer club makes it a likely target for bids.
VCI made a 300 million pound bid for Manchester United earlier this year, which was rejected.
Analysts believe Manchester United would be an attractive target for media companies due to potential income from pay-per-view television deals.

United News & Media secured control of Blenheim with an offer valuing the company at 592.5 million pounds.
The deal will create the world's largest trade exhibition group with a turnover of more than 500 million pounds based on 1995 figures.
United News has secured acceptances for 51 percent of Blenheim after offering five pounds per share.
United's chief executive Clive Hollick stated that the acquisition will be earnings-enhancing in the first full year.
United News shares increased by 31p to 674-1/2p after the announcement.
Blenheim shares increased by 22-1/2p to 496p following the announcement.
Dutch publisher VNU, which acquired a 15 percent stake in Blenheim, will not make a counter-bid and is likely to sell its stake.
Anglo-Dutch media group Reed-Elsevier has dropped out of the bidding for Blenheim.
The acquisition follows a series of bid approaches for Blenheim that began in June.
Blenheim operates more than 170 exhibitions worldwide but lacks a significant publishing portfolio.

The director-general of the BBC called for an increase in the British television licence fee.
John Birt stated that the BBC is the most successful cultural institution in the world.
Birt mentioned that the licence fee has fallen in real terms over the past decade.
The BBC's financial history was described by Birt as miraculous.
Birt indicated that an increase in the licence fee is needed to fund new services due to digital technology.
A colour television licence currently costs 89.50 pounds annually.
Licence income totals around 1.8 billion pounds each year, which constitutes 95 percent of BBC income.
The BBC plans to begin talks with the government to review the licence fee, which is currently pegged to inflation.
Any increase in the licence fee would take effect from April 1, 1997.
Birt noted that the BBC is towards the bottom of the European licence fee league table.

Glasgow-based Stakis Plc and Saudi billionaire Prince al-Waleed bin Talal are likely purchasers of the Metropole and Princess hotel chains from Lonrho Plc.
Lonrho Plc is undergoing a demerger and has received interest from potential buyers for its hotel chains.
The sale of the Metropole and Princess hotel chains could be completed within the next fortnight for more than 650 million pounds ($1 billion).
Stakis has approximately 46 British hotels and has not commented on reports regarding the purchase of the five Metropole properties.
Analyst Fraser Ramzan of Lehman Brothers stated that the deal would be an excellent fit for Stakis, but the size of the deal could cause concern.
Markets speculate that Stakis may plan a rights issue to fund the purchase of the Metropole hotels, valued at about 350 million pounds.
The Metropole group consists of five business and conference hotels located in London, Birmingham, Brighton, and Blackpool.
Millennium & Copthorne has ruled itself out of purchasing the Metropole hotels and is not in talks to buy them.
