Prince al-Waleed is believed to be negotiating the purchase of the Princess chain, which includes 10 properties in the United States, the Caribbean, and Mexico.
Financial sources indicate that al-Waleed has exclusive rights to negotiate a deal for the Princess chain at a price of $300 million.

A $22 billion deal between British Telecom Plc and MCI Communications Corp is expected to be announced on Sunday.
BT has scheduled a news conference for 1300 GMT on Sunday at its Central London headquarters.
BT is in merger talks with MCI Communications Corp.
Executives from BT and MCI were in separate board meetings on Saturday.
MCI is the number two U.S. long-distance phone company.
BT has a 20 percent stake in MCI.
BT and MCI operate a joint venture known as Concert, serving customers in over 50 nations.
Analysts speculate a price of $40 a share for MCI, valuing it at $28 billion.
The deal would be the second largest involving a U.S. company.
BT's board is meeting over the weekend to consider a proposal from MCI.

The $22 billion takeover of MCI Communications Corp marks the end of Sir Peter Bonfield's first year as chief executive of British Telecommunications Plc.
BT confirmed that it would buy the 80 percent of MCI it does not own.
Sir Peter Bonfield became chief executive of BT in January after the company split the roles of chairman and chief executive.
Sir Iain Vallance became BT chairman after the role split.
Bonfield's appointment was positively received by City commentators.
The Financial Times described Bonfield's appointment as a turning point in BT's transition from public sector utility to competitive services group.
Bonfield had a reputation for boosting revenue, curbing costs, and international expansion during his time at ICL.
Vallance stated that Bonfield's international experience and knowledge of the computing services industry would benefit BT's global expansion.
BT was in talks with Cable & Wireless about a merger shortly after Bonfield's arrival, but those talks ended unsuccessfully.
Bonfield aims for BT to be one of the most successful global telecom companies in 20 or 30 years.

British media company EMAP expects to resolve a boardroom dispute quickly.
Finance director David Grigson stated that an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) next month will address the boardroom conflict.
The EGM is scheduled for December 2 and aims to remove non-executive directors Ken Simmonds and Joe Cooke from the board.
Simmonds and Cooke opposed changes made to the company's articles at the annual general meeting in July.
The changes to the articles removed the requirement for at least five non-executive directors and allowed for a director's removal with a 75 percent board vote.
EMAP shares increased by 10p to 732.5p after the company reported strong first-half profits.
Pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit for the six months to September 30, 1996, grew by 34 percent to 50.6 million pounds.
EMAP recorded a one-off gain of 113.5 million pounds from the sale of its regional newspaper business to Johnston Press Plc.
EMAP has shifted its focus from regional newspapers to commercial radio, consumer magazines, and business communications.
The interim dividend was increased from 3.7p to 4.3p as EMAP expressed optimism for future growth.

Granada Group won control of Forte, a leading British hotelier, 10 months ago.
Granada Group reported a 37 percent rise in annual profits to 480 million pounds ($806 million).
Granada Group aims to boost profits at Forte by over 100 million pounds per annum.
Granada Group has already achieved 40 million pounds in profit improvements at Forte.
Turnover for the year ending in September grew by 60 percent to 3.82 billion pounds.
The total dividend was raised by 11 percent to 13p per share.
Granada acquired Forte in a 3.9 billion pound deal earlier this year.
Analysts were surprised by the lackluster reaction to Granada's strong results.
Granada operates two British commercial television stations and a chain of rental stores.
Granada plans to sell a group of top international hotels and the Welcome Break chain in early 1997.

Carlton Communications Plc purchased Westcountry Television for 85 million pounds ($143 million).
United News & Media was also seeking to acquire Westcountry Television.
Analysts believe high prices for takeover targets may reduce takeover activity in the ITV sector.
The ITV commercial television sector is undergoing consolidation due to new media ownership laws.
The two-licence ownership limit has been replaced by a cap of 15 percent of television audience.
The Westcountry deal adds the south-western corner of England to Carlton's existing licences.
Carlton, United News, and Granada Group Plc are the three main players in the ITV sector.
Westcountry's 1995 pre-tax profit was five million pounds, compared to Carlton's 123 million pounds operating profit.
United News holds a 20 percent stake in HTV but is not planning a full bid at this time.
HTV has a market capitalisation of approximately 315 million pounds.

Britons will learn the amount they will be asked to pay for the expansion of BBC radio and television services.
The BBC is lobbying the government for an above-inflation increase in the annual licence fee.
The government is expected to announce its decision regarding the licence fee by early to mid-December.
The BBC derives 95 percent of its funding from the annual fee paid by television set owners.
The current licence fee is 89.50 pounds ($150) and generated 1.8 billion pounds in the last financial year.
The BBC's commercial arm provided a net benefit of 77 million pounds in the last financial year.
The licence fee is guaranteed as a source of funding for the BBC for the next five years.
BBC Director-General John Birt launched a campaign for an increase in the licence fee at a conference in Edinburgh in August.
The BBC is believed to be seeking a rise of around five pounds to generate over 100 million pounds in extra revenue.
Annual inflation is currently 2.7 percent.

French radio group NRJ SA is seeking to enter the UK market by competing for a London FM licence.
NRJ operates approximately 500 stations across six European countries.
NRJ is targeting the youth demographic in London, claiming they are underserved by current radio stations.
Marc Pallain is the head of development at NRJ.
The Radio Authority will announce the winner of the FM licence in mid-January.
The winner of the licence will be chosen based on programme plans and financial viability.
The frequency for the new station was previously used by Melody Radio, which relocated due to interference.
The potential audience for the new station is nearly six million adults.
Twenty-five groups have submitted bids for the FM licence, including various demographic-focused stations.
Front-runners for the licence include Capital Radio, Atlantic, XFM, and The Edge.

Shares in Pearson Plc recovered on Wednesday after a trading statement.
Pearson's shares had dipped to a two-month low on Tuesday.
The company stated that trading in the second half of the year was in line with the first half.
Shares were 20 1/2p firmer at 710p by 095 GMT.
Analysts expressed relief that Pearson had not produced any negative surprises.
Pearson's total video retuning costs for the launch of Channel 5 are expected to rise to around 150 million pounds.
The retuning costs are nearly three times the initial estimate for dealing with video recorders affected by interference.
Channel 5 has been awarded an extra frequency to increase its coverage to 80 percent of the country.
Pearson's business plan for Channel 5 shows significantly higher rates of return than the original bid.
This year's losses from Mindscape are expected to be around 46 million pounds.

Large U.S. medical device manufacturers are expected to post strong profit gains for the third quarter.
Five of nine big device companies are expected to report year-over-year earnings gains of 20 percent or more, according to First Call consensus forecasts.
Stocks in larger companies, such as Medtronic Inc and Boston Scientific Corp, are rallying from a summer slump.
Investor sentiment is shifting towards larger companies as small-cap companies are struggling.
Major manufacturers are entering a new period of abundance, making them attractive to investors.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved 37 product marketing applications in its latest fiscal year, up from 27 in the prior year.
This increase in approvals has reduced the risk of bringing new products to market.
Continued growth in European and Asian consumer demand for U.S. medical devices is beneficial for larger U.S. companies.
The quarterly earnings forecasts for various companies include C.R. Bard at $0.47, Boston Scientific at $0.41, and Medtronic at $0.55.

Pall Corp and Memtec Ltd are both interested in acquiring Gelman Sciences Inc.
Analysts are uncertain if this interest will lead to a bidding war.
Memtec's American Depositary Shares experienced a rally, indicating some doubt about its commitment to the acquisition.
Gelman Sciences Inc. would complement the operations of both Pall Corp and Memtec Ltd.
Gelman shares closed at 29 on the American Stock Exchange after news of acquisition discussions with Pall.
Gelman reached a definitive agreement to be acquired by Memtec on August 30.
Memtec intends to proceed with the acquisition of Gelman.
Memtec seeks Gelman's membrane technology to enhance its competition with Pall and Millipore Corp.
Pall aims to acquire Gelman to expand its medical and process businesses and reduce competition.
Gelman sales for fiscal 1996 were $112 million, while Memtec sales for the same period were $175 million.

United Airlines ordered 51 new airliners valued at $4.4 billion from Boeing Co. and Airbus Industrie.
The majority of the order went to Boeing, but Airbus secured a significant portion of the deal.
United will buy 24 narrow-body A319 aircraft from Airbus, valued at $900 million based on list prices.
United will likely pay less than the list price due to special discounts.
United chose Airbus planes over competing Boeing 737-700s and 737-300s after evaluation.
United will buy 27 new wide-body planes from Boeing, including 19 747-400s, six 757s, and two 777s.
The Boeing order is valued at $3.5 billion based on list prices.
United may have received discounts of 10 percent to 15 percent off list prices from both Boeing and Airbus.
The new wide-body planes will replace older Boeing aircraft in United's fleet.
United is expected to order another 100 narrow-body planes over the next seven years to update its fleet.

Eli Lilly & Co's third-quarter profits are expected to be significantly higher than in 1995.
Analysts have concerns about Eli Lilly's profit margins.
Increased marketing costs for Prozac and Zyprexa may negatively impact profit margins.
Analyst Mariola Haggar from Deutsche Morgan Grenfell expressed concern that gross profit margin could fall below last year's level.
The gross margin for the third quarter of 1995 was 74.3 percent.
The First Call consensus of 20 analysts projects third-quarter Lilly profits of $0.64 per share, an increase of 18.5 percent from $0.54 per share a year ago.
Revenues for the quarter are expected to be approximately $1.8 billion, up from $1.63 billion in the previous year.
Shares in Lilly increased by 3/4 to 69-1/4 on Monday before the earnings report.
A one-time gain from the deal with Dura Pharmaceuticals for marketing rights to Ceclor CD and Keftab may boost the third quarter.
No significant revenue from Zyprexa is expected in the third quarter, but it is anticipated to contribute in the fourth quarter.

Baxter International Inc expects to maintain an annual gross profit margin in the 44 to 45 percent range.
Harry Kraemer, the chief financial officer, stated that the company will stay in the 44 to 45 percent range on an annual basis.
Baxter forecasts that 1996 sales will be about $6.2 billion, although Kraemer suggested this figure could be low.
Baxter reported third-quarter earnings of $0.65 per share, exceeding the consensus Wall Street estimate of $0.64 per share.
Year-ago profits for Baxter were $0.59 per share.
Sales for the third quarter were $1.31 billion, compared to $1.26 billion a year earlier.
Foreign exchange translations reduced third-quarter sales by about $60 million.
Kraemer stated that unfavorable currency exchange ratios continued to impact sales, particularly in Japan.
Baxter expects that 60 percent of sales and 75 percent of profits will come from outside the United States after acquiring Immuno International AG.
Baxter targeted 1996 cash flow of $500 million, with cash flow of $457 million reported in the first nine months of the year.

ClinTrials Research Inc expects to expand revenues by 35 to 45 percent per year.
The firm is the world's fifth-largest contract research organization.
William O'Neil is the chief executive of ClinTrials Research Inc.
O'Neil stated that drug and biotechnology companies spend $10 to $11 billion annually on research and development.
About $2.5 billion of R&D spending is outsourced to contract research organizations.
Five years ago, only five percent of R&D spending was outsourced.
R&D spending is growing at about 10 percent annually.
ClinTrials recently acquired BioResearch Laboratories Inc for $65 million.
The acquisition of BioResearch Laboratories was accretive to earnings and reduced ClinTrials' tax rate.
Eighty percent of ClinTrials' revenues come from major drug companies.

Outboard Marine Corp is five percent finished with a restructuring process.
The restructuring is expected to result in more charges against earnings in 1997 and possibly in 1998.
Stan Main is a spokesman for Outboard Marine Corp.
Shares in Outboard Marine Corp decreased by 1/4 to 15-3/4.
Outboard Marine Corp reported fourth-quarter profits that exceeded Wall Street estimates, excluding restructuring charges.
Analysts believe that a turnaround at Outboard Marine Corp is a long-term project.
Harriet Baldwin is an analyst at Lehman Brothers.
Outboard executives are scheduled to meet with analysts and investors in New York.
Greenway Partners purchased an 8.5-percent stake in Outboard Marine Corp.
Harry Bowman is the chief executive of Outboard Marine Corp.

Aon Corp expects to take a charge against earnings of about $100 million in the 1997 first quarter due to its purchase of Alexander & Alexander Services Inc.
Aon Chief Executive and Chairman Patrick Ryan stated that consolidating costs will occur in the first quarter after the acquisition closes.
Ryan described the $100 million charge as a 'guesstimate' at this stage.
Aon does not expect additional charges beyond the first quarter according to Ryan.
Ryan mentioned that a fair value charge will be included in the deal cost.
Ryan indicated that space costs and corporate redundancies have yet to be determined.
Aon would become either the largest or second-largest insurance brokerage through the acquisition of Alexander & Alexander.
Ryan noted that the comparison of Aon to rival Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc depends on how the companies' operations are counted.
Ryan stated that Aon needs to digest its recent acquisitions before considering further acquisitions.
Aon employs about 27,000 people, while Alexander & Alexander employs about 12,000.

U.S. retailers expect this weekend to conclude a holiday shopping season that is moderately better than last year's.
The current holiday shopping season is shorter by five days compared to last year.
Wayne Hood, a retail analyst at Prudential Securities in Atlanta, stated that it is too early to tell the impact of the weather on sales.
Warmer weather is forecast for much of the country this weekend after a recent cold snap.
Cold weather previously slowed shopping in Minnesota, the Dakotas, Iowa, and Nebraska, according to Susan Eich, a spokeswoman for Dayton Hudson Corp.
Cold, wet weather in the Northeast affected midweek shopping in the New York area.
Snow fell in Atlanta on Wednesday, and south Florida experienced a chill on Friday, but the retail impact was minimal.
Allen Roness, a retail analyst at J.W. Charles Securities in Boca Raton, Florida, reported that shopping activity is good in his area.
Edward Weller, a retail analyst at Robertson Stephens in San Francisco, indicated that California is experiencing strong retail activity.
Weller noted that clothing sales are strong, while home computer sales are weak and prices are decreasing.

Major retailers reported mixed results for the holiday sales season.
Retail stocks dropped following the preliminary holiday reports.
Bruce Missett, a Morgan Stanley retailing analyst, stated that the holiday was one of moderate growth.
J.C. Penney reported sales of $3.6 billion for the four weeks ended Dec. 28, a 23.2 percent increase from $2.9 billion in 1995.
Same-store sales at J.C. Penney increased 6.2 percent over 1995.
J.C. Penney did not release dollar figures for same-store sales.
J.C. Penney expected fourth-quarter earnings to not meet Wall Street expectations.
J.C. Penney stock dropped $1.75 to $47 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Dayton Hudson reported same-store sales increased 4.2 percent across its department stores, Target, and Mervyn's.
Dayton Hudson's department store sales increased 0.3 percent, Mervyn's sales decreased 4.1 percent, and Target sales increased 7.1 percent.

General Instrument Corp announced a three-way corporate break-up.
Analysts believe the break-up will unlock the value of the company's core high-tech communications systems business.
Hickman Powell, an industry analyst at Southeast Research Partners, stated that spinoffs often result in a greater sum of parts than the initial whole.
General Instrument plans to create NextLevel Systems Inc from its cable television, satellite, and telephone businesses.
CommScope Inc will be created from General Instrument's coaxial cable manufacturing business.
General Semiconductor Inc will be formed from General Instrument's electronic component manufacturing operations.
Richard Friedland, CEO of General Instrument, stated that investors will be able to value each new company on its own merits.
Shares in General Instrument increased by 1/4 to 23 at midday following the announcement.
NextLevel will focus on high-speed modems and television cable set-top boxes.
Analysts expressed concerns about how NextLevel will fund its growth after the break-up.

Eight of the top 10 publicly traded U.S. health maintenance organizations are expected to report lower or flat fourth-quarter profits.
The health maintenance organization industry is moving cautiously into 1997 after a difficult year.
Wall Street is becoming cautious on many HMO stocks due to narrow profit margins.
Merger and acquisition activity is supporting the share prices of firms seen as targets in the HMO sector.
Robert Hoehn, a managed healthcare analyst at Salomon Brothers, stated that consolidation will remain at a high level.
Oxford Health Plans Inc is expected to post profits 70 percent higher than the year-ago level.
PacifiCare Health Systems Inc is expected to show a 10 to 13 percent earnings improvement.
PacifiCare's quarter will be complicated by a pending acquisition of FHP International Corp.
Most HMOs faced a costly mismatch between medical cost inflation forecasts and premium increases in 1996.
Ed Keaney, an analyst at Volpe Welty, indicated that there may be room for some premium expansion in the current year.

Amoco Corp is basing its 1997 business plans on assumed prices of $18 to $19 per barrel for crude oil.
Amoco Corp is basing its 1997 business plans on assumed prices of $2.00 to $2.10 per thousand cubic feet for natural gas.
John Carl is the chief financial officer of Amoco Corp.
U.S. crude futures for March delivery closed at $24.24 per barrel on Wednesday.
Amoco shares rose 7/8 to 85-7/8 on Wednesday after reporting strong fourth-quarter and 1996 financial results.
Amoco plans to spend about $550 million on exploration in 1997.
Amoco's exploration spending in 1996 was about $610 million.
Amoco plans to keep its 1997 operating costs flat at the 1996 level.
Amoco reported that fourth-quarter chemical sector earnings fell compared to the previous year.
Paraxylene traded on the spot market Wednesday near $0.22 per pound.

Scott McNealy is the chairman of Sun Microsystems Inc.
McNealy stated that the growth of the Internet has led to significant technological innovation.
McNealy cited the launch of the Netscape Communications Corp Navigation browser and the Java computer language as examples of innovation.
McNealy believes that the Internet and Java pose a threat to Microsoft.
McNealy is on a 10-day visit to Australia and New Zealand with 2,500 Sun employees.
Microsoft has annual revenues of approximately US$8.6 billion.
Sun Microsystems has annual revenues of approximately US$7.00 billion.
Java allows users to operate across all computer operating systems, including Windows.
The Internet enables users to download word processing applications without purchasing Microsoft Office software.
McNealy claims that the Internet has not forced Sun Microsystems to change its business strategy.

The international partners in Australia's largest gas project plan to spend A$6.0 billion to double production.
This investment will make it Australia's largest single resources investment.
Woodside Petroleum Ltd is an Australian oil and gas producer involved in the North West Shelf gas project offshore Western Australia.
The partners plan to double production capacity to 14.5 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) per year.
Analysts believe the decision by the North West Shelf partners is unlikely to enhance the prospect of a co-operative development with the nearby Gorgon gas field.
Geoff Wedgwood, Woodside's corporate affairs manager, stated that the North West Shelf partners have their own plans for expansion.
Wedgwood mentioned that they have not seen a plan from the Gorgon partners that fits within their plans.
Cor Herkstroter, chairman of Royal Dutch/Shell's committee of managing directors, suggested that the expansion of the North West Shelf could not be justified without integrating it with another project.
Royal Dutch/Shell owns 34 percent of Woodside and is a partner in both the North West Shelf and Gorgon projects.
Woodside submitted the expansion plan to the project's eight Japanese power and gas utility customers at a meeting in Osaka.

Comalco Ltd is Australia's largest listed aluminium producer.
Comalco Ltd reported a 72 percent decline in net profit for the first half of 1996.
The decline in profit was attributed to a weaker metal price and a stronger Australian dollar.
Comalco's net profit for the six months to June 30, 1996, was A$43.9 million.
This profit was down from A$155.1 million a year earlier.
Comalco's sales fell 31.6 percent to A$806.9 million for the half.
The three-month aluminium contract on the London Metal Exchange fell nearly 13 percent.
The Australian dollar rose seven percent to around US$0.7900.
Comalco reduced its dividend to three cents a share for the first half.
The dividend was down from 12 cents a year ago and below expectations of five to six cents.

Rupert Murdoch's global media group, The News Corp Ltd, reported an 8.1-percent fall in net profit for the first quarter of 1996/97.
The reported net profits for the three months ended September 30 were A$283 million (US$223 million), down from A$308 million a year earlier.
Analysts had forecast net profit before abnormal items to be around A$320-330 million, which would have been an increase of about 15 percent.
Net profit before abnormals came in at A$285 million.
The poor financial results caused News Corp shares to fall sharply, impacting the entire Australian share market.
The share price decline resulted in a loss of over A$300 million in the group's market capitalisation.
The stock closed at A$6.95, down 18 cents or 2.52 percent, with over 4.7 million shares traded.
The weaker profit was attributed to poorer returns in U.S. TV, Australian newspapers, and book publishing.
Analysts stated that News Corp could still achieve a 20 percent rise in net profits for the 1996/97 year, primarily due to the U.S. television business underperforming.
News Corp's profit was supported by the success of the film Independence Day and its British newspapers and book publishing.

RGC Ltd is an Australian mineral sands and base metals miner.
RGC Ltd reported a 101 percent rise in annual operating profit to A$108.57 million for the year ended June 30, 1996.
The increase in profit was attributed to a boom in demand for aircraft and golf clubs.
RGC Ltd is 40 percent owned by British conglomerate Hanson Plc.
Sales increased by 54 percent to A$986.39 million in 1995/96 due to higher mineral sands and tin prices.
RGC Ltd has about 30 percent of the world market for titanium dioxide (TiO2).
RGC Ltd competes with South African miner Richards Bay Minerals for the title of the world's largest mineral sands miner.
RGC Ltd has operations in Australia, the United States, Papua New Guinea, and Indonesia.
RGC Ltd is looking for expansion opportunities in Bolivia, India, Sri Lanka, and the Ukraine.
RGC Ltd is one of three companies on the short-list to buy the tin assets of the Bolivian state-owned COMIB.

Westpac Banking Group is the second largest bank in Australia.
Westpac announced plans to expand its Asian activities through an alliance with Standard Chartered Bank Plc.
Westpac previously put most of its Asian activities up for sale 3-1/2 years ago.
Westpac's decision to sell Asian activities was influenced by a recession that affected profits.
Kerry Packer and Lend Lease Corp Ltd were potential predators for Westpac's share register at that time.
Westpac chief executive Bob Joss stated that the deal with Standard Chartered is of major importance.
Bob Joss described the alliance as a good strategic fit for Westpac's future growth.
Standard Chartered group chief executive Malcolm Williamson expressed commitment to the new relationship with Westpac.
The venture will focus on Singapore, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Thailand, and Malaysia.
Westpac plans to expand into Vietnam and China in about six months.

Macquarie Bank Ltd reported a record result for the six months ended September 30.
Macquarie Bank is 13.4 percent owned by the Brunei Investment Agency (BIA).
Macquarie Bank reported a 21.3 percent rise in first half net profit to A$46.03 million in the first half of 1996/97.
Executive chairman David Clarke stated that the first half result reflects more even contributions from business groups across the bank.
David Clarke expressed optimism about the second half of the fiscal year.
Managing director Allan Moss indicated that the equities, treasury, and commodities group accounted for most of the first half profit increases.
Moss reported that the Treasury and Commodities Group's first half result is the best since its formation in 1993.
Moss noted a near 400 percent increase in profit from Macquarie Equities Ltd, attributed to increased market share and market volume.
Macquarie's total operating income rose to A$232.69 million in the half, up from A$190.21 million a year earlier.
The Brunei government-owned BIA became Macquarie's largest shareholder after purchasing a 13.4 percent stake for A$151.7 million.

Holyman Ltd plans to expand operations in Europe and move into the Asian market.
Christopher Butcher is the managing director of Holyman Ltd.
Holyman currently operates in North America and northern Europe.
Butcher stated that Holyman could start operations in the Mediterranean.
Holyman is likely to expand into Asia as the cost structure for fast ferries improves.
Butcher mentioned that rising incomes in Asia would increase ferry service charges.
Simon Lennon is the company secretary of Holyman.
Holyman is considering fast ferry services from Darwin to Indonesia, with no decision expected for at least a year.
Holyman shares have more than doubled since January this year.
Holyman shares were listed at A$2.00 in April 1994 and reached a high of A$6.00 on November 11.

Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd aims to enter the Asian high-roller market.
The company seeks a tax break from the New South Wales government.
Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd holds a 12-year licence to operate the only legal casino in Sydney.
The company has been negotiating with the New South Wales government for 15 months regarding tax concessions.
Neil Gamble is the chief executive officer of Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd.
The Sydney casino is 26.3 percent owned by U.S. casino operator Showboat Inc.
Without a 10 percent tax concession on high-roller winnings, the Sydney casino is at a competitive disadvantage.
High-rollers require additional incentives to be attracted to the Sydney casino.
High-rollers may spend between A$100,000 and tens of millions of dollars on weekends.
The Sydney casino plans to open a A$1 billion permanent facility with 1,500 gaming machines and 200 gaming tables.

Qantas Airways Ltd and Ansett Airlines Ltd are planning aggressive cost-cutting programs.
Analysts believe these cost-cutting programs can be implemented without affecting services.
Both airlines are facing profit pressures due to a stronger Australian dollar, higher fuel prices, a soft domestic market, and international competition.
Peter Harbison, managing director of the Centre for Asia Pacific Aviation, stated that Australian airlines are considered high-cost operators compared to global standards.
Qantas announced an increase in its cost-cutting program by about A$100 million for the 1996/97 year, raising the target to A$430 million.
Ansett plans to cut A$150 million from its annual cost base of A$3 billion.
Harbison indicated that airlines, including Qantas and Ansett, will need to continue reducing costs.
Investors are particularly focused on Qantas due to its aggressive cost-cutting measures aimed at meeting profit estimates.
Qantas aims to cut costs across the airline without specifying particular areas.
Analysts suggest that Qantas can reduce costs by outsourcing engineering and maintenance and cutting costs in less visible areas like accounts and marketing.

British Airways Plc (BA) has no plans for new alliances over the next few years.
BA will extend its global reach by franchising its brand name to smaller airlines.
BA has an alliance with Qantas Airways Ltd.
BA formed an alliance with American Airlines in June, subject to regulatory approvals and a legal suit by USAir Group.
BA holds a 24.6 percent stake in USAir Group.
BA chief executive Robert Ayling stated that managing alliances is a challenge.
Ayling quashed reports of a potential alliance with Japan Airlines.
Ayling believes the Japanese airline industry will remain independent.
BA's four-year experiment with franchising its brand name to smaller airlines was successful.
BA signed its first franchise agreement outside of the European Union with Comair, South Africa's largest independent carrier.

Placer Dome Inc agreed to a deal with Highlands Gold Ltd that gives Placer control of the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea.
The deal ends a feud between Placer Dome and Highlands Gold.
Highlands Gold will remain a listed company and can develop base metal and gold projects in Papua New Guinea.
Placer Dome will pay Highlands A$316.1 million to buy Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera mine.
The Porgera mine is estimated to have produced 850,000 ounces of gold in calendar 1996.
Placer Dome previously offered Highlands A$276.8 million for its Porgera stake.
Highlands managing director Ian Goddard expressed satisfaction with the deal.
The restructuring plan involves cancelling all shares in Highlands except those held by Placer.
Highlands shareholders will receive a capital return of 65 cents cash per share and one share in Highlands Pacific.
Highlands will spin off a new company, Highlands Pacific Ltd, which will hold various projects in Papua New Guinea and Indonesia.

Stakis will buy Lonrho Plc's five Metropole hotels for 327 million pounds.
Stakis will fund the acquisition through a rights issue aimed at raising 222 million pounds.
Stakis operates 46 British hotels and 22 casinos.
Stakis's current market value is approximately 472 million pounds.
The rights issue is set at 82 pence per share.
Lonrho will generate net proceeds of 316 million pounds from the sale.
Lonrho will also receive 63 million pounds in dividends and tax relief from the sale.
The sale of Metropole Hotels is part of Lonrho's demerger process.
Lonrho had previously shelved plans for a 700 million pound flotation of its hotels.
Stakis expects the acquisition to boost earnings from the first year.

British Telecom (BT) announced a $20 billion merger with MCI Communications.
The merger with MCI Communications is significant for BT's position in the telecoms market.
BT already holds a 20 percent stake in MCI Communications.
The new entity formed from the merger will be called Concert Plc.
The merger is part of BT's strategy to expand internationally.
The merger occurs as global markets begin to liberalize.

Shares in British Telecommunications (BT) increased significantly on Monday following a $20 billion merger with MCI Communications.
The merger with MCI makes the BT/MCI combination the world's second largest international telephone group with annual revenues exceeding 25 billion pounds ($41 billion).
Analysts believe the merger will compel BT to improve its capital efficiency by increasing its borrowing.
Approximately 82.5 million BT shares were traded in London on Monday, with the stock closing at 373.5 pence, up 22.5 pence from the previous close.
Some analysts suggested buying BT shares up to 400 pence due to positive growth prospects in the telecoms market.
The merger creates the world's fourth largest telecoms group by sales, following NTT, AT&T, and Deutsche Telekom.
The deal allows BT to reduce its reliance on the regulated British telecoms market.
The merger includes a 2.2 billion pound special dividend for BT shareholders.
The merger increases BT's debt-to-equity ratio to 65 percent from under five percent.
Before the merger announcement, BT had a market value of approximately 22.6 billion pounds.

The UK telecoms market is highly competitive.
Analysts believe attempts to block the $20 billion merger between British Telecom and MCI will fail.
The merger's approval depends on the perceived openness of the UK market.
U.S. rules restrict foreign ownership of U.S. firms to 25 percent unless their home market is as competitive as the U.S. market.
If approved, the merger will create Concert Plc, the largest cross-border takeover in history and the second largest international telephone group.
AT&T has requested regulatory scrutiny of the merger between BT and MCI.
Analysts consider AT&T's claims about the competitiveness of the UK market to be unrealistic.
Britain's telecom market is more open than many European countries, which will only abolish state monopolies by January 1, 1998.
The European Commission previously approved BT's acquisition of a 20 percent stake in MCI.
The merger must be approved by the U.S. Department of Justice, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission, and Britain's Department of Trade and Industry.

British Telecommunications reported second quarter and first half profits that exceeded analyst forecasts.
BT's profits before tax, redundancy, and restructuring charges increased by 7.4 percent in the second quarter and 5.2 percent in the first half.
After accounting for redundancy costs of 235 million pounds and a charge of 60 million pounds for repurchasing government-held bonds, BT's half-year pretax profits were 1.6 billion pounds.
BT's pretax profits for the second quarter were 730 million pounds, which was slightly below the figures from 1995.
BT maintained its 20.5 million residential customer lines despite competition from cable companies.
BT's turnover increased by 4.5 percent to 7.37 billion pounds over the six-month period.
BT's inland calls business grew by one percent to over seven percent in the quarter on a 12-month moving average basis.
BT's chief executive, Sir Peter Bonfield, stated that the company is likely losing one to two percentage points of the growing British telecoms market.
Analyst James Ross from ABN AMRO Hoare Govett expects BT to report a full-year pretax profit of 2.1 billion pounds.
BT plans to adopt an aggressive strategy in the next two years as European telecoms markets are expected to open around 1998.

Odyssey Telecommunications is a U.S./Canadian mobile satellite communications group.
Odyssey Telecommunications is seeking $600-$800 million of the $3.2 billion needed to launch 12 satellites.
The joint project involves U.S. aerospace company TRW Inc and Canada's telecoms firm Teleglobe Inc.
Odyssey Telecommunications is one of four main competitors in the satellite communications market.
The company aims to provide voice, fax, and paging services globally using pocket telephones.
Odyssey Telecommunications International (OTI) has received letters of intent that are non-binding until financing is secured.
The launch of the satellites has been delayed by approximately three years.
The first round of financing is expected to be completed in three to four months.
The worldwide market for personal satellite telephones is estimated to be worth $12 billion in annual revenues by 2004.
Main competitors in the hand-held satphone market include Iridium, Loral Corp's Globalstar, Qualcomm, and ICO Global.

Telefonica de Espana is the leading telephone group in the Spanish speaking world.
Juan Villalonga Navarro is Telefonica's chairman and chief executive.
Telefonica serves a market of more than 300 million customers mainly in Spain and South America.
Telefonica faces its first home competitor, Retevision SA, next year.
The Spanish government plans to float the last 21 percent tranche of Telefonica early next year.
A third telecommunications licence will be awarded in early 1998.
Spain's mobile telephone market is growing faster than any in Europe.
In four years, mobile telephone penetration in Spain is expected to rise from seven to 27 percent.
Telefonica plans to reduce its workforce in Spain by 11,000 over the next four to five years.
Analysts have described Telefonica as one of the best stocks in Spain and strategically positioned in Europe.

Intel Corp launched its new Pentium chip with multimedia extension (MMX) technology on Wednesday.
The new MMX technology promises TV-quality video, stereo surround sound, and three-dimensional graphics for personal computers.
Intel has collaborated with more than 100 software developers to create programs for the new Pentium processors with MMX technology.
Intel's shares rose to record levels prior to the launch of the MMX technology.
Intel shares increased by four dollars to $143-3/8 on Tuesday but were down slightly in early Wednesday trade.
Ian Wilson, Intel's European technology director, stated that new multimedia software using MMX technology runs up to 60 percent faster than on previous Pentium processors.
Existing software runs up to 10-20 percent faster on the new MMX technology.
Intel expects the new technology to boost computer sales and become an industry standard.
The MMX chip will initially be offered with the 166 and 200 MHz Pentium processors.
A variety of computer manufacturers, including IBM, Compaq, Hewlett-Packard, Olivetti, and Toshiba, are offering the Pentium MMX processor.

Energis is a British telecommunications company.
Energis's parent company is the National Grid electricity transmission network.
The National Grid may sell a majority stake in Energis to strategic investors this summer.
Energis supplies telecom services to approximately 14,000 business customers.
Energis is preparing to announce a deal that will reduce the cost of European telephone calls.
Mike Grabiner is the chief executive of Energis.
Energis has engaged in discussions with all global carriers except BT for international partnerships.
Energis is seeking access to key metropolitan areas following the formation of Cable and Wireless Communications.
Grabiner indicated that the Grid might initially sell a minority stake in Energis.
Energis has been incurring losses of 100 million pounds per year.

NTT is considering an investment with British Telecommunications (BT) in France.
Analysts believe that such a deal would benefit BT significantly.
Nippon Telegraph and Telephone is the world's largest telecoms company.
NTT has approached multiple investment banks to assess an investment with BT in the French telecoms market.
BT is exploring options to enhance its investment in Cegetel, a new telecoms operator in France.
Cegetel is viewed as a primary competitor to France Telecom.
NTT's interest in the French market is focused on access to international traffic.
BT has been pursuing a partnership with NTT for several years.
NTT was recently authorized by the Japanese government to pursue international business.
Andrew Harrington, a telecoms analyst, stated that a partnership with NTT would be a significant advantage for BT.

Misys is a software supply company based in Britain with a valuation of 950 million pounds.
Misys is considering four or five international acquisition targets, each worth up to $30 million.
Chairman Kevin Lomax stated that Misys has previously acquired software trading firms in South East Asia, Ireland, the U.S., and Europe.
Misys is interested in businesses that operate within a strong international financial services market.
The company has 18.7 million pounds in cash and a low gearing level, providing it with cash flow and borrowing capacity for acquisitions.
Misys reported a 23 percent increase in pretax profits to 23.7 million pounds on revenues of 129.5 million pounds, which is a 10 percent rise.
Lomax believes that acquiring regional software companies could create significant shareholder value, especially in the banking industry.
Misys's banking division supplies software to 12,000 banks and has 4,000 installations.
The company's shares have nearly doubled in the last 12 months, rising from 567 pence to 1115 pence.
Misys announced a planned $60 million acquisition of Summit Systems, a New York company specializing in financial derivatives trading software.

British households are expected to pay less for water and receive better service from privatised utility companies in the next decade.
Ian Byatt is the industry regulator for water services in the UK.
Byatt expects privatised water companies to pass on efficiency savings to customers in 2000.
Byatt warned water companies that lower costs should lead to falling bills.
The price review for water services will be completed in December 1999.
New price curbs will be imposed on 29 water and sewerage companies in England and Wales starting April 1, 2000.
The Water Services Association stated that lower bills depend on new quality and environmental obligations set by Europe and Britain.
The Ofwat National Customer Council is urging Byatt to take strong action to reduce water bills.
Clive Wilkinson, deputy chairman of the Ofwat National Customer Council, criticized water companies for prioritizing shareholder profits over customer satisfaction.
Water groups have been the only utilities to raise prices since privatisation in 1989.

Sema Group is an Anglo-French information technology group.
Sema Group plans to focus on growth from its telecoms and business systems operations in 1997.
Marie-Claude Bessis is the director of communications for Sema Group.
Sema Group is seeking to expand into Germany and the U.S.
Sema Group aims to maintain robust organic growth in the financial year of 1997.
1997 will be a year of integration for Sema Group, not a year of acquisitions.
Sema Group has signed agreements with Global One and AT&T.
Sema Group is developing value-added services and two-way messaging for AT&T's wireless arm.
Sema Group raised 99 million stg through its first rights issue for acquisitions and growth last year.
Sema Group has 18 million stg of cash and no gearing.

Most software publishers are expected to report modest increases in their latest earnings.
The modest increases reflect a seasonal slowdown and a lack of new products this quarter.
Marshall Senk is an analyst at Robertson Stephens & Co. in San Francisco.
Senk stated that business is still good for large companies like Microsoft and Oracle.
Summer is considered the slow buying season for most of the software industry.
Analysts expect Microsoft to report substantially higher earnings for its first fiscal 1997 quarter.
Microsoft's expected earnings are attributed to strong sales of its networking software and business programs.
Microsoft is scheduled to report its results on October 21.
Better-than-expected sales of personal computers will contribute to Microsoft's revenue.
Microsoft makes about a quarter of its revenue from the sale of its Windows family of operating systems.

Apple Computer Inc. reported a profit of $25 million for its fiscal fourth quarter.
The profit of $25 million defied Wall Street's expectations for a loss.
Analysts noted a 23 percent drop in revenue for the quarter, which could impact Apple's future prospects.
Analysts expressed concerns that sluggish revenues might lead to reduced spending on research and development.
Kurt King, an analyst at Montgomery Securities, stated that Apple has never experienced such a significant sales drop before.
Apple's profit of 20 cents a share was attributed to cost cutting, lower memory chip prices, and a one-time gain of $17 million.
In the same quarter of the previous year, Apple earned $60 million, or 48 cents a share.
Apple's revenues fell from $3 billion to $2.32 billion.
Apple has lost customers to competitors such as Compaq, Dell, and Hewlett-Packard.
Gilbert Amelio, hired to revive Apple, has cut costs but has not increased sales.

Apple Computer Inc. is developing a modified version of its handheld Newton organizer into a portable computer for students.
The Apple eMate 300 will be unveiled on Monday and will cost $800.
The eMate 300 features a keyboard, a flip-up screen, and a rugged casing.
Apple plans to sell the eMate 300 directly to elementary and high schools starting early next year.
Three eMates can be purchased for the price of one $2,500 multimedia PC.
Jim Groff, general manager of Apple's information appliances group, stated that the federal government aims for a three-to-one student-to-computer ratio by the year 2000.
Analysts believe the eMate could help Apple maintain its position as a leading supplier of classroom computers.
Mike McGuire, a mobile computing analyst at Dataquest Inc., noted the potential of the eMate in classroom settings.
Apple's educational sales remain strong, but sales of IBM-compatible PCs are growing faster.
For the 1996-1997 school year, 56 percent of planned computer purchases by schools are Apple Macintoshs and 40 percent are IBM-compatible machines.

Apple Computer Inc. announced a price cut of up to 30 percent on its Power Macintosh personal computers.
The price cuts aim to make Apple's machines more competitive with Wintel PCs.
Apple will reduce the price of the Power Macintosh 9500/200 from $4,900 to about $4,200.
The entry-level Power Macintosh 7200/120 will see its price reduced from $2,300 to about $1,600.
The price reductions will be effective on November 2.
The price cuts range from 9 percent to 30 percent.
Apple has reduced its costs significantly due to a restructuring effort that began nine months ago.
Apple's computers have historically been priced higher than similar PCs from companies like IBM and Compaq.
Apple reported over $800 million in losses in the past year amid declining sales.
Analysts believe the price cuts may help Apple gain momentum and attract more customers.

Intuit Inc. shares increased by 24 percent on Wednesday.
Market speculation suggests that American Express Co. may acquire Intuit Inc.
Intuit's shares closed at $36.50 on Nasdaq after a surge of $7.
American Express shares rose to $48.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Officials from both Intuit and American Express declined to comment on the rumors.
An Intuit spokeswoman described the acquisition speculation as 'wild.'
Analysts believe American Express may be interested in acquiring Intuit to enter the online banking industry.
Intuit may be open to an acquisition offer due to concerns about its future.
Over 9 million users, primarily affluent individuals, use Intuit's Quicken software for financial management.
Intuit's growth has stalled due to competition from Microsoft Corp. and banks offering online banking.

Apple Computer Inc. plans to work with a restaurant operator to open cybercafes in the United States and Europe starting late next year.
Apple licensed its name and logo to London-based Mega Bytes International BVI.
Mega Bytes International BVI is a developer of theme parks.
Mega Bytes will develop a chain of eateries where patrons can surf the Internet, play games, and eat.
Apple stated that the restaurants are part of its plan to spread its brand into the everyday world.
The first restaurant is slated to open in Los Angeles in late 1997.
The restaurant will feature Apple's computers at every table.
Customers will have high-speed access to the World Wide Web, check out CD-ROM titles, and send e-mail.
Restaurants in London, Paris, New York, Tokyo, and other cities will follow.
Apple will only make money from the licensing agreement, and the terms of the agreement were not disclosed.

At this year's Comdex computer trade show, corporate computer buyers are the most sought-after individuals.
Personal computer makers and software vendors are relying on corporate customers due to disappointing consumer sales.
Many consumers are delaying computer purchases until early 1997 when new gadgets are expected to be released.
Corporate customers are purchasing new machines to replace older PCs that can run the latest business software from Microsoft.
Michael Winkler, senior vice president at Compaq Computer Corp., stated that a major upgrade cycle is occurring.
The release of Microsoft's Windows NT operating system and Office 97 is driving corporate sales.
Domestic PC shipments in the fourth quarter are expected to rise 20 percent to 8 million units, according to International Data Corp.
Jim McDonnell, a group marketing manager of PCs at Hewlett-Packard Co., indicated a strong outlook for 1997.
Stocks of most PC makers have increased recently, with Compaq, IBM, Intel, and Sun Microsystems seeing gains.
The fourth quarter has been disappointing for some PC makers focused on consumer sales.

Apple Computer Inc. fired co-founder Steven Jobs in 1985.
Jobs inspired Apple engineers to create the Macintosh computer.
Jobs' temper caused burnout among some engineers at Apple.
Apple rehired Jobs more than 11 years after his ousting.
Jobs' assignment is to revamp the software behind the Macintosh.
Apple's software revamp effort had been stalled for three years.
Apple hopes Jobs can inspire programmers to compete with Microsoft Corp's Windows operating system.
Apple's shares rose $1.25 or 5.6 percent to $23.50 after the news of Jobs' rehiring.
Apple agreed to acquire NeXT Software Inc. for $400 million.
NeXT Software Inc. offers an operating system that Apple needs to catch up with Microsoft.

Apple Computer Inc. Chairman Gilbert Amelio will outline a plan to revamp the Macintosh personal computer.
Apple acquired Next Software Inc. to assist in the revamp of the Macintosh.
Apple and other vendors will unveil new products at the Macworld trade show next week.
Analysts predict that the Macworld show will be more positive than last year's show.
In 1996, Apple's management under Amelio stopped significant financial losses.
Bob Roblin, senior vice president of marketing at Adobe Systems Inc., expressed satisfaction with Apple's decisions regarding the Mac.
Apple agreed to pay $400 million for Next, a company run by co-founder Steven Jobs.
Apple plans to integrate Next's operating system with the Mac operating system.
Macintosh programmers and executives require more technical details to develop new products.
Adobe will announce the latest version of PageMaker at the Macworld show.

Macromedia Inc. shares fell to a two-year low on Friday.
The decline followed the company's report of an unexpected third-quarter loss.
Macromedia indicated it could face weak sales for another quarter.
Analysts expressed concern that Apple Computer Inc.'s declining sales could negatively impact Macromedia's revenue from Macintosh software.
Shares of Macromedia dropped $4.19, or 31 percent, to $9.31 in Nasdaq trading.
This price is the lowest since December 1994.
Macromedia reported a loss of $2.36 million, or 6 cents a share, for its fiscal third quarter ended December 31.
This loss contrasts with a net income of $7.15 million, or 18 cents a share, in the same quarter the previous year.
Third-quarter revenue decreased by 9 percent to $28.1 million from $30.9 million.
Wall Street analysts expected Macromedia to report a net income of 14 cents a share.

Synopsys Inc. agreed to buy Epic Design Technology Inc. for about $428.1 million in stock.
The acquisition aims to gain expertise in the semiconductor design business.
Synopsys will issue 0.7485 of its shares for each of Epic's 13.7 million shares outstanding.
Based on Synopsys's closing stock price of $41.75, the payment for each Epic share is about $31.25.
Shares of Epic fell 87.5 cents to $31 in late Nasdaq trading.
Shares of Synopsys remained unchanged at $41.75 on Nasdaq.
Synopsys specializes in software for designing the overall framework of a microchip.
Epic specializes in software for designing individual microscopic circuits.
The acquisition is expected to give Synopsys an edge in the design automation industry.
Epic will become a unit of Synopsys, with Sang Wang as the head of the unit.

Informix Corp. filed a lawsuit against Oracle Corp. on Friday.
Informix accuses Oracle of stealing trade secrets by hiring its employees.
Oracle hired 11 employees from Informix's Portland, Oregon, research and development center.
All 11 employees quit Informix on Wednesday morning.
Informix's Chief Executive is Phil White.
Informix's stock fell by $1.50, or 6.6 percent, to $21.375 on Nasdaq.
Oracle's stock fell by 87.5 cents to $39.625 on Nasdaq.
Oracle officials described the lawsuit as 'ridiculous'.
The lawsuit seeks unspecified damages and was filed in Oregon Circuit Court in Portland.
Informix obtained a temporary injunction to prevent former employees from sharing trade secrets with Oracle.

Lower profits from base metals producers are negatively impacting corporate earnings for Canadian companies in the third quarter.
Richardson Greenshields of Canada analyst Dunnery Best forecasts significant declines in earnings for major base metal firms.
Best expects Alcan Aluminium Ltd's third-quarter earnings to decrease to US$0.35 a share from US$0.61 a share from the previous year.
Griffiths McBurney analyst Greg Misztela expressed concerns that the metal group may not report expected earnings numbers.
Best indicated that companies such as Inco Ltd, Noranda Inc, and Falconbridge Ltd are likely to see earnings declines.
Teck Corp is expected to be an exception due to its strong coal production.
Metal stock prices have declined following disappointing second-quarter earnings due to falling copper, nickel, and other prices.
Analysts predict that Canada's major banks will report significant earnings gains in the fourth quarter ending October 31.
The six major banks, including Royal Bank of Canada and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, have achieved record profits in recent years.
Richardson Greenshields has raised earnings estimates for Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce six times this year.

Toronto stocks ended mixed on Tuesday.
The market gained nearly 300 points in August.
Ron Meisels, President of P and C Holdings, stated that the market is giving back some of its gains.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index lost 12.8 points to close at 5173.9 points.
The key 300 index has experienced two consecutive losing sessions.
Advancing issues outnumbered declining ones 444 to 438.
310 stocks ended unchanged.
More than 88 million shares were traded, worth C$1.42 billion.
Since July 30, the key 300 index has increased from 4891 points to 5173 points.
Canadian markets will be closed on Monday, September 2, for Labor Day.

Toronto stocks increased by almost one percent on Tuesday.
This marked the 52nd record close of 1996.
The increase was attributed to rallying bank stocks and stronger bond and currency markets.
The Canadian dollar closed at C$1.3301 (US$0.7518), its strongest level since October 30, 1995.
The Canadian 30-year benchmark bond closed around C$114.55, yielding 6.807 percent.
The TSE gained 55.21 points to close at 5664.47.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 39.50 points to end at 6081.18.
Toronto traded a total of 105 million shares worth C$1.83 billion (US$1.37 billion).
Advancing issues outnumbered declines 505 to 445, with 300 stocks unchanged.
The financial services sector rose by 2.8 percent, leading 12 of Toronto's 14 sub-indices higher.

The Toronto Stock Exchange will change rules governing control blocks in its key 300 Composite Index on Friday.
Analysts believe that Barrick Gold Corp, Loewen Group Inc, and Petro-Canada will benefit from the rule changes.
Index funds will need to buy more shares of Barrick Gold Corp due to the changes in the index rules.
The Toronto Stock Exchange handles more than 80 percent of Canada's equity trading.
The relative weighting of 30 stocks will increase from 15 percent to 20 percent on Friday.
Relative weighting indicates the impact a stock has on the overall TSE 300 Composite Index.
A control block is defined as a group of shares owned by a single entity and is not included in a stock's weighting.
Petro-Canada's weighting will rise to 1.22 percent from about 1.03 percent due to the inclusion of the federal government's 18.26 percent holding.
The TSE is changing the definition of a control block to comply with Ontario Securities Commission reporting rules.
Barrick Gold Corp's weighting will increase to 3.28 percent from 2.84 percent as it will now be weighted based on 100 percent of its shares.

Heavily weighted bank stocks contributed to a stronger closing for the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday.
The TSE's key 300 composite index gained 34.61 points, ending at 5952.41.
Turnover on the TSE was 94.1 million shares worth C$1.4 billion (US$1.04 billion).
Declining issues outnumbered advancing ones 486 to 473, with another 288 shares trading flat.
Bank stocks are expected to perform well ahead of year-end results, starting with Bank of Montreal earnings on Tuesday.
Canada's big six banks are forecast to report record profits for the third consecutive year.
Analysts consider Canadian bank stocks to be undervalued compared to U.S. bank stocks.
The bank sector led eight of Toronto's 14 sub-indices higher, gaining nearly 3.3 percent.
The Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce rose C$2.25 to C$59.60 on 640,000 shares.
The Royal Bank of Canada gained C$2.10 to C$48.75 on more than one million shares.

Toronto stocks ended lower on Monday due to a decline in the gold sector.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index fell 31.70 points to 5984.97.
Trading volume was 92.6 million shares, valued at C$1.6 billion (US$1.2 billion).
The gold sector lost more than 2.5 percent after bullion prices decreased in New York.
February COMEX gold closed US$4.10 lower at US$370.90 an ounce.
RBC Dominion Securities strategist Dunnery Best stated that the gold index is adjusting after recent gains.
The TSE's 300 index has increased approximately 27 percent since the beginning of the year.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-indices finished lower, with golds and financial services leading the decline.
Falling stocks outnumbered advancing stocks 596 to 380, with 277 stocks trading flat.
Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd. were volatile ahead of a potential partnership with Barrick Gold Corp.

Toronto stocks closed higher on Tuesday.
The increase was driven by strength in the resource sectors.
Canadian gold stocks contributed significantly to the rise in Canadian stock prices.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index increased by 33.32 points to reach 5150.89 points.
The key index has risen from its July lows to levels not seen since early June.
The all-time high for Toronto's key index was 5248 points on May 28, 1986.
Market players are currently investing in resource stocks.
Trading volume reached 87.98 million shares valued at C$1.25 billion.
There is speculation about whether the Bank of Canada will ease short-term interest rates.
Gold stocks led all of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, gaining 1.38 percent.

Analysts forecast that the rally on the Toronto Stock Exchange will stretch through 1997 and may last until the turn of the century.
Michael Metz is the chief investment strategist with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc. in New York.
Michael Metz stated that the Toronto Stock Exchange is in the middle of a bull market.
Toronto's key 300 Composite Index jumped as much as 28 percent in 1996.
The 300 Composite Index was up 21 percent after a correction in December.
The Dow Jones industrial average was up 23 percent this year, down from a peak of 26 percent.
Toronto's market is the 10th most active worldwide.
Bond yields have dropped across the board this year, with 50 basis points shaved off the return of Canada's 30-year benchmark bonds.
Most of the seven analysts polled by Reuters predicted that Toronto's 300 index would break its all-time high of 6,018 points next year.
The index was at about 5,700 on a recent Friday.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key index closed at 6103.66 on Thursday.
The TSE 300 Composite Index increased by 38.32 points.
The index reached an intra-day high of 6112.32.
Toronto set records for the third time this year.
Stronger gold stocks contributed to the index's rise.
Ron Meisels stated that investors were interested in cheap gold issues.
Bullion prices weakened after the Dutch central bank sold 300 tonnes of gold reserves.
Trading volume was 121.9 million shares worth C$2.09 billion.
Most of Toronto's 14 sub-indices rose, except for four.
Gold stocks led the gains, followed by oils, banks, and consumer products.

The chief executive of Zellers aims to boost sales per square foot by more than a third over three years.
Millard Barron is the chief executive of Zellers and a former executive at Wal-Mart Inc.
Barron plans to increase sales from C$157 ($117) a square foot for fiscal 1997.
Barron stated that Zellers should achieve sales of C$225 ($168) to C$250 ($187) a square foot.
Zellers is a unit of Toronto-based Hudson's Bay Co.
David Brodie, a Wood Gundy retail analyst, called Barron's goal ambitious.
Brodie estimated that Wal-Mart had sales of C$220 ($164) a square foot in Canada.
Brodie estimated Zellers' market share had fallen to 42 percent since Wal-Mart's arrival in 1994.
Wal-Mart's Canadian market share was estimated at about 43 percent.
Zellers' fiscal 1996 operating profit was C$106.7 million ($79.8 million), down from C$215.6 million ($161.2 million) in 1995.

Toronto stocks ended mixed on Monday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 7.18 points to 6040.76.
Turnover on the Toronto Stock Exchange was 87 million shares worth C$1.29 billion.
Declining issues outnumbered advancing ones 510 to 460.
Another 296 issues ended flat.
Fred Ketchen, senior vice-president at ScotiaMcLeod, stated that stocks performed well due to strength in the gold sector.
Trading was thin ahead of the U.S. fourth quarter Employment Cost Index.
Alan Greenspan, U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman, expressed concern over rising wages last week.
Toronto's 14 sub-indices were evenly split.
The precious metals sector gained 1.6 percent.

The Toronto stock market achieved its sixth record close of the year on Tuesday.
The Toronto 300 Composite Index rose 4.48 points to close at 6145.41.
The turnover was 115.4 million shares worth C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion).
Investors purchased banks and financial service stocks in anticipation of unchanged short-term interest rates from the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee.
Ira Katzin, an investment advisor at RBC Dominion Securities, stated that the financial services sector was the most exciting group.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declining stocks 506 to 464, with 303 issues remaining unchanged.
The banks led the market with a 1.8 percent gain, followed by pipelines and utilities.
The TSE had eight weak sectors, including media, golds, and oils.
The Bank of Montreal's stock rose 1.15 to finish at 48.85 on more than two million shares.
Bank of Nova Scotia's stock gained 1.40 to close at 50 on 491,000 shares.

Toronto's stock market closed lower on Monday.
The 300 Composite Index fell 20.47 points to end at 6081.27.
Trading volume was 93.9 million shares worth C$1.4 billion.
The oil and gas sector declined by almost 2.4 percent.
Eight of Toronto's 14 sub-indices fell.
Falling sectors included conglomerates, transportation, and golds.
Consumer products, banks, and pipelines were among the sectors that gained.
Canadian 88 Energy Corp. withdrew its hostile bid for Morrison Petroleum Ltd.
Declines outnumbered advances 456 to 362.
Morrison shares fell to 9.65, Canadian 88 shares fell to 5.15, and Poco Petroleums Ltd. shares fell to 13.75.

China is not expected to be in the international market for sugar before mid-1997 due to high stocks and recovering domestic prices.
A lack of cash among state-run sugar processors could affect farmers' willingness to grow sugar cane.
China had up to two million tonnes of processed sugar in reserve after imports in 1995.
The actual figure of China's sugar reserves is considered a state secret.
China's sugar demand has not significantly increased over recent years.
China's economy in 1996 has not been strong, affecting sugar consumption.
Sugar is not considered an essential item in China.
The bulk of the Chinese sugar market is industrial.
Central authorities are expected to maintain tight control over the sugar industry.
A crackdown on smuggling has brought some control back to the sugar industry.

Asian traders reacted to reports that China had bought hundreds of thousands of tonnes of soybean oil.
Chinese authorities issued import licences for only a little over 100,000 tonnes of soybean oil.
Traders in Shanghai stated that those with import quotas were not in a hurry to import soybean oil due to high c&f prices.
A Chinese trader in Hong Kong noted that high domestic stocks and a near-record domestic rapeseed crop reduced demand for imported vegetable oil.
Rumours circulated on the Chicago Board of Trade that China may have purchased 173,000 to 200,000 tonnes of South American soybean oil recently.
Argentine soybean oil was trading at US$500 a tonne FOB for October delivery, while U.S. soybean oil was priced at $510 a tonne.
Asian traders indicated that current prices were $40 above what Chinese buyers would be willing to pay.
An official from COFCO stated that China had not issued new soybean oil quotas or import licences for 1996.
Quotas for 1995 expired at the end of June, and palm oil import quotas were issued in July.
Traders suggested that China might enter the vegetable oil market late in 1996 or early in 1997 to prepare for Chinese New Year.

China has banned imports of poultry from 10 U.S. states.
The ban threatens an export market worth about $500 million a year.
Chinese authorities fear that the poultry products carry highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI).
The affected U.S. states are Arkansas, Florida, Maryland, Utah, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Texas, and Wisconsin.
HPAI has not been found in the U.S. since 1984.
There is confusion among Chinese quarantine officials regarding HPAI and avian influenza (AI).
The AI virus can be found worldwide, particularly in wild fowl.
The AI virus has not been isolated from commercial poultry flocks in the United States.
The AI virus may have been detected in ostriches imported from the United States to China.
China is the second biggest market for U.S. poultry products, after Russia.

Chinese buyers of soybeans and soybean meal are defaulting or canceling contracts due to falling international prices.
A trader in Hong Kong stated that they have stopped doing business with Chinese buyers for now.
Traders in Hong Kong, Singapore, and China reported that Chinese soymeal buyers are delaying finance arrangements to negotiate lower prices.
Chinese buyers have defaulted on three to four cargoes of soymeal, each weighing 50,000 tonnes, since last week.
Chinese buyers are delaying opening letters of credit in hopes of reducing prices by two or three dollars.
Traders indicated that physical soymeal for prompt delivery is in tight supply and commands a premium.
Chinese traders have developed a reputation for dubious payment practices since entering international trading.
Some Chinese buyers cancel orders if prices fall after the order is placed, attempting to replace the commodity at a lower price.
Soybean meal has been a significant commodity for China in 1996, with 1.2 million tonnes arriving from South America since February.
Maximum Chinese orders of U.S. soybean meal in the past two weeks were 300,000 tonnes.

Chile is the world's biggest copper exporter.
China is the world's biggest copper importer.
Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Mariano Fernandez stated that Chile hopes to establish close trade and technical support ties with China.
Fernandez mentioned that there is Chinese interest in participating in mining projects in Chile.
Chile has an interest in providing services and technology for copper mining in China.
In 1995, Chile's total mining exports were worth US$7.85 billion, with $280 million earned from copper sales to China.
Chile is projected to produce almost one-third of the world's total copper in five years.
Chile has 25 percent of the world's copper reserves and mined 2.512 million tonnes of copper in 1995.
China's demand for copper in 1996 was officially estimated at one million tonnes.
China's copper imports for 1996 were expected to be 200,000 tonnes.

Chinese and U.S. scientists are making progress in discussions regarding China's ban on poultry imports from the United States.
The Chinese government banned all imports of poultry and poultry products from 10 U.S. states due to concerns about highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI).
The ban has not yet been implemented as China is awaiting input from U.S. experts.
The poultry export market affected by the ban is valued at approximately US$500 million annually.
Meetings between Washington's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) and China's Administration of Animal and Plant Quarantine (CAPQ) have been described as frank and positive.
Two APHIS experts arrived in Beijing to address the issue and will remain until a resolution is found.
There is no set timetable for the discussions, as the U.S. is committed to providing comprehensive information to the Chinese.
Meetings are scheduled to continue on Thursday and possibly Friday.
APHIS experts and U.S. officials assert that HPAI is not present in commercial flocks in the United States.
U.S. sources indicate that Chinese officials may have confused HPAI with less-virulent avian influenza (AI).

International trading companies are opposing a contractual stipulation by Chinese traders that allows for the reinspection and rejection of some cargoes arriving in China.
A Singapore grain trader stated that there is no reason for trading companies to accept these terms.
Chinese companies involved in the new contracts did not comment on reports regarding the reinspection rights for soybean and soybean meal cargoes.
The new terms permit Chinese buyers to inspect cargo upon arrival at a Chinese port, despite prior inspection before departure.
The stated purpose of the terms is to protect buyers from quarantinable pests or diseases in the cargo.
Traders expressed concern that the new terms could increase their risk if buyers use them to back out of deals as prices decline.
Traders surveyed by Reuters reported that their companies are refusing to accept the new contracts.
China has purchased between 1.5 million and two million tonnes of soybeans and soybean meal in the past three months.
Much of the purchased cargo is expected to arrive in China before the end of the year.
Soybean prices have significantly decreased since China's October 1 National Day holiday.

Canadian and Australian sales of malting barley to China may be limited by weather and disease issues.
Early snow in Canada damaged the barley crop, affecting the quality of grain available for export.
Sales of higher quality malting barley from Canada to China are expected to remain below 300,000 tonnes.
Canada has already sold close to 300,000 tonnes of malting barley to China in the current marketing year.
The Canadian marketing source stated that it would be lucky to reach 300,000 tonnes in sales to China.
Australian farmers have preferred disease-resistant strains of feed barley this year.
Frost in Victoria and South Australia may reduce the availability of malting barley by 100,000 tonnes.
The Australian Barley Board expects to have 400,000 tonnes of malting barley available for domestic sale and export.
The Australian Barley Board hopes to export 300,000 to 350,000 tonnes of malting barley to China.
Australia's total barley crop is estimated to be around 6.03 million tonnes, an increase from last year's 5.5 million tonnes.

Copper stored in Shanghai warehouses is being offered in small lots to European trading houses.
The copper is being offered for sale at a high premium to set a benchmark price for its eventual sale to China's strategic stockpile.
Estimates of copper reserves brought into China in recent months range between 100,000 and 150,000 tonnes.
A European trader in Beijing was offered copper by the China National Non-ferrous Metals Import and Export Corp (CNIEC) at around $2,100 a tonne.
The price of $2,100 a tonne reflects the London Metal Exchange (LME) cash price plus a premium of $130.
CNIEC has declined to comment on market talk regarding the copper.
The copper is said to be owned by Chinese trading firms that shipped it to Shanghai in anticipation of a purchase by the central stockpile.
Traders indicated that the copper likely belonged to China's state reserve, which lent around 85,000 tonnes of copper through CNIEC onto the LME between April and June 1995.
CNIEC's former president Fang Dachang stated that China was likely to take back the copper in the fourth quarter of the year.
The metal was taken from LME warehouses at about $2,400 a tonne before LME copper prices fell below $1,800.

China has up to a million tonnes of corn rotting in silos in the country's north.
Traders estimate that 500,000 to one million tonnes of corn is stored in northern silos in anticipation of exports.
Corn is grown predominantly in China's far northeastern provinces of Heilongjiang, Jilin, and Liaoning.
Corn began moving to northern ports, particularly Dalian, around May.
Traders had anticipated that two million tonnes of corn would be permissioned for export.
Concerns about national food security and domestic prices have kept China out of the world corn market.
Corn and rice exports were banned in December 1994 after stocks fell to low levels.
China imported 5.18 million tonnes of corn in 1995.
Corn imports in the first five months of 1996 totaled 400,000 tonnes.
Traders expected China's central grain authorities to allow corn exports to take advantage of high world prices.

China has banned poultry imports from Oklahoma and Missouri.
The ban was implemented to prevent a deadly epidemic.
The ban took effect on Monday.
China's Ministry of Agriculture confirmed the ban.
The ban was imposed due to five cases of a deadly poultry flu discovered between July and September.
Phillip Holloway is a representative for the Oklahoma state agriculture department.
Holloway stated that Chinese authorities are sensitive to disease profiles.
The virus involved is known as viscerotropic velogenic Newcastle disease (VVND).
VVND is considered a very dangerous disease for poultry.
Holloway noted that he had not heard of recent VVND cases in Oklahoma.

China's zinc industry is facing challenges due to the withdrawal of government subsidies.
Tight credit, expensive infrastructure, and over-manned mines and smelters are contributing to the industry's struggles.
Chinese zinc exports have slowed as sellers are unwilling to lower prices to world levels.
Chinese sellers are asking for high premiums, specifically LME plus US$70 to Hong Kong and Taiwan.
Three month LME zinc was quoted at $1,036/$1,038 a tonne in early trade on Monday.
Many Asian customers have stock to consume before purchasing from China.
China is not importing much zinc due to a 10 percent import duty and a 17 percent value-added tax.
China's exports of unwrought zinc and zinc alloys dropped to 117,293 tonnes in the first seven months of 1996.
The January-May export figure of 86,494 tonnes was down 25.5 percent compared to the same period in 1995.
China's zinc consumption is growing at about eight percent, while zinc output has risen faster than consumption.

Russia is expected to have a second consecutive bad grain harvest.
Russia will need grain imports despite a prediction by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin that output will meet demand.
Andrei Sizov of SovEcon Ltd. stated that the volume of grain produced in Russia will meet demand, but the quality will not.
Chernomyrdin forecasted a 1996 grain output of 77-78 million metric tons, which is higher than last year's 63.4 million tons.
Chernomyrdin claimed that the grain output would provide the population with bread and bread products until the 1997 harvest.
Georgy Zelinsky of Khleboproduktprogress indicated a shortage of first-class wheat in Russia.
Sizov predicted that Russian imports of grain and flour would rise to 5.0-6.0 million tons in the 1996/1997 crop year.
Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun stated that Russia may import up to 4.5 million tons of corn and soymeal, plus 500,000 tons of wheat from the United States, Canada, and/or Australia.
Zelinsky noted that domestic feed corn was in short supply, but corn for human consumption was not.
Industry sources indicated that Russia would likely buy grain in small lots rather than making large purchases.

Russia's Fuel and Energy Ministry is known as Mintopenergo.
Mintopenergo previously had significant control over the oil sector, including the ability to command drilling and restrict exports.
The ministry's influence has diminished as power has shifted to privately owned, vertically integrated oil firms.
Pyotr Rodionov is the current minister of Mintopenergo.
Oil companies believe the ministry could act as a lobby for their interests in the Kremlin.
Alexei Gorshkov is a spokesman for YUKOS, Russia's second largest oil company by reserves.
Mintopenergo lost responsibility for Gazprom when it was renamed in 1991.
Many oil specialists have left Mintopenergo for jobs in investment banks and oil firms.
Former minister Yuri Shafranik left to lead the board of the Tyumen Oil Company.
Matthew Sagers of PlanEcon stated that the ministry will not be as important as it once was.

Russia has significant gold reserves but is unlikely to develop them into a major market soon.
