Russia's Central Bank plans to create a domestic gold market to encourage commercial banks to finance mining.
Industry sources believe the new rules will not significantly reform Russia's gold production sector.
Tony Warwick-Ching, an analyst at CRU International, stated that it will take time for commercial banks to engage in the gold market.
The Central Bank's new rules allow limited domestic trading of gold and gold-backed loans through special accounts.
Yuri Kotlyar, acting chairman of the State Committee for Precious Metals and Stones, expressed that the new accounting procedures do not create an actual market.
Russian gold mines are required to sell their output to the state at fixed prices, often with delayed payments.
Russia's government is facing a budget crisis and has less money to finance gold production in 1996 compared to 1995.
Commercial banks financed only five tonnes of gold output in the previous year.
Moscow is hesitant to allow banks to export gold for financing due to concerns about losing control over the gold industry.

Russia's second-generation foreign oil projects require close ties to top government figures.
Western oil companies need strong Kremlin relationships and negotiating skills to access Arctic reserves.
Moscow has adopted a tougher attitude toward Western participation in oil production-sharing deals.
Support from President Boris Yeltsin is crucial for the oil sector's transformation.
Budgets may need to be redone after negotiations with demanding Russian partners.
Amoco Corp and YUKOS are engaged in complex negotiations regarding YUKOS shareholder Bank Menatep.
Menatep owns a 33 percent stake in YUKOS and controls an additional 45 percent stake formally owned by the government.
Amoco and YUKOS plan to invest approximately $50 billion to develop the Priobsk oil field in Siberia.
Russia's first-generation foreign oil deals favored Western partners with leading equity stakes.
Moscow officials now believe Russia should have at least equal status in oil deals.

Almazy- Rossii Sakha (ARS) is a Russian diamond company.
ARS president Vyacheslav Shtyrov stated that officials are competing for control over Russia's gem sector.
A trade agreement between ARS and De Beers could be signed by December.
Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin may delay signing the deal until next month due to a government investigation into ARS's finances.
The investigation into ARS's finances is believed to be part of maneuvers among government officials for influence over the company.
ARS supplies a quarter of De Beers' output and is Russia's sole authorized diamond exporter.
Under the proposed trade agreement, ARS would have the right to export $180 million of gems annually independent of De Beers.
This amount represents 5.8 percent of ARS's $1.38 billion in sales from the previous year.
The investigation into ARS follows allegations of unpaid taxes and breaches of hard currency regulations, with potential fines totaling $379 million.
Mikhail Nikolayev, president of the Sakha-Yakutia region, stated that ARS has no tax arrears to the federal budget.

Russia's demand for feed grains will exceed any output increases in its agriculture sector in the coming years.
Russia has completed its second poor harvest in two years, which is the third worst in 30 years.
Alexander Yukish, president of the Grain Union, stated that demand for grain will rise faster than production.
Russian farmers are struggling to obtain seeds, tractors, and fertilizers.
The agriculture sector in Russia is inefficient and has not adopted pro-market reforms.
Yukish claimed that Russia will need at least 120 million tonnes of grain when livestock levels and consumption return to 1990 levels.
Russian grains output has nearly halved in recent years and is not expected to recover for at least five to ten years.
Alexander Vasyutin, deputy head of the Agriculture Ministry's crops growing section, stated that Russia needs to produce more soymeal and maize.
Russia has been slaughtering livestock due to insufficient grain for feeding.
The preliminary official figure for Russia's 1996 gross harvest is 74.6 million tonnes, which is only eight percent above the previous year's harvest.

Russia is attempting to shift financing of its gold sector to commercial banks while maintaining control over exports.
Commercial banks in Russia are interested in sales abroad.
Moscow bullion officials view recent Central Bank decisions as a cautious step toward opening the gold industry.
Dmitry Smirnov, head of precious metals operations at Vneshtorgbank, commented on the significance of recent changes in accounting procedures for gold.
Smirnov does not expect a sharp rise in gold output in the near future.
Russian bullion officials aim to open up the domestic gold market due to budget constraints.
Canada reports that Russia has the world's third-largest untapped gold reserves but is the fifth-largest producer.
Gold output in Russia fell to about 130 tonnes in 1995 and is expected to decline in 1996 and 1997.
Approximately 130 banks have the right to trade gold domestically, but only five to eight can export it.
Western bullion bankers express concern that bank-financed output could significantly impact world markets.

A diamond deal between Russia and De Beers is delayed due to political issues in Moscow.
Bickering ministries and leadership changes in the Russian diamond industry are contributing to the delay.
Senior officials from both Russia and De Beers did not provide a timeline for when the deal would be signed.
Russian officials indicated that there may be no formal contract signed before 1997.
Vladimir Piskunov stated that the government has been reviewing a draft deal for at least a month.
Piskunov mentioned that unspecified pricing issues require further examination.
De Beers representatives in Moscow declined to comment on the situation.
Valentin Logunov, a spokesman for Almazy Rossii-Sakha, attributed the delay to significant changes in Russia's diamond industry.
De Beers controls approximately 75% of the global diamond market, while Russia accounts for about 25% of De Beers' sales.
Almazy Rossii-Sakha produced nearly all of Russia's diamonds and reported sales of $1.38 billion last year.

Russia's diamond industry is facing structural chaos and unauthorized exports.
The prospects for a trade deal between Russia and De Beers by 1997 are considered grim.
Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS) is Russia's near-monopoly diamond producer and De Beers' negotiating partner.
De Beers has given Russia until the end of 1996 to sign a trade deal or it will terminate the interim arrangement.
Valentin Logunov is a spokesman for ARS.
Logunov stated that it is uncertain if the Russian government will meet the deadline set by De Beers.
Russia supplies De Beers with about 20 percent of its total rough gem sales.
De Beers accounts for 75 percent of global rough diamond sales.
There is currently no formal trade agreement between Russia and De Beers.
Raymond Clark is the general director of De Beers' Moscow representation.

Russia's aluminium industry is now in private hands.
Russia accounts for about 15 percent of world aluminium output.
In 1997, Russia will not cut production or exports despite rising costs and low prices.
Russian smelters aim to turn profits.
Ownership of smelters has stabilized, allowing for more reliable metal sales.
Russia has restarted some idled aluminium production capacity after a global output cutting agreement expired.
Analysts are uncertain about the potential impact of Russian aluminium on global markets.
Igor Prokopov stated that 1996 primary aluminium output would rise 1.5 percent from 1995.
Russian primary aluminium exports in 1996 were estimated at 2.37 million tonnes.
Western shareholders are increasingly involved in the transparency of Russian aluminium exports.

Russia's oil industry earned higher export revenues in 1996 due to rising world prices.
Energy analysts expressed concern about the slow recovery of domestic demand for oil in 1997.
International oil prices increased by about 30 percent in 1996, reaching their highest level in six years.
Domestic producers exported large quantities of crude oil in 1996, taking advantage of high international prices.
Analysts indicated that higher domestic demand for Russian oil was not yet evident.
Eugene Khartukov stated that 1997 could either see a recovery in oil output or a further decline.
Russian crude oil output in 1997 could rise to 6.3 million barrels per day from an estimated 6.1 million barrels per day in 1996.
Russia's crude oil and gas condensate output decreased by two percent to 275.9 million tonnes from January to November 1996.
Exports of Russian oil increased by 4.7 percent year-on-year to 92.8 million tonnes during the same period.
Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Garipov reported that no exploration for new oilfields occurred in Russia in 1996.

Russia is importing Western grain to address its second consecutive poor harvest.
Traders reported that Russia lacks the financial resources to significantly participate in global grain markets this year.
Unnamed Russian organizations purchased several 12,000-tonne cargoes of U.S. No. 2 corn at the end of the previous year.
The grain was imported through the Baltic port of Riga.
Andrei Ambartsumyan, a vice-president at Exportkhleb, stated that there is enough grain in the domestic market but raised concerns about quality.
Ambartsumyan does not foresee any significant import orders.
Russia's harvest last year was 69.0 million tonnes, one of the worst in three decades.
Vladimir Totsky, vice-president of Russia's Grain Union, indicated that Russia will import grain this year to obtain necessary quality.
Anatoly Manellya of the Centre for Economic Trends estimated Russia's total grain imports for 1997 at 5.0-6.0 million tonnes.
There is no consensus on Russia's overall import plans, with some experts suggesting a trend towards importing ready-made food.

Russia announced plans to restructure Gazprom's operations.
Western analysts believe the restructuring will not change Gazprom's status as the world's largest gas company.
Jonathan Stern, vice-president of Gas Strategies, stated that Gazprom's proposal is more about commercialization than restructuring.
Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin indicated that the government would restructure Gazprom's domestic operations.
Yasin mentioned that the changes would not weaken Gazprom as an international corporation.
Gazprom accounts for 60 percent of Europe's gas imports.
Stephen O'Sullivan from MC Securities expressed skepticism about serious restructuring at Gazprom.
Gazprom controls 94 percent of Russia's gas production and most of its transmission.
Lira Rozenova, an adviser to Gazprom's chairman, stated that any changes would maintain the company's integrity.
Gazprom produced 575 billion cubic meters of gas in 1996, a one percent increase from the previous year.

France announced plans to sell state-owned defence and consumer electronics group Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe.
Lagardere Groupe owns missile maker Matra.
The French government preferred Lagardere's bid over Alcatel Alsthom SA's offer.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe's office stated that the merger would create a leading force in the world military industry.
The French government plans to invest 11 billion francs into Thomson.
Thomson is a leading maker of televisions under brands such as SABA and RCA.
Thomson specializes in defence electronics, including missile guidance systems.
Lagardere's conglomerate also owns publisher Hachette.
The French government will send both offers for Thomson SA to the independent Privatisation Commission.
The sale is expected to be concluded before the end of the year after clearance from the European Commission.

Air Liberte is a French regional airline that is under bankruptcy protection.
The airline has 1,400 staff members.
Air Liberte published a full-page advert in the Journal du Dimanche demanding to see takeover bids made to the administrators.
Offers for Air Liberte have been made by British Airways Plc, Virgin Express, a consortium led by Jacques Maillot, and pilot Fernand Denan.
The commercial court of Creteil is expected to decide on the takeover options early this week.
Air Liberte went into administration on September 26 with debts of about 1.5 billion francs.
The staff of Air Liberte blamed the French authorities for the company's difficulties.
The staff also blamed certain shareholders for abandoning the company before a recapitalization.
British Airways plans to pay 25 million francs for Air Liberte and aims to merge it with its French TAT unit.
Air Liberte owns about a quarter of the landing and take-off slots at Orly airport.

British Airways Plc (BA) has strengthened its position in France by partnering with French bank Groupe Rivaud in a bid for Air Liberte.
Groupe Rivaud is a founding shareholder in Air Liberte and previously partnered in a rival consortium.
The partnership between BA and Rivaud was formed after negotiations that began on Tuesday afternoon and concluded on Wednesday morning.
The BA/Rivaud bid is the only remaining offer for Air Liberte and is expected to be approved by the commercial court in Creteil on Friday.
Richard Branson's Virgin Express and commercial pilot Fernand Denan were also pursuing takeover offers for Air Liberte.
The BA/Rivaud proposal requires approval from Air Liberte's creditors and French authorities.
Air Liberte holds a 12 percent share of the domestic French market, while BA's TAT unit has an eight percent share.
Air France group is the dominant player in the French airline market.
British Airways plans to invest 440 million francs for a 70 percent stake in Air Liberte, while Rivaud will invest 190 million francs for the remaining 30 percent.
Rivaud will also write off over 500 million francs in existing convertible debt and provide Air Liberte with 50-60 million francs in new loan capital.

Air France is a French state-owned airline.
Air France stated it is prepared to face increased competition from British Airways Plc (BA) in the domestic market.
BA's TAT French unit announced a joint bid of 780 million francs ($151.2 million) with bank Rivaud for domestic carrier Air Liberte.
The joint bid will increase BA's share of takeoff and landing slots at Paris' Orly airport to 20 percent.
An Air France spokeswoman acknowledged that BA's increased presence in French aviation would have consequences for Air France.
Air France plans to improve its product and service while reducing costs and prices.
BA will manage its French assets from a distance initially.
TAT and Air Liberte will operate separately until at least 1999.
The Creteil commercial court will review the BA/Rivaud offer on Friday.
Air Liberte's creditors will have the final decision on the offer within a month.

Jacques Maillot is the chairman of travel group Nouvelles Frontieres.
Maillot has withdrawn from bidding for Air Liberte due to the financial commitment required.
Maillot is in talks to acquire airline AOM.
A 780 million franc bid by British Airways Plc French TAT unit and bank Rivaud is the only remaining bid for Air Liberte.
The Creteil commercial court is expected to approve the bid for Air Liberte on Friday.
Maillot stated that he remains a candidate for the takeover of AOM.
Maillot had planned to buy Air Liberte with the help of Royal Air Maroc, Club Mediterranee, and Rivaud.
AOM was created in 1991 by the merger of Air Outre Mer and Minerve.
AOM is owned by the Consortium de Realisation (CDR), a state entity.
AOM is valued at about one billion francs according to industry sources.

The planned sale of state-owned Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics has led to protests.
Shares in Lagardere Groupe fell nearly seven percent on Monday due to investor concerns about the Thomson sale.
French opposition parties, labor unions, and most French citizens oppose the government's plan to sell Thomson SA.
Thomson Multimedia workers protested against the sale and plan a demonstration in November.
The opposition to the sale may negatively impact foreign buyer interest in future French privatizations.
Lagardere's shares had previously risen by 32 percent after the government selected it to buy Thomson.
Thomson holds a 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF and owns 100 percent of Thomson Multimedia.
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis stated that the government's procedure was free from political criticism.
Lagardere's bid was favored due to its defense connections.
A survey found that 72 percent of voters disapproved of the sale price of Thomson Multimedia.

Daewoo Electronics is proposing to buy France's Thomson Multimedia.
Daewoo Electronics has pledged to make investments in Thomson Multimedia.
Bae Soon-hoon is the chairman of Daewoo Electronics.
Bae Soon-hoon stated that Daewoo Electronics would spend at least 10 billion French francs on Thomson Multimedia.
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis reaffirmed the government's intention to sell Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe and Daewoo.
Prime Minister Juppe called for a public debate on the sale of Thomson SA.
Thomson has debts of approximately 14 billion francs.
Lagardere plans to merge Thomson SA's profitable defence group with its Matra unit.
The Privatisation Commission is studying bids from Lagardere/Daewoo and Alcatel Alsthom.
Bae Soon-hoon indicated that the 10 billion francs investment is only the first stage of the acquisition.

Shares in Groupe Salomon SA fell sharply for the second consecutive day on Thursday.
The company's shares more than doubled in value this year prior to the recent decline.
Groupe Salomon SA is headed by Jean-Francois Gautier and is based in Annecy, France.
Rumours have negatively impacted the perception of the company.
Salomon executives were in London discussing first half sales figures during an investors' road-show.
One rumour involved a Japanese distributor going bankrupt, which could financially affect the company.
Another rumour suggested that the roadshow was not going well.
Salomon's shares were down 17 francs, or 3.83 percent, at 427 francs at 1141 GMT.
Olympic Sports Co, a distributor in Japan, applied for court mediation with debts of 34.83 billion yen.
Salomon's Japanese subsidiary, Salomon & Taylor Made Co, was trading at 810 yen, above its life low but below its year high.

The French government has initiated a consultation regarding interconnection costs charged by France Telecom.
Francois Fillon is the minister for Post and Telecommunications in France.
Fillon has requested comments from key players in the telecommunications sector by November 30.
The French ministry plans to publish two decrees at the start of 1997.
One decree will establish conditions and pricing principles for interconnection agreements.
The second decree will set a time limit for litigation procedures related to interconnection.
The proposed time limit for litigation is three months, extendable to six months with agreement.
France Telecom will continue to manage the national telecommunications infrastructure under the liberalisation plans.
Interconnection pricing is crucial for the business models of new telecommunications competitors.
Generale des Eaux's SFR is currently the largest client of France Telecom.

Several thousand employees of Thomson Multimedia protested in Paris and other towns against the planned sale of the company to Daewoo.
Workers traveled by bus to Paris to demonstrate in front of Thomson Multimedia's headquarters.
Protests also occurred in Rennes, Bordeaux, Nice, and Grenoble.
Thomson employees expressed anger over not being involved in the decision regarding the sale.
A protesting worker in Rennes stated that the sale to Daewoo is unacceptable.
The worker claimed that Thomson Multimedia produces high-quality products and does not want to produce low-quality products.
About a thousand people marched in Grenoble, with some chanting against Daewoo.
Industry Minister Franck Borotra stated that privatization is necessary to secure the future of Thomson Multimedia.
Borotra described Thomson Multimedia as being in a serious financial disaster.
Workers argued that Thomson Multimedia is fundamentally profitable.

The French government plans to complete the privatisation of Cie des Machines Bull by selling another stake of at least five percent.
The sale will reduce the government's share in Bull to below 50 percent.
The Paris Bourse suspended Bull's shares at the company's request until after the completion of the operation.
Japan's NEC, Motorola of the U.S., and France Telecom each hold a 17 percent stake in Bull and are expected to subscribe to the capital increase.
The French state currently holds a 36 percent stake in Bull and will first subscribe to the capital increase before selling shares to private investors.
IBM, which holds a 1.6 percent stake in Bull, is expected not to participate in the capital increase.
Dai Nippon Printing of Japan, which holds a 3.3 percent stake, has been invited to join the capital increase.
The Finance Ministry will decide on the issue price and the identity of the buyers after consulting the independent Privatisation Commission.
Interested parties have 15 days to express interest in blocks of at least 1.4 million shares of Bull.
Thierry Breton stated that the operation would allow Bull to decide on mergers or acquisitions in the restructuring of the European computer industry.

European governments and industry launched a high-technology programme called Microelectronic Developments for European Applications (MEDEA).
MEDEA is a two billion ecu programme for the 1997-2000 period.
MEDEA takes over from the Joint European sub-micron semiconductor initiative (JESSI).
Horst Nasko is the Austrian chairman of JESSI and now MEDEA.
Nasko stated that Europe had closed the technology gap in the past eight years.
Nasko emphasized the need for Europe to continue advancing in technology.
MEDEA will be based in Paris and will coordinate industry research programmes in six main areas.
Three of the six areas will focus on multimedia, communications, and automobile and traffic systems.
The other three areas will focus on semiconductor design and manufacturing techniques.
The semiconductor industry in Europe supports eight million jobs and experiences rapid technological changes.

National Mutual Holdings Ltd is an Australian life office.
National Mutual Holdings Ltd is expected to debut on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchanges on Tuesday.
The institutional offer for National Mutual Holdings Ltd closed six times oversubscribed.
The final price of the shares was A$1.60 each.
The indicative bidding range for institutions was A$1.35 to A$1.55.
National Mutual Holdings Ltd has a market capitalisation of A$2.7 billion upon listing.
Geoff Tomlinson is the managing director of National Mutual.
Share analysts predict that the shares could increase in value on the Australian and New Zealand exchanges.
Institutions received an average of about 15 percent of the allotments they sought.
Bill Chatterton is the director of equities at Morgan Stockbroking.

Foster's Brewing Group Ltd is seeking expansion through possible joint ventures in India and Vietnam.
Foster's executives stated that the company is well positioned for growth opportunities despite challenges in Canada and China.
Foster's chief executive Ted Kunkel emphasized the priority of seeking new direct investment opportunities after meeting current cash needs.
Foster's chairman John Ralph confirmed the consideration of joint venture breweries in Vietnam and India.
Ralph mentioned that the Vietnamese opportunity involves an existing plant.
Foster's has breweries in Shanghai, Tianjin, and Guangdong in China.
Foster's China operations are expected to break even or turn a profit in 1998/99 after a loss of A$17 million in 1995/96.
Molson Breweries, a 40-percent owned Canadian brewer by Foster's, has undergone a major restructure to focus on market share.
Kunkel forecasted higher operating profits from Carlton and United Breweries, Foster's Australian brewing unit.
Foster's plans to free up about A$400 million in non-performing assets and expects higher returns from its British pub chain.

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd is an Australian steelmaker.
BHP Steel is Australia's largest producer of raw steel.
BHP Steel raised the possibility of global steel companies forming alliances to build large steel mills in Asia.
Ron McNeilly is the chief executive of BHP Steel.
McNeilly stated that traditional steel mills may be more suitable for Asia than new-technology electric steel-making furnaces.
McNeilly noted that there is not enough scrap steel available in Asia.
Building large traditional steel plants requires billions of dollars in investment.
McNeilly expressed that the investment required for a single project is too risky to undertake independently.
BHP Steel is investing over A$500 million in new value-added steel production in Asia.
Asian steel consumption is expected to grow by almost two percent per year over the next four years.

ICI Australia Ltd reported a significant decline in annual net profit.
The decline in profit was attributed to sharply lower plastics prices.
Warren Haynes is the managing director of ICI Australia Ltd.
The net profit after abnormals for the year was A$197 million.
The financial year ended on September 30.
Trading profit from the plastic division fell to A$2 million in 1995/96 from A$73 million in 1994/95.
World plastics prices dropped significantly from mid-1995.
Plastic prices decreased by an average of US$400 per tonne since June 1995.
ICI Australia is 62.4 percent owned by Imperial Chemical Industries Plc.
The company produces approximately 300 tonnes of plastics annually.

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd is expected to report a fall in half year net profit on Friday.
Analysts predict BHP will post a first-half net profit of around A$760 million, down from A$811 million a year ago.
The expected result for the six months to November 30 will include roughly A$100 million in net proceeds from asset sales.
Analysts anticipate slight improvements in BHP's copper and steel divisions.
BHP's share price closed at A$17.31 on Monday after hitting A$15.58 in September.
The five analysts contacted by Reuters provided profit forecasts ranging from A$715 million to A$804 million.
Analysts agreed that the interim result would show signs of improved performance in copper and steel.
BHP Petroleum is expected to be BHP's biggest earner in the interim result.
BHP reported a 20 percent drop in pre-abnormal net profit of A$1.29 billion in 1995/96.
Most analysts expect a modest profit recovery for the full year 1996/97.

The Broken Hill Pty Co (BHP) reported a second-quarter profit that was weaker than expected.
BHP posted first-half net earnings of A$683 million before abnormals.
BHP's shares have declined over the past six months due to poor performance in its key markets of steel and copper.
BHP recorded an abnormal gain of A$107 million for the six months ending November 30.
Investors were not impressed with BHP's financial results.

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) is a century-old steel maker in Australia.
BHP has been warned it risks falling behind global rivals unless it restructures its ageing plants and develops a clear offshore strategy.
Standard and Poor's stated that BHP faces its toughest test as it aims to compete in rapidly developing Asian markets.
Taiwan's An Feng Steel Co Ltd plans to build a A$1.4 billion steel mill in Australia, which is seen as a challenge for BHP.
An Feng Steel and its partner Kingstream Resources NL plan to produce 2.4 million tonnes of steel slab annually for Asian markets.
BHP dominates the Australian steel market with products made from old-technology plants.
The youngest of BHP's three major steel mills opened 56 years ago.
BHP produces 636 tonnes of steel per worker per year using coal-fired blast furnaces.
New-technology mills using electric arc furnaces are expected to enable steel operators to reach 1,000 tonnes per worker by the year 2000.
BHP is expected to announce the results of a year-long review of its steel division's long-term strategy by May.

National Mutual Holdings Ltd will provide an indicative value for its shares on Wednesday.
The group's net tangible asset backing is A$2.36 billion or A$1.39 per share.
Retail investors are expected to receive a discount on the final price paid by institutions.
A stock analyst estimated the retail price for shares could be between A$1.30 and A$1.35.
Policy-holders own 49 percent of National Mutual Holdings, while French parent Axa owns the remaining 51 percent.
The demand from policy-holders will influence the availability of shares for institutional investors.
National Mutual has not commented on policy-holder demand for shares but noted high inquiry activity.
The company has not specified the retail and institutional portions of the offer.
Geoff Tomlinson, the chief executive, stated that the group's NTA is an indicator of the final offer price.
National Mutual would list on the Australian Stock Exchange at a price-earnings ratio of 11 if the issue price is A$1.39.

Coles Myer Ltd reported a 5.4 percent rise in sales revenue to A$9.9 billion for the six months to January 26.
Coles attributed its sales revenue increase to good management.
Coles holds almost 18 cents of every retail dollar spent in Australia.
David Jones Ltd reassessed its profit outlook after initially forecasting a 50 percent fall in interim profit.
David Jones reported overall sales of A$783 million for the first half year to January 25, which is only one percent lower than the previous year.
Retail analyst Simon Shakesheff stated that spending may have reached its lowest point but does not expect a dramatic turnaround.
Australian retail sales are at their lowest level in 35 years and have fallen in trend terms for the past five months.
Australia's jobless rate is currently at 8.6 percent.
Coles reported a 4.7 percent drop in retail sales for its specialist apparel chain, Katies, in the second quarter.

National Mutual Holdings Ltd is targeting China and Thailand as key markets.
National Mutual is owned 51 percent by Axa SA.
National Mutual plans to double its representation in mainland China by opening three more local offices.
National Mutual is awaiting an operating licence in China.
National Mutual has applied to open offices in Wuhan, Dalian, and Chengdu.
National Mutual already has offices in Shanghai, Guangdong, and Beijing.
National Mutual has been trying to enter China for over three years.
National Mutual has signed a cooperation pact with China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd.
National Mutual has donated HK$10 million to establish a China education fund.
National Mutual and Axa launched a US$500 million China investment fund in September.

Brian Quinn, a former chief executive of Coles Myer Ltd, is on trial in the Victoria Supreme Court for conspiracy to defraud.
Quinn has pleaded not guilty and claims he was set up.
The prosecution alleges that Quinn conspired to spend approximately A$4.0 million of company funds on renovations to his Melbourne home from 1982 to 1988.
The renovations included expanding the house, building a tennis court, spa, and pergola.
Prosecutor Paul Coghlan accused Quinn of excessive spending and waste.
Quinn and another former Coles manager, Graham Lanyon, allegedly conspired to misrepresent the work as being done on Coles stores.
Lanyon is accused of falsifying invoices to conceal the fraud, allegedly under Quinn's orders.
Defense lawyer Philip Dunn argues that Quinn was a victim of a corrupt maintenance department and contractors.
Quinn's home was owned by Coles until 1985, when he purchased it for about half its market value.
Prosecutors claim that renovations were conducted without board approval while Coles owned the house.

Comalco Ltd is Australia's biggest aluminium producer.
Comalco Ltd reported a loss for calendar 1996 due to weak aluminium prices, an adverse exchange rate, and higher smelting costs.
Comalco's net profit before abnormals decreased to A$32.9 million in 1996 from A$264.8 million in 1995.
Comalco's total loss for 1996 was A$16.8 million after accounting for abnormals.
Comalco's share price dropped eight cents following the loss announcement but recovered to A$6.80.
Comalco is 67 percent owned by global mining group RTZ-CRA.
Higher operating costs at Comalco's three smelters reduced group operating profit by A$32 million.
Comalco attributed higher operating costs to increased prices for raw materials and costs related to smelter upgrades and expansions.

Crown Ltd is an Australian casino company.
Crown Ltd stated that its earnings are likely to suffer due to lost time at its new casino complex in Melbourne.
Crown's share price has fallen amid doubts about its profit outlook.
A recent heatwave forced workers at the Melbourne site to stop working for several days.
Crown spokesman Gary O'Neill indicated that the heatwave could impact profit.
Crown planned to open its A$1.6 billion casino, hotel, and shopping complex in Melbourne in March.
Crown is now aiming to open the complex in late April or possibly May.
O'Neill mentioned that the Electrical Trades Union (ETU) stopped work 10 times this month due to temperatures exceeding 35 degrees Celsius.
Crown rejected a bearish earnings forecast made by accountants Ernst and Young.
Ernst and Young forecasted basic earnings per share of 3.76 cents for 1997/98, while brokers' average forecast was 14.8 cents.

Microsoft Corp. executives believe that the Internet will be the next mass medium.
Microsoft unveiled a new version of the MSN online service with a focus on entertainment programming.
The new MSN programs are organized into six core channels aimed at specific demographic groups.
MSN has become the No. 3 online service with 1.6 million subscribers in just over a year.
Microsoft executives expect to double the number of subscribers by mid-1997.
Microsoft plans to take market share from America Online Inc. through a $100 million marketing campaign.
Microsoft executives acknowledged that America Online has a deeper and broader selection of content.
Microsoft intends to target new online customers under 30 rather than trying to convert existing AOL customers.
Laura Jennings, a Microsoft vice president, criticized the previous MSN service for its ease of use.
The new advertising campaign will start with billboards and print ads, followed by television commercials in early November.

Microsoft Corp. reported profits of $614 million for the latest quarter, a 23 percent increase from $499 million in the same quarter of 1995.
Earnings per share for Microsoft were 95 cents, up from 78 cents a share in the previous year.
Revenues for Microsoft increased by 14 percent to $2.30 billion from $2.02 billion.
Microsoft's profits exceeded Wall Street's consensus expectation of 90 cents a share.
Microsoft shares rose to $136.375 in after-hours trading from an earlier close of $134 on Nasdaq.
Treasurer Greg Maffei stated that the 14 percent revenue increase was the smallest in the company's 21-year history.
Analyst Scott McAdams noted that Microsoft's operating profit margin reached a record 39.3 percent of revenues.
Microsoft executives indicated that business would benefit from an expected holiday surge in personal computer sales and the December release of Office 97.
CFO Mike Brown projected revenues for the current quarter could reach $2.4 billion, about 12 percent higher than last year's levels.
Sales of the Windows NT workstation increased by 400 percent compared to the previous year.

Boeing Co defense and space group President Gerald King stated that the company's planned acquisition of Rockwell International Corp's defense and space business is on track to close in early December.
King expects the defense and space group to account for 30 to 40 percent of Boeing Co's total revenues over time.
King anticipates that federal regulators will complete an antitrust review of the planned Rockwell deal early next month.
The acquisition proposal requires approval from Rockwell shareholders at a meeting scheduled for December 4.
King mentioned that the merger could face obstacles, but he believes it is likely to succeed compared to other industry deals.
Last year, Boeing's defense and space revenues were $5.58 billion, representing 29 percent of the company's total revenues of $19.52 billion.
This year, defense and space revenues are expected to remain nearly flat, while overall company revenues are projected to rise to about $22.6 billion.
The Rockwell acquisition is expected to add approximately $2.6 billion in revenue to the defense and space group next year.
King indicated that Boeing has no immediate plans for further acquisitions after the Rockwell deal.
The defense and space group is pursuing commercial opportunities, including the Sea Launch program, which is on track for an initial satellite launch in mid-1998.

Boeing Co. is expected to launch a stretch version of its 747 jumbo jet at the Farnborough Air Show in England.
Industry analysts predict that Boeing will announce two new models, the 747-500 and 747-600, on Monday.
Joe Campbell, an analyst at Lehman Bros., stated that the announcement of the airplanes is certain.
There is uncertainty about whether Boeing will announce large orders of $10 billion or more from launch customers.
The new models are expected to include a jet with 30 percent more capacity than the current largest commercial airliner.
Boeing is in discussions with at least six airlines about the new versions of the jumbo jet.
Boeing President Phil Condit mentioned that the board of directors discussed the new plane but had not made a decision on its launch.
The 747-600 is expected to hold 548 passengers and have a range of up to 8,900 miles.
The 747-500 is expected to hold 462 passengers and have a range of up to 10,000 miles.
Analysts believe the 747 stretch is essential for Boeing to maintain its dominance in the high-end market.

Boeing Co. is expected to launch a stretch version of its 747 jumbo jet at the Farnborough Air Show in England.
Industry analysts predict that Boeing will announce two new models, the 747-500 and 747-600, on Monday.
Joe Campbell, an analyst at Lehman Bros., stated that the announcement of the airplanes is certain.
There is uncertainty about whether Boeing will announce large orders of $10 billion or more from launch customers.
The new models are expected to include a jet with 30 percent more capacity than the current largest commercial airliner.
Boeing is in discussions with at least six airlines about the new versions of the jumbo jet.
Boeing President Phil Condit mentioned that the board of directors discussed the new plane but had not made a decision on its launch.
The 747-600 is expected to hold 548 passengers and have a range of up to 8,900 miles.
The 747-500 is expected to hold 462 passengers and have a range of up to 10,000 miles.
Analysts believe the 747 stretch is essential for Boeing to maintain its dominance in the high-end market.

American Airlines plans to place an order for about $6 billion worth of Boeing Co. airplanes.
Airline Chairman Robert Crandall was scheduled to make a major company announcement at a news conference.
Officials of Boeing and American declined to comment on the order reported in the Wall Street Journal and New York Times.
An airline spokesman confirmed that directors of its parent company, AMR Corp., were meeting.
American Airlines is expected to announce an order for more than 100 new Boeing jets, including 12 wide-body 777s and 75 narrow-body 737s.
The exact size of the initial order has not been revealed.
The orders are expected to be contingent on ratification by pilots of a new six-year contract.
The board of the pilots union was voting on a tentative labor pact reached in September.
Industry analysts believe American Airlines could order hundreds of Boeing jets over the next two decades.
American Airlines currently does not operate the 737 and plans to use it to replace 75 older 727 jets.

Microsoft Corp. plans to pay dividends to stockholders for the first time through a new issue of preferred shares.
Microsoft has not paid dividends in its 10 years as a public company and has a cash reserve of more than $7 billion.
The company plans to issue $750 million worth of the new class of preferred stock.
Chief Financial Officer Mike Brown stated that the company is responding to some investors' desire for an income-yielding stock.
The preferred shares will guarantee investors their principal in cash or common stock after three years, along with quarterly dividends.
Investors will have limited opportunities for stock appreciation compared to owners of Microsoft common stock.
The value of the preferred shares will be capped at a percentage to be established at the time of the offering.
Microsoft Chairman Bill Gates and other board members have previously resisted calls for a common stock dividend.
Treasurer Greg Maffei stated that the planned issue of preferred shares is consistent with the company's philosophy of reinvesting in the business.
The amount of the offering could increase to $862.5 million if underwriters Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley exercise options.

Boeing Co. agreed to acquire McDonnell Douglas Corp.
The acquisition received positive reactions from Wall Street.
Stock prices for both Boeing and McDonnell Douglas increased following the announcement.
The all-stock transaction is valued at nearly $14 billion.
Boeing's stock rose to $101.125 and McDonnell Douglas's stock rose to $62.375.
Boeing had previously reduced its workforce by 30 percent over five years.
Boeing completed the $3.2 billion acquisition of Rockwell International Corp.'s defense and space business.
Boeing won the right to compete for a significant military contract.
Boeing announced orders for $45.6 billion in new commercial jets.
Phil Condit became Boeing's CEO in April and initiated merger negotiations with McDonnell Douglas.

Pyramid Breweries Inc. warned of lower-than-expected sales and earnings for the fourth quarter.
Pyramid Breweries attributed the decline to increasing competition in the craft beer industry.
Pyramid expects sales to be 20 percent to 25 percent below last year's levels on a wholesale basis.
Pyramid anticipates breaking even for the quarter, contrary to analysts' projections of earning 9 cents a share.
In the previous year's fourth quarter, Pyramid reported gross sales of $7 million and net income of about $1 million, or 13 cents a share.
Pyramid's stock fell 12.5 cents to $4.125 a share after the announcement.
Pyramid's stock ended an abbreviated trading session 25 cents lower at $4.
Redhook Ale Brewery Inc. also warned of weak sales and was trading at $10.625 on Nasdaq.
Boston Beer Co., maker of Samuel Adams beer, was trading at $10 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analyst Diane Daggatt stated that not many new consumers are trying craft beers anymore.

Boeing Co. took orders for 717 jets valued at $53 billion last year.
Boeing had a 64 percent share of the world market for jets last year.
Boeing received net orders for 559 airplanes with a catalog value of $42.8 billion after excluding cancellations and conversions.
Airbus Industrie took orders for 301 jets worth $21.6 billion, giving it a 32 percent market share.
McDonnell Douglas Corp. took net orders for 38 jets valued at $2.2 billion, representing a 3 percent market share.
Boeing commercial airplane group President Ron Woodard stated that customers chose Boeing for its superior value.
Woodard expressed an expectation for 1997 to be as strong or stronger than 1996.
Boeing's order book exceeded analyst expectations and surpassed previous peak years from the late 1980s.
Boeing's previous best year for total orders was 1990, with 483 jets valued at $41.4 billion.
Boeing's total order figures include a $6.5 billion order from AMR Corp.'s American Airlines that was announced but not signed.

Microsoft Corp. is expected to report modest earnings growth for the latest quarter.
Analysts expect Microsoft to report earnings of 51 cents a share for its second quarter ended on Dec. 31.
This represents an increase of about 16 percent from the 44 cents a share reported a year earlier.
Sales are expected to rise about 14 percent to more than $2.5 billion.
Analysts consider this a strong performance against tough comparisons with the year-earlier period.
In the 1995 second quarter, sales soared 54 percent and net income jumped 48 percent.
Microsoft executives delayed the earnings report release from Thursday to Friday.
Analysts estimate that revenues from Office and its component applications account for up to 30 percent of Microsoft's total.
Strong growth in personal computer sales and acceptance of Microsoft's high-end Windows NT operating system are contributing to profits.
30 percent or fewer of corporate desktops have transitioned to the Windows 95 or Windows NT systems.

Microsoft Corp Chief Financial Officer Mike Brown expects earnings and revenues to rise sequentially in the fiscal third and fourth quarters compared to the second quarter.
Brown anticipates that the release of Office 97 will increase earnings in the third quarter from the $0.57 per share reported for the second quarter.
Brown predicts a small sequential increase in earnings for the fourth quarter.
Brown expects revenues and earnings growth in the 20 percent range for fiscal 1998 starting July 1, 1997.
Brown believes it is prudent to warn about slower growth in fiscal 1998 due to the absence of major revenue-enhancing upgrades.
Brown noted that the company has an opportunity to increase OEM revenue with the high-end Windows NT operating system.
Brown expects significant revenue growth from Windows NT to be more pronounced in fiscal 1999.
Brown stated that research and development spending will continue to grow faster than revenues in fiscal 1998.
Brown mentioned that the company's R&D spending currently exceeds an annual rate of $2 billion and may exceed $3 billion in the future.
Brown indicated that while the company has reduced its cost of goods sold this year, further reductions are unlikely next year.

Ivory Coast may slightly cut cocoa freight for the 1996/97 season.
Exporters and shipping lines believe that a decision on rates will not delay shipments.
Shipments are expected to start once export licenses and finances are secured.
A major shipping line manager stated that last year's rates have been incorporated into next year's costs.
A large fleet manager suggested that the government might reduce rates slightly due to decreased shipping costs since liberalization.
There is uncertainty regarding the completion of official forms due by October 15 for import and export data.
Shipping managers are attempting to arrange a meeting to discuss how to fill in the forms.
Cocoa shipments in 1995 were blocked from early October to mid-November due to a rejected 25 percent cut in freight rates.
A rate of seven percent was eventually agreed upon for cocoa and coffee shipments.
The exporters' forum GEPEX anticipates only a small rate change for the upcoming season.

The Inter-African Coffee Organization (IACO) will hold its annual meeting in Abidjan from November 17-19, 1996.
IACO's chief economist is Donald Kaberuka.
The indicative robusta price is currently 73 cents per pound.
The composite price for robusta and arabica is 99.29 cents.
Recommendations from IACO will be sent to the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).
The ACPC represents 80 percent of world coffee production.
The ACPC agreed to limit green coffee exports from its 14 members to 53.5 million 60-kg bags for the year ending June 1997.
Africa's total export allocation under the ACPC plan is 12,840,000 bags, which is 24 percent of the total ACPC target.
IACO's 25 members are concerned about low prices in the world markets.
IACO provisions allow for a review of the export plan after six months.

Ivory Coast is experiencing a prolonged dry spell that has affected the small rainy season.
Crop and weather analysts stated that the impact on mid-crop cocoa pod setting and main crop growth may not be clear until later this year.
A crop analyst noted that there are strange weather conditions, including harmattan and light rains in nearby areas.
The front that typically moves south in September has finally moved south over the weekend, but rains are still below average.
Weather data indicated that less than 50 percent of average October rains fell in Ivory Coast.
Data for early November was not available to assess the overall rainfall pattern.
A crop analyst mentioned that cherelle setting should be clearer later in November.
Buyers in Daloa reported that intermittent rains had started in the centre-west cocoa region, but more rain is needed for crop development.
Ivory Coast opened its 1996/97 cocoa marketing season late on October 24 due to previous rain deluges.
Crop analysts reported low soil moisture levels in some areas, which could affect pod sizes if sunny weather continues.

Cocoa arrivals at Ivory Coast's ports this season could be 25 percent below last season's record of 1.2 million tonnes.
Erratic weather and insect damage starting in July are contributing factors to the reduced cocoa arrivals.
Buyers and exporters around San Pedro predict cumulative arrivals to the end of November of around 250,000 tonnes.
Cumulative arrivals for December could be up to 300,000 tonnes.
Mid-December to February cocoa arrivals are expected to dip due to rains in July.
Harvests are expected to be later and more prolonged, but not exceed 900,000 tonnes.
Heavy rains in July and August negatively affected flowers for December and January pods.
Sunshine after August improved the outlook for March cocoa production.
Lighter rains starting in early November are expected to boost flowering for mid-crop pods.
Widespread wilting of smaller pods was observed on southwestern farms east and north of San Pedro.

Revised rules for Ivory Coast's electronic cocoa and coffee auction system have been agreed to stop overbidding.
Changes were agreed between marketing board Caistab, exporters, and the World Bank.
No date has been set for the implementation of the changes.
Bidders will be held to the price they offer rather than the second highest bid price.
Exporters will be allowed to buy 15 percent of contracts previously reserved for Caistab direct sales to traders abroad if prices are right.
Existing rules mean Caistab's 15 percent is withdrawn and submitted for later auction even when exporters are prepared to pay more.
Contracts will be awarded to the five highest bidders rather than one and scaled down pro rata if total demand outstrips supply.
Bids are made without knowing what quantities are on offer for a particular session.
The donor-backed auction was launched on May 2 as part of a $150 million World Bank loan deal.
Exporters and industry analysts estimate that up to 115,000 tonnes of cocoa have been sold forward for 1996/97.

Rains ended abruptly throughout most of Ivory Coast in the second 10 days of December.
Weather data showed average rain decreased to 8mm from about 45mm at the start of December.
Little or no rain fell at six of eight monitored stations in the 10 days to December 20.
A total of 65mm of rain fell compared to 400mm at nine stations in the first 10 days of December.
The northern Daloa area received 21.8mm of rain, and the far southwest around Tabou received 42.5mm.
Around 250mm of rain fell in San Pedro and Tabou alone in early December.
The inter-tropical weather front has not brought down Harmattan conditions.
Farmers began drying beans, but some exporters in Abidjan rejected moist beans.
Heavy rains in early December raised cocoa bean humidity levels to up to 11 percent.
Crop analysts expect mid-crop prospects to be boosted by another 20mm of rain by January.

Chad held multi-party parliamentary elections on Sunday.
There was little enthusiasm for the elections in Chad.
Some polling stations in the capital opened late due to unprepared voting materials.
Few queues formed at polling stations during the elections.
Some opposition candidates reported incidents of fraud.
About 30 international observers were present but reserved judgment on the elections.
There were no immediate reports of electoral unrest in Chad.
President Idriss Deby acknowledged Chad's democratic progress after voting.
Former national assembly leader Jean Bawoyeu Alingue expressed skepticism about voter turnout due to perceived fraud.
More than 650 candidates from 49 parties contested 125 seats in the national assembly.

Foreign Minister Saleh Kebzabo defended Chad's new policy of summarily executing alleged criminals.
Kebzabo stated that the policy was justified because the country's courts systematically freed wrongdoers.
Human rights groups report that scores of Chadians have been executed by security forces.
Eleven people were shot in public on New Year's Eve in Chad.
Kebzabo claimed that the policy has reduced levels of violence in Chad.
Kebzabo's comments were a confirmation of a decree issued by President Idriss Deby.
An order was leaked to reporters instructing police to ignore the courts when dealing with criminals caught in the act.
The policy reportedly came into force around the beginning of November.
Deby justified the policy by stating that the courts were corrupt and freed criminals.
Chad has faced insecurity due to civil war and conflict with Libya for over two decades until 1990.

Ivory Coast's 1996/97 coffee season began amid slow buying and reports of variable quality.
SIFCA, the largest Ivorian buyer, has started buying coffee.
The official opening of the coffee season was on November 14, 1996.
Coffee output for the 1996/97 season is estimated at 230,000-250,000 tonnes.
The previous season's output was 180,000 tonnes.
Buyers reported variable quality and humidity levels up to 15 percent in some areas.
Export limits for humidity are set at 13 percent.
Arrivals at San Pedro port by January 10 were reported at 3,337 tonnes.
Some farmers are being paid below the official recommended price of 500 CFA per kilo.
Prices offered for coffee range between 300 and 500 CFA per kilo, depending on area and quality.

Gum arabic is a commodity produced from the sap of acacia trees.
Gum arabic is used by companies such as Coca Cola Co, Hoechst, and bubble gum factories.
Gum arabic provides export currency for impoverished sub-Saharan states.
A senior U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) official stated that the gum arabic industry has suffered from low prices in recent years.
FAO's programme director Mahamat Ali Hassam mentioned that prices could increase as synthetic food substitutes lose favor.
Soft drink manufacturers consume 30 percent of the world's gum arabic output.
Gum arabic is used as a stabilizer and preservative in the food industry.
Chad is planning to improve the quality of its gum arabic to increase market access.
About 70-80 percent of the world's gum arabic output is produced in Africa, with Sudan being the largest producer.
FAO Chad director Pierre Gence stated that Chad has the potential to match Sudan's gum arabic output.

Ivory Coast's 1996/97 cocoa crop is expected to exceed one million tonnes.
Crop analysts and buyers attribute the expected increase to good January harvests and abundant flowering.
One crop analyst estimated that the total crop will be at least one million tonnes.
Arrivals of cocoa by January 27 were estimated at over 750,000 tonnes.
Industry estimates of arrivals up to January 20 ranged from 710,000 to 720,000 tonnes.
The previous season's cocoa crop was around 800,000 tonnes.
Attention is focused on rainfall figures and pod survival rates for mid-crop tonnage predictions.
Ivory Coast had a record cocoa crop of 1.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Crop analysts noted that pod loads were heaviest in younger hybrid tree farms in southwestern areas.
Farms north of San Pedro had noticeable late main crop pod loads, while older trees around Daloa and Gagnoa had few flowers and pods.

Europe's cocoa industry will issue a draft contract document for loose-bean bulk cocoa shipment techniques.
Louis Bensdorp is the Managing Director of the Netherlands Cocoa Association.
Bensdorp stated that discussions are ongoing with the AFCC and the Cocoa Association of London.
The new bulk cocoa contract will be based on cost, insurance, and freight (CIF) terms.
Mega-bulk refers to the trend of loading cocoa ships with loose beans instead of 60 kilo jute bags.
The trend of mega-bulk gained popularity after trial shipments from the Ivory Coast in 1996.
Another bulk technique involves using containers with drying agents to prevent water condensation damage.
Amsterdam is Europe's cocoa processing hub.
Bensdorp expects to receive 350,000 tonnes of cocoa in Amsterdam next year.
Labour and time savings, as well as better quality, have contributed to the growth of bulk techniques.

Ivory Coast will market its midcrop cocoa only if world price levels are favorable.
Ivory Coast Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze made this statement after a cocoa sector review.
Cocoa stocks around Ivorian ports in January were estimated to be close to 400,000 tonnes.
Cocoa futures in the London LIFFE terminal market reached 18-month lows on February 6.
May cocoa contracts were trading at 871 stg but increased to 886 stg by Friday's close.
Traders observed a slowdown in origin selling activity.
Ivory Coast's midcrop is typically of poorer quality than the main crop cocoa.
Industry buyers claim mixing midcrop with main crop cocoa undermines quality.
The Consultative Committee reviewed sector reforms including quality controls and auction rules.
Ivory Coast aims to process 50 percent of its annual cocoa output domestically by the year 2000.

Time Warner Inc reported a 32 percent increase in earnings before debt payments in the third quarter compared to the same period last year.
The company's cash flow for the quarter was $964 million.
Revenues for the three months ended September 30 were $4.877 billion, an increase from $4.344 billion a year ago.
Last year's third-quarter cash flow was $729 million.
Time Warner reported a net loss of $167 million, or 43 cents a share, for the quarter.
Net losses in the same quarter last year were $160 million, or 41 cents a share.
Net interest costs for the quarter were $276 million, up from $259 million in the previous year.
Preferred dividends increased to $76 million in the third quarter from $16 million.
Time Warner executives stated that debt reduction is a priority for the company.
Time Warner is in discussions to restructure its cable-television partnership with U S West Media Group.

Barry Diller is the chairman of Silver King Communications Inc.
Silver King Communications Inc. agreed to acquire Home Shopping Network for $1.27 billion in stock.
The acquisition is intended to help fund Silver King's broadcasting plans.
Diller stated that combining the two companies would expedite the development of Silver King's stations.
Silver King owns 12 U.S. television stations that were spun off by HSN in 1992.
The acquisition reunites Silver King with its former parent company, HSN.
Diller described speculation about launching a new national network as premature.
The cash flow from HSN is expected to assist Silver King in covering programming and development costs.
Diller plans to replace HSN programming on Silver King's stations with locally oriented news and sports shows.
Industry analysts believe the major market stations could attract significant audiences and increase in value.

Sunbeam Corp. plans to cut 6,000 jobs, which is half of its workforce.
Sunbeam Corp. will eliminate 87 percent of its product lines.
Albert Dunlap is the chairman of Sunbeam Corp.
Sunbeam Corp. reported its first quarterly loss since 1992.
The company lost $28.7 million in the third quarter as sales fell by 2 percent.
Sunbeam Corp. will reduce the number of its facilities from 53 to 14.
Sunbeam Corp. will take a charge of $300 million for one-time costs associated with the cuts.
Only $75 million of the $300 million charge will be in cash.
Sunbeam Corp. aims to double revenues to $2 billion by 1999.
Sunbeam Corp. plans to increase operating margins to 20 percent of sales.

Delta Air Lines Inc. was the world's first airborne crop-dusting service.
Delta Air Lines Inc. and Continental Airlines have been discussing a merger for several months.
A merger between Delta and Continental would create the world's largest airline.
Standard and Poor's Corp. may change its ratings on Continental and Delta debt based on the merger discussions.
A merger would fill gaps in each carrier's routes and attract regulatory attention.
Delta Air Lines is the nation's No. 3 carrier.
Delta posted its best earnings for a quarter at $238 million on revenues of $3.43 billion.
Delta has faced competition from United Airlines, American Airlines, and low-cost rivals like ValuJet Inc.
Delta has a history of acquiring other airlines, including Chicago and Southern Airlines in 1952 and Northeast Airlines in 1961.
Delta began its first trans-Atlantic flights to London in 1978.

A Florida judge indicated he was inclined to allow civil claims against the tobacco industry under state anti-racketeering laws.
Palm Beach County Circuit Judge Harold Cohen stated that the state can maintain the RICO actions.
The claims under state RICO laws were added to an existing lawsuit seeking at least $1 billion in compensation for treating smokers' illnesses.
Judge Cohen did not make a decision on the claims until the end of oral arguments.
Florida State Attorney General Bob Butterworth stated that a victory against tobacco companies using the RICO law could triple the damages claimed by the state.
A victory in Florida using its RICO law could allow other states to sue under their own RICO laws.
Lawyer Irving Nathan argued that lawsuits under anti-racketeering laws were intended to demonize cigarette manufacturers.
Nathan claimed that the RICO laws did not apply to the tobacco companies being sued in Florida.
The state of Florida filed a lawsuit against the tobacco industry in 1995 seeking $1 billion for health care costs related to smoking.
A jury trial for the suit is tentatively scheduled for August 1997.

H.J. Heinz Co chairman Tony O'Reilly stated that the U.S. food group is in deal talks with prospective buyers.
Heinz plans to sell substantial businesses by April 30.
O'Reilly mentioned that by the end of the fiscal year, the businesses will have a leaner focus.
O'Reilly did not disclose which businesses are for sale or estimate their potential cash value.
Heinz is in contact with four or five potential buyers.
Heinz will focus on six business clusters: food-service products, pet food, infant formula outside the United States, condiments such as ketchup, and weight-loss services and products.
An estimated one-third to one-fourth of Heinz's businesses are outside these focus areas.
Heinz has scheduled a Wall Street analysts' meeting in March regarding the asset sales.
O'Reilly stated that Heinz is expected to post a double-digit percentage profit increase in the fiscal year ending April 30.
Heinz reported quarterly share profits of $0.47, an increase from $0.42 a year earlier.

RJR Tobacco is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings.
RJR Tobacco stated that documents provided to Minnesota may indicate that its executives considered using additives to enhance nicotine in cigarettes.
RJR Tobacco mentioned that its executives contemplated increasing marketing efforts in 1980 to regain market share among U.S. teenagers from Philip Morris Cos.
RJR Tobacco and other tobacco companies are being sued by Minnesota and 17 other states for billions of dollars spent on treating smoking-related illnesses.
Trials related to these lawsuits are scheduled in Mississippi, Florida, and Texas this year.
RJR Tobacco expressed concern that anti-tobacco information might be selectively leaked to news organizations by opposing lawyers.
RJR Tobacco released three excerpts from 4.5 million pages of documents along with its explanations but will not release the full documents.
RJR Tobacco indicated that two documents suggested the company studied adding ammonia compounds in the 1970s to enhance nicotine effects.
RJR Tobacco quoted a 1973 document stating that if ammonia contributed positively to smoking satisfaction, the company would want to optimize this effect.
RJR Tobacco's deputy general counsel, Daniel Donohue, expects the Minnesota lawyers to use the documents to support claims of nicotine manipulation.

Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth stated that U.S. cigarette makers delayed revealing damaging information about the industry.
Cigarette makers ended pre-trial opposition to punitive damages in Florida's anti-tobacco lawsuit.
A court hearing on punitive claims is scheduled for January 24.
The court-sealed documents contain 27,000 pages of information about the industry's marketing and medical research.
Florida is one of 18 states suing U.S. cigarette companies to recover healthcare costs related to smoking.
A trial in the Florida lawsuit filed by Butterworth is set for August 4.
Philip Morris Cos Inc and other cigarette companies dropped pre-trial opposition to punitive claims due to concerns about bad publicity.
The state of Florida is seeking to recover $1 billion or more for Medicaid costs from 1994.
Philip Morris Cos Inc lawyer Gregory Little stated that the industry's decision had no legal effect.
Little expressed concern that the state's lawyers would present evidence against cigarette makers during the pre-trial hearing.

Lawyers representing flight attendants have begun notifying potential claimants about a class-action tobacco suit.
The mass mailing targets approximately 120,000 former and current flight attendants on U.S. airlines.
The suit seeks to find non-smoking flight attendants with ailments such as lung cancer.
The trial is scheduled to begin on June 2 in Miami's Dade County Court.
The class-action claims that illnesses among non-smoking flight attendants were caused by second-hand smoke from cigarettes on airplanes.
The suit seeks unspecified damages that could total billions of dollars.
Philip Morris Cos. Inc. and other leading U.S. tobacco companies are accused of hiding the dangers of second-hand smoke.
Richard Daynard, chairman of the Tobacco Liability Law Project, stated that this is the first time a class-action case against tobacco companies has reached notification.
Flight attendants' lawyer Stanley Rosenblatt estimates that 25,000 to 60,000 sick individuals may be included in the suit.
The suit alleges that second-hand smoke causes various ailments, including cardiac issues and cancer.

Quick & Reilly Group Inc agreed to buy Nash, Weiss Inc.
The acquisition is the largest deal Quick & Reilly has done.
Nash, Weiss buys and sells approximately 2,500 stocks listed on the Nasdaq.
Michael Sears, an analyst at Salomon Brothers, suggested the acquisition may lead to more deals involving market-makers in Nasdaq stocks.
Investors have reported price differences on Nasdaq stocks can exceed 10 percent.
Nash, Weiss profits from the spread between seller and buyer prices.
Quick & Reilly employs about 60 people at Nash, Weiss.
Quick & Reilly is known as a retail broker and also operates U.S. Clearing Corp.
Quick & Reilly owns JCC Specialist Corp., the second-largest market-maker on the New York Stock Exchange.
The acquisition is expected to increase the number of securities Nash, Weiss makes markets in from 2,500 to between 3,500 and 4,000.

A Florida judge allowed Arthur Reeves to take a back seat in a class-action trial against tobacco groups due to his complaints of intimidation.
Stanley Rosenblatt is the lawyer pursuing the class-action suit on behalf of ill and addicted smokers in Florida.
Arthur Reeves was one of the original six smokers in the class-action suit filed three years ago.
Rosenblatt stated that Reeves felt embarrassed and humiliated by investigators asking about him.
Rosenblatt claimed that private investigators for tobacco companies routinely check the backgrounds of people opposing them in court.
Rosenblatt requested that Frank Amodeo be substituted for Reeves as a witness in the trial scheduled for September 8.
Frank Amodeo began smoking at age 14 and has tried to stop smoking multiple times.
Amodeo currently takes liquid nourishment through a feeding tube because he cannot eat or drink.
Reeves is not withdrawing from the suit and will still share in any money awards from the trial.
Rosenblatt alleges that tobacco companies conspired to hide damaging medical evidence and mislead the public about smoking dangers.

Eastman Kodak Co sold its copier-marketing and service operations to Danka Business Systems Plc for $684 million.
Kodak's copier sales were $1.8 billion, resulting in only $20 million in annual operating profits.
Xerox Corp's executive Gill Hatch stated that Danka will have to compete aggressively in the copier market.
Danka's acquisition of Kodak's operations includes a 10-year alliance with Kodak.
Danka will offer a full line of copiers to various market segments worldwide.
Kodak is retaining its manufacturing and development operations in copiers and some key technology.
Kodak's remaining businesses will generate about $600 million in annual sales.
Danka will be the primary distributor of Kodak copiers and printers.
Kodak co-chief operating officer Carl Kohrt predicted profitability for Kodak's remaining copier businesses by the end of 1997.
The deal is expected to close by December 31.

A senior U.S. official praised Beijing's approach to international arms control.
John Holum is the director of the U.S. Arms Control and Disarmament Agency.
Holum expressed concerns over the possible proliferation of Chinese nuclear and missile technology.
Holum stated that the rebirth of arms control dialogue was a major step in bridging differences between Washington and Beijing.
Holum noted that Chinese positions have evolved in a constructive direction.
Holum acknowledged China's active role in arms control negotiations, including a global nuclear test ban and a cut-off of nuclear fissile material production.
Holum's meetings with Chinese officials are part of high-level talks to strengthen Sino-U.S. ties.
Sino-U.S. relations were strained by a 1995 visit to the U.S. by Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui and issues related to copyright, trade, and human rights.
Tensions escalated in March when China conducted missile tests near Taiwan, prompting the U.S. to send two aircraft carriers to the area.
Holum indicated that Sino-U.S. disputes had restricted discussions on arms control and proliferation issues.

Australia's Foreign Minister Alexander Downer announced an agreement with China to expand their security dialogue.
Downer stated that recent frictions had not spoiled growing ties between Australia and China.
Disagreements over Taiwan, a meeting with the Dalai Lama, and a security pact between Canberra and Washington were discussed during meetings with Chinese counterparts.
Downer expressed a desire for annual senior officials' talks about regional security issues.
Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen accepted an Australian proposal to broaden existing annual bilateral disarmament talks into a security dialogue.
Downer stated that the Australian government does not support a policy of containment of China.
Downer plans to meet the Dalai Lama when he arrives in Australia next month.
The Chinese premier did not directly mention Downer's upcoming meeting with the Dalai Lama.
A defense pact between Washington and Canberra was not raised as a concern by China during talks.
Downer fulfilled a pledge to raise the case of jailed Chinese-born Australian businessman James Peng during his trip to Beijing.

Chinese officials have called for a war on AIDS.
The nation is in danger of losing its last chance to slow the spread of the disease.
Peng Peiyun, minister of the State Family Planning Commission, stated that time is running out to strengthen safeguards against AIDS.
Peng Peiyun emphasized that the period until the end of the century is crucial for preventing the spread of AIDS.
Health Minister Chen Minzhang warned that drug abuse, prostitution, and illegal blood supplies could accelerate the AIDS epidemic in China.
Chen Minzhang noted that many Chinese people still know little about AIDS and HIV.
China's official total for the number of people infected with HIV is 4,305, with 131 having developed AIDS.
Experts estimate the actual number of HIV infections in China to be between 50,000 and 100,000.
Health Minister Chen stated that serious HIV/AIDS epidemics in neighboring countries may impact the domestic HIV epidemic.
Chinese health departments plan to crack down on illegal blood banks and collaborate with educational organizations to spread knowledge of AIDS.

BP Chemicals signed a letter of intent with Shanghai Petrochemical Co Ltd to establish a $2.5 billion ethylene plant in Shanghai.
The plant will have the capacity to produce 650,000 tonnes of ethylene per year.
Zhang Jianning, BP's Beijing manager of government affairs, stated that this project represents a significant development for BP in China.
BP's previous investments in China have primarily focused on upstream activities such as drilling and exploration.
Analysts predict significant growth in China's downstream petrochemicals industry due to increasing demand for products like ethylene.
Shanghai Petrochemical is majority-owned by China Petrochemical Corp, also known as Sinopec.
Lian Xiaolu, deputy director of Shanghai Petrochemical, indicated that a feasibility study for the project could take up to two years.
Completion of the ethylene plant could take up to eight years.
BP will hold a 50 percent stake in the ethylene plant, with the remaining stake held by Shanghai Petrochemical or shared with Sinopec.
Sinopec plans to increase its ethylene production capacity to around five million tonnes per year by 2000.

China claims it can produce enough grain to feed its growing population despite challenges.
The Chinese government released a draft white paper to address foreign concerns about potential grain shortages.
Agricultural officials stated that China could feed its population for decades.
The draft white paper asserts that China will contribute positively to the world's grain supply.
Some Western analysts believe China's expanding economy increases its demand for grain.
The Ministry of Agriculture's draft white paper dismisses Western fears about China's agricultural capabilities.
The document references historical skepticism towards China's ability to feed its population after the 1949 revolution.
China is expected to raise grain output by improving farmland protection, efficiency, irrigation, and reclaiming wasteland.
By 2000, China's population was projected to reach 1.3 billion, with a grain demand of 500 million tonnes.
By 2030, China's population is expected to peak at 1.6 billion, with a grain demand of around 640 million tonnes.

China stated that the jailing of dissident Wang Dan for 11 years is an ordinary legal matter.
A Chinese court sentenced Wang Dan for plotting against the government.
The trial of Wang Dan lasted less than four hours.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang claimed the trial would not harm Sino-U.S. relations.
Shen Guofang asserted that Wang Dan's case is unrelated to human rights issues.
Wang Dan was sentenced to 11 years in prison and stripped of political rights for two additional years.
International human rights activists condemned Wang Dan's trial as unfair.
Amnesty International described Wang Dan's trial as a parody of justice.
Foreign reporters were barred from attending Wang Dan's trial.
Wang Dan had previously served four years in prison for his involvement in the 1989 pro-democracy protests.

Chinese state media criticized a U.S.-funded radio news station on Friday.
The criticism included accusations of increased 'Cold War propaganda' by the United States and Western nations against Beijing.
Radio Free Asia broadcasts news to China in Chinese and was launched by the U.S. government.
The China Youth Daily claimed that Radio Free Asia aims to create chaos and sow dissent in Asian nations.
U.S. Undersecretary of State Lynn Davis visited China for talks on arms proliferation.
Secretary of State Warren Christopher is scheduled to visit China later this month.
The purpose of Christopher's visit is to improve U.S.-China relations, which have been strained by various disputes.
Chinese state media expressed a hostile tone regarding U.S.-China relations despite claims of warming ties.
China previously requested that the U.S. shut down Radio Free Asia, which was created by the U.S. Congress.
U.S. officials stated that Radio Free Asia's broadcasts would continue, and the station plans to expand its news coverage.

A senior U.S. arms control official expressed encouragement regarding Chinese efforts to control exports to unsafeguarded nuclear facilities.
Beijing stated that the main issue in recent talks was Taiwan.
The United States has been assisting China in placing controls on exports following a pledge by Beijing in May not to sell nuclear technology to Pakistan.
U.S. Undersecretary of State Lynn Davis made statements during a news conference about the progress in arms proliferation talks in Beijing.
Davis noted that there has been real success in China's commitments regarding proliferation and nuclear assistance to unsafeguarded facilities.
Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen urged the U.S. to cease arms sales to Taiwan during a meeting with Davis.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman stated that U.S. weapons sales to Taiwan are the primary issue in Sino-U.S. arms proliferation discussions.
The spokesman claimed that the U.S. violated the August 17 communique by exporting advanced weapons to Taiwan.
Cui Tiankai, the Foreign Ministry spokesman, indicated that the U.S. had broken its pledge to reduce arms sales to Taiwan.
In August, the U.S. Defence Department notified Congress of plans to sell Stinger missiles and launchers to Taiwan, which led to protests from China.

Beijing is hoping for a new post-election approach from Washington after four years of strained Sino-U.S. ties.
Bill Clinton won the election on Tuesday, which may not change the occupant in the White House.
Beijing hopes for a transformation of Clinton's policy on China during his second term.
Tong Tianqi, an international relations researcher, stated that Clinton may take a practical approach now that he does not need to attract votes.
Relations between Beijing and Washington have been strained by disputes over trade, human rights, arms proliferation, and Taiwan.
Both sides report that ties have warmed recently after high-level meetings.
Chinese officials welcome Clinton's victory as it represents stability in U.S. policy.
Clinton is a familiar face to Beijing leadership, and his understanding of China has grown over his first term.
China accuses the U.S. of obstructing its accession to the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
U.S. officials argue that China must do more to open its markets for favorable WTO terms.

Chinese leaders denounced Beijing's exclusion from the World Trade Organisation (WTO) as unjust.
Chinese minister for economic restructuring Li Tieying stated that protectionism or trade sanctions should not be policy tools in a world dependent on international trade.
Li Tieying claimed that a World Trade Organisation without China is incomplete.
