Intel's stock rose by $4.75 to an all-time high of $118.75 on Nasdaq following the news.
Texas Instruments' stock increased by $4.25 to $53 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Hewlett-Packard Co will launch a new type of printer called the 'mopier' to compete with copy machines.
The HP LaserJet 5Si Mopier allows users to make multiple original prints from their desktop.
Hewlett-Packard aims to capture a share of the $18.5 billion copier market with the new model.
Analysts predict that the mopier will challenge Xerox Corp and other copier manufacturers.
Sales revenues of mid-range copiers are projected to decline by $300 million to $1 billion by 2000.
Robert Fennell, an industry analyst at Dataquest, stated that the situation presents both a challenge and an opportunity for Xerox.
The market for midrange printers based on Canon Inc's engine is expected to grow by 500 percent this year compared to 1995.
The Mopier has a U.S. list price of $9,549, which is lower than midrange copiers priced between $13,000 and $20,000.
The Mopier includes features such as stapling and collating, and has a user-friendly interface.
The Mopier is designed to reduce the time spent by office workers on printing tasks and to decrease network traffic.

A product allows users to exchange electronic mail securely.
The product is popular among older adults in America.
USWeb Networks provides strong encryption on television-based Internet browsing devices.
U.S. Cold War munitions laws prohibit the export of strong encryption.
WebTV uses the strongest coding standard available for consumer communications.
Steve Perlman is the co-founder and chief executive of WebTV Networks.
WebTV employs 128-bit encryption, similar to that used in U.S. government communications.
Using a credit card over WebTV's encrypted communications is safer than using a telephone.
The Silicon Valley tech community supports WebTV's use of strong encryption.
Laws against the export of encryption date back to the Cold War.

International Business Machines Corp's Lotus Development Corp unveiled SmartSuite 97.
SmartSuite 97 will begin shipping in January.
Lotus President Jeff Papows stated that the company will continue to add Internet functionality.
A further upgrade for SmartSuite 97 is planned for the first quarter of 1998.
Jeff Papows commented on Netscape Communications Corp's ambitions in the corporate marketplace.
Lotus plans to build new features into its applications suite while undercutting Microsoft Corp's prices.
The estimated retail price of SmartSuite 97 is $399.
Current Lotus applications users can upgrade for $149.
Users purchasing SmartSuite by year-end 1996 will receive a free upgrade and a $50 rebate, making the effective price $99.
Users of certain recent Corel applications can trade them in for a free CD upgrade to SmartSuite by year-end.

Softbank Chief Executive Officer Masahoshi Son stated that the company will focus on growing its businesses organically and preparing for the launch of JSkyB over the next year or two.
Son mentioned that Softbank has completed commitments to 51 Internet startup companies from its venture capital fund, totaling $350 million.
The $350 million includes approximately $170 million from investment partners and the remainder from Softbank itself.
Softbank launched a 50-50 joint venture with Rupert Murdoch's News Corp in a digital satellite system known as Japan Sky Broadcasting, or JSkyB.
In June, Softbank and News Corp acquired 21.4 percent of Asahi National Broadcasting of Japan.
Softbank has become the world's largest computer-related magazine and book publisher and the largest producer of high-tech exhibitions and trade shows.
Softbank is also Japan's largest computer software, peripherals, and systems distributor.
Son's comments indicate a temporary halt to a buying spree that included the purchase of an 80 percent stake in Kingston Technology Corp for approximately $1.5 billion.
Softbank closed on a $2.1 billion acquisition of Ziff-Davis Publishing within the past year.
Softbank spent approximately $800 million for the Interface Group, which includes Comdex, the largest U.S. trade show.

The browser wars have shifted to a competition for efficient content delivery over the Internet.
The competition is moving from a 'pull' model to a 'push' model for information delivery.
Eli Barkat is the chief executive of BackWeb Technologies, a start-up based in San Jose, California.
Vivek Ranadive is the president of Reuters Holdings Plc's Tibco Inc. unit.
Electronic commerce over the Internet is expected to increase in 1997.
More than a dozen small high-tech start-ups are trying to define the content delivery space.
Jack Wilson is the managing editor of Technologic Partners' ComputerLetter.
There are over 50 million Web pages cataloged by search engines.
Many companies want to update customers and suppliers directly.
Ex Machina is providing a wireless news alerting system made by Global Village Communication Inc.

John Young is searching for a new manager to lead Novell Inc.
John Young was selected by Novell's board of directors to recruit new leadership.
Robert Frankenberg was the chairman and CEO of Novell for two years before the board decided to change direction.
John Young previously served as the CEO of Hewlett-Packard Co for 15 years until 1992.
Young does not intend to remain as chairman after completing the search for a new CEO.
Young estimates that the executive search will take four to six months if everything goes well.
Novell plans to launch a $20 million worldwide brand and product advertising campaign.
Novell aims to revamp its corporate image and unveil updated products.
The company is looking for a top executive who can operate quickly and understand customer needs.
Young prefers a 'street savvy' executive over someone who rapidly launches new products like Microsoft and Netscape.

WebTV Networks Inc. unveiled a new technology that enables full-screen, television quality video delivery from the Internet through conventional telephone lines.
Steve Perlman is the co-founder and chief executive of WebTV.
The new technology will be deployed in upcoming versions of WebTV's Internet service.
WebTV is a privately held company with equity investors including Microsoft Corp., Citicorp, VeriFone Inc., Times Mirror Co. Inc., and Lauder Partners.
The new technology, named VideoFlash, was demonstrated publicly for the first time at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas.
VideoFlash significantly speeds download times and increases video quality compared to existing systems.
National Geographic stated that VideoFlash is the first technology to provide acceptable quality video over an Internet link.
Larry Lux, vice president of National Geographic Interactive, claimed VideoFlash allows for a visual experience comparable to their television programming.
VideoFlash can achieve three to 10 times the video compression rates of existing technologies like MPEG.
Previous technology could take up to half an hour to download a 30-second video clip with poor quality.

Sun Microsystems Inc. reported a 41 percent increase in profits for the latest quarter.
The company's net income for the fiscal second quarter ended Dec. 29 was $178.3 million, up from $126 million a year ago.
Earnings per share increased to 46 cents from 32 cents.
Revenues rose nearly 19 percent to $2.08 billion.
The per share earnings exceeded Wall Street expectations of 42 cents, according to First Call.
Sun Microsystems Chief Financial Officer Michael Lehman stated that the current fiscal year is yielding strong financial results.
Lehman noted that Sun is gaining success in corporate intranets, the Internet, and extranets.
Gross profit margins increased to 50.4 percent, up more than 5 percentage points from the previous year.
Sun's order backlog rose to $470 million from $407 million in the first quarter.
Sun plans to announce new high-end computers, codenamed Starfire, next week.

Wheelock & Co Ltd is searching for a new partner for its Hong Kong fund management company.
NatWest Group has decided to withdraw from its joint venture with Wheelock NatWest Ltd.
Nicholas Sibley is the deputy chairman of Wheelock NatWest Ltd, a 50-50 joint venture between Wheelock and National Westminster Bank Plc.
NatWest wants to dispose of its stake in the fund management division after acquiring Gartmore Plc for 472 million stg.
Sibley stated that NatWest's acquisition of Gartmore means they will not provide support for Wheelock NatWest Investment Management.
Sibley expressed disappointment at NatWest's decision but stated that the corporate finance and equity stockbroking divisions are not at risk.
The joint venture became fully operational one year ago and offers corporate finance, equity stockbroking, and investment management services in Hong Kong.
Sibley noted that NatWest needed to improve its fund management capabilities, which the acquisition of Gartmore addressed.
Wheelock NatWest Investment Management is experiencing rising commissions and has recently completed its research division.
Sibley indicated that the firm expects significant growth in commissions over the next six months as they can offer full services to major institutions.

Ambitious plans to establish Islamic mutual funds in Indonesia include the cleansing of profits disallowed under Islamic law.
Islamic law prohibits Moslems from earning interest on bank deposits or investing in certain types of equities.
Nik Ezar Nik Bolia is the chief executive officer of Malaysia's DCB-RHB Unit Trust Management Berhad.
DCB-RHB has developed a method to work around Islamic law regarding interest.
The cleansing process removes the impact of interest earned and donates a portion of the total profit to charity.
DCB-RHB has attracted US$80 million into a domestic Islamic fund in Malaysia.
54 percent of Malaysia's population is Moslem.
More than 85 percent of Indonesia's population of nearly 200 million is Moslem.
Southeast Asia has a combined population of 220 million Moslems.
Malaysia's Bank of Islam has established panels of scholars to vet individual stocks for compliance with Sharia law.

NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank, agreed to buy out Wheelock and Company Ltd's stake in their joint venture, Wheelock NatWest.
The joint venture was a 50-50 partnership between NatWest Markets and Wheelock.
The announcement marks the end of the association between NatWest Markets and Wheelock.
Wheelock is a Hong Kong-based conglomerate led by Peter Woo Kwong-Ching.
NatWest Markets stated that recent trading scandals have complicated joint ventures under British rules in Asian markets.
John Howland-Jackson is the newly appointed chairman for Asia Pacific at NatWest Markets.
Both partners contributed US$125 million in capital towards the joint venture before ending their partnership.
NatWest Markets previously announced it was exiting the fund management arm of the joint venture due to its acquisition of Gartmore Plc.
Vincent Kwan, an analyst at Vickers Ballas, suggested that the acquisition may have caused disagreements between the shareholders.
Nicholas Sibley, managing director of Wheelock Capital, stated that Wheelock has no immediate plans to replace the joint venture with another financial services subsidiary.

Foreign cash is stable in Thailand, anticipating economic and stock market recovery.
Christopher Day, joint managing director at Thornton Management (Asia) Ltd, believes Thailand's recovery will be slow.
Most funds are neutral on Thailand compared to Morgan Stanley's Far East Asia ex-Japan free index.
Salomon Brothers reported that funds are neutral to overweight, while Nomura Research Institute indicated funds are neutral to underweight.
Thailand's stock exchange data showed a one-percent retail fund sell-off in October, leading most funds to a neutral position.
Stephen Leung, BZW Asia's chief investment officer, stated that the worst of the political and economic situation should be over.
Investor nervousness has decreased following the election of a new coalition government led by the New Aspiration Party.
The immediate direction of Thailand's SET index depends on cabinet appointments and new economic measures.
Christine Rowley, investment manager with LGT Asset Management, suggested a potential rally in the SET index if coalition leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh appoints capable cabinet members.
Jardine Fleming has lowered its corporate earnings forecast for 1996 from 14 percent to four percent due to declining price-earnings ratios.

Chinese planners aim to use domestic savings to build capital markets.
Andrew Lo is the chairman of the Hong Kong Investment Funds Association.
Lo met Vice-Premier Zhu Rhongji in Beijing.
Zhu Rhongji stated that China will release rules and regulations for a domestic funds industry by the end of the year.
Lo confirmed that Hong Kong's position as a financial center will continue after the handover to Chinese rule.
China views the development of capital markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen as complementary to Hong Kong.
China recognizes the importance of an active funds management industry for its national economy.
China's underdeveloped capital markets and non-convertible currency hinder foreign access to its funds industry.
Foreign investors are expected to provide expertise for the development of China's domestic funds industry.
Training sessions are being organized in Hong Kong by the Hong Kong Investment Funds Association and the Securities and Futures Commission.

Asian fund managers reported that California pension funds are expected to invest in Asia over the next five to ten years.
Richard Nicholas, managing director at Hambro Pacific Fund Management, stated that the pension funds have issued a positive assessment of Asia.
Seven pension funds with combined assets of $234 billion are exploring investment opportunities in Asia.
Christopher Ryan, managing director at HSBC Asset Management, noted that the presence of U.S. fund managers indicates renewed interest in Asia after previous economic slumps.
Ryan mentioned that the peak of U.S. investment activity in Asia occurred in 1993, but interest is building again.
William Crist, board president of CALPERS, indicated that the Shanghai Stock Exchange is currently too small and opaque for investment.
CALPERS, which manages $107 billion, is expected to focus on private equity stakes rather than purchasing shares in listed companies.
Ryan suggested that there will be increased interest in private equity funds and infrastructure investments.
Nicholas expressed that U.S. pension funds are recognizing Asia's economic health and the potential for regional portfolio allocation to reach 12 percent by the early 2000s.
Nicholas described the recent slowdown in Southeast Asia as a natural phase of economic development.

Investing in Asian telecommunications stocks involves risks due to a lack of sophistication and discrepancies in demand and regulation.
Analysts agree that telecom regulation is the most important factor affecting future performance of stocks in the region.
Jardine Fleming stated that understanding regulators is essential as regulatory issues significantly influenced Asian telecom stock performance last year.
Asian telecom regulators have promoted liberalization despite facing strong political and economic forces.
Regulators have issued licenses, which can negatively impact the prospects of primary telecom firms.
In low-penetration countries, issuing licenses is acceptable, but it poses risks in high-penetration markets like Hong Kong and Singapore.
Deregulation in Hong Kong and Singapore has led to a negative outlook on Singapore Telecom and Hongkong Telecom.
In low-penetration countries like Indonesia and the Philippines, regulators have granted concessions to build fixed lines, benefiting local telecom firms.
New local fixed lines in Indonesia and the Philippines are expected to increase earnings for PT Telkom and Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT).
In the cellular sector, major players are concerned about the issuance of too many licenses, which has led to loss of market share to second-tier players.

U.S. fund managers representing $234 billion in assets recently toured Asia.
The California Public Employees Retirement System (CalPERS) is included in the $234 billion in assets.
Stewart Aldcroft, sales director for Templeton, stated that CalPERS raises interest among fund managers due to its large investment capacity.
CalPERS expressed a preference for direct investment over listed equity.
William Crist, CalPERS board president, noted a lack of transparency in Chinese public companies.
Foreign access to Asian markets is often restricted due to concerns about economic disruption.
Hong Kong fund managers suggested private equity funds as a potential solution for investment needs.
Marcus Thompson, deputy managing director of HSBC Private Equity Management, reported that his funds hold $560 million, mostly from U.S. pension funds.
Cesar Zalamea, managing director of AIG Investment Corp (Asia) Ltd, described his fund's performance as tremendous but did not disclose specific details.
AIG Investment Corp (Asia) Ltd manages $2.38 billion, primarily from a few large U.S. pension clients.

Central bank independence is a debated topic in Hong Kong, especially before its return to China.
Chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa suggested changes to the reporting structure at the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).
Tung Chee-hwa will take over from Governor Chris Patten on July 1 when Britain cedes control of Hong Kong to China.
Tung indicated that the head of the HKMA might report directly to the chief executive instead of the Financial Secretary.
Hong Kong's reaction to Tung's comments was largely negative.
Experts acknowledge that the HKMA's powers are more limited than those of central banks in developed nations.
Eric Nickerson, head of currency at Bank of America, suggested that an additional layer between the chief executive and the head of the central bank might be beneficial.
An economist stated that politics, not economics, is driving the debate regarding the HKMA.
The HKMA's primary function is to manage the Hong Kong dollar, which is pegged at HK$7.80 to the U.S. dollar.
HKMA chief executive Joseph Yam stated that the HKMA has never experienced political interference in monetary management.

The correction in Hong Kong stocks occurred on Thursday following the news of Deng Xiaoping's death.
Fund managers had only 10 minutes to engage in bargain hunting after the news broke.
Ambrose Chang is the chief investment officer at Daiwa Capital Management in Hong Kong.
Traders attributed the quick recovery in stocks to a significant amount of short-covering.
One fund manager stated that the recovery was driven by futures trading.
The Hang Seng index initially dipped 92 points but closed up 305.01 points at 13,411.33.
The February index future ended 405 points higher at 13,485.
A head trader noted that hedge funds were caught off guard and faced difficulties.
Fund managers expect the Hang Seng to trade within a range of 13,000 to 13,800 in the near term.
U.S. interest rates and upcoming corporate earnings are anticipated to influence market direction.

Regent Pacific Group Ltd has a US$1 billion stake in Russian equity markets.
Regent Pacific decided to unwind a fund that planned to invest in Gazprom.
Jim Mellon is the managing director of Regent Pacific Group Ltd.
Regent Pacific chose to avoid a dispute with Gazprom over a US$200 million fund.
Gazprom restricts foreign investment to nine percent of its share capital.
Gazprom issues its shares in the form of American Depositary Shares (ADRs).
ADRs trade at four times the value of Gazprom's domestic shares.
Regent's fund was incorporated in Russia but had foreign institutional fundholders.
Mellon stated that the scheme was legal but Regent backed away from the dispute with Gazprom.
Regent owns between three and four percent of Hambros Bank.

Thailand's banking sector crisis prompted calls for an upgrade of Asia's financial infrastructure at an International Monetary Fund-Hong Kong Monetary Authority meeting.
IMF managing director Michel Camdessus stated that Asia needs a stronger financial infrastructure.
The banking system in Asia has not kept pace with economic development, creating a need for an overhaul.
Camdessus noted that prudential regulation and supervision have not kept pace with the complexities of the banking business.
Camdessus warned that unaddressed gaps in banking regulation could pose dangers for stability.
Thailand intervened to demand better provisioning by its banks due to asset quality problems.
Thailand's monetary policy was hampered by its currency, the baht, being pegged to a basket of currencies dominated by the dollar.
Speculators were encouraged by Thailand's poor economic situation and weak financial sector.
Gerald Corrigan, managing director at Goldman Sachs, stated that most countries need to strengthen supervisory oversight of financial institutions.
Mahmood Pradhan, a senior economist with the IMF, warned that deregulation has increased exposure to credit and foreign exchange risk.

Hong Kong has total fiscal reserves of HK$330 billion (US$42 billion) as of the 1997/98 budget figures.
This amount translates to more than US$6,500 for each person in Hong Kong.
The gross national debt in the United States is US$5.5 trillion, equating to US$20,500 for every child born there this year.
Financial Secretary Donald Tsang did not implement tax cuts in the 1997/98 budget.
Tsang emphasized the need for continuity and collaboration with China in his budget speech.
The budget surplus for Hong Kong this year is HK$15.1 billion, projected to rise to HK$31.7 billion in 1997/98.
Critics, including Emily Lau, expressed dissatisfaction with the government's spending on the needy, particularly the elderly.
Tsang reduced duties on wine from 90 percent to 60 percent.
Experts warned that the wealth gap in Hong Kong is likely to increase due to an influx of impoverished Chinese immigrants.
In 1995, Hong Kong raised the quota for mainland immigrants to 150 per day, primarily for family reunifications.

Wang Juntao is a prominent exiled Chinese human rights activist living in the United States.
Wang Juntao stated that his contacts with detained dissident Wang Dan do not justify the capital charge against him.
Wang Juntao has prepared written testimony rejecting the charges against Wang Dan.
The U.S.-based human rights group Human Rights in China reported that Wang Juntao has turned over testimonial materials to Wang Dan's relatives.
Wang Dan played a key role in the pro-democracy demonstrations in China in 1989.
Wang Dan has been charged with plotting to overthrow the government, which carries a maximum penalty of death.
Wang Dan has been detained since May 1995.
Wang Juntao was freed from prison on medical parole in 1994 and allowed to leave China for the United States.
Wang Juntao's research centre in the United States was dedicated to studying China's modernization drive.
Wang Dan acted as an honorary director of the research centre and did not participate in its activities.

China announced it would empower Hong Kong's courts to try off-duty Chinese soldiers after resuming control over Hong Kong in 1997.
The National People's Congress was expected to pass a law regarding criminal and civil cases involving troops stationed in Hong Kong.
Crimes committed by off-duty personnel will be handled by the courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Criminal cases involving on-duty soldiers will be handled by military courts.
Civil rights offences committed by off-duty members of the Chinese garrison will be dealt with by Hong Kong courts.
Civil rights offences committed by soldiers while on duty will be referred to China's Supreme People's Court.
Chinese lawmakers referenced British army practices in Hong Kong while drafting the measures.
Defence operations of the People's Liberation Army will not be subject to Hong Kong courts.
Troops stationed in Hong Kong will notify the Hong Kong SAR government in advance of military drills involving public interest.
Military personnel will be forbidden from participating in political or religious organisations in Hong Kong.

China stated that Sino-U.S. trade ties have improved.
China warned that major problems, including its delayed entry into the World Trade Organisation (WTO), still need resolution.
China hinted at possible retaliation against a U.S. decision to impose punitive charges on Chinese textile quotas.
Wu Yi, China's Foreign Trade Minister, said that two major issues concerning Sino-U.S. economic links need to be settled.
The two issues are China's failure to join the WTO and the lack of permanent Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trade status for Chinese goods in the U.S. market.
High-level exchanges between Beijing and Washington have helped ease friction over various issues.
Wu stated that the tension in the Sino-U.S. relationship has been alleviated.
Further progress in Sino-U.S. relations depends on Washington's stance towards China's entry into the WTO and its yearly review of MFN.
Washington annually reviews China's MFN status, which grants the lowest possible tariffs to trading partners.
China is one of the United States' largest trading partners, with U.S. companies selling about $12 billion worth of goods to China last year.

China is starting a new professional basketball league called the China New Basketball Alliance.
The China New Basketball Alliance was established by the State Sports Commission and Spectrum, a Hong Kong-based sports promotion company.
The new league aims to provide an alternative to the China Basketball Association, which consists entirely of Chinese players.
The China New Basketball Alliance will use National Basketball Association (NBA) rules.
Revenue for the league will be generated through ticket sales and television advertising.
Each of the eight teams in the league has hired four players and a head coach from the United States.
Only two American players from each team will be allowed on the court at any one time.
American players have been in China for weeks training with their new teammates.
U.S. coaches use translators to communicate with players during practice.
China's national basketball team finished eighth in the Atlanta Olympics, their best-ever performance.

China's Communist Party is promoting socialist values in Tibet.
The Communist Party has called for textbooks and publications to emphasize historical links between Tibet and China.
Delegates at a Communist Party meeting urged Tibet to adopt 'spiritual civilisation' to counter the influence of the Dalai Lama.
The Tibet Daily stated that protecting the unity of China and opposing the Dalai Lama's activities is a major task for building spiritual civilisation.
The Tibet Daily claimed that school textbooks and publications must reinforce the historical connections between Tibet and China.
Beijing asserts that Tibet has been part of China for centuries, a claim disputed by many Tibetans who seek independence.
The Tibet Daily emphasized the need for society to firmly establish the belief that Tibet is an inseparable part of China.
The Dalai Lama, who fled to India in 1959, is accused by the Tibet Daily of distorting religion to divide Tibet from China.
The Tibet Daily criticized the Dalai Lama's followers for allegedly inciting anti-Chinese protests.
China has called for increased promotion of atheism in Tibet, arguing that religious beliefs hinder economic development.

Chinese President Jiang Zemin will travel to Moscow in spring for a summit with Russian leader Boris Yeltsin.
The official Xinhua news agency reported that Jiang and Yeltsin are expected to sign agreements on arms reductions along the 4,300-km Sino-Russian border.
Chinese Premier Li Peng is scheduled to visit Moscow next month.
The forthcoming trips by Jiang and Li to Moscow were announced during a visit to China by Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.
Primakov met with both Jiang and Li during his visit.
Jiang stated that China's long-term policy towards Russia is based on good neighbourly friendship, equality, trust, mutually beneficial cooperation, and joint development.
Jiang emphasized that this guiding principle will not change despite any situational changes.
Jiang and Yeltsin last met during Yeltsin's tour of China in April.
Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen stated that both countries aim to make their border a bond of peace, stability, cooperation, and prosperity.
China and Russia reached a basic agreement on border demarcation in 1991.

Xujiachong village is located in Hubei province, China.
The village has a population of 2,480 people.
Xujiachong village is scheduled to be destroyed by the end of next year.
The destruction is due to the Three Gorges dam project, which will flood the area.
The Three Gorges project will relocate approximately 840,000 people from submerged areas.
Wang Jiazhu is the deputy general manager of the China Yangtze Three Gorges Project Development Co.
The estimated total number of people to be relocated could reach 1.2 million.
More than 12,300 people have already been resettled from Yichang county.
The evacuation of the reservoir area began in 1994 and will involve moving about 100,000 people from Yichang county.
The Three Gorges dam project was approved by Beijing in 1992.

China has sentenced two democracy activists to hard labour.
Fu Guoyong was sentenced to three years of re-education through labour.
Chen Ping was sentenced to one year of labour reform.
The sentences were reported by a fellow dissident to Reuters.
The activists were sentenced for publishing articles abroad about democracy.
Authorities branded their essays as counter-revolutionary.
Fu Guoyong was detained in late July for illegal political activities.
Chen Ping was arrested in August and sentenced alongside Fu.
Fu Guoyong previously served two years in a labour camp for his role in the Tiananmen Square demonstrations.
China is currently experiencing a crackdown on dissent.

China stated that Deng Xiaoping's health is relatively good and has not changed dramatically.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang commented on Deng's health during a news briefing.
Deng Xiaoping has not been seen in public since early 1994.
Speculation about Deng's health includes rumors of a recent hospital admission and reports of him being at home.
Deng has expressed a desire to witness the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule on June 30.
Deng oversaw the negotiations for the return of Hong Kong from British rule.
Deng's health has been a topic of speculation due to concerns about a potential power struggle following his death.
China Central Television is airing a documentary series about Deng's life.
President Jiang Zemin is considered the likely successor to Deng's political influence.
Analysts believe the documentary series was created to enhance Deng's image.

A U.S. forensics team has arrived in China to recover the remains of crew members from a crashed World War Two bomber.
The team is from the U.S. Department of Defence.
The focus of the team is to recover and identify the remains of the bomber's crew.
The bomber crashed on August 31, 1944, near Guilin, China.
The crash occurred while the bomber was returning from a bombing raid on Japanese ships around Taiwan.
Local villagers discovered the wreckage in a remote ravine last October.
U.S. officials learned of the wreckage when Chinese President Jiang Zemin provided a video and photographs to U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian gave U.S. Secretary of Defence William Perry two dog tags recovered from the crash site.
The Chinese government has cooperated in arranging the repatriation of the remains.
The cause of the crash is still unknown, and the forensic team will not investigate it during this trip.

China announced support for Hong Kong's efforts to expand foreign trade relations after the territory returns to Beijing's control in mid-1997, provided these efforts do not undermine China's sovereignty.
An Min, vice-minister of foreign trade, stated that Hong Kong would pursue a free trade policy to allow the free flow of commodities and capital after China resumes control.
Hong Kong will be allowed to formulate its own economic and trade regulations as long as they conform with the Basic Law, which is the territory's mini-constitution promulgated by Beijing.
All existing laws in Hong Kong will remain in force, except those that contradict the Basic Law or require amendments by the Hong Kong SAR legislature.
Hong Kong businessmen will retain preferential tax status for investments on the Chinese mainland after 1997.
China's tax laws will not apply to the Special Administrative Region, and Hong Kong compatriots will continue to receive preferential treatment given to foreign investors.
Foreign investors in China are subject to various fees that local businessmen do not have to pay, and they must hire employees through special government agencies.
Chinese firms will not enjoy any privileges when investing in Hong Kong after the handover, and mainland companies will be treated as overseas investors.
An Min stated that Chinese enterprises must follow internationally prevailing economic and trade rules and local regulations.
China proposed to abolish a series of laws on democratic elections and civil liberties when it resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong.

China warned Taiwan not to seek independence from the communist mainland.
China hinted that Taiwan would face disaster if it insisted on splitting from the mainland.
Taipei failed to respond to a 1995 call by Chinese President Jiang Zemin for reconciliation.
The official Xinhua news agency stated that Taiwan actively sought to separate from mainland China.
Xinhua urged Taiwan authorities to recognize that Taiwan is part of China.
Beijing views Taiwan as a rebel province and does not rule out the use of force to recover it.
Xinhua's commentary suggested the possibility of resuming quasi-official talks if Taiwan showed a sincere desire for unification.
Taiwan officials have dismissed Jiang's conciliatory gestures and are working to block economic and trade links with China.
Xinhua accused Taiwan authorities of advocating separation and undermining China's sovereignty.
Taiwan has prohibited direct trade and transport links with the mainland since 1949.

B.A.T Industries announced it is considering restructuring its operations.
B.A.T is searching for a partner for its financial services businesses.
B.A.T declined to comment on reports of failed talks with Commercial Union Plc.
Commercial Union Plc did not confirm or deny the rumors regarding talks with B.A.T.
B.A.T shares increased by 17p to 468-1/2p following the deal talk.
A spokesman for B.A.T stated that the company's position has not changed.
B.A.T has ruled out a demerger in the past but is now keeping an open mind.
B.A.T faces pressure to enhance shareholder value due to poor share price performance.
Litigation exposure in the U.S. tobacco business has negatively impacted B.A.T's share price.
Analysts suggest that B.A.T is looking for a partner to achieve critical mass in the competitive market.

Shares in British insurer Commercial Union (CU) increased on Friday.
Speculation exists that CU may be involved in a merger as part of industry consolidation.
CU shares closed at 663-1/2p after rising 19-1/2p in late trading.
BAT Industries has been linked to recent merger rumors with CU.
Both CU and BAT Industries have not confirmed whether merger discussions occurred.
BAT Industries stated it is open to finding a partner for its financial services arm.
The insurance industry in Britain is becoming increasingly competitive and fragmented.
Direct Line and other new entrants are contributing to increased competition in insurance sales.
Royal Insurance and Sun Alliance merged in July to form Britain's largest insurer.
Cost savings from a merger between CU and BAT Industries could increase combined operating profits by 20 percent.

Britain's Ladbroke Group Plc formed a global alliance with Hilton Hotels Corp.
The alliance reunites the Hilton brand worldwide for the first time in 32 years.
The agreement covers 400 hotels in 49 countries.
Ladbroke and Hilton denied any hidden agenda for a full merger.
Ladbroke Chief Executive Peter George stated the alliance is a first step in bringing the hotels business closer.
The deal includes sales and marketing, frequent customer programs, and development.
The alliance aims to fuel top-line growth and reduce confusion between the two groups.
Hilton has operated separately within and outside the U.S. since 1964.
HHC Chief Executive Stephen Bollenbach stated customers will perceive the companies as one for the first time in 32 years.
The companies plan to launch a worldwide loyalty program called Hilton HHonors Worldwide on February 1.

Lowndes Lambert Group Holdings Plc and Fenchurch Plc are merging.
Both companies are based in London.
The merger aims to cut costs and address falling margins in insurance broking.
The companies believe the merger will benefit clients, employees, and shareholders.
The merger is a response to industry over-capacity and intense competition.
The deal is expected to create a stronger and more competitive group.
Cost savings of at least five million pounds are anticipated within 12 months.
Fenchurch shareholders will receive 628 shares in the new company for every 1,000 shares they hold.
The new company will be named Lambert Fenchurch Group.
Lowndes reported a nine percent fall in pre-tax profits to 13.9 million pounds.

Abbey National called for Scottish Amicable to pause proposals to drop its mutual status.
Abbey National requested that policyholders be given time to consider an offer for Scottish Amicable.
Scottish Amicable rejected Abbey National's demand and requests for access to its financial information.
Scottish Amicable stated it would proceed with its plans according to its own timetable.
A spokesman for Scottish Amicable claimed that policyholders should receive information before Abbey National.
Scottish Amicable's plans for demutualisation and flotation are set to be published next week.
Abbey National argued that policyholders should compare ScotAm's plans with alternative offers.
Abbey National's offer is described as a firm offer based on published information.
Industry observers expect Abbey National's move to prompt an auction for Scottish Amicable.
Prudential expressed interest in the situation and is looking for acquisitions in the life assurance sector.

Willis Corroon reported a rise in 1996 profits.
Willis Corroon assessed that the insurance industry is facing problems of overcapacity and falling rates.
The company stated that insurance rates are declining almost universally.
Competition in the U.S. retail market is intensifying according to Willis Corroon.
Willis warned that the rise in sterling reduced 1996 profits by 3.1 million pounds.
Willis indicated that the reduced profits may impact 1997 results.
Profits from its Lloyd's members agency are unlikely to match the 1996 level.
Willis unveiled pre-tax profits for 1996 of 91.6 million pounds, an 83 percent increase over 1995.
Stripping out exceptional charges and disposals, profits from continuing operations were up 13 percent at 89.1 million pounds.
Willis's shares slipped eight pence to 131-1/2 pence after the results were announced.

Britons must reveal the results of genetic tests to obtain new life insurance policies under a new policy by the Association of British Insurers (ABI).
Life insurers will not require applicants to take genetic tests under the new scheme, which will last for two years.
The new policy is supported by all 440 member companies of the ABI.
The policy is a response to advancements in genetics in recent years.
Many U.S. insurance companies require applicants to undergo genetic testing.
Currently, Britons are asked to provide results of tests they have already undergone but are not required to take new tests for insurance qualification.
Doctors can diagnose common single gene defects and screen for susceptibility to certain cancers.
Experts predict that it will soon be possible to assess the risk of more common disorders like diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis.
The ABI spokesman stated that new genetic tests could benefit individuals by allowing them to adjust their lifestyles according to their health risks.
The ABI emphasized the importance of monitoring genetic test results to understand their financial impact on insurance companies.

Guardian Royal Exchange PLC reported a sharp fall in 1996 profits.
The company is considering a major acquisition within the next twelve months, possibly in the life sector.
Guardian attributed the profits decline to tough competition and the worst catastrophe weather claims in the U.S. in 75 years.
Bad weather and continuing subsidence losses in Britain also contributed to the profits decline.
Guardian may spend around one billion pounds ($1.6 billion) on a life acquisition.
The company has no plans to return capital to shareholders.
Guardian is not a major player in the UK life market.
An acquisition could provide Guardian with critical mass and economies of scale.
Analysts expressed concern about the possible goodwill write off from an acquisition.
Guardian's trading profits for 1996 were down over 17 percent at 281 million pounds before restructuring costs.

Prudential Corp Plc is Britain's largest life insurance group.
Prudential reported a rise in profits and expects strong performance in British operations for the coming year.
Prudential did not disclose details about negotiations with the Department of Trade and Industry regarding orphan assets.
Finance director Jonathan Bloomer stated that discussions with the DTI are ongoing and may take a long time.
Analysts believe Prudential aims to free up around three billion pounds of orphan assets.
Prudential's operating profits for the year rose over eight percent to 873 million pounds.
Profits from continuing operations were reported at 691 million pounds.
The dividend was raised by 10 percent to 17.3 pence per share.
Pru shares increased by seven pence to 570 pence by mid-morning following the profit announcement.
Chief executive Sir Peter Davis described the year as very successful and highlighted the strength of the group's core business.

The battle for control of Scottish Amicable became a three-way race on Friday.
Scottish Amicable received three initial bids from Abbey National Plc, Prudential Corp Plc, and Australian Mutual Provident (AMP).
Details of the bids were not released by Scottish Amicable.
A source close to the deal stated that it was unrealistic for other bidders to enter at this stage.
ScotAm agreed to make firm offers public if required by a bidder, but none had requested this.
The auction is a sealed-bid process, preventing bidders from seeing competing offers.
Jonathan Schwarz, AMP development director, stated that conducting discussions in public would be unwise.
Both Prudential and Abbey National had no additional comments beyond earlier statements.
Discussions with the three companies aim to obtain final offers by mid-March.
ScotAm chairman Sandy Stewart described the three proposals as an excellent outcome for this phase.

Royal & Sun Alliance Group Plc reported lower results in its first year since merging.
The company will seek shareholder approval to buy back up to five percent of its shares.
Large provisions for U.S. environmental claims and the strength of the pound negatively impacted the reported figures.
The group was formed through a six billion pound merger last year.
Operating profits fell to 706 million pounds from 915 million pounds in 1995 for the combined group.
The company's shares closed down 9-1/2 pence at 494 pence after an initial gain on buyback news.
A lower-than-expected net asset value and poor performance in the British motor insurance market contributed to market disappointment.
The company set aside 167 million pounds in provisions for U.S. asbestos and environmental claims from the 1960s and 1970s.
The dividend for the year was raised to 19 pence per share.
The operating figures did not include 201 million pounds related to consolidation costs, which were higher than analysts expected.

Three companies are expected to be in the running for control of Scottish Amicable at the deadline for final offers on Friday evening.
The companies are Prudential Corp, Australian Mutual Provident (AMP), and Abbey National.
The ScotAm board and its advisers SBC Warburg will weigh the offers.
A source close to Warburgs indicated that no additional bidders from outside the three front-runners are anticipated.
The evaluation of the offers is likely to occur behind closed doors.
None of the likely bidders have opted to make public details of their proposals.
ScotAm agreed to publish details of offers if requested by a bidder, but none have made such a request.
A source close to one of the bidders stated that they are not currently asking for their bid to be revealed.
ScotAm has established confidentiality agreements and requires acceptance of the board's final decision.
ScotAm has arranged for an independent tribunal to resolve any disputes arising from the takeover battle.

About three million Norwich Union policyholders will receive free shares under flotation plans.
The flotation plans announced on Thursday would value Norwich Union at about five billion pounds ($8 billion).
Almost two million policyholders will receive shares worth 800 pounds on average.
One million non-profit members will receive shares worth between 330 and 400 pounds.
The flotation is scheduled for June and is the first by a British insurer.
Norwich Union will rank among Britain's largest 50 companies after the flotation.
Norwich Union's 10,000 employees will each receive 150 shares.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson estimated the shares would be worth between 220 and 265 pence each if listed at the end of February.
Norwich Union plans to raise an additional 1.75 billion pounds through a new share offer in May.
Members will vote on the proposals at an extraordinary meeting in London on April 18.

A leading Chinese dissident, Wang Xizhe, has fled to Hong Kong.
Wang Xizhe is reported to be seeking asylum in the United States.
Wang was seen in Hong Kong and appeared to be in good health.
Wang has been missing from his home in Guangdong since Liu Xiaobo was arrested.
Liu Xiaobo was ordered to serve three years in a labour camp.
Wang started planning his departure after Liu Xiaobo's arrest.
Wang approached the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of the Democratic Movement in China for help.
The Hong Kong Alliance requested assistance from the Hong Kong government for Wang's asylum application.
Wang could leave Hong Kong for the United States as early as Sunday night.
Wang Xizhe had been active in recent months, issuing open letters to the government.

Wang Dan, a Chinese dissident, was sentenced to 11 years in prison in Beijing.
The sentencing of Wang Dan raised concerns in Hong Kong about potential restrictions on freedoms after the territory reverts to China.
Hong Kong activists condemned the verdict against Wang Dan.
A human rights group plans to lobby for a resolution at the United Nations to condemn China's human rights record.
A Beijing court found Wang Dan guilty of conspiring to subvert the government.
Wang Dan faced a potential maximum penalty of death for his charge.
Wang Dan was stripped of political rights for two years as part of his sentencing.
The trial of Wang Dan lasted less than four hours.
Legislator Bruce Liu expressed concerns that the Chinese government might apply similar standards in Hong Kong.
Robin Munro, director of the Hong Kong office of Human Rights Watch Asia, criticized the trial as extraordinarily short and a farce.

China's central bank governor, Dai Xianglong, stated that China would support Hong Kong's financial markets if requested after the handover.
Dai Xianglong expressed confidence in the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's ability to manage financial fluctuations.
Hong Kong will revert to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, 1997, under joint Sino-British treaties.
Hong Kong will maintain its own separate financial regime and currency after the handover.
Dai Xianglong denied reports of a 300 billion yuan fund being created to stabilize Hong Kong's financial markets.
The People's Bank of China will not replace the Hong Kong Monetary Authority or establish branches in Hong Kong.
Mainland financial institutions in Hong Kong will be subject to the same regulatory standards as local firms.
Beijing will not levy any tax in Hong Kong or use Hong Kong's Exchange Fund or other assets.
Mainland companies in Hong Kong's market will be treated equally to foreign or Hong Kong firms.
Dai Xianglong stated that while Shanghai's financial status will improve, it will not replace Hong Kong as an international financial center for a considerable time.

Commercial sponsors are supporting the annual Grand Prix in Macau.
There are concerns that a new Formula One track in Zhuhai, China, may attract sponsors away from Macau's Formula Three race.
Macau does not have a dedicated racing track; the race is held on the streets of the enclave.
This year, Macau has numerous sponsors including Elf, Budweiser, Corona, Omega, and Yokohama.
Stephanie de Kantzow, an organiser of the Macau Formula Three Grand Prix, stated that Zhuhai has not significantly impacted Macau's sponsorship.
The Macau Grand Prix began in 1954 and features a 6.2 km (3.8 miles) street circuit.
Notable past competitors in the Macau Grand Prix include Michael Schumacher and Damon Hill.
Yu Binglin, vice-mayor of Zhuhai, claimed that China does not intend to diminish Macau's role in international motor racing.
Elf's director of commercial activities, Michael Bonnet, expressed that as long as the Formula Three Grand Prix exists in Macau, Elf will continue to sponsor it.
Elf aims to establish motor racing schools in Asia to develop young drivers.

The United States envoy in Hong Kong is Richard Boucher.
Richard Boucher reminded China of its pledge to preserve Hong Kong's freedoms.
The handover of Hong Kong to China is scheduled for July 1.
Boucher stated that the handover is a key event in Sino-U.S. relations.
Boucher emphasized that the U.S. has interests in China and Hong Kong.
Hong Kong is promised far-reaching autonomy for 50 years under a Sino-British treaty.
Boucher quoted Confucius regarding the measure of good governance in Hong Kong.
Boucher highlighted the importance of freedoms such as speech, press, and assembly.
Boucher criticized the provisional legislature planned by China as unnecessary and unjustified.
There are approximately 37,200 U.S. citizens living in Hong Kong.

China endorsed Tung Chee-hwa as the leader of Hong Kong after its reversion to Chinese rule in 1997.
Tung Chee-hwa was the overwhelming choice of a Beijing-vetted panel to lead Hong Kong.
The Preparatory Committee, consisting of 150 prominent Hong Kong and Chinese citizens, recognized Tung's new role in Shenzhen.
The endorsement of Tung was proposed by Preparatory Committee vice-chairman Wang Hanbin.
Delegates at the session applauded to approve Tung's endorsement.
Tung Chee-hwa's father fled the Chinese communist revolution in 1949.
Tung will assume leadership when Hong Kong reverts to China on June 30, 1997.
Tung stated that gratitude for China's past support would not affect his leadership decisions.
Hong Kong newspapers reported Tung's victory as evidence that Hong Kong people could govern themselves.
Tung plans to take a hard line against interference from provincial leaders regarding Hong Kong's autonomy.

China responded to a request for talks from Hong Kong's Democratic Party by insisting the party must follow Beijing's rules.
Beijing stated that the Democratic Party must abide by the rules governing the creation of the Selection Committee.
The Selection Committee is a 400-member body that will choose Hong Kong's post-handover leader and provisional legislature.
Xinhua news agency, which acts as China's de facto embassy in Hong Kong, welcomed the Democratic Party's willingness to communicate.
The Preparatory Committee is a panel of members selected by China that oversees the transfer of sovereignty in Hong Kong.
Xinhua expressed hope that the Democratic Party would adhere to the Basic Law and rules set by the National People's Congress and the Preparatory Committee.
The Basic Law is Hong Kong's post-handover constitution, which was promulgated in 1990.
Xinhua indicated that the statement marks the first step towards communication between the Democratic Party and Beijing.
Hong Kong will revert to China at midnight on June 30, 1997.
The Democratic Party's advocacy for democracy has led to tensions with Beijing, which has labeled its leaders as subversives.

Tung Chee-hwa is planning to travel to major Western countries to raise the profile of Hong Kong.
The timing of Tung's trip depends on his workload and may occur before July 1.
July 1 marks the date when Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule after more than 150 years as a British colony.
Tung's spokeswoman, Elin Wong, stated that the trip aims to provide a real picture of Hong Kong.
The trip may include visits to the United States and some European countries.
This trip would be Tung's first outside China since being selected as Hong Kong's first post-handover chief in December.
Tung is expected to address misunderstandings in the West regarding the provisional legislature.
The provisional legislature was formed in December by a pro-China panel and will replace Hong Kong's elected legislature.
Hong Kong's British-run government and the pro-democracy camp oppose the provisional legislature.
Tung has criticized Western countries for not understanding the provisional legislature and other issues related to Hong Kong's handover.

Britain's Home Office has warned ethnic minority residents in Hong Kong that they will not receive British passports if they relinquished other passports to qualify.
The British government stated that applicants must be solely British before February 4 to qualify for full passports.
Anyone voluntarily renouncing another nationality on or after February 4 will not qualify for British passports.
Ethnic minorities in Hong Kong faced the risk of becoming stateless when China resumes sovereignty over the colony on June 30.
It is unclear whether ethnic minorities will be entitled to passports of the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region after the handover.
The condition set by Britain is viewed as an attempt to prevent ethnic minority residents from renouncing other passports to qualify for British ones.
Nari Dadlani, a prominent business leader in Hong Kong's Indian community, criticized the February 4 cut-off as inappropriate.
Dadlani stated that he would remain in Hong Kong even if granted full British citizenship and emphasized the need for an insurance in emergencies.
The British Home Office indicated that necessary legislation must be enacted before ethnic minorities can apply for British citizenship.
Successful applicants will be granted full British citizenship starting July 1.

Chinese flags flew at half mast across Hong Kong on Thursday morning.
Newspapers in Hong Kong were delayed due to the news of Deng Xiaoping's death.
Pupils at pro-Beijing schools in Hong Kong stood in silence to honor Deng Xiaoping.
Hong Kong newspapers featured banner headlines announcing Deng's death.
Deng Xiaoping had expressed a desire to visit Hong Kong after its reunion with China in July 1997.
A newspaper hawker noted that many papers were changing their main sections.
Some residents of Hong Kong expressed grief over Deng's death, while others took it in stride.
Ko Chiu, an 80-year-old resident, described Deng as a great leader who improved China.
Auyeung Pak, an 85-year-old resident, stated that Deng's death was normal for someone of his age.
Chinese flags at the Xinhua News Agency in Hong Kong flew at half-mast.

European parliamentarians urged Hong Kong people to speak up regarding fears of losing democratic freedoms.
The European Parliament will recommend that Britain contest China's decision to replace Hong Kong's elected legislature with an appointed interim chamber.
Graham Watson, a member of the British Liberal Democratic Party, stated that democracy is the way of the world and totalitarianism is evil.
Watson and three other members of the European Parliament met with Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa and other prominent figures.
Hong Kong will revert to China on July 1 after being a British colony for over 150 years.
There are concerns among Hong Kong's 6.4 million residents that their democratic freedoms will be diminished.
A provisional legislature crafted by China will replace the elected chamber in Hong Kong.
Tung Chee-hwa supports the proposed changes to the legislature, claiming they are necessary for social order.
The European parliamentarians criticized Britain for being late in promoting democracy and civil rights in Hong Kong.
The MEPs believe the United Kingdom should challenge the legality of the shadow legislature in the International Court of Justice.

China aims for a smooth resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong to facilitate reunification with Taiwan.
Jonathan Pollack is a senior advisor on international policy at the Rand think-tank in the United States.
Pollack expects the People's Liberation Army (PLA) to gain more influence under China's new leader Jiang Zemin.
Pollack stated that after the Hong Kong transition, China may pressure Taiwan to engage in discussions or negotiations.
Pollack believes that a successful transition in Hong Kong will serve as an example for future cooperation with Taiwan.
Hong Kong was a British colony for over 150 years and will revert to China at midnight on June 30.
Under Sino-British handover treaties, Hong Kong is guaranteed autonomy for 50 years, except in foreign affairs and defense.
The return of Hong Kong to China is framed by Beijing as a model for Taiwan's reunification.
Beijing considers Taiwan a renegade province since the civil war in 1949.
Pollack noted that Deng Xiaoping's death in February would increase the PLA's profile due to Jiang Zemin's need for military support.

International Business Machines Corp is discontinuing some unspecified research and development projects.
Louis Gerstner is the chairman and chief executive of IBM.
Gerstner announced the cost-cutting measures at a Gartner Group technology symposium.
IBM will cut projects for products and services it believes customers do not want.
The cost-cutting is part of a reallocation of IBM's $6.0 billion research budget for 1996.
Gerstner stated that IBM previously cut overhead expenses from its research projects.
Gerstner reviewed the entire research and development program with top IBM executives.
IBM spent a total of $6.01 billion on research in 1995.
Gerstner indicated that IBM is discontinuing projects, not products that customers depend on.
IBM remains in the home PC business due to the potential of the market, which may grow significantly.

Compaq Computer Corp. reported a 43 percent increase in profits for the third quarter.
The profit increase was attributed to higher sales of PCs and accessories and streamlined operations.
Compaq's net income for the three months ended September 30 was $350 million, or $1.26 a share.
This net income was an increase from $245 million, or 89 cents a share, in the same period in 1995.
Sales grew 25 percent to $4.5 billion from $3.6 billion.
Compaq's accessories business, which includes monitors and hard drives, grew significantly and remained profitable.
Compaq President Eckhard Pfeiffer stated that the company had strong financial performance and improved earnings.
Compaq plans to launch powerful computer workstations running Microsoft Corp.'s Windows NT operating system at the end of October.
The new workstations will be priced 50 percent below other workstations for engineers and other users.
Compaq expects a strong fourth quarter driven by Christmas sales of PCs.

International Business Machines Corp. reported a third-quarter profit of $1.29 billion, or $2.45 a share.
IBM's profit for the quarter was better than Wall Street had expected.
The company reported a loss of $538 million, or 96 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter.
Excluding a one-time charge of $1.8 billion from the previous year, IBM's earnings were $1.3 billion in the 1995 quarter.
Sales grew 8 percent to $18.06 billion from $16.75 billion.
Sales of mainframe computers declined.
IBM shares initially fell after the report but then rallied and closed at $130, up 75 cents.
The midday rally took IBM shares to a new high for the year of $135.375.
Chief Financial Officer G. Richard Thoman expressed confidence in IBM's prospects for the rest of 1996.
Analysts expressed concerns about potential negative impacts on fourth quarter results due to currency exchange rates, low memory chip prices, and restructuring costs.

Compaq Computer Corp. is the world's largest personal computer maker.
Compaq will launch its first computer workstations this week.
Keren Seymour is an analyst with International Data Corp.
Seymour stated that Compaq has the potential to threaten traditional vendors.
Compaq will unveil three systems in the personal workstation area.
The personal workstation market is valued at $15.1 billion.
Traditional workstations run on the UNIX operating system.
The market for traditional workstations is dominated by Sun Microsystems Inc., Digital Equipment Corp., International Business Machines Corp., and Hewlett-Packard Co.
Microsoft Corp's Windows NT operating system has been gaining market share.
The personal workstation market is growing at an average rate of 44 percent a year.

America Online Inc is the world's largest online service.
AOL has implemented changes and announced a major restructuring.
Steve Case is the chairman and CEO of AOL.
AOL added 250,000 new subscribers in October.
AOL's stock has declined and subscriber growth slowed during the summer.
Microsoft Corp relaunched the Microsoft Network at a flat price of $19.95 for unlimited access.
AOL introduced a flat rate pricing plan of $19.95 a month.
AOL will discontinue its direct Internet access service called GNN.
Lennert Leader is the chief financial officer of AOL.
AOL expects to generate more revenue from advertising and merchandising.

EchoStar Communications Corp. is a company in the direct broadcast satellite television business.
EchoStar Communications Corp. announced a price cut for satellite dishes.
Thomson, the U.S. unit of France's Thomson-CSF, matched EchoStar's new price of $199 for a satellite dish.
Thomson executives stated that the new price will impact the industry and increase sales.
The RCA brand digital satellite system's price was reduced by up to $200 per unit by Thomson.
DirecTV and U.S. Satellite Broadcasting Co. offered a $200 cash back promotion for consumers who pre-pay for one year of programming.
Programming costs on DirecTV range from $29.95 per month for 70 channels to $44.95 per month for 175 channels.
The lower price may hinder new entrants from entering the market profitably.
Uniden America Corp., Toshiba America Consumer Products Inc., Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd., and Matsushita Electric Corp of America plan to introduce new DSS systems.
Thomson has an estimated 45 percent market share of the digital satellite system dish market.

International Business Machines Corp acquired Edmark Corp for $80 million.
The acquisition will be central to IBM's focus on education in its consumer products unit.
Edmark will gain access to IBM's global distribution network.
Jim Firestone is the general manager of IBM's Consumer Division.
Firestone believes Edmark will be the core of IBM's educational activities.
Firestone was appointed to lead IBM's consumer business in July 1995.
IBM's previous attempts in the home PC market have not been successful.
IBM plans to focus on the family educational market and not on entertainment software.
IBM's Aptiva home PC is marketed as a family learning tool.
Richard Zwetchkenbaum is the director of consumer research at IDC/Link.

IBM's stock is currently hitting historic highs on Wall Street.
Daniel Mandresh of Merrill Lynch raised his 12-month price target on IBM to $195 from about $155.
Since the price target increase, IBM's shares have risen more than 20 percent.
IBM's shares touched $159 on Wednesday, a level last seen before the 1987 stock market crash.
IBM hit an all-time high of $175 in August 1987.
The stock ended at $152.75 on Wednesday, down $1.375 due to mild profit-taking.
IBM's shares are up about 68 percent since July 15, when they were at $91.
IBM's stock previously sank as low as $43 during a period of losses and restructuring.
Some analysts view IBM as a bellwether stock that is contributing to the rally in the Dow Jones industrial average.
IBM is trading at about 14 times its current earnings estimates, which is lower than the typical technology stock valuation of about 20 times.

Several computer retailers reported a sluggish start to the holiday season.
November sales among major computer retailers showed ongoing weakness and heavy promotions.
Analysts indicated that the combination of weak sales and heavy promotions may negatively impact personal computer sales this quarter.
Stephen Baker, an analyst at International Data Corp., described the situation as 'bad' rather than sluggish.
Circuit City Stores Inc. reported an 8 percent increase in sales over November 1995, but an 8 percent decline in sales at stores open at least a year.
Richard Sharp, Circuit City's chairman and CEO, stated that industry sales trends remained weak and promotional activity intensified.
Best Buy Co. Inc. noted an increase in discounts in the PC category in November.
Allen Lenzmeier, Best Buy's chief financial officer, reported that third quarter sales were below expectations, with a 4 percent increase overall.
Best Buy's sales in stores open at least one year fell 8 percent for the four-week period ending November, compared to a 15 percent increase the previous year.
Tom Courtney, a Montgomery Securities analyst, estimated that November sales in the computer category at Circuit City fell by 20 percent to 25 percent.

Netscape Communications Corp. and five regional Bell phone companies announced that the five Baby Bells will use Netscape's Navigator software as the main browser for their Internet access businesses.
The participating Bell companies are Ameritech Corp., Bell Atlantic Corp., BellSouth Corp., Pacific Telesis Group, and SBC Communications Inc.
Netscape's Navigator software has become the secondary browser to Microsoft Corp.'s Internet Explorer.
Analyst Abhishek Gami stated that Netscape is still a significant player in the consumer marketplace.
America Online Inc. and CompuServe Inc. have made deals with Microsoft to use Internet Explorer as their primary Internet browser.
Netscape shares increased by $3 to $63 in heavy trading on Nasdaq.
The five Bell companies represent a potential market of 72 million consumers and businesses across 26 states, including Washington, D.C.
Bell Atlantic has an agreement with Microsoft to offer Internet Explorer as an option to its customers starting in the first quarter of 1997.
The agreement includes a feature to simplify how users select an Internet service provider.
Pacific Bell has the largest Internet access business among the five, with 51,000 members.

International Business Machines Corp. announced it is reorganizing its global sales and services businesses under the brand IBM Global Services.
IBM's services business has operated under various names outside the United States.
The reorganization aims to clarify the IBM brand and boost efficiency.
Lucio Stanca has been named general manager of global marketing operations at IBM.
Lucio Stanca has led IBM operations in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa since autumn 1994.
Stanca will continue as chairman of the European, Middle Eastern, and African operations based in Paris.
Stanca will lead a new direct-marketing effort globally using the new structure and brand name.
IBM's previous direct marketing efforts lacked a consistent focus across regions.
IBM and its partners will discontinue the development of Microsoft Corp.'s Windows NT software for the PowerPC chip.
William Etherington will succeed Lucio Stanca as general manager of Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.

Personal computer makers will roll out multimedia PCs designed around a new chip by Intel Corp next week.
Intel will officially launch its P55C microprocessor with MMX technology on Wednesday.
The new chip offers much faster performance than earlier designs.
David Wu, a Chicago Corp analyst, stated that the impact of MMX will be significant in the second half of the year.
Wu noted that there is currently nothing new to drive sales in the consumer market other than better price performance.
CompUSA Inc reported disappointing sales of PCs during the holiday shopping season.
Analysts indicated that PC makers with a strong presence in the corporate market would not be significantly affected by weak consumer sales.
Consumer anticipation of new PCs contributed to weaker-than-expected sales as buyers waited for new products.
Companies expected to unveil new high-end PCs priced over $3,000 include Compaq Computer Corp, Dell Computer Corp, Gateway 2000 Inc, Toshiba America Corp, Sony Corp, and International Business Machines Corp.
Intel shares increased by eight to 138-3/8 after positive comments from two analysts.

Computer makers are expected to report solid fourth-quarter earnings.
The stronger dollar will negatively impact some large systems makers.
Most U.S. PC makers, except for Apple Computer Inc. and AST Research Inc., are expected to show strong sales growth.
Apple Computer Inc. forecasted an operating loss for its first quarter due to weak U.S. demand for its Performa consumer PC and shortages of notebook computers.
Intel Corp. reported fourth-quarter profits of $1.9 billion, exceeding Wall Street's estimates.
Analyst Eugene Glazer stated that business in the PC sector, excluding Apple, was strong.
Dell Computer Corp. and Gateway 2000 Inc. are benefiting from market shifts despite negative retailer comments.
Compaq Computer Corp. is likely to report strong earnings due to booming corporate sales.
Compaq generates about 20 percent of its revenues from consumer sales and the rest from corporate customers.
Companies like International Business Machines Corp., Digital Equipment Corp., and Unisys Corp. are expected to face negative impacts from a stronger dollar and sluggish European sales.

Ice cream sales in Europe declined during the summer of 2023.
Unilever lost an estimated 125 million pounds in sales and 50 million pounds in profits due to poor summer weather.
Impulse purchases of ice cream, which represent one third of all European ice cream sales, were particularly affected.
Coca-Cola reported a 10 percent decline in case sales in Germany, 17 percent in Britain, and 4 percent in France during the summer.
Wall's and Nestle are developing new products to increase winter ice cream sales.
Bird's Eye Wall's launched seven new product lines for the winter months.
Nestle is introducing products like its Christmas Log in France to balance seasonal sales fluctuations.
Children account for 40 percent of all impulse ice cream sales and take their longest holidays in the summer.
Wall's is the largest player in the British ice cream market, valued at about 1.0 billion pounds.
Wall's holds a 43 percent market share in Britain, while Nestle Lyons Maid has 12 percent, Mars has 7 percent, own label products account for 29 percent, and others make up 9 percent.

B.A.T Industries reported a nine percent rise in nine-month profits.
Profits for the nine months rose to 2.04 billion pounds from 1.87 billion pounds.
Profits in the third quarter rose to 714 million pounds from 680 million pounds.
Trading profit from financial services rose by three percent.
Profits from tobacco were seven percent ahead.
Overall cigarette sales rose by three percent, although volumes were lower in the United States.
Chief executive Martin Broughton stated that U.S. litigation, regulation, and science are the dominant issues affecting B.A.T's share price.
B.A.T shares fell from a high of 585 pence to around 434 pence.
B.A.T's stock market value decreased by nearly four billion pounds.
Broughton stated that a recent strategy review showed no value in demerging the company.

Whitbread Plc is expected to report a 10 percent rise in first half earnings.
Analysts estimate pretax profits for Whitbread for the six months to the end of August to be between 168 million and 175 million.
The previous pretax profit for the same period was 155.7 million.
Dividend forecasts for Whitbread range from 5.9 to 6.24p, an increase from 5.75p.
Ron Littleboy, an analyst at Nomura, stated that consumer spending has increased and Whitbread has shifted to higher margin premium beer.
Whitbread acquired David Lloyd Leisure for approximately 200 million stg and a chain of 16 Marriott hotels for about 185 million stg in August 1995.
John Beaumont, an analyst at Merrill Lynch, suggested that any surprises in earnings would likely come from the hotel side.
Whitbread's hotel company includes around 130 budget Travel Inns, with new openings occurring at a rate of about one every two weeks.
Whitbread manages approximately 2,200 pubs, primarily on 20-year leases.
The restaurant and leisure division of Whitbread includes TGI Friday, Pizza Hut, Costa Coffee, Thresher, and Beefeater.

Whitbread Plc reported a 14 percent increase in half year profits to 177.5 million pounds.
Chairman Sir Michael Angus expects growth in the company's markets to continue.
Chief executive Peter Jarvis stated that British consumers are spending more on leisure.
Jarvis believes the consumer position in Britain is favorable for at least two to three years.
The company's hotels business doubled profits and sales in the six months to August 31.
Like-for-like sales for Whitbread were up by 11 percent, with higher occupancy levels and room rates.
The number of foreign tourists to Britain is increasing, with spending of 13 to 14 billion pounds last year.
Whitbread acquired David Lloyd Leisure for 200 million pounds and a chain of 16 Marriott hotels for about 185 million in August 1995.
Whitbread plans to add about one low budget Travel Inn every 10 days to reach 300 by the end of the year 2000.
Sales from Whitbread's 2,200 leased pub estate were down three percent.

Kwik Save Group Plc is closing 107 shops as part of a restructuring plan.
Unions estimate that the closure of these shops could result in 1,000 job losses.
Kwik Save reported a 28 percent drop in annual profits to 90.3 million pounds.
Sales increased by 8.8 percent to 3.5 billion pounds in the same year.
The company maintained its final dividend at 14.05p, totaling 20p for the year.
Chief executive Graeme Bowler stated that the reorganization aims to address competition from superstores and discount groups.
Kwik Save's shares rose to a peak of 325 pence following the restructuring announcement.
A review by outside consultants indicated a need to improve the existing 979 stores and invest in staff and technology.
Kwik Save plans to invest 50 million pounds in its New Generation programme in the next year and 100 million the following year.
Finance director Derek Pretty estimated that less than 200 job losses would occur due to store closures, with 90 percent of staff being redeployed.

Allied Domecq is expected to report a significant decline in full-year profits.
The decline is attributed to a 320 million stg loss from the sale of its 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley.
Analysts forecast pretax profits for Allied Domecq to be between 560 and 581 million stg, down from 645 million stg the previous year.
The decline in profits is primarily due to issues in Allied's spirits division.
Factors affecting profits include the weak Mexican peso, challenging market conditions in Europe and America, and de-stocking in the United States.
The consensus forecast for Allied Domecq's total dividend is 23.6p.
Allied sold its stake in Carlsberg-Tetley to Bass for 200 million in cash in August.
Allied expected a loss of about 320 million stg from the sale of Carlsberg-Tetley.
After tax, the sale is projected to reduce reserves by approximately 200 million stg.
Analysts predict a 60 million stg drop in trading profits for Allied's spirits and wines division from the previous year's 488 million stg.

Northern Foods Plc reported flat profits due to falling world prices for dairy products.
Profits before tax and exceptional items increased by one percent to 57.8 million pounds for the six months ending September 30.
Northern Foods shares increased by 2.5 pence to 198 pence.
Jo Stewart, head of Northern's prepared foods division, stated there is no immediate prospect of improvement in commodity prices.
Sir Christopher Haskins, chairman of Northern Foods, advocated for Britain to join a single European currency.
World commodity prices for butter, skimmed milk, and bulk cream decreased by approximately 20 percent compared to last year.
Eden Vale Food Ingredients, a division of Northern Foods, was significantly impacted by the collapse in commodity prices, estimating a loss of about 6.0 million pounds.
The dairy business of Northern Foods reported operating profits of 21.6 million pounds, a decrease of 27 percent.
Northern Foods supplies about 33 percent of all milk in British supermarkets, having lost two percentage points of market share in the first half.
Most British consumers purchase milk from supermarkets at a price of about 28 pence per pint.

Tate and Lyle reported an 11 percent fall in full year profits to 276 million pounds ($463 million).
The earnings drop of more than 50 percent was attributed to its U.S. subsidiary Staley.
Tate and Lyle's shares rose by 9-1/2 pence to 479-1/2 after touching 482.
Company executives expressed optimism about the current trading environment for Staley.
Corn prices are now at $2.60 a bushel after a larger crop of 9.3 billion bushels this summer.
Larry Pillard, Tate's chief executive, stated that futures prices should remain around $2.60 a bushel.
Last year, corn prices reached unprecedented highs, peaking at five dollars a bushel.
Staley faced challenges last year due to high corn prices and increased competition.
This year, corn milling companies can divert excess capacity into ethanol production.
Gasoline prices have averaged 63 cents a gallon this year, peaking at 77.01 in April.

Brewer Bass Plc is expected to report a strong improvement in full-year earnings.
The improvement is driven by growth at Holiday Inns and Harvester restaurants.
Bass acquired the Harvester chain of 78 pubs for 165 million stg from Forte in July.
Analysts forecast pre-tax profits for Bass Plc to range from 665 to 675 million stg.
This is an increase from 599.1 million stg in 1995.
A dividend of 24.7p is anticipated.
Chairman Sir Ian Prosser reported a six percent increase in revenue per available room in US franchised hotels.
Analysts expect an eight percent increase in revenue per available room in Europe for the full year.
Profits from Holiday Inns are expected to be about 193 million stg, up from 164 million a year ago.
