If share prices of weak banks fall significantly, larger banks may find it easier to merge with them.
Recent selling of shares in the banking sector has contributed to a decline in Japanese share prices.
The banking sector represents one-quarter of the Tokyo Stock Exchange's market capitalization.
On a recent Monday, the Nikkei average closed down 609.70 points, or 3.37 percent, at 17,480.24.
The Nikkei is down close to 2,000 points since the beginning of the year due to economic concerns.
Japanese banks traditionally hold large amounts of shares in other companies, which has previously helped their balance sheets.

Matsui Securities Co Ltd announced it will cut its brokerage fees for stocks and convertible bonds traded over the counter by half, starting from March.
This is the first instance of a broker deviating from the norm in setting its fees in Japan.
Brokerage commissions for stocks listed on Japanese stock exchanges are fixed under the Securities and Exchange Act.
Fees for over-the-counter trade can be set within a range fixed by the Japan Securities Dealers' Association.
Brokers have typically charged uniform fees on stocks traded over the counter.
After Matsui's announcement, Paribas Capital Markets Ltd also cut its brokerage fees for stocks traded on Japan's over-the-counter market by half, effective from Friday.
Matsui stated that other companies in the industry pressured it not to make the fee change.
An executive at a medium-sized Japanese broker claimed that Matsui's decision would accelerate the liberalisation of stockbroking fees.
Ichiyoshi Securities Co Ltd announced it would not cut its fees for now and plans to differentiate its service by offering better information.
An advisory panel to the Finance Ministry is discussing the deregulation of stockbroking fees and is expected to make a final proposal by June.

Daiwa Bank was expelled from the United States one year ago.
Daiwa Bank incurred a $1.1 billion bond-trading loss in the United States.
Analysts believe Daiwa Bank's expulsion may have led to necessary restructuring measures.
Yukiko Ohara, a financial analyst at UBS Securities Ltd., stated that Daiwa eliminated management risks from its corporate structure after inspections by Japan's Finance Ministry and the Bank of Japan.
Ohara suggested that Daiwa could serve as a model for restructuring for other Japanese banks.
Daiwa's restructuring efforts are expected to boost its annual operating profits above 100 billion yen ($800 million) by the end of March 2000.
Daiwa forecasted operating profits of 80 billion yen ($640 million) for the year ending March 1997.
Daiwa bank director Akiyoshi Otani indicated that the damage from the bond-loss scandal was not as severe as initially feared.
Daiwa was ordered to shut down its U.S. operations in November 1995 due to a trader's unauthorized deals.
Daiwa pleaded guilty to conspiracy and fraud charges and paid $340 million in fines.

Trading on most of China's futures markets has dropped significantly due to pressure from Beijing to curb speculation.
Hedging has become virtually impossible in China's futures markets, according to traders and analysts.
The Shanghai Metal Exchange is the only market with sufficient liquidity and flexibility for companies to hedge risk.
Beijing has issued two documents encouraging securities markets while warning of future clean-ups and restructuring in futures markets.
There are rumors that Beijing plans to merge or close many of the 15 futures exchanges in China.
Xie Boxing, deputy manager of the Information Department of the Shanghai Cereals and Oils Exchange, stated there is no plan to merge or close exchanges according to feedback from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC).
Xie noted that liquidity in the rice market has decreased due to Beijing's statements, making hedging difficult.
An analyst mentioned that the crackdown on futures markets has eliminated the basis for hedging, leaving only speculators.
A trader from a Chinese futures company reported that trading volume for most commodity futures contracts is now too small for hedging operations.
A CSRC spokesman stated that authorities still want the futures markets to develop despite current problems, but declined to comment on rumors of closures or mergers.

The Shanghai Film Studio is one of the oldest and largest film-making operations in China.
The Shanghai Film Studio is competing against the Yongle cinema chain in a cinema chain war.
Zhu Yongde is the boss of the Shanghai Film Studio.
Zhu Yongde created his own chain of cinemas after Yongle refused to re-divide box office receipts.
Zhu Yongde stated that the Shanghai movie market is becoming increasingly important.
The Shanghai Film Studio has made minimal profits in recent years due to high demands from Yongle and other distributors.
Cinema attendance in Shanghai is below half of what it was before the 1980s television revolution.
Zhu Yongde proposed a profit split of 25 percent for Yongle and 25 percent for the film studio, but Yongle refused.
Yongle's spokeswoman stated that the Dongfang cinema chain was established to diversify ownership of cinemas and distribution.
Yongle currently receives 15 percent of box office receipts.

China's state debt became the top investment choice among local investors in 1996.
Market reform measures contributed to the popularity of state debt among investors.
Beijing issued 195.2 billion yuan worth of treasury bills and bonds for 1996.
The last batch of the seven-year bond was allocated to underwriters last Friday.
Reforms in the process for issuing treasury bills and bonds made them best sellers this year.
A public tender system was widely adopted for issuing state debt.
The Finance Ministry previously decided coupon rates and allocated state debt through administrative edict.
This year, the ministry organized public tenders for each new bond issue.
About 75 percent of each new batch of bonds was distributed based on public tender bids.
The remaining bonds were distributed according to administrative decision.

The threat of a Sino-U.S. textiles trade war is unlikely to go beyond verbal exchanges.
Chinese firms are reportedly performing poorly.
Li Shounan is the head of the general manager's office at Shanghai Lianhua Fibre Co Ltd.
Li Shounan stated that mutual concessions are expected to replace verbal warnings.
An official from Shanghai Sanmao Textile Co Ltd mentioned that the overall impact of the trade war is expected to be minimal.
A spokeswoman for Shanghai Jiafeng Co Ltd indicated that their products are involved in the dispute.
China's annual apparel and textile exports to the United States are estimated at around $4.2 billion.
Approximately 30 garment and textile companies are listed in Shanghai and Shenzhen.
Beijing announced a temporary ban on selected U.S. textiles and goods starting December 10 in retaliation for U.S. sanctions.
Washington announced a cut to China's textile import quota for 1995 by $19 million in September.

China's foreign currency B shares in Shanghai and Shenzhen increased on Wednesday.
Shanghai's B share index rose 5.49 percent to 49.689 points.
Shenzhen's B share index increased 8.25 percent to 111.35 points.
Brokers reported that rumors of government measures to support the markets contributed to the surge.
A broker at China Southern Securities stated that regulators were discussing ways to address the bearishness of the Hong Kong dollar-denominated stock market.
Overseas investors were buying selected stocks in Shanghai due to improved domestic economic conditions.
The recent rises in Shenzhen B shares were linked to a report from the Securities Times about the China Securities Regulatory Commission's concerns.
The chairman of the CSRC, Zhou Daojiong, mentioned that the poor performance of B markets negatively affected China's reform and open policy.
Chinese domestic institutional investors were leading the buying, with increasing amounts from overseas investors.
Most trading in China's B shares is conducted by domestic investors, despite the shares being intended for foreign investors.

Chinese authorities are not interfering with the illegal trade of B shares by domestic investors unless the market becomes too speculative.
B shares in China were created to attract funds from foreign investors.
The majority of B share trading in the past six months has been conducted by domestic investors in violation of regulations.
Analysts believe that the authorities will not take action as long as the markets do not become overly speculative.
Shenzhen's B shares have increased by more than 50 percent since mid-November, while Shanghai's B shares have risen over 15 percent in the same period.
Brokers attribute the volatility of B shares to rumors regarding potential changes to the ban on domestic investors.
The ban on domestic investors holding B shares is intended to prevent foreign exchange outflow.
Many domestic securities firms have opened B share trading accounts in Hong Kong.
B-share trading is officially restricted to individuals with foreign passports or residents of Hong Kong and Taiwan.
The Shanghai exchange has allowed flexibility in the interpretation of B share trading rules.

China has approved three foreign banks to conduct local currency business.
The three banks are Citibank, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank, and Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation.
The banks will be granted licenses to handle Chinese yuan business this month.
Foreign banks in China have previously been restricted to foreign currency business only.
Chinese banks have retained a monopoly on the local currency loan and deposit market.
The approved banks will be allowed to handle yuan deposits, loans, and other business.
More foreign banks are expected to be allowed to conduct local currency business from early next year.
Bankers expect that the business licenses will restrict foreign banks to dealing with foreign-funded firms.
Chen Yuan, deputy governor of the People's Bank of China, stated that licenses for foreign banks would be granted very soon.
There is currently no agreement on the tax rates for profits made by foreign banks conducting local currency business.

In 1996, China's financial markets made significant steps towards maturity.
Beijing is more willing to allow financial markets to take on economic control.
The Chinese securities, futures, and money markets are less than six years old.
These markets are still experiencing volatility and have a long way to go for standardisation and stability.
The central government previously referred to the markets as 'experimental' but now calls them 'in the initial stages of development.'
Beijing officially supported the stock markets in April 1996.
The Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges added a total of 178 companies in 1996.
The total market capitalisation of the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets is 1,271 billion yuan ($153 billion).
The treasury bill market issued a record 195.2 billion yuan worth of debt in 1996.
An interbank market for local currency was established in January 1996.

China's B share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen declined on Wednesday due to profit-taking and reports of tighter controls in Shenzhen.
The Shanghai B share index fell 3.649 points or 4.55 percent to 80.685 on Wednesday, with a trading volume of 95 million shares worth $44 million.
Shenzhen's B index decreased by 7.42 points or 3.83 percent to close at 186.45, influenced by discussions of tighter control over local investors trading B shares.
A foreign brokerage analyst in Shanghai described the decline as a technical correction following substantial increases in the markets over recent weeks.
Traders indicated that the correction is likely to continue for the rest of the week, but market sentiment remains positive with expectations of recovery next week.
Shenzhen securities authorities warned brokerages not to allow local investors to buy B shares unless the funds originate from outside the country.
The notice from Shenzhen authorities was issued at the request of the Foreign Exchange Management Bureau and the China Securities Regulatory Commission.
A broker stated that the implementation of the new policy would slow the inflow of fresh money into the market, but some Chinese investors could still participate.
Brokers in Shanghai reported no knowledge of the notice being distributed to them, and officials from the central bank and national regulator declined to comment.
In Shanghai, 34 out of 42 B shares traded declined, with cheap stocks leading the losses after recent speculative increases.

The Chinese authorities imposed a limit of 10 percent on the movement of any stock on one day in the country's two stock markets.
The Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges set daily movement limits for all shares and investment fund units at 10 percent in either direction, effective from next Monday.
Bids and asks exceeding the limits will be considered null and void, according to the announcement.
Brokerages are prohibited from accepting invalid bids and asks.
The announcements followed significant declines in the B share indices of Shanghai and Shenzhen, which fell 12.26 percent and 14.75 percent respectively on Friday.
The exchanges ordered brokerages to publicly disclose the top losing and gaining stocks and the names of key institutions involved in trading.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) approved the announcements.
Chinese brokers generally welcomed the new limits, stating they would help control erratic trading.
Some brokers believe the limits will benefit buyers and create buyers' markets.
A foreign broker in Shanghai stated that trading limits generally distort markets rather than rationalize trading.

China's stock markets increased on Wednesday after two days of declines.
Shanghai's B share index closed up 9.84 percent at 64.252 points.
Shanghai's A index closed up 7.34 percent at 1016.241 points.
Shenzhen's B share index closed limit-up 10 percent at 133.8 points.
Shenzhen's domestic A index gained 4.37 percent to 391.92 points.
The gains followed an announcement from Beijing about overheated stock markets.
Traders reported that investors were recovering from the shock of the crackdown.
The China Securities newspaper quoted exchange presidents as welcoming the crackdown.
Traders noted that institutional and overseas investors built new positions in the B share market.
Shanghai's B shares were priced at one-third the level of their A-share counterparts.

China's futures markets faced official disapproval in 1996.
Analysts predict tighter conditions for China's futures markets in 1997.
Some small exchanges in China's futures markets may be absorbed by larger ones.
There is no indication that the long-awaited Futures Law will be introduced soon.
Securities authorities have promised new regulations in the first half of 1997.
China's futures markets were established in the early 1990s.
Trading volumes on China's futures exchanges have decreased significantly in the past two years.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) banned several institutions from trading commodities futures in March.
The Shanghai Metal Exchange expects a total trade volume of 230 billion yuan in 1996.
The CSRC has imposed restrictions on daily price movements and total holdings for all commodity futures exchanges.

More foreign firms are beginning to profit from the China market.
Many foreign companies are still involved in loss-making ventures in China.
The number of foreign companies gaining market share in China is increasing.
China has become the second-biggest recipient of foreign investment funds in the world.
Coca-Cola, Kentucky Fried Chicken, and Lux soap are popular foreign brands in China.
A Western diplomat in Shanghai stated that more companies are entering the Chinese market.
Coca-Cola returned to China in 1979 after a 30-year absence.
Coca-Cola recorded its first profit from China operations 11 years after returning.
Coca-Cola operates 18 bottling plants in China.
Sales volume for Coca-Cola in China doubles every three years.

Weak metals prices will undermine third-quarter earnings for many North American metals producers.
Analysts surveyed by Reuters predict that earnings will be down year over year or quarter over quarter.
Manford Mallory, an analyst for Research Capital, stated that metal prices and volumes are down compared to a year ago.
Copper prices have fallen sharply since mid-June, while nickel and aluminum prices have also declined.
Gold prices are around US$380 an ounce.
Mallory indicated that most companies will report profits, but some will report losses.
Earnings in the mining sector were disappointing in the first quarter and dropped in the second quarter due to a scandal at Japan's Sumitomo Corp.
David Davidson, a base metals analyst with Wood Gundy, estimated that third-quarter earnings would be 10 to 15 percent lower than in the second quarter.
Phelps Dodge Corp reported third-quarter net income of US$80.2 million, down from US$211.8 million a year earlier.
Most large gold companies hedge part of their production to mitigate exposure to low gold prices.

Barrick Gold Corp, based in Toronto, is North America's largest gold producer.
Barrick reported lower third-quarter earnings due to an after-tax charge and higher operating costs.
Barrick's net income for the quarter was $21 million, or 6 cents a share, down from $67.7 million, or 19 cents a share, a year earlier.
Earnings were slightly below analysts' expectations.
Mining analyst Barry Allan stated that Barrick has transitioned from a growth company to one focused on maintaining its existing base.
Barrick's cash costs increased to $203 an ounce from $194 an ounce a year earlier.
The company incurred a $38 million loss to exit its Cerro Corona exploration project in Peru.
Barrick increased its exploration budget by more than 50 percent to $46.4 million for the first nine months of the year.
Barrick's shares rose C50 cents to C$36.15 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
In New York, Barrick's stock rose 37.5 cents to $26.875.

Barrick Gold Corp. completed its C$1 billion takeover of Arequipa Resources Ltd.
Barrick Gold Corp. is now the world's third biggest gold producer.
Ninety-three percent of Arequipa shareholders accepted Barrick's C$30 a share bid.
Barrick plans to buy the remaining shares of Arequipa Resources Ltd.
Barrick will spend at least C$512 million and issue about 13.4 million shares to complete the takeover.
The total value of the deal is C$1.02 billion based on Barrick's closing stock price.
The acquisition includes ownership of the Pierina gold deposit in Peru.
Experts speculate that the Pierina deposit has potential reserves of up to 12 million ounces of gold.
Barrick initially offered C$27 a share for Arequipa on July 11.
Barrick raised its offer to C$30 a share on August 16 to avoid a takeover battle.

The aging gold zone near Timmins is experiencing increased exploration activity.
The area has been mined since the early 1900s.
Most Canadian exploration companies are focusing on South America and Asia.
A few junior companies are continuing to explore in the Timmins area.
These junior companies are described as innovative and optimistic.
The junior companies aim to find gold in their home region.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd is facing a potential multi-billion-dollar lawsuit over the ownership of the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
PT Krueng Gasui, one of Bre-X's Indonesian partners, has threatened legal action in Canadian courts, claiming damages of US$1.9 billion.
Bre-X chief executive David Walsh expressed curiosity about the lawsuit threat being made in Canada regarding events in Indonesia.
Krueng Gasui claims to own up to 40 percent of the Busang deposit but only has undisputed ownership of 10 percent of one section.
Bre-X asserts that Krueng Gasui lacks the documentation to support its claims of ownership.
Bre-X received a letter from Krueng Gasui demanding a meeting before November 22 to resolve the dispute.
If Bre-X does not attempt to settle the dispute, Krueng Gasui will proceed with the lawsuit.
The dispute has caused the Indonesian government to delay issuing contracts necessary for Bre-X to continue work on the Busang deposit.
Analysts believe the lawsuit threat may incentivize Bre-X to settle with Krueng Gasui and its controlling businessman Jusuf Merukh.
The outcome of the lawsuit could depend on the Indonesian government's reaction.

Barrick Gold Corp. is negotiating with Bre-X Minerals Ltd. for control of the Busang gold discovery in Indonesia.
The negotiations are guided by the Indonesian government.
Bre-X discovered the Busang gold deposit in 1994.
Official estimates indicate Busang contains 47 million ounces of gold, with analysts suggesting it could rise to 100 million ounces.
Bre-X plans to keep 25 percent of its stake in Busang, while Barrick would receive 75 percent.
The Indonesian government has requested a 10 percent participation in the deal.
The Indonesian government wants a deal between Barrick and Bre-X finalized by December 4.
Development of Busang has been delayed due to disputes over ownership between Bre-X and its Indonesian partners.
Bre-X controls 90 percent of Busang.
Barrick spokesman Vince Borg stated that a deal between the companies is not guaranteed.

Shareholders are concerned about negotiations between Barrick Gold Corp and Bre-X Minerals Ltd regarding the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
Some Bre-X shareholders fear they may be forced into an unfavorable deal.
Some Barrick shareholders are worried about their reputation following any potential deal.
Michael Fowler, a gold analyst at Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion, stated that shareholders are very vocal about the situation.
Many large institutions hold shares in both Barrick and Bre-X.
Bre-X has been instructed by the Indonesian government to negotiate with Barrick Gold.
The Indonesian government wants Barrick to control 75 percent of the Busang stake and Bre-X to control 25 percent.
Both companies are considering giving a 10 percent stake to the Indonesian government.
Fowler emphasized that Barrick must treat Bre-X shareholders fairly to avoid negative consequences.
Retail shareholders, including Gregory Chorny, are expressing their concerns about the negotiations.

Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is negotiating a deal with Barrick Gold Corp.
The Busang gold deposit in Indonesia is estimated to contain more than 57 million ounces of gold.
The cost to mine the gold at Busang is estimated to be $96 per ounce.
The Indonesian government has mandated that Barrick Gold Corp. receive 75 percent of Bre-X's stake in the Busang deposit.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. will retain 25 percent of its stake in the Busang deposit.
The Indonesian government, led by President Suharto, has expressed a desire for a 10 percent stake in Busang.
Major figures in the gold mining industry are protesting the deal between Bre-X and Barrick as unprecedented and unfair.
John Willson, CEO of Placer Dome Inc., stated that Bre-X should have a say in choosing its partner.
Placer Dome, Newmont Mining Corp., and Teck Corp. were excluded from the bidding process for Busang.
Analysts speculate that Barrick may have influenced the Indonesian government through connections with prominent figures.

The rights to Bre-X Minerals Ltd.'s Busang gold discovery in Indonesia are uncertain.
The Indonesian government declared Barrick Gold Corp. as the winner of the rights.
Bre-X spokesman Steve McAnulty stated that negotiations are still ongoing.
Barrick spokesman Vince Borg confirmed that there is no signed agreement.
The Indonesian government reported that Barrick and Bre-X agreed to a 75-25 split of the deposit.
Umar Said, secretary-general of the Mines and Energy Ministry, stated that both companies can accept the government's suggestion.
Indonesia requested Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick and announce a deal by December 4.
After the deadline, both companies acknowledged reaching agreement on some issues, but others remain unresolved.
Michael Fowler, a gold analyst, commented that the situation is confusing and that some issues are still in the way of an agreement.
Bre-X hopes the Indonesian government will allow them to find a partner through an open bidding process.

Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp are negotiating a joint venture to mine the Busang gold discovery in Indonesia.
Bre-X's chief executive David Walsh stated that progress in negotiations with Barrick is slow.
Walsh mentioned that legal issues are hindering a full agreement between the two companies.
The Indonesian government advised Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick to operate Busang.
The Indonesian government requested a deal by December 4, but outstanding issues remained after the deadline.
The Indonesian government has expressed doubts about Bre-X's control over the Busang deposit, which is estimated to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.
Umar Said, Indonesia's secretary-general of mines, stated that Bre-X's previous application for contracts of work has been canceled due to various problems.
Bre-X and Barrick must jointly submit new applications for contracts of work on the Busang deposit.
Without contracts of work granted by the Indonesian government, Bre-X cannot exploit the gold find.
Walsh claimed that Bre-X's permits and applications for the gold property are in good standing.

Three Canadian mining companies are involved in a dispute over the Petaquilla copper-gold project in Panama.
The companies involved are Adrian Resources Ltd, Teck Corp, and Inmet Mining Corp.
Adrian Resources Ltd controls 52 percent of the Petaquilla project.
Adrian claims that a feasibility study conducted by Teck was incomplete and not compliant with existing arrangements.
Teck had an option to acquire up to 26 percent of the project by funding a feasibility study and operating the mine.
Adrian states that Teck has not fulfilled the initial requirement to proceed with its option.
Doug Turnbull, a consulting geologist for Adrian, stated that Teck did not complete its obligations.
Teck asserts that its feasibility study was a comprehensive assessment of the project.
Teck's senior vice president, Michael Lipkewich, mentioned that current metal price conditions make production commitment difficult.
Teck aims to resolve its issues with Adrian and continue exploration for higher grade ore.

Investors are interested in Black Swan Gold Mines Ltd due to anticipated drill results.
Fred Ketchen is the senior vice-president at ScotiaMcLeod.
Black Swan was the most active stock on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
The stock price of Black Swan was C$1.45 on Tuesday, down C$0.05.
Black Swan's stock traded 2.6 million shares on Tuesday.
Richard Simpson is a spokesman for Black Swan Gold Mines Ltd.
Drilling results from Black Swan's gold project in Brazil are expected to be released later this week.
The results from the drilling are described as very preliminary.
Analysts noted that institutional investors are placing bets on Black Swan due to market rumors.
Black Swan shares its Cata Preta gold project with Sul America Mineracao Ltda.

Czech consumer prices increased by 0.3 percent month-on-month in September.
The Czech Statistical Bureau reported a year-on-year inflation rate of 8.9 percent.
The September sliding 12-month average inflation rate was 8.7 percent.
A Reuters survey predicted a monthly increase of 0.6 percent for September.
Martin Kupka of Patria Finance stated that one month’s result does not significantly affect the average inflation rate.
The government raised its average inflation target for the year from eight percent to 8.3 percent.
A 0.2 percent monthly increase in the food, tobacco, and beverages sector contributed to the overall inflation result.
The CSU reported a 19 percent drop in potato prices, which affected the heavily-weighted food sector.
Radek Maly of Citibank expected a monthly increase of 0.5 percent for September.
The CSU noted a 1.1 percent drop in prices in the leisure sector.

Czech National Bank (CNB) Governor Josef Tosovsky stated that the central bank is committed to keeping the crown strong.
Tosovsky made these comments after a meeting with Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and top business executives.
The CNB aims to keep the crown within a daily fixed band against a mark/dollar basket.
Tosovsky indicated that the CNB would maintain the rate within a plus/minus 7.5 percent band against the mark/dollar cross rate.
Tosovsky dismissed speculation about moving the crown outside the established band.
Analysts have debated the need for a devaluation of the crown to boost exports and address a growing current account deficit.
The current account shortfall is projected to approach six percent of gross domestic product this year.
Tosovsky claimed that a stable crown has helped regulate inflation in the country.
He suggested that a stronger crown could aid in the restructuring of the Czech economy to enhance competitiveness.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced plans to provide more funds to export promotion agencies.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced that the 1997 Czech state budget plans an overall spending increase of 11.8 percent.
Klaus stated that he does not expect inflation to fall below eight percent next year.
Klaus indicated that spending increases would be largest for export supports, regional transportation, and housing.
The total expenditure for 1997 is projected to rise by 58 billion Czech crowns to 549 billion crowns.
Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik stated that the full cabinet should receive the draft budget for discussion on September 20.
Kocarnik confirmed that there was no discussion among ministers about anything other than a balanced budget.
Klaus's government has passed four consecutive balanced budgets.
The government plans to cut 1996 spending by another 9.3 billion crowns to balance this year's budget.
Fixed mandatory expenditures are forecast to rise by 14.0 percent, while discretionary spending is expected to rise by 9.9 percent.
State sector wages are planned to rise by a nominal 12.4 percent in 1997.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated that the large Czech foreign trade deficit is due to a temporary investment wave.
Klaus forecasted a perpetual, but smaller trade gap for the Czech Republic.
Klaus described the record 110.7 billion crown trade deficit in the first nine months of the year as 'not tragic'.
Klaus emphasized the importance of discussing the current account and the whole payment balance, not just the trade balance.
Klaus predicted that the Czech Republic would likely never have a positive trade balance in the long term.
Klaus attributed the current trade deficit to a temporary above-average rate of investment.
Klaus noted that the investment boom would ease, leading to a narrowing in the differential with savings.
Klaus identified a lack of natural resources, the structure of the Czech economy, and its geographical position as reasons for a perpetuated trade deficit.
In the first nine months of the year, imports rose by 15.2 percent to 551.2 billion crowns, while exports increased by 5.9 percent to 440.5 billion crowns.
The Czech Statistical Bureau forecasted that the foreign trade deficit would reach 163.3 billion crowns for the whole of 1996.

The Czech government is considering how to diversify its natural gas supplies, which currently come solely from Russia.
Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy stated that this decision will be one of the toughest for the cabinet.
Dlouhy plans to submit four options for securing future gas supplies but has not detailed them yet.
Dlouhy indicated that Russia will remain the dominant supplier of natural gas.
A source at Dlouhy's ministry confirmed a report listing four options for gas supply diversification.
The first option involves purchasing all natural gas from Gazprom with a long-term agreement until 2016 and price guarantees until 1998.
The second option includes purchasing some Russian gas indirectly through Nederlandse Gasunie NV and Wintershall, with supplies starting in 1998.
The third option is to finalize and maintain an agreement for Norwegian gas until 2017.
The fourth option involves limited purchases from Mobil Europe Gas Inc., Brigitta Erdgas und Erdoel, and British Gas plc.
The Czech Republic has reduced its dependence on Russian crude oil by building a new pipeline to Germany but remains dependent on Gazprom for natural gas.

The three-party Czech coalition cabinet agreed to find a new director for the country's secret service.
The former chief of the secret service resigned amid a political spying controversy.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus requested each coalition party to propose a candidate for the new director of the BIS.
Acting-director Stanislav Devaty resigned after accusations of spying and cover-up were made against the BIS.
Josef Lux, head of the Christian Democratic Union, accused the BIS of spying on him three years ago.
The Civic Democratic Alliance also made similar accusations against the BIS last year.
Jaroslav Jiru was appointed to lead the BIS until a new director is named.
The political situation intensified before the Senate elections, which are important for Klaus's government.
The Senate elections are seen as a significant indicator for the future of Klaus's centre-right cabinet.
Klaus expressed concern over statements made by opposition leader Milos Zeman regarding the Interior Ministry and BIS.

Czech power producer CEZ a.s. reported a nine-month net profit of 8.4 billion crowns, an increase from 7.4 billion crowns for the same period last year.
The profit increase was attributed to higher household electricity demand.
CEZ's gross profit for the period remained flat at 13.1 billion crowns.
Under Czech accounting standards, CEZ's profit for the first nine months was 7.04 billion crowns, up from 6.7 billion crowns last year.
CEZ maintained its profit forecast under Czech standards for the whole year at 8.1 billion crowns, the same as last year.
CEZ wrote off 4.1 billion crowns in the first nine months, compared to 3.4 billion crowns in the same period of 1995.
CEZ paid 4.7 billion crowns in income tax, down from 5.7 billion crowns last year.
Overall electricity demand rose by 5.5 percent during the period, with a projected record high of 55.3 terawatt-hours for the whole of 1996.
Household electricity consumption increased by 10.5 percent, while demand from large clients rose by almost two percent.
CEZ's short-term indebtedness increased due to unpaid receivables from regional distributors, totaling 3.2 billion crowns as of September 30.

Pavel Kysilka, vice-governor of the Czech National Bank (CNB), stated that the 'Big Four' state-controlled Czech banks need owners to secure their growth and international competitiveness.
Kysilka emphasized the need for strong, stable, sound, and efficient banks capable of competing in the European market.
The CNB has refined its concept for selling the state's stakes in the four largest banks, which was submitted to the government last month.
The state holds 49 percent in Komercni Banka a.s., 45 percent in Ceska Sporitelna a.s., 66 percent in Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. (CSOB), and 31.5 percent in IPB a.s.
The CNB's public plan includes a quick selloff of the IPB stake, a merger of CSOB and Sporitelna, and an incremental sale of Komercni shares.
The ultimate decision regarding the privatization of the 'Big Four' banks rests with the government.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has expressed opposition to the merger of CSOB and Sporitelna.
Klaus and the Finance Ministry have agreed that the IPB stake should be sold quickly to a strategic foreign investor.
Nomura and ING Bank NV are considered front runners for the IPB stake, while ABN Amro has also shown interest.
Martin Kocourek, Klaus's economic adviser, mentioned that Union Bank of Switzerland is seeking to arrange the sale of IPB's stake.

The Czech Republic could have a sugar surplus of 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes from this year's campaign.
High local production costs and a world sugar surplus will limit sugar exports from the Czech Republic.
The Agriculture Ministry plans to buy some surplus sugar for strategic reserves.
The Agriculture Ministry will prepare indirect support for exporters but will not provide direct export subsidies.
Producers are expected to sell as much sugar as possible domestically due to lower world prices.
Eva Divisova of the Agriculture Ministry stated that the surplus is expected to be up to 80,000 to 100,000 tonnes.
Total sugar production in the Czech Republic is projected to be between 520,000 and 540,000 tonnes raw value.
Net sugar exports from the Czech Republic in 1996 are expected to be about 4,000 tonnes.
Divisova did not disclose how much sugar the state would buy for reserves, citing it as confidential.
Slovakia is not importing sugar due to higher local output.

The Czech Republic's sole supplier of natural gas is Russia's Gazprom.
Gazprom has agreed to start talks on a long-term supply deal.
The proposed contract would involve supplies of 8.9 billion cubic metres (bcm) per year.
The Czech government aims to diversify its gas supplies.
The Czech Republic currently imports approximately nine bcm of natural gas a year from Gazprom.
The current contract with Gazprom is a three-year agreement ending in 1998, extendable for another three years.
The consumption of natural gas in the Czech Republic is expected to rise to about 12 to 13 bcm per year in several years.
The Czech Republic wants to cover the increase in consumption from alternative sources.
The aim is to bring the contract with Gazprom to a European standard of 15 to 25 years.
Talks will start with several potential partners to diversify gas supplies.

A reporter called the secretary of Mr. Novak at a major Czech industrial company.
The secretary stated that Mr. Novak's first name is Doctor.
Czechs place significant importance on academic titles.
Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda resigned from cabinet after using the title 'Doctor of Law' which he did not attain.
Jiri Pehe is the head of research at Prague's Open Media Research Institute.
Normal office discussions in the Czech Republic often include addressing colleagues by their academic titles.
Kalvoda completed law school but did not finish the certification process to become a doctor of law.
Kalvoda's colleagues and party used the title 'Doctor' in literature without his refutation.
Four other deputies in the lower house of parliament also used unauthorized academic titles.
Only one of the four deputies resigned from parliament, while the others have refused to resign.

The Czech ruling centre-right coalition agreed to name Vlasta Parkanova as justice minister.
Jan Kalvoda resigned last month after admitting to using an unattained 'Doctor of Law' title.
Coalition leaders decided to wait on choosing a replacement for Kalvoda as deputy prime minister.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus confirmed the approval of Parkanova's nomination at a news conference.
Parkanova could be officially appointed by President Vaclav Havel as soon as Tuesday.
Parkanova is 45 years old and currently serves as chief of staff at the Interior Ministry.
Parkanova would be the first woman in the Prague government since the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993.
The ODA requested to postpone the nomination of a new deputy prime minister until after their party congress in March.
Kalvoda's position as chairman of the ODA will also be decided at the March party congress.
The ODA has four seats in the 16-member cabinet under a coalition agreement with the ODS and KDU-CSL.

The Czech government approved rules for a tender to sell a 34 percent stake in Aero Vodochody a.s.
The tender is open to both domestic and foreign investors.
The winner of the tender will be announced on April 2.
Chemapol Group a.s., Boeing Co in alliance with Ceske Aerolinie a.s., and CIMEX Holding a.s. have shown interest in Aero.
Aero Vodochody is developing the L-159, a light training subsonic fighter.
The Czech army has signed a contract to buy 72 L-159s.
The Czech government approved a 3.26 billion crown package to clear Aero's debts.
Aero's basic capital was reduced from 962 million crowns to one million crowns.
The investor must pay most of the share price from their own assets.
The state will retain at least a 34 percent stake in Aero Vodochody.

A common Western view of Tibet is that it is an inaccessible, romantic, and mystic place where Chinese police torture Buddhist monks.
A widespread Chinese view of Tibet is that it is a mysterious and terrifying land where lanterns are made from human skin and skulls are used for goblets.
Robbie Barnett, who runs the London-based Tibet Information Network, claims that Tibet is used as a Cold War icon by anti-Chinese opportunists.
Tibetans engage in daily activities such as prostrating before Buddhist shrines, buying yak meat in the Lhasa market, and cycling to discos.
Lhasa, Tibet's capital, is one of the world's highest cities at 3,684 meters (12,087 ft).
Lhasa is undergoing a construction boom that is transforming its outskirts into a Chinese town.
Many Western human rights groups and pro-Tibet activists claim that Tibet is experiencing sinicisation and that wealth is concentrated among Han Chinese at the expense of Tibetans.
Beijing states that the Tibetan population in the region is 2.3 million, while the Han Chinese population is fewer than 100,000.
Official figures indicate that Tibet's economy is growing by about 10 percent a year, with rural per capita incomes around 600 yuan ($72) and urban incomes about 2,000 yuan ($240).
China compares the current standard of living in Tibet to the traditional feudal system that existed until after the People's Liberation Army entered Tibet in 1950.

Tibet's biggest leather factory polluted one of the world's cleanest rivers for 36 years.
The factory experienced significant financial losses before receiving aid from Germany in 1988.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl was impressed by Tibet's scenic beauty and Buddhist culture during his visit.
German aid and technicians helped modernize the leather factory, improving its environmental practices.
The factory reported its first net profit of 200,000 yuan ($24,000) last year.
Manager Li Jishan noted that conditions at the factory were poor when he arrived in 1961.
The leather factory was relocated to Lhasa in 1959 to supply leather for soldiers in Tibet.
The factory processes yak skins into shoes and handbags and is state-owned.
Li Jishan mentioned that the German side is strict about environmental protection.
German officials identified surplus labor as a problem at the factory, which is common in state-owned firms.

The Central Commission for Discipline Inspection of the Communist Party of China ordered members to obey party chief Jiang Zemin's call for ideological orthodoxy.
Failure to comply with the call for ideological orthodoxy may result in disciplinary punishment.
The People's Daily reported that the work style of the ruling party is considered a matter of life and death.
The commission emphasized the need for clean government and warned of corruption's threat to party rule.
Party organizations and members are urged to uphold the party's traditions and work style.
The call for ideological orthodoxy follows the party's annual policy-making plenum, which pledged to reinforce socialist values.
The discipline commission stated that violations of the plenum's decisions or disobedience to orders will lead to strict discipline.
The plenum asserted that spiritual civilization should not be sacrificed for economic reforms.
The commission called for a return to the communist puritanism associated with Chairman Mao Zedong.
Jiang Zemin has repeatedly warned that corruption poses a significant threat to the party's stability.

China's leadership has issued a directive promoting puritan Marxist values to counter Western influences.
Analysts believe this reflects a lack of innovative ideas among an ageing leadership.
A China analyst noted that the public's engagement with lengthy party documents has diminished.
The Communist Party issued a 15,000-character document warning against Western ideas like capitalism and parliamentary democracy.
The document urges vigilance against pornography and profit while promoting Marxist values.
A Western diplomat criticized the demand for ideological conformity as outdated and ineffective.
Chinese political analysts warn that the leadership's failure to adapt could lead to negative consequences.
An analyst stated that many people are no longer paying attention to the government's messages.
Analysts suggested that the leadership might resort to extreme propaganda to regain public interest.
The current Politburo is largely composed of members in their 70s who resist new ideas from younger advisers.

Wang Dan is a prominent dissident in China.
Wang Dan is expected to receive a harsh sentence for plotting to overthrow the government.
Wang Dan's mother, Wang Lingyun, stated he would plead not guilty at his trial.
The trial is set to begin at the Beijing Intermediate People's Court.
Wang Lingyun expressed concern that a harsh sentence is likely despite her son's innocence.
Court officials indicated that a verdict could be delivered within two days of the trial's start.
Wang Dan faces a minimum sentence of 10 years and a maximum penalty of death.
Human Rights Watch reported that the chances of acquittal for Wang Dan are slim.
Wang Dan's family found a lawyer to defend him with only one day to prepare.
Wang Lingyun, who has no legal background, will attend the trial as one of the defense lawyers.

China's economic growth is expected to accelerate in 1997 as Beijing increases economic activity before a Communist Party congress.
Xu Hongyuan of the State Information Centre stated that political factors may contribute to a renewed economic boom in 1997.
Xu warned that higher growth could lead to increased inflation and rising joblessness.
The gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 could reach 8,178 billion yuan ($985.3 billion), growing by 10.5 percent compared to an anticipated 9.6-9.7 percent increase in 1996.
GDP grew by 10.2 percent in 1995, and the Chinese government aims for an average growth of eight percent for the 1996-2000 Ninth Five-Year Plan.
Xu linked the higher growth forecast to the upcoming Communist Party congress, which is expected to address economic inefficiencies in state enterprises.
Diplomats and western economists believe Beijing may attempt to stimulate economic growth in 1997 to strengthen the current leadership's position before the party congress.
Xu forecasted retail price inflation to rise to about eight percent in 1997 from an expected seven percent in 1996.
Inflation was 14.8 percent last year, down from a high of 21.7 percent in 1994.
Speculation exists that China may reduce interest rates again, although central bank officials deny plans for significant changes to monetary policy.

China's bid to enter the World Trade Organisation (WTO) is being discussed by the world's richest nations this week.
Delegates from the Quad, which includes the United States, Japan, Canada, and the European Union, will meet for lunch on Tuesday during the WTO ministerial conference in Singapore.
The European Union is attempting to gain U.S. support for a phased accession process for China's entry into the WTO.
The United States requires China to comply with a 'road map' to open its markets and eliminate trade barriers before supporting its entry into the WTO.
China aimed to join the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade as a founding member of the WTO two years ago.
China's application to join the WTO faced opposition over entry terms, with Beijing arguing that the conditions were too stringent.
Negotiations regarding China's entry into the WTO are progressing slowly in Geneva.
The Quad meeting aims to reconcile differences between the United States and Europe regarding the terms for China's entry into the WTO.
EU Commissioner for Trade Sir Leon Brittan emphasized the need to restart negotiations for China's membership at the conference.
Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong supported China's entry into the WTO while reiterating that new applicants must meet necessary criteria.

China accused politics of delaying its application to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
China expressed a desire to join the WTO as soon as possible.
Long Yongtu, China's Deputy Minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, made these statements at a WTO ministerial meeting in Singapore.
Long claimed that some members are using the negotiation process to address bilateral trade disputes unrelated to WTO rules.
China was disappointed when it failed to join the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and the WTO at its inception two years ago.
The United States has opposed China's request to join the WTO as a developing country.
The United States argues that China's economy size necessitates entry as a developed nation.
The United States requires China to comply with a 'road map' to open its markets before it can gain U.S. support for WTO entry.
China believes the conditions of the road map are too demanding.
Long stated that China has a positive attitude towards joining the WTO but does not expect miraculous benefits from membership.

China identified its war on bourgeois decadence as the top news event of 1996.
Missile tests off Taiwan were also considered a top news event in China for 1996.
Improved ties with the United States and the jailing of a dozen dissidents were not included in China's top news events for 1996.
The top 10 news events in China for 1996 were selected by senior editors of major Communist Party-linked newspapers.
The list of top news events issued by the Xinhua news agency reflected the party line.
The annual plenum of China's ruling Communist Party in October was the top event selected by Beijing editors.
The plenum adopted a 15,000-word document promoting socialist ethics and opposing bourgeois Western liberalism.
Santa Claus was featured in department stores in Beijing and Shanghai during Christmas Eve.
The missile tests and live-fire war games near Taiwan ranked fourth in the top 10 news events.
China's resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong was the second news item on the list.

A bomb exploded outside a government office in Lhasa, Tibet on December 25.
Chinese authorities described the blast as 'an appalling act of terrorism'.
The explosion shattered windows for 100 metres around the site.
Local officials reported no casualties from the explosion.
The bomb was the largest set off by anti-Chinese activists in Tibet.
The explosion occurred at the Lhasa City Chengguan District Government Office.
A government official stated that the explosion could be heard from a long distance.
Local radio reported that the bombing was organized and planned by the Dalai Lama clique.
The Tibet Information Network reported that five people were wounded, including two nightwatchmen.
The Chinese government regularly blames followers of the Dalai Lama for anti-Chinese unrest.

China's parliament failed to pass an anti-corruption bill on Monday.
The proposed law faced debate over whether it should specifically target government officials.
Heated discussions occurred during the week-long session of the National People's Congress.
Disputes included the scope of the death penalty in proposed amendments to the criminal law.
The draft law on administrative supervision was withdrawn from voting.
The law was withdrawn due to disagreements among legislators about its name.
Some lawmakers wanted the bill named the Law On Administrative Supervision.
Others argued it should be called the Law on Supervision without reference to administration.
Qiao Shi suggested the issue be voted on at the next standing committee session in February 1997.
Debate included amendments that would define draft and dereliction of duty and increase the types of officials subject to the law.

China must reform state enterprises in 1997, according to Vice Premier Zhu Rongji.
Zhu Rongji reported that 75 percent of China's state firms lost money last year.
Total losses in the government sector reached 69 billion yuan ($8.3 billion) from January to October.
Zhu cited duplication of products, widespread smuggling, and surplus workers as the main reasons for state enterprise losses.
Zhu emphasized the need for reorganizing management in state enterprises to address growing losses.
He called for the promotion of re-employment projects for surplus workers or those laid off.
Zhu recommended standardizing the bankruptcy system and encouraging mergers to address loss-making state firms.
He advised against selling entire companies and suggested that enterprises should take on a portion of the ailing firm's debt.
The government plans to write off up to 30 billion yuan ($3.6 billion) in debt.

Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) plans to buy two new Airbus A320 aircraft and lease one Airbus A330.
The delivery of the two Airbus A320 aircraft is scheduled for 1998 and 1999.
Dragonair has options for five additional Airbus A320 aircraft.
A Dragonair spokesman stated that talks on new aircraft have been taking place but could not confirm the acquisition.
Dragonair currently operates a fleet of seven Airbus A320s and four A330s.
The airline has expressed a need for additional aircraft due to increasing demand.
Industry analysts view the expansion as a positive sign for future business prospects.
Slot restrictions at Hong Kong's Kai Tak airport are a major constraint for Dragonair's expansion.
Expansion would benefit Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, which owns an 18 percent stake in Dragonair.
Dragonair has recently started new services to Qingdao and Khaohsiung and has plans for additional routes to Chongqing, Urumqi, and Shantou.

Virgin Atlantic Airways is considering replacing its Airbus Industrie A340 aircraft with Boeing Co 747-400s due to high demand between Hong Kong and London.
David Woodward, general manager commercial for Virgin Atlantic Cargo, stated that aircraft availability and scheduling prevent an immediate change.
Woodward mentioned that the Hong Kong service has been highly successful and that there has been too little capacity.
There is a possibility that the aircraft change could happen in the near future.
A senior Virgin executive indicated that the carrier hopes to increase its daily flights from Hong Kong to London to 10 a week.
Virgin Atlantic has plans to start a London to Shanghai service.
Industry observers believe that the lack of slots at Hong Kong's overcrowded airport is a significant obstacle.
Larger aircraft are considered a short-term solution until Hong Kong's new airport opens.
Brinkley Chan, Virgin's assistant manager in Hong Kong, stated that there has been no progress on a proposal to add a freighter to its fleet due to low market rates between Hong Kong and Europe and low yields.

Salomon Brothers forecast long term growth prospects for Thai Airways International Ltd.
Peter Negline authored a 24-page equity research report recommending traders buy Thai shares below 50 baht.
The report states that Thai Airways has strong long term growth prospects due to a strong local economy.
Thai Airways has global alliances with Deutsche Lufthansa AG and United Airlines.
Thai Airways has a regional competitive advantage due to proximity to European markets and the stability of the baht currency.
Negline stated that a robust Thai economy should support strong passenger and cargo traffic growth.
Negline warned of lower yields affecting the airline's operations.
The report suggests that management should be able to ensure costs fall as fast as yield declines due to a new aircraft fleet.
The report highlights opportunities for growth in lower operating costs through cargo.
Thai Airways has focused on growing its cargo business over the last two years, with freight revenue tonne kilometres growing at 11 percent per annum.

Demand for space has eased slightly as a backlog is cleared and some airlines provide extra capacity.
Key ex-Hong Kong rates have continued to rise according to Reuters research.
Airlines and freight forwarders report brisk business as Hong Kong's peak season begins.
Airlines on European routes have raised rates for the second time within three weeks.
A rise of 50 HK cents per kg occurred on October 16 following a HK$2 per kg rise on October 1.
Transpacific demand is strong, allowing rates to firm slightly.
High demand on passenger flights is reducing bellyhold capacity for many airlines.
Sam Chung, chairman of the Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents, stated the market is strong, especially for the United States.
Two U.S. airlines have added extra aircraft to meet heavy trans-Pacific demand.
Polar Air Cargo is using two additional Boeing 747 freighters for routes between Hong Kong and Chicago and New York.

British Airways will carry an extra 70 tonnes of air cargo a week when it begins a new route over China.
The new route will be used for British Airways' twice-daily passenger services between Hong Kong and London.
Chris Humphrey is the regional cargo manager Pacific for British Airways.
The new northern route will result in shorter journey times for British Airways' Boeing 747-400 aircraft.
The aircraft will not need to carry as much fuel, allowing an increase in cargo payload by five to six tonnes per flight on average.
The new routing was negotiated during talks between the Chinese and British governments.
The new route also benefits British Airways' competitors, Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and Virgin Atlantic.
Cathay Pacific and Virgin Atlantic will also start the new shorter route on October 27.
The new routing via Urumqi in China will provide benefits for the winter schedule starting on October 27.
The extra capacity generated will be around 70 tonnes a week, comparable to adding another 747 freighter on the route.

British Airways World Cargo (BAWC) will employ a fourth weekly freighter between Hong Kong and London starting next year.
Chris Humphrey is the regional cargo manager Pacific for BAWC.
BAWC is optimistic about the economic growth prospects in Hong Kong and China.
BAWC currently operates three Boeing 747 freighters a week between Hong Kong and London Gatwick.
The freighters are wet leased from Atlas Air Inc.
Atlas Air uses converted passenger 747s for long-term wet-lease contracts.
BAWC reported an 18.5 percent increase in market share between January and July, measured by Freight Tonne Kilometres (FTK).
The average traffic increase for Association of European Airlines (AEA) carriers in the Asia Pacific Region was 8.2 percent.
Freight tonnage from Hong Kong to BA's worldwide network increased by 31 percent in the first half of the financial year from April to September.

DHL Worldwide Express plans to open 14 new offices in China within the next three years.
DHL will employ an additional 600 staff in China within the next three years.
DHL has a 30 percent market share in China and celebrates its tenth anniversary of operations there next month.
DHL expects China to account for 10 percent of all its sales within Asia by the year 2000.
DHL aims to expand its Chinese network from 19 to 26 offices by the end of this year and to 40 offices within the next three years.
The new offices will be established in joint ventures with Chinese partners in cities including Harbin, Pudong, and Kunming.
DHL's operations in China began in 1986 through a joint venture with Sinotrans.
DHL became the first joint venture to offer express links between domestic Chinese companies three years ago.
DHL does not operate its own fleet of aircraft in China, which provides a competitive advantage over rivals like Federal Express.
DHL has not yet started offering its Jumbo Box product to customers in China.

Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) is increasing its flights to Sendai in Japan from four to six a week starting October 29.
Philip Chen is the chief operating officer of Dragonair.
Dragonair has been serving Hiroshima since 1992 and Sendai since 1993.
Dragonair's services to Hiroshima and Sendai are considered successful.
One Airbus Industrie A320 from Dragonair's fleet will be used for the additional flights to Sendai.
On October 24, Airbus announced that Dragonair signed a contract for two additional A320s.
Dragonair has options for five more A320s and has leased another Airbus A330-300.
The new planes will support route expansion to China and other Asian destinations.
Hong Kong's new round-the-clock airport is expected to open in 18 months.

Lauda Air has reported significant passenger growth on the Hong Kong to Vienna route.
There has been a 34 percent increase in the number of passengers on this route over the past year.
Lauda Air's revenue from this route has grown by 42 percent in the past year.
Cargo revenue for Lauda Air is currently three percent below last year's level.
Lauda Air operates a Boeing 767-300 flight from Hong Kong to Vienna via Bangkok twice a week.
This flight averages eight to nine tonnes of belly cargo, with watches being a common item.
Sunny Yu, Lauda's Hong Kong general manager, cited a small price war and overcapacity as obstacles to cargo rates.
Lauda Air expects another double-digit rise in passenger numbers this year.
The current number of passengers flying between Hong Kong and Vienna is approximately 9,000.
Lauda Air faces slot restrictions at Kai Tak airport, limiting its ability to add more flight frequencies.

China Southern Airlines will start its first European service to Amsterdam on November 26.
Ma Ting Wei is the manager of the airline's advertising division.
China Southern plans to start flying to Los Angeles in mid-March next year.
Plans for a third international destination to Brisbane in Australia have not yet been finalized.
The service to Amsterdam and the Los Angeles link will both use Boeing 777 aircraft.
Two Boeing 777 aircraft have arrived, and two more will arrive at Guangzhou within the next two months.
The Amsterdam service will be the airline's 26th international route.
The new European destination is in response to customer demand.
The Amsterdam service is a result of an Air Service Agreement between the Dutch and Chinese governments.
The agreement took five years to finalize and allows KLM to fly to Beijing and Martinair to operate a freighter service to Guangzhou.

Federal Express Corporation (Fedex) is planning to utilize a former U.S. military base in the Philippines.
Fedex has its main Asian hub at the former U.S. naval base at Subic Bay.
Senior officials from Fedex have visited the former Clark U.S. air force base.
Clark International Airport Corporation's Operations Vice President, Tereso Isleta, stated that Fedex is expected to become the airport's first cargo operator next month.
The first flight of breeding cattle from Australia is expected to arrive at Clark International Airport in the next few weeks.
David Clarke, Asia Pacific public relations manager for Fedex, mentioned that the former base could serve as an alternative to Subic in case of bad weather.
Clarke emphasized Fedex's commitment to Subic Bay, where the company recently celebrated its first anniversary of operations.
Fedex plans to transport live breeding cattle from Sydney, Australia, using a specially adapted McDonnell Douglas MD-11 aircraft.
Fedex has experience in transporting thoroughbred horses in Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore, and the Middle East.
Clark International Airport Corporation is funded by the Philippines government's Bases Conversion Development Authority.

Air Hong Kong Ltd (AHK) chief operating officer is Stanley Hui.
AHK started its first trans-Pacific service on August 25.
Stanley Hui stated that the start of this service indicates the airline is headed in the right direction.
Hui described the start of the trans-Pacific service as an important milestone.
AHK did not make any profit in the first half of 1996 due to low yields.
AHK made its first profit last year, which Hui described as very healthy.
Four years ago, AHK was close to going out of business.
Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd acquired a 75 percent stake in AHK.
AHK cut loss-making routes and retired old aircraft.
AHK acquired three newly converted Boeing 747-200s.

An American airline completed a proving flight over Russian air space.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) stated this flight is an important milestone for the Future Air Navigation System (FANS) on trans-Pacific routes.
The United Airlines Boeing 747-400 flight took place from Chicago to Tokyo's Narita airport on November 15.
Singapore Airlines, Japan Airlines, and Cathay Pacific Airways Limited are expected to conduct more trials over the next three weeks.
FANS is the next generation air traffic management system that uses satellite navigation.
FANS technology is expected to provide competitive advantages such as reduced costs, more direct routes, and less fuel consumption.
The U.S. is working on a new bilateral agreement with Russia to develop air traffic control infrastructure in the Far East.
David Behrens mentioned that there have been challenges in getting demonstration flights approved by Russian authorities.
Airlines that have invested in FANS technology are awaiting approval for a new 'fast track' routing across the central Pacific Ocean.
Korean Airlines is expected to save 40 minutes on U.S. bound flights from Seoul with the implementation of FANS technology.

British Energy Plc announced job cuts that received criticism from unions and did not impress the stock market.
Philip Hollobone, a utilities analyst at Williams de Broe, stated that the job cuts do not improve British Energy's prospects.
British Energy plans to cut 1,460 jobs in Scotland and Wales to save 50 million pounds ($78 million) over three years.
The company will incur a one-off restructuring charge of 100 million pounds, which has already been accounted for.
Chief executive Robert Hawley indicated that further savings may be possible through reductions in office costs.
Union representatives criticized the job cuts as a high-risk strategy that could negatively impact training, standards, and safety.
The Nuclear Installations Inspectorate (NII) will review British Energy's plans and may take regulatory action if safety is compromised.
Hawley asserted that safety is the company's primary concern, rather than profit.
British Energy's stock market debut in July was affected by temporary closures of two reactors due to cracks.
The Conservative government has a 12 percent stake in British Energy and proceeded with its privatization despite public discontent.

The stock of media group Pearson closed higher on Monday.
Pearson shares closed 34-1/2 pence higher at 731p after reaching a high of 745p.
6.7 million shares of Pearson changed hands on that day.
An analyst stated that the price increase was due to management changes and revived bid speculation.
A report indicated that BSkyB might be planning a bid for Pearson worth over 4 billion British pounds.
BSkyB's chief executive, Sam Chisholm, denied any talks regarding a bid for Pearson.
A BSkyB spokesman confirmed that there were no discussions about a bid for Pearson.
Pearson owns the Financial Times, Penguin Books, and several television production companies.
Pearson appointed Marjorie Scardino as chief executive and Dennis Stevenson as chairman.
Analysts believe any potential bid for Pearson is likely to occur before the new management takes control.

Cable & Wireless has merged with its own Mercury telecoms business and the British operations of NYNEX, Bell Canada International, and Videotron to create Cable & Wireless Communications.
The merger created a company valued at $7.5 billion.
Cable & Wireless Communications reaches almost 2.5 million homes in Britain.
Oftel banned a promotion by BT that involved discounts on subscriptions to BSkyB due to a ban on BT's use of its network for entertainment.
BT shares fell by 5.5 pence to 348.5 pence following the Oftel decision.
BSkyB shares fell by 17 pence to 661.5 pence after the Oftel decision.
Cable & Wireless shares rose by 7.5 pence to 474.5 pence after the merger announcement.
BT expressed confusion over Oftel's decision and claimed the promotion was beneficial for customers.
The Conservative government plans to review BT's ban from cable television in 2001, with a possible early review in 1998.
The Labour party is currently leading in polls.

J. Sainsbury Plc announced plans to launch a jointly owned banking service with Bank of Scotland.
This will be the first supermarket banking service in Britain's food retailing business.
Sainsbury applied to the Bank of England for authorisation for the new bank.
The new bank will be owned 55 percent by Sainsbury and 45 percent by Bank of Scotland.
Sainsbury has about 690 supermarkets and other outlets in Britain.
Sainsbury's Shaw's chain has 105 stores in the United States.
Sainsbury also owns a stake in Giant, which has 169 U.S. outlets.
The new venture will be called Sainsbury's Bank and will offer telebanking services.
Sainsbury's Bank will target 12 million customers and will launch next year.
Sainsbury's Bank will offer Classic and Gold Visa cards along with account and card-based services.

Electricity stocks increased on Friday due to rumors of a U.S. buyer for one of five remaining regional utilities.
Analysts believe the upcoming results season could stimulate market activity.
Chris Perry, an analyst at Charterhouse Tilney, stated that there will be a focus on the companies' ability to distribute more cash.
Electricity sector companies will begin their half-year results season towards the end of November.
East Midlands Electricity's stock rose after a report suggested a potential bid from Houston Industries at around 750 pence per share.
Houston Industries had previously been expected to buy one of the regional electricity companies but shifted focus to acquiring NorAm Energy for $3.8 billion.
East Midlands Electricity's shares reached a high of 565 pence before closing at 562 pence, an increase of 44 pence.
Other independent power utilities also saw stock increases, including Yorkshire Electricity, Southern Electric, Northern Electric, and London Electricity.
Nigel Hawkins from Yamaichi stated that East Midlands Electricity is the most likely candidate for a bid due to its smaller size and focus on distribution.
Analysts noted that U.S. companies may not be the only potential buyers in the electricity sector, which has seen significant takeover activity since privatization in 1990.

CalEnergy of the U.S. made a $1.225 billion bid for British regional electricity company Northern Electric.
This is CalEnergy's second bid challenge for Northern Electric in just over a year.
Analysts believe Northern Electric may eventually accept an agreed bid.
Philip Hollobone from Williams de Broe stated that the bid price could rise to 650-657 pence per share from the current 630 pence offer.
CE Electric, which is jointly owned by CalEnergy (70 percent) and Peter Kiewit Sons (30 percent), offered 630 pence for each ordinary share of Northern Electric.
The deal also includes an offer of 103 pence per preference share.
CE Electric acquired 12.72 percent of Northern Electric at the bid price of 630 pence.
Northern Electric previously fended off a hostile bid from Trafalgar House, which is now owned by Sweden's Kvaerner.
Trafalgar House's previous bid included a special package worth 560 million pounds for shareholders.
CalEnergy chairman David Sokol described the offer as 'a very full price' and noted that the only disagreement with Northern Electric was on value.

J. Sainsbury Plc reported a fall in half year profits and sluggish sales.
Half year pretax profits for Sainsbury decreased to 393 million pounds from 456 million pounds in the same period last year.
Sainsbury announced a dividend payout of 3.5 pence per share, an increase from 3.4 pence.
Sainsbury experienced its first fall in full year profits for 22 years when it reported in May.
Sainsbury's shares rose by 11 pence to 366 pence by 1120 GMT.
Current sales from comparable stores, excluding petrol, are rising in line with inflation of around three percent.
Tesco reported a 7.5 percent gain in sales in September.
David Sainsbury stated that the company aims to improve sales performance.
Sainsbury introduced its Reward loyalty card four months ago to compete with Tesco's ClubCard.
Dino Adriano will take over as chief executive of the supermarket unit on March 8.

Dominion Resources agreed to a 1.3 billion pound bid for East Midlands Electricity.
East Midlands Electricity is one of five remaining British independent regional electricity companies.
East Midlands shares were trading below the 670 pence per share offer price.
Concerns emerged that the bid might face obstacles from British competition authorities.
Dominion Resources previously considered a bid at a price not much in excess of 608 pence per share.
East Midlands Electricity rejected the 608 pence per share price, stating it undervalued the company.
Dominion executives met with East Midlands management to discuss the takeover price.
East Midlands chairman Sir Nigel Rudd stated the board recommended the offer as fair value.
East Midlands shares were trading at 624 pence after an increase of 13 pence.
The Monopolies and Mergers Commission is expected to closely examine the deal.

Dominion Resources agreed to a 1.3 billion pound ($2.15 billion) bid for East Midlands Electricity.
East Midlands Electricity is one of five remaining British independent regional electricity companies.
East Midlands shares were trading below the 670 pence per share offer price.
Concerns emerged that the bid might face obstacles from British competition authorities.
Dominion Resources previously considered a bid at a price not much in excess of 608 pence per share.
East Midlands Electricity rejected the 608 pence per share price, stating it undervalued the company.
Executives from Dominion met with East Midlands management to discuss the takeover price.
East Midlands chairman Sir Nigel Rudd stated that the board recommended the offer as fair value.
East Midlands shares were up 13 pence at 624 pence after 1400 GMT.
Seven of the original 12 regional electricity companies have been bought since March after the government's protective golden share expired.

Northern Electric is a British regional electricity company.
Northern Electric plans to release results by the end of November to demonstrate that CE Electric's $1.225 billion bid undervalues it.
CE Electric believes its offer of 630 pence per share is full and fair.
Northern Electric's half-year figures will include important financial information to show the company's value.
Northern Electric stated that CE Electric suggested a price of 700 pence per share when announcing the bid.
CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy, denied that the 700 pence price was its proposal.
CE Electric has acquired nearly 30 percent of Northern Electric.
Northern Electric plans to pay a 56.5 pence special dividend in February 1997 if CE Electric's offer lapses.
Northern Electric's chairman David Morris stated that uncertainty about the bid's approval is affecting the share price.
The British government has approved takeovers of seven of the original twelve regional electricity companies in two years.

London Electricity is a British regional electricity company.
U.S. Entergy is reportedly planning a 1.2 billion pound bid for London Electricity.
London Electricity declined to comment on the bid speculation.
Shares of London Electricity rose to a high of 665 pence before settling at 662.5 pence.
The Wall Street Journal Europe reported that Entergy's bid could be around 700 pence per share.
Confidential Entergy documents indicated the company was seeking 1.1 billion pounds for an acquisition.
The documents referred to the target company with the code name 'Atlantic'.
Entergy spokesman Patrick Sweeney stated that Entergy is interested in the British market.
Sweeney denied a report about Entergy considering a bid for Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc.
The electricity sector has seen increased bid speculation among the remaining independent regional electricity companies.

British supermarket chain Safeway reported a seven percent rise in half-year profits.
Sales at Safeway are increasing, and the company is optimistic about Christmas sales.
Colin Smith is the chief executive of Safeway.
Safeway plans to open 450,000 square feet of additional space, equivalent to about 18 stores, in the next two years.
The expansion is expected to generate approximately 5,200 jobs.
Safeway's shares fell to a low of 362 pence before recovering to 370 pence.
The company reported half-year pretax profits of 228.2 million pounds, which was within forecasts.
Safeway paid a dividend of 4.4 pence per share, which is an increase from 4.05 pence.
Sales from existing stores increased by five percent in the first five weeks of the second half.
Safeway's strategy to attract family shoppers is reflected in sales growth that outperforms the industry average.

Eurotunnel announced a deal giving bank creditors 45.5 percent of the company in exchange for eliminating 1.0 billion pounds of debt.
The restructuring involves nearly nine billion pounds of debt and unpaid interest.
The deal aims to prevent Eurotunnel from going bankrupt.
Current shareholders will own 54.5 percent of the company after the deal.
Eurotunnel co-chairman Alastair Morton stated that interest payments have been fixed and capped.
Morton indicated that the plan provides financial stability for Eurotunnel in the medium term.
Eurotunnel is currently making a profit before interest.
The company has captured around half of the market in the busiest cross-Channel route.
Eurotunnel may pay its first dividend within the next 10 years, depending on performance.
French co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle mentioned that a dividend could be possible as early as 2004 if the company performs well.

Silvio Berlusconi lost an appeal in the London High Court regarding the transfer of documents to Italian authorities investigating fraud and false accounting.
The Serious Fraud Office seized 15 bags of documents from the office of lawyer David Mills in April.
David Mills represents Berlusconi's interests in Britain.
Judges Lord Justice Simon Brown and Mr Justice Gage rejected all grounds of Berlusconi's appeal.
Brown agreed to hear an application by the appellants that could lead to an appeal to the House of Lords.
Berlusconi is on trial in Milan on corruption charges.
The appeal was against a court ruling that the documents should be sent to Italy.
The documents are linked to allegations of fraud and false accounting amounting to 51 million pounds.
Berlusconi is suspected of using offshore companies to channel payments to politicians.
Brown stated that none of the applicants has been convicted of anything and that his comments should not imply guilt.

Mercury Asset Management will make acquisitions to enhance shareholder value.
Hugh Stevenson is the chairman of Mercury Asset Management.
Profits for Mercury Asset Management rose 29 percent to 81.8 million stg from 63.6 million stg in the first half of last year.
Cash reserves increased to 261.6 million stg from 189.9 million stg at the end of March.
Stevenson stated that the U.S. is an important market for Mercury Asset Management.
The company prefers a conservative balance sheet.
The interim dividend rose to 10 pence per share from six pence per share.
