Funds under management increased to 85.9 billion stg from 70.9 billion stg at the same point last year.
The current figure for funds under management includes 2.0 billion stg of net new business.
Stevenson mentioned that it is too early to assess the long-term effects of issues at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management.

Land Securities reported signs of rental growth in some sectors of the British property market.
Peter Hunt is the chairman of Land Securities.
Hunt stated that rental growth has been patchy so far.
Rental rate growth is expected to be slower than in the 1980s.
Land Securities reported a pre-tax profit of 128.9 million pounds for the first half of the financial year.
The previous pre-tax profit was 118.1 million pounds.
Land Securities announced an increased interim dividend of 7.35 pence.
The company has plans for major shopping centre schemes in Canterbury, York, and Sunderland.
The annual level of expenditure on the current development programme is expected to peak in the second half of the financial year.
Revenue profit decreased to 115.5 million pounds from 118.2 million pounds for the period.

British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke may cut tax credits on dividends to help fund expected cuts in income tax.
Roger Bootle, group chief economist at HSBC Markets, believes Clarke may target pension funds for resources.
A reduction of tax credits from 20 percent to 15 percent would affect tax-exempt pension funds and higher rate taxpayers with dividend income.
Coopers & Lybrand estimates that reducing tax credits could save the Inland Revenue around 1.0 billion pounds annually.
Coopers & Lybrand warns that this measure could hinder the Government's goal of encouraging private savings and may burden the corporate sector.
Bootle suggests that the proposed tax credit reduction may not be popular and could negatively impact the equity market.
Clarke has previously removed the tax credit on targeted share buy-backs and special dividends related to share consolidations and take-overs.
Most economists expect no significant changes to the basic structure of Corporation Tax in the upcoming budget.
Coopers & Lybrand indicates that minor measures may be introduced to support small businesses and entrepreneurs.
The profit-related pay scheme, which provides tax relief to employees based on company profits, may face challenges in the budget.

Royal Bank of Scotland reported a 15 percent rise in full year pretax profits to 695 million pounds ($1.2 billion).
Strong growth in UK and U.S. banking operations offset a dip at the insurance unit.
Chief Executive George Mathewson stated that the bank is reviewing options to expand market share in the south east of England.
Mathewson indicated that potential partners assume they should talk to Royal Bank due to its lack of penetration in the south east.
Royal Bank's rival, Bank of Scotland, announced a banking joint venture with retailer Sainsburys.
Abbey National announced it would offer financial services in conjunction with Safeway's loyalty card.
Mathewson did not rule out the possibility of Royal Bank acquiring an English home loans institution.
Any potential purchase would consider shareholder value and the strength of the brand name.
Some analysts have expressed doubts about Royal Bank's capital position for a major purchase, but Mathewson dismissed these doubts.
Royal Bank's U.S. bank Citizens reported profits of 61 million pounds, a 57 percent increase.

British bank Barclays sold its global custody business to investment bank Morgan Stanley.
The sale amount is undisclosed but is thought to be less than 50 million British pounds ($83 million).
The purchase by Morgan Stanley is part of the consolidation of the custody business.
The custody business includes safekeeping of securities, performance measurement, and stock lending.
Barclays Chief Executive Martin Taylor stated that global custody requires substantial investment in technology.
A Barclays spokeswoman indicated that the investment in technology would be considerable.
Morgan Stanley Europe chairman Sir David Walker said the transaction would enable a broader range of products for clients.
The combined custody assets of Barclays and Morgan Stanley would amount to approximately $390 million.
Chase Manhattan is the largest player in the global custody market with over $1 trillion in assets.
Barclays had the largest custody business in Britain, followed by Lloyds TSB and Royal Bank of Scotland.

Britain's Woolwich Building Society plans a stock market flotation in July valued at three billion pounds ($5.1 billion).
Members of the Woolwich Building Society are expected to receive an average windfall of over 1,200 pounds.
Qualifying customers will receive at least 450 free shares upon the Woolwich's conversion to public limited company (Plc) status.
The Woolwich has assets of more than 30 billion pounds and is the third largest building society in the UK.
The Woolwich expects to distribute 450 free shares to approximately 2.57 million people, including qualifying employees and pensioners.
Chief executive John Stewart stated that the Woolwich would be among Britain's top 10 banks and included in the FT-SE 100 index.
The Woolwich's market capitalisation is estimated to be between 2.96 and 3.38 billion pounds, with a mid value of 3.17 billion.
The expected price per share for the Woolwich is between 175 and 200 pence, with a mid-price of 187.5 pence.
The Woolwich is one of four building societies planning stock market flotations in 1997.
The Woolwich will be protected from takeover for five years after flotation, but could lose this protection under proposed legislation.

Lloyds Bank was fined 325,000 pounds ($550,000) by a British investment industry watchdog.
Lloyds Bank is expected to pay millions of pounds in compensation to disadvantaged customers.
The Investment Management Regulatory Organisation fined Lloyds for breaches of rules related to its pensions transfer business between April 1988 and June 1993.
Lloyds agreed to a settlement of disciplinary proceedings brought against it by IMRO.
This settlement is the fifth such settlement IMRO has made with firms guilty of improper sales of pension products.
IMRO stated that Lloyds did not obtain all relevant facts about the personal and financial circumstances of its customers for proper pension transfer advice.
IMRO indicated that Lloyds did not provide certain customers with all necessary information for making informed decisions on pension transfers.
Lloyds must pay IMRO's investigation costs of 63,000 pounds ($107,000) and contribute to its disciplinary costs.
Lloyds has offered redress to some customers and is reviewing approximately 2,600 transfer cases.
Lloyds TSB has made provisions totaling 165 million pounds ($279 million) for possible compensation payments related to the mis-selling of pension products.

Halifax Building Society is Britain's largest mortgage lender.
Halifax plans an initial public offering (IPO) in June that could be worth up to 12 billion pounds ($20 billion).
Halifax Chief Executive Mike Blackburn stated the IPO will represent the largest single extension of private share ownership in the UK.
Halifax has assets exceeding 100 billion pounds ($167.8 million).
Flotation adviser Deutsche Morgan Grenfell estimated a share price of between 390 and 450 pence ($6.54 to $7.55) per share for the IPO.
The estimated market worth of Halifax is between 10.4 billion pounds ($17.5 billion) and 12 billion pounds ($20.1 billion).
Analysts expect the final market worth to be at the top end of the estimated range due to positive market performance.
Halifax will allocate a basic 200 shares to each qualifying member in a flotation of 2.675 billion shares.
Halifax has 6.7 million investing members and two million borrowing members, with an overlap of 700,000.
The society must receive over 50 percent approval from investing members at its special general meeting on Feb. 24 for the proposal to pass.

Bankers in London hope to sign a package restructuring the 8.7 billion pounds ($14 billion) debt of Eurotunnel before the year-end deadline.
A banking source stated that the new deadline is more cautious than the previous optimistic deadline of April.
Eurotunnel and its creditor banks agreed to a nine-month extension of a debt payment standstill until the end of the year.
The debt standstill went into effect in September 1995 and was originally due to last for 18 months.
The extended standstill will allow interest to continue accruing but will not affect the debt deal applied to Eurotunnel's debt position as of October 15, 1996.
Interest and other charges due since the cut-off date will become payable when the debt deal goes into effect.
Last October, Eurotunnel and the steering committee of banks agreed on a restructuring deal that requires approval from 225 creditor banks and the company's shareholders.
The restructuring deal includes a 1.0 billion pounds swap of debt for equity at 130p per share and other financial instruments.
An amount of 4.0 billion pounds will remain as junior debt, paying a fixed interest rate until the end of 2003.
Eurotunnel shares fell to below 90p after the debt refinancing announcement last year but have remained relatively stable since.

Elizabeth Forsyth, a former aide of Asil Nadir, was released from court after her appeal against a five-year sentence for handling stolen money was allowed by three judges.
Forsyth is 60 years old and is also appealing against her money-laundering conviction.
Forsyth described her 10 months in prison as an experience and thanked the court for its understanding.
Forsyth was the chairman of South Audley Management, a firm established by Asil Nadir.
The appeal judges stated that Forsyth would not return to Holloway prison, indicating that her sentence was disproportionate.
Lord Justice Beldam stated that Forsyth should not serve any longer considering the time she has already served.
Forsyth's lawyer, Geoffrey Robertson, made a bail application for her release pending the outcome of the appeal.
Forsyth expressed her anticipation of going home and mentioned a family reunion with her son.
During her time in prison, Forsyth took up art and worked as a library orderly.
Forsyth commented on the legal system, stating that there is a lot wrong with it, but acknowledged the hard work of prison officers.

Lloyds TSB Group will begin the UK bank reporting season on February 14.
Analysts favor Lloyds TSB Group despite its trading at big premiums to the sector due to its well-positioned business mix.
Lloyds TSB is expected to report over 2.4 billion stg in pre-tax profit and a dividend per share of up to 13p.
Lloyds TSB is projected to have the highest return on equity in the sector at around 32 percent.
In 1995, Lloyds TSB made a pre-tax profit of 1.65 billion stg.
Peter Ellwood is the new chief executive of Lloyds TSB, taking over from Brian Pitman.
Brian Pitman remains at the bank as chairman.
Analysts do not expect a radical change of strategy at Lloyds TSB with Peter Ellwood's appointment.
David Poutney, a banking analyst at Panmure Gordon, expects Lloyds TSB to make a pre-tax profit of 2.45 billion stg and pay a dividend of 12.6p per share.
Poutney estimates that savings from the 1995 merger between Lloyds and TSB will rise to 350 million stg in 1998.

A senior U.S. Defence Department official dismissed Czech army detections of chemical agents released during the Gulf War.
The official stated that the incidents were not verifiable by American equipment.
U.S. Assistant Secretary of Defence Theodore Prociv said the Pentagon viewed the Czech findings as false alarms.
Prociv is in charge of the Pentagon division on chemical weapons use.
Prociv stated that without verification, a detection is not considered true.
Thousands of troops based in northern Saudi Arabia during the Gulf War reported respiratory ailments, skin rashes, and muscle pain.
Veterans groups have linked these conditions, known as 'Gulf War Syndrome', to exposure to low-level chemical agents.
The New York Times reported that U.S. commanders ignored warnings of chemical detections made by the Czech unit in January 1991.
Prociv said U.S. equipment could not verify the Czech warnings.
Pentagon officials admitted that over 15,000 American troops may have been exposed to nerve gas in March 1991.

Italy aims to help integrate former East Bloc countries into NATO.
Undersecretary for Foreign Affairs Piero Fassino stated that Italy supports integrating fringe candidates like Slovakia and Romania.
Fassino identified Hungary, the Czech Republic, Poland, and Slovenia as primary NATO members.
Fassino mentioned that Slovakia and Romania could potentially join NATO.
Fassino emphasized the importance of Slovakia and Romania executing agreements with Hungary to protect ethnic Hungarians.
Fassino stated that NATO's standards of democracy must be assessed before rejecting Slovakia and Romania.
Fassino argued that integration allows for the enforcement of NATO standards, while isolation does not.
Fassino cited Turkey as an example of ineffective pressure due to isolation from the EU.
Both the EU and the United States have criticized Slovakia for slow democratic reforms.
Fassino believes integrating Slovakia is more beneficial than isolating it due to its strategic geographical position.

The Czech consumer price index rose 0.5 percent in October.
Year-on-year inflation in the Czech Republic was 8.7 percent in October, down from 8.9 percent in September.
The moving 12-month average of inflation remained unchanged at 8.7 percent in October.
Food, drinks, and tobacco prices rose by one percentage point in October.
Clothing prices increased by 1.2 percent in October.
Analysts stated that the overall inflation result was in line with expectations or slightly lower.
Vladimir Kreidl, an analyst at Patria Finance, indicated that October's inflation result was slightly better than expected.
Kreidl maintained a forecast of nine percent for average inflation at the end of 1996, with 8.8 percent being achievable.
Vladimir Dlouhy, Industry and Trade Minister, expressed a desire for average inflation to be below 8.7 percent for the whole year.
The Czech government had forecast average inflation to slow to 8.0 percent in 1996.

Dr. Richard Salzmann is the president of Komercni Banka, the largest bank in the Czech Republic.
Salzmann believes the Czech banking system is fundamentally sound and improving despite some recent failures among smaller banks.
He advocates for increased fairness and transparency in the Czech economy to combat secrecy and prevent banks from being run as private fiefdoms.
Salzmann is running for a seat in the newly-established Czech Senate in the upcoming November elections.
He aims to restore good practices in the banking industry and improve the reputation of the Czech finance sector.
Salzmann emphasizes the importance of better risk management in banking.
Komercni Banka and three other large banks account for about 80 percent of all Czech banking activity.
These banks have increased their reserves to meet Western banking standards and have improved their risk management techniques.
Salzmann noted that the large banks have built up significant reserves in recent years.
He attributed the recent failure of Kreditni Banka a.s. to the greed and naivete of the bank's founders.

Volkswagen AG's Czech unit, Skoda Auto a.s., launched sales of the new sedan, the Octavia.
The Octavia is built on a common VW platform designed for the 1998 Audi A3 and upgraded Golf.
Skoda aims to expand its market penetration with the Octavia, its first post-Communist mid-sized car.
Skoda's strategic markets include central and eastern Europe, western Europe, and some Asian markets.
Skoda expects to sell Octavias in all of its 66 markets.
The Octavia received a positive reception at showrooms in Prague.
The car will be available in the domestic market with three petrol and two diesel engine options.
The top-of-the-line SLX automatic model is priced at 497,900 crowns, while the base model is priced at 335,700 crowns.
Skoda plans to produce 64,000 Octavias in 1997 and increase production to 90,000 in 1998.
Skoda Chairman Ludvik Kalma expects 20,000 Octavias to be sold annually in the home market.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party received 36 percent of the nationwide vote in the first round of Senate elections.
The centre-left opposition Social Democrats received 20 percent of the vote.
Only 35 percent of the electorate participated in the elections.
The Civic Democrats won three Senate seats outright in the first round and 73 candidates advanced to the runoff.
The Civic Democrats received less than 30 percent of the vote in June's general elections, resulting in the loss of their lower house majority.
Analysts predict a mild positive impact on local financial markets from the Civic Democrats' performance.
Radek Maly, an economist at Citibank Prague, stated that the low turnout makes it difficult to draw conclusions about voter sentiment.
The Czech crown has traded around 26.9 to the dollar and 17.8 to the mark, approximately 2.5 percent above parity with the central bank's mark/dollar basket.
Miroslav Nosal, an equities analyst at Patria Finance, indicated that a premature general election is unlikely and that the stock market is focused on macroeconomic fundamentals.
Nosal noted that poor regulation and transparency are already reflected in share prices, but many stocks remain attractive from a fundamental perspective.

The Czech Republic has its first Senate since before World War Two.
The governing coalition won 52 seats in the new upper house of parliament.
Voter turnout for the Senate elections was only 30 percent.
Many voters believe the Senate, which has limited powers, is unnecessary.
The coalition lost its majority in the lower house, the Chamber of Deputies, six months ago.
The Senate was established in the 1993 constitution after Czechoslovakia split into separate Czech and Slovak states.
Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) won 32 seats in the Senate.
The Social Democrats won 25 Senate seats.
The junior coalition parties, the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) and Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), won 13 and 7 seats respectively.
Analysts viewed the Senate elections as a gauge for potential early elections in the lower house.

The Czech crown firmed to its highest level against its mark/dollar basket on Thursday.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated that devaluation was not needed despite a widening trade gap.
By mid-morning, the crown was approximately 4.3 percent above its daily parity rate set by the Czech National Bank (CNB).
The crown was valued at 26.005 to the dollar and 17.600 to the mark at 1130 GMT.
The CNB fixed the crown 4.24 percent above parity with the basket after a 3.9 percent increase on Wednesday.
Dealers indicated that the crown could challenge 4.5 percent against parity before leveling off.
Klaus supported CNB Governor Josef Tosovsky's view that a stronger crown would benefit the economy in the long term.
Some economists have suggested devaluing the crown to improve the trade situation, but many believe it is not fundamentally necessary.
The Czech currency last dipped below the parity rate against the basket in mid-June.
Positive preliminary results for July's industrial production indicated a moderate recovery from disappointing June figures.

Czech President Vaclav Havel's health has improved after lung cancer surgery.
Havel had a small malignant tumor removed along with half of his right lung on December 2.
Havel required an emergency tracheostomy on Thursday due to severe breathing problems.
Presidential spokesman Ladislav Spacek stated that the worst is behind Havel.
Havel communicated by writing notes to doctors and staff during his recovery.
Czech Archbishop Miloslav Vlk led a national prayer mass for Havel at St Vitus Cathedral.
World leaders, including U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin, sent get-well wishes to Havel.
Havel entered the Third Surgical Clinic in Prague on November 25 due to pneumonia.
After surgery, Havel developed pneumonia in the opposite lung and had a fever.
Doctors estimate Havel will remain on a respirator for another four to six days.

Czech Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda resigned from the government and parliament for falsely using an academic title.
Kalvoda claimed to be a doctor of law, which was disputed amid concerns over the academic credentials of Czech politicians.
Mariana Cerna from the parliament's press office confirmed Kalvoda's resignation was delivered to the president.
Another member of parliament from the ruling coalition also resigned for the same reason as Kalvoda.
Three other deputies admitted to using false titles but did not resign.
Officials from Kalvoda's party, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), were unavailable for comment after his resignation.
It was unclear who would replace Kalvoda in the cabinet or his status within the ODA.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus planned to meet with Christian Democrat chairman Josef Lux and a member of Kalvoda's party to discuss the coalition's situation.
Pavla Jurkova from the Christian Democrats resigned her seat for falsely claiming a law doctorate.
Two members of Klaus's party admitted their law doctorates were false but did not resign.

The Czech Republic's coalition government is attempting to address the resignation of Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda.
Jan Kalvoda resigned after admitting to using a false academic title.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and coalition members are waiting for Kalvoda's party to meet before discussing his replacement.
President Vaclav Havel asked Kalvoda to reconsider his resignation.
Kalvoda resigned his cabinet posts and parliamentary seat unexpectedly.
Kalvoda stated that the title 'Juris Doctor' does not belong to him.
Kalvoda explained his resignation to President Havel, who is recovering from surgery.
The president's office issued a statement indicating that Havel would consider Klaus's request for Kalvoda's dismissal.
Four other members of parliament admitted to using the title 'Doctor of Law' falsely.
The ODA party is expected to meet to discuss Kalvoda's replacement and his future as party chairman.

Germany and the Czech Republic concluded talks on a joint declaration related to World War Two and the communist era.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec signed a protocol expressing regret for injustices on both sides.
The declaration includes Germany's sorrow for the Nazi occupation of Czech lands from 1938 to 1945 and Czech regret for the expulsion of ethnic Germans post-war.
The declaration represents Germany's reconciliation with its neighbors affected by Nazi occupation.
Klaus Kinkel stated that Germany recognizes its responsibility for the suffering caused to the Czech people by Nazi crimes.
The text was approved by both governments and is set to be signed by prime ministers in January.
Politicians from both countries are calling for changes to the text before final approval by parliaments and presidents.
Czech opponents argue that the text does not provide direct compensation to victims of Nazi aggression.
German groups are dissatisfied that the declaration does not address restitution for the expropriation of property from Sudeten Germans.
The declaration establishes a Czech-German Future Fund with Germany contributing 140 million marks and the Czech Republic contributing about one-seventh of that amount.

Chiroscience Group plc is testing two anti-cancer compounds.
Chiroscience Group plc plans to decide which compound will proceed to human trials before the end of the year.
Both compounds being tested by Chiroscience Group plc are MMP inhibitors.
MMP inhibitors are the same class of drug as British Biotech Plc's Marimastat.
MMP inhibitors are believed to stop cancer cells from spreading.
Chiroscience Group plc's chief executive is John Padfield.
John Padfield stated that Chiroscience hopes to have a competitor to Marimastat in early trials next year.
Chiroscience Group plc aims to begin Phase III trials in 1998.

General Motor Corp invested 300 million pounds ($474.9 million) in Vauxhall Motors.
The investment reflects confidence in Vauxhall's British operation and the international prospects for the Astra model.
The three-year investment will be used to modernise the Ellesmere Port plant in north-west England.
The Ellesmere Port plant manufactures Astra cars and vans.
The investment guarantees the livelihoods of 4,200 employees at the plant and will create at least 200 new jobs.
Nick Reilly is the chairman and managing director of Vauxhall Motors.
A decision on increasing the number of shifts at the plant could create hundreds more jobs.
The Astra model has been one of the top five sellers in Britain and Europe since its launch five years ago.
Vauxhall aims to maintain a market share of around 14.5 percent in 1996.
Vauxhall's profitability is improving after a decline in 1995.

Ethical Holdings Plc is a UK-based drug delivery company listed on the U.S. Nasdaq index.
The company expects research and development spending to continue to rise sharply as it targets the U.S. market.
Ethical Holdings reported a 32 percent rise in R&D spending to 10.4 million stg for the year ended August 31.
The company posted a pre-tax loss of 11.0 million stg after a profit of 3.4 million stg the previous year.
The results were affected by a one-off payment of 7.9 million stg for the repurchase of product rights from Drug Royalty Corp Inc.
Chairman and CEO Geoffrey Guy stated that the rise in R&D spending is likely to continue at a greater rate over the next couple of years.
Ethical Holdings is targeting the U.S. market despite having a relatively low profile there.
The company has 16 products on the market and focuses on four core areas: hormone replacement therapy, cardiovascular disease, asthma, and analgesia.
Ethical Holdings has acquired a South American skin patch company and established agreements in Japan for its morphine and cardiovascular drugs.
The company has applied for a U.K. licence for an HRT skin patch that aims to eliminate monthly bleeding in some women.

British Biotech Plc published evidence on Monday that its cancer drug Marimastat works.
Analysts stated that there is still a long way to go before Marimastat's potential as a blockbuster can be confirmed.
British Biotech's shares ended the day 19 pence lower at 210.
Some analysts forecast that Marimastat could have sales of $4 billion a year.
Marimastat is a new class of cancer drug.
Presentations on the drug's effectiveness at a science conference in Vienna were similar to data published in May.
Finance director James Noble stated that the company was cautious about its statement to avoid raising patients' hopes.
Noble claimed there is significant evidence that Marimastat increases the chances of survival in cancer patients.
The studies involved 381 cancer patients who continued taking Marimastat after the 28-day Phase II trial period.
The Oxford-based group confirmed that Marimastat caused joint pain in around 30 percent of patients after three to five months.

Dominion Resources Inc of the United States expressed interest in bidding for East Midlands Electricity Plc.
Dominion Resources Inc owns Virginia Power.
Dominion stated it would withdraw from bidding if East Midlands' share price continued to rise.
East Midlands' share price increased by 70.5 pence to close at 608 pence on Wednesday.
The market value of East Midlands exceeded 1.2 billion pounds due to the share price increase.
Dominion indicated it would not make an offer significantly above East Midlands' closing price.
Sources close to Dominion mentioned that if East Midlands' price increases further, Dominion would not proceed with the bid.
East Midlands has reportedly cut costs significantly and requires investment for growth.
East Midlands declined to comment on Dominion's statement.
Shares of other regional electricity companies in England and Wales also rose due to speculation about potential bids.

Allied Colloids Plc is a Yorkshire-based chemicals group.
Allied Colloids announced its acquisition of CPS Chemical Co Inc for $390 million.
David Farrar is the chief executive of Allied Colloids.
Allied Colloids has a strategy of organic growth.
CPS Chemical Co Inc is based in the U.S. and had sales of $157 million last year.
More than 30 percent of Allied Colloids' annual turnover comes from U.S. sales.
CPS has plants in Arkansas and New Jersey.
Allied Colloids plans to finance the acquisition partly through a two-for-seven rights issue to raise £173 million.
The acquisition is expected to enhance earnings in the first full financial year.
The combined workforce of Allied Colloids and CPS will be around 3,500 employees.

Courtaulds Plc is targeting sales growth of at least 10 percent a year in its coatings business until the end of the century.
Bob Wheeler is the finance director of Courtaulds European Coatings.
Courtaulds launched a multi-million pound restructuring of its European and U.S. coating operations in 1994.
Courtaulds will have spent around 75 million pounds on reorganizing its European manufacturing base by the end of 1998.
A similar amount is being spent in the United States for restructuring.
The coatings and sealants division supplies specialist paint and protective products to the marine and aerospace sectors.
In the six months through September 30, sales at the coatings division rose 4.6 percent to 501 million pounds.
Sales from the coatings division represented around 47 percent of Courtaulds' total sales.
Courtaulds has been represented in Hong Kong since the 1950s and is involved in every major market in the region.
Courtaulds has chosen its marine and yacht coatings site at Felling in northeast England for improvements in quality, productivity, and safety.

The UK government is selling AEA Technology Plc as part of its last privatisation venture.
Trade and industry secretary Ian Lang aims to raise around 200 million stg from the sale of AEA Technology.
AEA Technology is a spin-off from the Atomic Energy Authority and is based in Oxfordshire.
The government plans to retain a 'golden share' in AEA Technology for three years to veto takeover attempts.
The opposition Labour Party has raised concerns about security implications related to AEA Technology's role in monitoring UK nuclear submarine safety.
Peter Watson is the chief executive of AEA Technology.
AEA Technology generated 253.3 million stg in sales in the year to March.
The company has interests in decommissioning nuclear plants and providing safety expertise worldwide.
AEA Technology employs 3,500 people and has worked on various projects, including battery life extension for Sony Corp and assisting with chemical weapons destruction in the U.S.
The company aims to increase foreign sales from just over one-fifth to one-third of total sales.

Zeneca Group Plc predicts strong profit growth due to robust sales of new drugs and agro-chemicals.
Chief executive David Barnes expressed confidence that Zeneca will double its profit by the end of the century.
All three key businesses of Zeneca, pharmaceuticals, agro-chemicals, and speciality chemicals, are expected to contribute to profit improvement.
Zeneca's share price increased by more than 50 percent in the past 18 months, closing at 1631 pence.
Speculation has linked Zeneca with potential partners including Roche Holdings AG, Bayer AG, and Sanofi.
David Barnes stated that a takeover bid for Zeneca is unlikely, but shareholders should compare any offer with a promised 15 percent annual growth in earnings per share.
Barnes indicated that Zeneca prefers to acquire new products and technologies on a case-by-case basis rather than pursue large acquisitions.
Zeneca is focusing on the rollout of new products, including the asthma drug Accolate and the agro-chemical fungicide Amistar.
The company announced an expansion of its drug sales force in the United States by more than 20 percent.
Barnes forecast significant sales potential for Accolate and Seroquel, with both expected to exceed $400 million in sales.

Shareholders in Enviromed Plc removed the company's board on Friday.
Ron Zwanziger is the CEO of Selfcare Inc., Enviromed's largest shareholder.
Selfcare Inc. owns a 29 percent stake in Enviromed.
Enviromed's share price fell from around 112 pence in December 1994 to around 25 pence.
Selfcare Inc. produces tests for pregnancy and infectious diseases.
Selfcare Inc. proposed the removal of four board members, including managing director Thomas Murphy.
The extraordinary meeting took place in Dean's Yard, next to Westminster Abbey.
Proxy votes showed 49 percent support for Selfcare's proposal and just under 39 percent for the existing board.
Ron Zwanziger previously resigned from the board in April 1995 over a joint venture dispute.
Enviromed's pretax profit of 2.2 million pounds in the year to September 1994 turned into a loss of 8.2 million pounds a year later.

Shares in Medeva Plc increased by almost six percent to 296 pence on Thursday.
Medeva's shares rose to 289-1/2 pence in early afternoon trading, up 10 pence on the day.
The stock has risen more than 13 percent since the start of the year.
Medeva announced a partnership with Peptide Therapeutics Plc to develop alternative delivery methods for vaccines.
Medeva invested three million pounds for a 2.5 percent stake in Peptide Therapeutics Plc.
Peptide Therapeutics Plc's shares increased nearly 20 percent to 289 pence.
Medeva is developing a hepatitis B vaccine called Hepagene, which analysts believe has significant market potential.
Medeva's chief executive Bill Bogie stated that Hepagene could sell millions of doses annually.
Hepagene targets individuals who do not respond to existing hepatitis B vaccines.
Medeva is considering expanding production capacity for Hepagene or seeking additional output options.

Cambridge Antibody Technology Group Plc (CAT) plans to join the stock market.
CAT uses human antibodies to discover new drugs.
CAT aims to raise between 30 and 35 million pounds through a share placing.
CAT is valued at around 85 million pounds.
Kleinwort Benson Ltd is the sponsor for CAT's flotation.
Cazenove & Co is the broker for CAT's flotation.
CAT has been operating since 1990.
CAT is working to find drugs for inflammation, fibrosis, cancer, and obesity.
Two drugs from CAT are expected to enter human clinical trials this year.
The Bioscience Innovation Centre (BIC) plans to raise up to 6 million pounds through a share placing.

Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc is interested in forming a cancer drug partnership in the U.S.
RPR aims to become a major player in oncology within the next five years.
RPR President Tim Rothwell stated the company aims to rank in the top five or ideally the top three in cancer sales.
RPR ranked 15th in oncology sales in 1995.
Rothwell predicts that the drug Taxotere will achieve peak sales of at least $500 million over the next five years.
Sales of Taxotere are forecast to double in 1997 from around $90 million in the previous year.
RPR expects the brain cancer treatment Gliadel to be approved in the U.S. in 1998.
RPR is interested in partnerships or alliances in the U.S. market.
RPR is 68 percent-owned by France's Rhone-Poulenc SA.
Only 24 percent of RPR's sales are in the United States, compared to over 40 percent for many competitors.

Colombia's main oil workers' union is known as USO.
USO has a fiercely nationalistic stance and opposes multinationals.
USO will merge with smaller labor organizations to form an industry-wide front.
Hernando Hernandez is the leader of USO.
USO currently represents 5,700 workers of the state oil company Ecopetrol.
A general assembly will be held on Monday to approve the merger decision.
Hernandez believes the merger could lead to a 40,000-member 'super-union'.
Foreign oil companies fear the merger will strengthen USO's position in their fields.
USO has been accused of having ties with leftist guerrilla movements, which the union leaders deny.
The merger will include the Association of Oil Industry Workers (ASOPETROL) and SINTRAOXY.

Colombia has initiated the process to lift a constitutional ban on extradition.
Alfonso Valdivieso, the chief prosecutor, criticized the move as virtually meaningless.
A Senate panel approved draft legislation to lift the prohibition on extraditing Colombians late on Tuesday.
Valdivieso stated that the legislation prohibited as much as it allowed and could create bureaucratic obstacles.
He suggested that the legislation should be strengthened before a final vote in Congress.
The draft legislation was approved by an 11-8 vote in the Senate constitutional committee.
If the draft legislation passes seven more congressional votes, it would allow extradition in some isolated cases.
The legislation would not be retroactive, preventing extradition of certain criminals, including those jailed last year.
The legislation would also prevent extradition of criminals who voluntarily surrendered to Colombian justice.
U.S. authorities argue that Colombian justice is too lenient on drug traffickers.

The head of the International Coffee Organization is Celsius Lodder.
Celsius Lodder stated that moves toward just-in-time roasting and cuts in coffee inventories will lead exporters, traders, and processors to use sophisticated financial mechanisms to manage price volatility.
Lodder predicted growth in risk management measures such as options, futures, and secondary instruments, which will influence short and medium-term coffee prices.
Traditional methods of building up stocks will be replaced by these financial mechanisms as a buffer against market swings.
In some producer countries, growers may have to take on more responsibility for storing their crops, which could increase their costs.
Lodder compared risk management to an insurance contract, emphasizing its importance for exporters, traders, and processors.
He noted that growers and cooperatives will face higher costs and reduced cash flow due to increased storage responsibilities.
Lodder mentioned opportunities for niche marketing of specialist coffees in traditional markets despite stagnating overall demand.
He also highlighted potential new markets in the former Soviet Union and China.
Colombia's President Ernesto Samper and Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia were optimistic about selling Colombian coffee in China.

A former German secret agent and his wife were charged with abduction after an attempt to smuggle a kidnap victim out of Colombia.
The charges were announced by the chief prosecutor's office.
Werner Mauss, 56, is accused of being an international member of Colombia's National Liberation Army (ELN) or a mercenary negotiating ransom for abducted foreigners.
German government official Peter Hausmann stated that the government was informed of Mauss's mission and supported unconventional rescue methods.
Mauss and Silvia Schroder, 36, were arrested at Rionegro airport while attempting to transport Brigitte Schoene, a kidnap victim, to Venezuela.
Brigitte Schoene was kidnapped by the ELN in mid-August, which demanded $6 million for her release.
The chief prosecutor's office referred to Mauss and Schroder by one of their aliases, Juergen and Isabel Seidel.
The couple was remanded in custody following their arrest.
An executive secretary of Siemens-Colombia stated she hired the plane for Mauss's getaway on the orders of a top industrialist.
Security experts noted that Colombia has many foreign mercenaries involved in undercover missions related to kidnappings.

Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Bogota on Sunday to call for an end to the crime wave in Colombia.
Colombia is referred to as the kidnap capital of the world.
A small bomb exploded near the march location but did not cause any injuries.
At least 1,100 people have been abducted in Colombia this year.
More than half of the abductions this year were carried out by warring factions in Colombia's internal conflict.
National Police chief Rosso Jose Serrano participated in the march and viewed it as a challenge to leftist guerrillas.
Francisco Santos, founder of Pais Libre, stated that the march was a sign that civil society opposes kidnapping.
Santos was kidnapped six years ago by the Medellin cartel.
An estimated 15,000 to 20,000 people participated in the march, with organizers claiming the number was twice that.
Norberto Garcia's 14-year-old daughter Andrea disappeared almost a year ago while on her way to school.

Edgar Riano, a member of Colombia's main oil workers' union, was arrested on terrorist charges in Huila province.
The arrest of Edgar Riano occurred after the arrest of 12 others, 10 of whom were from the USO oil union.
All arrested individuals are accused of carrying out dynamite attacks on Colombia's oil pipelines and of having links to the National Liberation Army (ELN).
USO head Hernando Hernandez announced that the union would set a start date for an indefinite strike to protest the arrests.
The strike is also in opposition to government plans perceived as privatization of the state-run oil company Ecopetrol.
The USO has merged with smaller oil workers' associations, potentially spreading the strike to the private sector.
USO leaders were scheduled to meet with Colombian Interior Minister Horacio Serpa to discuss the arrests and the planned strike.
The government may declare the oil workers' strike illegal due to its impact on the economy.
Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar stated that Ecopetrol has enough fuel reserves to meet demand for 19 days.
A 24-hour stoppage by USO workers in mid-October halted the pumping of 350,000 barrels a day along two main oil pipelines.

British Petroleum Co Plc considers its Piedemonte prospect in eastern Colombia fundamental to its worldwide operations.
John Doust is the executive director of BP's local subsidiary, British Petroleum Exploration (Colombia) Ltd.
Doust predicted that the Piedemonte field could come on stream by the end of 1999.
The total cost of developing the Piedemonte field is estimated to be about $2.2 billion.
The Piedemonte field is estimated to contain between 600 million and one billion barrels of crude and condensates.
BP has identified three promising hydrocarbon formations in the 287,000 hectare block after exploring 15 percent of the area.
BP argues that the terms of its sliding scale association contract with Ecopetrol make it unprofitable to exploit the field.
Under the existing contract, Ecopetrol's share of profits increases from 50 percent to a maximum of 76 percent as production rises.
Doust stated that BP is seriously considering a proposal from Colombia's Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar regarding the rights to the block.
BP is reluctant to surrender rights to almost 50 percent of the block under the current offer.

Four people were killed and at least 33 injured in Monteria, Colombia, due to a bomb explosion.
The explosion occurred at the headquarters of the Fondo Ganadero in the afternoon.
Police chief Col. Gabriel Carrero attributed the attack to leftist guerrillas.
A day before the Monteria blast, a car bomb in Medellin killed a woman and injured 48 people.
Authorities linked the Medellin attack to drug traffickers working with leftist guerrillas.
Marxist rebels and right-wing paramilitary groups have been in conflict in northwest Colombia.
The Monteria blast was the second explosion in the town in two months.
An earlier explosion on October 21 injured 10 people and was blamed on the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).
It is unclear if the recent bomb is connected to a statement from a group called the Special Anti-paramilitary Commando.
Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra suggested the Medellin attack was retaliation for a new law against drug lords.

General Jesus Armando Arias led an assault on Colombia's Supreme Court in 1985 to address a hostage situation involving leftist rebels.
Arias stated that an attack could be an option to resolve the Japanese embassy residence siege in Lima.
Arias advised Peru's President Alberto Fujimori against conceding to the demands of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
Arias suggested that elite forces from the United States, Israel, or Britain could eliminate the rebels with minimal bloodshed if negotiations failed.
More than 100 people, including 11 judges, died during the 27-hour battle at Bogota's Palace of Justice in November 1985.
Arias claimed that training techniques for elite forces have improved, allowing for a potential recovery of the Japanese embassy residence with minimal damage.
Arias expressed that negotiating with the MRTA could set a dangerous legal precedent.
Arias, now a military academy instructor, maintained that the assault he led was the correct response to the violence of the M-19.
Former Justice Minister Enrique Parejo stated that the Colombian military acted against government orders during the Palace of Justice assault.
Parejo warned that Fujimori must maintain strict control over Peru's military to prevent further violence.

A U.S. pilot named Robert Martin, 35, was killed when his plane crashed in southeast Colombia.
The crash occurred in a jungle area on a Tuesday.
Robert Martin was flying a U.S.-registered Turbo Thrush T-65 crop-dusting plane.
He was fumigating illicit plantations of coca leaf, which is used to produce cocaine.
U.S. ambassador Myles Frechette confirmed Martin's death and stated he was the first U.S. pilot to die on such a mission in Colombia.
The cause of the accident will be fully investigated, with human error or mechanical failure being the most likely causes.
The crash took place in Guaviare province, a major coca producing region in Colombia.
Martin was one of six U.S. pilots assisting Colombia's drug crop eradication program.
The U.S. pilots were initially only allowed to train Colombian pilots but were later permitted to fly live missions.
Dyncorp, a Texas-based aviation company, employs the U.S. pilots, some of whom are former U.S. servicemen.

Colombian President Ernesto Samper decreed an economic emergency on Monday.
Samper warned that the economic and social stability of the country was under threat.
The economic emergency is the first in five years and has been decreed for 20 days.
The economic emergency could be extended for a maximum of 90 days.
All measures during the emergency can be introduced without the approval of Congress.
Further austerity measures are scheduled to be announced on Tuesday.
Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo announced measures aimed at slashing Colombia's foreign debt by more than $800 million this year.
Wilson Borja, head of the FENALTRASE public sector union, expressed fears that the government could cut as many as 19,000 state jobs.
The union was protesting against a 13.5 percent weighted pay increase, which was below annual inflation.
Samper stated that protests and strikes would lead nowhere due to the government's lack of funds.

Colombian police discovered a second multimillion-dollar drug stash aboard a yacht owned by three Britons.
The three Britons are Michael Hayne, 50, of Egham, Surrey, Stephen Alan Hayne, 27, of Ashford, Kent, and David Maurice Shaw, 49, of Oldham, Lancashire.
The three men were arrested on December 13 in Barranquilla on cocaine smuggling charges.
Officials discovered more than 425 pounds (194 kg) of highly pure cocaine aboard their U.S.-registered boat Perla del Mar.
A more exhaustive search revealed another 326 pounds (148 kg) of cocaine in the vessel's waste water tanks.
A DAS chief estimated the street value of the first haul at $50 million.
The drugs were coated with a mixture of burned oil and coffee to mask the smell.
The Britons are being held in custody in Barranquilla's El Modelo jail.
Michael Hayne claimed the situation was a 'huge mix-up' in a phone conversation with Reuters.
Michael Hayne and his son entered Colombia illegally from Venezuela, while Shaw entered legally from Trinidad.

Tottenham Hotspur chairman Alan Sugar stated that English soccer clubs could face financial ruin if they emulate big spenders like Newcastle United.
Tottenham posted a record pre-exceptional profit of 10.2 million pounds for the 14 months to July 31.
Tottenham increased its total dividend to 5p from 3p.
English soccer is experiencing growth due to increased television revenue and an influx of foreign talent.
Manchester United announced an annual profit of 15 million pounds.
Sugar warned that the Bosman Ruling, which allows players to become free agents at the end of their contracts, is detrimental to the football industry.
Sugar criticized Newcastle's signing of Alan Shearer for 15 million pounds, stating it would not be financially viable.
Tottenham reported a 14-month financial period due to a change in their financial year and took an exceptional charge of 7.3 million pounds.
The value of Tottenham's squad fell after the Bosman ruling ended the transfer fee system for out-of-contract players.
Sugar, who owns a 40 percent stake in Tottenham, acknowledged that profit figures are not meaningful to fans wanting new signings.

Shares in Premier Farnell dipped on Monday.
Premier Farnell posted half-year profits slightly below expectations.
Premier Farnell was created in April when Farnell Electronics completed a $2.8 billion takeover of Premier Industrial Corp.
Pre-tax profit for the six months to July 28 totalled 56.1 million pounds.
The pre-tax figure of 71.3 million pounds a year earlier was inflated by a large one-off gain.
Analysts had forecast profit in a range of 57.5 to 61.6 million pounds.
The failure to reach the forecast profit level resulted in a 10.5p decline in the share price to 670p.
The market for electronic components showed much lower levels of growth in 1996 than in recent years.
Premier Farnell does not expect any major change in market conditions for the rest of the year.
Chief executive Howard Poulson stated that the integration following the acquisition is progressing well.

Marjorie Scardino will become the chief executive of Pearson in January.
Scardino rejects the label of company insider.
Scardino has vowed to implement radical changes at Pearson if necessary.
Selecting an American woman to lead a British company raised concerns in the City of London.
Some analysts believe Scardino's appointment suggests continuity rather than change at Pearson.
Scardino is currently the chief executive of The Economist Group, which is 50 percent owned by Pearson.
Scardino claims that The Economist operates independently and that she is not part of the Pearson establishment.
Scardino has communicated with the Pearson board, which is open to radical change if needed.
Pearson has sold off various businesses to focus on Information, Education, and Entertainment.
Scardino has received positive feedback from Economist chairman Dominic Cadbury regarding her leadership.

The head of Channel 4 urged the government to reject moves to privatise the service.
Channel 4 chief executive Michael Grade stated that privatisation was on the political agenda.
Michael Grade called on the government to dispel the notion of privatisation.
The board of Channel 4 plans to oppose privatisation efforts.
Free marketeers in the Conservative party have suggested that Channel 4 could be sold.
Privatisation is not currently part of government policy.
Advocates of privatisation want it included in the Conservative manifesto for the upcoming general election.
Channel 4 was established in 1982 to transmit innovative and minority programming.
Channel 4 is a statutory, state-controlled corporation funded by advertising.
The BBC is funded by a licence fee paid by television owners.

Britain's Independent Television Commission (ITC) invited applications to run terrestrial frequencies for digital television.
Peter Rogers is the chief executive of the ITC.
The ITC aims to make 35 or 36 channels available on digital terrestrial television.
The ITC is seeking applications to operate four multiplexes, which can carry up to six digital channels each.
The BBC has been allocated its own multiplex, while ITV and Channel 4 will share one.
The ITC will award 12-year licenses based on criteria such as service rollout speed and programming appeal, without requiring cash bids.
Licenses are expected to be awarded in spring and broadcasting could begin by mid-1998.
BSkyB plans to launch a digital satellite service in late 1997, ahead of the terrestrial version.
Digital technology increases the number of channels and improves sound and picture quality.
A set-top box or decoder will be needed to receive digital services, but there is no current legislation for a common standard for decoders.

A $22 billion takeover of MCI Communications Corp would conclude Sir Peter Bonfield's first year as chief executive of British Telecommunications Plc.
British Telecommunications Plc is in talks with MCI, the second largest U.S. long-distance phone company, about acquiring the 80 percent of MCI it does not own.
Sir Iain Vallance became BT chairman when the company split the roles of chairman and chief executive in January.
Sir Peter Bonfield was appointed as chief executive of BT in January after previously leading ICL, a British computer company owned by Fujitsu Ltd.
The Financial Times described Bonfield's appointment as a positive event in BT's history and a turning point in its transition to a competitive services group.
Bonfield has a reputation for boosting revenue, curbing costs, and international expansion.
BT was previously in talks with Cable & Wireless about a merger that ended unsuccessfully in May.
Bonfield aims for BT to be one of the most successful global telecom companies in 20 to 30 years.
Bonfield believes BT's network of continental partners will help it become a pan-European operator.
Bonfield has identified Asia-Pacific as a region for BT's expansion.

British Telecom and MCI announced a planned $20 billion merger.
The merger is the largest trans-Atlantic takeover in history.
The merger would create a company valued at $40 billion serving 43 million customers in 70 countries.
The merger is expected to be reviewed by regulators in Britain, America, and Europe.
The new company will be called Concert and aims to compete with AT&T and other major telecommunications companies.
MCI currently holds about 20 percent of the U.S. long-distance market.
British Telecom's stock rose by $5.375 to $60.875 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement.
MCI's stock rose by 50 cents to $30.75, below the potential value of $39 per share.
Regulatory hurdles and the time required to complete the merger have caused concerns among analysts.
AT&T has requested thorough scrutiny of the merger from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission.

Shares in EMI Group Plc rose on Tuesday.
EMI Group Plc split from Thorn Plc three months ago.
Profit before tax and exceptional items for EMI rose nine percent to 112.5 million pounds in the six months to September 30.
Net interim dividend per share increased by 12.7 percent to eight pence.
EMI shares added 9-1/2p to 1,280-1/2p by 1330 GMT.
Chairman Sir Colin Southgate stated that the interim results were excellent.
Analysts indicated that EMI appeared in better shape than some competitors.
Finance Director Simon Duffy expressed confidence in the global music business growing by 6-8 percent annually in the medium to long-term.
EMI reported that sales in the United States were almost flat and declined slightly in France.
Turnover from the EMI Music division was down marginally at around 1.1 billion.

Granada Group reported a 37 percent increase in full-year profits to 480 million pounds ($804 million).
Granada Group plans to improve profits at Forte by over 100 million pounds ($167.5 million) per annum starting from 1996/97.
Granada Chairman Gerry Robinson described the results as 'very satisfying.'
Granada acquired Forte in a 3.9 billion pound ($6.5 billion) deal earlier this year.
Forte has improved profitability by approximately 40 million pounds ($67 million) under Granada's management.
Granada is reorganizing following the acquisition of Forte.
Granada sold London's Hyde Park Hotel for 86 million pounds ($144 million).
Granada expects to complete the sale of assets by early 1997.
Analysts estimate that the sale of assets will raise about 900 million pounds ($1.5 billion).
Granada plans to sell the Welcome Break chain of British motorway service areas in January or February of next year.

Premier League Sunderland aims to raise up to 12 million pounds ($20 million) through a flotation on the London Stock Exchange.
Sunderland won the league title for the sixth and last time in 1936.
Sunderland is among a growing number of clubs seeking to capitalize on the popularity of soccer in England.
Premier League rivals Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur have full stock market listings.
Clubs such as Chelsea trade on the secondary market.
Sunderland plans to use the new funds to complete a 15 million pounds stadium, reduce borrowing, and purchase new players.
Chairman Bob Murray stated that the proceeds will assist in retaining Premier League status and capitalizing on new opportunities.
Sunderland will move from their century-old Roker Park home to a new 42,000-capacity stadium at the end of the season.
Sunderland was promoted to the Premier League last season and forecasts that increased revenue will double turnover to 13.6 million pounds this season.
The new stadium is expected to increase season ticket holders from 17,000 to around 28,000.

Britons will learn the new annual licence fee for BBC services soon.
The BBC is lobbying for an above-inflation increase in the licence fee.
The government is expected to announce its decision by early to mid-December.
The BBC derives 95 percent of its funding from the annual licence fee.
The current licence fee is 89.50 pounds ($150).
The BBC generated 1.8 billion pounds from the licence fee in the last financial year.
The BBC's commercial arm provided a net benefit of 77 million pounds.
The licence fee is guaranteed as a source of funding for the next five years.
BBC Director-General John Birt is campaigning for an increase in the licence fee.
The BBC is believed to be seeking a rise of around five pounds.

Shares in British Sky Broadcasting (BSkyB) rose by 19p to 495-1/2p on Monday.
The rise in BSkyB shares followed the acceptance of new terms for channel supply by Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT).
BSkyB shares had previously fallen almost two pounds ($3.3) since mid-October.
BSkyB is 40 percent owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation.
The Financial Times reported that BSkyB was preparing to order set-top boxes for its digital satellite services.
Anthony de Larrinaga from broker Panmure Gordon noted that some funds were buying BSkyB shares due to positive news flow.
The OFT approved BSkyB's revised rate card for satellite channel supply to cable operators.
OFT Director General John Bridgeman stated that the changes increase flexibility for cable operators in marketing their services.
The Cable Communications Association criticized the OFT's decision and considered taking the issue to the European Commission.
BSkyB has over five million subscribers, with 3.3 million receiving the service via satellite dish and almost 1.9 million on cable.

Shares in Sunderland Plc debuted at 740 pence, a 25 percent premium to the offer price of 585 pence.
Sunderland's public offer of shares was 2.7 times oversubscribed.
A total of 2.15 million shares were sold during Sunderland's flotation.
On the day of the debut, Sunderland's share price was quoted at 732-1/2 pence, valuing the club at just under 60 million pounds.
Trading volume for Sunderland's shares reached 134,500.
Manchester United was the model for English soccer flotations and was floated in 1991.
Manchester United has a market value of approximately 380 million pounds.
Revenue from Manchester United's merchandising is comparable to its gate receipts.
Tottenham Hotspur has been quoted on the London Stock Exchange for several years.
Leeds United joined the market in August after being taken over by Caspian Group.

Heartport Inc received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for a new heart surgery technology.
The FDA approval was granted earlier than expected.
Analysts now predict Heartport will turn its first profit in 1998 instead of 1999.
Heartport plans to launch its port-access surgical system in the U.S. in mid-1997.
Heartport aims to equip six lead clinical training centers with port-access systems before the launch.
The company targets training 30 surgical teams by the end of the year.
Heartport's shares fell by 2 to 34-1/2 on Tuesday after rising on Monday.
Several medical technology firms are pursuing the market for minimally invasive heart surgery.
Heartport's technique involves stopping the heart and using a heart-lung bypass circuit.
Competitors like CardioThoracic Systems Inc and Medtronic Inc focus on beating-heart techniques.

Pharmacia & Upjohn announced that profits would fall short of expectations.
The company expects earnings of about 44 cents a share for the third quarter.
Analysts had expected earnings to be 10 cents higher than the company's forecast.
Pharmacia & Upjohn's stock dropped as much as $6.50 and closed down $5.25 at $34.875.
More than 18 million shares of Pharmacia & Upjohn changed hands by early afternoon.
The company cited foreign exchange problems, pricing pressures, and weak U.S. sales of older products as reasons for the profit shortfall.
Pharmacia & Upjohn was formed by the merger of Pharmacia AB and Upjohn Co.
The merger began operations in November 1995.
Analysts expressed concerns that the merger is not producing the expected synergies.
Pharmacia & Upjohn's Chief Executive John Zabriskie stated that the merger has resulted in a 3,000 person reduction in the workforce.

United Airlines has ordered $4.4 billion worth of airplanes from Boeing Co. and Airbus Industrie.
The majority of the order is for Boeing, with United ordering 27 wide-body jets valued at about $3.5 billion.
The wide-body jets include 19 jumbo 747-400s, six 757s, and two 777s.
United Airlines also ordered 24 narrow-body Airbus A319s valued at $900 million.
United is the first U.S. airline to order Airbus' latest model.
United chose Airbus planes over competing Boeing 737-700s and 737-300s after evaluation.
United Airlines stated that it benefited from substantial discounts from both manufacturers.
The ordered planes will be part of United's 'retire and replace' program to update its fleet.
The program is expected to generate more than $100 million in annual operating cost savings by 2000.
Delivery of all aircraft is scheduled to be completed by 2002.

Eli Lilly & Co expects marketing and administration costs in the fourth quarter to be slightly up or flat compared to the previous year.
This expectation indicates a slowdown from a 6.5 percent increase in the third quarter.
Charles Golden, Lilly's chief financial officer, stated that costs may increase by a couple of percent but will be below third-quarter growth rates.
Lilly's gross profit margin declined in the third quarter due to increased marketing costs for new products, including the anti-schizophrenia drug Zyprexa.
Zyprexa is expected to help lift sales in the fourth quarter, but a turnaround in margin trends is anticipated to take longer.
Golden indicated that improved margins may not occur until sometime next year.
Lilly's gross margin has declined for two consecutive quarters.
Analysts responded positively to Lilly's third-quarter results, noting no significant surprises.
Lilly reported third-quarter operating profits of $0.64 per share, matching Wall Street expectations.
An 11-percent sales gain was driven by the anti-depressant Prozac, human insulin Humulin, and increased revenues from PCS Health Systems.

Olympic Financial Ltd received expressions of interest from more than one potential acquirer.
Olympic expects to receive a formal acquisition offer within the next several weeks.
Olympic's stock price increased by 6-1/4 to 23-7/8 during heavy trading.
Jennifer Weichert stated that there is currently no offer or price on the table.
Weichert indicated that potential buyers are likely to be finance companies, regional banks, or conglomerates.
KeyCorp acquired AutoFinance Group Inc last September.
Southern National Corp is in the process of acquiring Regional Acceptance Corp.
John Coffey, an analyst, noted that banks are looking to recapture market share in the subprime auto lending market.
Olympic Financial makes loans to borrowers with weak credit histories.
The Consumer Bankers Association warned banks about the risks in the subprime business earlier this year.

TheraTx Inc does not expect the federal government to implement new guidelines for certain key Medicare reimbursement rates until the summer of 1997.
Donald Myll is the chief financial officer of TheraTx Inc.
Myll stated that the forthcoming government reimbursement change will pressure TheraTx's earnings.
TheraTx has been waiting for two years for action from the federal government on the reimbursement issue.
TheraTx's stock has been depressed due to market focus on the reimbursement issue.
TheraTx operates 29 nursing homes and provides rehabilitation services to other nursing home companies.
The rehabilitation division of TheraTx provides about 45 percent of the company's revenues.
Most revenues in the rehabilitation area come from Medicare.
The U.S. Health Care Financing Administration has been rewriting its reimbursement rules for therapy since October 1994.
Myll indicated that if HCFA proceeds with its reforms, TheraTx's 1997 earnings could be flat to down compared to 1996.

Patrick Arbor is the Chairman of the Chicago Board of Trade.
Arbor expects electronic technology to replace open outcry trading in 20 to 25 years.
Arbor made these comments after a speech at the University of Chicago.
The Chicago Board of Trade has previously stated that electronic trading supplements open outcry trading.
Arbor's son is 33 years old and is a member of the CBOT allowed to trade in the pits.
Arbor believes technology is the future of trading.
Electronic trading is currently a small part of the total trading volume on the CBOT but is growing rapidly.
In 1995, total trading volume on the CBOT was more than 210 million contracts.
Arbor predicted record-setting trading volume for the CBOT in 1996.
Electronic trading's average daily volume increased from 560 contracts in 1992 to 7,397 contracts in the first quarter of 1996.

Aon Corp. agreed to acquire Alexander & Alexander Services Inc. for about $1.23 billion.
Aon will pay $17.50 a share for Alexander & Alexander's common stock, totaling about $790 million.
Aon will pay about $437.5 million to holders of Alexander & Alexander's preferred stock.
Layoffs and office closings are expected to follow the acquisition as Aon aims to cut costs.
Aon employs about 27,000 people, while Alexander & Alexander employs about 12,000 people.
Alexander & Alexander is the fourth-largest insurance broker in the world.
Alexander & Alexander has operations in 80 countries, primarily in the United States, Canada, and Britain.
After the acquisition, Aon will become either the largest or second-largest insurance broker in the world.
Aon plans to begin a cash tender offer for Alexander & Alexander's common shares no later than Dec. 16.
Analysts expect Aon Chairman Patrick Ryan to lead the combined operations after the acquisition.

U.S. health maintenance organizations (HMOs) are expected to improve in 1997 after a year of lower profits and stock values.
Medical cost inflation is slowing, allowing HMOs to potentially raise premiums and restore profit margins.
Gary Frazier, a health care industry analyst at Bear Stearns, stated that the outlook for HMOs is better than in 1995 and 1996.
In 1996, medical costs rose faster than historical forecasts, affecting HMOs' ability to maintain profit margins.
HMO stock values declined sharply from March to July 1996, with 13 of the 16 largest publicly traded HMOs not regaining first-quarter highs.
United Wisconsin Services Inc., Oxford Health Plans Inc., and FHP International Corp. are the only three HMOs that have regained their first-quarter highs.
PacifiCare, WellPoint Health Networks Inc., and Aetna Inc. have experienced good recovery, while United Healthcare Corp. and Humana Inc. have seen only modest improvements.
Coventry Corp., Mid Atlantic Medical Services Inc., and Physician Corp. are still struggling after the downturn.
Robert Hoehn, an analyst at Salomon Brothers, noted that questions about pricing and margins persist in the industry.
Most analysts expect premiums to rise slightly faster than costs in 1997, but Peter Reilly from Milliman & Robertson indicated that premium increases have lagged behind cost increases.

General Instrument Corp is setting goals for NextLevel Systems Inc of 35-45 percent annual operating income growth and 22-25 percent annual sales growth on operating margins of 10-12 percent.
General Instrument chief executive Richard Friedland stated that growth rates could be higher this year.
Friedland sees stock price gains ahead for NextLevel, CommScope Inc, and General Semiconductor Inc.
Friedland expects CommScope and General Semiconductor to increase at above-average rates in the eight to 10 percent return range.
Friedland predicts NextLevel Systems will double over the next year to 18 months.
Shares in General Instrument rose by 1/4 to 22-7/8 after the announcement of a three-way split.
CommScope's management goals are 18 to 20 percent annual sales growth and 16 to 17 percent operating income growth with operating margins of 16 to 17 percent.
General Semiconductor's goals are 10 to 11 percent operating income growth on annual sales growth of 14-16 percent and operating margins of 20-21 percent.
General Instrument shareholders will receive one share in each of the new companies for each General Instrument share held.
Friedland mentioned that a reverse split may be necessary to comply with New York Stock Exchange rules.

General Instrument Corp. plans to split into three companies through a tax-free spin-off to shareholders.
The move is intended to boost the company's stock market value.
Wall Street welcomed the spin-off as a way to unlock the value of General Instrument's core high-tech communications business.
NextLevel Systems Inc. will be created from General Instrument's cable television, satellite, and telephone business.
CommScope Inc. will be formed from General Instrument's coaxial cable manufacturing business.
General Semiconductor Inc. will be established from General Instrument's units that make electronic components.
General Instrument will incur an after-tax charge against earnings of $55 million to $65 million for the fourth quarter due to the breakup.
The fourth-quarter charges will mainly consist of costs related to the transition to digital products and restructuring costs.
General Instrument expects fourth-quarter earnings to be in the range of 28 cents to 32 cents a share, excluding the charges.
Last year, General Instrument reported net earnings of $53.5 million, or 43 cents per share, in its fiscal fourth quarter.

Most U.S. nursing home and hospital companies are expected to report higher profits in the fourth quarter.
NatWest Securities industry analyst Marie Conway stated that companies have easy comparisons due to weak results last year.
Schroder Wertheim analyst William McKeever indicated there is more potential for downside to earnings than upside.
Pressing industry issues include unresolved Medicare and Medicaid reform and reimbursement rates for contract therapy services.
Scott & Stringfellow analyst George Shipp noted that little progress has been made in Washington regarding these issues.
The Morgan Stanley Healthcare Provider index of 15 top hospital management and nursing home stocks was near 326 on Tuesday.
The index increased from 288 at the start of the year.
Sun Healthcare Group Inc and Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp have lagged the sector due to various problems.
Earnings at Integrated Health Services Inc are forecast to be barely improved from last year after acquisitions.
Health Management Associates Inc is expected to lead the for-profit hospital sector in earnings gains.

Australian oil and gas companies are being acquired by foreign companies seeking undervalued stocks.
Analysts believe the oil and gas sector has a positive outlook due to higher oil prices and a deregulated gas market.
In 1996, approximately A$2.5 billion worth of takeovers were announced in Australia's oil and gas sector.
An additional A$600 million worth of asset sales occurred as some non-oil and gas companies exited the local market.
Timothy Savage, an analyst at Hartley Poynton, stated that overseas investors recognize the value of oil and gas assets in Southeast Asia.
Mobil Corp made a A$1.78 billion bid for Ampolex Ltd in February, marking the largest bid in the sector for that year.
Clyde Petroleum Plc acquired Crusader Ltd, while Premier Oil Plc and Cairn Energy Plc made bids for Discovery Petroleum NL and Command Petroleum Ltd, respectively.
Stuart Baker, an analyst at BT Securities, noted that Australian oil companies attracting foreign interest typically have offshore oil assets.
Baker indicated that companies that have attempted to establish an overseas presence have been taken over.
Analysts reported that the rise in oil prices has not influenced corporate activity in the sector.

St George Bank Ltd and Advance Bank Australia Ltd announced a merger plan on Monday.
The merger aims to create Australia's fifth largest bank with a market value of A$4.5 billion (US$3.55 billion).
Jim Sweeney is the managing director of St George Bank and will lead the enlarged group.
This is the fifth merger attempt by St George in the past two years.
Advance Bank shareholders will receive A$2.10 in cash, a 20 cent special cash dividend, and new St George shares valued up to A$5.00 per Advance Bank share.
The total offer value for Advance shares is A$7.30, valuing the bank at A$2.65 billion.
The merger will create a bank with assets of A$40 billion.
The merger is expected to position the new bank among Australia's top 25 listed companies.
Advance Bank shares increased by 57 cents or nine percent to close at A$6.85 following the merger announcement.
St George shares decreased by 40 cents or 4.5 percent to end at A$8.55.

The international partners in Australia's largest gas project plan to spend A$6.0 billion (US$4.7 billion) to double production.
This investment will make it Australia's largest single resources investment.
Woodside Petroleum Ltd is an Australian oil and gas producer involved in the North-West Shelf gas project offshore Western Australia.
The partners plan to double production capacity to 14.5 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) per year.
Analysts believe the decision by the North West Shelf partners is unlikely to enhance the prospect of a co-operative development with the nearby Gorgon gas field.
Geoff Wedgwood, Woodside's corporate affairs manager, stated that the North West Shelf partners have their own expansion plans.
Wedgwood mentioned that they have not seen a plan from the Gorgon partners that fits within their plans.
Cor Herkstroter, chairman of Royal Dutch/Shell Group's committee of managing directors, raised hopes for the development of both projects together.
Royal Dutch/Shell Group owns 34 percent of Woodside and has questioned the expansion of the North West Shelf on a stand-alone basis.
Woodside submitted the expansion plan to the project's eight Japanese power and gas utility customers at a meeting in Osaka.

Conrad Black wants to increase his stake in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd from 25 percent to 50 percent.
Black met with Australian Prime Minister John Howard before expressing his desire to raise his stake.
Black stated he would sell his stake in Fairfax if Australia's media ownership rules do not change.
Black described Australia's current media ownership rules as anachronistic.
Black indicated that he could not rule out selling his stake to Kerry Packer.
Black believes that Packer's proposed merger between his media empire and Fairfax is unlikely to succeed.
Black mentioned that U.S. accounting rules penalize companies with stakes higher than 50 percent in their associates.
Black will not apply for a higher stake until the Australian government concludes its study on media ownership.
Under current Australian media ownership rules, foreigners cannot own more than 25 percent of a newspaper group.
Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) proposed a merger with Fairfax contingent on liberalized media ownership rules.

News Corp Ltd is expected to meet a 20 percent rise in net profit before abnormals for the year to June 30, 1997.
Rupert Murdoch is the chairman of News Corp.
Australian media analysts stated that News Corp should easily meet the profit rise predicted by Murdoch.
News Corp reported a net profit before abnormals of A$285 million for the three months to September 30.
The net profit before abnormals of A$285 million for September 30 was slightly up from A$284 million a year earlier.
Analysts had forecast net profit before abnormal items to be around A$320-330 million, which is an increase of around 15 percent.
News Corp's results in Australian currency were affected by poor U.S. television results and a stronger local dollar.
In U.S. dollar terms, News Corp's operating income was seven percent higher in the first quarter.
Murdoch's 20 percent profit lift forecast was stated to be in U.S. dollar terms.
The second quarter is traditionally a stronger quarter for Fox Broadcasting and may benefit from the baseball World Series finals.

Australia's information technology and telecommunication industry welcomed a decision by Asia-Pacific leaders to reduce tariffs.
Fleur Bayley is the export manager of the Australian Informational Industry Association (AIIA).
Bayley stated that Australia has no trade barriers on IT&T equipment.
Local companies in Australia compete in markets with high tariff barriers.
The meeting in the Philippines involved 18 leaders of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies.
The APEC meeting endorsed a United States plan to free the annual US$500 billion global trade in computers, memory chips, and telecommunications equipment.
IT&T observers wanted more details about the tariff plan to assess its implications for the Australian sector.
One computer industry analyst indicated that the APEC plan is likely to benefit Australian IT&T exports but may not stimulate growth of technology imports into Australia.
Australia exported more than A$2.5 billion in IT&T goods in the 12 months to September this year.
Australia imported around A$9.6 billion worth of IT&T goods over the same period.

Westpac Banking Corp expects rapid revenue growth from its alliance with Standard Chartered Bank Plc for banking services in Asia.
David Morgan is the group executive of Westpac's Institutional and International Banking Group.
Morgan stated that he could not specify the revenue the alliance would produce in its first year.
Morgan also could not disclose how much Westpac had invested in the venture, which officially started on Wednesday.
The banks announced that there would be no exchange of equity between Westpac and Standard Chartered.
Morgan indicated that Westpac has made a substantial investment and will continue to invest as it expands its capabilities across Asia.
