Westpac has no plans to extend the alliance beyond Asia to the Middle East and Africa.
The venture will focus primarily on Singapore, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Thailand, and Malaysia.
Morgan mentioned that the venture plans to expand into Vietnam and China in about six months.

James Hardie Industries Ltd is expected to report a net profit before abnormals of between A$23 million and A$30 million for the six months ended September 30, 1996.
James Hardie reported a pre-abnormal net profit of A$31.4 million in the first half of 1994/95.
In October, James Hardie stated that the depressed local housing market would lead to a deterioration in first half profits.
BT Securities analyst Chris Haynes forecasts a net profit before abnormals of A$27 million for James Hardie in the first half.
Chris Haynes has a hold recommendation for James Hardie and expects a dividend of 6.5 cents per share.
A Sydney-based analyst forecasts a net profit before abnormals of A$23 million for the first half and about A$50 million for the year.
John North from J.B. Were & Son forecasts a first half pre-abnormal net profit slightly below A$30 million and an annual profit of A$55 million.
BZW Australia forecasts a net profit before abnormals of A$26.6 million for the half and about A$54 million for the 1996/97 year.
Fabian Babich from ABN AMRO Hoare Govett estimates a pre-abnormal net profit of A$26 million for the half.
Analysts expect James Hardie's results to improve in the 1997/98 year due to a projected recovery in the Australian housing industry.

Holyman Ltd plans to expand operations in Europe before entering the Asian market.
Christopher Butcher is the managing director of Holyman Ltd.
Holyman currently operates in North America and northern Europe.
Butcher stated that Holyman may expand into Asia as the cost structure for fast ferry operations improves.
Holyman is considering fast ferry services from Darwin to Indonesia.
Simon Lennon is the company secretary of Holyman Ltd.
Holyman has explored specific routes in China and Indonesia but found they did not fit the company's plans.
Holyman shares have more than doubled since January 2023, making them strong performers in the stock market.
Holyman was listed on the local bourse in April 1994 at A$2.00.
Holyman's main activities include fast ferry services, a gas pipeline, bulk commodity handling, and freight forwarding.

Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd has posted disappointing results since its listing in June 1995.
Chief executive officer Neil Gamble stated that the company's prospectus forecast was too optimistic.
Gamble believes the forecast was an over-estimate of reality compared to other parts of the industry.
Showboat Inc owns 26.3 percent of Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd.
The company holds a 12-year monopoly to operate the only legal casino in Sydney, Australia.
The company forecasted an operating profit after tax of A$37 million for 1995/96 but reported a net loss of A$4.68 million for the year ending June 30, 1996.
The casino opened a temporary site in September 1995 and plans to open a permanent casino in late 1997.
The company changed its balance date to December 31 from June 30 earlier this year.
Gamble reported a slow and steady improvement in results but did not provide specific forecasts.
The share price fell eight percent after George Soros sold down his stake in mid-November.

The Australian Stock Exchange's transport sector is expected to see modest gains over the next year.
The transport index rose about 30 percent during 1996.
The broader market increased six percent in 1996.
Brambles Industries Ltd and Mayne Nickless Ltd make up over half of the transport sector.
The transport sector has significantly outperformed in the last 12 months.
Factors contributing to the sector's performance include stock-specific issues.
TNT Ltd was taken over by PTT Nederland NV through a A$2 billion bid.
Mayne Nickless plans to sell its 25 percent stake in Optus Communications in 1997.
Qantas Airways Ltd's share price has underperformed compared to the transport sector.
Qantas shares are currently trading just above the A$2.00 price from its mid-1995 float.

Corporate Australia is expected to pursue takeovers in 1997, particularly in the banks, media, and resources sectors.
Brokers estimate that there were approximately A$8.5 billion worth of takeovers and share buy-backs in 1996.
The value of takeovers and share buy-backs increased from A$5.9 billion in 1995 and A$2.0 billion in 1994.
Takeovers and share buy-backs are viewed as methods to enhance growth in earnings per share.
The largest takeover in 1997 was the A$2.0 billion acquisition of TNT Ltd by Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV.
Chris Mackay, executive director at broker SBC Warburg, stated that there is rationalisation and international interest in Australian industries.
Analysts noted that Australia's low inflation and low economic growth prospects create favorable conditions for takeovers.
Merv Peacock, head of marketable securities at the Australian Mutual Provident Society, indicated that companies seek efficiencies through acquisitions due to low inflation.
Profits have been declining for 18 months, with industrials affected by the slowing economy and resource companies impacted by lower commodity prices.
Craig Drummond from J.B. Were & Son mentioned that gold could see significant takeover activity due to falling valuations.

Malcolm Williamson is the group chief executive of Standard Chartered Plc.
Williamson expects Standard Chartered to form more strategic alliances in Asia with U.S. and European banks.
In 1996, Standard Chartered formed joint ventures in Asia with Westpac Banking Corp, First Chicago NBD Corp, and Fleet Financial Services.
Williamson stated that Standard Chartered has more deals planned in Europe and America.
Standard Chartered will announce planned ventures when it releases its 1996 year results in late February or early March.
Standard Chartered has a network of branches throughout Asia and Africa, as well as offices in London, New York, and Sydney.
Williamson noted that it is difficult for foreign banks to enter Asia due to regulatory challenges in obtaining bank licenses.
Williamson indicated that there is no limit to the number of ventures Standard Chartered could establish with banks entering the Asian market.
Williamson expressed that Standard Chartered is unlikely to form another deal with an Australian bank that could affect its relationship with Westpac.
Williamson stated that Standard Chartered is not interested in equity swaps with banks it forms strategic alliances with.

Stakis Plc launched a cash call to fund a 327 million pound acquisition of Lonrho's five Metropole hotels.
Stakis aims to raise 222 million pounds through a four-for-seven rights issue at 82 pence per share.
Lonrho previously shelved plans for a 700 million pound flotation of its Metropole and Princess luxury resort hotels.
Prince al-Waleed bin Talal is considered a likely buyer for the 10 five-star Princess hotels.
Lonrho stated that the disposal of the Metropole hotels would generate net proceeds of 316 million pounds and 63 million pounds in dividends and tax relief.
Lonrho chairman John Leahy indicated that the sale of Metropole Hotels is a significant step in separating Lonrho's mining and non-mining assets.
The sale of the hotels is part of Lonrho's strategy to become a focused mining company.
Stakis was the front-runner to acquire the Metropole chain after Millennium & Copthorne Hotels withdrew from the bidding.
Stakis forecasted a profit before tax and exceptionals of not less than 30.6 million pounds for the year ending September 30.
Stakis expects the acquisition to enhance earnings from the first year and announced a final dividend of 1.2 pence per share.

British Telecom announced a $20 billion merger with MCI Corp.
The merger positions British Telecom as the second largest company in the international telecoms market.
The new entity formed from the merger will be called Concert Plc.
Concert Plc will serve 43 million customers in 70 countries.
MCI is the second largest long-distance phone company in the U.S. after AT&T Corp.
The merger is pending regulatory approval in both the U.S. and the U.K.
MCI shareholders will receive up to 2.3 billion pounds in cash and new Concert American Depositary Shares.
For each MCI share, investors will receive 5.4 new BT shares and $6.0 in cash.
BT will distribute a special dividend of 2.2 billion pounds to its shareholders.
BT already owns 20 percent of MCI.

The UK telecoms market is highly competitive.
Analysts believe attempts to block the $20 billion merger between British Telecom and MCI will fail.
The merger's approval depends on the perceived openness of the UK market.
U.S. rules restrict foreign ownership of U.S. firms to 25 percent unless their home market is as competitive as the U.S. market.
If approved, the merger will create Concert Plc, the largest cross-border takeover in history and the second largest international telephone group.
AT&T has requested regulatory scrutiny of the merger due to potential competition concerns.
Analysts consider AT&T's claims about the UK market's competitiveness to be unrealistic.
Britain's telecom market is more open than many European countries, which will only eliminate state monopolies by January 1, 1998.
The European Commission previously approved BT's acquisition of a 20 percent stake in MCI.
The merger must be approved by the U.S. Department of Justice, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission, and Britain's Department of Trade and Industry.

Dominion Resources executives began merger talks with East Midlands Electricity.
The talks aim to agree on a takeover price.
Dominion's chairman, chief finance officer, and attorneys met with East Midlands executives in London.
East Midlands Electricity's chairman is Nigel Rudd and the chief executive is Norman Askew.
Dominion Resources owns Virginia Power.
East Midlands Electricity rejected an offer from Dominion pitched at around 6.08 pounds sterling per share.
The rejected offer would value East Midlands at 1.2 billion pounds.
Dominion stated it was considering an offer at a price not much in excess of 608 pence per share.
East Midlands launched a stock buy-back to redistribute cash to shareholders.
East Midlands' stock ended at 6.12 pounds.

Telecoms analysts are divided on the financial merits of British Telecommunications's (BT) proposed $20 billion merger with MCI Communications.
Some analysts believe the merger is neutral, with synergy benefits offsetting the 30 percent premium paid by BT.
BT reported second quarter pretax profits of 730 million pounds ($1.21 billion), exceeding expectations.
BT is traditionally viewed as a less attractive stock compared to faster-growing UK rivals like Cable & Wireless.
Following the merger announcement on November 3, some brokers recommended buying BT's shares up to 400 pence.
BT's stock did not rise significantly after the MCI merger announcement, leading some analysts to change their recommendations from 'buy' to 'hold'.
MCI investors have been blamed for BT's underperforming shares after the merger announcement.
Some analysts believe BT's shares are fairly valued and dismiss projections of double-digit growth from the new BT/MCI group, named Concert.
Daiwa's telecoms analyst John Clarke predicts the merger will increase BT's five-year earnings per share growth from 5.5 percent to between seven and eight percent.
BT is paying a 35 pence special dividend to shareholders as part of the merger and forecasts a final dividend rise of 6.1 percent to 19.85 pence.

Northern Ireland Electricity (NIE) rejected price cut proposals from its watchdog.
NIE requested a referral to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).
Charles Coulthard, deputy director general for electricity supply in Northern Ireland, accused NIE of attempting to raise prices.
Coulthard's proposed plans would reduce NIE's revenues by over 300 million pounds over five years.
Coulthard stated that NIE's actions would increase electricity prices for customers in Northern Ireland.
Patrick Haren, NIE chief executive, dismissed Coulthard's statement as 'garbage' and 'quite disgraceful'.
Haren claimed that NIE's proposals would lower average domestic customer power bills by 35 pounds next year and 50 pounds by 2002.
NIE's shares fell to a year low of 322 pence, a loss of 11 pence.
Analysts were surprised by the review but did not expect NIE to request a lengthy MMC investigation.
NIE is proposing a 22 percent one-off price cut next year and a three percent cut in each of the next four years.

Britain opened its telecommunications market to 44 new international telephone operators.
The move aims to create a fully open long-distance telecommunications market 12 months ahead of the rest of Europe.
AT&T, Eurotunnel, and the Global One alliance are among the new competitors allowed to operate in Britain.
The rest of Europe is expected to achieve telecom liberalisation in 1998.
New rivals will be able to offer a full range of telecom services from January 1, 1997.
Science and Technology Minister Ian Taylor stated that liberalisation reduces prices and improves services.
Phone prices in the UK have decreased by 40 percent overall since 1984.
A total of 46 companies applied for telecommunications licenses, with 44 being granted.
International rivals previously operated by leasing lines from BT and Mercury.
The opening of the market may influence regulatory decisions regarding BT's proposed merger with MCI Communications Corp.

British Telecommunications Plc is likely to disregard Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's statement about pursuing an independent global market strategy.
BT has sought to collaborate with NTT to enter Asian markets.
BT's executives are scheduled to meet with NTT executives this month.
NTT recently received regulatory approval to offer international services.
NTT expressed a desire to pursue an independent approach to gain global customers.
Analysts believe NTT's statement may be a negotiating tactic.
BT's chairman, Sir Iain Vallance, will travel to Japan to meet NTT executives.
BT's chief executive, Sir Peter Bonfield, will also meet NTT and other organizations in Japan.
BT has an office in Japan and appointed its first regional director there this year.
BT has a minor link with NTT Data, which distributes its Concert Internet Plus services.

Energis is a British telecommunications company.
Energis's parent company is the National Grid electricity transmission network.
The National Grid may sell a majority stake in Energis to strategic investors.
Energis supplies telecom services to 13,000-14,000 business customers.
Energis seeks an international partner and local access to key metropolitan areas.
Mike Grabiner is the chief executive of Energis.
Energis has talked with all global carriers except British Telecommunications in its search for an international partner.
Grabiner stated that both Energis and the Grid initially see the Grid selling a minority stake in the business.
Energis is on track to sign an international partner this summer.
Grabiner mentioned that discussions with AT&T are not very active.

British companies are skeptical about Labour's promise not to discriminate unfairly between utilities regarding a potential windfall tax.
Labour plans to tax what it calls the excess profits of privatised utilities if it wins the next election, which is due by May 22.
Speculation suggests that Labour may aim to raise up to 10 billion pounds from this tax.
Companies in sectors such as electricity, water, gas, telecoms, airlines, and airports are considered possible targets for the tax.
Nigel Hawkins, a utilities analyst at Yamaichi, estimates that the 15 electricity groups could face a two billion pound tax bill.
Hawkins estimates that the 10 big water companies could be liable for one billion pounds, British Telecommunications for 1.5 billion pounds, and British Gas for 500 million pounds.
Labour may extend the definition of 'utilities' to include firms like BAA, Associated British Ports, British Steel, British Aerospace, and some bus companies.
None of the firms contacted by Reuters believed they should be affected by Labour's tax proposals.
United Utilities denied benefiting from a windfall, BT claimed it was neither a monopoly nor a utility, and BAA rejected the idea of the tax.
A spokeswoman for British Gas stated that the firm had made no provisions for a profit tax and preferred to see details of any proposals before commenting.

Two new TV groups applied to run Britain's key digital terrestrial television services.
BSkyB, Carlton Communications, and Granada Group are forming a new company called British Digital Broadcasting.
British Digital Broadcasting plans to offer an initial 15 channels, including subscription channels from the British Broadcasting Corporation.
CableTel, owned by U.S. company International CableTel, is competing with British Digital Broadcasting.
CableTel also owns NTL, one of two major British transmission companies.
Digital Terrestrial Network (DTN) plans to offer about 20 channels and interactive services.
DTN's Chief Executive is Jeremy Thorp.
Thorp stated that this development is significant for broadcasting since the introduction of color.
DTN has not disclosed specific sources for its programs but claims to have the best sources in the UK and U.S.
The BSkyB group may require up to 300 million pounds in peak funding if successful in winning licenses.

Human rights activists and the computer industry urged more effective policing of pornography and violence on the Internet.
There are stories about pornography, sexual violence against women and children, bomb-making recipes, incitement to racial hatred, and fraud schemes available on various websites.
Janet Henderson is a lawyer and rights strategy manager for Internet services at British Telecommunications.
Henderson stated that they acknowledge the problems and are not abdicating responsibility.
British Telecommunications has adopted a 'taste and decency' policy for its Internet access service.
Illegal material found through British Telecommunications' access is reported to the Internet Watch Foundation.
The Internet Watch Foundation was created to pass information about potentially illegal material to the police.
Henderson noted that the Internet allows anonymous worldwide distribution of violent material and child pornography.
Monika Gerstendorfer is a German human rights campaigner who noted the Internet facilitates communication for extreme political organizations.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet approved a bill to ban websites spreading Nazi propaganda and distributing hardcore pornography to minors.

The semiconductor industry's key indicator of computer chip demand rose in September to its highest level this year.
The Semiconductor Industry Association reported that the North American book-to-bill ratio rose to 0.99 in September from 0.93 in August.
The book-to-bill ratio indicates that manufacturers received $99 in new orders for every $100 in shipments in September.
Industry analysts had expected the ratio to be around 0.95.
New orders for chips increased to $3.19 billion in September, a 9 percent increase from August.
Shipments of chips rose to $3.22 billion in September, a 2.1 percent increase from August.
Douglas Andrey, director of information systems and finance for the Semiconductor Industry Association, stated that the numbers are the most positive seen all year.
Dan Klesken, an analyst at Robertson Stephens, stated that there is a PC-led recovery in the chip industry.
Shares of Intel Corp. rose $1.375 to $103 in after-hours trading, and shares of Micron Technology Inc. increased by 87.5 cents to $32.375.
Prices of memory chips have risen 30 percent to 50 percent since mid-September from their lows.

Apple Computer Inc is expected to report a loss in its fiscal fourth quarter ended in September.
The loss is attributed to declining sales of Macintosh computers.
Analysts believe Apple may resume profitability as early as the December quarter.
Todd Bakar, an analyst at Hambrecht & Quist, stated that the financial condition of Apple has improved.
Concerns about Apple's long-term viability have decreased.
Apple has reported significant losses in the past three quarters due to customer defections to IBM-compatible personal computers.
Apple has reduced its losses by cutting costs and laying off workers.
Wall Street expects Apple to post a loss of $0.30 a share.
In the fiscal fourth quarter last year, Apple reported net income of $60.1 million on revenue of $3.0 billion.
Apple's management under Gilbert Amelio has effectively cut expenses and improved cash flow.

Apple Computer Inc. reported a $25 million profit for the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996.
The profit was unexpected, as analysts had predicted a loss of 30 cents per share.
Apple's profit for the last three months of fiscal 1996 was 20 cents per share.
In the same quarter a year ago, Apple earned $60 million, or 48 cents per share.
Fourth-quarter revenue for fiscal 1996 declined 23 percent to $2.32 billion from $3 billion.
Apple's shares increased by as much as $4.25 to $30 a share in after-hours trading following the announcement.
Analysts attributed the profit to aggressive cost cutting, employee departures, and lower component prices.
Fred Anderson, Apple's chief financial officer, expects costs to increase slightly in the December quarter.
Apple reported $410 million in positive cash flow from operations during the quarter.
Apple reduced inventories by nearly $400 million since June and ended the quarter with over $1.7 billion in cash and short-term investments.

Tandem Computer Inc will introduce a line of machines based on personal computer technology.
Tandem specializes in making transaction-processing computers for banks and stock exchanges.
The new servers will be based on Intel Corp's Pentium Pro microprocessors and Microsoft Corp's Windows NT networking operating system.
The servers will include some of Tandem's technology for handling large volumes of transactions.
Tandem plans to target customers who want to establish an online presence.
This move represents Tandem's first step to reduce reliance on sales of proprietary software and technology.
Tandem's sales growth has stalled as customers have replaced some of its machines with cheaper computers from other companies.
Tandem unveiled a strategy to make servers based on off-the-shelf technology from Intel and Microsoft.
Other high-end computer makers have adopted similar strategies in the past.
Tandem plans to help existing customers set up networks using Microsoft's Windows NT networking software.

Bill Gates is the chairman of Microsoft Corp.
Bill Gates has a motto: 'A computer on every desk running Microsoft software.'
Microsoft executives aim to expand the use of Windows operating systems to various devices.
Microsoft plans to introduce Windows to subway token vending machines, handheld portables, and arcade video games.
Microsoft intends to allocate a significant portion of its research and development budget to automate management tasks of personal computers.
Microsoft's competitors include Sun Microsystems Inc. and Oracle Corp.
Sun Microsystems Inc. and Oracle Corp. are developing network computers that are simpler and cheaper than personal computers.
Microsoft controls about 80 percent of the world's desktop computers.
Paul Maritz is the group vice president at Microsoft.
Paul Maritz demonstrated software that can recognize spoken commands and automate network tasks.

Novell Inc. announced it will license its technology to other software companies to increase revenue.
Novell publishes computer networking programs.
The technology being licensed is called Novell Directory Services (NDS).
NDS is intended to help users find others on the Internet and share information.
Novell's strategy aims to adapt its corporate networking software for global information flow.
Michael Simpson is the director of marketing for Novell's Internet infrastructure division.
Simpson stated that a common infrastructure is necessary for electronic commerce.
NDS will allow users in large networks to communicate without needing specific electronic addresses.
The technology will enable communication across different computer and software standards.
Novell plans to license NDS to networking software companies, Internet service providers, and online services.

This year's Comdex is the world's most influential computer trade show.
Comdex will showcase unusual computers, including machines the size of paperback books.
Companies will introduce second-generation handheld computers that can perform tasks similar to desktop computers.
The trade show is expected to attract 250,000 attendees in Las Vegas next week.
Comdex will feature the digital video disc (DVD), an advanced compact disc for movies and computer information storage.
International Business Machines Corp. and Microsoft Corp. will present their competing approaches to simplifying personal computers at the trade show.
The PC industry is valued at $400 billion and is expanding into new areas such as living rooms and airline seats.
Tom Grueskin, marketing manager at Gateway 2000 Inc., stated that consumer product selection will diversify as more people gain experience with PCs.
Microsoft will introduce Windows CE, a program for handheld computers, at Comdex.
Several companies, including Compaq Computer Corp., NEC Corp., and LG Electronics Inc., will unveil devices using Windows CE.

Be Inc. is a private software company that Apple Computer Inc. is considering for acquisition.
Be Inc. will announce on Tuesday that it will license its BeOS operating system to Power Computing Corp.
Power Computing Corp. makes computers that are compatible with Apple's Macintosh.
Power Computing will have an exclusive license for BeOS until April 1997.
Apple has considered using Be's software after shelving its effort to rewrite the Macintosh operating system.
Be and Power Computing executives stated that their agreement does not threaten Apple's plans.
The agreement aims to provide fast machines appealing to users such as programmers and Webmasters.
Mark Gonzalez, marketing director at Be, stated that the agreement has no impact on any potential deal with Apple.
Be was founded in 1992 by the former head of Apple's research and development.
Be's software takes full advantage of the PowerPC microprocessor, which is used in Macintosh computers.

Apple Computer Inc. fired co-founder Steven Jobs in 1985.
Jobs inspired Apple engineers to create the Macintosh computer.
Jobs had a temper that burned out many engineers who admired him.
Apple rehired Jobs more than 11 years after he was ousted.
Jobs' assignment is to revamp the software behind the Macintosh.
Apple's software revamp effort had been stalled for three years.
Apple hopes Jobs can inspire its programmers to compete with Microsoft Corp's Windows operating system.
Apple's shares rose $1.25 or 5.6 percent to $23.50 after the news of Jobs' rehiring.
Apple agreed to acquire NeXT Software Inc. for $400 million.
NeXT offers a computer operating system that Apple needs to catch up with Microsoft.

Apple Computer Inc. is expected to lose $100 to $150 million in its fiscal first quarter.
Industry analysts view this loss as a serious setback to Apple's comeback plan.
Apple was relying on a strong Christmas season to attract customers and software developers.
Apple's share of the worldwide PC market fell to 5.4 percent from 8.7 percent in the same quarter a year ago.
In the U.S., Apple's share of the PC market decreased to 7.3 percent from 13.2 percent.
Apple attributed its financial shortfall to a shortage of PowerBook laptops and slow sales of its Performa line.
Consumer sales typically account for 40 percent of Apple's Christmas quarter revenue.
Apple expects revenue for the quarter ending December 27 to be about 10 percent less than the $2.3 billion reported in the September quarter.
Intel Corp. is set to release a new Pentium with MMX technology that improves graphics and sound capabilities.
Tim Bajarin stated that some consumers may be delaying purchases of Macintosh Performas in favor of Intel-based PCs.

Macromedia Inc. shares fell to a two-year low on Friday.
The decline followed the company's report of an unexpected third-quarter loss.
Macromedia indicated it could face weak sales for another quarter.
Analysts expressed concern that Apple Computer Inc.'s declining sales could negatively impact Macromedia's revenue from Macintosh software.
Shares of Macromedia dropped $4.19, or 31 percent, to $9.31 in Nasdaq trading.
This price is the lowest since December 1994.
Macromedia reported a loss of $2.36 million, or 6 cents a share, for its fiscal third quarter ended December 31.
This loss compares to a net income of $7.15 million, or 18 cents a share, in the same quarter the previous year.
Third-quarter revenue decreased by 9 percent to $28.1 million from $30.9 million.
Wall Street analysts expected Macromedia to report a net income of 14 cents a share.

Intuit Inc., Microsoft Corp., and Checkfree Corp. jointly developed a software standard called Open Financial Exchange.
Open Financial Exchange is a set of technical specifications designed to facilitate online banking.
The standard allows personal computers to communicate more easily with bank computers.
The standard will simplify tasks such as paying bills, transferring money between accounts, and checking balances online.
Approximately 50 banks are expected to adopt the Open Financial Exchange standard by fall.
Intuit Executive Vice President Bill Harris stated that new online banking products based on the standard will be unveiled by the three companies.
Intuit and Microsoft are competitors but are collaborating to accelerate the adoption of online banking.
Lewis Levin, head of Microsoft's desktop finance unit, mentioned that financial institutions requested the collaboration.
Karen Epper, an online banking analyst at Forrester Research, noted that the alliance eliminates conflicting standards previously proposed by the companies.
Intuit and Microsoft are the largest vendors of personal financial software and checkbook programs.

Informix Corp. filed a lawsuit against Oracle Corp. accusing Oracle of stealing trade secrets by hiring Informix employees.
Oracle hired 11 employees from Informix's research and development center in Portland, Oregon.
All 11 employees quit their positions at Informix on Wednesday morning.
Informix Chief Executive Phil White stated that Oracle's actions are a blatant effort to gain an advantage.
The lawsuit was filed in Oregon Circuit Court in Portland and seeks unspecified damages.
Informix obtained a temporary injunction preventing the former employees from sharing trade secrets with Oracle.
Informix charged Gary Kelley, a former vice president of product development, with breach of contract after he left for Oracle.
Oracle's stock price dropped to $39.875, while Informix's stock price fell to $21.25 during afternoon trading on Nasdaq.
Both Informix and Oracle develop database software for corporate computer networks.
Phil White expressed his intention to make the lawsuit a political cause to prevent talent raids in the high-technology industry.

Canada's largest stock exchange's key index closed at 5518 points on Monday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 25.5 points to reach 5518 points.
The 300 Index reached 5000 points on February 1.
ScotiaMcLeod's senior vice-president Fred Ketchen noted the index surpassed the 5500 barrier.
Analysts reported that overseas investors are interested in Canada due to falling interest rates and declining deficit financing needs.
Trading volume on the Toronto Stock Exchange totaled 858 million shares valued at C$1.25 billion.
Advancing issues outnumbered declining ones 561 to 420, with 276 shares trading unchanged.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indices gained ground, led by the gold sector which rose 1.2 percent.
Viridian Inc. announced a friendly merger with Agrium Inc. valued at C$1.33 billion.
Viridian shares increased by C$1.25 to C$17.75, while Agrium shares decreased by C$0.35 to C$18.55.

Investors helped drive the Toronto Stock Exchange to its 50th record close this year.
Michael Metz is the chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. Inc. in New York.
Toronto's key 300 Composite Index set its 50th record high close last Thursday.
The previous record for the most record closes in a year was 45 in 1987.
The 300 index has risen almost 19 percent this year.
Toronto posted no record closes from 1988 through 1992 after the stock market crash of October 19, 1987.
Analysts expect Toronto's latest bull run to extend to mid-1997.
Canada's inflation rate is about 1.4 percent.
The federal government has forecast its yearly borrowing requirements will drop to zero in 1998/99 from C$28.6 billion in 1995/96.
Canada's current account has reached a surplus for the first time since 1984.

Toronto stocks ended softer on Thursday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index slipped by 10.69 points to reach 5739.23 points.
The index had added more than 1.5 percent the previous day.
RBC Dominion Securities analyst Dunnery Best stated that it was time for a pause after the previous day's action.
COMEX December gold ended up US$0.90 at US$379.60 an ounce.
Gold hit a six-day intraday high at US$382.00.
The price of gold rose after comments by a Japanese official regarding the yen.
The U.S. dollar initially fell but recovered after a strong 30-year Treasury bond auction.
Toronto trading involved 99.8 million shares worth C$1.7 billion.
Advancing issues outnumbered declining ones 522 to 488.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index gained 60.55 points, closing at 5966.10 points.
This closing marked the 61st record close of the TSE 300 Composite Index in 1996.
The TSE reached a new intra-day high of 5986.80 points on Wednesday.
Toronto handles more than 80 percent of Canada's equities transactions.
The TSE gained 85 points over the past two sessions.
Subodh Kumar, chief strategist at Wood Gundy Inc, stated that the market is momentum-driven.
Kumar attributed the market's performance to lower interest rates and cash inflows from mutual funds.
Bond yields have dropped in Canada and the U.S. due to central banks slashing short-term interest rates.
Fred Ketchen, senior vice-president at ScotiaMcLeod, noted that Toronto's gains have lagged behind New York's for the past year and a half.
Toronto experienced a decline during Canada's political uncertainty in late 1995.

The Toronto market reached a record close on Tuesday due to strong buying interest in Barrick Gold Corp.
Barrick Gold Corp. is negotiating to gain control of a large gold deposit in Indonesia.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index gained 23.15 points to close at 5975.56.
Turnover on the Toronto Stock Exchange was 123 million shares worth C$2.12 billion (US$1.58 billion).
Barrick Gold is the world's third largest gold producer.
Barrick Gold is in talks with Bre-X Minerals Ltd. regarding the Busang discovery in Indonesia.
The Indonesian government requested Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-indices increased, led by golds, transports, consumer products, and real estate.
Declining issues outnumbered advancing ones on the broader market by 553 to 412.
Barrick Gold's stock rose C$2.45 to close at C$39.00, while Bre-X's stock fell C$2.20 to end at C$20.35.

The Toronto Stock Exchange closed weaker on Tuesday.
The TSE's key 300 Composite Index lost 44.24 points, finishing at 5940.73.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell nearly 80 points to 6442.
The Dow's loss was the largest in a single day since a 161-point drop in mid-July.
The TSE was affected by a decline in gold stocks and a sell-off on Wall Street.
The gold index on the TSE fell 2.7 percent.
Turnover on the TSE was 119.7 million shares worth C$2.1 billion.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-indices lost ground except for media and transportation.
Declining issues outnumbered advancing ones 575 to 424.
Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd. were active and rose C$0.95 to C$18.70 before being halted.

The Toronto stock market ended weaker on Friday but recovered most of its losses after a decline of nearly three percent.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 31.69 points to close at 5810.06.
The key index experienced its worst intra-day decline in nine years, sinking 171 points.
The 171-point decline was the most severe since a 176.5-point decline on October 22, 1987.
Trading volume was moderate, with 80.8 million shares changing hands worth C$1.4 billion (US$1.03 billion).
RBC Dominion Securities analyst Dunnery Best stated that Greenspan's comments triggered the market correction.
In a speech, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan warned of 'irrational exuberance' in financial markets.
By the end of Friday's session, the Dow Jones average lost 55.16 points.
Analysts noted that mutual fund institutions were bargain hunting on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-indices lost ground except for pipelines and industrial products.

Toronto's stock market closed at 6001.48 points on Monday.
The market was up 16.55 points from the previous close.
Turnover on the Toronto stock market was 111.7 million shares worth C$1.58 billion.
Fred Ketchen, a senior vice-president at ScotiaMcLeod, commented that the stock market performed well.
Toronto's stock market did not surpass its all-time high of 6018 points, set on November 28, 1996.
Canadian 88 Energy Corp. announced a C$652 million takeover offer for Morrison Petroleums Ltd.
Only four of Toronto's 14 sub-indices lost ground: consumer products, conglomerates, pipelines, and base metals.
The sectors that gained included oils, golds, transports, and industrial products.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declining stocks 544 to 435, with 294 stocks trading flat.
Morrison Petroleums was the most active stock, gaining C$1.45 to reach C$9.95.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key index posted a fourth record close for 1997 on Friday.
The TSE 300 Composite Index closed at 6138.80 after adding 35.14 points.
The TSE 300 Composite Index is on a seven session winning streak.
120.3 million shares were traded, worth C$1.85 billion ($1.38 billion).
The new lifetime high for the TSE 300 Composite Index is 6144.29 points.
John Ing, president of Maison Placements Canada, stated that stocks are performing well.
Gold stocks were reported to be strong, with Comex February gold rising $1.40 to $356.40.
Canadians are converting bank savings into tax sheltered pension funds ahead of a deadline for 1996 retirement plans.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, all but three increased in value.
Advancers outnumbered decliners 603 to 430, with 263 stocks trading unchanged.

Toronto stocks closed weaker on Tuesday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 37.92 points to finish at 6075.98.
This marked the Toronto Stock Exchange's second straight day of losses.
Trading volume was 120.9 million shares worth C$2.1 billion.
Gold stocks began the day stronger but turned softer due to volatile bullion prices.
MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie noted a negative reversal in gold.
Midland Walwyn analyst Dunnery Best stated that investors engaged in profit-taking.
Toronto had four record closing highs during a seven-day winning streak before Monday's decline.
Beattie indicated that short-term losses could be expected after a gain of about 215 points.
All 14 sub-indices in Toronto slipped except for transportation, pipelines, and real estate.

Barbara Amiel is a British-born journalist and the wife of Hollinger Inc. chairman Conrad Black.
Amiel writes a rightwing column for the Daily Telegraph, which is part of the Hollinger empire.
She has a significant following in Britain but is often criticized by Canadian journalists for her views.
Amiel has expressed that she does not receive the recognition in Canada that she receives in Britain.
She is currently the vice president of editorial in her husband's newspaper empire.
Hollinger Inc. acquired a majority shareholding in Southam Inc., increasing its control of the Canadian newspaper industry to over 40 percent.
This acquisition has raised concerns among Canadians about Hollinger's influence on media and job security for Southam journalists.
At a conference in Ottawa, Amiel stated that Conrad Black could speak for himself regarding his intentions.
Amiel continues to write for Maclean's magazine and has acknowledged the opportunities she has received in Canada.
Television personality Alan Edmonds believes that Amiel's rightwing bias has led to a lack of praise for her talents in Canada.

Toronto's stock market ended lower on Wednesday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index lost 33 points to end at 6112.41.
Turnover was 130.5 million shares worth C$2.04 billion ($1.52 billion).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 86.51 to close at 6746.90.
Investors sold stocks after the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee decided to keep short-term interest rates unchanged.
All but three of Toronto's 14 sub-indices slipped into negative territory.
Transportation posted the biggest decline among the sub-indices.
Morrison Petroleum Ltd. lost 0.15 to close at 10.15 on over three million shares.
Canadian 88 Energy Corp. shares rose 0.25 to close at 6.00.
Bank of Montreal lost 0.50 to finish at 47.95 after hitting a new high of 49.15 earlier in the session.

China has purchased between 600,000 and 800,000 tonnes of soybeans and soymeal.
A trader claimed responsibility for half of the 800,000 tonnes of beans and meal business with Chinese buyers in the past four trading days.
The total amount of beans and meal purchased since last Wednesday is estimated at 800,000 tonnes.
The purchases included 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes of beans and 500,000 to 600,000 tonnes of meal.
Chinese buyers entered the market immediately after the National Day holiday.
China celebrated the 47th anniversary of the People's Republic on October 1.
The National Day holiday resulted in the closure of government, business, and trade for three weekdays.
Soy product prices fell significantly on the Chicago Board of Trade due to concerns about a larger U.S. crop.
Reports indicated that China bought between 120,000 and 150,000 tonnes of soymeal for November/December delivery from the U.S., South America, and India.
Shipments of the purchased soy products are scheduled to begin in October/November for December/January arrival.

China has banned imports of some U.S. chicken meat due to concerns about a fowl plague.
U.S. officials stated that their chickens do not have highly pathogenic avian influenza.
A U.S. quarantine official confirmed that there is no record of highly pathogenic avian influenza in domestic poultry.
Highly pathogenic avian influenza was eradicated in the U.S. after an outbreak in the 1980s.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture representatives are expected to meet with Ministry of Agriculture officials to resolve the issue.
China's Administration of Animal and Plant Quarantine confirmed the ban by telephone.
U.S. officials in Beijing claimed that the ban was not based on sound scientific evidence.
Poultry meat is not considered a likely vehicle for transmission of avian influenza.
The ban could significantly impact U.S. poultry exports to China.
In 1995, 330,000 tonnes of U.S. poultry worth US$445 million were trans-shipped through Hong Kong.

Falling world metal prices have caused concern among Asian aluminium traders.
Up to 80,000 tonnes of aluminium is currently sitting in Chinese ports.
Consumers are now seeking to pay lower prices for aluminium.
A trader in Hong Kong reported that there is more than 80,000 tonnes of aluminium stuck in China.
Another source in Hong Kong stated that 35,000 to 40,000 tonnes of aluminium is stuck in Hong Kong and Shantou.
Chinese trading companies have a poor reputation for reneging on deals when prices fall.
Traders in Hong Kong and Beijing are waiting for news of distressed cargoes as prices decline.
The London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium stocks are currently at 961,450 tonnes.
The LME aluminium price has reached long-term lows in recent weeks.
LME three-month aluminium ended at US$1,337 a tonne, slightly above a low of $1,305.

Asian sugar traders and industry executives are optimistic about a stabilised Chinese market and potential profits for sugar mills.
Sugar prices in China are moving to levels that cover factory costs and provide profits.
White sugar prices in Beijing and Shanghai are around 4,400 yuan (US$530) per tonne.
Ex-factory prices in sugar-growing regions are 300-400 yuan higher than prices in major cities.
The lowest price for sugar in producing areas was 3,650 renminbi per tonne in 1996.
Transport costs to major cities add 150 to 200 yuan, plus handling costs.
Current sugar prices reflect when the sugar was purchased and stored.
Prices in Guangxi and Guangdong provinces have increased to between 4,500 and 4,700 yuan per tonne.
Annual Chinese sugar demand is estimated at eight to nine million tonnes.
The Chinese government has stopped sugar imports for the last three months.

China has agreed not to enforce a ban on imports of U.S. poultry until after quarantine talks in Beijing.
Chinese authorities have not issued a letter banning imports of U.S. poultry.
China confirmed a ban on imports of poultry and poultry products from 10 U.S. states due to fears of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI).
China is the second-biggest market for U.S. poultry products, after Russia, and the only market for chicken feet.
U.S. poultry exports to China in 1995 totaled $445 million.
The states affected by the ban are Arkansas, Florida, Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Texas, Utah, and Wisconsin.
Officials from Washington's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service are scheduled to arrive in Beijing for talks.
The U.S. agriculture attache in Beijing confirmed fears that U.S. poultry products bore the HPAI virus.
U.S. officials state that U.S. poultry is free of HPAI virus.
AI is prevalent worldwide, especially in wild fowl, but has not been isolated in commercial U.S. poultry flocks.

International copper prices are expected to remain high, affecting the China market.
A base metal trader in Hong Kong predicts the LME will test US$2,100 per tonne.
Copper prices on the LME surpassed US$2,000 per tonne, reaching $2,027 in late afternoon trading.
The international copper price is now higher than the domestic Chinese price, making imports unviable.
The most active February 1997 copper contract on the Shanghai Metal Exchange opened at 19,550 yuan ($2,355) per tonne.
China imposes a three percent import duty and a 17 percent value-added tax on copper imports.
A source at a Chinese listed company has 200 tonnes of copper to sell at a premium of $100 over the LME spot price.
The premium on copper, CIF to Hong Kong and Chinese ports, was $150 last week.
Traders in Hong Kong report that high LME prices are discouraging import business with China.
Chinese consumers' stocks of copper have been depleted, typically maintained at around 100,000 tonnes.

The London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc price rose to a five-month high in Asia on Thursday.
China is a major source of zinc in the Far East.
Traders believe the rise in zinc price will benefit China.
Three month LME zinc reached a price of $1,064/$1,069 a tonne on Thursday.
The previous day's closing price for LME zinc was $1,054 in London.
Rumors suggested that financier George Soros was making a speculative play in the zinc market.
Traders noted that a large, losing long position held by Asturiana de Zinc had been liquidated or transferred.
China's exports of unwrought zinc and zinc alloys increased by 16.7 percent in the first nine months of 1996 compared to the same period in 1995.
China's zinc production in 1995 was estimated at 1.05 million tonnes.
China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp (CNNC) projected domestic zinc demand would reach 900,000 tonnes by 2000.

Genetically-altered soybeans are causing little concern in China.
China is a major soybean importer with its own bio-engineering programmes.
Monsanto Co developed the first genetically-altered U.S. soybeans.
China has been involved in producing insect-resistant cotton and genetically-altered soybeans, corn, and rice.
Monsanto has faced opposition from environmental groups in the United States and Europe.
The genetically-altered soybeans are resistant to the weed killer Roundup, which is also a Monsanto product.
Chinese industry executives believe there is demand for pest-resistant soybeans in China.
Chinese research on genetically-altered crops is reportedly a decade behind Monsanto's efforts.
Monsanto is negotiating for cooperative projects in China.
Greenpeace activists in Hong Kong do not plan to campaign against the sale of genetically-altered beans in Asia.

Chinese grain sellers are reducing the price for exporting corn.
Chinese corn is being offered at $150 a tonne FOB.
U.S. corn is selling into Asian ports at $138 c&f a tonne.
A trader in Hong Kong stated that no one would pay the current price for Chinese corn.
Chinese sellers may be pressured to sell old crop due to an expected bumper new crop of 115 to 120 million tonnes.
Traders who bought corn in 1996 have been paying storage costs for over six months.
Offers for corn are being made by state-owned traders in Jilin and Heilongjiang provinces.
The March futures price on the Dalian Commodity Exchange was 1,550 yuan ($186) per tonne.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture predicted the 1996 corn crop would total 9.265 million bushels.
China lifted a ban on corn exports but set a minimum price of $170 a tonne.

Hundreds of thousands of tonnes of copper have moved through Chinese customs into central stocks.
Traders reported that the copper is not being sold despite high prices.
A South American industry executive stated that it was a good decision for China to buy good quality metal at 85 to 90 U.S. cents a pound.
China recently boosted its central copper reserves by 300,000 tonnes.
Most of the copper has cleared customs formalities, but a lag in customs reporting may delay the figures.
Few Chinese trading companies have the financial resources to buy and store substantial amounts of copper.
A modest rise in stocks held in London Metal Exchange warehouses in Singapore indicated that Chinese material is not being exported.
LME copper trading has been volatile, with a moderate rise in stocks pushing prices down due to profit-taking.
LME stocks are at 92,475 tonnes, while the spot price is at 2,470.50.
Traders in Asia are largely uninterested in the upcoming options expiry as China is not interested in selling.

Copper is being sold in small lots from China as traders seek to benefit from higher world prices.
Chinese traders are shipping copper to LME warehouses in Singapore.
The copper market is described as dull, with limited activity aside from Chinese copper movements.
Chinese traders are selling copper in lots of no more than 1,000 tonnes.
The selling is motivated by the desire to liquidate and generate cash for year-end.
Movements in LME warehouse stock levels in Singapore are linked to Chinese buying and selling.
Copper prices on the LME closed lower after a brief rally.
Traders expect copper prices to fall towards support at US$2,120 a tonne.
Zinc prices could rise to $1,200 a tonne in the first half of 1997, according to a Hong Kong trader.
A recent drawdown in LME zinc stocks was reported, with a decrease of 3,050 tonnes.

Tung Chee-hwa won the race for Hong Kong's future leader.
Tung Chee-hwa was elected by the Selection Committee, which consists of 400 members chosen by Beijing.
Tung Chee-hwa will become Hong Kong's Chief Executive when the colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
Tung Chee-hwa emphasized pragmatism and stability in his victory speech.
Tung Chee-hwa downplayed the importance of democracy in his speech.
Tung Chee-hwa stated that it is important to secure a smooth transition from British to Chinese rule.
Tung Chee-hwa received 320 votes in the final round of voting.
Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen declared Tung Chee-hwa as Hong Kong's most democratically elected leader to date.
The voting process has been criticized as undemocratic and unrepresentative of Hong Kong's population.
Tung Chee-hwa believes that the voting process is a step forward on the road to democracy for Hong Kong.

In 1996, China's leaders claimed they could feed a fifth of the global population on limited arable land.
Western analysts and grain industry leaders are skeptical about China's ability to achieve grain self-sufficiency.
Many industry sources believe China's leadership must disclose state grain reserves and food needs.
A consultant to the Chinese and U.S. grain industries suggested that transparency could help other nations plan for supply to China.
Official projections for 1996 grain output are expected to reach 485 million tonnes, following a 465 million tonne output in 1995.
China Agribusiness described the 1996 grain output projections as high, even for ministry officials.
Grain supply in China has increased by 55 million tonnes over the past two years.
The Chinese government predicts grain supply will reach 550 million tonnes annually by 2010.
China's population is expected to grow from 1.2 billion to over 1.4 billion.
China's net grain imports in the first nine months of 1996 were 7.4 million tonnes, with total imports expected to be eight to nine million tonnes for the year.

Russia is considering a freeze on domestic energy prices.
Energy analysts believe this move could prolong the recovery of the oil sector and slow economic reforms.
Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov has called for lower oil, gas, and electricity prices to support domestic industry.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin stated that President Boris Yeltsin may soon sign a decree to lower and freeze energy prices, specifically mentioning gas and electricity.
Energy analysts warn that frozen prices could negatively impact the Russian oil industry, which is the country's largest export earner.
Vadim Voronin, an energy specialist at the World Bank's Moscow mission, expressed concern that low reinvestment rates could lead to a decline in the oil industry.
The International Monetary Fund prefers domestic oil prices to align with world levels and has made this a condition of its $10 billion loan to Moscow.
James Bunch, an oil analyst at Renaissance Capital, stated that a price freeze would hinder reforms in liberalizing oil prices.
Rodionov's predecessor, Yuri Shafranik, suggested that domestic oil prices should be capped at 75 percent of world levels.
Domestic natural gas prices are significantly lower than their market cost, and electricity prices are heavily subsidized.

Yuri Shafranik is Russia's former fuel and energy minister.
Shafranik attempted to create a mega oil corporation by merging four privatized companies.
The companies involved in Shafranik's proposal were the Tyumen Oil Company, ONAKO, the Eastern Oil Company, and Slavneft.
Shafranik's merger proposal did not receive government support.
Shafranik is now trying to create a financial-industrial group that includes some of the firms he wanted to merge and second-tier players.
If Shafranik's merger had succeeded, it would have created Russia's largest oil producer.
The proposed company would have accounted for nearly one third of Russia's total oil output in 1995.
Russia is the world's third largest oil producer.
The proposed financial-industrial group would consist of the Tyumen Oil Company, SIBUR, the Eastern Oil Company, Slavneft, and the Eastern-Siberian Oil and Gas Company.
SIBUR and Eastern-Siberian do not have crude oil production units.

Russian parliamentarians plan to ask lawmakers to reject a bill outlining oil reserves open to production-sharing agreements.
The bill includes about 250 oil fields that hold 38 percent of proven Russian oil reserves.
The rejection of the bill is expected to impact planned investments in Russian oil, including a project by Amoco Corp.
Members of the audit chamber of parliament announced their intention to ask Duma deputies to reject the law early next month.
The call for rejection is seen as a setback for Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who has supported foreign oil investors.
Moscow is reportedly changing its policy to become more stringent with potential Western oil investors.
Duma Deputy Yuri Boldyrev stated that the audit chamber rejected the reserves list due to a lack of financial analyses from government officials.
Production-sharing contracts allow Western oil firms to finance and develop oil production while sharing output with the host country.
Boldyrev suggested that Moscow should reduce the number of reserves open to output-sharing to 10 or 15 per year.
Dan Westbrook, a senior executive at Amoco Eurasia Petroleum Company, expressed concern about delays in the process.

President Boris Yeltsin underwent surgery on Tuesday.
Russian oil and gas exports have remained stable despite political turmoil.
Russia is the world's third-largest crude oil producer and the largest natural gas producer.
Russian energy exports are significant for Europe and generate substantial revenue for Russia.
Traders prioritize government decrees regarding export tariffs over political events.
Yeltsin's surgery raised concerns about potential political uncertainty affecting oil and gas exports.
One third of Russia's daily oil output is exported outside the former Soviet Union.
Russian natural gas supplies heat one third of Europe.
Fluctuations in Russian oil exports are typically due to non-political events.
Analysts predict stable near-term exports due to flat domestic demand and economic recovery.

Transneft is a state oil pipeline firm in Russia.
Transneft has demanded a stronger role in a proposed new pipeline across Russia.
Transneft spokesman Ravil Polyanin stated that the firm wants an equity stake in the project.
Polyanin claimed that oil firms have not valued Transneft's technical expertise highly enough.
The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) includes companies such as Chevron, LUKoil, Mobil Corp, Rosneft, Oman Oil Company, British Gas Plc, Agip SpA, Kazakh Munaigaz, and Oryx Energy Company.
Kazakhstan, Oman, and Russia hold the remaining 50 percent stake in the CPC.
A CPC official indicated that a restructuring agreement would be signed next month.
The CPC aims to build a $1.5 billion pipeline from Kazakhstan's Tengiz oilfield to Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.
Concerns were raised about whether the CPC had resolved past hurdles related to Transneft's participation and financing.
Polyanin mentioned that it was premature to say all outstanding problems had been resolved.

Azerbaijan is attracting more foreign oil investment than Russia.
Azerbaijan needs to engage with Moscow to become a major world energy player.
Azeri oil officials announced a $1.5 billion agreement with Amoco Corp, Unocal Corp, Japan's Itochu Corp, and Saudi Arabia's Delta Nimir on December 14.
The $1.5 billion deal aims to explore reserves in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea.
This deal is the fourth multi-billion-dollar project Azerbaijan has secured since the Soviet Union's breakup in 1991.
Western oil companies are facing challenges with Russian-based deals due to legal issues.
Douglas Hill stated that the Azeri government has made efforts to attract foreign investors.
Foreign oil investment in Russia has significantly decreased, with less than $1 billion received out of a planned $60 billion.
Azerbaijan's $8 billion Azerbaijan International Operating Company project is set to begin production in the third quarter of next year.
Russia is seeking to involve LUKoil in Caspian oil projects to address the shift in focus towards high-yielding reserves.

Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits warned Norilsk Nickel about overdue taxes.
Analysts stated that Norilsk Nickel would not be liquidated or have its assets frozen.
Konstantin Chernyshev is an equities analyst at Moscow brokerage Rinaco Plus.
Chernyshev described Norilsk Nickel as a significant debtor to federal and regional budgets.
Livshits indicated that bankruptcy procedures apply to Norilsk Nickel.
Christopher Granville is the chief economist at United City Bank in Moscow.
Granville commented on the nature of Livshits's statements regarding Norilsk Nickel.
Russian tax authorities are under pressure from the International Monetary Fund to increase tax revenues.
The government has expressed concerns about the social infrastructure dependent on Norilsk Nickel.
Norilsk Nickel is the world's second-largest nickel producer.

Russia's Western oil joint ventures are struggling to export enough output to remain profitable.
Moscow is prioritizing domestic producers for pipeline space.
Joint ventures produce a small fraction of Russia's crude oil but rely on exports for profitability.
Russian energy officials are reconsidering the terms for foreign oil firms operating in Russia.
Julian Leigh from the Centre for Global Energy Studies stated that any increase in exports will come at the expense of joint ventures.
Russia's restrictions on export pipeline access indicate its willingness to allow foreign investors to export necessary volumes.
Most new projects will require new pipelines but will initially use existing ones.
Igor Ishkayev from the Tatex joint venture noted that larger companies like LUKoil have fewer export restrictions.
Only about six out of 40 joint ventures in Russia have the right to export 100 percent of their output until September 1997.
Access to Transneft pipelines is influenced by personal relationships and the interests of large producers.

Russia is facing competition from the return of Iraqi oil to world markets.
Russian Urals sour crude is similar in quality to Iraq's Kirkuk blend.
Iraq's Kirkuk blend was a main competitor of Russian Urals in the Mediterranean before Gulf War sanctions.
Sarah Anderson from Energy Security Analysis Inc suggested that Russia may need to price competitively.
Med refiners have a long history of purchasing Iraqi crude.
Sour Urals differentials in the Mediterranean have decreased due to the first Iraqi exports in six years.
Gavin Rankin from Troika-Dialog stated that Russian profits could be affected by the return of Iraqi oil.
Three Russian oil companies have signed contracts to buy 1.3 million tonnes of Iraqi oil, pending U.N. approval.
The three companies are Zarubezhneft, NK LUKoil, and Nafta-Moskva.
Analyst James Bunch noted that Russia's interest in Iraqi oil contracts may be related to obtaining transparent pricing.

Russia's aluminium sector will consolidate more in 1997.
Igor Prokopov is the director of Kontsern Alyuminiy, the producers' group for Russia's aluminium industry.
Domestic smelters in Russia are concerned about low world prices for aluminium.
Prokopov blames speculation for the low prices.
Russian primary aluminium output in 1996 is projected to be 2.79 million tonnes, a 1.5 percent increase from 1995.
Prokopov stated that 1997 production could rise by 1.5 to 2.0 percent.
Kontsern Alyuminiy estimates Russia's 1996 primary aluminium exports at 2.37 million tonnes.
Exports of primary aluminium, alloys, and semi-fabricated items from Russia rose seven percent from year-ago levels over January-October.
The State Customs Committee reports a 16 percent rise in aluminium exports.
Prokopov believes there is no basis for weak prices given supply and demand patterns.

Russia's metals sectors are key suppliers to world markets.
Most officials in the metals sectors are no longer concerned about Kremlin health issues.
Aluminium officials expressed minimal concern regarding President Boris Yeltsin's hospitalization for pneumonia.
Galina Stelmakova stated that Yeltsin's health would not affect aluminium production or exports.
Russia supplies 15 percent of the world aluminium market.
London Metal Exchange aluminium prices reached a seven-month high of $1,602.
Palladium prices increased due to Russia's failure to sign 1997 export contracts with Japan.
Yeltsin's illness is not expected to affect precious metals contracts, according to a senior official.
Contracts for supplying Japan depend on the Duma passing a federal budget.
Norilsk Nickel is monitoring the health crisis due to Yeltsin's previous support for state aid.

Russian oil company officials announced that Moscow will not impose a duty on heavy fuel oil exports this winter.
Traders expressed relief over the absence of export restrictions on mazut, which is essential for heating in European and Mediterranean markets.
Traders are nearly certain there will be no export duty, but remain cautious about potential unexpected changes in Russia.
Vladimir Tumarkin, chief spokesman for Rosneft, stated that a proposed duty plan by the Fuel and Energy Ministry was rejected by senior cabinet officials.
A second Rosneft official confirmed that there would be no duty on mazut exports.
Gennady Grigoryev, deputy head of Rosneft's financial-commercial directorate, indicated that it is too late for a duty to be implemented.
Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov had previously advocated for a duty but failed to gain support from Kremlin officials.
One Rosneft official noted that Rodionov did not convince government officials to agree to the proposed duty.
A senior trader at a European company expressed skepticism about the timing of the announcement regarding the absence of an export duty.
Russian heavy fuel oil exports typically decline from November to May due to freezing waterways and increased domestic consumption.

Bouygues is a French diversified conglomerate.
STET is joining Bouygues to become a leading player in France's telecommunications market.
The telecommunications sector in France was fully liberalized in 1998.
STET will take a 49 percent stake in a joint venture called Bouygues-STET.
Bouygues will hold a 51 percent stake in the Bouygues-STET joint venture.
Bouygues and STET plan to bid to run the telephone infrastructure of French state railways group SNCF.
Bouygues will compete with France Telecom and CEGETEL in the French telecommunications market.
STET will buy into the BDT holding company, which owns 51 percent of Bouygues Telecom.
BDT is valued at 13.75 billion francs.
STET will pay 1.71 billion francs to buy new shares in BDT during 1996 and 1997.

France announced plans to sell state-owned defence and consumer electronics group Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe for a symbolic franc.
The French government preferred Lagardere's bid over Alcatel Alsthom SA's offer.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe stated that the decision was based on defence industrial logic.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis mentioned that both offers were comparable financially and required a capital increase.
The French state will provide an 11 billion franc cash injection to Thomson SA before the sale.
Thomson SA owns 58 percent of Thomson-CSF and 100 percent of Thomson Multimedia.
Lagardere's bid for Thomson-CSF is 156 francs a share, totaling 7.8 billion francs.
Lagardere will retain 60 percent of Thomson Matra and the French state will hold a golden share.
Lagardere plans to sell Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea.
Daewoo has committed to creating 3,000 new jobs in France and maintaining French-based management for Thomson Multimedia.

France Telecom chairman Michel Bon stated that the company wants to grow internationally to offset competition in France.
From 1998, France Telecom will lose its monopoly position in France.
Generale des Eaux and Bouygues have formed international alliances to compete with France Telecom.
France Telecom aims to generate at least 10 percent of its sales from international markets.
France Telecom's international policy is based on three main goals.
One goal is to meet the international needs of clients through the Global One joint venture with Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp.
Another goal is to utilize its expertise in building modern infrastructure networks in Latin America and Indonesia.
The third goal is to find new growth areas to compensate for the impact of competition on sales in France.
Mobistar, in which France Telecom has a majority stake, is part of France Telecom's international policy.
Mobistar started operations six weeks ago and has 20,000 subscribers, aiming for a 25 percent market share by 2005.

British Airways Plc and French bank Groupe Rivaud submitted a bid for Air Liberte.
British Airways will hold 70 percent of the bid, while Groupe Rivaud will hold 30 percent.
The bid aims to continue the operations of Air Liberte and safeguard jobs.
Air Liberte has debts of approximately 1.5 billion French francs, equivalent to $290.7 million.
Creditors have the option to receive cash now at a discount or wait up to ten years for full payment.
The Creteil commercial court is scheduled to meet to discuss the bid.
Air Liberte founder Lotfi Belhassine will retain his position as chairman.
Air Liberte went into administration on September 26.
Other bidders included Richard Branson's Virgin Express and commercial pilot Fernand Denan.
British Airways plans to merge Air Liberte with TAT and intends to invest 440 million francs.

Jacques Maillot is the chairman of travel group Nouvelles Frontieres.
Maillot has dropped out of bidding for the French regional airline Air Liberte.
Maillot is planning to buy airline AOM and expects formal talks to start in weeks.
Maillot has had several talks with CDR executives and has started to exchange information.
AOM was created in 1991 by the merger of Air Outre Mer and Minerve.
AOM is owned by the Consortium de Realisation (CDR), a state entity.
Maillot announced he had withdrawn from talks on the rescue of Air Liberte due to the financial commitment required.
A 780 million French franc bid by British Airways Plc's French TAT unit and bank Rivaud is the only remaining bid for Air Liberte.
Maillot had planned to buy Air Liberte with the help of Royal Air Maroc, Club Mediterranee, and Rivaud.
Warburg had previously valued AOM at one billion francs, but Maillot noted the valuation was outdated.

Rhone-Poulenc SA announced a 13 percent rise in third quarter profits.
The profit increase would have been 25.1 percent without a product recall.
Rhone-Poulenc shares closed up 3.16 percent at 147 francs.
The company reported net income of 756 million francs compared to 669 million francs at the same stage last year.
Operating profit was 2.05 billion francs in the third quarter, up from 1.83 billion francs.
Net sales were 20.47 billion francs, an increase from 19.62 billion francs.
Rhone-Poulenc issued a profit warning on October 10 due to a product recall by the Centeon joint venture.
The recall is expected to cut six to seven percent from analysts' forecasts for 1996 results.
The market consensus for 1996 is 2.631 billion francs, with projections of 3.426 billion in 1997.
For the first nine months, net income was up 10.5 percent at 2.17 billion francs.

French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis stated that the procedure for the planned sale of Thomson SA is beyond criticism.
Arthuis mentioned that France's independent privatisation commission has the right to block the deal.
Arthuis expressed his conviction that the government's procedure is unassailable and that the law has been respected.
The privatisation commission is an independent body with full authority, according to Arthuis.
Thomson's planned privatisation has faced criticism in France.
The opposition Socialists and Communists in the National Assembly have called for a committee of inquiry into Thomson's privatisation.
The French privatisation commission is assessing the value of Thomson SA and its proposed sale to Lagardere Groupe and Daewoo Electronics.
The commission is expected to issue its decision in early December.
Commission members are appointed for five years and cannot hold any other function during that time.
The commission is currently chaired by Pierre Laurent, and its members include Pierre Alby, Andre Blanc, Daniel Deguen, Daniel Hua, Jean Serise, and Jean Pineau.

Storage Technology Corp signed a deal with the Swedish patent office for the sale of a disc-based storage system.
Storage Technology Corp is in talks with the Chinese patent office about a similar deal.
Storage Technology Corp previously sold a system to the European Patent Office.
Campbell McGarvie is the vice-president for Europe, Africa, and the Middle East at Storage Technology Corp.
McGarvie stated that it is too early to discuss the details of the Chinese deal.
Storage Technology Corp is based in Louisville, Colorado.
Storage Technology Corp specializes in the storage and retrieval of digital information.
Storage Technology Corp is moving away from digital documents to bit-map images.
Bit-map images can be used to store medical scans or video images.
Potential users of Storage Technology Corp's products include members of the medical profession and broadcasters.

French carmakers Renault SA and Peugeot PSA are in talks with the government on a long-term plan to rejuvenate their workforce.
Renault SA and Peugeot PSA did not confirm a report about seeking approval for a five-year plan to cut 40,000 jobs in exchange for hiring 14,000 young people.
The newspaper Les Echos reported that the cost of the proposed operations could be 30 billion francs ($6 billion).
Renault's chairman Louis Schweitzer and Peugeot's chairman Jacques Calvet wrote a letter to Prime Minister Alain Juppe in July with a proposal.
The Renault spokeswoman stated that discussions have occurred since the letter was sent, but the government has not yet replied.
Peugeot officials declined to comment on the existence of the letter but acknowledged the need to rejuvenate the workforce.
The average age of a car worker in France is 42 to 43 years, while competitors, especially Asian companies, have an average age below 30 years.
The Peugeot spokesman stated that older workers create a competitive handicap for Peugeot and Renault.
Renault's average worker age is 45 years, and the oldest factory is located at Flins, which dates from the war.
Renault had a worldwide staff of 139,950 people at the end of 1995, with 72,163 involved in car production in France.

Cie Generale des Eaux launched its bid to compete with France Telecom by starting a fixed-line telephone network in a residential area in Nice.
Philippe Glotin is the managing director of Generale's telecoms unit CEGETEL.
CEGETEL aims to achieve a market share in 2003 that would yield 40 billion francs in annual sales, with more than half from mobile communications.
CEGETEL competes with France Telecom in mobile telecommunications through its SFR unit and is allied with British Telecom Plc and MCI for business services.
SFR expects to have one million customers by March 1997, up from approximately 725,000 at the time of the statement.
The local residential telecommunications market is projected to represent 55 billion francs in annual sales by 2003.
Glotin aims for CEGETEL to gain a 40 percent share in mobile telecommunications, 20 percent in long-distance, and 10 percent in local loops.
CEGETEL has received permission from French authorities for a telecoms experiment in Nice and will offer residential telecoms services starting in 1997 using DECT technology.
The DECT technology used in Nice connects buildings to a telephone switch using radio waves, while internal connections use traditional telephone sockets.
The Nice experiment is expected to attract 1,000 to 3,000 subscribers by the end of 1997, and CEGETEL plans to invest three billion francs in local loops with radio links in the coming years.

Market talk suggests a possible demerger of Rhone-Poulenc into a chemicals company and a pharmaceuticals group.
A leading French broker claims that a demerger would boost Rhone-Poulenc's share value by a third.
Jean Borjeix, chief analyst at Jean-Pierre Pinatton, estimates Rhone-Poulenc's intrinsic value at 40 to 45 billion francs due to underperforming chemical activities and significant debts.
Borjeix states that separating the pharmaceutical activities from the chemical activities could increase the total group value to 60 billion francs.
Borjeix believes that an asset gain from a demerger would allow investors to wait for the operation to occur.
Pinatton forecasts a stable net attributable profit of 2.05 billion francs for Rhone-Poulenc in 1996, increasing to 2.5 billion in 1997.
Rhone-Poulenc reported a net attributable profit of 2.13 billion francs in 1995.
Demerger rumors were initially fueled by comments from managing director Igor Landau on May 28, indicating the company had studied the possibility but decided against it for the time being.
Borjeix believes management is concerned about shareholder value and that an asset disposal policy is ending, which may lead to a decision to split.
An analyst at a U.S. brokerage in London expressed doubt about the demerger, suggesting the company will focus on improving margins instead.

There is a debate in France regarding the viability of future competitors of a privatized France Telecom.
Analysts are examining interconnection charges and the cost of public service in relation to France Telecom.
The French government plans to sell about 20 percent of France Telecom in April and aims to eventually sell 49 percent.
French telecommunications minister Francois Fillon stated that interconnection charges must be comparable to those in other competitive countries.
Interconnection charges are payments that telecom rivals must make to France Telecom for network usage.
France Telecom plans to charge 0.16 francs per minute for local calls, 0.18 francs for regional calls, and 0.26 francs for national calls.
France Telecom claims its interconnection charges are among the lowest in Europe, with only Britain having cheaper local charges.
France Telecom's rivals argue that the interconnection prices are too high and exceed the internal charges used by France Telecom.
France Telecom is legally required to provide a public service that is accessible to everyone in France, and its rivals must share the costs.
A study cited by Les Echos estimates the cost of the public service at nine billion francs per year, while France Telecom's rivals estimate it at 4.5 billion francs.

Market talk suggests a possible demerger of Rhone-Poulenc into a chemicals company and a pharmaceuticals group.
A leading French broker claims that a demerger would boost Rhone-Poulenc's share value by a third.
Jean Borjeix, chief analyst at Jean-Pierre Pinatton, estimates Rhone-Poulenc's intrinsic worth to be between 40 to 45 billion francs.
Borjeix attributes the low valuation to underperforming chemical activities and significant debts.
He states that separating the pharmaceutical activities from the chemical activities could increase the total group value to 60 billion francs.
Borjeix believes that an asset gain of this size would allow investors to wait for the demerger operation.
Pinatton forecasts a stable net attributable profit of 2.05 billion francs for Rhone-Poulenc in 1996, increasing to 2.5 billion in 1997.
Rhone-Poulenc reported a net attributable profit of 2.13 billion francs in 1995.
Demerger rumors were initially fueled by comments from managing director Igor Landau on May 28.
An analyst at a U.S. brokerage in London expressed skepticism about the likelihood of a demerger, suggesting the company will focus on improving margins.
