The latest bull run in China's share markets began in April when Beijing announced market support.
Rumors about Beijing's plans have been the primary factor in trading since the bull run began.
Beijing authorities are attempting to encourage long-term investment based on economic fundamentals.
An executive from a major Chinese securities house stated that the crackdown highlights the risk of policy changes.
Beijing warned that it would not rescue investors if the stock markets crashed.
An analyst noted that the action has temporarily cooled speculative activity in the markets.
Investors shifted towards blue-chip shares and sold off lower-quality shares during the recent market shake-out.
Analysts indicated that the lack of supervisory mechanisms and regulations contributes to irregularities in the Chinese stock markets.

China named four foreign banks in Shanghai to conduct business in the local Chinese currency.
The four banks are the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp, Citibank, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank, and the Industrial Bank of Japan.
The People's Bank of China stated that the foreign banks would be allowed to conduct Chinese currency loans, deposits, and other business.
A report from Xinhua indicated that the chosen foreign banks would not be allowed to have outstanding local currency loans exceeding 35 percent of their foreign currency loans.
All foreign banks in China are currently restricted to doing business in foreign currency.
Foreign banks must adopt the same regulations that apply to Chinese financial institutions to conduct yuan business.
Foreign bank profits are taxed at a 15 percent rate, while Chinese commercial banks are taxed at 33 percent and state banks at 55 percent.
A foreign banker confirmed that formal notification was received but no business conditions were provided.
Another foreign banker stated that there has been no news regarding formal notification for his bank.
Jacques Bertholier, the China manager of Credit Lyonnais, expressed hope that his bank would be included in the next batch of banks approved for yuan business.

A small plane carrying two mineral explorers disappeared in a snow squall in the Canadian village of Nain.
The missing men were from Vancouver-based Castle Rock Exploration Corp.
Two hundred exploration companies are active in Labrador.
These companies have staked more than 250,000 claims in the past two years.
Approximately C$85 million has been invested by these companies so far this year.
About 184,000 diamond drill holes have been drilled in the area.
The Voisey's Bay nickel deposit is one of the largest base metals discoveries in the world.
The Voisey's Bay deposit was discovered in late 1993 by explorers looking for diamonds.
Diamond Fields Resources Inc. saw its stock rise from pennies to more than C$42 before being taken over by Inco Ltd.
Some mining companies are giving up, while a few are making long-term financial commitments to continue drilling.

Barrick Gold Corp is North America's largest gold producer and is based in Toronto.
Barrick Gold Corp reported lower third-quarter earnings due to an after-tax charge and higher operating costs.
Barrick's net income for the quarter fell to US$21 million, or US$0.06 a share, from US$67.7 million, or US$0.19 a share, in the same period a year earlier.
Barrick's earnings were slightly below analysts' expectations.
Barrick's cash costs rose to US$203 an ounce from US$194 an ounce a year earlier.
Barrick took a US$38 million hit to exit its Cerro Corona exploration project in Peru.
Barrick increased its exploration budget by more than 50 percent to US$46.4 million for the first nine months of the year.
Barrick's shares rose C$0.50 to C$36.15 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Barrick's stock rose 3/8 to US$26 7/8 in New York.
Barrick plans to develop its Pascua mine in Chile and its new Pierina property in Peru.

Barrick Gold Corp is considered the most likely partner for Bre-X Minerals Ltd in developing its Indonesian gold deposit.
Gold analyst Barry Allan from Gordon Capital stated that Barrick is the only potential front runner for this partnership.
Barrick Gold has invested over US$10 million in exploration in Indonesia and has acquired a large land position there.
Barrick's connection with a construction company owned by the daughter of Indonesia's President Suharto indicates strategic positioning for the Busang discovery.
Analysts believe Barrick has the best chance of successfully bidding for a stake in the Busang property due to its high stock price relative to its assets.
Bre-X shareholders are expected to seek a combination of cash and shares in any deal to maintain a stake in the Busang project.
Bre-X is searching for a major mining company to acquire all or part of the Busang discovery and to operate the mine.
A dispute with Bre-X's Indonesian partners has delayed the Indonesian government from granting essential contracts needed for the development of Busang.
Analysts indicated that without these contracts, a bid for Bre-X would be unlikely.
Placer Dome Inc also has the resources to bid for Bre-X, according to analyst Rick Cohen.

The gold zone near Timmins in northern Ontario has seen increased exploration activity.
Mining in the Timmins area has been ongoing since the early 1900s.
Some Canadian exploration companies are focusing on the Timmins area instead of South America and Asia.
Established producers in the Timmins area are investing millions of dollars into new exploration.
Lorne Luhta is a geologist for the Ontario Ministry of Northern Development and Mines.
Band-Ore Resources Inc. has gained attention for discovering mineralisation near Timmins.
Bruce Durham is the vice president of Band-Ore Resources Inc.
Other exploration companies have begun operations in the Timmins area following Band-Ore's discovery.
Royal Oak Mines Inc. has found more gold in its Timmins and Matachewan holdings.
Echo Bay Mines Ltd. is considering an open pit mine at Night Hawk Lake.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd is based in Calgary, Canada.
Bre-X could face a lawsuit over the ownership of the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
PT Krueng Gasui is one of Bre-X's Indonesian partners.
PT Krueng Gasui has threatened Bre-X and 19 others with legal action in Canadian courts, claiming damages of US$1.9 billion.
Bre-X's chief executive is David Walsh.
Krueng Gasui owns 10 percent of one section of the Busang discovery.
Krueng Gasui claims to own up to 40 percent of the entire Busang deposit.
Bre-X states that Krueng Gasui does not have the documentation to support its claims.
Bre-X received a letter from Krueng Gasui demanding a meeting before November 22 to resolve the dispute.
If Bre-X does not attempt to settle the argument, Krueng Gasui will sue.

Barrick Gold Corp. is negotiating with Bre-X Minerals Ltd. to gain control of the Busang gold discovery in Indonesia.
Acquiring a stake in Busang would help Barrick Gold Corp. become the world's biggest gold producer.
Barrick Gold Corp. is currently ranked third among gold producers.
Barrick Gold Corp. acquired Arequipa Resources Ltd. for about $800 million last summer.
Bre-X discovered the Busang gold deposit in 1994.
Official estimates indicate that Busang contains 47 million ounces of gold, with potential estimates rising to 100 million ounces.
Bre-X plans to keep 25 percent of its stake in Busang, while Barrick Gold Corp. would receive 75 percent.
The Indonesian government has requested that a 10 percent participation be given to them in the deal.
The Indonesian government wants Barrick and Bre-X to finalize a deal by December 4.
Development of Busang has been delayed due to disputes between Bre-X and its Indonesian partners.

Consolidated Eurocan Ventures Ltd is a small Canadian mining exploration company.
Eurocan is set to gain control of the Tenke Fungurume copper-cobalt deposit in Zaire.
The Zaire government has agreed to a deal with Eurocan, which is based in Vancouver.
Adolf Lundin, a financier based in Geneva, is backing Eurocan.
Gecamines, Zaire's state-owned mining company, will receive a 45 percent stake in the Tenke Fungurume deposit.
Eurocan will hold a 55 percent stake in the Tenke Fungurume deposit.
Eurocan expects to acquire the property for US$250 million and a commitment to develop it.
Andrew Milligan, president of Cornucopia Resources Ltd, stated that the deal is satisfactory for Eurocan.
Cornucopia Resources Ltd had previously formed a consortium to pursue the Tenke Fungurume project.
Ken MacLeod, president of International Panorama Resource Corp, commented on the deal indicating some stability in Zaire's business environment.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. and Barrick Gold Corp. are negotiating a deal regarding Indonesia's Busang gold deposit.
As of Wednesday, no final deal had been reached between Bre-X and Barrick.
Barrick spokesman Vince Borg stated that several points remain outstanding in the negotiations.
The Indonesian government directed Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick by December 4.
Under the proposed joint venture, Barrick would receive 75 percent of Bre-X's stake in the gold discovery, while Bre-X would retain 25 percent.
The companies were invited to consider giving the Indonesian government 10 percent of the gold find.
Bre-X announced that no new deadline had been set by the Indonesian Mines Ministry.
Sources indicated that Indonesian mining officials had left Jakarta and would return on December 9.
Umar Said, secretary-general of the Mines Department, stated that the Indonesian government would explore other options if a deal is not reached.
Bre-X's stock rose by C$1.30 to close at C$20.10, while Barrick's stock increased by C$1.45 to C$39.30.

North America's major gold companies are competing to become the world's biggest gold producer.
Hugh Leggatt is a spokesman for Vancouver-based gold firm Placer Dome Inc.
Placer Dome has made a $600 million bid for Highlands Gold Ltd. and the 25 percent of Placer Pacific Ltd. it does not already own.
Placer Dome plans to raise $300 million through a preferred share issue and sell off some small Canadian mine properties.
Placer Dome is interested in Bre-X Minerals Ltd., which discovered the Busang deposit in Indonesia.
Barrick Gold Corp. is based in Toronto and is currently the world's most profitable gold company.
Barrick Gold Corp. aims to surpass Anglo American Corp. and Gold Fields to become the world's largest gold company.
Jakarta has requested Barrick and Placer Dome to form a joint venture to develop the Busang deposit.
Newmont Mining Corp. was interested in Bre-X but shifted focus to Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp.
Homestake Mining Co. has made a $2.3 billion competing bid for Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd's status regarding the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia is unclear.
Bre-X issued three news releases on Thursday about its rights to the Busang deposit.
The Busang gold deposit is valued at at least $21 billion at current gold prices.
Bre-X stated that its exploration permits and applications for contracts of work on Busang are in good standing.
Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh claimed significant progress is being made toward the development of the Busang deposit.
Bre-X officials met with Umar Said, Indonesia's secretary general of the Ministry of Mines, to discuss their status with Busang.
Umar Said apologized for comments regarding the cancellation of permits and contract applications for Busang.
Indonesian mining officials informed Reuters that they stopped processing Bre-X's applications for contracts of work.
Bre-X and Barrick Gold Corp. must submit new applications for the permits jointly.
The Indonesian government previously encouraged Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick, with Barrick receiving 75 percent and Bre-X 25 percent.

Inco Ltd is the world's biggest nickel company.
Inco Ltd is exploring gold, copper, and zinc in Indonesia, Africa, Canada's Far North, Turkey, and Brazil.
Bob Horn is the vice-president of exploration at Inco.
Inco's target exploration area is Indonesia.
Inco sold TVX Gold Inc at a substantial profit.
The sale of TVX Gold Inc was not a strategic move to exit gold, but to exit that particular company.
Inco has budgeted US$24.8 million for field exploration in 1997.
Inco has formed alliances that could provide an additional US$15 million for exploration.
Inco produced 240 million pounds of copper, 3.775 million pounds of cobalt, 60,000 troy ounces of gold, and 403 million pounds of nickel in 1995.
Inco did not produce any zinc in 1995.

Falling gold prices have drained much of the life from the Toronto Stock Exchange's key gold index.
Analysts believe the decline in gold prices may continue.
Mike Jalonen, a gold analyst at brokerage Midland Walwyn in Toronto, stated that gold stocks are reflecting a $380 gold price.
Vahid Fathi, a mining analyst at Everen Securities in Chicago, suggested that people are writing the obituary for the Toronto gold index.
The Comex February gold price decreased from $370.90 to $355.70 an ounce since December 30.
Gold was priced at $356.60 in London on Thursday.
Gold prices have reached three-year lows due to a strong U.S. dollar, booming financial markets, low inflation, rising mine production, and rumors of central bank selling.
Most analysts predict further declines in gold prices, but there is no consensus on the extent or timing of recovery.
The gold index in Toronto has dropped more than nine percent since December 30.
Barrick Gold Corp. closed at C$35.55 on Wednesday, down from C$39.50 on December 30.

Czech consumer prices rose 0.3 percent in September.
Analysts expected a 0.6 percent rise in Czech consumer prices for September.
Year-on-year inflation in the Czech Republic stood at 8.9 percent in September.
Year-on-year inflation decreased from 9.6 percent in August.
The monthly rise in August was 0.2 percent.
The 12-month average inflation was 8.7 percent in September.
The Czech government raised its average inflation rate target for the year from eight percent to 8.3 percent.
A 19 percent drop in potato prices contributed to the overall result in the food, tobacco, and beverages sector.
Martin Kupka of Patria Finance stated that one month's result does not significantly affect the average inflation rate.
Radek Maly of Citibank expressed satisfaction with the September figures, expecting a monthly increase of 0.5 percent.

The Czech National Bank (CNB) announced conditions for a government scheme to buy smaller banks' doubtful debts.
The scheme aims to restore confidence in the country's banks.
The scheme is open to 13 small, private banks.
Participants must follow strict conditions and allow the CNB to make management changes.
The programme was approved by the cabinet on Wednesday.
The programme is not aimed at resolving issues at any one bank.
CNB Governor Josef Tosovsky stated that the programme is preventative and aims to strengthen confidence in the banking sector.
The decision to implement the programme followed the failure of Keditni Banka in August.
The plan is open to small private banks with total paid-in capital of 12.5 billion crowns and total assets not exceeding 30 billion crowns.
Konsolidacni Banka will buy the banks' doubtful assets at a nominal price.

Komercni Banka a.s. reported a 10 percent decrease in nine-month results.
The decline in net profit was attributed to accounting changes.
The bank's net profit under international accounting standards was 4.88 billion crowns, down from 5.44 billion crowns.
Komercni shares increased in value on the Prague Stock Exchange following the announcement.
Kamil Ziegler, the bank's finance division director, stated that the methodology was revised to exclude unpaid late fees and commissions.
The amount of unpaid late fees subtracted from accounting was 1.2 billion crowns.
Komercni's total assets rose to 432.04 billion crowns at the end of the third quarter, up from 336.21 billion crowns year-on-year.
The net interest margin decreased to 4.07 percent from 5.40 percent, but increased from 3.93 percent at the end of the first half.
Under Czech accounting standards, Komercni's gross profit for the period was 3.87 billion crowns, down from 6.83 billion crowns year-on-year.
Sandy Winthrop Chen from CS First Boston stated that the results were in line with expectations and indicated a strong performance.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced a state commission to address bureaucracy.
The commission is named the 'Commission for the Removal of Bureaucratic Burden'.
The commission will have a steering committee, a chairman, two vice-chairmen, two sections, six sub-commissions, and more members than Klaus's cabinet.
Klaus stated that the only bureaucrat working at the commission would be a secretary.
The commission's staff will number around 20 and will work part time.
Klaus's cabinet has 16 members.
The Czech bureaucracy has historical roots in the Austro-Hungarian empire and was further developed under communism.
Applications for documents such as company registrations, licenses, and work permits can take weeks or months to process.
Citizens often have to queue for hours to be attended to by bureaucrats.
Knocking on office doors for attention is prohibited.

Czech National Bank (CNB) Governor Josef Tosovsky stated that there is no need to hurry the privatisation of shares in Komercni Banka a.s.
Tosovsky mentioned that when the time comes to sell the state's approximately 49 percent stake in Komercni, it could be divided for sale to several investors.
Tosovsky indicated that a strategic partner is not necessary for the privatisation of Komercni.
The CNB does not currently have a strong consensus on how to proceed with Komercni's shares.
Tosovsky noted that it is possible to sell the shares to both domestic and foreign investors.
The CNB has submitted a broad plan to privatise shares in the 'Big Four' banks, which includes a merger of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. with Ceska Sporitlena a.s.
Tosovsky expressed a preference to wait several years before privatising state shares after the merger to analyze its effects.
Tosovsky stated that if the merger proposal is accepted, privatisation would be delayed until the merger is completed.
The Czech cabinet must approve any privatisation of shares in the Big Four banks.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus requested details from the CNB regarding a quick sale of the state's 31.5 percent of Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated that there is no reason to hurry the privatisation of the country's four largest banks.
Klaus mentioned that the privatisation does not have an exceptional level of urgency.
The cabinet will wait for the central bank to submit a more complete plan for the privatisation of the remaining state shares in the large banks.
Klaus indicated that the timing of the privatisation is not significant, whether it occurs two or three weeks later or sooner.
The central bank and the finance ministry have called for the rapid privatisation of the state's one-third stake in Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s.
Japan-based investment bank Nomura and Dutch ING Bank NV have shown strong interest in the IPB stake.
The Czech National Bank has called for the merger of Ceska Sporitelna a.s. with Ceskovslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s.
If the merger occurs, the plan is to privatise the new megabank several years later.
Klaus has expressed opposition to the merger plan, comparing it to merging Prague's two top soccer clubs.
Klaus reacted unfavorably to questions from foreign news agencies regarding the timing of IPB's privatisation.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) received 36.47 percent of the vote in the Senate elections.
The opposition Social Democrats received 20.27 percent of the vote in the Senate elections.
Voter turnout in the Senate elections was 35 percent.
The ODS's performance in the Senate elections was an improvement from their 29.6 percent in the lower house elections in June.
The lower house elections in June had a voter turnout of 76.4 percent.
Only three ODS candidates won outright in the first round of the Senate elections.
Seventy-six ODS candidates will face a run-off on November 22-23.
The Senate elections use a first-past-the-post system, unlike the lower house's proportional representation system.
The Central Election Commission reported a turnout of 35.03 percent in the Senate elections.
Zeman, a leader of the Social Democrats, expressed hope for higher participation in the second round of the Senate elections.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced that the government approved a plan to privatise part of the state's 31.5 percent stake in commercial bank IPB a.s.
Klaus tasked Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik with setting conditions for a tender to sell the stake in IPB.
No decision has been made regarding a central bank proposal to merge banks CSOB a.s. and Ceska Sporitelna a.s.
The government is committed to privatising its holdings in the country's four biggest banks.
Klaus stated that Kocarnik would submit criteria for selecting a strategic foreign partner to the cabinet with the help of a consultancy firm.
Representatives from the National Property Fund and the central bank will be involved in developing the tender.
Klaus did not specify how much of the government's stake in IPB would be sold to a strategic foreign partner.
Japan's Nomura and Dutch banks ING and ABN AMRO have shown interest in the IPB stake.
The central bank proposed a merger of CSOB, where the Czech government holds 66 percent, and Ceska Sporitelna, where it holds 45 percent.
Klaus expressed a cool reaction to the merger proposal and stated that no fundamental judgments on mergers were made.

The Czech Republic could have a sugar surplus of 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes from this year's campaign.
High local production costs and a world sugar surplus will limit sugar exports from the Czech Republic.
The Agriculture Ministry plans to buy some surplus sugar for strategic reserves.
The Agriculture Ministry will prepare indirect support for exporters but will not provide direct export subsidies.
Producers in the Czech Republic are expected to sell as much sugar as possible domestically due to lower world prices.
Eva Divisova of the Agriculture Ministry stated that the expected surplus will be up to 80,000 to 100,000 tonnes.
Total sugar production in the Czech Republic is projected to be between 520,000 and 540,000 tonnes raw value.
Net sugar exports from the Czech Republic are expected to be about 4,000 tonnes.
Divisova did not disclose how much sugar the state would buy for reserves, citing it as confidential.
Slovakia is not importing sugar from the Czech Republic due to higher output.

The Czech Agriculture Ministry halted a shipment of U.S. maize pending further study on its effects.
No maize from the shipment will be distributed in the Czech Republic until the study is finished.
Frantisek Havir of the ministry's agriculture production section stated that the Institute for Agricultural Production would conduct the study as soon as possible.
The state Veterinary Administration is halting the shipment of maize until it is decided whether the genetically-manipulated genes can pass into the food chain.
Protestors in Hamburg disrupted the loading of the shipment by chaining themselves to the trains bound for the Czech Republic.
There are no laws in the Czech Republic regulating how genetically manipulated products should be treated.
The exact location of the 33,000 tonne shipment was unknown.
The Czech chapter of Greenpeace continued the protest with five demonstrators dressing up as laboratory rabbits.
Vaclav Masku of Greenpeace stated that there is no legislation in the Czech Republic regulating genetically-modified materials.
It is illegal to market genetically modified maize in the EU, but Greenpeace claims cargoes may have already reached Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, and Portugal.

A reporter called the secretary of the new director at a major Czech industrial company.
The secretary stated that Mr. Novak's first name is Doctor.
Czechs place significant importance on academic titles.
Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda resigned after admitting to using the title 'Doctor of Law' which he did not attain.
Jiri Pehe is the head of research at Prague's Open Media Research Institute.
Colleagues in many Czech offices often address each other using titles such as 'Mr Engineer' or 'Mr Doctor'.
Jan Kalvoda completed law school but did not finish the certification process to become a Doctor of Law.
Kalvoda's colleagues and party used the title 'Doctor' in literature without his refutation.
Four other deputies in the lower house of parliament also used unauthorized titles and confessed.
Only one of the four deputies resigned from parliament, while three others refused to resign.

The Czech government delayed payments and forced early collections to claim a budget surplus in 1996.
Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik stated that it is unclear if 1996 budget measures will require spending cuts in 1997.
The 1996 budget showed a surplus of 419 million crowns on revenues of 482.797 billion crowns and expenditures of 482.378 billion crowns.
The surplus in 1996 was unexpected after the government projected a deficit of around one billion crowns in December.
The government took 650 million crowns in early repayment from the Deposit Insurance Fund and froze one billion crowns in infrastructure investment.
Kocarnik mentioned that ministries were asked to save as much as possible in December.
Banks Ceska Sporitelna a.s. and IPB a.s. agreed to delay their receipt of 800 million crowns in state support for housing loans.
Kocarnik indicated that the final 1996 budget result might still show a deficit due to pending bills until January 15.
The 1995 budget surplus was revised to 7.2 billion crowns from an originally reported 8.6 billion crowns.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus praised the 1996 budget figures as a sign of fiscal responsibility.

Bidders for a stake in Aero Vodochody a.s. must offer at least 950 million Czech crowns ($35 million) for the shares.
The tender for Aero Vodochody a.s. is open to domestic and foreign bidders seeking to revitalize the company.
Between 34 and 40 percent of Aero will be sold, depending on the issuance of new shares during the deal.
A steering committee will evaluate bids based on bidders' economic strength, obligations to other shareholders, and their strategic position.
The tender is expected to open by the end of the month.
Chemapol Group a.s., CIMEX Holding a.s., and Boeing Co in alliance with Ceske Aerolinie a.s. have shown interest in Aero.
Aero shareholders controlled by the state will pass their shareholders' rights to the new investor to allow management from a majority position.
The winner of the tender will be selected by the cabinet and should be known in April.
Strategic considerations may lead the steering committee to prefer a Czech domestic partner for Aero.
Shareholders of Aero approved a cut in the company's basic capital to one million crowns from 962 million as part of a financial restructuring plan.

Liu Xiaobo has been ordered to serve three years in a labour camp.
The sentence was imposed shortly after Liu Xiaobo was detained by police.
Wang Xizhe, a pro-democracy activist, is reported missing from his home in Guangzhou.
Police informed Liu Xiaobo's wife of the administrative sentence without providing a reason.
Liu Xia expressed anger over the lack of formal contact and justification for the punishment.
Liu Xiaobo was taken from his home by police with a search warrant, who also confiscated personal items.
The administrative punishment does not require a court trial and is under the authority of the public security bureau.
The use of re-education through labour against dissidents has increased in recent months.
Liu Xiaobo is a renowned literary critic known for his activism during the 1989 pro-democracy movement.
On September 30, Liu Xiaobo and Wang Xizhe issued a statement calling for freedom of the press and political rights in China.

China's pro-democracy activists have largely disappeared due to imprisonment, labor camps, and exile.
Liu Xiaobo was sentenced to three years in a labor camp.
Wang Xizhe, a veteran democracy activist, has disappeared.
Wei Jingsheng is a Nobel Peace Prize nominee and a veteran democracy activist.
Wei Jingsheng is regarded as the father of China's democracy movement.
Wei Jingsheng is currently serving a 14-year jail term.
Wei's family does not consider him a serious contender for the Nobel Peace Prize.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang stated that Wei Jingsheng is a criminal who has broken Chinese law.
Wei Jingsheng was jailed for 15 years for his involvement in the 1979 Democracy Wall movement.
Wei Jingsheng was released on parole in September 1993 after serving 14 and a half years.

Wang Dan is a detained Chinese dissident facing capital charges for plotting to subvert the government.
Evidence against Wang Dan includes writings critical of the state and accepting funds from abroad.
Wang Dan's trial is expected to begin next week, according to the New York-based Human Rights in China.
Wang Dan's family found a lawyer willing to defend him.
Wang Dan was a leader of the 1989 student demonstrations for democracy in Tiananmen Square.
The Beijing People's Intermediate Court informed Wang's mother that she had one day to find a lawyer for him.
The court chargesheet formally accused Wang Dan of plotting to subvert the government, a crime that carries a maximum penalty of death.
The indictment against Wang cited four major areas of evidence, including articles published in overseas magazines and newspapers.
Wang Dan served four years in prison for counter-revolutionary crimes related to the 1989 demonstrations.
Wang Dan participated in studies organized by the University of California, Berkeley, in the United States.

Winston Lord is the U.S. government's top Asia official.
Winston Lord held talks with Chinese Deputy Foreign Minister Liu Huaqiu in Beijing.
The discussions included a range of issues, including human rights.
Winston Lord arrived in Beijing on an unannounced visit.
A meeting with Foreign Minister Qian Qichen was on Lord's agenda.
Winston Lord was scheduled to leave for Japan on Thursday.
Nicholas Burns is a State Department spokesman.
Winston Lord is preparing for a visit next month by Secretary of State Warren Christopher.
U.S. officials criticized the sentencing of dissident Liu Xiaobo to three years in a labor camp.
There have been frictions between the U.S. and China over the treatment of dissidents.

A Beijing court sentenced Wang Dan to 11 years in prison.
Wang Dan was a student leader during the 1989 demonstrations for democracy.
The trial lasted less than four hours.
Wang Dan was convicted of plotting to overthrow the government.
The conviction marks the imprisonment of one of China's few remaining dissidents.
The sentencing occurred shortly after a visit by German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher is scheduled to visit China in late November.
Western diplomats believe the trial's swiftness and severity reflect a tightening of controls by the Communist Party.
The charges against Wang Dan carried a maximum punishment of death and a minimum of 10 years in prison.
Diplomats noted that the sentence was relatively light given the severity of the charges.

China's economic growth is expected to accelerate in 1997 as Beijing increases economic activity before a Communist Party congress.
Xu Hongyuan of the State Information Centre stated that political factors may contribute to a renewed economic boom in 1997.
Xu warned that higher growth could lead to increased inflation and rising joblessness.
The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1997 could reach 8,178 billion yuan ($985 billion), growing by 10.5 percent compared to an anticipated 9.6-9.7 percent increase in 1996.
GDP grew by 10.2 percent in 1995, and China aims for an average growth of eight percent for the 1996-2000 Ninth Five-Year Plan.
Xu linked the higher growth forecast to the upcoming Communist Party congress, which is expected to address economic inefficiencies in state enterprises.
Diplomats and western economists believe Beijing may attempt to stimulate the economy in 1997 to strengthen the current leadership's position before the party congress.
Xu forecasted retail price inflation to rise to about eight percent in 1997 from an expected seven percent in 1996.
Inflation was 14.8 percent last year, down from a high of 21.7 percent in 1994.
Xu indicated that foreign trade is expected to recover strongly after a slump in early 1996.

Intense haggling among trade ministers has brought a potential deal to free the global information technology market.
The United States and the European Union reported progress during the World Trade Organisation ministerial conference.
Officials indicated that differences on labour standards were narrowing.
WTO officials aim for a final declaration at the end of the ministerial meeting on Friday.
The EU, United States, Canada, and Japan are working towards an Information Technology Agreement.
EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan stated that significant progress was being made.
Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefksy agreed with Brittan's assessment but did not provide further details.
Negotiators are aiming for a quick agreement to encourage Asian trading partners to sign on by the end of the meeting.
Japan's Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda expressed hope for a significant agreement on trade liberalisation.
Malaysia's International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz stated that the goal of free commerce in information technology by the turn of the century was too ambitious.

China announced a major reform of its agricultural system on Wednesday.
The reform includes unifying the price the state pays for grain with the market rate.
Li Tieying, a Politburo member, outlined the reform plans in a speech in Shenzhen.
The reform aims to boost agricultural output next year.
The system of cotton purchasing will also be reformed.
China's central authorities currently buy grain from farmers at set prices below market rates.
A record harvest of 480 million tonnes is forecast for this year.
Analysts believe the time is right to unify the grain pricing system.
Officials expect grain supply to exceed demand in 1997.
Li stated that the state would separate national grain reserves from regional ones.

China has decided to replace the crime of 'counter-revolution' with the offence of jeopardising state security.
The maximum penalty for jeopardising state security remains the death penalty.
The proposal to rename the crime was included in a draft amendment to the Criminal Law submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.
The amendment reduces the scope of the crime from 15 offences to 10.
The amendment will be sent to the annual session of parliament for final ratification in March.
Wang Hanbin, vice-chairman of the Standing Committee, stated that the name change was made in consideration of changed circumstances and the overall interests of the country.
The crime of counter-revolution was established in China after Mao Zedong came to power in 1949.
Counter-revolution has historically been used to imprison individuals whose opinions were disapproved by the state.
Wei Jingsheng is a prominent dissident serving a lengthy jail term for counter-revolutionary crimes.
Wang praised the use of counter-revolutionary crime to safeguard state security but acknowledged that times have changed.

A music student named Ngawang Choephel was sentenced to 18 years in prison for spying in Tibet.
The bomb explosion in Lhasa is perceived as a significant event by observers.
A senior local government leader, Gyamco, indicated that a new campaign of intimidation in Tibet is necessary to address challenges to Beijing's sovereignty.
Gyamco called for a campaign to expose and criticize the Dalai Lama's supporters during a meeting of party officials in Lhasa.
The Dalai Lama is accused by Beijing of inciting anti-Chinese unrest in Tibet.
The Dalai Lama won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989 for his non-violent campaign for Tibetan autonomy.
The Dalai Lama fled China in 1959 after an uprising against Beijing's rule.
Police in Tibet have established new checkpoints and are questioning Tibetan guests and young Tibetan men.
Ngawang Choephel, a former Fulbright scholar, was arrested in 1995 while making a documentary about traditional music and dance in Tibet.
The harsh sentence given to Ngawang Choephel reflects the authorities' determination to suppress unauthorized activities in Tibet.

The largest bomb blast reported in Tibet occurred on Christmas Day outside a city government office in Lhasa.
The blast shattered windows in a radius of 100 meters and was the largest explosion reported in the region.
No casualties were reported from the explosion.
Analysts claim the blast marks a new level of desperation in anti-Chinese sentiment in Tibet.
Robbie Barnett of the Tibet Information Network stated that some individuals may resort to violence due to the perceived ineffectiveness of non-violence.
The region is primarily populated by devout Buddhists who have engaged in anti-Chinese protests, often led by monks and nuns.
Officials believe the Christmas Day blast was politically motivated and linked to followers of the Dalai Lama.
The Dalai Lama, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989, advocates for self-government and freedom of worship in Tibet.
The Dalai Lama has proposed talks with Beijing, but China insists on recognition of its sovereignty before negotiations.
Analysts suggest the bombing provides local authorities with justification for a stricter crackdown in Tibet.

China has placed the China Agribusiness Development Trust and Investment Corp (CADTIC) under administrative custody due to real estate losses.
The People's Bank of China ordered CADTIC to be managed by two state banks in early January.
The China Construction Bank took over CADTIC's domestic business, while the Bank of China took over its overseas business.
CADTIC was the largest investment trust company in China after the China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC).
Bankers stated that CADTIC overextended itself due to serious mismanagement.
CADTIC extended its business beyond its officially sanctioned scope of agriculture and suffered large losses from real estate investments.
The Ministry of Agriculture owns CADTIC.
An investigation into CADTIC's financial situation was initiated by the ministries of Agriculture and Finance a year ago.
Bank officials indicated that there were no current plans to close CADTIC, but a future sale was not ruled out.
China is increasing supervision of financial institutions, with expectations of new rules and more frequent checks.

The Hong Kong government is negotiating new overflight arrangements with several countries before the 1997 handover to China.
Hong Kong has previously operated under Britain's traffic rights umbrella.
The government stated that it must negotiate its own agreements for airlines to continue flying over key air routes.
The countries involved are located on routes from Hong Kong to Europe and Africa and are not signatories to International Air Services Transit Agreements.
The spokesman did not disclose the names of the countries or the most important negotiations.
Overflight fees will be discussed during the negotiations.
Industry observers noted that the government needs to finalize agreements before the handover.
Michael Arnold is Hong Kong's chief negotiator for the overflight agreements.
The Joint Liaison Group must approve any proposed deal.
The model overflight agreement was cleared by the Joint Liaison Group in September.

United Parcel Service of America Inc (UPS) is constructing a US$4 million Asia-Pacific hub in Taiwan.
The first aircraft to use the hub will arrive on September 10.
The first phase of the hub at Taipei's Chiang Kai Shek airport is scheduled to open on October 10.
The hub is expected to be fully operational by March next year.
Six Boeing aircraft, including two 747s, two 757s, and two 767s, will operate eight flights a day from Taipei six days a week starting in March.
UPS has won traffic rights to operate five frequencies a week from Bangkok.
Other cities to be linked to the Taipei hub include Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, and Osaka.
UPS's total investment in Taipei will amount to US$400 million.
Construction of the first phase of the 4,800 square meters sorting office began this month.
The first Taiwan-based aircraft will activate traffic rights awarded to UPS under the recent Japan-U.S. bilateral agreement.

British Airways plans to offer more passenger flights to Hong Kong.
British Airways will not change its current wet lease freighter service to Hong Kong.
Robert Ayling is the chief executive of British Airways.
Ayling stated that British Airways has successfully expanded its cargo business by using freighter capacity from outside the airline.
Ayling believes that Hong Kong is a good market for freight.
Ayling is visiting Hong Kong as part of a tour of key British Airways destinations.
British Airways has maintained a policy for the past ten years not to buy freighters.
British Airways currently offers a three times weekly service between London Gatwick and Hong Kong using a Boeing 747-200 freighter wet leased from Atlas Air Inc.
British Airways operates 14 Boeing 747-400 passenger flights a week to London, which offer belly cargo capacity.
British Airways hopes to increase its flight frequency to twice daily when slots at Heathrow become available.

Hong Kong civil aviation department statistics indicate that total air cargo handled in August increased by 6.7 percent compared to August of the previous year.
Air cargo imports for scheduled and non-scheduled flights in August totaled 59,910.5 tonnes.
Air cargo exports for scheduled and non-scheduled flights in August totaled 71,674.9 tonnes.
The top 15 countries for air cargo in August are listed with figures in tonnes.
Australia unloaded 2,675 tonnes and loaded 2,327 tonnes of air cargo in August.
Canada unloaded 1,836 tonnes and loaded 1,508 tonnes of air cargo in August.
China Mainland unloaded 1,841 tonnes and loaded 2,896 tonnes of air cargo in August.
France unloaded 1,720 tonnes and loaded 2,010 tonnes of air cargo in August.
Germany unloaded 3,365 tonnes and loaded 3,866 tonnes of air cargo in August.
Japan unloaded 5,570 tonnes and loaded 12,197 tonnes of air cargo in August.

Cathay Pacific Airways has successfully handled its first load of pigs destined for breeding in China.
The load consisted of 300 pigs with an estimated value of HK$2.8 million.
The pigs were flown from Taiwan to Hong Kong en route to breeding farms in China.
The pigs were housed in eight pallets within two and three deck boxes equipped with automatic watering.
The pigs have a higher skin temperature than humans and are sensitive to heat.
Taiwanese herdsman Li Siou Tong stated that water is sprinkled on the pigs to keep them cool.
The pigs are valuable breeds including Duroc, Landrace, and Yorkshire.
These pig breeds originated in Sweden, the Netherlands, and the United States.
The pigs are currently in Shenzhen, China, spending 45 days in quarantine.
Paulo Chan, Cathay's cargo standards and performance manager, stated this was the largest number of pigs flown by the airline.

Virgin Group's cargo unit in Hong Kong plans to move air freight to South Africa via a new service to Johannesburg from London.
Brinkley Chan is the Assistant Manager for Dyna Trans (Hong Kong) Limited, which is Virgin Atlantic Cargo's Hong Kong agent.
Chan stated that Virgin is offering a dedicated LD-3 container for cargo bound for South Africa on daily flights from Hong Kong to London.
Virgin's new service to Johannesburg from London began on October 2 and operates three times a week.
Chan described Virgin as a 'second class carrier' but believes the service can succeed.
Virgin will start a new shorter route to London from Hong Kong on October 27, allowing an extra six tonnes of freight to be carried westbound.
Direct services to South Africa from Hong Kong are provided by Cathay Pacific and South African Airways.
Indirect competition on the route includes Singapore International Airlines, Brazil's Varig, Gulf Air, and Emirates Airline.
Main exports from Hong Kong to South Africa will include electronics, clothing, and general freight.

Cathay Pacific Airways will add a fourth daily flight between Hong Kong and the Philippines.
The decision to add the flight is due to increasing demand.
A company spokeswoman informed Reuters about the new flight.
The increase in flights follows the conclusion of six years of negotiations between the Hong Kong government and the Philippines over a new Air Services Agreement.
The Confidential Memorandum of Understanding did not specify the number of additional flights or the increase in seat and cargo capacity.
Industry sources estimate the increase in capacity to be around 15 percent.
The Hong Kong government described the route as one of the busiest and fastest growing in Asia.
The new Airbus A340 flight will depart Hong Kong at 7:50 AM local time and return at 10:50 AM local time starting October 27.
Cathay Pacific's spokeswoman stated that the extra flight provides convenient connections to flights from Hong Kong to the USA and Canada.
Philippine Airlines currently operates four flights per day from Hong Kong.

Korean Air Ltd (KAL) reported an 8.4 percent rise in cargo weight on domestic and international flights in July compared to July of the previous year.
Korean Air Ltd (KAL) reported a 6.3 percent increase in cargo weight on domestic and international flights in August compared to August of the previous year.
Korean Air Ltd (KAL) reported a 2.6 percent drop in July's cargo load factor.
Korean Air Ltd (KAL) reported a 2.4 percent fall in cargo load factor during August.
In July, the international cargo weight was 560 tons, with a 9.4 percent change compared to the previous year.
In August, the international cargo weight was 547 tons, with a 13.4 percent change compared to the previous year.
In July, the domestic cargo weight was 16 tons, with a 28.1 percent change compared to the previous year.
In August, the domestic cargo weight was 16 tons, with a 25.1 percent change compared to the previous year.
In July, the total cargo weight was 576 tons, with a 9.8 percent change compared to the previous year.
In August, the total cargo weight was 563 tons, with a 13.7 percent change compared to the previous year.

Major airlines operating cargo flights to Europe will raise their ex-Hong Kong cargo rates by HK80 cents per kg from November 4.
The increase is intended to offset rising jet fuel prices.
Stanley Hui is the chief operating officer of AHK Air Hong Kong Ltd.
An emergency meeting of airlines was held in Hong Kong to discuss a fuel surcharge.
Airlines represented at the meeting included Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, Lufthansa Cargo, Air France, Martinair, and Cargolux.
British Airways World Plc was not represented at the meeting.
Philippe Bour is the regional cargo manager for Air France in Hong Kong.
Air France and Lufthansa Cargo will apply the rate increase from November 4.
Cargolux, Air Hong Kong, and other carriers will implement the increase a few days later.
Japan Airlines Co Limited reported a 60.7 percent slump in profits in the six months to September due to higher fuel costs.

Airbus Industrie is marketing cargo space aboard the Airbus A300-600 Super Transporter in Asia.
David Velupillai is the press relations manager for Airbus in China.
The Airbus A300-600 Super Transporter fleet has 800 hours a year available for wet lease.
The aircraft is known as the Beluga due to its large size and distinctive design.
The Beluga has a 7.4 metre high door and can carry more voluminous freight than any other aircraft.
Two of the four planned Beluga aircraft are used to transport large sections of fuselage and wings for Airbus.
Fuselage sections weighing up to 45 tons and 30 metres long are transported from Spain and Germany.
Airbus aims to profit from wet leases of outsize cargoes such as helicopters, aircraft engines, and space satellites.
The Beluga has been used to carry a satellite module to Toulouse from Turin, Italy.
The Beluga made its air show debut at Paris last year but is not being exhibited in China.

Polar Air Cargo will take delivery of its first Boeing 747-200F series aircraft at Hong Kong's Kai Tak airport on December 13.
The aircraft is fresh from a 'C' check at Hong Kong Aircraft Engineering Company.
The number of Boeing 747s in the Polar fleet will increase to 14 with this delivery.
Ned Wallace is the chief executive officer of Polar Air Cargo.
Polar's fleet is expected to increase by two to three 747s each year over the next five years.
The next 747-200F is scheduled for delivery in the first quarter of 1997.
Polar Air Cargo is recognized as a low-cost airline using first generation former passenger 747 aircraft converted for cargo.
Polar anticipates a significant increase in its Asian operations if the U.S. Department of Transportation finalizes a decision awarding it the new U.S.-Japan all-cargo route.
The Department of Transportation's favorable evaluation of Polar was partly due to its proposal to use Anchorage, Alaska as a hub for trans-loading traffic.
The final award of the Japan route will conclude a three-year strategy by Polar to create a global network of operations.

Landing fees at Hong Kong's Chek Lap Kok airport must be competitively priced compared to other regional airports, according to Peter Sutch, chairman of Cathay Pacific Airways Limited.
Reports indicate that fees at Chek Lap Kok airport may be double those at Kai Tak airport, raising concerns among airlines and groups like the Orient Airlines Association.
Cathay Pacific Airways Limited is particularly concerned about the new airport fees, as they will significantly impact long-term profitability.
The International Air Transport Association (IATA) Users' Group is monitoring the situation regarding the new airport fees.
Peter Sutch stated that competitive airport pricing is important for the airline industry and the economy of Hong Kong.
A spokesman for the Airport Authority, which manages Chek Lap Kok, mentioned that the consultation process for the fee structure is ongoing and will be revealed in the first or second quarter of next year.
Peter Sutch indicated that Cathay Pacific is considering raising passenger ticket prices and air cargo rates due to increased fuel costs.
IATA member airlines agreed on a three percent increase in air fares to address higher fuel bills.

Korean Air Lines Ltd's cargo load factor dropped 3.2 percent in the six months to end-June 2023 compared to the same period in 1995.
The cumulative cargo tonnage carried to end-June 2023 was 448,000 tonnes, an increase of 8.2 percent over last year's 414,000 tonnes.
International cargo in June 2023 increased by 11.1 percent to 60,000 tons, bringing the cumulative total to 335,000 tonnes, an 8.1 percent rise.
Domestic cargo in June 2023 reached 16,000 tonnes, a 6.7 percent increase from June last year.
The total cargo tonnage for June 2023 was 76,000 tonnes, which is 10.1 percent higher than in 1995.
The load factor for international cargo in June 2023 was 77.7 percent, down 0.1 percent from last year.
The domestic cargo load factor fell 1.8 percent to 38.7 percent compared to last year.
The cumulative totals for cargo load factors are down 0.1 percent compared to last June and 3.2 percent down for the year so far.
The international cargo flight tonnage kilometres (FTK) for June 2023 increased 16.4 percent to 407 million from 350 million last year.
The June FTK domestic total increased by 10.3 percent from 5 million to 6 million.

ASDA Plc is one of Britain's top four supermarket chains with approximately 13.1 percent of the market.
Tesco leads the market with 22.7 percent, followed by J. Sainsbury's with 19.3 percent.
Allan Leighton is the new chief executive of ASDA, having taken over on August 27.
Leighton succeeded Archie Norman, who became chairman and is pursuing a political career with the Conservative Party.
Norman is credited with improving ASDA's image and financial situation over the past five years.
Leighton aims to make ASDA the best supermarket rather than the biggest.
Leighton wants to increase the George clothing range to approximately 10 percent of total sales, targeting a £600 million annual business.
Clothing margins for ASDA are about twice those of groceries.
George Davies heads the George clothing brand, which is exclusive to ASDA.
Leighton believes that continuity in management is important but acknowledges the need for changes.

Shares in media group Pearson closed higher on Monday.
Pearson shares closed 34-1/2p higher at 731p.
Pearson shares touched a high for the year of 745p.
6.7 million shares of Pearson changed hands on Monday.
A sector analyst stated that the price was boosted by management changes and revived bid speculation.
BSkyB was reported to be planning a bid worth more than four billion pounds in cooperation with a U.S.-based media group.
BSkyB's chief executive, Sam Chisholm, denied any talks about a bid for Pearson.
A BSkyB spokesman confirmed that there were no talks taking place regarding a bid for Pearson.
Pearson owns the Financial Times, Penguin Books, and several television production companies.
Analysts believe any move on Pearson is likely to occur before new management takes control next year.

Cable & Wireless has merged with its own Mercury telecoms business and the British operations of NYNEX, Bell Canada International, and Videotron to create Cable & Wireless Communications.
The merger created a company valued at $7.5 billion.
Cable & Wireless Communications reaches almost 2.5 million homes for cable television.
Oftel banned a promotion by BT that involved discounts on subscriptions to BSkyB, citing discrimination.
BT shares fell by 7 pence to close at 346 pence following the Oftel decision.
BSkyB shares fell by 40 pence to close at 637 pence, a low for the day.
C&W shares rose by 4 pence to close at 470 pence.
Analysts believe that the stronger Cable & Wireless is perceived, the less pressure Oftel will place on BT.
BT expressed confusion over Oftel's decision and claimed the promotion was open to all BT users.
The Conservative government plans to review BT's ban from cable television in 2001.

J. Sainsbury Plc announced plans to launch a jointly owned banking service with Bank of Scotland.
This will be the first supermarket banking service in Britain's food retailing business.
Sainsbury has applied to the Bank of England for authorization for a new bank.
The new bank will be owned 55 percent by Sainsbury and 45 percent by Bank of Scotland.
The venture will be called Sainsbury's Bank and will offer telebanking services.
Sainsbury's Bank will target an audience of 12 million customers.
The bank will launch next year with Classic and Gold Visa cards and account services.
Sainsbury posted lower profits for the first time in 22 years last year.
Sainsbury launched its Reward loyalty card in June after Tesco Plc introduced its ClubCard.
Analysts warned that Sainsbury's Bank must offer attractive deals to secure customers.

The government blocked proposed bids for South West Water on Friday.
Analysts believe this decision makes mergers between water firms taboo.
The decision may encourage the creation of more multi-utilities.
Ian Lang, head of the Department of Trade and Industry, stated that the bids were against the public interest.
Ian Byatt, head of Ofwat, expressed that such mergers are not the best way to achieve efficiency for customers.
Wessex Water announced its intention to bid for South West Water on March 7.
Severn Trent entered the bidding process on March 21.
Analysts estimated that the bids could value South West Water at over 950 million pounds or around 750 pence per share.
The DTI's decision surprised the market, which anticipated conditional approval based on price cuts.
South West Water's shares fell to a low of 565 pence before recovering slightly.

CE Electric made a $1.225 billion bid for British regional electricity company Northern Electric.
Analysts noted that CE Electric's bid may indicate renewed interest in the remaining independent regional electricity companies.
CE Electric aims to acquire Northern Electric's expertise in supply to enhance its generation capabilities.
Northern Electric rejected CE Electric's bid, marking the second unwanted offer it has received in two years.
David Morris, chairman of Northern Electric, indicated that the company might consider a higher price.
CE Electric proposed negotiations at about 700 pence per share, while the initial offer was 630 pence.
CE Electric denied suggesting a price of 700 pence per share.
Northern Electric previously used a £560 million package of benefits to shareholders to fend off a hostile bid from Trafalgar House.
Analysts stated that Northern Electric lacks a cash pile, making it less attractive for acquisition based on cash reserves.
Potential other U.S. buyers for CE Electric include Houston Industries, Duke Power, Florida Power and Light, and Pacific Gas and Electric.

Britain's Northern Electric plans to release its half-year results earlier than scheduled.
Northern Electric rejected a hostile bid from CE Electric on Monday.
CE Electric's bid was for 630 pence per share.
Industry sources expect Northern Electric's results to be released next week.
Northern Electric previously fended off a bid from Trafalgar House with a 560 million pound package for shareholders.
David Campbell of Greig Middleton stated that the interim results could show a stronger balance sheet than expected.
CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy, indicated a price of 700 pence per share, which was denied by CE Electric.
CE Electric's bid was valued at $1.225 billion.
CE Electric has acquired approximately 13 percent of Northern Electric's shares since the bid.
Northern Electric's share price was trading at 631.5 pence on Friday, down two pence.

Dominion Resources, based in the U.S., agreed to a takeover of East Midlands Electricity for 1.3 billion pounds ($2.15 billion).
East Midlands Electricity is one of five remaining British independent regional electricity companies.
There are doubts about the deal passing UK competition authorities due to political pressures ahead of the May 1997 general election.
Executives from both Dominion and East Midlands stated they saw no reason for a referral to the UK's Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).
East Midlands shares closed at 623 pence, up 12 pence, amid concerns that trade secretary Ian Lang might halt the deal.
Seven of the twelve cash-rich regional electricity companies have been acquired since the expiry of a protective golden share last March.
Only two bids have been blocked by trade secretary Ian Lang this year.
Dominion Resources met with East Midlands management to discuss the takeover price.
East Midlands rejected an earlier bid from Dominion, stating it undervalued the company.
East Midlands chairman Sir Nigel Rudd stated that the current offer represents fair value for the business.

South West Water reported pretax profits of 72.9 million pounds for the six months ending September 30.
The company's profits increased by 35 percent compared to the previous year.
South West Water plans to raise its total dividend by 20 percent this year.
The company has committed to a dividend payout of 11.8 pence.
South West Water's finance director Ken Hill stated that a 35 percent increase in profit before tax is unlikely to occur at the end of this year.
The company closed its shares at 580 pence after reaching a high of 589 pence.
South West Water has announced a rebate of 15 pounds to customers following the blocking of takeover bids.
The company previously made a rebate of 10 pounds to customers.
South West Water announced an additional investment of 74 million pounds for environmental upgrades.
The company aims to focus on its core business and develop its non-regulated businesses.

Northern Electric announced it will release results by the end of November to demonstrate that CE Electric's $1.225 billion bid is inadequate.
Northern Electric's half-year figures, previously scheduled for December 5, will include important financial information about the company's value.
Northern Electric believes that CE Electric's offer of 630 pence per share is too low.
Northern Electric stated that CE Electric suggested a price of 700 pence per share prior to its hostile offer, a claim that CE Electric has denied.
CE Electric has acquired nearly 30 percent of Northern Electric's shares.
Northern Electric's shares increased by one penny to 610 pence by 1310 GMT.
Northern Electric plans to pay a 56.5 pence special dividend in February 1997 if CE Electric's offer lapses.
Northern Electric claims that uncertainty regarding the potential referral of CE Electric's bid to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission is affecting market reactions.
The government has approved takeovers of seven out of twelve regional electricity companies in under two years, with three being acquired by U.S. companies.
Northern Electric successfully fended off a hostile bid from Trafalgar House last year.

Entergy Corp called off talks with British regional electricity company London Electric.
Entergy stated it is still monitoring the electricity sector.
Entergy had exploratory discussions regarding a 1.2 billion pound takeover of London Electric.
Shares in London Electric initially surged on bid reports but later fell to a low of 630 pence before recovering to 661-1/2 pence.
Analyst Nigel Hawkins noted that Entergy's talks with London Electric have ended but did not rule out a hostile bid.
Northern Electric is facing a $1.225 billion bid from CalEnergy.
East Midlands has accepted a $2.15 billion offer from Dominion Resources.
Seven of the original 12 regional electricity companies have been sold, with three sold to U.S. companies.
Entergy denied interest in bidding for Yorkshire Electricity.
Southern Electric avoided a takeover by National Power when the government blocked the bid.

Welsh multi-utility Hyder's shares rose after a 25 percent increase in half-year profits.
Hyder reported pretax profits of 100.7 million pounds for the six months ending September 30.
This is an increase from 80.6 million pounds a year ago.
Hyder paid an interim dividend of 14.6 pence per share, up from 12.6 pence.
The results were in line with forecasts.
Hyder's shares increased by 13-1/2 pence to 755-1/2 pence by 1127 GMT.
Hyder stated that the electricity business Swalec should enhance earnings on a full-year basis.
Efficiency savings from merged services were reported to be ahead of target.
Hyder managing director Graham Hawker indicated that Swalec's savings were ahead of pre-bid targets.
Hyder expects the merger to cut operating costs by 46 million pounds in 2000.

Eurotunnel announced a deal giving its creditor banks 45.5 percent of the company in exchange for eliminating one billion pounds of its debt.
The restructuring ends months of negotiations between Eurotunnel and 225 banks to which it owes nearly nine billion pounds.
Shareholders will own 54.5 percent of the company after the deal.
Eurotunnel co-chairman Alastair Morton stated that the restructuring plan provides medium-term financial stability for the company.
Eurotunnel is currently making a profit before interest.
The company has taken around half of the cross-Channel market from European ferry companies.
Eurotunnel indicated that a strong operating performance could allow it to pay its first dividend within the next 10 years.
French co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle described the debt restructuring plan as 'an acceptable compromise' for shareholders.
The company plans to finalize and agree on the details of the restructuring plan before submitting it for approval in early 1997.
The debt-for-equity swap will be at 130 pence per share, reducing outstanding debt by one billion pounds.

Banking analysts expressed positive views on Bank of Scotland's joint venture with J Sainsbury.
One analyst upgraded his recommendation for Bank of Scotland.
Goldman Sachs and BZW maintained positive stances on Bank of Scotland.
SBC Warburg upgraded its recommendation on Bank of Scotland's stock to 'trading buy' from 'hold'.
Bank of Scotland's partnership with Sainsbury is expected to enhance its presence in the British market.
The joint venture aims to expand Bank of Scotland's retail customer base in England.
Bank of Scotland's operational efficiency may allow Sainsbury's Bank to offer better rates than Tesco's current offerings.
Analysts believe existing banks will not lose many accounts to Sainsbury's Bank.
Many consumers have multiple bank accounts, which may reduce the likelihood of switching to Sainsbury's Bank.
British banks like Barclays and Lloyds are focused on selling more products to their existing customers.

Ron Baker, a former Barings executive, rejects a lawsuit filed by Dutch bank ING Barings.
ING Barings claims that Baker owes repayment of a 100,000 pounds ($165,000) loan.
ING Barings confirmed it is suing Baker for 113,000 pounds, which includes the loan and interest.
The loan is alleged to have been paid in two tranches of 50,000 pounds each.
The last tranche was made two weeks before the collapse of Barings in February 1995.
Baker's lawyer, Lindsay Hill, stated that Baker does not owe any money to ING Barings.
Hill described the ING claim as not constituting a good claim against Baker.
Baker was head of financial products at Barings.
Baker claims that any money paid to him was insufficient to cover what he was owed.
Baker is currently focusing on a tribunal hearing regarding charges from Britain's Securities and Futures Authority (SFA).

BZW is the investment banking arm of Barclays Plc.
BZW has restructured its Global Markets division to compete with global rivals.
BZW conducted a review of its markets business to align staff profiles and skills with business needs.
Approximately 30 employees left BZW during the restructuring, including Alex von Ungern-Sternberg and Klaus-Peter Moeritz.
The departing employees included foreign exchange traders, metals traders, secretaries, and telephonists.
Bob Diamond is the chief of Global Markets at BZW since July.
Alex von Ungern-Sternberg left BZW because his role became substantially narrower after the restructuring.
Bill Harrison is the chief executive of BZW and joined from Robert Fleming.
Donald Brydon, a Barclays veteran, was not retained after the death of David Band, the previous head of BZW.
Diamond and Harrison are working on methods to make profitability more sustainable in the investment banking industry.

Royal Bank of Scotland is expected to raise its pre-tax profit from last year's 602 million stg.
Analysts expect Royal Bank's profits to rise to between 670 and 700 million stg.
The contribution from Direct Line low cost insurance is expected to be much smaller.
The total dividend is expected to be around 18.6 pence a share, compared to last year's 16.2 pence.
The pre-tax figures will include an exceptional gain of 70 million stg from the disposal of a 50 percent stake in Germany's CC Group.
Restructuring costs of around 23 million pounds are expected from an acquisition by Citizens, a New England subsidiary.
Analysts are generally pessimistic about Direct Line's performance, particularly in the motor insurance market.
David Poutney expects a pre-tax profit of 695 million stg, including exceptional items.
BZW analysts expect a pre-tax profit of 675 million stg.
Royal Bank is known to be interested in acquiring a building society to expand its presence in England.

Royal Bank of Scotland is reviewing its options to expand distribution channels in the south east of England.
George Mathewson is the chief executive of Royal Bank of Scotland.
Mathewson stated that many people are interested in a tie-up with Royal Bank due to its lack of penetration in the south east.
Royal Bank of Scotland announced a 15 percent rise in pretax profits to 695 million stg.
Royal Bank shares rose by 8p to 530p following the profit announcement.
Bank of Scotland announced a banking joint venture with retailer Sainsburys earlier this year.
Mathewson did not rule out the possibility of Royal Bank acquiring an English building society.
Any potential purchase would need to consider shareholder value and brand strength.
Mathewson stated that Royal Bank's capital ratios had strengthened over the past year.
Royal Bank's UK banking operations saw a 22 percent gain, while its New England banking unit Citizens experienced a 57 percent rise.

British bank Barclays sold its global custody business to U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley.
The sale price is undisclosed but is thought to be below 50 million pounds.
Morgan Stanley's purchase is part of a trend of consolidation in the custody business.
The custody business involves safekeeping of securities, performance measurement, and stock lending.
Barclays' Chief Executive Martin Taylor stated that global custody requires substantial investment in technology.
A Barclays spokeswoman indicated that the investment in technology would be considerable and ongoing.
Morgan Stanley's chairman Sir David Walker said the transaction would enhance their product offerings and strengthen their global franchise.
The combined custody assets of Barclays and Morgan Stanley will total approximately $390 million.
Chase Manhattan is the largest player in the global custody market with over $1 trillion in assets.
Barclays Global Custody employs 488 staff worldwide, with fewer than half transferring to Morgan Stanley.

Ailing Union Plc was formerly a significant entity in the London money market.
Union Plc announced it would not pay a final dividend for 1996.
Analysts suggested that Union Plc could be broken up to release shareholder value.
Union's profitable fees and commission businesses may be sold separately from its loss-making trading division.
Union has faced multiple crises in recent years.
Union has struggled to diversify from its traditional role as a discount house.
Union's market value is currently 25 million pounds.
The Bank of England plans to remove the exclusive right of seven discount houses to deal directly with it.
Union stated that this plan will significantly impact its future.
Union will write off Advance Corporation Tax (ACT) that it intended to carry forward.

British banks have made a positive start to 1997.
Share prices of British banks are buoyant.
The banking sector has outperformed the FTSE 100 index by around 20 percent over the past six months.
Analysts are confident that banks will continue to show good profit growth due to a benign economic environment.
Barclays and National Westminster are expected to offer further share buybacks.
HSBC and Standard Chartered are expected to benefit from their strong Far East franchise.
Analysts expect NatWest to spend possibly 300 million pounds on buying back shares.
Barclays has already spent around one billion pounds on share repurchases.
Lloyds TSB may join the share buy-back program, but not before 1998.
The strength of sterling is expected to keep inflation and interest rates low.

Halifax Building Society is Britain's largest mortgage lender.
Halifax announced a planned stock market flotation in June that could value it at up to 12 billion pounds.
Mike Blackburn is the chief executive of Halifax.
Halifax has assets exceeding 100 billion pounds.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is the investment bank adviser for Halifax.
The estimated market price per share for Halifax is between 390 and 450 pence.
Analysts expect the final market value of Halifax to be at the top end of the estimated range.
Halifax plans to offer 2.675 billion shares in the flotation.
Halifax has 6.7 million investing members and 2.0 million borrowing members.
Investing members will receive a basic allocation of 200 shares and a variable allocation based on account balances.

The London High Court adjourned a hearing regarding the handover of documents related to Silvio Berlusconi's business affairs to Italy.
The judge stated that the hearing could not be completed in the allotted two days.
Lawyers are scheduled to return in the first week of October before two new judges.
Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) seized 15 bags of documents from London lawyer David Mills earlier this year.
David Mills represents the business interests of Silvio Berlusconi, who owns three TV channels and the football club AC Milan.
The SFO expressed regret that the court could not hear the matter after nearly five months since the documents were seized.
The hearing is related to an appeal by Berlusconi, his company Fininvest, and others against a decision to hand over the papers to Italian magistrates.
The documents are linked to fraud and false accounting allegations totaling 41 million pounds at overseas companies moved from Switzerland to England.
Italian investigators suspect that Berlusconi's Fininvest may have used offshore companies to make payments to politicians.
Silvio Berlusconi is on trial in Milan for alleged complicity in bribing tax officials for lenient audits of Fininvest companies.

Ian Hopkins has been banned from being a director in the City for three years.
The ban was announced after a three-day disciplinary hearing.
The Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) stated that the formal announcement of the outcome would occur after the appeal process.
Hopkins was ordered to pay an unspecified amount of costs.
Hopkins did not appear before the tribunal and was not legally represented.
He will have 10 business days to lodge an appeal after receiving the full written judgment.
Hopkins was part of a group of former Barings executives facing disciplinary charges related to the bank's collapse.
Barings collapsed nearly two years ago due to unauthorized derivatives trades by trader Nick Leeson.
Hopkins claimed he tried to warn other Barings executives about the bank's dangerous position but was ignored.
The official Singaporean report criticized Barings executives for not heeding Hopkins's warnings.

The six major British banks will report their results next week.
Aggregate pre-tax profit for the banks is expected to exceed 12 billion stg for 1996.
The pre-tax profit for the banks was just over 10.8 billion stg in 1995.
Some banks are expected to return surplus capital to shareholders through share buybacks or dividends.
Lloyds TSB Group will report on February 14.
Lloyds TSB Group is expected to report over 2.4 billion stg in pre-tax profit.
Lloyds TSB Group is expected to have a dividend per share of about 13p.
Lloyds TSB Group is expected to have a return on equity of around 32 percent.
Barclays will report on February 18.
Barclays is expected to report profits of around 2.39 billion stg, up from 2.08 billion in 1995.

The Czech merchandise trade deficit increased by 16.4 billion crowns in July.
This increase is the largest monthly rise in the history of the Czech Republic.
The Czech Statistical Bureau reported that the seven-month trade deficit reached 85.3 billion crowns.
In June, the trade deficit was 14 billion crowns, leading to a half-year deficit of 68.87 billion crowns.
Radek Maly, an economist at Citibank Prague, stated that the trade gap is still widening.
Maly noted that a significant portion of the deficit is due to the investment needs of Czech industry.
Imports from January to July grew by 15.9 percent compared to the same period last year.
Exports increased by only 7.2 percent, primarily due to lower demand in Germany.
Machinery and transport equipment contributed 52.5 billion crowns to the total seven-month deficit.
The balance for consumer goods showed a surplus of 857 million crowns despite increased domestic demand.

Czech President Vaclav Havel expressed deep disturbance over a Chinese court's 11-year prison sentence for dissident Wang Dan.
Wang Dan was sentenced on charges of plotting to overthrow the government.
Havel described Wang's sentence as unacceptable.
Wang, 27, was jailed after a brief hearing on Wednesday.
Wei Jingsheng, a prominent figure in China's democracy movement, was previously jailed on similar charges.
Wei Jingsheng was freed in 1993 after serving part of a 15-year term for subversion.
Wei was rearrested in 1994 and sentenced to another 14-year term in December 1996.
Havel's statement emphasized solidarity with those advocating for justice and human rights globally.
Havel has been critical of China and previously met with Taiwan's Premier, which angered China.
The Czech Foreign Ministry protested the trial and judgment against Wang Dan.

Elections to the new Czech Senate will take place over the next two weekends.
Analysts believe that the indecisive electorate has already been factored into the financial markets.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's coalition fell two seats short of a majority in the lower house in June.
The Social Democrats performed strongly in the June elections, finishing in second place.
Analysts do not expect the Senate elections to indicate a clear political shift.
The three-party conservative government is expected to struggle to maintain its term through the year 2000.
A clear victory for the opposition Social Democrats over Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) could negatively impact the Czech crown and capital markets.
The Czech crown fell by one percentage point following the June election results.
The stock market lost more than four percent of its value after the June elections before stabilizing.
Recent opinion polls show ODS and the Social Democrats with around 25 percent support each.

The Czech government's tourism office forecast record income from foreign visits in 1996.
Income from foreign visitors in the Czech Republic could exceed $3.5 billion in 1996.
This forecast is an increase from the record $2.87 billion in 1995.
Jiri Cech is the director of the Economics Ministry's tourism division.
The Czech National Bank will release balance of payment figures for the first half of the year in September.
The first quarter balance of payments showed a net inflow of $261 million from tourism.
Total tourism receipts in the first quarter were $581 million.
Analysts forecast first half total tourism revenues at about $1.6 billion.
The overall current account posted a $505 million deficit in the first quarter.
The merchandise trade deficit has increased, with a record gap of 16.4 billion crowns in July.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus did not comment on whether the success of his Civic Democratic Party (ODS) in the Senate elections might lead to a push for new elections in the lower house.
Klaus's ODS received 36.47 percent of the total vote in the first round of Senate elections.
The ODS's performance in the Senate elections followed a loss of majority in the lower house elections in June.
In the June elections, the Social Democrats (CSSD) received 29.6 percent of the vote, while the ODS received 36.47 percent in the Senate elections.
The CSSD received 20.27 percent of the vote in the Senate elections, a decrease from their previous performance.
Voter turnout for the Senate elections was low, with only about one in three eligible Czechs voting.
Klaus stated that the country does not need another election and emphasized the need for functionality.
The ODS advanced 76 candidates to the runoff elections out of 81 constituencies and won three seats outright.
