The CSSD had 48 candidates in the runoff but did not win any seats outright.
Analysts noted that many Czechs viewed the upper house as redundant due to its limited legislative powers.

Czech Unipetrol a.s. announced a plan to convert shares in Kaucuk a.s. and Chemopetrol a.s. into Unipetrol shares.
The boards of Chemopetrol, Kaucuk, and Unipetrol agreed to swap one Chemopetrol share for between 1.05 to 1.20 Unipetrol shares.
The boards agreed to swap one Kaucuk share for between 1.10 to 1.25 Unipetrol shares.
The plan aims to complete the partial privatisation of Kaucuk and Chemopetrol.
An exact ratio for the share swap must be approved by general shareholders meetings.
Kaucuk and Chemopetrol shares have traded at similar levels for months.
Kaucuk shares were priced at 1,105 crowns on the Prague Stock Exchange before the announcement.
Chemopetrol shares finished at 1,106 crowns on the Prague Stock Exchange after the announcement.
The ratio range for the share swap was determined by appraising the assets and liabilities of the involved companies.
Equities analysts noted that immediate arbitrage possibilities were slim due to the announced conversion range.

The Czech crown rose to its highest level against its mark/dollar basket on Thursday.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated that devaluation of the crown was not needed despite a widening trade gap.
The crown rose to 4.5 percent above the cross rate of the two-currency basket late in the afternoon.
By mid-morning, the Czech currency was 4.3 percent above the basket, up from just under four percent at the opening.
The crown strengthened to 26.014 to the dollar and 17.591 to the mark by 1430 GMT.
The central bank set the crown at 4.24 percent above parity with the basket at its midday fixing.
Traders interpreted the central bank's midday fixing as a signal of contentment with the crown's rise.
The strength of the crown has been attributed to official comments dismissing the need for devaluation.
The trade balance showed a record monthly deficit of 16.4 billion crowns in July.
Klaus expressed that a stronger crown would be better for the economy in the long term.

Czech President Vaclav Havel underwent surgery that revealed a cancerous lung.
Havel's heavy smoking is believed to have caused the malignant tumor that was removed.
The tabloid Blesk published a headline reading 'CANCER' alongside a photo of Havel smoking.
Havel's surgery removed half of his right lung and is expected to allow for a full recovery.
Havel may return to work after the new year.
Havel is described as a multiple-pack-a-day smoker.
His spokesman indicated that Havel will likely only smoke occasionally after the surgery.
Havel is recognized for his role in the 1989 Velvet Revolution against communism.
Barbra Streisand stated that Havel is the only person she allows to smoke in her presence.
Czech surgeon Dr. Pavel Pafko noted that it is difficult to identify smoking as the primary cause of Havel's cancer.

Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik skipped a meeting with the Prague bourse's governing chamber for the second consecutive week.
Kocarnik canceled his participation in a meeting scheduled for Monday at two o'clock.
The Prague Stock Exchange spokesman Milan Vodicka confirmed Kocarnik's cancellation to Reuters.
The bourse's Chamber has been seeking stronger ministry action to address concerns about market transparency.
Kocarnik's ministry was invited to a future meeting, which the Chamber later declined.
The meetings were intended to discuss tougher regulatory actions regarding transparency and insider trading in Czech capital markets.
Jiri Spicka, director of the Finance Ministry's banking division, stated that Kocarnik was too busy preparing the state budget to attend the meeting.
The state budget is expected to go to the floor of parliament for its second reading in a session beginning on Tuesday.
Chamber Chairman Tomas Jezek criticized Kocarnik for lax regulation of capital markets during a party meeting.
Jezek warned that poor regulation could damage the country's balance of payments and lead to a devaluation of the crown.

Czech Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda resigned from the government and parliament for falsely using an academic title.
Another member of parliament from a coalition party also resigned for the same reason as Kalvoda.
Three other deputies admitted to using false titles but did not resign.
Kalvoda falsely claimed to be a Doctor of Law amid concerns about the academic credentials of Czech politicians.
Kalvoda delivered his resignation to the president.
Officials from Kalvoda's party, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), were not available for comment after his resignation.
It was unclear who would replace Kalvoda in the cabinet or his status within the ODA.
Kalvoda stated there would be no changes in the ODA party.
Pavla Jurkova, a member of the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL), resigned her seat for falsely claiming a law doctorate.
Two members of the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) admitted their law doctorates were false but did not resign.

Czech economic growth is expected to slow in 1997 before accelerating again due to an improving foreign trade balance, according to the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
Czech inflation is projected to ease in 1997 and more significantly in 1998.
The OECD forecasts that gross domestic product (GDP) growth will decrease to 4.6 percent in 1997 from 4.8 percent in 1996, and then rise to 5.3 percent in 1998.
Investment is expected to continue growing at double-digit rates, while household consumption will play a smaller role in GDP growth.
The current account deficit as a percentage of GDP is expected to decrease to 5.4 percent in 1997 from 5.8 percent in 1996, and further to 4.9 percent in 1998.
Export growth is projected to accelerate to 7.5 percent year-on-year in 1997 and 8.7 percent in 1998, up from 5.5 percent in 1996.
Import growth is expected to slow to 9.5 percent in the next two years from 11.3 percent in 1996.
The Czech National Bank has warned that the current account deficit could reach seven percent of GDP in 1996.
Annual inflation is expected to decrease to 8.5 percent in 1997 and 7.5 percent in 1998, down from 9.1 percent in 1996.
Unemployment is projected to rise to 3.6 percent in 1997 and 4.1 percent in 1998, up from about three percent in 1996.

The ancient Czech capital is Prague.
Michael Jackson is known as the self-styled 'King of Pop'.
Michael Jackson's 'HiStory' world tour starts on Saturday in Prague.
This concert is Michael Jackson's first in two years.
Michael Jackson was cleared of child molestation charges by a U.S. court due to lack of evidence.
Michael Jackson is expected to receive a welcome similar to that of heads of state upon his arrival in Prague.
Police have requested that Czechs stay away from the airport during Jackson's arrival.
Officials have encouraged well-wishers to line the route into the city.
Jackson's concert in Prague has not faced the same controversies as other stops on his tour.
A planned concert in Casablanca was canceled by Moroccan authorities.

Austin Reed Group Plc is a supplier of pinstriped suits to British businessmen.
The company reported a 64 percent increase in first-half profits to 2.3 million pounds.
Sales for the first half increased by 7.0 percent to 38.9 million pounds.
Women executives' return to favor contributed to the company's profit and sales growth.
Womens' clothing now accounts for around 20 percent of Austin Reed's sales.
The 1995 spring collection for women was not successful and required substantial discounts.
Austin Reed has approximately 50 stores in the UK and sells in Europe, Japan, and the U.S.
The company is experiencing a rise in UK consumer activity.
Autumn sales are currently ahead by around nine percent compared to the previous year.
Austin Reed plans to expand sales through German, French, and Italian retailers.

Daewoo Cars Ltd is the British motoring arm of Korean conglomerate Daewoo Corp.
Daewoo UK Ltd managing director Tong Won Rhie stated that the company is reviewing its UK marketing strategy for potential transfer to new markets.
Rhie mentioned that the UK strategy has proven to be a good model.
Daewoo's strategy involves selling directly to customers, bypassing car dealerships.
Daewoo operates in 12 European countries and plans to launch its models in five more.
In its first nine months of operation in Britain last year, Daewoo sold more than 13,000 cars.
By October 8 of this year, Daewoo had sold an additional 18,500 units in Britain.
Rhie stated that Daewoo has already reached its target of one percent market share in three years.
Daewoo was the first company to offer three years of free servicing on all models.
Rhie noted that the UK market is more sophisticated than many other countries, with higher consumer awareness.

New evidence about British Biotech Plc's anti-cancer treatment Marimastat will be presented next week.
British Biotech is making five presentations at the European Society of Medical Oncologists meeting in Vienna.
The presentations will include Marimastat's effects on ovarian, colo-rectal, pancreatic, and gastric cancer.
British Biotech will issue a general update on Monday morning.
The company is based in Oxford and is considered a bellwether for the U.K. biotech field.
Sentiment towards Marimastat significantly impacts the biotech sector.
Forecasts for Marimastat's annual sales range from a few hundred million dollars to up to $4 billion.
The data on Monday will come from patients who continued using Marimastat beyond Phase II clinical trials.
Yamaichi International analyst Erling Refsum hopes to see evidence of increased patient survival due to Marimastat.
Lehman Brothers analyst Ian Smith believes indications of Marimastat's effect on patient survival may be gleaned from the trials.

British Biotech Plc published evidence on Monday that its cancer drug Marimastat worked.
Analysts stated that there is still a long way to go before Marimastat's potential as a blockbuster product can be confirmed.
Shares in British Biotech Plc decreased by 14 1/2 pence to 217 pence in early afternoon trading.
The stock rose sharply last week ahead of the publication of the announcement.
Morgan Grenfell sold a sizeable chunk of its holding on October 29, which affected buying interest.
British Biotech presented trials of Marimastat at a cancer conference in Vienna.
The studies confirmed Marimastat's ability to reduce the rate of rise of cancer antigens.
There is a large scale trial underway for Marimastat in gastric cancer.
Some analysts noted that the announcement was largely a confirmation of Phase II data published in May.
Finance director James Noble stated that the company was cautious in its comments to avoid raising false hopes.

Dominion Resources Inc is reconsidering the price it is willing to pay for East Midlands Electricity Plc.
Analysts stated that Dominion must be realistic about acquiring East Midlands.
Dominion's interest in East Midlands was revealed by U.K. stock exchange regulators after East Midlands' share price increased by 13 percent.
Dominion indicated it would not offer much above Wednesday's closing price of 608 pence for East Midlands.
This valuation places East Midlands at just over 1.2 billion stg ($1.97 billion).
Industry sources mentioned that Dominion would withdraw if the market price increased further.
East Midlands' share price fell by 21 pence to 587 in midafternoon trading on Thursday.
Analysts believe an offer at 610 pence would likely not succeed.
610 pence would value East Midlands lower than Northern Electric Plc, which has a 659 million stg bid from CE Electric.
CE Electric's offer for Northern represents a P/E ratio of 9.3 based on earnings through March 1997.

BOC Group Plc reported that its healthcare business is likely to have a flat performance for the year ending September 1997.
Chief executive Danny Rosenkranz stated that the Ohmeda health business will face challenges in the U.S. markets.
Rosenkranz predicted that the healthcare business would start to recover next year.
The healthcare division's operating profits fell by 11 percent to 53.1 million stg.
BOC's full-year pre-tax profits rose by 10.6 percent to 444.9 million stg.
Sales for BOC increased by 6.7 percent to just over 4.0 billion stg.
The strong pound reduced the growth in fourth-quarter pre-tax profits by three percentage points.
Rosenkranz warned that a stronger sterling could negatively impact profits.
The healthcare division accounted for less than 13 percent of BOC's total sales.
Edwards Vacuum Products experienced a 28 percent gain in full-year operating profit to 90.3 million stg.

Albright & Wilson Plc reported that a drop in raw materials prices has not occurred.
Robin Paul is the chief executive of Albright & Wilson.
Costs have stabilized after sharp gains last year, but there has been a small net increase.
Albright & Wilson's performance improvement has had to come from its own efforts.
Cost increases added an extra 40 million stg to Albright & Wilson's bills in 1995.
Albright & Wilson is the world's biggest and lowest-cost producer of wet phosphoric acid.
Rises in phosphorous prices in China and Asia eroded gains from strong phosphate demand in the first half.
The strength of sterling could raise the cost of exports from the UK and reduce foreign earnings.
Most contracts are in place, so the strength of the pound is not expected to substantially affect 1996 results.
Albright & Wilson produces specialty chemicals, including flame-retardants and surfactants.

Blue Circle Industries Plc is a British building materials group.
The company reported a turnaround in its European heating operations.
Blue Circle plans to increase operating profits in the heating division ten-fold over the next three years.
The company's interim pretax profit rose by 11.7 percent to 116.3 million pounds.
The interim dividend increased by 6 percent to 4.25 pence.
The heating operations posted operating profits of nine million pounds in the first half of the year.
Blue Circle warned of no significant recovery in the British cement market.
Blue Circle shares fell by 5.5 pence to 373.5 pence.
Keith Orrell-Jones is the chief executive of Blue Circle.
The company aims for annual cost savings of 25 million pounds from restructuring its heating operations.

Zeneca Group Plc expects peak sales in excess of $400 million for its new asthma treatment Accolate and schizophrenia drug Seroquel.
David Barnes is the chief executive of Zeneca Group Plc.
Barnes stated that a substantial product has sales of $400 million plus.
Accolate is the first of a new generation of asthma drugs taken in tablet form.
Accolate aims to erode the market share of inhaled steroids.
Accolate was launched in the U.S. in October.
Barnes reported that experience with Accolate has been encouraging and sales are meeting expectations.
Zeneca announced a 21 percent expansion of its U.S. sales force.
Zomig is a migraine treatment obtained by Zeneca from Glaxo Wellcome Plc.
Barnes indicated that Zomig has substantial potential based on clinical data.

Shareholders in Enviromed Plc removed the company's board on Friday.
Ron Zwanziger is the chief executive officer of Selfcare Inc., Enviromed's largest shareholder.
Selfcare Inc. owns a 29 percent stake in Enviromed.
The share price of Enviromed fell from around 112 pence per share in December 1994 to around 25 pence.
Selfcare Inc. produces tests for pregnancy and infectious diseases.
Selfcare requested shareholders to support the removal of four board members, including managing director Thomas Murphy.
The extraordinary meeting took place in Dean's Yard, next to Westminster Abbey.
The board of Enviromed conceded defeat after proxy votes showed 49 percent support for Selfcare.
Ron Zwanziger became the non-executive chairman of the new board.
Zwanziger previously attempted to remove the board in April 1995.

Milumil babymilk powder was used by around 25,000 mothers in Britain and Ireland.
Milumil was withdrawn from stores and clinics in Britain and Ireland due to a Salmonella poisoning scare.
Milupa, part of Nutricia NV, announced the withdrawal of Milumil in Britain due to an unconfirmed link with 12 cases of Salmonella.
The withdrawal in Ireland followed consultations with the Irish government, despite no reported incidents there.
The Department of Health in Britain contacted the company after identifying 12 cases of Salmonella anatum infection in children under 12 months old.
The Health Department advised parents and carers to stop using Milumil immediately and ordered the withdrawal of all stocks.
Two of the children involved in the Salmonella cases were admitted to the hospital, but all have since recovered.
Nutricia's shares were suspended for about an hour in Amsterdam after a significant drop but later recovered some losses.
Milupa announced a thorough investigation at the French plant where Milumil was produced and suspended production of the product.
Sales of Milumil milk powder total between six and seven million pounds a year, with a market share of around five percent.

ICI Paints and Black & Decker are launching a new product called the Black & Decker Paintmate on Wednesday.
The Paintmate is a battery-operated roller system developed over two years and millions of pounds.
The Paintmate will be sold in DIY stores across Britain starting in April for 39.99 pounds ($65).
The Paintmate uses an air-filled bellow system to dispense paint from a two-litre refill bag onto a roller.
The Paintmate can be strapped to the back to reduce bending over while painting.
Black & Decker spokesman Richard Sanderson stated that the DIY market has not seen a product of such significance in a long time.
The companies aim to sell 500,000 Paintmates and one million bags of paint in the first year in Britain.
If successful in Britain, the Paintmate will be introduced in western Europe next year and then in the U.S. market.
ICI sells enough paint in the UK to decorate five million homes annually.
ICI Decorative Paints international marketing director Chris Harris believes the product will revolutionize home decorating.

British Biotech Plc stated that a rethink on drug giants forming alliances with fledgling biotechs is required.
Keith McCullagh is the chief executive of British Biotech.
McCullagh spoke at the IIR's Pharma Summit conference.
Many product partnerships fail because small drug discoverers relinquish control of their projects too early.
A project important to a biotech is often one of many for a large company and is not regarded with urgency.
Biotech projects often face bureaucratic delays and do not achieve the same priority as in-house discoveries.
Changes in management can lead to the failure of biotech-pharma alliances.
British Biotech's deals have been affected by changes in research and development management and overall control through mergers and acquisitions.
Success is more likely if the originating company continues to play an important role in ongoing development.
Biotech companies can maintain control of drug development in-house with partner funding or establish joint ventures.

At least 24 soldiers and leftist rebels died in fighting in three provinces of Colombia over the weekend.
The bloodiest clashes occurred in the Uraba region of northwest Colombia.
Ten soldiers and eight Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) insurgents died in battles in Uraba.
Gen. Rito Alejo stated that intensive counterinsurgency operations continued on Sunday.
In Huila province, the FARC dynamited a military convoy, killing four soldiers.
In Norte de Santander province, one soldier and one FARC rebel died in firefights.
Four suspected rebels were injured in Barranquilla when their bomb-making factory exploded.
Military experts claim the current guerrilla violence is the worst in over three decades.
The FARC launched a new offensive on August 30, killing 27 soldiers and taking at least 60 prisoner.
The FARC accused the army of planning to rescue the captives by force, which the army denied.

Colombia has initiated the process to lift a constitutional ban on extradition.
Alfonso Valdivieso, the chief prosecutor, criticized the move as virtually meaningless.
A Senate panel approved draft legislation to lift the prohibition on extraditing Colombians.
The draft legislation was approved by an 11-8 vote in the Senate constitutional committee.
Valdivieso stated that the legislation should be strengthened before a final vote in Congress.
The draft legislation would not be retroactive, preventing extradition of certain criminals.
The legislation would prevent extradition of criminals who voluntarily surrendered to Colombian justice.
U.S. authorities argue that Colombian justice is too lenient on drug traffickers.
Pablo Escobar led a violent campaign in the late 1980s and early 1990s to enforce the extradition ban.
Death threats against supporters of extradition have been reported in Cali.

The Colombian government may use special powers to implement stricter anti-drug laws.
Justice Minister Carlos Medellin stated that the draft laws would include confiscating drug barons' assets and should be retroactive.
The retroactivity of the laws has caused controversy regarding the constitutional ban on extradition currently debated in the senate.
Former justice minister Enrique Parejo believes lawmakers may support the decree to avoid backlash from drug traffickers.
Medellin expressed urgency in addressing the confiscation of drug traffickers' property if congress does not act.
President Ernesto Samper submitted tougher anti-drug proposals to congress in July to regain U.S. certification as an ally in the drug war.
The congress has faced delays due to political wrangling and poor attendance, preventing committees from reaching a quorum.
If congress does not pass the measures, the government may introduce the new anti-drug laws by decree by Thursday.
Political and legal analysts have raised concerns about the constitutionality of the government overriding congress.
Parejo indicated that the government fears decertification by the United States could lead to a crisis.

Colombia denied that its army was linked to paramilitary death squads.
Colombia's Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra stated that the world should focus on the alliance between leftist guerrillas and drug traffickers.
Esguerra claimed that narco-guerrilla groups are conducting a disinformation campaign globally.
Human Rights Watch issued a report titled 'Colombia's Killer Networks' which concluded that the military has created paramilitary groups.
The Human Rights Watch report stated that the military allows paramilitary groups to carry out political killings.
The report cited confidential defense documents indicating that U.S. military advisers contributed to the rise of death squads in Colombia.
Human Rights Watch's legal adviser Jamie Fellner alleged that top army commanders tolerated paramilitary groups in a systematic 'dirty war'.
Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International called for the suspension of U.S. and European military aid to Colombia until human rights violations are addressed.
Human Rights Watch estimated that $322 million in U.S. military aid to Colombia since 1989 was given to counterinsurgency battalions accused of rights violations.
A U.S. State Department spokesman stated there were no plans for tighter checks on military aid to Colombia.

Leaders of Colombia's three largest labour federations announced they would not sign a new wage and price control pact with bosses and the government.
They warned that 1997 could be a year of serious social unrest.
The annual social pact was first introduced by President Ernesto Samper in 1995.
The leaders condemned the social pact as a means to advance neoliberal policies at the expense of workers.
Luis Eduardo Garzon, chairman of the Unitary Workers' Confederation (CUT), stated that the social pact reflects neoliberal logic and aims to reduce worker pay to enhance industry competitiveness.
Garzon claimed the pact is a corporatist tactic that does not benefit the people.
Following internal elections in November, left-wing members, including those from the Communist Party, gained control of the CUT.
This year's pact included a 19.5 percent wage increase for workers based on a 17 percent inflation target.
Despite the wage increase, the cost of goods and services rose, leading to an inflation rate of almost 21 percent in the first 11 months of 1996.
The central bank set a 1997 inflation target of 18 percent.

Colombia's main oil union is the USO union.
The USO union has 5,700 members.
The USO union postponed a decision to launch an indefinite strike.
The postponement followed talks with the government.
The strike was in protest against the arrest of 11 members on terrorism charges.
The USO union is known for its fiercely nationalistic stance.
The union was scheduled to set a start date for the strike at a general assembly on Monday.
Industrial action was expected to begin soon after Monday's meeting.
The union head is Hernando Hernández.

A car bomb exploded in Medellin, killing one woman and injuring at least 15 others.
The explosion occurred outside the home of Juan Gomez Martinez, a regional newspaper editor and former provincial governor.
The bomb contained about 120 pounds (50 kg) of dynamite and detonated around 5:30 a.m.
The deceased woman was identified as Lucia Bernal, 60, who lived near the blast site.
Juan Gomez was not at home during the explosion, but one of his sons, Juan Camilo, was injured.
Police chief Gen. Alfredo Salgado stated that the motive for the attack is unknown.
Salgado mentioned that authorities are considering various possibilities for who may be behind the attack.
Juan Gomez is a member of the opposition Conservative Party and heads the El Colombiano newspaper.
A group called the Special Anti-Paramilitary Commando claimed responsibility for declaring war on paramilitary groups in Antioquia.
The group accused state governor Alvaro Uribe of sponsoring paramilitary groups.

Rosemberg Pavon, alias 'Comandante Uno', is a former Colombian rebel leader.
Pavon was involved in a 61-day takeover of the Dominican embassy in Bogota in 1980.
Pavon urged the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas to avoid bloodshed during a hostage situation in Lima.
The MRTA took up to 490 hostages in the Japanese embassy residence in Lima on Tuesday evening.
Pavon stated that the crisis in Lima was precarious and could lead to a bloodbath with one false move.
Pavon emphasized the need for calm and a rapid solution in negotiations.
He claimed that the MRTA, like the M-19, was fighting for social justice.
Pavon expressed a willingness to travel to Peru to help negotiate an end to the crisis.
He warned that the Peruvian government must avoid a repeat of the Palace of Justice incident from 1985.
The Palace of Justice incident resulted in about 100 deaths, including rebels and judges.

Colombia's military and leftist rebels are preparing for conflict in 1997.
Both sides predict that the guerrilla war will escalate in 1997.
Military experts and human rights activists warn that the conflict is ready to explode.
The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) stated that 1997 will be a year of greater struggles for social justice.
The FARC's struggle was blamed for many of Colombia's 25,000 murders in 1996.
More than half of Colombia was under emergency rule due to the conflict in 1996.
The FARC and the National Liberation Army (ELN) have been increasingly successful in attacking military targets.
Human rights attorney Carlos Rodriguez stated that there is no desire for peace from the government.
The FARC's raid on a jungle base at Las Delicias resulted in the deaths of 27 soldiers and the capture of 60 others.
The Colombian government plans to spend over $900 million on defense in 1997.

President Ernesto Samper sent a message of condolences to U.S. President Bill Clinton after a U.S. pilot was killed in Colombia.
Robert Martin, a 35-year-old pilot, died when his Turbo Thrush T-65 crop-dusting plane crashed in Guaviare province while fumigating coca leaf plantations.
Samper expressed condolences on behalf of the Colombian people and government for Martin's death.
Martin was one of six civilian pilots working in Colombia under contract with the U.S. State Department.
U.S. ambassador Myles Frechette stated that Martin was the first U.S. aviator to die on such a mission.
The involvement of U.S. personnel in drug operations raises concerns about national sovereignty among some Colombian politicians.
Martin had been training Colombian pilots in crop fumigation, but his role extended to frontline operations since October.
Crop-dusting planes are frequently attacked by armed gangs and guerrillas protecting drug plantations.
Police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano indicated that there was no evidence of gunfire causing the crash, suggesting human error or mechanical failure as likely causes.
An investigation into the crash is ongoing, and Martin's body was scheduled to be returned to the United States.

Colombian stocks experienced a significant rise in 1997 after three years of stagnation.
The Bogota IBB and Medellin IBOMED indices gained more than 22 percent in the first 10 sessions of 1997.
Brokers believe Colombian stocks are undervalued by as much as 25 percent.
Luis Fernando Uribe, head of the Medellin exchange, stated that market performance has exceeded expectations.
Bogota's IBB index gained about 22.5 percent despite minor declines due to profit-taking.
Medellin's IBOMED index increased by more than 23 percent after a nominal loss in 1996.
Trading volume on Colombia's exchanges was low, totaling $2.3 billion in 1996.
Factors supporting the stock market rally include perceptions of undervalued shares and a decrease in deposit rates.
Market analyst Stephen Edkins predicted overall share increases of 40 percent to 45 percent for the year.
Inflation in Colombia is forecasted to reach 18 percent in 1997.

Police arrested a U.S. pilot named Bradley Dale Brandt at Bogota's international airport.
Brandt was carrying a suitcase with at least 13.5 pounds (6.2 kg) of high grade heroin.
Brandt is 40 years old and originally from North Dakota, currently living in southern California.
He was detained while attempting to board a Colombian airline's ACES flight to Panama City.
Brandt claimed he had been framed and that the suitcase was not his.
He was wearing a commercial aviator's uniform at the time of his arrest.
Brandt's passport was issued in Los Angeles.
A police spokeswoman stated that the heroin was discovered during routine x-ray checks.
Earlier that day, airport police arrested a Mexican passenger with 93 pounds (42 kg) of cocaine in false-bottomed suitcases.
The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration estimates that Colombian drug cartels supply at least 80 percent of the world's cocaine.

Shares in Manchester United reached record highs on Friday.
Chief executive Martin Edwards stated that Manchester United is a likely bid target.
Edwards mentioned that any successful company is an attractive takeover prospect.
Edwards indicated that any proposals would be given serious consideration.
Manchester United's shares soared to over 5.0 pounds, valuing the club at over 300 million pounds.
The club's board stated they were not aware of any bid approaches.
United shares increased from under two pounds at the end of January.
The rise in shares was influenced by a new television deal signed by the Premier League with BSkyB.
Manchester United previously rejected a takeover bid from VCI valued at 300 million pounds.
The Times article mentioned Whitbread and Granada as potential bidders for Manchester United.

United News & Media secured control of Blenheim with an offer valuing the company at 592.5 million pounds.
The deal will create the world's largest trade exhibition group with a turnover of more than 500 million pounds based on 1995 figures.
United News has secured acceptances for 51 percent of Blenheim after offering five pounds per share.
United chief executive Clive Hollick stated that the acquisition will be earnings-enhancing in the first full year.
United News shares increased by 31 pence to 674-1/2 pence after the announcement.
Blenheim shares gained 22-1/2 pence to 496 after the announcement.
Dutch publisher VNU, which acquired a 15 percent stake in Blenheim, will not make a counter-bid and is likely to sell its stake.
Reed-Elsevier was regarded as a rival suitor to United but has dropped out of the running.
The acquisition ends a bidding saga that began in June when Blenheim received a bid approach.
Blenheim operates more than 170 exhibitions worldwide but lacks a significant publishing portfolio.

Shares in Pearson Plc fell on Thursday after the announcement of Marjorie Scardino as the new chief executive.
Marjorie Scardino is 49 years old and was previously the chief executive of The Economist Group.
Scardino will succeed Frank Barlow, who is retiring at the end of the year.
Market players expressed disappointment over Scardino's close ties with Pearson and the lack of an external executive appointment.
Pearson shares fell to a low of 668 pence after the announcement and ended the day 13 pence lower at 675 pence.
Dennis Stevenson was announced as the new deputy chairman and will take over as chairman next May.
Scardino stated that she is not a Pearson insider and emphasized the independence of The Economist board.
Scardino has a background in law and helped run the Pulitzer Prize-winning Georgia Gazette in the 1970s.
Scardino's main task is to bring focus to Pearson, which has a market capitalization of almost four billion pounds.
Pearson has focused on three divisions: Information, Education, and Entertainment.

Political opposition to the BBC's call for more public funding increased the urgency of joint venture talks between the BBC and two rival pay television groups.
The two rivals are U.S.-controlled Flextech and satellite broadcaster BSkyB, which is primarily owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp.
Both Flextech and BSkyB want to launch new subscription channels based on the BBC's programming.
The BBC is facing pressure to enhance its commercial activities after criticism of its request for an above-inflation licence fee increase.
BBC Director-General John Birt advocated for an increase in the licence fee during a speech at the Edinburgh International Television Festival.
The current licence fee is 89.50 pounds ($139.1) annually and has not seen a real increase since 1985.
Birt stated that additional funding is necessary for the BBC to maintain its quality in the digital era.
Politicians from both main political parties are opposed to the BBC's appeal for a licence fee increase.
The BBC aims to maintain its central role in broadcasting as the industry transitions to digital technology.
The BBC plans to offer a 24-hour news channel and supplementary programming to licence fee payers in the digital era.

Britain's Independent Television Commission (ITC) invited applications to run terrestrial frequencies for digital television.
Peter Rogers is the chief executive of the ITC.
The ITC aims to increase the number of channels available to viewers to as many as 35 or 36 on digital terrestrial television.
The ITC is seeking applications to operate four multiplexes, which can each carry up to six digital channels.
The BBC has been allocated its own multiplex, while ITV and Channel 4 will share one.
The ITC will award 12-year licences based on criteria such as service roll-out speed and programming appeal, without requiring cash bids.
Licences are expected to be awarded in the spring, with broadcasting potentially starting by mid-1998.
BSkyB plans to launch a digital satellite service in late 1997, ahead of the terrestrial version.
Digital technology allows for more channels and improved sound and picture quality, as well as interactive services.
A set-top box or decoder will be necessary to receive digital services, but there is currently no UK or European legislation for a common standard for decoders.

Executives from British Telecom Plc and MCI Communications Corp were attempting to negotiate a $22 billion merger.
The merger would make BT the world's second largest telecoms group.
MCI is the number two U.S. long-distance phone company.
MCI announced it was in talks about a takeover by BT.
BT has a 20 percent stake in MCI.
BT and MCI operate a joint venture called Concert, which serves customers in over 50 nations.
Analysts speculate on a price of $40 a share for MCI, valuing the company at $28 billion.
BT would need to pay about $22.1 billion for the remaining 80 percent of MCI.
The potential merger would be the largest in the telecommunications market and the second largest involving a U.S. company.
BT had previously unsuccessful merger talks with Cable & Wireless earlier in the year.

Investors on both sides of the Atlantic supported the planned $20 billion merger of British Telecom Plc and MCI Communications.
The merger boosted shares of British Telecom and MCI in stock market trading.
British, European, and U.S. regulators will closely scrutinize the merger amid opposition from rivals, including AT&T Corp.
British Telecom expressed optimism that the European Commission would approve the merger.
The merger is the largest cross-border takeover deal in history and will create one of the largest groups in the global telecommunications sector.
Britain's communications industry regulatory agency is studying the merger details and has not yet made a judgment.
BT Chief Executive Sir Peter Bonfield stated that it could take a year to clear all regulatory hurdles.
BT's shares increased by 32.5 pence to 383.5 pence, adding approximately £2 billion to the company's market value.
MCI's stock rose by $1.25 to $31.50, while AT&T's stock fell by $1.125 to $33.50.
The merger is expected to provide better service and lower international calling charges for customers.

Shares in EMI Plc increased on Tuesday after the company reported positive long-term prospects for the global music market.
EMI Plc demerged from Thorn Plc three months ago.
Profit before tax and exceptional items for EMI rose 9.4 percent to 112.5 million pounds in the six months to September 30.
Net interim dividend per share increased by 12.7 percent to eight pence.
EMI shares rose by 15p to 1,286p in a generally lower market.
Chairman Sir Colin Southgate described the interim results as excellent.
Finance Director Simon Duffy stated that EMI expects the global music business to grow by 6-8 percent annually in the medium to long-term.
Duffy noted that first half industry growth had been 5.5 percent, but this year was looking below that level.
EMI reported that sales in the United States were almost flat and declined slightly in France.
Turnover from the EMI Music division was approximately 1.1 billion pounds, but improved margins increased operating profits to 131.9 million pounds.

Britain's Granada Group reported a 37 percent increase in full-year profits to 480 million pounds ($804 million).
Granada Group plans to improve profits at Forte by over 100 million pounds per annum from 1996/97.
Granada chairman Gerry Robinson described the results as 'very satisfying'.
Granada acquired family-controlled Forte in a 3.9 billion pound deal earlier this year.
Forte has improved profitability by approximately 40 million pounds under Granada's management.
Granada is reorganizing following the acquisition of Forte.
Granada sold London's Hyde Park Hotel for 86 million pounds to Mandarin Oriental International Ltd.
Granada expects to complete the sale of assets by early 1997.
Analysts estimate that asset sales will raise around 900 million pounds.
Granada plans to sell the Welcome Break chain of British motorway service areas due to monopoly concerns.

Britain's Ladbroke Group and the U.S. Hilton Hotels Corp (HHC) announced a worldwide alliance.
The alliance will reunite the Hilton hotel brand after 32 years of separation.
HHC owns the Hilton name in the United States.
Ladbroke holds the rights to the Hilton name everywhere else through its Hilton International (HIC) subsidiary.
The two companies signed an outline agreement to reunite the brand, which was separated in 1964.
Ladbroke acquired HIC in 1987.
The alliance includes 400 hotels in 49 countries.
HHC and HIC plan to cooperate on sales and marketing, loyalty programs, and hotel development starting next year.
Ladbroke announced first half pre-tax profits of 72.8 million pounds ($113 million), a 29 percent increase from last year.
Ladbroke shares reached a 1996 high of 215p before slipping to 213p.

BSkyB reported a 66 percent rise in full-year profit to 257.4 million pounds.
Annual turnover for BSkyB climbed to more than one billion pounds.
The number of subscribers in Britain and Ireland for BSkyB rose to 5.5 million.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corp holds a 40 percent stake in BSkyB.
Profit for the year to June 30, 1996, was up more than 100 million pounds from the previous year.
The full-year dividend for BSkyB was 5.5 pence.
BSkyB shares fell seven pence to 530p in early trading.
BSkyB plans to launch a British digital television service next year.
BSkyB signed a deal with Kirch Gruppe to develop a digital platform in Germany.
BSkyB is expected to inject 200 million pounds into the alliance with Kirch Gruppe.

Wembley, England's home of soccer since the 1920s, will be the site of a new national stadium.
The Sports Council announced the selection of Wembley as the preferred location over Manchester.
The project will receive 120 million pounds in National Lottery funding.
Wembley and Manchester were the two leading candidates from five applicants last year.
Sports Council chairman Sir Rodney Walker stated that Wembley has greater potential to attract major international events.
The Sports Council has supported the English Football Association's bid to host the World Cup in 2006.
The Sports Council has also supported the British Athletics Federation's attempts to attract the world championships in 2001.
The Sports Council agreed in principle to provide up to 60 million pounds for a new Stadium of the North in Manchester.
Manchester has been awarded the Commonwealth Games in 2002.
The Sports Council is considering backing Manchester council's bid for 20 million pounds for a new swimming and diving complex.

Cellnet reported strong growth in its customer numbers.
Cellnet had 2.68 million UK customers at the end of 1996, up from 2.3 million a year earlier.
Vodafone reported a 20 percent increase in UK subscriber numbers over 1996, reaching approximately 2.8 million in December.
Analysts noted signs of an increase in the rate of subscriber growth for both Cellnet and Vodafone.
Vodafone gained a net 146,000 UK subscribers in the last three months of the previous year.
Cellnet's subscriber base grew by 143,000 in the last three months of the previous year.
Both Vodafone and Cellnet are transferring customers from older analogue networks to digital systems.
Vodafone has over 1.2 million UK customers on the digital network.
Cellnet has over 880,000 digital customers.
Orange shares increased by 2.5p to 188p on Friday.

The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved 46 new drugs for U.S. marketing in the federal fiscal year ending September 30.
The number of new drug approvals in fiscal 1995 was 26.
The FDA cleared 37 new medical devices during the same period, an increase from 27 the previous year.
Jim O'Hara is the FDA associate commissioner for public affairs.
O'Hara stated that the improvements in the review system have been ongoing for over 10 years.
Jeff Trewhitt is a spokesman for the Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PHARMA).
Trewhitt acknowledged improvements in the FDA's processes in recent years.
Two bills proposing more flexible and shorter FDA new drug reviews did not pass before Congress adjourned.
Analysts indicated that faster FDA approvals reduce research and development risks for drug and medical device companies.
A study showed that the FDA's median review time for new drugs approved in 1994 and 1995 was 1.3 years.

Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc is not realizing merger synergies as planned.
Shares of Pharmacia & Upjohn fell 6-1/2 to 34-7/8 after the company announced third-quarter profits would be below Wall Street estimates.
Independent drug industry analyst Hemant Shah stated that the merger is not going as smoothly as hoped.
Pharmacia & Upjohn was formed through the merger of Pharmacia AB and Upjohn Co and began operations in November 1995.
Analyst Mario Corso noted that there is no earnings guidance for the beginning of 1997.
The company projected cost savings of $500 million by 1998 and has reduced its workforce by 3,000 people to date.
Pharmacia & Upjohn attributed its third-quarter earnings disappointment to short-term disruptions from the merger.
Analyst Steve Lisi indicated that the company is not realizing expected synergies.
The company blamed currency translations for its third-quarter earnings shortfall, particularly involving the Japanese yen, Italian lira, and Swedish krona.
Pharmacia & Upjohn's top drugs face competition from generic equivalents, and there are few new products in the pipeline.

St. Jude Medical Inc's third-quarter profits were affected by a missed heart valve sale to Iran, tax law changes, and a dilutive acquisition.
Ronald Matricaria is the chief executive of St. Jude Medical Inc.
St. Jude Medical Inc will not rule out acquiring Cyberonics Inc in the future.
A proposed merger between St. Jude Medical Inc and Cyberonics Inc was called off on Wednesday.
St. Jude Medical Inc owns 18 percent of Cyberonics Inc but will not exercise its option to acquire the remainder.
Matricaria declined to comment on speculation regarding issues with data from medical trials for Cyberonics' device for treating epilepsy.
St. Jude Medical Inc is the world's largest maker of heart valves and a major producer of pacemakers and other medical devices.
St. Jude Medical Inc reported third-quarter earnings of $0.44 per share, an increase from $0.42 per share a year ago.
The heart valve business of St. Jude Medical Inc showed no growth in the third quarter due to the missed order from Iran.
Changes in U.S. tax law reduced St. Jude Medical Inc's earnings by about $0.02 per share in the third quarter.

St. Jude Medical Inc agreed to make four strategic transactions to enhance its position in the medical device business.
The total value of the transactions is $665 million.
Analysts believe the transactions will likely proceed despite some risks.
Shares of St. Jude traded down 1-1/2 to 37-1/8 after the announcement.
Kurt Kruger, a medical technology analyst, expressed concerns about the possibility of the deal not going through and dilution.
St. Jude's main transaction involves acquiring Ventritex Inc in a stock swap valued at $505 million.
Ventritex is the smallest of three companies in the $500 million market for implantable defibrillators.
St. Jude is making three smaller deals to resolve legal actions and free Ventritex from cross-licensing restrictions.
The smaller deals include acquiring assets from Telectronics Pacing Systems, Medtel, and certain intellectual property rights from Intermedics.
St. Jude is the world's largest maker of heart valves and has previously acquired Pacesetter Inc to become a leading manufacturer of heart pacemakers.

Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co. reported a 16 percent increase in earnings for the third quarter.
Net profits for the quarter rose to $398 million, or 95 cents a share.
The previous year's net profits were $344 million, or 82 cents a share.
The year-ago quarter included earnings of $5 million from discontinued operations.
Sales increased by 7 percent to $3.62 billion from $3.37 billion.
The results exceeded analysts' average forecasts of 93 cents a share.
3M's stock price increased by $2 to $73.25.
3M's third quarter was the first since the spinoff of its data storage and imaging businesses into Imation Corp.
Analysts expect 3M to achieve solid growth in the fourth quarter.
3M produces a wide range of products including Scotch tape, Post-it notes, and air filters.

Cellex Biosciences Inc expects to report a strong fiscal fourth quarter ending September 30.
Cellex anticipates moving into profitability next fiscal year.
Chief executive Richard Sakowicz stated that revenues this year will be substantially up from last year.
As of June 30, Cellex had $3.6 million worth of work in process.
Cellex was formed in 1983 and makes machines for growing cell cultures.
Cellex has 60-80 percent of the $10-$15 million world market for perfusion culture systems.
In December 1993, Cellex acquired LSL Biolafitte SA, a French maker of cell culture tanks.
Biolafitte has 10-15 percent of the $100-million world culture tank market.
About 80 percent of Cellex's revenues come from sales of tank systems.
For the nine months ended June 30, tank sales provided three-quarters of revenues totaling $10.7 million.

Baxter International Inc expects to record unspecified charges against earnings in the first quarter of 1997.
The charges are related to in-process research and development acquired through purchases of Research Medical Inc and Immuno International AG.
Michael Mussallem, Baxter group vice president, stated that the amounts of the anticipated charges have not been determined.
Mussallem indicated that the Research Medical charge will be substantial, potentially half the transaction value.
Baxter expects to have a better grasp on the estimated charges by the end of January.
Baxter announced it reached a definitive agreement to acquire Research Medical for about $236 million, or $23.50 per share.
Baxter expects to close its purchase of Immuno in two to six weeks.
Baxter agreed in August to buy Immuno for $715 million over three years.
The acquisition of Immuno was delayed due to lack of approval from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission and a postponed bond issue.
Baxter stated that the Research Medical acquisition is expected to be accretive to earnings in 1998, but not significantly so.

Aon Corp acquired Alexander & Alexander Services Inc for $1.23 billion.
The acquisition price of $1.23 billion is considered reasonable by industry analysts.
Aon will pay $317.5 million in cash for Alexander & Alexander's Series B preferred shares.
American International Group Inc (AIG) purchased the Series B preferred shares for $200 million in June 1994.
Analyst Gary Ransom stated that AIG benefited from the transaction.
Aon previously purchased Inchcape Plc's Bain Hogg Group unit for $250 million.
Analysts expected Aon to make a major acquisition.
Thomas Rosencrants, an analyst, stated that the deal is beneficial for both Aon and Alexander & Alexander.
Patrick Ryan is expected to lead the combined operation after the merger.
Frank Zorb, the chief executive of Alexander & Alexander, is expected to step aside after the merger.

Holiday sales for top U.S. retailers are currently disappointing.
Wall Street is withholding judgment on the retailing fourth quarter profit outlook until all sales data is available.
UBS Securities retailing analyst Annie Erner stated that there is nervousness about retailers' upcoming reports, which is affecting stock prices.
Shares in most retailers fell after J.C. Penney Co Inc announced that its fourth-quarter earnings would not meet expectations.
Dayton Hudson Corp reported early holiday results that were not impressive.
Nordstrom Inc warned of lower holiday sales, contributing to concerns among retail analysts.
Analysts remain confident that major retailers like Sears Roebuck and Co, May Department Stores, and Federated Department Stores will meet or exceed expectations.
Shares in Sears, May, and Federated fell despite analysts' confidence.
Toys R Us Inc and Saks Holdings Inc were the only major retail stocks to perform well amid a general decline.
Bed Bath & Beyond Inc reported good same-store sales for December, which raised hopes for specialty retailers.

Eli Lilly & Co's new anti-schizophrenia drug, Zyprexa, is expected to receive approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
Zyprexa is known generically as olanzapine.
Approval of Zyprexa would position Lilly ahead of other new anti-schizophrenia medications entering the U.S. market.
Lilly spokesman Edward West stated there have been no indications of issues from the FDA that could cause a delay in approval.
Wall Street analysts predict that FDA approval for Zyprexa could occur this month.
The FDA has not scheduled an advisory committee hearing for Zyprexa.
Analysts believe Zyprexa will likely be approved without committee deliberations.
Zyprexa received a positive opinion from the European Union's Committee for Proprietary Medicinal Products in June.
Analysts expect European marketing approval for Zyprexa to follow.
Competing products from Abbott Laboratories Inc, Zeneca Group Plc, and Pfizer Inc are expected to enter the market within the next 12 months.

Ford Motor Co. may sell its interest in Budget Rent a Car.
Ford holds non-voting preferred shares and an option to acquire Budget's common shares.
The common shares of Budget are owned by investor John Nevin.
Ford could sell its option or direct the sale of the common shares.
If a sale occurs, Budget would be the fifth major rental car agency to change hands since 1994.
WEFA Group automotive consultant George Magliano stated that the car rental business is not profitable.
Jon LeSage, editor of Auto Rental News, noted that there is a new interest in the rental car business from investors.
Ford declined to comment on a Wall Street Journal article regarding a potential sale to Team Rental Group Inc. for $350 million.
No agreements have been reached regarding the sale of Budget, according to spokeswoman Kimberly Mulcahy.
Ford's planned purchase of Budget was intended to improve its performance.

Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp. agreed to buy Value Health Inc. for about $1.3 billion in stock.
The acquisition caused Columbia shares to fall by $1 to $39.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Some analysts believe the acquisition indicates Columbia's intention to compete with health insurers and HMOs.
Ken Laudan, a healthcare industry analyst, stated that Columbia's intentions are now clear.
Other analysts view the acquisition as a defensive move to gain buying power similar to its customers.
An unidentified analyst suggested that Columbia aims to offer integrated and affordable healthcare services.
Columbia Chairman Richard Scott stated that Value Health fits well into Columbia's integrated delivery system.
Value Health had 1995 revenues of nearly $1.9 billion.
Value Health's stock price dropped from the high $50s to $21.875 before the acquisition announcement.
The proposed Columbia stock transaction is worth about $23.35 per share based on previous closing prices.

Australian oil and gas companies are being acquired by foreign companies.
Analysts predict a positive future for the sector due to higher oil prices and a deregulated gas market.
In 1996, approximately A$2.5 billion worth of takeovers were announced in Australia's oil and gas sector.
An additional A$600 million worth of asset sales occurred as some non-oil and gas companies exited the local market.
Local oil groups with low share prices and overseas assets are attracting foreign companies.
Timothy Savage, an analyst at Hartley Poynton, stated that overseas investors recognize the value of oil and gas assets.
Mobil Corp made a bid of A$1.78 billion for Ampolex Ltd in February, marking the largest bid in the sector for the year.
Clyde Petroleum Plc acquired Crusader Ltd, and Premier Oil Plc and Cairn Energy Plc made bids for Discovery Petroleum NL and Command Petroleum Ltd, respectively.
Stuart Baker, an analyst with BT Securities, noted that companies with offshore oil assets have been the focus of takeovers.
Baker also mentioned that the rise in oil prices was not the primary reason for corporate activity in the sector.

St George Bank Ltd announced a merger with Advance Bank Australia Ltd valued at A$2.65 billion.
This merger is St George's fifth attempt in the past two years.
The merger would create Australia's fifth largest bank with assets of A$40 billion and a market capitalisation of A$4.5 billion.
St George plans to offer A$7.30 for each share in Advance Bank.
Advance shareholders would receive A$2.10 in cash, a 20 cent special cash dividend, and new St George shares valued up to A$5.00.
The total offer value represents a 20 percent increase over the average Advance Bank share price over the previous five trading days.
Advance shareholders will also receive an interim dividend of 20 cents, payable in February.
St George plans to raise A$360 million in a new capital raising to fund the bid.
The merger is expected to reduce annual combined expenses by 15 percent or A$140 million before tax.
Advance shares increased by over 10 percent following the announcement.

The Australian Gas Light Co (AGL) is interested in Tenneco Inc's Australian assets if they are put up for sale.
AGL's managing director is Len Bleasel.
Tenneco has announced a restructure that includes a proposed merger of its energy arm with El Paso Energy Corp.
Bleasel stated that AGL has received inquiries about potential interest in Tenneco's assets.
Bleasel mentioned that AGL would wait to see the outcome of the Tenneco-El Paso restructure.
Tenneco's Australian assets include a 1700 km pipeline in South Australia and a 760 km gas pipeline in southwest Queensland.
AGL is a broad-based energy company and is interested in asset sales across the country.
A Tenneco Australia spokeswoman stated that no decision has been made regarding the future of Tenneco's Australian assets.
AGL's main market is New South Wales, with additional businesses in Victoria, Western Australia, and the Northern Territory.
AGL has interests in China, Poland, and Chile.

CSR Ltd is expected to report a net profit before abnormals of between A$146 million and A$160 million for the six months to September 30.
CSR stated that its 1996/97 first half profit was likely to be 20 percent lower than previously expected.
Analysts have adjusted their 1996/97 profit estimates for CSR after a profit warning issued last month.
Annual profit forecasts for CSR now range between A$250 million and A$272 million.
CSR reported a nine percent fall in net profit before abnormals of A$193.4 million in the 1995/96 first half.
Sean Cooney from ANZ Securities forecasted CSR's first half pre-abnormals net profit to be A$156.6 million.
Greg Burns at BZW Australia forecasted CSR's first half net profit to be A$160 million and annual profit to be A$260 million.
Mark Cotton from Prudential Bache Securities forecasted CSR's pre-abnormal net profit for the half to be A$160 million and A$272 million for the year.
Michael Brown at McIntosh Securities forecasted CSR's net profit before abnormals to be A$146 million for the half and around A$250 million for the year.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett's Fabian Babich forecasted CSR's pre-abnormal net profit for the half to be between A$145 million and A$150 million and about A$260 million for the year.

Rupert Murdoch's global media group, The News Corp Ltd, reported an 8.1 percent fall in net profit for the first quarter of 1996/97.
Analysts had forecast a healthy rise in net profit for News Corp.
News Corp reported net profits of A$283 million for the three months ended September 30, down from A$308 million a year earlier.
The weaker profit was attributed to poorer returns in U.S. TV, Australian newspapers, and book publishing.
Analysts had forecast net profit before abnormal items to be around A$320-330 million, which would be an increase of around 15 percent.
Net profit before abnormals for News Corp came in at A$285 million.
A Sydney-based media analyst described the results as 'very flat' and not as expected.
The analyst indicated that News Corp could still achieve a 20 percent rise in net profits for the 1996/97 year.
News Corp's profit was bolstered by the success of the movie Independence Day and its British newspapers and book publishing.
Independence Day grossed more than US$670 million worldwide, making it the third highest-grossing film in box office history.

The Australian government plans to toughen the rules for the rollout of optic fibre cable.
Optus Communications' chief executive officer is Zygmunt Switkowski.
Switkowski stated that the new rules could make Optus' cable rollout plans uneconomic.
Optus is rolling out fibre optic cables overhead on existing telephone poles at a cost of around A$3.0 billion.
Switkowski mentioned that underground cabling could add hundreds of millions of dollars to Optus' cost base.
The Australian government requires Optus and Telstra Corp to obtain local council approval for cable installation.
The new cable rollout rules will start on July 1, 1997.
The telecommunications industry in Australia will be liberalised on July 1, 1997.
Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston announced the cable rollout changes.
Several councils have taken Optus Vision to court, but the rollout has continued under the current telecommunications regime.

Placer Dome Inc announced plans to expand in the Asia-Pacific region through takeover offers worth a total of US$600 million for two Australian-listed gold miners.
Placer Dome launched takeover offers for Highlands Gold Ltd and a mop-up offer for Placer Pacific Ltd.
If successful, Placer Dome will control PNG's biggest gold mine, the Porgera mine, which is expected to produce over 940,000 ounces of gold in calendar 1996.
John Willson, Placer Dome's CEO, stated that the takeover recognizes the prospectivity of the Asia-Pacific region.
Willson indicated there are no plans to acquire more assets in the Asia-Pacific region.
Placer Pacific has increased its exploration activity in Asia in recent years, with programs in China, Indonesia, and the Philippines.
The takeover bids were well received by investors, causing shares of Highlands and Placer Pacific to rise.
Highlands stated that Placer Dome's offer of 75 cents for each Highlands share was inadequate.
Placer Pacific advised its shareholders to take no action on the bid.
Placer Pacific was partly floated in 1986 by its parent company, which plans to buy out the remaining 24.6 percent it does not own through a share swap.

James Hardie Industries Ltd reported a first half net profit of A$27.6 million for the six months ended September 30, 1996.
The reported net profit represents a 12.1 percent fall before abnormals.
James Hardie is 27.23 percent owned by New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd.
Managing director Keith Barton expects the second half result to be significantly down on the first half.
Analysts expect full year earnings forecasts to be trimmed from A$53-A$54 million to around A$50 million.
The outlook for U.S. businesses is very positive for the second half of 1996/97 and into 1997/98.
The outlook for Australian operations is described as bleak in the short term.
James Hardie stated that profit for the full year will reflect a marked deterioration on last year's results.
The first half downturn was attributed to a fall in earnings from Australian building products due to lower housing starts.
U.S. fibre cement production sold out during the six months to September, and production capacity was increased by more than 40 percent.

Australian airlines and tourist operators are concerned about Australia's declining share of Japanese tourists taking overseas holidays.
An action plan has been formed by these operators to address the decline.
The details of the action plan are guided by Qantas Airways Ltd and Ansett Airlines Ltd.
Ansett Airlines Ltd is jointly owned by News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd.
Qantas and Ansett are experiencing lower yields due to reduced airfares on the Japan route.
Col Hughes, Qantas' group general manager Pacific and Japan, stated that the decline in market share is serious for the A$14-billion Australian tourism industry.
Australia's share of the Japanese market has fallen by 0.5 percentage points over the past eight months.
Hughes indicated that Australia is losing market share to Europe and the United States, particularly Hawaii.
The Australian government plans to cut 25 percent of the budget for the Australian Tourism Commission (ATC).
Craig Wallace, Ansett's general manager of international services, suggested increasing capacity on the Japan route to boost tourist numbers.

Neil Gamble is the chief executive officer of Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd.
Gamble expressed hope for tax concessions on earnings from foreign gamblers despite previous rejections.
Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd has a 12-year monopoly to operate the only legal casino in Sydney, Australia.
The casino operator has been negotiating with the New South Wales state government for 15 months for a tax rate similar to other Australian casinos.
Gamble was appointed CEO in mid-October after leaving Australis Media Ltd.
Gamble has discussed the tax issue with NSW state premier Bob Carr, who plans to make a decision in early 1997.
The casino seeks a 10 percent tax rate concession to compete with rival operators Crown Ltd, Jupiters Ltd, and Burswood.
Gamble stated that without the tax concession, the Sydney casino is uncompetitive in the high-roller market.
High-rollers typically spend between A$100,000 and tens of millions of dollars at casinos.
The high-roller market is valued at approximately A$200 million for Australian casinos, with Sydney's share being about A$100 million.

Qantas Airways Ltd and Ansett Airlines Ltd are planning aggressive cost-cutting programs.
Analysts believe these cost-cutting programs can be implemented without affecting services.
Both airlines are facing profit pressures due to a stronger Australian dollar, higher fuel prices, a soft domestic market, and international competition.
Peter Harbison, managing director of the Centre for Asia Pacific Aviation, stated that Australian airlines are considered high-cost operators compared to global standards.
Qantas announced an increase in its cost-cutting program by about A$100 million for the 1996/97 year, raising the target to A$430 million.
Ansett plans to cut A$150 million from its annual cost base of A$3 billion.
Harbison noted that airlines worldwide, including Qantas and Ansett, will need to reduce costs for the foreseeable future.
Investors are particularly focused on Qantas due to its aggressive cost-cutting measures aimed at meeting profit estimates.
Qantas has not disclosed specific areas for cost cuts but aims to reduce costs across the board.
Analysts indicated that Qantas could cut costs by outsourcing engineering and maintenance and reducing expenses in less visible areas like accounts and marketing.

Corporate Australia is expected to pursue takeovers in 1997, particularly in the banks, media, and resources sectors.
Brokers estimate that there were approximately A$8.5 billion worth of takeovers and share buy-backs in 1996.
The value of takeovers and share buy-backs increased from A$5.9 billion in 1995 and A$2.0 billion in 1994.
Takeovers and share buy-backs are viewed as methods to enhance growth in earnings per share.
The largest takeover in 1997 was the A$2.0 billion acquisition of TNT Ltd by Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV.
Chris Mackay, executive director at broker SBC Warburg, stated that there is rationalisation and international interest in Australian industries.
Analysts noted that Australia's low inflation and low economic growth create favorable conditions for takeovers.
Merv Peacock, head of marketable securities at the Australian Mutual Provident Society, indicated that companies seek efficiencies through acquisitions due to low inflation.
Profits have been declining for 18 months, with industrials affected by the slowing economy and resource companies impacted by lower commodity prices.
Craig Drummond from J.B. Were & Son predicted increased takeover activity in the gold sector due to falling gold valuations.

Kerry Packer is Australia's biggest gambler and a patron of Las Vegas casinos.
Packer's media group, Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL), acquired management control at Sydney Harbour Casino.
PBL will spend A$340 million on a 10 percent stake in Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd (SHC) and 85 percent of the management contract from Showboat Inc.
PBL chairman Brian Powers stated that the investment would yield attractive financial returns over time.
Powers described the transaction as a major move into the gaming industry for PBL.
PBL aims to build a third core business alongside its television and publishing businesses.
PBL has an option over part of Showboat's remaining 16.1 percent stake in SHC.
Showboat president Kell Houssels stated that the transaction allows for a superior return on investment while maintaining a major ownership position in the Sydney casino.
Kerry Packer has sought control of the Sydney casino for the past three years.
Packer previously led a consortium that bid for the Sydney casino license in 1994 but lost to a Showboat-led consortium.

British Telecom announced a merger with MCI Communications to create a $54 billion group.
The merger is the largest in Britain's corporate history.
The new entity will be called Concert Plc and will serve 43 million customers in 70 countries.
BT already owned 20 percent of MCI prior to the merger.
The merger aims to combine BT's financial resources with MCI's market expertise.
MCI shareholders would receive up to $3.8 billion in cash and new Concert American Depositary Shares.
BT plans to pay its shareholders a special dividend of 35 pence per share, totaling an estimated two billion pounds.
Analysts estimate the total value of the deal to be about $22 billion.
The new company will have headquarters in London and Washington and operate under the BT and MCI brand names.
BT has been seeking a major acquisition since its failed merger with Cable and Wireless in May.

British Telecom announced its agreement to acquire the rest of MCI Communications.
The merged company will be called Concert Plc.
Concert Plc will be the world's second-largest telecommunications group.
British Telecom already owned 20 percent of MCI Communications.
The total value of MCI is $25.2 billion.
British Telecom will issue stock and cash worth $20.1 billion for the 80 percent of MCI it does not own.
The deal is the largest between a British and American company.
Concert Plc will have 43 million business and residential customers in 70 countries.
MCI shareholders will receive 0.54 new American Depositary Shares for every MCI share.
Each Concert ADS is equivalent to one British Telecom American Depositary Share and $6 cash.

British Telecommunications merged with MCI of the U.S.
Analysts suggested that BT's shares should be valued at around four pounds each.
The merger is described as the biggest trans-Atlantic deal in history.
By 1306 GMT, almost 56 million BT shares had been traded.
BT's stock price increased by 28.5 pence to 379.5 pence.
One analyst noted that the merger would change perceptions of BT's international operations.
The analyst estimated BT's true stock value at nearer 4.30 pounds.
Analysts were divided on the impact of the $20 billion MCI merger on BT's share price.
BT's revenues are currently governed by a regulatory price cap for 60 percent of its income.
BT's share of the European population for which they will have a license could rise to 90 million.

Dominion Resources executives were in bid talks with East Midlands Electricity to negotiate a takeover price.
The meeting included Dominion's chairman, chief finance officer, lawyers, and East Midlands' chairman Nigel Rudd and chief executive Norman Askew.
The meeting took place in London at 1700 GMT.
East Midlands Electricity stated it would reject any offer around 608 pence per share.
An offer at 608 pence per share would value East Midlands at 1.2 billion pounds ($2 billion).
Dominion Resources indicated it was considering an offer not much above 608 pence per share.
East Midlands Electricity launched a share buy-back to redistribute cash to shareholders.
East Midlands' shares ended at 612 pence, an increase of 8.5 pence.
Analysts suggested Dominion would need to start bid talks at 650 pence per share.
The Labour Party has threatened to impose a windfall tax on utilities if it wins the next general election.

British Telecommunications Plc (BT) has been a privatised business for twelve years.
BT's staff has been reduced by half during this period.
BT has few growth prospects in a competitive market.
BT's market performance has been negatively affected by disputes with industry regulator Don Cruickshank.
BT's shares have underperformed compared to rivals in the FTSE telecoms sector by almost six percent since early June 1995.
BT's shares have lagged the FTSE All-Share index by over 20 percent.
Analysts believe that investors in the European telecommunications sell-off have less risk under a more lenient regulatory regime.
The regulatory regime for Deutsche Telekom is described as supportive and provides high earnings visibility until 2001.
BT employs about 130,000 staff and has a debt-to-equity ratio of around seven percent.
Since 1994, approximately 110,000 jobs have been eliminated at BT.

British Telecommunications (BT) and MCI are seeking to partner with Nippon Telegraph and Telephone (NTT).
The Japanese government has decided to restructure NTT into three parts under one holding company.
BT has expressed support for NTT's restructuring as a step towards liberalizing Japan's telecoms market.
BT aims to merge with MCI to create a new company called Concert Plc.
BT believes that a partnership with NTT would enhance its position in the Asian telecoms markets.
Analysts have noted that establishing partial ownership of NTT could lead to earnings dilution for BT.
John Tysoe, a telecoms analyst, stated that a partnership with NTT would be highly beneficial for BT.
Foreign companies face challenges in acquiring stakes in NTT due to high costs and earnings dilution.
There are foreign ownership restrictions on NTT that will remain in place until next year.
BT is interested in forming a global alliance with NTT, potentially through a marketing agreement.

Orange Plc announced that customers will be able to use mobile phones for chatting, data transfer, and faxing in Germany, France, Switzerland, Malaysia, Thailand, and Singapore by the end of 1997.
Orange has a roaming agreement with Swiss PTT.
Colin Tucker, the technical and operations director of Orange Group, expressed hope for future roaming in Hong Kong and Scandinavia.
Orange has 573,000 subscribers who can access enhanced services after passing credit checks and paying a 250 stg deposit.
Orange has a full roaming agreement in Germany and a partial agreement in France focused on Paris.
Talks are ongoing to expand roaming agreements to more European and Asian countries.
The financial details of the Swiss roaming agreement are confidential.
Initially, only subscribers in Geneva can use Swiss PTT's Natel City network, with plans to expand to Basel and Zurich by early 1997.
Orange aims to provide customers with the best value for money through its roaming services.
Orange's technology is based on DCS-1800, similar to Vodafone Group and British Telecom's Cellnet.

Cable & Wireless (C&W) announced the appointment of Graham Wallace as chief executive of Cable and Wireless Communications.
Cable and Wireless Communications was formed by merging C&W's Mercury unit, Nynex Corp's NYNEX CableComms Group, Bell Cablemedia Plc, and Videotron Holdings Plc.
Richard Brown, chief executive of C&W, stated that Graham Wallace was their first choice for the position.
Graham Wallace is currently a director at Granada Group and has experience in television from his time at BSkyB.
C&W is primarily a telecommunications business and has limited experience in television.
An analyst expressed skepticism about Wallace's suitability for the cable business.
C&W's shares decreased by 2.5 pence to 485.5 pence, while NYNEX CableComms shares increased by 5.5 pence to 108.5 pence.
C&W plans to finalize the cable merger in the spring.
Richard Brown acknowledged that the merger is complicated but stated that it is on track.
Brown indicated that a finance director would be announced next.

Angry British businesses expressed dismay after news of another overhaul of telephone prefixes.
Telecommunications watchdog Oftel announced plans to create billions of new phone numbers.
Britain has barely recovered from 'PhONEday' in April 1995, when many old numbers were made obsolete.
Simon Sperryn, chief executive of the London Chamber of Commerce & Industry, stated that changes mean more disruption and cost to businesses.
PhONEday cost British Telecommunications 100 million pounds ($166 million).
Companies have to pay thousands of pounds to notify business contacts and change stationery and logos when numbers change.
London dialing codes will be lengthened by a uniform 020 prefix in the year 2000.
Current London codes of 0171 and 0181 will be shortened to 7 and 8, respectively, to be dialed after 020.
Northern Ireland, Cardiff, and southern English coastal cities will each get a new prefix starting with 02.
Prefixes of 03 to 06 are being kept for future generations.

British Telecommunications Plc (BT) is seeking regulatory approval for a $20 billion merger with MCI Communications Corp.
The proposed merger is the largest transatlantic deal in history.
The merger is being reviewed by British, American, and European regulators.
Regulatory approval in America depends on the openness of the British telecom market compared to the U.S. market.
AT&T Corp has claimed it lacks the competitive advantages in Britain that BT will have in the U.S. after acquiring MCI.
AT&T is requesting BT to lower its transit costs for transporting calls.
AT&T wants equal access to the British market, allowing customers to connect without dialing special numbers.
BT is unlikely to change its policy on equal access due to cost-effectiveness concerns.
BT may consider adjusting its transit charges as part of the negotiations.
The European Commission is expected to investigate the merger further, with a decision due soon.

British Telecommunications (BT) admitted to not sharing the same culture as its merger partner MCI Communications.
BT reported robust third quarter profits due to healthy demand for its products and services.
BT's chief executive, Sir Peter Bonfield, acknowledged the cultural pitfalls of mergers.
Commentators have described BT as 'staid' and MCI as 'spunky'.
Sir Peter Bonfield stated that MCI staff he met were enthusiastic about the planned $20 billion merger.
BT expects European and American regulators to approve the merger by autumn.
BT's third quarter pretax profits rose to 909 million pounds from 829 million pounds.
BT announced plans to buy the 80 percent of MCI that it did not already own.
The new group formed from the merger will be called Concert Plc.
BT aims to become the second telecom operator in continental Europe as markets open to competition in 1998.

Shareholders in Hanson Plc approved the final part of the group's four-way split-up.
About 98 percent of shareholders voted for the plan.
The approval allows the Energy Group division to be spun off on Monday.
Hanson Plc was a prominent conglomerate in the 1980s under Lord Hanson and Lord White.
Hanson announced its split into separate tobacco, chemicals, energy, and building companies in January.
