The Energy Group includes Peabody Coal and Eastern.
Peabody Coal is the world's largest private coal producer.
Eastern is Britain's fourth-largest electricity generator and distribution business.
Analysts believe the company has good growth prospects but is difficult to value due to its diversity.
David Campbell forecasts earnings growth of around 12 percent annually over the next two years.

Yahoo! Inc. reported a third quarter loss of $1.2 million, or 4 cents a share.
The loss in the third quarter was smaller than analysts' expectations of 7 cents a share.
In the same quarter of the previous year, Yahoo! reported a loss of $371,000, or 2 cents a share.
Sales for the third quarter increased to $5.2 million from $288,000 in the year-ago quarter.
The company spent $4 million on sales and marketing in the third quarter, compared to $275,000 a year ago.
Research and development expenses rose to $1.36 million in the third quarter.
The number of advertisers on Yahoo! increased to 340 in the third quarter from 230 in the second quarter.
Yahoo! recorded more than 1 billion hits in the quarter ended September 30.
The average number of page views per day in September was over 14 million, up from 9 million in June.
Yahoo! is an online directory that helps users find specific sites and articles on the Internet.

Apple Computer Inc. reported a $25 million profit for the last three months of its fiscal year.
Apple's profit for the quarter was 20 cents a share, contrary to expectations of a loss of around 30 cents a share.
This was the first time Apple reported a profit this year.
The operating results included a gain of $17 million, or 14 cents a share.
Apple's stock price increased by $2.25 to $28 a share in after-hours trading following the announcement.
Analysts attributed the better-than-expected performance to improved manufacturing efficiencies, lower component costs, and reduced operating expenses.
In the same quarter the previous year, Apple earned $60 million, or 48 cents a share.
Revenues for the three months ended in September fell to $2.32 billion from $3.0 billion a year ago.
For the full year, Apple posted a loss of $816 million, or $6.59 a share.
In fiscal 1995, Apple earned $424 million, or $3.45 a share.

Apple Computer Inc. will unveil a new family of portable PowerBook computers on Monday.
The new PowerBook 1400 family will be sold in mid-November with prices starting at $2,500.
The PowerBook 1400 family will feature a built-in CD-ROM drive and a bigger screen.
The models are designed to appeal to small office users and students.
The lack of a CD-ROM drive in Apple's portable computers has hindered its competition with International Business Machines Corp., Compaq Computer Corp., and Dell Computer Corp.
Analyst Bruce Steven stated that the new family will not put Apple in a leadership role but will help it compete.
Apple plans to introduce another new series of PowerBooks in the first half of 1997 with advanced multimedia and communication capabilities.
The PowerBook 1400 will replace the recalled PowerBook 5300 model.
The PowerBook 1400 will be based on a mid-range PowerPC microprocessor.
The estimated retail price for the 1400 models will range from $2,500 to $4,000 in the United States.

Apple Computer Inc. plans to release a new line of computers in 1998 that will run a new operating system.
The new operating system will be developed from scratch.
Chief Executive Gilbert Amelio stated that the new operating system will surpass Microsoft Corp.'s Windows software.
Amelio mentioned that Apple needs to distinguish itself beyond market share due to being a minority player in the marketplace.
Amelio did not provide details on the new software's appearance or its advantages over Windows.
He claimed the new software would change how people use applications like word processing and spreadsheets.
Earlier in the year, Apple announced it would abandon the overhaul of its Macintosh operating system, known as Copland.
Apple programmers will use some components of Copland but will start from scratch.
Amelio stated that improving Apple's operations and product lines is a priority before increasing revenue and market share.
Apple reported a profit of $25 million for the last three months of fiscal 1996, down from $60 million the previous year.

Cisco Systems Inc. reported a 77 percent increase in fiscal first quarter profit from operations.
The company's earnings before gains and charges rose to $320.8 million, or 47 cents a share, for the three months ended Oct. 26.
This is an increase from $181.4 million or 28 cents in the same quarter a year ago.
Net income for the quarter totaled $180.9 million, or 26 cents a share, after accounting for a $174.6 million charge for the acquisition of Telebit Corp. and a $55.1 million gain from the sale of a minority investment.
Revenues increased by 80 percent to $1.43 billion from $798.3 million.
Wall Street expected Cisco to report a profit from operations of 46 cents, according to First Call.
Analysts noted that Cisco had a solid quarter, alleviating concerns about slowing sales of networking equipment.
Cisco maintained its gross margins at 65 percent, which was better than analysts had expected.
The company attributed higher profits to strong sales across all its product lines.
Cisco's stock closed at $61.75, gaining $1.125 for the day, but slipped 25 cents to $61.50 in after-hour trading.

Novell Inc. announced it will license its technology to other software companies to increase revenue.
Novell publishes computer networking programs.
The technology being licensed is called Novell Directory Services.
Novell aims to establish Novell Directory Services as a foundation for finding people and sharing information on the Internet.
The licensing move is part of Novell's strategy to adapt its corporate networking software for global information flow.
Michael Simpson is the director of marketing for Novell's Internet infrastructure division.
Simpson stated that a common infrastructure is necessary for electronic commerce.
Novell Directory Services will help users in large networks communicate without needing complex electronic addresses.
The technology will allow communication across different computer and software standards.
Novell plans to license the technology to networking software companies, Internet service providers, and online services.

Microsoft Corp announced that it has sent the final version of Office 97 to factories.
Office 97 is expected to be Microsoft's biggest revenue generator in 1997.
Office 97 is a package of Microsoft's top-selling business programs.
Office 97 is the biggest new product from Microsoft since the release of Windows 95.
Analysts expect Office 97 to increase Microsoft's revenue by about 15 to 20 percent this year.
About half of Microsoft's $8 billion in revenue came from business applications last year.
Pete Higgins, Microsoft group vice president of applications, reported that the development team celebrated after sending the final version to manufacturing.
Office 97 features better ties to the Internet, help tools for users, and a new component called Outlook.
The standard edition of Office 97 will cost about $239 for users of existing versions of Office.
Office 97 will be available on a limited basis in December and more broadly in early January.

Bay Networks Inc. paid $99 million in cash and stock to acquire NetICs Inc.
The acquisition provides Bay Networks with Fast Ethernet switches.
Fast Ethernet switches are popular for increasing information flow in corporate networks.
Bay Networks' competitors Cisco Systems Inc. and 3Com Corp. have also acquired Fast Ethernet technology recently.
Bay Networks agreed to pay approximately $55 million in stock and $44 million in cash for NetICs.
NetICs has not reported any revenue to date.
Bay Networks will charge a substantial portion of the purchase price against earnings for the quarter ending in December.
Bay Networks' stock was trading at $21.50, down 12.5 cents on the New York Stock Exchange.
Dick Eyestone, senior vice president of Bay Networks, stated that the acquisition keeps the company updated with emerging technology.
NetICs will remain located in Acton, Mass., and was founded in 1995 by a group of engineers.

Apple Computer Inc. rehired co-founder Steve Jobs and purchased NeXT Software Inc. for $400 million.
Analysts warned that the acquisition may not significantly improve Apple's market share or financial performance.
John Rossi, an analyst at Robertson Stephens & Co., stated that Apple has a strategic mess despite the acquisition.
Apple needed an operating system after its previous attempt failed.
NeXT's technology provides a foundation for a new operating system but is not impressive enough to differentiate Macintosh from Windows computers.
An unidentified Wall Street analyst commented that hiring Jobs will not resolve Apple's issues.
NeXT sold only 50,000 computers in four years before shifting focus to software.
Some analysts expressed disappointment that Apple chose NeXT over Be Inc., a software company founded by former Apple executive Jean-Louis Gassee.
Ike Nassi, a former Apple executive, stated that the technology direction of the acquisition is positive.
Apple shares increased by 12.5 cents to $23.625 following the announcement.

Apple Computer Inc. expects a loss of up to $150 million in the latest quarter.
Apple shares fell $3.875 to $17.875, the lowest level since mid-July.
More than 16.8 million shares of Apple were traded, making it the most active issue on Nasdaq.
Industry analysts had expected Apple to post a small loss in the Christmas quarter.
Montgomery Securities analyst Kurt King stated that the loss indicates serious questions about Apple's long-term position in the consumer market.
Apple reported weak demand for its Performa personal computers, leading to an operating loss of $100 million to $150 million in its first fiscal quarter.
Apple may need further restructuring aimed at cutting another $1 billion in costs.
The company's financial troubles make it harder for customers to justify choosing a Mac over Windows PCs.
Intel Corp. is expected to unveil a new generation computer chip that could boost sales for PCs powered by Microsoft software.
Experts believe that the perception of Apple's financial trouble could deter potential customers.

Apple Computer Inc. reported a $120 million loss in the first quarter of fiscal 1997.
Apple does not expect to return to profitability until September 1997.
The loss was attributed to slow sales of Performa desktop computers during the Christmas quarter.
The loss of $120 million equaled 96 cents a share, compared to a loss of $69 million, or 56 cents a share, in the previous year.
Sales for the first fiscal quarter ended on December 27 fell to $2.13 billion from $3.15 billion.
Apple plans to develop additional restructuring programs during the second quarter.
The goal of the restructuring programs is to reduce the break-even point to $8 billion in annual revenues.
Apple aims to return to profitability by the fourth fiscal quarter, which ends on September 26, 1997.
Apple Chief Financial Officer Fred Anderson stated that the company's financial position remains sound.
Apple exited the quarter with $1.8 billion in cash and showed improvements in inventory management.

Apple Computer Inc. reported a $120 million loss in its fiscal first quarter.
Apple does not expect to report a profit until September.
Apple expects revenue for the current fiscal year to drop about 13 percent to between $8 billion and $8.5 billion.
Apple's loss equaled 96 cents a share, compared to a loss of $69 million or 56 cents a share in the same quarter last year.
Sales for the quarter ended Dec. 27 fell to $2.13 billion from $3.15 billion.
Apple attributed the quarterly loss to slow sales of Performa desktop computers during the Christmas quarter.
Analyst Lou Mazzucchelli stated that consumer concerns about Apple's future affected sales.
Apple plans to unveil its second restructuring program in two years to cut operating costs by $400 million.
Apple aims to reduce its break-even point to $8 billion in annual revenues to return to profitability by the end of September.
Standard & Poor's lowered Apple's corporate credit and debt rating, putting the company's debt into junk bond status.

The video game software industry has shown improvement after a period of decline.
Electronic Arts Inc., Activision Inc., and Spectrum Holobyte Inc. reported better-than-expected results for the December quarter.
Strong sales of games for personal computers and next-generation video game consoles contributed to the positive results.
The industry had been struggling while consumers awaited the release of advanced game machines from Sony Corp., Sega Enterprises, and Nintendo Corp.
The release of the PlayStation and Nintendo 64 has revitalized the video game industry.
David Farina, an analyst at William Blair & Co., stated that sales of video game systems are strong.
Electronic Arts reported a net income increase of 25 percent to $36.7 million for its fiscal third quarter.
Activision's net income more than doubled to $4.12 million in its Christmas quarter.
Spectrum Holobyte reported a net income of $5.7 million in the December quarter, exceeding Wall Street expectations.
Analysts predict strong earnings will continue into the March quarter due to consumer purchases of new PCs with Intel Corp.'s MMX technology.

Graham Savage resigned as chief financial officer of Rogers Communications Inc. on Monday.
Savage had been with Rogers Communications Inc. for 21 years.
The company stated that Savage resigned to 'pursue other interests.'
Analyst Andrew McCreath described Savage's departure as the most detrimental to the company in recent times.
Analyst John Drolet expressed concern that Savage's resignation is not good for Rogers and suggested that other employees might leave.
Rogers Communications Inc. owns Rogers Cantel, a wireless communications firm.
The company has sold U.S. and Canadian assets in the past year to reduce its debts.
Rogers accumulated most of its debt when it acquired Maclean Hunter Ltd. and the Toronto Sun group for C$3.1 billion.
As of June 30, Rogers' total long-term debt increased to C$4.88 billion from C$4.07 billion a year earlier.
In 1995, Rogers reported revenue of C$2.69 billion.

Toronto stocks reached their 51st record close of 1996 on Monday.
The rally in interest-sensitive issues was attributed to expectations of a cut in Canadian interest rates.
MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie stated that the market is anticipating another Bank of Canada cut.
Canada's central bank has reduced short-term interest rates 19 times since May 1995, decreasing the key bank rate by 4.75 percent.
Beattie predicted that bank stocks would continue to rally if there is another Bank of Canada cut.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index gained 17.95 points to close at 5609.26 points.
The overall market was mixed, with declining issues outnumbering advances 478 to 447 and 300 issues unchanged.
A total of 88.7 million shares were traded, worth C$1.28 billion (US$958 million).
The financial services sector increased by more than two percent on Monday.
Edper Group Ltd. receipts rose C$7.50 to close at C$78.50 amid speculation regarding the World Financial Center in New York.

The Toronto Stock Exchange posted its 53rd record close of 1996 on Wednesday.
The TSE 300 Composite Index closed at 5749.92 points after gaining 85.45 points.
A total of 118.1 million shares were traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
The value of shares traded was C$2.18 billion (US$1.64 billion), the third highest ever.
Michael Metz of Oppenheimer & Co, Inc. stated that Toronto is generally under-owned in North America.
Canadian bank stocks have seen increased foreign interest following upgrades by Morgan Stanley.
Best stated that the valuation range of Canadian banks is appropriate compared to U.S. peers.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-indices increased except for gold issues, which declined.
The conglomerate group gained more than five percent.
Bank of Montreal's stock rose C$0.95 to C$45.00 on over three million shares traded.

Toronto stocks ended lower on Thursday due to investor profit-taking and a sell-off in gold issues.
The Toronto Stock Exchange key 300 Composite Index lost 43.9 points, ending at 5922.2 points.
The 300 Index nearly reached the 6000-point level the previous day.
Ron Meisels, president of P & C Holdings Ltd, stated that some profit-taking was justified after the Index's rise this month.
The 300 Index gained more than five percent since the beginning of November.
Trading volume was heavy, with 124 million shares traded worth C$1.85 billion (US$1.38 billion).
Weak gold bullion prices contributed to the decline in Toronto's gold stocks.
London gold prices fell to their lowest level in nearly two years, dropping to as low as C$375.70 an ounce.
Only three of Toronto's 14 sub-indices rose: conglomerates, oils, and pipelines.
The gold sector lost nearly 2.9 percent, followed by declines in banks, transports, and consumer products.

The Toronto Stock Exchange posted a record close on Wednesday.
The TSE's key 300 Composite Index rose 10.85 points to 5986.41.
Trading volume was 108.2 million shares worth C$1.9 billion (US$1.4 billion).
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, eight rose, led by conglomerates, banks, pipelines, and media.
Falling sectors included oils, transports, and real estate.
Barrick Gold Corp. led Toronto's active issues after a deal for a majority share in an Indonesian gold deposit.
Bank of Nova Scotia posted its first C$1 billion ($750 million) annual profit on Wednesday.
Declining stocks outnumbered advances 556 to 437, with 294 shares unchanged.
U.S. markets will be closed on Thursday due to the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday.
Barrick Gold rose 0.75 to 39.65 on more than 7.1 million shares.

The Toronto stock market ended weaker on Wednesday.
Investor profit-taking occurred in every sector except for gold.
The TSE's key 300 Composite Index dropped 30.08 points to 5910.65.
The 300 index has fallen 106 points or more than 1.7 percent since Monday.
MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie stated that the market is shaky and some investors are taking profits.
Trading involved 111.3 million shares worth C$1.8 billion.
ScotiaMcLeod senior vice-president Fred Ketchen described the situation as a middle-cycle correction and expects it to be short-lived.
Ketchen believes Toronto will continue to rise due to lower returns in fixed income markets compared to equities.
The gold sector rose nearly three percent, preventing a further decline in the index.
Declining issues outnumbered advancing ones 581 to 428, with 272 unchanged.

The Toronto Stock Exchange experienced a steep decline this week.
Analysts expect Canada's biggest equity market to resume its upward trend and outperform Wall Street in the New Year.
On Friday, Toronto's 300 Composite Index posted its largest intraday drop in nine years, losing 171 points or almost three percent to 5670.
This was Toronto's biggest intraday fall since October 22, 1987.
The index has decreased from a record of 6018 on November 28.
By Friday afternoon, Toronto stocks recovered slightly, down 40.55 points to 5801.20.
Toronto's losses on Friday were influenced by comments from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan regarding U.S. equity markets.
Profit-taking affected Toronto stocks this week as investors cashed in on recent gains.
Investment adviser Ron Meisels forecasted more weakness in the next few weeks before a return to strength.
Meisels predicted that Toronto would likely outperform New York in the first quarter of 1997.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index closed at a new all-time high of 6055 points on Tuesday.
The index increased by 53.38 points to end at 6054.86.
The trading volume was 129.3 million shares worth C$2.1 billion ($1.55 billion).
The previous record of 6018.65 points was set on November 28, 1996.
The rally was partly influenced by a rise in Wall Street, which closed at 6762.29 after gaining 53.11 points.
Intel Corp. reported stronger-than-expected fourth quarter earnings, with earnings per share increasing to $2.13 from $0.98 a year earlier.
The start of the 1996 pension season contributed to the rally in Toronto.
Dunnery Best from Midland Walwyn noted the beginning of the RRSP season.
Josef Schachter from Schachter Asset Management stated that fund managers were compelled to invest due to incoming fund money.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-indices increased, except for gold, which declined due to lower bullion prices.

The chief executive of Zellers aims to boost sales per square foot by more than a third over three years.
Millard Barron is the chief executive of Zellers and a former executive at Wal-Mart Inc.
Barron plans to increase sales from C$157 ($117) a square foot for fiscal 1997 ending Jan. 31.
Barron stated that Zellers should achieve sales of C$225 ($168) to C$250 ($187) a square foot.
Zellers is a unit of Toronto-based Hudson's Bay Co.
David Brodie, a Wood Gundy retail analyst, called Barron's goal ambitious.
Brodie estimated that Wal-Mart had sales of C$220 ($164) a square foot in Canada.
Brodie estimated Zellers' market share had fallen to 42 percent since Wal-Mart's arrival in 1994.
Wal-Mart's Canadian market share was estimated at about 43 percent.
Zellers' fiscal 1996 operating profit plunged to C$106.7 million ($79.8 million) from C$215.6 million ($161.2 million) in 1995.

The Toronto stock market closed lower for the third consecutive day on Wednesday.
The decline in the Toronto stock market was influenced by losses on Wall Street.
Ron Meisels, a Montreal-based portfolio consultant, stated that Canada often follows New York's market trends.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index fell by 17.31 points to close at 6058.67.
Trading volume on the Toronto Stock Exchange was 123.1 million shares, valued at C$1.97 billion.
Wall Street experienced volatility due to disappointing fourth quarter earnings from International Business Machines Corp.
Meisels described Toronto's three-day decline as a healthy breather after earlier strong gains.
Toronto's 14 sub-indices were evenly split between gaining and losing sectors.
The sectors that declined included gold, oil, base metals, and consumer products.
Air Canada shares increased by 0.75 to 8.00 on a volume of ten million shares.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key index ended higher on Wednesday.
The overall market finished mixed in thin trading.
Many money managers decided to invest in fixed income investments.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 24.57 points to close at 6071.28.
The turnover was 105.3 million shares worth C$1.4 billion ($1.04 billion).
Almost all of Toronto's 14 sub-indices ended higher except for transportation.
Declining stocks outpaced advances 492 to 483, with 281 issues unchanged.
Michael Metz, chief strategist at Oppenheimer & Co Inc, described the market as jittery.
Jim Doak, director of investment research at ScotiaMcLeod, noted that people are being cautious.
Many mutual fund managers are trading cautiously and awaiting market direction.

Toronto stocks closed on a firmer note on Friday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 29.85 points to reach 6101.74.
111 million shares were traded worth C$1.74 billion ($1.29 billion).
North American markets surged after the release of the U.S. January jobless rate, which edged up to 5.4 percent from 5.3 percent.
The job market has not tightened enough for employers to bid up wages.
The Federal Reserve may not raise interest rates.
Bonds rallied, dropping yields, leading Canadian investors to the Toronto stock market.
Advances on the Toronto Stock Exchange outnumbered declines 507 to 490.
Toronto's 14 sub-indices saw banks rise the most, adding two percent to hit a new high of 5972.59 points.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 82.74 points to 6855.80.

Chinese importers are expected to use import quotas for 1.3 million tonnes of palm oil to manage world and domestic prices.
China had significant stocks of edible oil, reported to be 2.8 million tonnes by the end of October 1995.
Traders indicated that China's stock could keep it out of the palm oil market until early 1997.
Malaysian palm oil futures prices reacted to news of China's approval for 1.3 million tonnes of palm oil imports.
A Singapore trader described the market reaction as panic short-covering and speculative interest.
Import licences issued in 1995 were for six months and could be extended.
Malaysian Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik stated that China approved imports of 1.3 million tonnes of palm oil between August 1996 and March 1997.
Malaysia is expected to provide 80 percent of China's palm oil, with the remainder from Indonesia.
The benchmark third position November crude palm oil futures contract was up 20 ringgit to 1,180 ringgit (US$473.33) a tonne.
Domestic Chinese palm oil prices were around 6,500 yuan ($783) a tonne.

China has banned imports of some U.S. chicken meat due to concerns about a fowl plague.
U.S. officials stated that American chickens do not have highly pathogenic avian influenza.
A U.S. quarantine official confirmed that there is no record of highly pathogenic avian influenza in domestic poultry.
The disease affects birds but does not transmit to meat or people.
Washington's agriculture attache in Beijing reported that China blocked imports of chicken meat from 10 U.S. states.
China's Administration of Animal and Plant Quarantine confirmed the ban by telephone.
A senior diplomatic source noted confusion regarding the ban on poultry meat versus poultry chicks.
A quarantine official in Beijing confirmed the ban on chicken imports but declined to provide details.
U.S. officials claimed that any ban by China on U.S. chicken meat imports was not based on sound scientific evidence.
China is the second-largest market for U.S. poultry products after Russia.

Asian grain traders were not surprised by fears that China has been cancelling soybean and soybean meal orders due to falling world prices.
A Hong Kong trader reported that prices have dropped by US$10 per tonne since Friday.
The trader stated that if cheaper material is available, buyers will likely purchase it.
The trader also mentioned that there is no unsold cargo in the market and that most has been committed.
CBOT soymeal prices closed lower on Monday amid fears of cancellations by China.
Soymeal prices closed unchanged to $4 lower, with October down $1.60 to $235.10 per tonne.
Traders reported that China purchased between 600,000 and 800,000 tonnes of soybeans and soybean meal last week.
These sales will be reflected in U.S. Department of Agriculture figures released this week.
Chinese buyers are known for their price sensitivity and are looking for better prices to increase profit margins.
China is currently in the peak soymeal consumption season and is expected to import significant quantities before the end of 1996.

Up to 100,000 tonnes of copper is held in Shanghai bonded warehouses.
Industry sources claim that this copper probably belongs to China's strategic state reserve.
Around 40,000 tonnes of the copper have been moved to warehouses near the northern port of Yingkou.
The copper was channeled into Shanghai by the China National Nonferrous Metals Import and Export Corp (CNIEC) in June and July.
It is unclear whether the 40,000 tonnes of copper have cleared customs.
The strategic reserve is administered directly by the central government's State Planning Commission.
Traders have suggested that the reserve could negotiate concessions on duties.
Once the copper arrives in Yingkou, it is subject to monitoring by the State Planning Commission.
Traders are unsure of the ownership, exact size, and future plans for the Shanghai stockpile.
CNIEC lent around 85,000 tonnes of copper onto the London Metal Exchange between April and June 1995.

China has agreed not to enforce a ban on imports of U.S. poultry until after quarantine talks in Beijing next week.
Chinese authorities have not issued a letter banning imports of U.S. poultry.
China confirmed a ban on imports of poultry and poultry products from 10 U.S. states due to fears of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI).
China is the second biggest market for U.S. poultry products, after Russia, and is the only market for chicken feet.
U.S. poultry exports to China in 1995 totaled US$445 million.
The states affected by the ban are Arkansas, Florida, Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Texas, Utah, and Wisconsin.
A delegation from Washington's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) will arrive in Beijing for talks with China's Administration of Animal and Plant Quarantine (CAPQ).
U.S. officials state that U.S. poultry is free of HPAI virus.
Chinese quarantine personnel are reportedly confused about the difference between HPAI and avian influenza (AI).
AI is prevalent worldwide, especially in wild fowl, but has not been isolated in commercial U.S. poultry flocks.

U.S. officials believe a visit by senior agricultural experts to China will resolve a deadlock affecting the Chinese market for U.S. poultry products.
A U.S. agriculture official stated that they have sufficient evidence to convince Chinese officials that there is no problem with U.S. poultry products.
Two senior U.S. agriculture officials arrived in Beijing from Washington for meetings with Chinese quarantine and agriculture officials.
The discussions will focus on a ban imposed by China on imports of poultry and poultry products from 10 U.S. states due to concerns about highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI).
China's ban on U.S. poultry imports was announced on October 10 but has not yet been enforced as Chinese officials are awaiting input from U.S. experts.
The initial talks will concentrate on the technical and scientific aspects of the poultry import dispute.
The U.S. side indicated that the issue could escalate to a trade dispute if China does not accept U.S. scientific evidence regarding HPAI.
U.S. officials noted that China's recent approval of two bovine semen centers and nine embryo transfer centers for importing U.S. veterinary technology is a positive development.
Bilateral meetings on plant health and wheat imports are scheduled for November.
U.S. diplomats and agriculture officials assert that HPAI is not present in U.S. commercial flocks, having been eradicated in the mid-1980s.

U.S. officials reported that talks aimed at preventing a Chinese ban on U.S. poultry imports were successful.
A Chinese ban on poultry imports from 10 U.S. states, valued at nearly US$500 million annually, is now unlikely to be enforced.
A U.S. diplomat in Beijing expressed optimism that the issue has been resolved and does not expect further correspondence from China.
A two-man team from Washington's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) met with China's Administration of Animal and Plant Quarantine (CAPQ) for two days.
The purpose of the talks was to assure CAPQ that U.S. poultry does not carry the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus.
Ray Miyamoto, the APHIS area director in Beijing, stated that CAPQ's primary concerns were adequately addressed.
CAPQ intends to write a report regarding the discussions, which may or may not be shared with APHIS.
The meetings concluded on Thursday, and CAPQ did not provide immediate comments.
U.S. sources characterized the talks as frank, open, and candid, indicating positive prospects for future discussions on plant quarantine issues.
Washington claims that a Chinese ban on wheat imports from certain U.S. areas is a non-tariff trade barrier.

Genetically-altered soybeans are causing little concern in China.
China is a major importer of soybeans and has its own bio-engineering programs.
Monsanto Co developed the first genetically-altered U.S. soybeans.
China has been involved in producing insect-resistant cotton and genetically-altered soybeans, corn, and rice.
Monsanto has faced opposition from environmental groups in the United States and Europe.
The genetically-altered soybeans are resistant to the weed killer Roundup, which is also a Monsanto product.
Industry executives believe China would be interested in pest-resistant soybeans due to insect problems in their crops.
Chinese research on pest and insecticide resistant crops is reportedly a decade behind Monsanto's efforts.
Monsanto is negotiating for cooperative projects in China.
Greenpeace is preparing to picket a ship believed to be carrying Monsanto soybeans in Hamburg.

Around 300,000 tonnes of copper is being added to China's central reserve authorities.
About a third of the copper quantity is currently clearing through customs.
Shanghai bonded warehouses have held up to 100,000 tonnes of copper.
The ownership and purpose of the copper have been contentious since June.
Japanese Sumitomo Corp reported massive copper-trading losses totaling US$2.6 billion.
The copper was reportedly bought by China National Non-ferrous Metals Import/Export Corp (CNIEC).
Central authorities bought the copper to cover 85,000 tonnes lent to the market in March 1995.
A European trader stated that the 85,000 tonnes was additional to the tonnages undergoing customs formalities.
Between 40,000 to 50,000 tonnes of copper was shipped from Shanghai to bonded warehouses in north China.
Another 50,000-60,000 tonnes will be delivered to Chinese ports in January or early February.

Copper stored in Shanghai warehouses is being offered in small lots to European trading houses.
The copper is being sold at a high premium to set a benchmark price for its eventual sale to China's strategic stockpile.
Estimates of copper reserves brought into China in recent months range between 100,000 and 150,000 tonnes.
A European trader in Beijing was offered copper by the China National Non-ferrous Metals Import and Export Corp (CNIEC) at around $2,100 a tonne.
The price of $2,100 a tonne reflects the London Metal Exchange (LME) cash price plus a premium of $130.
CNIEC has declined to comment on the market talk regarding the copper.
The copper is said to be owned by Chinese trading firms that shipped it to Shanghai in expectation of a purchase by the central stockpile.
Traders indicated that the copper probably belonged to China's state reserve, which lent around 85,000 tonnes of copper through CNIEC onto the LME between April and June 1995.
CNIEC's former president Fang Dachang stated that China was likely to take back the copper in the fourth quarter of the year.
The metal was taken from LME warehouses at about $2,400 a tonne before three month LME copper prices fell below $1,800.

Far East traders stated that China is unlikely to need to buy rice on the international market due to flood damage to domestic crops.
No inquiries for rice from China were reported by traders in China, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Thailand.
A Chinese trader in Shanghai ruled out large demand from the central grain reserve, COFCO, or the grain bureaux.
China's Futures Herald reported that flood damage has reduced the early rice harvest but total output for 1996 is expected to be unaffected.
The increase in the area under rice cultivation this year is expected to mitigate the impact of the reduced early harvest.
Rice imports require central government approval, and the process of issuing quotas and licenses can take weeks or months.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies reported that flooding in Hunan has prevented farmers from planting rice for the autumn harvest.
Thorir Gudmundsson stated that many farmers lost the first crop of rice and are now dependent on food aid until their next crop.
The Chicago Board of Trade reported that the notion of China needing to import rice provided support to rice futures prices.
Chicago rice futures prices have remained steady over the past three months, according to traders.

U.S. experts are working to assure China that their chicken is safe.
It is difficult to determine the origin of poultry exported to China due to the scale of processing in the United States.
A U.S. agriculture expert stated that it is impossible to identify the origin of chickens in a shipment from Arkansas.
A senior U.S. diplomatic source mentioned that poultry shipments could be certified as free from quarantinable diseases.
U.S. poultry exports to China are valued at approximately US$500 million annually.
A disease scare occurred when the Chinese press reported a ban on poultry from Oklahoma and Missouri.
Chinese quarantine officials confirmed the ban, linking it to viscerotropic velogenic Newcastle disease (VVND).
VVND was discovered in Oklahoma and Missouri during the summer.
A Chinese quarantine official stated that the ban would remain in effect despite U.S. claims about the disease being confined to pet birds.
A U.S. source reported meeting with Chinese quarantine officials and mentioned upcoming talks on agricultural issues in California.

China has a surplus of steel, leading to increased competition among suppliers.
Prices of steel have decreased by 10 percent or more in recent months.
Cold-rolled steel prices range from $400 to $430 per tonne, while galvanized steel is priced up to $100 less.
Reports indicate that hundreds of thousands of tonnes of galvanized steel are stored at Chinese ports, but these reports are unverified.
China is receiving a large amount of cheap steel, primarily from the former Soviet Union.
Industry executives have a pessimistic outlook on the recovery of the Chinese steel market.
Official Chinese press reports indicate that steel imports in the first five months of 1995 were 6.83 million tonnes, an increase of 18.9 percent from the same period in 1994.
Steel exports during the same period decreased by 31.8 percent to 2.59 million tonnes.
The influx of European steel makers into Asia has increased the variety of quality products available in China.
China's steel stockpile is estimated at 30 million tonnes, according to Jason Zheng from Morgan Stanley.

Russia's Gazprom plans to double exports to Europe by 2010 primarily through the Yamal pipeline project.
The Yamal pipeline project is estimated to cost $40 billion.
Energy analysts have expressed concerns about the timing of the Yamal project due to oversupply in Europe.
A senior European energy specialist stated that Europe is at saturation level for the next 10 years.
The Yamal-Europe project aims to build a gas pipeline network of 4,107 km from the Yamal peninsula to Germany via Belarus and Poland.
Gazprom intends to raise capital for the Yamal project by offering American Depositary Shares.
The Yamal system will have an initial capacity of 83 billion cubic metres per year, with 52 bcm allocated to Western Europe.
Gazprom aims to increase its export capacity to 124 billion bcm by 1997 and 154 bcm by 1999.
Sales outside the former Soviet Union were 117.4 bcm in 1995.
Gazprom has secured Western credits for parts of the Yamal link but lacks financing for the main system.

Russia announced plans for lower electricity and rail transport prices to boost industrial output.
President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree cutting wholesale electricity charges for industrial and residential customers by an average of 10 percent from November 1.
The decree aims to reduce rail transport charges by setting tariffs based on new electricity pricing rules.
Yeltsin's decree includes plans to create a wholesale natural gas market by next year.
The decree aims to improve tax collection by addressing pricing structures.
Privatised aluminium smelters in Russia expect to save money due to lower electricity and transport costs.
Western economists expressed doubt about the sustainability of Yeltsin's decree, viewing it as a short-term solution to the budget deficit.
Boris Arlyuk, managing director of Alumconsult, stated that Russia's average industrial electricity prices are higher than global rates.
Russian smelters often do not pay full price for electricity, contributing to a cycle of non-payments among aluminium plants and regional utilities.
The decree includes provisions for gas and electricity producers to be liable for taxes on debt collection proceeds.

Russia's new grain traders are struggling to succeed in a market that is free of state control but lacks basic market structures.
Preliminary data from the State Statistics Committee indicates that this year's gross grain harvest in Russia is 74.6 million tonnes, an eight percent increase from the 30-year low of 30 million tonnes in 1995.
The absence of local equivalents to the Chicago Board of Trade or Canadian Wheat Board leaves traders to navigate market rumors and search for grain.
Traders describe the current market as chaotic, with producers preferring cash on delivery and a general distrust of financial sophistication due to the legacy of Soviet collective farming.
Independent agriculture analyst Andrei Sizov of SovEcon Ltd consultancy stated that there are excellent arbitrage opportunities in agricultural commodities from Russia and former Soviet republics like Ukraine and Kazakhstan.
Western commodities houses are actively engaging in arbitrage involving products such as sunflower oil from Russia and wheat from Ukraine.
There is disagreement among industry sources regarding trading strategies in the post-Soviet market, which lacks clear rules and where the state is no longer a major player.
The Russian government has refrained from participating in the grain market, relying on private traders to compensate for the country's worst grain harvest in three decades.
Arkady Zlochevsky, president of OGO, noted that the domestic grain market is challenging this year due to a lack of cash among traders and unreliable deliveries from Ukraine.
Russian farmers are demanding prices above world levels, selling third-class bread-making wheat for 0.97 to 1.00 million roubles per tonne.

Russia's tax officials are seeking a larger share from rough diamond exports.
Industry sources hope a deal with South Africa's De Beers will proceed.
The prosecutor general's office accused Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS) of financial irregularities.
Pavel Kovylin, first deputy director of ARS's Central Selling Organisation, expressed optimism about the De Beers agreement.
ARS is the world's second largest diamond producer.
ARS's sales of uncut gems rose six percent in 1995 to $1.38 billion.
ARS is the sole official exporter of diamonds in Russia.
ARS reached a preliminary agreement with De Beers to export rough gems in February.
The agreement is awaiting government approval after undergoing review in various ministries.
The prosecutor general's press service is investigating ARS's finances for alleged unpaid taxes and breaches of currency regulations.

Russia is implementing tighter regulations for exporters of non-ferrous scrap metals.
Industry sources stated that Russian supplies will still reach Western markets despite these regulations.
Kevin Norrish, a copper specialist at CRU International, noted that there was a significant surge in scrap exports after the Soviet Union's break-up, but that trend has ended.
Norrish indicated that the domestic market for scrap metals in Russia is tighter than before, resulting in less scrap being sent to Western Europe.
Proposed licensing of exporters is not expected to negatively impact sales abroad, according to Norrish.
Other sources believe that European markets will remain more attractive for Russian exporters than the domestic market.
Moscow aims to license the export of scrap ferrous and non-ferrous metals to ensure steady supplies for domestic processing.
A decree on licensing for scrap exports could be signed by the end of the month, according to Russian news agencies.
The Industry Ministry sought to limit scrap exports to two million tonnes per year but agreed to a licensing plan instead.
A senior source at Tsvetmetexport stated that scrap material is more expensive abroad than in Russia.

Rosneft is a state oil holding firm in Russia.
Rosneft announced it would protest against a local decision to award Exxon Corp the right to develop Arctic oilfields.
Exxon was declared the winner of a tender to develop the Central Khoreiverskaya oilfields in the Timan-Pechora area.
Rosneft spokesman Vladimir Tumarkin stated that Exxon's bid would give it too many privileges.
Tumarkin claimed that Exxon's bid violates the tender terms by granting exclusive rights to resources.
The protest indicates a change in Moscow's policy towards Western energy companies.
Rosneft bid jointly with a subsidiary and Amoco Corp in the tender.
Exxon would have a 50 percent stake and negotiate with Rosneft, KomiTEK, and Arkhangelskgeoldobycha for the remaining 50 percent.
The Central-Khoreiverskaya oilfields contain approximately 160 million tonnes of oil and require about $1.5 billion to develop.
Kazakov, a member of the regional tender committee, stated that the tender process was conducted normally.

A multinational group is attempting to build a $1.5 billion oil pipeline linking Kazakhstan and Russia.
The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) includes eight international oil companies and the states of Russia, Kazakhstan, and Oman.
CPC aimed to finalize a new restructuring deal on Friday afternoon.
There is uncertainty regarding the involvement of Russia's Transneft oil pipeline monopoly in the deal.
Transneft is seeking to take a significant equity stake in the pipeline project.
Western oil executives expressed concerns about Transneft's potential role as a shareholder and decision-maker.
The companies involved in CPC include Chevron (15%), LUKoil (12.5%), Mobil (7.5%), Rosneft (7.5%), British Gas Plc (2%), Agip SpA (2%), Oryx Energy Company (1.75%), and Munaigaz (1.75%).
The remaining 50 percent stake in the project is divided between Russia (24%), Kazakhstan (19%), and Oman (7%).
Transneft wants to acquire the Russian government's 24 percent stake in the project.
The proposed pipeline will connect Kazakhstan's Tengiz oil field to Russia's Black Sea oil export outlet in Novorossiisk.

Western oil companies are frustrated by Moscow's delays on foreign investment laws.
A study was presented by Western oil companies to convince Russian officials that Russia will benefit significantly from oil deals.
The study outlines benefits from six production-sharing contracts requiring $129 billion in expenditure.
Foreign oil firms have invested only a small fraction of the required total due to high taxes and a flawed production-sharing law.
A top Western oil executive stated that no investments will occur without a firm legal base.
The document was prepared by the Petroleum Advisory Forum and a group of Russian academics.
The study claims that six major international projects requiring $102 billion in Western funding would generate $591 billion in total benefits.
According to the study, Russia would receive 87 percent of the total benefits from these projects.
The projects would create up to 550,000 jobs and raise real gross domestic product by $450 billion.
State revenues would increase by $257 billion and Russian private sector revenues by $258 billion.

Russia's Finance Ministry stated that Moscow is ready to cooperate with De Beers on a deal to support the diamond market.
The Russian Finance Ministry has not received official communication from De Beers regarding a new trade agreement for exporting Russian rough gems.
De Beers announced that it would cancel its interim arrangement with Russia if a formal deal was not reached by 1997.
First Deputy Economy Minister Vladimir Panskov stated that an agreement with De Beers is necessary to avoid damaging the world diamond market.
De Beers controls approximately 75% of the world diamond market, while Russia accounts for about 25% of the rough gems sold by De Beers.
A five-year deal between Russia and De Beers expired in December 1995 and was replaced by a memorandum in February 1996.
Panskov noted that differences of opinion had emerged between Russian diamond producer Almazy Rossii-Sakha, domestic gem processing plants, and De Beers during negotiations.
A senior official from Almazy Rossii-Sakha indicated that the Russian government had been slow in progressing the deal with De Beers but expected a resolution in 1997.
Lev Safonov, first vice president of Almazy Rossii-Sakha, stated that if the interim agreement was terminated before a new deal, trade would continue under different conditions.

Russia's Rosneft oil firm retained its asset AO Purneftegaz after a Moscow court ruling.
An arbitration court ruled that AO Purneftegaz would remain with Rosneft, ending a dispute with SIDANKO.
Dan Lubash, managing director of Emerging Markets Europe at Merrill Lynch, stated that the decision is crucial for Rosneft's survival.
Rosneft has lost most of its assets in recent years due to privatization under President Boris Yeltsin.
The court ruling may help Rosneft maintain its operations by allowing it to keep a company with significant untapped reserves.
Vladimir Tumarkin, Rosneft's press director, described the ruling as a victory for Rosneft.
Purneftegaz is a Western Siberian oil producer that produced over eight million tonnes of crude in 1995.
Purneftegaz's ownership has been contested between Rosneft and SIDANKO since a 1994 government resolution awarded it to SIDANKO.
The arbitration court ruled against SIDANKO's lawsuit to reverse the 1995 decision that returned ownership to Rosneft.
Purneftegaz accounted for about two-thirds of Rosneft's total production of 13 million tonnes last year.

Russia's aluminium industry reported strong output figures for 1996.
The Kontsern Alyuminiy producers' group stated that Russian primary aluminium output in 1996 was 2.87 million tonnes.
The 1996 output figure was an increase from 2.79 million tonnes in earlier estimates and 2.67 million tonnes in 1995.
Russia is one of the world's top aluminium producers, accounting for 15 percent of global output.
Forecasts indicate that Russian aluminium output will rise by 1.5-2.0 percent in 1997.
Russia's total primary aluminium capacity is approximately 3.20 million tonnes.
Analysts noted that no new investments are expected to fundamentally reshape the Russian aluminium sector.
Western trading houses became more active in Russia in 1996 to address raw materials supply issues.
A senior source from Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG stated that serious investments in modernisation are not anticipated in 1997.
Seventy percent of the region's alumina is used as the raw material for aluminium production.

Russia's oil sector has experienced a reduction in output declines.
Dan Lubash is the managing director of Emerging Markets Europe at Merrill Lynch.
Russia's crude oil output in 1996 was 293 million tonnes, a two percent decrease from 1995.
1996's crude oil output was the lowest for Russia in nearly three decades.
Russia was the world's third-largest oil producer in 1996.
Russia's oil output peaked at 570 million tonnes in 1987.
In 1996, Russia's oil output was 51 percent of the 1987 record level.
Stephen O'Sullivan is the associate director of oil and gas at MC Securities in London.
Analysts noted signs of recovery in the second quarter of 1996.
Russian gross domestic product fell by six percent in 1996.

A decision on the fate of Air Liberte is expected at the start of next week.
No bidder has formally submitted an offer to acquire Air Liberte.
Dominique Leveque is the president of the Creteil commercial court.
Leveque denied reports of a 1400 GMT deadline for bids.
Bids for Air Liberte can be submitted today, either in the afternoon or evening.
The court will make a statement about the bids on Tuesday afternoon at the earliest.
The court has six months to study the situation regarding the bids.
Air Liberte's cash position cannot sustain another six months.
British Airways is preparing a bid to merge Air Liberte with its French TAT unit.
Air Liberte owns 20 to 25 percent of the slots at Orly airport.

Jean-Luc Lagardere is the chairman of Lagardere Groupe.
Lagardere Groupe will not sell Thomson's digital television technology to Daewoo Electronics.
Lagardere selected Daewoo as a partner to guarantee jobs at Thomson's French production units.
The French government selected Lagardere to buy state-owned Thomson SA for one franc.
Lagardere's bid for Thomson included an 11-billion francs capital injection.
Lagardere was bidding against Alcatel Alsthom for Thomson.
Lagardere Groupe plans to merge its Matra defense business with Thomson's unit Thomson-CSF.
Lagardere agreed to sell Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo for a symbolic franc.
Lagardere received news of winning the bidding during an official dinner at a Picasso exhibition.
Lagardere faces criticism from some French media and labor unions for selling the Multimedia business to Daewoo.

Daewoo Electronics attempted to address French critics of its planned acquisition of Thomson Multimedia with job and investment promises.
Bae Soon-hoon, chairman of Daewoo Electronics, did not discuss financial details of the proposed takeover until the French government's decision became final.
The French Privatisation Commission and the European Commission must approve the deal for the acquisition to proceed.
The French government selected Lagardere Groupe to purchase state-owned Thomson SA for one franc after an 11 billion franc capital injection.
Lagardere plans to merge its Matra Defence Espace unit with Thomson-CSF and sell Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo for one franc.
A rival French bid for Thomson Multimedia could potentially emerge, according to the financial newspaper La Tribune.
Sagem, which previously withdrew from the bidding process, was reported to be preparing a rival bid, but Sagem denied this.
Bae dismissed the idea of a rival bid, stating that Daewoo has been following the government's procedures for six months.
Bae stated his intention to make Thomson Multimedia profitable and pledged to create 5,000 jobs in France over five years.
The partnership between Thomson Multimedia and Daewoo is expected to create a 13 billion franc investment plan and generate a total of 6,600 jobs in final assembly and 2,500 jobs in component production.

British Airways Plc (BA) has strengthened its position in France by partnering with French bank Rivaud in a bid for Air Liberte.
Rivaud is a founding shareholder in Air Liberte and previously a partner in a rival consortium.
The agreement between BA and Rivaud followed extensive negotiations that began on Tuesday afternoon and concluded on Wednesday morning.
The BA/Rivaud bid is currently the only offer remaining for Air Liberte and is expected to be approved by the commercial court in Creteil on Friday.
Richard Branson's Virgin Express and commercial pilot Fernand Denan were also pursuing takeover offers for Air Liberte.
The BA/Rivaud proposal requires approval from Air Liberte's creditors and French political authorities.
Air Liberte holds a 12 percent share of the domestic French market, while BA's TAT unit has an eight percent share.
Air France group remains the dominant player in the market.
BA plans to invest 440 million francs ($85.3 million) for a 70 percent stake in Air Liberte, while Rivaud will invest 190 million francs for the remaining 30 percent.
Air Liberte's current debt is reported to be 800 million francs.

Air France is a French state-owned airline.
Air France stated it is prepared to face increased competition from British Airways Plc in the domestic market.
British Airways' TAT French unit announced a joint bid of 780 million francs for domestic carrier Air Liberte.
The joint bid will increase British Airways' share of takeoff and landing slots at Paris Orly Airport to 20 percent.
An Air France spokeswoman acknowledged that British Airways' increased presence in French aviation would have consequences.
Air France plans to improve its product and service while reducing costs and prices.
British Airways is expected to acquire a 70 percent stake in Air Liberte after approval from the Creteil commercial court.
Air France Europe holds an 80 percent market stake on its operated routes and 60 percent of the total French market.
European liberalization of the airline industry will fully open French airspace to competition starting in April 1997.
British Airways acquired a 49.9 percent stake in TAT in 1993 and the remaining shares in July 2022.

Rhone-Poulenc SA announced a 13 percent rise in third quarter profits.
The company's net income was 756 million francs, compared to 669 million francs at the same stage last year.
The rise in earnings would have been 25.1 percent without an expensive product recall.
Operating profit for the third quarter was 2.05 billion francs, up from 1.83 billion francs.
Net sales increased to 20.47 billion francs from 19.62 billion francs.
Rhone shares rose nearly two percent to 145.30 francs following the earnings announcement.
Rhone-Poulenc issued a profit warning on October 10 due to a product recall related to its Centeon joint venture.
The company took an 81 million franc charge in the third quarter and expects a total charge of 100 to 200 million francs for 1996.
Finance director Jean-Pierre Tirouflet stated the recall would reduce analysts' forecasts for 1996 results by six to seven percent.
For the first nine months, net income increased by 10.5 percent to 2.17 billion francs.

The planned sale of Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics has led to protests.
Shares in Lagardere Groupe fell more than five percent due to concerns about the Thomson sale.
French opposition parties, labor unions, and polls indicate that most French people oppose the sale of Thomson Multimedia.
Thomson Multimedia workers protested against the sale and plan a demonstration in November.
The opposition to the sale may negatively impact foreign buyer interest in future French privatizations.
Lagardere's shares had previously risen by 32 percent after being selected to buy Thomson Multimedia.
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis stated that the government's procedure for the sale was free from political criticism.
Thomson owns 58 percent of Thomson-CSF and 100 percent of Thomson Multimedia.
Lagardere intends to merge its Matra unit with Thomson-CSF and sell Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo.
A survey found that 72 percent of voters disapproved of the sale price of Thomson Multimedia.

Daewoo Electronics launched a charm campaign in France with newspaper advertisements.
The campaign was in response to criticism regarding Daewoo's plans to acquire Thomson Multimedia.
Daewoo is the 34th largest company in the world.
The acquisition involves purchasing Thomson Multimedia for one symbolic franc.
France's Privatisation Commission will decide in early December on the sale of Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe.
Lagardere Groupe plans to sell Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo after a capital injection of 11 billion francs.
Thomson Multimedia specializes in televisions and video recorders and is a leader in digital video technology.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe announced a parliamentary debate on the deal, but there will be no parliamentary vote.
Daewoo claimed its electronics arm has sales figures comparable to Thomson Multimedia, with profits that Thomson lacks.
Daewoo stated it has made investments in France and has established ties with French companies.

Electricite de France (EDF) made an 850 million franc asset gain by selling its 10 percent stake in Sydkraft AB to Statkraft SF.
EDF chairman Edmond Alphandery stated that the deal marks the beginning of an alliance with Statkraft.
The alliance with Statkraft will focus on cooperation in hydroelectric projects in southeast Asia.
EDF is selling 6.808 million class A and 12.395 million class C shares in Sydkraft AB for 2.130 billion francs.
The sale will increase Statkraft's stake in Sydkraft to 15 percent.
The formal transfer of ownership will occur in November.
EDF acquired its stake in Sydkraft two years ago but changed its strategy in April.
EDF's Northelec unit obtained a 25 percent stake in Graningeverkens AB, Sweden's sixth largest power group.
EDF has a shareholders' pact with the Versteegh family, giving them a combined 54 percent ownership of Graninge.
Alphandery indicated that EDF would continue its expansion in the Mercosur area and southeast Asia.

Cie Generale des Eaux launched its bid to compete with France Telecom by starting a fixed telephone network in Nice.
Philippe Glotin is the managing director of Generale's telecoms unit Cegetel.
Cegetel aims to achieve a market share yielding 40 billion francs in annual sales by 2003.
More than half of Cegetel's projected sales in 2003 will come from mobile communications.
Cegetel's SFR unit already competes with France Telecom in mobile telecommunications.
Cegetel is allied with British Telecom Plc and MCI for business services.
SFR expects to have one million customers by March 1997.
The local residential market in Nice is expected to represent 55 billion francs in 2003.
Cegetel aims for a 40 percent share in mobile communications, 20 percent in long-distance, and 10 percent in local loops.
Cegetel has received permission from French authorities for a telecoms experiment in Nice.

Jet Multimedia aims to compete with Netscape Communications and Microsoft.
Jet Multimedia's France Explorer browser is intended to become the French standard.
France Explorer will be distributed for free at the start of 1997.
France Explorer will allow access to the Internet, multimedia servers, and France's Minitel database from home personal computers.
Jet Multimedia's founding chairman Eric Peyre will officially launch the program on December 12.
The software will use a new France Telecom service for Internet access.
France Telecom will open a service called 'The Internet Kiosk' in January.
The Internet Kiosk will provide access to the Internet using special telephone numbers.
Jet Multimedia does not aim to profit from the software but wants users to utilize their phone number and existing servers.
Jet Multimedia was founded in 1989 and specializes in electronic publishing and multimedia technology.

Lord Weinstock is the chairman emeritus of Britain's General Electric Plc.
Lord Weinstock stated that GEC is ready to deal with whoever wins ownership of Thomson SA.
Serge Tchuruk is the chairman of Alcatel Alsthom.
Serge Tchuruk expressed readiness to make a new offer for Thomson SA if the current offers' validity deadline passes.
The French government decided to sell Thomson SA for one franc to Lagardere Groupe after a cash injection of 11 billion francs.
The decision to sell Thomson SA awaits approval from the European Commission and France's Privatisation Commission.
The European Commission's decision could be due in the first half of December.
The Privatisation Commission will make its decision after the European Commission's stance is known.
The French Finance Ministry acknowledged that the sale may not be completed before December 31.
Lagardere plans to merge Thomson's defence unit with its Matra Defence Espace unit and sell Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics for one franc.

French Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon granted a telecoms operating licence to Societe Nationale des Chemins de Fer (SNCF).
The licence is part of the liberalisation of the telecommunications sector in France.
The licence granted to SNCF's Telecom Developpement unit is for 15 years.
The licence allows SNCF to offer telecommunications services as an alternative to the France Telecom network.
SNCF must detail the assets for the Telecom Development unit and obtain approval for its tariffs.
The operating licence includes technical standards, privacy issues, and interconnection obligations.
The SNCF licence is the second licence for alternative infrastructure in France.
The first licence for alternative infrastructure was granted to Eurotunnel unit TransManche.
Licences will soon be granted to MFS Communication Co and Colt Telecom Group.
The SNCF licence covers an existing network of 8,000 kilometres of optic fibre and radio links, which will expand to 12,000 kilometres.

Optus Communications Ltd is considering whether to continue supporting the Australian Rugby League (ARL) after a court defeat against News Corp.
Optus Communications chairman Russell Fynmore stated that discussions are ongoing regarding the support for the ARL.
Fynmore indicated that the future of the ARL and its rival Superleague will depend on financial backing for both leagues.
Optus Vision owns the pay-television broadcast rights to the ARL and is five percent-owned by Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL).
PBL's Channel Nine holds the free-to-air broadcast rights to the ARL.
The ARL faced a significant setback when the Federal Court upheld News Corp's appeal against previous rulings that banned Superleague.
Superleague is set to begin its competition next season, potentially leading to competition between two leagues for TV audience share.
News Ltd executive chairman Ken Cowley expressed openness to talks with the ARL.
Cowley stated that he aims to maximize the number of fans watching Superleague.
Cowley dismissed claims that ARL chairman Ken Arthurson could resign to facilitate a merger between the two leagues.

The computer software and instruction kit for a death machine will soon be available on the Internet.
Dr Philip Nitschke developed the death machine used in the world's first legal mercy killing.
Bob Dent was connected to the machine by Nitschke in Australia's Northern Territory.
The death machine allows users to administer lethal injections using a computer interface.
Nitschke plans to demonstrate the machine at an euthanasia conference in Melbourne.
The machine is used in the Northern Territory, which has the world's only voluntary euthanasia law.
Dent, a 66-year-old former carpenter, initiated the lethal drug flow by entering three computer commands.
The computer program confirms the patient's decision to proceed with euthanasia three times.
Nitschke is creating an euthanasia home page in response to interest in Dent's death and the new law.
A doctor cannot lawfully connect a patient to the machine outside the Northern Territory.

Pasminco Ltd forecasts a tough year of cost-cutting due to a weak zinc market and a strong Australian dollar.
David Stewart is the chief executive of Pasminco Ltd.
David Stewart stated that the company will have a difficult year.
Pasminco reported a net profit of A$41 million for the year to June 30.
The net profit of A$41 million was a tripling compared to the previous year.
World zinc prices have not changed significantly since August.
A stronger Australian dollar has negatively impacted Pasminco's first quarter profit for 1996/97.
David Stewart indicated that the first quarter result is below last year due to the Australian dollar's impact.
For every one-cent rise in the Australian dollar against the US dollar, Pasminco experiences a A$7.5 million decrease in after-tax profit.
The Australian dollar was on average five cents stronger in the first quarter than its average throughout 1995/96.

Pacific Dunlop Ltd reported a challenging outlook due to intense competition and low margins.
The company plans to implement cost-cutting measures and pursue acquisitions to improve its share price.
Chairman John Gough addressed shareholder concerns about the company's weak share price at the annual meeting.
Gough forecasted a profit recovery for the year ending June 30, 1997.
He stated that results for the first six months would be significantly lower than the same period last year.
Gough defended the board against criticism regarding failed ventures in the food and cardiac-implant sectors.
Pacific Dunlop is involved in litigation related to its former subsidiary, Telectronics Pacing Systems Inc.
Telectronics halted production for 13 months due to a defect in a pacemaker component.
Telectronics was sold for A$170 million to St Jude Medical Inc.
Pacific Dunlop recorded gross abnormal losses of A$340 million from Telectronics in its 1995/96 accounts.

The Broken Hill Pty Co (BHP) reported a 9.8-percent decline in first-half profits.
BHP's net profit for the six months to November 30 was A$790 million, down from A$867 million for the same period last year.
BHP's profit was boosted by an abnormal gain of A$107 million.
BHP's share price initially rose to A$17.59 after the profit announcement but later settled at around A$17.20.
BHP's stock closed at A$17.48, which was 43 cents higher than the previous day's close.
Analysts expressed disappointment with BHP's results, with one describing it as 'pretty lousy.'
BHP's pre-abnormal net profit was A$683 million, a 15.8 percent decrease compared to the same period in the previous year.
BHP's managing director John Prescott indicated that the second quarter showed improvement in performance.
BHP's petroleum division was the largest earner for the quarter, generating A$253 million, which included an abnormal gain of A$107 million.
BHP's copper operations in North America returned to profitability.

BHP has agreed to pay its local steel workers a 10-percent pay rise over two years.
The wage deal covers over 13,000 workers at BHP steel plants across Australia.
The deal is below the initial demand of 15 percent by the Australian Workers Union (AWU).
The AWU claims to represent about 80 percent of BHP steel workers.
Mick Eagles, an AWU organiser, stated that low inflation is pressuring unions to lower wage expectations.
Eagles believes that a 10-percent outcome over two years will be seen as an achievement.
The Australian Manufacturing Workers Union (AMWU) aims for an annual wage rise of over five percent in the metal trades industry.
Vince Theuma from the AMWU stated that the BHP deal could weaken other unions' positions in wage negotiations.
BHP described the wages agreement as satisfactory and part of a strategy to cut costs.
BHP initially offered an eight percent pay rise over two years.

Harvey Norman is an Australian furniture, whitegoods, and computer retailer.
The company reported that it is trailing behind its target for 15 percent annual sales growth.
Cool summer weather impacted December sales for Harvey Norman.
Managing director Michael Harvey stated that December sales grew by double digit figures compared to the same month a year ago.
Excluding sales from new stores, turnover in December rose only about five percent.
Harvey Norman aims for a sales increase from A$1.043 billion to A$1.2 billion for the financial year 1996/97.
Michael Harvey described the retail trading environment as the worst in the company's 15-year history.
Harvey Norman has not provided a profit forecast but believes it will not follow the path of other retailers that announced profit downgrades.
The company reported a dip in net profit after abnormals of A$30.41 million in 1995/96.
Unseasonably cool weather has dampened sales of air conditioners, refrigerators, fans, outdoor furniture, and barbecues.

Over half a million people insured with National Mutual Holdings Ltd have purchased shares in the company.
National Mutual plans to list on the Australian and New Zealand exchanges next month.
Half of National Mutual's 1.2 million policy-holders have elected to take up their entitlement to shares.
Geoff Tomlinson is the managing director of National Mutual.
The offer price for retail investors is set at A$1.50 per share.
The price range for institutional investors is between A$1.35 and A$1.55 per share.
National Mutual will be among the top 50 companies by market capitalisation once listed.
The retail price of A$1.50 per share results in a market capitalisation of about A$2.5 billion.
National Mutual is the first major Australian life insurer to demutualise and list on the Australian market.
National Mutual Asia Ltd is the second-biggest life office in Hong Kong and is seeking a licence to operate in China.

Foster's Brewing Group Ltd reported a 13 percent rise in pre-tax earnings to A$185 million for the six months to December 31.
The increase in earnings was attributed to strong performance by its home brews.
Carlton and United Breweries (CUB) recorded an 11.5 percent surge in profit before interest and tax.
CUB commands 55 percent of the local beer market, up from 53 percent a year ago.
Foster's 40-percent-owned Molson Breweries negatively impacted the group's bottom line, resulting in a profit of A$169.4 million, a 2.4 percent increase from the previous year.
Foster's incurred a A$20 million abnormal loss for restructuring costs at Molson.
Molson Breweries is facing potential further losses due to an arbitration dispute with Coors Brewing Co.
Foster's Chinese operations reported A$10.2 million in losses in the first half from joint-venture breweries.
Despite losses, revenue and sales volumes in China rose in the first half, with operations expected to break even around 1999.

Pacific Dunlop Ltd is an Australian industrial conglomerate.
Pacific Dunlop reported a 28 percent drop in net profit to A$84 million for the six months ending December 31.
The reported net profit fall was within stock market forecasts.
Pacific Dunlop expressed a bullish outlook for the future.
A stockbroker stated that the comments accompanying the results were upbeat.
The stockbroker believes the stock will increase in value.

Major Australian banks are increasing their focus on Asia as conditions worsen in Australia.
Three of Australia's largest banks have recently renewed their interest in Asian markets.
Ken McLay, a banking analyst at Standard and Poor's Group, noted that banks are pushing harder into Asia.
All four of Australia's major banks are seeking opportunities for income in Asia's growing markets.
The Reserve Bank of Australia has encouraged banks to expand into Asia.
National Mutual Holdings Ltd and Colonial Mutual are increasing their presence in Asia.
Colonial Mutual recently bought out its Asian joint venture for US$163 million.
Six months ago, the Reserve Bank of Australia expressed disappointment in local banks' lack of expansion into Asia.
Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) has been the most focused on Asia among Australian banks.
Westpac Banking Group had previously withdrawn from Asia but re-entered the market in November with a partnership with Standard Chartered Bank Plc.

RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd is the world's biggest mining house.
RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd is expected to report a 26 percent fall in net profit before exceptional items for calendar 1996.
The expected net profit for RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd in 1996 is US$1.067 billion.
In 1995, RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd made US$1.441 billion in profit.
Analysts' forecasts for RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd's profit in 1996 range between US$1.04 billion and US$1.097 billion.
The decline in profit is attributed to falling copper and aluminium prices and issues with the Bingham Canyon copper smelter in Utah.
Copper prices fell below 90 U.S. cents a pound after the Sumitomo Corp trading scandal in June.
Aluminium prices dropped 16 percent in 1996.
RTZ-CRA's iron ore sales decreased by six percent despite an increase in annual output.
Coal earnings for RTZ-CRA are expected to fall by 10 percent in 1996.

A startup software company named Intermind Corp. launched a product on Tuesday to address information overload on the Internet.
Intermind Corp. was formed a little more than a year ago by a software consultant and a former Microsoft Corp. executive.
The product, called Intermind Communicator, allows users to seek customized information from websites that use the program.
Users can receive notifications similar to electronic mail when new content is available on websites they visit.
Intermind President David Arnold stated that the software aims to facilitate more sophisticated interactions between consumers and publishers.
High-tech companies like Apple Computer Inc. and Visio Corp. will use the system to send customers technical bulletins or product information.
David Strom, an industry consultant, described the software as the ultimate in custom publishing and narrowcasting.
Intermind Corp. aims to distribute 2 million copies of the software, which is free for non-commercial users, by the end of the year.
Commercial users will pay a fee based on revenue generated or subscribers reached.
The software is compatible with Microsoft's Windows 95 and Windows NT platforms and will be available for Windows 3.1 within one week.

Microsoft Corp. is expected to report a slowdown in earnings growth due to a sales surge last year from the launch of Windows 95.
Industry analysts expect Microsoft to post earnings of 90 cents a share for its fiscal first quarter, up 15 percent from last year's 78 cents.
Last year's fiscal first quarter, Microsoft reported net income of $499 million.
Analysts expect Microsoft's revenues for the period ending September 30 to be in the $2.3 billion range, up from $2.02 billion.
Microsoft's growth rate is still healthy, but it faces difficult comparisons to last year when revenues and earnings grew more than 46 percent.
Chris Galvin of Hambrecht and Quist noted that last year's September quarter was strong due to the initial release of Windows 95.
Microsoft's profit margins are rising as the company sells more software by preloading it onto new computers or selling licenses to large customers.
Analysts expect Microsoft's business to gain momentum through the fiscal year as Windows NT gains acceptance and a new version of Office is rolled out in December.
For the full fiscal year, analysts predict earnings and sales will be up about 20 percent over last year.
Scott McAdams of Ragen MacKenzie believes Windows NT will significantly drive earnings in the December quarter and early 1997.

Microsoft Corp Chief Financial Officer Mike Brown expects the company's revenues to rise sequentially in the next two quarters from the $2.3 billion reported for the three months ended September 30.
Mike Brown stated that the company's cost of goods sold could decline slightly in the long term from the 10.9 percent of revenue reported, which is already down from 16 percent a year ago.
Brown anticipates revenue growth in December and March, attributing December's growth to holiday season cyclicality and March's growth to the release of the Office 97 suite of business applications.
Brown noted that cost ratios are falling due to increased use of CD-ROMs for software distribution instead of diskettes and the popularity of enterprise software licenses over retail sales.
Brown mentioned that the company's spending on research and development is on target, with plans to spend $2.1 billion in the current fiscal year ending June 30.
Brown reported that unearned revenue on the company's balance sheet increased to $651 million as of September 30 from $560 million three months earlier.
Brown indicated that unearned revenue would rise further due to growth in the subscription model of sales, such as licenses and upgrades.

Boeing Co. reported a 13 percent increase in profits for the third quarter.
Boeing's net income for the three months ended on Sept. 30 was $254 million, or 74 cents a share.
This net income increased from $225 million, or 66 cents a share, in the same quarter of 1995.
Sales for Boeing rose to $5.60 billion from $4.38 billion in the previous year's third quarter.
Boeing delivered 54 airliners in the third quarter, an increase from 51 airliners delivered in the same quarter last year.
Boeing's stock fell $1.50 to $95.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Boeing plans to increase overall production to 36 airplanes a month by next year's third quarter.
