Munro suggested that Wang was likely to leave Hong Kong soon but could not specify his destination.
Washington has a history of granting asylum to political critics of Beijing since the Tiananmen Square crackdown in 1989.
Human rights sources indicated that it was unlikely Wang would speak publicly in Hong Kong.

Wang Dan, a Chinese dissident, was sentenced to 11 years in prison.
The sentence has raised concerns that critics of the Chinese administration in Hong Kong may face similar consequences.
Britain will hand Hong Kong back to China in 243 days after over 150 years of colonial rule.
The sentence imposed on Wang Dan led to discussions in Hong Kong about future subversion laws.
Hong Kong has historically been a refuge for Chinese dissenters, with around 80 mainland dissidents living in exile there.
Hong Kong has a significant anti-communist democracy movement that has been labeled subversive by Beijing officials.
The Basic Law, which is Hong Kong's future constitution, mandates the creation of laws to prohibit anti-constitutional activities, including subversion.
There is speculation regarding what actions future laws will prohibit and how they will be legislated.
Eric Li, a member of the pro-Beijing political camp, stated that he disputes the idea that Hong Kong dissidents will face the same fate as Wang Dan.
Martin Lee, head of Hong Kong's Democratic Party, expressed concern that a similar law could lead to imprisonment for Hong Kong dissidents.

Tung Chee-hwa is a shipping magnate.
In the 1980s, Tung Chee-hwa's family company faced financial difficulties.
Tung Chee-hwa is a candidate for the leadership of Hong Kong.
China's Selection Committee will choose a chief executive for Hong Kong in the coming month.
Tung Chee-hwa received 30.2 percent in a recent popularity poll.
Ti Liang Yang received 27.5 percent in the same poll.
Peter Woo received 8.7 percent in the same poll.
Simon Li received 3.3 percent in the same poll.
Tung Chee-hwa was a senior member of a preparatory committee for Hong Kong's governance.
Governor Chris Patten praised Tung Chee-hwa as an impartial and honest counsellor.

Tung Chee-hwa's family company faced financial difficulties in the 1980s.
Beijing provided financial assistance to Tung Chee-hwa during the 1980s.
Tung Chee-hwa is a candidate to become Hong Kong's next leader.
The Selection Committee will choose a Chief Executive for Hong Kong in the coming month.
Tung Chee-hwa received 206 votes in the first round of balloting.
Yang Ti Liang received 82 votes in the first round of balloting.
Peter Woo received 54 votes in the first round of balloting.
Recent opinion polls indicate that Yang Ti Liang is slightly more popular than Tung Chee-hwa.
Tung Chee-hwa was a senior member of a Preparatory Committee for Hong Kong's governance.
Tung Chee-hwa resigned from his position at Orient Overseas (International) Ltd to pursue his leadership bid.

Yang Ti Liang is a former top judge vying to lead Hong Kong after China's takeover.
Yang Ti Liang believes Hong Kong needs a neutral and impartial leader who is tolerant towards dissent.
Yang Ti Liang is one of three candidates for Hong Kong's first chief executive after the British handover to China.
Yang Ti Liang received 82 votes in the first round of voting by a 400-member China-backed Selection Committee.
Tung Chee-hwa, a shipping tycoon, received 206 votes in the same round and is considered the frontrunner.
Peter Woo, another entrepreneur, received 54 votes in the first round.
Yang Ti Liang has been depicted as the people's favorite in some recent opinion polls.
Yang Ti Liang's campaign headquarters is a modest office rented in a hotel.
Yang Ti Liang claims his greatest strength is his long experience as a fair and unbiased arbiter.
Yang Ti Liang has no business or political connections due to his 30 years as a judge.

Hong Kong shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa was rated by a poll as the best candidate to deal with China.
A Beijing-controlled committee is vetting candidates to run Hong Kong as Britain prepares to hand back the territory in 215 days.
Britain will return Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty on June 30 at midnight.
The Selection Committee consists of 400 members and is conducting a three-day vetting process.
The winner of the selection will be announced on December 11.
A poll conducted by the Chinese University of Hong Kong showed that 73 percent of respondents believe Tung can communicate best with the Chinese government.
Only 7.2 percent of respondents thought former chief judge Ti Liang Yang could communicate well with Beijing.
Businessman Peter Woo received only two percent support for his communication abilities with Beijing.
The poll indicated that 31 percent of respondents believed Yang was most likely to speak out against Beijing.
Tung criticized the Democratic Party for its anti-China stance during questioning by the committee.

Britain and China are in disagreement over key issues related to the handover of Hong Kong to Beijing in 1997.
The issues include citizenship rights, subversion, and troop deployments.
There are 210 days remaining until the handover under British governance.
Sino-British talks are scheduled to begin on Wednesday under the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group (JLG) forum.
Recent discussions have shown a lack of progress on major details of the handover.
Chinese and British experts did not reach an agreement on the deployment of an advance party of troops into Hong Kong.
A dispute arose over a proposed liberal anti-subversion law from Britain.
A British representative stated that progress has been slower than desired but acknowledged the importance of the subject.
China has dropped its demand for the advance party of troops to be armed, and the current debate is focused on troop numbers.
Negotiators are set to discuss citizenship and right of abode issues, with concerns about Hong Kong citizens living abroad.

Tung Chee-hwa was previously a retiring man who avoided the limelight and kept his political views secret.
Tung Chee-hwa has emerged as a leading candidate to become Hong Kong's first post-colonial leader.
Tung Chee-hwa has adopted a tough-talking conservative stance and supports China's political positions.
Tung Chee-hwa has changed his attire from pinstripe suits to jeans and sportswear to connect with local communities.
Tung Chee-hwa's family company received financial assistance from Beijing in the 1980s.
The Selection Committee in China will choose the chief executive of Hong Kong after Britain returns the colony to Beijing in mid-1997.
Tung Chee-hwa received 206 out of 400 votes in the first round of balloting, leading his rivals.
A recent poll indicated that 47 percent of the public supports Tung Chee-hwa, while 29 percent support Yang Ti Liang.
Tung Chee-hwa has stated intentions to legalize the Communist Party and criticized the Democratic Party for being anti-China.
Tung Chee-hwa has called for pro-China patriotism in schools and emphasized executive-led rule.

Martin Lee is the head of the Democratic Party, the largest pro-democracy group in Hong Kong.
Martin Lee described Tung Chee-hwa as a pro-China yes-man.
Lee stated that preparations for the sovereignty change in Hong Kong are a disaster.
Tung Chee-hwa is favored to win the position of chief executive of Hong Kong.
Tung Chee-hwa is indebted to Beijing due to a financial bailout of his family firm in the 1980s.
Lee expressed that the people of Hong Kong need a defender of their system.
Lee believes that Tung Chee-hwa will act as a spokesman for China rather than protect Hong Kong's rights.
The British government is returning Hong Kong to China under the Joint Declaration treaty.
Lee denied accusations that the Democratic Party is anti-China.
Lee stated that the Democratic Party supports the return of sovereignty over Hong Kong to China.

Tung Chee-hwa is the chief executive designate of Hong Kong.
Tung Chee-hwa won a leadership victory and aims to gain public confidence for the transition to China.
The 150-member Preparatory Committee endorsed Tung Chee-hwa as Hong Kong's future leader.
Tung Chee-hwa is 59 years old and was born in Shanghai.
Tung Chee-hwa promised to be regularly available to the press.
Tung Chee-hwa aims for cooperative relations with Hong Kong's Democratic Party and the outgoing colonial administration.
Tung Chee-hwa addressed a gathering of 100 Hong Kong journalists in three languages: Mandarin, Cantonese, and English.
Tung Chee-hwa expressed confidence in the credibility of a proposed 60-member provisional legislature.
The Preparatory Committee is working on procedures for selecting the provisional legislature on December 21.
Hong Kong's Democratic Party condemned the provisional legislature and plans to challenge its legality in court.

Tung Chee-hwa was scheduled to fly to Beijing on Tuesday to be recognized as Hong Kong's first Chinese leader.
Tung Chee-hwa was selected as Hong Kong's future chief executive last Wednesday.
Tung Chee-hwa was to meet with China's President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng in Beijing.
Jiang Zemin indicated in January that Tung Chee-hwa was Beijing's preferred candidate for leadership.
Britain is set to transfer sovereignty of Hong Kong to China on June 30, 1997.
Tung Chee-hwa's initial responsibilities will include forming an advisory cabinet called the Executive Council.
Speculation exists that China will influence the composition of the future government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
The colonial government announced it would limit assistance to Tung Chee-hwa in forming a government-in-waiting.
Constitutional Affairs Secretary Nicholas Ng stated that a mass exodus of senior officials to the new government would not occur.
The transition period has faced disputes over various issues, affecting cooperation between the colonial administration and the incoming government.

China plans to create a new legislature in Hong Kong to replace the elected body when it resumes control of the territory next year.
On Saturday, 400 Hong Kong individuals, selected by China, will meet in Shenzhen to appoint 60 legislators for Hong Kong.
The new legislature will be called the 'provisional legislature' and will be established after China disbands the elected Legislative Council.
The Selection Committee will choose the new parliamentarians and previously elected Tung Chee-hwa as chief executive.
China will regain control of Hong Kong at midnight on June 30 next year, ending over 150 years of British rule.
The Hong Kong public, who supported pro-democracy groups in recent elections, did not participate in the selection processes organized by China.
The Democratic Party, Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy group, is boycotting the selection process and has expelled a member for running in it.
Tung Chee-hwa stated that Britain must accept the reality of the new legislature and warned against challenging its legitimacy.
Chris Patten criticized the provisional legislature, stating that many candidates were previously defeated in elections.
The Democratic Party is organizing protests against the provisional legislature, and China has increased security at the border.

Hong Kong's Police Commissioner Eddie Hui expressed confidence that the police could manage disturbances after the July 1 handover to China without assistance from the People's Liberation Army.
Hui reported that crime in Hong Kong had decreased by 14 percent in 1996, reaching a 15-year low.
Hui stated that despite the departure of senior officers, mainly expatriates, the police force could still effectively address crime problems, including mass disturbances.
China will resume sovereignty over Hong Kong on July 1, 1997, after 150 years of British colonial rule.
Concerns have been raised in Hong Kong about potential law and order issues during the handover.
Some officers taking early retirement have expressed fears that the police force may become corrupt after the handover.
Pro-democracy politicians have warned that China might impose repressive laws and use PLA troops to maintain order.
Hui indicated that he did not foresee any situation requiring assistance from the PLA.
Peter Wong, Police Deputy Commissioner for Operations, stated that the police were not under pressure from China regarding their handling of demonstrations.

Bouygues has formed a joint bid with Italy's STET to operate the telephone network of rail operator SNCF.
Cie Generale des Eaux announced partnerships for its Cegetel telecoms unit last month.
The state-owned RATP Paris Metro operator established a unit to utilize its 300 kilometers of track.
Bouygues' stock increased by 4.62 percent to 510 francs following its alliance with STET.
The breakup of France Telecom's domestic monopoly began in 1998 under European Union competition rules.
Bouygues and Generale des Eaux aim to capture a significant share of the long-distance call market and business networks.
Generale des Eaux chairman Jean-Marie Messier projected that Cegetel would contribute 15 percent of group sales and 25 percent of cash flow by 2003.
Lyonnaise des Eaux is focused on communications rather than telecommunications.
Analyst Annick Santer stated that communications is less risky and not as profitable as telecommunications.
Lyonnaise Communications had sales of 1.4 billion francs in 1995 and a net profit of 69 million francs.

French President Jacques Chirac aims to create a national defence giant to compete with U.S. conglomerates through the merger of Lagardere's Matra and Thomson-CSF.
The French government announced its preference for Lagardere Groupe's bid for Thomson SA over Alcatel Alsthom's bid.
Both bids have been referred to the independent Privatisation Commission.
Noel Forgeard, chairman of Lagardere's Matra unit, has campaigned for the acquisition of Thomson-CSF's defence arm.

Matra specializes in air-to-air missiles, while Thomson-CSF produces ground-to-air missiles.
The merger will enhance a joint venture between Matra and British Aerospace Plc to form Matra BAe Dynamics.
Lagardere aims to create a single European satellite giant through its Matra Marconi Space joint venture with GEC Plc.
The merger will integrate detection, communications, and weapons systems, positioning Thomson Matra as a powerful systems player.
The U.S. defence industry has consolidated through $40 billion in mergers and acquisitions, creating large firms like Lockheed Martin.

The French government plans to sell Thomson SA to the Lagardere conglomerate.
Thomson Multimedia will be sold to Daewoo Electronics for one franc.

Jacques Delors, former president of the European Commission, preferred to maintain a European presence in consumer electronics.
A report indicated that an unidentified French businessman was preparing a bid for Thomson Multimedia.
The French government preferred Lagardere's bid over a rival offer from Alcatel Alsthom.
Jospin accused President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe of allowing the sale to Daewoo to benefit from state financing.
Thomson Multimedia is expected to make significant profits in 1999 from technology licenses.
The technology licenses will contribute at least one billion francs in revenue starting in 1999.

The French government approved Snecma's acquisition of SEP.
Snecma currently owns 51 percent of SEP.
Snecma aims to buy out minority shareholders to fully own SEP.

If 95 percent of shares are acquired, a mandatory buy-in will occur.
SEP manufactures engines and boosters for Ariane rockets.
Snecma produces civilian and military aero engines.
The acquisition reverses a previous policy by former chairman Bernard Dufour.
Snecma's new chairman, Jean Paul Bechat, stated that asset sales should not cover operating losses.

State-owned Air France is under pressure from the French government to buy Airbus jets instead of Boeing long-haul jets.
Air France chairman Christian Blanc suggested using a mix of Boeing and Airbus planes for a new long-haul fleet.
The planned new long-haul fleet is expected to cost around $1 billion.

Blanc stated that there is no conflict in operating both Airbus 340 and Boeing 777 aircraft.

Any decision regarding aircraft purchases will require ratification from Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
France's state-owned Aerospatiale is a senior partner in Airbus, along with British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA.
Blanc aims to run Air France as a commercial entity, free from political intervention, and is preparing the airline for privatization and deregulation.

Air France reported earnings of 802 million francs ($158 million) in the first half of the year.
The profit estimate for the six months to September 30 compared with a loss of 335 million francs a year ago.
Air France placed an order for 20 Boeing and Airbus aircraft, including options.
The airline ordered 10 Boeing 777 twinjets and five Airbus A340s.
Air France confirmed five orders made in June and options for a further five Airbus A340s.
Air France chairman Christian Blanc received support from Prime Minister Alain Juppe for the Boeing purchase.
The orders for the Boeing 777-200 version could be worth around $2.7 billion at catalogue prices.
Airbus would potentially gain $1.75 billion from the orders.
Transport Minister Bernard Pons stated that Air France is obliged to buy Boeing to meet commitments made in 1989.
Air France had outstanding orders with Boeing worth $994 million and $2 billion in options.

Europe's aircraft industry announced plans for a 100-seater jet to be built with China as part of the Airbus family.
Italy's Alenia will enter new Airbus programmes.
Boeing and McDonnell Douglas are cooperating on future wide-body jets, including two stretched versions of the Boeing 747.
British Aerospace Plc (BAe) stated that a specific agreement has been reached regarding the new 100 seat jet family.
BAe is a partner in the European Airbus Industrie consortium and the AIA joint venture with China.
Airbus and Alenia will establish a new company to lead European participation with China and Singapore.
Singapore Technologies Aerospace is a partner in the project.
The new offering completes the bottom end of the Airbus range and consolidates Airbus' position in the Asian market.
Alenia will be involved in derivatives of current products, including the A340-600 and the A3XX large aircraft.

Airbus partners must accelerate plans to convert the partnership into a single company.
Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas announced a $13.3 billion merger plan.
The merger will create the world's largest aerospace firm with 1997 sales of about $48 billion and 200,000 employees.
Airbus shareholders need to act quickly due to the merger, according to an anonymous aerospace executive.
Airbus is a consortium consisting of France's Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA.
An Airbus spokesman stated that the U.S. merger would not change the competitive threat to Airbus.
Boeing is acquiring McDonnell Douglas, which has not been a competitor in the civilian aircraft business for several years.
McDonnell Douglas decided to drop plans for the MD-XX wide body passenger jet in October.
Airbus historically holds around a 30 percent market share, while Boeing holds about 60 percent and McDonnell Douglas 10 percent.
Airbus expects to secure firm orders for over 300 aircraft in 1996, valued at around $20 billion.

The French government announced it would reveal its plans to sell the Thomson-CSF state defence electronics firm early in the New Year.
The sale of Thomson-CSF will be covered by a 1986 privatisation law.
The finance ministry stated that the sale process will be slower than if it had been conducted under a 1991 privatisation decree.
The independent Privatisation Commission required the state to reconsider its plan to sell Thomson SA to the Lagardere Groupe conglomerate.
The state decided to privatise Thomson SA in two parts, starting with the sale of Thomson-CSF followed by Thomson Multimedia.

The Council of State ruled that the Thomson-CSF sale is covered under the 1986 act.

The four partners of the Airbus consortium signed an agreement to restructure Airbus into a limited liability company by 1999.
Airbus Industrie stated that establishing Airbus as a single corporate entity is an important step in the consolidation of the aerospace industry in Europe.
Airbus is currently a partnership between Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA), and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA).

The new entity will have a single management structure that will add control over engineering, testing, production, procurement, and customer service.
The transfer of assets associated with the new functions will depend on their essentiality and detailed valuation, to be completed by the end of 1997.
Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot stated that Airbus will become a single company before the end of 1999 with the same shareholding structure.
Currently, Airbus operates mainly as a sales and marketing organization while the four partners manufacture the planes.
The restructuring plans were prompted by the merger announcement between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas in December.
Airbus stated that the restructured company would improve operational efficiency and allow for new strategic partnerships and potential external participation.

The European Airbus consortium is conducting studies on a 555-seat passenger plane.
Boeing has decided to scale back work on a larger jumbo jet, the 747-X, due to market conditions.
Boeing is diverting half of the 1,000 staff working on the 747-X project to smaller planes.
An Airbus spokesman stated that they are confident the A3XX will meet market needs.
Airbus claims that major airlines are encouraging in their collaboration on the A3XX.
Airbus believes airlines prefer an all-new plane over Boeing's 747-X.
Airbus aims to launch the A3XX product family in 1998 for service in 2003.
Airbus seeks to increase its aircraft market share to at least 50 percent by the end of the decade.
Airbus forecasts a market of 1,383 planes seating more than 400 passengers over the next 20 years.
Boeing estimates demand for only 470 planes seating 500 or more, which would not yield a return on investment.

Canal Plus is merging with Nethold to create one of the world's largest pay-TV groups.
Nethold is jointly held by Richemont SA and MIH Holdings Ltd.

The stock of American Medical Response Inc. fell sharply for the second consecutive session on Wednesday.

Rite Aid Corp plans to integrate Thrifty PayLess Inc into its operations.

CSX Corp agreed to acquire Conrail Inc. in a cash and stock transaction valued at $8.4 billion.

British Airways and USAir Group Inc have a three-year partnership that is nearing collapse.

British Airways holds a 24.6 percent stake in USAir, which is based in Arlington, Virginia.

British Airways plans to form an alliance with AMR, the parent company of American Airlines.

Food Lion Inc. will buy Kash n' Karry Food Stores Inc. for $341 million.
Food Lion and Kash n' Karry had previously discussed a transaction earlier in the year but stopped talks in August.
Kash n' Karry shareholders will receive $26 per share in cash under the agreement.
Food Lion will refinance $221 million of Kash n' Karry debt.
Food Lion is a unit of Belgian retailer Delhaize.
Food Lion is one of the 10 largest U.S. supermarket chains with over 1,100 stores in 14 states.
Kash n' Karry operates 100 food stores and other facilities in west central Florida.
Food Lion plans to invest up to $150 million to improve Kash n' Karry stores over the next four years.
The transaction is expected to increase earnings per share for Food Lion and result in cost savings.
The deal has been approved by Kash n' Karry's board of directors and is expected to close by early 1997.

Tom Rattigan was nominated to lead a dissident slate of directors in a proxy fight against RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
Rattigan stated that the current management has shown little progress in solving the company's problems.
Carl Icahn nominated Rattigan to the dissident slate on Monday.
Icahn held a 7.3 percent stake in RJR as of October 25.
The dissident slate supports an immediate spinoff of RJR's 80.5 percent owned Nabisco Holdings Corp food business.
RJR insists it wants to spin off Nabisco but claims it is not the appropriate time to do so.
Rattigan began discussions with Icahn several months ago and signed up with him on November 1.
Rattigan intends for the slate to pursue a global settlement of tobacco litigation claims.
Icahn stated in a letter to RJR CEO Steven Goldstone that the board nominees would raise the company's annual dividend to $2 per share.
Rattigan was hired by Icahn as a consultant on November 1 for $2 million.

Norfolk Southern Corp is expected to raise its $9.1 billion offer for Conrail Inc.
Norfolk Southern's current bid is $100 per share.
Industry analysts speculate that Norfolk Southern could raise its bid by as much as 10 percent.
Carole Neely of Brown Brothers Harriman & Co stated that a raised bid would make it superior.
Conrail and CSX revised their merger pact to increase the cash amount in the transaction.
The revised transaction values Conrail shares at about $8.463 billion, or $93 per share.
The original value of the Conrail-CSX transaction was $8.418 billion, or $92.50 per share.
Renee Johansen of Wheat First Butch Singer believes Norfolk Southern will respond to shareholder dissatisfaction.
Conrail formally rejected Norfolk Southern's cash bid.
The CSX-Conrail agreement involves a cash and stock transaction.

Conrail Inc. revised its takeover agreement with CSX Corp. to provide more cash to shareholders.
The proposed railroad merger is valued at nearly $8.5 billion.
Investors criticized the revised cash-and-stock deal, stating it is below the rejected offer from Norfolk Southern Corp.
Conrail's board reaffirmed that a merger with CSX is a superior strategic combination despite a higher offer from Norfolk Southern.
Conrail Chairman David LeVan stated that the new agreement increases value for Conrail shareholders.
A source indicated that the Conrail board met late Tuesday night to finalize the new agreement with CSX.
The merger would create one of the largest transportation companies in the world with a rail system of approximately 29,000 miles in 22 eastern states.
Under the revised offer, CSX will pay $110 cash per share for 40 percent of Conrail shares.
The remaining 60 percent of Conrail shares will be exchanged at a ratio of 1.85619 CSX shares for each Conrail share.
Norfolk Southern has offered to pay $100 a share for all of Conrail's outstanding shares.

Mattel Inc president Jill Barad stated that the proposed acquisition of Tyco Toys Inc is not expected to face antitrust problems.
Barad claimed that the acquisition should fuel earnings in the first year of the transaction.
Mattel announced plans to buy Tyco in a stock transaction valued at about $755 million.
The combined market share of Mattel and Tyco would be less than 20 percent of the overall toy market.
The deal includes a topping fee of $40 million payable to Mattel if another company makes a higher bid for Tyco.
The transaction also includes a break-up fee of $15 million if it is not completed within a year.
The transaction is expected to be completed in the first half of 1997.
Barad did not specify anticipated cost savings associated with the transaction.
Barad approached Tyco about the transaction on September 29 in a meeting with Tyco CEO Gary Baughman.
The proposed transaction would significantly boost Mattel's position in the boys' toy market.

Conrail Inc. and CSX Corp. have received court approval for their $8.6 billion merger plan.
CSX Corp. needs to gain approval from shareholders who prefer Norfolk Southern Corp.'s higher bid.
CSX's cash tender offer for 19.9 percent of Conrail shares was oversubscribed.
Norfolk Southern Corp. made a $10 billion all-cash offer for Conrail shares, which Conrail rejected.
Conrail stated that merging with CSX provides more strategic benefits than accepting Norfolk Southern's offer.
Norfolk Southern extended its tender offer through midnight EST on December 16.
As of Thursday afternoon, approximately 1.4 million Conrail shares had been tendered under Norfolk Southern's offer.
Lawyers and financial advisers are considering plans to persuade Conrail shareholders to approve the merger.
Options being considered include increasing the stock portion of the deal or revising payment terms for investors.
CSX and Conrail have acknowledged discussions about increasing the value of their merger agreement.

Barney's Inc has entered a financial agreement with Dickson Concepts International Ltd.
The agreement may attract potential bidders for Barney's, a New York luxury retailer.
Barney's filed for bankruptcy nearly a year ago.
Dickson and Saks Holdings Inc have previously shown interest in Barney's.
Neiman Marcus Group Inc and Canada's Holt Renfrew are also considered potential bidders.
Barney's has stated that it is not for sale but is open to discussions with potential investors.
Barney's will pay Dickson up to $1 million for a financial review.
Dickson will submit a recapitalization proposal to Barney's as part of the agreement.
Barney's has been operating under bankruptcy protection since January.
The agreement with Dickson requires approval from the bankruptcy court.

An independent shareholder advisory firm recommended that investors of Conrail Inc reject a key provision in the railroad's proposed acquisition by CSX Inc.
Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) suggested that shareholders defeat a proposal that would permit CSX to pursue its proposed $8.5 billion stock and cash transaction.
Senior analyst Peter Gleason noted Norfolk Southern Corp's rival $10 billion cash bid that has been rejected by Conrail.
Gleason stated that all shareholders should be treated equally in any merger transaction and that opting out of the fair price provision would not be in shareholders' best interest.
Conrail investors are being asked to waive a Pennsylvania law that requires an all-cash payment by CSX.
CSX has already bought 19.9 percent of Conrail in a cash tender offer.
CSX and Conrail announced a merger that calls for CSX to buy 40 percent of Conrail in cash and the rest in stock.
ISS disputed Conrail's argument that the CSX offer is a better fit, stating that both potential combinations would create an East Coast railroad powerhouse.
Gleason wrote that CSX's takeover does not treat all Conrail shareholders fairly and that the agreement has denied shareholders the possibility of accepting a higher payment for their shares.
Under the agreement between Conrail and CSX, Conrail would be prohibited from entering a pact with another company before July 1997.

Western Resources Inc. offered to buy the rest of ADT Ltd. for $3.5 billion in cash and stock.
The acquisition would make Western Resources the top provider of electronic security services in the nation.
Western Resources currently owns 27 percent of ADT.
Western Resources plans to take its bid directly to ADT's shareholders.
Western Resources intends to call a special meeting to replace ADT's board of directors.
Western Resources Chairman John Hayes stated that the transaction offers compelling benefits.
Western Resources proposed to pay $22.50 for each share of ADT, consisting of $15 in stock and $7.50 in cash.
The offer represents a 12 percent premium over ADT's closing stock price of $20.125.
Industry experts described the bid as low and indicative of a hostile transaction.
ADT shares increased to $23.25 following speculation of a higher transaction price.

The Justice Department requested the Supreme Court to lift a lower court suspension of federal rules regarding local telephone monopolies.
The request was made on behalf of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC).
The Justice Department stated that the lower court's suspension could negatively impact consumers by delaying competition in the local phone market.
A U.S. appeals court in St. Louis suspended key provisions of the FCC's interconnection order.
The interconnection order outlines how long-distance carriers and cable-TV operators can operate in the local phone market.
The rules were frozen while the appeals court considers a challenge to the FCC order by GTE Corp. and other local carriers.
Opponents of the FCC order argue that the FCC exceeded its authority granted by Congress.
The FCC mandated that regional Bell companies lease their lines to new competitors at discounts of 17 percent to 25 percent.
The appeals court panel indicated that the opponents have a strong chance of convincing the court that the FCC's rules conflict with the law.
Long-distance carriers AT&T Corp. and MCI Communications Corp. also requested the Supreme Court to lift the stay.

Canada plans to develop its own satellite-TV industry.
Canada will not rely on U.S. companies such as Tele-Communications Inc. to start the business.
The Federal Communications Commission rejected a bid by TCI and TelQuest Ventures to beam TV programs to the U.S. from Canadian satellites.
The Canadian satellites were intended to beam shows to Canadian households using small dishes.
Telesat Canada, a Montreal-based satellite-communications company, was to launch the satellites.
John Manley, Canada's minister of industry, plans to invite Canadian companies to bid for the ownership and operation of two Canadian satellites.
Manley stated he would revoke support for Telesat's access to satellite slots unless the FCC approved the bid.
The FCC rejected TCI and TelQuest's requests because the Canadian government had not officially licensed the satellites.
The dispute involves objections from the Clinton administration regarding Canadian satellites beaming programs into the U.S.
U.S. officials argued that Canadian regulations discriminate against U.S. programmers by requiring Canadian content in broadcasts.

Regulators proposed to set aside $2.3 billion a year to link schools and libraries to the Internet at discounted rates.
The proposal does not endorse President Clinton's call to provide free Internet access to schools and libraries.
Eligible institutions could purchase access to the computer network at discounts ranging from 20 percent to 90 percent.
FCC Chairman Reed Hundt stated that schools will be able to connect every classroom to the Information Highway.
The Internet proposal is part of a broader plan to overhaul the universal service program for affordable phone service.
The FCC must adopt rules regarding the proposal by early May.
The proposal aims to generate lower phone rates through increased competition.
Some board members expressed concerns that the plan may be too ambitious and could increase rates.
Under the Internet provision, less affluent institutions and those in high-cost areas would receive larger discounts.
The average discount for institutions is expected to be 60 percent, with one-third of schools receiving at least an 80 percent discount.

The nation's distillers reversed their 48-year-old voluntary ban on broadcast advertising of liquor.
Distillers stated that whiskey and gin should be treated like beer and wine.
The announcement followed the presidential election and occurred before the holiday season.
Seagram Co. Ltd. began airing TV ads for its Royal Crown and Chivas Regal whiskey in June.
The ad campaign has faced criticism from lawmakers, regulators, and President Clinton.
Fred Meister is the president of the Distilled Spirits Council of the United States (DISCUS).
Meister claimed that the absence of spirits from advertising has led to misconceptions about their social treatment.
The reversal of the voluntary ban was included in DISCUS's 'code of good practice.'
FCC Chairman Reed Hundt opposed the decision and indicated potential new rules against liquor advertising.
Consumer advocates criticized the decision, claiming it would target children and teens.

A survey of 679 parents concluded that television industry moguls should specify sexual and violence content of shows.
80 percent of parents preferred a ratings system that specified the level of violence, sex, or bad language.
The survey was conducted by the National Parent Teacher Association, the Institute for Mental Health Initiatives, and University of Wisconsin researchers.
TV executives are working to complete a ratings system within the next month.
Executives favor an approach similar to the alphabetical code used by the Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA) for movies.
The survey sponsors and Rep. Edward Markey want a system that covers both content and viewer age.
Markey stated that parents want comprehensive information about every program.
A provision in the new communications law requires TV makers to install a 'V-chip' in all new sets.
The 'V-chip' can be used with the upcoming ratings to block shows considered too violent or racy.
Markey expressed concern that it would be unfortunate if the TV industry ignored the survey results.

Regulators took steps to reduce the cost of overseas phone calls for consumers and businesses.
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) aims to save U.S. callers billions of dollars.
The FCC plans to unveil a proposal next month to cut charges U.S. carriers pay foreign phone monopolies.
Americans spend about 16 cents a minute for domestic calls and an average of 99 cents a minute for overseas calls.
FCC Chairman Reed Hundt stated that the high cost of overseas calls hinders the development of a global information highway.
The new rules target countries with open phone markets to competition from U.S. carriers.
Countries mentioned by FCC officials include Canada, Britain, Chile, Sweden, Europe, and Mexico.
The FCC will waive rules limiting U.S. carriers' ability to negotiate cheaper rates with foreign companies in open markets.
Don Gips, head of the FCC's International Bureau, stated that the new rules will allow competitive pressures to govern the telecommunications market.
AT&T Corp. Vice President Gerry Salemme indicated that the new rules could significantly reduce costs for American consumers.

The state of Alaska has requested the Federal Communications Commission to ban broadcast advertising of hard liquor.
The petition from Alaska is supported by former U.S. Surgeon General C. Everett Koop.
Lawyers believe the petition could generate public debate or lead to rules restricting liquor promotions.
Attorney Nick Allard stated that a state asking the FCC to intervene legitimizes the commission's involvement.
The FCC is divided on the issue of liquor advertising.
FCC Chairman Reed Hundt supports banning liquor ads if TV stations do not comply with a voluntary ban.
Two of the FCC's four commissioners have expressed doubts about the FCC's authority to act on the matter.
The FCC has not yet decided how to respond to Alaska's request or a bipartisan request from 26 members of Congress.
The Federal Trade Commission has opened an investigation into alcoholic beverage advertising on TV.
Alaska's petition claims that advertising distilled spirits will increase alcohol use among young people.

Television and Hollywood moguls unveiled a new system to rate TV programmes on Thursday.
The new rating system is intended to help parents control their children's viewing habits.
Broadcast and cable-TV networks will display six ratings categories starting January 2.
The ratings will appear as a small icon in the upper left-hand corner of the TV screen.
The age-based rating system is similar to the motion-picture industry ratings that have been in place for 28 years.
The new ratings will apply to nearly all shows, including cartoons and talk shows, but news and sports programmes will be exempt.
President Bill Clinton described the new ratings as a significant improvement over the previous lack of a system.
Clinton stated that the ratings would assist families in selecting appropriate television programming for children.
The rating categories include TV-G, TV-PG, TV-14, TV-M, TV-Y, and TV-Y7.
Jack Valenti, president of the Motion Picture Association of America, led the group that developed the television ratings.

Regulators set aside a portion of airwaves to allow schools, businesses, and communities to send video images, data, and voice over local wireless networks.
The Federal Communications Commission's decision allows schools to create high-speed wireless networks that can connect to the World Wide Web.
Creating a wireless network can help schools avoid the costs associated with rewiring buildings for high-capacity phone lines.
Commissioner Susan Ness stated that a wireless connection is a cost-effective alternative to pulling wire through walls and ceilings in many buildings, including schools.
Hospitals, community groups, companies, and libraries can also create local high-speed networks or connect with nearby facilities.
Users of the new spectrum will not need an FCC license, similar to users of baby monitors and cordless phones.
High-speed wireless networks can transmit more data than traditional phone lines.
Computers equipped with antennas are expected to enable the creation of these networks by consumers, businesses, and hospitals.
Companies are set to produce the technology needed for the spectrum now that it has been set aside by the FCC.
The FCC has set power limits on different spectrum bands to prevent interference with existing users, such as satellites and government radar systems.

Newt Gingrich's intercepted telephone call has highlighted the ease of eavesdropping on cellular calls.
Cases of eavesdropping on cellular calls are seldom prosecuted despite daily violations of the law.
Rep. Billy Tauzin has called for hearings into cellular privacy following the incident involving Gingrich.
Federal law prohibits the intentional interception or disclosure of telephone call contents, regardless of the phone type.
Experts note that there are very few publicly known cases of eavesdropping on cellular calls.
Justice Department spokesman John Russell stated that the law regarding cellular calls is seldom enforced.
People often do not realize when they have been overheard on their cell phones.
Sen. Charles Robb faced controversy in 1991 over an illegal tape recording of a cellular call but was not indicted.
In 1990, an intercepted cell-phone conversation involving then-Rep. Bill Sarpalius led to fines for two unrelated men.
Clifford Fishman, a law professor, indicated that violations of eavesdropping laws are difficult to detect.

U.S. Vice President Al Gore defended last year's telecommunications law against critics.
Gore stated that the Clinton administration has no plans to reopen the telecommunications act.
Gore described the current year as the first year of a process of change regarding the law.
Several key provisions of the telecommunications law have yet to be implemented.
The telecommunications law was enacted on February 8 of the previous year.
The law removed 62-year-old legal barriers and encouraged competition among various service providers.
Critics, including Senator John McCain, argue that the local phone market remains a monopoly.
The long-distance market is dominated by AT&T Corp, MCI Communications Corp, and Sprint Corp.
Prices for communications services are rising, with cable-TV rates increasing by 7.8 percent last year.
Gore noted that the increases in cable-TV rates are not a result of the new law.

The Media Research Centre conducted a study on the television industry's new ratings system.
The study reviewed 150 hours of shows from six broadcast networks: ABC, CBS, Fox, NBC, UPN, and WB.
The study concluded that the age-based ratings system, which began on January 1, is confusing and contradictory.
The study found that 61 percent of shows received a TV-PG rating, although about half of these shows contained obscenities.
The study noted that words such as 'ass,' 'bastard,' and 'son of a bitch' were common in PG-rated shows.
The study reported inconsistencies within different episodes of the same series.
An episode of CBS's 'Moloney' received a TV-14 rating for a bloodless depiction of a shooting.
A subsequent episode of 'Moloney' received a lesser PG rating despite showing a bloody torture scene.
Brent Bozell, chairman of the Media Research Centre, stated that the new ratings system is a failure.
Kathryn Montgomery of the Centre for Media Education claimed that the ratings do not accurately reflect show content.

Nolan Bushnell founded Atari Corp. and created Chuck E. Cheese restaurants.
Bushnell aims to introduce high-tech jukeboxes and video games linked to the Internet in public places.
Bushnell stated he believes people can use the Internet through these devices.
Three devices named TeamNet, MusicNet Plus, and TouchNet were presented to reporters.
Aristo International Corp. plans to launch these machines worldwide early next month.
Bushnell and Aristo have invested over $10 million in the development of these machines.
The TeamNet machine allows two teams of up to eight players to compete via an Internet connection.
TouchNet is a coin-operated countertop touch-screen computer for playing games and sending messages.
The U.S. market for coin-operated games is currently valued at $6.8 billion annually.
Bushnell founded Atari in 1972 and opened the first Chuck E. Cheese restaurant in 1977.

Netscape Communications Corp. reported quarterly revenues of $100 million in the third quarter.
Netscape's third quarter net income was $7.7 million, or 9 cents a share.
A year ago, Netscape earned $175,000 on sales of $23.3 million.
Netscape President and Chief Executive Jim Barksdale stated that the third quarter of 1996 was a landmark quarter for the company.
Wall Street analysts expected Netscape to report revenues of $85 million to $90 million.
Netscape's quarterly revenue exceeded the $80.7 million it posted for the entire year of 1995.
For the first nine months, Netscape earned $12 million, or 14 cents a share, on sales of $231 million.
A year earlier, Netscape lost $7 million, or 10 cents a share, on sales of $44 million.
In after-hours trading, Netscape shares reached as high as $44.875.
Barksdale indicated that indirect sales through third parties accounted for 60 percent of overall sales.

Sun Microsystems Inc launched the Javastation network computer, its first machine to compete with low-end personal computers.
Analysts do not expect immediate high sales for the Javastation.
Evan Quinn, an analyst at International Data Corp, stated that the Javastation may begin competing with low-end PCs in a couple of years.
The entry-level Javastation will be available in December.
The entry price for the Javastation is $742.
The entry-level model will contain eight megabytes of memory.
A fully configured Javastation system will ship for $995 and include memory, a keyboard, a mouse, and a fourteen-inch monitor.
Sun Microsystems aims to appeal to corporate clients looking to reduce costs for upgrading and maintaining office PCs.
Microsoft Corp plans to enter the market with a light version of its Windows operating system.
International Business Machines Corp launched its first network computer model last month.

Odwalla Inc. is a specialty juicer company headquartered in Half Moon Bay.
Odwalla Inc. was founded 16 years ago on the premise that fresh, natural fruit juices nourish the spirit.
Greg Steltenpohl is a co-founder of Odwalla and expressed shock over the E. coli outbreak associated with their apple juice products.
Odwalla has experienced annual sales growth of more than 40 percent and reported $59.2 million in sales for the fiscal year ending August 31, 1996.
Odwalla is estimated to account for more than 70 percent of the fresh-juice market in the seven Western states and Vancouver, British Columbia.
Odwalla uses cold processing to retain vegetable and biological nutrients and emphasizes freshness in its marketing.
Odwalla has mobilized 175 trucks and drivers to recover recalled bottles from over 4,600 outlets.
Odwalla executives offered refunds for any drinks purchased, including those not among the recalled varieties.
Odwalla will pay for medical treatment for anyone who became ill from consuming its products.
Odwalla shares increased by $1.13 following the incident.

Diamond Multimedia Systems Inc plans to unveil advances in marketing enhanced video and audio technologies.
On Monday, Diamond will launch a deal with Toshiba Corp's Toshiba America Information Systems unit.
The deal will deliver one of the first DVD-ROM products to the retail market.
Chief Executive Bill Schroeder stated the company's plans.
Diamond will announce new proprietary 3-D audio software.
Diamond plans to enter the market for machines running Microsoft Corp's Windows NT system.
On Tuesday, Diamond plans to launch a new plug-and-play video conferencing product.
The video conferencing product will include a color camera and a microphone.
The estimated retail price of the video conferencing product is $399.
Schroeder stated that the company is on track to increase revenues and margins in its current fourth quarter.

Next week's Comdex computer industry show will feature Internet startups with limited resources.
Approximately 60 companies will present to potential investors at the first Comdex Venture Outlook.
Richard Shaffer is the principal of Technologic Partners, which organized the executives for the event.
Shaffer stated that many new Internet companies are being created daily.
Shaffer described the Internet as the most significant development in computing in the last 20 years.
Comdex organizers Softbank Corp. hired Shaffer's group to showcase young private companies focused on Web innovation.
Kim Polese is the chief executive of Marimba Inc., which was formed by members of Sun Microsystems' original Java team.
Marimba recently launched its Castanet software development tools for Internet applications.
Mark Goldstein is the Chief Executive of NetAngels, which has notable investors including Esther Dyson and Nicholas Nicholas.
David Arnold leads InterMind, a startup backed by Craig McCaw, which has launched the InterMind Communicator.

Intel Corp President and Chief Executive Andy Grove stated that by the year 2011, microprocessors may hold one billion transistors and deliver 100,000 million instructions per second.
Grove delivered the opening keynote address at the Comdex trade show, which celebrated the 25th anniversary of the first microprocessor.
Microprocessors are semiconductors invented by Intel engineers in 1971 that serve as the brains of PCs.
Grove claimed that by 2011, microprocessors could run at 10 gigahertz, which is four times the frequency of a microwave oven.
This speed would be approximately 50 times the frequency of the current top-of-the-line microprocessors.
Speeds of 100,000 MIPS would be 100,000 times the speed of Digital Equipment Corp's VAX 1180s.
The microprocessor of 1996 delivers 400 MIPS, running at a frequency of 200 megahertz with 5.5 million transistors.
This performance meets or exceeds a 1989 projection by Intel engineers of 100-MIPS machines at 150 megahertz.
The microprocessor of 2011 might fit on a die the size of a half dollar, or 1.8 inches, which is three times the current 0.6-inch die size.
The line width resolution of computer microprocessors may reach 0.07 micron by 2011, compared to 0.35 today.

A few years ago, one company led the market for groupware technology.
Groupware enables workers at different locations to collaborate on business projects using computers.
The rise of the Internet has created new opportunities for using groupware software more widely.
The market for groupware is driven by corporations' desire to use cheaper Internet technologies.
Some estimates suggest the groupware market may reach $10 billion by the year 2000.
Netscape Communications Corp. experienced explosive growth after going public in August 1995.
Netscape is focusing on using Internet technologies for building corporate intranets.
Intranets use inexpensive software to link people across an organization and provide access to information via a browser.
Microsoft Corp. is incorporating Internet technology throughout its products in response to Netscape's rise.
Lotus Development Corp. pioneered the groupware market with its Lotus Notes products.

High technology venture fund investment increased by 50 percent in the third quarter.
Overall U.S. venture investment rose by 25 percent compared to the same period last year.
The Price Waterhouse LLP National Venture Capital Survey reported that high technology industries received $1.32 billion in the third quarter.
High technology investments accounted for two-thirds of the total $2 billion invested during the third quarter.
Software investments more than doubled from the previous year to $596 million in the third quarter.
Total venture-backed investments in the U.S. for the first nine months of 1996 reached $7 billion.
The total venture-backed investments for the full year last year was reported at $7.5 billion.
The third-quarter total of $2 billion was a decrease from the $2.8 billion recorded in the second quarter.
Startup and early-stage companies received 46 percent of the venture capital investment, totaling $600 million.
Funding for Internet-related companies remained high, with 62 companies receiving funding in the third quarter.

In 1997, Internet users are expected to see more features aimed at making the Internet more lifelike.
Increased demand is likely to cause frequent communications breakdowns.
Robert Metcalfe is the inventor of Ethernet technology and founder of 3Com Corp.
Metcalfe is currently the vice president of technology at International Data Group in Boston, Massachusetts.
Metcalfe noted that congestion leads to the term 'World Wide Wait' and contributes to Internet crashes.
Major outages can be caused by minor events, such as a rodent chewing a power cable or a software error.
Over the summer, more than six million customers of America Online Inc. experienced a 19-hour service outage due to a software problem.
In October, a failure at BBN Corp.'s Stanford University Internet facility disrupted access for 400 high-tech firms for nearly a day.
Experts predict similar outages in the future as telecommunications companies and Internet providers struggle to meet demand.
New features expected in 1997 include advanced graphics and animated characters for communication in virtual chat rooms and games.

Netcom On-Line Communication Services Inc is shifting its focus to higher-value business services.
Netcom is leaving the consumer sector to other providers.
David Garrison is the Chairman and Chief Executive of Netcom.
Netcom has grown sixfold in three years.
Netcom aims for annualized growth in the 40-50 percent range.
Netcom will release new pricing plans in February, which will be above the current $19.95 access fee.
Netcom is discontinuing its current access fee, which Garrison believes is not beneficial for customers or shareholders.
The new services may provide higher quality access and could include bundled software tools or online Web-hosting services.
Most consumer-oriented Internet access providers charge $19.95 a month for unlimited access.
Netcom expects to gain 20,000 to 30,000 new paying customers in the fourth quarter, bringing the total to about 580,000.

KLA Instruments Corp. and Tencor Instruments announced a merger in a stock deal.
The merger will create a semiconductor capital equipment company with combined revenue exceeding $1 billion.
Analysts stated that the merger creates a significant player in the semiconductor capital equipment market.
The new company will provide one-stop shopping for chip process and diagnostics equipment.
The deal is valued at approximately $3.4 billion, based on 85.6 million shares outstanding after the stock swap.
The merger is subject to regulatory and shareholder approval and will be accounted for as a pooling of interests.
Under the merger agreement, KLA shares will be exchanged for Tencor shares on a one-to-one basis.
The combined company will employ more than 3,900 people worldwide.
The merger is expected to close during the quarter ending June 30, 1997.
KLA is based in San Jose, and Tencor is based in Milpitas, California.

Sun Microsystems Inc reported a 41 percent increase in profits for the latest quarter.
The company's revenues reached record levels, driven by sales of server computers and power desktop systems.
Net income for the fiscal second quarter ended December 29 was $178.3 million, up from $126 million in the same quarter the previous year.
Earnings per share increased to 46 cents from 32 cents.
Revenues rose nearly 19 percent to $2.08 billion.
Earnings per share exceeded Wall Street expectations of 42 cents, according to First Call.
Gross profit margins increased to 50.4 percent, up more than 5 percentage points from the previous year.
Sun's order backlog rose to $470 million from $407 million in the first quarter.
The backlog was less than the $522 million backlog at the end of the 1996 fiscal year.
Sun plans to announce new high-end computers, codenamed Starfire, next week.

Experts at a mutual fund conference stated that Indonesia's funds industry will remain dormant without government intervention.
Venkatagiri Mudeliar, deputy general manager of Dresdner Thornton Asset Management in Singapore, emphasized the need for a push from the government.
Indonesia's mutual funds industry faces challenges, including high returns from bank deposits that can reach 17 percent per annum.
More than 60 percent of pension fund assets, valued at US$2.4 billion, are held in bank deposits.
Seven newly-established mutual funds have assets of about US$642 million, which are similarly invested in bank deposits.
Recommended measures at the conference included tax benefits for mutual fund investors and an educational drive about mutual fund investments.
Felia Salim, director of the Jakarta Stock Exchange, reported that discussions for a tax break for mutual fund investors are ongoing.
Over 40 percent of the Jakarta Stock Exchange's budget for 1997 is allocated to educating the public about mutual fund benefits.
Foreign investment in Indonesia is restricted to 49 percent, limiting incentives for establishing investment management subsidiaries.
Paul Smith, managing director at the Bank of Bermuda in Hong Kong, noted that foreign fund managers are hesitant to invest in Indonesia's domestic mutual fund market.

Zero tax and limited regulation are attracting billions of dollars into offshore mutual funds.
The Cayman Islands is a notable location for tax-free offshore mutual funds.
Anthony Travers is a senior partner at Maples and Calder in Hong Kong.
Anecdotal evidence indicates that nearly US$900 billion has been drawn into offshore mutual funds.
The entire mutual fund industry is sometimes valued at US$5 trillion.
High taxation levels deter mutual funds from establishing in developed markets.
Offshore regions allow mutual funds to avoid tax while accessing lucrative investment areas.
Investing in offshore mutual funds can involve withholding tax and marketing issues.
Offshore mutual funds face restrictions on marketing to investors in the United States and the United Kingdom.
Offshore retail funds can be marketed in Europe if they comply with specific regulations.

Guinness Flight Asia expects Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index to rise to 14,000 points soon.
The selection of Hong Kong's new chief executive next month could support the Hang Seng Index.
The chief executive will be announced on December 11.
Hong Kong will return to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
Guinness Flight is maintaining a heavily overweight position on the Hong Kong stock market.
Nerissa Lee, investment director at Guinness Flight, holds a three-month target of 14,000 points for the Hang Seng Index.
Lee believes money will flow into Hong Kong as the preferred market in Asia.
Hong Kong is expected to benefit from credit easing in China.
Guinness Flight is also overweight in China, expecting strong recovery in company profits.
Lee forecasts Chinese economic growth of 9.8 percent this year and 10.2 percent next year.

Rival fund managers in Hong Kong condemned Jardine Fleming Investment Management (JFIM) for front-running.
Gregory Neumann, executive director at Scudder Stevens and Clark Asia Ltd, expressed that it is appalling for a respected portfolio manager to profit at the expense of clients.
Most fund managers were shocked by the severity of JFIM's actions and expressed concern about Hong Kong's regulatory integrity.
A five-month investigation by the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) revealed late allocation of trades by Colin Armstrong.
The investigation concluded that Armstrong's late trades, many involving his personal account, allowed him to benefit from changes in trading prices.
Jardine Fleming was fined 700,000 sterling for its actions.
JFIM's former chief executive Robert Thomas had his registration revoked in the United Kingdom and Hong Kong.
London-based Jardine Fleming Asset Management lost its authorisation.
Deborah Glass, SFC director, stated that Jardine Fleming's credibility is at stake and that the SFC will monitor their compliance.
Gary Greenberg, deputy managing director at Peregrine Asset Management, suggested that the Jardine Fleming incident may indicate broader issues in Asia's emerging markets.

Hong Kong business groups opposed U.S. attempts to link China's most favoured nation (MFN) trading perks with Beijing's handling of Hong Kong.
U.S. Congressman Jim Kolbe is leading a 22-member delegation from the House of Representatives to Beijing.
Kolbe stated that the United States will likely monitor Hong Kong for at least a year before granting China permanent MFN status.
Mark Michelson, former chairman of the American Chamber of Commerce, expressed that conditioning or removing MFN during the transition period would have a devastating effect on Hong Kong.
China currently enjoys MFN status, which is subject to annual review.
Hong Kong commentators believe that permanent MFN status for China is unlikely in 1997.
Frank Martin, president of the American Chamber of Commerce, stated that it would have been an opportune time for Congress to extend permanent MFN status if it were not for the return of Hong Kong to China.
Legislation on permanent MFN has been submitted to Congress but has not yet been voted on.
China argues that full MFN status is essential for healthy Sino-U.S. relations.
The Hong Kong government has always supported China's application for MFN status but declined to comment on Kolbe's remarks.

Economic commentators in Hong Kong are expressing concerns about rising stock and property prices ahead of the British colony's return to Chinese sovereignty on July 1.
There are worries that rising price pressures could create a bubble based on the assumption that China will support Hong Kong's economy during the transition.
Ian Perkin, chief economist with the Hong Kong Chamber of Commerce, noted a growing belief in local markets that there is little downside risk due to China's expected support.
Domestic confidence in China's commitment to economic stability in Hong Kong is high, leading to concerns about price instability.
Economists are revising their inflation forecasts for 1997 upwards due to increasing stock and luxury property prices.
Salomon Brothers has raised its 1997 forecast for Hong Kong's benchmark consumer price index to seven percent from 6.6 percent.
Sudden strength in Hong Kong's stock market was initially seen as a sign of confidence in the colony's future under China.
Speculation in the luxury property market emerged in November, raising concerns among economists.
The Hong Kong government has supported anti-speculation measures and warned of intervention if speculation affects lower property market segments.
Economists believe that property price volatility will eventually lead to overall inflation, despite being currently limited to the high-end market.

Hong Kong people prepared to celebrate the Year of the Ox, their last Lunar New Year under British rule.
Hong Kong has a population of 6.3 million people.
Residents engaged in last-minute shopping and traveled to China to visit relatives.
Children participated in throwing empty red 'lai see' money pockets at each other.
Ng Chak Kwong expressed a desire for a prosperous year during the celebrations.
The Lunar New Year festivities occurred amid rising political tension in Hong Kong.
The Democratic Party collected 20,000 signatures opposing proposed changes to civil liberties laws.
The international community protested China's plans regarding Hong Kong's civil liberties.
Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen stated that Hong Kong's return to China would end a long period of humiliation for China.
Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa defended Beijing's proposed changes but faced skepticism.

Impoverished women from mainland China are increasingly working as prostitutes in Hong Kong.
A deportation policy is driving away Thai and Filipina women from the sex trade in Hong Kong.
Mainland Chinese women now dominate the prostitution workforce in Mongkok, Hong Kong.
The number of mainland Chinese prostitutes is rising to meet demand after the departure of other nationalities.
Two-way permits allow Chinese nationals to visit Hong Kong for limited short periods.
Working as a prostitute is not illegal in Hong Kong unless the woman is on a tourist visa.
Pimping and soliciting are offenses in Hong Kong.
Policy changes in 1994 allowed police to arrest and imprison prostitutes on visitor's visas.
The number of arrests of two-way permit holders working as prostitutes in Mongkok increased from 967 in 1995 to 1,026 in 1996.
The number of arrests of Filipinas, Thais, and Malaysian women fell from 273 in 1995 to 106 in 1996.

Hong Kong business groups praised Deng Xiaoping as a great leader following his passing.
Brigadier Christopher Hammerbeck stated that the short-term impact of Deng's passing on business would be limited.
Ian Christie described Deng as a great man of vision for his economic reforms and the 'one country, two systems' policy.
Mark Michelson expressed that it would have been better if Deng had witnessed the Hong Kong handover on July 1.
Michelson noted that there has been a leadership succession associated with the transition in Hong Kong.
The collective leadership in place is led by President Jiang Zemin.
Most business groups did not speculate on the long-term implications of Deng's death.
The South China Morning Post raised concerns about a possible power struggle in Beijing following Deng's death.
The Trade Development Council stated that Deng will not be forgotten for his contributions to Hong Kong's trade growth.
Michael Sze highlighted that Hong Kong's ranking in world trade improved from 23rd in 1979 to 8th today.

Deng Xiaoping, a key figure in Hong Kong's stability, has died.
Deng was the architect of the 'One country, two systems' policy.
Hong Kong is set to return to China on July 1 this year.
Deng's open-door policy transformed Hong Kong's economy into a service center.
His death is considered an important milestone for Hong Kong.
The immediate impact of Deng's death on Hong Kong affairs is expected to be small.
The long-term effects of his death may be significant as Hong Kong transitions to a Special Administrative Region of China.
Economic reforms initiated by Deng are expected to continue.
In 1995, Hong Kong accounted for $80 billion of direct investment in China.
George Leung, an economist, predicts that Hong Kong will not see double-digit growth rates again.

Analysts predict that Asia will suffer only minor damage from a shake-out in Thailand's banking sector.
Carmen Welso is a banking analyst with ING Barings in Hong Kong.
The Thai government has acknowledged that its banks and finance companies are facing a liquidity problem due to bad debts linked to the property sector.
The Bank of Thailand has ordered banks and finance companies to raise provisions for sub-standard loans and has asked 10 finance firms to boost capital.
Analysts expect a wave of consolidation in Thailand's financial services sector.
Thailand currently has about 90 finance companies, but one analyst suggested it needs only about five.
Indonesia and the Philippines may restrict property lending rules to avoid Thailand's situation.
Development Bank of Singapore owns part of Thai Danu Bank, which announced a merger with Finance One Plc.
Finance One is Thailand's largest finance company.
Citibank, HSBC Holdings Plc, and ING Barings are considered likely buyers of Thai banks, although foreign ownership is restricted to 25 percent.

Foreign investors seeking access to China could consider the road industry.
The road industry in China needs more than US$6 billion in foreign investment to complete four national highways by 2000, according to SBC Warburg.
Low rates of investment are largely responsible for clogged highways in China.
As of the end of 1994, 1,500 counties and 190,000 villages in China had no road access.
The growth in civilian vehicles in China has risen at a compound rate of 13.4 percent each year between 1978 and 1995.
The total length of highways in China increased by an average of 1.6 percent a year between 1978 and 1995.
SBC Warburg stated that insufficient investment is the main reason behind the slow development of China's highway network.
China plans to build a network of 12 national trunk routes totaling 30,000 km by 2010, with the first four highways to be completed by 2000.
The total construction cost for the highway network is estimated at 540 billion yuan ($65 billion) over 10 years, with most funding coming from domestic sources, the World Bank, and the Asian Development Bank.
SBC Warburg estimated that as much as $6 billion will need to come from foreign investors.

Chinese President Jiang Zemin spoke on the 60th anniversary of a communist military ordeal.
Jiang Zemin aimed to strengthen his control over the army by urging soldiers to follow the party line.
Western diplomats believe Jiang's ability to succeed Deng Xiaoping depends on winning military support.
Jiang referenced the Long March as an example of the Communist Party's leadership over the army.
Jiang stated that every army comrade must adhere to the party's principles without wavering.
Jiang advised officers and soldiers to follow the direction of communist leaders and enforce the party line.
Jiang claimed the PLA's survival during the Long March and victory in 1949 was due to the Communist Party's leadership.
Jiang called for the army to remain loyal to the party, socialism, the motherland, and the people.
Jiang wore a military green Mao suit during his address to military leaders and veterans.
Other party and army leaders expressed support for Jiang, who holds multiple powerful positions in China.

Colombian Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia visited China to discuss cooperation on narcotics trade.
Colombian officials aim to sign an agreement with China to enhance information exchanges and police training against drugs.
Mejia stated that China expressed a strong desire to cooperate on drug-related issues.
Mejia noted that Colombia has limited knowledge about narcotics trafficking in Asia.
Mejia emphasized the need for mutual understanding between Colombia and China regarding narco-trafficking.
Colombian President Ernesto Samper mentioned that Beijing supports Colombia's anti-drug efforts.
Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen called for drug-consuming nations to reduce domestic drug use.
General Rosso Jose Serrano stated that there is no known connection between Colombian and Chinese drug traffickers.
A U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration report indicated that Colombia is the top supplier of high-grade heroin to the United States.
The report stated that 62 percent of heroin confiscated in the United States originated from Colombia.

China has urged Tibet to embrace atheism to counter the influence of the Dalai Lama.
Beijing criticized the European Union for allowing a meeting between European Parliament officials and the Dalai Lama.
China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang expressed dissatisfaction with the EU regarding the meeting.
China called on officials in Tibet to promote atheism and socialist beliefs to reduce the Dalai Lama's influence.
The Tibet Daily stated that atheistic education is necessary to oppose the Dalai Lama's teachings.
Beijing denies accusations of human rights abuses and religious persecution in Tibet.
The Tibet Daily claimed that traditional Buddhist beliefs hinder development in the region.
The newspaper accused the Dalai Lama of attempting to separate Tibet from China.
The Dalai Lama fled Tibet in 1959 after a failed revolt against Chinese rule.
The Dalai Lama won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989 for his campaign for autonomy.

U.S. Vice-President Al Gore could visit China in early 1997 if he is re-elected next month.
Eileen Claussen, U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for Oceans and International Environmental and Scientific Affairs, stated that a proposal for Gore's visit has been reviewed with no real disagreement.
Claussen mentioned that Gore is interested in establishing a sustainable development forum with Chinese Premier Li Peng.
No specific date has been set for Gore's visit to China.
Claussen indicated that discussions are ongoing regarding the terms of reference for the visit.
A visit by Gore could improve Sino-U.S. relations, which have been strained.
Sino-U.S. ties reached a low point after the U.S. allowed Taiwan's President Lee Teng-hui to visit in June 1995.
China considers Taiwan a rebel province and seeks to isolate it diplomatically.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher is scheduled to visit Beijing in November.
Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian plans to visit Washington before the end of the year.

U.S. Undersecretary of State Lynn Davis has begun talks with Chinese officials in Beijing on arms proliferation issues.
Davis arrived in Beijing last Thursday and was scheduled to hold talks on Monday and Tuesday.
Davis is the undersecretary for arms control issues and will discuss a range of topics with Chinese officials.
Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Robert Einhorn visited Beijing last week prior to Davis's arrival.
John Holum, director of the U.S. Arms Control and Disarmament Agency, also visited Beijing recently.
Davis is expected to discuss the implementation of a peaceful nuclear cooperation accord from 1985 that would allow U.S. firms to sell nuclear power reactors to China.
China has sought foreign technology with potential military value through lucrative business contracts.
China's official Xinhua news agency reported that U.S. firms could gain billions in nuclear energy contracts if the 1985 agreement is implemented.
Li Donghui, deputy-general director of the China National Nuclear Corp's international cooperation bureau, stated that negotiations on the agreement are ongoing.
The 1985 pact has not been implemented due to U.S. concerns about China's nuclear technology sales to unsafeguarded facilities, particularly in Pakistan.

The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit this month may reveal conflicting views between regional powers and a Chinese delegation.
The United States, Japan, and Canada aim to lower trade barriers at the APEC summit.
China is seeking easy credit from wealthier APEC members at the summit in the Philippines.
There is a fundamental tension between China and most other APEC states regarding trade and economic cooperation.
Analysts state that the Subic summit will provide Chinese president Jiang Zemin an opportunity to enhance cross-Pacific ties.
The summit will allow for private talks between the Chinese delegation and the United States, as well as possibly Taiwan.
China is concerned that free trade could harm its struggling state sector and lead to social unrest.
China is suggesting that APEC members should provide financial support in exchange for access to its markets.
Beijing may seek the establishment of a special APEC fund to assist developing countries in the region.
The summit offers Jiang Zemin a chance to engage with other world leaders and improve Sino-U.S. relations.

Wang Dan is a jailed Chinese dissident suffering from severe throat and back problems.
Wang Dan is serving an 11-year sentence for plotting to overthrow the government.
Wang's mother, Wang Lingyun, reported his health issues after visiting him in Jinzhou prison, Liaoning province.
Wang is experiencing throat inflammation, back ailments, and a prostate problem.
Medical specialists examined Wang and informed him that the prison lacks facilities to treat his conditions.
Wang's condition could worsen with the onset of winter due to the prison's cold and dry environment.
Wang Lingyun stated that the family plans to petition the courts to review Wang's case.
A Chinese court recently rejected Wang's appeal and upheld his prison sentence for subversion.
Wang Lingyun mentioned that her son appeared in good spirits during her visit.
Wang has previously served four years in prison for his involvement in the 1989 student demonstrations.

China warned the United States to stop selling arms to Taiwan.
China stated that arms sales to Taiwan could ruin Sino-U.S. relations.
The official China Daily claimed that Washington's arms sales would destroy the warming Sino-U.S. relationship.
Chi Haotian is on a two-week visit to the United States.
Taiwan's procurement of U.S. weapons could undermine peaceful reunification with mainland China.
Beijing aims for reunification with Taiwan at any cost.
Chi Haotian held talks with President Bill Clinton and Defence Secretary William Perry.
Beijing and Taipei split at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
Sino-U.S. relations were strained in March due to U.S. military actions near Taiwan.
Washington recognizes Beijing as the sole legal representative of all China but maintains the right to arm Taiwan.

China is airing a primetime television series about Deng Xiaoping.
The documentary is receiving mixed reviews from Beijing residents.
The series consists of 12 parts and focuses on Deng Xiaoping, who is 92 years old.
A 35-year-old journalist expressed admiration for the series and stated that Deng should be honored for China's economic development.
Deng Xiaoping has not been seen in public for nearly two years and appeared frail in his last public appearance.
There is speculation about Deng's health, including rumors of hospitalization and reports of fading lucidity.
Analysts believe the documentary will help define Deng's legacy for the current Communist Party leadership.
The latest episode of the series covers the period after the 1949 Communist revolution and discusses Deng's market-oriented economic policies.
Some viewers noted that the series does not compare Deng's policies with those of Mao Zedong.
The series has not mentioned Deng's second wife, who left him in 1932.

China warned the United States that warming Sino-U.S. ties could be complicated by confrontations over human rights.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang stated that the human rights issue should not interfere in China's internal affairs.
Shen Guofang claimed that using the human rights question to pressure the Chinese government would complicate relations.
Sino-U.S. relations deteriorated in 1995 and 1996 due to clashes over human rights and other issues.
Sino-U.S. ties have recently started to recover with high-level official meetings.
