Analysts believe sentiment remains bullish for the coming weeks.
SPT Telecom, CEZ, and Komercni Banka fell sharply, dragging the PX50 index down 0.28 percent to 598.0 points.
Marco Anderegg of Patria Finance stated that there seems to be good support at the current level.
Foreign investor interest remains solid according to Marco Anderegg.
SPT Telecom shares closed down 75 crowns at 3,700.
CEZ shares were down 28 crowns to 1,202.
Komercni Banka shares lost 25 crowns to 2,620.
A local trader suggested that the market's weakness may be short-lived and prices could begin rising again soon.
The PSE has gained 9.7 percent so far in 1997.

British hotels and betting group Ladbroke Group Plc announced the closure of its property arm.
Ladbroke Group Plc will sell its remaining properties to focus on its core businesses of hotels and betting and gaming.
Brian Wallace is the group finance director of Ladbroke.
The cost of the closure is estimated at 52.3 million pounds ($84.4 million).
The closure cost will mainly cover losses from the sale of property and a provision to write down the remaining portfolio.
Ladbroke's 1996 accounts will include a non-operating exceptional charge of 17.6 million pounds.
The exceptional charge mainly represents losses on disposals of investment properties announced during 1996.
Analysts noted that the closure and property sales removed uncertainty for Ladbroke in 1997.
Ladbroke is expected to report a profit rise of around 30 percent for 1996.
The portfolio sold to Minerva Plc had a book value of about 34.6 million pounds and consisted of around 10 commercial and residential properties.

Michael Marks was the chairman of British stockbroking firm Smith New Court before it was taken over by Merrill Lynch.
Michael Marks was appointed chief operating officer for Europe, the Middle East and Africa at Merrill Lynch.
Michael Marks was previously co-head of global equities and will remain as deputy chairman of Merrill Lynch International.
Michael Marks's appointment as chief operating officer comes into force on June 16.
Michael Marks stated that the realignment emphasizes the importance of London as a financial center.
Merrill Lynch International will have a coordinating role to ensure clients are well served.
Under the new structure, there will be five chief operating officers for Merrill's international regions.
Kevin Watts was made chief operating officer for the Asia-Pacific region.
Merrill Lynch's new structure includes a U.S. private client group, an international private client group, an asset management group, and a corporate and institutional client group.
Michael Marks began his career in the City of London with Smith Brothers in 1960.

A future Labour government may overhaul Britain's Securities and Investments Board (SIB).
The SIB must find a new chairman.
The Labour Party plans to streamline London's regulatory bodies if it wins the upcoming elections.
The SIB was established in 1985.
The SIB is responsible for ensuring the regulatory system works efficiently.
Chairman Sir Andrew Large will resign at the end of May.
Industry sources believe the new chairman may not come from Britain's frontline regulators.
The SIB supervises frontline regulators that authorize firms to conduct investment business in Britain.
Sir Andrew Large stated that most changes he was overseeing have been completed.
The appointment of a new SIB chairman will be significant due to the potential change in government.

A Chinese court rejected a plea of insanity by bank robber Guo Song and sentenced him to death.
Guo Song was convicted along with two accomplices for a series of bank heists in Beijing.
The court proceedings were observed by foreign reporters to highlight a crackdown on crime.
Guo Song appeared unrepentant during the court session.
The Beijing Number One Intermediate People's Court convicted Guo Song of robbing three bank cash delivery vans.
The presiding judge stated that the court did not accept Guo Song's plea of insanity.
Psychiatric tests indicated that Guo Song had total control over his mental faculties during the crime.
Guo Song, 32 years old, did not speak during the 20-minute hearing.
Guo Song has two weeks to file an appeal to the Higher People's Court.
Guo Song was previously sentenced to four years for rape and was found guilty of shooting four bank guards.

China introduced rules governing direct shipping links with Taiwan on Tuesday.
The new regulations allow only wholly Chinese-owned or Taiwan-owned shipping companies or joint ventures involving Chinese or Taiwanese shipowners to operate between the two sides.
Xinhua news agency reported that Xiamen and Fuzhou would be the first ports opened to direct shipping links with Taiwan.
Taiwan's Nationalist government has banned direct air and shipping links with China since 1949.
Civilian aircraft and vessels have circumvented the ban by stopping in third countries or territories.
Taiwanese businessmen have invested more than $20 billion into China and are eager for direct transport links.
Taiwanese authorities have been reluctant to lift the ban on direct transport links.
The Chinese Ministry of Communications must approve shipping companies wishing to operate routes between the two sides.
The ministry has 45 days to decide on shipping company applications according to the new regulations.
The central bank of Taiwan denied a report about studying how to control capital outflows to China.

China's stock markets are currently overheating.
The People's Daily newspaper warned of a potential crash similar to the Wall Street collapse of 1929.
China's foreign currency B share market in Shanghai rose by about 80 percent between November 11 and December 10.
The Shenzhen stock market increased by about 100 percent before experiencing sharp declines.
The Shanghai B-share market fell by 12.26 percent on a recent Friday.
The Shenzhen stock market dropped by 14.75 percent on the same day.
The Shanghai A-share index decreased by 5.51 percent.
The Shenzhen A-share index declined by 4.84 percent.
The commentary stated that the government would not intervene to support the markets during downturns.
The commentary suggested that bank savings are the safest investment method.

Australian Treasurer Peter Costello announced financial reforms on Wednesday.
The reforms are the largest since 1983.
The reforms loosen restrictions on bank and life office mergers and foreign takeovers of banks.
Costello did not allow mergers between Australia's big four banks: Westpac, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ), National Australia Bank (NAB), and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Costello announced the abolition of the 'Six Pillars' policy.
The 'Six Pillars' policy prevented mergers between major banks and two largest pension and life insurance groups.
Costello stated that the Treasurer will retain powers to reject mergers under relevant banking and insurance laws.
Costello indicated that major domestic banks would not be allowed to merge at this time.
Costello announced the end of the outright ban on foreign takeovers of Australian banks.
Costello emphasized that large-scale transfer of Australian ownership of the financial system to foreign hands would be contrary to the national interest.

Australia's anti-monopolies watchdog is examining claims of collusion against the four major banks.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has asked the banks to explain why they cut their mortgage rates by the same amount within hours of each other.
ACCC Chairman Allan Fels stated it was unusual for the banks to all move quickly to cut their rates by the same amount.
Fels mentioned that the ACCC does not claim to have evidence of collusion but is seeking an explanation from the banks.
National Australia Bank, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, and Westpac Banking Corp all cut their standard variable mortgage rates by 0.35 percent to 7.2 percent.
The banks made these cuts hours after the Reserve Bank reduced official rates by 0.5 percent to 5.5 percent.
Government and opposition politicians, along with consumer groups, have suggested that the banks colluded to limit the passing on of the official rate cut to customers.
Fels indicated that the commission would request details of any communications between the banks on the day of the rate cuts.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia denied collusion with other major banks and stated it had not discussed interest rates with them.
CBA Managing Director David Murray emphasized that the bank believes in competition and would cooperate fully with the ACCC.

Treasurer Peter Costello announced financial reforms in Australia on Wednesday.
The reforms are the largest since 1983.
The reforms loosen restrictions on bank and life office mergers and foreign takeovers of banks.
Costello did not allow mergers between Australia's big four banks: Westpac, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ), National Australia Bank (NAB), and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Costello warned that foreigners would not be allowed to buy a significant portion of Australia's banking sector.
Costello announced the abolition of the 'Six Pillars' policy.
The 'Six Pillars' policy prevented mergers between major banks and two largest pension and life insurance groups.
The 'Six Pillars' policy was introduced by former Labor treasurer Paul Keating.
Costello's government set up the Wallis Inquiry to reform Labor's policies.
The government decided that mergers among the four major banks will not be permitted at this time.

U.S. Robotics Corp's stock increased on Wednesday due to speculation about a faster analog modem.
U.S. Robotics is based in Skokie, Illinois.
U.S. Robotics announced at an Oppenheimer & Co investors conference that it is exploring new technologies, including higher speed modems.
U.S. Robotics previously stated that it did not believe 33.6 kilobits per second was the fastest speed for modems.
An Oppenheimer analyst noted that the presentation about the faster modem was more detailed than previous discussions.
Oppenheimer analyst Steven Levy mentioned that this was the first time U.S. Robotics discussed the topic with slides.
Rockwell International Corp's semiconductor systems unit plans to demonstrate 56 kilobit transmission capabilities at a trade show in November.
Analysts believe that a modem capable of 56 kilobits would enhance Internet communication over standard telephone lines.
U.S. Robotics holds approximately an 80 percent share of the modem market for online services and a 38 percent share for desktop modems.
U.S. Robotics declined to comment on whether it was close to releasing a faster modem.

The U.S. bank megamergers of 1995 have been completed.
First Bank System Inc announced the acquisition of U.S. Bancorp for nearly $9 billion.
Steven Schroll is a banking analyst at Piper Jaffray.
Schroll stated that 1997 is starting similarly to 1995.
SNL Securities LP reported $12.85 billion in bank and thrift acquisitions announced in 1997.
In 1995, there were $74.4 billion in bank deals.
In 1996, bank deals fell to $46.27 billion.
Regulatory barriers to mergers between banks, insurance companies, and securities firms are likely to be lowered.
Frank Barkocy is an analyst at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.
Barkocy noted that the recent deal could lead to increased merger and acquisition activity.

Wallace Computer Services Inc has strong business fundamentals.
Analysts believe a change in the shareholder profile of Wallace Computer Services Inc will protect it from a bid by investor Guy Wyser-Pratte.
Judith Scott is an analyst at Robert W. Baird.
Judith Scott stated that Wallace has created shareholder value.
Moore Corp Ltd abandoned its 13-month takeover campaign in early August.
Martin McDevitt Jr. is an analyst at Cleary Gull Reiland and McDevitt.
Martin McDevitt Jr. noted a substantial change in the profile of the Wallace shareholder base since August 6.
Most of the selling of Wallace stock since early August is attributed to arbitrageurs.
McDevitt believes the current shareholder base is likely composed of long-term investors.
Wyser-Pratte controls a 2.3 percent stake in Wallace and filed proxy materials with the SEC.

Canadian police announced on Wednesday that they laid more charges in a sex scandal involving young boys at Maple Leaf Gardens.
Police filed 50 additional charges of sexual abuse against Gordon Stuckless, 47, a former backstage helper at Maple Leaf Gardens.
Gordon Stuckless now faces a total of 52 charges, including indecent assault, gross indecency, and buggery.
Stuckless and another former employee, John Paul Roby, allegedly lured teenage boys to the arena with free tickets and autographs.
John Paul Roby is currently facing 75 charges of sexual abuse.
Toronto police detective Dave Tredrea stated that the investigation is ongoing.
Police reported that the abuse occurred in the back rooms of the arena, sometimes during hockey games or events.
The scandal may involve up to 90 victims from the late 1960s to early 1990s.
The allegations surfaced after Martin Kruze, 34, came forward with claims of sexual abuse starting when he was 13.
Retired deputy police chief Walter Tyrrell has been appointed to review security at Maple Leaf Gardens.

Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd. resumed trading on Wednesday.
Trading volumes overwhelmed the computer system on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Bre-X's stock fell C65 cents to C$3.20 on the TSE on Wednesday.
Trading was stopped in late morning due to heavy order volumes and technical difficulties.
Bre-X had a turnover of 11.7 million shares during the abbreviated trading session.
The stock was halted all day on Monday and resumed trading for 22 minutes on Tuesday.
Bre-X's market value decreased by almost C$3 billion last Thursday.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. revealed that drilling samples from the Busang property showed insignificant amounts of gold.
Bre-X stock continued trading on Nasdaq and other exchanges despite issues on the TSE.
Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh claimed that tampering with core samples was impossible.

Canada's top securities regulator is probing Bre-X Minerals Ltd for potential breaches of insider trading and disclosure laws.
The Ontario Securities Commission has been investigating Bre-X Minerals since the end of 1996.
The OSC confirmed that the investigation relates to breaches of continuous disclosure requirements or insider trading provisions.
The OSC has not determined if there is enough information to begin formal proceedings against Bre-X.
The investigation is focusing on potential breaches of Ontario's Securities Act.
A group of Canadian Bre-X shareholders launched a class action lawsuit on Thursday.
Bre-X Minerals faces five court actions in the United States.
The Toronto Stock Exchange halted trading of Bre-X shares on Thursday due to heavy order volumes.
A report on Bre-X's assay program confirmed the company's original findings but raised new questions about the gold project.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. revealed that early drilling samples from the Busang gold property showed only tiny amounts of gold.

General Motors Corp. workers ratified a new labour contract.
The United Auto Workers union reported that 85 percent of the workers who voted approved the contract.
The approval margin is the largest in 20 years.
The contract affects more than 386,000 hourly workers at GM, Ford Motor Co., and Chrysler Corp.
Negotiations at GM led to a national strike by the Canadian Auto Workers in October.
Local UAW strikes occurred at two GM plants and extended into November.
GM estimated that the walkouts would reduce its fourth quarter profits by approximately $700 million.
Costs associated with the UAW pact are expected to be around $170 million.
The GM contract follows the pattern set by Ford and Chrysler, including a guarantee to maintain 95 percent employment of its UAW hourly workforce.
The GM pact includes restrictions to prevent the shifting of parts work to outside suppliers.

Ford Motor Co. reported a 2.2 percent decline in U.S. light vehicle sales in November.
The decline in Ford's sales was attributed to a significant drop in car sales, despite gains in truck sales.
General Motors Corp. reported a 12 percent drop in November sales.
Chrysler Corp. reported a 1.4 percent increase in November sales.
Ford sold 290,774 cars and light trucks in November, down from 297,362 a year earlier.
Domestic car sales for Ford fell 11.3 percent to 52,101 units.
Light truck sales for Ford rose 5.7 percent to 175,606 units.
Ford's import car sales fell 48.2 percent to 1,597 units.
Robert Rewey, Ford's group vice president of sales and marketing, stated that the retail market is shifting from cars to light trucks.
Ford's combined sales of the Explorer, Mountaineer, and Expedition sport utility vehicles rose 38 percent to 55,343 units.

General Motors Corp. experienced a 50.8 percent drop in fourth quarter earnings from continuing operations.
Wall Street had anticipated the earnings drop from General Motors Corp.
General Motors Corp. generated strong cash, raising hopes for a strong performance in 1997.
At year-end, General Motors Corp.'s cash and marketable securities exceeded $17 billion.
General Motors Corp.'s cash and marketable securities increased by $2.5 billion from September 30, 1996.
General Motors Corp.'s cash and marketable securities increased by $6.8 billion from a year earlier.
$1 billion of General Motors Corp.'s fourth quarter cash increase was due to a tax refund.
Analysts noted a $1.5 billion increase in cash from operations affected by strikes.
General Motors Corp.'s fourth quarter North American production volume fell by 11.4 percent.
General Motors Corp. reported a $124 million loss in North America for the fourth quarter.

Ford Motor Co announced it would cut 1,300 jobs at its Halewood plant near Liverpool, England.
The job cuts represent almost one third of the Halewood workforce.
The Halewood plant will not build the planned new model of the Escort car, due in 1999.
Production of the new Escort model is likely to transfer to factories in Spain and Germany.
Ford stated that Halewood could become the European source for a planned new vehicle, which is still a concept.
Halewood will continue to produce the current Escort model through 2000.
David Gorman, European vehicle operations manager for Ford, commented on the future of the Halewood plant.
Local MP David Alton reported that Ford indicated the job losses would occur through voluntary redundancy.
The proposed job cuts will reduce Halewood's workforce to just over 3,000 from a peak of 14,000 in the 1960s.
Workers expressed anger over the job cuts, attributing them to British labour laws and the lack of the European Union's Social Chapter.

Tomkins Plc is a UK conglomerate with businesses in baking and engineering.
Tomkins Plc is expected to see a rise in half-year pretax profits.
Analysts predict six-month profits of around 160 million stg, up from 126.1 million stg the previous year.
The average forecast for the half-year payout is 3.0 pence per share, up from 2.70 pence last time.
Tomkins shares have recently gained following a 'buy' recommendation from Kleinwort Benson analysts.
Tomkins was listed as one of the nine stocks to buy in 1997 by Credit Lyonnais Laing.
Tomkins shares are currently at 278 pence, down two pence.
The group board obtained permission for a buyback of up to 10 percent of its shares in 1995.
Tomkins currently has around 400 million stg in cash.
Analyst Ian Rennardson from Credit Lyonnais stated that the group has not indicated a buyback at the interim stage.

Britain's building sector has shown signs of recovery in the domestic housing market.
Sales in the housing market are increasing.
Housebuilders are expected to benefit from the recovery.
RMC Plc, Redland Plc, and BPB experienced a decline in their share prices.
RMC's shares fell by 36p to 903.5.
Redland's shares closed 5.5p lower at 330.
BPB's shares decreased by 13p to 362.5p.
Blue Circle's shares dropped by 7.5p to 368.
Concerns about the German economy and the rising value of the pound are affecting building material companies.
Germany accounts for up to 40 percent of profits for some building materials firms.

New York state utility regulators approved the $23 billion merger between Nynex Corp. and Bell Atlantic Corp.
The approval is subject to conditions that must be agreed upon by the companies by the end of March.
Consumer groups opposed the merger and criticized the decision as a sellout.
New York was the last state in Nynex's six-state service region to approve the merger.
The merger would create the largest local phone company in the United States, serving customers in 12 Northeastern states and Washington.
John O'Mara, Chairman of the New York State Public Service Commission, stated that improved service quality and tangible benefits for ratepayers are requirements for approval.
O'Mara indicated that there would be no immediate rate reduction but conditions attached to the merger could lead to rate reductions in the future.
Federal regulators are reviewing the merger's competitive implications, which is delaying the process.
Bell Atlantic spokesman Eric Rabe stated that the companies expect the deal to close after April 22.
The combined company must keep major operations in New York state and maintain its headquarters there, as agreed by both companies.

America Online Inc. plans to place advertising on company-sponsored discussion areas.
The company aims to expand its revenue base beyond mainly subscriber fees.
America Online is based in Dulles, Virginia.
The company expects to generate 360 million ad impressions every month from chat rooms.
An analyst estimated that this program could generate $15 million to $25 million in new revenues in 1997.
Impressions are the standard way of measuring the impact of individual ad promotions in the advertising industry.
America Online stock rose $3.75 to $43.75 a share on the New York Stock Exchange.
Bob Pittman is the president of America Online Networks.
Over 70 percent of America Online members engage in chat, logging 1 million hours of chat every day.
Brian Oakes, a Lehman Brothers analyst, estimated that chat rooms account for about 23 percent of online usage time among America Online subscribers.

America Online Inc. plans to launch a national Internet service in Japan in mid-April.
America Online Inc. aims to make Japan its biggest international market within a couple of years.
AOL Chairman Steve Case stated that Japan is a significant market opportunity for AOL.
AOL Japan Inc. is a joint venture involving America Online, Mitsui & Co. Ltd., and Nihon Keizai Shimbun Inc.
America Online owns a 50 percent stake in AOL Japan, Mitsui owns 40 percent, and Nikkei owns 10 percent.
AOL Japan will offer multimedia features not available on other Japanese online services.
Leading online service providers in Japan include Nifty-serve, PCVAN, and ASCIINet.
AOL Japan's service will be provided in the Japanese language.
AOL Japan will charge a monthly fee of 980 Japanese yen for three hours of use.
New members of AOL Japan will receive a 10-hour free trial in the first month.

Nomura Securities reported that two directors were involved in suspected illegal deals.
Speculation is increasing that similar scandals may occur at other brokerages.
Daiwa Securities Co Ltd's share price fell due to speculation about a news conference regarding a probe by the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC).
A Daiwa spokesman stated that the SESC has been conducting a routine inspection since March 3.
Two directors at Nomura resigned after the brokerage disclosed their involvement in illegal deals and funneling funds to a corporate client linked to a former racketeer.
This incident occurred six years after a scandal involving improper compensation to favored clients affected Japan's securities industry.
Top executives at Nomura and Nikko Securities Co Ltd resigned in 1991 due to improper compensation and dealings with gangsters.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto criticized Nomura for damaging the reputation of Japan's brokerage industry.
Hashimoto expressed regret over the situation and emphasized the need for Nomura to recognize the damage done to confidence in Japan's securities industry.
Salesmen at other Big Four brokerages are receiving inquiries from customers concerned about potential involvement in scandals.

Japan's deposit insurance system is expected to seek loans from banks through a tender later this year.
Financial sources indicate that this move could raise concerns about the adequacy of funds to protect depositors.
The tender aims to repay stopgap loans provided by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to the Deposit Insurance Corp of Japan (DIC).
The DIC borrowed 500 billion yen ($4.13 billion) from the BOJ last month to pay 1.03 trillion yen ($8.5 billion) to a liquidation scheme for Kizu Shinyo Kumiai.
The tender is scheduled to occur after June, following half-yearly payments of deposit insurance premiums by financial institutions.
In the tender, banks will indicate interest rates on loans, and the DIC will select those with lower rates.
A bank official expressed concerns about the DIC's ability to protect depositors' money in the event of a large bank failure.
The deposit insurance system was established in 1971 to prevent financial crises and protect depositors from financial failures.
The DIC has used a total of 2.05 trillion yen ($16.9 billion) in the past five years to bail out troubled financial institutions.
The DIC is required to provide funds to wind up failed regional bank Hanwa Bank and small credit union Sanpuku Shinyo Kumiai.

Nomura Securities Co Ltd revealed a scandal involving suspected illegal deals one month ago.
Masashi Suzuki is the new president of Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Suzuki stated his intention to restore trust in the company.
Suzuki mentioned that staff and branch managers are struggling due to customer rebukes.
On March 6, Nomura announced that two of its directors were involved in illegal deals.
The illegal deals involved transferring money from a Nomura account to a corporate client's account.
Prosecutors and officials from Japan's securities watchdog raided Nomura on March 25.
The corporate client involved in the scandal has been linked to a sokaiya.
Suzuki took over as president on March 14 after Hideo Sakamaki stepped down.
Nomura will establish a compliance committee chaired by president Suzuki to prevent future wrongdoing.

The property market in the Pudong zone of Shanghai is improving due to official pressure on foreign banks to relocate there.
The overall outlook for Shanghai's office property market is negative, with vacancy rates around 30 percent.
Vacancy rates in Shanghai's office property market are expected to rise to 60 percent by the end of 1997 due to new buildings.
The Lujiazui district in Pudong has been designated as the future 'Wall Street of Asia' by Chinese authorities.
Transport difficulties and an office space glut have previously deterred people from moving to Pudong.
Sam Crispin, a senior manager at First Pacific Davies, stated that there has been a rapid shift in interest from banks moving to Pudong.
Foreign banks have been instructed by the Shanghai city government to establish headquarters in Pudong to conduct local currency business.
Eight foreign banks have recently received approval to conduct local yuan business and are setting up operations in Pudong.
Crispin estimated that Lujiazui's office vacancy rate is currently around 75 percent and will likely remain stable for the rest of the year.
James Hawkey, research manager for Jones Lang Wootton, reported that the vacancy rate in Pudong is currently 69.7 percent, which is typical for a newly-developed area.

China is planning major reforms of its government debt markets in 1997.
The reforms aim to make the debt markets more responsive to market forces and flexible in their rates.
Reforms in 1997 will focus on creating a more market-driven secondary market.
Measures taken last year improved the primary market, including the introduction of a public tender for setting coupons.
A senior official stated that reforms will improve coordination between the primary and secondary markets.
Deputy Finance Minister Liu Jibin emphasized strengthening the role of underwriters as market makers in the secondary market.
Market makers will be required to invest consistently in the state debt market and stabilize prices during fluctuations.
A market maker system and off-floor trading will be introduced in 1997.
China began state debt issues in the early 1980s, initially making purchases compulsory for certain groups.
By the early 1990s, purchases of government debt became voluntary, but state-run banks were still required to underwrite allocated amounts.

Deng Xiaoping, the paramount leader of China, died on Wednesday.
Analysts stated that Deng's death removed a major element of uncertainty from China's financial markets.
The health of Deng Xiaoping had been a sensitive and volatile factor for the markets in recent years.
A Hong Kong stock analyst based in Shanghai said the official announcement removed the main disturbing factor in the markets.
The analyst expressed hope that the new focal point of concern would be more economic fundamentals.
Local Chinese brokers agreed that Deng's death removed a key negative factor from the markets.
Bruce Richardson, Shanghai representative of HG Asia, noted that traders were relieved the wait was over.
Richardson mentioned that there had been predictions of a deep drop in the markets following Deng's death, which would present a buying opportunity.
Stock markets in China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan moved higher on Thursday after initial volatility.
Some analysts predicted a power struggle following Deng's death, while others viewed the current leadership structure as stable.

The fight for control of Indonesia's Busang gold deposit has become a public relations battle.
Barrick Gold Corp.'s founder and Chairman is Peter Munk.
Peter Munk promoted Barrick's history, financial structure, and mining capabilities.
Placer Dome Inc.'s President is John Willson.
John Willson has lobbied in Indonesia for the opportunity to bid on Busang.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. discovered the Busang deposit and currently controls it.
Bre-X has hired public relations firm Hill and Knowlton to improve its image.
The Indonesian government has instructed Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick to develop the gold deposit.
Placer Dome has expressed interest in bidding on the deposit by merging with Bre-X.
The Indonesian government has directed Bre-X and Barrick to negotiate a deal with their Indonesian partners at Busang.

Trade ministers from 18 Asia-Pacific countries were urged to support renewed talks for free and open trade in financial services.
Official documents showed that senior officials requested ministers at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Montreal to note the successful re-launch of the financial services negotiations.
Officials recognized that flexibility may be needed regarding transition periods for some participants.
Officials urged all APEC participants in these negotiations to strive toward achieving a permanent, most favored nation-based agreement by December 1997.
Trade ministers from Canada, the United States, the European Union, and Japan announced in Toronto that they would prioritize negotiations in financial services for world trade liberalization talks.
Talks broke down last year after the United States withdrew due to disappointment in offers from other countries.
At the Toronto meeting, the Quad leaders urged Asia and Latin America to improve their offers to the World Trade Organization.
APEC's support was likely to be seen as a significant boost for the talks.
APEC leaders were urged to consider expanding an agreement liberalizing trade in information technologies forged last December.
The United States and the European Union expressed hope that China would join the Information Technologies Agreement as a step toward China's bid to join the World Trade Organization.

The European Union's trade commissioner is Leon Brittan.
Leon Brittan criticized Canada for not taking action against the U.S. Helms-Burton law.
The Helms-Burton law penalizes foreign firms for doing business in Cuba.
Brittan stated that the EU has challenged the United States and made substantial progress.
Canada has not taken action against the Helms-Burton law through NAFTA.
The European Union threatened to challenge the United States over the Helms-Burton law through the World Trade Organization.
In April, the European Commission reached a deal with the U.S. regarding the Helms-Burton law.
The deal involved the EU suspending its action in the WTO and the U.S. suspending a key clause in the Helms-Burton law.
Canadian Trade Minister Art Eggleton mentioned that Canada has a NAFTA challenge available if needed.
Canada is on a U.S. 'watch list' for its copyright legislation.

The Czech Republic ended its dependence on Russian natural gas supplies on Monday.
The Czech Republic signed a final delivery contract with Norwegian suppliers Statoil, Saga Petroleum, and Norsk Hydro.
The contract will transport 53 billion cubic metres of gas to the Czech Republic over the next 20 years.
Officials from Czech state monopoly gas importer Transgas and the Norwegian suppliers signed the deal.
Transgas Director Miroslav Grec announced that deals were completed with transporters Netra GmbH and Verbundnetz Gas AG.
The gas will be shipped from a north-German terminal at Emden to the Czech border.
The contract is for 20 years, with supplies starting in May this year.
The signing of the contract ends the Czech Republic's dependence on natural gas supplies from Gazprom.
Czech natural gas consumption is currently slightly over nine billion cubic metres per year.
Projections indicate that demand will rise to 13.8 billion cubic metres in 2010.

The Czech Republic's plan to diversify natural gas supplies has been delayed for several weeks.
The Industry and Trade Ministry announced the delay on Tuesday.
Miroslav Konvalina is the spokesman for the Industry and Trade Ministry.
The ministry is gathering and analyzing information before presenting the issue to the government.
A plan was expected to be submitted to the government in January.
The ministry did not provide a reason for the delay.
Government representatives have held talks on limited deliveries from Norway.
The ministry is considering four options for securing gas supplies.
Russia is expected to remain the dominant supplier regardless of the plan accepted.
The Czech Republic consumes around eight to nine billion cubic metres of natural gas per year.

Czech National Bank (CNB) Governor Josef Tosovsky stated that media reaction to the failure of Kreditni Banka a.s. temporarily destabilised the banking sector.
Tosovsky claimed that the banking sector is basically sound.
Tosovsky reported that the four largest banks in the Czech Republic are on a firm footing after a period of consolidation.
Tosovsky mentioned that the four biggest banks have a market value of about 110 billion crowns.
Tosovsky noted that in 1990, the four largest banks had a negative market value.
Tosovsky indicated that these four banks represent more than 70 percent of the banking sector.
Tosovsky attributed the decline in confidence in Czech banks to public uproar following the collapse of Kreditni Banka.
Tosovsky blamed the media and politicians for the decline in confidence.
Kreditni Banka was the 11th bank to require assistance from the central bank.
Tosovsky stated that the CNB is prepared to function as the last resort creditor in cases of liquidity problems.

Deng Xiaoping's death after an 18-year rule creates a power struggle in China's communist political elite.
Deng Xiaoping failed to establish a firm succession structure.
Jiang Zemin is Deng Xiaoping's anointed successor.
Diplomats and political analysts expect Jiang Zemin to tighten his grip on power.
Jiang Zemin's position is precarious due to the absence of a proper succession structure.
Geremie Barme, an Australian sinologist, states that Jiang Zemin must now face an uncertain political future alone.
Deng Xiaoping was the last leader of China's communist era with a strong revolutionary background.
Jiang Zemin has built a powerbase, particularly in the military, to strengthen his position.
Tai Ming Cheung, a Hong Kong-based analyst, notes that Jiang Zemin understands the military's importance in political power.
Jiang Zemin's accumulation of the positions of party boss, state president, and head of the armed forces is unprecedented in the 20th century.

North Korea celebrated Kim Jong-il's 55th birthday on a Sunday.
Kim Jong-il is referred to as the 'Dear Leader' in North Korea.
A shooting incident occurred in South Korea involving a prominent North Korean defector.
South Korea accused North Korea of attempting to assassinate the defector.
Kim Jong-il's birthday celebrations were intended to mark his formal accession to power after Kim Il-sung's death.
The celebrations were diminished due to severe food shortages caused by flooding.
The planned live coverage of the birthday celebrations was cancelled without explanation.
North Korean diplomats expressed strong admiration for Kim Jong-il outside the South Korean mission in Beijing.
South Korean officials reported an assassination attempt on Li Il-nam, related to Kim Jong-il's ex-wife.
Chinese security was heightened around the South Korean mission in Beijing where Hwang Jang-yop sought asylum.

U.S. and Chinese negotiators were engaged in talks to finalize a new textile accord and a deal on market access.
The negotiations took place on Saturday night as a deadline for a trade war approached.
U.S. officials indicated that an agreement might be close to completion.
Chief U.S. textile negotiator Rita Hayes expressed confidence in reaching an accord on renewing a 1994 textile agreement.
Hayes stated that significant progress had been made and that negotiations were expected to conclude that day.
The United States extended the deadline for the textile accord by one day from January 31.
Hayes believed the extension was necessary to allow for a fresh start in negotiations.
The Sino-U.S. textile pact was originally set to expire on December 31 but was extended for one month.
U.S. officials did not confirm whether penalties on China would be enforced if no agreement was reached by the new deadline.
China has threatened to retaliate against U.S. imports but has postponed such actions to facilitate ongoing talks.

Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals Limited (HACTL) will implement a computerized rota system later this year.
Yueng Kwok Keung is the deputy managing director of HACTL.
The new system aims to improve air cargo handling efficiency.
HACTL is expected to be the first to use the new system.
HACTL has 2,000 employees who will have input on their shifts and days off.
Rostering is a challenging issue in the air cargo industry due to variable workloads.
The new system allows workers to bid for days off and shift preferences using points.
The rostering system is a result of a joint venture between business and academia.
The Hong Kong government funded research for the system at Hong Kong's Chinese University.
Yueng believes the new system can be adapted for other industries with complex work patterns.

Cathay Pacific and the Hong Kong government's Civil Aviation Department (CAD) disagree on the reasons for delays at Hong Kong's Kai Tak airport.
Peter Li, Cathay's time performance manager, attributes delays to congestion at the airport and air traffic control.
The Hong Kong Civil Aviation Department (CAD) rejects the claim that air traffic control is the cause of delays.
The CAD states that congestion is the true cause of delays at Kai Tak airport.
Cathay Pacific defines a delay as more than 15 minutes after the scheduled arrival or departure.
In 1996, departure delays from Hong Kong rose to 61 percent of flights, up from 48 percent in 1995.
Cathay Pacific does not provide detailed information on the extent or number of delays.
Other airlines flying into Hong Kong are also frustrated by the constraints at Kai Tak airport.
The new airport at Chek Lap Kok is expected to open in 15 months.
The CAD has been reviewing ways to enhance capacity to handle increasing demand.

TNT Express Worldwide plans to double its staff in China and open five new branches within the next year.
Bryan Chan is the general manager for Hong Kong at TNT Express Worldwide.
TNT has applied for full landing rights at Shanghai and Xiamen to extend its Asian Air Express freighter service.
TNT uses two British Aerospace 146 and a Boeing 727 freighter for its overnight delivery service.
TNT's overnight delivery service operates between Manila, Hong Kong, Singapore, Jakarta, Taipei, and Seoul.
It took TNT five years to gain rights for its six existing destinations.
Eric Wong is the newly appointed general sales manager for Hong Kong at TNT.
TNT currently has nine branches in China located in Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, Dalian, Shenzhen, Qingdao, Nanjing, Hangzhou, and Guangzhou.
TNT operates in a joint venture with the state monopoly Sinotrans Group in China.
TNT plans to employ 300 more staff and open new offices in Xiamen, Shenyang, Xian, Wuhan, and Ningbo.

Entergy agreed to a 1.267 billion pound ($2.11 billion) takeover of London Electricity.
The agreement was reached after previous talks were called off in November.
Entergy chairman Ed Lupberger stated that London chairman Sir Bob Reid negotiated a generous price.
The bid valued London shares at 705 pence each.
Shareholders of London Electricity will retain the right to receive a 14.3 pence interim dividend.
Reid claimed the offer represents fair value for London Electricity and is in the best interests of its stakeholders.
London's shares reached a high of 690 pence before settling at 685 pence.
Entergy's offer was made through Entergy Power UK Plc.
Entergy joins Dominion Resources and CalEnergy in pursuing regional electricity companies.
The British government approved CalEnergy's bid with conditions, opening the market for further bids.

Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc reported lower than expected half year profits.
Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc increased its dividend by 11 percent.
Chief executive Roger Young stated the company aims to deliver dividend improvement by expanding the business.
Pretax profits decreased to 61.3 million pounds from 61.7 million pounds.
The expected pretax profits were between 63 million and 70.7 million pounds.
The dividend was set at 5.28 pence per share.
Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc's shares fell by 1.5 pence to 316.5 pence.
Low rainfall impacted profits, leading to increased coal usage at a cost of 6.3 million pounds.
Chairman Lord Wilson expressed confidence in an encouraging result for the full 12 month period.
Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc is the preferred bidder for a 50 percent stake in Keadby power station.

Tesco Plc plans to form a 50-50 joint venture in financial services with Royal Bank of Scotland.
Royal Bank of Scotland will take over Tesco's interest-paying ClubCard Plus account.
The joint venture will launch a credit card during the summer.
Tesco expects an investment of around 40 million British pounds ($65 million) in the first year of the venture.
Analysts believe the move may reduce price-cutting among supermarkets.
The new venture is expected to post a small loss in its first year.
The venture is projected to turn a profit in the second or third year.
Marketing director Tim Mason stated that Tesco hopes to achieve profits similar to those of Marks & Spencer from its financial services.
Marks & Spencer's financial services generated about 61 million pounds ($99 million) last year.
Tesco is the third of Britain's four major supermarket chains to enter financial services.

Martin Owen leads NatWest Markets, which reported a 90 million pound loss on derivatives trading.
Owen is described as friendly, talkative, and has a soft Welsh accent.
Owen trained as an accountant and is actively involved in the Salvation Army.
NatWest's investment banking strategy has faced criticism for aggressive expansion and expensive acquisitions.
NatWest Markets expanded in the United States by purchasing Greenwich Capital for $590 million and Gleacher for $135 million.
Owen has successfully integrated the various parts of NatWest Markets, despite rising costs.
Some market observers believe Owen struggles with the mergers and acquisitions aspect of the business.
Owen's career began at NatWest's treasury and capital markets operations after working for Dow Corning Corp and HTV.
Owen earned an external doctorate in risk management from the University of Southern California.
NatWest Markets profits increased by 158 million pounds to 462 million in 1996, but losses from options wiped out remaining profits.

Northern Rock Building Society announced that 900,000 members will receive 500 free shares when it floats on the stock exchange later this year.
The estimated market price of the shares will be between 260p and 295p.
The maximum valuation of the society is 1.3 billion pounds ($2.1 billion).
The value of the shares will range from 1,300 to 1,475 pounds based on a valuation by J. P. Morgan.
The flotation day is expected to be October 1.
Northern Rock has assets of 13.7 billion pounds and is the seventh largest building society in the UK.
Adam Applegarth, executive director of Northern Rock, stated that the society could remain independent and grow organically.
Draft legislation before parliament indicates that converting societies making acquisitions will lose their five-year protection from takeover.
A special general meeting will be held in Newcastle upon Tyne on April 15, requiring 75 percent of investing members and a simple majority of borrowing members to vote in favor of the proposal.
Northern Rock plans to establish a foundation to receive five percent of the company's pretax profits, which would have been approximately eight million pounds in 1996.

HSBC Holdings Plc's leasing unit announced plans to buy Eversholt for 726.5 million pounds.
The deal involves purchasing Eversholt's shares for 453.4 million pounds and repaying 273.1 million pounds in debt.
The Eversholt deal has faced criticism from opposition politicians.
Labour Party leader Tony Blair described the anticipated profits for Eversholt's management as 'entirely unjustified'.
Blair claimed that the expected gains for managers after 14 months of ownership could be seen as 'profiteering'.
Blair's allegations were based on an incorrect figure of 900 million pounds for the deal.
Eversholt was previously bought from the government for 580 million pounds.
The Labour Party plans to release a dossier regarding the financial gains from rail privatisation.
Graham Picken, chief executive of Forward Trust, stated that they paid a fair market price for Eversholt.
Candover Investments plc reported that its investment in Eversholt increased in value to 100.4 million pounds due to the sale.

Czech politicians and pundits criticized Michael Jackson for his concert on Saturday.
Columnists in Czech dailies described Jackson's high-tech two-hour show as more video game than concert.
Stanislav Pechacek from Denni Telegraf criticized Jackson's performance for poor vocals and sound quality.
Prague has hosted large concerts since the 1989 revolution, including two by the Rolling Stones.
Jackson's visit generated significant hype and included the erection of a giant statue of him.
Jackson opened his concert by emerging from the floor in gold-plated astronaut's armor.
The concert featured three large Jumbotron screens and a stage design combining a Greek temple and a space station.
Columnists expressed concerns about Jackson's singing and the surrounding Cult of Personality.
Jan Lacina from Lidove Noviny described Jackson as a bizarre product of American pop culture.
The Christian Democratic party criticized Jackson for not removing his fedora when meeting President Vaclav Havel.

The Czech cabinet will adopt a package mixing investment incentives with budget and import cuts.
The package aims to spur economic growth.
The cabinet is set to announce its stimulus measures on Wednesday.
Analysts expect share market repairs and savings promotion steps to be included in the package.
The government aims to reduce budget and trade deficits while boosting growth.
Analysts do not expect direct manipulation of the exchange rate to aid exports.
Some analysts suggest allowing the crown to ease below its corridor of plus/minus 7.5 percent from the mid-point of a mark/dollar basket.
Josef Poeschl believes lower interest rates are needed.
Andrew Kenningham expects lower interest rates to be delayed until more data on slowing growth is available.
Analysts agree that the cabinet should enhance market regulation, with many suggesting a U.S.-style Securities and Exchange Commission.

Josef Korbel was a former Czechoslovak diplomat who died in 1977.
Josef Korbel had a Jewish heritage.
Madeleine Korbel Albright is the daughter of Josef Korbel.
Madeleine Albright was born in Prague in 1937 as Marie Jana Koerbelova.
Albright's family fled Czechoslovakia after the 1948 Communist coup.
Albright was raised as a Catholic.
Albright discovered that three of her grandparents died in concentration camps.
Josef Korbel's democratic heritage influenced his daughter, Madeleine Albright.
Albright served as the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations.
Albright criticized leaders such as Fidel Castro, Saddam Hussein, and Serbian aggression in Bosnia.

Zeneca Group Plc is Britain's third-largest drugs company.
In 1996, Zeneca reported sales exceeding five billion pounds.
In 1996, Zeneca's profits surpassed one billion pounds for the first time.
Pre-tax profits before exceptional charges increased by 15 percent to 1.01 billion pounds.
After exceptional charges, pre-tax profit increased by 58 percent to 975 million pounds.
Sales rose by nine percent to 5.363 billion pounds in 1996.
The dividend was raised by 13 percent to 35.0 pence per share.
Zeneca's share price reached a new record high of 19.38 pounds.
Chief executive David Barnes stated the results indicated progress towards his target of doubling profits by the end of the century.
Barnes set a target of increasing earnings per share by an average of 15 percent between 1996 and 2000.

Imperial Chemical Industries Plc announced plans to explore various business reshaping opportunities.
The company is considering flotations, asset swaps, sales, and acquisitions.
Group finance director Alan Spall stated that ICI would use all available tools to shift its portfolio.
Spall indicated that ICI would be a very different company by the turn of the century.
The company aims to reduce its reliance on heavy industrial assets and income.
ICI plans to strengthen its position in less cyclical areas such as polyurethanes, acrylics, performance chemicals, and paints.
Spall mentioned that the entire industry is engaged in asset swap discussions, including ICI.
He referenced a recent $30 million acquisition of a Puerto Rico paint company and a previous purchase of Bunge Paints in South America.
Spall noted that there are numerous potential acquisitions on the horizon.
He highlighted that since the demerger in 1993, output per employee has been growing by eight percent per year.

Peptide Therapeutics Plc announced that there is potential for further product alliances.
Peptide Therapeutics Plc signed two high-profile deals in three weeks.
Peptide finance director John Brown stated that protease inhibitors are of interest.
Peptide is developing technology for rapid identification of protease inhibitors.
Protease inhibitors block enzymes crucial for a virus's reproduction.
Protease inhibitors have been successfully used against the HIV virus.
John Brown mentioned that protease inhibitors have many therapeutic possibilities, including for herpes.
Peptide's agreement with SmithKline Beecham Plc involves developing allergy vaccines.
SmithKline Beecham Plc will pay Peptide 6 million stg immediately.
SmithKline Beecham Plc will take over Peptide's lead project, a vaccine for allergic reactions.

Colombia's largest truck drivers' association is preparing for a second nationwide stoppage in five months.
The Colombian Truckers' Association (ACC) includes 5,000 owner-operators and at least 180,000 drivers.
The ACC represents an estimated 80 percent of all truck drivers in Colombia.
The start date for the strike will be set at a meeting on March 22.
A private exporter expressed concern that the strike could delay 250,000 60-kg bags of coffee scheduled for April shipment.
Another exporter described the strike threat as serious and noted potential delays for March exports due to the Easter bank holiday.
A fax sent to ACC members indicated that a new stoppage would be announced at the March 22 meeting.
Mario Quiroga, a member of the ACC's national directorate, stated that initial plans were to start the strike before Easter.
The ACC previously staged an 11-day strike in October that delayed the shipment of at least 250,000 60-kg bags of coffee.
The truckers are renewing their strike call due to unmet terms of a 19-point deal established to end the October stoppage.

Seventy captured troops are scheduled for release this weekend.
The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) has held sixty soldiers for more than nine months.
Ten marines were captured in combat in January.
The release is set to occur in Cartagena del Chaira, located in a demilitarized zone in Caqueta province.
President Ernesto Samper ordered 5,000 troops to withdraw from the area for 32 days.
The accord on releasing the troops has initiated dialogue between the FARC and the government for the first time in six years.
Pierre Gassmann, head of the International Committee of the Red Cross in Colombia, stated that the meeting is a positive development.
Some analysts believe the army seeks revenge against the FARC.
Eduardo Pizarro, a political violence expert, described the capture of the troops as a significant victory for the FARC.
The FARC commander Joaquin Gomez will oversee the handover ceremony.

Richard Howitt, a European legislator, alleged that British Petroleum Co Plc is involved in a 'conspiracy of silence' over human rights abuses in eastern Colombia.
Howitt admitted that he had no evidence directly linking BP to the deaths of social leaders in Casanare province after a week-long fact-finding mission.
BP's Colombian subsidiary, British Petroleum Exploration (BPX), has denied charges of links to rights abuses committed by right-wing paramilitaries and the army.
BPX condemned all violations against civic leaders in a statement issued on Friday.
Howitt stated that BP should take a more active stance in favor of human rights and suggested that BP staff may have direct liability in the actions.
Howitt expressed disbelief that BP managers are unaware of human rights abuses committed in their name.
The claims against BP were supported by articles in the British press based on a multi-agency report from 1995.
The 1995 report documented the murders of seven peasant or social leaders who protested against BP's operations since 1991.
BP is not mentioned by name in the report's conclusions, which attributed the killings to paramilitaries and the army.
BP figures indicate that the company spent more than $17 million on social, education, environmental, and infrastructure programs in Casanare between 1991 and 1996.

United News & Media posted a profit rise of more than 20 percent on Thursday.
The group made significant progress since a merger earlier this year that effectively doubled its size.
Pre-tax profit before exceptional items from the group totalled 151.9 million pounds in the six months to June 30.
Last year's restated figure for pre-tax profit was 125 million pounds.
Market reaction to the figures was broadly favourable, with United shares closing 5p higher at 710.5p.
The figures were the first since the merger between United News & Media and MAI.
The merger, completed in April, created a company with a market capitalisation of more than three billion pounds.
United News & Media owns British national newspapers The Daily and Sunday Express and Daily Star.
The group operates commercial television franchises in southern and eastern England.
Chief executive Lord Hollick stated that a review of the group's businesses would be completed by the end of the year.

Shares in British publisher Dorling Kindersley Holdings Plc lost almost 20 percent of their value on Tuesday.
The company warned that profits would fall short of last year's level.
Traders wiped over 40 million pounds ($64 million) off Dorling's value.
The company cited tough conditions in the U.S. retail book market, currency movements, and increased investment in its direct selling business as factors affecting profits.
Dorling restated its profits for the year to end-June 1996 to 12.9 million pounds ($20.5 million) from 17.4 million pounds.
The restatement reflects a change in the way Dorling accounts for multimedia development costs.
Managing director Rod Hare stated that profits would fall 'somewhat short' of 12.9 million pounds but did not specify an amount.
The warning was the second in little more than three months.
Dorling shares fell 60p to 261p by 1025 GMT.
The company's value has halved to around 180 million pounds since the warning about the likely impact of sterling strength in early December.

PolyGram reported lower earnings for 1996.
PolyGram believes that sales growth in the music sector will recover strongly.
Alain Levy is the president and chief executive officer of PolyGram.
Levy stated that he believes sales could grow at an annual rate of more than five percent.
The global music market was valued at $40 billion in 1996.
The global music market grew by only three percent in 1996.
PolyGram has a strong release schedule for 1997, including albums by U2, Elton John, and Van Morrison.
PolyGram, Bertelsmann, Sony Music, EMI, and Warner account for more than two-thirds of global music sales.
PolyGram's net income after tax and extraordinary items fell to 608 million guilders in 1996.
PolyGram is cutting around 550 jobs as part of its restructuring efforts.

The Food and Drug Administration is investigating the death of a third recipient of an implantable defibrillator made by Ventritex Inc.
FDA spokeswoman Sharon Schneider confirmed the investigation and reported the third death of a patient with a Ventritex defibrillator.
The FDA does not know the exact nature of the problem related to the deaths.
The FDA is uncertain if the third death was caused by the same issue that caused the other two deaths.
The stock price of Ventritex fell by $1.25 to $18.125 due to market rumors about the death.
The proposed stock purchase of Ventritex by St. Jude Medical Inc. is valued at $505 million.
A spokesman for St. Jude stated that the company would review the deal due to the three deaths associated with Ventritex devices.
St. Jude spokesman Peter Gove indicated that the company plans to conduct additional due diligence regarding the acquisition.
Ventritex general counsel Mark Meltzer reported that a patient with a Ventritex implantable defibrillator died on January 22.
On January 16, Ventritex was authorized by the FDA to reprogram 5,605 implantable defibrillators in patients.

Consolidation in the nursing home and sub-acute medical care services industry accelerated with the announcement of two mergers.
Healthsouth Corp agreed to acquire Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp in a stock transaction valued at $1.6 billion.
The acquisition of Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp includes debt assumption.
Sun Healthcare Group agreed to buy Retirement Care Associates Inc and Contour Medical Inc for $328 million in stock and cash.
Both mergers indicate that the nursing home and sub-acute medical care services industry is rapidly consolidating.
William McKeever, an analyst at Schroder Wertheim, stated that the consolidation is likely to continue for a while.
Healthsouth, based in Birmingham, Ala., had revenues of $1.55 billion in 1995.
Horizon/CMS, based in Albuquerque, N.M., operates the second-largest rehab hospital chain in the U.S. and has 267 nursing homes.
Sun Healthcare's acquisition will increase its total number of nursing homes to 380 in the U.S. and U.K.
Vencor Inc agreed to acquire TheraTx Inc for $550 million, indicating potential for more mergers and acquisitions in the industry.

Dennis Jones is the chief executive of Jones Medical Industries Inc.
Dennis Jones stated he is comfortable with the First Call consensus earnings forecast of $0.23 per share for the fourth quarter.
The forecast of $0.23 per share implies earnings of $0.79 for the year.
Jones Medical Industries Inc. earned $0.16 per share in the fourth quarter a year ago.
Jones Medical Industries Inc. earned $0.50 per share in all of 1995.
Shares in Jones Medical Industries Inc. were down 1-1/4 to 31-3/4 on heavy trading.
Jones Medical Industries Inc.'s stock price was extremely volatile throughout last year.
Institutional holding of Jones Medical Industries Inc. stock grew to over 50 percent from 15 percent of total outstanding shares.
Jones Medical Industries Inc. expects to report year-end financial results in the second week of February.
Jones Medical Industries Inc. has made four acquisitions since August 1995.

The Australian government appointed stockbrokers on Thursday to manage the proposed sharemarket float of Telstra Corp.
The Telstra float will be the largest privatisation in Australia.
The float is estimated to raise a minimum of A$8.0 billion (US$6.32 billion).
Finance Minister John Fahey stated he wants the Telstra float to occur by the end of the year.
Fahey indicated that it is unclear if the float timing will be affected by the float of other international telephone companies.
J.B Were & Son, CS First Boston, and ABN AMRO/Rothschild were appointed as global co-ordinators for the float.
Joint lead managers for the float include J.B Were, Ord Minnett, CS First Boston, Goldman Sachs/Macquarie Bank, Daiwa, ABN AMRO/Rothschild, and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The float will not be underwritten in Australia, where 65 percent of the offer is to be sold.
Shares offered in the United States will be underwritten and listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
Two percent of the offer is set aside for Telstra employees, and foreign investors are entitled to 35 percent.

Seven Network Ltd's managing director is Gary Rice.
Gary Rice expects a slightly better performance in the second half of 1996/97 compared to the previous year.
Rice stated that he expects a slight improvement in general performance terms in the second half.
Rice confirmed that he anticipates a better performance for the whole year.
Seven Network Ltd reported a 31.5 percent fall in net profit to A$62.98 million for the 26 weeks ending December 28.
Rice believes the advertising market will be marginally better in 1996/97 compared to 1995/96.
Rice noted signs of improvement in advertising from some sectors.
Seven Network Ltd has no plans for further major cost cuts.
In October, Seven retrenched 43 staff to streamline costs.
Seven invested US$250 million in Hollywood studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) for control of the studio.

Larry Irving is a telecommunications adviser to U.S. President Clinton.
Larry Irving stated that demands for cheaper telephone services by businesses would drive liberalisation in the telecommunications markets of the APEC region.
Irving claimed that the biggest advocates of change in telecommunications law are business people in the United States, Australia, and New Zealand.
Irving noted that industrialists, not telecom companies, are demanding better services and cheaper prices.
Irving is the head administrator of the National Telecommunication Informational Agency (NTIA).
Irving stated that countries cannot afford not to liberalise their telecom markets to maintain a competitive edge.
Irving claimed that countries that liberalise their telecommunications markets would create more telecom-related jobs than those with state-owned monopolies.
Irving cited Chile, Mexico, and New Zealand as APEC countries with open telecom markets.
Irving reported that 400,000 jobs were created in the U.S. telecommunications and information technology industry last year.
Gregorio San Martin Ricci, Chile's undersecretary of communications, stated that more jobs have been created in Chile's telecom industry since deregulation in the late 1980s.

The BBC announced plans to enter the domestic commercial television market.
The BBC is partnering with Flextech Plc to offer up to eight new pay television channels.
Flextech is majority-owned by Tele-Communications International Inc.
Flextech is contributing 22 million pounds and can provide 118 million pounds in credit facilities for the ventures.
Flextech and BBC Worldwide announced a joint venture to create digital subscription television channels in Britain, the Channel Islands, the Isle of Man, and the Irish Republic.
The two groups plan to form two joint ventures to combine the BBC's skills with Flextech's funds and management knowledge.
The principal deal involves developing and launching new pay-television channels in Britain.
The second deal involves buying and developing UK Gold in analogue and later in digital formats.
Flextech's chief executive Roger Luard stated that the joint ventures represent a major opportunity for Flextech's development in the multi-channel television market.
The eight planned channels will include various genres such as factual programmes, comedy, drama, and sports.

Cable and Wireless Communications (CWC) will float a 14.7 percent stake in London and New York early next week.
The flotation is not large enough to enter the FTSE.
CWC was formed in 1996 by merging the Mercury unit of Cable and Wireless Plc with three British cable TV units of NYNEX Corp and Bell Canada.
Analysts have valued CWC at around 4.5 billion pounds ($7.3 billion).
The recommended offer for shares in CWC closed on Friday at 1330 GMT.
Experts expect trading to start on Monday at 1330 GMT.
Over 65 percent of shareholders accepted the deal when CWC's prospectus was issued in March.
Richard Brown is the incoming chairman of CWC and chief executive of Cable and Wireless.
CWC will provide a broad range of voice and data services and, in some regions, multichannel TV and internet services.
CWC's core business will be telephony provided by Mercury.

British Telecommunications and MCI Communications Corp. are entering the South America market.
British Telecom formed a strategic alliance with Portugal Telecom to access Brazil.
Portugal Telecom announced that MCI formed a joint venture with Telefonica de Espana.
British Telecom did not confirm the joint venture announcement.
Telefonica denied that a deal was signed with MCI.
MCI stated that the announcement of the joint venture was made in error.
The nature of the error regarding the joint venture announcement is unclear.
British Telecom's shareholders are voting on a merger with MCI worth 12.3 billion pounds.
Speculation exists about a potential deal between Telefonica Internacional and Concert.
British Telecom is taking a 1 percent stake and MCI a 0.5 percent stake in Portugal Telecom.

The video game software industry has shown improvement after a period of decline.
Three major game developers reported better-than-expected results for the December quarter.
The companies that reported results are Electronic Arts Inc., Activision Inc., and Spectrum Holobyte Inc.
Strong sales of games for personal computers and next-generation video game consoles contributed to the positive results.
The Sony PlayStation is one of the next-generation video game consoles mentioned.
The video game software industry had been struggling while consumers awaited new game machines from Sony Corp., Sega Enterprises, and Nintendo Corp.
The industry lacked blockbuster games to attract customers to stores.
The release of the PlayStation and Nintendo 64 revitalized the video game industry, according to analysts.
Electronic Arts reported a 25 percent increase in net income for its fiscal third quarter, reaching $36.7 million.
Activision's net income more than doubled in the Christmas quarter to $4.12 million.

Apple Computer Inc. stock rose on Thursday.
The stock gained 87.5 cents to $18.875 on trading of 4.9 million shares.
The stock traded as high as $19.125 earlier in the day.
Prince al-Waleed bin Talal bought a 5 percent stake in Apple for $115 million.
Larry Ellison intends to form an investor group to buy a majority stake in Apple.
The New York Times reported that Apple is seeking to sell itself and has approached Sun Microsystems Inc.
Sun Microsystems attempted to buy Apple in late 1995, but negotiations failed over price.
Apple negotiated with International Business Machines Corp. about a merger two years ago, but IBM also declined over price.
Former Apple executives have not heard of any recent moves by Apple to approach potential buyers.
Apple has reported financial losses of close to $1 billion over the past five quarters.

Rational Software Corp. agreed to buy Pure Atria Corp. in a stock deal valued at about $839 million.
Both Rational Software Corp. and Pure Atria Corp. experienced a decline in their stock prices after Pure Atria announced lower than expected first-quarter earnings.
Analysts suggested that Rational Software Corp. could face similar difficulties as Pure Atria in managing acquisitions.
Kris Tuttle, an analyst at Soundview Financial Group, questioned Rational's decision to acquire Pure Atria given its competitive position.
Rational Software's stock fell by $9.75, or 42 percent, closing at $13.625.
Pure Atria's stock fell by $7.75, or 44 percent, closing at $10 on the Nasdaq.
Both companies were among the most active stocks on Nasdaq and were the biggest percentage losers in U.S. trading.
Under the acquisition terms, Rational would pay 0.9 of its shares for each of Pure Atria's 39.92 million shares outstanding.
The value of the acquisition deal decreased by 42 percent to about $489 million due to the stock slide.
Rational Software Corp. specializes in methodology tools, while Pure Atria specializes in development and testing tools.

T. Eaton Co. Ltd. filed for court protection from its creditors on Thursday.
T. Eaton Co. Ltd. plans to close some of its department stores as part of a restructuring effort.
Eaton's President George Eaton stated that it is too early to predict the future of specific stores.
T. Eaton Co. Ltd. has estimated annual sales of C$1.25 billion ($912 million).
The company arranged financing of C$555 million ($405 million) from an unspecified major financial institution.
T. Eaton Co. Ltd. filed for a court order to continue the operations of its retailing division.
Canadian department stores have lost market share due to a weak economy and competition from Wal-Mart Stores Inc.
Eaton's has about 90 outlets across Canada.
Analyst John Winter predicted that about half of the stores, approximately 40, will close.
Rumors have emerged about a possible takeover of Eaton's by a U.S. chain, with J.C. Penney Co. Inc. and Dayton Hudson Corp. mentioned as potential suitors.

Toronto's key stock index closed higher on Tuesday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 45.65 points to end at 6126.92.
Declining issues outnumbered advances 515 to 479.
The banking sector performed well according to MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie.
Canada's six biggest banks reached record heights after Goldman Sachs upgraded ratings on five of them.
The financial services sector rose more than 1.7 percent.
The gold sector experienced problems as gold prices dropped.
Trading volume was 102.9 million shares valued at C$1.76 billion.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-indices increased, led by consumer products, banks, conglomerates, and oils.
The Royal Bank of Canada closed at 54.85, below its new high of 55.30.

Canadian department store retailers are facing challenges due to the presence of U.S. retailer Wal-Mart.
Eaton's chain filed for bankruptcy protection on Thursday.
Analysts predict that Eaton's may close up to half of its approximately 90 stores.
There is speculation that a U.S. retailer might acquire all or part of Eaton's chain.
T. Eaton Co. Ltd. is Canada's fifth largest department store chain with annual sales of C$1.67 billion.
Eaton's received court permission to continue operations while negotiating a restructuring plan.
Eaton's arranged financing of C$555 million from General Electric Capital Canada Inc.
Wal-Mart has captured 43 percent of the Canadian retail market share since its arrival in 1994.
Several Canadian retailers have declared bankruptcy in recent years.
Rumored suitors for Eaton's include J.C. Penney Co. Inc., Dayton Hudson Corp., Dillard Department Stores Inc., Federated Department Stores Inc., and Nordstrom Inc.

Tin production at one of China's biggest mines has been cut due to summer flooding.
The Gejiu Tin Mine in southern Yunnan province was damaged by floods in June and July.
Sheng Weichung is the deputy general manager of Deng's Yunnan Tin Corp.
Deng's Yunnan Tin Corp is the Hong Kong representative and trading arm of Yunnan Tin Corp.
Yunnan Tin Corp is China's biggest tin producer.
In 1995, Yunnan Tin Corp produced 20,000 tonnes of tin.
The Gejiu mine was the biggest mine for Yunnan Tin Corp.
Business has been slow in China due to a soft world market and domestic industry restructuring.
China expected to produce 45,000 tonnes of tin in 1996.
Total Chinese tin production for the first half of 1996 was down 6.14 percent compared to the same period in 1995.

World zinc prices have risen to levels not seen for more than four years.
Chinese zinc producers will increase output to take advantage of rising prices.
A source at the Zhuzhou smelter stated that output would be boosted from April.
Zhuzhou's exports for the first three months of 1997 are expected to reach 20,000 tonnes.
Zhuzhou has been exporting metal to Japan to benefit from the GSP policy.
Some Western industry sources question how quickly Chinese producers can capitalize on the price increase.
Significant amounts of Chinese zinc have been delivered to warehouses in Singapore.
Traders estimate that up to 75,000 tonnes of zinc are stored in Singapore.
The worldwide zinc supply is expected to become tight in the second half of 1997.
Zinc prices on the London Metal Exchange reached $1,304 a tonne before settling at $1,296.

Deng Xiaoping ruled China and declined the personality cult surrounding Chairman Mao Zedong.
Deng Xiaoping died on a Wednesday.
Following Deng's death, there was an increase in demand for Deng-related merchandise.
More than 80 branches of the state-run Xinhua bookstore in Shanghai received Deng posters.
Thousands of sets of pictures titled 'The Architect of China's Opening, Reform and Modernisation -- Deng Xiaoping' were flown to Shanghai from various publishing houses.
People of all ages, including members of the People's Liberation Army and students, waited in line in Beijing to buy Deng portraits.
During Deng's leadership, the Chinese public rarely saw images of him.
Deng Xiaoping maintained a low public profile after the Cultural Revolution.
Deng retired from his last official post in 1991 and largely disappeared from public view.
After Deng's death at 92, state stores and media were ordered to produce memorials and mementoes.

Russian refineries are under pressure from growing domestic demand for transport fuels and cleaner specifications in export markets.
Analysts state that significant changes in the composition of the Russian barrel are not expected in the next three to five years.
Pavis Shahidi is a refining expert at Bechtel International Inc in London.
All upgrading projects at Russian refineries are still awaiting financing.
Russia has 28 major refineries that plan to install conversion systems and are in talks with international lending institutions for financing.
The total cost of major proposals for upgrades at Russian refineries is around $12 billion.
Peter Lukyanov is from Universal Oil Product in Moscow.
Conversion levels at Russian refineries are 50-55 percent, while leading foreign facilities achieve 75-80 percent conversions.
Only 10 percent of current refining capacity in Russia uses deeper treatment technologies, and there are no hydrocrackers in the country.
Heavy fuel oil, or mazut, comprises 40 percent or more of oil product output in Russia.

Norilsk Nickel is the world's second largest nickel producer.
Norilsk Nickel averted a dockworkers' strike on Monday.
Norilsk Nickel is experiencing dire financial straits.
Norilsk Nickel has warned employees about potential cutbacks.
A group of workers at Norilsk called off their threat to stop loading metals for export from the port of Dudinka.
Norilsk Nickel's spokesman is Sergei Vetchinin.
Analysts were surprised by Norilsk Nickel's financial troubles.
Ruslan Fedorovsky is a metals trader at Barclays Physical Trading Ltd in London.
Lay-offs at Norilsk could affect 80,000 non-production employees.
Norilsk Nickel plans to pay off 800 billion roubles of delayed wages by November.

Russian demand for imported sugar has increased earlier than usual before the beet harvest.
Traders reported less price volatility and more consolidation in the domestic sugar market.
A senior trade source stated that demand is normal and prices are stabilizing.
There is sugar arriving at the ports and demand is good according to the senior trade source.
Raws need to arrive by mid-July to be processed at domestic refineries before the beet crop takes over.
A second senior trade source indicated that the Russian market is currently strong with good demand for sugar.
Traders discussed market speculation about sugar backlogs at the Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.
A backlog of Cuban raws at Novorossiisk has decreased slightly to 80,700 tonnes.
The port expects to receive around 200,000 tonnes of raws, likely of Cuban origin, this summer.
Indian refined white sugar stocks in port warehouses are approximately 400,000 tonnes, but senior trade sources believe this figure is exaggerated.

French Caisse Nationale de Credit Agricole will take full control of merchant bank Banque Indosuez from Compagnie de Suez on December 23.
The total price for the transaction is 11.9 billion francs.
Credit Agricole purchased a 51 percent stake in Banque Indosuez in July for 6.3 billion francs.
Credit Agricole will pay the remaining 5.6 billion francs on Monday.
Compagnie de Suez expects to report a 300 million franc capital gain from the transaction in its 1996 annual result, which will be published on April 2.
Under the original sale terms, Credit Agricole was to buy an additional 29 percent in July 1997 and the remaining 20 percent on January 1, 2000.
Compagnie de Suez spokeswoman Michele Meyzie stated that the decision to speed up the transaction was mutual.
Credit Agricole is restructuring its activities and believes full control of Indosuez will facilitate this process.
An audit concluded on June 30 showed the value of Indosuez was 11.790 billion francs, plus some interest.
In May, the value of Banque Indosuez was estimated at 11.85 billion francs.

Gaz de France plans to spend billions of francs upgrading its infrastructure.
Gaz de France's infrastructure upgrades are in response to a demand growth estimated at three percent a year.
