Chairman Pierre Gadonneix opposes European rules aimed at liberalising the gas industry.
Gadonneix believes that long-term commitments are needed rather than a focus on the short term.
Gadonneix stated that an abundance of gas in the short term does not negate the need for long-term deals.
Gadonneix noted that European liberalisation for gas cannot replicate the effects seen in the electricity sector.
Only Britain and the Netherlands export gas within the European Union, while other member states depend on imports.
Gadonneix is not against a spot market as long as it does not harm long-term commitments.
Gaz de France will have spent 4.5 billion francs on transport and distribution in 1996 and plans to spend five billion in 1997.
Gadonneix does not support allowing large clients to order natural gas directly from producers.

Alcatel Alsthom is in talks with Aerospatiale and Dassault about a joint offer for the government's 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe stated that a decision regarding the privatisation of Thomson-CSF would be made before the end of February.
An Alcatel spokesman confirmed discussions with Aerospatiale and Dassault regarding a joint bid.
Industry sources reported that Alcatel chairman Serge Tchuruk informed the government about plans to form an alliance with Aerospatiale and Dassault.
Alcatel lost to Lagardere Groupe in the bidding for state-controlled Thomson SA in October.
The government suspended the sale of Thomson SA on December 4 due to issues raised by the independent Privatisation Commission.
A decision regarding the relaunch of the sale of Thomson-CSF was expected at the end of January.
Prime Minister Juppe indicated that the decision about the sale procedure would now be made in February.
President Jacques Chirac expressed a desire to restructure the French defence industry around a merger of Aerospatiale/Dassault and Thomson-CSF.
Aerospatiale is state-owned and will be the main shareholder of the merged group with Dassault.

RTZ-CRA is the world's biggest miner.
RTZ-CRA announced a major realignment of its operations.
London is the capital of RTZ-CRA.
RTZ-CRA was formed from a merger of RTZ Plc and CRA Ltd in 1995.
RTZ-CRA will manage its global businesses along six main product lines: aluminium, copper, energy, industrial minerals, iron ore, and gold and other minerals.
RTZ-CRA generated revenues of around US$8 billion in calendar 1996.
RTZ-CRA will reduce its Melbourne office staff by 100 jobs.
A total of 200 jobs will be eliminated worldwide.
CRA chairman John Uhrig stated that the merger has not yet produced a better outcome for shareholders.
RTZ-CRA will take a one-off restructuring charge of US$40 million this year.

Shell Australia Ltd wants to integrate the North West Shelf and Gorgon gas projects off northwest Australia.
Shell is a part owner in both the North West Shelf and Gorgon projects.
Shell dismissed the option of developing Gorgon as a stand-alone project with its own liquified natural gas (LNG) plant.
Shell is working to jointly develop Gorgon and the North West Shelf.
Shell Australia chief executive Roland Williams stated that constructive discussions would soon begin.
Williams did not provide a timetable for a decision regarding the projects.
Shell owns one-sixth of the North West Shelf project, which has a production capacity of 7.5 million tonnes per annum (MTPA).
The other partners in the North West Shelf project include The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, the MiMi consortium, Chevron Corp, British Petroleum Co, and Woodside Petroleum.
Shell owns two-sevenths of the Gorgon gas field, which has a production capacity of 6 MTPA and is still subject to feasibility studies.
The other partners in the Gorgon project include Chevron, Texaco Inc, and Mobil Corp unit Ampolex Ltd.

RTZ-CRA announced a major realignment of its operations.
London is confirmed as the capital of RTZ-CRA.
RTZ-CRA was formed from a merger in 1995 between RTZ Plc and CRA Ltd.
RTZ-CRA will manage its global businesses along six main product lines: aluminium, copper, energy, industrial minerals, iron ore, and gold and other minerals.
The group generated revenues of around US$8 billion in calendar 1996 from operations on all six continents.
RTZ-CRA plans to reduce its Melbourne office staff by 100 jobs.
CRA chairman John Uhrig stated that the merger has not yet produced a better outcome for shareholders.
The restructuring will have Australian-based executives manage aluminium, energy, and iron ore businesses from Brisbane, Melbourne, and Perth.
The Salt Lake City office of Kennecott copper and the Johannesburg office will be closed.
Chief executive Leon Davis stated that the new structure aims to eliminate barriers and improve efficiency.

Microsoft Corp, Intel, and Compaq Computer Corp have proposed standards for a new generation of televisions.
The proposed television protocol was unveiled at a broadcasters' conference in Las Vegas.
Craig Mundie, Senior Vice President of Microsoft, stated that the proposed protocol would also be recommended as a standard for multimedia PCs.
The companies are proposing the adoption of three out of 18 advanced technical standards set forth by a television industry coalition.
The proposal aims to allow significant improvement in picture quality and transmission of related information and data to personal computers and televisions.
Robert Stearns, Senior Vice President of Compaq, stated that advanced television would provide viewers with a different experience.
Stearns suggested that advanced television would allow viewers to interact with programming in various ways.
The executives indicated that equipping personal computers to decode and display new television signals would add little cost, perhaps less than $150.
The emergence of advanced television is creating a new class of big-screen personal computers that combine features of computers and televisions.
The U.S. Federal Communications Commission has called for a rollout of digital television technology in the nation's 10 biggest markets within 18 months.

Unionized workers have filed a class-action lawsuit against Albertson's Inc.
The lawsuit claims that Albertson's pressures employees to work overtime without pay.
The United Food and Commercial Workers Union represents 31,000 of Albertson's 85,000 employees.
Seven members of the union filed the lawsuit in King County Superior Court in Seattle.
The lawsuit seeks back wages that could total millions of dollars.
A similar action is being prepared by employees in California.
Albertson's has about 165 stores in California.
Joe Peterson, a special assistant to UFCW international President Douglas Dority, stated that back pay sought could run into millions.
The union has sworn statements from more than 1,500 Albertson's employees regarding off-the-clock work.
Michael Read, a spokesman for Albertson's, denied the charges and stated the company is concerned about off-the-clock work allegations.

Microsoft Corp. purchased Interse Corp., a privately held developer of Web site analysis software.
The terms of the deal for Interse Corp. were not disclosed.
Interse Corp. is based in Sunnyvale, California and has 30 employees.
A Microsoft executive stated that Interse's market focus tool would be added to Microsoft's BackOffice line of server products.
Details on how the software will be repackaged have not been worked out.
Interse's market focus tool ranges in price from $695 to $6,995 depending on features.
The tool allows Web site operators to track visitor behavior.
Bill Gates, Microsoft Chairman and CEO, stated that understanding usage patterns is important for delivering targeted content.
Terry Myerson, CEO of Interse, will join Microsoft and continue to work on the technology.
Steve Harmon, a senior investment analyst with MecklerMedia Corp., commented on the importance of customized Web pages.

Heavy wet season rains in April favoured Ivorian cocoa midcrop growth.
Harvests are expected to match forecasts of over 150,000 tonnes.
Official weather data for the first 10 days of May totalled 292.6 mm.
The previous 10 days had 789.2 mm of rainfall.
Wet season rains are expected to peak in June.
Small dry season conditions are expected in July and August.
Steady June rains would favour pod growth and bean sizes.
Harvest volumes are projected to reach between 150,000-200,000 tonnes.
Early May rains were concentrated north of main cocoa growing areas.
Ivory Coast produced a bumper 200,000 tonnes mid-crop in its record 1.2 million tonnes harvest year.

Plans to build cocoa factories in Ivory Coast will increase national processing capacity to 360,000 tonnes in 1997/98.
The target for cocoa processing capacity in Ivory Coast is 500,000 tonnes by the year 2000.
Ivory Coast's commodities minister is Guy-Alain Gauze.
Cargill, Touton, Cemoi, STF-CI, Orebi, and Shanghai are chocolate processors planning to build factories in Ivory Coast.
Ivory Coast is the world's largest cocoa exporter.
Ivory Coast aims to process 50 percent of its annual cocoa crop by the year 2000.
Ivory Coast produced a record 1.2 million tonnes of cocoa in 1995/96.
Ivory Coast is set to harvest over 1.1 million tonnes of cocoa in 1996/97.
Callebaut-Barry will increase its processing capacity to 100,000 tonnes from 90,000 tonnes by the year 2000.
Cocoa accounts for 40 percent of Ivorian export earnings.

A week of heavy rains in Ivory Coast's cocoa belt has improved prospects for a large mid-crop.
Up-country buyers and crop analysts stated that more rain is needed.
A leading agent reported heavy rains of five or six hours a day for the past week in central areas around Gagnoa and Daloa.
Crop analysts indicated that the rains favored late mid-crop pod setting and overall bean sizes.
Drought from mid-January to late February had threatened harvest volumes.
One analyst noted that March had been dry but expected rains to increase to a June peak.
Analysts plan to provide a figure on the mid-crop in April.
Early estimates suggest the current tree crop is over 100,000 tonnes, with over 150,000 possible if rains remain favorable.
Ivory Coast set a record cocoa crop of 1.2 million tonnes in 1995/96 after a mid-crop of 200,000 tonnes.
Main crop harvests totaled 920,000-960,000 tonnes in early March, with private forecasters predicting a total crop of up to 1.1 million tonnes.

Office Depot stopped building superstores after agreeing to merge with Staples Inc.
Industry analysts stated that Office Depot will need to regain its footing if it remains independent.
Mark Mandel of The Chicago Corp suggested that Office Depot needs to rebuild management and define its company identity.
The merger deal between Staples and Office Depot was reached in September.
The merger would have created a dominant office-supply retailing force with about 1,000 stores.
Rival OfficeMax operates between 700 and 800 superstores.
Federal regulators stated that the merger would harm price competition for office supplies in some markets.
The companies criticized the Federal Trade Commission's decision regarding the merger.
Staples CEO Thomas Stemberg indicated that Staples may challenge the FTC ruling in court.
After the FTC ruling, Staples shares rose while Office Depot shares fell.

Florida's anti-tobacco activists recently won a Supreme Court victory.
Florida has a law that allows the state to sue cigarette makers.
Opponents of the law are campaigning to repeal Florida's third-party medical liability act.
The current legislative session in Florida is scheduled to last until May.
Jodi Chase is the general counsel for Associated Industries of Florida Inc.
Bills to repeal the medical-liability law have been introduced in both houses of the Florida legislature.
Gov. Lawton Chiles vetoed a repeal bill two years ago.
The Supreme Court refused to take up a tobacco industry challenge to the constitutionality of the law.
A trial in a billion-dollar lawsuit against the tobacco industry is scheduled for August 4 in West Palm Beach, Florida.
The Coalition to Clear the Air for Florida Taxpayers is preparing a media and organizing campaign to support the law.

A former U.S. surgeon general will testify in a class-action trial regarding cigarette makers' actions in the 1970s.
Dr. Jesse Steinfeld will testify on behalf of approximately 60,000 non-smoking flight attendants.
The flight attendants claim damages for illnesses allegedly caused by second-hand smoke on passenger jets.
A jury trial in Dade County Court is scheduled to begin on June 2.
This trial will be the first class-action suit against the tobacco industry in the United States.
A second class-action suit on behalf of all Florida smokers is scheduled for trial in Miami in September.
Rosenblatt claims that the tobacco industry impeded public access to information about the dangers of second-hand smoke.
Steinfeld is also scheduled to testify for Mississippi in a lawsuit against tobacco companies regarding Medicaid costs.
Twenty-one states, including Florida, have filed similar lawsuits against tobacco companies.
The plaintiffs will also call a former tobacco company employee who claimed he was instructed to destroy evidence of health risks.

China's relations with the United States are expected to improve in 1997.
Disputes over Taiwan, trade, and the return of Hong Kong to Beijing rule could negatively impact relations.
Beijing and Washington are both interested in developing stability in their relationship.
A Beijing-based Western diplomat stated that there will still be problems in Sino-U.S. relations.
The November meeting in Manila between Chinese President Jiang Zemin and U.S. President Bill Clinton may lead to improved relations.
Guangming Daily reported that serious differences still exist between China and the U.S.
U.S. policy towards Taiwan, the return of Hong Kong, and China's entry to the World Trade Organisation are crucial issues.
Hong Kong will revert to Beijing's rule on June 30 after being a British colony for over 150 years.
Beijing leaders are concerned that a harsh approach to Hong Kong could provoke U.S. Congressional backlash.
A Chinese analyst indicated that Hong Kong's return could exacerbate trade disputes with the U.S.

China told U.S. President Bill Clinton not to worry about Chinese human rights and Hong Kong's future freedoms.
Beijing's rights record was stated to speak for itself.
China assured that liberty in Hong Kong was guaranteed.
Clinton expressed that Washington had made less progress than hoped in influencing Chinese rights policies.
Clinton warned that Hong Kong's value to China might decrease if liberties were lost after its return to Beijing's rule.
A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman stated that different views on human rights exist due to differing national conditions.
The reaction from China was described as mild by Beijing's standards.
Chinese and U.S. officials met in Beijing to discuss trade and human rights.
China's official Xinhua news agency reported only on Clinton's defense of his engagement policy towards China.
Concerns over the future of Hong Kong were deemed unfounded by the Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman.

China and the United States made progress in talks on a new textile accord on Thursday.
Negotiations could extend late into the night before a deadline for agreement.
Chief negotiator Rita Hayes stated that progress had been made on market access.
The two sides still had significant issues to resolve on the third day of talks.
The talks aim to renew a 1994 textile accord and address U.S. penalties on Chinese exports.
Washington could significantly cut China's textile quotas if no agreement is reached before January 31.
Hayes indicated that a lot of work was needed on the final day of negotiations.
The Sino-U.S. textile pact was scheduled to expire on December 31 but was extended by one month.
The United States has threatened penalties and raised concerns about a trade war over Chinese textile exports.
China has threatened to retaliate by banning imports of some U.S. textiles but has delayed action for further talks.

AT&T Corp's core businesses performed better in the last quarter of 1996 after struggling during much of the year.
Rising bad debts from business customers are causing concern among analysts.
Traffic volumes increased by 3.2 percent, which was better than the expected 2.5 percent.
AT&T is losing market share at a rate of three percentage points a year.
An extra $200 million provision for uncollectible revenue affected earnings for the fourth quarter.
AT&T's operating net was $0.76, compared to $0.68 in the previous year, but below the $0.79 consensus of analysts.
Increased provisions will cost AT&T $100 million each quarter.
Bette Massick, an analyst at Bear Stearns, lowered her earnings estimate for AT&T for 1997 to $3.20 from $3.65 per share.
AT&T has lowered customer turnover and maintained its market share in business services.
AT&T's operating losses in the credit card business fell to $4 million in the fourth quarter from $35 million in the third quarter of 1994.

AT&T Corp. will have salespeople arriving at customers' doorsteps to promote their long-distance service.
The salespeople will be from Shaklee Corp., which has 500,000 sales agents.
Shaklee's sales agents will begin selling AT&T phone service face-to-face starting in January 1997.
Shaklee sales representatives will sell to friends, colleagues, and neighbors, not to strangers.
Joseph Nacchio is the executive vice president of AT&T's consumer and small business division.
Shaklee is part of Yamanouchi Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd. of Japan.
Shaklee currently sells nutritional supplements, personal care products, household cleaners, and water treatment products.
Shaklee has a strong presence among ethnic minorities, non-English speakers, and in inner cities.
AT&T aims to expand its presence in communities through the alliance with Shaklee.
AT&T's market share in the long-distance market has decreased from 90 percent to about 55 percent over the last decade.

Long distance telephone companies and regional Bells are expected to show consistent growth in core operations in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Investors are wary about growing competition in the phone company sector.
Phone company stocks fell sharply in 1996 despite a rising broad market.
Analysts state that investors will remain reluctant until regulatory and competitive uncertainties are resolved.
Guy Woodlief, an analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds, commented on investor reluctance due to uncertainties.
The long distance industry is expected to average revenue growth of eight percent.
Call growth in the long distance industry is projected at ten percent.
Price weakness in the long distance market is expected to accelerate as regional Bells enter the market.
Richard Klugman of PaineWebber believes that the entry of Bells into long distance will take significant regulatory work.
GTE Corp is already providing long distance service and has forecasted 750,000 new customers in 1996.

Quaker Oats Co's Snapple beverage business has posted operating losses for two years since its acquisition for $1.8 billion.
Robert Cummins, managing director of Schroder Wertheim, stated that Snapple has likely declined as much as it will.
Quaker Oats Co faces challenges in recovering its investment in the Snapple business.
Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez indicated that Quaker has a long way to go to achieve a return on its investment.
Quaker Chairman William Smithburg acknowledged that Snapple has been a disappointment.
Snapple's sale volume declined in 1996 compared to the previous year, resulting in an operating loss before amortization.
William Smithburg expressed optimism for a turnaround in Snapple for 1997 and promised an end to operating losses.
Being cash positive means Snapple would post a profit after amortization costs.
Analysts have suggested that flat sales and reduced costs could help Snapple break even in 1997.
There are rumors that Quaker may consider selling the Snapple business, but Smithburg declined to comment on these rumors.

DeKalb Genetics Corp reported better-than-expected fiscal first quarter results.
DeKalb Genetics Corp expects higher margins and increased market share for its U.S. and Canadian seed corn operations this year.
Thomas Rauman is the chief financial officer of DeKalb Genetics Corp.
Rauman stated that DeKalb will be $4 per unit in gross margins better in North American seed.
DeKalb expects to sell more seed corn this year than last year.
International income for DeKalb nearly doubled to $5.9 million in the first quarter ended November 30.
Rauman indicated that international income is likely to increase by a double-digit percentage for all of fiscal 1997.
DeKalb is the number two North American seed corn supplier with about an 11 percent market share.
Analysts expect DeKalb to see sharply higher earnings in fiscal 1997.
DeKalb earned $1.03 a share in fiscal 1996.

Kellogg Co's profits for 1996 are under pressure from price cuts and promotions.
Kellogg Co plans to take necessary steps to preserve its category leadership.
Analysts suggest that Kellogg may cut prices or increase promotions.
Chairman Arnold Langbo stated that Kellogg will direct efforts away from deep price promotion.
Langbo emphasized that Kellogg is unwilling to compromise its leadership position.
Earlier in the year, Kellogg, General Mills Inc, and Post Cereal division of Philip Morris Cos Inc cut retail prices.
Analyst David Rabinowitz noted that consumers want lower prices.
Analysts expected Kellogg to report earnings below last year's $3.48 a share.
Kellogg's guidance for earnings has changed, with projections differing from previous estimates.
Kellogg believes third quarter earnings will be about 20 percent below the $1.05 per share earned in 1995.

Hong Kong's chief judge is Sir Ti Liang Yang.
Sir Ti Liang Yang announced his candidacy for the territory's leadership on Tuesday.
Yang's announcement raised concerns about a conflict of interest regarding his role in the judiciary.
Lawyer Martin Lee stated that it is important for the public to have confidence in the independence of Hong Kong's judiciary.
Yang expressed that the decision to resign should be made by the executive, society, government, Chinese side, and the public.
Calls for Yang's resignation came from both political opponents and some members of the pro-Beijing camp.
Pro-China politician Tsang Yok-sing stated that Yang should resign as Chief Justice but welcomed his candidacy.
Law professor Nihal Jayawickrama argued that Yang should resign now that he has entered politics.
Hong Kong has 300 days until it reverts to Chinese rule, ending British governance.
Pro-Beijing publisher Xu Simin pledged to nominate Yang for leadership.

Hong Kong's Democratic Party welcomed a pledge from future leader Tung Chee-hwa regarding basic freedoms after the handover to China.
Some activists protested during a meeting organized by Tung's aides to gather public opinions on his plan to reduce civil liberties.
An opinion poll indicated that 90% of Hong Kong students do not believe China will allow the territory its promised autonomy after the handover.
Concerns have increased in Hong Kong about a potential loss of freedom after the handover from Britain.
Tung Chee-hwa defended proposed restrictions on the right to demonstrate and foreign funding of political groups.
Tung stated that laws in the United States regarding demonstrations are stricter than those proposed in Hong Kong.
Tung assured that the future government is determined to preserve the freedoms currently enjoyed by the people of Hong Kong.
Tung emphasized that peaceful and lawful demonstrations should continue as part of Hong Kong's culture.
Anthony Cheung, vice president of the Democratic Party, expressed cautious support for Tung's assurances but questioned the substance of his proposals.
Pro-democracy councillors disrupted a public consultation on Tung's plan at Hong Kong's Space Museum, claiming it was a fake consultation.

Hong Kong's future government has canceled a session of the provisional legislature due to a shortage of trained staff.
The canceled session was scheduled to address a draft law on new flags.
Tung Chee-hwa will rule Hong Kong after the British handover on June 30.
Bob Howlett, a spokesman for Tung's office, stated that the draft bills are not ready because there are not enough people.
Michael Suen, Tung's coordinator, determined that there are not enough draftsmen to prepare the planned laws.
Tung's office expressed a commitment to complete the drafting of essential bills before the July 1 handover.
British Governor Chris Patten has refused to provide additional staff from the Hong Kong civil service to assist Tung's office.
Tung's office currently has only two law drafters on its staff.
China will resume sovereignty over Hong Kong under a 1984 treaty that allows for 50 years of virtual autonomy.
Kerry McGlynn, Patten's spokesman, expressed that no legislation should proceed before June 30 to avoid legal challenges after the handover.

Labour unions at Renault SA called for a one-hour strike at all Renault plants in France, Belgium, and Spain.
The strike was in response to the announcement of the closure of Renault's Vilvoorde plant near Brussels.
Reports indicated that jobs would be lost in France due to the closure.
Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer agreed to meet staff at the Belgian plant where 3,100 jobs will be cut.
The time and place for the meeting with staff had not been set.
The announcement of the Vilvoorde plant closure caused political backlash, including a denunciation from Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene.
Renault's spokeswoman did not comment on reports of 3,000 job cuts planned in France.
An industry source indicated that fewer than 3,000 jobs would be cut in 1997.
Renault's new car sales in France dropped 24.6 percent last month after a 33.6 percent decline in January.
French unemployment was reported at 12.7 percent, and the government refused to support a plan to cut 40,000 jobs in the car industry.

Thomson-CSF is a French defence electronics firm.
Thomson-CSF posted 1996 results showing a return to profit after three years of losses.
Thomson-CSF reported a net attributable profit of 745 million francs in 1996.
Thomson-CSF had a net loss of 791 million francs in 1995.
Sales for Thomson-CSF increased by 2.2 percent to 36.27 billion francs.
The return to profit was mainly due to the sale of Thomson-CSF's 19 percent stake in Credit Lyonnais.
Chairman Marcel Roulet stated that the company is now focused on defence electronics.
The French state is attempting to privatise Thomson-CSF as part of a defence industry restructuring.
Alcatel Alsthom, Dassault Aviation, and Aerospatiale are bidding for Thomson-CSF.
Thomson-CSF's operating profit rose 5.6 percent to 2.07 billion francs despite market challenges.

Air France announced a transatlantic alliance with Delta Air Lines and Continental on Monday.
The alliance is part of Air France's strategy to form global links.
Delta and Continental introduced registration facilities at Air France's hub at Paris Charles de Gaulle airport.
Flights and operations have officially transferred from Paris Orly airport to Charles de Gaulle airport.
Air France's hub at Charles de Gaulle is now linked to five major U.S. hubs.
The U.S. hubs linked to Air France include New York's JFK, Atlanta, Cincinnati, New York-Newark, and Houston.
Bob Coggins, Delta's executive vice president for marketing, stated that the partnership offers opportunities to flow traffic to Paris and beyond.
The alliances allow Air France and the U.S. carriers to share Frequent Flyer programs and revenues on flights.
Air France plans to implement a code-sharing program with Delta and Continental, pending a bilateral air treaty agreement between the French and U.S. governments.
Air France's new summer schedule and U.S. partnerships are expected to increase its traffic by 20 percent this year.

The chairman of CSX Corp is John Snow.
John Snow is reasonably confident but guarded that Conrail shareholders will approve a provision of the planned $9.2 billion railroad merger.
CSX will remain committed to the union even if the measure is defeated.
John Snow described Norfolk Southern Corp's latest attempt to thwart the transaction as a desperate act.
Conrail shareholders will vote on a provision that will enable CSX to pay cash and stock for Conrail.
Norfolk Southern's $10.3 billion offer was rejected by Conrail.
Norfolk Southern offered to buy 9.9 percent of Conrail if shareholders defeat the measure.
John Snow admitted that the Norfolk Southern offer is probably creating some confusion in the market.
The proposed merger prevents Conrail or CSX from entering a partnership with another party before 1999.
John Snow stated that if Conrail shareholders defeat the vote, Conrail can call a new meeting.

ITT Corp. met with financial advisers to assess a $6.5 billion bid from Hilton Hotels Corp.
Some Wall Street analysts suggested that ITT's best defense might be to pursue an acquisition.
Industry experts indicated that ITT could prevent the takeover by making a large casino or hotel purchase.
Thomas Ryan of Bankers Trust stated that ITT has many connections on Wall Street and in the gaming industry.
ITT is expected to reject Hilton's offer, but sources said no decision has been made and no acquisition talks are ongoing.
ITT's board will consider Hilton's bid at a scheduled meeting next Tuesday.
Hilton's offer values ITT at $55 per share and includes the assumption of $4 billion in debt.
ITT's stock price fell to $56.875 after rising earlier in the week.
ITT's financial advisers are expected to review Hilton's official bid documents filed with the SEC.
Industry experts believe a significant acquisition by ITT could make Hilton's takeover too costly.

The bidding war for Conrail Inc is nearing its conclusion.
Legal and regulatory battles are expected to follow the bidding war.
CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp are the rival bidders for Conrail.
Industry analysts believe CSX and Norfolk Southern will not increase their offers for Conrail significantly.
Anthony Hatch is an analyst at NatWest Securities Corp.
CSX revised its merger agreement with Conrail to provide an additional $870 million to shareholders.
The revised deal is valued at $9.3 billion, or approximately $102 per Conrail share.
A source close to CSX indicated that the revised deal aims to conclude the bidding war.
Norfolk Southern increased its all-cash offer to $10.5 billion, or $115 per share.
Norfolk Southern is legally challenging a provision that prevents CSX or Conrail from seeking other merger partners until 1999.

U.S. Judge Harold Greene oversaw the dismantling of the old Ma Bell.
Judge Greene is concerned that a merger involving AT&T Corp could create a corporate monolith.
Judge Greene advises regulators to be very cautious regarding any merger of AT&T and SBC Communications Inc.
In 1982, Judge Greene ordered the breakup of the Bell system monopoly.
Judge Greene presided over the consent agreement that created seven regional Baby Bell companies and the new AT&T.
AT&T is in talks to merge with SBC Communications Inc. in a transaction estimated to exceed $50 billion.
The proposed merger would be the largest deal in history.
Judge Greene stated that the breakup was based on the assumption that competition could not exist with a massive company.
Judge Greene believes that market conditions have not significantly changed since the breakup of the Bell monopoly.
Judge Greene hopes that regulators will be cautious in approving the merger.

The Justice Department is investigating possible bid rigging during airwaves auctions for wireless phone licenses.
Documents obtained by Reuters indicate that the Justice Department's antitrust division is looking into illegal schemes among bidders.
The Federal Communications Commission has raised more than $20 billion since 1995 by selling licenses for personal communications services (PCS).
A Justice Department spokeswoman confirmed the investigation into anticompetitive conduct by bidders related to the FCC's auctioning of spectrum for PCS.
The spokeswoman did not comment on whether the investigation covers all three major PCS auctions.
Sources indicate that the Justice Department is seeking information from companies about all PCS sales.
The investigation documents focus on a PCS auction that ended in mid-January and raised $2.5 billion.
The auction involved the sale of 1,479 PCS licenses nationwide in three different blocks.
A third of the licenses in the auction were reserved for small-company bidders.
Top bidders in the auction included units of Sprint Corp., AT&T Corp., and BellSouth Corp.

Rupert Murdoch is making a public pitch for his $1 billion Sky satellite-broadcast venture.
Murdoch's Sky venture is intended to compete with cable television.
Stephen Effros is the president of the Cable Telecommunications Association.
Effros expressed concern that Murdoch is trying to accumulate excessive power.
Murdoch is lobbying Congress for legislation that would benefit his new venture.
Sky is expected to appeal to a Senate Commerce Committee hearing.
Sky is set to launch in early 1998.
Sky is expected to offer more than 500 channels of high-quality digital TV and Internet services.
Direct broadcast satellite operators have nearly 5 million subscribers.
Murdoch aims to attract a significant portion of the cable industry's 65 million subscribers.

Hewlett-Packard Co. will launch new models of computer servers on Monday.
The new HP 9000 line of servers is more than double the speed of their predecessors.
The new servers are based on H-P's latest PA-RISC 8000 microprocessor.
Hewlett-Packard claims that the new servers outperform those of its rivals.
The launch will put pressure on Sun Microsystems and other competitors like IBM, Silicon Graphics, and Digital Equipment Corp.
The introduction of the new servers follows a sluggish transition to PA-8000-based workstations in June.
Carol Mills, worldwide general manager for HP's Unix server business, stated that the market is growing at over 50 percent a year.
Mills identified new applications such as data warehousing and using servers as alternatives to mainframes as key market opportunities.
HP's new server lines complete its transition to 64-bit microprocessors for Unix machines.
The HP 9000 K-Class models range in starting price from $52,200 to $77,200.

Intel Corp. will launch two networking products on Monday.
The products are aimed at increasing the use of powerful computers.
Intel's Internet and Communications Group (ICG) is based in Hillsboro, Oregon.
Intel is introducing a networking hub that allows speeds from 10 Mbps to 100 Mbps.
The Intel Express 10/100 Stackable Hub will be priced at $99 per port in some configurations.
Traditional 100 Mbps hubs are priced between $150 and $175 per port.
Slower 10 Mbps hubs are priced at $70 per port.
The Intel Express 10/100 Stackable Hub can be stacked up to eight units high.
Intel is launching the Intel 82558, the industry's first single chip Fast Ethernet product.
The Intel 82558 supports networking speeds of 10 or 100 Mbps.

Ira Magaziner is a senior advisor to President Clinton for policy development.
Magaziner stated that electronic commerce over the Internet could become the world's largest trade category within the next decade if it is not over-regulated.
Magaziner made these comments during a keynote speech at an Internet Tax Policy Conference.
He emphasized that the Internet must remain a free market for electronic commerce to grow.
Magaziner claimed that with the right environment, trade across the Internet could surpass any other trade category in five to ten years.
He warned that poor policy decisions could lead to 30 to 40 years of trying to correct mistakes.
The Clinton administration proposed a global electronic commerce framework last month.
The draft policy suggests making cyberspace a duty-free zone with no new taxes and minimal governmental regulation.
Magaziner noted that he is aware of a dozen countries considering imposing duties on Internet transactions.
The draft document is available on the White House home page, and the administration is collecting responses to finalize the policy paper by March.

Institutional investors supported China's efforts to reduce stock market speculation.
Investors warned that Hong Kong's market volatility is expected to persist.
Stewart Aldcroft is the director of sales and marketing for Templeton Franklin Investment Services (Asia) Ltd.
The Hang Seng index closed at 14,112.55, up 188.21 points or 1.35 percent.
The Hang Seng index experienced a total drop of 907 points over five consecutive trading sessions ending on Thursday.
The index's fluctuations were influenced by China's actions, property market concerns, and a downgrade by Merrill Lynch.
Red chips are stocks related to China that have shown significant volatility since February.
Red chips have outperformed the rest of the Hong Kong market but lost about one-third of their gains since January.
Templeton and other international institutions have avoided investing in red chips.
China fund performance figures show various funds with significant gains, attributed to investments in red chips.

A contingent of China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) will arrive in Hong Kong next week.
The PLA contingent consists of 40 unarmed soldiers.
The arrival of the PLA personnel is an advance guard prior to Britain's formal handover of Hong Kong to China.
The sovereignty switch will occur at midnight on June 30.
The PLA personnel will not wear uniforms outside their barracks and will have no security role.
Michael DeGolyer, a political analyst at Hong Kong's Baptist University, stated that the PLA has a central role in China.
The diplomatic status of other Chinese representative offices in Hong Kong has been uncertain at times.
The PLA is recognized as China's designated protector of both party and state.
Tung Chee-hwa is the first post-colonial leader of Hong Kong, appointed by China in December.
There are increasing signs of strain in the Sino-British relationship.

Hong Kong held a vote in favor of the status quo on Wednesday.
Tung Chee-hwa appointed Donald Tsang as the manager of the US$19 billion Land Fund after July 1.
The appointment of Donald Tsang was seen as a vote of support for him.
Donald Tsang is considered one of Hong Kong's most senior civil servants.
Bob Broadfoot of the Political and Economic Risk Consultancy commented on Tsang's appointment.
Broadfoot noted that Tsang's appointment indicated he was not being marginalized.
Tung's decision to appoint Tsang as chairman of the Land Fund Committee was made before Hong Kong becomes a Special Administrative Region of China.
Tsang's continued role as Financial Secretary after the handover was uncertain earlier this year.
Tung previously suggested changes to the reporting structure at the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
The Land Fund was established in 1984 and now exceeds HK$150 billion.

At least two people were killed in a bomb explosion on a public bus in Beijing.
About 30 people were taken to hospitals following the explosion.
The explosion occurred in Beijing's western shopping district of Xidan at around 6:30 p.m. (1030 GMT).
The explosion engulfed a bus in flames and caused passengers to scramble to escape.
A witness reported seeing a woman come out of the bus with her hair on fire.
Workers at an emergency center reported picking up about 30 injured people.
A young man reported seeing about nine people seriously hurt in the explosion.
A police official stated that some people were suffering from burns but did not provide further details.
The motive for the bombing was not immediately known, and it was unclear if any arrests had been made.
Exiled Uighur nationalists in Kazakhstan claimed responsibility for similar bombings in Xinjiang.

Chinese police cordoned off a South Korean embassy compound on Thursday.
North Korean diplomats were present outside the South Korean embassy compound.
An official from Seoul met with Kim Ha-jung, the most senior North Korean to defect.
Beijing officials avoided meeting Kim Ha-jung due to anger over Seoul's actions.
South Korean sources reported that the Seoul Foreign Ministry envoy was meeting Chinese officials regarding defector Hwang Jang-yop.
Hwang Jang-yop is a senior aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il.
Hwang Jang-yop is 73 years old and one of the chief architects of North Korean communism.
Hwang Jang-yop is the highest-ranking official from North Korea to seek asylum in South Korea.
China's Foreign Ministry spokesman expressed anger over not being notified in advance about Hwang's transit through Beijing.
South Korean embassy officials accused North Koreans of attempting to enter the consular office.

Weeping crowds mourned the death of Deng Xiaoping in his birthplace, Paifang village.
Authorities sent armed police to maintain order during the mourning.
Thousands of mourners gathered in Guang'an county, Sichuan province.
Some mourners fell to their knees and wept.
Deng Xiaoping passed away at the age of 92 on Wednesday night.
Deng was known as the architect of market-oriented reforms in China.
The museum at Deng's former residence was overwhelmed by visitors after his death was announced.
Approximately 3,000 people visited the museum the day after Deng's death.
The People's Armed Police were deployed to maintain order at the museum.
Mourners displayed white flowers to express their grief over Deng Xiaoping.

Lloyd's of London received a vote of confidence when Commercial Union took a role in the Lloyd's insurance market.
Commercial Union acquired a majority stake in Marlborough Underwriting Agency Limited.
Marlborough Underwriting Agency Limited is responsible for running syndicates at Lloyd's.
This acquisition represents the first active participation by a major composite insurer in Lloyd's.
The move may negatively impact Names, who have unlimited liability and traditionally backed the insurance market.
Equitas, a company set up to manage Lloyd's pre-1993 liabilities, has uncertain long-term prospects.
Lloyd's has changed significantly since it faced over eight billion pounds in losses between 1988 and 1992.
Corporate capital now accounts for around 44 percent of Lloyd's market capacity of 10.3 billion pounds.
The number of Names has decreased to below 10,000 for the first time since the mid-1970s.
In 1989, there were over 34,000 Names in Lloyd's.

B.A.T Industries is a British tobacco-to-insurance group.
B.A.T Industries stated it is confident that tobacco-related lawsuits in the United States will not materially impact its bottom line.
Chairman Lord Cairns mentioned that the company should prepare for occasional reversals, particularly at the lower court level.
B.A.T's American subsidiary is Brown & Williamson.
Brown & Williamson is facing multiple lawsuits, including 24 cases from individual states seeking to recover funds for treating tobacco-related illnesses.
B.A.T reported flat first quarter pre-tax profits.
B.A.T chief executive Martin Broughton declined to comment on reports of a potential $300 billion settlement regarding the lawsuits.
Broughton also did not comment on the possibility of the tobacco industry relying on insurance coverage to offset claims.
Insurance issues are described by Broughton as complex, with various policies containing different exclusion clauses.
B.A.T reported a rise in group pre-tax profits to 591 million pounds in the first three months of the year.

Around three million members of British insurer Norwich Union will be able to buy shares at a 10 percent discount in a planned offering ahead of the company's flotation on June 16.
Norwich is to raise 1.75 billion pounds ($2.9 billion) of fresh capital in the offering and up to a further 670 million pounds to fund cash payments to its half million overseas members.
The company has increased its estimate of the price of the new shares to between 240 pence and 290 pence.
The group's brokers Kleinwort Benson had previously given a guide price of between 220 pence and 265 pence.
Members of the insurance group, which is Britain's third largest with seven million customers worldwide, are to be offered extra shares at a fixed discount of 25 pence.
A member is defined as someone who holds a Norwich life insurance, pension, or annuity policy.
Holders of non-life policies such as house contents or car insurance do not qualify as members.
Members will receive around 1.3 billion free shares worth around 3.4 billion pounds under flotation plans.
The value of the 300 shares minimum allocation to with-profits policyholders will increase by at least 60 pounds and could be worth as much as 870 pounds.
Norwich expects to be valued at between 4.9 and 5.6 billion pounds on flotation, which would place it in the FTSE 100 index of Britain's largest quoted companies.

Hong Kong is preparing for its return to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after being a British colony for 150 years.
The city is undergoing changes to improve its appearance for the handover ceremony.
Roads and lanes leading to the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre have been cleared of street-sleepers.
Potted plants and ornamental iron fences have replaced the street-sleepers.
Lighting displays depicting dragons, dolphins, and orchids have been installed to celebrate the handover.
Britain will hand Hong Kong back to China in 12 days.
Over 4,000 VIPs, including heads of state and ministers, will attend the handover ceremony.
Approximately 8,000 foreign reporters have been flown in to cover the event.
Hotels in Hong Kong have trained staff to answer questions from VIPs and reporters about the city.
Hong Kong police are involved in security measures, including metal detectors for guests at hotels.

Hong Kong property prices have decreased by 10 percent from recent peaks.
Analysts predict that property prices in Hong Kong are likely to fall further.
Speculators are becoming nervous due to recent government actions to cool the market.
Transactions in the Hong Kong property market have declined.
Some buyers have chosen to forgo deposits instead of completing contracts.
Raymond Ngai, a property analyst with UBS Securities, stated that sentiment in the property market has turned bearish.
Ngai predicted that property prices could fall by up to 20 percent by the end of the current quarter.
Prices have already fallen by five to 10 percent from recent peaks, according to property brokers.
The government has implemented measures to increase the supply of new flats in the market.
The prime lending rate has increased by 25 basis points to 8.75 percent.

Publisher Penguin group and Chinese activists launched a compilation of letters and essays by Wei Jingsheng.
The book is titled 'The Courage To Stand Alone'.
China's Foreign Ministry denounced the publication of the book.
The book contains excerpts of hundreds of letters written by Wei Jingsheng during his imprisonment.
Wei Jingsheng was imprisoned for 14 years from 1979 to 1993, mostly in solitary confinement.
Wei Jingsheng is regarded as the father of China's democracy movement.
Wei was jailed in 1979 for counter-revolutionary incitement after advocating for democratic change.
Wei obtained his letters just before his release from jail in September 1993.
Wei was detained again in 1994 and sentenced to an additional 14 years for treason.
Wei is currently in a jail in Hebei province and has health issues including arthritis and high blood pressure.

America Online Inc. was hit with two lawsuits from subscribers on Wednesday.
AOL experienced a computer glitch that caused a partial outage of its system for nearly four hours.
The outage occurred from 3:45 p.m. EST until about 7:30 p.m. EST.
AOL's system was able to accommodate 124,000 subscribers during the outage.
Normally, AOL accommodates about 258,000 users simultaneously.
The problem was identified as an interface board issue in a router device.
AOL's network returned to full capacity by 8 p.m. EST.
The outage was not related to increased member usage after switching to unlimited use for $19.95 a month.
AOL previously experienced a significant network outage in August last year that lasted almost 19 hours.
Two lawsuits were filed in New York state court this week, claiming breach of contract and deceptive trade practices.

International Business Machines Corp. introduced its next generation mainframe computer family on Tuesday.
The new systems are twice as fast as currently available models.
Ross Mauri is the vice president of System 390 hardware development at IBM.
Mauri reported phenomenal feedback and significant demand for the new servers.
IBM is likely to be sold out of its new mainframe production for the year based on initial customer reactions.
Mainframes are large computers that store data for major corporations worldwide.
Mainframes are used by banks for transactions, airlines for reservation systems, and insurance companies for claims processing.
Despite predictions of their decline, mainframes have seen a resurgence as data repositories accessible via the Internet and intranets.
The new mainframe servers utilize IBM's third generation CMOS processor technology.
IBM introduced two new lines of System 390 servers: the IBM S/390 Parallel Enterprise Server and the IBM S/390 Multiprise 2000.

International Business Machines Corp. and 15 U.S. and Canadian banks formed a company called Integrion Financial Network.
Integrion Financial Network will offer electronic banking services in North America.
The services will be available to U.S. and Canadian banks starting early next year.
IBM Chairman Louis Gerstner stated that this venture represents a significant advancement in electronic commerce.
Integrion will develop an electronic bill payment system and provide software for member banks' customers.
Consumers will access the Integrion network via the Internet or commercial online services.
Electronic commerce could grow to $600 billion a year within 10 years, according to Gerstner.
Currently, electronic commerce is approximately $700 million a year.
Integrion will be owned and operated by the member banks and IBM.
The IBM Global Network will serve as the base network for electronic banking.

Unilever NV/Plc reported a 15 percent rise in pre-tax profits for 1996.
Unilever's pre-tax profit rose to 2.66 billion pounds ($4.4 billion).
Unilever's revenues increased by 6 percent to 33.52 billion pounds ($54.7 billion).
Unilever's stock surged following the reported results and the planned sale of its speciality chemicals businesses.
Analysts had forecasted a pre-tax profit of 53 billion pounds ($4.13 billion).
Chairman Niall FitzGerald stated that the overall economic situation in 1997 is likely to be generally favorable.
FitzGerald warned about market conditions in Europe, particularly in France and Germany.
Unilever plans to sell its speciality chemicals businesses to focus on growth in consumer goods operations.
The four units being sold have combined revenue of 3.0 billion pounds ($4.9 billion) and operating profit of 415 million pounds ($678 million) in 1996.
The four companies employ 15,800 people in more than 35 countries.

Shares in Bass Plc are likely to be held back until Britain's Trade and Industry secretary Ian Lang decides on its proposed merger with Carlsberg-Tetley.
Ian Lang announced that the Bass deal would be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
The Monopolies and Mergers Commission is due to report before March 24, 1997.
Bass shares fell 6p to 781p following the announcement.
John Wakley, an analyst at Lehman Brothers, stated that the stock is likely to be inactive until March.
Dermott Carr, an analyst at Nikko, indicated that the market will hold onto Bass shares until a decision is made.
Many analysts expect Ian Lang to defer a decision until after the next general election, which will be called by May 22.
Wakley suggested that the decision may be deferred to avoid negative public relations from potential job losses.
If the merger does not proceed, analysts estimate a maximum loss of 60 million for Bass, with most estimates between 30-40 million.
Bass stated it would take a one-off charge of 75 million stg for restructuring and expects annual cost savings of 90 million stg within three years.

Vaux Plc reported a nine percent rise in its pretax profits to 34.8 million pounds.
Sir Paul Nicholson is the chairman of Vaux Plc.
Nicholson stated that the new financial year has started well with increased beer sales.
Nicholson noted that consumers are feeling good, benefiting Vaux's hotels.
Vaux's 30 mid-market Swallow hotels had a profit increase of 4.3 million to 24.1 million pounds in 1996.
Nicholson reported a six percent increase in Christmas bookings over the next two weeks.
Nicholson mentioned a three percentage point increase in bookings over the next three months.
Vaux's beer sales rose one percent in the year to September 30, 1996, while the overall market declined by 0.5 percent.
The brewing and wholesaling side of Vaux improved profits by 25 percent to 4.52 million pounds.
Vaux owns 868 pubs, with 163 managed, and plans to convert 25 more from tenanted to managed pubs.

Talks aimed at settling a dispute between the United Auto Workers and Johnson Controls Inc. continued on Thursday afternoon.
Ford Motor Co. prepared to idle light truck production lines at three plants.
Johnson Controls spokesman Jeff Steiner stated that talks were ongoing as of mid-afternoon.
The strike entered its 10th day on Thursday.
About 500 UAW workers walked off the job on January 28 at two Johnson Controls seat plants in Plymouth, Michigan, and Oberlin, Ohio.
The plants conduct final seat assembly for the Ford Expedition and Econoline and Club Wagons.
Ford plans to idle its Michigan Truck Assembly plant and part of two other facilities in Ohio.
Ford spokesman Bert Serre stated that the company would suspend production at the plants if the dispute was not resolved.
The shutdown would idle about 6,800 hourly workers.
Ford has continued to make and store Expeditions and Econolines using temporary seats to finish production.

Bargaining between union and American Axle Manufacturing Inc. negotiators was expected to continue up to the midnight Friday deadline.
The deadline was set to avoid a strike that would paralyze General Motors Corp.'s U.S. light truck production.
About 7,200 United Auto Workers union members were ready to walk off the job at five plants in Detroit, Three Rivers, Mich., and Buffalo, N.Y.
The walkout would occur if no agreement was reached on a new three-year contract.
American Axle was spun off from GM into a private company in 1994.
American Axle supplies virtually all of the rear axles for GM's pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles.
The company also makes axles for Chrysler Corp. and axle shafts for Ford Motor Co.
Tight inventories at American Axle and Dana Corp. could lead to GM's light truck plants running out of parts by early next week.
Analysts indicated that GM could lose $20 million a day in after-tax profits if it had to suspend light truck production.
UAW membership among independent suppliers has dropped dramatically over the last 20 years, with less than 20 percent belonging to the UAW.

Thousands of auto dealers attended their annual convention in Las Vegas last year.
There is concern among dealers about the rise of no-haggle superstores.
This year's convention will take place in Atlanta starting Saturday.
Republic Industries Inc. is controlled by billionaire investor Wayne Huizenga.
Republic Industries Inc. may be the largest auto dealer group in the nation.
Republic Industries Inc. owns the AutoNation USA superstore chain.
Republic Industries Inc. has acquired six dealer groups within two months.
CarMax, owned by Circuit City Stores Inc., is considering buying existing dealerships.
John Sinclair, owner of Sinclair Ford, stated that the changes are unsettling for dealers.
Montgomery Securities estimated Republic's 1997 franchised dealership revenues at $2.5 billion.

China's state-run steel companies need to reduce their payrolls.
Top officials believe these companies can survive in a competitive marketplace.
Liu Qi is the minister of Metallurgical Industry.
Liu Qi expressed confidence in state enterprises in the steel industry.
Many companies in the steel sector have begun reducing staff.
The trend of staff reduction is expected to continue in the coming years.
China's steel industry currently employs 4.5 million people.
Liu Qi stated that Anshan Steel has 190,000 employees, with only 70,000 directly producing steel.
Liu Qi indicated that restructuring would not lead to large numbers of layoffs.
Seventy percent of China's 107 large and medium-sized steel companies were profitable last year.

Farmers near Beijing marked the death of Deng Xiaoping on Thursday.
Farmers prioritized making a living over memorials for Deng Xiaoping.
Deng Xiaoping died at the age of 92 on Wednesday.
Some farmers expressed gratitude for Deng Xiaoping's leadership.
Chinese state media announced Deng's death early on Thursday.
Deng Xiaoping's policies improved rural incomes for many farmers.
Shi Huaiqing stated that his life is better now than in the past due to Deng's policies.
Shi Huaiqing can now raise and sell sheep privately without repercussions.
A retired farmer surnamed Zhao reported that he is better off than before.
Some individuals expressed disappointment over slow income growth and corruption linked to Deng's reforms.

China vowed to keep banks out of the stock market.
China accused big financial institutions of fuelling a speculative bubble.
Vice Premier Zhu Rongji warned bankers they could face jail for diverting funds into the stock market.
Zhu stated that funds not in company accounts or bank credits used for stock market speculation would be investigated.
Zhu indicated that those responsible would be sacked and offenders pursued under criminal law.
The Financial News attributed a rise in share prices last year to institutional speculation.
The Financial News reported that a speculative bubble emerged in the stock markets at the end of last year.
Beijing warned investors that the state would not bail them out from stock market losses.
China has attempted to prevent state-run banks from fuelling stock market speculation.
Brokers expressed concern that driving institutional money away from the market could reduce turnover.

A top federal regulator urged banks to be more careful in issuing credit cards.
The American Bankers Association reported that late payments by consumers reached a record level at the end of last year.
In the fourth quarter of 1996, late payments jumped to 3.72 percent of credit card accounts.
The 3.72 percent late payment rate is the highest since the American Bankers Association began tracking delinquencies in 1980.
The late payment rate increased from 3.34 percent a year earlier.
Personal bankruptcies are at record levels.
Bank losses from credit card loans are growing.
Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig oversees almost 3,000 nationally chartered banks.
Ludwig stated that there was a 44 percent growth in credit card losses and a 50 percent increase in credit card delinquencies during the past year.
Bank charge-offs on credit cards increased to 6.5 percent in January from 4.7 percent a year earlier.

Ten leading U.S. high-technology companies lobbied in Washington for stronger laws against piracy.
Executives from Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp met with senators, reporters, Vice President Al Gore, and Commerce Secretary William Daley.
The executives presented research showing the software industry significantly contributes to economic growth.
Bill Gates stated that the PC software industry is fast-growing and innovative.
Research for the Business Software Alliance indicated the software industry was worth $102.8 billion in 1996.
The software industry directly employed 619,000 people and paid $36.4 billion in wages in 1996.
An additional 1.4 million American workers were indirectly employed due to the software industry.
The software industry grew at an annual rate of 12.5 percent since 1980, outpacing the U.S. economy.
Piracy cost the software industry $11.2 billion in 1996, with a significant portion occurring in China.
The executives advocated for relaxing export limits on encryption technology to promote software sales.

A new class of financial derivative based on credit risk is growing in popularity.
U.S. banking regulators are assessing complex financial derivatives.
Most derivatives are linked to interest rates or currencies.
Credit derivatives are based on the value of loans, bonds, or other lending vehicles.
William Kroener is the general counsel of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp.
Bank regulators issued preliminary guidance to bank examiners concerning credit derivatives in August.
The guidance emphasized that banks should have policies for managing risks from credit derivatives.
Regulators requested banks to clearly list credit derivative activity in their call reports.
Regulators are considering the amount of capital a bank must set aside for its credit derivative portfolio.
Christine Cumming is a senior vice president in the bank supervision group of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

East European markets increased this week, with Poland and Hungary leading in foreign buying.
Warsaw and Budapest reached year-highs during the week.
Romania and Slovenia also experienced significant increases.
Bratislava and Prague saw slight increases but lacked upward momentum.
The Warsaw Stock Exchange achieved three consecutive 33-month highs this week.
Heavy turnover was noted on the Warsaw Stock Exchange.
Post-fixing buying on Thursday contributed to another high on Friday.
Analysts predicted a profit-taking correction for the following week.
The Warsaw Stock Exchange has risen 23 percent since December 10.
Analysts expect 16,000 points to provide strong support for the WIG index next week.

The Prague Stock Exchange gained ground on Thursday.
Analysts are not convinced that the bourse's fortunes have turned around.
The rise in the bourse is attributed to thin domestic buying.
The bourse has gained in 15 of the past 16 sessions.
Analysts see little change in market sentiment amid mostly domestic trading.
The PX50 index closed up 0.56 percent at 521.1 on Thursday.
The bourse is about nine percent higher than its low in mid-November.
The Czech market has been plagued by poor legislation affecting minority shareholders.
The Securities Registry is bound by law to provide services related to securities transactions.
Local brokers prefer the Securities Registry for its privacy and faster settlement process.

Czech trading firms experienced a trade deficit that nearly doubled year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997.
Analysts stated that the trade deficit figures were in line with forecasts.
The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) released a survey indicating the trade deficit for the quarter should rise to about 45 billion crowns.
The trade deficit for the first quarter of 1996 was 27.1 billion crowns.
Martin Kupka, an economist at Patria Finance, predicted that the deficit situation would gradually worsen throughout the year.
The CSU forecasted the overall 1997 trade deficit to rise to between 211-219 billion crowns.
The CSU reported a record trade deficit of 160.3 billion crowns in the previous year.
The survey conducted by the CSU included estimates from firms that accounted for 20 percent of all import business and 36 percent of exports last year.
A total of 170 firms were polled in the CSU survey, with a 67 percent response rate.
Total imports in the first quarter of 1996 were 174.3 billion crowns.

Hammerson Plc's chief executive is Ron Spinney.
Ron Spinney expects the British market to perform well over the next two years.
Hammerson Plc announced a 21.3 percent rise in pre-tax profit for 1996 to 70.0 million stg.
The pre-tax profit for 1995 was 57.7 million stg.
Net asset value (NAV) per share rose 3.2 percent to 388 pence from 376 pence.
Hammerson turned over 15 percent of its portfolio in the past year.
Hammerson invested 50 million stg on improving existing properties.
Hammerson embarked on an 800 million stg development programme.
Hammerson plans to spend around 115 million stg on its existing portfolio and developments.
Hammerson's gearing is currently 58 percent.

Members of the Woolwich voted to change its mutual status to a publicly listed bank.
The vote was held during a special general meeting.
More than 95 percent of savers and borrowers who voted approved the proposals.
Individual members will receive an average share windfall of 1,200 pounds.
The handout will include at least 450 shares to around 2.57 million qualifying members and pensioners.
Approximately 1,200 members attended the meeting, with many expressing dissatisfaction with the conversion.
The vote was largely decided by a postal vote.
Woolwich Plc plans to offer a full range of personal financial services after its flotation.
The flotation is expected to occur in July and is valued at 3.0 billion pounds.
The Woolwich aims to expand into pensions and other financial areas, potentially through friendly mergers.

Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) is involved in a probe into alleged irregularities in three Morgan Grenfell investment funds.
The investigation has extended beyond Britain to include overseas elements.
Holding companies listed in Luxembourg are being investigated as part of the inquiry.
The SFO is in contact with Britain's Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO).
IMRO will share any relevant material with the SFO.
The SFO investigates and prosecutes major financial crimes in the City of London.
A senior SFO lawyer has been briefed by IMRO regarding the investigation.
Overseas authorities in the U.S., Luxembourg, and Switzerland are involved in the investigation.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell reported that nearly eight percent of the suspended funds were redeemed after they resumed trading.
IMRO's probe into Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) has led to the suspension of two fund managers.

Residents of a town in Xinjiang, China, returned to work on Wednesday after the Lunar New Year holiday.
Officials vowed to address separatism following a riot that resulted in 10 deaths.
Zhang Youlian is the deputy director of the foreign affairs office of the Yili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture.
Zhang Youlian stated that there is a resolve to deal with ethnic separatist elements.
Police arrested between 200 and 300 people in the crackdown after the riot.
About 1,000 Uighurs participated in a riot in Yining, Yili prefecture.
The riot was one of the largest and most violent demonstrations for independence in Xinjiang in several years.
The riot left 10 people dead and 144 wounded, with all victims being Han Chinese.
132 of the wounded were civilians and 12 were members of the paramilitary armed police.
Authorities had sealed off the town but planned to reopen the airport on Friday.

China is considering restrictions on foreign investment in textiles and garments.
Li Qiming is the director of the State Statistical Bureau's department of industry and transportation statistics.
Li Qiming stated that the production capacity of some traditional industries in China is excessive.
Li Qiming mentioned that losses of state enterprises in textiles and garments exceed the national average.
China plans to curb textile output and unnecessary expansion in the industry to reduce losses in the state sector.
China has set a target to phase out obsolete textile equipment, including 10 million cotton spindles.
In 1995, 429 state textile enterprises reported losses of more than five million yuan each.
The combined losses of these state textile enterprises reached 5.21 billion yuan in 1995.
A survey conducted by the bureau showed that foreign investment is concentrated mainly in electronics, telecommunications, textiles, garments, and food processing.
By the end of 1995, there were 59,311 wholly foreign-owned and Sino-foreign joint ventures in China.

Chinese police arrested Abudu Heilili, the suspected ringleader of a riot in Xinjiang.
The riot occurred last week and resulted in at least 10 deaths and 144 injuries.
Abudu Heilili is 29 years old and belongs to the Uighur ethnic minority.
Heilili was in police custody and under interrogation following the riot.
Heilili was unemployed and had previously led a less violent anti-Chinese demonstration in August 1995.
Heilili was released after the 1995 demonstration following 'ideological education'.
Police detained 200 to 300 people after last week's riot.
The death toll from the riot could rise, with up to seven people reported missing.
Of the injured, 132 were civilians and 12 were members of the People's Armed Police.
Authorities issued circulars warning of severe punishment for the rioters and aimed to combat separatism.

The Commonwealth Bank of Australia's (CBA) home loan portfolio has shown solid growth.
CBA's profit outlook has improved slightly due to this growth.
CBA is expected to report a profit rise of about one percent for the six months to December 31.
CBA has warned since early 1996 that margin pressure would lead to flat profits for the year to June 30.
Some analysts believe CBA has been more optimistic in recent months.
Analysts forecast a net profit before abnormals for CBA of between A$535 million and A$560 million for the six months.
CBA's home loan portfolio grew 10.3 percent to A$28.8 billion in the year to November.
Home lending growth by all banks rose 7.5 percent during the same period.
CBA's share of home lending by banks increased to 22.3 percent from 21.7 percent over the year.
Analysts expect CBA's bad debts and provisioning to remain stable and not negatively impact profits.

The federal government is expected to release the Wallis Inquiry's report into Australia's financial system later this week.
The Wallis Inquiry was set up in June last year and is chaired by businessman Stan Wallis.
The Inquiry released a 415-page discussion paper in late November that canvassed various options for reform.
The Inquiry's report was presented to the government last month.
The report will make recommendations about mergers, foreign investment, ownership of banks, prudential regulation, and deposit insurance.
The report will address whether the government should abandon the current 'Six Pillars' policy that stops mergers between the four major banks and two major life insurance and superannuation groups.
The six pillars include Westpac Banking Corp, National Australia Bank Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, and Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) Society.
The report will consider whether the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) and the Treasurer should continue to have the power to reject or approve a bank merger.
The report will evaluate whether the current ban on foreign takeovers of the big four banks should be scrapped.
The report will assess whether to combine the functions of the four regulatory bodies into a single body for prudential regulation and consumer protection.

The Seven Network Ltd is expected to report a 25-30 percent higher pre-abnormal annual net profit on Monday.
Analysts believe the profit rise may disguise a second half profit slowdown.
A Sydney analyst stated that second half sales growth is likely to be modest due to competition from the Ten Network and Nine Network.
The Seven Network had the Australian TV rights to the Atlanta Olympic Games.
The median forecast for Seven's pre-abnormals net profit for the year to June 30 is A$114 million.
Forecasts for Seven's net profit range from A$105 million to A$120.7 million.
The A$114 million forecast compares with A$88.5 million posted in 1994/95.
The 1994/95 figure was negatively impacted by a bungle over discounted advertising rates costing Seven A$20-30 million.
Seven managing director Gary Rice expected a better second half in 1995/96 than the second half of 1994/95.
Seven expects advertising sales in 1995/96 to be six to seven percent higher for the year.

Mercury Finance Co. announced it is suspending payment of a previously announced dividend.
The company is attempting to secure short-term financing as it accumulates debt.
Mercury Finance Co. has been unable to refinance $61 million in commercial paper that matured.
An additional $127 million in debt is due between Thursday and February 14.
The company has been in violation of certain loan covenants since last week.
Mercury Finance Co. was unable to pay $17 million in commercial debt.
The company announced accounting irregularities that resulted in an overstatement of earnings by about $90 million.
The accounting misstatements were linked to unauthorized entries by former controller James Doyle.
Doyle's lawyer has accused Mercury Finance Co. of a 'charade' and stated that Doyle is cooperating with federal authorities.
FBI agents served a search warrant seeking financial records from Mercury Finance Co.

U.S. retailers are expected to post sales gains in the single digits for March.
Sales at low-end discount stores are contributing to the expected sales gains.
Department store performance was nearly flat compared with a year ago.
Michael Niemira is an analyst at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd.
Niemira expects comparable-store sales to be up about 5 percent or slightly less.
An early Easter could depress sales at stores that were closed on the holiday.
Winter storms in much of the northern part of the nation may have held sales back.
William Armstrong is an analyst at Fahnestock & Co. Inc.
Armstrong expects overall retail sales for March to increase by 2 percent to 4 percent.
J.C. Penney Co. Inc. reported a 3.7 percent decline in comparable-store sales in March.

Retailers in the nation are expected to post modest sales gains for February.
Analysts predict a rise of about 4 percent in same-store sales for February.
Warm weather had a mixed impact on retail sales results.
Sales of apparel increased due to warm weather in the Northeast.
Sales in some hardline areas were depressed by warm weather.
Carson Pirie Scott & Co. reported an 8.2 percent rise in same-store sales for February.
Michael Niemira, an analyst at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, suggested that Carson's strong sales might indicate positive trends for smaller retailers.
Sears, Roebuck and Co. is expected to have sales gains of about 2 percent to 4 percent.
Merrill Lynch analysts noted that Sears' sales were affected by its automotive business and weak performance in hard lines.
J.C. Penney Co. is expected to exceed the average with same-store sales gains of about 9 percent.

Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. has extended its review of an Indonesian gold mining project until June 30.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. announced the extension on Wednesday.
Freeport is a partner in the Busang project in Indonesia.
Freeport requested the extension to consider the findings of the Strathcona audit.
Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. is expected to deliver a report on Busang to Bre-X on Thursday or Friday.
Bre-X plans to issue a press release on the report before North American financial markets open on Monday.
Freeport-McMoRan's preliminary tests found 'insignificant' amounts of gold at Busang on March 26.
Bre-X estimates that Busang contains about 71 million ounces of gold.
Panic selling of Bre-X shares resulted in a loss of almost C$3 billion from the company's market value last month.
Bre-X shares fell 32 cents Canadian to C$3.48 in heavy trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

Canadians are experiencing a winter of dismay related to ice hockey.
Ice hockey in Canada is facing issues such as sex scandals, fraud trials, and a decline in team performance.
This year marks the 25th anniversary of Canada's victory in the 1972 Summit Series against the Soviet Union.
Paul Henderson scored the winning goal in the final game of the 1972 Summit Series.
There are concerns that Canada is losing its grip on ice hockey.
The current season began with Canada losing to the United States in the final of the inaugural World Cup of Hockey.
Computer-enhanced pucks and NHL expansion into U.S. markets are causing concern among hockey purists.
A sex scandal involving young boys has emerged at Maple Leaf Gardens, home of the Toronto Maple Leafs.
Two employees of Maple Leaf Gardens have been charged in connection with a pedophile ring involving up to 60 victims.
Graham James, a junior hockey coach, pleaded guilty to sexually assaulting two players in the 1980s.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is based in Calgary, Alberta.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. reported a gold discovery at the Busang deposit in Indonesia.
Doubts about the Busang deposit and the death of chief geologist Michael de Guzman led to a decline in Bre-X's stock.
Shares of Bre-X were halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange after a report indicated the Busang deposit was smaller than previously estimated.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. is a partner in the Busang project.
Freeport stated that its due diligence on the Busang site was not complete.
Bre-X shares fell to a 52-week low of C$14.25 during trading.
Bre-X closed down C$2.25 at C$15.20 on 9 million shares traded.
Michael de Guzman, the chief geologist of Bre-X, died after falling from a helicopter in Indonesia.
Analysts expect rumors about the Busang deposit to continue until Freeport completes its review.

Chrysler Corp. has developed a new method to extract hydrogen from gasoline.
This method could reduce the timeline for introducing super-efficient electric cars powered by fuel cells by 10 years.
Fuel cells generate electricity through a chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen, using a platinum catalyst.
Chrysler's fuel cell system can extract hydrogen from normal gasoline.
The system is expected to provide a 50 percent increase in fuel efficiency over conventional internal combustion engines.
Francois Castaing, Chrysler's vice president of vehicle engineering, stated that hydrogen needs to be processed from gasoline on-board vehicles.
Castaing noted that hydrogen is not a practical fuel choice today due to a lack of filling stations.
The proposed system would allow drivers to refuel at normal gasoline stations, although the car would have a smaller tank.
The on-board refinery system is expected to cost about $30,000, which is 10 times more than a conventional internal combustion engine.
Chrysler aims to have a working test vehicle within three years and estimates that fuel cells could become commercially viable by 2010 to 2015.

U.S. sales of General Motors Corp. cars and trucks in November dropped nearly 12 percent from a year ago.
Total U.S. vehicle sales for General Motors in November fell to 336,815 from 382,372 a year earlier.
GM car sales decreased by 22.5 percent to 179,150 units.
Total truck sales rose 4.2 percent to 157,665 units despite strike-related production losses.
Walkouts by the United Auto Workers and Canadian Auto Workers unions reduced the availability of several GM vehicle models.
Sales of key high-volume models that GM is replacing were down significantly due to model changeovers.
Lincoln Merrihew, an auto analyst with DRI/McGraw-Hill, stated that GM's car market share is expected to struggle for about six months.
Production of the Chevrolet Corsica and Beretta compact cars was recently ended, resulting in a sales drop of 89 percent to 1,494 units.
Chevrolet, GM's largest division, had November sales of 169,110, a drop of more than 13 percent from 194,973.
