For the first 11 months of 1996, GM dealers sold 4,447,147 total vehicles, down 1.7 percent from the same period of 1995.

The United Auto Workers union has chosen Ford Motor Co. to lead labor contract negotiations with the Big Three U.S. automakers for the second consecutive time.
UAW vice president Ernest Lofton notified Ford executives of the decision on Tuesday.
The union is not viewing Ford as a traditional 'strike target' in the negotiations.
Ford is the lead company in resolving the UAW's 1996 negotiations.
The selection of Ford will allow it to negotiate an agreement that will serve as a pattern for General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp.
Contracts covering nearly 400,000 U.S. hourly workers at Ford, General Motors, and Chrysler expire on September 14.
Ford faces the threat of a national strike if it fails to reach an agreement before the contract expiration.
Ford spokesman Jon Harmon stated that the company is negotiating with the UAW at both the subcommittee level and the main table.
Ford employs about 104,000 UAW members and negotiated the current pact in 1993.
The UAW's top priorities in the 1996 negotiations include improved job security and restrictions on shifting work to lower-cost suppliers.

UK defence to industrial giant GEC Plc announced potential job cuts of up to 1,000 at its two newly-acquired businesses.
The job losses will primarily affect AG Power Transmission and Distribution and Hazeltine Corp of the U.S.
The expected cost of the job cuts is 45 million stg of a total 160 million charge.
An additional 50 million of the total charge relates to asset write-downs at two other units.
Finance director David Newlands did not disclose the names of the two companies with reduced asset values.
Newlands stated that the asset write-downs were necessary for the disposal of those companies.
Newlands mentioned that the first sale of companies marked for disposal is expected to occur before Christmas.
The remaining portion of the 160 million charge relates to restructuring within the remaining firms.
Newlands indicated that George Simpson, the successor to former managing director Lord Weinstock, began his role in September.
GEC reported a decline in half-year profits to 261 million stg from 402 million stg after accounting for the 160 million charge.

Wickes Plc is a British do-it-yourself retailer.
Wickes Plc's former bosses are being investigated for fraud.
Wickes Plc warned it faced receivership unless investors supported its financial restructuring.
The financial restructuring includes a 53 million pound rights issue.
Accounting irregularities dating back five years were discovered at Wickes Plc.
Wickes Plc announced a major refinancing plan that includes a cash call and possible sale of its continental business.
Wickes chairman Michael von Brentano stated that a vote against the plans could lead to receivership.
The refinancing plan includes a capital reduction of 100 million pounds and new banking facilities of 52 million pounds.
Wickes Plc expects to make a loss before tax in 1996 of not more than 56 million pounds.
Wickes Plc will not pay an interim dividend in 1996 or 1997, but may pay a final dividend in 1997.

Talks between the British and U.S. governments on an open skies pact were postponed for two weeks due to the illness of a senior British negotiator.
The talks were scheduled to begin in Washington with representatives from both governments and main transatlantic carriers.
A spokesman for the British government confirmed that the lead official is in hospital and the meeting has been cancelled.
The European Commission began a separate series of private hearings in Brussels regarding the proposed British Airways and American Airlines alliance.
The British Airways and American Airlines alliance is conditional on the open skies pact being finalized.
British and U.S. carriers expressed regret over the delay of the Anglo-U.S. talks.
Sources indicated that the postponed talks were not expected to result in a final deal.
Scott Yohe, senior vice-president of government affairs at Delta Air Lines Inc, stated that full agreement was not possible in the current round of talks.
The British government wants to link the open skies talks with the BA/AA alliance, while the U.S. prefers to keep them as separate issues.
Britain is awaiting a final verdict from the Office of Fair Trading regarding the BA/AA alliance, particularly concerning the divestment of 168 landing slots at Heathrow airport.

MCI Communications Corp. reported flat quarterly earnings despite a rise in revenues.
MCI earned $295 million, or 42 cents a share, in the first quarter.
MCI's earnings were unchanged from a year ago and in line with analysts' consensus estimates.
Revenues grew 8.7 percent to $4.9 billion from $4.1 billion.
Gerald Taylor, chief executive of MCI, stated that the company demonstrates strong overall revenue growth and profits.
MCI and British Telecom announced a merger valued at $23 billion.
The merger is expected to create the world's second-largest telecommunications group.
The deal is subject to regulatory approval and is expected to close in the fall.
Long-distance revenues rose 8.2 percent to $4.4 billion from $4.1 billion.
MCI expects revenue and traffic growth rates to slow in coming quarters.

International Business Machines Corp. announced a 2-for-1 stock split.
The stock split was approved by IBM's board and is subject to shareholder approval for an increase in authorized shares.
The stock split will double the number of shares traded and halve the stock's price.
Industry analysts believe the stock split provides only a temporary boost unless IBM can demonstrate growth in its core computer business.
Nomura Securities analyst Daniel Ries stated that IBM's management must show sustained growth for the stock to recover.
IBM's stock price rose by $5 to $150.75 following the announcement of the split.
IBM's stock is included in the Dow Jones industrial average and is widely held by individual and institutional investors.
The stock split may reduce the psychological focus on IBM's previous record high of $175 set in 1987.
Soundview Financial analyst Gary Helmig described the stock split as not significant, stating it primarily increases daily share volume.
Analysts noted that the split may make IBM shares more affordable for smaller investors.

WavePhore Inc unveiled a service that broadcasts data to home personal computers via television signals.
The service is called WaveTop and allows users to bypass bottlenecks in the Internet.
WaveTop will broadcast entertainment and information programming nationwide through TV signals.
The service aims to avoid clogged phone lines and overstrained computer networks that slow Internet connections.
Sandy Goldman is the vice president of WavePhore's consumer unit.
Initially, WaveTop will carry stereo broadcasts of a music radio station, real-time news, educational programs for children, and new software to home PCs.
WaveTop will begin U.S. operations in September.
WaveTop will be the first wireless data broadcast medium delivering audio, video, software, and real-time data to home PCs.
The system will be free to consumers who own a broadcast-ready personal computer equipped with a TV tuner.
WavePhore has a pact with the Public Broadcasting Service's 250 local stations to broadcast via an unused portion of their signals.

Nomura Securities Co Ltd is Japan's largest brokerage firm.
Industry sources and analysts believe Nomura will recover from the current scandal.
An executive at a foreign securities house stated that it is unlikely Nomura will fail as it has the strongest distribution network in Japan.
The crackdown on Nomura is seen as part of Japan's efforts to create free, fair, and global markets.
The executive noted that other local brokers lack the capability to take over Nomura's market share.
Japanese prosecutors raided Nomura as part of an investigation into payments linked to 'Sokaiya' racketeers.
Nomura directors are being investigated for making illegal payments to a company associated with a racketeer.
The payments were allegedly made to prevent disruption during a Nomura annual meeting.
Payoffs to racketeers violate Japan's commercial code and are subject to legal penalties.
Nomura's share of trading volume at the Tokyo Stock Exchange has decreased from 14.3 percent to 6.4 percent.

Nomura Securities Co Ltd stated it could post parent current profits for the current business year despite expected penalties.
Analysts indicated that Nomura's results for 1997/98 would depend on the actions of the Ministry of Finance (MOF) after an investigation.
Japanese prosecutors and the Securities and Exchange Council (SESC) are investigating Nomura's suspected illegal stock deals.
The investigation is linked to a 'sokaiya' racketeer who extorts money from companies.
The SESC is expected to recommend punitive action against Nomura to the MOF.
Analysts noted that Nomura's ability to post a profit this year depends on the timing and duration of any punitive suspension of operations.
Ayako Sato, an analyst at UBS Securities Ltd, stated that if the investigation concludes in May and punishment ends before September, Nomura could avoid severe consequences.
Another unnamed analyst suggested that a prolonged punitive suspension could hinder Nomura's ability to post a profit.
Market sources indicated that authorities might suspend Nomura's underwriting operations and stock dealing for up to three months as a penalty.
Takamichi Arata, a Nomura director, claimed that the company could still post profits due to expenditure cutbacks, even if business is suspended.

The president and 15 board members at Nomura Securities Co Ltd resigned on Tuesday.
The resignations were in response to a racketeering scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Masashi Suzuki was appointed president of Nomura just a month before the resignations.
The scandal has negatively impacted the reputation of Japan's biggest securities firm.
Prosecutors and the securities watchdog are investigating potential payments made by Nomura to a racketeer known as 'sokaiya'.
Junichi Ujiie, a managing director at Nomura, aims to establish a more open management system.
Ujiie stated that there was an atmosphere discouraging free discussion among executives at Nomura.
Nomura has previously been involved in scandals, including a 1991 incident where it was punished for favoring certain clients.
Hideo Sakamaki, who resigned as president last month, testified that Nomura paid over 70 million yen to a racketeer.
The Ministry of Finance is likely to suspend some of Nomura's operations for about three months as punishment for the scandal.

Wenzhou is a city in China known for its capitalist practices within a socialist framework.
Residents of Wenzhou believe that mourning Deng Xiaoping should involve making more money.
Wu Hao, an advertising company manager, stated that Deng Xiaoping was crucial for modern China and Wenzhou.
Deng Xiaoping died at the age of 92 on a Wednesday.
Deng Xiaoping's policies shifted China away from Marxist practices that had caused starvation and industrial collapse.
Wenzhou has experienced significant economic growth since Deng's reforms began in 1979.
Wenzhou's private firms contribute 75 percent of the city's annual industrial output.
The national average for private firm contribution to industrial output in China is 10 percent.
Zhou Ping, a shoe factory owner, credited Deng Xiaoping for the city's economic success.
A young businessman in Wenzhou prioritized making money over mourning Deng Xiaoping.

China approved four more foreign banks to handle local currency business on Thursday.
The four new banks are Standard Chartered Bank, Sanwa Bank, Daiichi Kangyo Bank, and Shanghai-Paris International Bank.
Shanghai-Paris International Bank is a joint venture between Banque National de Paris and the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China.
The approved banks can take deposits and make loans in yuan only after moving operations to the Pudong district of Shanghai.
Chinese authorities aim to make the Pudong development zone the country's premier financial district.
Foreign banks are only allowed to conduct local currency business from offices in Pudong.
Foreign bankers believe the approval of banks is driven by a desire to boost property prices in Pudong.
The first four banks approved for local currency business were Citibank, Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp, Industrial Bank of Japan, and Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd.
Approved banks can only accept yuan deposits from foreign-funded firms, foreign individuals, or Chinese enterprises that have received loans from the banks.
Lance Browne, Standard Chartered's chief executive for China, stated that the approval is a positive development for their business in China.

China's securities authorities are attempting to ban domestic investors from the foreign currency B share market.
Brokers believe that the ban has little chance of success.
Chinese brokerages in Shanghai and Shenzhen have started re-registering investor accounts to identify domestic investors trading B shares.
B shares are theoretically reserved for foreign investors only.
Stock analysts suggest that the process of removing local investors from B shares may lead to a compromise with the securities authorities.
Many investors are seeking a trustee to continue trading B shares.
Domestic investors with B share accounts must find a foreigner or someone with residence rights outside China to certify their trading.
In Shanghai, it is reported that obtaining a trading certificate may be relatively easy, while Shenzhen is enforcing stricter regulations.
Those who obtain the trading certificate can retain their accounts and continue trading B shares legally.
Domestic investors have accounted for at least half of B-share trading in recent months.

Barrick Gold Corp dropped out of the race to control the Busang gold find in Indonesia.
Freeport-McMoran Copper and Gold Inc won the right to mine the Busang deposit.
Analysts warned that the struggle for control of Busang may not be over.
Placer Dome Inc expressed hope of acquiring a stake in Busang.
Fred Ketchen, vice-president of ScotiaMcLeod, stated that the situation is far from over.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd announced a deal with Freeport regarding the Busang gold find.
Under the deal, Freeport will own 15 percent of the Busang find, Bre-X will keep 45 percent, and Indonesian interests will take 40 percent.
Barrick Gold Corp decided to give up its quest for Busang after the deal was announced.
Vince Borg, a spokesman for Barrick, stated that going beyond their proposal would not be in the best interest of shareholders.
Bre-X shares opened at C$25 and fell to C$23.50 by midafternoon on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

Fears of a U.S. interest rate hike affected Canadian financial markets this week.
Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen did not indicate whether he might raise Canada's rates in response to U.S. actions.
Thiessen stated that there will always be an impact on Canada from international changes in interest rates.
Thiessen mentioned that Canada has more room to maneuver regarding interest rates than before.
Investor concerns arose that the Federal Reserve would hike U.S. interest rates next Tuesday.
The Bank of Canada is expected to hold rates steady while the U.S. may increase rates.
Warren Jestin, chief economist for Bank of Nova Scotia, stated that inflation is under control and there is no reason for rates to rise.
Economists predicted that the Bank of Canada might eventually tighten monetary conditions if the Canadian dollar continues to weaken.
The Bank of Canada dropped short-term interest rates 11 times last year, compared to one U.S. rate cut.
Statistics Canada reported that Canada's core consumer price index for February rose 1.5 percent on the year.

Canada aims for consensus among Asia-Pacific trade ministers in Montreal to target environmental products and services for trade liberalisation.
Canadian Trade Minister Art Eggleton expressed a particular favor for environmental goods and services and technologies.
The meeting is part of a three-day session of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
Analysts indicate that Eggleton faces pressure to achieve concrete outcomes from the APEC trade ministers' meeting.
The meeting is intended to set the agenda for an APEC summit in Vancouver, British Columbia, in November.
Senior Canadian trade officials believe Canada can easily gather support for environmental technologies.
Last year, the 18 APEC members initiated a global agreement on liberalising the information technology market.
Karen Minden, director of the APEC Studies Foundation for Canada, stated that APEC must capture leaders' attention to be effective.
Canada is the chair for APEC this year and aims to demonstrate productivity at the upcoming summit.
Critics argue that previous summits have focused on rhetoric rather than concrete free trade measures.

Czech power utility CEZ a.s. reported lower first half profits.
The decline in profits was attributed to a prolonged battle over price agreements with regional distributors.
CEZ's net profit according to international accounting standards decreased to 5.95 billion crowns from 6.26 billion crowns in the previous year.
The firm's net profit calculated according to Czech accounting standards fell to 5.1 billion crowns from 5.57 billion crowns year-on-year.
CEZ is the largest firm in the Czech Republic in terms of revenues.
CEZ and six out of the eight regional power distributors have been in disputes over long-term supply agreements.
CEZ charged 1,020 crowns per megawatthour in the first quarter and 1,033 crowns in the previous year as deposit payments.
Distributors owed CEZ almost two billion crowns at the end of the first half.
CEZ's operating revenues according to international standards rose to 28.51 billion crowns from 26.09 billion crowns.
CEZ plans to pay its first-ever dividend of 3.3 percent of the 1,000 crown nominal value of its shares.

Ceska Sporitelna a.s. is the largest Czech savings bank.
In 1996, Ceska Sporitelna a.s. reported an audited net profit of 1.89 billion crowns ($65 million), up from 263 million crowns in 1995.
The profit figures were based on Czech accounting standards.
Jaroslav Klapal is the general director of Ceska Sporitelna a.s.
Klapal indicated that the profit result allows for a higher dividend than the previous year's five crowns per share.
Kamil Ziegler is the deputy CEO of Ceska Sporitelna a.s.
Ziegler stated that results under international accounting standards would be released in mid-April.
Ziegler estimated that the profit under international standards would be similar, possibly lower by 100 million crowns.
The bank's balance sheet decreased to 359 billion crowns at the end of 1996 from 368 billion crowns in 1995.
Ceska Sporitelna a.s. reduced its interbank market exposure to 28.4 percent of total assets in 1996 from 40 percent in 1995.

The lower house of the Czech parliament approved a post-World War Two reconciliation agreement with Germany.
The approval followed four days of debate and was carried by 131 votes to 59.
Germany's parliament had previously approved the declaration in January by a large majority.
The Czech debate included opposition from ultra-right Republican and Communist deputies.
Opposition deputies viewed the pact as a sellout to Bonn and attempted to obstruct the final vote.
The Czech government views the approval of the declaration as necessary for NATO and EU membership.
The agreement expresses Germany's regrets for the Nazi occupation of the Czech lands and Prague's sorrow for the expulsion of 2.5 million ethnic Germans.
The bilateral agreement establishes a fund for general victim compensation programs but does not address restitution to expropriated ethnic Germans.
The parliamentary preamble references speeches by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec, asserting that post-war property restitution questions are closed.
The largest opposition party, the Social Democrats (CSSD), requested that references to Klaus and Zieleniec's speeches be included in the preamble.

China's President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng visited Deng Xiaoping for the Chinese New Year.
The visit was reported by state media on Wednesday.
The report did not comment on Deng Xiaoping's health.
Deng Xiaoping is 92 years old.
Deng Xiaoping's reforms transformed China into an economic powerhouse.
Deng Xiaoping has not been seen in public since the 1994 Chinese lunar new year festival.
Deng Xiaoping is believed to be in fragile health and has fading lucidity.
Deng Xiaoping lives in a guarded compound in Beijing.
Jiang Zemin and other leaders also visited other veteran leaders from the 1980s and early 1990s.
Speculation about Deng Xiaoping's health includes rumors of hospitalization and reports of little change in his condition.

China issued new media directives on Sunday.
Journalists are ordered not to advocate sex, violence, and superstition.
Reports should be filled with patriotism and socialism.
The guidelines are part of a crackdown on ideas that conflict with party principles.
The All China Journalists' Association issued a communique to reporters.
The association established a hotline for the public to report rule-breaking journalists.
The directives are reminiscent of the Cultural Revolution's political campaigns.
The China News Workers' Association issued a six-part directive via Xinhua.
Reporters are urged to serve the people and expose corruption.
The directive specifies acceptable topics and tones for news coverage.

China bank deposits grew last year, but at a slower rate than in 1995 due to two interest rate cuts.
State media reported that bank deposits would remain the top choice for private investors due to a lack of other opportunities.
Investment funds have failed to attract investors and exist on a small scale.
Investment funds could become a target for private funds in 1997, according to the China Daily Business Weekly.
Investment in housing and insurance could become alternatives for small investors in 1997.
Small investors experienced losses in the stock markets and corporate bonds and failed to buy state debt due to competition.
Stamps, coins, antiques, and art would continue to be important for families with savings.
New bank deposits in China from January to November totaled 820.19 billion yuan, an increase of 12 percent year-on-year.
Total private savings in China's banks amounted to 3,791.73 billion yuan at the end of November.
A sharp cut in retail inflation to about 6.0 percent encouraged individuals to deposit money in banks.

The International Air Transport Association (IATA) is concerned that landing fees at Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok (CLK) airport could be the highest in the world.
IATA's director general Pierre Jeanniot expressed hope that fee increases over those at the existing Kai Tak airport would be reasonable.
Jeanniot stated that the increases should consider the economic impact on both airlines and Hong Kong.
Jeanniot spoke after a speech at the Hong Kong International Aerospace Forum, which included representatives from the Airport Authority.
Hong Kong IATA representative Gilbert Chow reported that new research indicated fees at CLK could be up to four times higher than at Kai Tak.
If confirmed, landing fees for a Boeing 747 at CLK could be around US$12,000.
The research was based on revenue forecasts and expected flight numbers at CLK, derived from the business plan provided to IATA by the Airport Authority.
The Airport Authority has stated that charges for landing and aircraft parking will not be announced until next year after consultations with airlines.
IATA's director of corporate communications, William Gaillard, stated that a quadrupling of fees would be unreasonable and could cause significant damage.
Hong Kong's Civil Aviation Department reported that current landing fees for a Boeing 747 are about US$3,000.

The International Air Transport Association (IATA) supports plans for a single air traffic control centre for all airports in the Pearl River delta region in southern China.
IATA director general Pierre Jeanniot spoke at the Hong Kong International Aerospace Forum.
All three existing air traffic service providers in Hong Kong, China, and Macau accepted the concept of a unified air traffic control centre after a meeting in Guangzhou.
Jeanniot stated that all airlines would benefit from unified air traffic control through lower costs, faster transit times for overflights, and reduced pilot workload.
Jeanniot could not provide a timescale for the introduction of the unified air traffic control centre.
Jeanniot did not specify the location of the overall centre or its cost.
Jeanniot expressed concerns that three air traffic control centres could be inefficient and potentially dangerous.
Jeanniot emphasized the importance of coordinating local capacity at busy crossroads.
There is agreement that air traffic control should be integrated in the Pearl River delta region.
Air traffic is continuously increasing in the Pearl River delta region, with major airports in Guangzhou and Shenzhen, and new airports in Zhuhai and Macau.

Lamar Durrett is the president and chief executive officer of Air Canada.
Lamar Durrett has expressed frustration at being denied permission by the Canadian government for daily flights from Vancouver and Toronto to Hong Kong.
Air Canada began its Hong Kong to Vancouver link in December but is limited to four flights per week.
Air Canada wants to compete with Cathay Pacific Airways Limited from Toronto.
Cathay Pacific Airways Limited currently operates 21 flights per week on the Hong Kong-Canada non-stop route.
Canadian Airlines International has nine non-stop flights a week from Hong Kong to Vancouver.
Durrett stated that the Canadian government has refused to reconsider the bilateral agreement for daily services to Hong Kong.
Durrett mentioned that Air Canada is making no progress in breaking the impasse despite ongoing lobbying efforts.
Durrett indicated that the minister of transport, the cabinet, and the prime minister are aware of Air Canada's desires.
Air Canada currently uses Boeing 747 Combi aircraft on the Hong Kong route and will not increase passenger capacity with a Boeing 747-400.

London Electricity is a British regional electricity company.
London Electricity reported a dip in half-year profits on Thursday.
The company's pretax profits for the six months to September 30 were 69.3 million pounds.
This profit figure is down from 84.5 million pounds a year ago.
The decline in profits was affected by a pricing review that took effect earlier this year.
London Electricity increased its interim dividend to 14.3 pence per share.
The previous interim dividend was 11.5 pence per share.
An analyst noted that the dividend increase was better than expected and boosted shares.
Shares of London Electricity rose by 15 pence to 655 pence by 1315 GMT.
Chairman Sir Bob Reid stated that the priority remains the distribution network.

Northern Electric is a British regional electricity company.
CE Electric is a U.S. company that made a bid of 650 pence per share for Northern Electric.
Northern Electric announced a 17 percent expected rise in its year dividend to 50 pence per share.
Northern Electric plans to merge its supply business with another regional electricity company to achieve cost savings of over 28 million pounds.
Nigel Hawkins is a utilities analyst at Yamaichi.
Northern Electric spent 560 million pounds on shareholder benefits to fend off a previous bid from Trafalgar House.
David Morris is the chairman of Northern Electric.
CE Electric raised its bid from 630 pence per share and set a deadline of December 20 for the bid decision.
Northern Electric indicated a price of 700 pence per share before CE Electric's bid.
Northern Electric is in talks with a possible partner in its Sovereign upstream gas business.

Northern Electric Plc attempted to remain independent by appealing the extension of an offer by CE Electric.
CE Electric's offer gives it a majority of shares in Northern Electric Plc.
Britain's takeover panel was meeting to consider Northern's application to appeal the decision to extend the bid.
The panel extended the deadline on CE Electric's 782 million pound bid from December 20 to December 24.
The panel's extension was a reaction to BZW's failure to disclose a 250,000 pound fee related to its performance in the bid.
CE Electric controlled 49.77 percent of Northern Electric Plc before the deadline extension.
After the deadline extension, CE Electric increased its control to 50.13 percent.
Acceptances after the initial deadline require consent from the Takeover Panel.
Northern Electric Plc is appealing the extension to nullify late acceptances and retain independence.
Dealing in Northern Electric's shares was temporarily suspended pending the appeal process.

Barclays Plc shares fell on Tuesday after the bank reported 1996 pretax profits at the lower end of expectations.
Barclays shares were down 55-1/2 pence at 1144p in afternoon trade.
The shares hit a low of 1131p following the profit report.
Barclays reported a 13 percent increase in pretax profits to 2.36 billion pounds, including a 70 million pounds gain on disposals.
Analysts downgraded Barclays stock after meeting with the company.
SBC Warburg analysts cut the stock rating to 'hold' from 'buy'.
There was a 29 percent fall in operating profits at BZW to 204 million pounds.
Barclays announced it would return 500 million pounds to shareholders in the next twelve months.
Barclays raised its dividend by 21 percent to 31.5 pence.
Barclays chief executive Martin Taylor defended the results and stated that UK banking figures were strong.

Britain's Woolwich Building Society will float on the stock exchange this summer.
Woolwich Building Society reported a pretax profit of 392 million pounds in 1996, an 18 percent increase.
Woolwich chief executive John Stewart aims for growth in all company businesses after becoming a listed company.
Net mortgage lending for Woolwich increased by 50 percent to 1.4 billion pounds.
Woolwich's administrative expenses rose by less than one percent.
Woolwich's cost-to-income ratio decreased from 48.9 percent to 45.8 percent.
John Stewart stated that the draft building societies legislation could impact Woolwich's acquisition strategy.
The current form of the legislation would remove a building society's five-year immunity from takeover if it acquires another financial sector company.
Woolwich is Britain's third largest building society and will be quoted in the FTSE 100 index after flotation.
Woolwich aims to increase its business in unit trusts, life and general insurance, core mortgage business, and personal loans.

HSBC Holdings Plc, based in London, reported a 23 percent increase in profits for 1996.
Chief Executive John Bond predicted a challenging year ahead due to increasing competition.
Bond stated that HSBC has a strong capital position and a solid balance sheet.
HSBC announced a pretax profit of 4.52 billion pounds ($7.3 billion) for 1996.
The reported profit was around the middle of market expectations.
Bond indicated that HSBC's British unit, Midland Bank, would continue to grow organically.
Midland Bank reported a pretax profit increase of more than 20 percent.
HSBC's capital ratios were described as strong by Bond.
HSBC had a return on capital of 21.3 percent in 1996, up from 20.7 percent in 1995.
Bond expressed confidence in Hong Kong's transition from British to Chinese rule and mentioned HSBC's license to trade in the Chinese yuan.

Congressional approval to expand NATO to former communist Europe is not assured.
Top aspirants must prove they can pay their way for NATO expansion.
Joseph Biden is the ranking Democrat on the Senate foreign relations committee.
Biden stated that expansion is not a 'done deal'.
Biden is concerned about growing neo-isolationism in the United States.
Biden listed Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, and Slovenia as top candidates for NATO expansion.
Biden believes questions about the readiness of applicants to pay have not been addressed in Poland or the Czech Republic.
NATO is expected to invite countries to join at a July summit in Madrid.
Achieving the two-thirds vote required in the Senate to approve the NATO charter change may be difficult.
The Clinton administration estimated the cost for expanding NATO eastward to be between $27 billion and $35 billion up to the year 2009.

Czech politicians are facing skepticism regarding NATO membership.
Opinion polls indicate that Czechs are less supportive of NATO compared to Hungarians and Poles.
Less than 40 percent of Czech citizens support NATO membership.
Czech Senate Chairman Petr Pithart stated that many view NATO as merely military maneuvers.
Pithart believes there is a lack of respect for the Czech army affecting views on NATO.
Pithart thinks skepticism towards the army contributes to the lower support for NATO compared to Poland and Hungary.
Czech Republic, Poland, and Hungary are expected to be invited to join NATO at a July summit.
NATO membership is a primary foreign policy goal for the Czech government.
Disdain for the Czech army developed after World War Two and during 40 years of communism.
Pithart and current Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus oppose a referendum on NATO membership.

Czech National Bank (CNB) Governor Josef Tosovsky stated that he sees no sense in the recent sharp rise of the crown.
Tosovsky mentioned that a marked reduction in money supply growth has created good conditions for lowering inflation and interest rates.
The central bank will remain cautious, and lowering the M2 growth rate is the main goal according to Tosovsky.
The crown has surged since the New Year despite a worsening trade balance.
An unprecedented 24 billion crowns ($862 million) in new Eurobonds have been issued in the currency.
Tosovsky expressed that he does not see any rational reason for the strengthening of the crown in recent days.
The central bank is comfortable with the crown's rise, which has climbed to nearly five percent above parity with its mark/dollar basket.
The CNB widened the band for fixing the crown to 7.5 percent either side of the midpoint of the basket almost a year ago.
Tosovsky stated that a strong crown is the long-term policy of the central bank.
The crown slipped on Thursday morning due to Tosovsky's comments but recovered to 27.770 crowns to the dollar and 16.925 to the mark.

British Gas Plc is preparing to split into two companies.
British Gas Plc reported a decline in half-year profits.
The historic cost net profit for the first half was 565 million pounds.
The historic cost net profit decreased from 635 million pounds the previous year.
Pretax profit fell to 926 million pounds from 1.003 billion pounds.
British Gas Plc reported a net loss of 8.0 million pounds in the second quarter.
The interim payout to shareholders remained unchanged at 6.40 pence.
British Gas is in discussions with the industry regulator Ofgas regarding price controls.
Prolonged cold weather contributed an additional 218 million pounds to operating profits.
The company's industrial and commercial division experienced losses of 180 million pounds.

British Biotech Plc's finance director James Noble resigned unexpectedly.
Chief executive Keith McCullagh stated that the transition is smooth and the management team is strong.
McCullagh reported that major shareholders are confident about the company's situation.
Analysts were surprised by Noble's resignation as the company prepares to launch its first products.
McCullagh indicated that Noble had been considering his future for some time before his resignation.
McCullagh described Noble's departure as amicable and praised his contributions to the company.
Noble raised over 300 million stg for the company's development and managed shareholder relations.
Noble has not accepted another position but is considering various opportunities.
McCullagh mentioned that Noble may prefer working in start-up operations rather than large international businesses.
The company plans to hire a new finance director with strong international operating experience.

Shares in Cortecs International Plc could rise by more than 60 percent if upcoming news on one of its leading drugs is positive.
Cortecs president Michael Flynn expects to announce the interim result of a key European Phase III trial on Macritonin at the end of next week or early the following week.
Flynn stated that positive results will be used as pivotal data for the first applications for registration in Europe.
Cortecs has developed a tablet form of calcitonin, which increases bone retention of calcium and slows the loss of bone mass.
Analysts believe oral calcitonin will have advantages over the existing injected form and the nasal spray version marketed by Novartis AG.
The market for existing drugs related to osteoporosis is around $800 million a year and is expected to grow as the population in the developed world ages.
Nomura analyst Nick Woolf issued a strong buy note on Cortecs and stated that shares could rise to 420 pence if trial data is positive.
Woolf indicated that shares could almost double if the news is good and emphasized the importance of the trial results.
Shares in Cortecs were trading at 256-1/2 pence, below their March 21 high of 291 pence and their April 1996 peak of 450 pence.
Yamaichi International analyst Erling Refsum values Cortecs' portfolio of drugs at around 1.5 billion stg compared to its current market capitalization of just over 300 million stg.

A trade fair for personal security gadgets took place in Colombia on Wednesday.
The entry fee for the Expo Seguridad fair was $285.
Colombia has the highest kidnap rate in the world.
Three guerrilla forces in Colombia specialize in extortion and attacks on multinationals.
Drug gangs in Colombia are heavily armed.
Industrialists, government officials, defense experts, and wealthy individuals attended the fair in Bogota.
William Silva is a salesman with A1A Security, a Colombian firm based in Miami.
Silva offered a $600 wristwatch that functions as a camera.
The price for fitting a Range Rover with armor plating was around $150,000.
Colombia is a leading market for sales of armor-plated vehicles in Latin America.

Colombian public sector workers began a nationwide strike on Tuesday.
The strike disrupted air traffic, transportation, telecommunications, and other services.
Union leaders stated that this could be the country's biggest labour dispute in 20 years.
About 800,000 public sector workers were expected to join the protest action.
The government warned that leftist guerrilla groups were planning attacks to coincide with the strike.
There were no immediate reports of violence or serious acts of vandalism, except for a bus being torched outside Ibague.
National radio reported that services appeared to be functioning at or close to normal, despite serious public transport shortages.
Traffic flow in Bogota was light, resembling a quiet Sunday afternoon.
All state-run universities and schools were closed, and long lines of people were seen stranded at bus stops in working-class districts.
The strike was called to press for a 21.5 percent wage hike, while the government offered a weighted 13.5 percent increase.

Thousands of people fled violence and are camped out in the jungles of northwest Colombia.
A Red Cross aid worker reported that these people may soon run out of food.
The risk of epidemics is rising among the displaced population.
More than 3,000 people, mostly women and children, are sleeping under shelters or in the open air near Mutata.
Many displaced individuals are concerned about 1,500 relatives believed to be fleeing along jungle tracks.
The fighting involves leftist guerrillas, right-wing paramilitaries, and the army in the Rio Salaqui basin of Choco province.
Adalberto Arrieta from the Red Cross stated that food is being rationed due to a lack of supplies.
Multiple cases of diarrhoea and fever have been reported among the refugees.
The British government is sending $80,000 in emergency aid to Uraba, including food and tents.
Colombian officials admitted they were ill-prepared to handle the situation.

Pearson Plc chief executive Marjorie Scardino sold its 10 percent stake in Hong Kong broadcaster TVB for 111.1 million pounds.
The stake in TVB was bought by Shaw Brothers (Hong Kong) Ltd and associates.
This sale is the first major strategic move by Marjorie Scardino since she took over at Pearson last month.
Scardino stated that the investment in TVB was no longer effective for developing Pearson's television business or other interests in the region.
Pearson acquired the stake in TVB two years ago for 106.2 million pounds and received dividends of 3.5 million pounds on it.
Share analysts expressed approval of Scardino's early move to improve the focus of the business.
Analysts noted that Pearson had recovered its investment in TVB.
Greg Dyke, head of Pearson's television arm, was reportedly affected by the sale, and speculation arose about his future with the company.
Moody's downgraded Pearson's debt rating, citing weakened debt protection measurements due to recent acquisitions.
Scardino has promised to improve Pearson's profit performance despite the company facing challenges with its major assets.

PolyGram reported an 18 percent fall in earnings.
PolyGram's 1996 net income after tax dropped to 608 million guilders from 741 million guilders in 1995.
PolyGram held its dividend at 0.95 guilders per share.
PolyGram's results topped market forecasts.
PolyGram shares surged 4.80 guilders to 88.10 on the Amsterdam stock exchange.
PolyGram took a post-tax charge of 114 million guilders to reorganise its music operations.
PolyGram cut approximately 400 jobs as part of its reorganization.
Global music sales rose to $40 billion in 1995 from $14 billion in 1986.
The rate of growth in global music sales slowed to an estimated three percent last year.
PolyGram is restructuring its Motown unit and moving its headquarters from Los Angeles to New York.

BSkyB is a British pay television operator.
BSkyB plans to launch a 200-channel digital satellite service.
BSkyB is the dominant force in British pay TV.
BSkyB confirmed it will launch digital satellite service later this year.
BSkyB's plan is not affected by its digital terrestrial television alliance with Carlton Communications and Granada Group.
BSkyB, Carlton Communications, and Granada Group formed British Digital Broadcasting.
British Digital Broadcasting is applying for licenses to run DTT networks in Britain.
BSkyB's pre-tax profit rose 26 percent to 133.7 million pounds in the six months to end-December.
BSkyB reported record subscriber growth of 434,000 in the last three months of last year.
BSkyB has over six million customers in Britain and Ireland.

Chronimed Inc has halted shipments of generic blood glucose test strips.
The halt could reduce Chronimed's fiscal third-quarter earnings by up to $0.06 per share if shipments do not resume.
Norman Cocke is the chief financial officer of Chronimed.
Chronimed's shares fell by 2-7/8 to 12-1/8.
Analysts estimate Chronimed's earnings for the quarter ending in late March to be $0.14 per share.
Chronimed earned $0.11 per share in the three-month period ended March 29, 1996.
Quik Check strips are manufactured by Diagnostic Solutions Inc, based in Irvine, California.
Quik Check strips are designed for use with the OneTouch blood glucose monitor manufactured by Johnson & Johnson.
Chronimed is the exclusive distributor of Quik Check strips.
Shipments were voluntarily halted after the FDA raised questions about the consistency of test results.

Humana Inc. reported lower quarterly profits due to charges for restructuring.
The stock of Humana rose on optimism over its new president's turnaround plan.
Humana is the fifth largest health maintenance organization in the United States among for-profit HMOs.
Humana posted fourth-quarter net income of $22 million, or 13 cents a share, down from $49 million, or 30 cents a share, in the previous year.
Quarterly premium revenues for Humana were $1.81 billion, up from $1.49 billion in the year-ago period.
For the full year, Humana's net income decreased by 94 percent to $12 million, or 7 cents a share, from $190 million, or $1.17 a share.
Humana reported revenues of $6.7 billion, up from $4.6 billion in 1995.
Humana's stock rose 37.5 cents to $18.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Gregory Wolf became president of Humana in September and is implementing a plan to cut costs and withdraw from unprofitable markets.
Humana took a special charge against earnings of $10 million related to severance costs for eliminating 700 to 900 jobs.

Biogen Inc expects to begin European marketing of Avonex within the next 30 days.
James Tobin is the President and Chief Operating Officer of Biogen Inc.
Biogen expects European sales of Avonex to eventually match U.S. sales.
Avonex sales in 1996 totaled $76.5 million.
Biogen's total sales in 1996 were $277 million, an increase from $151.7 million in 1995.
Biogen launched U.S. sales of Avonex in May 1996.
Avonex has significantly increased Biogen's revenue stream.
Avonex reduces the frequency and severity of multiple sclerosis flares.
Avonex competes with Schering AG's Betaseron and Teva Pharmaceuticals Industries Ltd's Copaxone.
Biogen plans to expand revenues by selling more Avonex and obtaining approvals for additional uses.

Telstra Corp reported a 38.4-percent fall in net profit for the 1996/97 first half.
The decline in profit was attributed to the costs of shedding almost a third of its workforce.
Telstra is to be partially privatised by the end of the year.
Telstra is in talks with global telecom carriers about forming possible alliances.
Telstra reported a net profit after abnormals of A$742.0 million in the six months to December 31, 1996.
This net profit is a decrease from A$1.20 billion a year ago.
Redundancy costs were A$1.03 billion in the half-year period.
Staff levels decreased by 7,000 to about 69,500 during the half.
Telstra's plan announced last September includes cutting about 22,000 jobs by the end of fiscal 1998/99.
Revenue grew by 4.6 percent to A$7.77 billion in the December half.

Qantas Airways Ltd reported a 2.4 percent rise in net profit for the 1996/97 first half.
Qantas warned that its Japan routes were unlikely to repeat the profitability of the early 1990s.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc.
Qantas reported a net profit of A$151.6 million for the six months ended December 31.
The net profit result was towards the higher end of market expectations, which ranged from A$116 million to A$154 million.
Qantas aimed to at least match the A$246.2 million net profit recorded in 1995/96 for the year to June 30.
Qantas stated that revenues were not expected to grow quickly and fuel prices were forecast to remain high.
Qantas chairman Gary Pemberton attributed the growth in first half profit to the airline's cost-cutting program.
Qantas made cost savings of A$237 million in the half year and expected full year cost savings to exceed A$430 million.
Revenue from Japan fell about 30 percent to A$315 million in the first half.

Boral Ltd shares topped the turnover charts on Friday.
Investors increased their investment in the building material sector due to a change in sentiment for the housing sector.
Boral shares rose by 13.6 cents or 3.71 percent to close at A$3.806.
The turnover for Boral shares was 8.8 million shares.
Boral shares reached an intra-day high of A$3.91, the highest level since March 1994.
Pioneer International Ltd shares closed at their highest level since the 1987 sharemarket crash, up 14.4 cents or 3.55 percent at A$4.20.
CSR Ltd shares ended 14 cents or three percent higher at A$4.81, the highest level since August 1994.
Chris Haynes, a building materials analyst at BT Securities, stated that there is positive sentiment around the stocks.
Australian housing finance data expected next Thursday may show evidence of an industry upturn after a two-year depression.
Boral and Pioneer reported lower profits for the six months to December 31, 1996.

Orange Plc is Britain's youngest mobile telephone company.
Orange Plc reported a pretax loss of 229.1 million pounds in its first full year since flotation.
The pretax loss increased from 140.5 million pounds in 1995.
Turnover for Orange Plc rose 171 percent to 619 million pounds, including acquisitions.
Analysts do not expect Orange Plc to become profitable at the operating level before 1998.
Orange Plc has a market share of 11.5 percent despite entering the market late.
The customer base of Orange Plc has exceeded 850,000.
Managing director Hans Snook stated that the company plans to reach 96 percent of the British population by the end of the year.
Orange Plc was floated last March at 205 pence per share.
The stock price of Orange Plc traded at 218 pence on Tuesday, a rise of four pence on that day.

Cable and Wireless Plc (C&W) is Britain's second biggest telecommunications group.
Analysts believe a bid by C&W for Sprint Corp may be possible but is not feasible in the short term.
C&W declined to comment on a report about a possible $15 billion bid for 80 percent of Sprint.
Analysts have suggested an alliance called Global One between Sprint, Deutsche Telekom AG, and France Telecom as a potential partner for C&W.
Some analysts consider the report about C&W's interest in Sprint to be premature.
Oliver Ehrenberg, a telecommunications analyst at Robert Fleming Securities, stated that a bid by C&W is not feasible due to its ongoing cable merger.
Ehrenberg noted that 80 percent of Sprint could cost around $16 billion with a usual bid premium of 30 percent.
C&W has a market capitalization of only $18 billion.
Ehrenberg mentioned that C&W's gearing levels would be about 90 percent after the merger, making the deal financially unfeasible.
C&W has stated it regularly communicates with Sprint, Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom, and AT&T Corp.

B.A.T Industries Plc announced that its U.S. subsidiary will pay $1.7 billion as part of a downpayment on a deal involving the tobacco industry, legislators, and public health authorities.
B.A.T expressed that it might withdraw support for the deal if significant changes occur during the legislative process.
B.A.T's Brown & Williamson unit is the third largest cigarette maker in the U.S. and produces brands such as Kent and Lucky Strike.
B.A.T's shares closed at 566.5p, down 22.5p.
Most analysts view the deal as broadly positive and some predict that B.A.T's shares could rise to 670p.
The agreement includes tougher regulations on tobacco products and advertising in exchange for immunity from large legal claims.
Individual legal claims can still be made under significant restrictions, including no claims for punitive damages.
Tobacco companies have acknowledged that tobacco is addictive, and funds from the levy will be allocated for treating smoking-related illnesses.
Mark Duffy, a tobacco analyst at SBC Warburg, stated that the settlement was tougher than initially expected by the market.
The deal requires approval from the U.S. Congress and has been agreed upon with U.S. state attorneys, plaintiff's lawyers, and public health representatives.

Gilbert Amelio is the Chairman of Apple Computer.
Amelio announced the suspension of Apple's executive cash bonus plan until the company returns to profitability.
Amelio stated that his highest priority is to make Apple profitable as soon as possible.
When Amelio took over Apple Computer Inc. one year ago, the company faced five crises.
Amelio described Apple as being financially broke with tight liquidity.
Apple announced a restructuring a day before Amelio's comments.
Apple reported a $120 million loss in the first quarter of fiscal 1997.
Apple officials expect to begin making profits again by the end of the 1997 fiscal year in September.
Apple's executives received substantial bonuses last year when the company reported an unexpected fourth-quarter profit.
Amelio received a $648,000 bonus in addition to his $990,000 base salary.

Apple Computer Inc. plans to release an operating system that will work on personal computers based on Intel Corp. chips and on Apple computers.
Apple will release programming tools that allow companies to write software for Apple computers and convert it to run on PCs with Intel chips and Microsoft Corp.'s Windows software.
Apple's strategy aims to prevent software companies from abandoning Apple products.
Apple Chairman Gilbert Amelio stated that the new development environment offers promise for those seeking business on both Mac and Windows platforms.
Apple has previously released operating system software that runs only on Apple-designed hardware.
Apple's next-generation operating system is code-named Rhapsody and will run on both Apple-designed computers and PCs based on Intel chips.
Richard Zwetchkenbaum, an analyst at International Data Corp., commented that entering the PC market provides Apple an opportunity to showcase its technology.
Apple has been working on improvements to the Macintosh to differentiate it from PCs for the past two years.
Apple previously relied on the ease-of-use of its computers as a selling point until the release of Windows 95 diminished its impact.
Apple plans to spend the week convincing programmers to invest in writing software for Rhapsody.

Apple Computer Inc. announced plans to consolidate its independent marketing and development units into fewer groups.
The consolidation aims to cut costs and focus on selling computers in key markets.
Steve Wozniak will rejoin Apple as a part-time advisor to Chairman Gilbert Amelio.
Wozniak is one of the co-founders of Apple and invented the company's first computer 20 years ago.
Apple is based in Cupertino, California.
The company is examining all aspects of its business and will decide on job cuts by the end of the month.
Apple is considering dropping some product lines, including the Newton handheld computer, to reduce expenses by 20 percent by the end of the year.
Guerrino De Luca, the new head of Apple's global marketing, stated that simplicity makes the reorganization appropriate for Apple.
Apple executives indicated that specific details about job cuts and financial impacts will be provided at the end of the month.
George Scalise, head of Apple's operations, noted that the organization allows Apple to focus on markets and leverage strengths built over the past six to eight months.

Eaton's department store chain is under bankruptcy protection.
Eaton's has placed 31 of its 85 stores under review.
Eaton's has a supplier debt of C$150 million (US$110 million).
T. Eaton Co. Ltd. is Canada's fifth largest retail chain.
Eaton's has annual sales of C$1.67 billion (US$1.22 billion).
Eaton's plans to renegotiate leases for the stores under review.
Eaton's filed a restructuring plan on February 27.
Eaton's is expected to close some stores under review due to mounting losses.
Eaton's owes C$160 million (US$118 million) to Bank of Nova Scotia and Toronto-Dominion Bank.
U.S. vulture brokerages have purchased up to C$40 million (US$29 million) of Eaton's supplier debt.

Toronto stocks ended mixed in active trading on Tuesday.
A rally in heavyweight bank stocks was offset by profit-taking in other groups.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 5.26 points to close at 6247.78.
The trading volume was 105.75 million shares worth C$1.67 billion ($1.23 billion).
Declining issues outpaced advances 525 to 463, with 307 stocks unchanged.
Ira Katzin, investment advisor at RBC Dominion Securities, stated that all activity was centered in the bank sector fueled by solid earnings.
The financial services group, which accounts for 17.55 percent of the 300 index, jumped almost 2.1 percent after two big Canadian banks reported strong first-quarter earnings.
Bank of Montreal and Bank of Nova Scotia reported sharply higher first quarter profits.
Bank of Montreal gained 1.10 to 49.50 on 899,000 shares, while Bank of Nova Scotia jumped 1.25 to 52.90 on 1.1 million shares.
Sherritt International ended up 1.00 at 59.00 on 7.9 million shares after reaching a 52-week high of 60.

Toronto stocks reached a record close on Wednesday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 10.64 points to close at 6248.86.
This was the 10th record close of 1997.
The index set a new intra-day high of 6260.73 points.
Trading volume was 128.5 million shares worth C$1.97 billion ($1.44 billion).
Dunnery Best, director of private client investment at Midland Walwyn, attributed gains to gold stocks.
The gold sector increased by over one percent.
The base metal sector rose nearly two percent.
Advancing issues outnumbered declining issues 561 to 448, with 282 stocks unchanged.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. rose 0.70 to close at 21.50 after announcing an agreement on the Busang gold discovery.

China's role as a world trading partner is attributed to reformist leader Deng Xiaoping.
Diplomats and analysts stated that fully opening China's food markets remains a challenge.
U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright visited Beijing to promote China's integration into the international market.
China's agricultural trade is perceived by trading partners, particularly Washington, as having political barriers.
Quarantine issues are significant in Sino-U.S. trade, particularly regarding restrictions on grain imports.
U.S. grain officials reported that Chinese restrictions related to TCK smut fungus could result in a loss of up to $500 million in annual wheat sales for the U.S.
A high-ranking U.S. diplomatic source indicated that progress was being made in talks regarding agricultural trade issues.
The source noted that the challenge lies in opening the state-controlled grain trade.
A senior representative of a major U.S. grain trading house expressed skepticism about short-term changes in China's import markets.
Chinese authorities are beginning to acknowledge the necessity of grain imports while aiming to meet 85 to 90 percent of their own grain needs.

Chinese zinc producers are expected to export due to high international prices.
High exports may lead to a domestic supply squeeze and increased prices in China.
London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc prices have risen by around $50 a tonne since the start of 1997.
LME zinc prices reached the highest levels in nearly two years.
Three month LME zinc was priced at $1,137/39 a tonne in early trade in London on Monday.
The market was consolidating after a peak price of $1,157 last week.
Torch Metal in Hong Kong has exported 30,000 tonnes of Chinese zinc this year.
Torch Metal has an additional 50,000 tonnes of zinc to sell in 1997.
A major Chinese smelter sold between 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes of zinc in late December at 9,800 yuan ($1,180) a tonne FOB.
The five percent zinc export tax was eliminated on January 1, 1997.

China set a budget deficit target of 57 billion yuan ($6.87 billion) for 1997.
The 1997 budget deficit target is less than one percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Hoong Yik-Luen is the head of China research at ING-Barings.
Hoong Yik-Luen stated that a budget deficit around one percent of GDP is healthy for a developing country.
Finance Minister Liu Zhongli announced a 7.2 percent cut in the budget deficit from 61.442 billion yuan in 1996.
The 1996 budget deficit was 10.8 percent below target.
China issued a total of 196.742 billion yuan in debt last year, which was 1.485 billion yuan above the targeted figure.
The 1997 target for domestic and overseas debt is 248.596 billion yuan ($29.95 billion), an increase of 27.3 percent from 1996.
An analyst in Shanghai noted that government authorities are realizing there is a lot of money domestically.
The popularity of bonds is attributed to the lack of investment alternatives.

Western oil joint ventures in Russia are facing challenges due to high taxes and uncertain policies from a new energy minister.
An independent U.S. energy consultant in Moscow stated that there is a lack of good investment vehicles for joint ventures.
Zarko Stefanovski, an oil analyst at T. Hoare & Co brokerage in London, estimated net revenue for joint ventures at about $4.40 per barrel of oil produced and exported from Russia.
Current costs per barrel include $2.70 for operations, $2.75 for transport, $2.00 in excise duty, $0.65 in pipeline tax, $1.30 in mineral royalties, and $0.35 in road and housing taxes.
Russia imposes a 35 percent profits tax based on revenue, not profit.
A Western oil man expressed concerns about constantly changing taxes affecting budget adjustments and company morale.
Approximately 40 Western ventures produce and export Russian oil, totaling about 250,000 barrels per day.
Russia's total oil production is approximately 6.2 million barrels per day.
A Western energy consultant in Moscow noted that while the export tax is eliminated, other taxes have compensated for it.
Joint ventures were initially seen as a simpler way to access Russia's oil resources, which may hold five percent of the world's proven reserves.

LUKoil is one of the world's largest oil companies.
LUKoil plans to move its upstream business from Siberia to the Caspian and Gulf regions.
The decision is influenced by the challenging economics of oil production in Russia.
LUKoil's strategy highlights issues such as expensive reserves, low domestic demand, and a struggling economy in Russia.
LUKoil spokesman Pyotr Neyev stated that the company is not interested in increasing oil output in Russia due to pipeline capacity limits, small export terminals, and low domestic demand.
LUKoil is preparing for a shareholders' meeting where it will discuss net cash profits of 3.87 trillion roubles ($673 million).
LUKoil intends to invest in projects in Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and Iraq.
LUKoil aims to produce at least one quarter of its oil outside Russia by the beginning of the next millennium.
LUKoil has a 52.5 percent stake in a $4 billion production-sharing project in Iraq's Western Qurnah.
LUKoil has significant stakes in various projects in Azerbaijan and is exploring opportunities in Algeria.

Russia's energy sector will have fewer domestic players due to mergers and acquisitions among newly-privatised oil companies.
Producers are looking to improve production and refining margins by consolidating downstream and upstream operations.
Analysts believe that a shakeout of the sector's vertically-integrated companies and independent firms is inevitable after 1998.
Stephen O'Sullivan, director of oil and gas at MC Securities in London, stated that not all oil companies can survive.
Moscow has transformed old Soviet production associations into vertically-integrated companies, resulting in imbalances between production and refining.
Russia has a refining overcapacity of 6.8 million barrels per day, exceeding the current output of around 5.8 million barrels per day.
Dan Lubash, managing director of Emerging Markets Europe at Merrill Lynch in London, noted that margins in a transitioning market move quickly.
LUKoil announced plans to acquire Norsi-Oil, an independent refiner, seeking a major equity stake in the plant.
Analysts reported that producers are frustrated with lower profits from refineries where they conduct tolling operations.
SIDANCO and Sibneft are competing for Rosneft, the state oil holding firm, which is slated for privatisation.

The French government is considering whether to privatise defence electronics group Thomson-CSF through a public sale or private placement.
The method of sale will significantly influence the restructuring of the French defence industry.
The decision has major implications for the entire defence sector in Europe.
Government sources indicated that the decision, initially expected at the end of January, will likely be delayed until early February.
The government is examining all aspects of the politically-sensitive dossier related to Thomson-CSF.
An official source stated that the decision will be made shortly but not on the current day.
The cabinet will make the final decision, and there is currently no proposal ready for ministers.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe aims to avoid embarrassment similar to the suspension of a previous privatisation plan involving Lagardere Groupe.
The earlier plan included the privatisation of Thomson-CSF and Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
The French government has decided to separate the sales of TMM and Thomson-CSF.

French conglomerate Generale des Eaux is in talks with Havas about Canal Plus.
Generale des Eaux and Havas issued a joint statement confirming discussions about audiovisual activities.
The announcement was made before the stock exchange opened.
Press reports indicated that Generale des Eaux would become the key shareholder in Havas.
This would make Havas the biggest shareholder in Canal Plus.
Generale des Eaux and Havas will not comment further until board meetings on February 6.
A corporate source confirmed that Alcatel Alsthom is in talks to sell part of its 21.2 percent stake in Havas to Generale des Eaux.
Generale des Eaux owns almost 20 percent of Canal Plus.
Canal Plus is merging with Nethold to create Europe's largest subscription television company.
Other major shareholders in Canal Plus include Societe Generale with 4.5 percent and Caisse des Depots et Consignations with 6.9 percent.

French food group Saint Louis acquired a 15 percent stake in Ebro Agricolas.
Ebro Agricolas is Spain's biggest sugar company and second-largest food group.
Saint Louis shares rose two percent to 1,355 francs after the acquisition.
The acquisition was welcomed by analysts.
Saint Louis's Generale Sucriere unit purchased the stake from Banco Santander.
The deal was reported to be for 17.14 billion pesetas, equivalent to $129.4 million.
Ebro Agricolas has a market value of 110 billion pesetas and annual sales of 154 billion pesetas.
Ebro Agricolas holds a market share of 54 percent in the sugar sector.
Saint Louis already owns about 21 percent of Sociedad General de Azucarera de Espana.
Ebro Agricolas acquired a 21.8 percent stake in Azucarera from Banco Central Hispano in November.

A new diamond mine project in north Australia is likely to proceed.
Aberfoyle Ltd has a minority interest in the Merlin project alongside Ashton Mining Ltd.
The final feasibility study for the Merlin project is described as encouraging.
Aberfoyle managing director Mike Eager stated that both companies expect the project to be developed, though not initially at a large scale.
The feasibility study is nearly complete and has been discussed by the two companies.
The report from the feasibility study is due before Ashton's board on June 19.
A final decision on the project is expected by the end of the September quarter.
Ashton owns 77.5 percent of the Merlin project, while Aberfoyle owns the remaining percentage.
The feasibility study assumes an initial mining capacity of 500,000 tonnes of ore per year.
Ashton reported that diamonds recovered from Merlin were 35 percent gem quality.

Woodside Petroleum Ltd announced it would increase exploration spending in 1997.
The company aims to diversify away from the North West Shelf gas fields.
Woodside reported a 58 percent increase in annual net earnings to A$191 million for 1996.
Woodside's shares rose to A$8.97 on Wednesday, an increase of 31 cents from Tuesday's close.
Woodside plans to more than double exploration spending in 1997 to A$120 million.
Over half of the exploration spending will focus on the Timor Sea.
Woodside plans to drill 12 to 14 exploration wells, with eight or nine outside the North West Shelf.
North West Shelf's proven gas reserves increased by 60 percent to 24.4 trillion cubic feet at the end of 1996.
Oil reserves rose by 11 percent to 175 million barrels, and condensate reserves increased by 21 percent to 690 million barrels.
The partners in the North West Shelf plan to double annual LNG production to 14 million tonnes by 2003 at a capital cost of A$6 billion.

Colonial Ltd is an Australian financial services group.
Colonial Ltd made its debut on the Australian share market on Monday.
Colonial shares opened at A$3.31.
The opening price of A$3.31 was above the A$3.10 paid by institutional investors.
The public share offer for Colonial closed last Friday.
Members of the public paid A$2.60 for shares in the A$690 million float.
In late morning trade, Colonial shares were trading around the opening price.
Colonial Ltd had a market capitalisation of A$1.9 billion.
Colonial Ltd is now among the top 50 Australian companies.
Peter Smedley is the managing director of Colonial Ltd.

Egghead Inc. will close 77 of its 156 stores to focus on profitable locations and its Internet business.
Egghead sold its corporate sales unit in April 1996, which generated half of its revenue.
Egghead will take a $30 million charge against earnings in the current fiscal fourth quarter for restructuring.
Terry Strom, Kurt Conklin, and Ron Smith will leave Egghead, and George Orban will replace Strom as CEO.
Strom will continue to work as a consultant for Egghead.
Egghead lost $10.7 million in fiscal 1996 on sales of $403.8 million.
Egghead lost another $7.6 million in the first three quarters of fiscal 1997.
The reorganization is expected to reduce Egghead's losses in fiscal 1998 by cutting almost $20 million from annual operating expenses.
Egghead's stock fell from nearly $14 last June to close at $5.375 in Nasdaq trading.
Egghead began in 1984 as a single shop in suburban Seattle and once had more than 200 stores.

Boeing Co. plans to enter the airline maintenance business within the next several months.
Larry Clarkson is the president of Boeing Enterprises, a division of Boeing's commercial airplane group.
Clarkson stated that Boeing is negotiating with several potential partners for the maintenance business.
Boeing may begin by forming a joint venture to provide maintenance for airlines using outside contractors.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Boeing is considering taking over heavy-maintenance operations of several major carriers, including British Airways Plc.
Clarkson indicated that taking over the total maintenance of a major airline would take time and is complicated.
A spokeswoman for British Airways declined to comment on Boeing's plans.
Industry analysts believe Boeing's move into maintenance would diversify its business beyond airplane manufacturing and weapons systems.
Bill Whitlow of Pacific Crest Securities commented that entering the maintenance business could be beneficial if it does not conflict with customers.
Boeing had $4.4 billion in cash at the end of last year and is expected to generate at least $1.5 billion in excess cash annually after acquiring McDonnell Douglas Corp.

Microsoft Corp. stock increased by 10 percent to a record close of $107.625 on Nasdaq.
The increase followed an 85 percent rise in quarterly earnings reported by Microsoft.
Microsoft's earnings exceeded Wall Street estimates by 23 percent.
Nearly 29 million shares of Microsoft changed hands on the day of the stock surge.
Scott McAdams, an analyst at Ragen MacKenzie, described the quarter as the best he has ever seen.
Microsoft executives warned that they could not maintain the current growth pace.
Analysts predict that Microsoft's growth will slow over the next five quarters.
Analysts noted that Microsoft's strong earnings reflect strength in the personal computer industry.
Rob Enderle, a senior analyst with Giga Information Group, stated that strong returns from Microsoft and Intel indicate an ongoing upswing.
Drew Brosseau of Cowen & Co. reported that only 20 percent of large organizations had transitioned to 32-bit operating systems by the end of 1996.

A Sino-French group has submitted a proposal to build a cocoa processing factory in Ivory Coast.
The factory is intended to supply Chinese chocolate manufacturers.
Philippe Mian is a cabinet technical advisor to Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan.
The Ivorian government will study the proposal this week to clarify its position on financial support.
Managers from Touton S.A. and Shanghai Collin met with Prime Minister Duncan to discuss the investment.
The proposed investment for the new factory is 12 billion CFA.
A new company called Societe Ivoirienne de Cacao (SICAO) would be established if the proposal is approved.
Ivory Coast aims to process 50 percent of its annual cocoa production locally by the year 2000.
CEPICI reported that the initial investment proposed for the project is eight billion CFA, increasing to 12 billion CFA over two years.
Plant construction could begin as early as September.

Chad faced cereal shortages in 1997.
Chad appealed for aid from foreign donors to replenish 50,000 tonnes of emergency cereal stocks.
The appeal was made by President Idriss Deby.
Chad acknowledged a shoot-to-kill policy against some criminals in 1996.
Human rights groups reported that petty grain pilferers were executed for stealing small amounts from public markets.
Donors accused Chad's officials of exacerbating food shortages.
Chad typically maintains 25,000 tonnes as an emergency buffer stock and another 25,000 tonnes for immediate emergency use.
Joseph Alain Charriere, the U.N. World Food Programme's representative in Chad, stated that stocks had been emptied for political reasons.
Chadian officials claimed urgent action was needed as women struggled to set aside private stocks during regular droughts.
The Director of Food Security, Ali Adoum Djourou, reported a cereal deficit of just under 200,000 tonnes for the 1996/97 period.

Central African leaders welcomed President Mobutu Sese Seko's decision not to seek reelection.
The decision is seen as a potential pathway for a peaceful end to Zaire's civil war.
Mobutu and the presidents of Gabon, Chad, Congo, Central African Republic, and Equatorial Guinea urged the transitional parliament to fill the vacant post of speaker.
The speaker is Mobutu's constitutional successor in the event of his death or incapacity.
A statement issued after a summit in Libreville noted Mobutu's health problems as the reason for not standing for reelection.
The statement indicated new prospects for a negotiated political settlement of the conflict.
The heads of state invited Zaire's political forces to proceed with the election of a president to ensure normal functioning of institutions.
Mobutu, who has prostate cancer, met with fellow leaders during a morning session.
Laurent Kabila and his rebels control three quarters of Zaire and demand Zairean nationality for ethnic Tutsis.
U.S. special envoy Bill Richardson stated that a fresh summit is crucial for a peaceful transfer of power.

Jose Martinez is the legal defender of Dosal Tobacco Co.
Martinez works at the Miami law firm Martinez, Gutierrez & DeCordoba.
Dosal Tobacco Co. is a small, family-owned company based in Opa-Locka, Florida.
Dosal Tobacco Co. produces a few million cigarettes a year.
Philip Morris Cos. Inc. is the largest cigarette maker in the world.
Philip Morris shipped nearly 231 billion cigarettes in the United States last year.
Dosal Tobacco Co. is named in three anti-tobacco lawsuits in Florida and one in Michigan.
Dosal's main customer is the Florida prison system.
Dosal makes a brand called Competidora, which is favored by elderly Cuban emigres in south Florida.
Martinez is serious about eliminating the legal threat to Dosal.

General Electric Co. Chief Executive Jack Welch defended his $28.2 million in salary, bonuses, and incentives for 1996.
Welch stated that market forces determined pay packages for top U.S. executives.
Stockholders at GE's annual meeting defeated a proposal to limit Welch's pay to $1 million unless put to a shareholder vote.
The proposal to limit Welch's pay received 9 percent of the votes cast.
Ninety-one percent of the votes cast supported Welch's existing compensation arrangements.
Bill Patterson of the AFL-CIO group stated that Welch's compensation was 148 times more than the average pay of GE's 239,000 employees.
The proposal to cap Welch's pay was made by a Teamsters union pension fund.
Patterson claimed that Welch's pay was a source of bitterness and cynicism for many GE workers.
Welch noted that stock options were now distributed to about 22,000 GE employees, compared to only 200 in 1988.
Welch received $6.3 million in salary, $15.1 million from a long-term incentive program, and $6.2 million from exercising options on GE stock in the previous year.

Leading cruise ship operators aim to export American culture abroad.
Cruise operators must tailor holidays to local markets and tastes.
Europe and Asia are identified as promising markets for Carnival Corp. and Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd.
The North American leisure cruise business has grown significantly over the past three decades.
Carnival Cruise Lines bookings increased by 37 percent in the last three months.
Carnival Cruise Lines shipboard berths rose by 13 percent during the same period.
Walt Disney Co. will launch cartoon-themed cruises next year aboard two new ships.
The cruise industry is currently experiencing a ship-building spree.
Carnival Destiny can carry 2,600 passengers, while Royal Caribbean is building ships for 3,100 passengers.
Most cruise customers are from the United States and Canada, and offerings are primarily American.

Washington's top textile trade negotiator is Rita Hayes.
Talks with China on a textile accord were likely to extend late into the night before a Friday deadline.
The talks aimed to renew the 1994 textile accord and resolve a dispute over U.S. penalties on Chinese exports.
Rita Hayes stated that significant cuts to China's textile quotas could occur if an agreement was not reached before the January 31 deadline.
The Sino-U.S. textile pact was scheduled to expire on December 31 but was extended by one month.
Washington and Beijing were seeking to ease tensions over Chinese exports of textiles via third countries.
The United States threatened multi-million dollar penalties over the textile export issue.
Rita Hayes expressed optimism about completing the talks but noted that both sides needed to work hard.
The United States imposed $19 million worth of penalties on Chinese textile imports last September.
China has threatened to retaliate by temporarily banning imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods, and alcoholic drinks.

Tsingtao Brewery is located in Shandong province, China.
Tsingtao Brewery became the first Chinese company to list on the Hong Kong stock exchange in 1993.
Analysts claim that Tsingtao Brewery is facing competition from foreign beer makers.
A Beijing-based beer industry analyst stated that Tsingtao has become complacent.
Tsingtao Brewery relies heavily on its brand-name prestige.
Tsingtao Brewery plans to increase production to 500,000 tonnes in the current year.
Tsingtao Brewery aims to raise annual output to 1.4 million tonnes by the year 2000.
Tsingtao was considered a luxury commodity under communist China's command economy.
Tsingtao Brewery's market share has decreased from 100 percent to approximately 70-80 percent.
Tsingtao Brewery was founded in 1903 and initially targeted German residents in Qingdao.

China claimed it restrained inflation while maintaining strong economic growth in 1996.
China predicted it will perform better in 1997 despite government-sector losses and slumping individual incomes.
The State Statistical Bureau reported that China's gross domestic product grew by an estimated 9.7 percent to 6.8 trillion yuan in 1996.
