Inflation in China fell to 6.0 percent in 1996 from 14.8 percent in the previous year.
Ye Zhen, a bureau spokesman, stated that China's economy had stabilized after a period of high inflation and rapid growth.
Ye Zhen described the national economy's performance as a successful 'soft landing.'
Preliminary estimates indicated that annual economic growth in 1997 was expected to rise to 10.5 percent.
Ye Zhen stated that inflation in 1997 would remain at the same level as in 1996.
China set a target of 8.0 percent growth for 1996, down from 10.2 percent in 1995 and 11.8 percent in 1994.
Jason Kwok, chief economist at Citibank Hong Kong and China, noted that price rises have been largely controlled.

Citizens Utilities Co. aims to be among the largest eight or ten U.S. telephone companies by the year 2000.
Citizens Utilities Co. plans to achieve this by acquiring companies in small local telephone markets across the country.
Ronald Spears is the vice president for Citizens' telecom business.
Citizens is currently the 15th-largest U.S. phone company.
Citizens is looking for new properties on both the western and eastern seaboards, particularly in the South and Southwest.
Citizens Utilities Co. is a major stakeholder in Centennial Cellular Corp.
Citizens owns Electric Lightwave Inc., which provides telecommunications services in five western cities.
Citizens is seeking regulatory changes in markets where it is the incumbent local phone company.
Citizens plans to file with New York state regulators to request price cap regulation for its 250,000 customers in upstate New York.
Citizens acquired its New York business from GTE Corp. in 1993.

Anne Bingaman has been named president of LCI International Inc.'s local telecommunications division.
Bingaman will also hold the title of corporate senior vice president.
Bingaman will have an operating role that includes relationships with local-exchange carriers and state utility commissions.
LCI International Inc. is based in McLean, Virginia.
Bingaman stated that LCI is an impressive group that matches her temperament.
Bingaman's appointment is notable for giving a former U.S. official a business operating role.
Bingaman expressed that she was attracted to the role because it allows her to be hands-on.
Bingaman believes her inexperience in business will not be a disadvantage due to her knowledge of the telephone business.
Bingaman headed the antitrust division of the Justice Department from 1993 to 1996.
LCI has received permission to offer local telephone service in 17 states and the District of Columbia.

Gail McGovern is the new executive vice president for the consumer and small business division at AT&T Corp.
McGovern's main challenge is to boost AT&T's share in the consumer long-distance market.
Analysts believe McGovern will bring a fresh approach to her role.
Richard Klugman of brokerage PaineWebber stated that McGovern's experience is primarily on the business side.
McGovern, aged 44, succeeded Joseph Nacchio, who left AT&T to join Qwest Communications Corp. as chief executive.
McGovern's top priority is to improve revenue growth and retain customers.
McGovern stated that reducing churn will be a top priority in 1997.
As the most senior woman employed by AT&T, McGovern is responsible for more than half of the company's revenues.
McGovern plans to apply service packaging strategies used in the business market to consumer customers.
AT&T's market share in the long-distance market has decreased from a near-monopoly in 1984 to around 55 percent today.

McDonald's Corp. plans to launch its biggest nationwide promotion featuring 55-cent sandwiches.
The price of a Big Mac is approximately $1.95.
McDonald's aims to attract customers amid intense competition in the fast-food industry.
McDonald's has more than 20,000 units worldwide and over 12,000 in the United States.
McDonald's declined to provide specifics on its promotion plan.
Spokesman Jack Daly stated the company hopes to launch a national value-price promotion.
Charles Gonzales, a McDonald's franchisee, indicated the promotion will feature a different sandwich for 55 cents each month with the purchase of french fries and a drink.
The promotion is expected to start with the Big Mac and will also include breakfast sandwiches.
Analysts suggested the promotion could lead to a price war in the fast-food market.
McDonald's stock fell by $2.625 to $44.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.

BAB Holdings Inc acquired Chesapeake Bagel Bakery for $29 million.
BAB Holdings Inc plans to buy more independent chains to expand its national presence.
Michael Evans is the president of BAB Holdings Inc.
BAB is currently focused on integrating Chesapeake Bagel Bakery.
BAB will operate stores under the Big Apple Bagels and Chesapeake names.
Bagels are becoming increasingly popular as a substitute for bread in the U.S.
BAB expects to have 800 units after five years, up from 285 units post-acquisition.
Analyst Ernest Andberg of R.J. Steichen & Co believes bagel restaurants have significant growth potential.
R.J. Steichen rates BAB's stock as a buy.
BAB makes its bagels from scratch on premise, which helps serve smaller markets.

Dayton Hudson Corp. announced that its Mervyn's division will exit Florida and Georgia.
Mervyn's will close 10 additional stores as part of its restructuring efforts.
The total number of outlets being reduced from Mervyn's chain is 35 out of 300 stores.
Pamela Rucker, a spokeswoman for the National Retail Federation, stated that the retail industry is over-saturated.
Susan Eich, a spokeswoman for Dayton Hudson, reported that Mervyn's stores in Florida and Georgia are modestly profitable but have below-average operating margins.
Eich noted that high fixed costs and limited market penetration influenced the decision to exit Florida and Georgia.
Mervyn's has 128 stores located in California.
Dayton Hudson operates a total of 1,101 stores, including 736 Target discount department stores.
The actions at Mervyn's will result in a pretax charge of $134 million for the fiscal fourth quarter.
Dayton Hudson expects to generate about $350 million in cash from real estate transactions to reduce debt and pursue growth opportunities.

China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) will send an advance party into Hong Kong next Monday.
The advance party will arrive more than two months before Beijing formally resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong.
Hong Kong announced an accord on the troop movement on Tuesday.
The accord ended months of deadlock over the size and role of a PLA advance guard.
The agreement allows for the arrival of 40 advance personnel of the future Garrison in Hong Kong from April 21.
The advance personnel will not be armed and will not enjoy any special legal status or privileges.
The PLA advance guard will have no defence or security role.
The PLA advance guard's work will not affect the British troops garrisoning Hong Kong until the handover on June 30.
The PLA advance guard will prepare facilities for the PLA garrison, which will take over defence duties from the British army's 'Black Watch' regiment on July 1.
The PLA garrison might eventually consist of up to 10,000 troops.

Moslem unrest in China's far-west region is not expected to lead to an ethnic breakup similar to the Soviet Union or Yugoslavia.
Experts believe more violence is possible in Xinjiang, and Beijing will respond accordingly.
Urumqi, the capital of Xinjiang province, experienced three bus bombings on Tuesday that killed at least four people.
The bus bombings were believed to have been carried out by Moslem separatists.
Xinjiang is populated by Moslem minority groups, including the Uighurs.
The bombings occurred on the same day as the funeral of China's leader Deng Xiaoping.
Two weeks prior to the bombings, at least 10 people were killed and hundreds of Moslems were arrested in riots in Yining, a border town in Xinjiang.
In response to the bombings, China's government ordered controls on explosives.
Barry Sautman, an expert on Chinese politics, stated that heightened police protection may not prevent bombings.
Most experts believe that Moslem separatism in Xinjiang does not pose a serious threat to China's territorial integrity.

Donald Tsang is the finance chief of Hong Kong.
Tsang presented the last budget under British rule on a Wednesday.
The budget was drafted with cooperation from Beijing.
The budget will cover the period straddling Britain's handover of Hong Kong to China on July 1.
Tsang stated that Hong Kong will remain financially independent of Beijing.
The Basic Law will serve as Hong Kong's constitution after the sovereignty change.
Beijing has stated it will not remove any taxes from Hong Kong.
The Basic Law ensures that Hong Kong will maintain independent finances and manage its own economic policy.
The budget for the year starting April 1 was crafted jointly with Beijing through the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group.
From July 1, the preparation of Hong Kong budgets will be solely the responsibility of Hong Kong.

The French government announced the procedure for privatising Thomson-CSF on Wednesday.
The announcement includes minimum financial terms and conditions for the sale.
This is the government's second attempt to sell Thomson-CSF after a failed attempt last year.
The successful bidder must acquire more than 50 percent of Thomson-CSF's capital and voting rights.
The government aims to select the winning bidder by June 30.
Bidders must have at least five billion francs in equity capital and the same amount in turnover in non-consumer and defence electronics.
The government will retain a 'golden share' to veto changes in ownership.
In a group bid, the lead company must hold more than a third of Thomson-CSF's capital and voting rights.
Bidders must declare their interest by 1100 GMT on March 28.
Offers must be submitted by 1100 GMT on May 7, and bidders must make an irrevocable offer within four months.

The French government is ready to relaunch the privatisation of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF.
The French government appointed key executives to oversee the sale of Thomson-CSF.
The industry and finance ministries issued a joint statement regarding the privatisation of Thomson-CSF.
An attempt to sell the whole Thomson electronics group last year was rejected by the independent Privatisation Commission.
The Privatisation Commission rejected the sale of parent company Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe for one franc.
Marcel Roulet has been made responsible for the sale of Thomson-CSF on a full-time basis.
Thierry Breton has been appointed as chairman of state-owned Thomson SA and Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
The government will inject 11 billion francs into TMM, pending approval from the European Commission.
TMM will be sold gradually through an opening up of its capital.
Thomson-CSF is 58 percent owned by Thomson SA and will be sold separately from TMM.

France will not allow Britain's General Electric Co Plc (GEC) to bid for the state's stake in Thomson-CSF for national security reasons.
GEC expressed regret over the rejection but indicated it was still pursuing options.
GEC is in discussions with two French groups, Lagardere Groupe and Alcatel Alsthom, which are allowed to bid.
The Finance Ministry received offers for the 58 percent stake from Lagardere and Alcatel, which is bidding with Dassault Industrie.
The French government has declared the proposals by Lagardere Groupe and Alcatel Alsthom and Dassault Industrie as admissible.
The proposal by GEC was not admitted because selling more than 50 percent of Thomson-CSF to a foreign company is against national security interests.
Industry Minister Franck Borotra stated that GEC could still participate in the Thomson-CSF privatization if it collaborates with a French bidder.
Analysts in London believe it was unlikely for GEC to win the tender against French companies.
GEC stated it aimed to combine with GEC-Marconi to create a leader in defense electronics and enhance European competitiveness against U.S. companies.
The French government has encouraged accepted candidates to outline their plans for industrial partnerships in their final offers for Thomson-CSF.

Conrail Inc. plans to proceed with a shareholder meeting on Friday.
Norfolk Southern Corp. is attempting to thwart Conrail's planned $9.2 billion merger with CSX Corp.
CSX Chairman John Snow described Norfolk Southern's efforts as a 'desperate act.'
Norfolk Southern suffered two defeats in its attempts to block the Conrail-CSX transaction.
A federal judge and a regulatory agency denied Norfolk Southern's attempt to block the merger.
Norfolk Southern's $10.3 billion bid for Conrail has been rejected.
Norfolk Southern announced it would buy 9.9 percent of Conrail stock if shareholders defeat a key measure.
Conrail is asking shareholders to waive a Pennsylvania law requiring CSX to pay for Conrail in cash.
The proposed Conrail-CSX transaction involves a mixture of cash and stock.
Votes on the shareholder measure are expected to be tallied by early next week.

Tyco International Ltd will not pursue a hostile takeover of American Standard Cos Inc.
American Standard rejected Tyco's unsolicited merger offer last month.
David Brownell is the Senior Vice President of Tyco International Ltd.
David Brownell stated that Tyco has historically not engaged in hostile takeovers.
Tyco is focusing on other initiatives after the rejection of the merger offer.
Tyco is open to friendly discussions with American Standard management.
Tyco has not attempted to contact American Standard since the merger offer was rejected.
American Standard disclosed that it received an offer from Tyco.
American Standard has decided to remain independent and will not hold discussions with Tyco.
Tyco offered $50 per share, totaling approximately $3.9 billion, for American Standard.

Chief executives of Conrail Inc., CSX Corp., and Norfolk Southern Corp. are expected to hold a meeting this week.
The meeting could help advance a railroad merger.
Final details for the meeting had not been set by late Monday.
The meeting is likely to occur by the end of the week.
Conrail's David LeVan, CSX's John Snow, and Norfolk Southern's David Goode agreed to discuss a planned $9.5 billion merger.
The merger was first announced in October.
The merger has faced challenges due to a rival $10.3 billion bid from Norfolk Southern.
Conrail has rejected the Norfolk Southern offer, stating that the CSX deal is a better fit.
Conrail shareholders previously rejected a key measure needed for the CSX transaction to proceed.
Attorneys for the three railroads worked on draft confidentiality agreements over the weekend.

Alcohol and tobacco companies are using the Internet to promote products to underage youth.
The Centre for Media Education (CME) issued a report calling for investigations into these promotions.
The CME claims some promotions may be illegal.
The Federal Trade Commission is investigating television liquor and beer advertisements.
The CME report states that urgent action is needed to protect young people from online marketing of alcohol and tobacco.
The report claims that new advertising forms appealing to youth are inherently unfair and deceptive.
Industry officials, including Jack Dougherty from Anheuser-Busch, deny targeting youth.
Dougherty stated that the Budweiser website is aimed at beer drinkers aged 21 and older.
The study found that over 35 major alcoholic beverage brands have established websites.
The study identified various marketing techniques that use interactive web features appealing to young people.

A researcher stated that the newest breed of cellular telephones is less secure than previously thought.
Researchers have uncovered a flaw in the technology designed to ensure caller privacy over advanced digital cellular phones.
The results of the research are expected to be announced on Thursday.
The flaw allows eavesdroppers to determine the number a caller dials on a cellular handset.
David Wagner, a graduate student at the University of California at Berkeley, stated that digital cellular safeguards are stronger than analogue safeguards but not as strong as previously thought.
The system was intended to protect the privacy of dialed digits.
The encryption technology used to scramble information is weak enough for eavesdroppers with a digital scanner to access the digits.
The researchers from Berkeley and Counterpane Systems stated that their findings are a setback for the U.S. cellular phone industry.
There have been previous problems uncovered with new digital phones regarding the safeguards meant to protect what a caller says.
Some experts argue that the flaws reflect shortcomings in the development process of privacy measures.

Regional Baby Bell phone companies have succeeded over long-distance rivals in a regulatory battle.
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) decided against ordering a significant cut in payments made by long-distance carriers to Baby Bells for local network access.
Long-distance carriers such as AT&T Corp pay the Bells $23 billion each year for access to local phone networks.
Bell executives were concerned that cuts could result in a loss of up to $10 billion in revenues.
Consumer groups and long-distance companies advocate for immediate cuts of $2 billion to $3 billion.
Analyst Scott Cleland stated that the Bells have avoided a significant financial setback.
The FCC is set to vote on new rules next week.
Customers who make many long-distance calls may see a significant decrease in their bills.
Wireless phone subscribers could face a monthly increase of one percent to two percent due to new fees.
Customers with multiple phone lines who make few long-distance calls may see a rate increase of around $1 or more.

Netscape Communications Corp.'s lead antitrust lawyer wrote a letter to the Justice Department.
The letter urged immediate action against Microsoft Corp. for anti-competitive behavior.
The letter was dated August 12 and made available to Reuters on a Tuesday.
The letter represents an escalation of a dispute between Netscape and Microsoft.
Gary Reback is the outside attorney representing Netscape.
Reback suggested that the issue be turned over to the Federal Trade Commission.
The letter accused Microsoft of making written offers to various parties for side payments or discounts.
These inducements were allegedly made to make competitors' browsers less accessible than Microsoft's.
The letter claimed that Netscape uncovered additional steps Microsoft took to eliminate competition.
Microsoft's spokeswoman Claire Lematta dismissed the letter as unsubstantiated and a marketing document.

Hewlett-Packard Co. stock surged in heavy trading on Wednesday.
The surge occurred a day after Hewlett-Packard reported strong first-quarter profits.
The first-quarter profits were the highest for Hewlett-Packard in eight years.
Morgan Stanley & Co., Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, and Goldman Sachs & Co. upgraded their ratings on Hewlett-Packard's stock.
These firms raised earnings estimates for Hewlett-Packard amid renewed confidence in the company's growth and cost management.
Hewlett-Packard's stock rose $7.375, or nearly 13 percent, to close at $56.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Hewlett-Packard was the most active issue on the New York Stock Exchange with a volume of more than 9.1 million shares.
The stock traded as high as $57.50, close to its record high of $57.63 reached the previous spring.
Hewlett-Packard reported profits of $912 million, or 87 cents a share, on revenues of $10.3 billion for the first quarter ended January 31.
In the same quarter the previous year, Hewlett-Packard earned $790 million, or 75 cents a share, on revenues of $9.3 billion.

Intuit Inc. announced it would exchange its Intuit Services Corp. bill payment and bank services unit for $260 million worth of CheckFree Corp. stock.
Intuit is based in Mountain View, California.
Intuit pioneered personal and small business financial software.
Intuit launched an initiative to accelerate the adoption of electronic financial data exchange and communications over the Internet.
Intuit's decision to trade its private network bank services business was well-received by Wall Street.
Intuit acquired its private network bank services business in 1994.
Intuit's stock rose by $2.125 to $32.25 on the Nasdaq.
CheckFree's stock increased by $3.19 to $21.25.
Lehman Brothers analyst Michael Stanek stated that Intuit received an excellent price from CheckFree.
Scott Cook, Intuit's co-founder and chairman, indicated that advances in Internet safety and reliability have shifted Intuit's strategic focus.

Hong Kong is showing high confidence in its future according to political analysts.
Michael DeGolyer is a political analyst at Hong Kong's Baptist University.
Hong Kong's economy is transmitting positive news with the handover to China 41 days away.
The property market in Hong Kong is booming.
The Hang Seng index of blue chip stocks is reaching record highs.
Optimism about improved access to China is contributing to the stock market's performance.
Standard & Poor's has recently upgraded Hong Kong's debt rating.
A Reuters survey confirmed overwhelming business confidence among Hong Kong's top companies.
A Credit Lyonnais survey revealed that ordinary Hong Kong people are holding more financial assets in the local currency.
A growing number of citizens are investing in China-related stocks.

Fears are rising in Hong Kong regarding a potential negative outcome from a symbolic gesture by the Democratic Party.
The Democratic Party of Hong Kong plans to occupy the chamber of parliament to express anger at the elected assembly's dissolution.
Bob Broadfoot manages the think-tank Political and Economic Risk Consultancy.
Bob Broadfoot expressed concern that if something goes wrong during the protests, it would be detrimental for Hong Kong.
Democratic Party vice-chairman Yeung Sam confirmed a plan to protest the swearing-in of a new legislature after Hong Kong returns to Chinese control.
The protest will highlight the issue of the Beijing-appointed interim legislature replacing the existing democratically-elected parliament.
Yeung Sam stated that a delegation of Democrats intends to enter the Legislative Council chamber to pledge support for democracy.
The protest is scheduled to occur simultaneously with the swearing-in ceremony of the new provisional legislature.
U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and British Prime Minister Tony Blair have pledged to avoid the swearing-in ceremony.
Yeung Sam reiterated the party's commitment to peaceful protest but mentioned the possibility of 'radical' action if obstructed.

China has declared support for the Hong Kong dollar.
Foreign exchange experts believe a successful assault on the Hong Kong dollar is unlikely.
Jim Rohwer is an Asian emerging markets strategist for C.S. First Boston in Hong Kong.
Chen Yuan is the deputy governor of the People's Bank of China.
Chen Yuan stated that Beijing is ready to defend the Hong Kong dollar if necessary.
The Hong Kong dollar peg was set in 1983 at HK$7.80 to the US dollar.
The peg serves as Hong Kong's first line of defense against economic instability.
The peg has withstood significant events, including the Tiananmen massacre and the global stock market crash of 1987.
Hong Kong's foreign exchange reserves are around US$60 billion.
Hong Kong has access to China's reserves of $90 billion and repurchase agreements with several Asian nations.

Deng Xiaoping was an avid bridge player.
Deng Xiaoping enjoyed croissants and milk.
Deng Xiaoping liked playing at the seaside with his grandchildren.
Deng Xiaoping sent in the army to crush unarmed, rebellious students.
Deng Xiaoping was a chain-smoker.
Deng Xiaoping kept a spittoon at his feet during meetings with foreign dignitaries.
Orville Schell described Deng Xiaoping as unsentimental and humorless.
Henry Kissinger referred to Deng Xiaoping as a 'nasty little man'.
Deng Xiaoping ruled China during the 1980s and much of the 1990s.
Deng Xiaoping was 1.50 metres tall.

China has raised concerns about local authorities who kidnap and extort to protect regional interests.
These actions are considered forms of corruption that undermine the ruling Communist Party's power.
Beijing plans to launch a nationwide crackdown on local power abuse from April to June this year.
The magazine Outlook criticized regional authorities for protecting local companies through illegal means.
Many courts and law authorities favor local firms in cases involving parties from other regions of China.
The magazine claims that the goal of local authorities is often to protect local interests and obtain financial returns.
Such corruption is linked to growing individualism that threatens Communist Party rule.
Chinese President Jiang Zemin has attempted to eliminate abuse of official power, labeling corruption as a virus.
Analysts suggest that the results of Jiang's anti-graft drive have been inconsistent due to local officials' autonomy.
Local authorities have illegally seized bank funds or assets from firms from other regions and have used kidnapping to extract money.

Chinese authorities imposed a curfew on a town in northwestern Xinjiang.
At least 10 people were killed in a separatist riot last week.
The riot involved 1,000 Muslim separatists of the Uighur ethnic minority.
The riot occurred in Yining, where rioters smashed cars, burned shops, and attacked Han Chinese.
Both Han Chinese and Uighurs were killed or injured during the riot.
A Chinese source described the riot as one of the most violent in years in Xinjiang.
Moslems are the majority in Xinjiang, while ethnic Han Chinese make up 38 percent of the population.
A local resident reported that a circular was issued ordering people not to go out after dark.
Local officials described the riot as a small incident fueled by unidentified foreign hostile forces.
The riot began when a Chinese policeman attempted to arrest a Uighur criminal suspect.

British regulators announced plans to expedite compensation payments for victims of pension misselling by banks and insurance companies from the late 1980s and early 1990s.
The Personal Investment Authority (PIA) regulates the pension industry in the UK.
The PIA set new targets for firms to complete reviews of outstanding pension misselling cases.
Regulators established criteria for legally binding guarantees to reassure victims about compensation.
Twenty-four companies with the highest number of cases have individual timetables for settling priority cases.
All other regulated firms must complete 90 percent of priority cases by the end of December 1997 and the remainder by December 1998.
The 24 companies responsible for three quarters of the cases include Prudential Corp, Legal & General, Norwich Union, Allied Dunbar, and Royal Sun Alliance.
The PIA warned that failure to meet the established timetables would result in disciplinary action.
The guarantee system allows firms to settle cases more quickly by providing benefits that mirror those of occupational schemes if rejoining is not possible.
A review launched in 1994 revealed that only 50,300 assessments have been completed out of 570,000 cases for review.

The British pound's strength negatively impacted Sedgwick Group Plc's profits in the first quarter of the year.
Sedgwick Group Plc reported a pre-tax profit of 43.5 million pounds, down by 1.8 million pounds from the previous year.
The strong pound reduced Sedgwick's profits by 3.4 million pounds.
Sedgwick Group Plc is seeking a listing for its shares on the New York Stock Exchange, with trading expected to begin in June.
Chairman Sax Riley stated that 40 percent of the group's business comes from North America, making the listing a logical step.
Sedgwick's results followed a similar decline in profits reported by British rival Willis Corroon, which cited the pound's strength as a factor.
Excluding currency effects, Sedgwick's pre-tax profits increased by four percent compared to the previous year.
Sax Riley described the results as encouraging despite the negative impact of exchange rates and a weak insurance rating environment.
Shares in Sedgwick increased by two pence to 130-1/2 pence following the results, which met analyst expectations.
An analyst noted that there were no surprises in the results and mentioned ongoing merger speculation between Sedgwick and Willis.

Lloyd's of London is awaiting the implications of a shake-up in Britain's financial services regulatory system announced on Tuesday.
No decision has been made regarding Lloyd's position in the new regulatory regime.
The new regulatory regime will replace existing self-regulatory organisations (SROs) with a Securities and Investments Board (SIB).
The SIB will have tougher powers and an extended remit.
Lloyd's announced it supports giving up 300 years of self-regulation for supervision by an external authority, specifically the SIB.
A Treasury spokesman stated that the Labour government is sympathetic to the proposals but no decision has been made.
Discussions are ongoing regarding how Lloyd's, building societies, and insurance will be handled under the new arrangements.
Lloyd's has not yet discussed its proposals with the government.
The proposed changes would allow the Council to retain day-to-day regulatory responsibility while being subject to external oversight by the SIB and the Department of Trade and Industry.
Legislation will be needed to amend both the Insurance Companies Acts and the Financial Services Act.

Hong Kong's business community welcomed U.S. President Bill Clinton's decision to renew China's trade privileges.
The business community hopes the U.S. Congress will not oppose the renewal of China's Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trading status.
The extension of China's MFN status is important to Hong Kong as it prepares for its return to Chinese rule on July 1.
Erica Ng is the assistant manager of international affairs at the Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce.
Christopher Hammerbeck is the executive director of the British Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong.
Clinton announced the renewal of China's MFN status for another year on Monday.
The renewal of China's MFN status is expected to face opposition from Congress.
Frank Martin is the president of the American Chamber of Commerce (AmCham) in Hong Kong.
The chambers of commerce estimate that Hong Kong could lose up to US$30 billion annually in trade if China's MFN status is not renewed.
If China loses its trading privileges, Hong Kong's GDP growth could decrease by about three percentage points and approximately 86,000 jobs could be lost.

The British army packed up its radio station in Hong Kong into a shipping container.
Britain will depart Hong Kong at midnight on June 30.
The British Forces Broadcasting Service (BFBS) plans to continue broadcasting until the handover.
The new BFBS station is located in a 20-foot container at the Prince of Wales Barracks.
Commodore Peter Melson declared the new BFBS station open in an informal ceremony.
The container is equipped with a disc-jockey, studio equipment, and soundproof styrofoam walls.
A staff of 15 will operate the station until the handover.
The container will be loaded onto the supply and troop ship Sir Percivale on June 29.
BFBS has operated in Hong Kong since 1971 and peaked at a staff strength of 45 in 1990.
The British army has been reducing its presence in Hong Kong since last year.

An advance party of the Chinese army will take position in Hong Kong on Monday.
The advance party consists of 40 members.
The advance party will arrive in Hong Kong on Queen Elizabeth's birthday.
The People's Liberation Army (PLA) troops will march into Hong Kong on July 1.
Britain will end over 150 years of rule in Hong Kong on July 1.
The advance party is led by Major-General Zhou Borong.
The advance party will arrive in Hong Kong in eight PLA staff cars and trucks from Shenzhen city.
The advance party will be in full uniform but unarmed.
More than 1,000 people protested in Hong Kong against curbs on civil liberties on Sunday.
Tung Chee-hwa plans to enforce curbs on protests and ban foreign funding for local political groups.

JAMtv is an online company that started six months ago.
JAMtv was founded by a music promoter from Chicago.
JAMtv aims to turn personal computers into personalized jukeboxes.
JAMtv will unveil a music network on the Internet using multimedia technology from Intel Corp.
JAMtv plans to broadcast live concerts and link with radio stations for programming.
JAMtv intends to sell CDs and merchandise and provide daily news and reviews.
JAMtv is collaborating with BackWeb, a leading push technology company.
Howard Tullman is the chief executive of JAMtv.
JAMtv spun out from Jam Productions Ltd, a concert producer in Chicago.
Jerry Mickelsen is the chairman of JAMtv.

International Business Machines Corp announced that its $23 billion Global Services business will become a separate IBM group.
IBM Chairman Louis Gerstner stated in the company's annual report that the company plans to hire thousands more employees, primarily in Global Services.
IBM indicated to analysts that it would likely add as many new employees in 1997 as it did in 1996, with a significant portion in Global Services.
IBM's worldwide headcount grew to 241,000 in 1996, up from 225,000 in 1995, largely due to the expanding services business.
In 1995, IBM's employment increased from 220,000 in 1994, marking the first growth in employment in 10 years.
Gerstner expressed pride in the job growth resulting from IBM's transformation in his letter to shareholders, describing 1996 as a solid year.
When Gerstner took over IBM in April 1993, he cut 25,000 jobs and took a significant restructuring charge.
The Global Services unit, which designs, installs, and services computers, was previously part of IBM's Sales and Services group.
IBM's Sales and Services group will be renamed the Sales and Distribution Group, still led by Senior Vice President Ned Lautenbach.
Dennie Welsh, general manager of Global Services, will be promoted to senior vice president and will report directly to Gerstner.

America Online Inc is facing negative news and losing users.
Competitors of America Online Inc are attempting to attract dissatisfied AOL users.
CompuServe Corp plans to run its first Super Bowl ad called the 'Busy Signal.'
The Super Bowl ad by CompuServe will not mention AOL directly.
CompuServe's ad is intended to highlight AOL's connectivity issues.
CompuServe is also launching a print campaign focused on reliability.
CompuServe has not disclosed the budget for its advertising campaign.
Gail Walls, an acting vice president at CompuServe, stated that their network is strong.
CompuServe exited the consumer business two months ago.
AT&T Corp's WorldNet Internet access service is gaining subscribers from dissatisfied AOL members.

Hillsdown Holdings plc reported a 10.5 percent increase in its 1996 pretax profits to 150.5 million pounds.
The increase in profits corresponds to 242.7 million dollars.
Chairman Sir John Nott stated that the business climate in 1997 looks favorable.
The scare over mad cow disease affected Hillsdown's meat business but increased poultry and fish sales.
Trading profit on canning, preserves, biscuits, and drinks rose to 63.6 million pounds in 1996 from 40.5 million pounds.
Earnings from chilled foods remained flat at 21.2 million pounds.
Profits from the meat and produce division fell to 9.1 million pounds from 12.4 million pounds in 1995.
Profits from the poultry, furniture, and housebuilding division increased from 36.2 million pounds to 46.8 million pounds.
Earnings from Britain rose by approximately 35 million pounds to 146.5 million pounds.
Trading profits in mainland Europe were flat at about 30 million pounds due to the poor state of the German economy.

Grand Metropolitan Plc announced it is selling its national food businesses in Europe.
The company aims to focus on its major international brands: Pillsbury, Green Giant, Haagen-Dazs, and Old El Paso.
Paul Walsh is the chief executive of GrandMet's Pillsbury Company.
Walsh stated that there is strong interest in the businesses for sale and acceptable price indications.
The sell-off is expected to be completed by January 1997.
The businesses for sale in Britain include Shippams, Peter's Savoury Products, Memory Lane Cakes, and Fleur de Lys.
Other businesses on the block include Hofmann-Menu and Goldstein in Germany, Brossard in France, Suzy in Italy, Desobry in Belgium, and Driehoek in the Netherlands.
Analysts expect the businesses to sell for approximately 140 million pounds ($220 million).
The combined sales of these businesses last year were 370 million pounds, with an operating profit of 10 million pounds.
GrandMet's European foods business had sales of $1.2 billion before the announcement, which are forecast to fall to about $450 million after the sale.

Growth in fast-food, snacking, and eating out in Britain is driving profits at food retailer Watson & Philip.
Watson & Philip owns a chain of 526 Alldays convenience stores.
Colin Glass is the chief executive of Watson & Philip.
There has been a major demographic shift with an increasing number of single occupancy households or households where both people work.
Customers are spending more on prepared food rather than food they cook at home.
Watson & Philip's shares increased by 44p to 389p, making it the stockmarket's biggest climber.
Alldays reported a 2.2 percent increase in sales in comparable stores for the year to October 27, 1996.
Group pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits for Watson & Philip were 20.1 million pounds, up 11 percent.
Alldays had an operating margin of 5.4 percent, up from 4.9 percent.
Watson & Philip plans to open about 150 more Alldays stores in 1997, aiming to increase the network to 1,000 by the millennium.

Marathon labor contract talks are ongoing at American Axle & Manufacturing Inc.
The United Auto Workers (UAW) is negotiating a new three-year contract for 7,200 hourly workers.
Negotiations had lasted for 35 hours as of 5 p.m. Saturday.
A strike deadline set by the UAW expired without any picket action.
Union members continued working during the negotiations.
American Axle's five plants are located in Detroit, Three Rivers, Mich., and Buffalo, N.Y.
A strike at American Axle would halt light truck production at General Motors Corp.'s 11 North American truck plants.
American Axle supplies rear axles for GM's pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles.
American Axle also produces axle shafts used by Ford in its F-150 pickup trucks and other vehicles.
Analysts estimate that GM could lose after-tax profits of $20 million a day if light truck production is suspended.

Ford Motor Co. showcased a concept coupe with extra side doors, adjustable pedals, and telescoping dashboard gauges.
Pontiac premiered the 'Rageous' at the North American International Auto Show.
The Rageous is a two-door concept car that can carry a four-by-eight foot sheet of plywood with the tailgate down.
The Rageous has a driver's side door compartment that can hold a pistol.
Automakers are introducing vehicles with extra doors, larger trunks, and temperature-controlled cupholders.
The new Chevrolet Corvette has structural changes that make it easier to enter.
The Chevrolet Corvette has over 12 cubic feet of cargo room.
Volkswagen is testing a two-door concept car called the Coupe CJ, designed for the American market.
The Coupe CJ can seat four people and has nearly 15 cubic feet of trunk space.
Chrysler Corp. is displaying the Dakar, a four-door concept version of the Jeep Wrangler.

Negotiators for Johnson Controls Inc. and the United Auto Workers spoke for several hours late Monday and early Tuesday.
The discussions occurred after Ford Motor Co. announced it would re-start its Expedition production line with seats from Lear Corp.
Jeff Steiner is a spokesman for Johnson Controls Inc.
Steiner expressed hope for additional discussions between the two sides.
No talks were held later Tuesday, and Steiner characterized the negotiations as adjourned.
The two sides had not spoken since late Thursday, Feb. 6.
About 500 UAW members at JCI seat plants in Plymouth, Mich., and Oberlin, Ohio, walked off the job on Jan. 28.
The JCI plants make seats for Ford's Expedition, Econoline, and Club Wagon vehicles.
Ford suspended production on three assembly lines in Michigan and Ohio, idling 6,800 workers.
Johnson Controls Inc. has a total of 34 plants in the United States.

Deng Liqun, an 81-year-old Chinese ideologue, denied authorship of two essays critical of China's reforms.
Deng Liqun was a former Communist Party propaganda chief and secretary to Chairman Mao Zedong.
Deng stated that the author of 'The 10,000 Word Essay' was Li Yanming.
Deng did not provide further identification of Li Yanming.
Deng smiled and shrugged when asked if he supported Li Yanming's views in 'The 10,000 Word Essay'.
Deng was attending an economic summit in Beijing focused on assessing China's business climate.
The summit emphasized the successes of the reform program launched in 1979 by Deng Xiaoping.
Several speakers at the conference called for tougher reforms of China's state-owned enterprises.
China's propaganda officials suspended a magazine and banned articles by a bankruptcy expert after a debate on the essay.
The Press and Publications Administration suspended the Economic Work Monthly after it published a critical article.

China rejected Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten's criticism of its proposal to abolish laws in Hong Kong.
China stated that the proposal was an internal affair.
Beijing reminded Britain that it is no longer a weak government.
China will not tolerate other countries imposing their will on it.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang referred to Patten's criticism as a so-called statement.
Shen Guofang stated that the government of China today is not the pre-1949 government.
Patten condemned a move by the Preparatory Committee to repeal or amend 25 laws after the transfer of power.
Hong Kong will become a Special Administrative Region of China after the handover.
The Preparatory Committee has the authority to review existing Hong Kong laws for conflicts with the Basic Law.
Shen Guofang claimed there would be no significant change to existing laws.

China has begun shipping corn from Heilongjiang and Jilin provinces to other parts of the country.
The shipments aim to reduce northern stockpiles and prevent further declines in weak prices.
Domestic corn prices are under pressure and are expected to continue declining.
Permission has been granted to ship 1.5 million tonnes of corn from Heilongjiang and Jilin provinces.
The government hopes to increase prices in growing regions to benefit farmers.
Farmers typically sell their crops to middlemen, usually state companies.
Some shipments of corn have already started.
An official stated that the shipments should not significantly affect prices.
Domestic corn prices have decreased by more than 30 percent since early last year.
China's estimated corn output for 1996 is 118.5 million tonnes, an increase from 106 million tonnes in 1995.

A coalition of corporations lobbied on Capitol Hill for relaxed export restrictions on computer encoding technology.
The Senate Commerce Committee will mark-up the Promotion of Commerce Online in the Digital Era Act of 1996, known as Pro-CODE.
The Pro-CODE bill aims to abolish most export restrictions on encryption technology.
Under current law, only weak encryption programs created in the United States can be sold abroad.
Domestic use of encryption is not regulated in the United States.
High-tech industry companies claim they are losing business to foreign competitors not bound by U.S. export restrictions.
Multinational companies in other industries state that export restrictions hinder their ability to conduct business overseas.
Gregory Garcia, director of international trade affairs for the American Electronics Association, stated that the current situation is unacceptable.
The Pro-CODE bill has bipartisan support in the Commerce Committee and is sponsored by Senators Conrad Burns and Pat Leahy.
The Clinton administration opposes the Pro-CODE bill, citing concerns about law enforcement and intelligence operations.

Congress is reviving the debate over encryption export policy this week.
Encryption has become a critical component of electronic commerce and global communications on the Internet.
The Clinton administration has a new policy allowing freer export of encryption products.
The new policy allows the export of stronger encryption than previously allowed.
The new policy requires companies to incorporate features allowing the government to access software keys within two years.
The government claims it needs the ability to crack strong encryption to catch criminals and terrorists.
Most high-tech companies are frustrated with the new policy and want to export very strong encryption without government access features.
Privacy advocates oppose the current Clinton policy, arguing it gives too much power to the government.
The Senate Commerce Committee will hear testimony on two bills to remove almost all export restrictions.
Industry representatives and privacy advocates will testify at the hearings.

The Clinton administration has developed a plan to reform U.S. banking laws.
The administration will announce its positions in the coming weeks.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin will present the plan at a House Banking Committee hearing on June 3.
Under Secretary John Hawke is a key architect of the administration's plan.
Hawke is scheduled to speak on Wednesday regarding the administration's stance on banking and commerce.
There is general agreement in Congress and the finance industry about removing barriers between banking, securities, and insurance.
There is disagreement about allowing banks to merge with securities and other firms.
The administration's position has changed over the past several months.
A task force initially recommended eliminating all barriers between financial sectors.
The administration is now said to favor allowing limited combinations of financial and non-financial activities.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus supports the creation of an independent market regulator.
Analysts believe that more than just the creation of a regulator is needed to revive confidence in the Prague bourse.
Klaus stated that the Czech bourse is moving towards becoming a normal market after its creation under the mass voucher privatisation programme of 1992-95.
Klaus acknowledged that the transition to a normal market would happen gradually.
Analysts and traders indicated that concrete results are necessary to attract investors back to the market.
Jan Sykora, a broker at Wood and Company, commented that the government's recognition of the problem is a positive trend.
Sykora noted that confidence in the Czech market has been significantly reduced, particularly among foreign investors.
The Prague Stock Exchange has experienced a decline, losing about 20 percent since the beginning of September due to a selloff by foreign investors.
Radim Bajgar of ING Barings described Klaus' comments as positive but emphasized that results are essential for the market.
There is criticism regarding the lack of transparency in Czech markets, especially concerning the Securities Centre's failure to provide detailed price information.

Britain's Bass plc has increased its stake in Pivovar Radegast a.s. to 30.07 percent.
Jan Sikora is the Director of Radegast.
Bass raised its stake in Radegast by about 10 percent.
The source of the stake purchase was not disclosed by Sikora.
CTK news agency reported that Bass purchased 9.97 percent of Radegast from Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Praha.
Raiffeisen and Bass officials could not confirm the CTK report.
Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. is Radegast's largest shareholder with a 34 percent stake.
A fund managed by Ceska Pojistovna holds a 30 percent stake in Radegast.
In July, Bass acquired an initial 20 percent stake in Radegast.
Radegast posted a gross profit of 281.5 million crowns over the first nine months of 1996.

The Prague Stock Exchange reached a year-high on Thursday.
The rise was attributed to strong gains in blue chip stocks.
Analysts noted that bullish sentiment was limited by low liquidity and low foreign investor interest.
SPT Telecom and CEZ are the two most-capitalised issues on the exchange.
SPT Telecom and CEZ together account for over one-third of the PX50 index.
Both SPT Telecom and CEZ reached 52-week highs on Thursday.
The PX50 index increased by 1.1 percent to 586.5.
SPT Telecom shares rose by 85 crowns to 3,660.
CEZ shares increased by 34 crowns to 1,193.
The PSE index has gained 8.7 percent in 1997.

Premier Farnell criticized BZW over a profits warning.
Howard Poulson is the chief executive of Premier Farnell.
Poulson suggested that BZW mishandled a profits warning.
The criticism is damaging to BZW in the short term.
A banking analyst stated that problems with client relationships are common.
BZW is part of Barclays Plc, a British banking giant.
BZW is facing scrutiny from the Takeover Panel regarding its role in a takeover defense for Northern Electric.
The Takeover Panel is investigating a late disclosure of a fee clause by BZW.
The fee issue led to an extension of CE Electric's offer for Northern Electric.
Barclays's chairman Andrew Buxton expressed confidence in BZW's ability to recover from setbacks.

Hambro Countrywide Plc is a British estate agency and financial products group.
The company reported a pre-tax profit of 30.8 million pounds for 1996, recovering from a pre-tax loss of 3.9 million pounds in 1995.
Managing director Harry Hill stated that the company anticipates further growth.
Hill noted that the British housing market is improving, with regional differences in performance.
London and the south east are experiencing faster growth compared to other areas.
Hill does not believe that housing prices will rise unsustainably.
He mentioned that there is significant momentum in the housing market expected to sustain through this year and next.
Hambro Countrywide is 52 percent owned by British merchant bank Hambros Plc.
The company acquired Faron Sutaria & Co for 7.45 million pounds, which has five branches in London.
Hill indicated that the acquisition would allow for additional revenue through mortgages and financial services.

Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) is involved in a probe into alleged irregularities at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
MGAM is the funds arm of Deutsche Bank's UK-based investment bank.
The SFO is in contact with the British investment watchdog IMRO.
IMRO will share any relevant material with the SFO.
The SFO investigates and prosecutes major financial crimes in the City of London.
IMRO's probe into MGAM has led to the suspension of two fund managers.
Trading was briefly halted in three MGAM funds, which have around 90,000 small investors.
Trading in the three funds resumed after a £180 million ($280 million) bail-out by Deutsche Bank.
The investigation is focusing on links between suspended fund manager Peter Young and Fiba Nordic Securities.
Fiba Nordic Securities has been a broker and valuer for funds managed by MGAM.

A survey published in Beijing indicated that most Chinese have not forgiven Japanese atrocities from World War Two.
The survey was conducted by the official China Youth Daily in December and involved 15,000 people nationwide.
99.4 percent of respondents believed young Chinese should remember Japan's occupation of China from 1931 to 1945.
More than 97 percent of the respondents were under 40 years old.
According to Beijing, 35 million Chinese were killed or wounded by Japanese troops during the occupation.
81.3 percent of respondents associated Japan with the Rape of Nanjing.
Japanese troops entered Nanjing in 1937 and committed acts of rape and massacre, resulting in up to 250,000 Chinese deaths.
More than 97 percent of respondents opposed attempts by Japanese officials to downplay wartime atrocities.
94.9 percent of respondents opposed Japan's membership in the United Nations Security Council.
85.1 percent believed Japan aimed to become a military superpower, and 70.7 percent viewed Japan as a new threat to peace in Asia.

China Jialing Industrial Co Ltd is a motorcycle manufacturer founded by the military.
The Chinese government holds a 75 percent stake in China Jialing Industrial Co Ltd.
Jialing was the largest motorcycle manufacturer in China as of the mid-1990s.
Jialing began producing civilian products in 1979.
Market competition increased significantly for Jialing in 1994 and 1995.
Jialing's sales dropped from 4.6 billion yuan in 1995 to 3.5 billion yuan in 1996.
After-tax profits for Jialing fell from 460 million yuan in 1995 to 270 million yuan in 1996.
China has approximately 300 motorcycle plants with a total annual production capacity of 20 million units.
Only 10 motorcycle manufacturers in China produce more than 100,000 units annually.
China produced 7.83 million motorcycles in 1995 but sold only 6.1 million.

China denied that its worsening pollution is a threat to the world environment.
China accused developed countries of fabricating the idea of a 'China environmental threat' to monopolize global resources.
The official China Daily described the 'China environmental threat' theory as a rumor and sensationalism.
China claimed it has done more to clean up its environment than developed countries during their initial stages of industrialization.
China announced plans to spend up to 320 billion yuan ($38.6 billion) over the next five years to curb pollution.
As of last November, China had shut down almost 57,000 small polluting factories to limit environmental damage.
Most of the closed factories produced paper, fertilizers, electroplates, or extracted sulfur.
More than 20,000 environment officials were deployed across China to inspect factories and close down polluting units.
China stated that developed countries should bear the major responsibility for the current state of world environmental pollution.
China's annual per capita income was reported to be $400, and it is committed to protecting the environment.

Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd (CCA) is an Australian-based soft drink bottler.
CCA announced it had settled the final details of a share swap deal with San Miguel Corp of the Philippines.
The deal aims to create the world's second largest Coca-Cola bottler.
CCA originally announced the deal in April.
Some San Miguel shareholders protested the deal, claiming it would limit their boardroom influence and undervalue cashflows.
CCA confirmed the initial terms of the deal, which involve CCA buying San Miguel's stake in a soft drink bottling joint venture in exchange for a 25 percent stake in CCA.
The Coca-Cola Co, CCA's parent group, will see its shareholding in CCA diluted from 36 percent to 33 percent.
The deal is valued at A$3.7 billion (US$2.8 billion) and will result in annual sales of almost A$4 billion.
The number of San Miguel representatives on the CCA board will increase from three to four.
CCA's shares initially rose by 62 cents to A$16.02 following the confirmation of the deal.

The consortium building the 2000 Olympic Stadium in Sydney has sought permission from the International Olympic Committee to sell Games tickets overseas.
The Stadium Australia group aims to raise A$364.4 million (US$282.4 million) by selling packages of Olympic tickets, equity, and stadium memberships.
The group has struggled to find local buyers for its financing scheme.
The underwriters have extended their deadline for the Olympic float due to a lack of local buyers for the 34,400 packages.
Each package sells for A$10,000.
Stadium Australia wants to sell the ticket component of the package separately to overseas buyers.
The underwriters must fund the project regardless of whether all the packages are sold.
The stadium is due to open in 1999 at a cost of A$660 million.
Each 'Gold' package includes one seat at each of the stadium sessions during the Olympics, a seat at most sporting events at the stadium until 2029, and 1,000 shares in the Stadium company.
City brokers reported that only about one third of the packages had been sold.

The Australian government ordered Canwest Global Communications Corp to reduce its stake in the Ten television network.
The order reflects the Australian government's opposition to more foreign ownership of local media.
Treasurer Peter Costello ruled that Canwest must cut its stake from 76 percent back to 57.5 percent.
Canwest raised its stake earlier in the year through associated local companies.
A government authority stated that the increased ownership broke foreign control rules.
Prime Minister John Howard expressed that he does not want foreign investment in Australian media to increase.
The Australian government is reviewing cross-media ownership rules set by the former Labor government.
The government is expected to drop cross-media ownership rules, allowing Kerry Packer to launch a takeover bid for John Fairfax Holdings Ltd.
Howard stated that a proposal by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd to increase its Australian television holdings collapsed.
Kerry Stokes accused Howard of favoring Packer in his review of media laws.

Reliance Acceptance Corp borrowed from its bank credit lines.
The short-term commercial debt market has been closed to sub-prime lenders for most of the week.
Howard Silverman is the chairman of Reliance Acceptance Corp.
Reliance is the auto lending unit of Cole Taylor Financial Group Inc.
Sub-prime lenders have had trouble securing commercial debt due to issues with Mercury Finance Co and another firm.
Mercury Finance Co overstated its earnings by about $90 million over the last four years.
Mercury Finance Co is currently in default and negotiating with its lenders for short-term financing.
Jayhawk Acceptance Corp may have to file for reorganization under the U.S. Bankruptcy code.
Sub-prime lenders use commercial debt with maturities of 270 days or less to fund purchases of loans from auto dealers.
Reliance's bank debt costs about 200 basis points more than commercial debt.

Mosinee Paper Corp expects capital expenses to double in 1997.
Mosinee Paper Corp plans to spend about $40 million in 1997.
Daniel Olvey is the chief executive of Mosinee Paper Corp.
In recent years, Mosinee Paper Corp has spent about half of $40 million on capital expenses.
Mosinee Paper Corp is adding a large number of paper-converting lines at its Bay West commercial towel and tissue unit.
Mosinee Paper Corp paid down $31 million in debt in 1996.
About 55 percent of Mosinee Paper Corp's $314.5 million in revenues came from specialty paper in 1996.
Daniel Olvey expects towel and tissue to account for more than 50 percent of revenues in the next couple of years.
Mosinee Paper Corp is adding about 30 percent capacity to its Bay West towel paper converting plant.
Mosinee Paper Corp produces about 99,000 tons of towel and tissue each year from 140,000 tons of waste paper.

FBI agents searched the headquarters of Mercury Finance Co. on Monday.
Mercury Finance Co. announced a change in leadership after revealing bookkeeping problems.
The company overstated its earnings by millions of dollars due to these bookkeeping issues.
William Brandt Jr. was named president and chief executive officer of Mercury Finance Co.
Brandt replaced John Brincat, who resigned but remains an employee and board member.
FBI agents arrived at Mercury's headquarters in Lake Forest, Illinois, with a search warrant.
The FBI was seeking financial records during the search.
Mercury stated it was cooperating fully with the FBI's investigation.
The company discovered bookkeeping problems that led to a $90 million overstatement of earnings over four years.
The misstatements were attributed to unauthorized entries by former controller James Doyle, who was dismissed.

Toronto is Canada's biggest city.
A citizens' revolt has emerged against Ontario's ruling Conservatives due to proposed changes in Toronto.
Ontario's Conservative Premier is Mike Harris.
Mike Harris proposes merging Toronto and six neighbouring municipalities into a single 'megacity' of 2.4 million people.
The new 'megacity' would represent about eight percent of Canada's population of 30 million.
Harris plans to change how public services are delivered and funded.
Opponents of the merger fear it will increase taxes and lead to urban decay.
Toronto Mayor Barbara Hall stated that government is elected by the people for the people.
A recent referendum showed that residents voted three to one against the merger, but the vote was not binding.
High-profile Canadian figures, including Norman Jewison, Norman Seagram, and Margaret Atwood, oppose the merger plan.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. stated that the Busang gold mystery may be solved by late next week.
Bre-X reported that Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. is expected to issue an interim report on its findings by the end of next week.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc. reported preliminary tests found 'insignificant' amounts of gold on March 26.
Panic selling of Bre-X shares resulted in a loss of almost C$3 billion or 80 percent of the company's stock market value.
Investors are awaiting Strathcona's findings regarding the Busang project.
Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh stated that a press release will be issued upon receiving and reviewing the interim report.
Confusion over Bre-X's announcement led to heavy selling on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Bre-X shares fell to a session low of C$2.50 but recovered to finish down C35 cents at C$3.25 on 8.9 million shares.
Freeport's annual meeting is scheduled for Tuesday, April 29 in New Orleans.
Bre-X holds a 45 percent stake in Busang, Freeport holds 15 percent, the Indonesian government holds 10 percent, and local companies hold the remaining 30 percent.

Barrick Gold Corp is the world's second largest gold producer.
Barrick Gold Corp stated that Indonesia and Canada's mining sectors are innocent casualties of the Busang gold controversy.
Peter Munk is the chairman of Barrick Gold Corp.
Peter Munk was a former bidder for Busang.
The Bre-X Minerals Ltd saga has tarnished the reputations of Indonesia and Canada among foreign investors.
Peter Munk described the Busang affair as creating backlash.
Munk stated that the success of other Canadian mining companies should not be affected by the controversy surrounding one junior gold prospector.
Munk claimed that the Canadian mining industry is second to none.
Munk's comment about a 'rogue' operation did not imply that he believed there was no gold at Busang.
Bre-X has estimated that the Busang site contains about 71 million ounces of gold.

General Motors Corp. announced changes to its marketing organization.
GM will replace the heads of its Buick and Cadillac divisions.
Buick and Cadillac divisions have experienced slow sales in recent years.
John Grettenberger, Cadillac General Manager, and Ed Mertz, Buick General Manager, will depart on February 1.
The departures of Grettenberger and Mertz will increase the number of GM division chiefs who have left in the past year to four.
John Rock, Oldsmobile General Manager, announced his retirement effective at year-end.
James Perkins retired as Chevrolet General Manager earlier this year.
John Middlebrook succeeded Perkins as Chevrolet General Manager.
GM is reducing the power and independence of its divisions to focus on its brands.
GM plans to move division staffs to its new corporate headquarters at Detroit's riverfront Renaissance Centre.

Chrysler Corp. reported better-than-expected fourth quarter earnings due to strong sales of light trucks.
Chrysler's net income for the fourth quarter was $807 million, or $1.12 per share, after $279 million in charges.
Excluding special charges, Chrysler's operating earnings were a record $1.09 billion, or $1.51 per share.
In the fourth quarter of 1995, Chrysler posted profits of $1.04 billion, or $1.33 per share.
Chrysler's full-year 1996 net income was $3.53 billion, or $4.74 per share, including $347 million in special charges.
Chrysler's full-year 1996 net income fell short of its 1994 all-time record of $3.71 billion.
On a pretax basis, Chrysler earned $6.09 billion for all of 1996, a record that topped 1995's $3.45 billion.
Chrysler announced that its 79,000 U.S. employees will receive average profit-sharing checks of $7,900 in February.
Comerica Bank economist David Littman estimated that the profit-sharing payments could boost Michigan's economy by $356 million.
Chrysler's stock rose $1.50 a share to close at $36 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Chrysler Corp. will report record earnings for 1996.
Chrysler's record worldwide sales for 1996 are 2.97 million vehicles.
Robert Eaton is the chairman of Chrysler Corp.
Chrysler's previous annual profit record was $3.713 billion in 1994.
Chrysler earned $2.025 billion in 1995.
Chrysler's sales in 1995 were limited to 2.61 million units due to the launch of its current line of minivans.
Chrysler expects to exceed its 1996 sales results in 1997.
Chrysler plans to produce about 190,000 more trucks in 1997 than in 1996.
Chrysler plans to unveil the Dodge Durango at the Detroit auto show.
Chrysler stock dropped 12.5 cents to $35.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.

LucasVarity is an Anglo-U.S. auto-components-to-aerospace company.
LucasVarity announced it is reviewing offers for 13 companies designated for disposal.
Victor Rice is the chief executive of LucasVarity.
Victor Rice stated that the group expects to enter active negotiations for the sale of non-core units soon.
Only eight of the 13 businesses marked for sale were identified in the restructuring statement.
Major businesses like aerospace and electronics are not among the unnamed five companies for sale.
Victor Rice did not provide a timeline for when the first disposals would occur.
The restructuring plans will lead to the divestment of 13 businesses and 3,000 job cuts worldwide over two years.
Victor Rice indicated that post-merger savings are expected to be virtually double the original expectations.
Annual operating savings are projected to reach 120 million stg by January 31, 1999.

The British government warned it would refer the proposed transatlantic alliance between British Airways Plc and American Airlines to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission unless conditions are accepted.
Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang stated that final clearance for the alliance depends on an open skies deal between the British and U.S. governments.
Lang supported conditions proposed by the Office of Fair Trading regarding the alliance.
Lang claimed that without suitable undertakings, the alliance would likely lead to a significant loss of actual and potential passengers on competing routes.
The latest open skies talks ended in London without a deal being signed.
Industry sources indicated there was no new date for further talks due to uncertainty over the BA/American deal.
The conditions for clearance of the alliance include BA and American dropping 168 slots at London Heathrow airport.
The government wants BA to remove a clause in its agreement with USAir that prevents competition on transatlantic routes.
Both BA and American should be prepared to reduce services on the London to Dallas Ft Worth route if a new entrant wishes to enter.
Will Whitehorn, spokesman for Virgin Atlantic Airways, expressed doubt that BA and American would meet the conditions and suggested the alliance would still be anti-competitive.

Stagecoach Plc's shares increased by 138 percent in a year.
Stagecoach Plc promised more growth this year due to overseas acquisitions.
Brian Souter is the executive chairman of Stagecoach Plc.
Stagecoach Plc has a total gearing of 567 percent.
Brian Souter stated that Stagecoach Plc has the financial capacity to make major acquisitions.
Stagecoach Plc is targeting rail and bus firms in the Nordic region and examining the Pacific Rim.
Stagecoach Plc has a 17 percent market share in the British bus market and aims to reach 25 percent.
Stagecoach Plc is delaying acquisitions in the British bus market until after the upcoming election.
Stagecoach Plc expects to have 230 million pounds in free cash in two to three years.
70 percent of Stagecoach Plc's total debt of 830 million dollars is fixed for seven years at 7.19 percent.

AT&T Corp. reported a 17 percent decline in first-quarter profits.
AT&T's profit decline was attributed to competition in long-distance services and investments in new businesses.
AT&T warned that second-quarter results might also be weak.
BellSouth Corp. reported an 11 percent increase in operating earnings.
BellSouth's earnings growth was due to an increase in customer lines and strong growth in wireless operations.
AT&T earned $1.13 billion, or 69 cents a share, on revenues of $13.05 billion in the first quarter.
In the first quarter of 1996, AT&T had a net income of $1.36 billion, or 85 cents a share, on revenues of $12.85 billion.
AT&T's earnings per share for the first quarter met Wall Street's expectations.
AT&T's first-quarter revenue growth was driven by local telephone service and wireless services.
AT&T's long-distance calling volume increased by 6.7 percent compared to the same period in 1996.

Shareholders of MCI Communications Corp are expected to vote in favor of the proposed merger with British Telecommunications Plc.
The shareholder vote is a milestone for the $23 billion cross-border merger.
The merger will create a combined company known as Concert Plc with $40.6 billion in revenues.
The merger awaits regulatory approvals in Washington, London, and Brussels.
Company officials are confident the merger is on track to close in the fall of 1997.
The annual shareholder meeting will be held in Wilkes Barre, Pennsylvania.
The agenda for the annual meeting includes the shareholder vote, election of directors, and election of auditors.
Wilkes Barre was chosen for the meeting because it is the hometown of William McGowan, the founder of MCI.
Bert Roberts, MCI's chairman and chief executive, is expected to discuss the benefits of the merger in his speech.
Industry analysts expect Roberts to reveal early products and services resulting from the merger.

NCR Corp reported a small profit in the fourth quarter of 1996.
NCR Corp experienced year-over-year gains in profit margins.
NCR executives stated that matching computer industry growth rates is a distant goal.
NCR Chief Financial Officer John Giering indicated that profits are affected by a 75 percent tax rate.
Giering stated that NCR is unlikely to reduce its tax levels to industry norms of 35 to 40 percent before 1999.
Giering's goal is for NCR's U.S. operations to break even in profitability in 1997.
NCR is already profitable in its overseas operations, which contributed to half of its $7 billion in 1996 revenues.
NCR aims for a 9 to 12 percent growth rate from core operations over the next several years.
Giering expects NCR to achieve gross profit margins in the mid-30 percent range within three years.
NCR ended 1996 with $1.2 billion in cash and $76 billion in debt.

Nomura Securities Co Ltd paid more than 70 million yen ($555,000) via stock deals into accounts linked to a racketeer.
Hideo Sakamaki is the former president of Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Hideo Sakamaki stepped down from his position last month due to the payoff scandal.
Internal investigations at Nomura discovered five irregular stock deals involving the money transfer.
Masashi Suzuki is the replacement for Hideo Sakamaki as president of Nomura.
Fifteen board members of Nomura will also resign as part of a management reshuffle due to the scandal.
One irregular stock deal involved a transaction of more than seven million shares of a commercial bank on March 15, 1993.
Hideo Sakamaki testified before a committee of the Upper House of parliament.
Prosecutors and the securities watchdog are investigating Nomura for deals involving the racketeer, known as 'sokaiya'.
The Ministry of Finance is likely to suspend some of Nomura's operations for about three months as punishment for the scandal.

Hideo Sakamaki resigned as president of Nomura Securities Co Ltd on Friday.
Sakamaki became an adviser to the company after his resignation.
Masashi Suzuki took on the role of president in addition to being chairman.
Sakamaki stated he should take responsibility as the top official of the company.
The scandal involved two directors who resigned after making suspected illegal deals.
The illegal deals were linked to a corporate client associated with a former sokaiya racketeer.
Sakamaki claimed the scandal was not endemic to Nomura but did not know if other executives were involved.
The nation's securities watchdog is investigating the suspected illegal deals.
Nomura pledged to strive to win back public trust.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka indicated that regulators will likely investigate Japan's other Big Four brokerages.

Most of Japan's second-tier brokerages expect to incur losses in the current business year due to falling Tokyo stock prices.
Many of these firms had anticipated profits for the 12 months ending March 31 after experiencing losses the previous year.
The decline in stock prices has negatively impacted their financial outlook.
Nine brokerages reported that the drop in the Tokyo stock market forced them to take write-offs on shares, especially in banks.
The stock market slump was caused by concerns about the economic recovery and banking issues.
Commission income decreased as investors became less active in the market.
An executive at Okasan Securities Co Ltd stated that they had to report appraisal losses on shareholdings due to a sharp decline in stock prices since January.
The nine brokerages that revised their earnings forecasts include Okasan, Sanyo Securities Co Ltd, New Japan Securities Co Ltd, Kankaku Securities Co Ltd, Tokyo Securities Co Ltd, Cosmo Securities Co Ltd, Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd, Wako Securities Co Ltd, and Yamatane Securities Co Ltd.
Kokusai Securities Co Ltd did not revise its existing profit forecast.
Predicted losses for the brokerages range from 1.5 billion yen ($12.1 million) to 22 billion yen ($178 million).

The Chinese yuan is expected to remain stable despite the death of Deng Xiaoping.
Dealers attribute the stability of the yuan to the central bank's dominance of the market.
The yuan has been slowly but steadily strengthening against the U.S. dollar.
The yuan closed at 8.2940 against the U.S. dollar on Friday.
There was little change in the central government or economic policy following Deng's death.
Market participants had anticipated Deng's death, resulting in no strong market response.
Political uncertainty could lead to increased selling of the yuan by foreign companies.
The central bank's control is expected to maintain the stability of the yuan even in case of political instability.
Trading volumes on the Shanghai Foreign Exchange System average between $200 million to $300 million daily.
China's foreign exchange reserves were reported at $105 billion at the end of 1996.

China's stock markets began returning to normal on Friday.
All markets were up in steady morning trade.
Analysts stated that the negative impact of Deng Xiaoping's death faded.
Both retail investors and institutions began building positions.
Some investors believe Deng's death will benefit the markets in the long term.
By midday on Friday, Shanghai's foreign currency B share index was up 1.03 percent.
The domestic A share index in Shanghai was up 3.12 percent.
In Shenzhen, the B share index rose 2.76 percent.
The A index in Shenzhen was up 0.7 percent.
Analysts noted that the relatively short mourning period indicated a desire to dispel gloom quickly.

China's financial authorities launched a campaign in early 1995 to force state banks out of the stock markets.
The campaign aimed to reduce bank risk and eliminate widespread irregularities.
Analysts reported that the campaign has been effective in stopping the use of state assets for stock market trading.
A banker from the Bank of China stated that the process of separating banks from stock and investment businesses has largely been completed.
In early 1995, Chinese state-run banks owned over 1,000 securities offices with combined assets exceeding 40 billion yuan.
By the end of 1996, most of these securities offices had been sold, closed, or made independent.
Bank shares in securities brokerages were largely sold to the brokerages and major industrial firms.
The 'Commercial Bank Law' was promulgated in mid-1995, banning banks from trading in stocks or engaging in trust and investment business.
Financial authorities fined or criticized branches of major banks and securities houses in late 1996 for illegally providing credit for initial public offerings.
By the end of 1996, China's four largest state-owned banks had largely exited the trust and investment business.

A Canadian federal election is expected to be called this weekend.
Reform Party leader Preston Manning has faced charges of racism in his party.
The Reform Party and the Conservative Party are competing for the right-wing vote.
Reform won the third most seats in its first national election campaign in 1993.
The Conservative Party won only two seats after nine years in power.
Reform has been accused of racism during its 3-1/2 year term in Parliament.
Manning accused the Conservatives of selecting candidates based on race.
A Conservative official stated he sought candidates who were not Sikh.
Manning urged the media to challenge the Conservatives on their comments.
The ruling Liberals are expected to call an election for June 2.

Nickel prices have been low in the third quarter.
Canada's nickel producers had expected an increase in prices and profits.
Inco Ltd and Falconbridge Ltd are Canada's two major nickel producers.
Falconbridge's CFO Lars-Eric Johansson stated that low metal prices will likely reduce third-quarter earnings.
Copper prices fell after Sumitomo Corp reported unauthorized trading losses of US$1.8 billion.
Copper has recently shown signs of recovery.
Johansson attributed low nickel prices to struggling European and Southeast Asian economies.
Johansson expressed hope that nickel demand would increase, possibly in the fourth quarter or early next year.
Inco's executive vice president of marketing Peter Salathiel mentioned the potential for a nickel price spike.
Salathiel indicated that a glut in stainless steel has negatively impacted nickel prices.

Busang is one of the world's richest gold deposits.
Peter Munk is the founder of Barrick Gold Corp.
David Walsh is the chief of Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
Bre-X discovered Busang in East Kalimantan, Indonesia.
The Indonesian government has instructed Barrick and Bre-X to form a joint venture.
Munk is known for his aggressive business style and extensive resources.
Barrick Gold Corp. is North America's largest gold company.
Munk has a history of focusing on gold and not diversifying into other metals.
Munk founded Clairtone Sound Corp. in the 1950s, which eventually failed in 1971.
Walsh transitioned from being a stockbroker to focusing on mining after initial failures in oil and gas exploration.

The Czech Republic is expected to have its first budget deficit.
Deputy Finance Minister Miroslav Havel stated the deficit for 1996 will be around 1.7 billion crowns.
The Czech Republic has had three surplus budgets since the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993.
As of Wednesday, revenues totaled 482.8 billion crowns and expenditures were 484.5 billion crowns.
