Havel indicated that more bills may be delivered after the deadline, increasing expenditures.
The government attempted to avoid a deficit by freezing some outlays until 1997.
The budget has been affected by lower-than-expected tax revenue and delayed repayments to Russia.
The original 1996 budget was approved as balanced at 497.6 billion crowns, but was later reduced to 491 billion crowns due to spending cuts.
Parliamentary budget committee chairman Jozef Wagner expressed concern about the impact of government payment adjustments on the 1997 budget.
The 1997 budget was approved with expenditures and revenues forecast at 549.1 billion crowns, based on an expected economic growth of 5.4 percent.

A U.S.-led consortium won a Czech Defence Ministry tender on Thursday.
Unisys Corp announced it would appeal the decision.
Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny announced the consortium led by Electronic Data Systems Corp and Digital Equipment Corp won a 1.3 billion crown ($44 million) contract.
The contract is for information systems to help Czech armed forces become compatible with NATO.
Unisys won an original four billion crown supply tender last August, which was later cancelled due to irregularities.
A commission evaluating bids in the latest tender put Unisys narrowly ahead of EDS-Digital.
The ministry decided to ignore the commission's recommendation due to the consortium's lower price and greater experience.
Jan Vesely, director of the Czech unit of Unisys, stated the company would appeal directly to the ministry.
Unisys claimed the EDS bid did not cover all required components.
The installation of the staff information system is a step towards compatibility with NATO's military command.

Czech engineering group Skoda a.s. won an order to supply trolleybuses worth more than $170 million to the city of San Francisco.
This order is the largest order of Czech goods ever to the United States.
Skoda spokesman Jaroslav Hudec stated that the electrically powered buses would be produced in the Czech Republic and assembled at Skoda's subsidiary, Electric Transit International (ETI) in Baltimore.
Hudec described the victory in this tender as an extraordinary success due to the expected volumes of supplies and the prestige of the U.S. market.
Plzen-based Skoda is no longer affiliated with the Czech car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s.
Skoda aims to offer western-quality units with the cost advantage of eastern European production.
The San Francisco contract may enable Skoda to win more business in the United States.
Electric Transit International (ETI) President Ladislav Tetal stated that the order would replace San Francisco's entire fleet of 300 buses.
The deal must be approved by the San Francisco Board of Supervisors in a vote scheduled for April 22.
Skoda has made more than 12,000 trolleybuses since 1936 and is pursuing joint ventures to build trolley buses in Russia and Iran.

China's parliament chairman is Qiao Shi.
Beijing has no plans to expand direct elections for local congress deputies beyond the county level.
Qiao Shi stated that the National People's Congress is not merely a rubber stamp.
Qiao Shi emphasized the importance of developing a real legal system in China.
Qiao Shi acknowledged that China still has a long way to go in developing its legal system.
China has passed several laws and regulations in recent years to strengthen its parliament.
Critics have described China's parliament as a rubber stamp for the ruling Communist Party's decisions.
Under Qiao Shi's chairmanship, some members of the parliament have shown opposition to certain measures.
Qiao Shi criticized the idea that decisions should be made by an individual or a small group of people.
Direct elections for deputies to the people's congresses at the township level have been held since 1995.

China began six days of mourning for Deng Xiaoping on Thursday.
Deng Xiaoping ruled China for 18 years and was 92 years old at the time of his death.
The Communist Party, the State Council, and the Central Military Commission expressed grief at Deng's death.
Deng Xiaoping's funeral is expected to take place on February 25.
Deng died at 9:08 p.m. in Beijing, according to the official Xinhua news agency.
Deng was in the advanced stages of Parkinson's disease and died of respiratory failure.
Doctors performed an emergency tracheotomy in an attempt to save Deng.
Deng's career spanned much of the 20th century, from the last emperor to the birth of China as a nuclear power.
Deng Xiaoping's influence lasted until his death, and he retired in 1990.
Flags were flown at half-mast in Tiananmen Square and at Chinese embassies worldwide.

Deng Xiaoping is a 92-year-old paramount leader of China.
Deng Xiaoping's health has been reported as fragile.
Japanese and Hong Kong newspapers speculated about Deng's health on Wednesday.
Deng was critically ill after suffering a brain haemorrhage, according to Nihon Keizai Shimbun.
Diplomatic sources in Beijing reported that Deng's health worsened and he was in critical condition on February 18.
Jiang Zemin and Li Peng cut short out-of-town trips to visit Deng in Beijing.
Sources close to the People's Liberation Army indicated that Deng had recently suffered a brain haemorrhage.
The Chinese leadership advised senior party and government officials not to leave the country unless necessary.
Ming Pao reported that Deng was recuperating at home with a team of doctors.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang stated that there had been no significant change in Deng's health.

The cause of a fire on a Malaysian Airline System Bhd Airbus A330-300 aircraft at Singapore's Changi airport is under investigation.
The fire occurred on January 4 during a routine overnight check.
Airbus Industrie instructed all airlines operating A330 and A340 jets to deactivate a specific hydraulic pump system on January 8.
The hydraulic pump system is used as a backup for the aircraft's cargo doors and is not active during flight.
A total of 140 A330 and A340 aircraft operated by 25 airlines are affected by the instruction.
The hydraulic pump system was previously implicated in fires involving an Air France A340 and an Air Mauritius A340.
The MAS spokeswoman stated that the airline is assessing the damage and cannot estimate repair costs or downtime.
There is no serious effect on flight schedules according to the MAS spokeswoman.
MAS operates 11 A330 aircraft in its regional network.
MAS is awaiting an accident report from Singapore's civil aviation department before making further comments.

An electronic document language translator is expected to be commercially available within 18 months.
The translator will offer benefits for the air cargo industry.
Edi Leong is the market development director for CargoNet.
Leong stated that the translator will allow a shopfloor worker in China to read a purchase order in Chinese that was received from an American company in English.
Leong claimed that the translator will speed up business processes by automating them.
Leong mentioned that people worldwide have been working on a translator for a long time.
Some universities have developed a working model of the translator.
Industry observers noted difficulties in developing a Chinese to English translator due to the complexity of characters.
Not every English word has a Chinese equivalent, according to industry observers.
CargoNet's shareholders include Hong Kong International Terminals and the Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents.

Polar Air Cargo is reducing the number of freighters it operates from Hong Kong to the U.S. until the end of December.
David Sung is the Hong Kong sales manager for Polar Air Cargo.
From December 16, Polar Air Cargo will operate one or two Boeing 747 freighters to the U.S. east coast.
Polar Air Cargo usually operates five flights per week to the U.S. east coast.
Ex-Hong Kong trans-Pacific rates are decreasing by five U.S. cents per week until the end of December.
Demand for cargo space is falling because most goods have already reached the U.S. Christmas market.
David Sung stated that there is an 8-10 percent drop in demand for every week after the end of November.
Polar Air Cargo will adjust its schedule and reduce flights from five to one or two until the end of December.
All flights for Polar Air Cargo were full during the peak period, which was the best in the past five years in Hong Kong.
Demand for cargo space is currently dropping off according to David Sung.

Yorkshire Electricity is a favored target for a takeover bid.
There are only two independent firms left in the regional power sector after takeovers in 1996.
Analysts believe that the lack of an emerging offer dampens takeover expectations.
Nigel Hawkins is an analyst with Yamaichi.
The Conservative government must call a general election by May.
Ten regional electricity companies have received bids from the current government.
The Labour party is currently ahead in opinion polls and may be less favorable to takeovers.
Yorkshire Electricity is estimated to have a price of around 1.4 billion pounds.
Southern is the only other independent regional electricity company left.
Potential buyers for Yorkshire Electricity are seen as U.S. firms.

CalEnergy Inc. raised its offer for Northern Electric Plc to 782 million pounds ($1.29 billion).
The deadline for the offer is set for December 20.
Northern Electric rejected the offer from CalEnergy's subsidiary, CE Electric UK Plc.
CE Electric Chairman David Sokol expressed hope that Northern Electric would endorse the raised bid.
The revised offer is 650 pence ($10.55) per share, up from 630 pence ($10.23) per share.
Northern Electric Chairman David Morris stated that CE Electric's offer does not reflect Northern Electric's true value.
CE Electric has acquired nearly 30 percent of Northern Electric's shares.
Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang will decide by December 16 whether to refer the takeover to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
Northern Electric's shares closed at 600 pence ($9.87).
An unnamed analyst suggested that the latest offer likely undervalues Northern Electric but may still succeed.

British supermarkets will seek ways to improve profitability in 1997.
Price will remain an important factor for supermarkets in 1997.
Analysts predict a focus on higher margins in 1997.
Dave Stoddart is an analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite.
An unnamed analyst stated that achieving profitable sales growth is challenging.
ASDA is known for being the cheapest among major chains Tesco, J. Sainsbury, and Safeway.
ASDA's spokesman stated that while margins are important, the focus will remain on price.
In 1996, supermarkets experienced a petrol price war that squeezed margins.
ASDA had a 10.2 percent sales growth from existing stores in the first half of 1997.
ASDA's market share was 14.8 percent at the end of 1996, placing it in third place.

The Halifax Building Society had a market flotation of 12 billion stg in June.
Analysts believe that Halifax's capital could be both a problem and an opportunity.
Chief executive Mike Blackburn stated that Halifax could increase its mortgage market share from 20 percent to 25 percent.
Halifax has a tier one capital ratio of 14 percent.
Analysts warn that Halifax must prove it can generate a decent return on equity (ROE) with its capital.
Hugh Pye, a banking analyst at BZW, estimates that Halifax needs to reduce its capital by 3.0 billion stg to reach a normal capital ratio of eight percent.
Pye described Halifax's situation as both an opportunity and a problem.
Halifax is hesitant about the prices of financial sector assets but aims to strengthen its long-term savings operation and core mortgage market.
Blackburn indicated that Halifax would focus on expanding long-term savings products due to strong growth potential.
Analysts expect Halifax to return some capital unless it can spend it on acquisitions or organic growth.

HSBC Holdings is making a larger investment in Brazil following a recent investment in Mexico.
Analysts view the investment in Latin America with enthusiasm but caution.
Major countries in Latin America, including Mexico, Argentina, and Brazil, have made significant economic and political progress.
Latin America is considered a growing market with opportunities for well-run banks.
HSBC purchased Bamerindus for 1.0 billion reais ($945 million) after the Brazilian central bank closed the bank due to losses.
400 million reais of the purchase price was allocated to goodwill, infrastructure, and intangible assets.
Douglas Flint, HSBC's finance director, confirmed that the payment was made in cash and denied rumors of discounted Brazilian debt in the transaction.
Banco HSBC Bamerindus will retain desired assets from the old Bamerindus, with the remainder left with the shell.
Flint stated that Bamerindus would be expanded after addressing its previous liquidity issues.
HSBC has appointed 50 executives to manage Bamerindus and has a history of opportunistic acquisitions.

Members of the Halifax Building Society met on Monday to decide on converting the society into a public company.
Halifax Building Society is Britain's largest mortgage lender.
Thousands of Halifax members attended the meeting.
The conversion proposal is valued at 12 billion pounds ($19.5 billion).
Halifax members are expected to support the conversion proposal by an overwhelming majority.
Halifax members will receive a basic 200 shares, estimated to be worth around 1,000 pounds ($1,620).
The estimated value of the shares is likely to increase to around 1,500 pounds by the time of flotation.
Some Halifax members oppose the conversion, wanting to retain the society's mutual roots.
The Halifax Action Group claims the conversion document is biased and does not present arguments against conversion.
The action group plans to lodge a case with the Building Societies Commission for approval of the conversion.

Seven years after the Velvet Revolution, journalists in Prague do not have to check their political views at the gate to Prague Castle.
Journalists are now expected to hide casual attire under more serious clothing.
On a Monday, spokesmen for the Czech president, prime minister, and both houses of parliament issued a joint statement regarding media attire.
The joint statement requested media to respect the normal protocolled parts of life of the historical areas of institutions.
The statement implied that journalists should pay attention to the society dress of their reporters.
If enforced, the statement would mark the end of an era for the eclectic European press corps.
Many journalists believe the statement is open to subjective interpretation.
A Czech reporter questioned the definition of society dress, asserting that their attire reflects their society.
Vaclav Havel, a key figure in the 1989 coup, led the transition to a free press in Prague.
Government and presidential news conferences in Prague often feature casual clothing, though business suits are becoming more common.

Czech Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Rudlovcak resigned on Thursday.
The resignation was accepted by Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik.
Jiri Spicka was named as Rudlovcak's replacement.
Rudlovcak faced heavy criticism for his management of capital markets.
Investors and media criticized Rudlovcak and the ministry for their performance in regulating funds and equities markets.
The capital markets are frequently accused of being opaque and having insider trading.
Rudlovcak stated that his continuation as deputy minister would not be profitable due to a long-term media campaign against him.
Criticism of Rudlovcak intensified after cases of asset stripping by Czech investment fund managers were revealed.
One case involved the investment fund Trend, where shareholders were arrested for transferring major holdings out of the fund.
The Czech Value Fund welcomed Rudlovcak's resignation, viewing it as a positive sign for tighter regulation of capital markets.

President Vaclav Havel paid tribute to Bohumil Hrabal on Tuesday.
Havel called Hrabal one of the great contemporary writers of prose.
Bohumil Hrabal fell to his death from the fifth floor of a Prague hospital on Monday.
Hrabal was being treated for arthritis at the time of his fall.
Doctors reported that Hrabal fell while trying to feed pigeons.
Bohumil Hrabal was 82 years old at the time of his death.
Havel stated that Hrabal wrote ruggedly beautiful texts.
Havel recalled writing a student essay on Hrabal.
Havel and Hrabal had a friendship that lasted throughout their lives.
Hrabal's works were suppressed under the Czechoslovak communist authorities but circulated in samizdat.

Avalon Oil Plc announced plans to seek funding in London for its oil exploration joint venture with FAO Gazprom.
Avalon Oil chairman John Wieczorek stated that British investors are ahead of U.S. investors in Russian projects.
Wieczorek mentioned that no Russian ventures have been taken public in the United States.
Avalon intends to seek a listing on Britain's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) to raise funds for the joint venture Stimul.
The joint venture Stimul aims to exploit oil reserves at Orenburg in southern Russia.
Avalon is looking to raise approximately 35 million pounds to finance its 49 percent stake in Stimul.
Other companies, including Melrose, JKX Oil and Gas, and Dana, are also involved in developing gas and oil reserves in the former Soviet Union.
Gazprom, which produces nearly a quarter of the world's natural gas, is interested in Avalon's new technology.
Stimul currently produces 2,850 barrels of oil per day and aims to increase production to 18,500 barrels per day next year.
Avalon plans to drill around 160 horizontal producing wells and 50 vertical wells at Orenburg over the next six years.

SmithKline Beecham Plc expects anti-depressant Paxil/Seroxat to become its best-selling drug by the end of the year.
Hugh Collum, finance director of SmithKline, stated that it is probable Paxil/Seroxat will be the biggest selling product by the end of the year.
Sales of Paxil/Seroxat increased by 42 percent last year to 706 million stg.
Paxil/Seroxat is competing with Eli Lilly & Co's Prozac.
Collum mentioned that the added indication of panic disorder gives Paxil/Seroxat uniqueness compared to Prozac.
Collum did not provide sales targets for Paxil but expressed optimism about its performance.
Prozac sales exceed $2 billion a year.
Collum highlighted Havrix hepatitis A vaccine, Hycamtin for ovarian cancer, and anti-emetic Kytril as potential strong growth products.
SmithKline does not expect drugs from its DNA research link with Human Genome Sciences until after the turn of the century.
SmithKline's debt levels decreased to 1.64 billion stg at the end of 1996 from around 1.8 billion at the start of the year.

Chiroscience Group Plc announced a research alliance with Alcon Laboratories Inc.
The alliance will allow Chiroscience to test its drug programmes in a new therapeutic area.
John Padfield is the chief executive of Chiroscience Group Plc.
The partnership will provide Chiroscience access to Alcon's rapid screening skills for new drugs.
Alcon will use Chiroscience's library of compounds in its high-intensity biological test system.
Alcon will retain rights to develop any resulting ophthalmic and optic drugs.
Alcon is a major eyecare company that produces contact lenses, solutions, and prescription drugs.
Padfield stated that ophthalmology is a growing area due to ageing populations and increased spending.
Chiroscience's programme with Alcon will focus on MMP inhibitors, PNP inhibitors, and PDE IV inhibitors.
Chiroscience's work on MMP inhibitors may also benefit conditions like corneal ulceration and recovery from eye surgery.

Four days of combat occurred around a mountain town 30 miles east of Bogota.
Military experts claim the Colombian army's counterinsurgency strategy has a fatal flaw.
The flaw is the belief that helicopters can win the war.
The battle involved leftist rebels and the Colombian army.
A Western defence attache stated that more helicopters are not the solution to winning the war.
The Colombian military is scheduled to receive U.S.-made Blackhawks and Russian-produced Mi-17 helicopters this year.
The defence attache expressed skepticism about the Russian helicopters.
Fighting began when two companies of heliborne troops were attacked near San Juanito.
At least 19 soldiers are reported dead, with dozens wounded or missing.
Attempts to fly in reinforcements were thwarted as Blackhawk helicopters came under fire from FARC guerrillas.

San Jose was a mountain village in northwest Colombia.
A right-wing death squad ordered the villagers to leave.
The paramilitary gang consisted of 40 members.
The gang shut down the weekly market in San Jose.
Shopkeepers were forbidden from selling all but small quantities of food.
The gang feared the village was a supply post for leftist guerrillas.
Four villagers were killed and their bodies were buried in a shallow grave.
Only 11 families remained in San Jose after the order to leave.
Dario Alvarez expressed a preference to stay and die in their homes rather than flee.
The situation in San Jose reflects similar tragedies in other villages in the Uraba region.

Union leaders restarted talks with government ministers on Thursday morning.
The strike by public sector workers is now in its third day.
Interior Minister Horacio Serpa expressed hope for 'serene and sincere' negotiations.
Serpa stated that the government has limited room for manoeuvre due to a fiscal deficit.
Union representatives expressed mild optimism about the negotiations.
The strike involves an estimated 800,000 state workers.
Union demands include a 21.5 percent pay hike and an end to the planned privatisation of industries.
The last round of negotiations ended without agreement when the government offered a 13.5 percent pay increase.
Hernando Hernandez, leader of the main oil workers' union, expressed concern about a rapid breakthrough.
Luis Eduardo Garzon, leader of the Unitary Workers' Confederation, indicated state workers may compromise if the government does.

EMI is one of the world's top five music companies.
EMI expects strong sales in the current quarter to lead to modest profit growth this year.
EMI has artists including The Beatles and The Spice Girls.
EMI reported a profit before tax and exceptional items of 293.3 million pounds ($480 million) in the nine months to December 31.
The profit before tax and exceptional items fell about six percent compared to the previous period.
The fall in profit would have been under one percent at constant exchange rates.
The strength of sterling reduced operating profit by 16 million pounds during the period.
Finance Director Simon Duffy stated that EMI expects to meet analysts' forecasts for full year pre-tax profit of 380-400 million pounds, excluding exceptional gains.
Duffy expressed confidence in achieving the profit target despite an expected 25 million pound loss due to currency factors.
EMI's pre-tax profit for 1996 was 367 million pounds.

Newcastle United season ticket holders can buy shares in a flotation.
The initial interest in Newcastle's listing surprised some analysts.
Prices of listed soccer clubs have fallen in recent weeks.
Charlton Athletic is trading at a discount after joining the junior Alternative Investment Market.
Newcastle's status and players like Alan Shearer attract investors.
Each Newcastle season ticket holder will receive 370 shares for an investment of 500 pounds.
Newcastle made 15 percent of the shares available to individuals.
The offer price for Newcastle shares is set at 135p, valuing the club at 193 million pounds.
Aston Villa is planning a flotation to raise 15-20 million pounds, valuing the club at over 120 million pounds.
Leicester City is considering a flotation after reaching the League Cup final.

BSkyB Plc is a British pay television company.
BSkyB is part of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp media empire.
BSkyB aims to lead in the development of digital television in the UK.
David Chance is the deputy managing director of BSkyB.
BSkyB has approximately 5.5 million subscribers.
BSkyB plans to launch 200-channel digital satellite services in the UK later this year.
BSkyB is 40 percent owned by News Corp.
News Corp has formed an alliance with EchoStar Communications Corp to offer satellite services in the U.S.
The U.S. venture will operate under the name American Sky Broadcasting (ASkyB).
BSkyB is collaborating with Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc to apply for digital terrestrial television licenses.

Humana Inc. reported lower quarterly profits due to charges for restructuring.
The stock of Humana rose on optimism over its new president's turnaround plan.
Humana is the fifth largest health maintenance organization in the United States among for-profit HMOs.
Humana posted fourth-quarter net income of $22 million, or 13 cents a share, down from $49 million, or 30 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter.
Humana's quarterly premium revenues were $1.81 billion, up from $1.49 billion in the previous year.
For the full year, Humana's net income decreased 94 percent to $12 million, or 7 cents a share, from $190 million, or $1.17 a share.
Humana reported revenues of $6.7 billion, up from $4.6 billion in 1995.
Humana's stock rose 37.5 cents to $18.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Gregory Wolf became president of Humana in September and is implementing a cost-cutting plan.
Humana took a special charge against earnings of $10 million related to severance costs for job eliminations.

WMX Technologies Inc. Chief Executive Officer Phillip Rooney has resigned.
Rooney's resignation occurred a week after an investment group controlled by George Soros demanded his ouster.
Rooney stated he quit to prevent distractions from the public debate over the company's leadership.
WMX Chairman Dean Buntrock will serve as acting chief executive while the board searches for a new CEO.
WMX is based in Oak Brook, Illinois.
WMX's stock rose $1.875 to $34.75 on the New York Stock Exchange following the news of Rooney's resignation.
Richard Sporrer, an industry analyst, suggested that Rooney's departure may accelerate WMX's restructuring efforts.
On February 4, WMX announced plans to divest $1.5 billion in assets, cut 3,000 jobs, and buy back 50 million shares of stock.
Major shareholders have continued to pressure WMX despite the company's restructuring plan.
Rooney had been chief executive since June 1996 and was previously the chief operating officer from 1984 to 1996.

Triarc Cos Inc plans to apply marketing principles used for Mistic to Snapple.
Michael Weinstein is the chief executive of Triarc Beverage Group.
Triarc will acquire Snapple from Quaker Oats Co for $300 million.
Dennis Rodman will not endorse Snapple.
Triarc's successful formula for Mistic included edgy advertising, distributor relationships, colorful labeling, and cold-bottle street sales.
Triarc will consult distributors and review consumer research on Snapple after the acquisition closes.
Triarc aims to innovate in packaging, product, and advertising for Snapple.
Snapple sales in 1996 were about $550 million, down eight percent from 1995.
Triarc has not set Snapple sales targets and is taking a long-term approach.
Triarc is 25-percent owned by financiers Nelson Peltz and Peter May.

Optus Communications Pty Ltd is Australia's second largest telecom carrier.
Optus expects a strong result for the June 30 year and aims for a sharemarket float in 1997.
Optus reported a net profit of A$58.9 million for the six months ended December 31, 1996.
The net profit of A$58.9 million is an increase from A$7.1 million a year earlier.
Mayne Nickless Ltd is a 25 percent shareholder of Optus.
Optus reported a profit of A$60.3 million for the 1995/96 year.
Optus had a loss of A$17.0 million in the 1994/95 year.
Sales for Optus rose 31.2 percent to A$1.19 billion.
Revenue from Optus's mobile business contributed to the sales increase.
Optus's chief executive officer is Ziggy Switkowski.

Neil Gamble is the chief executive officer of Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd.
Neil Gamble expects to receive a tax break for high spending gamblers from the New South Wales government.
Neil Gamble made his statements on Monday.
Neil Gamble expressed confidence in a favorable tax regime being approved.
Neil Gamble spoke to Reuters in an interview.
The New South Wales state government informed Neil Gamble that a decision would be made in the first quarter of 1997.
The tax break is described as long awaited by Neil Gamble.
Neil Gamble anticipates an imminent decision from the government.
The tax regime is intended for high spending gamblers.
The statements were made regarding the New South Wales government.

Publishing and Broadcasting (PBL) is an Australian media group controlled by billionaire Kerry Packer.
PBL reported a lower net profit for the first half of 1996/97 due to weaker television and magazine advertising sales.
PBL is approximately 45 percent owned by the Packer family.
PBL reported a net profit of A$104.30 million (US$82 million) for the six months ended December 31, 1996.
The net profit for the first half of 1996/97 decreased from A$107.66 million a year earlier.
PBL noted that the previous year's result was boosted by an abnormal gain.
PBL expects earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) to be slightly higher for the year ending June 30, 1997, compared to the previous year.
James Packer is the managing director of PBL and is Kerry Packer's only son.
PBL is Australia's largest magazine publisher and the Nine Network is the largest TV network in Australia.
PBL's overall sales fell 2.2 percent to A$581.56 million for the half.

Cable and Wireless Plc is Britain's second biggest telecommunications company.
Cable and Wireless Plc reported record annual profits.
The company stated it is biding its time before choosing any global partners.
C&W confirmed it is still in talks with telecoms alliances such as Global One.
Pre-tax profits after exceptional items increased by 12 percent to 1.42 billion pounds.
The total dividend was raised by 11 percent to 11.1 pence for the year to March 31.
Group turnover rose by 13 percent to just over 7.0 billion pounds.
Underlying profits were in line with expectations.
C&W's shares eased by 6.6p to 506p at 1140 GMT.
C&W merged its British telephone subsidiary Mercury with three cable television companies to create Cable and Wireless Communications.

General Cable is a British cable television and telecoms group that is currently losing money.
General Cable is acquiring Imminus Ltd for 33 million pounds ($53 million).
16 million pounds of the acquisition will be allocated to four directors of Imminus Ltd to retain them.
General Cable reported annual pretax losses of 29.8 million pounds.
Finance director David Miller stated that the acquisition was the right decision at the right time and price.
General Cable has been speculated to have held takeover talks with Telewest Communications Plc and Comcast UK Cable Partners Ltd.
General Cable aims to maximize shareholder value.
The company sees no immediate advantage in merging or being taken over.
Chairman Sir Anthony Cleaver mentioned that the group would continue discussions with others in the industry.
General Cable has completed 57 percent of its regional network and plans to finish the rollout by 2001.

Computer experts claim that applets, baud rates, and Java are not important without cryptography.
New technology is driving significant growth in Internet communication.
Companies are developing complex codes to make information unintelligible.
Cryptography is defined as encoding data, establishing authenticity, and preventing unauthorized use.
Cryptography is viewed as essential for the future of virtual businesses.
Confusion exists regarding terms and acronyms related to cryptography.
A member of the audience at the 'Encryption Feasibility Summit' expressed confusion about cryptographic terms.
Nearly 200 million people are expected to be connected to the Internet in the coming years.
Investment bankers Takumo Amano and Robert Blohm state that the Internet market is crucial to the U.S. economy.
The Internet market contributed approximately $200 billion to the U.S. gross domestic product last year.

Apple Computer Inc. plans to cut 4,100 jobs in a restructuring aimed at returning to profitability.
The restructuring is the second major overhaul in the last 12 months.
The restructuring will result in a $155 million charge in the second quarter ending in March.
This charge is in addition to a planned $325 million charge for the purchase of Next Software Inc.
The job cuts include 2,700 full-time employees and 1,400 contract workers.
The number of job cuts is slightly less than what some analysts had expected.
Apple plans to begin notifying employees about the layoffs later this month.
Apple has suffered from missed opportunities, management turmoil, and failed strategies in recent years.
Apple Chairman Gilbert Amelio stated that the restructuring aims to boost Apple's core business.
Apple has posted more than $900 million in losses over the last five quarters.

Intel Corp. reported that its first-quarter net income more than doubled.
Intel expects little revenue growth in the second quarter.
Intel is the world's biggest chipmaker.
The number of chips Intel shipped in the first quarter was flat compared to the fourth quarter.
Analysts suggested that Intel's new line of Pentium microprocessors is not boosting personal computer sales.
Peter Andrew, an analyst at AG Edwards, stated that it was a solid quarter showing Intel's dominance.
Peter Andrew also noted that the flat revenue projection could upset some people.
Intel's net income rose to $1.98 billion, or $2.20 a share, from $849 million, or $1.02 a share, in the same quarter a year ago.
First-quarter revenue rose 39 percent to $6.45 billion from $4.64 billion in the same quarter a year ago.
Intel plans to boost marketing expenses by 7 percent to 9 percent in the second quarter.

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. reported a first-quarter profit of $12.95 million or 9 cents a share for the quarter ended March 30.
The profit for the first quarter was lower than the profit of $25.3 million or 18 cents a share in the same quarter a year ago.
Wall Street analysts expected AMD to report a loss of 3 cents a share.
AMD's first-quarter revenue rose 1.4 percent to $552 million from $544.2 million a year ago.
AMD's revenue for the most recent quarter was about $10 million higher than Wall Street expected.
Analyst Mark Edelstone stated that the company is profitable and starting an incredible product cycle.
AMD shares rose $1.875 to $41.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
AMD shares rose an additional $1.75 to $43 in after-hours trading.
AMD Chairman Jerry Sanders reported that all of the company's businesses improved over the fourth quarter.
AMD plans to ramp production to ship hundreds of thousands of AMD-K6 MMX processors during the current quarter.

Sears Canada Inc is Canada's third largest department store chain.
Sears Canada announced that retail revenues could grow by 8.6 percent or more in 1997.
Sears Canada reported a first-quarter loss of C$0.03 a share in 1997.
The first-quarter loss in 1996 was C$0.23 a share.
Wood Gundy retail analyst David Brodie had forecast a loss of C$0.10 a share for Sears Canada.
Sears Canada reported a first-quarter retail revenue increase of 8.6 percent from the previous year.
Consolidated revenues for Sears Canada increased to C$875.1 million from C$821.7 million.
Sears Canada plans to spend C$300 million over three years to upgrade its 110 outlets.
T Eaton Co Ltd may close up to 31 of its 85 outlets after entering bankruptcy protection.
Sears Canada shares rose 0.25 to 14 in Toronto on Monday.

Toronto's key stock index ended softer on Monday.
The decline was influenced by weak gold shares and fears of a Canadian interest rate hike.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index closed at 5679.33, down 4.31 points.
The index is down more than 10 percent since its lifetime high of 6348.02 on March 11.
Turnover on the exchange was 63.6 million shares worth C$965.6 million.
The Canadian dollar closed at C$1.3994 after central bank intervention.
Dunnery Best is the director of private client investing at Midland Walwyn.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 60.21 points to close at 6451.90 on Monday.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indices were weak, led by gold, consumer products, and real estate.
Ballard Power Systems Inc. rose 3.25 to 39.50 after Daimler-Benz AG acquired a 25 percent stake.

Canada's Philip Environmental Inc. plans to acquire Houston-based Allwaste Inc. and Serv-Tech Inc. in two deals worth $612 million.
The acquisition will create North America's biggest recycling firm.
Philip Chief Executive Allen Fracassi expressed excitement about the opportunity during a media conference call.
The deals are expected to create North America's largest metals recycling and industrial services company.
The new company will have annual revenues exceeding $1.6 billion, 8,000 employees, and 215 operating locations in North America, Europe, and South America.
Philip will swap 0.611 of a Philip share for each Allwaste share for a total consideration of $540 million.
The Allwaste deal includes the assumption of about $133 million in debt.
Philip will exchange 0.403 of a Philip share for each Serv-Tech share in a deal valued at $72 million, including the assumption of $21 million of debt.
Serv-Tech generated more than $140 million in revenues in 1996.
Analyst Peter von Ond revised his 1998 earnings estimate for Philip to C$1.70 a share after the news.

Sugar producers in China are concerned about potential imports affecting the domestic market.
Domestic sugar prices in Guangxi province are below 4,000 yuan per tonne.
Some sugar prices in Guangxi province have dipped to 3,700 yuan per tonne.
The break-even price for sugar producers is above 4,000 yuan per tonne.
Factories need prices between 4,200 and 4,300 yuan per tonne to be profitable.
China plans to import 690,000 tonnes of sugar in 1997.
350,000 tonnes of the 1997 sugar imports will come from Cuba.
The 1996/97 sugar crop in Cuba is forecasted to be close to 4.5 million tonnes.
The remainder of China's 1997 sugar imports will come from Thailand and Australia.
China's total sugar imports in 1996 were 1.25 million tonnes, a decrease of 57.5 percent from the previous year.

Far East metal traders expect China to avoid major copper purchases until the end of April.
The head of a trading house in Hong Kong stated that the right time for copper purchases is later in April.
End-users are making small parcel purchases of 500 to 2,000 tonnes due to depleted inventory.
Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) have been around $2,300 a tonne for the past couple of months.
LME copper finished at $2,372 a tonne last Thursday before the Easter holiday.
China's peak copper consumption season coincides with the end of winter and the start of construction projects.
A trader in Beijing reported that China is producing sufficient amounts of cathode from its own concentrate supplies.
Shanghai Metal Exchange figures indicate there are 14,828 tonnes of copper held on warrant in exchange warehouses.
Japan's General System of Preferences (GSP) for tariff-free zinc imports from designated developing countries closed on March 31.
Brokerage house Brandeis projected GSP imports of zinc to reach 90,000-100,000 tonnes this year, with 70,000 tonnes expected from China.

China is currently importing about 100,000 tonnes of soybean oil a month.
Traders expect China to increase soybean oil imports as new licences become available.
Most of the available vegetable oil in Chinese markets is palm oil.
Palm oil is selling at a premium to soybean oil.
Palm oil costs $596 a tonne FOB at Malaysian ports.
Freight charges add $25 per tonne to palm oil.
The c&f price for palm oil on arrival in China is $621 a tonne.
South American soybean oil is arriving in China at about $560 a tonne c&f.
China purchased a total of 35,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean oil for February shipment.
China's total soybean oil imports in 1996 were 1.3 million tonnes.

Gazprom pushed back a plan to issue more share look-alikes for foreigners.
Gazprom stated it needed time to clear out its debts to allow its stock to appreciate.
Gazprom challenged the government to assist with tax and payment issues.
Eduard Ivanov is the director of securities at Gazprom.
Gazprom plans to issue a second tranche of American Depositary Shares (ADS) next year.
The exact timing for the ADS issuance has not been set.
Gazprom still plans to issue convertible bonds this year.
Gazprom accounted for 26 percent of Russia's 1996 tax revenue.
Gazprom has a market capitalization of $16.5 billion.
Gazprom accounts for over one-third of global gas reserves and 95 percent of Russian gas output.

Russia's aluminium sector leaders stated there are few chances of output disruptions due to a dispute over Western participation.
A senior official close to the Bratsk smelter indicated that renationalisation of the sector is not impossible.
The official claimed that all smelters have a unified position of solidarity and that output will not be affected.
Oleg Presman, deputy chief executive of the Krasnoyarsk smelter, mentioned that top aluminium executives in Russia are drafting a letter to Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov.
Kulikov expressed concerns about foreign presence in the aluminium sector and stated that a probe into alleged crimes in the sector was justified.
Kulikov wrote a letter to Trans-World executive chairman David Reuben, emphasizing the need for domestic producers to be protected from foreign companies.
Trans-World Group holds approximately 30 percent of Bratsk, 11 percent of voting shares in Krasnoyarsk, and a non-controlling stake in Novokuznetsk smelter.
Domestic aluminium executives defended the presence of foreign companies like Trans-World, claiming they have supported Russian plants through tolling arrangements.
The senior official warned that ending tolling would jeopardize the Russian aluminium sector and questioned how smelters would raise $2 billion for raw materials.
Russia's primary aluminium exports were the largest in the world last year, totaling 2.44 million tonnes out of a domestic output of 2.87 million tonnes.

Russia's LUKoil announced a new reserves audit on Monday.
LUKoil claims to be the world's single largest oil firm based on this audit.
The audit was conducted by U.S. engineers Miller & Lents.
LUKoil reported total proven oil reserves in Russia of 10.7 billion barrels.
This figure is an increase from the 10.5 billion barrels reported in 1996.
Energy analyst James Bunch stated that LUKoil is at the top of the list for publicly-traded oil companies.
Bunch also noted that LUKoil is not larger than the major international oil producers known as the Seven Sisters.
The Seven Sisters include Royal Dutch/Shell, British Petroleum, Exxon, Texaco, Chevron, Mobil, and Gulf Oil Corp.
Saudi Aramco is identified as the world's single largest oil company.
Analysts indicated that LUKoil's competitors have larger reserves when natural gas is converted to oil equivalent.

Shareholders of Thomson SA approved an 11 billion franc state capital injection.
The French government is reviewing how to relaunch the privatisation process of Thomson SA.
A government official stated that they need time to consider their next steps regarding privatisation.
Industry Minister Franck Borotra met with Thomson worker representatives who opposed the privatisation plans.
The French government announced the suspension of the sale of Thomson SA on Wednesday.
Thomson SA owns 58 percent of Thomson-CSF and all of Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
Approximately 200 Thomson workers marched in Paris to support 15 employees who walked from the Angers plant.
The industry ministry stated that Franck Borotra intends to pursue the privatisation of Thomson.
The government suspended the sale of Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe due to disagreements over terms.
Thomson SA had debts of 25.3 billion francs at the end of 1995, with significant amounts owed by TMM and Thomson-CSF.

France Telecom has been ordered by France's new telecommunications supervisor to review a proposal for a list of prices for its infrastructure.
Jean-Michel Hubert is the president of the Autorite de Regulation des Telecommunications (ART).
ART held a meeting with all operators on the day before the news conference.
The catalogue of interconnection charges is important for the economic viability of future entrants into the French market.
France Telecom is slated for partial privatisation in the spring.
Hubert hopes to provide an opinion on the draft decree on interconnection at the start of February.
Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon aims to publish the final decree before the end of February.
ART is seeking to make a decision on the price list before the partial sale of France Telecom.
ART started its legal existence on January 6, taking over regulatory and licensing authorities from the Ministry of Telecommunications.
ART is independent and will act as an arbitrator in disputes between operators.

Merck & Co. Inc. and Rhone-Poulenc SA announced a merger of their animal health businesses.
The merger will create a new company that will be the world leader in the animal health sector.
Merial Animal Health is a 50/50 joint venture between Merck and Rhone-Poulenc with estimated 1996 sales of $1.750 billion.
Merial will be the market leader in biology products, veterinary drugs, and poultry drugs.
Merial is expected to overtake Pfizer-Smithkline Beecham, Bayer, and Novartis.
Igor Landau, managing director of Rhone-Poulenc, stated that the merger would cut costs and affect jobs.
Landau indicated that the impact of the merger would not be most pronounced in France.
Merck will make an unspecified payment to Rhone for the 50/50 parity.
Merck was ranked No. 2 in animal health in 1995 but was overtaken by Novartis in 1996.
Merial will benefit from the launch of new Merck products and a jointly developed product will be ready in three years.

Australia's Maritime Union launched rolling bans on Indonesian shipping on Wednesday.
The bans are a protest against the arrest of Indonesian labour leaders and Australia's failure to address human rights with Indonesia.
The bans are designed to hold up ships for 24 hours and could apply to all types of commodity exports to Indonesia.
Jakarta stated that the union's action could harm bilateral relations.
Ghaffar Fadyl, a spokesman for Indonesia's Foreign Ministry, expressed regret over the incident.
Fadyl indicated that the business sector would likely react strongly to the bans.
In 1995, Indonesia purchased A$2.4 billion worth of Australian commodities.
The bans are in response to the arrests of labour leaders Muchtar Pakpahan and Dita Sari and ongoing repression after the July riots in Jakarta.
Australian Prime Minister John Howard did not press Indonesia on human rights during his recent visit.
The first ship affected by the bans is the Bogasari Empat, which will be delayed for 24 hours before departing Fremantle.

The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is engaged in printing foreign currency.
The RBA's printing presses are located in a heavily guarded facility on the outskirts of Melbourne.
The RBA prints foreign banknotes such as Thai baht, Singapore dollars, Indonesian rupiah, and Kuwaiti dinars.
The foreign banknotes printed by the RBA are made of plastic using patented technology.
Robert Larkin is the chief executive of the RBA's printing division, Note Printing Australia.
Plastic banknotes made by the RBA last longer in circulation than paper banknotes.
Before switching to plastic notes in 1988, the RBA printed about 600 million local banknotes each year.
Currently, the RBA prints only 150 million Australian banknotes a year.
The RBA aims for 75 percent of its banknotes printed in Melbourne to be for export within three years.
Canadian commercial printers Dura Note and Domtar Inc also produce plastic banknotes.

National Australia Bank reported record half-year net earnings of A$1.14 billion (US$885 million) for the six months ended March 31.
Managing director Don Argus stated that NAB feels vulnerable to foreign takeover.
Argus suggested that a government freeze on mergers between the four big local banks has exposed them to foreign takeover threats.
NAB is ranked as the most profitable bank in Australia by KPMG management consultancy.
The government has maintained a ban on big-bank mergers until competition widens and intensifies.
An official inquiry recommended allowing big banks and major life offices to merge, but the freeze remains in place.
Argus criticized the government's position, stating that competition is unrelenting and could pressure NAB's ability to deliver record profits.
NAB shares ended at A$18.11 on Thursday, down 23 cents from Wednesday's close but still at historical highs.
Offshore income accounts for 37 percent of NAB's net earnings, bolstered by earnings growth from subsidiaries in the UK, Ireland, the US, and New Zealand.
Net profit from NAB's Asian business more than doubled to A$15 million from A$6 million a year ago.

Microsoft Corp., Intel Corp., and Compaq Computer Corp. proposed standards for a new generation of televisions.
The proposed television protocol was unveiled at a broadcasters' conference in Las Vegas.
Craig Mundie is the Senior Vice President of Microsoft.
The proposed standards are recommended for multimedia PCs to be detailed at an industry meeting in San Francisco.
The companies are proposing adoption of three out of 18 advanced technical standards set by a television industry coalition.
The proposal aims to improve picture quality and allow transmission of related information and data to personal computers and televisions.
Robert Stearns is the Senior Vice President of Compaq.
Stearns stated that advanced television would allow viewers to interact with programming in various ways.
Equipping personal computers to decode new television signals would add little cost, estimated at less than $150.
The Federal Communications Commission called for a rollout of digital television technology in the nation's 10 biggest markets within 18 months.

Microsoft Corp. reported a third-quarter profit of $1.04 billion, an 85 percent increase.
The profit exceeded analysts' expectations.
The increase in profit was attributed to strength in the Windows business and the Office 97 upgrade.
Microsoft's net income was 79 cents per share, compared to 44 cents per share in the same quarter last year.
Revenues reached a record $3.21 billion, a 45 percent increase from $2.21 billion in the previous year.
Analysts had forecast earnings of 64 cents per share and revenues of about $2.9 billion.
Microsoft's Chief Financial Officer Mike Brown expects growth to slow over the next year.
Analyst Scott McAdams expressed surprise at Microsoft's performance and predicted a rise in stock price.
Microsoft's stock fell to $98.125 in Nasdaq trading but rose to $102.75 in after-hours trading.
Revenues from the Office 97 bundle contributed to application and content revenues of $1.53 billion, a 24 percent increase.

Boeing Co. reported that its first-quarter profit more than doubled.
Boeing Co. reported a 70 percent increase in sales in the first quarter.
Boeing Co. earned $313 million, or 87 cents a share, in the first quarter.
Boeing Co. earned $119 million, or 35 cents a share, in the same quarter a year earlier.
Boeing Co.'s revenue increased to $7.32 billion from $4.29 billion.
Boeing's net income was 13 percent below the Wall Street consensus of $1 a share.
Boeing's stock fell $6.625 to close at $95.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts indicated that Boeing's earnings were affected by higher-than-expected expenses.
Boeing stated that it is incurring significant overtime costs to increase production.
Boeing expects profit margins to be lower for the rest of the year due to new model deliveries.

Ivory Coast's power capacity is set to increase by one third.
Domestic demand for power in Ivory Coast is low.
Power engineering firms and distributors indicated that export customers will be needed.
Ivory Coast has about 1,200 megawatts (MW) of installed power capacity.
There are no large industrial users of power in Ivory Coast.
One of the top 10 power consumers in Ivory Coast is a hotel.
Marcel Zadi Kessy is the president of Compagnie d'Electricite Ivoirienne (CIE).
CIE expects to rely on power exports due to domestic market limitations.
ABB and five other bidders submitted proposals to build a $300 million, 450 MW gas-fired power plant near Abidjan.
The gas-fired power plant at Azito is expected to start operating within 12 months with an initial capacity of 300 MW.

Port arrivals of Ivorian coffee for the 1996/97 season totaled about 150,000 tonnes by March 16.
This is an increase from about 110,000 tonnes in the 1995/96 season.
One industry buyer stated that the 1996/97 crop is larger than the previous year.
Forecasts for the 1996/97 crop are upwards of 230,000 tonnes.
Marketing for the 1996/97 crop has been delayed due to a large cocoa crop.
Ivory Coast produced around 180,000 tonnes of mainly robusta coffee in the 1995/96 season.
Ivory Coast has slated 230,000 tonnes for the 1996/97 season.
A mild flowering period from January to March 1996 contributed to the 1996/97 harvest.
Exporters reported that 120,000 tonnes had been taken to Abidjan and 30,000 tonnes to San Pedro since mid-November.
Port sources indicated that coffee exports to mid-March were just over 40,000 tonnes.

Rains in Ivory Coast's southern cocoa belt increased in late February.
Weather and crop analysts reported that the overall rainfall deficit into March has not stressed trees significantly.
A national weather centre spokesman stated that rains have continued along the south coast and in forest areas.
The spokesman indicated that rains are expected to move further north soon.
Crop analysts noted that trees are beginning to show some reaction to prolonged dry weather but no signs of damage.
An analyst mentioned that there was over 200 percent of normal rains in December and January.
Ivorian commodities minister Guy-Alain Gauze stated that the 1996/97 crop would be less than one million tonnes.
Gauze expressed skepticism about recent rain, stating that it was not sufficient.
Official data showed average rainfall of 12.24 mm in the last eight days of February.
Some industry forecasters raised 1996/97 crop estimates after strong main crop arrivals.

A Miami television journalist produced a news report on niche-brand cigarettes.
The journalist was removed from the pool of standby jurors in Florida's secondhand smoke trial.
The journalist was among 15 people questioned by a judge and lawyers.
The journalist produced a report for Fox station WSVN Channel 7 on cigarette marketing.
Tobacco lawyers objected to the journalist's inclusion in the juror pool.
Tobacco lawyers claimed the journalist's report negatively portrayed tobacco companies.
A tape of the journalist's report was shown in court and included interviews with various individuals.
Judge Robert Kaye sided with the tobacco lawyers and removed the journalist from the juror pool.
The standby jurors pool currently numbers 18, with 60 needed to seat a jury of six.
A court official stated that a second round of screening will be required to find alternates.

Knight-Ridder Inc agreed to buy the Kansas City Star and three other daily newspapers owned by ABC Inc for $1.65 billion.
ABC Inc is a division of Walt Disney Co.
Knight-Ridder will divest Knight-Ridder Information Inc, its online information service for business and professional users.
Knight-Ridder owns the Miami Herald and Detroit Free Press.
Knight-Ridder is the second-largest newspaper group behind Gannett Co. Inc.
John Morton is an independent newspaper analyst who stated that the information business is very competitive while the newspaper business is not.
The Disney/ABC newspapers include The Kansas City Star, the Fort Worth and Arlington Star-Telegrams, the Belleville News-Democrat, and The Times Leader in Wilkes-Barre, Pa.
Revenue for the Disney/ABC newspaper group was $500 million in 1996.
Knight-Ridder sold its Knight-Ridder Financial business news unit for about $275 million to Global Information Corp.
Knight-Ridder plans to finance the deal by issuing $660 million in convertible preferred stock and assuming $990 million of pre-existing debt.

Florida's anti-tobacco activists recently won a high-court victory.
Florida's government has a law that allows it to sue cigarette makers.
Opponents of the law plan to continue efforts to repeal Florida's third-party medical liability act.
The current legislative session in Florida is scheduled to last until May.
Jodi Chase is the general counsel for Associated Industries of Florida Inc.
Bills to repeal the medical-liability law have been introduced in both the upper and lower houses of the Florida legislature.
Gov. Lawton Chiles vetoed a repeal bill two years ago.
Harold Lewis is the chief inspector general for Gov. Chiles.
The U.S. Supreme Court refused to take up a tobacco industry challenge to the law's constitutionality.
A trial in the billion-dollar lawsuit against the tobacco industry is scheduled for August 4 in West Palm Beach, Florida.

China and the United States signed a new textile agreement on Sunday.
The agreement ended the threat of a cross-Pacific trade war.
U.S. officials stated that they gained assured access to Chinese textile markets.
The agreement granted China a U.S. import quota slightly larger than the previous 1994 textile pact.
Penalties imposed by Washington on Chinese imports remained in force under the deal.
Beijing agreed to withdraw its threat of retaliation according to U.S. textile negotiator Rita Hayes.
The four-year textile accord was signed by Rita Hayes and Li Dongsheng.
The negotiations for the deal extended beyond the original three-day schedule to six days.
Chinese Foreign Trade Minister Wu Yi stated that the delegations reached a rather ideal conclusion.
The accord resolved a dispute over U.S. penalties on Chinese exports and focused on market access.

China expects to reach a formal agreement with Tokyo on the details of Japan's yen loans.
China warned that politics should not interfere with economic aid.
A Japanese mission reached a basic agreement with Chinese officials on projects to receive 180 billion yen.
The 180 billion yen is part of Tokyo's 1996-2000 soft loan package.
Talks on the loans had been stalled due to disputes over territory, history, and China's nuclear testing programme.
China Daily Business Weekly reported that Japan and China plan to sign a formal contract on the 1996 yen loans.
Officials from the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation warned against political interference in economic relations.
Yu Zhensheng stated that China is against political conditions attached to economic cooperation.
The loans are seen in China as an unofficial form of reparation for wartime damage caused by Japan.
Sino-Japanese ties have been strained by issues such as nuclear testing and territorial disputes.

China criticized Washington for its policy of 'human rights diplomacy'.
The China Daily newspaper stated that Sino-U.S. ties are being harmed by this policy.
There are currently no prospects for resolving disputes over China's human rights record.
The China Daily claimed that U.S. human rights diplomacy is undermining cooperation between the two countries.
The newspaper accused Washington of using sensationalized human rights issues to contain China.
The United States is said to exploit human rights issues for self-interest.
Washington denies pursuing a policy of containment against China.
Sino-U.S. differences over human rights have been overshadowed by trade and other disputes.
Chinese missile tests near Taiwan prompted a response from Washington with aircraft carrier deployments.
The China Daily suggested that future Sino-U.S. relations may be characterized by distrust.

Global One's shareholders are pleased with the venture's establishment in its first year.
Global One was not judged by its losses in 1996.
Global One was established in January 1995 by Sprint Corp, Deutsche Telekom AG, and France Telecom.
Global One provides global telecom services to multinational firms and carries other telecom firms.
Klaus Czerwinski is the vice president of corporate communications at Global One.
Global One lost almost $370 million in 1996, exceeding the expected loss of $250 million.
Czerwinski did not disclose the total losses for Global One in 1996 until the books are closed.
Sprint took $62 million in charges for Global One losses in 1996.
Sprint owns one third of the European part of Global One and half of the non-European part.
Sources indicated that unexpectedly higher losses led to threats of job cuts, but Czerwinski was not aware of any planned cuts.

Sprint Corp reported that its core local and long distance operations are performing strongly.
Sprint Corp's results in 1997 will be affected by investments needed for future growth.
Ronald LeMay, chief operating officer of Sprint, stated that core operations are producing at unprecedented levels.
Sprint Corp is investing in future growth, which will impact its earnings per share in 1997.
Sprint Corp has informed analysts about expected increased spending in 1997.
Sprint Corp will report its 1996 results on February 4.
First Call's consensus of analysts estimated Sprint's earnings per share at $2.93 for 1996.
Analysts noted that MCI Communications Corp also indicated increased spending, but AT&T Corp did not.
AT&T Corp has experienced lowered analyst estimates due to anticipated increased spending.
Sprint has bid $550 million in the U.S. government auctions for D and E bands of radio spectrum.

BellSouth Corp does not feel pressure to seek a merger.
BellSouth Corp sees little value in current merger deals.
Ron Dykes, chief financial officer of BellSouth, stated that there has been no compelling value proposition in recent mergers.
Dykes believes there are few efficiencies in neighboring Bells merging.
Dykes finds buying long distance assets less attractive than competing with Internet service providers.
Dykes expressed skepticism about vertical takeovers in industries where BellSouth lacks expertise.
Dykes believes that filling out service provision in BellSouth's nine-state region is the best strategy for success.
Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp have merged, as have SBC Communications Inc and Pacific Telesis Group.
Dykes stated that BellSouth does not want to own assets of declining value in the long distance industry.
BellSouth has a deal to use AT&T Corp's network for long distance service and expects to serve customers in at least two states by year-end.

Ralcorp Holdings Inc has undergone recent divestitures, effectively cutting itself in half.
Ralcorp is attempting to reduce costs to make its cereal business profitable by next year.
Joe Micheletto is the president of Ralcorp Holdings Inc.
Ralcorp was spun off by Ralston Purina Co in March 1994.
Ralcorp completed the sale of its branded cereal and snack business to General Mills Inc for $570 million.
Ralcorp's annual cereal sales from private-label cereal are $274 million, down from $660 million.
The sale of the branded business left Ralcorp with an oversized infrastructure for its reduced operations.
Ralcorp plans to implement cutbacks to return its cereal business to profitability in fiscal 1998.
Ralcorp will incur a $20 million charge in its second quarter due to staff cuts and other costs.
Ralcorp sold its ski resort operation to Vail Resorts Inc for $310 million on January 3.

General Mills Inc expects a recovery in sales volume in the U.S. ready-to-eat cereal market.
General Mills is the number two player in the $9.0 billion U.S. ready-to-eat cereal market.
Stephen Sanger is the Chairman of General Mills.
The total U.S. cereal category saw a 1.5 percent rise in physical sales volume in the past 12 months.
The growth in the U.S. cereal category was only 0.5 percent in the prior 12 months.
Sanger believes domestic volume gains will move back toward a long-term trend of three percent category growth.
Per capita consumption of the U.S. ready-to-eat cereal market grew to 11.4 pounds in 1996 from 9.3 pounds in 1986.
Cereal's share of the breakfast market grew to nearly 30 percent from 28.8 percent over the past five years.
General Mills plans to introduce one more cereal by the end of fiscal 1997 in May.
After acquiring branded cereals from Ralcorp Holdings Inc, General Mills gained about 2.5 percentage points of domestic market share.

Vita Food Products Inc sells kosher seafood and other specialty products.
Vita Food Products Inc is looking for acquisitions to increase annual sales four-fold within the next five years.
Stephen Rubin, president of Vita, stated that with the right acquisitions, annual sales could reach $75 million to $100 million.
Vita's sales were $21.4 million in 1995.
Vita expects to complete at least one acquisition by the end of the year.
Acquisition targets for Vita include companies that sell kosher food or products that could be certified as kosher.
One of the acquisition targets is related to seafood.
Over 95 percent of Vita's sales are kosher products.
Jay Dembsky, chief financial officer of Vita, estimated that the kosher food market is growing by 10 to 11 percent annually.
Vita plans to introduce two new products in 1997: a line of hummus and frozen salmon burgers.

Tung Chee-hwa is a shipping tycoon considered a favorite to govern Hong Kong after its return to China in 1997.
Tung Chee-hwa's company, Orient Overseas (International) Ltd, posted a legal notice seeking shareholder approval for deals linked to his brother-in-law's companies.
The Hong Kong business press interpreted the announcement as preparation for Tung's leadership bid.
The Hong Kong Economic Journal suggested the notice was likely Tung's final preparation for his candidacy for Chief Executive.
Analysts noted that the legal notice was unusually detailed.
The Hong Kong Economic Times' political editor stated the notice aimed to justify business circumstances and alleviate future political pressure on Tung's integrity.
Tung is the chairman of Orient Overseas (International) Ltd.
Tung's firm's purchase of shipping containers from his brother-in-law's companies could have been targeted by media scrutiny.
Political analysts indicated that the notice could help mitigate speculation against Tung.
Tung is considered a frontrunner for leadership due to his perceived admiration from both Britain and China.

Britain will hand Hong Kong back to China in less than 100 days.
The handover will end a century and a half of colonial rule.
The handover will also end a century and a half of Chinese national shame.
A two-day holiday celebration will occur, marked by fireworks and gun salutes.
The handover will take place at midnight on June 30 in Hong Kong.
Hong Kong's population is approximately 6.4 million people.
Prince Charles and Chinese President Jiang Zemin will attend the handover in Hong Kong.
Former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and Lee Kuan Yew will also be present.
Deng Xiaoping, China's paramount leader, died last month.
The joint handover ceremony will be held indoors at a new extension of Hong Kong's Convention Centre.

Tung Chee-hwa is the chief executive-designate of Hong Kong.
Tung Chee-hwa is a Confucian who emphasizes harmony and order.
Tung Chee-hwa's new offices have a view over a waterfall in Hong Kong Park.
Tung Chee-hwa's office is located on the seventh floor.
The transfer of sovereignty from British to Chinese rule will occur at midnight on June 30.
Tung Chee-hwa previously served as chairman of the Orient Overseas shipping company.
Tung Chee-hwa expressed concerns about political rifts and anxiety over lost freedoms.
Tung Chee-hwa criticized the Democratic Party for lobbying against China's plans for Hong Kong.
Tung Chee-hwa's new office is located in a prime commercial district of Hong Kong.
Tung Chee-hwa indicated he will not move into Government House due to concerns about 'fung shui'.

Air France aims to break even in 1997 and be privatised quickly.
Air France will lose its national monopoly on April 1 when domestic air travel in the European Union opens to competition.
Jean-Claude Baumgarten is a special adviser to Air France chairman Christian Blanc.
Baumgarten confirmed that Air France is on track for break-even and a share sale in late 1997 or early 1998.
Air France estimates a 200-million franc loss for 1996/97 at its international airline.
Losses at Air France Europe are expected to be less than a forecast 800 million francs.
A merger between Air France and Air France Europe must be completed before privatisation.
Air France Europe ground staff went on strike due to concerns over pay and conditions related to the merger.
A two-day strike by Air France Europe flight crew is scheduled to start on Easter Monday over similar pay concerns.
Air France Europe is expected to be close to break-even in 1997/98.

Thomson-CSF is a French defence electronics company.
Thomson-CSF posted a net profit of 745 million francs ($129 million) for 1996.
Thomson-CSF reported a net loss of 791 million francs ($137 million) for 1995.
Sales for Thomson-CSF increased by 2.2 percent to 36.27 billion francs ($6.3 billion).
The French government is attempting to privatise Thomson-CSF as part of a defence industry restructuring.
Alcatel Alsthom, Dassault Aviation, and Aerospatiale are bidding for Thomson-CSF.
Lagardere, supported by British Aerospace Plc, is also bidding for Thomson-CSF.
Thomson-CSF's operating profit rose by 5.6 percent to 2.07 billion francs ($358 million).
Thomson-CSF incurred an exceptional charge of 824 million francs ($143 million) for restructuring costs.
Thomson-CSF's consolidated pretax profit was 1.30 billion francs ($225 million), compared to a loss of 437 million francs ($76 million) the previous year.

The French government announced its readiness to relaunch the privatisation of Thomson-CSF.
Key executives have been appointed to oversee the sale of Thomson-CSF.
The French government stated that necessary decisions for the privatisation of Thomson-CSF have been made.
An attempt to sell Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe last year was rejected by the Privatisation Commission.
Marcel Roulet has been made responsible for the sale of Thomson-CSF on a full-time basis.
Marcel Roulet will now serve only as chairman of Thomson-CSF.
Thierry Breton has been appointed as chairman of Thomson SA and Thomson Multimedia.
Thierry Breton will be responsible for privatising Thomson Multimedia and will propose a sale soon.
The government plans to inject 11 billion francs into Thomson Multimedia by the summer, pending European Commission approval.
Thomson-CSF is 58 percent owned by Thomson SA and will be sold separately from Thomson Multimedia.

CVS Corp. is the fifth-largest chain of drug stores in the United States.
CVS Corp. will acquire Revco D.S. Inc. for $2.8 billion in stock and the assumption of $900 million of debt.
The merger will create the second-largest drug store chain in the United States.
The combined company will have about 4,000 stores and annual sales of $13 billion.
The new company will be named CVS and will retain the CVS headquarters in Woonsocket, R.I.
Revco's headquarters in Twinsburg, Ohio, will be phased out after the merger.
Most of the 1,000 employees at Revco's headquarters are likely to lose their jobs.
CVS Chief Operating Officer Thomas Ryan stated that the company will retain about 98 percent of Revco employees.
Revco Chief Executive Officer Dwayne Hoven will leave the company after the merger is completed.
The merger is not expected to generate significant antitrust concerns due to little geographic overlap between CVS and Revco.

ITT Corp. met with financial advisers to assess a $6.5 billion bid from Hilton Hotels Corp.
Some Wall Street analysts suggested that ITT's best defense might be to pursue an acquisition.
Industry experts indicated that ITT could avoid a takeover by making a large casino or hotel purchase.
Thomas Ryan of Bankers Trust stated that ITT has many connections on Wall Street and in the gaming industry.
ITT is expected to reject Hilton's offer, but no decision has been made and no acquisition talks are ongoing.
ITT's board will consider Hilton's bid at a scheduled meeting next Tuesday.
Hilton's offer values ITT at $55 per share and includes the assumption of $4 billion in debt.
ITT's stock fell to $56.875 after rising earlier in the week due to speculation about Hilton raising its bid.
ITT's financial advisers are expected to review Hilton's official bid documents filed with the SEC.
Industry experts believe a significant acquisition by ITT could make Hilton's takeover too costly.

Western Resources Inc. offered to buy ADT Ltd. for $3.5 billion in cash and stock.
The acquisition would make Western Resources the top provider of electronic security services in the nation.
Western Resources aims to dominate the fragmented security industry.
Western Resources holds a 27 percent stake in ADT.
Western Resources plans to take its offer directly to ADT shareholders.
Western Resources intends to call a special meeting to replace ADT's board of directors.
Western Resources Chairman John Hayes stated that the transaction offers compelling benefits.
Western Resources proposed to pay $22.50 for each share of ADT, consisting of $15 in stock and $7.50 in cash.
The offer represents a 12 percent premium over ADT's closing stock price of $20.125.
ADT will review the offer and has advised shareholders to await a recommendation from its board.

Regulators are expected to adopt an overhaul of the nation's telephone charges.
The Federal Communications Commission aims to ensure affordable phone service for Americans.
The FCC hopes the overhaul will encourage competition in the $200 billion phone industry.
FCC Chief Economist Joseph Farrell stated the goal is to reform charges and subsidies for better competition.
The new rules are designed to keep basic residential phone rates at current levels.
Customers making many long-distance calls are expected to see their monthly phone bills decrease.
Customers with multiple phone lines who make few or no long-distance calls are expected to see their costs increase.
The changes aim to cover the $2 billion to $3 billion cost of wiring schools, libraries, and rural hospitals to the Internet.
AT&T Corp. promised to lower its long-distance rates by 5 percent to 15 percent if the FCC agrees to reduce access charges.
Industry officials expect the FCC to ratify the reduction, allowing AT&T to offer its first major rate cut since 1992.

Regulators were set to give broadcasters free licenses for high-definition digital television.
High-definition digital television will begin reaching viewers in the top 10 markets within 18 months.
Federal Communications Commission officials agreed on rules for the roll-out of digital TV broadcasts.
The FCC scheduled a public meeting to approve the rules regarding digital TV broadcasts.
Critics argue that broadcasters are receiving a multi-billion dollar giveaway through free use of airwaves.
Congress decided to allow broadcasters to receive new licenses free of charge.
The FCC has valued the digital airwaves at up to $70 billion.
Broadcasters are required to return their existing analogue licenses to the government by 2006.
Digital TV offers crystal-clear pictures and CD-quality sound.
The top 10 markets for digital TV broadcasts are New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Philadelphia, San Francisco, Boston, Washington, Dallas-Fort Worth, Detroit, and Atlanta.

Pocket Communications Inc. filed for bankruptcy protection from its creditors.
Pocket Communications Inc. was the No. 2 bidder at a government wireless phone auction.
Pocket Communications Inc. bid $1.4 billion for 43 licenses for cellular service.
Pocket Communications Inc. defaulted on $80 million in loans.
The government auction totaled $10.2 billion.
Pocket Communications Inc. is the first company from the 1996 auction to file for bankruptcy protection.
Pocket Communications Inc.'s creditors include Asian entrepreneurs and Siemens AG and L.M. Ericsson.
Pocket Communications Inc. filed under Chapter 11 of the federal bankruptcy code.
The Federal Communications Commission suspended a March 31 payment deadline for PCS companies.
Pocket Communications Inc.'s bankruptcy filing may affect other auction winners seeking investment.

Sun Microsystems Inc unveiled its first mainframe-class server on Wednesday.
The entry into the mainframe market is valued at $50 billion.
Ed Zander is the president of Sun Microsystems Computer Co.
Zander expects the new machines to sell for an average price of more than $1 million.
The Ultra Enterprise 10000 servers can compete with mainframe computers on many performance measurements.
Zander stated that the sales cycle for the new servers would be longer than for Sun's traditional Unix products.
Sun expects to sell more of its Ultra Enterprise 5000 and 6000 midrange servers due to the new high-end machine.
The new server will begin shipping in volume in March.
C.B. Lee, a senior analyst at Sutro & Co, stated that the new server would be useful for complex database applications.
Montgomery Securities analyst Kurt King noted that the new machines may improve investor sentiment regarding competition from PCs.

Hewlett-Packard Co. agreed to acquire VeriFone Inc. in a stock swap worth $1.18 billion.
VeriFone will be operated as an independent unit of Hewlett-Packard.
VeriFone stockholders will receive one HP share for each VeriFone share.
Forrester Research estimates the market for business to business electronic commerce will increase from $600 million last year to $66 billion in the year 2000.
Forrester Research estimates consumer retail business will rise to $7 billion from $530 million in 1996.
Karen Epper, a Forrester Research analyst, stated that VeriFone will be significant in online payment.
Hewlett-Packard is the second-largest U.S.-based computer equipment company.
VeriFone had net revenue of $472 million in its 1996 fiscal year.
The acquisition price of $1.18 billion was based on HP's closing stock price of $50.50 a share.
VeriFone estimates that its systems handled more than $520 billion of the $800 billion in electronic transactions conducted in the United States last year.

USWeb Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Joe Firmage announced the launch of the second stage of the company's business plan.
USWeb plans to acquire affiliates in six U.S. metropolitan areas.
Joe Firmage started USWeb 13 months ago in Santa Clara.
The second phase of the plan involves expanding corporate-owned operations.
USWeb intends to expand internationally, particularly in Southeast Asia and Japan, by the end of October.
Next year, USWeb will focus on achieving profitability.
Firmage stated that the company aims to leverage its existing infrastructure starting January 1998.
USWeb seeks to achieve economies of scale in the market for services related to building Internet sites and intranets.
In its first phase, USWeb established franchises in 54 locations across 26 states.
USWeb was rated third for brand awareness among information technology executives, behind AT&T Corp and MCI Communications Corp.

The issue of corruption is a major concern for the people of Hong Kong after its return to China.
