Tung Chee-hwa is the future leader of Hong Kong.
Tung Chee-hwa's efforts to address fears about civil rights have overshadowed concerns about corruption.
Corruption has consistently ranked as the top concern in local surveys related to Hong Kong's return to China.
Michael DeGolyer is a political scientist at the Baptist University of Hong Kong.
DeGolyer stated that corruption was the primary concern in surveys conducted in July 1996, December 1996, and February 1997.
Political analysts believe that rising corruption associated with Hong Kong's handover to Chinese rule has significant implications.
Professor Joseph Cheng is from the City University of Hong Kong.
Cheng stated that the prosperity of Hong Kong relies on upholding the rule of law and respect for due process.
The Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) is recognized as vital to Hong Kong's reputation for business integrity.

Hong Kong's stock market has been reaching record highs in anticipation of business as usual after China takes control on July 1.
Not all share the optimism regarding Hong Kong's future competitiveness.
A group surrounding former shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa is anxious about Hong Kong's competitiveness.
Some advisers to Tung Chee-hwa support intervening in Hong Kong's economy.
There is uncertainty about what has made Hong Kong an economic success.
Key factors in Hong Kong's economic success include being a free port, having strong markets, easy international access, and a firm defense of the rule of law.
These key features are common in cities around the world.
Many believe Hong Kong's success relies on less quantifiable elements, including a 'borrowed time, borrowed place' mentality.
Chinese emigres in Hong Kong have used ingenuity and determination to become wealthy.
The success of Hong Kong Inc is feared to be more accidental than by design.

Hong Kong regulators are monitoring a dispute between Taiwan and Hong Kong regarding two call warrants linked to the Taipei index.
Bill Weeks is a spokesman for Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC).
Taiwan is considering legal action against the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong over the listing of two call warrants.
The two call warrants are issued by Peregrine Derivatives Ltd and Union Bank of Switzerland.
The SFC approved the concept of listing derivative warrants in Hong Kong.
The precise form of the warrants was determined by the Hong Kong exchange.
The Taiwan Stock Exchange claims the Taiwan weighted index is its proprietary product.
The Taiwan Stock Exchange expressed serious concern and objection to the new products.
The dispute is primarily a legal matter involving copyright and trademark issues.
The Hong Kong stock exchange stated that similar products are listed and traded in Luxembourg.

China called for a solution to the crisis involving a North Korean official in Seoul's mission in Beijing.
China suggested that Hwang Jang-yop sought refuge of his own free will.
Hwang Jang-yop is a senior aide to North Korea's leader Kim Jong-il.
Xinhua reported that Hwang arrived in Beijing on February 11 and stayed at the North Korean embassy.
Hwang left the North Korean embassy in Beijing the following morning and entered the South Korean embassy.
Pyongyang previously claimed that Hwang was kidnapped.
China expressed hope that the relevant parties would seek a proper solution to the incident.
Hwang remained in Seoul's consular compound after talks between South Korean and Chinese officials failed.
South Korean Foreign Ministry spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung stated that no real progress was made in talks with China regarding Hwang.
A South Korean Foreign Ministry official indicated that resolving the defection issue through direct talks with North Korea is impossible.

Chinese suitors are increasingly using Valentine's Day to express their feelings.
Rose merchants are experiencing significant profits on Valentine's Day.
Valentine's Day was banned during China's Cultural Revolution from 1966 to 1976.
Valentine's Day has become a day for public expressions of affection in China.
The Beijing Flower Supermarket supplies 80 percent of fresh flowers in the capital.
Sales at the Beijing Flower Supermarket are expected to increase by 400 percent on Valentine's Day.
Kong Li from the Beijing Huaxianzi Flower Delivery Co estimates that about one million flowers will be sold on Valentine's Day.
The flower industry in China began to grow in the mid-1980s.
Deng Xiaoping's reforms in 1992 significantly boosted the flower sector in China.
Fresh roses for Valentine's Day are primarily flown to Beijing from Guangzhou and Kunming.

Premier Li Peng stated that China would pursue a foreign policy of opening to the world, as initiated by Deng Xiaoping.
Li emphasized the importance of ties with the United States and Europe.
Li made these statements at the annual session of China's National People's Congress in Beijing.
Li placed less emphasis on relations with Japan, despite it being China's biggest trading partner.
Li delivered his speech in the Great Hall of the People, a venue associated with Maoist-era policies.
Li expressed a desire for further improvement in Sino-U.S. relations and strengthening of Sino-European relations.
China criticized the United States for failing to honor the terms of the Shanghai Communique during its 25th anniversary.
Relations between China and the United States deteriorated in 1995 and early 1996 due to various disputes.
Li briefly mentioned Sino-Japanese relations and expressed a wish for their normal development.
Li stated that China opposes interference in the internal affairs of other countries and claimed that a developed China would not pose a threat to any country.

Royal Bank of Scotland's telephone-based insurance subsidiary Direct Line believes the motor insurance cycle has bottomed.
Direct Line forecasts profits for the year will exceed last year's levels.
Direct Line is Britain's largest motor insurer.
Direct Line reported a small rise in pre-tax profits to eight million pounds for the six months to the end of March.
This is an increase from five million pounds twelve months ago.
George Mathewson is the chief executive of Royal Bank.
Mathewson stated that signs in the market indicate prices are beginning to recover.
The expected rise in profits for the current year is partly due to firming motor rates and improved claims experience.
The full effects of the recovery in the motor market are not expected to be fully reflected until next year.
Direct Line experienced an 86 million pound decline in profits to 26.5 million pounds last year due to intense competition.

Norwich Union is a British mutual insurer.
Norwich Union announced an increase in the members' offer for its flotation to 1.2 billion pounds.
The increase in the offer is due to strong demand from members.
Approximately 400 million pounds worth of shares will be reclaimed from the public offering to satisfy member demand.
Originally, 800 million pounds worth of shares were set aside for member applications.
Members are purchasing shares at a 25 pence per share discount to the public offer price.
The flotation marks the end of Norwich Union's status as a mutual insurer after over 200 years.
Demutualisation will allow Norwich Union to separate its life operations from its general insurance business.
The flotation is expected to value Norwich Union at around 5.5 billion pounds.
Nearly three million Norwich policyholders will receive 1.3 billion free shares in addition to discounted shares.

The Securities and Investments Board (SIB) is Britain's top financial regulator.
On Thursday, the SIB launched a 400,000 pound advertising campaign.
The campaign aims to increase public awareness of the review into pensions mis-selling.
The campaign is titled 'Have You Lost Out On Your Pension?'.
The advertisements will appear in the national press from Thursday to Sunday.
The campaign coincides with the mailing of questionnaires to individuals potentially mis-sold pensions.
The SIB stated that it is vital for investors to respond to the questionnaire.
Regulators recently moved to expedite compensation payments to victims of pension mis-selling.
Companies involved have been given an ultimatum to settle outstanding cases by the end of next year.
As many as 1-1/2 million people may have been wrongly advised regarding personal pensions.

Hong Kong's future lawmakers supported Beijing-backed plans to dilute civil liberties in the territory.
The pro-democracy camp protested against the future lawmakers' support for these plans.
The democratic camp accused the future lawmakers of selling out the people of Hong Kong.
Tsang Kin-shing, a legislator of Hong Kong's current elected chamber, expressed a lack of hope in the future lawmakers.
Tsang Kin-shing stated that the future lawmakers were acting in their own advantage.
The provisional legislature met in Shenzhen city to discuss the plans proposed by Hong Kong's future leader, Tung Chee-hwa.
The plans include requiring police permits for political protests and banning foreign funding of political groups.
Protests against the plans have come from Hong Kong's lawyers, human rights activists, Britain, and the United States.
Tung Chee-hwa argued that the curbs are necessary to preserve social order in Hong Kong.
The 60-member interim chamber agreed with the broad principles of the planned curbs.

Betty Tung is a middle-aged woman and a songwriter.
Betty Tung's solo debut occurred on a stage with Hong Kong popstars.
She has written the lyrics for a song that will be heard when Hong Kong rejoins China on July 1.
Betty Tung has been overshadowed by her husband, Tung Chee-hwa.
Tung Chee-hwa is the prospective leader of Hong Kong and an ex-shipping tycoon.
Betty Tung and Tung Chee-hwa will be Hong Kong's leading couple from midnight June 30.
Britain will hand over Hong Kong to China on July 1.
Betty Tung announced a musical gala on July 1 while elegantly dressed in a blue navy suit.
The song 'The Homecoming' features in the 'Hong Kong Medley' during the gala show.
Betty Tung stated that she does not know musical notes and downplayed her contribution to the song.

Hong Kong's luxury property market has declined since March 1997.
Property experts and developers predict a consolidation of the market before recovery in the third quarter of 1997.
Peter Lee, chairman for Asia with Jones Lang Wootton (JLW), stated that the market will consolidate barring further political and economic factors.
Charles Wheatman, Pacific director at JLW, indicated there may be a slight softness in the market for the next two months.
Prices of all types of flats have decreased by approximately 10 percent since March 1997.
The government implemented measures to curb high property prices in response to public anger.
Flats can now be pre-sold 15 months before completion, an increase from the previous 12 months.
Developers are required to offer flats in batches of no less than 20 percent of the total available.
Banks raised prime lending rates by 25 basis points to 8.75 percent, impacting the property market.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd believes its luxury development on Repulse Bay Road will not be affected by the recent price downturn.

International Business Machines Corp. reported fourth-quarter earnings that were slightly better than expected.
IBM's service business, growth in software sales, and tight expense controls contributed to the earnings report.
IBM's net income rose 17.6 percent to $2.0 billion in the quarter from $1.7 billion in the year-ago period.
Earnings per share increased from $3.09 to $3.93 due to 7 percent fewer shares outstanding.
Wall Street analysts expected earnings of $3.88 per share on average, according to First Call.
Some analysts suggested that IBM stock might face profit-taking pressure following the earnings report.
Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, described the results as excellent but anticipated brief selling.
David Takata, an analyst at Gruntal & Co., noted mixed results, with strong software and services but disappointing mainframe revenues.
IBM reported a 22 percent increase in service revenues and a rise in personal computer sales, while mainframe sales fell.
Overall revenues increased by 5.6 percent to $23.14 billion from $21.92 billion.

America Online Inc signed a marketing agreement with Tel-Save Holdings Inc.
The agreement provides AOL with an upfront payment of $100 million in cash.
Tel-Save will gain access to eight million AOL users through this deal.
AOL will promote Tel-Save's lower-cost long distance telephone service to its members.
AOL will receive warrants to buy shares of Tel-Save.
Analysts stated that the deal demonstrates AOL's ability to monetize its subscriber base.
Bob Pittman, chief executive of AOL Networks, commented on the deal's significance.
AOL must repay the $100 million, with the first $43 million due over ten quarters.
Tel-Save currently serves about 500,000 small and medium-sized businesses.
Tel-Save claims its long-distance service offers lower costs than competitors like AT&T Corp, MCI Communications Inc, and Sprint Corp.

CompuServe Corp is in talks to be acquired by America Online Inc.
The acquisition would bring new members to AOL and expand its corporate and international presence.
CompuServe and H&R Block Inc confirmed they were in discussions for a possible business combination.
H&R Block owns about 80 percent of CompuServe.
Industry sources indicated that AOL was involved in talks to buy CompuServe, possibly in an all-stock transaction.
Frank Dzubeck, president of Communications Network Architects, stated that the talks have intensified due to AOL's financial issues.
An H&R Block spokeswoman confirmed external discussions regarding a possible business transaction with CompuServe.
AOL declined to comment on the rumors of talks with CompuServe.
AOL shares increased on Tuesday but fell on Wednesday as analysts expressed concerns about the potential acquisition.
Analysts Jamie Kiggen and Abhishek Gami expressed skepticism about the value of acquiring CompuServe and its implications for AOL.

Sir Ian Prosser is the chairman of British brewer to leisure group Bass Plc.
Prosser warned shareholders that the business was running slightly behind its forecasts.
Bass shares fell by 21-1/2p to 831p following the trading statement.
The company's hotel chain Holiday Inn has made progress in the first 13 weeks of the year.
The rate of growth in dollar profits for Holiday Inn is below last year.
Brokers estimate Bass will report pretax profits of between 798 million and 670 million pounds in 1997.
In America, franchise revenue per available room from Holiday Inns grew by 7.0 percent in the first 13 weeks of the year.
In Europe, RevPar growth was 7.5 percent, while in Asia it fell by 4.0 percent due to a softening Chinese market.
In Bass Taverns, managed house turnover grew by 9.0 percent and food revenues increased by 21 percent.
Profits at Bass's other leisure retailing businesses were slightly ahead of last year, except for Gala.

B.A.T Industries Plc reported a five percent rise in 1996 profits to 2.495 billion pounds.
The profit increase was impacted by an exceptional charge of 160 million pounds for U.S. environmental claims.
Excluding the charge, profit rose by seven percent.
Chairman Lord Cairns stated that B.A.T dismissed any liability for damages claimed by smokers in U.S. lawsuits.
B.A.T kept an open mind on its corporate structure but did not announce any concrete plans.
Some analysts were disappointed over the exceptional insurance charge and hoped for news on a possible demerger of B.A.T's tobacco and insurance arms.
B.A.T shares fell by 20 pence to 530 pence in early trade.
Cairns expressed confidence that B.A.T Industries has no potential liability in U.S. tobacco litigation.
Cairns mentioned that the tobacco industry does not intend to offer a settlement but is open to evaluating proposals from third parties.
Michael Prideaux, B.A.T director of public affairs, stated that the company is keeping an open mind regarding a demerger.

Unilever NV/Plc reported a 15 percent rise in annual profits.
Unilever plans to sell its speciality chemicals units.
The sale of the speciality chemicals units is expected to raise up to 5 billion British pounds ($8.17 billion).
Pre-tax profit for Unilever rose to 2.66 billion pounds ($4.4 billion).
Revenues for Unilever increased by 6 percent to 33.52 billion pounds ($54.7 billion).
Unilever shares increased by 86-1/2 pence to 1,479-1/2 ($24.17) in London.
Chairman Niall FitzGerald stated that the sale would allow Unilever to focus on growth in consumer goods operations.
FitzGerald indicated that the economic situation in 1997 is likely to be generally favorable for Unilever.
FitzGerald expressed skepticism about improvements in economic conditions in Europe, particularly in France and Germany.
Analysts estimate that the sale of the chemicals business could fetch between 4.5 billion to 5 billion pounds ($7.35 billion to $8.17 billion).

The National Automobile Dealers Association annual convention will not be returning to Atlanta soon.
CarMax management requested a local policeman to remove three reporters from the CarMax lot in Norcross, Atlanta.
The policeman informed the reporters that people associated with the convention were banned from the store.
The incident illustrates the friction and hostility caused by new used car superstores and mega dealers.
Used car superstores account for a small fraction of the 40.8 million used cars sold in 1996.
H. Wayne Huizenga's Republic Industries Inc. is actively buying new vehicle dealerships.
Republic Industries owns the AutoNation USA chain and recently added two dealer groups.
Republic's estimated revenues for 1997 are projected to exceed $2.8 billion.
CarMax and Republic are significantly changing the traditional franchised dealer system.
Yale Gieszl, a Toyota Motor Corp. executive, criticized CarMax and stated Toyota would not grant them a new car franchise.

General Motors Corp. reported a fourth quarter earnings decline of more than half due to labor strife.
GM's fourth quarter earnings were $786 million, or 92 cents a share, down from $1.6 billion, or $1.95 a share, in the previous year.
The earnings figures exclude results from Electronic Data Systems Corp., which was spun off in June 1996.
GM's fourth quarter revenues decreased to $40.95 billion from $41.35 billion.
For the year 1996, GM earned $4.95 billion, or $6.06 a share, down from $6.03 billion, or $7.14 a share, in 1995.
Revenues for 1996 increased to $164.1 billion from $160.3 billion.
U.S. and Canadian auto workers struck GM plants in October and November 1996.
A United Auto Workers strike at two Dayton, Ohio brake plants disrupted GM's North American production for over two weeks.
The strikes reduced GM's full-year earnings by $1.2 billion and caused a fourth quarter loss of $124 million in North American operations.
GM's fourth quarter included extraordinary items that reduced earnings by $762 million, including $700 million in strike costs.

After 19 months of confrontations, six striking newspaper unions made an unconditional offer to return to work at Detroit's two major daily papers.
Al Derey is the head of the Metropolitan Council of Newspaper Unions.
Derey stated that the action was a tactic to expose the papers to financial losses if they do not agree to a fair contract.
Derey claimed that the strike has not ended and that the offer is a new strategy to win a fair contract.
About 2,500 workers walked off their jobs at the Detroit Free Press and Detroit News in July 1995 after contract talks collapsed.
The Detroit Free Press and Detroit News are editorially independent and have separate owners.
Knight-Ridder Inc. owns the Detroit Free Press.
Gannett Co. Inc. owns the Detroit News.
The papers have published every day since the strike began, although initially they published a single joint edition.
Since the start of the strike, circulation at the papers has fallen 30 percent and advertising revenues are down between 15 percent and 20 percent.

Citizens in China mourned the late leader Deng Xiaoping on Saturday.
The mourning was spontaneous due to a lack of official memorial activities.
State television broadcasted official tributes to Deng and memorial activities organized by Chinese officials in various cities.
In Beijing, the state did not encourage public mourning, leading citizens to organize their own tributes.
In Deng's home village of Paifang, tens of thousands of mourners gathered in the courtyard of his birthplace.
In Chengdu, mourners filled People's Square, with the crowd exceeding 10,000 by nightfall.
Many mourners in Chengdu carried candles and gathered around a statue of Mao Zedong.
Crowds in Chengdu thinned on Friday and Saturday, but many people were openly weeping over Deng's death.
In Shenzhen, hundreds of people visited a giant Deng billboard that had become a makeshift shrine.
Mourners placed wreaths and streamers with messages of gratitude for Deng's reforms at the billboard.

Premier Li Peng stated that China wanted a swift end to the crisis involving a senior North Korean defector in South Korea's mission in Beijing.
Li Peng indicated that stability on the Korean peninsula was a key consideration in resolving the standoff.
Li mentioned that conditions were nearly ripe for solving the problem regarding Hwang Jang-yop.
Hwang Jang-yop has sought refuge in Seoul's Beijing consulate since February 12.
Hwang Jang-yop is a senior ideological theoretician and top aide to Kim Jong-il.
Hwang has expressed a desire to go to South Korea.
Foreign diplomats have suggested that Hwang would likely be allowed to leave for a third country before traveling to Seoul.
The defection of Hwang Jang-yop has embarrassed Beijing, presenting a dilemma between North Korea and South Korea.
Li reiterated that China had jurisdiction over Hwang's asylum request since it was made in Beijing.
Li stated that China does not recognize the right of diplomatic asylum by foreign embassies or consulates in its territory.

China has significantly damaged its architectural heritage during its rapid development.
Beijing's old courtyards have been destroyed due to recent development.
The Beijing city wall, built to protect against invaders, has been largely dismantled.
The wall was dismantled after the communist takeover in 1949.
Beijing is attempting to restore a portion of the city wall.
Residents of Beijing are returning bricks to aid in the wall's restoration.
Approximately 30,000 bricks from the old wall have been donated for the restoration project.
The bricks are currently stored on a city lot for use in the restoration.
The wall was primarily constructed during the Ming dynasty, with some sections from the Yuan dynasty.
Large sections of the wall were demolished in the 1950s for the creation of Tiananmen Square.

Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato introduced legislation to prohibit banks from charging additional fees to non-customers using their automated teller machines.
About 54 percent of all automated teller machines impose a surcharge on non-customers, according to a survey by the General Accounting Office.
Alfonse D'Amato stated that ATMs were supposed to reduce costs and pass savings to consumers.
D'Amato claimed that banks are now saying ATMs are no longer cost-effective.
D'Amato accused banks of charging multiple fees to consumers for withdrawing money.
Consumer groups urged lawmakers to enact a ban on ATM surcharges.
Edmund Mierzwinski, programme director at the U.S. Public Interest Research Group, stated that surcharges threaten smaller banks.
Mierzwinski warned that if small bank customers switch to big banks to avoid surcharges, big banks may raise their fees due to reduced competition.
Banks denied that surcharges amount to double-dipping and argued that consumers benefit from the proliferation of ATMs funded by surcharge revenues.
Ed Yingling, executive director of the American Bankers Association, stated that consumers should decide if they are willing to pay for ATM convenience.

Federal bank regulators are urging U.S. financial institutions to prepare for potential computer problems in the year 2000.
Many computers and software programs only record the last two digits of a year, which could lead to confusion between the year 2000 and the year 1900.
Confused computers could cause issues such as bounced checks, missed loan payments, and miscalculated interest rates for banks.
Regulators informed Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato about the dangers associated with the year 2000 issue.
The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency have formed an interagency working group to address the year 2000 issue.
Comptroller Eugene Ludwig stated that the costs of making systems year 2000 compliant will be substantial and may impact some banks' earnings.
Experts believe that even well-prepared organizations will face some problems related to the year 2000 issue.
Nicholas Retsinas, director of the Office of Thrift Supervision, warned that the year 2000 rollover could pose substantial risks to the financial services industry.
Analysts estimate that corporations and governments may need to spend $300 to $600 billion worldwide to fix the year 2000 problem.
Bank examiners will inquire about year 2000 preparations this year to ensure solutions are implemented before the end of 1999.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin outlined a plan to overhaul Depression-era laws governing the U.S. financial sector.
The Clinton administration favored allowing banks to enter the securities and insurance fields.
Rubin stated that the lines separating insurance, securities, and banking industries have blurred due to new financial services and products.
The administration proposal was originally expected in March and is alongside several bills already introduced in Congress.
Rubin expressed a desire to work with Congress on this initiative.
Increased competition in financial services is expected to benefit consumers, generating savings of up to $15 billion a year.
The new proposal did not take a firm position on allowing banks to combine with non-financial, commercial firms.
Some lawmakers, smaller banks, and consumer groups oppose allowing banks to combine with commercial firms.
Insurance companies and securities firms argue they are intertwined with non-financial interests and need to compete with banks.
Rubin outlined two possible approaches regarding mixing banks with commercial firms.

The Czech Republic recorded its first budget deficit in 1996.
The budget deficit was 1.56 billion Czech crowns, equivalent to $57.28 million.
This was the first budget shortfall since the Czech Republic became a sovereign nation in 1993.
The Finance Ministry reported that revenues for 1996 totaled 482.8 billion crowns.
Expenditures for 1996 were 484.3 billion crowns.
The original 1996 budget was balanced at 497.6 billion crowns.
The forecast expenditure was later reduced to 491 billion crowns due to budget cuts.
Parliament approved a balanced budget plan for 1997 with both expenditures and revenues forecast at 549.1 billion crowns.
The 1997 budget was based on an expected economic growth of 5.4 percent.
Independent analysts forecasted economic growth for 1997 at under five percent.

The United States offered the Czech Republic free use of seven Navy Hornet aircraft for five years.
The U.S. Navy representatives offered to lease seven McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet fighter planes to the Czech Republic under a no-cost, five-year agreement.
The offer includes six single-seat F/A-18A and one two-seat F/A-18B aircraft.
The offer also includes the supply of replacement parts, pilot and ground personnel training programs, and support equipment at cost.
Lockheed Martin, SAAB and British Aerospace, and Dassault Aviation are also competing for post-Cold War business in central Europe.
It is unclear whether the aircraft in the U.S. offer will be used or new.
Czech pilots could begin training in the planes in six months.
Delivery of the aircraft is expected 18 months after the contract is signed.
McDonnell Douglas plans to locate production of components for the Hornet at Czech light jet maker Aero Vodochody.
The Czech government is debating aircraft purchases due to proposed cuts in defense spending.

The Czech Republic's trade deficit nearly doubled in January year-on-year.
The Czech Statistical Bureau reported a January trade deficit of 13.6 billion crowns.
The January trade deficit in 1996 was 7.86 billion crowns.
Imports grew by 8.2 percent year-on-year.
Exports contracted by 2.5 percent.
Raw material exports decreased by 11.8 percent.
Petr Tomek of Zivnostenska Banka stated that the figures were better than expected.
The Czech Statistical Bureau forecasted the 1997 trade deficit to rise to about 215 billion crowns.
Overall nominal imports for January were 60.04 billion crowns.
Exports for January totaled 46.45 billion crowns.

Merrill Lynch purchased an equities research and sales boutique in Italy.
The acquired firm is Carnegie Italia SpA, based in Milan.
Merrill Lynch previously acquired FG Inversiones in Spain for 3.7 billion pesetas ($29.5 million).
Merrill Lynch also bought British equities specialist Smith New Court last year.
Tony Morrongiello will lead Merrill Lynch's local institutional equity sales in Milan.
Merrill Lynch's Italian equity sales, research, and trading teams will collaborate with Morrongiello's team.
Paul Roy stated that the acquisition would enhance client service and leverage in the market.
Christopher Reeves identified Italy as a growth area for Merrill Lynch in various financial sectors.
Carnegie agreed to sell its Italian operations to Merrill Lynch to obtain capital for expansion in the Nordic region.
Merrill Lynch has previously relied on personnel from London and New York for investment banking deals in Europe.

National Westminster Bank Plc announced it would complete an internal investigation into a 50 million pound trading loss as quickly as possible.
A NatWest spokeswoman stated that the internal inquiry is ongoing.
NatWest revealed mispricing errors in the interest rate options book at its investment banking arm, NatWest Markets.
NatWest is employing an outside firm to assist with the investigation.
The investigation will include a thorough review of NatWest's control systems and is expected to take several weeks.
The Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) has been informed of the errors.
NatWest did not confirm whether it had meetings with the SFA over the weekend.
The Bank of England stated it would be looking into the situation.
Kyriacos Papouis was named as the interest rate options trader involved in the mispricing issue.
NatWest has not confirmed Papouis's involvement and he could not be reached for comment.

Judith Mayhew is the new head of the Corporation of London.
Mayhew stated that London will defend its share of foreign exchange trading after the introduction of a single European currency.
Mayhew emphasized the importance of maintaining market share.
The Corporation of London is the local authority for London's financial hub.
Mayhew identified three main challenges for the Corporation.
The first challenge is the survival of the Corporation to represent the views of the City.
The second challenge is to ensure that London is the primary market for the euro.
The third challenge is to ensure that LIFFE dominates the derivatives market for the European single currency.
Mayhew believes it is important for Britain to remain involved in negotiations regarding the single currency.
Mayhew stated that the Corporation aims to increase the number of global banking headquarters in the Square Mile.

A Chinese court sentenced dissident Li Hai to nine years in prison for prying into state secrets.
The trial was held behind closed doors.
A family member of Li Hai expressed surprise at the sentence.
Li Hai was initially charged with leaking state secrets.
Li's family and lawyer argued that he was not a civil servant and had no access to state secrets.
The court lacked evidence to convict Li of leaking state secrets.
Li's relative believed the appeal process had already started.
The appeals trial is also expected to be held behind closed doors.
Li Hai has not been allowed to meet his family since his detention in May 1995.
Li Hai was first arrested in May 1990 for his role in the 1989 student demonstrations for democracy.

A Chinese court has agreed to hear a lawsuit by Liu Nianchun accusing the government of illegal incarceration.
Liu Nianchun's wife stated that finding a defense lawyer has been difficult.
Beijing's Chaoyang District Court has accepted Liu Nianchun's lawsuit.
Liu Nianchun's family lacks financial resources to hire a lawyer.
Several lawyers have faced government pressure not to take Liu Nianchun's case.
Beijing's Dongcheng District Court has agreed to hear Wang Hui's lawsuit against the police.
Wang Hui accused police of illegally detaining her from May 16 to June 13.
Wang Hui also accused five guards at a detention center of beating her after the guards had been drinking.
Wang Hui demanded 10,000 yuan in compensation, a public apology, and punishment of the guards.
Liu Nianchun and Zhou Guoqiang are both serving three-year sentences of re-education through labor.

China's propaganda machine praised the selection of Hong Kong's first post-colonial chief executive as the beginning of true democracy.
The China Daily described the election of Tung Chee-hwa as a significant moment in Hong Kong's democratic development.
Tung Chee-hwa was elected by a 400-member Selection Committee chosen by Beijing.
Tung Chee-hwa will officially assume the role of chief executive when Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on June 30, 1997.
Major Chinese newspapers reported on Tung's election with prominent coverage and images.
The official Xinhua news agency characterized Hong Kong-style democracy as distinct from both the mainland and the West.
Xinhua stated that Hong Kong is establishing a democratic system that is lawful, open, fair, civilized, and orderly.
China plans to dismantle Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council after the handover and replace it with an appointed legislature.
Xinhua criticized British rule in Hong Kong, claiming there was no democracy during that period.
Xinhua asserted that China's resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong provides an opportunity for democratic development.

Macquarie Bank Ltd is Australia's largest locally-owned investment bank.
Macquarie Bank posted an annual profit of A$116.94 million for the year to March 31.
Macquarie's net profit increased by 25.4 percent compared to the previous year.
The return on average shareholder funds for Macquarie was 25.2 percent.
Macquarie raised its annual dividend to 43 cents from 36 cents the previous year.
Earnings per share for Macquarie rose to 74.9 cents from 61 cents.
Analysts had forecast a net profit of around A$105 million for Macquarie.
Macquarie's Corporate Advisory division had 130 advisory mandates during the year.
Simon Hannes, a senior corporate advisory executive at Macquarie, was charged with insider trading.
Macquarie's managing director Allan Moss stated that the Hannes matter did not affect corporate advisory work.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia warned that proposed changes to Australia's prudential regulation system could lead to significant collapses.
David Murray is the Managing Director of Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Murray stated that proposals to regulate banks and non-banks within the same prudential system are too risky.
Murray compared the proposed system to the U.S. savings and loan sector before its collapses in the 1980s.
Murray criticized the plan to increase competition in the banking payments system and remove the Reserve Bank of Australia's prudential supervision role.
Murray's criticism is the first major opposition to the Wallis report since its release.
The Liberal/National government is considering the recommendations from the Wallis Inquiry.
Murray's comments were labeled as emotive scare-mongering by an audience member at a CEDA luncheon.
Murray emphasized the importance of debating Wallis' plan and being critical of it.
The Reserve Bank currently requires banks to meet strict prudential requirements and restricts non-banks from issuing cheques.

Bank of Melbourne Ltd announced a A$1.435 billion takeover bid by Westpac Banking Corp.
The takeover bid valued Bank of Melbourne at 2.1 times net assets.
Bank of Melbourne and Westpac will merge their retail operations in Victoria.
The merged entity will trade under the Bank of Melbourne brand name with local management.
The merger is subject to the approval of Treasurer Peter Costello and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
Westpac will offer A$9.75 for each Bank of Melbourne ordinary share, including a 90 cent per share special dividend.
Shareholders can choose to receive the A$8.85 balance in cash or in the form of one Westpac share plus up to A$1.85 in cash.
Westpac will offer A$15.36 in cash for each converting preference share or a combination of Westpac shares and cash up to A$1.36.
The offer represents an earnings multiple of 15.2 times 1997 prospective earnings as forecast by Barceps.
The ACCC will examine the merger proposal over the next several weeks.

Mercury Finance Co. secured $50 million in short-term financing from Bank of America.
The financing provides Mercury with the ability to work on longer-term financing.
Some competitors in the automotive financing market are interested in purchasing Mercury's assets.
Mercury has directed interested parties to Salomon Brothers, its adviser.
The financing from Bank of America is secured by Mercury's assets.
The funds will be used for day-to-day operating expenses and upcoming interest payments.
Mercury continues to serve customers at all its locations.
Mercury was unable to refinance $61 million in short-term debt that matured through February 5.
Another $127 million in debt is due between February 5 and February 14.
Mercury had to restate its earnings downward by about $90 million due to accounting discrepancies.

Mercury Finance Co. announced it would be unable to pay $17 million in commercial debt due on Friday.
The company's stock lost nearly 90 percent of its value, dropping from $13 to $1.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The stock traded over 27 million shares and fell as low as $1.625.
Mercury Finance Co. had more than 172 million shares outstanding as of early November, resulting in a loss of over $2.2 billion in market capitalization.
The company reported problems in its bookkeeping that led to an overstatement of earnings by $90 million over four years.
Due to downgrades from several debt rating services, Mercury Finance Co. could not issue new short-term debt to repay maturing debt.
Standard & Poor's Corp. and Fitch Investors Service downgraded the company's commercial paper to a default rating.
Mercury Finance Co. was in discussions with its lenders regarding its working capital needs but could not predict the outcome.
The company retained Salomon Brothers Inc. to advise on its current and future capital needs.
A class-action lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court in Chicago, accusing Mercury Finance Co. of violating securities laws.

TCF Financial Corp. is a bank holding company.
TCF Financial Corp. signed a letter of intent to acquire Winthrop Resources Corp. for about $326 million.
Under the agreement, TCF will offer one share of its stock for every 1.2877 shares of Winthrop in a tax-free pooling of interests.
TCF has suspended its share repurchase program due to the pending acquisition.
Winthrop Resources Corp. has leased assets of $327 million and specializes in leasing high technology and business equipment.
Winthrop Resources Corp. is based in Minneapolis.
Winthrop will become a subsidiary of TCF Bank Minnesota after the acquisition.
The deal values Winthrop at $36.50 a share based on a TCF stock price of $47.
TCF shares fell to $46.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The deal is expected to close by the third quarter, pending negotiation of a definitive agreement and approvals.

Molson Cos Ltd will hold its annual shareholder meeting on Wednesday.
Molson Cos Ltd is under pressure for a stock buyback.
Molson Cos Ltd is searching worldwide for a brewing acquisition.
The meeting marks the debut of a new chief executive.
The new chief executive aims to lead the company's return to its brewing roots.
Molson is close to completing the C$1 billion sale of its Diversey Corp chemicals unit.
Molson is looking for overseas opportunities to expand its core brewing business.
Some investors are pushing for a share buyback due to concerns about acquisition costs.
Molson owns 40 percent of Canada's largest brewer, Molson Breweries.
Molson Breweries is also owned 40 percent by Foster's Brewing Group Ltd and 20 percent by Miller Brewing unit.

Ontario Finance Minister Ernie Eves stated that the government was ahead of its revised deficit target for 1996/97.
Eves indicated that the province may balance its budget before the year 2000.
Eves mentioned that he does not feel obligated to accelerate the timetable for the next stage of the government's planned 30 percent income tax cut.
The Conservative government will present its second full budget on May 6 since taking power in 1995.
Eves revised the 1996/97 deficit down to C$7.67 billion from an original forecast of C$8.2 billion.
Eves suggested that the economy performed well and that the deficit might be slightly better than the revised figure.
Eves declined to comment on predictions that the 1996/97 deficit would fall below C$7 billion.
Some analysts speculated that the government could eliminate the deficit by fiscal 1999/2000, one year ahead of plan.
Eves stated that balancing the budget ahead of schedule would require significant economic growth.
Eves confirmed that he would use conservative economic forecasts in the upcoming budget.

Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd. increased on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
The stock price of Bre-X rose C$1.22 to close at C$3.62.
Bre-X traded 17 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
The stock reached a session high of C$5.75 during late afternoon trading.
Bre-X has faced controversy due to preliminary tests by Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. indicating the gold deposit may contain insignificant amounts of gold.
The announcement of preliminary test results caused panic selling of Bre-X shares, reducing the company's market value by over 80 percent.
Reports indicated that Freeport received independent tests of the Busang deposit, which were disputed by Freeport and Bre-X officials.
Freeport's spokeswoman stated that testing is ongoing and no assay results have been communicated to Freeport.
Bre-X commissioned Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. to conduct an audit of its Busang project, with results expected in early May.
Bre-X released drill results from 22 holes at the Busang property, with 16 holes showing varying amounts of gold and six holes showing no significant amounts.

Chrysler Corp. developed a new method to extract hydrogen from gasoline.
The new method could accelerate the introduction of super-efficient electric cars by 10 years.
Chrysler's system uses normal gasoline to obtain hydrogen.
The future car powered by this system is expected to have a 50 percent increase in fuel efficiency over current cars.
Cars using this hydrogen extraction system would be more expensive than internal combustion engine cars.
Chrysler officials stated the system could be commercially viable between 2010 and 2015.
Drivers of gasoline fuel cell cars would refuel at normal gasoline stations.
Chrysler aims to have a working test vehicle within three years.
Francois Castaing, Chrysler's vice president of vehicle engineering, stated that hydrogen needs to be processed from gasoline on-board vehicles.
The on-board 'refinery' system faces significant development hurdles and currently costs about $30,000.

Canada's Magna International Inc. will acquire Douglas & Lomason Co. for about $135 million in cash.
Magna made a $31-a-share tender offer for all of Douglas & Lomason's 4.45 million common shares outstanding.
Douglas & Lomason shares rose 37.5 cents to $26.125 on Nasdaq prior to the merger announcement.
The acquisition will enhance Magna's North American car and truck seating business.
Douglas & Lomason had 1995 revenues of $561 million.
Douglas & Lomason was finding it difficult to compete for new seating contracts from automakers.
Douglas & Lomason earned $11.2 million on sales of $299 million in the first six months of 1996.
Some analysts suggested the deal was encouraged by Ford Motor Co. to strengthen Magna's competitiveness.
Douglas & Lomason currently supplies seats for the Ford Contour and Mystique cars.
Magna's traditional strength has been in instrument panels, door panels, and other interior components.

Chrysler Corp. broke ground on a $10 million historical museum.
The museum will be located on the grounds of Chrysler's corporate headquarters and technical center.
The museum will cover 35,000 square feet and house vintage vehicles, company archives, and a theater.
This museum will be the first company-owned museum among Detroit's Big Three automakers.
Mercedes-Benz AG and Bayerische Motoren Werke AG have museums in Stuttgart and Munich, respectively.
Chrysler's Historical Museum will eventually open to the public and aims to instill pride in employees.
The project indicates Chrysler's confidence in its future and a shift in its fortunes since financial difficulties in 1980 and 1991.
Chrysler nearly sold its collection of vintage vehicles in the late 1970s to raise cash.
Chrysler's largest shareholder, Kirk Kerkorian, has encouraged stock buybacks totaling $4 billion over two years.
Eaton indicated that Lee Iacocca's role in Chrysler's history may be featured in the museum.

Ford Motor Co announced 1,300 job cuts at its plant in northwest England.
Unions raised the possibility of strikes in the British automobile industry following Ford's announcement.
Ford's Halewood factory near Liverpool received a global quality award for 1996.
Ford stated that the new version of its mid-range Escort would not be built at the Halewood factory.
The new Escort model is likely to be built in Spain and Germany.
Ford's proposed job cuts will reduce Halewood's workforce to just over 3,000.
Halewood's workforce peaked at 14,000 in the 1960s and was around 4,500 before the cuts.
British Prime Minister John Major described Ford's decision as 'very surprising' and contrary to investment trends in the UK.
Unions plan to hold mass meetings at Ford plants to discuss potential protest actions against the job cuts.
Workers will be asked to support measures, including a ballot for strike action, to secure the future of Halewood.

1,300 jobs were cut at Ford Motor Co's Halewood plant in Northern England.
The job cuts at Ford dented Northern England's record of attracting foreign firms.
Cheap local labor, flexible employment rules, and government laws have attracted foreign investors to Northern England.
Companies that have invested in Northern England include Nissan Motor Co, Siemens, Samsung Co, and Vauxhall.
Prime Minister John Major stated that the job cuts went against the trend of investment.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke commented that 'You can't win them all.'
Professor Charles Bean of the London School of Economics stated that low firing costs make foreign companies more likely to create jobs in the UK during good times and cut jobs during tough times.
Christine Kennedy, a spokeswoman for Northern Development Co, claimed that foreign investment has contributed to the regeneration of the north.
Inward, the north west's corporate development body, reported that 2,600 jobs were created in the region in the financial year 1995/96.
Liverpool Chamber of Commerce policy executive Peter Rigby noted that the discovery of oil and gas in Liverpool Bay could create up to 2,000 jobs.

Racal Electronics announced an alliance with ITT Defence for a defense contract.
The defense contract is valued at two billion pounds ($3.4 billion).
David Elsbury is the chief executive of Racal Electronics.
The alliance could yield joint savings of 100 million pounds in development costs.
The Bowman communications contract decision is due by March 1997.
The contract is important for Racal's future earnings and for Siemens of Germany.
The winner of the Bowman contract could receive an estimated two billion pounds in follow-through export orders.
Winning the contract would create 6,500 new jobs.
If Racal loses the contract, it may need to downsize the company.
Racal's costs to date for the contract are between 30 and 50 million pounds.

3Com Corp. proposed a $6.6 billion acquisition of U.S. Robotics Corp.
The acquisition proposal caused a drop in the stocks of 3Com and U.S. Robotics.
3Com's stock fell $4 to $35 and was the most heavily traded issue on Nasdaq.
More than 40 million shares of 3Com changed hands on Nasdaq.
U.S. Robotics' stock dropped $1.875 to $59.125 and was the second-most active share on Nasdaq.
Analysts claimed the proposed stock swap undervalued U.S. Robotics.
Eric Buck, an analyst at Donaldson Lufkin, criticized the terms of the deal.
The offer involved stock and options valued at $7.3 billion.
Peter Swartz, a Salomon analyst, described the deal as a 'take-under' rather than a takeover.
U.S. Robotics Chairman Casey Cowell stated the sale price was not too low.

A coalition of 28 computer and communications equipment makers announced a plan to develop a common standard for faster modems.
The coalition aims to create modems that operate at speeds up to 56 kilobits per second.
U.S. Robotics Corp. is not a member of the coalition.
U.S. Robotics is the leading maker of consumer modems and is credited with pioneering the development of 56-kilobit modems.
U.S. Robotics began shipping its 56-kilobit modems earlier in the week of the announcement.
3Com Corp. announced it would acquire U.S. Robotics in a deal valued at $6.6 billion.
Faster modems will reduce the time required to access web pages or download software.
The 56-kilobit-per-second speed would double the speed of current 28.8-kilobit-per-second modems.
The standards group is called the Open 56 Forum and includes support from companies like Rockwell International Corp., Lucent Technologies Inc., and Motorola Inc.
U.S. Robotics was invited to join the Open 56K Forum shortly before the coalition's announcement.

Lucent Technologies Inc expects its consumer products unit to show substantial profit gains in 1997.
Lucent Technologies Inc expects a return to revenue growth in the consumer products unit by the December quarter.
Chief Financial Officer Don Peterson stated that profitability improvements will mainly come from cost-cutting.
Lucent Technologies Inc reported a 41 percent decline in consumer product revenues in the second quarter ended in March.
Consumer products comprised a small fraction of total revenues of $5.15 billion in the March quarter.
The consumer products unit was the only Lucent unit not to see double-digit growth in the March quarter.
The division's revenues fell to $174 million in the March quarter due to the closing of phone center stores and reduced revenue from phone rentals.
Lucent's carrier network systems division revenues increased by 23.3 percent to $2.93 billion.
Lucent's business communications unit revenues rose by 14.1 percent to $1.3 billion.
Lucent's semiconductor revenues gained 18.3 percent to $615 million.

Two troubled banks in Japan took action on Tuesday to address financial issues.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd announced a radical restructuring.
Hokkaido Takushoku Bank found a merger partner.
These actions are part of a broader effort by the banking industry to prepare for financial deregulation in Japan.
Nippon Credit Bank will cease overseas operations and sell its Tokyo headquarters and other properties.
Nippon Credit Bank plans to write off bad loans totaling 460 billion yen ($3.7 billion).
Hokkaido Takushoku Bank will merge with Hokkaido Bank Ltd and cease overseas operations.
Nippon Credit Bank expects the restructuring to boost earnings by 50 billion yen ($403 million) over five years.
The Japanese government is supporting Nippon Credit Bank's survival by urging other banks to accept newly floated shares.
Financial analysts have criticized Nippon Credit Bank's restructuring plan as insufficient to address its bad loan issues.

Japanese prosecutors raided Nomura Securities Co Ltd on Tuesday.
The raid is part of a widening investigation into payments linked to racketeers.
Prosecutors and officials from the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) conducted the raid.
The raids signal a potential showcase for Japan's efforts to improve business practices and deregulate the economy.
Ninety officials conducted searches at ten other locations alongside the raid on Nomura's headquarters.
Deputy chief prosecutor Kunihiro Matsuo stated the investigation involves a Nomura director's illegal payment of 38 million yen to a company linked to a racketeer.
The payment was made to avoid disruption of a Nomura annual meeting.
The raids included searches of the homes of the racketeer and Nomura director Shimpei Matsuki.
Nomura directors Shimpei Matsuki and Nobutaka Fujikura resigned after internal probes revealed illegal activities.
Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki stepped down on March 14 and became an adviser to the company.

Japan's Finance Ministry is unlikely to take punitive actions against Nomura Securities Co Ltd for some time.
The Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) plans to file a complaint against Nomura with prosecutors this week.
The SESC usually recommends punitive action to the Finance Minister after prosecutors complete their investigation.
The duration of the prosecutors' investigation depends on how far they intend to pursue the case.
Japanese newspapers reported that the SESC plans to file a complaint against former Nomura executives and Nomura itself.
Tokyo prosecutors plan to launch a full-scale investigation of the Nomura scandal.
Nomura is suspected of violating the Securities and Exchange Law and the Commercial Code.
Nomura is suspected of illegally using discretionary stock dealings to compensate a corporate client for stock trading losses.
The term 'sokaiya' refers to individuals who extort money from companies by threatening to disrupt shareholders' meetings.
Japan's commercial law has prohibited payoffs to sokaiya since 1982.

China is likely to slow the pace of reform in its financial markets.
Stability is the top priority for China's leaders this year.
China's leaders are managing multiple significant issues, including the return of Hong Kong and the Communist Party's 15th Congress.
Bold reforms in the financial sector are unlikely before these pressing issues are resolved.
Pressure to advance financial reforms will increase throughout the year.
One European banker stated that the intention will be to maintain tight control until after the Party Congress.
A Shanghai brokerage analyst indicated that new regulations and changes will be approached cautiously.
The main policy regarding financial markets is expected to remain unchanged.
The development of the stock market is not expected to change despite Deng Xiaoping's death.
The Beijing leadership is awaiting the release of the long-delayed Securities Law, Futures Law, and Investment Fund Law.

China is building a network of major toll highways to supplement its railway system.
China plans to float stock for many of the roads to fund the highway expansion.
Some brokers question the decision to use equity to finance the highway construction programme.
Chinese officials estimate that $65 billion will be needed for highway construction in the next five years.
Funding shortfalls for highway construction are expected to be between 15 to 25 percent of the total.
China's first international-standard highways began to appear at the beginning of this decade.
By the end of 1996, China had 3,258 km of express highway.
There are plans to add a further 900 km of toll road in 1997.
Two Chinese highways have already listed shares on stock exchanges, with more expected to follow.
Anhui Expressway successfully listed in Hong Kong last November, encouraging more highway listings.

China financial markets experienced an initial drop in stock prices following the death of Deng Xiaoping.
Analysts warned that trading could be volatile for some time after Deng's death.
Foreign brokers predicted strong buying by foreign investors due to the removal of the 'Deng factor'.
Most shares in Shanghai opened at the 10 percent limit-down level after Deng's death.
Shanghai's domestic A share index increased by 0.28 percent to 1007.731 points by the end of trading.
The foreign currency B share index decreased by 0.7 percent to 64.675 points by the end of trading.
Shenzhen's B share index rose by 1.26 percent to 143.53 points, while the A share index fell by 2.11 percent to 350.59 points.
Alex Conroy, a stock analyst with ING-Barings, noted that the speed of the market's reaction was surprising.
Brokers indicated that prices were supported by bargain hunting and heavy support-buying by domestic institutions.
The foreign exchange market remained unaffected by Deng's death, with the Chinese yuan closing at 8.2939 against the U.S. dollar.

Hundreds of mining prospectors are currently exploring a 617,500-hectare area in the Temagami region of Northern Ontario.
The Ontario government made this land available for exploration for the first time in 23 years.
There is a shortage of experienced prospectors in the area.
Big companies have trained local high school track teams to assist in the prospecting efforts.
Provincial government geologist Elaine Basa stated that the area has a lot of potential and is like virgin territory.
Up to 600 prospectors, many hired by international mining companies, are searching for gold or base metals.
The land is located near existing gold mines and old copper and base metal mines.
The Ontario government closed off the area in 1973 after a local Indian band laid claim to the land, which was struck down in 1991.
Major international mining companies, small explorers, and independent prospectors are participating in the staking rush.
Prospectors have 31 days to file their claims after staking the corners of their properties.

Canada is raising the amount of investment required from prospective immigrants seeking to settle in the country.
Immigration Minister Lucienne Robillard announced the increase on Friday.
Foreigners seeking to live in Canada may be granted an immigrant visa by pledging to invest in the economy.
Robillard stated that the required investment amount would be raised to avoid abuse and ensure adequate economic impact.
The basic selection criteria for investor entry to Canada will not change.
The amounts needed to invest, the ways in which that capital can be used, and the administration of the program will change.
Robillard claimed that the changes are intended to ensure growth and employment at the local level.
Robillard denied that passage into Canada was for sale and stated that citizenship is not for sale in the country.
Investors account for about three percent of total immigration to Canada each year.
The current investment requirement is $250,000 Canadian, which will be raised to C$450,000 for Quebec, Ontario, Alberta, and British Columbia, and to C$350,000 for the rest of Canada.

There is a large discrepancy between two recent statistical reports on job creation in Canada.
The payroll report showed the creation of 301,000 jobs in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The labor force survey showed the creation of about 86,000 jobs in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The labor force survey includes self-employed and agricultural workers and measures the unemployment rate.
Statistics Canada officials downplayed the discrepancy between the two reports.
The unemployment rate in Canada has remained just below 10 percent.
Mike Sheridan is the director-general of labor and household surveys at Statistics Canada.
Sheridan stated that the two surveys do not measure the same thing in the short term.
For all of 1996, the labor force survey showed an increase of 186,000 jobs, while the payroll numbers showed an increase of 195,000 jobs.
Economists tend to place more weight on the labor force survey than the payroll numbers.

Unisys Corp is based in the U.S.
Unisys Corp appealed to the Czech Economic Competition Office against a Defence Ministry decision.
The Defence Ministry awarded an army contract to a consortium of Electronic Data Systems and Digital Equipment Corp.
Unisys submitted a proposal for investigation of the Defence Minister's decision.
Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny rejected a first round appeal by Unisys and IBM Corp.
Vyborny believes his decision to award a 1.3 billion crown army information system deal to EDS-Digital was correct.
The installation of the staff information system is intended to enhance compatibility with NATO's military command.
Vyborny chose EDS-Digital despite a recommendation from a steering committee to select Unisys's bid.
Unisys claims that the price of EDS-Digital's bid was not weighted according to tender rules.
Unisys won a four billion crown supply tender last year, which was cancelled due to irregularities.

Czech ultra-right Republicans staged a demonstration as German Chancellor Helmut Kohl arrived to sign a post-war reconciliation accord.
The demonstration took place at Prague's Liechtenstein Palace.
About a hundred supporters of the Republican Party protested during Kohl's arrival.
Protesters yelled slogans such as 'go home' and 'Czech lands for the Czechs.'
Some protesters carried banners with slogans referencing the 1938 Munich Agreement.
Kohl waved to the demonstrators as he entered the palace.
The accord includes expressions of sorrow from Bonn for the Nazi occupation of the Czech lands from 1938 to 1945.
The accord also includes Prague's regret for the post-war expulsion of 2.5 million Sudeten Germans.
The accord includes German support for Czech membership in the European Union and NATO.
Republican Party chairman Miroslav Sladek stated that the document aims to finalize the liquidation of the Czech nation.

The Czech Agriculture Ministry announced plans to privatise Budejovicky Budvar n.p.
Budejovicky Budvar n.p. brews Czech Budweiser beer.
The privatisation will occur through a management buyout.
Talks with Anheuser Busch Cos broke down last year.
Jiri Stehlik is the head of the ministry's privatisation department.
The plan includes selling a 10 percent stake in Budvar to management.
Management will have the option to buy an additional 41 percent stake.
The plan follows the breakdown of talks with Busch over the Budweiser trademark.
Budvar is located in Ceske Budejovice, which is known as Budweis in German.
The government aims to keep Budvar primarily in Czech hands during privatisation.

Deng Xiaoping attempted political reform in China.
Deng Xiaoping's political reform is considered a failure.
Jiang Zemin was Deng Xiaoping's anointed heir.
Deng Xiaoping died at the age of 92.
Deng Xiaoping raised the prospect of democracy in China.
Tens of millions of peasants were given the right to elect local representatives under Deng Xiaoping.
Deng Xiaoping failed to establish a power transfer structure.
Deng Xiaoping viewed political reform as essential for the survival of Communist Party rule.
Deng Xiaoping aimed to separate party and government roles.
Deng Xiaoping's reforms led to a system where the party influenced the government.

Chinese President Jiang Zemin refused a request from his predecessor, Zhao Ziyang, to attend the funeral of Deng Xiaoping.
Jiang did not provide a reason for barring Zhao from attending the memorial rites.
Deng Xiaoping died in Beijing at the age of 92.
Deng's memorial rites are scheduled to be held in the Great Hall of the People on Tuesday.
Zhao Ziyang was in Hangzhou for the Chinese lunar New Year when he learned of Deng's death.
Zhao sent a request to Jiang and other leaders to return to Beijing after Deng's death.
Zhao lives under virtual house arrest in Beijing and requires approval from top leadership to move around China.
Jiang rejected Zhao's request despite Deng's family and some party veterans agreeing to allow him to attend the funeral.
Zhao renewed his request on February 21, but the leadership had not responded.
Zhao has not been seen in public since May 19, 1989, when he visited students at Tiananmen Square.

China criticized U.S.-based Human Rights Watch for defending political prisoners it claims are convicted rapists and swindlers.
The official Xinhua news agency stated that the World Report 1997 contains malicious and slanderous attacks against China's human rights situation.
Beijing views criticism of its human rights record as interference in its internal affairs.
China prioritizes fulfilling the rights of its 1.2 billion people to food and clothing.
Xinhua quoted an official stating that the report mislabels criminals convicted of hooliganism, swindling, bribery, embezzlement, and endangering state security as 'dissidents' and 'political prisoners'.
China has jailed several dissidents for crimes including hooliganism and plotting to subvert the state.
Some dissidents have been sentenced to up to three years of re-education through labor.
Robin Munro from Human Rights Watch/Asia stated that China is trying to discredit and undermine human rights charges instead of responding to criticisms.
The report confirmed that Guo Haifeng received a five-year jail term for hooliganism.
Xinhua reported that Guo Haifeng later committed rape against six women, which it classified as hooliganism.

Richard Stirland is the director-general of the Orient Airlines Association (OAA).
Stirland expressed concern about potential cost increases at Hong Kong's new airport.
The new airport at Chek Lap Kok is set to replace Kai Tak in 1998.
Stirland stated that charges at the new airport may double.
The OAA represents 16 major carriers in Asia, including Singapore Airlines Ltd, Japan Airlines Co Ltd, Thai Airways International Ltd, and Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd.
Stirland indicated that some cargo airlines may choose to fly to cheaper alternatives like Macau, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen.
He compared the situation to Europe, where freighter operators use smaller, cheaper airports instead of major ones like Heathrow or Paris-Charles de Gaulle.
Currently, a two-hour stop in Hong Kong costs around US$24,000, while it costs $23,000 at Singapore's Changi.
The new Hong Kong Airport Authority stated that charges will inevitably rise, but claims of doubling are considered speculation.
Cathay Pacific expressed concern that rising fees would negatively impact airlines and Hong Kong's status as a regional hub.

Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals Limited (HACTL) is developing a new computerised memory system.
The new system aims to ensure pallets fit into aircraft on the first attempt.
The deputy managing director of HACTL is Yueng Kwok Keung.
HACTL's new system is provisionally called the Pallet Contour Identification System.
The system is designed to save time, money, and reduce disputes with truck drivers.
Arriving cargo will pass through a gantry with precise measurement sensors.
The sensors send high-speed signals to a computer to create a three-dimensional picture.
A memory bank contains a catalogue of all possible container contours and dimensions of aircraft using HACTL.
If a container fits, the computer identifies it as 'good to go'; if not, it is rejected.
HACTL plans to test the prototype in the second quarter of the year at Kai Tak.

Air Canada reported a profit on its Hong Kong-Vancouver route, which is celebrating its first year of operations.
Lamar Durrett is the president and chief executive officer of Air Canada.
Air Canada carried 34,000 passengers on the Hong Kong-Vancouver route in its first year.
The average load factor for the Hong Kong-Vancouver route was 65 percent.
Projected passenger revenue for the Hong Kong-Vancouver route until the end of the year is Canadian $192 million.
Air Canada carried 4.7 million kilos of cargo on the Hong Kong-Vancouver route.
Cargo revenue for the Hong Kong-Vancouver route was just under C$12 million.
47 percent of cargo from Hong Kong was destined for Canada, while 53 percent was sent to the U.S. via Toronto.
Air Canada started the Hong Kong-Vancouver route on December 20 of the previous year using Boeing 747 Combi aircraft.
Air Canada currently operates the Hong Kong-Vancouver route four times a week.

British supermarket group Safeway reported that sales growth had slowed since early January.
Safeway indicated that inflation was around zero.
Analysts expressed concerns that consumer spending cuts could negatively impact the supermarket sector.
Safeway stated that same store sales increased by 5.2 percent in the five weeks to January 4.
Over the first 16 weeks of the second half of the financial year, Safeway's sales growth slowed to 4.5 percent.
Deputy chairman David Webster informed Reuters that inflation, excluding petrol, was currently around zero after a 0.3 percent rise during the Christmas period.
Safeway warned that lower inflation and slower sales could affect profits.
Safeway holds approximately 7.8 percent of Britain's grocery market.
Safeway's shares fell by 25.5 pence to 363.5 pence, making it the third largest loser on the London exchange.
Profit forecasts for Safeway were reduced by 10 million pounds to 430 million pounds.

Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc reported half year profits affected by a pricing review.
The company increased its dividend by 33 percent.
Yorkshire's pretax profits for the six months ending September 30 were 80.8 million pounds.
The previous pretax profits for the same period were 110.6 million pounds.
Yorkshire paid out a dividend of 15.8 pence.
The company plans to provide further benefits to shareholders despite recent tax changes.
Yorkshire stated it has the financial capability to grow its energy supply and generation businesses.
Chief executive Malcolm Chatwin indicated a return of value to shareholders is expected by the end of the current financial year.
Shares in Yorkshire slipped three pence to 758.5 pence.
Chairman Christopher Hampson stated the company's strategy is to be competitive in core energy businesses while providing value for stakeholders.

Northern Electric Plc lost a bid to remain independent.
CalEnergy Co Inc made a bid of 782 million pounds ($1.31 billion) for Northern Electric Plc.
CalEnergy's CE Electric gained control of Northern Electric with 50.3 percent of the votes.
The margin of victory for CalEnergy was 300,000 shares.
The bid process extended beyond its original deadline due to its competitive nature.
Prudential Corp attempted to block CalEnergy's bid by purchasing nearly one million Northern shares.
David Sokol is the chairman and chief executive of CE Electric.
Northern Electric stated it would not make an immediate statement regarding the takeover.
The Takeover Panel rejected Northern's appeal to reverse the deadline extension.
Northern Electric is the tenth of the twelve cash-rich RECs privatized in 1990 to be taken over.

Prudential Corp announced an injection of funds into Scottish Amicable's life fund.
Prudential's chief executive is Sir Peter Davis.
Davis stated that the fund injection likely secured Prudential's bid for Scottish Amicable.
The offer utilized Prudential's balance sheet and life fund.
Prudential is providing up to 1.3 billion stg to the ScotAm life fund.
ScotAm will operate as a separate entity under Prudential.
The capital injection will allow ScotAm to adopt a more flexible investment policy.
The investment could lead to a higher proportion of equity investments and potentially increased returns.
The merger creating Scottish Amicable Life requires approval from policyholders at a special general meeting in June.
The merger is subject to a 75 percent vote in favor by eligible members.

Prudential Corp Plc reported an eight percent rise in first half profits to 421.0 million pounds.
The profit in dollars is approximately 655 million.
Prudential's chief executive is Peter Davis.
Prudential is interested in acquiring a home loan lender to expand its customer base.
Peter Davis did not specify which building society Prudential is in talks with.
Prudential plans to launch a telephone banking business next month.
Prudential raised its interim dividend by 9.4 percent to 5.8 pence per share.
The first-half data included 33 million pounds of start-up costs for the new banking operation.
Funds under management at Prudential rose by four percent since the end of 1995 to 85 billion pounds.
Profit from Prudential's fund management business increased to 14 million pounds from eight million in the previous year.

Capel-Cure Myers Capital Management is in talks with ABN AMRO Hoare Govett regarding a potential offer for CCM.
Capel-Cure Myers Capital Management is controlled by Canadian Insurance Group.
John Henderson is the chief executive of Capel-Cure Myers Capital Management.
ABN AMRO confirmed plans to buy Capel-Cure Myers Capital Management.
Tanno Massar is a spokesman for ABN AMRO.
The planned deal aligns with ABN AMRO's goal of expanding in asset management.
Capel-Cure Myers Capital Management has 4.5 billion pounds under management and employs around 450 staff.
Canadian Insurance acquired its stake in Capel-Cure Myers Capital Management after Central Capital Corp of Canada went bankrupt in 1992.
Capel-Cure Myers Capital Management was previously owned by Australia & New Zealand Banking Corp.
ABN AMRO aims to expand its London operations through fund management acquisitions.

Volkhard Koehler is the outgoing vice-chairman of Czech Skoda Auto a.s., a unit of Volkswagen AG.
Koehler rejected a report from Der Spiegel connecting him to a VW bribery affair as 'nonsense'.
Koehler was replaced on Skoda's board unexpectedly last week.
Der Spiegel reported that Koehler prevented an investigation into a bribery affair linked to VW employees.
Der Spiegel also claimed Koehler was involved in dubious real estate transactions.
Milan Smutny, a Skoda spokesman, stated that Koehler spoke to economic corruption investigators in Braunschweig.
The investigators confirmed that Koehler was not the subject of any investigation.
VW chairman Ferdinand Piech stated that corruption allegations involved a nearly double-digit sum in the millions of marks.
Piech mentioned that only one employee has been suspended in connection with the bribery allegations.
VW's purchasing division approved a 74 million mark contract for a Skoda paint factory and a 38 million mark contract to expand the facility.

Michael Jackson launched his first concert tour in three years on Saturday in Prague.
The concert aimed to restore Jackson's career, which was affected by allegations of child molestation.
Jackson opened the concert in gold-plated astronaut's armor and performed his song 'Scream'.
The stage design combined elements of a classical Greek temple and a space station.
Jackson performed many hits from his 20-year career during the concert.
The 'HIStory World Tour' will last three months and include stops in Europe, Africa, and Asia.
No concert dates are scheduled for the Americas during this tour.
Approximately 120,000 spectators attended the concert in Prague's Letna Plain.
Czech President Vaclav Havel attended the concert but stated that Jackson's music 'isn't close' to him.
The tour is intended to support the 'HIStory' album, which has not sold as well as Jackson's 1982 album 'Thriller'.

Standard & Poor's (S&P) gave investment grade ratings to three of the four largest Czech banks.
The high ratings were partly due to an implied safety net for the banks provided by the state.
S&P issued long-term ratings of BBB-minus to Komercni Banka a.s., Ceska Sporitelna a.s., and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s.
S&P assigned short-term ratings of A3 for counterparty risk to the three banks.
The ratings for the three banks were lower than the Czech Republic's sovereign rating of A.
The ratings were similar to those issued to the Slovak, Polish, and Greek central banks.
The ratings were one grade above Hungarian sovereign debt.
S&P did not give a rating for IPB a.s., the third largest Czech bank.
Komercni Banka a.s. held 25 percent of Czech deposits and 26 percent of the credit market.
The Czech government holds a 48.7 percent stake in Komercni Banka a.s.

The value of Scotia Holdings Plc dropped on Tuesday after regulators declined to approve one of its lead drugs.
Shares in Scotia Holdings Plc fell 23 percent to 437 1/2 pence.
The Medicine Controls Agency (MCA) was not willing to give marketing approval to Tarabetic.
Tarabetic is a drug aimed at relieving sensory impairment in diabetics.
More than 100 million pounds was lost from Scotia Holdings Plc's market capitalisation.
Scotia Holdings Plc's market capitalisation was valued at around 337 million pounds by the close of trading.
The MCA's Committee on the Safety of Medicines questioned the effectiveness of Tarabetic based on trials at 12 different centres.
Scotia Holdings Plc has around 18 months of cash left on its books.
Analyst John Savin issued a sell note for Scotia Holdings Plc, indicating the need for major refinancing.
Analyst Erling Refsum stated that Scotia Holdings Plc was undervalued and that an update on its laser technology treatment could restore the price drop.

Shares in Zeneca Group Plc increased by 35 pence to 18.55 pounds ($30.06) on Friday.
A U.S. Appeals Court dismissed a patent challenge to Zeneca's drug Nolvadex.
The ruling prevents Novopharm Ltd from marketing a generic version of Nolvadex before Zeneca's patent expires in 2002.
Analysts indicated that the ruling was anticipated and attributed the rise in Zeneca's shares to rumors of a Roche bid.
The Swiss magazine Cash reported that Roche Holdings AG was planning to announce a takeover of Zeneca.
Cash suggested Roche would offer between 21 and 22 pounds per share for Zeneca.
Analyst Stephen Putnam stated that the rise in Zeneca's shares was likely due to Roche bid rumors.
London analysts expressed skepticism about the 21-pound offer, suggesting bidding would start at 30 pounds.
Zeneca's patent victory has enhanced its appeal to potential bidders due to its strong product portfolio.
Nolvadex is the world's top-selling breast cancer treatment, with sales totaling 2.7 billion pounds since its launch.

Medeva Plc is a British-based drugs group.
Medeva Plc announced that it has established a structure for growth in the U.S. market.
The majority of Medeva's sales and profits are generated in the U.S. market.
Bill Bogie is the chief executive of Medeva Plc.
Medeva acquired the Rochester business from Rhone Poulenc Rorer Inc.
Medeva plans to operate all its U.S. operations under the name Medeva Pharmaceuticals.
Medeva intends to switch its American Depositary Receipt (ADR) listing to the New York Stock Exchange.
Medeva has a fully integrated sales force in the U.S. consisting of 264 part- and full-time staff.
The proportion of operating profits from U.S. operations increased from 79 percent to 86 percent after the acquisition of Rochester.
Sales from U.S. operations increased from 62 percent to 69 percent after the acquisition of Rochester.
