Clarke's profit warning resulted in a loss of more than 290 million stg in stock market value.
According to the National Association of Cider Makers, the cider market grew by 4.1 percent to 115 million gallons in the 12 months to September 1996.

Ford Motor Co.'s sales decreased by 6.3 percent in August.
Ford reported U.S. sales of 297,726 in August, down from 317,621 in the same month last year.
Sales of domestically produced cars fell by 6.8 percent to 134,110.
Sales of pickup trucks, minivans, and sport/utility vehicles totaled 161,549, a decline of 4.4 percent.
Ford's sales for the first eight months of 1996 lagged behind Honda Motor Co.'s Accord by 1,409 units.
Ford's results contributed to a 2.3 percent total industry decline to 1,307,858 units for August.
Total sales of North American-built cars decreased by 6.7 percent to 608,140.
There was a 3.7 percent increase in domestically produced light trucks, totaling 513,376.
The seasonally adjusted annual selling rate for August was 15.8 million units.
Ford forecasts total industry U.S. sales for 1996 to be between 15.4 million and 15.5 million units.

Andrew Card is the president and chief executive officer of the American Automobile Manufacturers Association.
Andrew Card predicted that the Republican-led Congress will accept President Clinton's challenge to improve partisan relations.
The American Automobile Manufacturers Association supports President Clinton's agenda for a leaner government and a balanced federal budget.
Andrew Card stated that the second Clinton administration presents both opportunities and concerns for the auto industry.
Card emphasized that federal regulators need to better understand the issues facing the Big Three automakers.
Card mentioned that the Big Three automakers are responsible for about 700,000 direct jobs and account for about 4.5 percent of the nation's gross domestic product.
Including suppliers and dealers, the Big Three automakers generate approximately 2.3 million jobs.
Card expressed concern about the value of the yen being at a 46-month low, which affects the competitiveness of domestic automakers.
The yen is currently valued at about 118 to the dollar, an increase from 79 over the past 18 months.
Card warned that proposed 'irresponsible standards' for the National Ambient Air Quality Standards could negatively impact U.S. economic growth.

Workers at two Johnson Control Inc. seat assembly plants went on strike on Tuesday.
Ford Motor Co. announced it would not accept non-union made seats until the dispute is resolved.
Bob King, director of United Auto Worker Region 1A, described the strike as a major victory.
More than 300 workers at the Plymouth, Michigan plant walked off the job at 6 a.m. Tuesday.
The strike was initiated after contract negotiations broke down late Monday.
About 200 employees at a Johnson Controls seat plant in Oberlin, Ohio also went on strike.
Workers at both plants agreed to be represented by the UAW in a new labor contract last fall.
The Plymouth plant assembles seats for Ford's Expedition SUV, while the Ohio plant makes seats for Ford's Econoline vans.
Johnson Controls stated it would make efforts to continue production, including hiring replacement workers if necessary.
UAW spokesman Karl Mantyla indicated the union was seeking wage parity with other seat suppliers.

China observed the first 'tombsweeping' day since Deng Xiaoping's death on a Saturday.
There were few outward signs of remembrance for Deng Xiaoping during the event.
Thousands of residents from Beijing visited Babaoshan cemetery for the Qingming festival.
The Qingming festival is traditionally a day for tidying ancestral graves.
Many attendees treated the event as a family occasion rather than a political one.
A Beijing resident stated that her visit was a family matter with no connection to political leaders.
Students from Sichuan, Deng's native province, gathered at the cemetery for a personal reason.
Deng Xiaoping died on February 19 at the age of 92 and was cremated at Babaoshan.
Deng's ashes were scattered at sea according to his wishes, leaving no specific place for public remembrance.
The People's Daily newspaper chose to remember Deng by showing photographs of him planting trees since 1979.

China's major state banks reported profits last year.
Some profits were sharply higher than in 1995.
Analysts stated that this indicated banks were beginning to act like commercial banks elsewhere.
Fees from credit cards and electronic banking services contributed to new income.
Loans were being extended with greater care to limit risk.
The banking system's bad debts from past loans were likely being disguised by the results.
Write-offs by the banks or the state were expected in the coming years.
An official at the Industrial and Commercial Bank in Shenzhen stated that big banks were gradually becoming real commercial banks.
The Industrial and Commercial Bank of China reported profits of 14.5 billion yuan last year, up from 4.6 billion yuan in 1995.
The Bank of China earned 8.2 billion yuan and the China Construction Bank made 2.76 billion yuan.

China may need to adjust the mix of its treasury debt next year to ensure an active response from domestic institutions.
Finance ministry officials were meeting in Beijing to discuss bond market trends.
The issue of China's debt mix could be a focus of the talks.
A Shenzhen analyst stated that there is too much non-tradeable type of debt.
Non-tradeable debt is not attractive to institutions or individual investors.
China is issuing about 250 billion yuan ($30.1 billion) of state debt this year, most of it domestic.
More than half of the total state debt is for non-tradeable voucher or certificate type treasury debt.
Investors receive a certificate that can be redeemed before maturity for their funds.
Non-tradeable debt is not listed on the stock exchanges in Shanghai or Shenzhen, and no active secondary trading exists.
Last year, non-tradeable debt accounted for about one-tenth of total government debt issued.

The Clinton administration supported congressional efforts to reform U.S. banking laws.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin presented a plan to eliminate the Glass-Steagall Act barriers.
The administration's plan was due to Congress by March 31.
There was a nearly two-month delay in submitting the plan.
Congress has attempted to reform banking laws for over a decade.
Interest groups have historically blocked banking legislation.
Recent court and regulatory decisions have granted banks new authority.
Insurance companies and securities firms are now seeking a level playing field.
David Farmer, a lobbyist for the Alliance of American Insurers, expressed renewed hope for reform.
Rubin will provide more details of the plan in testimony before Congress on June 3.

The U.S. Commerce Department approved an application from Sybase Inc to export computer encoding products.
Sybase Inc officials reported the approval on Wednesday.
About a dozen companies have received permission to export products with encryption this year.
Sybase's products appeared to bypass strict U.S. export rules in effect since the beginning of the year.
Tom Parenty is the director of data and communication security at Sybase.
Parenty expressed surprise at the approval and wrote a letter outlining differences in their approach versus the regulations.
To export powerful encryption, a company must include features that allow the government to access software keys.
Companies can export medium-strength encryption by promising to include key recovery features within two years.
Sybase's products will allow for key recovery only for stored data, not for live communications.
Sybase supports legislative proposals to eliminate most export restrictions.

Scientists are working on the next generation of the Internet.
The first challenge is to convince the U.S. Congress to fund the project.
The next generation network has encountered roadblocks on Capitol Hill.
Scientists, including John Gibbons, will address concerns at a Senate hearing.
Some lawmakers are concerned that the project lacks focus and is similar to Internet2.
The next generation Internet project aims to send data at 1,000 times the speed of today's Internet.
Clinton pledged $100 million annually for five years to build the super high-speed network.
The funding was to come from reallocating existing research funds, but this plan is facing issues.
The House of Representatives passed a budget that bars spending on the next generation Internet.
28 senators expressed concerns about the advisory board's composition in a letter to Gibbons.

The Czech Republic recorded its first budget deficit in 1996.
The government attempted to achieve a fourth consecutive surplus.
In December 1996, the government froze some outlays and required early repayment on credit to address a projected deficit.
The Finance Ministry announced a definitive budget deficit of 1.562 billion crowns for 1996.
Revenues for 1996 totaled 482.8 billion crowns, while expenditures were 484.3 billion crowns.
The Czech Republic had three consecutive year-end budget surpluses since the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993.
Finance ministry officials indicated that the deficit could increase due to late bill submissions.
The 1996 budget was initially approved as balanced at 497.6 billion crowns but was later revised to 491 billion crowns due to spending cuts.
Parliamentary budget committee chairman Jozef Wagner expressed concern about the impact of government payment adjustments on the 1997 budget.
The 1997 budget was approved with both expenditures and revenues forecast at 549.1 billion crowns, based on an expected economic growth of 5.4 percent.

The Budapest Stock Exchange reached a record high on Friday.
A foreign-buying induced bull run occurred in eastern Europe this week.
Markets in the region rose, with Budapest and Warsaw recording year-highs.
Romania and Slovenia also experienced significant increases.
Bratislava and Prague saw slight increases with minimal upward momentum.
The Warsaw Stock Exchange achieved four consecutive 33-month highs this week.
Heavy turnover was noted on the Warsaw Stock Exchange.
Analysts predicted a profit-taking correction was likely to occur later.
The Warsaw Stock Exchange has risen 25 percent since December 10.
Maciej Matusiak, an analyst at PKO BP brokerage, suggested investors would start taking profits next week.

The Czech crown fell sharply on Thursday following comments from the central bank.
The central bank expressed dissatisfaction with the recent rise of the Czech crown.
Dealers believe the Czech crown remains attractive and should stabilize by the end of the week.
The Czech crown is one of post-Communist Europe's most stable currencies.
The crown has reached record highs in recent weeks due to demand from over 30 billion crowns in Eurobond issues since the start of the year.
The crown was trading at 3.48 percent above parity against the dollar basket.
The crown fell over 60 basis points from its opening and about 200 points lower from Tuesday's record fixing at +5.51.
Analysts believe the country's high interest rate differential and overall economic stability should limit further drops in the crown's value.
The central bank's repo rate is at 12.4 percent, and the discount rate has been at 10.5 percent since last June.
CNB spokesman Martin Svehla stated that the central bank has the option to intervene in the market when necessary.

Nick Durlacher is the chairman of the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA).
The head of Britain's financial markets watchdog stated that volatile markets and new financial tools contributed to recent investment banking failures.
Durlacher emphasized the need for firms to focus on control and compliance in addition to profitability and market share.
The SFA announced it would not publish controversial changes to its rules until they align with standards proposed by the Securities and Investments Board (SIB).
Durlacher noted that the growth of derivatives over the last 10 years has created new management challenges.
Durlacher mentioned that senior managers are making outdated mistakes.
The investment banking industry is experiencing a volatile job market.
Durlacher highlighted that bonuses and the 'star system' are factors firms need to consider.
The SFA's proposals aim to make senior executive officers more accountable for catastrophic failures in their firms.
Durlacher expressed hope that the proposals would be finalized by the end of April.

A proposed reform of Britain's state pensions system aims to prevent burdens on future taxpayers.
The ruling Conservative government unveiled these proposals on Wednesday.
Workers would be responsible for providing for their old age under the proposed reform.
Roger Taylor, deputy chairman of Royal & Sun Alliance, described the plans as a significant shift in financial services.
Taylor believes the proposals would encourage other governments to implement similar changes.
If enacted, the proposals are expected to generate additional business in three to four years.
Tony Baker, deputy director general of the Association of British Insurers, stated the proposals are beneficial for the industry.
The opposition Labour Party is ahead in opinion polls and wants to retain the basic state pension.
Labour also aims to develop new second pensions for those not in occupational pension schemes.
The banking and life insurance industry is preparing for changes regardless of the election outcome.

Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) is involved in the probe into alleged irregularities in three Morgan Grenfell investment funds.
The investigation by the SFO extends beyond Britain.
The SFO is in contact with Britain's Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO).
The SFO is not conducting its own investigation.
A senior SFO lawyer has been briefed by IMRO.
Overseas authorities in the U.S., Luxembourg, and Switzerland are involved in the investigation.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell reported that nearly eight percent of the three Morgan Grenfell investment funds had been redeemed.
The funds were suspended due to suspected irregularities but resumed trading after Deutsche Bank removed certain unlisted securities.
IMRO's investigation has led to the suspension of two fund managers at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
The probe is focusing on links between suspended MGAM fund manager Peter Young and UK-based broker Fiba Nordic Securities.

Deng Xiaoping, China's paramount leader, died of respiratory failure on Wednesday.
Deng was 93 years old by Chinese reckoning.
Jiang Zemin is the anointed successor of Deng Xiaoping and holds the positions of Communist Party chief, state President, and head of the armed forces.
Diplomats and analysts expect calm in China following Deng's death.
There is speculation about whether Jiang Zemin will reverse Deng's economic reforms.
A power struggle among potential successors to Deng is anticipated.
China faces multiple issues including unemployment, a widening wealth gap, corruption, and a one-party system.
Analysts predict that the country may experience a period of mourning and political maneuvering.
Tai Ming Cheung, a Hong Kong-based Sinologist, stated that there will be an emphasis on stability and internal security.
Jiang Zemin appears to have consolidated his power base, but political rivals are expected to compete for influence.

China and South Korea negotiated on Friday regarding the defection of Hwang Jang-yop.
Hwang Jang-yop is a top North Korean official who has taken refuge in Seoul's mission in Beijing.
Pyongyang officials aimed to persuade Hwang Jang-yop to return to North Korea.
Talks in Singapore between South Korean Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha and Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen did not resolve the deadlock over Hwang Jang-yop.
Hwang Jang-yop is 73 years old and is the most senior Pyongyang official to flee North Korea.
A South Korean embassy official stated that negotiations over Hwang Jang-yop had begun in Beijing.
Hwang Jang-yop spent a second night in the South Korean embassy compound with an aide.
China is involved in the dispute between North Korea and South Korea regarding Hwang Jang-yop.
China's Qian stated that more time is needed to investigate the incident.
Hwang Jang-yop is in good health and spending his time reading while in the embassy.

Guo Song was sentenced to death by a Beijing judge for bank robbery.
Guo Song killed four bank guards and stole several payrolls.
Guo Song's execution could occur by January 1 due to amendments to the Criminal Procedure Law.
The judge delivered the verdict during a trial that was videotaped by a court clerk.
Court hearings in China are described as resembling theatre.
A judge-turned-lawyer stated that verdicts may be decided beforehand in Chinese trials.
Defendants in China are presumed guilty before being proved innocent.
Suspects can be detained for extended periods, and lawyers receive the bill of indictment shortly before trial.
Criminal law professor Qu Xinjiu commented that the amendments approved by the National People's Congress represent a significant improvement.
Lawyer Li Shuguang expressed concerns about the preparedness of judges and prosecutors for upcoming judicial reforms.

BHP Petroleum and Phillips Petroleum agreed that BHP should be the sole operator of the Bayu-Undan gas field.
The Bayu-Undan gas field is located in the Timor Sea.
The estimated cost of developing the Bayu-Undan gas field is A$4 billion.
The field has proven and probable reserves of 3.1 trillion cubic feet (tcf).
The Bayu-Undan gas field is divided into two sides: the 'Bayu' side and the 'Undan' side.
The 'Bayu' side is owned by a Phillips-led joint venture that includes Oryx Energy Co and Hardy Oil & Gas Plc.
Phillips holds a 60 percent stake in the 'Bayu' side of the field.
The 'Undan' side is owned by a BHP-led joint venture that includes Petroz, Santos Ltd, and Inpex Sahul.
BHP holds a 42.417 percent stake in the 'Undan' side of the field.
The ZOCAs were established by a treaty between Australia and Indonesia.

Analysts expected that Fisher and Paykel Ltd would post a slightly lower profit in 1996/97.
Gary Paykel is the chief executive of Fisher and Paykel Ltd.
Gary Paykel stated that local analysts' reports were accurate regarding profit expectations.
The analysts referenced include J.B. Were and Hendry Hay McIntosh.
Analysts forecasted Fisher and Paykel's full year net profit would fall to about NZ$38 million from NZ$39.25 million in 1995/96.
Fisher and Paykel reported a first half net profit of NZ$19.2 million in early November.
Fisher and Paykel could not make a profit forecast for the full year.
New Zealand market conditions were described as tough by Gary Paykel.
Fisher and Paykel lost an exclusive distribution agreement with Noel Leeming, impacting sales.
Fisher and Paykel signed an exclusive distribution agreement with Harvey Norman Holdings Ltd for New Zealand stores.

HSBC Holdings Plc, Citicorp, and Standard Chartered Plc are considered the most interested in acquiring Australia's major banks following the lifting of a foreign takeover ban.
Treasurer Peter Costello announced the end of a ban on foreign takeovers of Australia's four largest banks.
Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp are viewed as the most vulnerable to foreign takeovers.
Mike Pulman, an analyst at ABN AMRO, stated that HSBC is regarded as the top predator among potential acquirers.
Other potential acquirers mentioned include Lloyds TSB, ABN AMRO, Citicorp, and Deutsche Bank.
Analysts believe HSBC is unlikely to pursue ANZ due to its strong Asian presence through its Grindlays unit.
National Australia Bank Ltd is considered the least likely target for takeover due to its significant overseas assets and size.
Anusha Srinivasan, a banking analyst at Shaw Stockbroking, noted that NAB's foreign assets may not attract bidders already in those markets.
Westpac is seen as the most likely candidate for a takeover among the weaker banks due to its management's receptiveness to bids.
Standard Chartered Plc is identified as the most likely acquirer of Westpac, having already formed an alliance with the bank.

Banyan Strategic Realty Trust will report funds from operations (FFO) of $0.03 a share for the 1996 fourth quarter.
The FFO for the 1996 fourth quarter is down from $0.07 a share a year ago.
Leonard Levine is the chief executive of Banyan Strategic Realty Trust.
Banyan expects FFO for the year ended December 31 to be $0.34 a share, up from $0.32 a share a year ago.
Banyan expects FFO to increase in 1997 to between $0.50 and $0.55 a share.
The company's target for 1998 FFO is $0.65 to $0.70 a share, not including additional acquisitions.
By June 30 of this year, Banyan expects to own 19 properties in the Midwest and Southeast.
Banyan's strategy is to spread risk by focusing on smaller real estate markets and properties.
Banyan aims to improve its revenue stream and sell properties at a profit.
Leonard Levine expects Banyan to explore an equity offering within the next 12 months to raise market capital.

Mercury Finance Co. is in negotiations to extend $50 million in short-term financing from Bank of America.
The financing was granted to Mercury in February to help with daily operating expenses and interest payments.
Mercury has faced issues including overstated earnings, an FBI investigation, and multiple shareholder lawsuits.
The loan is due on Monday unless Mercury secures waivers from lenders.
A spokesman for Mercury stated that discussions for the extension were ongoing and an announcement was expected before the market opens on Tuesday.
Analyst Thomas Kmiotek indicated that Mercury expected to receive the extension.
Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co. downgraded Mercury's senior debt rating from triple-C to double-D after Mercury failed to pay $15 million in debt.
The $15 million debt was the first medium-term note due since Mercury's financial troubles began.
On January 29, Mercury announced it would lower its earnings over the last four years by about $90 million due to accounting discrepancies.
Mercury has defaulted on millions of dollars in debt, has been served with a search warrant by the FBI, hired a new CEO, and is involved in multiple lawsuits.

Cobra Electronics Corp expects to report increases in revenue and profits in 1997.
Cobra Electronics Corp reported a profitable year in 1996, its first year in the black since 1989.
Cobra Electronics Corp reported revenue of $90.3 million and net income of $601,000 in 1996.
Cobra Electronics Corp had revenue of $90.4 million and a loss of $1.1 million in 1995.
Cobra Electronics Corp completed a cost-cutting program in 1996.
Cobra Electronics Corp is introducing a system called Safety Alert.
The Safety Alert system allows drivers to receive signals alerting them to emergency vehicles and other hazards.
The Safety Alert detector will be sold for about $69.95.
The transmitter for the Safety Alert system will sell for about $300.
Cobra Electronics Corp currently has about 15 percent of the detection market and expects to grow its market share to 20 to 25 percent by the end of the year.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is a Canadian mining company.
Bre-X's Busang gold find is now considered worthless.
Bre-X's Busang discovery was claimed to be the richest find of the century.
A report by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. stated that the falsification of the Busang discovery was unprecedented in mining history.
Patrick Sheridan, a veteran mine promoter, compared the Bre-X scandal to the Windfall affair.
The Windfall Oils and Mines Ltd. affair was Canada's biggest national mining scandal before Bre-X.
The Windfall affair occurred in the 1960s during a copper and zinc rush in northern Ontario.
George and Viola MacMillan were the promoters involved in the Windfall affair.
The Kelly Commission investigated the Windfall affair and found no evidence of wrongdoing by the MacMillans.
Martin Frobisher believed he found gold on Baffin Island in 1575, but it was determined to be worthless iron pyrites.

The Busang gold controversy has negatively impacted Canada's junior mining sector.
Investment advisors predict that many investors will be scared off in 1997 due to the controversy.
John Kaiser, editor of a financial newsletter, stated that the Busang bust has ended the current junior resource market cycle.
Fund managers are expected to reduce their holdings of junior mining stocks following the Bre-X saga.
Kaiser predicted a funding drought for junior mining companies that will likely last through the rest of the year.
Retail investors are expected to remain inactive because they believe the market cycle is over.
Kaiser anticipates a return of the bull market in 1998.
Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd is conducting an independent audit of Bre-X's Busang project.
Preliminary tests by Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc indicated that the Busang deposit may contain insignificant amounts of gold.
The selloff of Bre-X shares last month resulted in a loss of almost C$3 billion from the company's stock market value.

Ontario Finance Minister Ernie Eves is expected to deliver the 1997/98 budget next month.
The 1997/98 budget will be released on May 6.
Eves revised the 1996/97 budget deficit to C$7.67 billion.
The revised deficit is down C$508 million from the original budget forecast.
Economists predict the final 1996/97 deficit figure could be around C$7 billion.
Eves is expected to improve his C$6.6 billion deficit forecast for 1997/98.
Nesbitt Burns senior economist Doug Porter stated the deficit may come in below C$6 billion.
The government's contingency reserve is used to reduce the deficit if not needed for unexpected spending.
Royal Bank of Canada economist Craig Wright expects a deficit of around C$7 billion in 1996/97, falling to about C$6 billion in 1997/98.
Eves reported that government revenues grew almost C$1.2 billion higher than projected due to a rebounding economy.

Robert Lutz is the Vice Chairman of Chrysler Corp.
Lutz has reduced his corporate responsibilities.
Lutz considers himself an integral part of Chrysler's product creation activities.
Lutz gave up his president and chief operating officer titles on January 1.
Lutz's change in title is in anticipation of his 65th birthday in February.
Lutz is credited with improving Chrysler's product development operations.
Lutz instituted a system of super-efficient 'platform teams' for vehicle development.
Lutz acts as a coach and mentor for engineers and product executives.
Chrysler Chairman Robert Eaton took over Lutz's chief operating officer duties.
Lutz plans to gradually ease himself out of Chrysler before turning 70.

General Motors Corp. informed analysts that its fourth-quarter North American incentive and marketing costs were higher than previously estimated.
As a result of GM's announcement, analysts reduced their earnings estimates for the company by hundreds of millions of dollars.
GM's product mix in Europe is expected to be weaker than anticipated, with the low-margin Corsa subcompact comprising a larger portion of sales.
GM's new product launch costs remain high.
Analysts lowered their estimates for GM's earnings by 45 cents to 50 cents per share, leading to a decline in GM stock by $1.375 to close at $54.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Burnham Securities analyst David Healy estimates that GM will earn $435 million, or 52 cents per share, in the fourth quarter, excluding extraordinary items.
GM plans to take a charge of $170 million, or 22 cents per share, for lump-sum payments to United Auto Workers members as part of a new contract.
GM disclosed that strikes in the United States and Canada during the quarter reduced its fourth-quarter profit by about $700 million.
In the fourth quarter of 1995, GM earned $1.87 billion, or $1.98 per share.
Analyst Michael Ward stated that GM may view the fourth quarter as a 'cleanup quarter' and could accelerate some costs to improve next year's results.

Chrysler Corp. named Robert Lutz vice chairman on Thursday.
Robert Eaton was given the title of president and will take on more day-to-day operating duties.
The chief operating officer position that Lutz held was left vacant.
Lutz is expected to stay on for two more years.
Chrysler's board increased its share buyback program to $2 billion for 1997.
Chrysler raised its annual dividend to $1.60 a share from $1.40.
The new quarterly dividend of 40 cents a share is payable on January 15 to stockholders of record as of December 15.
Chrysler has raised its dividend seven times in the past three years.
Chrysler has increased its dividend payout by 433 percent since September 1993.
Chrysler switched international and product development duties between Thomas Gale and Francois Castaing.

Britain cleared U.S. utility CE Electric's 782 million pound hostile takeover bid for Northern Electric.
The clearance occurred just days ahead of a final deadline for shareholders to accept the offer.
Trade and industry minister Ian Lang stated that CE Electric provided assurances to address regulatory concerns.
The bid is for 650 pence per share and closes next Friday.
Northern Electric claims the bid 'short changes' investors.
Prudential Corporation owns more than 11 percent of Northern Electric's shares and has purchased additional shares at 600 pence each.
Prudential traditionally supports the target company's board in hostile takeover situations.
CE Electric claims to have major investors on its side and is confident of winning the takeover.
David Sokol, CE Electric's chairman and chief executive, stated that the decision for shareholders is clear.
Northern Electric's share price increased by 41 pence to 643.50 following the news of the deal being cleared.

Tomkins Plc reported a 34 percent increase in pretax profits for the six months to November 2, amounting to 168.8 million pounds.
The dividend increased from 2.7 pence to 3.06 pence compared to the previous year.
Gregory Hutchings is the executive chairman of Tomkins Plc.
Hutchings stated that the results represent another period of outperformance for Tomkins.
Tomkins shares fell by 3.5 pence to 274 in the market after buy-back hopes were dismissed.
Hutchings ruled out the possibility of returning Tomkins's 366.8 million pound cash reserve to shareholders this year.
Hutchings indicated that Tomkins is looking at acquisition opportunities instead of a share buy-back.
Tomkins is likely to pursue several smaller acquisitions, potentially worth up to 200 million pounds.
The company has experienced earnings per share growth for 12 consecutive years.
Gates Corp contributed 259.5 million in sales and 20 million in profit in its first 14 weeks after acquisition.

The British government warned that it would refer the proposed trans-Atlantic alliance between British Airways Plc and American Airlines to Britain's Monopolies and Mergers Commission unless conditions were met.
Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang stated that final clearance for the alliance would depend on an open skies deal between Britain and the United States.
Lang supported conditions proposed by Britain's Office of Fair Trading regarding the alliance.
Lang claimed that without suitable undertakings, the alliance would likely lead to a significant loss of actual and potential passengers on competing routes.
The latest open skies talks in London ended without a deal signed.
Industry sources reported no new date for further talks, attributing the deadlock to uncertainty over the British Airways-American deal.
The conditions for clearance of the alliance included British Airways and American Airlines dropping 168 slots at London Heathrow airport.
AMR Corp., American Airlines' parent company, stated that the terms were not a deal breaker but were more severe than those imposed by other regulatory authorities.
British Airways responded that unconditional divestiture of slots was unprecedented and should be based on fair market value.
The government requested British Airways to remove a clause in its agreement with USAir that restricts competition on trans-Atlantic routes.

3Com Corp and U.S. Robotics Corp are merging.
The merger is valued at $6.6 billion in stock.
This merger is the largest deal in the computer network industry.
The merger aims to create a competitor to Cisco Systems Inc in the Internet access business.
Analysts are divided on the merger's potential to compete with Cisco.
Bear Stearns analyst Eric Blachno commented on Cisco's market leadership.
Frank Dzubeck, an industry analyst, questioned the merger's viability.
Dzubeck compared the merger to the 1994 Bay-Wellfleet-Synoptics deal.
3Com is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
U.S. Robotics is located in Skokie, Illinois.

America Online Inc. plans to place advertising in company-sponsored discussion areas.
The company aims to expand its revenue base beyond subscriber fees.
America Online is based in Dulles, Virginia.
The advertising program is expected to generate 360 million ad impressions monthly.
An analyst estimated the program could generate $15 million to $25 million in new revenues in 1997.
Impressions measure how many times an ad is viewed.
America Online stock rose $3.75 to $43.75 a share on the New York Stock Exchange.
Bob Pittman is the president of America Online Networks.
Over 70 percent of America Online members participate in chat.
America Online logs 1 million hours of chat every day.

Cascade Communications Corp shares experienced a significant decline on Friday.
The decline was triggered by comments made during a conference call.
The comments raised concerns about future earnings for Cascade Communications Corp.
Several analysts downgraded their ratings on Cascade Communications Corp.
Analysts expressed concern that growth rates for Cascade's core frame-relay switching business may decrease.
The expected growth rates for the core business may drop to industry levels of 30-50 percent.
Previously, the growth rates for Cascade's core business were over 100 percent.
The stock price of Cascade Communications Corp fell by 19-3/4 to 44-3/8.
All gains in the stock price since April were lost.
Cascade Communications Corp was previously considered a high-flying data networking stock.

A criminal complaint was filed against Nomura Securities Co Ltd on Tuesday.
The complaint reveals a widening circle of players in a pay-off scandal involving Nomura.
Japan's Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) filed the complaint with prosecutors.
The complaint alleges that Nomura, two former executives, and a former general manager compensated a client for investment losses.
Company executives asked junior staff to conduct illegal deals to compensate clients for stock trading losses.
The SESC decided not to take action against the junior staffers involved in the illegal deals.
The SESC took action against former Nomura directors Shimpei Matsuki and Nobutaka Fujikura.
Both Matsuki and Fujikura resigned on March 10 after an internal probe found they made discretionary deals banned under Japanese securities law.
Former general manager Osamu Fujita made transactions under Fujikura's orders.
Nomura continued making illegal compensation payments even after a scandal in 1991.

Sanwa Bank Ltd intends to list its shares in New York.
Sanwa Bank aims to become a global player in the financial sector.
Naotaka Saeki is the president of Sanwa Bank.
Sanwa Bank is one of Japan's six biggest commercial banks.
Sanwa Bank had assets of 51.96 trillion yen at the end of September 2023.
Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd is the only Japanese bank listed in New York.
Sanwa Bank cannot be listed on the New York Stock Exchange until it records a profit for three consecutive years.
Sanwa Bank posted a parent current loss of 259.87 billion yen in 1995/96.
Sanwa Bank forecasts a parent current profit of 50 billion yen for 1996/97.
Sanwa Bank aims to boost its return-on-equity ratio to 12 percent.

Two banks in Japan took action to address financial problems on Tuesday.
Hokkaido Takushoku Bank will merge with Hokkaido Bank Ltd.
Hokkaido Takushoku Bank will cease its overseas operations.
The merger aims to create a 'super-regional' bank.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd is expected to announce a restructuring plan.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd's restructuring will include government funding and bankruptcy filings for affiliates.
Hokkaido Takushoku Bank stated it had to retrench to manage bad loans.
The merger between Hokkaido Takushoku Bank and Hokkaido Bank is set to be completed by April 1998.
The merger will result in the elimination of 2,000 jobs.
Hokkaido Takushoku Bank will close six overseas branches and seven representative offices.

Reform of China's non-equity capital markets is expected to continue over the next year.
Industry analysts believe Deng Xiaoping's death will have little or no impact on the capital markets.
Trading on the state debt and local currency interbank markets has not been significantly affected by Deng's death.
Analysts believe Beijing will not postpone the development of the interbank market.
A Shanghai-based interbank trader reported that trading has been normal, although volume has decreased slightly.
A state debt trader noted that there are signs of a smooth transition of leadership.
Prices of state debt spot contracts remained stable despite Deng's death.
A senior China analyst in Hong Kong suggested that Deng's death could slow the pace of capital market reforms.
Retail price inflation in China fell to 6.1 percent in 1996 from 14.8 percent in 1995.
Traders indicated that the state debt repurchase markets in China performed well despite Deng's death.

Citibank NA started operations in Shanghai's Pudong development zone on Monday.
Citibank aims to gain an early start in the local Chinese currency business.
A senior Citibank executive stated that there are only modest profit opportunities in the early stages of local currency operations.
John Beeman is Citibank's Country Corporate Officer for China.
Beeman expects the Chinese central bank to issue detailed regulations for foreign banks doing Chinese yuan business in March.
Citibank hopes to offer local currency products and services in April, pending inspection of their branch.
Citibank is one of eight foreign banks approved to conduct Chinese yuan business.
Foreign banks in China have been restricted to foreign currency transactions until now.
The Shanghai city government wants to develop Pudong into a financial center.
The office vacancy rate in the main business area of Pudong is estimated at more than 70 percent.

Trading on China's capital markets will be influenced by technical factors this week.
The death of Deng Xiaoping was already discounted as a factor in the markets.
Analysts noted that trading on Thursday and Friday was calm and mature.
Investors are monitoring for changes in policies or leadership in China.
Analysts believe there is little chance of political problems affecting the markets in the short term.
A stock analyst stated that the markets would trade without impact from Deng's death.
It is expected to take at least a month before new leadership appointments are made in Beijing.
Trading volumes are anticipated to be low as investors are hesitant to take large positions.
Both the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock markets rose on Thursday and Friday despite Deng's death.
The Finance Ministry announced it would issue 123 billion yuan in treasury notes from March 1 to October 20.

Softwood lumber prices may remain high or increase after Canadian lumber companies receive a new quota on April 1.
Gilbert Garant is a commodity broker in Montreal for Whalen, Beliveau and Associates.
Gilbert Garant believes that prices will rise.
Softwood lumber was trading at approximately US$370 per thousand board feet on Friday.
The price of softwood lumber was about US$320 before the quota system began a year ago.
April 1 marks the beginning of the second year of the Canada-U.S. agreement limiting Canada's softwood lumber exports.
The quota system restricts fee-free exports from the four top exporting provinces to 14.7 billion board feet per year.
Companies that exceed their quotas must pay a fee between US$50 and US$100 per 1,000 board feet.
Statistics from mid-March indicated that Canada had exported about 98 percent of its quota.
Patricia Mohr is the vice-president of economics at Scotiabank in Toronto.

Barrick Gold Corp is now the world's second largest gold producer.
Barrick Gold Corp's 1996 gold production was 3,148,801 ounces.
Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd's 1996 gold production was 3,125,631 ounces.
Barrick Gold Corp expects 1997 production to exceed three million ounces.
Barrick Gold Corp's proven and probable reserves increased to 51 million ounces.
Barrick Gold Corp reported 25 million ounces of gold in the resource category.
Barrick Gold Corp aims to become the world's largest gold company.
Barrick Gold Corp is seeking control of the Busang deposit in Indonesia.
Drilling at Barrick's Pierina property in Peru expanded reserves to 6.5 million ounces.
Barrick's Pascua mine in Chile has reserves of 10 million ounces.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd has chosen J.P. Morgan and Co as a financial adviser.
Bre-X has hired Republic National Bank of New York as a corporate adviser.
The two advisers will work together to help Bre-X find a suitable partner.
Bre-X aims to sell 25 percent of its Indonesia gold deposit project.
A Bre-X spokesman stated that they have been approached by major gold companies.
Bryan Coates has been hired as vice-president and corporate controller at Bre-X.
Coates has 15 years of experience in international gold mining.
Bre-X is expected to open bidding for its Busang deposit soon.
A contract of work from the Indonesian government is expected in the coming weeks.
Drilling at the Busang deposit has outlined 46.92 million ounces of gold.

The Czech government announced a series of economic measures on Wednesday.
The measures aim to jump start the economy.
The government admitted that GDP growth would decline in 1997.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus released an 11-page plan detailing the measures.
The measures include cuts of almost five percent to budget expenditures.
Public sector wage growth will be limited to 7.3 percent.
The measures aim to improve the economy and complete the transformation of the Czech economy.
Klaus stated that achieving half of the 5.4 percent GDP growth forecast would be considered a success.
The statement criticized the central bank for its tight monetary policy.
The crown is fixed daily by the central bank at +/- 7.5 percent of the mid-point of its dollar/mark basket.

The Czech parliament began debate on a reconciliation agreement with Germany.
The Prague government views the agreement as important for EU and NATO membership.
Opposition deputies consider the agreement a betrayal.
The ultra-right Republican Party and the Communists oppose the agreement.
Opponents claim the agreement allows Germany to evade responsibility for Nazi atrocities.
Deputies voted to prioritize the declaration on the agenda.
Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl signed the declaration last month.
The declaration expresses regret for the Nazi occupation and sorrow for the post-war expulsion of ethnic Germans.
The text includes German support for Czech EU and NATO membership.
The CSSD leadership has allowed its members a free vote on the declaration.

Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik revealed details of his plan to restructure energy prices.
Kocarnik's plan could lead to the rapid privatisation of energy distributors.
The plan includes a two-step rise in electricity, natural gas, and heating rates for households.
The first increase is scheduled for July 1, and the second will occur a year later.
Average electricity rates for households would rise 35 percent in July to 1.49 crowns per KWh.
The price for industrial customers would remain flat at 1.70 crowns per KWh.
Household rates are currently cross-subsidised by revenues from industry.
Gas prices would also increase by 35 percent in the first stage of the plan.
Half of the electricity rate hike would come from a VAT increase on energy and fuels to 22 percent from five percent.
The second increase, planned for mid-1998, would depend on the cost levels of energy companies.

China historically concealed the death of an emperor by filling his carriage with fish to mask the smell.
Currently, China uses vague language to obscure information about the health of its leaders.
Deng Xiaoping is 92 years old and has not been seen in public for over three years.
The Communist Party of China has kept Deng's health information secret, providing only brief statements about his condition.
A Western diplomat stated that in Chinese culture, a leader cannot be seen to be dying until their death occurs.
The death of a Chinese emperor or communist leader has historically led to power struggles.
When Qin Shi Huangdi died in 210 BC, his prime minister concealed his death by hiding the body with fish.
Mao Zedong's death in 1976 was announced within 12 hours of his passing.
The Communist Party is attempting to prevent information about Deng's health from reaching the public.
The health of the nation's leader is believed to be linked to the stability of the nation.

If every person in Russia and Germany turned on their televisions, that would equal the number of Chinese who have watched a documentary on Deng Xiaoping.
An official from China Central Television (CCTV) stated that there is a high viewership for the documentary.
The documentary was launched on New Year's Day and is a 12-part series.
The official estimated that 28 percent of the 800 million Chinese with television access, or 224 million people, watched the documentary at 8:00 p.m. for the past 12 days.
About 40 million people watch the nightly evening news in China.
The documentary's ratings surpass those of recent popular soap operas.
The documentary cannot match the viewership of the Lunar New Year's Eve spectacle.
Deng Xiaoping faced little competition from other television channels during the documentary's airing.
The decision to run the series followed a last-minute edict from CCTV officials.
Deng Xiaoping has not been seen in public for nearly three years due to his desire to retire and his failing health.

China's President Jiang Zemin has become the leader of China after seven years as the heir apparent to Deng Xiaoping.
Jiang Zemin is 70 years old.
One of Jiang's pressing tasks is to identify his own successor.
Diplomats believe finding an heir is crucial for Jiang to fend off challenges from younger men and power-hungry elders.
Geremie Barme, an Australian Sinologist, stated that Jiang is now the incumbent leader facing a succession crisis following Deng's death.
China's leadership has presented a united front since Deng Xiaoping's death at the age of 92.
Some analysts suggest that this united front may be a facade.
The transfer of power in imperial China was rarely smooth.
Jiang Zemin must confront his own mortality and fend off other aspirants to power, including Qiao Shi, Zhu Rongji, and Li Peng.
Political pedigree and respect for age are highly valued in the Chinese political system.

Cathay Pacific Airways Limited is the first airline to test fly a new 'sharks skin' aircraft coating.
The coating could reduce fuel costs and revolutionize air travel.
One of Cathay's four Airbus A340-300 aircraft has been partly covered by transparent, plastic adhesive foils.
The foils contain fine ridges or riblets that resemble the texture of sharks' skin.
Scientists discovered that sharks swim faster due to fine ridges on their skin that reduce drag.
Airbus Industrie hopes the streamlining principle can be transferred to aircraft, reducing fuel burned by up to one percent.
The fuel bill savings over an aircraft's lifetime could be significant amid rising fuel prices.
Airbus has been conducting trials with the U.S. manufacturer 3M for several years.
Cathay is the first scheduled airline to apply the latest technology, higher durability film.
The experiment is expected to last between one and five years, with regular checks by Airbus and 3M engineers.

Northwest Airlines Cargo freighters have averaged 96.7 percent utilization on ex-Hong Kong flights over the past 12 months.
Alexander Wong is the cargo sales and marketing manager for Northwest Airlines in Hong Kong.
38,000 tonnes of cargo have been moved to and from Hong Kong on Northwest's trans-Pacific routes.
The past year has seen unusual highs and lows in cargo movement for Northwest Airlines.
February and March were the slowest months for Northwest Airlines in recent years.
October and November were the busiest months for Northwest Airlines in recent years.
Northwest Airlines is experiencing a similar volume of cargo as last year.
1996 was not as healthy for Northwest Airlines as 1994 and 1995.
Northwest Airlines lost US$6 million and eight million pounds of freight in the first three months of the year.
Yield for Northwest Airlines has increased slightly over the past two months but remains 8-10 percent below the 1995 level.

Cathay Pacific Airways Limited welcomed the approval for a second runway at Manchester airport.
Cathay Pacific is not planning to increase flight frequency into Manchester in the near future.
A second runway at Manchester airport will allow Cathay Pacific to optimize arrival and departure timings in the medium term.
A spokeswoman for Cathay Pacific made these statements to Reuters.
Cathay Pacific currently operates daily flights to Manchester airport.
The daily flights to Manchester are via Amsterdam, Frankfurt, or Paris.
The source of the information is Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom.
The contact number for Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom is +44 171 542 7706.
The fax number for Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom is +5017.

CE Electric claimed 50.03 percent of Northern Electric in a bid.
CE Electric needs takeover panel approval for additional acceptances to declare victory.
CE Electric held 49.77 percent of Northern Electric by its deadline on December 20.
The British takeover panel extended the final deadlines for the bid.
The deadline for the 782 million pound offer was extended to 1300 GMT on Christmas Eve.
Any acceptances after CE Electric's Friday deadline require panel consent.
The Financial Times reported that the panel felt shareholders were not treated fairly.
CE Electric stated that the panel prohibited Northern's advisers from purchasing shares before the close of CE Electric's final offers.
The panel cleared share purchases by Northern's advisers, which amounted to 2.32 percent of Northern.
Northern Electric is the only one of the original 12 cash-rich Recs to have successfully fought off a takeover bid.

Kingfisher Plc announced it would cut 1,200 jobs from the Norweb retail chain.
Kingfisher purchased Norweb in November 1996.
Kingfisher plans to close 28 Norweb retail stores.
Kingfisher will also close 26 Comet stores.
Kingfisher intends to upgrade Comet out-of-town stores, increasing the total from 225 to 250 locations.
26 Norweb retail stores in new locations will be converted to Comet stores.
Comet will proceed with plans to close all 57 high street sites of Norweb retail by the beginning of March.
Norweb's workforce before the job cuts was approximately 2,800 employees.
Kingfisher acquired Norweb retail for 51 million pounds from United Utilities.
Kingfisher issued a 200 million pound bond, likely for restructuring debt.

Northern Electric is a British regional electricity company.
Northern Electric is facing a hostile takeover bid from U.S. company CE Electric.
The Takeover Panel has launched an investigation into the circumstances of the bid.
The bid from CE Electric is valued at 782 million pounds, equivalent to 1.3 billion dollars.
The investigation will consider the actions of Northern's advisers, BZW.
BZW received a 250,000 pound payment from Northern in addition to a 1.5 million pound fixed fee.
BZW has denied any wrongdoing regarding the payment.
The Takeover Panel may investigate BZW and Schroders' acquisition of 2.32 percent of Northern Electric's shares.
CE Electric's shareholder acceptances for its bid increased to just over 50 percent by Monday.
Northern Electric has launched an appeal against the decision to extend the bid deadline.

Lloyds TSB Group is Britain's largest retail bank.
Lloyds TSB Group has started an in-depth review of business opportunities overseas.
Peter Ellwood is the chief executive of Lloyds TSB Group.
Ellwood stated that overseas expansion has been challenging for British banks.
Lloyds TSB Group is considering potential growth opportunities in different parts of the world.
The decision on where to invest will depend on the bank's products, services, and available distribution channels.
Lloyds is evaluating whether to enter markets organically or through acquisition.
Ellwood mentioned that Lloyds is assessing risks associated with expanding into Australia, Latin America, North America, and Europe.
Lloyds has historical connections with Latin America and is interested in expanding consumer finance products in Brazil.
Lloyds TSB has been identified as a candidate for expansion into Australia.

HSBC Holdings Plc is based in London.
HSBC reported a 23 percent rise in profits for 1996.
John Bond is the chief executive of HSBC.
Bond stated that HSBC faces a challenging year ahead due to increasing competition.
HSBC derives 55 percent of its profits from the Asia-Pacific region.
HSBC announced pretax profits for 1996 of 4.52 billion pounds ($7.3 billion).
HSBC increased its annual dividend by nine pence per share to 41 pence.
Midland Bank, a unit of HSBC, reported pretax profits up more than 20 percent.
HSBC's tier one capital ratio rose to 9.9 percent from 9.5 percent at the end of 1995.
HSBC had a return on capital of 21.3 percent in 1996, compared to 20.7 percent in 1995.

Britain's securities market watchdog disciplined former Barings executive James Bax.
The cases of managers blamed for Barings' collapse have been completed.
Barings collapsed in February 1995 due to 800 million pounds in losses from unauthorized derivatives trades by trader Nick Leeson.
Nick Leeson is currently imprisoned in Singapore.
The SFA initiated proceedings against nine former senior executives of Barings.
Peter Baring and Andrew Tuckey were not proceeded against by the SFA.
The nine executives include Peter Norris, Ron Baker, James Bax, Geoff Broadhurst, Tony Gamby, Tony Hawes, Ian Hopkins, George Maclean, and Mary Walz.
Only Ian Hopkins and Ron Baker have outstanding business with the SFA.
Barings was taken over by Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV and now operates as ING Barings.
Britain's Department of Trade has started legal proceedings that could ban the Barings nine plus Tuckey from being directors of any British company for up to 15 years.

Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec stated that his country views Russian hints of economic reprisals for Prague's entry into NATO as frivolous and absolutely unacceptable.
Zieleniec said it is frivolous to connect the expansion of NATO with Czech-Russian relations and to threaten economic sanctions in this context.
Moscow's ambassador to Prague, Nikolai Ryabov, warned that key bilateral agreements with Russia might be jeopardized if the Czech Republic joined NATO.
Ryabov indicated that the Czech Republic's entry into NATO could result in a damaging loss of arms markets for Moscow.
Ryabov hinted that Moscow could reconsider economic deals with Prague if it proceeded with NATO membership.
Ryabov mentioned that agreements fundamental to the Czech Republic, such as gas deliveries and nuclear energy, could lead to future problems between the countries.
Zieleniec stated that Ryabov's comments highlighted the reasons for the Czech Republic's desire to join Western organizations.
Zieleniec expressed that demands like those from Ryabov emphasize the importance of joining key Western political, economic, and security organizations.
The Czech Republic, Poland, and Hungary are expected to be among the first former-Soviet Bloc countries invited to join NATO at a July summit in Madrid.
In 1996, total Czech trade turnover with Russia grew by 9.8 percent to $2.8 billion, with Czech exports to Russia at $694 million and imports from Russia at $2.1 billion.

Zieleniec indicated that Ryabov's statement highlighted the reasons for the Czech Republic's desire to join western organizations.
Zieleniec stated that the demand made by Ryabov underscores the importance of joining key western political, economic, and security organizations as soon as possible.
Zieleniec believed that Ryabov's interview on Russian television was primarily for media consumption.
Czech trade turnover with Russia increased by 9.8 percent in 1996 to $2.8 billion, with Czech exports to Russia at $694 million and imports from Russia at $2.1 billion.

The Czechs have a history of success at the Oscars.
Jan and Zdenek Sverak won an Academy Award for their film 'Kolya'.
'Kolya' tells the story of an ageing bachelor who takes in an abandoned Russian boy during the 1989 Velvet Revolution in Prague.
'Kolya' won the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film.
President Vaclav Havel sent a victory telegram to the Sveraks in Los Angeles.
Havel expressed pleasure at the success of the film and noted it was the first Czech film to win an Oscar in many years.
Czech media celebrated the win for Jan Sverak and Zdenek Sverak.
'Kolya' is the first Czech foreign language film to win an Oscar since 'Closely Observed Trains' in 1968.
Elmar Klos won the best foreign film Oscar in 1966 for 'The Shop On Main Street'.
Milos Forman, a Czech director, won Oscars for 'Amadeus' in 1985 and 'One Flew Over The Cuckoo's Nest' in 1976.

British Gas Plc announced a sharp deterioration in interim profits.
Chairman Richard Giordano stated that the company is in a realistic phase of negotiations with producers over gas supply contracts.
Giordano identified take or pay contracts as a major factor behind growing losses in the industrial and commercial division.
British Gas is obligated to buy gas at prices above market rates due to these contracts.
The company is paying around 20 pence per therm for gas compared to market rates of 10 to 13 pence.
Progress on renegotiating these contracts is described as a gradual process.
Giordano reported that losses in the industrial and commercial division rose to 180 million stg from around 50 million stg the previous year.
The first-half results were improved by a 200 million pound benefit from severe winter weather.
Giordano forecasted full-year losses of close to 400 million stg for the industrial and commercial division.
Ofgas is requesting Transco to reduce charges to gas suppliers by 20 percent in 1997 and by 6.5 points below inflation for the following four years.

Coats Viyella Plc reported lower first-half results.
Coats Viyella Plc is confident it will return to profit growth in 1997 after restructuring.
The first-half pretax profit fell 34 percent to 47 million pounds due to reorganisation costs.
The first 17.2 million pounds of reorganisation costs were announced in March.
An additional 38 million pounds of costs will be charged against second-half earnings.
Chief executive Neville Bain stated that charges will be taken this year for a clean basis in 1997.
Bain predicted a good return to profit in 1997.
Coats' shares increased by 4-1/2 pence to 164 pence following the announcement.
Bain expressed confidence in achieving cumulative annual cost savings of 10 million pounds in the second half of 1996, 25 million pounds in 1997, and 35 million pounds in 1998.
The reorganisation will involve shedding 7,750 jobs, including nearly 3,000 in Britain.

Vanguard Medica Plc is a young drug discovery group.
Vanguard announced it could wait longer than expected before seeking additional funding.
Vanguard floated on the stock exchange in May, raising 46.4 million stg.
The funds raised are intended to support its drug pipeline, which includes migraine and kidney failure drugs.
Vanguard's commercial director is Nick Heightman.
Vanguard reported a pretax loss of 3.7 million stg for the six months ending June 30, which is an increase from 1.8 million stg the previous year.
The loss is attributed to the costs associated with moving migraine drug VML 251 and anti-inflammatory drug VML 295 through trials.
Heightman stated that results of Phase II trials for the migraine drug were expected by July 1997, but are now anticipated in the first quarter of the following year.
Analysts indicate that the migraine drug accounts for about half of Vanguard's current stock market valuation.
Vanguard's shares fell by 5.5 pence to 495 pence on Thursday.

Protesters armed with rocks, sticks, and bottles clashed with police in Bogota's main plaza on Tuesday.
The clashes occurred on the first day of a nationwide strike by state workers.
Leftist rebels announced their support for the indefinite work stoppage.
The Bogota-based 13th Army Brigade reported at least 42 arrests on terrorist charges.
More than 50 guns were seized during the army's operation against agitators.
Union leaders claimed the strike had the total support of approximately 800,000 public sector employees.
The strike disrupted airports, telecommunications, oil production, government administration, and emergency health services.
Running battles occurred in Bogota's Plaza Bolivar involving 200 young protesters.
The rally of about 30,000 striking workers outside Congress ended shortly after the violence began.
State workers are demanding a 21.5 percent wage increase and an end to repressive labor legislation.

Police and military forces were recalled to barracks in Colombia on Sunday.
All school and university classes were canceled in Colombia on Sunday.
Colombia prepared for a threatened national strike on Tuesday.
The national strike is expected to be the largest in 20 years.
Talks between union chiefs and government ministers broke down on Sunday.
More than 800,000 state workers are planning to participate in the strike.
Labor leaders expressed concerns that the government might use claims of rebel assaults as a pretext for a crackdown on striking workers.
State workers are demanding a 21.5 percent pay hike.
The government offered a weighted 13.5 percent pay increase to state workers.
The government stated that the salary demands exceed its current financial capacity.

The Colombian government passed legislation to increase jail terms for drug traffickers.
The legislation was expedited through Congress after being stalled for six months.
The new law raises the maximum penalty for drug-related offenses from 24 years to 60 years.
President Ernesto Samper plans to sign the bill into law before the end of the week.
Samper described the bill's passage as evidence of Colombia's commitment to combat the drug trade.
The vote occurred one week before the United States was set to decide on Colombia's certification as a reliable ally in the drug fight.
Decertification could lead to economic sanctions against Colombia for not adequately addressing drug trafficking.
Justice Minister Carlos Medellin stated that Colombia produces strong laws to combat drug trafficking.
U.S. Ambassador Myles Frechette criticized the new sentencing guidelines for not meeting U.S. standards.
Colombia is set to sign a maritime accord with the United States to help intercept drug shipments at sea.

Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc believes any bid would need to be at a premium to its current share price.
Ward Thomas is the chairman and chief executive of YTT.
Ward Thomas stated that a bid from Granada Group Plc is extremely likely.
Granada Group Plc holds a 27 percent stake in YTT.
YTT is an ITV commercial television broadcaster serving northern cities such as Leeds and Newcastle.
YTT shares have increased by approximately 80 percent over the past 14 months.
The current share price of YTT is around 12.50 pounds ($20.07).
YTT's market value is approximately 800 million pounds, including warrants.
Ward Thomas suggested that a realistic bid would need to be around 17 pounds per share.
United News & Media Plc holds a 14 percent stake in YTT and operates ITV franchises for southern and eastern England.

Reed Elsevier Plc reported an 11 percent rise in profit for 1996.
Reed Elsevier warned that currencies could depress earnings for the current year.
Co-chairman Nigel Stapleton stated that the strength of sterling could reduce headline earnings by five percent this year.
Pre-tax profits for Reed Elsevier rose to 805 million pounds from 723 million pounds.
Turnover from continuing operations increased to 3.38 billion pounds from 3.21 billion pounds.
Analysts had forecast profits between 808 and 821 million pounds.
Reed International Plc proposed a two-for-one share split to take effect in May.
Reed shares were down 23.5 pence to 1,150.5 pence at 1145 GMT.
Elsevier NV shares in Amsterdam decreased by 1.70 guilders to 30.80 guilders.
The full-year dividend for Reed shareholders was raised by 11 percent to 27.2 pence per share.

Britain's Express Newspapers announced plans to shed around 85 jobs.
Express Newspapers is putting its Daily and Sunday Express national titles under a single editorial team.
Express Newspapers is part of United News & Media.
Express Newspapers plans to invest around 10 million pounds to improve the quality of the two newspapers.
The planned job cuts will cost approximately six million pounds in redundancy charges.
The Daily Express has average sales of around 1.2 million copies.
The Daily Express had a circulation of over four million in the 1960s.
The Daily Mail sells more than two million copies daily.
Express Newspapers plans to offer colour supplements on Saturdays and Sundays.
Richard Addis will take charge of the papers seven days a week.

Health Care and Retirement Corp expects to maintain a rapid rate of profit growth.
Health Care and Retirement Corp is open to a large strategic transaction if the right opportunity arises.
Geoffrey Meyers is the chief financial officer of Health Care and Retirement Corp.
Health Care and Retirement Corp recorded earnings growth of more than 20 percent in every quarter since going public in 1991.
The earnings growth for this year is reported to be $1.47, which represents 19 percent growth.
Health Care and Retirement Corp has provided guidance of 18 to 20 percent growth for the following year.
The company reported revenues of $782 million in 1996, compared to $713.4 million in 1995.
The underlying growth rate in revenues for Health Care and Retirement Corp is about 10 percent.
Health Care and Retirement Corp made an acquisition of a company called Milestone this year.
The acquisition of Milestone is expected to add another three to four percent to revenue growth.

Diametrics Medical Inc plans to be profitable by the third quarter of 1998.
Diametrics Medical Inc aims to generate revenues of $3.5 million in 1996, $8 million in 1997, and $18 million in 1998.
David Giddings is the chief executive of Diametrics Medical Inc.
Diametrics Medical Inc is a maker of hospital-bedside blood gas analysis systems.
Diametrics reported a year-end loss of $23 million in 1995.
Diametrics expects to launch its new IRMA SL blood gas analyzer system this month.
The IRMA SL blood gas analyzer is a portable, four-pound instrument.
The IRMA SL measures blood levels of oxygen, acidity, carbon dioxide, electrolytes, and red blood cell volume faster than competing systems.
Diametrics' workforce has decreased from 223 to 174 employees after an 18-percent cut.
Shares in Diametrics were trading at 5-1/4, up 3/8.

Boehringer Mannheim Corp is a unit of Corange Ltd.
Data released at an American College of Cardiology conference indicated comparability between Boehringer's Retavase and Genentech's Activase in the market for clot-busting drugs.
Gregory Fulton is the director of marketing for Boehringer's pharmaceuticals unit.
The GUSTO III study results showed that Retavase did not save more lives than Activase.
In the GUSTO III trial, 10,139 patients received Retavase and 4,921 patients received Activase.
Retavase did not provide a statistically significant benefit in 30-day mortality compared to Activase, according to Genentech.
Genentech stated that Retavase failed to prove it was better than Activase.
Fulton acknowledged that the results of the study were clear.
The 30-day mortality rate was 7.43 percent for Retavase and 7.22 percent for Activase.
The total intracranial bleeding rate was 0.91 percent for Retavase and 0.88 percent for Activase.

Muhammad Yunus is the head of Grameen Bank.
Grameen Bank makes money by lending to some of the world's poorest people.
Ninety-four percent of Grameen's borrowers are women.
Grameen Bank provides loans without requiring collateral or credit ratings.
Grameen Bank has attracted more than two million customers since its establishment in 1976.
Yunus claims that 98 percent of loans from Grameen Bank are repaid.
Yunus's goal is to help poor people escape poverty.
The World Bank has appointed Yunus as chairman of its policy advisory group for lending programs to the poor.
The first Micro-Credit Summit aimed to ensure that 100 million of the world's poorest families receive credit by 2005.
CGAP was formed with the financial backing of the World Bank and European Commission to support micro-lending banks.

John Fairfax Holdings Ltd is Australia's oldest newspaper group.
John Fairfax Holdings Ltd is expected to unveil lower half year earnings for 1996/97.
Analysts estimate Fairfax will report a net profit before abnormals of between A$37 million and A$42 million for the first half.
Fairfax reported a 23.2 percent fall in net profit to A$62.43 million for the 1995/96 half.
Analysts expect improving advertising revenue and lower newsprint costs in the second quarter.
Nola Hodgson, an analyst at HSBC James Capel, estimates a net profit of A$38 million to A$39 million for Fairfax.
Vince Pepe at Burdett Buckeridge and Young estimates a net profit of A$40 million for the half and A$75.1 million for the 1996/97 year.
Fairfax reported a net profit before abnormals of A$102 million in the 1995/96 year.
Fairfax profits have been declining for the past 18 months due to higher newsprint costs and falling advertising revenue.
Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd owns about 15 percent of Fairfax.

Telstra Corp and Optus Communications Pty Ltd are major investors in Australia's pay television industry.
Telstra and Optus are facing upcoming sharemarket floats and challenges in a deregulated telephone market.
Foxtel, Optus Vision, and Australis Media Ltd are the three main players in Australia's pay-TV industry.
These three companies have incurred losses of nearly A$1.5 billion since 1993.
Rationalisation among the pay TV operators may involve sharing cable and satellite facilities and ending exclusive programming.
A telecommunications analyst stated that rationalising the pay TV industry would be beneficial for all parties involved.
The market valuations of Telstra and Optus could increase with industry rationalisation.
Optus and Telstra confirmed they were in talks about sharing infrastructure during their profit results release for the six months to December 31, 1996.
Telstra is investing about A$4 billion in a fibre-optic cable network for its Foxtel service.
Optus Communications is spending A$3.0 billion on a rival cable network.

Shares in Carlton Communications rose by 10p to 526.5p.
Shares in Granada rose by 13p to 848.5p.
Carlton Communications and Granada were awarded three key licences to operate multi-channel digital terrestrial TV in Britain.
BSkyB was required to sell its 33 percent stake in the consortium British Digital Broadcasting due to competition concerns.
Carlton and Granada will buy out BSkyB's one-third stake and become joint owners of the new company.
BSkyB will continue to provide programmes for the group for 75 million pounds ($125.1 million).
Oftel warned the ITC against allowing BSkyB to provide programmes due to competition concerns.
British Digital Broadcasting beat a rival bid from Digital Television Network to operate the licences.
Michael Green, chairman of British Digital Broadcasting, stated that going digital is a significant change for British television.
British Digital Broadcasting plans to invest 300 million pounds into the venture to build infrastructure and organize programmes.

A high-level think tank called for a global regulatory framework to combat crime risks on the Internet.
The Centre for the Study of Financial Innovation (CSFI) stated that without effective regulation, the Internet could lead to financial scandals.
CSFI claimed that the lack of regulation could undermine national financial market regulations and leave consumers unprotected.
The CSFI conducted a comprehensive study on the Internet's potential impact on the financial services industry.
The CSFI noted that the Internet offers significant opportunities for financial services.
CSFI director Andrew Hilton stated that the Internet provides a low-cost distribution medium, up to 10 times cheaper than others.
The CSFI warned against paranoia regarding cybercrime, citing a lack of objective information.
The extensive use of cryptography makes online business more secure than providing credit card information over the phone.
The CSFI suggested implementing a 'kitemark' for regulated firms, increased use of firewalls, and tighter security procedures for staff.
Andrew Large, chairman of the Securities and Investment Board, indicated that the movement towards a global marketplace may necessitate global regulation.

Telewest Communications Plc reported widening annual losses.
Telewest's telephony and cable television margins were below market expectations.
Telewest may delay building its national network due to heavy investments needed for multi-channel digital television.
Telewest's annual losses before tax increased to 249.9 million pounds from 114.67 million pounds.
Telewest's turnover increased to 290.27 million pounds from 144.78 million pounds, excluding franchise acquisitions.
Telewest is expected to lose its position as Britain's biggest cable operator due to a merger involving Cable and Wireless Plc's Mercury unit.
Telewest's shares decreased by three pence to 117-1/2p after the results were announced.
Telewest's telephony margins were reported at 67 percent and cable television margins at 42 percent.
Telewest's finance director Charles Burdick indicated the company might seek additional funds for investment plans.
Telewest has approximately 900 million pounds of debt and has secured a 1.2 billion pound bank facility.

Informix Corp. is facing declining sales of its database software products.
Informix Corp. plans to raise cash and is considering refinancing its leases.
The company has not yet decided whether to refinance its leases.
Informix Corp. aims to raise capital to offset upcoming operational losses.
Informix Corp. is considering refinancing leases on land in Santa Clara, California.
The company believes it will acquire necessary financing, but there is no assurance it will be available.
Failure to raise working capital could adversely affect Informix's business and financial condition.
Informix Corp. is based in Menlo Park, California, and is the second-largest publisher of database software.
Informix reported a first-quarter loss of $140.1 million on revenue of $133.7 million.
Informix's shares increased by 24 percent to $11.375 based on speculation of a potential acquisition.

Sequent Computer Systems Inc expects its revenue to increase at least 30 percent in 1997.
The expectation of revenue growth is based on strong sales of the new NUMA-Q computer.
Casey Powell is the chairman and chief executive of Sequent.
Sequent specializes in making computers that use multiple Intel Corp Pentium microprocessors.
A Sequent machine has similar processing power to an International Business Machine Corp mainframe computer.
Sequent's new NUMA-Q line offers increased power at a lower cost compared to mainframes.
Scott Butler is an analyst at Jensen Securities.
Companies such as Boeing Co, Unocal Corp, and Ford Motor Co have purchased Sequent machines.
A quarter of Sequent's fourth-quarter revenue of $183.2 million came from NUMA-Q sales.
In 1996, Sequent had a net income of $7.77 million on revenue of $595.4 million.

Apple Computer Inc. plans to release an operating system that will work on personal computers based on Intel Corp. chips and on Apple computers.
Apple will release programming tools that allow companies to write software for Apple computers and convert it to run on PCs based on Intel chips and Microsoft Corp.'s Windows software.
Apple's strategy aims to prevent software companies from abandoning Apple products.
Apple Chairman Gilbert Amelio stated that the new development environment offers promise for those seeking business on both Mac and Windows platforms.
Amelio mentioned that applications can be written once and released for both platforms with simple recompilation.
Apple has previously released operating system software that runs only on Apple-designed hardware.
Apple's next-generation operating system is code-named Rhapsody and will run on Apple-designed computers and PCs based on Intel chips.
Richard Zwetchkenbaum, an analyst at International Data Corp., commented that entering the PC market provides Apple an opportunity to showcase its technology.
Apple has been working on improvements to the Macintosh to differentiate it from PCs for the past two years.
Apple acquired Next Software Inc. to facilitate a software overhaul and use Next software as the foundation for the next-generation operating system.

Cognos Inc had a strong fiscal year in 1998.
Cognos Inc has $100 million in cash.
Ron Zambonini is the Chief Executive of Cognos Inc.
Cognos Inc's fiscal year 1997 ended on February 28.
Cognos Inc's revenues grew 34 percent to US$51.3 million in the third quarter of 1997.
Cognos Inc's net earnings for the first nine months of fiscal 1997 rose to US$23.5 million.
Cognos Inc plans to release six new products and versions in the first quarter.
Cognos Inc acquired Right Information Systems Ltd for $8 million in cash and stock.
Cognos Inc plans to expand operations in Europe, particularly in Germany, Italy, and Scandinavia.
Cognos Inc's shares were down from a 52-week high of 53.50.

Toronto's key stock index ended higher on Thursday.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 29.80 points to close at 5828.62.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 21.27 points to finish at 6658.60.
Toronto's index extended a rally from Wednesday, which was 55 points.
MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie stated that markets are fragile.
Beattie noted that investors want to take advantage of any strength to sell.
Toronto's gold group increased nearly 2.2 percent due to firmer COMEX gold prices.
The key June gold contract rose $1.00 to $344.30.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-indices posted gains, with golds leading.
Trading volume was 100 million shares worth C$1.54 billion.

The Toronto stock market reached a record close on Tuesday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's Composite Index rose 20.62 points to end at 6238.22.
Turnover on the Toronto Stock Exchange was 138.47 million shares worth C$2.52 billion.
This turnover was the second highest value ever for the TSE.
Ira Katzin is an investment advisor at RBC Dominion Securities.
Canadians are contributing to tax-sheltered pension plans before the March 1 deadline.
Canada's Finance Minister Paul Martin presented the 1997/98 budget after market close.
