Kmart produced earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of A$50.6 million in the first half of 1995/96, down from A$93.2 million the previous comparable half.
Coles' supermarket division is also seen improving as sales have held up in the food sector.

Papua New Guinea's Australian-listed stocks rallied on Thursday.
Foreign investors reacted positively to the peaceful resolution of a 10-day political crisis in Papua New Guinea.
Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan decided to step aside, which calmed the political situation.
David Walker, Head of Mining Research at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, stated that the parliamentary process worked and avoided military control.
Walker noted that there is an expectation for mid-year elections to be brought forward.
Chan stepped down due to pressure related to his hiring of mercenaries to suppress an uprising on Bougainville island.
Orogen Minerals Ltd closed up eight cents at A$3.10.
Oil Search Ltd closed up 13 cents at A$2.70.
Lihir Gold Ltd rose two cents to A$2.15.
Collins and Leahy Ltd closed up 25 cents at A$3.50.

Natwest Markets Australia Ltd aims to maintain its leading market share in equities broking in Australia in 1997.
Natwest Markets Australia Ltd will avoid the mortgage securitisation sector.
Peter St George is the chief executive of Natwest Markets Australia Ltd.
Natwest Markets Australia Ltd currently has a 9.8 percent market share in equities broking in Australia.
Natwest Markets Australia Ltd plans to broaden and deepen its market penetration.
Natwest Markets Australia Ltd needs to widen its research and distribution activities to adapt to changes in the Australian stock market over the next two to three years.
The privatisation of Telstra Corp and the sale of government-owned airports will change the market.
The demutualisation of The Australian Mutual Provident Society will also impact the market.
Natwest Markets Australia reported a 40 percent rise in operating profit before tax to A$70.5 million for calendar 1996.
Natwest's debt and corporate finance divisions will focus on non-government debt operations and avoid securitised mortgage deals.

Caterpillar Inc is concerned that the continued strength of the dollar could pressure its pricing.
The impact of the dollar's strength was minimal in the first quarter of the year.
Douglas Oberhelman is the chief financial officer of Caterpillar Inc.
Caterpillar Inc has restructured its business to manage an overvalued dollar.
The restructuring includes increased overseas production.
The dollar is at a multi-year high against the yen.
Oberhelman stated that pricing competition from Japanese competitors could occur later this year due to the strong dollar.
Oberhelman indicated that continued strength of the dollar could lead to price erosion later in the year.
Caterpillar expects profits in 1997 to rise from 1996 due to moderately higher sales.
Caterpillar reported net income of $394 million for the first quarter, an increase from $296 million a year ago.

Hyatt Hotels Corp. will spend $1 billion over the next three years to acquire 20 to 30 hotels.
Target properties will be upscale hotels and resorts in the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean.
Hyatt has already made two deals typical of its expansion plan.
A Hyatt affiliate purchased the Grand Hyatt San Francisco, which Hyatt has managed since 1973.
Hyatt will take over management of the Hotel Nikko Atlanta after acquiring the hotel in partnership with Blackstone Real Estate Partners.
The Hotel Nikko Atlanta will be renamed the Grand Hyatt Atlanta.
Hyatt's plan was facilitated by a recent reorganization of some Pritzker family holdings.
The Pritzker family formed Hyatt Equities L.L.C., a real estate acquisition company.
Hyatt Equities consolidates the family's hotel real estate interests into one company.
Hyatt Equities debt will be rated by Standard and Poor's and Moody's.

Warm weather increased sales of spring merchandise in February.
Flooding in the Midwest may negatively impact retail results in March.
Most winter clothing was sold out by January and early February.
Retailers were adequately stocked for spring merchandise.
Salomon Bros. reported a 4.7 percent increase in same-store sales in February.
The same-store sales increase in February was lower than the 5.2 percent rise a year ago.
January same-store sales rose by 7.3 percent.
Harry Ikenson, an analyst at Rodman & Renshaw Inc., stated that early trends for spring fashion are positive.
William Kellogg, chairman of Kohl's Corp., noted that clearance merchandise levels were lower than the previous year.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc. reported a 6.7 percent increase in same-store sales.

The Busang rumor mill was active on Wednesday.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc extended its review of the Busang gold project.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd announced that Freeport was granted an extension for its due diligence review until June 30.
Freeport requested the extension to consider the findings of the Strathcona audit.
Rumors about Busang began after Freeport's preliminary due diligence tests found insignificant amounts of gold.
Panic selling of Bre-X shares resulted in a loss of almost C$3 billion or 80 percent of the company's market value last month.
Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd is expected to deliver a key report on Busang to Bre-X on Thursday or Friday.
Bre-X plans to issue a press release on the report before North American financial markets open on Monday.
Freeport spokeswoman Kristin Lemkau stated that the request for the extension was made within the past week.
Bre-X shares closed down C32 cents at C$3.48 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is considering merger offers at the right price.
Bre-X is currently focused on developing the Busang gold discovery with existing partners.
David Walsh is the Chief Executive of Bre-X.
Bre-X owns 45 percent of the Busang discovery.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc. owns 15 percent of the Busang discovery.
PT Askatindo Karya Minerals and PT Amsya Lyna and partners own 30 percent of the Busang discovery.
The Indonesian government owns 10 percent of the Busang discovery.
Bre-X executives estimate that the Busang gold field may contain as much as 200 million ounces of gold.
Placer Dome Inc. stated that its $5 billion merger offer for Bre-X is no longer feasible.
Bre-X's partners do not have rights of first refusal if Bre-X receives a third-party offer.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd's chief executive and senior geologist were recognized as Canada's top prospectors in March.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc withdrew from the Busang gold project after a consultant's report deemed it a fraud.
The consultant's report stated that Busang was the biggest fraud in mining history.
Freeport confirmed its own poor test results from the Busang site.
Freeport's chief executive Jim Bob Moffett noted that the first sign of issues at Busang was from PT Indo Assay Laboratories.
PT Indo Assay Laboratories could not find significant amounts of gold in Freeport's samples.
Moffett attempted to contact Bre-X Minerals Chief Executive David Walsh and Chief of Exploration John Felderhof.
Both Walsh and Felderhof were in Toronto to receive awards at a gala ceremony hosted by the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada.
Bre-X's chief geologist, Michael de Guzman, attended the conference in Toronto.
A report by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd stated that the Busang discovery was falsified on an unprecedented scale.

Chrysler Corp. agreed to sell Pentastar Electronics Inc. to a management-led investment group for less than $50 million.
Pentastar Electronics is based in Huntsville, Ala., and produces electronic test equipment for tanks and military systems.
Pentastar Electronics has about 350 employees and annual sales in the $50-million range.
The terms of the sale to PEI Acquisition Corp. were not announced, but the price is less than Pentastar's annual revenues.
Chrysler hopes to close the sale before the end of 1996, but conditions may delay it into 1997.
A company spokeswoman did not disclose whether Chrysler would book a gain on the deal.
The new company will operate as PEI Electronics Inc. and negotiated changes to the United Auto Workers contract at the plant.
The deal preserved UAW wages and benefits for current workers but allowed PEI to hire new workers at lower wages.
PEI won permission to change work rules and job classifications to improve efficiency.
PEI expects to hire about 200 new workers over the next 12 months as it executes expansion plans.

United Auto Workers leaders will likely choose a strike target among the Big Three automakers in the next few days.
The UAW has less than two weeks to craft a pattern-setting labour agreement.
UAW Vice President Ernest Lofton stated that the UAW is focusing on General Motors Corp. and Ford Motor Co.
Chrysler Corp. is not likely to be the lead company because it is the Canadian Auto Workers' strike target.
Labour contracts for about 400,000 UAW and 53,000 CAW hourly workers expire on September 14.
The Canadian Auto Workers have extended their deadline until September 17.
Lofton indicated that the U.S. target selection needs to happen this week.
Some UAW officials suggested an announcement could occur as early as Tuesday.
Historically, the UAW's target choice has been made before Labour Day.
UAW President Stephen Yokich delayed the target choice to allow a company to demonstrate willingness to meet union demands.

Chrysler Corp unveiled five concept cars on Sunday.
The concept cars include two new versions of the Jeep Wrangler sport/utility vehicle.
One of the concept cars is a new Dodge roadster based on the Plymouth Prowler chassis.
Another concept car is an affordable Neon-based small car with a roll-back top.
There is also a 1940s-style 'dual-cowl' convertible among the concept cars.
Thomas Gale is Chrysler's new product development chief.
Gale stated that no decision has been made to take any of the concept cars to market.
Chrysler will monitor consumer reactions to the vehicles at this year's auto show circuit.
Positive public reaction has previously led Chrysler to put concept cars into volume production.
The concept cars were unveiled at the start of Detroit's North American International Auto Show.

Ford Motor Co's Halewood plant in England employs four and a half thousand workers.
A meeting between Ford management and unions is scheduled for Thursday to discuss the plant's future.
Reports indicate that Ford may announce 1,500 job cuts at the meeting.
A Ford spokesman declined to comment on speculation regarding the plant's future.
Ford has not issued any statements regarding workforce reductions or plant restructuring in Britain.
A statement from Ford is expected at midday on Thursday.
The Transport and General Workers Union is involved in the discussions and will hold a press briefing at the plant.
The unions stated they had not received confirmation of job cuts from Ford prior to the meeting.
Ford's group boss Alex Trotman warned last year about taking drastic actions to address losses in Europe.
Analysts believe it is unlikely that Ford will close the Halewood plant and eliminate all 5,000 jobs.

BAA Plc is a British airports group that operates London Heathrow, Europe's largest airport hub.
BAA Plc reported a 6.2 percent increase in pretax profits for the nine months ending December 31.
The pretax profits for the period were 397 million pounds, equivalent to 636.5 million dollars.
Total revenue for the period increased to 1.06 billion pounds from 987 million pounds.
76.6 million passengers traveled through BAA's airports, which include Gatwick and Stansted.
Airport and traffic charge revenue was 385 million pounds, an increase of 5.5 percent.
Retailing revenue reached 475 million pounds, up 10 percent, resulting in net retail income of 331 million pounds, which is an 11 percent increase.
Property income rose by 8.4 percent to 168 million pounds.
BAA's shares fell by seven pence to 525 pence per share following the report.
BAA is submitting bids to operate overseas airports and has decided to reduce its stake in a bid group for three Australian airports.

Britain approved CE Electric's 782 million pound bid for Northern Electric.
CE Electric's bid is valued at $1.3 billion.
Analysts believe CE Electric is likely to succeed in acquiring Northern Electric.
CE Electric holds a 29 percent market share.
Ian Lang is the trade and industry minister who approved the bid.
CE Electric is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy.
CE Electric increased its bid to 650 pence per share from 630 pence on December 6.
The deadline for acceptances of the bid is December 20.
Northern Electric claims the bid undervalues the company and suggests a price of 700 pence per share.
Prudential Corporation owns more than 11 percent of Northern Electric's shares.

A device was introduced that turns a personal computer into an automated teller machine capable of dispensing card-based electronic cash.
Fischer International Systems Corp. developed the device, which costs $60 and can be inserted into the floppy disk drive of any PC.
The device enables PCs to read 'smart cards,' which can perform electronic cash transactions and store bank account balances.
Smart cards are gaining popularity in Europe for store purchases and telephone calls and are beginning to be adopted in the United States.
The device may stimulate home banking by allowing consumers to perform financial transactions without visiting a bank branch or ATM.
Fischer President Michael Battaglia stated that a low-cost, easy-to-use 'bridge' between smart cards and personal computers was previously missing.
The product, named Smarty, connects PCs to banks or retail outlets via the Internet.
Fischer holds key patents for smart card readers that fit into 3.5-inch floppy drives, making Smarty adaptable for 200 million personal computers.
The device allows consumers to use banking cards for purchases, reducing the need to carry cash.
Fischer is collaborating with major U.S. and European financial services firms and is in discussions with home banking software providers like Intuit Inc. and Microsoft Corp.

New York state utility regulators approved the $23 billion merger between Nynex Corp. and Bell Atlantic Corp.
The approval is subject to conditions that must be agreed upon by the companies by the end of March.
Consumer groups opposed the merger and criticized the decision as a sellout.
New York was the last state in Nynex's six-state service region to approve the merger.
The merger would create the largest local phone company in the United States, serving customers in 12 Northeastern states and Washington.
John O'Mara, Chairman of the New York State Public Service Commission, stated that improved service quality and tangible benefits for ratepayers are requirements for approval.
O'Mara indicated that there would be no immediate rate reduction but conditions attached could lead to rate reductions in the future.
The merger is currently under review by federal regulators for its competitive implications.
Bell Atlantic spokesman Eric Rabe stated that the companies expect the deal to close after April 22.
State Attorney General Dennis Vacco expressed concern that the decision did not adequately protect ratepayers.

AT&T Corp. reported a 17 percent decline in first-quarter profits.
AT&T's profits were affected by competition in long-distance services and investments in new businesses.
AT&T warned that second quarter results might also be weak.
BellSouth Corp. reported an 11 percent increase in operating earnings.
BellSouth's earnings growth was attributed to an increase in customer lines and strong wireless operations.
AT&T earned $1.13 billion, or 69 cents a share, on revenues of $13.05 billion in the first quarter.
In the first quarter of 1996, AT&T had a net income of $1.36 billion, or 85 cents a share, on revenues of $12.85 billion.
AT&T's earnings per share for the first quarter met Wall Street's expectations.
AT&T's first quarter revenue increase was driven by growth in local telephone service, business long-distance services, and wireless services.
BellSouth earned $693 million, or 70 cents a share, on revenues of $4.8 billion in the three months ended March 31.

Nippon Credit Bank Ltd announced a partnership with Bankers Trust.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd has a significant amount of real estate loans from the 1980s asset bubble.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd is considered one of the most endangered large banks in Japan's banking sector.
On April 1, Nippon Credit Bank Ltd announced its withdrawal from international operations.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd is selling prime real estate and issuing new shares to rebuild its capital.
Bankers Trust will assist Nippon Credit Bank Ltd in securitizing some of its loans.
The partnership will allow Nippon Credit Bank Ltd to maintain customer services after its withdrawal from overseas business.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd is considering a capital tie-up with Bankers Trust.
Industry analysts noted that a foreign bank taking a stake in a Japanese bank would be unprecedented.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd's debentures were downgraded to junk-bond status by Moody's Investors Service.

Japanese prosecutors raided Nomura Securities Co Ltd on Tuesday.
The raid was part of a widening probe into payments linked to racketeers.
Prosecutors and officials from the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission conducted the raid.
The raids were preceded by media tip-offs about their imminence.
The action against Nomura may signal Japan's efforts to clean up business practices.
Deputy chief prosecutor Kunihiro Matsuo stated the raids were to investigate illegal payments by a Nomura director.
The illegal payment involved 38 million yen ($309,000) to a company run by a relative of a racketeer.
Nomura director Shimpei Matsuki was involved in the scandal and resigned along with fellow director Nobutaka Fujikura.
Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki stepped down on March 14 and became an adviser to the company.
Nomura is a major player in the yen bond market and has seen clients suspend business since the scandal.

Nippon Credit Bank Ltd had 10 trillion yen of its senior debt cut to junk levels by Moody's.
The downgrade by Moody's is expected to raise costs for Nippon Credit Bank.
Financial analysts view the downgrade as a vote of no-confidence in Japan's financial sector reforms.
Nippon Credit Bank is undergoing a restructuring program monitored by Japan's Ministry of Finance.
Nippon Credit Bank described the downgrade as regrettable and based on a misunderstanding of its business situation.
Moody's downgraded NCB debentures from Baa3 to Ba1 due to expected outside assistance needs.
The downgrade places NCB debentures below investment grade, classified as junk-bond status.
Moody's action indicates doubts about Japan's financial authorities' ability to manage potential bank failures.
This is the first instance of Moody's assigning junk status to the senior debt of a Japanese bank.
The Ministry of Finance expressed surprise at Moody's decision and stated that Japanese bank debentures are secure.

Shanghai's economy grew 13 percent in the previous year.
Shanghai's economy is expected to see slightly slower growth in 1997.
Unemployment in Shanghai is rising.
The statistics bureau of Shanghai announced these economic updates.
Sun Zuyao is the director of Shanghai's statistics bureau.
The GDP growth rate for Shanghai in 1997 is expected to differ from 1996 by around one percentage point.
Shanghai's economy has been growing at more than 14 percent a year since 1992.
Shanghai's GDP for 1996 was reported at 287 billion yuan.
The number of unemployed workers in Shanghai rose 20 percent during 1996.
The number of 'xiagang' workers in Shanghai increased to 270,000 by the end of 1996.

A Chinese court sentenced a U.S. businessman to 10 years in jail for smuggling garbage.
The businessman was fined 500,000 yuan ($60,000) and ordered to be deported.
William Ping Chen confessed to smuggling banned goods, including 238 tonnes of garbage and waste medical items, between July and December 1995.
The Shanghai Number One People's Intermediate Court found Chen guilty of smuggling 'foreign garbage' for profit.
Chen has the right to appeal the court's decision.
Chen is likely to be deported swiftly if he waives his right to appeal.
A U.S. consulate official stated that they prioritize the welfare of U.S. citizens in such situations.
Chen, aged 56, was arrested in June of the previous year.
Chen continued to import banned waste items despite warnings from officials.
The court's verdict stated that Chen caused serious damage to the environment of China.

Foreign business people expect Deng Xiaoping's death to have almost no effect on economic policies in China.
Analysts claim foreign investment is essential for the Chinese government's efforts to reduce unemployment and stimulate economic growth.
There is no expectation of a fundamental shift in economic policy following Deng Xiaoping's death.
Lance Browne, Standard Chartered Bank's China manager, anticipates no change in policy toward foreign banks.
Browne believes the pace of business expansion for foreign banks in China is unlikely to increase.
A Western diplomat in Shanghai stated that business operations are not expected to be impacted by Deng's death.
Foreign businesses have faced increased profit pressure due to the reduction or elimination of preferential policies.
The diplomat noted that any tightening of policies regarding foreign business privileges was already occurring prior to Deng's death.
An American businessman in Shanghai reported no impact from Deng's death but noted growing concerns about profit and approval issues.
An investment analyst with ING-Barings stated that foreign funds are crucial for maintaining economic growth and reducing unemployment in China.

The target date to start mining at the Voisey's Bay metals deposit is 1998.
Stewart Gendron is the new president of Inco Ltd.'s Voisey's Bay Nickel Co.
Gendron stated that the 1998 deadline is a 'tight' deadline.
Inco intends to produce 270 million pounds of nickel annually at Voisey's Bay.
Inco also intends to produce 200 million pounds of copper and a significant amount of cobalt at the site.
Inco has forecasted initial production of 23 million pounds of nickel and 15 million pounds of copper in 1998.
Inco's acquisition of Voisey's Bay was delayed for three months due to a lawsuit involving Diamond Fields Resources executives.
The acquisition of Voisey's Bay has made Inco the largest nickel producer in the western world.
Analysts estimate that Inco will control 38 percent of the world's nickel market after the acquisition.
Gendron and his team are involved in environmental issues and negotiations with local aboriginal groups.

Canada's French-language televised debate for the June 2 federal election was cut short when moderator Claire Lamarche collapsed.
Claire Lamarche is a well-known television personality in French-speaking Quebec.
Lamarche collapsed while moaning about the heat in the room.
The five political party leaders were present when the moderator collapsed.
Arnold Amber, one of the organizers of the debate, stated that the debate should not continue under the circumstances.
All political parties agreed that the debate should not continue.
The party leaders left the venue without speaking to the media.
Political scientist Ken McRoberts commented that the moderator's collapse made the debate anti-climactic.
Gilles Duceppe is the leader of the separatist Bloc Quebecois.
The debate was about two hours into its scheduled 2-1/2 hours when the moderator collapsed.

The ruling Liberals are far ahead in the polls for Canada's June 2 federal election.
The main question in the campaign is which opposition party will place second.
Reg Whitaker is a political scientist at York University in Toronto.
Whitaker stated that there is no realistic option aside from the Liberals.
The opposition parties are competing for small markets.
Polls show the Liberal party with a consistently strong lead despite opposition criticism.
The Bloc Quebecois has been the official opposition since the last election in 1993.
The Bloc Quebecois aims to promote Quebec independence rather than form a federal government.
Prime Minister Jean Chretien called the June 2 election.
In the last election in 1993, the Liberals won 177 seats, the Bloc Quebecois won 54 seats, the Reform Party won 52 seats, the New Democrats won nine seats, and the Conservatives won two seats.

Engineering group Skoda a.s. won an order to supply trolleybuses worth more than $170 million to the city of San Francisco.
This order is the largest order of Czech goods ever to the United States.
Skoda spokesman Jaroslav Hudec stated that the electrically powered buses would be produced in the Czech Republic.
The buses will be assembled at Skoda's subsidiary, Electric Transit International (ETI) in Baltimore.
Hudec described the victory in this tender as an extraordinary success due to the expected volumes of supplies and the prestige of the U.S. market.
Skoda, based in Plzen, is no longer affiliated with the Czech car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s.
Skoda aims to offer western-quality units with the cost advantage of eastern European production.
The San Francisco contract may lead to more business opportunities for Skoda in the United States.
ETI's president, Ladislav Tetal, stated that the order would replace San Francisco's entire fleet of 300 buses.
The deal must be approved by the San Francisco board of supervisors in a vote scheduled for April 22.

The Czech opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) held a party conference on Friday.
The CSSD aims to present itself as a potential leader if Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) fails to maintain its coalition.
A general election in the Czech Republic is not scheduled until 1998.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's government has struggled since losing its majority in lower house elections last June.
CSSD chairman Milos Zeman called for party unity at the conference.
Zeman criticized members who broke ranks during key parliamentary votes.
The CSSD finished second in the June general elections, three percentage points behind the ODS.
Internal conflicts within the CSSD have increased since the June elections.
A rift occurred in December over the 1997 budget when some CSSD deputies supported the government's draft.
Analysts believe the conference is important for determining the party's future political direction.

Engineering group Skoda a.s. won an order to supply over $170 million in trolleybuses to the city of San Francisco.
This order is the largest supply of Czech goods ever to the United States.
Skoda spokesman Jaroslav Hudec stated that the electric-powered buses would be produced in the Czech Republic.
The buses will be assembled at Skoda's subsidiary, Electric Transit International (ETI) in Baltimore.
Hudec described the victory in this tender as an extraordinary success due to the expected volumes of supplies and the prestige of the U.S. market.
Skoda, based in Plzen, is no longer affiliated with the Czech car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s.
Skoda aims to offer western-quality units with the cost advantage of eastern European production.
The San Francisco contract could lead to more business opportunities for Skoda in the United States.
Skoda has produced over 12,000 trolleybuses since 1936.
Local Czech media reported that the San Francisco order could be for about 250 single-section and higher capacity buses.

Xi Yang was a Hong Kong reporter.
China jailed Xi Yang for stealing state secrets.
Xi Yang was released from a 12-year sentence after two weeks of difficulties for China regarding Hong Kong.
Xi Yang was released on Saturday after being jailed since October 1993.
A Western diplomat stated that Xi Yang's release was a gesture to show concern for human rights.
Beijing prison authorities notified Xi Yang of his release at 8:00 a.m. on Saturday.
Xi Yang was paroled because he showed signs of repentance, according to Xinhua news agency.
China considered Xi Yang's article in the Hong Kong Ming Bao newspaper as theft of state secrets.
Central bank clerk Tian Ye was jailed for 15 years for leaking information related to Xi Yang's article.
Diplomats indicated that Xi Yang's harsh sentence served as a warning to the media in Hong Kong.

China plans education sessions for the Uighur minority in Xinjiang after a riot left nine people dead and nearly 200 wounded.
Officials aim to teach Uighurs about patriotism and discourage future unrest.
Zhang Yuliang is the director of the propaganda department of the Xinjiang regional Communist Party committee.
Zhang Yuliang stated that a circular will be distributed throughout Xinjiang regarding the incident.
Authorities have issued emergency circulars to combat separatism in the region.
Police in Yining are interrogating suspected ringleaders of the recent riot.
The revised death toll from the riot is nine, including four policemen.
At least 198 people were wounded in the riot, with about 50 suffering serious injuries.
200 to 300 people were arrested following the riot, which involved around 1,000 participants.
The riot was triggered by a Uighur criminal suspect resisting arrest.

China has called for a crackdown on independence activities in Tibet.
The exiled Dalai Lama is referred to as a 'fake' religious leader by Chinese officials.
The Tibet Daily reported that a senior regional party official stated the Dalai Lama's activities damage social stability.
Regional deputy Communist Party secretary Gui Jinlong emphasized the need to eliminate the Dalai Lama's influence in Tibet.
Officials reported victories in their crackdown on crime and unrest in Tibet last year.
Gui Jinlong stated that police need to target those seeking independence in Tibet.
Guo outlined three main tasks for 1997 to ensure stability in Tibet.
The first task is to deepen criticism of the Dalai Lama.
Guo described the Dalai Lama as a political subversive and a religious sham.
China blames pro-independence unrest in Tibet on the Dalai Lama, who fled to India in 1959.

EVA Air plans to start a new freighter service from Taipei to Brussels later this year.
K. W. Nieh is an airline spokesman for EVA Air.
EVA Air will replace its McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighter service from Taipei to Amsterdam via Dubai with an MD-11 Combi aircraft.
The new MD-11 freighter service to Brussels is proposed to start in May or June.
EVA Air will take delivery of two more McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighters by the end of this year.
EVA Air will also receive the first of two new Boeing 747-400 passenger aircraft.
EVA's MD-11 freighter fleet will increase to five with the new deliveries.
EVA's current fleet of 28 aircraft is expected to rise to 34 by next year.
Cargo revenue for EVA Air is expected to exceed 35 percent of total revenue when last year's financial figures are published in March.
EVA Air has no plans to start a dedicated freighter service from Taipei to Hong Kong.

Members of the Orient Airlines Association (OAA) operate the greatest concentration of Boeing 747 cargo aircraft in the world.
The information comes from the magazine Orient Aviation, which covers the association's affairs.
The OAA consists of 16 member airlines, with Ansett Australia being the 17th member.
The most common aircraft type among OAA airlines is the Boeing 747.
The OAA has a fleet of 382 Boeing 747 aircraft, of which 42 are freighters.
The OAA's 42 freighters represent the greatest concentration of cargo aircraft in the world.
OAA airlines operate a total of 1,156 aircraft, with 69 percent being wide-body aircraft.
The fleet of OAA airlines is expected to grow by about 32 percent by the year 2001.
The average age of OAA aircraft is 7.7 years.
EVA Air has the youngest fleet among OAA members, with an average aircraft age of 2.3 years.

KLM Cargo plans to increase air cargo rates in northern Asia by five to ten percent in the first quarter of the new year.
Tom Presnail is the regional director of sales for KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV.
Tom Presnail communicated this information to Reuters from his Tokyo office.
The exact amount of the rate increase has not yet been decided.
A decision regarding the rate increase will be made by the end of January.
The rate increase is expected to take effect sometime after the decision is made.
Tom Presnail expressed a preference for a blanket rate rise on all routes, though it may vary in some markets.
Tom Presnail is responsible for KLM Cargo flights to Tokyo, Osaka, Hong Kong, Taipei, Seoul, and Beijing.
The planned rate rise is attributed to significant increases in fuel costs and general cost increases.
Current demand for cargo space aboard KLM's Asian freighters is reported to be strong.

The British government approved a hostile bid for Northern Electric from U.S.-based CE Electric.
Shares in the remaining independent British regional electricity companies Southern, London, and Yorkshire gained as the market speculated on further offers.
The government cleared CE Electric's bid of 650 pence per share with conditions to address financial queries.
Northern Electric's shares closed at 641 pence after peaking at 650 pence.
Analysts believe the 782 million pound bid from CE Electric, which is 70 percent-owned by CalEnergy, is likely to be successful.
London's shares rose to 680 pence, Southern's shares rose to 778 pence, and Yorkshire's shares rose to 760 pence.
East Midlands Electricity agreed to a $2.15 billion takeover by Dominion Resources at 670 pence per share.
Seven of the original 12 regional electricity companies have been sold to predators since March 1995.
Three of the sold regional electricity companies are South Western, Seeboard, and Midlands, which were sold to U.S. companies.
London and Yorkshire are considered the most likely takeover targets among the remaining regional electricity companies.

Dixons Group Plc reported a 53 percent increase in profits and an eight percent rise in sales in the first half.
The company's shares fell 27 pence to close at 511 pence due to profit taking and concerns over planned tax increases.
Analysts noted that the shares were experiencing profit-taking after recent out-performance.
Dixons' pretax profits for the six months ending November 9, 1996, reached 57.5 million pounds, up from 37.5 million pounds.
The company paid a dividend of 2.4 pence, an increase from 2.05 pence.
Sales from existing stores increased by eight percent in the first half and maintained this figure in the first eight weeks of the second half.
Chairman Sir Stanley Kalms described Christmas trading as highly satisfactory.
Managing director John Clare stated that consumer spending was growing but not booming.
PCs and accessories accounted for approximately 26 percent of the group's total sales in the first half.
Dixons' PC World division saw total sales increase by 96 percent in the first half, or 21 percent when excluding new selling space.

The panel supervising a bid by CE Electric extended its offer for Northern Electric until Tuesday.
The outcome of the contest was expected by midnight on Friday.
CE Electric's offer was for 782 million pounds ($1.30 billion) at 650 pence a share.
The Takeover Panel declined to comment on the situation.
The Financial Times reported that the Takeover Panel had stopped the clock amid allegations of irregularities.
CE Electric is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy of the United States.
CE Electric held nearly 30 percent of Northern Electric prior to Friday's deadline.
Northern Electric claimed to have the backing of its largest institutional investor, the Prudential, which holds around 11 percent.
Northern Electric has faced a second hostile takeover, having previously fended off Trafalgar House for 560 million pounds last year.
Northern Electric claimed that the CE Electric bid undervalued it and called for a higher price.

SBC Warburg is the investment banking arm of Swiss Bank Corp.
SBC Warburg reported a loss on a 300 million pound share deal.
The share deal is under investigation by Britain's financial markets watchdog.
The deal involved the liquidation of part of the Kleinwort European Privatisation Investment Trust (KEPIT).
SBC Warburg is estimated to have lost around two million pounds on the deal.
Peter Corrigan, head of French equities at SBC Warburg, resigned last Friday.
Britain's Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) is probing the deal.
SBC Warburg did not include a special provision for the loss in its 1996 results.
Marcel Ospel, an executive at SBC, stated that the bank is supporting the investigation.
SBC Warburg's spokesman claimed that KEPIT was not disadvantaged by the share sale.

The Halifax Building Society plans to float for around 12 billion stg on the stock exchange in June.
Mike Blackburn is the chief executive of the Halifax Building Society.
Mike Blackburn stated that the Halifax Building Society has headroom for increasing its mortgage market share by acquisition.
Blackburn mentioned that the Halifax Building Society could reach a 25 percent mortgage market share without attracting the attention of the Office of Fair Trading.
The Office of Fair Trading is the competition watchdog in the UK.
Blackburn indicated that the Halifax Building Society is not currently engaged in any acquisition discussions.

Lloyds TSB reported a 52 percent increase in profits for 1996.
The reported pretax profits for 1996 were 2.505 billion pounds.
The profits for the previous year were 1.650 billion pounds.
Lloyds TSB raised its dividend by 20 percent to 13.2p per share.
Earnings per share increased by 63 percent to 31.2p.
Analysts expressed concerns about the sustainability of future income growth.
Lloyds shares initially eased 7p to 485 but later stood unchanged at 502p.
The bank's bad debt provisions decreased by 44 percent to 327 million pounds.
Specific provisions for bad and doubtful debts fell to 357 million pounds from 459 million pounds in 1995.
Profit from the problem country debt portfolio increased to 127 million pounds from 50 million pounds.

The right-wing Czech coalition government ended nine months of ruling with a parliamentary minority on Tuesday.
A former opposition deputy, Tomas Teplik, crossed the aisle to join Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS).
Teplik was recently expelled from the opposition Social Democratic Party (CSSD).
Teplik's switch gives the ruling coalition 100 seats in the 200-seat lower house of parliament.
The coalition had been in a minority since the general elections last June.
ODS parliamentary caucus voted to accept Teplik.
Financial analysts welcomed the news, stating it would increase confidence in the Czech economy.
Jan Pudil, director of the investment house WoodCommerz, commented that this would take away political questions and focus investors on macro-economic fundamentals.
The coalition lost its large majority in parliament last June after a strong showing by the centre-left Social Democrats.
Josef Wagner, another former CSSD member, declared himself an independent after being expelled for voting with the ruling coalition.

The Czech National Bank (CNB) put Agrobanka a.s. under forced administration due to liquidity problems.
The liquidity problems at Agrobanka arose from the failure of Kreditni Banka a.s.
This is the CNB's 12th intervention into a commercial bank since the post-Communist period.
The CNB will guarantee all of Agrobanka's obligations during a temporary forced administration period.
CNB Governor Josef Tosovsky instructed the big banks to prepare up to six billion crowns to help Agrobanka's liquidity.
Agrobanka has four billion crowns in basic capital.
The 'Big Four' banks are Ceska Sporitelna, Komercni Banka, Investicni a Postovni Banka, and Ceskoslovensko Obchodni Banka a.s. (CSOB).
The state holds a significant stake in all but CSOB of the 'Big Four' banks.
The CNB stated that Agrobanka's problems are related to liquidity, not solvency.
The CNB will guarantee all deposits at Agrobanka and ensure sufficient financial sources for the bank.

Czech President Vaclav Havel called on the new Senate to give final approval to a post-World War Two reconciliation pact with Germany.
Havel's speech to the Senate was his first since the upper house was elected in November.
Havel urged Senators to rise above the contentious debate in the lower house regarding the pact.
The lower house's debate on the pact included opposition from Communist and ultra-right Republican deputies.
The reconciliation pact was approved by a large majority in the lower house last month.
The declaration expresses Germany's regret for the 1938-45 occupation of Czech lands and Czech sorrow for the expulsion of ethnic Germans after the war.
The declaration was signed by both the Czech and German governments in January.
The agreement aims to resolve political issues from World War Two and its aftermath.
Havel emphasized the importance of building strong relations with Germany for the benefit of Europe.
Havel's speech also addressed the constitutional role of the Senate and marked his return to public life after surgery.

Glaxo Wellcome Plc announced an 18 percent increase in pre-tax profits.
Pre-tax profits rose to 2.964 billion pounds ($4.8 billion) from 2.505 billion pounds ($4.04 billion).
Sales increased by 9 percent to 8.341 billion pounds ($13.45 billion).
Shareholders received a 13 percent increase in the dividend to 34.0 pence.
Sales of Zantac fell 14 percent last year but remained the world's best-selling drug at 1.931 billion pounds ($3.1 billion).
Zantac has been the world's best-selling drug since 1986.
Glaxo merged with Wellcome in 1995.
Sales of Zovirax were steady at 812 million pounds ($1.3 billion).
Glaxo expects to at least maintain profits at the 1996 level over the next two years.
Sales of newer products launched since 1990 increased by 650 million pounds ($1.05 billion) to 2.0 billion pounds ($3.2 billion).

Unilever Plc plans to sell most of its speciality chemicals businesses.
The disposal programme could net up to five billion pounds ($8.17 billion) for Unilever.
The four businesses involved are National Starch & Chemical Co, Quest International, Unichema International, and Crosfield.
These businesses had total sales of around three billion pounds last year.
The businesses employ nearly 16,000 people in 35 countries.
The move could allow Unilever to pursue a major acquisition in its core food, detergents, and personal product businesses.
Unilever is responding to a shake-up in the chemicals sector due to overcapacity and competition from the United States and Asia.
Unilever's businesses have profit margins of more than 14 percent.
Analysts believe the businesses are likely to be sold in large segments.
Speculation exists regarding potential buyers, including Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc and other U.S. firms.

Britain's Courtaulds Plc is focusing on Tencel, industrial coatings, and plastic packaging.
Chief executive Gordon Campbell stated that viscose and acrylics will decrease in sales contribution in the future.
Gordon Campbell gave his first major interview since becoming CEO in July.
Courtaulds was the first company to produce a manmade fibre commercially in 1905.
The company has experienced a decline in viscose demand due to changing fashions and competition from Asian producers.
Concerns about viscose have negatively impacted Courtaulds' share price, leading to its removal from the FTSE 100 in December.
Courtaulds shares closed at 363.5 pence on Wednesday, down 35 percent from a 12-month high of 490 pence in October.
Campbell noted tentative signs of recovery in viscose but expressed caution about the situation.
Last month, Courtaulds closed 20 percent of its European viscose capacity and shifted workers to a new Tencel plant in Grimsby.
Courtaulds aims for Tencel sales to reach close to $500 million a year by the end of the century, which would be less than 10 percent of total sales.

A judge ordered the arrest of Colombia's army chief, Gen. Harold Bedoya.
The judge was criticized for succumbing to pressure from leftist guerrillas.
The arrest warrant was issued after the army refused to lift barricades blocking a demonstration.
The demonstration was organized by thousands of peasants opposed to the compulsory eradication of coca plantations.
Colombian landowners and political commentators claimed that leftist rebels linked to cocaine traffickers influenced the judge.
The Colombian Cattlemen's Federation stated that local authorities and peasants operate under pressure from narcoguerrillas.
Alejandro Ramirez is the local judge who issued the arrest warrant against Bedoya.
Gen. Bedoya faces 30 days in prison for defying an order to remove barricades.
President Ernesto Samper ordered an inquiry into the judge's decision, which is under review by a higher court.
The government stated that the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) was behind the peasant demonstration.

Gloria Cuartas is the mayor of Apartado.
Cuartas witnessed two gunmen behead a child outside a school.
The gunmen threw the severed head toward Cuartas.
A rival gang arrived and a shootout erupted shortly after the incident.
Cuartas has been advocating for peace in the violent region of Uraba since taking office in January 1995.
She aims to create a neutral space to protect civilians from the ongoing conflict.
Cuartas believes the attack on the child was intended to intimidate her into resigning.
The perpetrators of the child's murder were never brought to justice.
Cuartas was elected as a consensus candidate supported by various political parties, including the Liberal and Conservative Parties and the Patriotic Union.
Apartado has a population of 80,000 and experienced three massacres last year, resulting in over 350 deaths.

Government officials flew to northern Colombia on Friday to persuade prisoners to lay down their weapons and release hostages.
A jail riot in Valledupar, Cesar province, left four guards confirmed dead.
A crack anti-kidnap force took up positions around the jail.
The local police chief raised the possibility of launching a rescue operation for the hostages.
A group of 10 convicts leading the revolt demanded two helicopters for an airlift from the jail.
One of the convicts, a former leader of the M-19 leftist rebel movement, called for political asylum in Cuba.
Government human rights ombudsman Jose Fernando Castro is heading the mediation team.
About 550 inmates seized control of the jail after overpowering 18 guards.
The National Prisons Institute initially reported five guards killed in the shoot-out.
Valledupar mayor Tito Pumarejo confirmed that four bodies of prison guards were removed from the jail by Red Cross workers.

Channel 5 is a British terrestrial television channel set to launch next month.
David Elstein is the chief executive of Channel 5.
Channel 5 aims to achieve a five percent share of UK viewing by the end of the year.
ITV has an audience share of over 35 percent.
Channel 5's annual programme budget is 110 million pounds.
Dawn Airey is the Director of Programmes at Channel 5.
Channel 5 is owned by a consortium that includes Pearson, United News & Media, CLT, and Warburg Pincus.
Channel 5 will go on air on March 30.
Channel 5 plans to be available to around 40 million people at launch.
Channel 5's audience is expected to grow to 45-46 million by the end of the year.

Millwall is an English soccer team that is currently facing a financial crisis.
Analysts believe Millwall's situation serves as a warning for investors in soccer stocks.
Millwall Holdings Plc has called in administrators to manage the company while seeking a financial rescue package.
Shares in Millwall are suspended on the London Stock Exchange.
Before suspension, Millwall shares were valued at 4p each, down from 20p when issued seven years ago.
Vinay Bedi of stockbrokers Wise Speke stated that not all soccer stocks will outperform the market.
Shares in premier league clubs Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur, and Caspian have nearly tripled in value over the past year.
Revenue growth for these clubs has been driven by a television deal with BSkyB and anticipated pay-per-view income.
Newcastle United recently announced plans to raise up to 50 million pounds through flotation.
Analysts indicate that investing in clubs outside the premier league carries greater risk.

Newcastle United FC will debut on the stock market in April, valuing the club at almost 200 million pounds.
NatWest Markets reported that the offer price will be between 120 and 135 pence per Ordinary share.
The valuation of Newcastle United is estimated to be between 172 and 193 million pounds.
The flotation is expected to raise 47.4 million pounds net.
Trading for Newcastle United's shares will begin on April 2.
Ten percent of the shares will be available to the public.
Newcastle United is among a growing number of British soccer clubs joining the stock market.
The value of listed soccer clubs has increased over the past year due to investor interest.
Newcastle United has invested 50 million pounds since 1992 in player recruitment.
Cameron Hall will retain a 57 percent stake in Newcastle United after the flotation.

CardioThoracic Systems Inc is exceeding its internal targets for increasing the number of cardiac surgeries worldwide.
The company uses equipment for operating on a beating heart without cracking the chest.
Surgeons at 12 centers around the world are performing about 11 surgeries per month with the company's new devices.
This is an increase from none a year ago.
Richard Ferrari is the chief executive of CardioThoracic Systems Inc.
More than 200 minimally invasive direct coronary artery bypass surgeries using the company's equipment have been performed to date.
Three-quarters of these surgeries have been single blood-vessel grafts.
The complication rate for these surgeries is one percent, which is lower than traditional procedures.
The company plans to train more surgeons to use its equipment.
CardioThoracic is comfortable with analysts' estimates of 1997 sales reaching about $11 million.

Guidant Corp expects no material impact on its financial results from a halt in shipments to Europe of its Ventak AV implantable defibrillator.
Chief executive Ronald Dollens stated that the impact would not exceed $1 million.
Guidant Corp believes it will return to the market in Europe within four to six weeks.
The company halted shipments of the Ventak AV due to technical problems.
Approximately 200 Ventak AV devices have been implanted in patients since its approval in Europe in November.
The Ventak AV is not approved for sale in the United States.
The problem with the device is mechanical and cannot be fixed by reprogramming.
If a problem is present, removal and replacement of the device may be necessary.
Guidant does not anticipate delays in U.S. Food and Drug Administration clearance.
Guidant's shares increased following the announcement of year-end results, with sales hitting $1.05 billion, a 13 percent increase over 1995.

St. Jude Medical Inc is proposing a $505 million stock acquisition of Ventritex Inc.
Stephen Wilson is the chief financial officer of St. Jude Medical Inc.
Wilson stated that the acquisition will likely proceed despite three recent patient deaths related to Ventritex medical devices.
Wilson mentioned that the deaths are serious but do not deter St. Jude Medical from moving forward with the transaction.
Shares in St. Jude Medical Inc increased by 3/8 to 36-7/8.
Ventritex confirmed the death of a third recipient of its implantable defibrillators.
Wilson praised Ventritex for its handling of the situation regarding the patient deaths.
St. Jude Medical intends to conduct due diligence to understand the impact of the deaths on the franchise value.
Wilson estimated that federal regulatory review of the acquisition may take another three to four weeks.
St. Jude Medical expects to exceed $1 billion in sales in 1997, even without the acquisition of Ventritex.

Seven Network Ltd is expected to report a rise in net profit for the first half of the 1996/97 year.
The expected rise in net profit is attributed to an acquisition and regaining market share.
Analysts expect Seven Network to report a net profit of between A$59 million and A$65 million for the 26 weeks ended December 28.
Seven reported a net profit of A$91.88 million in the 1995/96 half, but no tax was paid.
Seven is expected to report half year results on Wednesday.
Seven has stated it expects to pay full income tax during 1996/97.
Seven has not paid a full tax rate since relisting on the Australian Stock Exchange in 1993.
Seven's 1996/97 half is a week shorter than the 27 week period in the 1995/96 half.
Analysts estimate that Seven's pre-tax profit would be A$96.5 million over a 27 week period, up from A$93 million a year earlier.
Analysts expect Seven to report underlying profit growth on a like-for-like basis.

Seven Network Ltd chairman Kerry Stokes stated that Seven would likely sell pay-tv firm Optus Vision to an international phone company if successful in litigation against Optus Vision shareholders.
Seven claims that fellow shareholders in Optus Vision breached the Optus Vision shareholders' agreement.
Seven is a two percent shareholder in Optus Vision.
Seven stated that successful litigation would allow it to acquire Optus Vision at a discount to its full valuation.
Kerry Stokes mentioned that Seven is in discussions with international telecommunications and informational technology companies.
Stokes, who owns about 20 percent of Seven, indicated that Seven would have 12 months to sell Optus Vision.
Optus Vision is investing A$3 billion in a fibre optic cable network in Australia for pay TV and telephone services.
Stokes noted that there is more interest from companies in using Optus Vision assets for telephone services than for pay TV.
Seven received two offers to buy the rest of Optus Vision, one for A$648.74 million and another for A$533.80 million.
Litigation between Seven and other Optus shareholders is scheduled to be heard in the New South Wales Supreme Court on February 24.

St George Bank Ltd managing director Jim Sweeney stated that the bank aims to achieve higher cost savings from the Advance Bank Australia Ltd merger than the A$140 million currently targeted.
Sweeney mentioned that the bank's private aim is to exceed the A$140 million cost savings target.
Sweeney indicated that he will not provide disappointing news regarding costs over the next 12 to 18 months.
The St George-Advance merger received final approval from the Supreme Court of New South Wales for Advance's capital reduction programme.
The merged bank will operate under the name St George and will have a larger balance sheet.
The larger balance sheet will allow the bank to introduce new products that could increase revenue.
Sweeney stated that the bank is focusing on both costs and revenue, with announcements expected in the coming weeks to boost revenue.
Sweeney expressed excitement about a potential revenue advantage for the merged bank but did not provide further details.
The merged bank will double the size of St George to A$40 billion in assets and may consider outsourcing some activities to reduce costs.
Sweeney commented on the patchy state of the country's mortgage market and expressed disappointment in the strength of new home starts.

First Leisure Corp Plc reported a five percent decline in first half profits.
The company warned that early second half trading was not as good as expected.
Pre-tax profits for the six months ending in April were 17.2 million pounds on a turnover of 88.8 million pounds.
The company's shares fell by 17.5 pence to 318.5p following a negative trading statement.
The interim dividend was set at 2.64p per share, which was below expectations of 2.7-2.75p.
A leisure analyst described the results as disappointing and indicated a need to revise profit estimates.
First Leisure attributed poor performance in its bingo hall division to good weather in May.
Chairman Michael Grade acknowledged past operational mistakes and expressed confidence in a new management team.
Grade stated that bingo remains a popular leisure activity in the UK and that the company had not captured its market share.
Comparable sales in the company's bingo halls fell by 25 percent in the first half.

BSkyB has lost two top executives and an equity stake in terrestrial digital TV.
Shares in BSkyB fell by 14.5p to 483p on Monday.
The value of British Sky Broadcasting has decreased by around 1.7 billion pounds since last week.
Analysts forecast further weakness in BSkyB shares.
Jason Crisp, a media analyst at SocGen, stated that there has been a re-rating of BSkyB shares.
Another broker suggested that BSkyB shares could only be valued at 450p in optimistic scenarios.
Negative reports in newspapers contributed to the decline in BSkyB shares.
The Financial Times reported that BSkyB could be excluded from bidding for new digital TV licenses.
The Independent Television Commission advised BSkyB to drop its one-third stake in a consortium with Carlton Communications and Granada Group.
Credit Suisse First Boston estimated the fundamental value of BSkyB shares to be about 450p in optimistic cases and 350-400p in more reasonable scenarios.

Cable and Wireless Communications (CWC) is a new cable telephone and television company in Britain.
CWC made its market debut valued at around 4.5 billion pounds ($7.3 billion).
The free float of CWC was 14.7 percent.
CWC was formed when the Mercury subsidiary of Cable and Wireless Plc merged with three cable TV units of NYNEX Corp and Bell Canada.
CWC's shares started at 300 pence and rose to 306 pence in early trade.
CWC's dual flotation occurred on both the London and New York stock exchanges.
Analysts expected CWC to be valued at an average of 4.5 billion pounds.
CWC's core business will be telephony provided by Mercury.
CWC has 1.1 million residential and 80,000 business telecom customers.
CWC plans to offer services to six million customers by 2001.

Technology stocks increased on Wednesday due to investor optimism about upcoming earnings reports from major companies.
Analysts have recently issued optimistic investment recommendations, stating that technology stocks are undervalued.
Bruce Lupatkin, director of research at Hambrecht & Quist Group Inc., believes it is time to invest in technology infrastructure stocks.
Lupatkin views the recent decline in stocks like Cisco Systems Inc., Netscape Communications Corp., and Oracle Corp. as a buying opportunity.
Cisco Systems Inc. shares rose $4.50 to $52.375 on Nasdaq trading with 18 million shares traded.
Intel Corp. shares increased $7.375 to $140.625.
Microsoft Corp. shares gained $3.94 to $94.25.
Oracle Corp. shares rose $1.50 to $40.50.
Analysts have noted that technology sales are slowing due to a strengthening dollar and weak sales in Europe and Japan.
John Skeen and Thomas Thornhill from Montgomery Securities Inc. believe recent lows in stocks like Cisco, Oracle, and Intel represent buying opportunities.

Apple Computer Inc. plans to release an operating system that will work on personal computers based on Intel Corp. chips and on Apple computers.
Apple will release programming tools that will allow companies to write software for Apple computers and convert it to run on PCs based on Intel chips and Microsoft Windows software.
Apple Chairman Gilbert Amelio stated that the new development environment holds promise for those seeking business on both Mac and Windows platforms.
Apple's next-generation operating system, code-named Rhapsody, will run on Apple-designed computers and PCs based on Intel chips using Microsoft Windows software.
Apple has previously released operating system software that only runs on Apple-designed hardware.
Apple has been working on improvements to the Macintosh to differentiate it from PCs for the past two years.
Apple relied on its computers' ease-of-use as a selling point until Microsoft's release of Windows 95 diminished its impact.
Apple abandoned an effort to revamp the Macintosh Operating System last year and acquired Next Software Inc. to aid in the software overhaul.
There are concerns among programmers that the new operating system may not run products designed for the older Mac operating system.
Apple's stock ended unchanged at $17.5625 on Nasdaq after the announcement.

Vantive Corp. announced that Federal Express Corp. will use its help-desk software for a customer service project.
The project is expected to be a significant source of revenue for Vantive.
Federal Express will initially use Vantive's software to set up a system for tracking internal troubleshooting projects.
Federal Express plans to use Vantive's products to establish a help desk for troubleshooting Fedex terminals in customer mail rooms.
Jim Colson, Fedex's vice president of technology services, stated that Vantive's software could be deployed to 60,000 Fedex employees within three years, depending on performance.
The terms of the transaction between Vantive and Federal Express were not disclosed.
Vantive charges a fee of up to several thousand dollars for each workstation.
Analysts believe the agreement with Federal Express could generate significant revenue for Vantive in the coming years.
Ed Bierdeman, an analyst at Dakin Securities, estimated that Vantive will earn about $4 to $5 million in revenue from Federal Express in 1997.
Vantive, based in Santa Clara, California, develops software that helps companies enhance their customer service departments.

Canada's Philip Environmental Inc. plans to acquire Houston-based Allwaste Inc. and Serv-Tech Inc. in two deals worth $612 million.
The acquisition will create North America's biggest recycling firm.
Philip Chief Executive Allen Fracassi expressed excitement about the opportunity during a media conference call.
The deals are expected to create North America's largest metals recycling and industrial services company.
The combined company will have annual revenues exceeding $1.6 billion, 8,000 employees, and 215 operating locations in North America, Europe, and South America.
Philip will swap 0.611 of a Philip share for each Allwaste share for a total consideration of $540 million.
The Allwaste deal includes the assumption of approximately $133 million in debt.
Philip agreed to exchange 0.403 of a Philip share for each Serv-Tech share in a deal valued at $72 million, including the assumption of $21 million of debt.
Serv-Tech generated over $140 million in revenues in 1996, and Philip expects its earnings to be boosted by the Serv-Tech deal.
Analyst Peter von Ond revised his 1998 earnings estimate for Philip to C$1.70 a share from C$1.60 a share.

Toronto stocks ended weaker on Tuesday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index lost 25.26 points to 6129.28.
Trading involved 106.6 million shares worth C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 58.92 points to 6896.56.
Canada's banking group dropped almost one percent.
Ron Meisels is a Montreal-based portfolio consultant.
Meisels stated that Toronto's market had traded in a narrow range recently.
Investors debated a possible hike in U.S. interest rates.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indices fell, led by consumer products, base metals, banks, and transports.
Wascana Energy Inc. was active after Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd. announced a C$20.50 ($14.97) all-cash bid.

Gendis Inc will post extensive losses in fiscal 1998.
The losses are due to the bankruptcy of its Greenberg Stores Ltd unit.
Greenberg Stores Ltd was forced into bankruptcy with almost 1,500 layoffs.
President Allan MacKenzie stated that the losses would be multi-millions.
The losses from the bankruptcy will be reported separately from ongoing operating results.
Gendis is based in Winnipeg.
Greenberg declared bankruptcy and sold 89 of its 169 stores to SAAN Stores Ltd.
This resulted in the closing of 80 stores and approximately 1,500 layoffs.
Gendis will take the largest loss among Greenberg's creditors after acting as its chief banker.
Deacon Capital analyst Bill Chisholm estimated that Gendis would need to write off Greenberg's assets, with a charge of around C$65 million.

China's corn exports could double to more than two million tonnes for the year.
A Singapore-based trader commented on the size of China's corn export program.
China's corn sales to South Korea since the start of 1997 were 690,500 tonnes.
China's corn sales to South Korea could reach 1.5 million tonnes for the year.
Spot sales to Southeast Asia brought China's total corn exports close to 1.5 million tonnes.
Japan has not yet purchased corn from China due to past issues with export bans.
The Top Margin Committee in South Korea bought 126,500 tonnes of Chinese corn.
Sale prices for Chinese corn were reported at $140.95 and $142.90 per tonne, including freight.
Freight costs between northern China and South Korea were about $10 per tonne.
China's 1996 corn harvest was a record 118 million tonnes.

Far East metals traders awaited the London Metal Exchange (LME) reaction to reports that Australia's MIM will halve 1997 zinc supplies to Europe.
MIM Holdings Ltd is holding talks with customers worldwide regarding the impact of reduced zinc production this year.
Nick Stump, chief executive of MIM, declined to comment on a Reuters report about the reduction of zinc supplies to Europe.
Stump stated that there is a shift to Asia, but the extent is uncertain.
LME zinc prices were expected to rise following the news of reduced supplies.
A Chinese trader in Hong Kong predicted that zinc prices would reach new highs.
LME zinc recently traded at two-year highs of $1,174 per tonne.
The last trade on Friday was $1,169, which was an increase of $33 per tonne.
China exports approximately a quarter of its annual zinc output.
Official figures show that 1996 exports of unwrought zinc and zinc alloys rose to 226,777 tonnes.

China has an abundance of steel.
Suppliers are competing for market share in China.
Competition among suppliers is driving prices down.
Steel prices have fallen by 10 percent or more in recent months.
Cold-rolled steel prices range from $400 to $430 per tonne.
Galvanized steel prices are up to $100 less than cold-rolled steel.
China is receiving a large influx of cheap steel, particularly from the former Soviet Union.
Most industry executives have a pessimistic outlook for the recovery of the Chinese steel market.
China's imports of steel billet and rolled steel in early 1995 totaled 6.83 million tonnes, an increase of 18.9 percent from the previous year.
Exports of steel products from China decreased by 31.8 percent to 2.59 million tonnes in the same period.

Gazprom announced a delay in issuing more share look-alikes for foreigners.
Gazprom stated it needed time to clear its debts before its stock could appreciate.
Gazprom challenged the government to cooperate on tax and payment issues.
Eduard Ivanov is the director of securities at Gazprom.
Gazprom plans to issue a second tranche of American Depositary Shares (ADS) next year.
The exact timing for the ADS issuance has not been set.
Gazprom intends to start issuing convertible bonds this year.
The ADSs will be sold on U.S. markets.
Gazprom accounted for 26 percent of Russia's 1996 tax revenue.
Gazprom has a market capitalization of $16.5 billion and accounts for over one-third of global gas reserves.

Gazprom announced restructuring and cost-cutting plans.
Gazprom downplayed discord with the government regarding its future.
Rem Vyakhirev is the chairman of Gazprom's board.
Gazprom plans to shed 100,000 jobs this year, which is 26 percent of its workforce.
Vyakhirev stated that Gazprom would remain a monopoly and would not be split up.
Internal restructuring at Gazprom will create up to six units for various functions.
Gazprom is politically influential and well-connected in Russia.
The International Monetary Fund and some government officials have criticized Gazprom for its financial practices.
Vyakhirev claimed that he and government officials are working together on Gazprom's activities.
Russia holds 34 percent of the world's gas reserves and 27 percent of its output.

Russia faces the challenge of reforming its natural monopolies to support long-term economic growth.
Analysts believe that reforming prices and increasing competition in the gas, electricity, and railway sectors is a difficult task.
The monopolies are criticized for operating similarly to how they did during the Soviet era.
Production costs were not a concern, competition was absent, and prices were disconnected from reality during the Soviet period.
Prices for industrial consumers in Russia have significantly increased as market conditions have developed.
Domestic customers pay a lower price that does not reflect actual costs.
Price distortions are negatively impacting the economy, leading to issues such as unpaid supplies and budget revenue shortfalls.
Jochen Wermuth, an economist and adviser at the Finance Ministry, advocates for abolishing cross-subsidies and introducing differentiated price structures to enhance competition.
The International Monetary Fund is pushing for major reforms in Russia's monopolies as a condition for a $10 billion loan.
Gazprom, the world's largest gas company, is criticized for not fully restructuring its production and distribution processes.

SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV reported a 19 percent rise in 1996 earnings to $625.5 million.
SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV warned about the first quarter of 1997 after a weak end to 1996.
The profit warning and lower fourth quarter results surprised the market.
SGS-Thomson's share closed nearly 12 percent lower at 379.40 francs in Paris.
The turnover for SGS-Thomson's shares was 542 million francs ($98 million).
The French blue-chip index closed 1.35 percent higher.
SGS-Thomson's fourth quarter earnings were down by 15.5 percent to $142 million.
SGS-Thomson's share price rose from 154.50 francs in July to 433 francs on January 20.
SGS-Thomson's president and CEO Pasquale Pistorio expressed caution about the first quarter of 1997.
The world semiconductor market fell by eight percent in 1996, making it the third worst year on record for the industry.

French state agencies met on Friday to approve an 11 billion franc ($2.09 billion) capital injection of state aid in electronics group Thomson SA.
The French government is reviewing options for reviving the sale of Thomson SA.
Thomson labour unions, supported by other labour groups, planned a demonstration in Paris to demand the cancellation of the group's privatisation.
The privatisation of Thomson SA was suspended earlier this week.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis is under political pressure to restore France's reputation on international markets.
Arthuis is working on how to relaunch the sale process of Thomson SA.
The decision to suspend the privatisation outraged South Korea due to disagreements over the sale terms of Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics.
State shareholders held an extraordinary meeting at Thomson's Paris headquarters to vote on the capital increase.
Representatives of France Telecom and the CDR state holding company met to agree on the aid package, which requires approval from the European Commission.
A spokesman for Philips Electronics denied a rumour about an official complaint regarding the Thomson sale.

Total SA reported a 50 percent increase in its 1996 net income to 5.6 billion francs.
The increase in net income was attributed to higher oil prices, a firmer dollar, improved refining margins, and productivity gains.
The profit figure was in line with financial analysts' expectations.
The profit would have shown a 150 percent increase if 1995 special charges of 1.5 billion francs were considered.
Operating income rose by 37 percent to 10.2 billion francs on 30 percent higher sales of 176 billion francs.
Total chairman Thierry Desmarest noted that the profit improvement was higher than the 25 percent rise at U.S. oil majors.
Elf reported its 1996 net income would be between 7.3 and 7.5 billion francs, a 40 percent increase from 5.3 billion in 1995.
Total shares increased by 0.76 percent to 477.70 francs while the blue-chip index decreased by 0.65 percent.
Total stated that a more favorable operating environment in 1996 accounted for more than half of the 3.3 billion franc increase in operating income.
Desmarest predicted a decline in oil prices in 1997 due to the return of Iraq to the market and increased production by non-OPEC members.

A state-owned power station and coal mine in Australia was sold for A$4.86 billion.
This sale is the largest privatisation in Australia.
A consortium of U.S. utilities CMS Energy Corp and NRG Energy Inc, along with Australian investors, purchased the assets.
The sale was announced by Victoria state premier Jeff Kennett.
The sale followed a bidding war that included American Electric Power Co Inc and AES Corp.
The power station has a capacity of 2,000 megawatts.
This sale surpasses last year's sale of half of Commonwealth Bank of Australia, which was valued at A$4.0 billion.
Loy Yang A is considered the most efficient electricity generator in Australia.
CMS Energy holds a 50 percent equity stake in Loy Yang A, while NRG Energy Inc has a 25 percent stake.
Horizon Energy Investment Ltd holds a 25 percent stake in Loy Yang A and plans to issue shares to the public next year.

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) announced the closure of Australia's oldest steel-making plant.
BHP stated that the plant could no longer compete with Asian competitors.
BHP's Newcastle mill opened in 1915 and was significant in Australia's industrial development.
The Newcastle mill will shut down its blast furnaces by the end of 1999.
The closure is part of a major overhaul of BHP's global steel business.
BHP chief executive John Prescott announced the closure and stated it would end 2,500 workers' jobs.
Prescott emphasized that the purpose of the changes is to ensure a viable industry going forward.
BHP may face industrial action from trade unions due to the closure.
One trade union stated that the closure could destroy up to 12,000 jobs nationwide.
A mass meeting of Newcastle workers is expected to consider calling a strike against BHP.

The consortium believed to be the winning bidder for Australia's Loy Yang A power station has minimized the U.S. dollar-component of the A$4.75 billion deal to about US$500 million.
A corporate source stated that there is no significant impact from a foreign exchange perspective.
The consortium comprises U.S. utilities CMS Energy Corp, which holds about 50 percent, and NRG Energy Inc and Horizon Energy Investments Ltd, each holding about 25 percent.
Local currency dealers estimated that about A$400 million to A$500 million cover was taken on Monday ahead of the deal's announcement.
The announcement of the deal is likely to occur around midday.
Horizon is a vehicle for Australian institutions led by Macquarie Bank's Infrastructure Trust of Australia Group Ltd.
The consortium's capital structure is designed around a high gearing ratio of around 75 percent.
Bank debt, indexed bonds, and subordinated debt account for almost A$3.6 billion of the A$4.75 billion bid.
All of the debt and a quarter of the equity component will be raised in Australia, with the balance of the equity funded offshore.
The foreign exposure of the Loy Yang A consortium has already been covered.

An Electronic Arts executive stated that the company is focusing on personal computers and CD-ROM devices as game platforms.
Bing Gordon is the executive vice president of marketing for Electronic Arts.
Bing Gordon expressed surprise at the success of the Nintendo 64 in North America.
The Nintendo 64 was launched last year after several delays and became a significant electronics hit during the holiday season.
Electronic Arts is likely to focus on other platforms due to Nintendo's decision to continue using more expensive cartridges.
Sony Corp and Sega Enterprises Ltd have switched to CD-ROMs as game media.
Bing Gordon stated that low manufacturing costs in media are important for the growth of interactive entertainment.
Electronic Arts plans to launch its first game for the Nintendo 64, a version of FIFA soccer, in March or April.
Electronic Arts opened a game development studio in the Seattle area.
The new Electronic Arts studio employs 55 developers, with about 40 coming from the acquisition of Manley & Associates Inc.

Teledesic Inc. is a communications startup mostly owned by Bill Gates and Craig McCaw.
Teledesic selected Boeing Co. to build and deploy its planned $9 billion satellite network.
Boeing will invest up to $100 million in Teledesic, acquiring a 10 percent stake in the company.
Teledesic plans to launch 288 low-orbiting satellites by 2002.
David Twyver is the Chief Executive Officer of Teledesic.
Teledesic considered all major aerospace companies before choosing Boeing as the prime contractor.
Boeing's contract with Teledesic is significant for its defense and space business growth.
Boeing is expanding its space business through acquisitions, including Rockwell International Corp. and planned purchase of McDonnell Douglas Corp.
Teledesic has reduced its initial satellite network plan from 840 small satellites to a smaller number of larger satellites.
Teledesic's network aims to provide communication comparable to land-based fiber optics.

Delta Air Lines Inc. is nearing a decision on an aircraft order worth at least $2.5 billion.
Boeing Co. is reportedly trying to persuade Delta to become its long-term supplier for all jet needs.
The deal being considered could have broad ramifications for the aviation industry.
Boeing is negotiating with Delta on a sole-source agreement that could involve up to 100 jets worth about $6 billion.
Delta spokesman Bill Berry declined to comment on the reported Boeing proposal.
Berry acknowledged that Delta was considering a purchase beyond its stated goal of two dozen wide-bodied jets.
Delta is in final discussions with both Boeing and Airbus Industrie.
Boeing Chairman Phil Condit stated that a sale to Delta was far from certain.
Boeing stock rose to $108.125 and Delta stock rose to $85.75 in New York Stock Exchange trading.
Delta's current fleet consists of 531 jets, two-thirds of which are Boeing.

Exports of Ivorian cocoa totalled 150,000 tonnes in January.
The cumulative total for the 1996/97 season reached 416,000 tonnes since October 1.
Warehouses are reported to be full according to a port source.
Latest figures on cocoa arrivals at ports are not immediately available.
Arrivals are widely expected to total 800,000 tonnes since October 1.
Total dedicated warehouse space is estimated at close to 400,000 tonnes.
Bean humidity levels are reported to be around 7.5-8.0 percent.
Export standards allow a maximum of eight percent humidity and 105 beans per 100 grammes.
Break bulk shipment of cocoa is more popular with clients than shipment in containers.
Exporters expect a total crop of around a million tonnes.

African coffee ministers will meet on Thursday to discuss cutting robusta exports.
The meeting follows a January agreement among world producers.
Some officials believe that disease and drought make cuts unnecessary in certain countries.
African producers agreed to cut robusta exports by a total of 850,000 60-kilo bags between January and June 1997.
The purpose of the cuts is to increase prices.
Individual country quotas will be decided later.
