A spokesman for the Inter-African Coffee Organisation (IACO) stated that they will ensure a transparent and effective implementation of the export programme.
IACO chief economist Donald Kaberuka mentioned that ministers will decide on Africa's share and how to handle shortfalls.
Eight countries will participate in the talks: Uganda, Ivory Coast, Cameroon, Kenya, Zaire, Tanzania, Madagascar, and Ethiopia.
Uganda is Africa's largest robusta producer, with production figures of approximately 4,644,397 60-kilo bags in 1996.

Ivorian port cocoa stocks are up to 175,000 tonnes.
Cocoa arrivals are about 1,000 tonnes a week.
April and May exports will reduce cocoa stock levels.
The main cocoa season runs from October to April.
Cocoa arrivals will decrease until early May.
Stocks in Abidjan are at 100,000 tonnes.
Stocks at the second port of San Pedro are at 75,000 tonnes.
Some exporters are short of cocoa for immediate shipment.
The Caisse may have issued too many contracts.
Latest bean sizes are around 90-105 beans per 100 grams.

Tobacco company lawyers are defending against the $5 billion Broin secondhand-smoke lawsuit.
Tobacco lawyers are successfully removing jurors who believe secondhand smoke likely causes disease.
Trial consultants reported that tobacco lawyers have excluded many nurses from the jury pool.
Thirty-two individuals passed initial screening for the Broin trial out of more than 75 questioned.
The jury will decide if cigarette companies like Philip Morris and RJ Reynolds Tobacco are liable for health issues among flight attendants.
The flight attendants, including Norma Broin, allege that secondhand smoke from passengers caused their illnesses.
Smoking on U.S. passenger jets was banned in 1988.
Stanley Rosenblatt is involved in the flight-attendants lawsuit against tobacco companies.
The ideal juror for tobacco lawyers is described as a conservative white male smoker with minimal education.
Tobacco lawyers can block up to 27 potential jurors without explanation during jury selection.

Tobacco industry lawyers accused the judge of failing to reject potential jurors with anti-cigarette prejudices.
Five additional people passed initial questioning in the class-action case, increasing the potential-jurors pool to 16.
Court officials stated that 80 or more potential jurors are needed to select a six-member jury and 12 alternates.
The case involves U.S. cigarette makers' liability for lung cancer and other smoking-related ailments among 60,000 non-smoking flight attendants.
Jury selection is expected to continue for several weeks.
Jury selection began on Monday.
Dade County Circuit Court Judge Robert Kaye has asked follow-up questions to potential jurors after initial questioning by lawyers.
A Miami police department payroll clerk expressed a belief that cigarettes should be banned and showed more sympathy for flight attendants than tobacco defendants.
Judge Kaye asked the clerk if she could make a fair decision based on evidence, to which she affirmed.
Tobacco lawyer Edward Moss protested the judge's questioning and requested the clerk be eliminated from consideration due to perceived bias.

Jose Martinez is the legal defender of Dosal Tobacco Co.
Martinez works at the Miami law firm Martinez, Gutierrez & DeCordoba.
Dosal Tobacco Co. is a small family-owned company based in Opa-Locka, Florida.
Dosal Tobacco Co. produces a few million cigarettes a year.
Philip Morris Cos. Inc. is the largest cigarette maker in the world.
Philip Morris shipped nearly 231 billion cigarettes in the United States last year.
Dosal Tobacco Co. is named in three anti-tobacco lawsuits in Florida and one in Michigan.
Dosal's main customer is the Florida prison system.
Dosal's DTC brand cigarettes are sold to inmates in Florida.
Dosal also produces a brand called Competidora, favored by elderly Cuban emigres in south Florida.

China's state firms are increasing efforts to produce sellable products.
As of the end of October, inventories across 380,000 enterprises in China totaled 540 billion yuan.
The inventory amount is 80 billion yuan higher than at the beginning of 1996.
State Statistical Bureau spokesman Ye Zhen stated that 150 billion yuan of the total inventory is unreasonable.
Many state-owned firms have struggled to adapt to consumer-led markets.
Excessive investment in certain industries has led to large stockpiles of unsold goods.
There are approximately 1.5 billion unsold men's shirts in China.
Chinese officials attribute investment concentration to competition issues, including losses and monopolies.
Beijing aims to reduce blind investment in certain industries, but regional defiance may hinder efforts.
The value of outstanding accounts owed by 380,000 state firms reached 900 billion yuan by the end of October.

A new copper production group is being established in Yunnan province, China.
Yunnan Copper Industry (Group) Co was formed after the merger of Yunnan's largest copper mines, bureaux, and a major smelter.
The group has a five-year plan to increase mineral production.
General manager Zhou Paixiang stated that electrolytic copper output would increase to 150,000 tonnes a year by 2000.
The group's mines are expected to extract about 60,000 tonnes of copper ore annually from Yunnan's mountains.
Group president Zou Shaolu mentioned that the formation of the group aims to improve resource distribution and efficiency.
The group plans to address the shortfall between mine output and smelter demand by purchasing copper on domestic and international markets.
Copper imports for the smelters are projected to exceed 50,000 tonnes annually by 2000.
The Yunnan group currently accounts for approximately one-ninth of China's copper output.
The group also engages in mining other minerals such as gold, silver, and zinc, and produces various consumer goods.

China and the United States reached an agreement on Sunday to extend a deal on textiles.
The agreement was announced by an official with China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation.
The two sides will sign the agreement in a ceremony shortly.
The agreement followed all-night talks between U.S. chief textile negotiator Rita Hayes and Chinese officials.
The talks were about renewing a 1994 textile accord and resolving a dispute over U.S. penalties on Chinese textile exports.
Rita Hayes expressed confidence in reaching an accord during last-ditch talks.
The deadline for multi-million dollar penalties on China's exports was extended by one day from January 31.
The Sino-U.S. textile pact was scheduled to expire on December 31 but was extended by one month.
Washington imposed $19 million worth of penalties on imports of Chinese textiles last September.
China threatened to retaliate by temporarily banning imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods, and alcoholic drinks.

AT&T Corp. will separate Lucent Technologies Inc. as a distinct company at the end of this month.
AT&T announced its plan to split into three businesses a year ago.
AT&T has 3.3 million shareholders, more than any other U.S. corporation.
Lucent Technologies had an initial public offering of stock in April.
On September 17, AT&T stock will lose rights to 82.4 percent of Lucent shares.
After the split, AT&T will consist only of telecommunications services and computing businesses.
The final part of the split will occur around the end of 1996, when shareholders will receive stock in NCR.
Shareholders on September 30 will receive one new Lucent share for every three AT&T shares they hold.
Temporary classes of stock will be created for AT&T and Lucent in the weeks leading up to the September 30 split.
The trading symbol for AT&T 'when issued' stock will be T wd.N.

AT&T Corp recorded a $200 million rise in bad debt and uncollectibles in the fourth quarter.
AT&T sees a need for an industrywide drive to address customers who fail to pay their telephone bills.
Richard Miller is the Chief Financial Officer of AT&T.
The $200 million rise in bad debt was the main reason AT&T fell short of consensus estimates for the fourth quarter.
AT&T's operating net was $0.76 in the fourth quarter, compared to $0.68 in the year-earlier period and below the $0.79 First Call consensus.
Miller stated that there are emerging behaviors that need to be addressed as an industry.
The majority of the problems AT&T faced in 1996 were in the business market, but there was also an increase in uncollectibles in the consumer area.
AT&T reported increases in business fraud, delinquency, and bankruptcies during the period.
Miller indicated that half of the $200 million was for catch-up on past underprovisioning and the other half was incurred in the fourth quarter.
In 1996, AT&T had $9 billion of account receivables and $7.1 billion of financial receivables, with a total of $1.3 billion allocated to allowances including uncollectibles.

Sprint Corp is exploring options to extend its local phone services across the U.S. in a post-deregulation environment.
Sprint's cable TV allies are currently not participating in local phone services.
Sprint executives indicated that the company will initially resell local circuits from regional Bells.
Sprint's relationship with cable companies is currently limited to wireless services.
Sprint PCS is a wireless partnership involving Sprint, Tele-Communications Inc, Comcast Corp, and Cox Communications Inc.
Sprint PCS is building a digital network across the U.S. for Personal Communications Services.
The extension of local phone service is a challenging aspect of Sprint's 1994 strategy to combine wireless and wired phone services with cable TV.
Sprint has seven million local phone customers, primarily in rural and suburban areas.
Sprint aims to expand its service to between 10 and 20 cities by the end of 1997.
Sprint is negotiating resale agreements with regional Bells and expects some to be finalized within 30 days.

General Mills Inc is the number-two U.S. cereal maker with a roughly 27-percent market share.
General Mills expects record performance in fiscal 1997.
General Mills Chairman Stephen Sanger stated the company expects record earnings, record volume, and record market share.
In fiscal 1996, General Mills earned $3.00 a share with sales of $5.42 billion.
General Mills experienced seven percent domestic volume growth and 13 percent international volume growth in fiscal 1997.
General Mills is expected to reach its volume target of four percent growth for the first nine months of fiscal 1997.
General Mills expects a decline in cereal prices to reduce earnings for fiscal 1997 by about $0.20 a share.
General Mills' acquisition of the branded cereal and snacks business of Ralcorp Holdings Inc is expected to reduce earnings by about $0.05 a share.
In the first half of fiscal 1997, General Mills posted a profit of $1.80 a share and sales of $2.88 billion.
General Mills' goal is to grow earnings per share over the long term and to achieve a return on capital of at least 25 percent.

Maytag Corp. reported that its earnings for the fourth quarter more than doubled from the previous year.
Maytag returned to profitability for the full year.
Hoover floor care line contributed to Maytag's earnings growth.
Hoover posted double-digit gains in sales for both the quarter and the year.
Maytag anticipates a slow start for its earnings in 1997 due to marketing costs for new products.
New products include another Hoover upright floor cleaner, refrigerators, and washing machines.
Chairman Leonard Hadley stated that earnings performance is expected to improve after mid-year.
Maytag's 1996 profits were aided by lower raw material costs and results from its joint venture partner in China, Hefei Rongshida.
For the fourth quarter, Maytag reported earnings of $35.3 million, or 36 cents a share.
For the year, Maytag posted a profit of $136.4 million, or $1.34 a share.

McDonald's Corp. reported a 12 percent rise in fourth-quarter profits.
McDonald's income rose to $410.0 million from $366.8 million a year ago.
The income figure includes a $48.7 million after-tax charge.
The charge is related to plans to close about 115 low-volume satellite units in the United States.
As of Dec. 31, McDonald's had 2,218 satellite units.
Satellite units typically have a limited menu and are located in non-traditional sites like shopping malls.
McDonald's plans to open fewer satellite restaurants in 1997 and emphasize full-scale units.
McDonald's is trimming its overall restaurant opening plan for 1997 to between 2,400 and 2,800.
More than 70 percent of new restaurants will be outside the United States.
McDonald's U.S. operating income fell 28 percent in the fourth quarter, including the charge.

Chinese officials sent positive signals about Beijing's future handling of Hong Kong.
Diplomats indicated that China and Britain agreed on a VIP guestlist for a handover party.
Hong Kong will revert to communist-ruled China at midnight on June 30 after being a British colony for 150 years.
Hong Kong is to retain its separate capitalist system for 50 years.
Chinese officials assured Hong Kong that there will be no influx of mainland Chinese.
Chinese officials stated that the future garrison will not misbehave.
Wang Fengchao, deputy head of Beijing's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, dismissed fears of a migrant influx.
Wang stated that there are strict rules on entry into Hong Kong and children of illegal immigrants will not be allowed in.
Major-General Xiong Zi Ren stated that the People's Liberation Army will not interfere in local government or business affairs.
Wang announced a grace period for Hong Kong emigrants to return and keep their permanent residency rights.

Hong Kong's future government has canceled a sitting of a controversial legislature due to a shortage of trained staff.
The legislature was preparing new laws ahead of the territory's handover to China.
Tung Chee-hwa will rule Hong Kong after the British pull out at midnight on June 30.
A session of the provisional legislature scheduled for Saturday to discuss a draft law on new flags has been dropped.
Only a briefing will take place instead of the legislative session.
Bob Howlett, a spokesman for Tung's office, stated that the draft bills are not ready due to a lack of personnel.
Tung's coordinator, Michael Suen, concluded that there are not enough draftsmen to prepare the planned laws.
British Governor Chris Patten has refused to send more staff from the Hong Kong civil service to assist Tung's office.
The office currently has only two law drafters on its staff.
China will resume sovereignty over Hong Kong under a 1984 treaty that allows the territory virtual autonomy for another 50 years.

An American businessman is planning a marketing revolution in the hospitality sector.
Howard Ruby is a corporate housing specialist.
Ruby aims to develop the serviced apartment business into a full-fledged industry.
The serviced apartment sector has historically been less prominent than hotels.
Ruby states that the serviced apartment industry has been largely unnoticed for the past twenty years.
Ruby's company, Oakwood International, is based in Los Angeles.
Ruby's group has launched a joint venture with a subsidiary of Lend Lease in Singapore.
The joint venture plans to provide 10,000 serviced apartments in Asia.
Ruby anticipates significant growth in the serviced apartment sector in China.
Oakwood is the largest national provider of serviced apartments in the United States.

Sanofi posted a net profit rise of 11 percent for the year 1996.
The company's net earnings for 1996 were 1.74 billion francs ($308 million).
Net earnings in 1995 were 1.58 billion francs.
Sales for 1996 were 23.65 billion francs, an increase of three percent from the previous year.
Earnings per share rose eight percent to 16.80 francs.
Analysts expected an average earnings per share figure of 17.3 francs according to Edinburg Financial Publishing.
Analysts expected an average earnings per share figure of 17.1 francs according to Jacques Chahine Finance in Paris.
Healthcare sales rose five percent, while turnover in the beauty segment fell by five percent.
The beauty segment's sales fell to 3.8 billion francs on a like-for-like basis from 1995.
Yves Rocher posted growth in both sales and net earnings, while Nina Ricci reported declines in sales and earnings.

Airbus Industrie criticized a deal between Delta Air Lines Inc and Boeing Co as anti-competitive.
Delta Air Lines Inc announced a $6.7 billion order for 106 Boeing aircraft.
Delta's deal with Boeing makes Boeing its sole aircraft supplier for the next 25 years.
The total number of aircraft in the Delta deal could reach 644 with options.
The Delta deal is potentially worth more than $15 billion.
American Airlines previously entered into an exclusive deal with Boeing.
An Airbus spokeswoman stated that Boeing is attempting to eliminate competition through exclusive deals.
The Airbus spokeswoman claimed that such deals could harm airlines and passengers by allowing Boeing to raise prices.
Boeing holds approximately 60 percent of the global civil aircraft market.
Airbus is a consortium of four European companies and is in talks to convert into a limited liability company by 1999.

The French government announced its readiness to relaunch the privatisation of Thomson-CSF.
Key executives have been appointed to oversee the sale of Thomson-CSF.
The industry and finance ministries issued a joint statement regarding the privatisation.
An attempt to sell Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe last year was rejected by the Privatisation Commission.
Marcel Roulet has been made responsible for the sale of Thomson-CSF on a full-time basis.
Marcel Roulet will only serve as chairman of Thomson-CSF.
Thierry Breton has been appointed as chairman of Thomson SA and Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
Thierry Breton will be responsible for the privatisation of TMM and will propose a sale procedure.
The government plans to inject 11 billion francs into TMM by the summer, pending European Commission approval.
The sale of TMM will be conducted gradually through an opening up of its capital.

Conrail Inc. rejected a $10.5 billion takeover offer from Norfolk Southern Corp.
Conrail believes its proposed $9.3 billion merger with CSX Corp. is a better corporate combination.
Conrail Chairman David LeVan stated that a merger with CSX is in the best interests of Conrail and its constituencies.
The rejection of Norfolk Southern's offer occurred one day after CSX and Norfolk Southern raised their bids for Conrail.
Industry analysts believe CSX and Norfolk Southern are unlikely to increase their offers significantly.
Both CSX and Norfolk Southern will continue their competition in court, before regulators, and in the marketplace.
CSX raised its offer for Conrail to provide shareholders with an additional $870 million.
The revised deal between CSX and Conrail is valued at $9.3 billion, or about $102 per Conrail share.
Norfolk Southern increased its all-cash offer to about $10.5 billion, or $115 a share.
Industry experts suggest that Norfolk Southern aims to maintain the price difference while contesting part of the Conrail-CSX agreement in court.

ITT Corp is expected to defend against an unsolicited bid from Hilton Hotels Corp.
Hilton Hotels Corp has made a $6.5 billion offer for ITT Corp, which includes a 29 percent premium.
Wall Street experts believe the premium offered by Hilton is insufficient to acquire ITT Corp.
A trader stated that the franchise value of ITT Corp exceeds Hilton's offer.
Hilton Hotels Corp has announced a cash and stock offer for ITT Corp and may increase the offer if allowed to review ITT's financial data.
ITT Corp's stock price has declined due to gaming construction disruptions and competition.
ITT Corp's shares were trading at about 65 in June and closed at 42-5/8 on Monday.
Traders anticipate a rebound in ITT Corp's stock price due to a $2.5 billion capital expenditure program.
ITT Corp is focusing on a $2.5 billion capital spending program to expand and update its casino operations.
ITT Corp's chief operating officer Robert Bowman indicated that the company may pursue hotel acquisitions this year.

Norfolk Southern Corp. launched an effort to oppose a planned $9.1 billion merger between Conrail Inc. and CSX Corp.
Norfolk Southern proposed to buy a 9.9 percent stake in Conrail for $115 per share.
Norfolk Southern's takeover offer for Conrail has been rejected.
Norfolk Southern made its offer directly to Conrail shareholders.
Conrail shareholders are scheduled to vote on a key provision at a special meeting in Philadelphia.
Conrail has rejected Norfolk Southern's $10.3 billion cash offer.
Conrail believes the $9.1 billion transaction with CSX provides more strategic benefits.
Conrail is asking shareholders to waive a Pennsylvania law regarding CSX's purchase of Conrail shares.
If the provision is waived, CSX will buy another 20 percent of Conrail shares for $110 per share.
Norfolk Southern stated that its 9.9 percent offer would not require action from Conrail's board.

Opponents of U.S. trade concessions to China are expected to challenge President Bill Clinton's decision to renew China's favored trading status.
Supporters of the president's decision to renew China's most favored nation (MFN) status for another year are confident of victory.
Opponents include social conservatives and organized labor, who are preparing for a political fight.
The coalition of opponents criticizes China's policies on human rights, labor rights, religious rights, trade, and abortion.
Opponents are motivated by concerns over the transfer of Hong Kong to China and allegations of illegal campaign contributions by Beijing.
A congressional aide indicated that the presence of Hong Kong and campaign finance issues will make the fight tougher.
House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich stated that this year's decision will be closer than last year's vote to support Clinton on MFN.
Advocates and opponents expect that the president's policy will ultimately survive despite the opposition.
Gingrich criticized Clinton for not using his announcement to advocate for human rights and democratic freedoms in China.
Congress will vote later this summer on whether to overturn Clinton's decision, starting with the House.

Some Baby Bells provided advice to foreign regulators on opening overseas phone markets.
The advice given by Baby Bells is now being used against them in the U.S. regarding their monopolies.
Consumer advocates and long-distance carriers, including AT&T Corp., are using the Baby Bells' statements to challenge their control of the local phone market.
The local phone market is valued at $100 billion and is controlled by regional Bell phone companies.
Gene Kimmelman, co-director of Consumers Union, described the situation as an example of hypocrisy.
Kimmelman noted that the Baby Bells make arguments against their monopoly status similar to those made by consumer advocates and competitors.
BellSouth Corp. and U S West Inc. endorsed a pricing method for phone networks in 1995 that is important for new competitors.
The Baby Bells oppose this pricing method when it comes to their own networks for long-distance companies and others.
The Baby Bells are seeking to overturn Federal Communications Commission rules that promote competition through a similar pricing system.
BellSouth spokesman Bill McCloskey stated that the arguments made by the Baby Bells were from a time before the need for a single corporate policy.

Regulators are set to announce approval of plans for a new type of radio service that offers CD-quality sound.
The new radio service can be heard coast-to-coast.
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has resolved differences over allocating two available radio licenses.
Four companies are seeking to offer Digital Audio Radio Service (DARS): CD Radio Inc., American Mobile Radio Corp., Digital Broadcast Satellite Corp., and Primosphere.
The new service will be broadcast nationwide via satellite and will require listeners to buy a special radio and antenna.
The service is likely to be subscription-based.
FCC's approval is expected to be announced soon, possibly as early as Monday.
The auction of the two licenses will be limited to the four companies that applied in the early 1990s.
The auction date is expected to be set before April 15.
The FCC agreed to require license winners to provide discounted advertising rates and equal time to political candidates running for federal office.

Intel Corp. executives announced that the company will invest cash and technical expertise in a new company for delivering multimedia content via satellite to personal computers in Europe.
The investment will be formally announced at the CeBIT technology trade fair in Hannover, Germany.
This investment marks Intel's first foray into personal computer delivery services.
Intel has previously sought to promote technologies that enhance the use of personal computers globally.
Intel will hold a minority stake in the newly formed European Satellite Multimedia Services S.A. (ESM).
Leslie Vadasz, Intel senior vice president, stated that Europe has significant satellite usage, making it a suitable location for this service.
Industry sources estimate the value of Intel's investment at $15 million.
Luxembourg's Societe Europeenne des Satellite (SES) will hold a majority stake in ESM, which will also be based in Luxembourg.
The new company will launch ASTRA-NET, a communication system utilizing SES's existing ASTRA satellite system.
The first business-to-business communications links through ASTRA-NET are expected to be operational in the second half of the year.

Cisco Systems Inc chief executive John Chambers stated that the networking industry's overall business was growing in 1997.
Chambers predicted a market growth rate of 30 to 50 percent for the foreseeable future.
Cisco's second quarter results exceeded Wall Street estimates.
Cisco reported a net income of $339.5 million for the second quarter to January 25, a 62 percent increase from $209.7 million a year earlier.
Net sales for Cisco rose to $1.59 billion, a 73 percent increase from $918.5 million a year earlier.
Cisco's pro forma net income was $351.9 million, or $0.51 a share, which exceeded the mean analysts estimate of $0.50 a share.
Chambers indicated that Cisco expected to acquire another 10 to 12 companies in the current year.
Chambers noted opportunities for internal products, joint development projects, and acquisitions in almost every market segment.
Cisco shares fell to 64-1/4 in after-market trade after initially closing at 67-1/8.
Some analysts expressed concerns that Cisco's earnings number had fallen short of expectations.

Some high-technology industry executives believe the Internet gold rush may be over.
Frank Gill is the executive vice president and general manager of Intel Corp.'s Internet and Communications Group.
Gill stated that there is not a lot of gold left in the Internet gold rush.
Gill is one of five keynote speakers at the Spring Internet World 97 conference in Los Angeles.
The conference is expected to feature many new product announcements from Internet start-up companies.
Top executives from Apple Computer Co., International Business Machines Corp., and Digital Equipment Corp. are also expected to speak at the conference.
The Internet start-up explosion peaked nearly a year ago.
Yahoo! Inc. went public at a valuation that peaked at over $1 billion on its first day of trading.
Venture capital investment continues at a strong pace despite a slowdown in the Internet public offering market.
Gill believes that the number of start-ups will not slow down, but their stock valuation expectations will become more realistic.

Some Asian central banks have intervened to defend their currencies.
Institutional investors continue to avoid the Asian region.
Concerns about the region's economic fundamentals and growth prospects have deepened.
David Semple is a regional strategist at Peregrine Asset Management.
Semple stated that there is a downturn in investment and economic growth in Asia.
High income growth in Asia has not resulted in high economic growth.
Exports from Asia have not recovered as quickly as expected.
Some analysts have downgraded growth projections for the region.
Corporate earnings in Asia have disappointed investors.
There have been net outflows of investment from Asia throughout the year.

U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich expected to discuss allegations of illegal funding to the Democratic Party by Beijing during his visit to China.
Gingrich considered the allegations a domestic issue.
Gingrich made these statements before leaving for Beijing on a 10-day Asian tour.
The Washington Post reported that the Federal Bureau of Investigation warned six members of the U.S. Congress last year about being targeted by China for illegal campaign funds.
U.S. Vice President Al Gore discussed the issue with Chinese Premier Li Peng in Beijing.
Li Peng denied the allegations of illegal funding.
Gore stated that proof of payments would make the allegations a serious matter.
Gingrich described the campaign financing scandal as a serious domestic issue.
Gingrich claimed that the issue was an American problem involving violations of American law.
Gingrich called for cooperation from Asian nations on investigations related to the allegations.

Hong Kong has total fiscal reserves of HK$330 billion (US$42 billion) as of the 1997/98 budget figures.
This amount translates to more than US$6,500 for each person in Hong Kong.
The gross national debt in the United States is US$5.5 trillion, equating to US$20,500 for every child born there in 1997.
Financial Secretary Donald Tsang did not implement tax cuts in the 1997/98 budget.
Tsang emphasized the need for continuity and cooperation with China in his budget speech.
The budget surplus for Hong Kong this year is HK$15.1 billion, projected to rise to HK$31.7 billion in 1997/98.
Critics, including Emily Lau, expressed dissatisfaction with the government's spending on the needy, particularly the elderly.
Lau described the budget surplus as 'utterly obscene' and highlighted the plight of impoverished residents.
Tsang reduced duties on wine from 90 percent to 60 percent.
In 1995, Hong Kong increased the quota for mainland immigrants to 150 per day, primarily for family reunions.

Chinese authorities imposed a curfew on a town in the Xinjiang region.
At least 10 people were killed in a separatist Moslem riot in Yining last week.
About 1,000 Moslem separatists of the Uighur ethnic minority participated in the riot.
The riot involved smashing cars, burning shops, and attacking Han Chinese.
Both Han Chinese and Uighurs were killed or injured during the riot.
The riot was described as one of the most violent in years in Xinjiang.
Yining is located 50 km from the border with Kazakhstan.
A circular was issued ordering people not to go out after dark.
The riot began when a Chinese policeman attempted to arrest a Uighur suspect.
Local authorities deployed about 1,000 police and paramilitary forces to control the situation.

Negotiators from China and the United States resumed talks on Saturday regarding a new textile accord and market access.
The deadline for a cross-Pacific trade war was extended by one day.
Chief U.S. textile negotiator Rita Hayes expressed confidence in reaching an agreement on Saturday.
Hayes stated that significant progress had been made during the negotiations.
Hayes and Chinese officials worked late into Friday night to address issues related to a 1994 textile accord and U.S. penalties on Chinese exports.
The United States extended the deadline for the textile accord to allow for further negotiations.
Hayes indicated that the U.S. side was focused on two main demands: market access and a level playing field for the textile industry.
Disagreement over market access in China was identified as a major obstacle in the negotiations.
Industry representatives expressed optimism about the possibility of a deal despite the challenges.
Washington imposed $19 million in penalties on Chinese textile imports last September due to quota evasion.

Talks to resolve the fate of Hwang Jang-yop, a high-level North Korean defector, have entered the eighth day in Beijing.
Hwang Jang-yop is currently at Seoul's consulate in Beijing.
Chang Moon Ik is a spokesman for the South Korean embassy.
Chang stated that negotiations are ongoing regarding the crisis involving Hwang Jang-yop.
Chang did not confirm China's involvement in the discussions.
Reports suggest that North Korea may be ready to abandon attempts to recover Hwang Jang-yop.
Hwang Jang-yop is ranked 24th in the hierarchy of North Korea and was a senior aide to Kim Jong-il.
Kim Jong-u is the head of North Korea's Overseas Economic Cooperation Committee.
A Japanese newspaper reported that Kim Jong-u indicated Pyongyang was ready to let Hwang go.
The North Korean Foreign Ministry hinted at a softening stance regarding Hwang's defection.

Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) faced a failed takeover bid led by Andrew Regan.
Andrew Regan is 31 years old.
CWS's satisfaction at defeating Regan is tempered by concerns about its independence.
The chances of Regan succeeding in his takeover bid were considered slim.
The takeover attempt has raised awareness of CWS's under-utilised assets.
Banking observers believe CWS remains a target for future takeover attempts.
CWS has a complex ownership and voting structure that complicates hostile takeovers.
Regan planned to make a bid through his company Lanica Trust Plc.
CWS reported a 10 million pound fall in profits for the year before tax.
Regan's planned offer for CWS was 1.2 billion pounds through a company called Galileo Group.

Norwich Union is a British insurer that started trading on the stock market this week.
Norwich Union's public offer of shares was priced at 290 pence per share for successful applicants and 265 pence for members.
The public offer raised around 2.4 billion pounds ($3.9 billion) for Norwich Union.
Norwich Union is valued at over 5.6 billion pounds.
Norwich Union is Britain's third largest quoted insurer, behind Prudential Corp and Royal & Sun Alliance.
Many applicants will receive fewer shares than requested due to high demand.
Members applied for nearly four times as many shares as were available.
The institutional offer was covered ten times.
Members applying for up to 1,500 pounds worth of shares will receive their full allotment.
Norwich Union had to reclaim 400 million pounds worth of shares from the public offering to satisfy member demand.

Commercial Union Plc reported a strong rise in first quarter profits.
Pre-tax operating profits rose to 102 million pounds, up from 83 million pounds last year.
The results were in line with expectations.
Commercial Union shares slipped 13-1/2 pence to 736p.
Excluding the impact of sterling, profits advanced 46 percent.
Profits and new business sales in the life business rose 25 percent.
General insurance profits increased to 67 million pounds, up three million pounds over 1996.
Weather claims in the U.S. fell 23 million pounds to six million pounds after a milder winter.
Life profits over the quarter increased to 62 million pounds from 58 million pounds last year.
Commercial Union acquired 73 percent of French life assurer Societe d'Epargne Viagere in April.

Speculation exists in Hong Kong about a possible link between Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd and a Chinese partner.
Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd did not comment on its future shareholding structure.
Deputy chairman Richard Brown stated that it was not the right time to provide specific details.
There are rumors in the press regarding potential partnerships with state Chinese enterprises.
Hongkong Telecom is 58.5 percent-owned by Cable & Wireless Plc.
Analysts suggest that both Hongkong Telecom and Cable & Wireless Plc may consider a mainland partner due to the upcoming handover.
Hongkong Telecom reported a 12.5 percent rise in net profit for the year ending March 31, amounting to HK$11.18 billion.
China's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications and China United Telecommunications Corp have been identified as potential partners by local press.
A China Unicom official expressed interest in acquiring a stake in Hongkong Telecom.
A seasoned China observer believes that Hongkong Telecom will attract Chinese interest from state enterprises.

Hong Kong and Taiwan shipping representatives met on Friday to discuss direct shipping links after Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule.
George Chao is the head of the Hong Kong Shipowners' Association.
Chao stated that sensitive details of protocol need to be resolved for direct shipping links to continue after July 1.
The issue of which flag ships should fly was a primary topic of discussion.
Chao mentioned that shipping between Taiwan and Hong Kong faces questions regarding flags after July 1.
Ships registered in Hong Kong and Taiwan currently fly each other's flag when entering each other's territorial waters.
This practice will end after the sovereignty handover on July 1 due to Hong Kong's future constitution observing the 'one-China' principle.
China views Taiwan as a rebel province since the Nationalist government fled there in 1949.
Chang Liang-jen, deputy secretary-general of the Straits Exchange Foundation, prefers to maintain the status quo in shipping links.
Taipei proposed that both Taiwan and Hong Kong ships lower all flags and use telex communications for identification before entering each other's waters.

Future legislators in Hong Kong passed a series of laws on Saturday.
The laws will come into effect after Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
The provisional legislature consists of 60 members and met in Shenzhen, China.
The meeting was presented with bills by officials from the future administration led by Tung Chee-hwa.
A bill governing residency rights in Hong Kong passed through two readings.
Three bills governing the membership of municipal bodies passed through all three readings.
Proposed bills must go through three readings before July 1 to be ratified as post-handover laws.
The provisional legislature was formed under Beijing's auspices in December.
The current elected chamber will be disbanded on July 1.
The Democratic Party plans to file a lawsuit against the provisional legislature claiming it is illegal.

Microsoft Corp. unveiled Office 97, a next-generation software for office computers.
Office 97 includes Microsoft Word, Excel, Access, and PowerPoint.
Office 97 features document collaboration and seamless Internet access.
Bill Gates stated that Office is central to Microsoft's Internet strategy.
Microsoft has 55 million users of Microsoft Office applications.
Nearly 10,000 retail outlets placed advance orders for Office 97.
Office 97 became available in stores on Thursday.
Microsoft sold 3 million copies of Office 97 through corporate licensing agreements.
Many large business users have not upgraded to Windows 95 or Windows NT, which are required for Office 97.
Microsoft claims over 80 percent of improvements in Office 97 were based on customer feedback.

America Online Inc. announced a refund plan to appease customers dissatisfied with busy signals.
The refund plan is part of a preliminary deal with 36 state attorneys general.
New York threatened to sue America Online if no relief was offered to consumers.
Analysts stated that the refund plan could improve America Online's near-term financial results by offsetting marketing expenses.
America Online's stock rose 25 cents to $37.875 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement.
Steve Case, Chairman of America Online, did not estimate the cost of the refunds.
Analysts believe that restrictions on refunds will limit the financial impact on America Online.
Jamie Kiggen estimated the refunds could cost America Online between $10 million and $15 million.
Brian Oakes estimated the worst-case cost of refunds at $16 million.
America Online's refund plan allows members to request a one-month credit or a monetary refund based on usage.

Computer makers are expected to report solid fourth-quarter earnings.
The fourth quarter is normally the strongest quarter of the year for computer makers.
The stronger dollar will hurt some big systems makers.
Most U.S. PC makers, except for Apple Computer Inc. and AST Research Inc., are expected to show strong sales growth.
Strong sales growth is fueled by hefty corporate buying.
Apple Computer Inc. is the first to report its first-quarter results.
Apple forecasted an operating loss for its first quarter due to weak U.S. demand for its Performa consumer PC and shortages of notebook computers.
Dean Witter analyst Eugene Glazer stated that business in the PC sector, other than Apple, was strong.
Some market share was going to direct marketers like Dell Computer Corp. and Gateway 2000 Inc.
Compaq Computer Corp. is likely to report strong earnings, benefiting from corporate sales.

The growth in fast-food, snacking, and eating out in Britain is driving profits at food retailer Watson & Philip.
Watson & Philip owns a chain of 526 Alldays convenience stores.
Colin Glass is the chief executive of Watson & Philip.
There has been a major demographic shift with an increasing number of single occupancy households or households where both people work.
Customers are spending more on prepared food rather than food they cook at home.
Watson & Philip's shares were 44p higher at 384p.
The product at Alldays will be consumed or start to be consumed within two minutes of the customer being in the store.
Watson & Philip has adopted two strategies aimed at achieving profit growth: changing the product mix and opening more stores.
The company plans to open about 150 more Alldays stores in 1997, mainly in the Midlands and North England.
Watson & Philip will franchise Dunkin' Donuts from its owner Allied Domecq.

Vaux Group Plc is a British brewer and hotels company.
Beer sales to independent pubs rose six percent compared to last year.
The increase in beer sales is attributed to a new supply contract with a big pub chain.
Sales to the free on-trade were up 2.4 percent in the year ending September 30.
Vaux increased its beer sales by one percent during its financial year.
The overall beer market declined by 0.5 percent during the same period.
Vaux improved its market share in the north east of the country.
About 40 percent of Vaux beer is sold to its own tied estate of 749 pubs.
Vaux launched two new nitrokegs, Double Maxim and Lampton's, during the year.
Bookings for the Christmas period were six percent up compared to last year.

Britain's United Biscuits (Holdings) Plc expects its margins in Europe to remain firm and to increase over the next two to three years.
Managing director Eric Nicoli stated that the company expects margins to reach 10 percent in all its businesses within two to three years.
Currently, United Biscuits' margins are around 10 percent in Britain and four percent in mainland Europe.
The company reported a more than doubling in pretax, pre-exceptional annual profits to 109.1 million stg.
United Biscuits shares were 7-1/2p higher at 246p in early trade.
United Biscuits has entered a phase of consolidation after a disposal program, focusing on organic growth.
Over the last two years, United Biscuits has sold its American snack operation Keebler and exited from Portugal and Spanish snacks.
The company has also sold one of its Italian snack businesses and withdrawn from Turkey and Brazil.
United Biscuits sold the Ross Vegetables Products business in Britain.
Eric Nicoli mentioned that the markets are competitive, but the company expects another year of good progress.

Federal-Mogul Corp announced a restructuring that ends its effort to build a global auto parts retail empire.
The company will return to its core manufacturing and distribution business.
Federal-Mogul will incur $264 million in pre-tax charges for the restructuring and special one-time items from the fourth quarter.
The company's stock increased by $1.50 to $25 a share following the announcement.
Nicholas Colas, an analyst at CS First Boston, stated that the restructuring is a prudent move for the company.
Colas noted that Federal-Mogul lacked in-house retail expertise during its expansion into retail.
The restructuring marks a reversal of efforts by former chairman and CEO Dennis Gormley, who resigned in September.
Gormley spent approximately $500 million on acquisitions since 1992, with less than one-third related to international retail expansion.
Federal-Mogul Chairman and CEO Dick Snell stated that retail operations can be better managed by others.
The company plans to cut about 2,900 jobs, which is 18.5 percent of its worldwide workforce of 15,700.

Investigators are recovering the remains of 28 adults and one infant from a commuter plane crash.
The crash site left a blackened crater in a field.
John Hammerschmidt is a senior member of the National Transportation Safety Board.
Hammerschmidt stated that the cockpit voice and flight recorders had not been recovered.
Hammerschmidt expressed confidence that the recorders would eventually be found.
The cockpit voice and flight recorders provide detailed information on the final seconds before a crash.
Search efforts are hampered by temperatures near zero Fahrenheit and ground blizzards.
Workers can only stay in the search area for 15 to 20 minutes at a time.
The plane involved was a 30-seat, Brazilian-built Embraer 120 operated by Delta Comair.
The plane crashed during its approach to Detroit's Metropolitan Airport after taking off from Cincinnati.

Ford Motor Co was selected as the lead negotiator with the United Auto Workers union.
Analysts questioned what Ford had to concede to become the first negotiator among the Big Three automakers.
J.P. Morgan analyst David Bradley noted that being first is advantageous for Ford.
Chrysler Corp was previously believed to be the UAW's likely choice to start contract talks.
Some analysts thought General Motors Corp had a chance to be selected as well.
Union officials confirmed Ford's selection but did not provide further comments.
Ford executives stated they are encouraged by the tone of the negotiations.
Analysts speculated that Ford may have shown willingness to support union organizing among its suppliers.
The UAW may consider a contract longer than the traditional three years in exchange for Ford's cooperation.
Michael Ward, an analyst at PaineWebber Inc, suggested that Ford would prefer a five or six-year agreement.

China's President Jiang Zemin met with members of the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday.
The meeting aimed to boost ties with the American Congress.
The congressional delegation consisted of 22 representatives, the largest ever to visit China.
Jiang Zemin stated that improving Sino-U.S. relations is in the interests of both countries.
Jiang mentioned having good discussions with President Bill Clinton in Manila in November.
Jiang and Clinton agreed on an exchange of presidential visits in 1997 and 1998.
Beijing and Washington have been trying to mend ties strained by disputes over Taiwan, trade, and human rights.
Analysts noted that China's leadership, particularly Jiang, wanted to strengthen ties with Congress.
Congress had pushed for Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui's visit to the U.S. in 1995, which angered Beijing.
Jim Kolbe, leading the congressional delegation, stated that Chinese leaders recognized the need for contacts with Congress.

China published a list of anti-dumping rules to protect local companies from foreign competition.
Chinese economists believe the rules will help domestic companies protect their market share.
The rules aim to provide a legal framework for protection against unfair competition.
Cheng Xiusheng, an economist from the State Council development research centre, stated that many Chinese companies struggle against unfair trade practices.
Cheng Xiusheng noted that other countries have imposed anti-dumping duties on Chinese products.
The published rules grant the government the authority to determine if imported goods receive official subsidies.
The rules allow for the imposition of anti-dumping duties on foreign goods.
Cash guarantees can be required to ensure payment under the new rules.
The rules set a maximum investigation length of 12 months, with special cases allowed to take 18 months.
The rules empower the state to retaliate against countries imposing discriminatory countervailing duties on Chinese goods.

China has achieved new successes in its fight against inflation.
Economists stated that price rises in China this year could be well below target.
Some economists believe inflation has been reduced with a modest impact on growth.
Chen Dezun is the head of the price research institute of the State Planning Commission.
Chen Dezun predicted inflation of between three and four percent this year.
The benchmark retail price index rose 1.7 percent in March and 2.6 percent for the first quarter of the year.
China forecast a 6.0 percent rise in retail prices this year.
China's economic growth is expected to exceed 10 percent this year.
The inflation figure for the first quarter was below Premier Li Peng's estimate of 3.0 percent.
Zhong Jiyun is an economist at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

The International Monetary Fund opened a website on Thursday providing information about economic data in 18 member countries.
Jack Boorman is the director of the IMF's policy and review department.
Boorman stated that the IMF has been urging countries to report data more timely and based on good statistical systems.
The 1994-95 Mexican peso crisis emphasized the need for timely and accurate data about developing countries.
The website does not include actual data from the countries but provides contacts for obtaining that information.
Boorman mentioned that good statistical citizenship helps to inform markets.
The purpose of the system is to ensure that markets receive better data in a timely manner.
The website's address is http://dsbb.imf.org.
The site lists information about the frequency, schedule, and types of economic and financial data released by countries subscribed to the Special Data Dissemination Standard.
The countries listed on the site are Argentina, Canada, Denmark, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Malaysia, Mexico, the Netherlands, Norway, Peru, the Philippines, Singapore, Slovenia, Switzerland, Thailand, Britain, and the United States.

U.S. lawmakers are redrafting a legislative proposal to modernize U.S. banking laws.
The redraft will rely heavily on the Clinton administration's reform plan.
The new draft of the proposal is expected to be finished by Friday.
The House Banking Committee will begin formal consideration of the proposal next week.
Committee spokesman David Runkel stated the goal is to include areas of general agreement in the bill.
Runkel mentioned the intent is to use as much of the Treasury Department's language as appropriate.
The most controversial questions will be resolved during the mark up as lawmakers offer amendments.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin unveiled the administration's plan to overhaul U.S. banking laws on May 21.
Rubin urged Congress to scrap the 1933 Glass-Steagall Act to allow banks to enter other financial sectors.
At least four major areas of disagreement remain that will be the focus of the scheduled June 11 mark up.

Bankers Trust New York Corp. and Alex. Brown Inc. have merged.
The merger indicates that the nation's banking laws are outdated.
Karen Shaw Petrou is the president of the consulting firm ISD/Shaw.
Petrou stated that the banking industry is modernizing despite Congress's slow progress on legislation.
Legislators have debated repealing the Glass-Steagall Act of 1933 for over a decade.
The Glass-Steagall Act prohibits banks from offering certain financial services like securities or insurance.
Federal courts and bank regulators have reduced the impact of Glass-Steagall in the past year.
Larry LaRocco is a bank industry lobbyist and former congressman.
LaRocco claimed that Glass-Steagall is effectively dead and that other issues need to be addressed.
Bankers Trust announced it would acquire Alex. Brown in a stock deal valued at $1.7 billion.

The Prague Stock Exchange's 1997 bull run ended on Thursday as investors took profits.
Analysts predicted little change in the bourse's fortunes over the short-term.
The PX50 index retreated 9.0 points, or 1.43 percent, to 618.6.
The PX50 index had increased over 16 percent since the beginning of the year.
The PX50 index reached a two-year high of 629.0 on Tuesday.
SPT Telecom, CEZ, and Komercni Banka each fell more than 2.2 percent at the price fixing.
Jan Sykora of Wood and Company stated that the market is thin and profit-taking causes it to collapse.
Analysts expect Komercni to be hardest hit among blue chips after rising over 25 percent since the start of the year.
The Central Securities Registry began publishing stock trade information on February 4.
The Finance Ministry's markets supervision department has been transformed into a Bureau for the Control of Securities.

A wave of high-yielding Czech crown Eurobonds has flooded the debt market since the beginning of the year.
Interest rates have eased and arbitrage opportunities have declined.
Ota Otepka, chief bond trader at ING Barings, stated that the Euro-madness is over.
Issuers have rushed to take advantage of a stable, strong currency and interest rates above 11 percent.
Nearly 30 billion crowns worth of Eurobonds were issued in just over four weeks.
The appetite for crown Eurobonds appeared insatiable due to high interest rates and favorable currency conditions.
Interest rates have eased by 60-70 basis points since the start of the year, leading to a drop in yields.
Jan Pudil of WoodCommerz suggested that lead managers may have been overly optimistic about foreign investors' appetite.
More than 20 bond issues were launched in crowns by top-rated, retail-friendly issuers.
Analysts estimate that about 90 percent of the crown bonds were bought by retail investors from Germany, the Benelux countries, and Switzerland.

The Czech trade deficit for December was 18.0 billion crowns ($650 million).
The full year 1996 trade deficit was a record 160.33 billion crowns.
A Reuters survey forecasted a December deficit of about 16 billion crowns.
The December 1995 trade gap was 14.3 billion crowns.
The overall trade deficit for 1995 was 95.7 billion crowns.
Imports for 1996 totaled 755.3 billion crowns, a year-on-year rise of 12.7 percent.
Exports in 1996 totaled 594.95 billion crowns, a year-on-year increase of 3.5 percent.
Machinery imports for 1996 reached 288.5 billion crowns, an increase of 16.1 percent over 1995.
Imports of raw materials, unprocessed goods, and chemical products totaled 327.9 billion crowns, a 10.2 percent year-on-year increase.
Exports in the raw materials, unprocessed goods, and chemical products sector reached 280.6 billion crowns, but contracted by 4.2 percent year-on-year.

British banks have developed a greater understanding of the needs of small firms, according to a report from the Bank of England.
The Bank of England's report was released on Wednesday.
Howard Davies is the deputy governor of the Bank of England.
Davies stated that relationships between small firms and their banks have improved from a low point four years ago.
Davies expressed that there is still much to be done in financing small firms.
The report identified small exporters and ethnic minority businesses as areas needing particular attention.
Bank finance is the main form of external finance used by small firms, defined as businesses with a turnover up to and including a million pounds a year.
Asset-backed finance has been increasing as a proportion of external finance for small firms.
There was a 19 percent increase in the number of firms using factoring services in 1996.
The report noted that term loans now account for around two thirds of the total 35 billion pounds of bank lending to small firms.

NatWest Markets' senior management did not know about the interest rate options pricing problem until three days before the losses were made public.
A NatWest spokeswoman stated that senior management did not know until February 25 that there was potentially something of significance.
The spokeswoman denied a weekend newspaper report suggesting that NatWest knew of the losses before they were revealed.
NatWest revealed that the mispricings totaled 90 million pounds ($144 million).
The mispricings were discovered during normal pricing reviews.
NatWest was unable to estimate the loss until February 28, when it was estimated at 50 million pounds.
The initial discovery of the loss came through a more intensive review across the investment bank's trading areas.
The extent of the mispricings became clear about a month after the initial discovery.
Martin Owen, the chief executive of NatWest Markets, stated he would forgo 200,000 of a 500,000 pound bonus due to the affair.
Kyriacos Papouis, the former NatWest options trader, has not commented on the losses and has resigned from Bear Stearns.

Britain lost an independent corporate finance adviser with the sale of Phoenix Group to Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
The financial details of the deal were not disclosed, but speculation suggested it was worth around 50 million pounds.
The sale would make multi-millionaires of Phoenix's top directors, who are major shareholders.
Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette aimed to acquire Phoenix's British mergers and acquisitions expertise.
Some experts considered the price paid for Phoenix to be high given its relatively slim revenues and profits.
Phoenix was established in 1981 and was acquired by Morgan Grenfell in 1987.
Phoenix regained its independence in 1990 through a management buyout led by Martin Smith, Philip Seers, and David Reid Scott.
In 1996, Phoenix advised on transactions worth around 2.5 billion pounds.
In August of the previous year, Phoenix was ranked second by Acquisitions Monthly among British-based independent corporate finance houses.
The new firm will be called DLJ Phoenix, with Martin Smith as chairman and all 25 directors and staff retained.

China has jailed two Mongolians for up to 15 years on charges of separatism and espionage.
Amnesty International reported that Hada, 41, was sentenced to 15 years in prison and Tegexi, 30, was sentenced to 10 years.
Chinese courts rejected the appeals of Hada and Tegexi last month and upheld their original sentences.
Hada and Tegexi were held for a year in solitary confinement without charges or a trial.
Amnesty International stated that no evidence has been made public to show that Hada and Tegexi were involved in any criminal activity under international standards.
Amnesty International called for the immediate and unconditional release of Hada and Tegexi.
The Amnesty report could not be independently confirmed.
Eight others were detained in December for alleged involvement in nationalist separatist activities but were subsequently released.
Hada and Tegexi were being detained in poor conditions and their health was suffering.
Hada has a recurrence of tuberculosis and it is unknown if he received any medical treatment in prison.

Beijing's propaganda machine has accused the United States of using the Dalai Lama as a tool to Westernise and break up China.
The Tibet Daily claimed that Western countries, led by the United States, have targeted China with their Westernisation and disintegration campaign.
The Tibet Daily stated that the Dalai Lama clique is used by the West to implement an anti-Chinese strategy.
The Dalai Lama received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989.
Sino-U.S. relations have been strained by disputes over Tibet, Taiwan, human rights abuses, and copyright piracy in China.
China blames followers of the Dalai Lama for periodic unrest in the Himalayan region bordering India.
The Dalai Lama seeks autonomy and freedom of worship in Tibet.
The Dalai Lama fled to India in 1959 after an uprising against communist rule.
The Tibet Daily criticized Western criticism of China's human rights record, stating that sovereign rights are more important than human rights.
Chinese authorities have offered a reward of one million yuan for information on a bomb set off outside government offices in Lhasa.

Chinese police arrested the suspected ringleader of a riot in Xinjiang that resulted in at least 10 deaths and 144 injuries.
Local officials reported the arrests on Wednesday.
Authorities issued emergency circulars to local officials to combat separatism in Xinjiang.
Severe punishment was warned for the rioters involved in last week's events.
Government units were ordered to form vigilante squads in Yining to guard against potential separatist attacks.
Zhang Youlian is the deputy director of the foreign affairs office for the Yili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture.
Police arrested Abudu Heilili, a 29-year-old Uighur, and began interrogating him after the riot.
Heilili was previously involved in a less violent anti-Chinese demonstration in Yining in August 1995.
Following the 1995 protest, Heilili was released after undergoing political indoctrination.
Police rounded up 200 to 300 people after last week's riot, with many suspects released after questioning.

Rural Press Ltd announced on Thursday that it is not confident of an economic turnaround needed to increase its profit for the full year to June 30, 1997.
Managing director Brian McCarthy expressed that a significant turnaround in consumer markets and real estate is some time away.
McCarthy stated that he does not foresee much improvement until at least the middle of the year.
Rural Press reported a four percent rise in net profit for the six months to December, amounting to A$16.96 million.
Rural Press declared an unchanged dividend of four cents per share.
The company warned that trading in the first five weeks of the second half had been below last year.
Rural Press indicated that it needs an improvement in the economy to continue its history of profit rises for the full year.
McCarthy noted that earnings before interest and tax would have fallen marginally in the half year on a like-for-like basis before acquisitions.
McCarthy attributed the slight profit fall on a like-for-like basis to weak real estate and retail sectors, which are key sources of advertising income.
Rural Press' share price closed unchanged at A$4.10, despite an overall market rise of one percent to a record high.

Boral Ltd reported a lower net profit for the first half year.
Boral Ltd stated it is poised to take advantage of an upturn in the house building sector.
Tony Berg is the managing director of Boral.
Boral's building materials division is positioned to exploit the upturn.
Boral reported a net profit of A$93.16 million for the six months to December 31.
The net profit of A$93.16 million is down from A$169.71 million in the same period a year earlier.
The decrease in net profit was largely due to a A$49.5 million abnormal profit from an asset sale in the previous year.
Net profit pre-abnormals fell to A$96 million from A$120 million the previous year.
Market expectations for pre-abnormals net profit were about A$90 million.
Analysts noted that the result was slightly above expectations due to stronger performance from Boral's U.S. building materials operations.

Allan Fels is the chairman of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
Fels expressed a neutral attitude regarding Westpac Banking Corp's A$1.435 billion bid for Bank of Melbourne Ltd.
Fels confirmed that he informed Westpac two years ago that the ACCC would be hesitant to allow a takeover of Bank of Melbourne.
The ACCC acknowledged that structural change may occur to allow a future takeover.
Fels stated that the ACCC evaluates mergers on a case-by-case basis.
Fels mentioned that the earlier informal discussions with Westpac occurred in September 1995.
During the 1995 discussions, wider issues about regional mergers were addressed.
Fels indicated that the ACCC had issued a statement suggesting hesitation about Westpac's bid for Bank of Melbourne at that time.
Fels clarified that the hesitation regarding Westpac-Bank of Melbourne only applied at that time.
Fels did not agree with claims of significant structural change in the regional banking sector.

Mercury Finance Co.'s agreement to buy a consumer finance business fell apart on Thursday.
Mercury Finance stated that phony bookkeeping entries had inflated its earnings.
Mercury Finance fired its chief accountant due to the inflated earnings.
The officer blamed for the overstated earnings may be cooperating with federal authorities.
BankBoston Corp. terminated its agreement to sell its Fidelity Acceptance Corp. unit to Mercury Finance.
The deal was valued at 32.7 million shares of Mercury stock.
When the deal was announced on January 10, the stock was worth about $458 million.
Mercury Finance stock closed at $14.875 on the New York Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
Traders reported that Mercury Finance stock was changing hands at $4.25 overseas.
Mercury Finance stated that its 1996 earnings would be restated to $56.7 million from $120.7 million.

Hyatt Hotels Corp. will spend $1 billion over the next three years to acquire 20 to 30 hotels.
The target properties will be upscale three- to five-star hotels and resorts in the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean.
Hyatt has already made two deals that are typical of its expansion plan.
A Hyatt affiliate purchased the Grand Hyatt San Francisco for $125 million plus $5 million in debt.
Hyatt will take over management of the Hotel Nikko Atlanta after acquiring it for $90 million in partnership with Blackstone Real Estate Partners.
The Hotel Nikko Atlanta will be renamed the Grand Hyatt Atlanta.
Hyatt operates 176 Hyatt hotels and resorts around the world.
Hyatt purchased 12 hotels in the past three years.
The more aggressive acquisition stance is seen as a response to acquisition plans by Hyatt's competitors.
Hyatt Equities L.L.C. was formed to consolidate the Pritzker family's hotel real estate interests.

Kmart Corp. will spend $750 million over the next three years to convert nearly all of its outlets to a new concept called 'Big Kmart.'
The Big Kmart concept aims to help shoppers save time and money by reorganizing merchandise and displaying it in wider aisles.
Chairman Floyd Hall stated that the new store represents a significant change for Kmart.
The Big Kmart concept is expected to increase sales at existing stores by 20 percent per square foot.
297 stores have been converted to the Big Kmart format so far.
Another 333 stores are scheduled for conversion in 1997.
Most of Kmart's more than 2,000 traditional stores will be converted by 1999.
Big Kmart stores are the same size as traditional stores, ranging from 60,000 to 80,000 square feet.
The Big Kmart concept organizes merchandise into three areas: home fashions, children's apparel and toys, and consumables.
Big Kmart stores will feature a new Pantry department with food and household products.

Canada's top securities regulator is probing Bre-X Minerals Ltd for potential breaches of insider trading and disclosure laws.
The Ontario Securities Commission has been investigating Bre-X Minerals since the end of 1996.
The OSC confirmed that the investigation relates to continuous disclosure requirements and insider trading provisions.
The OSC has not determined if there is enough information to begin formal proceedings against Bre-X.
The investigation is focusing on potential breaches of Ontario's Securities Act.
A group of Canadian Bre-X shareholders launched a class action lawsuit on Thursday.
Bre-X Minerals faces five court actions in the United States.
The Toronto Stock Exchange halted trading of Bre-X shares due to heavy order volumes on Thursday.
A report on Bre-X's assay program confirmed the company's original findings but raised new questions.
Panic selling resulted in a nearly C$3 billion loss in Bre-X's market value last Thursday.

Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. withdrew from the Busang gold project.
The Busang gold project was previously claimed to be the richest find of the century by Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
A report by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. stated that the Busang discovery was falsified on an unprecedented scale.
Freeport-McMoRan confirmed its poor test results from the Busang site through the Strathcona report.
Freeport announced it would notify Bre-X of its withdrawal from the Busang project based on its contractual agreement.
Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh stated that investigators would uncover the details of the scandal.
Strathcona found evidence of tampering with Bre-X's core samples.
Strathcona's tests revealed only trace amounts of gold at the Busang site.
The report indicated that a gold deposit worth mining was unlikely to be found at the Busang site.
Nusamba Group, linked to Indonesian President Suharto, also withdrew from the Busang project.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is based in Calgary, Alberta.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. reported a gold discovery at the Busang deposit in Indonesia.
Doubts about the Busang deposit and the death of chief geologist Michael de Guzman led to a decline in Bre-X stock.
Trading of Bre-X shares was halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange due to a report from an Indonesian newspaper.
The report claimed that Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. found the Busang deposit to be smaller than Bre-X's estimate of 71 million ounces.
Freeport-McMoRan stated that its review of the Busang site was not finished.
Bre-X stock fell to a 52-week low of C$14.25 during trading.
Bre-X closed down C$2.25 at C$15.20 with a trading volume of 9 million shares.
Michael de Guzman, the chief geologist of Bre-X, died after falling from a helicopter in Indonesia.
Indonesian officials suggested that de Guzman may have committed suicide, and his body has not been found.

Chrysler Corp. reported better-than-expected fourth quarter earnings.
Chrysler's fourth quarter earnings were $807 million, or $1.12 per share.
Chrysler incurred $279 million in special charges during the fourth quarter.
Excluding special charges, Chrysler's operating earnings were $1.09 billion.
In the same quarter the previous year, Chrysler posted net income of $1.04 billion, or $1.33 a share.
Chrysler's stock increased by $1.625 to $36.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Chrysler reported full-year 1996 net income of $3.53 billion, or $4.74 per share.
Chrysler's 1996 profit was lower than its 1994 record of $3.71 billion due to $347 million in special charges.
Chrysler earned $6.09 billion on a pretax basis for all of 1996, a new calendar-year record.
Chrysler's U.S. employees received average profit-sharing checks of $7,900 in 1996.

General Motors Corp.'s board of directors approved a $2.5 billion stock buyback programme.
General Motors Corp. raised its dividend by 25 percent.
GM shares decreased by $1.875 to $60.625 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analyst David Healy from Burnham Securities stated that the stock market punishes failure to generate positive surprises.
Some analysts had predicted a dividend increase of up to 50 percent and a stock buyback of up to $5 billion.
GM announced that stock repurchases would occur over the next 12 months.
The stock repurchases would reduce the number of GM's automotive shares by slightly more than 5 percent.
GM raised its quarterly dividend on automotive shares to 50 cents from 40 cents.
GM ended 1996 with a cash balance of $17 billion, up from $10.2 billion at the end of 1995.
GM Chairman Jack Smith stated that the automaker will consider additional stock buybacks in the future.

Comerica Inc. announced it will cut 1,890 jobs, or about 16 percent of its workforce.
The job cuts are part of an effort to reduce costs and increase revenues by $110 million annually by the first half of 1998.
Comerica incurred a $90 million pretax charge against its fourth-quarter earnings due to restructuring actions.
Comerica's fourth-quarter earnings fell to $60.8 million, or 52 cents a share, from $106.5 million, or 92 cents a share, in the previous year.
Comerica had $34 billion in assets at the end of 1996.
The actual number of employees laid off may be less than 1,890 due to attrition, a hiring freeze, and reinvestment actions.
Comerica has about 12,000 employees in Michigan, Texas, California, and Florida.
The job cuts will occur in all four states and will take place between now and mid-1998.
Comerica plans to close about a dozen branch offices.
Comerica earned $417.2 million, or $3.55 a share, for the full year, an increase from $413.4 million, or $3.54 a share, in 1995.

Tomkins Plc reported a 34 percent increase in pretax profits for the six months to November 2, totaling 168.8 million pounds.
The dividend increased from 2.7 pence to 3.06 pence compared to the previous year.
Executive chairman Gregory Hutchings stated that the results indicated another period of outperformance for Tomkins.
Hutchings forecasted that Tomkins shares should continue to outperform the sector.
Hutchings ruled out the possibility of a share buyback this year, citing sufficient acquisition opportunities.
Hutchings indicated that the group was likely to pursue a number of smaller acquisitions, potentially worth up to 200 million pounds.
Tomkins shares were down four at 273-1/2p by 1115 GMT on the day of the report.
Analysts had expected profits of around 160 million pounds.
Hutchings expressed optimism about the second half, noting healthy order books and satisfactory market conditions.
Tomkins' acquisition of Gates Corp for $1.1 billion contributed 259.5 million in sales and 20 million in profit in its first 14 weeks.

Talks between the British and U.S. governments on an open skies pact were postponed for two weeks due to the illness of a senior British negotiator.
The talks were scheduled to begin in Washington on Tuesday with representatives from both governments and major transatlantic carriers.
A spokesman for the British government confirmed that the lead official is in hospital and the meeting has been cancelled.
The European Commission began a series of private hearings in Brussels regarding the proposed British Airways and American Airlines alliance.
The British Airways and American Airlines alliance is conditional on the open skies pact being finalized.
British and U.S. carriers expressed regret over the delay of the Anglo-U.S. talks.
Sources indicated that the current round of talks was not expected to result in a final deal.
Scott Yohe, senior vice-president of government affairs at Delta Air Lines Inc, stated that full agreement was not possible in the current round of talks.
The British government aims to link the open skies talks with the BA/AA alliance, while the U.S. wants to keep them as separate issues.
Britain is awaiting a final verdict from the Office of Fair Trading regarding the BA/AA alliance, particularly concerning the divestment of 168 landing slots at Heathrow airport.

Hanson Plc announced the final stage of its four-way demerger will occur on February 24.
The Energy Group division of Hanson Plc will be spun off as a separate company.
Energy Group is considering acquisitions in Britain and America.
Energy Group has started talks with a U.S. power marketing company.
The demerger is subject to shareholder approval.
Shareholders will receive one Energy share for every 10 existing Hanson shares held.
Hanson shareholders will vote on the proposal at an extraordinary general meeting on February 21.
After the demerger, the remaining Hanson group will consist of building firms.
Energy is expected to rank inside Britain's top 100 blue chips and the Fortune 500 in the U.S.
Derek Bonham is the executive chairman of Energy's new management team.

Sony Corp. will unveil an Internet-based staging area called 'The Station at Sony.com' on Monday.
The Station allows consumers to sample, play, and purchase Sony's television, film, music, and video games.
The Station represents a major push by Sony to enhance its presence on the Web.
The Station offers features comparable to a full-scale online network like America Online Inc.
Sony officials believe The Station could make Sony the top entertainment brand on the Web.
Mitchell Cannold, president of Sony Online, stated that The Station brings together the best of Sony's offerings.
The goal of The Station is to be the primary online entertainment destination for users of all ages.
The Station allows users to sample and buy music and film clips and communicate in chat rooms.
The Station features a 'StationPass' that connects users with other StationPass holders.
The Station offers various games and contests, including interactive entertainment for children and online versions of TV game shows.

Nynex Corp. has until Monday to respond to charges of bad faith regarding an agreement with MCI Communications Corp.
The agreement would have allowed MCI to enter Nynex's local market in New York state.
MCI filed a motion against Nynex asking the state Public Service Commission (PSC) to impose sanctions for not signing the interconnection agreement.
The interconnection agreement would enable MCI to provide local phone access in New York state.
State Attorney General Dennis Vacco filed papers seeking to bar Nynex from offering long-distance service due to discrimination against local-service rivals.
Vacco has criticized the proposed Bell Atlantic Corp. takeover of Nynex on anticompetitive grounds.
Nynex operates 11.1 million local service lines, while competitors have less than 100,000 local service lines according to state regulators.
Nynex spokesman Mark Marchand disagreed with Vacco's assessment of their draft application for long-distance service.
Nynex has signed full interconnection deals with competitive access providers, including MFS Communications, Teleport Communications Group, and WinStar Communications.
Most new entrants into the New York local service market focus on profitable niches in the business services market.

Bay Networks Inc unveiled a set of products and strategies to compete in high-speed networking.
David House is the chairman and chief executive of Bay Networks.
House outlined the company's new 'Adaptive Networking' strategy.
The 'Adaptive Networking' strategy aims to make Internet-based networks easier to upgrade.
House stated that the goal is to create networks that are invisible to the user.
House compared computer networks to electricity and water infrastructures.
Bay Networks announced a new application-specific networking chip capable of carrying up to 1.5 million packets of Internet data per second.
The new Route Switch Processor (RSP) integrates the manageability of routers with the speed of switches.
The RSP chip is designed to address the demand for high-speed Internet transmission and reduce congestion on data networks.
House stated that the RSP chip would allow Bay to reduce switch product prices from $5,000 to $500 per connection over time.

Japanese prosecutors raided Nomura Securities Co Ltd on Tuesday.
The raid was part of a widening investigation into payments linked to racketeers.
Prosecutors and officials from the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) conducted the raid.
The raids signal a potential crackdown on business practices in Japan.
Ninety officials raided ten other locations in conjunction with the headquarters raid.
Deputy chief prosecutor Kunihiro Matsuo stated the investigation focused on a Nomura director's illegal payment of 38 million yen to a company linked to a racketeer.
