The payment was made to avoid disruption of a Nomura annual meeting.
The raids included searches of the homes of the racketeer and involved Nomura director Shimpei Matsuki.
Matsuki and fellow director Nobutaka Fujikura resigned after internal probes revealed violations of Japanese securities law.
Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki stepped down on March 14 in response to the scandal.

Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd and Hokkaido Bank Ltd announced a merger to take place next April.
Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd and Hokkaido Bank Ltd will withdraw from overseas operations by next March.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd announced a restructuring plan that includes halting overseas operations and selling its Tokyo headquarters.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd is the smallest of Japan's three long-term credit banks.
Yushiro Ikuyo, first vice-president of Smith Barney International Inc, criticized the merger agreement between the two Hokkaido banks.
Yushiro Ikuyo stated that the restructuring program of Nippon Credit Bank falls short of solving its bad loan issues.
Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd are among Japan's weakest banks.
Moody's Investors Service assigns its lowest 'E' ratings to Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd.
Moody's stated that no U.S. banks have received an 'E' rating.
Problem loans at Hokkaido Takushoku Bank totalled 936 billion yen, accounting for 13.34 percent of loans outstanding.

Nomura Securities is facing a scandal that has damaged the industry's image.
Analysts and market sources believe Nomura will struggle to regain investor trust.
The California Public Employees' Retirement Fund announced it is suspending business with Nomura.
The suspension follows a scandal involving illicit transactions linked to corporate racketeers.
The California Public Employees' Retirement Fund does not plan to take legal action against Nomura.
Nomura is experiencing its second major scandal in six years.
Nomura is expected to implement a program to prevent future scandals at the urging of the Finance Ministry.
The program is likely to include the establishment of a compliance committee with senior management.
Nomura's senior executives are expected to accept salary cuts in response to the scandal.
Hideo Sakamaki, the president of Nomura, resigned last Friday.

Guan Jiansheng was sentenced to 17 years in prison for embezzlement and accepting bribes.
Guan was the former head of Shanghai International Securities Co (SIS).
Guan was convicted of accepting 294,000 yuan ($35,000) in bribes and misappropriating 2.4 million yuan in public funds between 1992 and 1994.
The sentencing of Guan has sent a message that no one is exempt from legal consequences in the stock markets.
Analysts believe the impact on market prices from Guan's sentencing will be minimal due to the timing of the announcement.
The announcement of Guan's sentencing was made on February 3, just before the Chinese lunar new year market holiday.
Guan's sentencing is seen as a warning to brokerage officials against illegal securities trading.
Beijing's recent crackdown on the stock markets indicates a tougher attitude from securities authorities.
Guan was removed from his position as SIS president after the brokerage was implicated in a state debt futures trading scandal in February 1995.
SIS was later merged with Shanghai Shenyin Securities Co to form China's largest brokerage, Shenyin & Wanguo.

China announced a preferential tax rate of 15 percent for foreign banks doing local yuan business.
Foreign banks are limited to dealing with foreign-funded firms registered in Shanghai.
Foreign bankers expressed surprise at the 15 percent tax rate, which is the same as their foreign currency business tax rate.
The tax rate for Chinese banks doing the same business with the same clients is 33 percent.
Bankers with local Chinese commercial banks stated they were not worried about the decision.
The scope of local currency business for foreign banks is expected to be highly restrictive for years.
The official Xinhua news agency reported that four foreign banks were chosen by the People's Bank of China for local currency deposit and loan business.
The four foreign banks are Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp, Citibank, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank, and the Industrial Bank of Japan.
Foreign banks can only serve foreign-funded enterprises registered in Shanghai and must open RMB accounts in the central bank's Shanghai branch.
All foreign banks in China are currently restricted to doing business in foreign currency.

China has a growing army of young urban professionals mobilized by the reforms of Deng Xiaoping.
These young professionals are pursuing wealth and success in a capitalist environment.
Their tools for success include cellphones, well-cut suits, and accessories.
A university graduate working for a foreign insurance company in Shanghai stated that making money and seeking personal success is a common goal.
Before Deng Xiaoping's reforms, capitalist self-interest was often met with criticism or punishment.
Chinese yuppies are primarily found in Shanghai, which is the center of China's economic boom.
Many young professionals work for foreign companies and earn at least 2,500 yuan ($301) per month.
A computer engineer expressed a desire to earn more money to become rich, noting a higher salary than their parents.
A young manager at a foreign bank in Shanghai stated that he prefers to stay in China for his career rather than going abroad.
Analysts believe that the group of young professionals is crucial for China's future development.

Canada has a youth unemployment rate of 16.6 percent.
The unemployment rate for the general population in Canada is 9.3 percent.
Alexa McDonough is the leader of the New Democratic Party.
McDonough criticized the Liberals for betraying a generation of Canadians.
The number of Canadian young people with jobs has decreased in recent years.
In 1996, the employment rate for Canadians aged 15 to 24 was 51.1 percent.
The employment rate for youth in Canada was 50.5 percent in March.
The difference between the employment rate and the unemployment rate includes young people in school or who have stopped looking for jobs.
Statistics Canada reported that the labor market has become more precarious for young people in the 1990s.
The Liberals have a youth employment strategy that includes summer jobs and reductions in unemployment insurance premiums for small businesses.

The February jobs report for Canada was weak.
Canada's unemployment rate in February was 9.7 percent.
The unemployment rate remained unchanged for three months.
The U.S. jobless rate in February was 5.3 percent.
Canada lost 18,700 jobs in February.
Full-time employment in Canada dropped by 38,000 from January.
Part-time employment in Canada increased by 19,300.
Women lost 44,000 full-time jobs in February.
Youth aged 15 to 24 lost 22,000 jobs in February.
The federal election in Canada may occur as soon as June.

Canada's budget deficit is shrinking.
Politicians are debating whether to cut taxes or raise government spending ahead of the June elections.
Many Canadians are seeking tax relief.
Some Canadians are advocating for increased spending on social services instead of tax cuts.
Toronto social worker criticized the focus on tax cuts, emphasizing the need for job creation.
Canada's unemployment rate is 9.3 percent.
The governing Liberals called for a June vote, 3.5 years into their five-year term.
The Reform and Conservative parties are promoting tax cuts.
Canada has the highest personal income taxes among the seven leading industrial nations.
The New Democratic Party (NDP) opposes tax cuts and wants to raise corporate and capital gains taxes.

The Czech government directed three ministers to oversee an investigation into the failure of Kreditni Banka a.s.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced the investigation at a news conference.
Czech National Bank Governor Josef Tosovsky will join Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda, and Interior Minister Jan Ruml in overseeing the probe.
The government authorized the group of three ministers to inquire into the issue using existing standard mechanisms.
Authorities have been investigating the Kreditni case since the central bank rescinded its licence in August.
Findings from the investigation might lead to changes in Czech legislation.
Kreditni Banka was majority owned by Ceska Pojistovna a.s.
Opposition leader Milos Zeman blamed Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik and his ministry for lax banking supervision.
The central bank welcomed the probe and stated it could help solve other cases related to banking supervision.
Eleven banks have failed since the liberalisation of the sector began in 1992.

The Czech government approved a 20-year contract for natural gas supplies from Norway.
The approval was announced by Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy.
The contract aims to end total dependence on Russian gas.
The deal was approved by Czech and Norwegian ministers last month.
Russia's gas company RAO Gazprom criticized the deal as economically unjustified.
Financial details of the contract have not been disclosed.
Norwegian gas is expected to cost more than Russian supplies.
A consortium of Norwegian firms, including Statoil, Norsk Hydro ASA, and Saga Petroleum A/S, is involved in the deal.
The gas supplies will start at 1.4 million cubic metres a day, increasing to about three billion cubic metres annually.
The total supply over 20 years is expected to be 53 billion cubic metres.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated that improving the regulation of Czech capital markets is on his agenda.
Klaus criticized foreign critics who claim that improvements in capital market regulation are coming too slowly.
Klaus spoke at a banking and finance forum in Prague.
Klaus mentioned that he disagrees with critics who expect Czech capital markets to equal those of Wall Street or the City of London.
Klaus described the critics' attitude as high-brow and doctrinal, stating it does not help the situation.
Klaus acknowledged that finding the right extent of capital market regulation is an imminent task.
Foreign equity analysts and investors criticize Czech markets for a lack of quality company information and clear pricing of shares.
Many analysts compare the Czech capital markets unfavorably to Poland's more stringent regulations.
Klaus stated that the country has too many banks and investment funds, many of which are poorly managed.
The Finance Ministry's capital markets oversight office has increased its activity against illegal asset-stripping by managers of smaller Czech investment funds.

Deng Xiaoping's health is deteriorating.
Jiang Zemin and other leaders have cut short out-of-town trips to return to Beijing.
Jiang Zemin is the Communist Party chief, state president, and head of the army.
Jiang Zemin returned to Beijing from a visit to Ganzhou in Jiangxi province.
Premier Li Peng also returned to Beijing from a tour of Guangdong province.
Sources indicate that Jiang Zemin and Li Peng returned to see Deng Xiaoping.
Deng Xiaoping is 92 years old.
Deng Xiaoping lives in a guarded compound behind the Forbidden City in Beijing.
There are increasing rumors in Beijing about Deng Xiaoping's failing health.
Deng Xiaoping has not been seen in public since the 1994 Chinese Lunar New Year festival.

China warned the Vatican not to interfere in its religious affairs.
China stated that missionary work and appointments of bishops are the prerogative of Beijing.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang made these statements during a news briefing.
Chinese authorities maintain strict control over religious activities due to concerns about local instability.
Shen Guofang commented on a meeting between the Pope and Taiwan Vice-President Lien Chan.
China wants the Vatican to sever ties with Taiwan, which it considers a rebel province.
Lien Chan is the highest-ranking Taiwanese official to visit the Vatican.
China expressed irritation over a statement by Pope John Paul regarding the treatment of Catholics in Hong Kong.
The Pope appointed Monsignor Joseph Zen as coadjudicator bishop of Hong Kong last year.
Chinese Catholics must belong to the state-controlled Chinese Catholic Patriotic Association to worship openly.

Beijing's parliament began the process of upgrading Chongqing to become China's fourth municipality.
Chongqing is a port on the Yangtze river in southwestern Sichuan province.
Approval by the National People's Congress will allow Chongqing to make its own decisions and handle its own finances.
Provincial authorities in Sichuan opposed the decision to upgrade Chongqing.
Chongqing's area will expand to include two outlying cities and a prefecture.
Chongqing's population is expected to increase from 14 million to 30 million.
The decision will facilitate the relocation of about one million people for the Three Gorges dam project.
A municipality in China has the same status as a province and is under the direct authority of the central government.
The other three municipalities in China are Beijing, Shanghai, and Tianjin.
Premier Li Peng stated that upgrading Chongqing would enhance management of the Three Gorges scheme and support economic development in western China.

Exports to North America totaled 22,835 tonnes.
Hong Kong maintained its position as the top regional air cargo hub.
Civil Aviation Department statistics indicate a 15.19 percent increase in total cargo handled in November compared to the same month last year.
Air cargo imports reached 66,257.73 tonnes.
Air cargo exports reached 90,473.44 tonnes.
The statistics for October 1996 include various regions with specific tonnage figures.
Africa unloaded 158.86 tonnes and loaded 354.19 tonnes.
Asia - others unloaded 4,297.56 tonnes and loaded 5,143.29 tonnes.
Australasia unloaded 3,744.77 tonnes and loaded 3,297.38 tonnes.
Total air cargo handled in November was 156,731.17 tonnes.

Hong Kong's Airport Authority will reveal the estimated level of charges for the new airport early in the new year.
A spokesman for the Airport Authority stated it is premature to speculate on the level of charges at Chek Lap Kok.
The Airport Authority is consulting with airlines and the government regarding future charges.
The estimated level of charges will be submitted to the Civil Aviation Department and the Executive Council for approval.
The spokesman could not provide an exact date for when the charges would be published.
The International Air Transport Association (IATA) expressed dismay over rumors of drastically increased charges at Kai Tak airport.
An IATA official estimated that a Boeing 747 would have to pay US$12,000 for each landing at Chek Lap Kok.
The existing most expensive landing fee is US$9,000 at Osaka's Kansai airport.
IATA stated that revenues from the redevelopment of Kai Tak should be used to offset costs at Chek Lap Kok.
Hong Kong's new airport and associated infrastructure projects are scheduled to open in April 1998.

The Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents (HAFFA) will raise some freight charges starting January 1.
HAFFA chairman Sam Chung communicated this information to Reuters.
The majority of rates, including handling and documentation, terminal charges, and attendance fees, will not increase.
HAFFA aims to keep freight costs down to maintain Hong Kong's status as Asia's leading air freight center.
HAFFA raised tariffs this year only on essential, mainly labor-intensive items.
Hong Kong's overall economic situation remains good, but salaries and overheads have increased significantly.
Increases in selected rates are deemed necessary to keep pace with rising costs.
There will be a 6.2 percent increase in air freight flat pack cartage charges to HK$1.40 per kg.
Devanning charges will rise by 3.5 percent to 29.5 cents per kg.
Container field station loading and unloading charges will increase by 6.7 percent to HK$160 per consignment.

Britain's United Utilities may wait two to three years before earning profits from a contract for water and sewerage services in Manila.
Analysts stated it is difficult to assess likely profits until further details of the deal are released.
One unnamed analyst estimated potential profits could be around five million pounds ($8.17 million) a year.
The Manila Water Company (MWC) won a contract for water supply and sewerage in Manila's east zone.
MWC comprises United Utilities, Bechtel Corp of the U.S., and local conglomerate Ayala Corp.
The Philippines government awarded the deal after MWC submitted the lowest water tariff of 2.32 pesos per litre.
The lowest tariff submitted by MWC is 26.3886 percent of the existing fee of 8.78 pesos.
Other groups had bid upwards of 60 percent of the existing tariff in the contract.
MWC posted the lowest bid in the west zone, but that contract was awarded to France's Lyonnaise des Eaux SA and Benpres Holdings Corp.
The concession runs for 25 years and requires MWC to serve 4.6 million of Manila's population of approximately 12 million.

Northern Electric is a British regional electricity company.
CE Electric is a U.S. group that made a bid of 782 million pounds ($1.3 billion) for Northern Electric.
If Northern Electric is taken over by CE Electric, it will be the tenth of the twelve regional electricity companies privatised in 1990 to be acquired.
Northern Electric is the only regional electricity company that has successfully resisted a takeover attempt.
Northern Electric thwarted a bid from Trafalgar House with a 560 million pound defense last year.
The bid from CE Electric is opposed by Northern Electric and closes at 1300 GMT on Friday.
If the bid from CE Electric succeeds, six regional electricity companies will be in or moving into U.S. ownership.
If Northern Electric is acquired, only two independent regional electricity companies will remain: Southern and Yorkshire.
Yorkshire is the only regional electricity company that has never attracted a firm bid.
Southern Electric's takeover by National Power was blocked by the British government in April.

British utility stocks rose on Friday.
Southern Electric announced a share buyback worth up to 156 million pounds ($252.8 million).
Analysts believe Southern's move could provide tax benefits.
Southern's announcement followed a similar plan by Yorkshire Water announced on Thursday.
Southern will offer a share consolidation that gives all holders free B shares.
Southern will buy back these shares at a fixed price of 60 pence per existing ordinary share.
Southern's shares increased by 13 pence to 800-1/2 pence by early afternoon.
Other utility stocks, including South West and Anglian, also rose in value.
Analysts stated that the moves by Southern and Yorkshire Water would decrease reserve capital.
Labour has proposed a windfall levy on excess profits of utilities but has not provided details.

Britain's takeover watchdog sanctioned BZW, the investment banking arm of Barclays Bank, for its conduct during a bid defence for Northern Electric.
The Takeover Panel criticized BZW for failing to disclose all relevant facts during hearings over the deal.
The strongest sanction the panel can impose was given to BZW, and no further action is intended.
Alistair Defriez, director general of the panel, stated that the panel has no power to impose a fine.
BZW expressed that it was pleased the panel found it did not deliberately conceal the performance fee.
There was no suggestion that the performance fee was an inducement for BZW to buy Northern shares.
The case involved a 782 million pound bid for Northern Electric by CE Electric, a unit of CalEnergy Co Inc.
Northern Electric failed in its defence against CE after losing an appeal to reverse an extension of the offer period.
The panel ruled against Northern, and BZW was criticized in the press for losing the bid for its client.
BZW acknowledged it should have considered the performance fee relevant to the panel's deliberations.

Lloyds TSB Group Plc reported a 52 percent rise in pretax profits for 1996.
The pretax profit figure was 2.505 billion stg.
Banking analysts expressed concern for future income growth despite the profit increase.
The profit figure was just above top expectations.
Lloyds Abbey Life and Cheltenham & Gloucester reported higher than expected gains.
John Leonard, a banking analyst at Salomon Brothers, stated that the results were not as impressive as they appeared.
There was a 44 percent drop in bad debt provisions to 327 million stg.
Analysts Leonard and David Poutney did not plan to increase their profit forecasts for 1997.
Poutney advised clients to hold shares but indicated he was now a seller.
Lloyds TSB shares were down 5-1/2p at 496-1/2p at 0900 GMT.

An army of financial market regulators were prepared to investigate NatWest Markets on Sunday.
NatWest Markets is the investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank.
NatWest Markets announced a 50 million pound ($81.4 million) loss in its options trading book on Friday.
The Securities and Futures Authority and the Bank of England will work together to investigate the situation at NatWest Markets.
A Bank of England spokesman stated that supervisors would discuss the events at NatWest.
The Bank of England spokesman could not confirm a formal joint investigation with the Securities and Futures Authority.
The Serious Fraud Office is not currently involved in the investigation of NatWest Markets.
A banking source suggested that the situation may involve a trader attempting to recover from a loss.
A spokeswoman for NatWest Markets confirmed the suspension of a senior options trader named Neil Dodgson.
NatWest Markets is conducting a thorough review of its control systems following the incident.

The Czech cabinet is expected to undergo changes as Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) agreed to discuss this with its coalition partners.
The leadership of ODS has faced criticism and declining approval ratings.
Prime Minister Klaus had previously insisted that immediate personnel changes were unnecessary.
Klaus stated that ODS leadership agreed to open discussions on government reconstruction with coalition partners.
ODS deputy chairman Miroslav Macek indicated that cabinet changes should be finalized by the end of June.
Government spokesman Ivo Strejcek mentioned that coalition leaders might meet on Tuesday but did not specify the agenda.
Klaus's government has faced criticism for economic slowdown and issues related to financial crime, healthcare, and education.
The country is experiencing macroeconomic problems, including a current account deficit exceeding nine percent of GDP and declines in industrial output.
Political instability has contributed to the depreciation of the Czech currency, the crown.
Opinion polls show that support for Klaus's ODS is at a record low, while support for the opposition Social Democrats has increased.

Aung San Suu Kyi received an honorary doctorate in absentia from Prague's Charles University.
The honorary doctorate was awarded as a show of Czech solidarity with Burma's democrats.
Michael Aris, Suu Kyi's husband, accepted the honor on her behalf.
Suu Kyi has been largely confined to her house by military rulers.
The military rulers have stated that Suu Kyi would not be allowed to return to Burma if she left.
The Doctor of Law degree was awarded on the 20th anniversary of Prague's Charter 77 human rights declaration.
Suu Kyi was recognized for her active participation in the fight for democracy, freedom, and human rights.
Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) won a landslide victory in the 1990 election.
The military government rejected the results of the 1990 election, preventing the NLD from taking power.
Czech President Vaclav Havel promised support and solidarity to Burma's democrats.

Pop singer Michael Jackson launched his first tour in two years in Prague on Tuesday.
Promoters erected a huge statue of Michael Jackson on a hill in Prague.
The statue of Jackson is located where a monument to Soviet boss Josef Stalin once stood.
Jackson's three-month 'HIStory' tour through Europe, Africa, and Asia begins on Saturday.
A concert on Prague's Letna Plain is expected to draw 130,000 attendees.
Jackson arrived in Prague four days early to do sightseeing.
Jackson emerged from his jet at Prague airport's VIP terminal in a gold lame and red outfit.
Several hundred fans greeted Jackson at the airport, and he hugged some who presented gifts.
Jackson traveled to his hotel in a Rolls Royce, escorted by police and a convoy of luxury cars.
Thousands of fans gathered at the hotel on the river Vltava to see Jackson.

Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc is interested in forming a cancer drug partnership in the U.S.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc aims to become a major player in oncology within the next five years.
RPR President Tim Rothwell stated the company aims to be in the top five, ideally the top three, in cancer sales.
RPR ranked 15th in oncology sales in 1995.
Tim Rothwell predicted that the drug Taxotere would achieve peak sales of at least $500 million over the next five years.
Sales of Taxotere are forecast to double in 1997 from around $90 million last year.
Tim Rothwell stated that the brain cancer treatment Gliadel should be approved in the U.S. in 1998.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc is interested in alliances in the U.S. market.
Tim Rothwell noted that only 24 percent of RPR's sales are in the United States.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc's growth strategy includes enhancing its position in key therapeutic areas such as thrombosis, asthma/allergy, and anti-infectives.

Courtaulds Textiles Plc reported a first-half loss after one-off charges.
The company plans to spend 30 to 35 million pounds on restructuring, mostly in the second half of 1996.
Courtaulds made a pre-tax loss of 8.5 million pounds compared to a profit of 6.4 million in the first half of the previous year.
Excluding exceptional charges, pre-tax profit fell to 600,000 pounds from 10.3 million pounds.
Colin Dyer, the new chief executive, aims to quickly reorganize the company, including further disposals and creating four product-led divisions.
The decline in profits was mainly in the fabrics division due to weak demand in the U.S. and continental Europe for lace and reorganisation costs in Britain.
The company plans to shed jobs in Britain and western Europe and increase production in low wage economies, particularly in Asia.
Courtaulds has sold around half of its hit list of a dozen problem businesses, with three disposals announced last week.
The disposals will account for 160 million pounds of turnover, with announced disposals nearing half of that amount.
Courtaulds took a 9.1 million pound restructuring charge in the six months to June and expects to generate cost-savings of 10 to 13 million pounds a year by 1998.

Britain's biggest chemical company ICI reported a 37 percent drop in profits before tax and exceptional charges in 1996.
ICI's profits before tax and exceptional charges fell to 603 million pounds in 1996 from 951 million pounds the previous year.
The dividend payout from ICI increased by 6.7 percent to 32.0 pence.
Both profit and dividend figures were at the lower end of market expectations.
ICI attributed the profit drop to price falls in the chlorine, titanium dioxide, and polyester markets, higher oil prices, and a stronger pound.
The paints business at ICI saw operating profits increase by 60 percent to 171 million pounds.
Shares in ICI fluctuated, reaching a peak of 780 pence before falling to 754.5 pence.
Traders expressed concerns over the strength of sterling and disappointment with ICI's full-year figures.
ICI plans to reposition itself as a producer of 'light' chemicals and move away from the industrial market.
Finance director Alan Spall stated that ICI would be 'a very different company' by the turn of the century.

President Ernesto Samper called on prisoners in northern Colombia to lay down their weapons and release their hostages.
The riot in Valledupar jail left four guards dead.
Negotiations to end the prison siege cannot begin until a group of 10 convicts surrender.
A crack anti-kidnap force is in place near the jail.
The local police chief did not rule out a rescue operation for the hostages.
Samper stated that the national government will not seek a solution until the hostages are released and the inmates lay down their arms.
The prisoners released a 14-year-old girl and a prison administrator but were still holding 13 hostages.
The inmates took control of the jail after overpowering 18 guards and confiscating their weapons.
Four prison guards were confirmed dead, and the death toll could be higher according to a national Prisons' Institute official.
The majority of prisoners demanded an end to overcrowding and better conditions.

Convicts led a riot in a jail in northern Colombia.
At least five guards died during the riot.
The regional human rights ombudsman reported the incident.
The inmates demanded to be flown out of the jail by helicopter.
Some inmates were convicted leftist guerrillas and others were former police officers.
The inmates requested 10 parachutes.
A jailed leader of the M-19 rebel group demanded political exile in Cuba.
About 550 prisoners seized control of the jail compound in Valledupar, Cesar province.
The prisoners took 16 hostages, including the jail's deputy director and a 14-year-old girl.
The Valledupar prison is designed to house 200 convicts but currently holds more than 550.

Horacio Serpa resigned from his position as Colombia's Interior Minister on Tuesday.
Serpa resigned to prepare for a presidential bid.
President Ernesto Samper accepted Serpa's resignation and wished him success.
Serpa's resignation letter indicated a close political and personal friendship with Samper.
The resignation comes before the May 31 deadline for candidates to step down from public office.
Serpa is a member of the ruling Liberal Party.
Serpa has been the Interior Minister since August 1994.
Serpa defended Samper against accusations of financing his 1994 election campaign with drug money.
Samper was cleared of wrongdoing in a congressional inquiry last year.
Serpa is under investigation for allegedly accepting illicit donations.

Shares in British mobile telephone operator Orange Plc rose on Monday after the company reported it had more than doubled its total subscriber base to over 785,000 customers during 1996.
Orange was priced at 205p when it was floated 10 months ago.
Orange's shares added 4p to reach 192p after the company announced it had added 125,000 customers in the last three months of 1996.
The last quarter of 1996 was reported as Orange's best ever quarter.
One 2 One, a joint venture between Cable & Wireless Plc and a unit of US West Media Group, reported it gained 85,000 customers during the Christmas 1996 period.
One 2 One's total subscriber base reached 545,000, representing an eight percent market share.
Analyst James Ross of broker ABN AMRO Hoare Govett stated that the final quarter had been quite good for mobile phone companies and the trend was positive after four disappointing quarters.
Vodafone Group reported a 20 percent annual increase in subscriber numbers to approximately 2.8 million at the end of December.
Cellnet, which is 60-percent owned by British Telecommunications, ended the year with 2.68 million UK customers, up from 2.3 million at the end of 1995.
Analysts indicated that Orange shares had good upside potential despite their volatility in the market.

Shares in Yorkshire-Tyne Tees, a British commercial television broadcaster, fell on Tuesday.
Yorkshire-Tyne Tees reported an 80 percent rise in interim profit.
Pre-tax profit for the six months to June 30 increased to 13.3 million pounds from 7.4 million pounds a year ago.
The interim dividend was raised to 6.8 pence from 3.7 pence.
The company stated that the profit improvement occurred despite disappointing advertising sales performance.
Yorkshire-Tyne Tees is based in Leeds, England.
The company experienced a smaller than expected increase in total ITV advertising revenues and a slight decline in its share of that income.
Higher programme sales and cost controls compensated for the sales shortfall.
Yorkshire shares fell by 30p to 1210 by 1440 GMT.
Granada holds a 24 percent stake in Yorkshire and has been expected to make a takeover bid.

Shares in British media group EMAP Plc fell about three percent on Monday.
EMAP announced that managing director David Arculus is leaving for United News & Media.
David Arculus is 50 years old and joined EMAP in 1972.
Arculus will become chief operating officer at United News on April 7.
His responsibilities at United will include consumer publishing, television, trade magazines, and exhibitions.
Clive Hollick, chief executive of United, stated that Arculus has a proven record in building media businesses.
United News completed its management team after a three billion pound merger with MAI last year.
United shares increased by 17p to 704.5p following the announcement.
EMAP shares decreased by 25p to 787.5p after the announcement.
EMAP has been expanding its operations beyond its original regional newspaper base.

Patterson Dental Co expects to report fiscal third-quarter earnings in the range of $0.41 to $0.42 per share.
The First Call consensus for fiscal third-quarter earnings is $0.37 per share.
Patterson Dental Co's chief executive is Peter Frechette.
Patterson expects net income for the quarter to be between $8.9 and $9.1 million.
Patterson had net income of $0.32 per share in the year-ago quarter.
Patterson acquired the Colwell division from Deluxe Corp in October.
Patterson paid nearly $60 million in cash for the Colwell division.
Patterson expects earnings of $1.06 to $1.07 per share for the nine-month period ended January 25.
Patterson had net income of $0.92 per share in the third quarter of the preceding fiscal year.
Patterson's Canadian sales account for less than 10 percent of total revenues.

Dean Buntrock is the chairman and acting chief executive of WMX Technologies Inc.
Nell Minow is a principal at Lens Inc, a major stockholder of WMX.
Minow stated that Buntrock should remain in his position long enough to find a new CEO before stepping down.
Minow expressed that a successor would not want the job if Buntrock remains too involved.
Buntrock founded WMX in Oak Brook, Illinois, and served as chief executive from 1968 until June 1996.
Phillip Rooney replaced Buntrock as chief executive in June 1996.
Rooney resigned on Tuesday after an investment group controlled by George Soros demanded his ouster.
WMX appointed John Sanford as its new chief financial officer earlier this month under shareholder pressure.
Minow expressed dissatisfaction with Sanford and suggested that he should be reassigned or removed.
WMX shares were down 3/4 to 34 following the announcement of the sale of its 19-percent stake in ServiceMaster LP for $626 million.

United Wisconsin Services Inc expects its medical-loss ratio to decline to levels not seen in years if there are no new healthcare reform initiatives from Washington.
Thomas Hefty is the chief executive of United Wisconsin.
Hefty stated that the medical-loss ratio could fall into the seventies.
United Wisconsin's medical-loss ratio was 81.9 percent in June, down from 88.3 percent a year earlier.
The medical-loss ratio represents the share of premium revenues spent on covering HMO members' healthcare costs.
Premium revenues remaining after covering member costs are a significant source of profits for HMOs.
Hefty believes the HMO industry is poised for better performance in 1997 and 1998.
Hefty noted that the biggest uncertainty in the market is the reaction to the election.
When the Clinton administration proposed healthcare reform in 1994, medical cost inflation decreased and HMO profits increased.
Hefty mentioned that enrollment at United Wisconsin is growing despite some loss in the Milwaukee HMO due to price increases.

Australian Telecommunications Minister Richard Alston stated that the Asia-Pacific region should lower telephone charges to stimulate usage and promote economic growth.
Alston emphasized the importance of ensuring that users benefit from advancements in telecommunications.
Alston mentioned that providing access to people who have lacked it is essential by extending network reach and lowering prices.
Alston claimed that real cost reductions in telecommunications are possible but less likely under monopoly arrangements.
Alston cited Optus Vision's example of offering local telephone calls at 20 cents per call, which is 25 percent cheaper than state-owned Telstra's charges.
Australia's conservative government plans to sell one-third of Telstra in the 1997/98 financial year.
The APEC ministers meeting aims to coordinate a regional telecommunications policy known as Asia-Pacific Information Infrastructure (APII).
Alston stated that the development of the APII would encourage business activity and growth in the region.
Alston asserted that lower prices for telecommunications services would stimulate economic activity.
APEC includes Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, and the United States.

Qantas Airways Ltd is Australia's flag carrier.
Qantas is expected to post a flat result for the six months ended December 31, 1996.
A higher Australian dollar and higher fuel charges are keeping Qantas profits under pressure.
Analysts expect Qantas to report a pre-abnormal net profit of between A$116 million and A$154 million.
Most estimates for Qantas' pre-abnormal net profit are around A$148 million.
Qantas reported a pre-abnormal net profit of A$148.1 million in the first half of 1995/96.
The local Australian dollar hit a six-year high of US$0.8215 in December 1996.
The Australian dollar was around US$0.7650 on Tuesday afternoon prior to the report.
Qantas increased its cost cutting target by A$100 million to A$430 million for 1996/97.
Qantas cut A$468 million out of costs in the 1995/96 year.

A U.S. telecommunications official stated that business demands for cheaper telephone services will drive liberalisation in the APEC telecommunications markets.
Larry Irving is a telecommunications adviser to U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Larry Irving claimed that business leaders are the biggest advocates for changes in telecommunications law.
Irving stated that industrialists are demanding better services and lower prices in telecommunications.
Irving is the head administrator of the National Telecommunication Informational Agency (NTIA).
Irving mentioned that countries cannot afford to avoid liberalising their telecom markets to maintain a competitive edge.
Irving noted that countries that liberalise telecommunications markets would create more telecom-related jobs than those with state-owned monopolies.
Irving cited Chile, Mexico, and New Zealand as APEC countries with open telecommunications markets.
Irving reported that 400,000 jobs were created in the U.S. telecommunications and information technology industry last year.
Gregorio San Martin Ricci, Chile's Undersecretary of Communications, stated that more jobs have been created in Chile's telecommunications industry since deregulation in the late 1980s.

Psion Plc is a British hand-held computer company.
Psion Plc's shares fell by 19.2 percent on Monday, closing at 407.5p.
The decline in shares was attributed to a slowdown in sales and concerns over the strength of sterling.
Some analysts predict that Psion's stock could drop to 350p in the next six months.
Psion launched its first handheld Organiser 13 years ago.
The new Series 5 product is described as the first fully-functional, pen-orientated, portable computer that fits into a hand.
Chairman David Potter acknowledged that the group's performance would be affected until the new 32-bit computers are established.
Analyst Keith Woolcock warned that Psion could earn less profit this year than last year.
The strength of sterling has negatively impacted Psion's gross margins by about three percentage points.
Woolcock noted that the new machines will not be sold in volumes before autumn, presenting a significant problem for Psion.

Cable and Wireless Plc is Britain's second biggest telecommunications company.
Cable and Wireless Plc reported record annual results on Wednesday.
Cable and Wireless Plc is currently biding its time before choosing any global partners.
Cable and Wireless Plc confirmed it is still in talks with telecoms alliances such as Global One.
Pre-tax profits after exceptional items for Cable and Wireless Plc jumped 12 percent to 1.42 billion pounds in the year ended March 31.
Stripping out one-off items, profits were only two to four percent higher than last year, according to analysts.
Cable and Wireless Plc raised its total dividend 11 percent to 11.1 pence for the year to March 31.
Group turnover for Cable and Wireless Plc rose 13 percent to just over 7.0 billion pounds.
The shares of Cable and Wireless Plc fell 20p to 492.5p despite underlying profits being in line with expectations.
Cable and Wireless Plc merged its British telephone subsidiary Mercury with three cable television companies to create Cable and Wireless Communications.

Analysts stated that a strategic deal between Spain's Telefonica and British Telecommunications Plc's Concert partnership would change the European telecoms alliance landscape.
Such an alliance would challenge AT&T Corp, which is a rival of BT.
Paul Staples, head of telecoms research at Schroders, believes that the alliance will cause AT&T to reconsider its position in Europe.
Juan Villalonga, Telefonica's chairman, does not expect a future partner to take a stake in Telefonica's South American subsidiary TISA.
Villalonga did not rule out a share swap between Telefonica and a foreign operator.
Speculation exists that Telefonica de Espana may exit AT&T's Unisource alliance with Dutch, Swedish, and Swiss telecoms groups.
Villalonga indicated that Telefonica expects to announce a deal in four to six weeks.
Industry sources suggest that Telefonica may partner with BT and MCI to form an alliance across Europe and the Americas.
BT announced that Austria's PTA selected Concert as a strategic partner but declined to comment on rumors.
Telefonica's TISA operates in South American markets including Peru, Argentina, Chile, Venezuela, Colombia, and Puerto Rico.

The number of personal computers shipped worldwide rose by 15.4 percent in the first quarter.
Compaq Computer Corp. and International Business Machines Corp. led the strong sales.
Dataquest reported this information on a Sunday.
The first quarter is traditionally a slow time for PC makers.
The industry is projected to grow by 19 percent for 1997.
Bill Schaub is the director of computer research at Dataquest.
The industry shipped 18.7 million machines in the first three months of the year.
Compaq shipped 1.87 million units, an 18 percent increase from 1.59 million units last year.
Dell Computer Corp. had the biggest shipment increase, rising 62 percent to 945,000 units.
Apple Computer Inc. shipped only 602,000 units and did not rank in the top five PC makers.

Citrix Systems Inc. stock increased by 69 percent on Monday.
Microsoft Corp. agreed to license Citrix's software technology for upcoming versions of Microsoft Windows NT.
Citrix will receive an initial fee of $75 million from Microsoft.
Citrix may earn up to $100 million in royalties from Microsoft products using its technology.
Citrix shares rose by $13.375 to $32.625 on Nasdaq, with a trading volume of 12.9 million shares.
Citrix develops software that allows older PCs or terminals to run programs designed for Microsoft's Windows.
The agreement alleviated concerns about Citrix's future after a previous stock decline in February.
Microsoft agreed to incorporate Citrix's multi-user technology into Windows NT.
The agreement facilitates Citrix's ability to sell additional products to Windows NT customers.
Microsoft also agreed to license technology from Prologue Software SA.

Sony Corp. cut the U.S. price of its PlayStation video game machine by 25 percent to $149.
The price cut is expected to boost the entire video game industry.
Sony cut the price of all new software titles for the PlayStation to $49.
The PlayStation is now $50 cheaper than the Nintendo 64.
Analysts suggest Sony's move could force Nintendo to cut its prices.
Mike Wallace, an analyst at UBS Securities, stated that hardware price cuts are beneficial for the industry.
Wallace noted that a larger installed base of video game machines is important for the industry.
Sony's price cut could lead to a significant increase in PlayStation units in use in the U.S. by Christmas.
Sony officials stated they still make money on each PlayStation despite the price cuts.
Nintendo officials are analyzing Sony's price cut and currently have a backlog of orders for the Nintendo 64.

Mitel Corp is a telecommunications firm.
Mitel Corp's growth in the computer telephony integration business is lagging expectations.
Chief Executive John Millard made this statement to Reuters.
Mitel's computer telephony integration unit did not achieve forecast results.
Mitel warned investors that it expected fourth-quarter earnings to fall to C$0.10 a share.
This is a decrease from C$0.14 a share in the same period the previous year.
Mitel took a C$13 million restructuring charge due to increased operating costs and price cuts by rivals.
Millard stated that explosive growth in the CTI area might take another year.
Mitel plans to release several CTI and PBX products later this year.
Mitel's shares closed at 7.45 in Toronto and were unchanged at 5-3/8 in New York.

The Toronto Stock Exchange (TSE) transitioned to decimal trading from fractions in 2023.
A study by doctoral student Jeff Bacidore at Indiana University's Graduate School of Business indicated that trading volume did not increase after the transition.
The study was published in a July discussion paper and was obtained by Reuters.
The TSE is Canada's largest stock exchange and ranks third in North America.
All of Canada's five equities markets, except for Winnipeg, adopted trading increments of five cents on April 15.
TSE officials aimed to attract business from U.S. exchanges with the move to decimal trading.
Bacidore's study found that trading volume remained statistically the same in the nine weeks following the change compared to the previous nine weeks.
Susan Crocker, the TSE's senior vice-president of equities and derivative markets, criticized the study for its short time frame.
Fred Ketchen, a proponent of decimalization, also stated that it was too early to assess the impact of the change.
Bacidore's study found that decimalization reduced earnings for traders due to narrower spreads.

Toronto stocks closed one percent higher on Tuesday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 64.22 points to close at 5743.55.
On Monday, the index was down more than 10 percent from its lifetime high of 6348 points set on March 11.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 6587.16 after surging 135.26 points.
Toronto's gains were limited by a two percent drop in its gold group due to weak gold prices.
Montreal-based analyst Bill Ram stated that the market was following the U.S. side, which was strong on consumer price index numbers.
The U.S. Labor Department reported a 0.1 percent rise in the consumer price index for March.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had predicted a 0.2 percent gain in the consumer price index.
Turnover on the Toronto Stock Exchange was moderate with a volume of 77.1 million shares worth C$1.35 billion.
Among Toronto's 14 sub-indices, 11 rose, led by banks, conglomerates, and utilities.

China's soybean importing season is nearing its end.
Far East traders are focusing on 1997 due to depleting high oil stocks and a domestic crop decline.
China's soybean imports in 1996 reached 600,000 tonnes as of Thursday.
Import expectations for 1996 total 800,000 tonnes.
A Hong Kong trader reported a potential Panamax deal at $320 a tonne FOB for U.S. and South American beans to Tianjin.
Joint venture feed mills are the buyers for the beans.
Domestic buyers are limited due to taxes and charges making imports uneconomical.
Domestic soybean prices are around 3,000 yuan ($361) a tonne.
The Dalian Commodities Exchange September contract is at 3,730 yuan ($449).
Traders believe current world prices are $10-$15 too high for Chinese buyers.

Old and young couples danced in Shanghai's People's Square on Thursday.
Many dancers were unaware of the death of Deng Xiaoping.
A 70-year-old man quoted an ancient Chinese saying about death.
The government had prepared for the transition of power for a long time.
People gather in the square daily to dance and exercise.
There was general apathy in Shanghai regarding Deng Xiaoping's death.
Deng Xiaoping's death was first reported on Shanghai radio at 6 a.m. on Thursday.
Shanghai television stations repeatedly broadcast news of Deng's death.
Shanghai radio stations aired dirges and historical accounts of Deng's contributions.
Many people in Shanghai were confident in the government's ability to manage the transition.

China's sugar factories face financial difficulties due to low prices and high debts.
Chinese producers could earn $15-20 a tonne by exporting white sugar to Asia.
Recent Indonesian purchases of Thai sugar have tightened regional supply.
Asian buyers may need to seek sugar from alternative sources.
Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and the Philippines could show interest in importing sugar from China.
The China Sugar Association stated that exports are unlikely to happen soon.
International sugar prices are currently not favorable for Chinese producers.
The current premium on white sugar over raw sugar is $70 a tonne.
Far Eastern white sugar has an additional $20 premium due to cheaper regional freight rates.
Guangxi's sugar reserves currently hold between 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes.

Russia will buy Iraqi oil as Baghdad prepares to export more crude.
Yuri Agababov is the deputy general director of Zarubezhneft.
Zarubezhneft is coordinating Russian contracts for Iraqi oil under the United Nations' oil-for-food deal.
The United Nations renewed a $2 billion, 180-day programme for Iraq to export oil.
The programme aims to raise cash for humanitarian needs and reparations for Gulf War victims.
Russian companies purchased nearly 28.54 billion barrels of Iraqi oil under the first 180-day programme.
This amount represented 23.4 percent of the total 121.6 million barrels Iraq was allowed to export.
Agababov plans to lead a delegation of Russian companies to Baghdad to negotiate contracts with SOMO.
Russia has a historical trading relationship with Iraq and is interested in Iraq's financial stability.
LUKoil holds a 52.5 percent stake in a $4 billion production-sharing project in Iraq's Western Qurnah oil field.

Russian oil refiners are considering upgrades to produce lighter products for export markets.
Hydrocrackers and fluid catalytic crackers are expensive plants that produce lighter materials like gasoline, naphtha, diesel, and jet fuel.
Heavy fuel oil constitutes around 40 percent of Russia's oil output.
Most Russian refiners utilize less sophisticated processing technologies.
Only three percent of Russian refining capacity comes from cracking processes.
Boston Consulting Group estimates that by 2000, Russia could add 254,000 barrels per day of catalytic cracking capacity and 131,000 barrels per day of hydrocracking capacity.
These increases could raise Russia's total product output to 5.9 million barrels per day by 2000 from 5.2 million barrels per day.
Boston Consulting Group Vice-President Charbel Ackermann stated that increasing light products capacity would not reduce heavy products capacity.
Russia's 28 major refineries have submitted 28 formal requests for loans to international lenders for upgrades, but funding has not been secured.
Kirishi refinery plans to install a $750 million hydrocracker with Chevron's assistance.

Russia has removed secrecy from the Sukhoi Log gold field and invited investors.
The Sukhoi Log gold field is located in southeastern Siberia's Irkutsk region.
Sukhoi Log has gold reserves of about 35 million troy ounces.
Lenzoloto produced about five tonnes of gold last year.
Russia's total gold production in 1996 was 124 tonnes.
Lenzoloto plans to tender a 49 percent stake in one of its units that holds the right to develop Sukhoi Log.
Star Mining Corporation NL is the preferred bidder for the stake in Lenzoloto.
Sukhoi Log's peak output could reach 60 tonnes a year in the future.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin ordered transparency regarding Sukhoi Log's gold reserves.
A feasibility study of Sukhoi Log has been completed but Lenzoloto has not seen the document.

Thomson SA is a French state-owned electronics group.
Thomson SA did not comment on a report from Le Monde regarding its management's preference for a market float for Thomson-CSF.
The French government plans to privatize Thomson SA by selling its 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF and later selling Thomson Multimedia.
The planned sale of Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe was suspended by the government after objections from the Privatisation Commission.
Le Monde reported that during a supervisory board meeting, Thomson SA management indicated a preference for a market sale over a private placement.
An unnamed supervisory board member stated that a market float would allow for a quicker sale.
A Thomson spokesman stated that discussions during board meetings are part of the company's private life.
Chairman Marcel Roulet's official position is that the Finance Ministry should decide on the sale process.
Roulet sent a letter to the government advocating for a market sale, referred to as an Offre Publique de Vente (OPV).
The sale of Thomson-CSF is scheduled for early 1997, while the sale of Thomson Multimedia may take until 1998.

Logica Plc acquired Axime Ingenierie SA for 161 million francs.
Logica Plc plans to continue its expansion program after the acquisition.
Duncan Craig is a board member of Logica and spoke to Reuters about the acquisition.
Logica is interested in expanding in Germany, Italy, and Scandinavia.
Axime Ingenierie has 1,000 staff and 360 million francs in sales.
Axime Ingenierie was a loss-making and non-core part of Axime SA.
Axime SA is merging with Sligos.
The French unit will be renamed Logica SA, and Christian Chevallier will remain as chief executive.
Logica expects a small positive effect on earnings for the financial year ending June 30.
Last year, Logica reported a pre-tax profit of 24.7 million sterling on sales of 284.8 million sterling.

France Telecom announced it was cutting its call tariffs to boost telephone use ahead of its flotation in 1997.
The full liberalisation of the market is scheduled for 1998.
Chairman Michel Bon stated that the first sale of shares in France Telecom could occur from the second half of April.
The timing of the sale and details of the capital to be sold depend on market conditions and Finance Minister Jean Arthuis' decisions.
The government will not sell more than 49.9 percent of France Telecom.
The government plans to sell about 20 percent of France Telecom in the spring.
France Telecom will reduce a number of call rates starting March 4, with further cuts in October 1997 and 1998.
Monthly standing charges will increase despite the call rate reductions.
Bon stated that if traffic rises by six percent in 1997, the cuts will benefit France Telecom's business model.
France Telecom will cut national call rates by 17.5 percent on March 4 and by a further 21 percent in October 1997.

Shares in Crown Ltd, Australia's most successful casino, fell on Friday.
Crown shares closed at a 16-month low.
Crown shares have decreased by 27 percent since mid-January.
Concerns about rising costs and delays at the A$1.55 billion casino complex have affected investor confidence.
Crown plans to move into its new riverside home in Melbourne in April.
Crown uses private jets to bring its best customers into the country.
Crown plans to buy a private golf course for about A$40 million for exclusive use by its customers.
Crown is negotiating to buy management rights to its casino from Hudson Conway Ltd for an estimated A$300 million.
Crown has raised over A$500 million in equity and debt since August.
Crown's profit outlook was downgraded in an independent accountant's report last month.

Coles Myer Ltd is experiencing challenges in its apparel business.
Chief executive Dennis Eck expressed caution about the profit outlook for the company's apparel divisions.
Coles reported a 6.5 percent increase in sales revenue to A$4.559 billion for the quarter ending April 27.
Total sales for Coles for the year to date reached A$14.5 billion, reflecting a 5.7 percent increase.
Coles' supermarkets division recorded a 12.3 percent increase in sales revenue for the quarter compared to the same quarter last year.
The Kmart chain of stores showed improvement with a 5.8 percent rise in sales revenue.
Sales at Coles' women's wear business, Katies, and its Target and Myer Grace Bros stores declined.
Eck suggested that cold and wet weather could positively impact fashion sales.
A Sydney-based retail analyst noted that weather conditions have contributed to weak apparel sales.
Eck stated that apparel represents no more than 16 percent of Coles' overall business and defended the company's position in the apparel market.

Mayne Nickless Ltd aims to sell its stake in Optus Communications Pty Ltd by July.
Mayne Nickless Ltd has a 25 percent stake in Optus Communications Pty Ltd, estimated to be worth about A$1 billion.
Bob Dalziel is the managing director of Mayne Nickless Ltd.
Mayne Nickless Ltd reported a half-year net profit characterized as reasonable.
Net earnings after abnormal items for Mayne Nickless Ltd fell 13.8 percent to A$43.14 million for the six months to end December.
Bob Dalziel stated that the result hid a rise in underlying profitability.
Bob Dalziel forecasted a strong full-year result for Mayne Nickless Ltd.
Mayne Nickless Ltd incurred nearly A$20 million in interest payments over the half year for its Optus investment.
Bob Dalziel assured ratings agencies Standard and Poor's and Moody's Investors Service that Mayne aimed to sell its stake by July.
Bob Dalziel ruled out a float of Optus by July due to ongoing litigation.

Microsoft Corp. reported a third-quarter profit of $1.04 billion, an 85 percent increase.
The profit exceeded analysts' expectations.
The increase in profit was attributed to the strength in the Windows business and the Office 97 upgrade.
Microsoft's net income was 79 cents a share, compared to 44 cents a share in the same quarter last year.
Revenues reached a record $3.21 billion, a 45 percent increase from $2.21 billion in the previous year.
Analysts had forecast earnings of 64 cents a share and revenues of about $2.9 billion.
Microsoft's Chief Financial Officer Mike Brown expects growth to slow over the next year.
Analyst Scott McAdams expressed surprise at Microsoft's performance and predicted a rise in stock price.
Microsoft's stock fell to $98.125 in Nasdaq trading but rose to $102.75 in after-hours trading.
Revenues from the Office 97 bundle contributed to application and content revenues of $1.53 billion, a 24 percent increase.

Nike Inc. is the world's largest maker of athletic footwear.
Nike reported a 24 percent increase in first-quarter profits.
The profit increase reflects strong global demand for Nike's shoes and apparel.
Nike announced a two-for-one stock split, its second in two years.
For the three months ended Aug. 31, Nike earned $226.1 million, or $1.53 a share.
This profit is an increase from $182.1 million or $1.25 a share a year ago.
Nike's revenues increased by 34 percent to $2.28 billion from $1.70 billion last year.
The earnings were slightly better than the $1.51 a share expected by industry analysts.
Nike took orders for $3.5 billion in footwear and apparel through January, a 66 percent increase over the previous year.
U.S. sales of Nike footwear surged 27 percent to over $1 billion in the quarter.

Microsoft Corp.'s Expedia Internet travel service sold more than $1 million in travel tickets this week.
This week was the best sales week for Expedia since its launch four months ago.
Josh Herst is the lead product manager for Expedia.
Sales increased when American Airlines launched a fare war after President Clinton blocked a strike by its pilots.
Microsoft is investing heavily in the travel sector as a form of electronic commerce.
Forrester Research reported that travel generated $126 million in retail sales over the Internet in 1996.
Computer software and hardware generated $140 million in retail sales over the Internet in 1996.
Forrester estimates that the travel industry will generate $1.6 billion in annual sales over the Internet by 2000.
Analysts give Expedia high marks and expect Microsoft to remain a major player in the Internet travel market.
Microsoft has about 100 people working on Expedia, including journalists building a database of destination information.

Port arrivals of Ivorian cocoa for 1996/97 totaled around 1.02-03 million tonnes by May 12.
This is a decrease from 1.11 million tonnes by the same date in the 1995/96 year.
Weekly arrivals at Abidjan and San Pedro dropped to 5,000 tonnes in the week to May 12.
This is a decline from about 50,000 tonnes during the final week of the main crop (October-April).
There are concerns that the size of the May-September mid-crop will be disappointing.
An Abidjan-based crop analyst stated that the mid-crop has been weak so far but remains optimistic.
The main crop for Ivory Coast totaled around 1.04 million tonnes by April 27.
This is compared to about 1.06 million tonnes in 1995/96, which had a larger mid-crop of just under 200,000 tonnes.
Early forecasts for the 1996/97 crop were cautious, as arrivals exceeded the official full-year forecast of up to 950,000 tonnes.
Local crop analysts do not expect the 1996/97 crop to set a new record but believe it will be close if mid-crop forecasts of 150-180,000 tonnes are accurate.

The 1996/97 cocoa harvest in central Ivory Coast could be earlier and more prolonged if good rains continue.
Antoine El-Hayek, a private buyer based in Daloa, stated that October and November will be the strongest months for the harvest.
El-Hayek mentioned that a total harvest of 950,000 tonnes would be surprising and that the harvest depends on good rain before January.
He also noted that mould is a danger due to humidity and lack of sun, making drying difficult.
Other buyers expect the main crop quality in 1996/97 to be better than in 1995/96 because farmers can spend more time treating the smaller harvest.
Forecasters predict a main crop of 850,000 to 900,000 tonnes for 1996/97, compared to one million tonnes in 1995/96.
Pod sizes observed between Daloa and Gagnoa suggest an early start to the season and a bigger harvest in early 1997 than further south.
There was little flowering observed, indicating weaker March harvests.
Good quantities of early main-crop cocoa were seen drying on roadsides between Daloa and Gagnoa.
Makkram Haddad, a private buyer, stated that buyers were not stocking 1995/96 mid-crop cocoa and that little was being stored by farmers.

Wilt disease affecting Zaire's coffee trees emerged three years ago.
A revolt in eastern Zaire has hindered efforts to study and control wilt disease.
Christian Feruzi is the Commercial Director of the Zairean Coffee Office (OZACAF).
Production and export data since the war began in October 1996 is limited and contradictory.
No coffee from rebel-controlled eastern regions was included in the export data.
Approximately 10,000 tonnes of coffee were exported from western regions from October to December 1996.
IACO and Zaire are conducting a study to assess the recoverability of coffee production.
Rebels under Laurent Kabila control much of eastern Zaire and are preparing to attack Kisangani.
Coffee exports accounted for 15 percent of Zaire's export revenue before the war.
Most arabica coffee is grown around Goma and in the eastern hills of North Kivu.

Philip Morris Cos. Inc. Chief Executive Geoffrey Bible stated that the company is open to reasonable measures to resolve anti-tobacco lawsuits in the United States.
Bible declined to comment on negotiations between cigarette companies and anti-smoking forces regarding a resolution of lawsuits and regulations.
Bible expressed that Philip Morris is willing to work with government officials on new regulations for tobacco sales.
The tobacco industry is currently involved in a court battle against new restrictions on sales to minors imposed by the Food and Drug Administration.
Bible indicated that Philip Morris supports restrictions on young people purchasing cigarettes.
Philip Morris launched a program two years ago to limit cigarette access for individuals under 21.
Bible stated that Philip Morris does not want kids to smoke.
Anti-smoking groups claim that the tobacco industry targets advertising to encourage youth smoking.
Philip Morris intends to vigorously fight against hundreds of individual, state, and class-action lawsuits.
Negotiators from the tobacco industry and anti-smoking activists recently met to discuss settling litigation against the industry.

A Florida judge ordered Liggett Group to deliver internal industry documents for a lawsuit against U.S. tobacco companies.
Courts in Texas and Illinois have issued similar orders regarding Liggett Group documents.
Liggett Group is the fifth largest cigarette maker and is owned by Brooke Group.
Liggett Group struck a deal with 22 states for $30 billion related to Medicaid costs for treating sick smokers.
The Florida judge is Harold Cohen of Palm Beach County Circuit Court.
Cohen ordered a review of about 20 Liggett documents within 10 days that may affect public safety.
Florida law allows trade-secret protections to be overridden if public safety is at stake.
Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth urged the judge to review the Liggett documents.
Butterworth stated that the documents would be made public if deemed relevant to public health.
Cohen scheduled a jury trial for the Florida lawsuit to start on August 4.

Sterling Software Inc will close its $165 million purchase of Texas Instruments Inc software unit on June 14.
The acquisition will help Sterling's financials almost immediately, according to the company's chief executive, Sterling Williams.
Sterling Software will spend approximately three to four minutes integrating Texas Instruments' 1,300 staff and 62 facilities worldwide.
The acquisition will enhance both profits and revenues for Sterling Software almost immediately.
Sterling Software's cash holdings remain largely intact after the Texas Instruments deal and will be used for more acquisitions.
Sterling Software will have about $600 million in cash after the Texas Instruments acquisition.
Sterling Software was founded in 1981 and has completed more than two dozen acquisitions.
The Texas Instruments acquisition will add $250 million in annual revenues to Sterling Software.
The acquisition will more than double the portion of Sterling Software revenues that come from applications software operations.
Sterling Software had fiscal 1996 revenues of about $440 million.

Bao Zunxin is a Chinese dissident who spent years in jail after the 1989 pro-democracy demonstrations in Beijing.
Bao Zunxin sent an open letter to the National People's Congress calling for tougher anti-corruption laws.
Bao Zunxin stated that existing laws are inadequate to cope with endemic graft.
Bao Zunxin emphasized the need for more openness and fuller disclosure of officials' private assets.
In his letter, Bao Zunxin claimed that without an end to corruption, there will not be peace in China.
Bao Zunxin noted that corruption has infiltrated every level of government.
Bao Zunxin mentioned that requiring only officials above the county level to declare their property is insufficient.
Petitions to parliament are risky for dissidents in China and have often been met with silence or detention.
Bao Zunxin was taken by public security officials for a week-long 'tour' to Qingdao after granting an interview to a French reporter.
Many Chinese believe that corruption has increased as economic reforms weaken social controls and create profit-making opportunities.

Hainan Airlines plans to buy 10 airliners from Boeing Corp in the next two years.
The fleet expansion will be funded by bonds, loans, and China's first public airline share issue.
Hainan Airlines has agreed on a basic contract with Boeing for four 737-400s and three 737-800s.
Chen Feng is the chairman and president of Hainan Airlines.
Hainan Airlines is waiting for approval from China's aviation authorities to buy three Boeing 767 aircraft.
The cost of each Boeing 767 is estimated to be around $60-70 million.
Delivery of the Boeing 737s and 767s is expected to begin in 1998.
Hainan Airlines plans to bring into operation seven new Metro 23 light aircraft from Fairchild Aircraft Inc in 1998.
Hainan Airlines currently operates nine Boeing 737s and a few turboprops and executive jets.
The airline plans to issue about 80 million foreign currency B shares to be listed on the Shanghai bourse.

China criticized Taiwan's plan to ship nuclear waste to North Korea.
China claims the plan is an attempt by Taiwan to divide the country and harm China's relations with North Korea.
China expressed concern about the environmental impact of the contract for shipping nuclear waste.
The contract involves Taiwan shipping up to 200,000 barrels of low-level nuclear waste to North Korea.
China's Foreign Ministry spokesman is Shen Guofang.
Shen Guofang stated that China's government and people oppose Taiwan's actions.
China views Taiwan's nuclear waste plan as an attack on its goal of reunification.
China considers Taiwan a renegade province.
China has diplomatic relations with both North Korea and South Korea, neither of which recognizes Taiwan.
Taiwan asserts that its nuclear waste shipment complies with international regulations and will be securely packed.

Nextwave Telecommunications Inc is planning to set its delayed initial public offering in the next two weeks.
Nextwave has spent $4.7 billion on wireless licenses for the third largest network in the U.S.
Nextwave intends to file an amended S1 to the SEC in the next couple of weeks.
Nextwave planned to go public last summer but faced delays and parted ways with lead manager Merrill Lynch in the fall.
Nextwave must amend the S1 document it sent to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Smith Barney and Lehman Brothers are set to be co-lead managers of the $200 million equity offering.
CIBC Wood Gundy is leading the $300 million debt offering for Nextwave.
Nextwave's total outlay may exceed $8 billion when including the $3-3.5 billion cost to build the network.
The build-out is financed by $1.4 billion in unconditional vendor financing and $2.1 billion in conditional vendor financing.
Nextwave has pre-sold 35 billion network minutes of use, equivalent to the entire U.S. cellular industry's 1994 traffic.

The merger of MCI Communications Corp and British Telecommunications Plc is valued at $20 billion.
The merger follows a two-year courtship between the two companies.
The planned merged entity will be named Concert.
Concert was originally conceived in July 1994 to provide services for multinational corporations.
Insiders believe the integration of networks, billing, support, and customer service will be a critical test for the merger.
The initial partnership, now called Concert Communication Services, faced challenges due to internal conflicts.
Daniel Briere, a consultant at TeleChoice Inc, noted that early conflicts were destructive.
A computer and software for pre-paid Concert calling cards in Britain were delayed due to design disputes between BT and MCI.
A videophone product developed by BT for MCI failed, resulting in significant financial losses.
BT controls 90 percent of the British market, while MCI has less than 20 percent of the U.S. long-distance market.

Cable & Wireless Plc (C&W) and NYNEX Corp are merging with Bell Atlantic Corp.
C&W and NYNEX have one alliance and a second is in progress.
A full merger between C&W and NYNEX could occur by late 1997.
An unidentified investment banker stated that the U.K. cable alliance increases the likelihood of a merger.
C&W announced it would merge its U.K. Mercury unit with three cable TV and telephone operators, including NYNEX CableComms Group.
NYNEX owns 67 percent of NYNEX CableComms Group.
Sources indicate that the merger process is slow and may face hurdles.
NYNEX's merger with Bell Atlantic will not be completed until the first quarter of 1997.
Concerns about C&W's assets in Hong Kong may delay decisions regarding the merger.
C&W Chief Executive Richard Brown stated that talks with NYNEX have progressed beyond the U.K. cable deal.

Breakfast cereal price wars are affecting major cereal makers negatively.
Kellogg Co. is the largest cereal maker in the United States.
Kellogg Co. is expected to report flat earnings for the latest quarter.
Ralcorp Holdings Inc. is likely to report lower earnings.
Price cuts and promotions in the cereal business have hurt results at Kellogg and Ralcorp.
Kellogg has lost sales to competitors like General Mills Inc.
General Mills Inc. reported a 7.5 percent increase in earnings in its latest quarter.
General Mills' increase in market share was partly due to promotions.
Kellogg's market share decreased from 35 percent to about 33 percent.
Kellogg purchased Lender's Bagels from Kraft Foods Inc. for $455 million.

Tony the Tiger is associated with Kellogg Co.
Kellogg Co. will launch chocolate-flavored Frosted Flakes in the United States.
Kellogg Co. plans to launch Frosted Flakes in China, India, and Thailand starting this month.
Frosted Flakes is the top-selling cereal in the United States.
Frosted Flakes is already sold in Europe, Latin America, Australia, and South Africa.
Kellogg Co. accounts for about one-third of the $9 billion U.S. cereal market.
Cocoa Frosted Flakes are fat-free and cholesterol-free.
Frosted Flakes ranks second worldwide behind Kellogg's Corn Flakes.
Kellogg's international cereal sales grew by about 4 percent in 1996.
Kellogg's domestic volume was down about 4 percent in 1996.

Mark Whitacre, a former executive of Archer Daniels Midland Co., filed a lawsuit against FBI Agent Brian Shepard.
The lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court of the Central District of Illinois.
Whitacre alleges that Shepard violated his constitutional rights, inflicted emotional distress, and committed assault and battery.
Whitacre's lawsuit targets Shepard in his official capacity as an FBI agent, effectively suing the FBI.
Chicago attorney James Shapiro stated that the lawsuit is akin to suing the entire FBI.
The FBI press office declined to comment on Whitacre's lawsuit due to policy regarding pending litigation.
A Justice Department spokesman was not available for comment at the time of the report.
Whitacre acted as a government informant from 1992 to 1995 during an antitrust investigation of Archer Daniels Midland.
Whitacre was fired from his position as president of ADM's BioProducts Division in August 1995.
Archer Daniels Midland has accused Whitacre of stealing approximately $9 million.

The red Communist flag of China is flying in Hong Kong.
Thousands of red flags are present in Hong Kong.
The handover of Hong Kong to Beijing took place at midnight on June 30, 1997.
Red Chinese flags are displayed in the Kam Tin district of the New Territories more than five months before the handover.
Flags featuring Hong Kong's floral emblem, the purple bauhinia, have been raised in Kam Tin.
Tang Wing-yuen organized a tribute to celebrate Hong Kong's departure from British rule.
Kam Tin's main street is decorated with bunting and small Chinese flags.
Flags are displayed on various buildings in Kam Tin, including offices and homes.
A large banner at the Kam Tin rural council building welcomes Hong Kong's reversion to China.
Most buildings in Hong Kong still display Britain's Union Jack, while the bauhinia flag is also appearing.

China has made an overture to include critics in the selection of Hong Kong's future leadership.
Analysts believe this move may divide the democratic camp in Hong Kong.
Foreign Minister Qian Qichen stated that the 400-member body will choose the chief executive and legislators after July 1, 1997.
Qian's remark suggested that the selection body could include individuals with differing views on democracy.
The remark was perceived as an olive branch towards Hong Kong's Democratic Party, which has been excluded from transition arrangements.
The gesture contrasts with China's previous harsh criticism of the Democratic Party.
Political analyst Nihal Jayawickrama suggested that Beijing may be trying to unite the democrats after failing to divide them.
Democratic Party leader Martin Lee rejected the idea of joining the Selection Committee, viewing it as recognition of an illegitimate body.
The Democratic Party argues that China's plan to appoint a new provisional legislature lacks legal basis.
Some analysts believe China aims to enhance the legitimacy of the Selection Committee by including democrats.

The leader of Hong Kong's democrats plans to challenge Beijing's proposed laws against civil rights in court.
Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen has called for a rewrite of textbooks in Hong Kong schools to align with China's principles.
Hong Kong was ceded to Britain by China during the 19th century opium wars.
Hong Kong is set to revert to Chinese sovereignty on July 1.
Pro-China politician Chung Sze-yuen stated that the China-appointed shadow legislature could pass laws before midnight on June 30.
The shadow legislature will replace Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council after the handover.
Some pro-China politicians have stated that the shadow legislature should adopt important laws before the sovereignty transfer.
Martin Lee, chairman of Hong Kong's Democratic Party, stated that his party would take legal action if the provisional legislature enacted laws.
Britain, the pro-democracy camp, and major law organizations oppose the provisional legislature, claiming it undermines democracy.
The Economic Journal warned that the provisional legislature could set a dangerous precedent by making laws without legal authority.

Gerard Mestrallet is the head of Cie de Suez.
Mestrallet is considering a merger with Lyonnaise des Eaux.
The market anticipates that Mestrallet will lead the merged group.
Brokers believe that Suez and Lyonnaise will merge to create a utilities group valued at 79 billion francs.
The merger is expected to revitalize both companies.
The leadership of the merged group is seen as crucial for determining which company will dominate.
Suez has a significant cash reserve and 50 billion francs in capital but lacks industrial identity.
Jerome Monod, chairman of Lyonnaise, is preparing for retirement.
Mestrallet has been the head of Suez for two years after a boardroom battle.
Mestrallet previously worked at Suez's Belgian unit, Societe Generale de Belgique.

Boeing Co. may expand into aerospace services.
Boeing is looking for foreign partners.
Phil Condit is the Chairman and Chief Executive of Boeing.
Boeing is awaiting regulatory approval for a merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp.
