The merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp. would create a firm with annual sales of $48 billion and 200,000 employees.
Boeing's core activities include civil aircraft, defense, and space.
Boeing's new business will build on its knowledge of aerospace customers.
Boeing has a joint venture with FlightSafety International for airline training.
Boeing expects the McDonnell merger to generate around $1 billion in savings.
Phil Condit stated that there is little overlap between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas businesses.

Eurotunnel reported a reduction in first-half losses.
Eurotunnel's losses after interest totaled 3.04 billion francs ($597 million).
This loss represents an improvement of 618 million francs ($121 million) from the same period in 1995.
Since March, Eurotunnel has broken even at the operating level before financial charges.
French co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle stated that Eurotunnel is economically viable but needs to reduce its debt burden.
Eurotunnel is seeking to refinance 72 billion francs ($14 billion) of debt and unpaid interest owed to its 225-member bank syndicate.
Eurotunnel has been in negotiations with banks since it froze payments on junior-ranked loans a year ago.
A mandate for two mediators appointed by a Paris court to assist in negotiations expires at the end of September.
Ponsolle expressed hope for an agreement by the end of September, while British co-chairman Alistair Morton allowed eight weeks for negotiations.
Morton indicated that he would resign at the end of October after the debt talks are completed.

CVS Corp and Revco D.S. Inc have merged to create a significant presence in the U.S. Northeast and Southeast drugstore markets.
The merger is expected to mark the end of major mergers among the largest players in the drugstore industry in the near term.
Numerous small publicly held and private drugstore chains are still operational and may seek mergers or acquisitions to compete with larger companies.
Marty Murrer, managing director at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, stated that several companies in the sector are seeking strategic advice.
Arbor Drug Inc, Genovese Drug Stores Inc, and Duane Reade Inc are potential candidates for consolidation in the drugstore sector.
The merger between Revco and CVS is seen as a significant development following a challenging year for Revco.
A previous merger agreement between Revco and Rite Aid worth $1.8 billion was terminated due to antitrust concerns.
Revco made a hostile bid for Big B Inc, which was initially rejected but later resulted in a friendly $380 million deal.
The merger has led to a positive response from shareholders, increasing Revco's share price to 40-1/2.
The $2.8 billion deal values Revco at approximately 40 per share and is expected to enhance CVS's market position and expansion efforts.

Norfolk Southern Corp. launched an effort to oppose a $9.1 billion merger between Conrail Inc. and CSX Corp.
Norfolk Southern proposed to buy a 9.9 percent stake in Conrail for $115 per share.
Norfolk Southern's takeover bid has been rejected several times.
Norfolk Southern made its offer directly to Conrail shareholders.
Many Conrail shareholders are unhappy with the proposed Conrail-CSX transaction.
Conrail shareholders are scheduled to vote on a key provision related to the merger on Friday in Philadelphia.
Conrail has rejected Norfolk Southern's $10.3 billion cash offer.
Conrail believes the $9.1 billion transaction with CSX provides more strategic benefits.
CSX currently owns 19.9 percent of Conrail shares and plans to buy another 20 percent for $110 per share if a Pennsylvania law is waived.
Norfolk Southern stated that its 9.9 percent offer would not require any action by Conrail's board.

The chairman of ITT Corp, Rand Araskog, rejected an offer to meet with Hilton Hotels Corp's chairman, Stephen Bollenbach.
Hilton Hotels Corp launched a $6.5 billion hostile takeover of ITT Corp.
Araskog stated it would be inappropriate for the executives to meet or for Bollenbach to address the ITT board.
Araskog's letter to Bollenbach was described as brief and formal.
An ITT spokesman declined to comment on the situation.
A Hilton spokesman could not be reached for immediate comment.
Bollenbach's request to ITT was disclosed in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on January 31.
Hilton's offer is valued at $55 per share and includes acquiring about $4 billion of ITT debt.
Wall Street experts expect ITT to reject Hilton's offer, considering it too low.
Most experts estimate ITT is worth at least $65 per share.

Plans for a new type of radio service that could be heard coast-to-coast are facing potential issues.
Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt stated that any company should be allowed to bid for the two available licenses.
Hundt opposed an existing FCC plan to limit the auction of the licenses to four applicants.
The FCC is divided on the issue of the auction.
Hundt expressed that the auction should be open to anyone interested in Digital Audio Radio Service (DARS).
An open auction could generate significant revenue for the government.
MCI Communications Corp. paid $683 million for the last remaining satellite slot for television broadcasts.
The four DARS applicants are CD Radio Inc., American Mobile Radio Corp., Digital Broadcast Satellite Corp., and Primosphere.
CD Radio Chairman David Margolese expressed displeasure with Hundt's remarks but advised caution in interpretation.
An American Mobile Radio spokeswoman indicated a preference for limiting applicants to the current four and for those four to decide on license allocation.

A year after the ValuJet Inc. crash, the top airline regulator suggested it would be impractical to force air carriers to install fire-safety equipment in passenger cargo holds in less than three years.
The Federal Aviation Administration plans to propose the installation of smoke detectors and fire suppressors in all passenger cargo holds over three years.
House lawmakers accused the FAA of dragging its feet on the installation issue despite years of warnings from safety regulators.
Lawmakers raised the possibility of a speedier timetable for the installation of fire-safety equipment.
Barry Valentine, acting head of the FAA, stated that grounding the fleet could expedite the installation process.
Representative John Fox expressed that the public would prefer safer flights, even if it meant slower service.
Airline executives announced plans to install smoke detectors and fire-suppression systems in their aircraft after initially resisting the requirement.
FAA officials faced criticism from lawmakers and the chairman of the National Transportation Safety Board for not implementing new safety rules more aggressively after the ValuJet crash.
The FAA announced plans to issue fire-safety equipment rules that will affect about 3,000 aircraft six months ago, but has not yet unveiled a formal proposal.
ValuJet flight 592 crashed into the Florida Everglades last May, killing 110 people due to a fire in the cargo hold caused by oxygen generators, which have since been banned from transport on commercial airliners.

The government's latest airwaves auction is expected to generate less money than the $1.8 billion Congress anticipated.
As of late Friday, the auction had raised $12.1 million.
Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt stated that the auction will not meet budget expectations.
The auction began on Tuesday.
Bidding among 23 companies, including BellSouth Corp., Comcast Corp., and a Bell Atlantic Corp./Nynex Corp. joint venture, appears to be winding down.
Analysts believe that spectrum sales will not significantly help eliminate the budget deficit.
Analyst David Roddy of Deloitte & Touche Consulting Group commented that the sale of the spectrum was too much and too fast.
Analyst Elliott Hamilton from Strategis Group stated that there is not an endless supply of valuable spectrum.
The WCS auction is the FCC's 14th airwaves sale.
The Clinton administration proposed to raise $36.1 billion through spectrum sales in its 1998 budget.

Four publicly traded startup companies focused on helping users navigate the World Wide Web are competing in the market.
The companies involved are Yahoo! Inc., Excite Inc., Infoseek, and Lycos Inc.
These companies aim to establish themselves as leading brands for Internet navigation.
John McCarthy, director of research for interactive technology strategies at Forrester Research, stated that the stakes are high for establishing navigation hubs on the Internet.
McCarthy noted that users require more sophisticated search capabilities than the initial scattershot approach.
Successful companies in the next 12 to 18 months may attract attention and acquisition offers from larger industry players.
McCarthy mentioned that Oracle, Microsoft, and Netscape will likely not remain passive in this competitive landscape.
All four companies are working on improving personal services and expanding their reach both domestically and internationally.
Yahoo! was founded two years ago by two Stanford University graduate students.
Yahoo! plans to launch country services for Britain, Germany, and France in the near future.

Novell Inc. named Eric Schmidt as its chairman and chief executive officer on Tuesday.
Eric Schmidt was a key architect of Sun Microsystems Inc.'s Internet and Java language strategy.
Schmidt will join Novell on April 7.
Schmidt is tasked with revitalizing Novell, which competes with Microsoft Corp.
Novell has sold software applications WordPerfect and Quattro Pro in the last 18 months.
These applications were acquired by former Novell CEO Ray Noorda in an unsuccessful attempt to compete with Microsoft.
Analysts believe Schmidt has the energy and intellect to refine Novell's strategy and attract developers.
Schmidt stated that leading Novell fulfills a lifelong dream of running a company in the industry.
Schmidt has been a prominent advocate for Internet development and the promotion of the Java language.
Novell has the No. 1 market share in network operating systems despite competition from Microsoft.

@Home Network CEO Tom Jermoluk stated that the $48 million raised allows the company to be selective about the timing of an initial public offering (IPO).
Jermoluk mentioned that the company is not seeking other forms of capital after announcing a private placement in preferred stock.
The private placement accounts for about 4.5 percent of the company and values @Home at $1.07 billion.
This valuation is nearly 20 times the company's initial value in 1995.
Jermoluk indicated that @Home was designed to eventually go public but did not provide a specific schedule for the IPO.
He noted that the raised cash provides flexibility for the company regarding market conditions.
Despite its high valuation, @Home is heavily dependent on its partners to build out cable networks.
Jermoluk stated that hundreds of millions of dollars are required to upgrade the partners' systems to accommodate @Home.
He estimated that a conservative investment requirement would be $50 per home for the 45 million homes in North America.
@Home has begun residential deployment in more than half a dozen cities with its primary investment partners.

U.S. interest rates are currently a focus for investors in Asia.
Guinness Flight Asia Ltd reported an increasing divergence in the region's markets.
Investors are becoming more discerning in their market choices.
Market performance across Asia is now highly divergent.
Funds are flowing to markets with strong investment stories and avoiding weak ones.
Fund managers have a greater responsibility to get asset allocations correct.
High expectations for earnings growth are often linked to high GDP growth rates.
Short-term results can be misleading due to high bank lending growth and overheating property markets.
Long-term growth opportunities exist in Asia despite some cyclical slowdowns and structural problems.
Guinness Flight emphasized the importance of stock picking and management quality for successful investments.

The funds management industry in Hong Kong is experiencing significant changes.
Christopher Day, formerly of Thornton Management (Asia) Ltd, stated that the industry is in turmoil.
Day left Thornton Management after its amalgamation with other fund units of Dresdner Bank.
At least four senior dismissals have occurred in the industry recently due to consolidation.
Finance houses are competing for position in the growing market for retail mutual and pension funds.
Day mentioned that many companies aspire to become leaders in fund management.
Morgan Stanley Group Inc merged with Dean Witter, Discover & Co for US$10.7 billion last February.
Banks are interested in funds management to shift income from loans to investment management income.
There is a cultural clash between banking and funds management that could affect compliance.
Some fund managers are uncomfortable in large fund houses and are moving towards niche operations.

Anson Chan is one of Asia's most powerful women.
Anson Chan is the top civil servant in Hong Kong.
Chan is preparing for political upheaval in Hong Kong.
Tung Chee-hwa is the future leader of Hong Kong.
Anson Chan is 57 years old.
Chan is described as tough and charming.
Tung Chee-hwa is a conservative without a political track record.
Chris Patten is the departing colonial governor of Hong Kong.
Civil servants run the Hong Kong government as part of the colonial legacy.
Anson Chan will become Tung Chee-hwa's second-in-command.

Three bombs exploded on buses in Urumqi, Xinjiang, China.
At least four people were killed in the explosions.
The blasts injured at least 60 people.
The explosions occurred on the same day as Deng Xiaoping's final rites in Beijing.
One bomb exploded on Tuanjie Street.
A fourth bomb was found before it detonated.
State media in Urumqi did not report the incidents.
No one has claimed responsibility for the blasts.
This was the first known violence in Xinjiang since riots in Yining in February.
Chinese leaders have expressed concern over the threat from Islamic fundamentalism.

China urged calm while negotiating with South Korea regarding a North Korean asylum-seeker.
The asylum-seeker is stranded in Seoul's mission in Beijing.
Pyongyang officials expressed a desire to lure the asylum-seeker back home.
China warned of a potential standoff due to its involvement in the conflict between South Korea and North Korea.
Hwang Jang-yop, a leading North Korean ideologue, is seeking to leave North Korea.
Hwang has spent three days with an aide in Seoul's consular office.
A Chinese bullet-proof car was waiting outside the consular office.
Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen met with South Korean counterpart Yoo Chong-ha in Singapore.
The talks between Qian and Yoo did not resolve the deadlock over Hwang's situation.
Hwang Jang-yop's defection is seen by Seoul as a significant intelligence opportunity.

The South Korean flag flew at half-mast at Seoul's mission in Beijing on Friday.
A senior Pyongyang defector, Hwang Jang-yop, is currently at the Seoul mission in Beijing.
Talks regarding Hwang's fate were stalled due to the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
Chinese and South Korean officials met on Thursday to discuss Hwang's situation.
The meeting was focused on maintaining a dialogue channel rather than finding a swift solution for Hwang.
Hwang has been at the mission for 10 days.
An embassy official stated that a resolution to the situation was unlikely due to Deng's death.
China declared six days of mourning for Deng.
Seoul officials decided to temporarily refrain from discussing Hwang's defection with Chinese officials.
Hwang's defection has created diplomatic challenges for China between North Korea and South Korea.

British composite insurer Commercial Union Plc reported a rise in first quarter profits.
The increase in profits was attributed to a decrease in U.S. weather claims.
Chief executive John Carter described the company's prospects as excellent.
Commercial Union's shares decreased by 10-1/2 pence to 739 pence after the profit figures were released.
Pre-tax operating profits rose to 102 million pounds, up from 83 million pounds the previous year.
Excluding the impact of sterling, profits increased by 46 percent.
Profits and new business sales in the worldwide life business rose by 25 percent.
Net assets per ordinary share increased by 23 pence to 568 pence.
Commercial Union noted that the UK general insurance rating environment remained competitive.
Weather claims in the U.S. fell by 23 million pounds to 6 million pounds due to milder winter conditions.

Equitas was created to manage Lloyd's of London's pre-1993 losses.
Equitas received a qualified opinion on its first set of accounts.
Equitas faces difficulties in unwinding 10.4 billion pounds of liabilities.
David Newbigging is the chairman of Equitas.
Equitas described its initial five months of operation as satisfactory.
Auditors Coopers & Lybrand cited significant uncertainties regarding claims provisions.
Claims experience may differ from estimated liability to a material degree.
Necessary adjustments could potentially eliminate shareholders' funds of 588 million pounds.
Jane Barker is the finance director of Equitas.
Equitas was formed as part of Lloyd's 'Reconstruction and Renewal' plan.

A vehicle to reinsure orphan syndicates could free thousands of Lloyd's of London Names currently trapped in the insurance market.
Plans for this vehicle were published on Tuesday.
John Rew is the co-founder of publisher and market analyst Chatset.
John Rew has invited Names to fund a feasibility study on a Name-owned company to re-insure orphan syndicates.
John Rew is seeking to raise 600,000 pounds ($972,000) for the study.
One third of the raised funds will be devoted to the feasibility study.
If the study is successful, a prospectus will be issued to set up the syndicate.
There are around 13,000 Names trapped on more than 50 syndicates for 1993 that are still open due to uncertainty surrounding liabilities.
The 1993 year would normally have closed at the end of 1995.
Lloyd's requires that reinsurance be backed by another syndicate to close a syndicate.

Britain and China are set to discuss Beijing's request to deploy more troops in Hong Kong before the territory reverts to Chinese rule on June 30.
Top officials from Britain and China on the Joint Liaison Group (JLG) expressed confidence that the matter would soon be resolved.
Beijing's request for more People's Liberation Army (PLA) troops in Hong Kong emerged last week and became controversial.
British officials stated that London would not agree to China's request as the British garrison remains responsible until the handover.
A British representative on the JLG indicated that both sides would soon discuss the issue.
Zhao Jihua, China's representative on the JLG, stated that Beijing believes it is necessary to deploy more troops in Hong Kong before the handover.
China has requested a few hours before the midnight handover ceremony to deploy its main force.
Beijing has sent an advance party of 200 soldiers to prepare garrison, supply, and communication facilities.
Britain insisted that the advance party of soldiers be unarmed and wear uniforms only in barracks.
Many Hong Kong residents are concerned about the arrival of the PLA due to memories of the Tiananmen Square crackdown in 1989.

Sing Tao Holdings Ltd is facing a probe by the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) at its Hongkong Standard Newspapers Ltd unit.
Media analysts predict a drop in advertising revenues at Sing Tao's English-language papers.
Ben Kwong is the research director at Dharmala Securities.
Hongkong Standard Newspapers is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sing Tao Holdings Ltd.
Hongkong Standard Newspapers publishes the English-language Hongkong Standard and Sunday Standard newspapers.
Advertisers may withhold or hesitate to place ads until they receive clarification on circulation figures from the company.
The ICAC raided the Hongkong Standard offices as part of an investigation into fraudulent inflation of circulation figures.
The ICAC arrested four current employees and two former staff members during the investigation.
The ICAC investigation revealed a scheme involving the deliberate excess printing of over 10,000 extra copies of newspapers each day.
Trading in Sing Tao shares resumed after a one-day suspension, closing HK$0.075 lower at HK$2.90.

Deng Pufang is the eldest son of the late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping.
Deng Pufang expressed that his father would have regretted not witnessing the handover of Hong Kong to Beijing.
Deng Xiaoping engineered Hong Kong's return to China under the 'one country two systems' policy.
Deng Pufang visited Hong Kong to promote a medical action plan for preventing and treating blindness.
Deng Xiaoping died on February 19 at the age of 92.
Deng Xiaoping served as China's paramount leader for almost two decades.
Deng Pufang was injured in a fall during the Cultural Revolution.
Deng Pufang stated that his family had not yet requested permission from Beijing to attend the handover.
Deng Pufang expressed gratitude on behalf of his family for the condolences received from Hong Kong residents after his father's death.
Britain ruled Hong Kong for 156 years before agreeing to return it to China in the Joint Declaration of 1984.

America Online Inc. was hit with two lawsuits filed by New York law firms.
The lawsuits are class actions on behalf of clients and AOL members.
The lawsuits were filed in New York state court.
These lawsuits follow a class-action lawsuit filed in Los Angeles.
The Los Angeles lawsuit was filed on behalf of five subscribers.
The Los Angeles lawsuit seeks damages for fraudulent and malicious representation.
Two state attorney generals are in discussions with America Online regarding consumer complaints.
New York state Attorney General Dennis Vacco and Wisconsin state Attorney General Jim Doyle are involved in the discussions.
AOL switched its members to unlimited access for $19.95 a month.
Many subscribers are unable to log onto the system during peak hours.

The stock of International Business Machines Corp. fell on Thursday.
The decline was influenced by fears regarding IBM's first-quarter earnings.
A report highlighted recent cuts in analysts' earnings estimates for IBM.
The overall stock market experienced its fourth sharp sell-off in five days.
Investors were concerned that a strong March employment report could lead to an interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve.
IBM's stock price fell to $128.875 before closing at $131.375, down $2.375.
IBM was the third most-active stock on the New York Stock Exchange with a trading volume of 4.6 million shares.
The decline in IBM's shares began after a Wall Street Journal article was published in London.
The article suggested that analysts might continue to cut IBM's earnings estimates due to a strong dollar and a product transition.
IBM's first-quarter earnings report is scheduled for April 23.

IBM shares fell on Friday after negative comments from three Wall Street firms.
The firms stated that a stronger dollar and a product transition will hurt IBM's earnings.
IBM's stock fell $4.25 to $132.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
More than 5.3 million shares of IBM were traded on that day.
Jay Stevens, an analyst at Dean Witter, stated that people are realizing it will be a bleak quarter for IBM.
Stevens continued to recommend accumulating IBM stock despite the negative outlook.
Analysts identified currency fluctuations and expected weakness in mainframe sales as factors hurting IBM's earnings prospects.
Morgan Stanley cut its earnings estimates for IBM, predicting better earnings toward the end of the year.
Morgan Stanley reduced its earnings per share estimate for IBM to $2.80 from $2.97 for the second quarter.
IBM reported profits of $5.4 billion on revenues of $75.95 billion for the full year of 1996.

Tate & Lyle Plc issued a profits warning on Thursday.
The strength of sterling on foreign exchange markets reduced profits by 7.1 million pounds in the first quarter.
Results for the half year to March 1997 are expected to be below those for the corresponding period but above those achieved in the second half of the 1996 financial year.
The company made pretax profits of 168.2 million pounds in the six months to March 30, 1996.
Full year profits for Tate & Lyle were 276.3 million pounds, down 11.2 percent on the year.
If current exchange rates prevail, full-year results would be marginally lower than the 1996 year.
Tate shares gained 10 pence to 435 after remarks about the performance of its North American unit Staley were less negative than expected.
The currency impact was due to the translation of foreign currencies and the EU Common Agricultural Policy currency mechanism.
The revaluation of the green pound reduced profits at Tate & Lyle Sugars by 1.6 million pounds in the first quarter.
Excluding the currency impact, profit before tax for the quarter was below the corresponding period last year.

Cadbury-Schweppes reported healthy first-half results on Wednesday.
Cadbury-Schweppes is positive about its expected full-year performance.
Chief executive David Wellings stated that the group is trading in line with plans.
Cadbury-Schweppes aims to be one of the top three world confectionery firms by the end of the decade.
For the half year to June 15, the company reported a 12 percent rise in pretax profits to 231 million pounds.
Sales increased by 13.3 percent to 2.293 billion pounds for the same period.
Chairman Dominic Cadbury stated that the outlook for the year is positive with further growth expected.
Analysts' forecasts for pretax profits ranged from 218 million to 232 million pounds after restructuring costs.
The group's confectionery business posted a three percent profits rise to 105 million pounds.
Cadbury's factories in Russia and China began operations in the first half of the year.

Whitbread Plc has reported a sound business performance in the last three months.
Peter Jarvis is the chief executive of Whitbread Plc.
The performance of core businesses in December, January, and February has been sound according to Jarvis.
Whitbread will report its full year results ending February 28, 1997 on May 7.
Whitbread Inns experienced like-for-like sales growth in food and drink of between four and five percent.
Overall sales for Whitbread Inns have been well into double digits.
In mid-January, Whitbread reported an eight percent increase in sales for the five-week period from December 1, 1996 compared to the previous year.
Whitbread's beer company had a strong Christmas performance in take-home beer.
Whitbread's market share in take-home beer is at its highest ever.
Whitbread plans to open another 50 Pelican restaurants by the end of the 1997 financial year.

American Axle & Manufacturing Inc. reached a tentative contract with the United Auto Workers before a strike deadline.
The agreement was reached minutes before the 7 a.m. strike deadline on Monday morning.
Details of the agreement are withheld pending ratification by about 7,200 UAW members at five plants.
The five plants are located in Detroit, Three Rivers, Mich., Buffalo, N.Y., and Tonawanda, N.Y.
UAW President Stephen Yokich and Vice President Richard Shoemaker described the pact as an excellent new agreement.
Company officials did not respond to telephone calls regarding the contract.
Negotiations continued through a midnight Friday deadline and nearly non-stop over the weekend.
UAW members remained on the job and did not put up picket lines during negotiations.
A strike could have forced General Motors Corp. to suspend production at its 11 North American light truck plants.
American Axle supplies rear axles for GM's pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles.

Federal-Mogul Corp aims to pay off $185 million in debt in 1997.
Federal-Mogul Corp intends to reduce its total debt to capital ratio to under 60 percent by the end of 1997.
Dick Snell is the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Federal-Mogul Corp.
Federal-Mogul Corp's goal for return on invested capital in 1997 is 12 percent.
Federal-Mogul Corp has earned between 4.5 percent and 6 percent on its capital over the last three years.
Federal-Mogul Corp's cost of capital is 12 percent.
In 1998, Dick Snell would like Federal-Mogul Corp to earn a 10 percent return on sales.
Federal-Mogul Corp announced a broad restructuring that will exit the international retail business.
The restructuring resulted in a $264 million pre-tax charge for Federal-Mogul Corp.
Federal-Mogul Corp reduced its debt by $104 million in 1996.

Miss Manners, whose real name is Judith Martin, has made positive comments about car dealers.
John Peterson is the outgoing president of the National Automobile Dealers Association.
Peterson delivered a speech that criticized the media's portrayal of traditional car dealerships.
Peterson stated that traditional franchised dealers will remain the dominant system for selling new cars and trucks.
In 1996, Miss Manners expressed surprise at the courteous service she received at car dealerships.
Peterson acknowledged that traditional dealer franchises face challenges from used car superstores like CarMax and AutoNation USA.
Franchised dealers increased sales by three percent and profits by 25 percent in a year when superstores grew rapidly.
There were 23,000 franchised dealerships in operation at the end of the year.
Of the approximately 15 million new light vehicles expected to be sold in 1997, 14.5 million will be sold by the franchise system.
A survey by the Newspaper Association of America indicated that over 90 percent of new-vehicle buyers are satisfied or very satisfied.

Three bombs exploded on buses in Urumqi, Xinjiang, China.
At least four people were killed in the explosions.
The blasts occurred in rapid succession on Tuesday afternoon.
The explosions wounded at least 60 people.
Police patrolled the streets and checked suspicious bags and packages following the blasts.
The violence was the first reported in Xinjiang since riots in Yining on February 5 and 6.
No one has claimed responsibility for the bombings.
Urumqi is the capital of the mainly Muslim region of Xinjiang.
Chinese leaders have expressed concern over the threat from Islamic fundamentalism.
The bombs exploded at around 6:40 p.m. local time.

The United States and China are not on the verge of a breakthrough in their relations.
U.S. Vice President Al Gore and House Speaker Newt Gingrich visited China.
Analysts stated that both sides can claim gains from these visits.
The key objective of the visits was to move closer to an exchange of presidential visits.
Gore's visit was said to bring the two sides one step closer to this goal.
Gore reassured Chinese officials that the U.S. remained committed to an exchange of visits between President Bill Clinton and President Jiang Zemin.
Officials from both countries were working on specific dates for the presidential visits.
The United States and China have been working to ease tensions over issues such as Taiwan, trade, and human rights.
Gore's talks with Chinese leaders addressed key areas of disagreement, with a milder reaction from China than in the past.
Jiang expressed satisfaction with the increasing number of congressional visits to China regarding the Taiwan issue.

China's President Jiang Zemin delivered a eulogy for Deng Xiaoping.
Jiang Zemin praised Deng Xiaoping's role in the recovery of Hong Kong.
Jiang Zemin pledged peaceful reunification with Taiwan.
Jiang Zemin stated that Deng Xiaoping's 'one country, two systems' formula allows capitalist and socialist systems to coexist.
Jiang Zemin claimed that the complete reunification of China is the aspiration of the entire Chinese nation.
Jiang Zemin delivered his speech at Beijing's Great Hall of the People.
Deng Xiaoping guided negotiations with Britain that led to a 1984 accord regarding Hong Kong.
The 1984 accord stipulates that Hong Kong will return to Chinese rule on June 30.
Under the accord, Hong Kong is to retain its capitalist system and a high degree of autonomy for 50 years.
Jiang Zemin indicated that the Taiwan question will eventually be settled.

The U.S. government is updating thousands of computer systems and software programs to address the year 2000 problem.
Sally Katzen is coordinating the repair effort as the administrator of the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs in the Office of Management and Budget.
Sally Katzen expressed confidence that all major systems will be fixed.
Legislators in Congress are interested in the year 2000 problem and have urged agencies to take action.
Most congressional staff are aware of the year 2000 problem, although some agencies, like the air traffic control system, are lagging.
Representative Steve Horn stated that Congress will continue to address the year 2000 problem until it is resolved.
Steve Horn is the chairman of the Government Reform Committee's Management, Information and Technology subcommittee.
The subcommittee has received testimony from government and private-sector experts regarding the year 2000 problem.
The latest survey indicated that all government agencies are aware of the year 2000 problem and most are prepared to implement fixes.
The Defence Department and the Social Security Administration have extensive plans to address the year 2000 problem before December 31, 1999.

The number of consumers and businesses filing for U.S. bankruptcy protection reached 335,073 in the first quarter of 1997.
This figure represents a 26 percent increase from 266,149 in the first quarter of the previous year.
Consumers accounted for more than 321,000 of the bankruptcy petitions, approximately 96 percent of the total.
This consumer filing figure reflects a 27 percent increase from the previous year.
Samuel Gerdano, the executive director of the American Bankruptcy Institute, stated that the record pace of bankruptcies correlates with growth in consumer spending and debt.
Gerdano indicated that the pace of bankruptcies in the first quarter of 1997 suggests that the total for the year will exceed the 1996 record.
Advanta Corp. reported a loss of 43 cents per share for the first quarter, surprising Wall Street.
George Salem, a banking industry analyst, noted that credit card debt is significantly influencing bankruptcy trends.
Salem mentioned that bankruptcies are negatively impacting credit card company profits.
Hawaii experienced the largest increase in bankruptcies with a 61 percent rise over the 12 months ending March 31, 1997.

The Internet Society announced a plan to provide seven new top-level domains.
The plan was endorsed by Digital Equipment Corp., MCI Communications Corp., and UUNET Technologies Inc.
The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority endorsed the plan.
The International Telecommunications Union, World Intellectual Property Organization, and International Trademark Association also backed the plan.
New domain names such as 'firm,' 'arts,' and 'web' will be added starting in the third quarter of 1997.
The plan establishes an arbitration and mediation procedure for resolving disputes over names.
Hasbro Inc. won a lawsuit to regain control of the address 'candyland.com.'
Internet Society President Donald Heath stated that responsible self-governance is key for the Internet's potential.
MCI Senior Vice President Vincent Cerf emphasized the importance of sound processes for Internet administration.
Network Solutions Inc. currently registers addresses under most existing top-level domains.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) issued forecasts for 1997 predicting a slight economic upturn.
The CSU expects real GDP growth for 1997 of 4.0-5.0 percent following an estimated 4.1 percent growth rate for 1996.
The CSU forecasts average annual inflation to ease to 7.5-8.0 percent from 8.8 percent.
The CSU predicts the current account deficit will grow to 137-145 billion crowns from an estimated 110.6 billion crown shortfall in 1996.
Analysts warned that widening current account and trade deficits could undermine the economy.
David Lubin, an economist at HSBC Midland, stated that the forecasts are credible but not very encouraging.
The CSU estimates the current account shortfall will be between 8.6-9.1 percent of GDP in 1997.
The CSU forecasts the trade deficit to widen to 202-212 billion crowns from a deficit of 160.3 billion crowns in 1996.
The trade gap was attributed to a 12.7 percent rise in imports in 1996, while exports rose only 3.5 percent.
The CSU expects exports to grow 4.5-6.5 percent in 1997, while import growth should ease to 9-12 percent.

The Prague Stock Exchange gained ground on Thursday.
Analysts are not convinced that the fortunes of the Prague Stock Exchange have turned around.
The rise in the Prague Stock Exchange is attributed to thin domestic buying.
The Prague Stock Exchange lost close to 20 percent during most of autumn.
Key investors sold off positions in the Prague Stock Exchange.
The Prague Stock Exchange has gained in 15 of the past 16 sessions.
The PX50 index was up 0.25 percent at 519.5 at its daily price fixing on Thursday.
The Prague Stock Exchange is 8.3 percent higher than its low in mid-November.
The Czech market has inadequate legislation that fails to protect minority shareholders.
The Securities Registry is bound by law to provide services related to securities transactions.

The United States offered the Czech Republic free use of seven Navy Hornet aircraft for five years.
The U.S. Navy representatives offered to lease seven McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet fighter planes to the Czech Republic under a no-cost, five-year agreement.
The offer includes six single-seat F/A-18A and one two-seat F/A-18B aircraft.
The offer also includes the supply of replacement parts, pilot and ground personnel training programs, and support equipment at cost.
Lockheed Martin, SAAB and British Aerospace, and Dassault Aviation are also competing for business in central Europe.
The Czech government is debating decisions on buying aircraft due to proposed cuts in defense spending.
The Czech Republic, Poland, and Hungary are seen as leading candidates for early NATO membership.
Czech defense officials stated they need about 24 fighters to replace their aging Soviet-made MiG-21s.
New western-made advanced fighters are considered too expensive at over $20 million per fighter.
Czech pilots could begin training in the planes in six months, with delivery of the aircraft 18 months after the contract is signed.

Lawyers for Peter Young stated there are no grounds for allegations of criminality against him.
No allegations of criminality have been made in the proceedings served on Peter Young.
Peter Young was suspended by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) due to suspected irregularities in three funds.
Two of the funds with suspected irregularities were managed by Peter Young.
Peter Young's personal assets were frozen after an injunction obtained by MGAM and Royal Bank of Scotland.
Trading in the affected funds was halted last Monday but resumed on Thursday after a cash injection by Deutsche Bank.
The cash injection amounted to 180 million pounds ($280.7 million).
The investigation focuses on the valuation of unlisted high-technology stocks in the funds.
The Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) is investigating the situation.
The Serious Fraud Office (SFO) has not taken official action but is in contact with IMRO regarding the developments.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is unlikely to offer Nicola Horlick her job back.
Banking sources stated that the decision regarding Horlick's reinstatement is now in her hands.
Horlick's resignation last week means that DMG's Morgan Grenfell Asset Management is no longer obliged to discuss her reinstatement.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is preparing to launch a campaign to strengthen its pension fund business following Horlick's resignation.
Horlick was suspended for allegedly attempting to lure staff to another firm.
DMG spokesman James Murray denied that pension firms were considering moving their business from DMG's funds.
Morgan Grenfell Asset Management has written to all its pension fund clients to address concerns following Horlick's suspension and resignation.
Some clients, including Westminster City Council, Dumfries and Galloway County Council, and the Merchant Navy Officers' Pension Fund, have expressed concern about events at MGAM.
The Railway Pension Trustee Company, which has 1.25 billion pounds with MGAM, stated it would maintain close contact with MGAM officials.
Horlick denied the allegations of trying to lure staff away from MGAM during an interview with BBC television.

The head of Britain's financial markets watchdog, the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA), stated that former Barings treasury chief Ian Hopkins broke precedent by refusing to be bound by SFA rules.
The SFA banned Ian Hopkins from being a director in the City for at least three years due to his involvement in the 1995 collapse of Barings bank.
Nick Leeson, a trader based in Singapore, is serving a jail sentence for his role in the collapse of Barings bank, which resulted in losses of nearly $1.4 billion.
Ian Hopkins was ordered to pay 10,000 pounds ($15,800) towards the SFA's costs after an independent tribunal found him to be no longer a 'fit and proper person' to be a director of an SFA regulated firm.
Nick Durlacher, the SFA's chairman, stated that the situation with Hopkins was difficult because it was without precedent.
Durlacher mentioned that the SFA had never confronted a situation where someone signed a contract to be bound by their rules and then ignored them.
Ian Hopkins is one of nine Barings executives who have been disciplined by the SFA.
Hopkins claimed he attempted to 'blow the whistle' on irregularities in the Singapore operation but that his warnings were ignored by other managers.
Durlacher commented that the tribunal judged Hopkins' whistleblower claims to be weak, noting he had an unreconciled balance of 100 million pounds for three months.
Durlacher denied that Hopkins was treated more harshly than others due to his refusal to recognize the SFA's authority and stated he had only one telephone conversation with him.

Deng Xiaoping is in good health according to Beijing Vice-Mayor Zhang Baifa.
Zhang Baifa stated that Deng may not be able to visit Hong Kong when it reverts to Chinese rule in mid-1997.
Zhang reported that Deng is currently in Beijing.
Deng Xiaoping is 92 years old.
Zhang mentioned that Deng expressed a desire to go to Hong Kong, even if it meant using a wheelchair.
Zhang cautioned that it would be difficult for Deng to travel due to his age and health risks.
Deng oversaw the negotiations for the return of Hong Kong from Britain to China.
Deng has expressed a hope to witness the transfer of power in Hong Kong.
Chinese officials privately indicated that Deng would not attend the handover ceremony.
Deng has not been seen in public since early 1994.

Jiang Zemin is the boss of China's Communist Party.
Jiang Zemin urged Taiwan not to create new obstacles to ties.
Jiang's comments were reported by major Chinese newspapers.
Jiang made his remarks one day after the election of Hong Kong's first post-colonial chief executive.
Hong Kong is set to revert to China on June 30, 1997, after 150 years of British rule.
Jiang called for Taiwan to return to China, stating that reunification is the will of the people.
Beijing and Taipei have been rivals since 1949, following the Chinese civil war.
Lee Teng-hui is Taiwan's first native-born president.
Taiwan denies ambitions for independence and claims commitment to reunification under democracy.
Jiang warned that forces seeking Taiwan's independence threaten peaceful reunification.

China has pledged to open its insurance, stock, retail, wholesale, and banking sectors to foreign investment.
This pledge is part of China's effort to gain entry to the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
From 1997 to 2000, China is expected to widen access to its insurance and stock markets for foreign investment.
The China Daily reported this information, quoting Ma Jixian from the State Economic and Trade Commission.
The pledge was included in a unilateral action plan submitted by China to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
Foreign insurers will gain access to markets outside Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou before the end of the decade.
China's insurance market was previously dominated by the state-owned People's Insurance Group.
Currently, only three foreign insurers can write policies in China: American International Assurance Co Ltd, Tokio Marine and Fire Insurance Co Ltd, and a joint venture with a domestic insurer.
Foreign stock companies will be allowed to handle A shares, which are currently restricted to Chinese nationals.
China plans to reduce its average import tariffs from 23 percent to about 15 percent.

Coca-Cola Amatil (CCA) Ltd is an Australian-based soft drink bottler.
CCA announced the final details of its share swap deal with San Miguel Corp on Wednesday.
The deal aims to create the world's second largest Coca-Cola bottler.
CCA initially announced the deal in April.
Some San Miguel shareholders protested the deal's terms regarding board influence and cashflows.
CCA confirmed the initial terms of the deal, which involves CCA buying San Miguel's stake in a soft drink bottling joint venture in the Philippines.
In exchange, San Miguel will receive a 25 percent stake in CCA.
The Coca-Cola Co, CCA's parent group, will see its shareholding in CCA diluted from 36 percent to 33 percent.
The deal is valued at A$3.7 billion and will result in annual sales of almost A$4 billion.
The number of San Miguel representatives on the CCA board will increase from three to four.

Brambles Industries Ltd is a transport equipment hire and logistics firm.
Brambles Industries Ltd announced it is on track to achieve a full year net profit of about A$240 million.
John Fletcher is the chief executive of Brambles.
John Fletcher stated that analysts should not assume first half profit growth will continue into the full year.
The existing market expectations for the full year remain stable according to Fletcher.
The average forecast from the Barceps survey for the 1996/97 year is A$240.3 million.
This forecast represents a nearly 12 percent increase from the A$214.8 million pre-abnormal net profit of 1995/96.
Brambles reported a first half net profit increase of 14.3 percent to A$117.2 million.
Brambles expects the rate of profit improvement to slow in the second half due to difficult trading conditions.
Fletcher indicated that economic conditions in Australia are subdued in the transport and logistics sectors.

The Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) announced an 11 percent rise in first half profits.
CBA reported a 33 percent increase in business lending.
CBA's net profit for the six months to December 31 rose to A$602 million from A$542 million a year earlier.
CBA managing director David Murray stated that business volumes were pleasing.
Murray indicated that the results could lead to a better than expected full year result.
CBA had previously expected competition in the home loan market to squeeze margins and keep profits flat.
Analysts had forecasted a profit of between A$535 million and A$560 million for CBA.
CBA's shares increased by 47 cents to A$13.88 following the profit announcement.
CBA announced an interim dividend of 45 cents per share, an increase of seven cents from the previous interim dividend.
CBA cut its variable home mortgage rates by up to 0.7 percentage points.

TCF Financial Corp. and Standard Financial Inc. signed a definitive agreement for TCF to acquire Standard Financial for $424 million in stock and cash.
The acquisition deal was announced two days after Marshall & Ilsley Corp. announced its acquisition of Security Capital Corp. for about $945 million in cash and stock.
Both acquisitions aim to increase market share in the Midwest banking sector.
Marshall & Ilsley expects to increase its market share to 19.2 percent in Wisconsin.
Firstar Corp. is the second largest bank in Wisconsin with 12.1 percent of deposits.
The acquisition of Standard Financial will strengthen TCF's franchise in Chicago.
William Cooper, chairman of TCF, stated that the merger will produce long-term revenue enhancements and meaningful cost savings.
TCF expects to save about $4 million annually after combining operations with Standard Financial.
The combined company will have $10 billion in assets and 276 financial services offices.
Standard stockholders may choose to receive cash, TCF shares, or a combination of both in the acquisition.

Sears, Roebuck and Co will spend more than $500 million to revamp and expand its off-the-mall tire and battery stores under the new National Tire and Battery name.
Sears plans to spend more than $1 billion through the year 2002 on its entire auto group to add stores and convert some existing stores.
Sears sold 25 million tires and 8.5 million batteries through its Sears Tire Group in 1996.
Sears will combine most of its 275 Tire America and National Tire Warehouse Stores under the National Tire and Battery name.
Sears plans to add about 100 National Tire stores over the next five years.
Sears hopes to add about $120 million in annual revenue for the tire group when the expansion is completed.
Sears' tire group had $2.3 billion in revenues in 1996.
The new stores will have a high-tech, open feel, allowing customers to watch the work being done on their cars.
Sears will price competitively in individual markets.
Sears is targeting younger, higher income customers with higher performance car needs for the off-the-mall stores.

First Bank System Inc. will acquire U.S. Bancorp in an $8.5 billion stock deal.
The acquisition will make First Bank the 14th-largest bank in the United States.
The deal will provide First Bank with a presence in the Pacific Northwest.
The acquisition is expected to result in the loss of about 4,000 jobs.
U.S. Bancorp shareholders will receive 0.755 share of First Bank common stock for each share of U.S. Bancorp they own.
The purchase price for U.S. Bancorp shares is $56.53 based on First Bank's trading price of $74.875.
Analyst James Schutz stated that the deal values U.S. Bancorp at about 19.2 times its 1996 earnings.
First Bank expects pretax cost savings of about $340 million from the merger.
First Bank plans to take pretax charges of $625 million for costs related to the merger.
First Bank anticipates an 8 percent addition to earnings per share by 1999.

Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd. were active on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday.
Exchange officials stated that problems affecting recent trading in Bre-X stock were resolved.
Bre-X closed down C25 cents at C$3.18 with a turnover of eight million shares.
On Nasdaq, Bre-X fell 25 cents to $2.375.
Bre-X reached a session high of C$3.78 amid market rumors about positive test results from the Busang gold site.
An analyst mentioned that rumors from Strathcona contributed to the stock's rise before it fell.
Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. has not commented since being hired by Bre-X to audit the Busang gold site.
The final results of Strathcona's review are expected in early May.
Bre-X faced issues after Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. reported low gold amounts in drilling samples from the Busang property.
The TSE halted trading in Bre-X shares three times that week due to heavy order volumes and a computer system issue.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd.'s Busang gold discovery may not be as rich as projected.
The news about Bre-X's gold discovery affected the mining world and Canadian markets.
Securities regulators are investigating the situation.
Gold shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange fell more than 300 points or almost 3.0 percent.
The decline in gold shares impacted the entire market.
Canadian regulators are collaborating with Toronto exchange officials on the investigation.
A spokesman for the Ontario Securities Commission stated that they are working with the TSE.
Bre-X's stock was halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange and Nasdaq due to questions about its gold discovery.
Bre-X's stock price fell from C$250 to C$15.50 before the halt.
Bre-X admitted that test samples from the Busang gold property may have been overstated.

Barrick Gold Corp. is the world's second largest gold producer.
Barrick Gold Corp. reported a net income of $55 million or $0.15 a share in the first quarter of 1997.
Barrick Gold Corp.'s net income fell from $72 million or $0.20 a share in the previous year.
Gold production from Barrick's 10 producing mines fell by 88,147 ounces to 712,368 ounces in the first quarter of 1997.
Barrick Gold Corp. expects production to be substantially higher in the second half of 1997.
Barrick Gold Corp. aims to achieve a production target of over 3 million ounces for the year.
Barrick Gold Corp.'s gold production was 3,148,801 ounces in the previous year.
Barrick Gold Corp.'s earnings in 1996 were $218 million or $0.60 a share, including writedowns.
Analyst Michael Jalonen expects Barrick to earn about $0.70 a share in 1997, excluding writedowns.
Barrick's stock rose C25 cents to C$32.85 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday.

Dow Corning Corp. announced it would set aside up to $2 billion for silicone breast implant claims under a $3 billion bankruptcy reorganization plan.
Dow Corning is seeking a trial to determine whether silicone breast implants cause diseases.
The bankruptcy plan was filed with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Bay City, Mich.
Dow Corning plans to allocate an additional $1 billion to pay commercial creditors.
Dow Corning, based in Midland, Mich., is a joint venture between Dow Chemical Co. and Corning Inc.
The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in May 1995 due to lawsuits from women alleging medical problems from implants.
Dow Corning introduced silicone gel breast implants in 1964 and was the largest manufacturer until a FDA moratorium in 1992.
The reorganization plan includes a $600 million fund for out-of-court settlements.
An additional $1.4 billion would be available for implant claims if a trial proves that implants caused disease.
Dow Corning asserts that scientific studies have not shown a link between implants and disease.

General Motors Corp. will consolidate all of its commercial truck production in Flint, Mich.
GM will discontinue some engineering work in Flint and Lansing, Mich.
The consolidation will expand the workforce at the Flint truck plant by up to 3,000 jobs by the year 2001.
The Flint truck plant currently employs about 2,000 workers.
The closure of the truck and bus chassis plant in Detroit will affect 494 employees.
Production will be moved from Detroit to Flint in the year 2000.
About 90 engineers from the Detroit plant will be transferred to GM facilities in Pontiac, Mich.
GM will shift production of medium-duty commercial trucks from Janesville, Wis., to Flint in 2001.
The Janesville truck line employs about 1,000 people.
GM will invest about $500 million in the Flint truck plant to prepare it for medium-duty truck production.

Chrysler Corp. will report record earnings for 1996.
Chrysler's record worldwide sales for 1996 are 2.97 million vehicles.
Robert Eaton is the chairman of Chrysler Corp.
Chrysler's previous annual profit record was $3.713 billion in 1994.
Chrysler earned $2.025 billion in 1995.
Chrysler expects to exceed its 1996 sales results in 1997.
Chrysler plans to produce about 190,000 more trucks in 1997 than in 1996.
Chrysler will unveil the Dodge Durango at the Detroit auto show.
Robert Lutz is the Vice Chairman of Chrysler.
Lutz recently gave up his president and chief operating officer titles.

Ford Motor Co announced it would cut 1,300 jobs at its Halewood plant near Liverpool, England.
The job cuts represent almost one third of the Halewood workforce.
The Halewood plant will not build the planned new model of the Escort car, due in 1999.
Production of the new Escort model is likely to transfer to factories in Spain and Germany.
Ford stated that Halewood could become the European source for a planned new vehicle, which is still a concept.
Halewood will continue to produce the current Escort model through 2000.
David Gorman, European vehicle operations manager for Ford, commented on the future of the Halewood plant.
Local MP David Alton reported that Ford indicated the job losses would occur through voluntary redundancy.
The proposed job cuts will reduce Halewood's workforce to just over 3,000 from a peak of 14,000 in the 1960s.
Workers expressed anger over the job cuts, citing British labour laws and the absence of the European Union's Social Chapter.

Hanson Plc reported a record 1.8 billion British pounds ($2.9 billion) in pretax profits for the last fiscal year.
Hanson Plc began a four-way split of its operations on October 1.
Hanson Plc spun off Imperial Tobacco and Millennium Chemicals in the fall.
Hanson Plc's energy group is due to be spun off by February.
Hanson Plc's final results showed profits topping forecasts and increasing from 1.22 billion ($1.98 billion) last year.
The profits were inflated by a one-time gain of 609 million pounds ($989 million).
Earnings per share were 25.6 pence (14.6 cents) compared to 18.2 pence (29.5 cents) last year.
A dividend of 1 pence (1.6 cents) will be paid.
The building materials and equipment divisions saw profits slip to 231 million pounds ($375 million) from 237 million ($385 million).
The combined value of Hanson and the demerged companies was 195 pence ($3.17) on December 1, 1995, and now stands at 150 pence ($2.43).

Ford Motor Co announced 1,300 job cuts at its Halewood plant in northwest England.
Ford is switching production of a new model to plants in Spain and Germany.
The new version of the mid-range Escort model will not be built at Halewood.
The proposed job cuts will reduce Halewood's workforce to just over 3,000.
Halewood's workforce peaked at 14,000 in the 1960s.
Workers believe the new model will be built at Ford's plants in Valencia, Spain, and Saarlouis, Germany.
Ford has not confirmed where the new model will be built.
Trade unions blamed the decision on a lack of legal protection for British workers.
Britain has opted out of the European Union's Social Chapter, affecting working conditions.
Ford stated that Halewood would continue to make the current Escort model through the year 2000.

3Com Corp. will acquire U.S. Robotics in a deal valued at $6.6 billion.
The merger will create a counterweight to Cisco Systems Inc.
This merger is the largest ever in the computer network industry.
The combined company will have more than $5 billion in annual revenues.
The combined company will employ more than 12,000 employees in 130 countries.
Each share of U.S. Robotics will be swapped for 1.75 shares of 3Com.
The deal is valued at $6.6 billion based on the $39.125 closing price of 3Com stock.
3Com closed at $39 and U.S. Robotics closed at $61 on Nasdaq.
U.S. Robotics is the world's largest maker of consumer modems.
3Com is based in Santa Clara, California.

Xerox Corp. reported higher fourth-quarter profits from continuing operations.
Sales of digital products rose by 26 percent, offsetting flat sales of black and white copiers.
Xerox agreed to sell part of its Talegen insurance holdings for $450 million, including assumption of debt.
Xerox's board voted to raise the dividend by 10 percent.
Xerox reported earnings of $426 million for the latest quarter, up 12 percent from $379 million in the 1995 quarter.
The 1995 earnings figure excludes a $1.6 billion charge related to the planned sale of Talegen.
Sales increased to $5.08 billion from $4.76 billion.
Earnings exceeded forecasts by a few cents per share, according to First Call.
Xerox stock closed up $1.375 at $59.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Xerox announced the sale of Talegen's Coregis unit for $375 million in cash and the assumption of $75 million in debt to General Electric Co.'s GE Capital unit.

A device that turns a personal computer into an automated-teller machine was introduced by Fischer International Systems Corp.
The device costs $60 and can be inserted into the floppy disk drive of any PC.
The device enables PCs to read 'smart cards,' which can perform electronic cash transactions and store bank account balances.
Smart cards are gaining popularity in Europe for store purchases and telephone calls.
Smart cards are beginning to be used in the United States as a replacement for cash in ordinary purchases.
The device may stimulate home banking by allowing consumers to perform financial transactions without visiting a bank branch or ATM.
Smarty is the name of the product that allows PCs to link to banks or retail outlets via the Internet.
Fischer holds key patents for smart card readers that can be inserted into 3.5 inch floppy drives.
The device can be used in home or office PCs and laptops, enabling wider use of banking cards for purchases.
Fischer is working with major U.S. and European financial services firms and home banking software providers to promote the device.

The top executive at Nomura Securities is preparing to step down over a scandal.
Nomura Securities is being investigated by Japan's securities watchdog.
Nomura admitted that certain deals appear to have broken the law.
President Hideo Sakamaki has offered to step down after the investigation is completed.
Nomura declined to comment on the report of Sakamaki's resignation.
Sakamaki's predecessor stepped down in 1991 over a similar scandal.
Financial authorities indicated that Nomura could face stern penalties if violations are confirmed.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka stated that strict steps will be taken against Nomura after the investigation.
Two Nomura directors are involved in suspect deals that allegedly violated the law.
Nomura has a history of controversy and faced penalties in the early 1990s for compensating favored clients.

Dozens of Japanese banks may close their foreign operations in the next few years due to problem loans.
Two of Japan's top 20 banks have announced plans to shut down their overseas branches.
Analysts suggest that many other Japanese banks should also close their foreign operations to improve profitability.
Yushiro Ikuyo, first vice president of Smith Barney International Inc, stated that Japanese banks need to cut unprofitable assets overseas to boost return on equity.
Ikuyo noted that many Japanese banks are primarily providing services to Japanese customers abroad rather than engaging with local customers.
Ikuyo predicted that the number of Japanese banks operating abroad could decrease to about a third of the current 85 in the coming years.
Japan has a total of 149 banks.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd and Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd announced restructuring plans that include exiting overseas operations.
Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd plans to merge with Hokkaido Bank Ltd, which closed its overseas offices last year due to lack of profitability.
Financial authorities in Japan do not object to the closure of overseas operations by Japanese banks.

Nippon Credit Bank Ltd announced it expects to unveil a restructuring plan in early April.
The restructuring plan is expected to include selling real estate and shutting down some overseas operations.
Tadao Iwaki, senior managing director of NCB, denied that the restructuring plan was finalized.
Iwaki stated that the bank has been working on a restructuring plan for a long time.
NCB cannot provide a specific date for unveiling the plan until earnings results for the current business year become clearer.
Banking sources indicated that the restructuring plan would involve shutting down some overseas branches and selling real estate, including its Tokyo headquarters.
Iwaki mentioned that the steps in the restructuring plan should be considered.
This is the second news conference in two months where NCB has denied various reports, including one about being on the verge of collapse.
Moody's Investors Service downgraded NCB's debenture ratings to junk levels due to concerns about its problem loans.
The Ministry of Finance asked commercial banks if they would assist NCB in its restructuring efforts.

China is establishing a national state debt trading market called the China State Debt Clearing System.
The new market aims to connect all state debt trading floors across the country.
The China State Debt Clearing System will gradually take over state debt trading from current markets.
The Shanghai stock exchange will play a minor role in the new trading system.
Currently, most state debt trading in China is regional.
Traders in different regions cannot clear their positions across different markets.
The new market will allow traders to bid and ask on any market nationwide through a computer network.
Major participants in China's state debt markets include state banks, securities houses, state enterprises, and wealthy individuals.
China's securities rules prohibit credit trading of state debt, but some trading centers have accepted margin requirements.
The Wuhan Securities Exchange Centre, Tianjin Securities Exchange Centre, and STAQ system reportedly accumulated debts of up to 50 billion yuan.

Shanghai's port will be expanded to improve container handling.
The approach channels of Shanghai's port will be deepened to accommodate large container ships.
Shanghai's port's container throughput rose 29 percent to 1.97 million units last year.
Shanghai's port's container throughput is expected to rise by 21 percent to 2.3 million units this year.
The aim for Shanghai's port is to reach three million units by the end of the century.
Shanghai port has been hampered by shallow approach channels and silt build-up from the Yangtze River.
The current depth of the approach channels is seven metres.
The plan is to deepen the approach channels by five metres to reach a depth of 12.5 metres.
The deepening of the approach channels is planned to be achieved within the next 10 years.
Investment in new facilities and reconstruction at Shanghai port is expected to drop below last year's 1.1 billion yuan.

China has begun to issue new stock trading regulations to organize its share markets.
Industry analysts stated that the authorities decided to issue non-controversial sections of the Securities Law first.
China's two stock markets are growing rapidly, increasing the need for detailed regulations.
An executive from a Chinese securities house indicated that new rules are expected to be part of the future Securities Law.
Since late last year, around a dozen new sets of regulations have been issued by central securities authorities.
New regulations include annual checks on the operations of listed companies and rules on initial public offerings.
The central government aims to prevent irregularities in securities trading as it becomes more active.
China began drafting the Securities Law in 1992, but disputes have delayed its completion.
Responsibility for managing the stock markets is divided among several parts of the central government.
Current regulations are scattered and not comprehensive, leading to widespread irregularities in transactions.

Peter Munk is the chairman and chief executive of Canada's Barrick Gold Corp.
Peter Munk lost the battle for the Busang gold deposit to Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc.
Peter Munk expressed faith in Indonesia and its mining law despite the loss.
Munk wished Freeport-McMoRan good luck with the Busang gold deposit.
Munk and a team of executives, including former U.S. President George Bush and former Canadian Prime Minister Brian Mulroney, attempted to win control of Busang.
Barrick Gold initially dominated negotiations for control of Busang.
Busang was discovered and is 90 percent owned by Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
Busang contains at least 71 million ounces of gold, valued at about $25 billion.
The Indonesian government instructed Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick and set a deadline for February 17.
Muhammad 'Bob' Hasan was appointed by the Indonesian government to make the final decision regarding Busang.

TVX Gold Inc is taking steps to become a major mining company.
TVX Gold Inc has hired three senior executives to help achieve its goals.
Cliff Davis is the new senior vice-president of North American operations at TVX.
David Murray is the recently appointed president and chief operating officer of TVX.
Ken Sangster is the senior vice-president of European operations at TVX.
The three new executives have previous experience working together at RTZ-CRA Corp Plc.
TVX Gold Inc was established as a separate entity from Inco Ltd in 1993.
TVX Gold Inc aims to produce 1.1 million ounces of gold annually by the year 2000.
TVX Gold Inc has interests in Canada, Greece, Brazil, Ecuador, Chile, the Czech Republic, and Russia.
TVX Gold Inc's stock has been rumored as a takeover target for major gold producers.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is involved in a significant gold discovery in Borneo, Indonesia.
The situation surrounding Bre-X includes elements of suspense, international intrigue, politics, legal issues, and financial stakes.
Barrick Gold Corp. from Toronto appeared to have a deal with Bre-X until recently.
Placer Dome Inc. from Vancouver made an offer for Bre-X that is under consideration by the Indonesian government.
Teck Corp., another Vancouver mining company, expressed interest in making a bid for Bre-X and its Busang deposit.
The Busang deposit in Kalimantan contains at least 57 million ounces of gold, valued at $21 billion.
Analysts believe the Busang deposit could contain over 100 million ounces of high-grade, low-cost gold.
The Indonesian government instructed Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick and submit their proposal for approval.
Some Bre-X shareholders hired lawyers to protect their interests in the negotiations.
Barrick claims it was selected for its experience, environmental record, and financial strength.

The Czech Agriculture Ministry announced plans to privatise Budejovicky Budvar n.p.
Budejovicky Budvar n.p. brews Czech Budweiser beer.
The privatisation will occur through a management buyout.
Talks with Anheuser Busch Cos. broke down last year.
Jiri Stehlik is the head of the ministry's privatisation department.
The plan includes selling a 10 percent stake in Budvar to management.
Management will have the option to buy an additional 41 percent stake later.
The plan follows failed talks with Busch regarding the Budweiser trademark.
Budvar is located in Ceske Budejovice, which is known as Budweis in German.
The government aims to keep Budvar primarily in Czech hands during privatisation.

Czech engineering group Skoda a.s. won an order to supply more than $170 million in buses to the city of San Francisco.
This order is the largest supply of Czech goods ever to the United States.
Skoda spokesman Jaroslav Hudec stated that the electric-powered buses would be produced in the Czech Republic.
The buses will be assembled at Skoda's subsidiary, Electric Transit International in Baltimore.
Hudec described the victory in this tender as an extraordinary success due to the expected volumes of supplies and the prestige of the U.S. market.
Skoda, based in Plzen, is no longer affiliated with the Czech car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s.
Skoda aims to offer western-quality units with the cost advantage of eastern European production.
The San Francisco contract could lead to more business opportunities for Skoda in the United States.
Skoda has produced over 12,000 buses since 1936, many of which operate in cities throughout the former communist bloc.
Local Czech media reported that the San Francisco order could be for about 250 single-section and higher capacity buses.

The Czech government directed three ministers to oversee an investigation into the failure of Kreditni Banka a.s.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced the investigation after questions arose regarding banking oversight.
Kreditni Banka a.s. was shut down by the central bank after reportedly losing about 12 billion crowns.
Czech National Bank Governor Josef Tosovsky will join Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda, and Interior Minister Jan Ruml in the investigation.
The government authorized the group of ministers to inquire into the issue using existing standard mechanisms.
Authorities have been investigating the Kreditni case since the central bank rescinded its license in August.
Findings from the investigation may lead to changes in Czech legislation.
Local media reports suggest that the failure of Kreditni Banka was due to murky loans connected to shareholders.
Opposition leader Milos Zeman blamed Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik for lax supervision of banks.
The central bank welcomed the investigation into potential criminal actions related to Kreditni's failure.

China issued a directive to publishers to produce more good books, fewer mediocre books, and no bad books.
The directive was issued by the China Press and Publications Administration during a meeting.
The directive emphasizes the strengthening of professional ethics in China's publishing industry.
The campaign aims to eliminate ideas that differ from Communist Party ideology.
The directive states that publishing houses must not sell off publication codes.
Publication codes are necessary for any book or magazine to be published in China.
The directive prohibits accepting money or favors from authors for printing their works.
Good books are defined as those that are educational, such as science books.
Bad books include those that violate religious policy, are subversive, pornographic, or depict violence.
The China Publishers' Association stated that bad books also include those advocating ethnic separatism and revealing state secrets.

Deng Xiaoping died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection.
The Communist Party announced Deng's age as 93.
Deng Xiaoping was born on August 22, 1904.
China adds a year to a person's age after the lunar new year.
The announcement of Deng's death was issued by the official Xinhua news agency.
Deng died at 21.08 (1308 GMT) in Beijing.
The Communist Party and government expressed profound grief over Deng's passing.
Deng was in the advanced stages of Parkinson's disease and died of respiratory failure.
Doctors performed an emergency tracheotomy on Deng before he died.
Additional police were seen around the Zhongnanhai government compound in central Beijing after the announcement.

Deng Xiaoping took power in China in 1979.
In 1979, an urban Chinese needed a year's salary to buy a black and white television.
By 1997, the average city dweller could afford a refrigerator, a washing machine, and a color television.
Some urban Chinese could buy their own homes by 1997.
Deng Xiaoping's rule followed the Cultural Revolution from 1966 to 1976.
Deng's economic reforms aimed to improve the economy after three decades of Stalinist central planning.
Deng believed that economic prosperity would help maintain the Communist Party's power.
Barry Naughton wrote about Deng's willingness to adopt non-intervention policies.
Deng allowed private business and free market forces into the command economy.
From 1978 to 1995, the average per capita income of urban Chinese increased by 1,500 percent.

Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd has decided to buy three more Airbus Industrie A340 long range aircraft.
The purchase will increase the airline's air cargo opportunities.
Ray Jewell is the cargo marketing and sales manager for Cathay Pacific Cargo.
Jewell stated in an interview with Reuters that the new aircraft can carry between 15 and 17 tonnes of belly space cargo plus passengers in normal weather conditions from Hong Kong to Toronto.
Other possible destinations for the new aircraft from Hong Kong to Europe are being studied.
The A340's ability to fly ultra-long distances will allow some existing routes to become non-stop destinations.
Jewell expressed confidence that the new aircraft will benefit the air cargo side of the business.
Cathay Pacific currently operates four A340-200 and three A340-300 aircraft.
The new Airbus A340-300 models are scheduled for delivery in the second and third quarters of 1998.
The delivery coincides with the opening of Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok and increased flight schedules.

Lufthansa Cargo reported good demand for air freight services between Germany and China.
Christian Sedelmaier is the managing director for China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan at Lufthansa Cargo.
Sedelmaier stated that mainland companies are rushing to meet a year-end deadline for import tax changes.
Many joint venture companies are importing machinery that is tax exempt until the end of December.
Leading German companies such as Volkswagen and Siemens are importing large amounts of industrial machinery into China via Lufthansa Cargo.
Sedelmaier mentioned a rush for additional transportation requirements on flights to China due to the tax change.
Lufthansa Cargo's capacity until the end of the year is insufficient to meet demand.
Companies have missed the deadline to send machinery by sea, benefiting Lufthansa Cargo.
Lufthansa Cargo is trying to arrange charter flights to accommodate demand.
Lufthansa Cargo currently offers one dedicated freighter service a week between Frankfurt, Beijing, and Shanghai.

Major airlines including Lufthansa Cargo and Air France Cargo have raised their ex-Hong Kong air cargo market rates to European destinations by HK$1 per kilo.
The rate increase is effective from January 1.
The rate increase is in addition to an 80 HK cents per kilo fuel surcharge imposed by some airlines before Christmas.
The fuel surcharge was implemented to cover increases in aviation fuel costs.
The Hong Kong Shippers' Council protested against the surcharge and lobbied the Hong Kong government's Civil Aviation Department to declare it illegal.
Some airlines agreed to withdraw the fuel surcharge but raised market rates instead.
Airlines including Alitalia, Emirates, Cargolux, Virgin Atlantic, Martinair, Swissair, and Air Hong Kong have increased ex-Hong Kong rates by HK$1.80 per kilo.
Lufthansa Cargo raised its rate by HK$1 from January 1 and is maintaining an 80 cents surcharge.
Air France Cargo raised its market rate by HK$1 from January 1 and continues with its 80 HK cents fuel surcharge.
Cathay Pacific Airways Limited raised its rate by HK$1.50 from January 1 without imposing a fuel surcharge.

Northern Electric Plc lost a hostile bid from CalEnergy Co. Inc. for 782 million British pounds ($1.31 billion).
CalEnergy's CE Electric gained control of Northern Electric with 50.3 percent of shareholder votes.
The margin of victory for CalEnergy was 300,000 shares.
The bid process extended beyond its original deadline due to the close competition.
Insurer Prudential Corp. attempted to block CalEnergy's bid by purchasing nearly 1 million Northern shares.
CE Electric Chairman David Sokol expressed a desire to work with Northern Electric's management for a smooth transition.
Northern Electric stated it would not make an immediate statement regarding the takeover.
CalEnergy stock rose by 37.5 cents to $30.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Britain's Takeover Panel rejected Northern's appeal to reverse the deadline extension for the bid.
Northern Electric previously faced a hostile takeover attempt from Trafalgar House, which it fended off with 560 million pounds ($937 billion).

Northern Electric is a British electricity company.
Northern Electric released half year results and year forecasts on a Friday.
