John Kapoor remains chairman and owns 60 percent of Option Care.
Option Care and its franchisees operate 190 facilities in 39 states.

Village Roadshow Ltd expects stronger second half earnings due to the expansion of its cinema operations.
Peter Foo is the group general manager of Village Roadshow Ltd.
Village Roadshow Ltd reported a 27 percent rise in net profit to A$26.1 million for the 1996/97 first half.
Cinemas account for about 40 percent of Village's A$172.95 million in 1996/97 first half sales.
Village Roadshow Ltd is not interested in acquiring the resort island businesses of Qantas Airways Ltd.
The resorts offered by Qantas Airways Ltd include Great Keppel, Brampton, Bedarra, and Lizard Islands.
Village Roadshow Ltd is focused on its cinema rollout and is satisfied with its existing holiday resort business, Daydream Island.
Village is about 19 percent owned by MAI Plc, a unit of United News and Media Plc.
Village Roadshow Ltd is looking to work with MAI Plc on co-production projects.
Village Roadshow Ltd holds a 53 percent stake in Austereo Ltd, which reported an 11 percent rise in 1996/97 first half profit to A$17.15 million.

News Corp Ltd shares increased on Tuesday after a deal with EchoStar Communications Corp.
The deal involves offering U.S. subscription television service.
News Corp shares traded over A$120 million (US$93 million) in Australia.
News' ordinary shares rose 37 cents or 5.51 percent to A$7.09.
Non-voting preferred shares increased 40 cents or 7.1 percent to A$6.03.
Greg Matthew, executive director of equities at Mercantile Mutual, commented on the stock's volatility.
Under the deal, News Corp will contribute US$1 billion in assets for a 50-percent stake in EchoStar.
MCI Communications Corp will acquire part of News Corp's stake, resulting in 40 percent ownership for News Corp.
The deal is valued at approximately A$2.6 billion, equating to about 65 cents per News Corp share.
The service is expected to launch in early 1998 and aims to compete with cable TV operators.

The Australian government appointed stockbrokers on Thursday to manage the proposed sharemarket float of Telstra Corp.
The Telstra float will be the largest privatisation in Australia.
The float is estimated to raise a minimum of A$8.0 billion (US$6.32 billion).
Finance Minister John Fahey stated he wants the Telstra float to occur by the end of the year.
Fahey indicated that it is unclear whether the float of other international telephone companies will affect the timing.
J.B Were & Son, CS First Boston, and ABN AMRO/Rothschild were appointed as global co-ordinators for the float.
Joint lead managers for the float include J.B Were, Ord Minnett, CS First Boston, Goldman Sachs/Macquarie Bank, Daiwa, ABN AMRO/Rothschild, and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The float will not be underwritten in Australia, where 65 percent of the offer is to be sold.
Shares offered in the United States will be underwritten and listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
Two percent of the offer is set aside for Telstra employees, and foreign investors are entitled to 35 percent.

One 2 One is a British mobile telephone company jointly owned by Cable and Wireless Plc and U S West Inc.
One 2 One stated that it is not in talks about joining Cable and Wireless Communications.
Analysts have speculated that One 2 One may join Cable and Wireless Communications.
Cable and Wireless Communications is Britain's largest telephone and television cable company.
Cable and Wireless Communications was formed by the merger of C&W's Mercury phone unit and three British cable divisions of NYNEX Corp and Bell Cablemedia Plc.
A potential deal would require U S West to sell its 50 percent stake in One 2 One.
U S West is also a major shareholder in Telewest Communications Plc, a rival of Cable and Wireless Communications.
Jan Peters, managing director of One 2 One, stated there are no plans or negotiations to join Cable and Wireless Communications.
Peters mentioned that both investors are committed to One 2 One and that the company could benefit from deals with CWC and Telewest.
One 2 One is launching four new customer packages called One 2 Weekend, One 2 30, One 2 100, and One 2 200.

Ameritech Corp is a U.S. local telecoms company.
Ameritech Corp is in merger or acquisition talks with several European security monitoring firms worth $200-$500 million each.
Dennis LaComb is the international affairs director of Ameritech.
Ameritech hopes to double its current $4.0 billion European investments over the next few years.
The majority of Ameritech's international investment is in Europe.
Ameritech has taken stakes in privatisations abroad in countries such as Hungary and New Zealand over the past six years.
Ameritech has a conservative approach of focused and disciplined investment.
Ameritech is America's second biggest security monitoring group.
Ameritech aims to become the pan-European market leader in security monitoring.
Ameritech is considering firms in Germany, France, Scandinavia, and Britain for potential deals.

Concerns about the loss of two top executives and an equity stake in terrestrial digital TV have negatively impacted BSkyB shares.
BSkyB shares fell 14.5p to 483p in afternoon trade.
Around 1.7 billion pounds ($2.8 billion) has been lost in the value of British Sky Broadcasting since last week.
Analysts predict further weakness in BSkyB shares.
News Corp Ltd is the largest shareholder in BSkyB.
Jason Crisp, a media analyst at SocGen, stated that there has been a re-rating of BSkyB shares and it is expected to continue.
Another broker suggested that BSkyB shares could only be valued at 450p in optimistic scenarios.
Negative reports in newspapers contributed to the decline in BSkyB shares.
The Financial Times reported that the Independent Television Commission advised BSkyB to drop its one-third stake in a consortium with Carlton Communications and Granada Group.
SocGen's Crisp noted that BSkyB shares should be trading nearer to 400p due to various negative factors affecting the company.

Informix Corp is investing in a new generation of database software products.
Informix aims to increase its revenue by 30 percent in 1997.
Phil White is the CEO of Informix.
Informix's top priority is to enhance marketing rather than sales.
Phil White stated that Wall Street believes he is investing too heavily due to insufficient revenue growth.
Informix is based in Menlo Park, California.
Informix develops computer programs for storing and retrieving corporate information.
Informix's flagship database product is used by companies such as MCI Communications Corp and CS First Boston.
In December, Informix introduced Universal Server, which can handle various types of data including text, numbers, photographs, maps, sound, and video.
Informix's stock has lost more than half its value in the past 12 months.

Versant Object Technology Corp is a database software company.
Versant expects to do more business with MCI Communications Corp.
David Banks is the CEO of Versant.
Versant is based in Menlo Park, California.
MCI is still a customer of Versant.
Versant's stock declined significantly after MCI halted a major project.
Versant supplied MCI with fundamental software for the halted project, code-named Horizon.
In 1996, Versant's sales of software to MCI totaled about $4.8 million.
MCI placed a $3.9 million order for Versant software in June.
MCI paid Versant $4.4 million after renegotiating the contract in the fourth quarter.

Apple Computer Inc. announced it will cut 4,100 jobs, nearly a third of its workforce.
Apple will discontinue its consumer computer line to reduce costs and return to profitability.
The restructuring will cost Apple a total of $250 million in charges to earnings over the next three quarters.
Apple expects revenue for its fiscal second quarter to decline by 22 percent to about $1.6 billion due to weak Macintosh sales.
Apple plans to drop its Macintosh Performa PCs to focus on its more profitable Power Macintosh line.
Chairman Gilbert Amelio stated that it is painful to lay off employees who have worked hard to improve Apple.
Amelio indicated that Apple needs to cut $500 million in annual costs to break even this year.
Analysts noted that Apple was bold to cut jobs and discontinue a key brand but lacks a clear sales recovery plan.
Apple will not ship its revamped operating system, code-named 'Rhapsody,' until at least June 1998.
The job cuts will include 2,700 full-time employees and 1,400 contract workers, with 60-day notices to be given later this month.

Toronto stocks ended mixed on Monday.
Weak gold and forestry stocks offset strong bank issues.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 15.57 points to close at 6242.42.
The index was short of its life-time high of 6260.73 reached on February 19.
Declining issues outnumbered advances 506 to 497.
277 stocks were unchanged.
Toronto's trading volume was 95.4 million shares worth C$1.5 billion.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 76.58 points to close at 7008.20.
The rise in New York was aided by strength in high-technology stocks.
Toronto's financial services sector rose 48 points.

Yogen Fruz World-Wide Inc is proposing to expand by partnering with Subway Restaurants and PepsiCo Inc's KFC unit.
The partnership with fast food chains is part of a trend called co-branding.
Yogen Fruz has over 2,920 outlets and is the world's largest frozen yogurt franchisor.
First Marathon Securities analyst Perry Caicco has a 52-week share price target of C$6.00 for Yogen Fruz.
Shares of Yogen Fruz on the Toronto Stock Exchange rose by 0.35 to 4.84 in late trading.
The increase in share price was influenced by news that Gordon Capital will issue an analyst's report on Yogen Fruz.
First Marathon helped underwrite a private placement of five million special Yogen Fruz warrants at C$4 each.
Yogen Fruz is testing its products with Subway in 20 U.S. locations.
Yogen Fruz is also experimenting with KFC in some outlets in Panama.
Destination Products International, an offshoot of Cott Corp, is exploring selling new flavors of Yogen Fruz in U.S. grocery stores.

Toronto stocks closed lower on Wednesday due to fears of Canadian interest rate hikes.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index decreased by 20.92 points to 6122.84.
Trading volume was 93.6 million shares worth C$1.3 billion ($949 million).
Ron Meisels, a Montreal-based portfolio consultant, stated that Canadian markets usually react to U.S. market changes a day later.
U.S. markets declined after a quarter-point rise in the U.S. Fed Funds rate.
Meisels expressed concern that Canada might experience similar interest rate increases.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes, 10 declined, particularly in banks, pipelines, transportation, and consumer products.
The sectors that performed well included real estate, gold, utilities, and industrial products.
Declining issues outnumbered advancing issues by a ratio of almost two to one, with 639 declines and 348 advances.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. faced trading halts due to reports of 'insignificant amounts of gold' in its Busang discovery in Indonesia.

China may have sufficient copper supplies for the next few months, reducing the need to purchase on the world market.
Copper stored in Shanghai warehouses could be around 100,000 tonnes, according to a Chinese trader.
Shanghai Metal Exchange (SME) reported copper stocks at 16,772 tonnes, which is approximately two months' supply.
A Chinese trading source confirmed that Shanghai warehouses held 80,000 tonnes of central reserve copper.
There have been ongoing discussions about a potential 100,000 tonnes of copper stockpiled in Shanghai, which officials have denied knowledge of.
An additional 200,000 tonnes of copper were reportedly channeled into China following trading losses revealed by Japan's Sumitomo Corp.
The copper moved out of bonded warehouses and through customs in October and November 1996 was possibly purchased by China National Non-ferrous Metals Import/Export Corp.
Analysts from Shanghai Colub Consultant Co estimated China's carryover copper stocks from 1996 imports could be as high as 250,000 tonnes.
China Daily Business Weekly reported a 1996 stockpile of 170,000 tonnes of copper to address the domestic supply/demand gap in 1997.
Official figures indicated that 1996 imports of raw and uncast copper increased by 32.7 percent to 714,248 tonnes, with net imports at 580,600 tonnes.

China has decided to resume corn exports.
China's decision could pressure the United States and other producers to discount their grain.
A U.S. trader predicted a price war due to China's decision.
Traders reported that U.S. corn prices are already being discounted by US$3-$4 a tonne.
China banned overseas sales of corn in December 1994 to rebuild central stocks.
Total sales of Chinese corn to Southeast Asia could reach 300,000 tonnes by the end of the week.
Some traders believe the sales do not indicate a full lifting of the export ban.
Other traders suggest the sales could signal an influx of Chinese corn onto the world market.
Chinese corn sales this year could reach one million tonnes according to some traders.
At least 76,000 tonnes of corn have been confirmed sold to South Korea for April/May arrival.

Chinese sugar processors have begun hoarding white sugar.
Traders and industry watchers reported this trend on Wednesday.
Factories are reluctant to sell sugar to stabilize prices.
Factories aim to recover their costs by holding onto their product.
Wholesale prices for white sugar in China have not exceeded 3,800 yuan per tonne for several weeks.
The breakeven point for sugar factories is around 4,000 yuan per tonne.
No price movement is expected before the lunar new year holiday.
Guangdong and Guangxi are China's main sugar-producing provinces.
Total sugar production for the current season is expected to be 6.6 million tonnes.
China's annual sugar demand is estimated at eight million tonnes.

Russia expects an increased grain harvest but lower carryover stocks this year.
Industry sources indicate that Russia is unlikely to make significant imports soon.
Arkady Zlochevsky is the head of the OGO commodities trading company.
Zlochevsky mentioned that soy and maize buying is a possibility for Russia.
Zlochevsky has been purchasing some Brazilian and Argentine soymeal.
Farm Minister Viktor Khlystun stated that Russia may import 4.0-4.5 million tonnes of maize and soymeal and 500,000 tonnes of food wheat.
Khlystun's import figures are intended to supplement the 1996 harvest and low carryover from the previous year.
A senior Western grains source noted that Russia's grain needs do not guarantee imports.
Russian 1996 net grain harvest predictions range from 69 to 75 million tonnes.
Khlystun has not approached major Western grains exporters in Moscow regarding potential purchases.

Russia's net grain harvest is expected to fall below the official forecast of 75-77 million tonnes.
Andrei Sizov of SovEcon Ltd revised his forecast down to about 68 million tonnes from a previous 70 million tonnes.
Russia lost 2.9 million hectares of grain to drought.
It is likely that the lost area will not be harvested due to high costs exceeding the value of the grain.
The Western Siberian harvest is described as mixed, with good quality grain but a slow harvest.
Sizov estimates the output in Western Siberia at 9.3 million tonnes.
Some crops in Western Siberia are likely to be left to rot due to incomplete harvesting.
A senior Western grains source stated that the government would likely declare the net grain harvest at 72 million tonnes.
The source noted that the government has under-reported the actual total for the last two years.
An Agriculture Ministry spokeswoman confirmed that the ministry is maintaining its forecast of 75-77 million tonnes.

Russia's top aluminium smelters reported unsuccessful attempts to fix contracts with Ukraine's main raw materials supplier.
Ukraine is courting a rival smelter in Tajikistan instead of supplying Russia.
Russia is seeking supply contracts from Ukraine's Mykolayivsky Hlynozemny plant for alumina.
Russian metals officials stated that Mykolayivskiy has been reluctant to supply alumina to Russia.
Bratsk and Krasnoyarsk smelters in Russia have received no alumina supplies from Ukraine this year.
Yuri Shlaifshtein, a board member at Bratsk, stated that no agreement has been reached with Mykolayivskiy over supplies.
Shlaifshtein claimed that Mykolayivskiy is asking prices above world levels for alumina.
Hennady Bushtruk, deputy commercial director of Mykolayivskiy, indicated that the plant planned to sell 90 percent of its 1997 output to Russia, but no contracts were signed.
Shlaifshtein mentioned that Mykolayivskiy was asking around $270 per tonne for alumina.
Mykolayivskiy has a production capacity of one million tonnes of alumina per year.

French chemical group Rhone-Poulenc SA and Merck & Co Inc of the U.S. announced a merger of their animal health activities.
The merger will create a new 50/50 joint venture company named Merial.
Merial is expected to have estimated sales of $1.750 billion in 1996.
Merial will be the market leader in biology products, veterinary drugs, and poultry drugs.
Merial will surpass Pfizer-Smithkline Beecham, Bayer, and Novartis in the animal health sector.
Igor Landau, managing director of Rhone-Poulenc, stated that the merger would cut costs and affect jobs.
Merck will make an unspecified payment to Rhone for the 50/50 parity.
The joint venture will merge the animal health activities of Rhone Merieux and Merck AgVet.
John Preston from Merck will lead the joint venture in the first few years, followed by Louis Champel from Rhone.
Rhone Merieux's main product, Frontline, had sales of $85 million in 1996 and expects to double sales in 1997.

French conglomerate Generale des Eaux is in talks with Havas regarding Canal Plus.
Generale des Eaux and Havas issued a joint statement confirming discussions about audiovisual activities.
The announcement was made before the stock exchange opened.
Press reports indicated that Generale des Eaux would become the key shareholder in Havas.
Havas would then become the biggest shareholder in Canal Plus.
The companies will not provide further comments until board meetings on February 6.
A corporate source confirmed that Alcatel Alsthom is discussing the sale of part of its 21.2 percent stake in Havas to Generale des Eaux.
Generale des Eaux owns almost 20 percent of Canal Plus.
Canal Plus is merging with Nethold to create Europe's largest subscription television company.
Generale des Eaux would transfer its Canal Plus stake into Havas, potentially doubling Havas's stake in Canal Plus.

The French telecommunications market will open to full competition in 1998.
Analysts believe the market is becoming more competitive despite denials from Nippon Telecom and Telegraph Co (NTT) about entering the market.
1997 is expected to be a year full of alliances and deals in the telecommunications sector.
A Paris-based analyst stated that companies need to act now to be present in France after liberalization.
The Financial Times reported that NTT plans to invest $500 million for a 10 percent stake in Cegetel alongside British Telecom Plc.
A spokesman for Cegetel stated that no changes are planned in its shareholding capital.
Cegetel's capital structure will remain as announced in September, involving British Telecom, Mannesmann, and SBC Communications Inc.
British Telecom will hold approximately 25 percent, SBC will hold 15 percent, and Mannesmann will hold 10 percent of Cegetel.
NTT stated it is not considering investing in the French telecommunications market.
From January 1, 1998, France Telecom will lose its monopoly but will remain majority state-owned and responsible for public telecommunications services.

Woodside Petroleum Ltd is an Australian oil and gas producer.
Woodside is expected to report a 44 percent increase in annual profit on Wednesday.
The increase is attributed to the first full year of production from the Wanaea-Cossack fields.
Petroleum analysts forecast Woodside's net profit before abnormal items to be between A$194 million and A$217 million for calendar 1996.
The average forecast is A$202.8 million, which is a 44 percent increase from 1995's pre-abnormal profit of A$140.5 million.
Analysts indicated that the 1996 result could have been better if production problems at Wanaea-Cossack had been resolved.
David Cliff, an analyst with Burdett, Buckeridge and Young, stated that the brokerage revised its forecast to A$196.6 million for 1996.
The Wanaea-Cossack fields began production in November 1995.
Production issues have prevented output from reaching the design capacity of approximately 115,000 barrels per day.
Woodside's hedging book also contributed to limiting profits in 1996.

Pasminco Ltd is a zinc producer.
Pasminco Ltd plans to issue shares on the Australian stock market.
The share issue aims to fund the development of the Century zinc project, estimated to cost A$1 billion.
Pasminco has engaged J.B. Were and SBC Warburg as underwriters for the equity issue.
Bronwyn Constance is the executive general manager of finance at Pasminco.
Pasminco expects to announce its market plans within three months.
Pasminco aims to raise up to A$1 billion from equity and debt markets for the Century zinc deposit.
The Century zinc deposit is one of the largest in northern Australia.
Pasminco has approached both domestic and international banks for a syndicated loan.
Pasminco has conditionally agreed to buy the Century project and associated deposits for A$345 million from RTZ-CRA.

Australia's Trust Bank is seeking a strategic equity partner.
Trust Bank is inviting offers for a 49 percent stake.
Trust Bank aims to increase its visibility and presence.
Australian banks and foreign entities not aligned with Trust Bank's expansion goals are excluded from the partnership search.
Managing director Paul Kemp stated that quick profit-seekers will not be considered as partners.
Kemp addressed media speculation regarding interest in the stake for issuing credit cards in Australia.
Kemp emphasized that Trust Bank seeks a partner with a broader vision for financial services beyond credit cards.
Trust Bank has assets of approximately A$1.8 billion.
Trust Bank is the dominant home lender in Tasmania.
Trust Bank has four branches outside of Tasmania but has national ambitions.

Microsoft Corp. is launching its online venture, Sidewalk, on Thursday.
Sidewalk will initially be launched in Seattle and expand to 10 to 15 cities by the end of the year.
Cities included in the expansion are New York, Washington, San Francisco, and Sydney, Australia.
Microsoft has a cash reserve of $10 billion.
Analyst Larry Gerbrandt believes Microsoft will be a major presence in the local news market.
Microsoft's strategy focuses on listings for entertainment and leisure activities.
Gayle Troberman, consumer marketing manager for Sidewalk, stated that consumers have less free time.
The Seattle Sidewalk site allows users to personalize content and set reminders for events.
The site features articles from about 14 full-time journalists and searchable databases of rated movies, restaurants, and events.
Michael Fancher, executive editor of The Seattle Times, expressed concern about competition from Microsoft.

Boeing Co. formed an entrepreneurial organization called Boeing Enterprises.
Boeing Enterprises will seek joint ventures and acquisitions related to commercial airplanes.
Lawrence Clarkson is the senior vice president of planning and international development at Boeing.
Lawrence Clarkson will serve as president of Boeing Enterprises.
Boeing Enterprises is part of Boeing's commercial airplane group.
Clarkson stated that Boeing Enterprises is seeking significant projects and could grow rapidly in the next year.
Clarkson indicated that ongoing negotiations would likely not involve new airplane models.
Boeing Enterprises will manage the joint venture with General Electric Co. to market the 737 as a business jet.
Clarkson mentioned that Boeing is studying the possibility of collaborating with Asian manufacturers to build a new small jet.
Clarkson has been with Boeing since 1987 and previously worked at Pratt & Whitney.

Microsoft Corp Chief Financial Officer Mike Brown expects fourth quarter results to be similar to the third quarter.
Mike Brown described the third quarter as 'sizzling.'
Mike Brown anticipates Microsoft's growth to slow over the next five quarters due to difficult comparisons and a lack of major new upgrades.
The current fourth quarter is expected to show results similar to the $1.04 billion in net income and $3.21 billion in revenues from the period ending March 31.
Mike Brown indicated that the first quarter of fiscal 1998 could show a sequential downturn.
Mike Brown expects results to rise sequentially after the first quarter of fiscal 1998.
The high-end Windows NT Workstation operating system is being pre-loaded on some new personal computers.
The mix shift of Windows NT Workstation is not yet material to Microsoft's OEM revenues.
Mike Brown expects a spike in revenues from the Office 97 upgrade to begin to tail off in the current quarter.
The next upgrade of Office will not be released until fiscal 1999.

Ivory Coast is destroying some cocoa farms in its protected forests.
The impact on the 1996/97 cocoa output will be minimal according to forestry officials and crop analysts.
A state forest agency (SODEFOR) manager stated that nothing has really been done regarding the evictions.
Tanoh Yao, a south coast area manager, mentioned that officials are waiting for practical policies to proceed with evictions.
Ivory Coast reported in March that 30 percent of protected forests were illegally occupied by up to 450,000 farmers and their relatives.
These farmers were growing up to 100,000 tonnes of cocoa, which is roughly one-tenth of the 1996/97 cocoa crop.
World Bank officials estimated the illegal cocoa output at around 50,000 tonnes.
A March 7 decree stated that officials would systematically destroy all plantations in parks and reservations.
The decree included a 'decontamination' period for individual cases and time for farmers to leave their farms.
Donors reported that protected forest cover has decreased from 13 million hectares at independence in 1960 to 3.6 million hectares.

Ivory Coast's cocoa mid-crop could match harvest forecasts of over 150,000 tonnes.
Bean sizes are expected to be down from the record 1995/96 season.
Crop analysts and exporters reported on Thursday that the mid-crop development seems to be progressing well.
Good peak wet season rains in June will determine the final mid-crop tally.
This year's bean sizes are not expected to match the mainly exportable grades seen in the record 1995/96 year.
Last year's mid-crop was 200,000 tonnes and was considered exceptional.
Crop analysts expect bean sizes to return to more normal levels in the range of 110-120, with lowest grades possibly touching 150.
Ivory Coast's main crop reached around one million tonnes by April 27.
Crop analysts reported that plantation soil moisture levels had dropped in some areas after heavy rains in April.
Crop analysts returning from farm inspections reported little harvesting and drying of cocoa.

Rains continued across Ivory Coast's cocoa belt in late April.
The onset of wet season patterns was confirmed by weather and crop analysts.
Mid-crop and early 1996/97 main crop prospects were boosted.
A favorable weather pattern developed in April with strengthening rains.
A band of rain that usually sits 200 km south of the tropical weather front was over cocoa areas.
Official rainfall data for the third 10 days of April totaled 789.2 mm.
Rains fell mainly in south coast areas between Abidjan and Tabou.
Overall 1997 rainfall was put at just below average by one crop analyst.
End-April rains were likely to have brought rainfall levels back to average.
The total 1996/97 cocoa crop is expected to be near last year's record of 1.2 million tonnes.

Republic Industries is expected to meet full-year 1997 share-profit estimates of $0.70.
Mike Karsher is the chief financial officer of Republic Industries.
All four segments of Republic Industries performed well in the first quarter of 1997.
The diversified services group of Republic Industries plans to accelerate the opening of AutoNation used-car superstores in 1997.
Karsher stated that the new superstores would not contribute to 1997 full-year profits due to initial losses.
Republic Industries is currently on an acquisition campaign.
In the past six months, Republic Industries acquired major car-rental agencies such as Alamo and various car dealerships in the United States.
For the first quarter of 1997, Republic Industries reported a doubling of share profits to $0.08 compared to the same period in 1996.
The share profits for the first quarter of 1997 were $0.01 higher than the consensus of Wall Street analysts' forecasts.
Net income for Republic Industries grew to $28.9 million in the first quarter of 1997, up from $12.4 million in the same period in 1996.

Cigarette makers are negotiating with anti-tobacco activists regarding smoking lawsuits.
The discussions focus on tighter government regulation of tobacco and eliminating sales pitches to youths.
Less than 5 percent of the negotiation time has been spent discussing financial matters.
The talks began about two weeks ago between industry executives and anti-tobacco leaders.
The next session of talks is scheduled for Sunday in Chicago.
A second session is planned for Monday, with a break for the Passover holiday.
No additional talks are scheduled for the following week.
State attorneys general are involved in the negotiations regarding Medicaid costs.
Washington politicians and some health groups have criticized certain proposals as insufficient.
Tobacco company stock prices rose due to speculation about a potential settlement.

A settlement among state governments and tobacco companies would not resolve many anti-smoking lawsuits.
There is a $5 billion claim scheduled for trial on June 2.
Stanley Rosenblatt is a lawyer involved in the Broin class-action suit for flight attendants claiming injuries from secondhand smoke.
Rosenblatt's case is significant as it is the first class-action suit against cigarette makers to survive preliminary legal challenges.
Rosenblatt's case is also the first trial of a claim for damages from secondhand smoke.
There are approximately 1,000 anti-tobacco lawsuits against tobacco companies in U.S. courts.
Norwood Wilner secured a $750,000 jury judgment against Brown & Williamson in 1996.
Wilner has a trial scheduled for August 4 for a case involving a woman with lung cancer.
Wilner lost a suit on May 5 for smoker Jean Connor against RJ Reynolds Tobacco Co.
There are additional anti-tobacco cases expected to go to trial in 1997, including a class-action for Florida smokers and a secondhand smoke case in Mississippi.

China ordered two 747 airliners from Boeing Co.
The deal is valued in the multimillion dollar range.
U.S. Ambassador to China James Sasser stated that the deal was hastened by upcoming visits from U.S. congressmen.
The jets will be powered by Pratt and Whitney engines.
The delivery of the jets is scheduled for 1999 to Air China.
The contract is valued at $383 million.
Air China previously purchased three 747-400s in July of the previous year.
A bipartisan delegation of around 22 U.S. congressmen is scheduled to visit Beijing next week.
The visit is expected to address issues such as the Sino-U.S. trade balance and human rights.
The United States reported a trade deficit with China of nearly $29 billion in the first nine months of the previous year.

Beijing's young people attended Catholic churches on Christmas Eve.
Young men and women stood on their seats in St Joseph's church to watch the midnight mass.
Around 10,000 people were expected to visit St Joseph's throughout the evening.
More than 1,000 people attended the Chinese-language midnight mass at St Joseph's.
Only a small fraction of the visitors at the mass were Christians.
A worshipper in her 70s stated that most attendees were non-believers.
One young visitor admitted to attending church for fun and not believing in God.
The atmosphere at the church resembled that of a nightclub, according to a U.S. visitor.
Hundreds of mostly youthful onlookers visited St Joseph's before the midnight mass.
Beijing has an estimated 70,000 Catholics, and all are banned from acknowledging the Vatican.

A British minister stated that a World Trade Organisation (WTO) without China is incomplete.
Ian Lang is the president of Britain's Board of Trade.
Lang made his comments during a news conference in Beijing.
Lang expressed support for China's application to join the WTO.
Lang emphasized that China's accession must be on the same terms as other countries.
Lang mentioned the importance of not diluting the strength of the WTO.
Beijing has been seeking to join the WTO with developing country status.
Some Western nations believe China's economy is too large for developing country status.
A WTO working group is scheduled to meet in Geneva later this year to negotiate China's accession.
Lang indicated that China and Britain are expected to sign a memorandum of understanding next month regarding Chinese companies listing on the London Stock Exchange.

GTE Corp. offered a nationwide long distance calling plan that is one cent cheaper than AT&T Corp.'s flat-rate plan.
GTE's flat rate plan is called 'GTE's One Easy Rate,' charging 14 cents a minute at any time.
GTE's One Easy Rate has no monthly or enrollment fee.
The plan is available to consumers in 27 states where GTE offers local or wireless services and long distance.
GTE may expand the plan to 23 additional states where it offers only long distance services.
AT&T charges 15 cents per minute for its One Rate plan.
MCI Communications Corp. charges 14.5 cents for its True Rate plan.
Sprint Corp. charges 15 cents for its Sense Day plan.
GTE's existing long distance rates are 27 cents a minute during peak hours and 14 cents off peak.
GTE entered the long distance business in March 1996 and signed up 800,000 customers by the end of that year.

Regional telephone companies reported strong fourth-quarter results.
The growth was driven by increasing demand for Internet phone lines, wireless services, caller ID, and call waiting.
Companies' shares are affected by competition with long distance companies.
NYNEX Corp. reported a net income increase of 10 percent to $416.5 million in the fourth quarter.
NYNEX's revenue increased by 0.9 percent to $3.33 billion.
Bell Atlantic Corp. reported a profit decrease to $346 million in the fourth quarter.
Bell Atlantic's sales grew to $3.4 billion.
Excluding one-time items, Bell Atlantic's operating income increased by 7.3 percent to $424 million.
Bell Atlantic and NYNEX agreed to merge in April 1996.
Bell Atlantic earned $1.88 billion on revenue of $13.1 billion for the year.

BellSouth Corp reported strong earnings for the fourth quarter.
BellSouth's earnings were one cent above consensus estimates.
The company experienced strong access line growth and cellular customer expansion.
BellSouth's earnings per share before one-off items increased by 12.3 percent to $0.64 from $0.57 a year ago.
The First Call consensus for earnings per share was $0.63.
Total operating revenues rose six percent to $5.05 billion from $4.76 billion in the fourth quarter.
Operating expenses rose 5.7 percent, excluding year-ago charges.
BellSouth's access line growth was 4.7 percent in the fourth quarter compared to a year earlier.
This access line growth was below the previous quarter's growth of 4.9 percent.
SBC Communications Inc and Ameritech Corp reported moderation in line growth.

Quaker Oats Co. may take a charge of up to $1 billion to write down its Snapple beverage business.
The charge may not appear in Quaker Oats' fourth quarter earnings report expected next week.
BT Securities analyst John O'Neil estimated the charge to write down Snapple could be close to $1 billion.
In November, Quaker Oats announced it would review Snapple to determine if a charge was necessary.
Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Michael Mauboussin stated the probability of a write-down is reasonably high.
Mauboussin also estimated the charge could be about $1 billion.
Quaker spokesman Ronald Bottrell confirmed a review of Snapple's operations is ongoing but did not comment on a potential charge.
Sanford Bernstein analyst Steven Galbraith believes Quaker will be compelled to take a charge for Snapple.
Galbraith suggested Quaker could avoid a write-down if it sold Snapple along with Gatorade.
Speculation exists that Quaker is considering selling both Snapple and Gatorade.

Kellogg Co. warned about lower earnings for the year.
Kellogg's stock fell $1.125 to $67.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Kellogg's third-quarter earnings are expected to be about 20 percent below $1.05 a share.
Kellogg posted net income of $230 million a year earlier.
Kellogg expects full-year profits for 1996 to be less than $3.48 a share.
Kellogg posted net income of $761.6 million in 1995 before one-time charges.
Kellogg attributed the decline in third-quarter profits to competitive promotions by other cereal companies.
Kellogg and other cereal makers cut retail cereal prices earlier this year.
Kellogg has reduced promotional spending for more than two years.
Kellogg accounts for nearly one-third of the U.S. cereal market.

Kellogg Co. reported a profit for the fourth quarter.
Kellogg Co. reversed a year-ago loss.
The U.S. and British breakfast cereal markets are difficult.
Kellogg is the largest producer in the $9 billion U.S. ready-to-eat cereal market.
Kellogg's domestic cereal sales fell in the quarter.
Analysts estimated the drop in domestic cereal sales was about 5 percent.
Kellogg had a profit of $87.3 million or 42 cents a share in the quarter.
Kellogg reported a loss of $71.6 million or 33 cents a share in the 1996 quarter.
Sales fell 6 percent to $1.56 billion from $1.66 billion.
Kellogg's restructuring is meant to save at least $160 million in savings this year and in future years.

A dispute over civil liberties in Hong Kong has escalated into a diplomatic issue involving Britain and the United States.
Britain and the United States have warned China to respect a treaty pledge regarding basic freedoms in Hong Kong.
The dispute intensified after a Beijing-controlled panel proposed to eliminate Hong Kong laws on civil liberties and elections.
The proposed changes include modifications to part of Hong Kong's Bill of Rights.
China is set to take control of Hong Kong's governance in five months.
London and Washington issued warnings to Beijing regarding the proposed changes.
China has stated that the matter is an internal affair.
Hong Kong's future leader, Tung Chee-hwa, attempted to reduce tensions surrounding the dispute.
The controversy arises from China's plans to remove liberal political arrangements established by Britain in Hong Kong.
China plans to replace the elected Legislative Council with an appointed provisional legislature on July 1.

The United States signed an air services agreement with Hong Kong.
The agreement guarantees future aviation links after Hong Kong's return to China.
Washington expressed concern about rising landing fees at Hong Kong's new airport.
The new airport at Chek Lap Kok is set to open in one year.
Hong Kong's airport authority chief stated discussions with the airline industry are still possible.
U.S. Consul-General Richard Boucher indicated that high landing and parking fees are a concern.
Boucher called for competitive rates for landing and parking at Chek Lap Kok.
Airlines have reported that landing costs could be three to four times higher than at the current Kai Tak airport.
Hong Kong Secretary for Economic Services Stephen Ip mentioned that airport officials are consulting with airlines.
The agreement allows the U.S. to select carriers for non-stop services from three additional gateways.

China continued with a plan to reduce political freedoms in Hong Kong following the death of leader Deng Xiaoping.
Deng Xiaoping was the architect of the 'one country two systems' formula for Hong Kong.
Deng Xiaoping died the previous week.
Thousands of Hong Kong residents participated in a mourning ceremony for Deng Xiaoping.
China's parliament approved a plan to amend or discard several Hong Kong laws.
The laws affected include those related to democratic elections and civil liberties.
The amendments will reduce the bill of rights and laws on political parties and public protests.
These laws were part of Britain's efforts to establish democracy in Hong Kong before the end of British rule.
China accused Britain of violating the 1984 Sino-British handover treaty.
Chris Patten criticized China's National People's Congress for ignoring the wishes of Hong Kong residents.

There was premature talk of a merger between Airbus and Lockheed Martin.
Patrice Kreis is the vice president for corporate communications at Aerospatiale.
Kreis stated that Airbus and Lockheed Martin have interests that could benefit from a merger.
Kreis commented on a report from the London Times regarding merger talks between Airbus and Lockheed Martin.
Kreis indicated that it is too early to discuss a merger between Airbus and Lockheed Martin.
Kreis mentioned that European aerospace and defense companies need to consolidate before pursuing transatlantic mergers.
Key steps for Airbus include changing its partnership into a limited liability company.
Kreis emphasized that Airbus's survival is linked to civilian aircraft, military aircraft, space, and weapons systems.
The creation of large aerospace companies in the United States is pressuring Europe to consolidate.
Aerospatiale is restructuring through a merger with Dassault Aviation and the privatization of Thomson-CSF.

The French government announced the procedure for privatising Thomson-CSF on Wednesday.
The announcement included minimum financial terms and conditions for the sale.
This is the government's second attempt to sell Thomson-CSF after a failed attempt last year.
The successful bidder must acquire more than 50 percent of Thomson-CSF's capital and voting rights.
The government aims to select the winning bidder by June 30.
Bidders must have at least five billion francs in equity capital and the same amount in 1995 turnover in non-consumer and defence electronics.
The government will retain a 'golden share' to maintain control over ownership changes.
In a group bid, the lead company must hold more than a third of Thomson-CSF's capital and voting rights.
Bidders must declare their interest by 1100 GMT on March 28.
Offers must be submitted by 1100 GMT on May 7, and bidders must make an irrevocable offer within four months.

Cie de Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux SA are expected to announce a merger deal on Friday.
The merger will end the independence of Cie de Suez, which was created in the 19th century to build the Suez Canal.
The boards of Cie de Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux SA will meet on Friday to approve the merger terms.
The Lyonnaise board has already backed the merger.
Lyonnaise chairman Jerome Monod stated that the merger with Suez was an excellent plan, but the terms had not yet been fixed.
A source close to the merger talks indicated that the share parity would be 41 Suez shares for every 20 Lyonnaise shares.
Suez stock was down 0.04 percent at 282.90 francs ($48.79) on a volume of 171,495 shares.
Lyonnaise stock was down 0.37 percent at 540 francs.
The market was down 0.63 percent.
Suez is expected to pay out either 3.6 or 3.8 billion francs for the 1996 dividend.

Mid-American Waste Systems Inc filed for bankruptcy on Wednesday.
Mid-American Waste Systems Inc signed an agreement to sell most assets to USA Waste Services Inc.
Mid-American Waste Systems Inc is based in Ohio.
Mid-American Waste Systems Inc suffered financial losses due to acquisitions and development projects.
Melville Cody of Williams MacKay Jordan & Co Inc stated that Mid-American was highly leveraged and losing money.
Mid-American will sell nearly all its assets to USA Waste Services for $180 million in cash and stock.
The transaction is subject to bankruptcy court approval.
Mid-American's chief executive Gene Meredith was unavailable for comment on Wednesday.
Mid-American sold its Atlanta assets to Republic Industries Inc nearly a year ago.
USA Waste Services' revenue increased from about $4 million in 1990 to an estimated $2 billion in 1997.

Norfolk Southern Corp was preparing to buy nearly 10 percent of Conrail Inc.
The purchase would further cement a stalemate in the fight for control of Conrail.
Conrail and CSX Corp. were assessing their strategy after a shareholder defeat.
The proposed merger between Conrail and CSX was valued at $9.4 billion.
About 53 percent of Conrail's outstanding shares were voted against a key measure.
Norfolk Southern promised to acquire 9.9 percent of Conrail for $115 a share.
The 9.9 percent investment is the maximum amount Norfolk Southern can purchase without triggering Conrail's poison pill defense.
CSX needs approval from Conrail shareholders to proceed with its transaction.
Conrail is prohibited from merging with another company until 1999 under its pact with CSX.
Conrail plans to schedule another shareholder vote regarding the proposed transaction with CSX.

ITT Corp expects the sale of its non-core assets to take up to six months.
The Madison Square Garden properties are likely to be sold more quickly.
ITT Corp has held high-level talks with Cablevision Systems Corp about acquiring its 50 percent stake in Madison Square Garden.
No deal has been struck between ITT Corp and Cablevision Systems Corp.
Cablevision is considered the primary potential acquirer of the Madison Square Garden stake.
ITT Corp has held discussions with potential buyers about other properties, including its international telephone directories business.
The discussions about other properties are not in advanced stages.
ITT Corp has hired Morgan Stanley to assist with the asset sales.
ITT Corp is also being advised by Lazard Freres and Chase Securities.
ITT Corp rejected a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid from Hilton Hotels Corp.

Rupert Murdoch is making a public pitch for his $1 billion Sky satellite-broadcast venture.
Murdoch's Sky venture is intended to compete with cable television.
Stephen Effros is the president of the Cable Telecommunications Association.
Effros expressed concern that Murdoch is trying to accumulate excessive power.
Murdoch is lobbying Congress for legislation that would benefit his new venture.
Sky is expected to launch in early 1998.
Sky is projected to offer over 500 channels of high-quality digital TV and Internet services.
Sky will retransmit local TV broadcasts representing more than 75 percent of U.S. TV households.
Direct broadcast satellite operators have nearly 5 million subscribers, an increase from nearly zero three years ago.
Industry analysts believe Murdoch has the motivation, capital, experience, and confidence to succeed against cable operators.

The Clinton administration supports legislation to prevent state and local governments from taxing the Internet.
The proposed bill would impose an indefinite moratorium on Internet taxes by state and local governments.
The bill would not affect existing taxes on goods and services ordered through the Internet if they are the same as mail-order taxes.
The moratorium aims to give the Clinton administration time to develop a plan for addressing taxes on electronic commerce.
Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers expressed support for the Internet Tax Freedom Act.
Summers stated that unreasonable taxation of the Internet could hinder its growth and electronic commerce.
State and local officials oppose the bill, claiming it infringes on their powers and creates budget problems.
Timothy Kaine, a council member from Richmond, Virginia, spoke against the bill on behalf of state and local organizations.
The National Governors Association also opposes the bill.
Some states have begun imposing taxes on companies that provide Internet access or related services.

The government's latest auction of airwaves raised $13.6 million.
The auction concluded on a Friday.
The total amount raised was significantly less than the $1.8 billion expected by Congress.
Some wireless communications market licenses sold for $1 each.
Ken Johnson is a spokesman for Representative Billy Tauzin.
The Federal Communications Commission sold rights for spectrum that allows Internet access over airwaves.
Top bidders included BellSouth Corp., Bell Atlantic Corp.-Nynex Corp., and Comcast Corp.
BellSouth Corp. bid $6.2 million for 22 licenses in various cities.
Licenses for Guam and American Samoa received no bids.
The FCC auctioned 128 licenses starting April 15.

Apple Computer Inc. is seeking outside investment in its Newton computer group.
Larry Tesler is the chief scientist at Apple.
Apple is particularly focused on investment for its eMate product.
Apple has decided to stop funding at least a dozen technology projects.
The Newton unit was not discontinued during last month's restructuring.
Larry Tesler stated that Apple is receiving positive reviews for its latest Newton offerings.
Demand for the eMate, priced around $800, is strong.
A small group of Apple executives is exploring alternatives to increase investment in the Newton business.
Apple plans to cut spending by an average of 25 percent across the company.
Apple is set to report its second quarter results on April 16.

Microsoft Corp Chief Technology Officer Nathan Myhrvold announced plans to triple the size of the company's basic research arm.
Microsoft's basic research staff will increase from 180 to 540.
Myhrvold stated that research has made significant contributions to Microsoft products.
Every major Microsoft product line includes features developed in its research labs.
Microsoft has allocated $2 billion for research and development spending in the fiscal year ending June 30, 1997.
Microsoft Research currently receives between $20 million and $40 million, or one to two percent of the overall budget.
Myhrvold expressed a desire to increase Microsoft Research's budget to about five percent of the overall budget.
Myhrvold and Rick Rashid stated that Microsoft's commitment to basic research could surpass that of established laboratories like Bell Labs.
Research at Microsoft includes projects on speech recognition and synthesis.
Myhrvold predicted that effective speech applications are three to five years away and that future innovations will significantly enhance current technology.

Internet stocks have gained prominence in the investment arena alongside Intel Corp and Cisco Corp.
Many investors are uncertain about the market outlook for 1997.
Tech sector stocks have declined due to uncertainty regarding the 1997 market.
Investment in technology stocks is shifting from momentum investing to value investing, according to some investors and analysts.
Keith Benjamin is a senior research analyst at Robertson Stephens who covers Internet media content and services companies.
Investors are being more selective than they were a year ago when Internet stocks were highly sought after.
One investor for a European fund stated that investors are looking for stable revenue streams and annuity-type businesses.
Some investors expressed frustration with the number of business plans presented, particularly those related to Internet companies.
Robert Herwick is the head of Herwick Capital Management and noted the recent sell-off in networking stocks could affect chip-makers.
Micron Technologies Inc. reported a 50 percent increase in spot prices for 16-megabit computer memory chips in recent weeks.

Anson Chan is Hong Kong's top civil servant.
Anson Chan has indicated a rift and rising tension in the new Beijing-approved administration.
The handover of control from Britain to China is scheduled for July 1.
Anson Chan has called for prompt elections, a credible legislature, and respect for civil liberties.
Anson Chan stated she is prepared to resign if asked to accept policies that conflict with her principles.
Anson Chan is 57 years old and is the deputy to departing colonial governor Chris Patten.
Anson Chan has been asked to remain in her position as second-in-command to future leader Tung Chee-hwa.
Tung Chee-hwa is a conservative and former shipping magnate.
Anson Chan's remarks suggest speculation of rifts between Tung and his top officials.
Anson Chan expressed strong support for the gradual introduction of democracy in Hong Kong.

A panel of experts stated that merging the Hong Kong dollar with China's renminbi is impossible in the short-term and unlikely in the long-term.
The experts indicated that a currency merger could only be considered once China's capital account is fully open.
The experts estimated that it could take at least five years for China's capital account to be fully open.
T.C. Chan, head of investment banking for Citibank in Hong Kong, stated that the renminbi is not a fully-convertible currency.
Chan claimed that Hong Kong needs a convertible currency to maintain its status as an international financial centre.
The agreements governing Hong Kong's reversion to Chinese control and the Basic Law provide for 50 years of autonomous control of Hong Kong's monetary system.
Chan asserted that the merging of the Hong Kong dollar with the renminbi is legally not possible.
Andrew Freris, managing director at Bank of America in Hong Kong, stated that reforming state-owned enterprises (SOEs) is key to convertibility for China.
Freris noted that SOEs have compromised China's banking sector due to their debt.
Freris expressed that the establishment of a fully-functioning interbank market is necessary for market-determined interest rates.

Tung Chee-hwa is the future leader of Hong Kong.
Tung Chee-hwa returned from meetings with Chinese officials on Wednesday.
Tung Chee-hwa expressed a softer stance on plans to restrict civil liberties after the handover to China.
Tung Chee-hwa stated he would tolerate public calls for his resignation and burning of his effigy.
Tung Chee-hwa emphasized the importance of public order in Hong Kong.
Tung Chee-hwa described Hong Kong society as stable and successful.
Tung Chee-hwa's proposals would require police permission for public demonstrations and prohibit foreign funding for local political parties.
Tung Chee-hwa claimed his proposals are less restrictive than laws in most North American cities.
Tung Chee-hwa's inner cabinet is drafting legislation to change the laws.
Tung Chee-hwa reiterated his commitment to a democratic society in Hong Kong.

A powerful earthquake struck northwest China on Saturday.
The earthquake killed at least two people and injured three.
About 50 people died in a tremor in January in the same area.
The earthquake measured 6.0 on the Richter scale.
The earthquake jolted Jiashi county in Xinjiang at 2.04 p.m. (0604 GMT).
An official reported that two people have died and two have been seriously injured.
A total of three people had been injured according to a seismological official in Urumqi.
Residents, many of whom are sheep herders or cotton farmers, were frightened by the tremor.
Many buildings around the local television station had cracked but none had collapsed.
Authorities in Jiashi started relief activities and aid teams from other parts of Xinjiang were preparing to help.

The China-appointed committee handling the handover of Hong Kong voted to support Beijing's decision to roll back civil liberties.
Only one of the 150 members of the Preparatory Committee voted against the motion to approve Beijing's plans.
Ten committee members abstained from the vote.
The vote was held at the close of a two-day session in Beijing.
Frederick Fung, chairman of the Hong Kong Association for Democracy and People's Livelihood, cast the sole dissenting vote.
Allen Lee, chairman of the pro-China, pro-business Liberal Party, abstained from the vote.
China's Basic Law is claimed to fully protect Hong Kong's future autonomy and residents' political and civil rights.
Beijing plans to repeal or amend 25 of Hong Kong's laws and ordinances, including parts of the Bill of Rights and regulations on public assembly.
Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten criticized the plan as a proposal to dilute the territory's civil liberties.
Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's post-colonial leader, supported Beijing's plans and stated that the Basic Law provides freedom and rights.

Chinese authorities imposed a curfew on a town in northwestern Xinjiang after at least 10 people were killed in a separatist riot.
The riot occurred last Wednesday when 1,000 Muslim separatists of the Uighur ethnic minority protested against Beijing rule.
At least 10 people were killed and many were wounded during the riot.
Both Han Chinese and Uighurs were killed or injured in the riot.
A Chinese source stated that the riot was among the most violent in years in Xinjiang.
Moslems are the majority in Xinjiang, while ethnic Han Chinese make up 38 percent of the population.
A local resident reported that a circular was issued ordering people not to go out after dark.
Local officials described the riot as a small incident fueled by unidentified foreign hostile forces.
The Chinese source reported that at least 10 people were killed, including one police officer, and many were wounded and arrested.
The riot erupted after a Chinese policeman attempted to arrest a Uighur criminal suspect.

The long-term prospects for Lloyd's reinsurance vehicle Equitas are uncertain.
Equitas is part of the recovery plans of the world's oldest insurance market.
A report from auditors Coopers & Lybrand indicated 'significant uncertainties' about claims against Equitas.
Equitas was established to run off Lloyd's pre-1993 losses.
The report warned that Equitas could be pushed into insolvency.
Management of Equitas took a relatively positive view of the audit.
The board has emphasized the doubts regarding the project's success or failure.
Analysts state it is too early to determine the company's eventual liabilities and funding adequacy.
Equitas' accounts showed a reduction of 122 million pounds in the surplus of assets to liabilities.
Approximately 40 percent of Equitas' 10.4 billion pounds of discounted liabilities are related to asbestos, pollution, and health claims.

Insurance broker C.E. Heath announced that senior management were in advanced talks about a possible buyout of the company for just under 100 million pounds.
The buyout would value the shares at 143 pence each, a premium of 63 percent over the day's opening price.
Group chief executive John Mackenzie Green is involved in the possible offer.
Non-executive directors are considering the buyout approach.
Over three million shares changed hands on the day of the announcement.
The high stock activity prompted the company to release the news early.
The success of the bid depends on fund management group PDFM, which owns 22 percent of Heath.
Hambros holds a 13 percent stake in Heath.
Fidelity also has a 13 percent stake in Heath, and Equitable Life owns just under five percent.
Heath has transitioned from being an underwriter, broker, and computer services business to a pure, medium-sized broker.

Prudential Corp is Britain's largest life insurance group.
Prudential Corp announced it will increase its exposure to the personal financial services market.
Prudential Corp will take a near 30 percent stake in St James's Place Capital.
St James's Place Capital is seeking to buy the 49 percent of J. Rothschild Assurance that it does not already own.
Prudential Corp recently purchased mutual insurer Scottish Amicable.
J. Rothschild Assurance was set up by St James's co-founder Sir Mark Weinberg in 1992.
J. Rothschild Assurance targets high net-worth individuals and manages approximately 1.7 billion pounds for its policyholders.
In 1996, J. Rothschild Assurance announced a 41 percent growth in new business.
Prudential Corp has agreed not to increase its holding in St James's for at least a year unless a third-party bid is attracted.
Prudential Corp will pay around 39.6 million pounds for 30.5 million St James's shares.

A minority of active democrats in Hong Kong fear that Chinese rule will bring repression of liberties.
These activists are campaigning for better guarantees from Beijing.
They plan protests as Britain hands Hong Kong back to China on June 30.
Some supporters of the activists are branded as 'subversive' by China.
The leaders of the pro-democracy movement vow to enter parliament as Britain hands over Hong Kong.
Pro-democracy campaigners are sceptical about China's pledge of self-rule for Hong Kong for 50 years under the 'one country, two systems' formula.
There are concerns that the future administration under Tung Chee-hwa will curb rights and civil liberties in Hong Kong.
An interim 60-member lawmaking chamber will replace the existing elected legislature when Hong Kong reverts to China.
The interim chamber has passed laws that will ban foreign funding for political groups and require police permits for protests.
Chinese officials have warned against any advocacy of independence for Taiwan or Tibet.

Tung Chee-hwa is the future leader of Hong Kong.
Hong Kong's handover to China is scheduled for midnight June 30.
Tung Chee-hwa made a donation of 50,000 sterling (US$81,500) to Britain's Conservative Party in 1992.
Tung Chee-hwa plans to ban foreign funding to local political groups and curb demonstrations after the handover.
Critics have accused Tung Chee-hwa of hypocrisy and double standards regarding his political funding.
Tung Chee-hwa's popularity has declined in recent polls.
Martin Lee, leader of Hong Kong's democracy movement, met U.S. President Bill Clinton at the White House.
Martin Lee received an assurance from Clinton that Hong Kong is important to the United States.
Clinton warned China to abide by Sino-British treaties regarding Hong Kong's self-rule.
Nihal Jayawickrama stated that Tung Chee-hwa's proposed restrictions on political freedoms are influenced by China.

Britain will close its last Hong Kong naval base, HMS Tamar, on Friday.
The closure of HMS Tamar is located on Stonecutters Island.
Britain will return Hong Kong to China on July 1 after more than 150 years of colonial rule.
The island will house the Chinese garrison after the handover.
The Royal Navy launched a new book on Thursday marking its history in Hong Kong since 1840.
Major-General Bryan Dutton is the commander of the British Forces in Hong Kong.
Dutton stated that the closure of HMS Tamar represents a sad ending to a historical era.
HMS Tamar is home to three patrol craft: HMS Plover, HMS Peacock, and HMS Starling.
Over 200 marines from the Royal Navy will parade as the White Ensign is lowered for the last time.
Lo Ying, a cleaner who has worked with the Royal Navy in Hong Kong for over 50 years, will also be retiring.

Microsoft Corp.'s corporate rivals include International Business Machines Corp., Netscape Communications Corp., Oracle Corp., and Sun Microsystems Inc.
These companies announced a collaboration on network computing standards to enable their products to work together.
The collaboration aims to allow software developers to create software that connects computers via corporate networks, business-to-business networks, and the Internet.
The companies stated that their collaboration is open to broad industry participation.
Steve Mills, general manager of IBM Software Solutions, expressed a goal for an industry groundswell to develop from this initiative.
Microsoft has faced criticism for attempting to extend its dominance by developing software based on closed, proprietary standards.
The issue of proprietary standards is sensitive for the Internet, which has traditionally operated on open standards.
The results of the collaboration will be submitted to an industry standards group later this year.
Each company involved pledged to ensure their next major products adhere to the new standards this year.
The collaboration aims to create a unified approach to an Internet development architecture called CORBA.

International Business Machines Corp acquired Lotus Development Corp for $3.5 billion in June 1995.
Jeff Papows is the president of Lotus Development Corp.
Papows described the merger as a 'marriage made in heaven' during an interview at Lotusphere.
Papows stated that IBM kept its promise to leave Lotus alone after the acquisition.
The two companies gradually began to trust each other after the merger.
Employee exits from Lotus stabilized to a normal industry attrition rate after the acquisition.
Lotus's concern about losing most of its intellectual capital did not materialize.
IBM chairman and CEO Louis Gerstner stated that the merger was working with 'irrefutable' evidence.
The number of Lotus Notes users reached 9.5 million in 1996, doubling from the previous year.
Papows noted that IBM's global reach and sales force contributed to the success of the merger.

International Business Machines Corp is expected to report solid fourth quarter earnings on Tuesday.
Some negative impact from currency is also expected for IBM's fourth quarter earnings.
IBM will report earnings after the U.S. stock market closes for the first time in recent memory.
Wall Street estimates for IBM's earnings range from $3.13 to $4.32, with a consensus of $3.88 a share.
IBM reported earnings of $3.09 a share a year ago, including charges.
Steve Milunovich, a Morgan Stanley analyst, believes it will be a good quarter for IBM.
Milunovich does not expect a blowout quarter for IBM.
The U.S. dollar strengthened in the fourth quarter, which could negatively impact IBM's earnings by as much as $0.25.
Analysts expect IBM to have bigger expenses this quarter for its restructuring.
In the third quarter, IBM had restructuring costs of about $200 million for employee buyouts.

Cadbury-Schweppes Plc is expected to report an eight percent rise in first half profits.
Mark Duffy is a food manufacturing analyst at SBC Warburg.
Duffy stated that the success of the relaunch of the 7UP brand is a main question for Cadbury-Schweppes.
Sprite, owned by Coca-Cola, has seen an aggressive marketing push and is the fastest growing brand in the U.S. after Cadbury's Dr Pepper.
Analysts forecast pretax profits for Cadbury-Schweppes to range from 218 to 232 million stg.
The expected dividend is 5.1 pence, up from 4.9 pence.
A restructuring cost of approximately 35 million is anticipated, with about 25 million from the closure of a smaller production plant in France.
Most profit improvement is expected to come from Dr Pepper in the U.S.
Cadbury-Schweppes bought Dr Pepper/7UP in January 1995 for $1.71 billion.
Cadbury's U.S. drinks business is expected to report about 112 million stg in trading profit.

Scottish and Newcastle is Britain's largest brewer.
Brian Stewart is the chief executive of Scottish and Newcastle.
Scottish and Newcastle is committed to its Center Parcs holiday resorts.
Profits from Center Parcs resorts decreased by 11 percent to 39 million pounds.
The decline in profits is attributed to weak economic conditions in mainland Europe and facility improvements in the Netherlands.
Analysts have questioned the decision of Scottish and Newcastle to enter the leisure market.
Bookings in UK Center Parcs are reported to be strong and ahead of the previous year.
Scottish and Newcastle does not plan to build new Center Parcs in the next year.
Brian Stewart expressed optimism about the future prospects of the leisure division.
Scottish and Newcastle expects to continue supplying beer to most of Inntrepreneur's 3,000 tied pubs.

Greenalls Plc is experiencing a strong level of Christmas bookings.
Consumer confidence is increasing according to managing director Peter Daresbury.
Christmas is a critical period for hotel, pub, and restaurant companies in Britain and mainland Europe.
Up to 20 percent of annual turnover for these companies is generated in December.
Greenalls owns the De Vere Hotels chain, 2,360 pubs, and 470 off-licenses.
Greenalls reported a 47.9 percent rise in pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits to 148.7 million for the year ended September 27.
Hotel occupancy and conference business have improved as the corporate sector has become more buoyant.
De Vere Hotels' revenue per available room rose 10.8 percent, and occupancy levels increased to 74.4 percent.
Greenalls plans to invest 170 million in business development for 1997/98, with 40 million allocated for rolling out pub concepts.
Greenalls Inns operates 920 outlets nationally, with 514 being managed food houses.

Roger Smith was the former Chairman of General Motors Corp.
Roger Smith purchased Hughes Aircraft Co. for $5.1 billion.
The purchase of Hughes Aircraft Co. was intended to develop space-age technologies for cars.
Raytheon Corp. agreed to purchase Hughes defense operations for $9.5 billion.
The original cost of Hughes Aircraft Co. was covered by the sale to Raytheon Corp.
If valued at Thursday's closing stock price, Hughes would be worth $25.2 billion.
About 25 percent of the Class H shares of Hughes were traded publicly.
GM's purchase of Hughes has been financially beneficial for General Motors.
The integration of Hughes technology into GM products has not been successful according to some analysts.
David Healy stated that the idea of combining aerospace technology with the automobile business was unrealistic.

Ford Motor Co. reported an 82 percent increase in profit to $1.2 billion in the fourth quarter.
Ford's earnings per share for the fourth quarter were $1.
The fourth quarter results included a $132 million charge for one-time items.
A year earlier, Ford earned $660 million, or 49 cents a share.
For the year 1996, Ford's net income rose 7 percent to $4.45 billion, or $3.64 a share.
Fourth-quarter revenues were $38.8 billion, compared to $34.6 billion a year earlier.
Revenues for the year increased to $147.0 billion from $137.1 billion in 1995.
Ford's U.S. automotive operations reported a profit of $628 million for the fourth quarter.
Ford's non-U.S. automotive operations lost $238 million in the fourth quarter.
Ford expects improved automotive earnings in 1997.

Federal-Mogul Corp. has ended its effort to build a global auto parts retail empire.
Federal-Mogul Corp. announced a restructuring that focuses on its core manufacturing and distribution business.
Federal-Mogul Corp. is based in Southfield, Michigan.
The company incurred $264 million in pre-tax charges for the restructuring and special one-time items in the fourth quarter.
Federal-Mogul Corp. has approximately $2 billion in annual sales.
The company plans to reduce its workforce by about 2,900 jobs, which is 18.5 percent of its total workforce of 15,700.
The restructuring resulted in a net loss of $220.2 million for the fourth quarter of 1996.
In comparison, the company reported a loss of $49.1 million for the fourth quarter of 1995.
For the entire year of 1996, Federal-Mogul Corp. lost $211.1 million, but would have made a profit of $34.7 million before special items.
In 1995, the company reported a loss of $9.7 million.

A top Chinese official for contacts with Taiwan ruled out an early resumption of talks on reunification.
The China Daily reported that the official claimed Taiwan's leaders were pursuing 'splittist' policies.
Tang Shubei is the vice-chairman of the Association for Relations across the Taiwan Strait (ARATS).
Tang Shubei stated that Taiwanese authorities did not want the handover of Hong Kong to go smoothly.
Tang suggested that Taiwanese authorities might try to disrupt the transfer of power regarding Hong Kong.
Tang stated that in the long term, the mainland and Taiwan should negotiate cross-strait issues under the 'one-China' policy.
Tang indicated that the atmosphere for talks would not improve unless Taiwan's leaders halted their 'splittist' activities.
China and Taiwan have been rivals since the Nationalist government fled to Taiwan after its defeat in the Chinese civil war in 1949.
Beijing regards Taiwan as a renegade province and attempts to isolate it diplomatically.
Tang called for the United States to halt arms sales to Taiwan.

Boeing Co signed a $685 million contract to sell jets to China.
Vice President Al Gore attended the signing ceremony.
The contract involves the sale of five 777-200 jets.
The signing ceremony took place at the Great Hall of the People.
Chinese Premier Li Peng was present at the ceremony.
Air China will take delivery of the planes in 1998 and 1999.
Ronald Woodard is the president of Boeing Commercial Airplane Group.
Woodard stated that the contract faced delays due to political differences between China and the United States.
A year ago, China and the United States had tensions over various issues.
The Gore visit aimed to ensure improved Sino-U.S. relations.

China is set to regain control of Hong Kong in 100 days.
Beijing has bypassed British authorities in appointing local leaders in Hong Kong.
China intends to reshape Hong Kong's political landscape to align with its own governance style.
Plans include dismantling the elected legislature and reducing civil liberties laws.
China has dismissed British objections regarding its plans for Hong Kong.
Chinese Premier Li Peng stated that Beijing would implement the 1984 Sino-British agreement as it sees fit.
Li Peng described British plans to monitor the agreement's implementation as unrealistic.
Under the 1984 accord, China promised Hong Kong a high degree of autonomy for 50 years post-handover.
Tung Chee-hwa, selected by a Beijing-vetted group, has aligned closely with China's official positions.
Beijing has expressed approval of Tung Chee-hwa's stance on various issues related to Hong Kong.

A bill to protect homeowners from paying unnecessary mortgage insurance was passed by the House of Representatives.
The Homeowners Insurance Protection Act was adopted by a vote of 421 to seven.
The act would cancel mortgage insurance once the homeowner has built up sufficient equity.
Representative Henry Gonzalez stated that many people are paying for insurance they no longer need.
Gonzalez urged the Senate to quickly pass the measure.
Consumer advocates claim these policies cost homeowners millions of dollars a year.
Michelle Meier, counsel for government affairs at Consumers Union, expressed optimism about the Senate moving forward with the bill.
The mortgage insurance industry warned that the automatic cancellation proposal would raise costs for loans with low down payments.
Suzanne Hutchinson of the Mortgage Insurance Companies of America criticized the bill for imposing unnecessary government mandates and controls.
Currently, mortgage lenders require insurance for borrowers making a small down payment, such as 5 percent.

Sun Microsystems Inc decided to use powerful computer encoding software made in Russia.
The decision increased pressure on the Clinton administration to relax U.S. export controls on similar products made by American companies.
Encryption products scramble information and require a password or software key to be readable.
Encryption is a critical component of global communications and online commerce over the Internet.
Encryption can prevent unauthorized access to telephone calls and credit card numbers sent over the Internet.
Encryption can also be used by drug cartels or terrorists to evade law enforcement surveillance.
Clinton administration officials oppose exporting powerful U.S. encryption programs unless they allow government access to the software keys.
FBI Director Louis Freeh stated that the encryption 'genie' is not yet 'out of the bottle.'
Rep. Bob Goodlatte criticized the current export control policy and introduced measures in Congress to relax these controls.
The bill introduced by Goodlatte was passed by the House Judiciary Committee and is awaiting action by the International Relations Committee.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin outlined the Clinton administration's plan to allow banks to enter the securities and insurance businesses.
The plan aims to eliminate legal barriers that have been in place for 60 years since the Great Depression.
Rubin stated that the lines separating insurance, securities, and banking industries have blurred due to new financial services and products.
The plan would enable banks, securities firms, and insurance companies to compete under a uniform set of regulations.
Rubin claimed that increased competition from the plan could generate savings of up to $15 billion a year for consumers.
The administration's proposal was highly anticipated and was expected to be introduced in March.
House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach welcomed the plan but noted that some substantive issues remained unresolved.
Bankers Trust New York Corp. Chairman Frank Newman stated that the administration plan would provide momentum for reform.
Consumer advocates expressed disappointment that the proposal lacked adequate protections for bank customers purchasing insurance.
Rubin indicated that the proposal did not take a firm position on allowing banks to combine with non-financial commercial firms.

Czech consumer inflation continued its gradual downtrend in January.
Analysts do not expect a loosening of the central bank's tight monetary policy in the short-term.
The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) reported January inflation at 1.2 percent month-on-month.
The year-on-year inflation rate in January was 7.4 percent, down from 8.6 percent the previous month.
The key sliding average inflation figure decreased to 8.7 percent from 8.8 percent in December.
The key sliding average inflation figure was down from 9.1 percent in January 1996.
Kamil Janacek, chief economist at Komercni Banka, stated that the January number is about one percentage point lower than a year ago.
The CSU reported that food, drinks, and tobacco products rose 1.3 percent in January.
Transportation costs rose 3.6 percent in January, and housing costs rose by 1.3 percent.
The Czech National Bank (CNB) is expected to maintain high rates in the near term.

Czech annual average consumer inflation in 1996 was 8.8 percent.
The inflation rate in 1995 was 9.1 percent.
The Czech Statistical Bureau reported the inflation figures.
The government's original inflation forecast for 1996 was eight percent.
Analysts expressed optimism about the central bank's monetary policies.
Martin Kupka is an economist at investment bank Patria Finance.
CSU reported month-on-month inflation for December was 0.5 percent.
Year-on-year consumer prices in December were 8.6 percent higher.
CSU chairman Edvard Outrata stated that 1996 core inflation remained around five percent.
The CSU indicated that price increases in foodstuffs, leisure, and textiles accounted for 80 percent of the monthly CPI rise.

The Prague Stock Exchange backed off last week's year-high due to profit taking on Monday.
Market sentiment remains bullish for the coming weeks, according to analysts.
SPT Telecom, CEZ, and Komercni Banka fell sharply, dragging the PX50 index down 0.28 percent to 598.0.
SPT Telecom accounts for 20 percent of the PSE's market capitalization.
CEZ accounts for 14 percent of the PSE's market capitalization.
Komercni Banka accounts for 11 percent of the PSE's market capitalization.
SPT Telecom shares closed down 75 crowns at 3,700.
CEZ shares closed down 28 crowns at 1,202.
Komercni Banka shares closed down 25 crowns at 2,620.
