The PSE has had a steady uptrend since 1997 after a slump in the fourth quarter of 1996.

Morgan Stanley merged with Dean Witter Discover.
The merger will create a more competitive force in the European investment banking market.
A banking analyst stated that other banks will see a stronger competitor due to the merger.
Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter agreed to form a financial entity called Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover & Co.
The market capitalization of the new entity is $21 billion.
Both U.S. and European investment banks are seeking more business in continental Europe and Britain.
The merger will provide considerable backing for Morgan Stanley's European aspirations.
Dean Witter's U.S. retail network could serve as an additional distribution network for Morgan Stanley products.
Dean Witter employs about 120 people in London, with around 35 in institutional equities sales.
Morgan Stanley employs around 2,000 people in its Canary Wharf headquarters.

NatWest Markets experienced a turbulent week that ended with a shake-up of its global debt markets arm.
Three senior staff members departed from NatWest Markets during this week.
NatWest's investment banking arm stated that there was no connection between the management changes and reported losses of 90 million pounds ($144 million).
The losses were accumulated over two years due to systematic mispricings of interest rate options derivatives.
Britain's Serious Fraud Office is monitoring the options situation but is not investigating the reported losses.
The Bank of England and the Securities and Futures Authority are scrutinizing the reported losses.
The management shake-up in NatWest's debt markets division indicates a shift in power to managers from Greenwich Capital.
Gary Holloway and Chip Kruger are the co-chief executives of the new global debt markets division.
Johan Hattingh and Alby Cator were among the senior managers who left NatWest as part of the restructuring.
NatWest has created 10 main areas of responsibility within the debt markets division following the internal announcement of changes.

Nicola Horlick announced her resignation from Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) on Thursday.
Horlick was reported to have been offered a promotion at MGAM shortly before her resignation.
A spokesman for Horlick stated that she planned to take legal action against her former employer over constructive dismissal.
Horlick was the head of the British pension fund business at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's MGAM.
Horlick was suspended at MGAM pending an internal investigation into a potential breach of her contract.
The suspension prompted reports of unease among large pension fund clients at MGAM.
The dispute with MGAM involved allegations that Horlick attempted to take members of her team to Dutch bank ABN AMRO.
Horlick received news of her promotion to managing director from MGAM chief executive Robert Smith just days before her resignation.
MGAM faced issues last year due to misvaluations in three of its funds and the sacking of fund manager Peter Young, who is under investigation by the Serious Fraud Office.
Horlick indicated that a group of fund managers demanded she be given more authority due to turmoil following the Peter Young affair.

China criticized Britain's protests against proposed amendments to Hong Kong laws.
China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang stated that the British protest was unacceptable, unreasonable, and unwise.
Shen Guofang claimed that Britain was forcing its will upon others regarding Hong Kong.
Shen asserted that Hong Kong is China's internal affair and that no other country has the right to interfere.
Britain lodged a strong protest against China's plans to dilute laws guaranteeing civil liberties in Hong Kong.
The British Foreign Office reported that junior minister Jeremy Hanley expressed serious concern over the proposals to Chinese ambassador Jiang Enzhu.
Hanley stated that Hong Kong's bill of rights and related legislation were consistent with the Basic Law.
China accused Britain of violating the Basic Law by introducing laws guaranteeing civil liberties in Hong Kong after the handover.
Shen defended China's plan to amend or repeal 25 laws and ordinances as reversing unilateral changes made by Britain.
A Chinese envoy to Hong Kong attributed the British protest to Chris Patten, the last British governor of Hong Kong.

China's stock markets are currently overheating.
The People's Daily newspaper warned of a potential crash similar to the Wall Street collapse of 1929.
China's foreign currency B share market in Shanghai rose by about 80 percent between November 11 and December 10.
The Shenzhen stock market increased by about 100 percent before experiencing sharp declines.
The Shanghai B-share market fell by 12.26 percent on Friday.
The Shenzhen B-share market dropped by 14.75 percent.
The Shanghai A-share index decreased by 5.51 percent.
The Shenzhen A-share index declined by 4.84 percent.
The People's Daily commentary stated that the stock markets are in an abnormal situation with increasing market risk.
The commentary indicated that the government would not intervene to support the markets during downturns.

Beijing has pledged to allow more imports of U.S. textiles under a new deal.
Washington does not expect to close its textile trade gap with China.
Chinese and U.S. negotiators signed a new textile agreement in Beijing.
The new textile agreement ended the threat of a trade war between the U.S. and China.
The agreement ensures U.S. access to China's textile markets.
China exported $6.5 billion worth of textiles to the United States in 1995.
The United States imported only $64 million worth of textiles from China in 1995.
U.S. textile exports are sluggish due to China's high tariff rates and non-tariff barriers.
The new agreement granted China a U.S. import quota larger than the previous 1994 textile pact.
China pledged to reduce its tariffs on textile imports.

Westfield Holdings Ltd is Australia's largest shopping mall owner.
Westfield Holdings Ltd announced that its U.S. arm would list on the New York Stock Exchange in May.
Westfield Holdings Ltd aims to raise US$400 million in an initial public offering.
Westfield America Inc plans to use the proceeds to spend US$500 million on acquisitions in the United States.
The acquisitions will include buying out Westfield's partners in existing shopping malls and purchasing new malls.
The resulting group will be the fourth largest listed shopping mall owner in the United States, according to chairman Frank Lowy.
Westfield America Trust will list its U.S. vehicle CenterMark Properties Inc as Westfield America Inc.
Westfield America Inc will dilute its 67.2 percent stake in CenterMark to about 50 percent.
Westfield America Inc will first purchase Westfield Holdings' 50 percent stake in the Garden State Plaza shopping centre for US$145 million.
Westfield America Inc will have about US$210 million available to buy out partners and acquire new malls.

The federal government will release the Wallis Inquiry's report into Australia's financial system on Wednesday at midday (0200 GMT).
The government is expected to respond to some parts of the report.
The Wallis Inquiry was set up in June last year and is chaired by businessman Stan Wallis.
The inquiry released a 415-page discussion paper in late November that canvassed various options for reform.
The Inquiry's report was presented to the government last month.
The report will make recommendations about the current 'Six Pillars' policy regarding mergers between major banks and life insurance groups.
The six pillars include Westpac Banking Corp, National Australia Bank Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, and Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) Society.
The report will address whether the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) and the Treasurer should continue to have the power to reject or approve bank mergers.
Wallis expressed a preference for treating the financial sector like any other sector under competition policy.
The report will consider whether to scrap the current ban on foreign takeovers of the big four banks.

Stadium Australia chairman Peter Ritchie stated that underwriters would not sell unsold passes at a discount ahead of the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games.
Ritchie mentioned that the underwriters aim to sell approximately A$200 million worth of unsold passes at prices above the float's offer prices over the next couple of years.
Ritchie expressed confidence that the unsold passes would sell for more as the Games approach.
Ritchie assured existing gold members that the passes would not be discounted as the Games get closer.
Ritchie confirmed a market speculation of a A$200 million-plus shortfall in the A$364.4 million float of Stadium gold and platinum passes.
The float offered 35,000 passes, which included main stadium tickets to the 2000 Olympics, a 30-year stadium membership, and an equity stake in the stadium.
Ritchie estimated that about 40 percent of the passes had been sold.
The underwriters for the float include ANZ Securities, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Macquarie Bank Ltd, and ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
The underwriters must fund the project regardless of the number of packages sold to ensure the completion of the 110,000-seat stadium, which is scheduled to open in 1999.
The Stadium Australia float closed after being open for almost six months, which is more than twice as long as most share offers.

Caterpillar Inc. reported a first quarter profit of $394 million.
The profit of $394 million is the best quarter in the company's history.
The profit is up 33 percent from a year ago.
Caterpillar expects 1997 profits to be higher than the $1.4 billion posted in 1996.
The expectation for higher profits is based on anticipated moderately higher sales.
Caterpillar's earnings were $394 million, or $2.08 a share.
The earnings of $2.08 a share exceeded the Wall Street consensus of $1.69 a share.
Sales and revenues for the quarter were $4.26 billion.
A year earlier, Caterpillar earned $296 million, or $1.53 a share, on revenues of $3.84 billion.
Gross profit margins rose to 26.8 percent of machinery and engine sales from 24.5 percent a year ago.

Harnischfeger Industries Inc. offered to buy Giddings & Lewis Inc. for about $747 million.
The offer includes the assumption of Giddings & Lewis debt.
The offer is priced at $19 per share.
The offer values Giddings & Lewis at approximately $747 million based on 33.2 million outstanding shares.
The offer represents a premium of about 40 percent over Giddings & Lewis's closing price of $13.625 per share.
Harnischfeger Chief Executive Officer Jeffery Glade stated that the company would take on significant debt to finance the deal.
Glade claimed that financing for the deal was fully in place with no contingencies.
Glade expected the deal to add to Harnischfeger earnings immediately upon closing.
The transaction would create an enterprise with combined 1996 revenues of $3.6 billion.
Giddings & Lewis did not comment on its discussions with Harnischfeger.

Harnischfeger Industries Inc made a $19 a share tender offer for Giddings & Lewis Inc.
Industry analysts believe that Harnischfeger's offer may be the best Giddings can receive.
Thomas Burns Jr., an analyst at NatWest Securities, stated that there is unlikely to be a higher bid than Harnischfeger's.
Shares of Giddings & Lewis increased by 6-3/4 to 20-3/8 on Monday.
The increase in Giddings & Lewis shares suggests some buyers expect a higher bid.
William Cooke, an analyst at McDonald & Co, believes that $19 a share represents full value for Giddings & Lewis.
Cooke expressed that Harnischfeger is optimistic in assuming it can double Giddings & Lewis's earnings in the near future.
Harnischfeger aims to use Giddings & Lewis to expand in the industrial products aftermarket service business, estimated to be an $80 billion market.
Some analysts noted that acquiring Giddings & Lewis introduces significant uncertainty for Harnischfeger shareholders.
J. Blair Brumley, an analyst at Dain Bosworth, downgraded Harnischfeger's rating from buy to hold.

A consultant's report was released on Tuesday regarding the Busang gold project in Indonesia.
The Busang gold project was previously promoted by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd. as a significant discovery.
Shareholders sold their shares in Bre-X on Tuesday.
Investigators and analysts are examining how the fraud at Busang occurred.
Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. conducted an audit of the Busang project.
Strathcona's report indicated that tampering at Busang was difficult to believe initially.
Bre-X's last resource estimate claimed there were 71 million ounces of gold at Busang based on 16,400 samples.
Strathcona concluded that most of the gold in Bre-X's samples likely came from another source.
The report suggested that tampering likely occurred at Bre-X's storage warehouse in Samarinda.
Strathcona noted that Bre-X officials had previous studies indicating abnormalities in the Busang gold find.

William Resources Inc is a Canadian gold mining company.
William Resources Inc expects to achieve over 200,000 ounces of gold production in 1997.
William Resources Inc has the financial resources to withstand a weak gold market.
The company reported promising early tests of its Ballarat East project in Australia.
William Resources Inc has put its plans for the Ruster's Roost project on hold.
The company provided a favorable update on its operations in Scandinavia and Brazil.
William Resources Inc is selling its disappointing Mexican project.
In 1996, William Resources produced an annualized 100,000 ounces of gold at an average cash cost of US$349 per ounce.
The Bjorkdal mine in Sweden, acquired in December 1996, is expected to exceed 100,000 ounces in 1997 at a cash cost of US$216 per ounce.
The Jacobina project in Brazil is forecasted to produce 65,000 ounces of gold in 1997 at a cash cost of US$285 per ounce.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is based in Calgary, Canada.
Bre-X expects to receive a report from Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. regarding the Busang find in Indonesia.
The report is anticipated to be received over the weekend.
Bre-X plans to release the findings of the report on Monday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange is preparing for increased trading activity in Bre-X shares when the report is released.
Steve McAnulty is a spokesman for Bre-X.
Bre-X hired Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. to review its Busang project due to emerging doubts about the gold find.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc. reported on March 26 that its preliminary tests found insignificant amounts of gold at the Busang site.
Bre-X has estimated that the Busang site contains approximately 71 million ounces of gold.
Panic selling of Bre-X shares resulted in a loss of nearly C$3 billion from the company's market value after Freeport's announcement.

Ford Motor Co. agreed to sell its interests in Budget Rent a Car Corp. to Team Rental Group Inc. for about $350 million.
Team Rental Group Inc. is based in Daytona Beach, Florida, and operates 13 Budget franchises with 155 locations.
Team Rental Group Inc. also leases commuter vans in 22 states and sells used vehicles.
Ford Vice Chairman Ed Hagenlocker stated that the sale is in the best interests of Budget and Ford.
The sale of Ford's preferred stock in Budget is not expected to close until March.
Ford will book an unspecified gain on the deal in its fourth quarter 1996 earnings.
The gain will partially reverse a $437 million after-tax write-off Ford took on its investment and loans to Budget.
The deal will add cash to Ford's finances, moving it closer to a future stock repurchase program.
Ford executives indicated that stock repurchases will be considered after cutting automotive costs by $1 billion and increasing cash reserves above $7 billion.
Ford's decision marks a shift to reduce its rental car holdings and reverses a previous plan to acquire full ownership of Budget.

Ford Motor Co. will restructure its Halewood car plant in England but will not close it.
Some job losses are expected at the Halewood plant.
Susanne Wegerhoff is a Ford spokeswoman based in Brentwood, England.
Ford will announce operating changes for the Halewood plant after a meeting with major unions.
Wegerhoff denied a report that Ford was threatening to close the Halewood facility.
Wegerhoff stated that Halewood has a future and that a plan will be discussed to secure it.
London's Observer newspaper reported that Ford wanted to cut 500 jobs at Halewood.
The Halewood plant employs 6,500 workers and produces Ford's European-designed Escort sub-compact cars.
Ford's losses in Europe increased to $472 million in the third quarter of 1996.
Industry analysts consider the Halewood plant the least efficient of Ford's three Escort plants in Europe.

General Motors Corp. will gain $9.5 billion in value from selling Hughes Aircraft Co.
General Motors will gain about $100 million in annual savings from no longer writing off Hughes' goodwill.
General Motors writes off about $25 million each quarter associated with its 1985 purchase of Hughes' defense assets.
The write-offs will end after the sale to Raytheon Co. closes, expected by midyear.
The deal, known as 'Project Triple Play,' includes the spin-off and merger of Hughes' defense business with Raytheon.
Hughes' Delco Electronics business will shift into General Motors' automotive operations.
Most of the $4.4 billion in cash from the deal will be injected into Hughes' telecommunications business.
General Motors Chief Financial Officer J. Michael Losh stated that the cash will help complete Hughes Electronics' $3 billion acquisition of PanAmSat Corp.
General Motors plans to use the cash to fund the growth of its DirecTV satellite broadcasting business and Hughes Network Systems business.
General Motors stockholders will control 30 percent of Raytheon after the Hughes merger.

GKN Plc is a UK auto-components group.
A U.S. court awarded $398 million in damages to franchisees against GKN Plc.
Analysts predict GKN's shares could decline further if the judgement is not overturned on appeal.
One analyst estimates shares could fall by 6.6 percent from the last closing level of 1045 pence per share if the judgement stands.
GKN's shares have already decreased by three percent to 1009.5 pence during the current session.
Another analyst predicts shares could drop by 50 pence if GKN loses the appeal.
The second analyst believes the judgement is a market shock but not significant to GKN's operations.
GKN stated that damages could increase to $554 million under the North Carolina Unfair Trade Practices Act.
The analyst noted that GKN has 240-250 million pounds of free cash reserves unrelated to customer advance payments.
The analyst has rated GKN as a 'sell'.

Britain announced the preferred bidders for two more passenger rail franchises.
The Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf) selected Great Western Holdings Ltd as the preferred bidder for the North West Regional Railways franchise.
Great Western Holdings Ltd's bid group is owned 51 percent by existing management and employees, with FirstBus and 3i venture capital each owning 24.5 percent.
The Thameslink franchise was awarded to GOVIA, which includes Go-Ahead Group Plc and VIA-GTI.
There are three remaining franchises to be awarded before the British election deadline in May 1997.
The remaining franchises include ScotRail and North East Regional Rail.
The privatisation of Britain's rail industry began in 1995 and included the sell-off of rail infrastructure under Railtrack.
Chris Moyes, Go-Ahead's commercial director, stated that the Thameslink line has significant potential for revenue.
Trevor Smallwood, chairman of FirstBus, mentioned that the winner of the Central Trains deal could see revenues of around 70 million pounds.
Go-Ahead's shares increased by 36 pence to 515, National Express's shares rose by 26 pence to 547, and FirstBus's shares increased by 12.5 pence.

Nissan Motor Co announced a 215 million pound ($357 million) investment in its British plant at Sunderland.
The investment aims to build a new model and will create 800 jobs at Nissan UK.
An additional 2,700 jobs are expected to be created in British supplier firms due to this investment.
The announcement followed Ford Motor Co's decision to cut 1,300 jobs at its Halewood plant in Liverpool.
Nissan plans to add a third model to the production line at Nissan Motor (UK) Ltd (NMUK).
The investment will be used for production equipment, including moulds for the new car.
Nissan will produce models in the Pulsar range, known as the Almera in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, starting from 2000.
The decision to build a third model in Europe was reviewed internally by Nissan's European vice-president and Ian Gibson.
Ian Gibson, chief executive of Nissan UK, stated that the investment is a vote of confidence for Sunderland.
Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang welcomed Nissan's decision as a significant development in their European presence.

Shares of 3Com Corp slid on Monday.
Shares of U.S. Robotics Corp slid on Monday.
Traders reported that prospects dimmed for a new suitor for Robotics shareholders.
The merger agreement between 3Com and Robotics is valued at $7.3 billion.
The merger agreement requires either party to pay up to $160 million if the deal falls through.
3Com closed on Monday at 32-13/16, down 19/64.
U.S. Robotics shares closed at 55-3/8, down 7/16.
The merger terms require 3Com to exchange 1.75 shares of its stock for each Robotics share.
The value of the 3Com offer to Robotics shareholders has decreased from $68 to $57-27/64.
Analysts indicated that shareholder dissatisfaction extends into mid-level management at Robotics.

AT&T Corp. withdrew its application with the U.S. government for a license to launch new communications satellites.
AT&T's decision to cancel its application to the Federal Communications Commission followed the disposal of several existing satellite businesses.
AT&T has completed its exit from the satellite operations business.
AT&T stated that investment in new Ka-band satellite technology was a drain on capital resources.
AT&T's renewed focus is on its core long-distance business and key growth areas like wireless, online, and local services.
Ka-band refers to radio frequencies that handle two-way voice and data communications.
The new class of satellites would have allowed AT&T to offer next-generation communications services such as video, data transmission, and high-speed Internet services.
AT&T spokesman Gary Morgenstern stated that satellites are not core to the company's focus.
AT&T continues to offer satellite-based services through its minority investment in the Direct TV venture of Hughes Electronics Corp.
AT&T's Ka-band project was formally known as the AT&T VoiceSpan Satellite System.

New York State utility regulators are set to approve the Bell Atlantic Corp/NYNEX Corp merger.
The approval is subject to several conditions that will be set forth prior to a final vote on Thursday.
Regulators will consider requiring the combined company to permanently locate its headquarters in New York.
Regulators will consider requiring the combined company to reduce rates.
Regulators will consider requiring the combined company to issue $300 million in rebates.
Regulators will consider requiring the combined company to improve customer service.
The merger would create the nation's largest local phone operator.
The merger still faces hurdles in Washington and New York, which is currently withholding its approval.
The Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission are conducting increased scrutiny of the merger.
New York State Attorney General Dennis Vacco is conducting an ongoing anti-trust review of the merger.

Japan's major asset management firms suspended business with Nomura Securities.
The suspension follows Nomura Securities revealing suspected illegal deals.
The suspension will significantly reduce Nomura's commission income on bond and stock transactions.
Commission income from bond and stock transactions accounts for 28.5 percent of Nomura's total revenue.
Nomura Investment Management Co. also suspended business with Nomura Securities.
Orders from Nomura Investment Management Co. accounted for about 20 percent of Nomura's total orders.
An official at Nomura Investment Management stated the action was taken out of consideration for customers.
Asset managers faced pressure from customers, particularly public pension funds, to halt orders to Nomura.
Nomura admitted to irregular deals linked to corporate racketeers.
Two Nomura directors resigned after raising at least 70 million yen in profits from shady transactions.

Japan experienced its first failure of a life insurance firm in its post-war history on Friday.
Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co was ordered to start shutting down its business by the Finance Ministry.
The Finance Ministry instructed Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co to halt most business, except for servicing current customers.
This was the first order against a life insurance company since the financial system was restructured after World War Two.
Financial analysts stated that the move would accelerate the restructuring of Japan's life insurance industry.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka announced that Nissan Life decided to discontinue business during an emergency board meeting.
Mitsuzuka pledged to protect all policyholders of Nissan Life to prevent concerns over the financial system.
The Finance Ministry indicated it would not use tax money to liquidate Nissan Life as it did for failed housing loan companies.
Mitsuzuka attributed Nissan Life's failure to poor management of its investment portfolio.
Nissan Mutual Life had liabilities exceeding assets by about 200 billion yen ($1.58 billion).

Japanese prosecutors raided Nomura Securities Co. Ltd.
The raid was part of a widening investigation into payments linked to racketeers.
The raid occurred at Nomura's headquarters in central Tokyo.
Prosecutors and officials from the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission conducted the raid.
The raids were publicized in advance, indicating a significant investigation.
Deputy chief prosecutor Kunihiro Matsuo stated the raids were to investigate illegal payments made by a Nomura director.
The illegal payment was 38 million yen ($309,000) to a company run by a relative of a racketeer.
The scandal involved Nomura directors Shimpei Matsuki and Nobutaka Fujikura, who resigned after internal probes.
Nomura President Hideo Sakamaki stepped down on March 14 and became an adviser to the company.
Nomura is a major player in the financial markets and has seen clients suspend business due to the scandal.

China's foreign currency B share markets are expected to recover in 1997 due to an improving national economic outlook.
Analysts stated that the fundamentals of most B share firms remain poor.
The B share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen have experienced significant fluctuations in recent weeks.
The B share markets are approximately 50 percent up from their low points a couple of months ago.
Analysts expect additional solid gains in 1997 once 1996 results are released by the end of April.
The basic problems with the B share markets, such as poor quality companies and low liquidity, are unlikely to be resolved in 1997.
A Shanghai stock analyst predicted that Shanghai's B share index could breach the 105-point historical high.
Most 1996 results are expected to show little improvement over the negative results of 1995.
Shanghai B share firms posted a net negative profit growth of 16.3 percent in 1995.
Brokers in Shenzhen expect the B share market to perform strongly in 1997 due to interest rate cuts.

Key companies on China's foreign currency B share markets were expected to report slightly better results for 1996 after a dismal 1995.
Analysts predicted more progress for B share companies in 1997.
B share companies were lagging behind the growth of China's economy.
Gains in 1996 were expected to be followed by stronger performance in 1997 due to two interest rate cuts and lower inflation.
Bruce Richardson, chief analyst for HG Asia in Shanghai, stated that improvements were expected but not yet realized.
Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co Ltd expected 1996 post-tax profits of 590 million yuan, up from 585 million yuan in 1995.
Shanghai Diesel Engine Co Ltd and Shanghai Tyre and Rubber also expected improved results in 1996 compared to 1995.
Jiang Dengfu, a senior B share analyst with Shenyin & Wanguo Securities, noted that improvements in B share companies' results were lagging behind the national economy.
Shanghai's B share firms posted a net year-on-year profit fall of 13.8 percent in 1994 and 16.3 percent in 1995.
Analysts attributed the poor results to management issues and Beijing's tight credit policy since mid-1993.

Zhang Xuexiong is a top businessman in Shanghai.
Zhang expressed no doubts about policy changes after the death of Deng Xiaoping.
Zhang's company, Shanghai Haolaixi Food Co Ltd, is a major supplier of confectionery in Shanghai.
Zhang started his company in 1989 with 90,000 yuan in capital.
The company made a profit of 10,000 yuan in its first year.
Last year, the company had a profit of over one million yuan.
Zhang expects the company's profit to rise to over three million yuan in 1997.
Jiang Zemin stated in his eulogy to Deng that multiple forms of production would continue to be allowed.
Zhang plans to reduce his workforce by more than half when he installs automatic packaging machinery.
Zhang was sent to work in the countryside during the Cultural Revolution and returned to Shanghai in 1984.

A Canadian federal election is not expected to be called until this weekend.
Reform Party leader Preston Manning faced charges of racism in his party.
The Reform Party and the Conservative Party are competing for the right-wing vote.
Reform won the third most seats in its inaugural national election campaign in 1993.
The Conservative Party won only two seats after nine years in power.
Reform has faced accusations of racism during its 3-1/2 year term in Parliament.
Manning accused the Conservatives of selecting a candidate based on race.
A Conservative official stated he sought candidates who were not Sikh to distinguish from Sikh candidates.
A Conservative spokesman dismissed Manning's remarks as electioneering.
The ruling Liberals are expected to call an election for June 2.

Canadian mining companies are concerned about the strengthening Canadian dollar.
Vic Wells is a spokesman for Anvil Range Mining Corp.
Anvil Range Mining Corp. suspended zinc and lead mining at its Faro property due to the stronger Canadian dollar.
Analysts predict the Canadian dollar will rise to 80 U.S. cents in 1997.
George Miller is the president of the Mining Association of Canada.
Canada is the world's largest producer of potash, uranium, and zinc.
Canada is the world's second-biggest producer of nickel after Russia.
Companies that produce metal in Canada are affected by the strengthening Canadian dollar.
Alan Thomas is the chief financial officer of Noranda Inc.
A one U.S. cent change in the Canadian dollar affects Noranda's bottom line by C$20 million.

Canada supports the U.S. bid to speed up free trade talks among 34 countries in North and South America.
Charles Larabie is a Canadian foreign affairs spokesman.
Ministers from the 34 countries were meeting in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, to decide when to start formal negotiations for the Free Trade Area of the Americas.
Brazil and its supporters want to negotiate in stages with tariff cuts until last.
The United States is pushing for more concrete decisions and a faster pace in talks.
The group aims to achieve a free trade deal by 2005.
Canada has a backup plan to join the South American free trade bloc Mercosur if FTAA negotiations do not progress quickly.
Mercosur involves Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, and Paraguay, with Chile and Bolivia as associate members.
Canada sees two major impediments to formalizing free trade talks for the FTAA: President Bill Clinton's lack of fast-track authority and Brazil's cautious approach.
Trade between Brazil and Canada was worth about C$2.5 billion in 1996.

Czech engineering group Skoda a.s. is a local agent for U.S.-based McDonnell Douglas Corp. (MD).
Skoda a.s. is proposing a barter deal to encourage the Czech government to buy MD's F/A-18 'Hornet' fighter aircraft.
Skoda's spokesman Karel Samec stated that his firm would provide trucks and other goods in return for planes.
The Czech military is considering upgrading its fleet and is cash-strapped.
McDonnell Douglas chose Skoda a.s. as an intermediary for the deal.
The decision to buy planes depends on the Czech government and the Defence Ministry.
The Czech Republic, Poland, and Hungary are seeking to upgrade their military fleets to be compatible with NATO.
McDonnell Douglas is competing against Lockheed Martin, SAAB, and France's Mirage for the Czech military contract.
The Czech government has delayed a decision on purchasing the planes due to proposed cuts in defense spending.
The Czech military has indicated it would need about 24 fighters to replace its old MiG-21s.

Czech engineering concern Skoda a.s. agreed to cooperate with Czech steelmaker Trinecke Zelezarny a.s. on steel production and privatisation projects.
Skoda stated that the deal aims to improve efficiency in the Czech steel industry through modernisation coordination.
Skoda produces heavy iron finished and semi-finished goods.
Both companies will specialise and coordinate in unspecified areas of production to reduce costs.
Skoda's spokesman Karel Samec indicated that selected products would be manufactured in the cheaper of the two mills.
Samec mentioned that the cooperation scheme may be applied to other companies in the future.
Samec noted that cooperation and participation in privatisation is necessary due to stagnation in global steel production.
Samec did not specify which privatisation projects Skoda was considering.
The Industry and Trade Ministry plans to sell 19 percent stakes in Nova Hut a.s. and Vitkovice a.s.
Trinecke Zelezarny is one of the four largest steel mills in the Czech Republic, located in Trinec.

The Czech Republic was expected to have its first budget deficit in 1996.
Deputy Finance Minister Miroslav Havel stated the deficit would be around 1.7 billion crowns ($61.77 million).
The Czech Republic had three surplus budgets since the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993.
As of Wednesday, revenues totaled 482.8 billion crowns and expenditures were 484.5 billion crowns.
Havel indicated that more bills might inflate expenditures further.
The government attempted to reduce a projected deficit of over five billion crowns in December by freezing some outlays.
The budget was affected by lower-than-expected tax revenue and delayed repayments to Russia.
The original 1996 budget was approved as balanced at 497.6 billion crowns, but was later reduced to 491 billion crowns due to spending cuts.
Parliamentary budget committee chairman Jozef Wagner expressed concern about the impact of government payment adjustments on the 1997 budget.
The 1997 budget was approved with spending and revenues forecast at 549.1 billion crowns, based on an expected economic growth of 5.4 percent.

China's four oldest Special Economic Zones (SEZs) grew almost twice as fast as the rest of China last year.
Foreign investment in the SEZs slowed, indicating structural weaknesses in their economies.
Officials from the State Council's SEZ Office attributed the slowdown in foreign investment to a government initiative to attract funds to underdeveloped regions.
The SEZs shifted their policy to attract larger and high-technology investments.
The average GDP growth of the SEZs in Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou, and Xiamen was 15.16 percent in 1996.
The nationwide GDP growth was 9.7 percent in the same year.
The total GDP of the four SEZs was 177.5 billion yuan, equivalent to $21.3 billion.
Shenzhen's GDP was 95 billion yuan, accounting for more than half of the total GDP of the SEZs.
Xiamen had the highest growth rate at 19.25 percent, while Zhuhai had the lowest at 8.9 percent.
The average industrial output growth of the four SEZs was 17.49 percent in 1996, with a total output value of 218.9 billion yuan.

China did not comment on the health of Deng Xiaoping on Tuesday.
Jiang Zemin and other leaders cut short their trips to visit Deng Xiaoping.
The State Council declined to comment on rumors regarding Deng's health.
Deng Xiaoping is 92 years old.
Taiwan's top policymaker on mainland affairs described Deng's condition as serious.
Jiang Zemin returned to Beijing after cutting short a visit to Ganzhou.
Premier Li Peng returned to Beijing after curtailing a tour of Guangdong.
Deng Xiaoping lives in a guarded compound behind the Forbidden City in Beijing.
Diplomats noted that the travel of top leaders indicates Deng's health status.
Chinese sources reported increasing rumors about Deng's failing health.

The seven-year-old reincarnation of Tibet's second holiest Living Buddha is Gyaincain Norbu.
Gyaincain Norbu was selected by China.
He spends his days memorizing Buddhist sutras, playing football, and learning to use a computer.
The Beijing Review magazine reported on Gyaincain Norbu's life.
The report did not clarify whether Gyaincain Norbu lives in Tibet or Beijing.
Many Tibetans regard Gyaincain Norbu as a pretender to the spiritual mantle of the 10th Panchen Lama.
The 10th Panchen Lama died in 1989.
Chinese sources claim Gyaincain Norbu lives in Beijing under state protection.
The exiled Dalai Lama has named another boy as the reincarnation of the 10th Panchen Lama.
The 11th Panchen Lama led a ceremony at the Yonghe Lamasery in Beijing on November 22.

Illegal mobile phone use across the Chinese border interrupts air traffic control communications with airline pilots flying in and out of Hong Kong.
Industry sources reported to Reuters that cross-border action to address the problem appears to be effective.
The Hong Kong Aircrew Officers' Association stated that Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) is a persistent issue.
Pilots have complained of a loud buzzing in their ears due to RFI, forcing them to change frequencies to maintain contact with air traffic control.
Hong Kong's Kai Tak airport is considered one of the world's most difficult airports to land at.
RFI is widely attributed to mobile phones and pagers operating on illegal frequencies in Guangdong province.
A Hong Kong-based Boeing 747 freighter pilot expressed safety concerns related to RFI.
The pilot noted that RFI can lead to incomplete radio messages and complicates communication during peak times.
John Findlay, general secretary of the aircrew officers' association, acknowledged RFI as a concern but indicated that the situation has improved recently.
The Hong Kong government's Civil Aviation Department stated that RFI is under urgent investigation by the Office of Telecommunications Authority (OFTA) and that a team has been established in China to address the issue.

Hong Kong Civil Aviation Department statistics indicate that cargo handled in October increased by 10.35 percent compared to the same month last year.
Air cargo imports in October reached 64,843.64 tonnes.
Air cargo exports in October reached 89,461.59 tonnes.
The statistics include regional figures for October 1996 for all flights.
Africa unloaded 151.20 tonnes and loaded 320.54 tonnes in October 1996.
Asia - others unloaded 4,244.56 tonnes and loaded 5,613.22 tonnes in October 1996.
Australasia unloaded 3,537.29 tonnes and loaded 3,418.21 tonnes in October 1996.
Continental Europe unloaded 10,857.35 tonnes and loaded 11,388.83 tonnes in October 1996.
Japan unloaded 6,580.89 tonnes and loaded 14,376.34 tonnes in October 1996.
Mainland China unloaded 1,963.18 tonnes and loaded 2,950.68 tonnes in October 1996.

Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals Limited (HACTL) set a new handling record of 5,700 tonnes in one day.
HACTL managing director Anthony Charter reported to Reuters that the total throughput for November was 150,000 tonnes.
The throughput of 150,000 tonnes in November represents a 16 percent increase in year-on-year growth.
November's export growth was 18 percent.
Imports increased by 12.8 percent in November.
Charter stated that growth for the year is expected to be no more than five to six percent.
Charter described the new daily record of 5,700 tonnes as pleasing and indicative of a market pick up in October and November.
Charter noted that it has been a very strong peak season this year.
HACTL has a monopoly on all air cargo handling at Kai Tak airport.
HACTL is jointly owned by Swire Aviation Ltd, Jardine Matheson, Wharf (Holdings) Ltd, Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, China National Aviation Corp, and Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd.

Dixons Group Plc reported a 53 percent increase in first half profits.
Dixons Group Plc experienced an eight percent increase in sales.
Dixons Group Plc's shares fell 20 pence to 518 pence by 1130 GMT.
An unnamed analyst noted that profit-taking was affecting Dixons shares.
Dixons Group Plc's pretax profits for the six months to November 9, 1996, were 57.5 million pounds.
Dixons Group Plc paid a dividend of 2.4 pence, up from 2.05 pence.
Sales from existing stores increased by eight percent in the first half.
Dixons Group Plc's chairman, Sir Stanley Kalms, stated that Christmas trading was highly satisfactory.
Managing director John Clare indicated that consumer spending was growing but not booming.
PCs and accessories accounted for around 26 percent of Dixons Group Plc's total sales in the first half.

Dixons Group Plc reported an eight percent increase in Christmas sales.
Dixons managing director John Clare stated that there is growth in the consumer economy.
Clive Vaughan, a retail consultant at Verdict, noted that there is no return to the spending culture of the 1980s.
Analysts observed that many shoppers delayed purchases until the last minute due to Christmas falling on a Wednesday in 1996.
Consumers are more discerning and prefer to pay for quality and invest in durable goods.
Hugh Clark of the British Retail Consortium stated that the high street remains competitive on price and quality.
British money supply data indicated a higher than expected increase in December month-on-month figures.
Harrods reported a ten percent increase in sales during the Christmas period, exceeding budget by two percent.
Michael Cole, Harrods director of public affairs, described the Christmas sales as very strong and consistent.
Merchant Retail Group reported an 18.6 percent increase in same store sales for its Perfume Shop chain during the Christmas period.

ASDA reported a gain in first half results and sales.
Analysts indicated there are signs of continued growth for ASDA.
ASDA's pretax profits before exceptionals were 160.1 million pounds, an increase from 138.3 million pounds a year ago.
ASDA paid a dividend of 0.81 pence per share, up from 0.72 pence.
Sales from existing stores increased by 10.2 percent compared to the previous year.
ASDA's market share increased by 0.5 points to 10.6 percent.
Chairman Archie Norman stated that keeping it simple has been key to ASDA's success.
ASDA's shares reached a high of 125 pence before falling to 123.25 pence.
ASDA's sales gain was the highest in the industry for the period.
ASDA implemented a three-year 'Renewal' strategy in the early 1990s, followed by a 'Breakout' strategy this year.

HSBC Holdings Plc is an international bank based in London.
HSBC reported a 23 percent rise in profits for 1996.
John Bond is the chief executive of HSBC.
John Bond predicted a challenging year ahead due to increasing competition.
HSBC's pretax profits for 1996 were 4.52 billion pounds.
The annual dividend per share increased by nine pence to 41 pence.
Midland Bank, HSBC's British unit, is expected to grow organically.
HSBC's tier one capital ratio rose to 9.9 percent in 1996.
HSBC had a 21.3 percent return on capital in 1996.
HSBC was granted a licence to trade in the Chinese yuan.

HSBC Holdings Plc will announce pre-tax profits for 1996 of above 4.6 billion stg.
In 1995, HSBC's pre-tax profits were 3.672 billion stg.
HSBC is expected to raise its dividend to around 40p per share from 32p.
HSBC is the parent company of Hongkong Bank, Hang Seng, Midland Bank in the UK, and Marine Midland in the U.S.
Analysts expect HSBC's margin in Hong Kong to have faced downside pressure in the second half of 1996.
HSBC's margin in Hong Kong improved by 25 basis points in the first six months of 1996.
Analysts expect the overall margin to have been maintained in 1996.
HSBC's Hong Kong mortgage business is expected to have continued to flourish.
Marine Midland reported a 34 percent increase in net income to $380 million for the year.
Analysts do not expect any strategic changes in HSBC's investment banking operations.

British banks involved in investment banking are facing renewed scrutiny of their policies.
Barclays and NatWest aim to build global investment banks to compete with Wall Street firms.
BZW, a Barclays unit, reported a 29 percent decline in profits for 1996.
In 1996, large profits were reported by major American investment banks, particularly in bond markets.
Barclays' chief executive Martin Taylor defended the cash investment in BZW.
Taylor stated that the depressed returns were due to high spending and that BZW would be weaker without the investment.
Taylor has recruited high-profile individuals, such as Bill Harrison from Flemings, for BZW's development.
NatWest Markets experienced a 90 million pound loss on derivatives, impacting its reputation and morale.
Chief executive Martin Owen acknowledged that the loss affected NatWest Markets but claimed it was only a minor issue.
Analysts question the value of investment banking for shareholder returns compared to banks like Lloyds TSB.

The Czech industrial sector is in weak shape according to Jiri Huebner, the EBRD Czech team leader.
The average return on equity among large Czech firms was 3.5 percent last year.
There has been a sharp slowdown in output in the early months of 1997.
Over 90 percent of typical Czech companies did not pay or declare any dividends.
A key problem in the Czech industrial sector is the debt loads of company owners from leveraged buyouts.
The average level of debt leverage among the fifty largest Czech companies is about 43 percent.
The average level of debt leverage at engineering companies is about 58 percent.
Uncertainty about poorly regulated capital markets has kept foreign equity investment low.
Czech companies face internal cash constraints for financing new investments and modernization.
Huebner suggests that Czech managers should take strong initiatives to restructure firms.

Czech railway unions announced a nationwide strike starting at midnight on Monday.
The strike is demanding a complete overhaul of the rail system.
The planned strike will last for 48 hours.
The strike aims to shut down passenger and freight traffic on domestic and international lines in the Czech Republic.
Zdenek Jilek is the executive secretary of the Association of Unions of Rail Workers (OSZ).
The OSZ stated that if their demands are not met, they will prolong the strike.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus commented that a new development plan for the railways had been negotiated with union leaders.
The unions are accused of being impatient for results regarding the railway issues.
Teachers and school workers have initiated a separate alternating strike for pay increases and more funding for teaching resources.
The OSZ represents over 100,000 Czech rail workers, excluding train drivers.

The Czech government plans to consider a spending cut proposal next week to balance the 1996 budget.
The Finance Ministry is proposing cuts of more than one percent from the 1996 budgets of every ministry.
The proposed cuts are due to a projected revenue shortfall of 6.6 billion crowns and an over-expenditure of 2.7 billion crowns.
Deputy Finance Minister Miroslav Havel stated that a total cut of roughly 9.3 billion crowns is needed.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's government has passed four consecutive balanced budgets.
Klaus has been recognized as post-Communist Europe's tightest fiscal manager.
The finance ministry's plan will be discussed in next week's government session.
The proposed cuts will not affect pensions or civil service wages.
The cuts will reduce expenditures on materials and other non-investment outlays across all ministries.
The budget cuts, if approved, would reduce the 1996 state budget to 291 billion crowns.

Unilever Plc plans to sell most of its speciality chemicals businesses.
The disposal programme could net up to five billion pounds ($8.17 billion) for Unilever.
The four businesses involved are National Starch & Chemical Co., Quest International, Unichema International, and Crosfield.
These businesses had total sales of around three billion pounds ($4.9 billion) last year.
The businesses employ nearly 16,000 people in 35 countries.
Analysts believe the move could allow Unilever to pursue a major acquisition in its core food, detergents, and personal product businesses.
Unilever is responding to a shake-up in the chemicals industry due to overcapacity and competition from the United States and Asia.
Unilever's speciality chemicals businesses have profit margins of more than 14 percent.
Analysts suggest that National Starch could sell for 1.3 to 1.5 times its annual sales.
Speculation exists regarding potential buyers for different segments of Unilever's chemicals businesses.

BOC Group Plc launched a breathable, liquefied version of air on Thursday.
The product is a mixture of liquid oxygen and liquid nitrogen.
This gas can create temporary cold stores in minutes and provide super-cold conditions for testing aircraft engines.
BOC claims this is the first gas of its kind that can be breathed safely.
Food retailers have shown great interest in this gas for creating temporary chilled stores.
BOC's managing director of technology, Deb Chatterji, stated that existing technology allows for temporary cold storage.
The gas was developed in Britain and the United States.
BOC estimates annual sales could be between 20 million pounds and 200 million pounds.
BOC originally aimed to enable refrigerated lorries to keep their loads cool for multi-drop deliveries.
BOC is the first company to launch this gas commercially.

SmithKline Beecham Plc reported a 14 percent increase in pre-tax profits for 1996, totaling 1.545 billion pounds.
SmithKline Beecham Plc's sales increased by 13 percent to 7.93 billion pounds in 1996.
The strong pound negatively impacted SmithKline Beecham's fourth-quarter pre-tax profits by 35 million pounds.
SmithKline Beecham's full-year pre-tax profits were reduced by approximately 29 million pounds due to currency effects.
SmithKline Beecham increased its annual dividend by 25 percent to 17.85 pence.
SmithKline Beecham's shares rose by 14.5 pence to 896.5 pence in late afternoon trading.
Chief executive Jan Leschly stated that the company's results validate its strategy, including gene-based drug discovery and high investment in research and development.
SmithKline Beecham has five new drugs in late-stage clinical trials, each with potential sales of 300 to 500 million pounds annually.
Jan Leschly ruled out any merger that would not enhance the drug pipeline.
SmithKline Beecham's prescription drug sales increased by 14 percent to 4.76 billion pounds, driven by products launched in the last five years.

A new generation of drug lords is emerging in Colombia due to the production and export of heroin.
Col. Leonardo Gallego is the anti-narcotics chief in Colombia.
Gallego stated that new groups are becoming involved in the heroin trade.
Existing groups may also participate in the heroin trade by switching substances.
62 percent of the heroin on U.S. streets comes from South America, primarily Colombia.
Colombia has displaced Southeast Asia as the major source of heroin.
Gallego believes that Colombia could be producing as much as five tonnes of heroin a year.
Approximately 12,000 acres of Colombia's rural drug farms are sown with opium poppies.
Poppy cultivation in Colombia began after 1991.
Colombian authorities have agreed to destroy 9,885 acres of poppy and 44,500 acres of coca leaf this year.

An explosion in La Picota prison in Bogota killed inmate William Infante.
William Infante was a convicted contract killer associated with the Medellin drug cartel.
The explosion occurred while Infante was making a bomb in his cell.
Investigators believe Infante was preparing an attack on fellow prisoner Leonidas Vargas.
Leonidas Vargas is an ally of the late head of the Medellin cartel's military wing.
A source from the National Prison Institute (INPEC) stated that vendettas between former Medellin cartel members are being investigated.
The source ruled out speculation that the bomb was intended for the Rodriguez Orejuela brothers or other Cali cartel members.
The two wings of La Picota prison are completely separate, preventing Medellin convicts from reaching Cali cartel members.
Investigations are ongoing to determine the type of explosive used and how it was smuggled into the prison.
Justice Minister Carlos Medellin stated that overcrowding in Colombia's jails has led to corruption and disorder.

Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo described a court decision overturning the government's state of economic emergency as bizarre and prejudicial.
Ocampo pledged to respect the court ruling.
The government plans to submit bills to Congress covering measures in emergency decrees issued by President Ernesto Samper.
The bills are expected to be submitted as early as next Tuesday.
President Ernesto Samper declared a state of economic emergency on January 13.
The economic emergency was declared due to a sharp economic slowdown in 1996 and large inflows of dollars that strengthened Colombia's peso.
The fiscal deficit increased to 4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) last year, compared to 0.2 percent in 1995.
The emergency plan aimed to increase tax revenues and combat tax evasion, which was estimated to cost the government $2 billion per year.
The emergency measures included a 16 percent sales tax on services provided by foreign-based companies and a 6 percent tax on new loans contracted abroad.
Luis Carlos Villegas, head of the National Industrialists' Association, stated that the court ruling would guide the government on reasonable measures.

British Sky Broadcasting (BSkyB) plans to launch a 200-channel digital satellite service in Britain in late 1997.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corp is the leading shareholder in BSkyB.
BSkyB is expected to order a million digital decoders at a cost of 250 million pounds ($405 million).
BSkyB shares increased by 0.5p to 580.5p by midsession on Thursday.
Share analysts believe the report about BSkyB's plans confirms their expectations.
Digital television will provide viewers in Britain with a greater range of channels and clearer pictures.
Digital satellite services have already been launched in the United States and several European countries.
Britain is pioneering digital terrestrial television (DTT), which will be broadcast from land-based transmitters.
DTT is scheduled to begin in mid-1998 and will offer approximately 36 channels.
Carlton Communications Plc supports DTT and may collaborate with Mirror Group for its application.

Shares in Pearson Plc gained on Wednesday.
Marjorie Scardino is the new chief executive of Pearson Plc.
Marjorie Scardino is the first woman to head one of Britain's leading companies.
Scardino stated that Pearson's profit performance has been inadequate.
Disposals are expected as Scardino aims for greater focus on core businesses.
Pearson shares increased by 8.5 pence to 738.5 pence.
Scardino was previously the chief executive of The Economist Group.
Scardino spent her first day meeting employees at Pearson's central London headquarters.
Analysts hope for swift action from Scardino to improve the company's focus.
Pearson's businesses include the Financial Times, Penguin books, and a television production arm.

Pearson Plc's new chief executive is Marjorie Scardino.
Marjorie Scardino promised to improve the financial performance of Pearson but stated it would be 'evolution not revolution'.
Pearson posted an operating profit of 181.3 million pounds in 1996 after a 100 million pound charge for improper accounting at its Penguin USA unit.
Profit before tax, excluding exceptional items, rose seven percent to 251.8 million pounds.
The total dividend was increased to 18 pence per share from 16.5 pence.
Marjorie Scardino became the first woman to head a leading British company in January.
Scardino had been in her position for 49 days at the time of the announcement.
She stated that decisions would be made speedily but not hastily.
Scardino noted that Pearson had stellar assets, but not all had performed well.
Pearson shares fell 14 pence to 760 pence in a generally lower market.

Quaker Oats Co sold its Snapple beverage business for $300 million.
The sale price was lower than analysts' expectations.
John McMillin, a Prudential Securities food industry analyst, estimated Snapple's value at $600 to $700 million.
Analysts expressed relief that Quaker was ending its Snapple venture.
John O'Neil, a BT Securities food industry analyst, stated that the burden of Snapple was lifted from Quaker Oats.
Quaker's shares rose to 37-7/8 after the announcement.
Triarc Cos Inc, which is acquiring Snapple, saw its shares increase to 16-3/4.
Quaker Oats purchased Snapple for $1.8 billion two-and-a-half years ago.
Snapple sales declined by eight percent in the United States and Canada in 1996.
Quaker Oats' other products include Gatorade and various cereals.

Quaker Oats Co was unable to reverse the decline of Snapple sales.
Triarc Cos Inc agreed to acquire Snapple for $300 million in cash.
Triarc Cos Inc previously rescued the Mistic beverage line.
Quaker Oats Co labored for 2-1/2 years without success in reversing Snapple's sales decline.
Triarc's acquisition of Snapple may affect its proposed spinoff of Mistic, Royal Crown soft drinks, and Arby's restaurants.
Triarc spokesman Martin Shea stated they are waiting for an IRS ruling on the spinoff.
Analysts suggested that the acquisition shows Triarc's commitment to rationalizing its assets.
John Maxwell, a food industry analyst, praised the new management team at Triarc.
Triarc was formed during the junk-bond era by Victor Posner.
Triarc has sold 16 businesses, paid off $500 million in debt, and raised $200 million in cash in the past four years.

Eli Lilly & Co is involved in a legal battle in Kentucky related to Prozac's liability issues from the early 1990s.
Eli Lilly requested the Kentucky Court of Appeals to stop a hearing scheduled for Thursday in Louisville.
The hearing is presided over by Jefferson Circuit Judge John Potter.
The hearing may disclose the details of a settlement between Lilly and the plaintiffs regarding the Joseph Wesbecker case.
Eli Lilly has acknowledged that the Joseph Wesbecker case was settled in part.
Lilly had previously stated that it reached a pre-verdict agreement in the case involving an unspecified amount of money.
Lilly spokesman Edward West confirmed that a high-low agreement was made for the settlement of the trial's compensatory and punitive damage phases.
Judge Potter amended the Wesbecker verdict to state that the case was 'dismissed as settled.'
Joseph Wesbecker committed a mass shooting in 1989 while on Prozac and other drugs, resulting in eight deaths and twelve injuries.
Survivors and victims' families sued Eli Lilly for $50 million, claiming Prozac contributed to Wesbecker's actions.

Optus Communications Pty Ltd is Australia's second largest telecommunications carrier.
Optus expects a strong result for the year ending June 30.
Optus aims for a sharemarket float in 1997 despite litigation delays.
Optus reported a net profit of A$58.9 million for the six months ended December 31, 1996.
The net profit of A$58.9 million is an increase from A$7.1 million a year earlier.
Sales rose 31.2 percent to A$1.19 billion, driven by revenue from its mobile phone business.
Sales are expected to continue the strong trend in the second half of 1996/97.
Optus reported a profit of A$60.3 million for the 1995/96 year.
Optus plans a sharemarket float in 1997, pending the outcome of litigation with Seven Network Ltd.
Optus has invested about A$605 million into Optus Vision, which is expanding its cable network.

Singapore's Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan stated that APEC members must balance liberalising telecommunications markets with maintaining local control.
Mah Bow Tan discussed the benefits of liberalisation and the need to protect local companies from foreign competition.
Mah Bow Tan indicated that the benefits of liberalisation are clear but must be balanced with local profit considerations.
Mah Bow Tan mentioned that discussions regarding these issues are taking place at the APEC forum.
Mah Bow Tan offered to host the next APEC telecommunications and information technology ministers meeting in Singapore in mid-1998.
Mah Bow Tan highlighted the significant investment requirements in the region's telecommunications infrastructure.
Mah Bow Tan noted that most of the required investment is likely to come from the private sector.
Mah Bow Tan stated that there are many investment opportunities for companies in Singapore and other countries, including America, Canada, Australia, and Japan.
In May, Mah Bow Tan accelerated Singapore's plans to end the local telephone monopoly by Singapore Telecom to the year 2000 from 2007.
Singapore plans to open its cellular phone market to competition next year, and Mah Bow Tan announced a further sell-down of Singapore Telecom, leaving the government with a 75 percent ownership.

Qantas Airways Ltd is expected to exceed its net profit forecast of A$237 million for the year ending June 30, 1996.
Analysts predict Qantas will report an annual net profit before abnormals between A$237 million and A$249 million.
Qantas is expected to pay a second half dividend of 13 cents, totaling 16.5 cents for the year.
The airline's results are anticipated to benefit from lower costs since becoming publicly owned in July 1995.
A Melbourne analyst expects Qantas' profit to be around A$240 to A$245 million, driven by cash flow directed towards debt repayment.
ANZ McCaughan aviation analyst Yasmin Allen expects Qantas to report a profit of A$237 million for 1995/96.
Another Melbourne-based analyst forecasts Qantas will report a net profit equal to the prospectus forecast of A$237 million.
A Sydney-based analyst forecasts a net profit before abnormals of A$239.1 million for the year.
The Department of Transport reported that Qantas had a 37.9 percent international market share in April.
Qantas, which is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc, forecasted a 41.1 percent international market share for the year ending June 30, 1996.

British Telecommunications Plc stated it would consider a legal challenge to any government windfall tax on its profits.
The company reported an increase in annual pretax profits to 3.2 billion pounds from 3.02 billion pounds.
Chairman Sir Iain Vallance claimed the company owed it to its investors to fight any Labour plans to tax its earnings.
Vallance expressed that if the company faced a significant tax, it would challenge it legally for the benefit of shareholders.
Vallance indicated that the company would be disappointed to start a partnership with Labour under such circumstances.
Vallance mentioned he would not have voted for Labour if a windfall tax on BT had been included in their manifesto.
The government plans to impose a one-off tax on what it describes as the 'excess profits' of privatised utilities.
Labour aims to raise funds to assist the young and long-term unemployed but has not specified which firms will be targeted.
BT's Vallance argued that it would be unreasonable to classify BT alongside utilities for taxation purposes.
BT intends to continue its 'superhighway' agreement with Labour to provide free wiring for schools and hospitals.

Vodafone Group is Britain's biggest mobile telephone group.
Vodafone raised headline annual profits by 13.5 percent.
Vodafone plans to overhaul its distribution strategy to stimulate market growth.
Vodafone has more than four million customers worldwide.
Vodafone's pre-tax profits reached 539 million pounds ($880.8 million).
Vodafone's turnover grew 25 percent to 1.749 billion pounds.
Vodafone's dividends rose 20 percent to 4.81p.
Vodafone reported a maiden operating profit from international operations of 10.5 million pounds.
Vodafone's chief executive Chris Gent stated that subscriber growth in Britain is likely to slow this year.
Vodafone might cut tariffs next year to attract new customers.

Shares in Cable and Wireless Plc increased by 26.5p to 524p by 1130 GMT on Friday.
Market hopes suggest that Cable and Wireless Plc is close to sealing a deal with China regarding Hong Kong Telecom.
Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd announced that Cable and Wireless Plc is in discussions with China on future cooperation.
Cable and Wireless Plc stated that discussions with China have been ongoing for some time.
Analysts expect Cable and Wireless Plc to reduce its 59 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecom due to Hong Kong reverting to Chinese rule.
Hong Kong Telecom's shares reached a new year high of HK$19.25, indicating significant mainland Chinese access.
Some experts believe that while growth potential in China is clear, the ability to achieve attractive returns from investments remains unproven.
Analysts are considering the size of the stake Cable and Wireless Plc would sell and the terms of the deal with China.
China Everbright Group has secured a 7.74 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecom at a 15 percent discount.
C&W's brokers, ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, noted that British-controlled Hong Kong companies have previously been sold to the Chinese at substantial discounts.

Apple Computer Inc. Chairman Gilbert Amelio announced the suspension of merit bonuses for executives until the company reports consistent profits.
Amelio expressed disappointment over Apple's $120 million loss in the latest quarter and declining revenue.
Amelio stated that his highest priority is to return the company to profitability as soon as possible.
The bonus freeze applies to the portion of bonuses tied to performance goals.
The freeze will remain in effect until the board decides to rescind it.
The suspension of bonuses occurred after Apple's second restructuring in two years.
Apple reported a $120 million loss a month prior to the announcement.
Apple plans to cut costs by $400 million by the end of its fiscal year in September.
Amelio indicated that cost reductions would involve job cuts and possible discontinuation of product lines.
Industry analysts expect Apple to cut between 2,000 and 3,000 jobs from its workforce of 13,000.

Intel Corp. will release the Pentium II microprocessor this week.
A glitch in the Pentium II microprocessor could affect the launch.
Richard Dracott is the marketing manager at Intel.
About a dozen personal computer makers plan to use the Pentium II microprocessor.
Intel is investigating reports of a floating point glitch in the chips.
The floating point glitch could cause computational errors.
A similar problem occurred with the original Pentium chip in 1994.
The problem appears to occur during obscure calculations.
Intel is testing the chips to determine the extent of the problem.
Intel has no plans to recall the affected chips at this time.

Larry Ellison, Chairman of Oracle Corp., confirmed he has formed an independent investor group to explore a takeover of Apple Computer Inc.
This is not the first time Ellison has expressed interest in leading a bid for Apple.
Apple Computer Inc. is struggling to regain profitability in the competitive PC industry.
Apple's stock rose by $1.875 to $18.625 in Nasdaq trading after news of Ellison's renewed interest in a takeover.
Ellison stated that he and an undisclosed investor group set up an email address to gauge investor support for acquiring Apple.
Ellison asked what the top priority should be for the investor group if they successfully acquired Apple.
Ellison has expressed a desire to buy Apple to prevent Microsoft Corp. from dominating the computer industry.
Ellison mentioned he would seek to raise $1 billion to acquire a majority stake in Apple.
Ellison stated that any bid would be independent of Oracle, although Oracle's stock fell by $1.125 to $39.375.
Apple is valued at $2.17 billion based on its stock price, while Ellison's stake in Oracle is worth about $6 billion.

The Toronto stock market ended mixed on Friday.
The key index of the Toronto Stock Exchange remained above 6,200 points.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index closed at 6214.24 after slipping 11.84 points.
Turnover on the Toronto Stock Exchange was 126.4 million shares worth C$1.84 billion.
Katherine Beattie, an analyst at MMS International, stated that the market lost points due to profit-taking by investors.
The key index gained 105 points during the week after opening at 6109.15 on Monday.
Beattie suggested that the market may correct after reaching a lifetime high of 6225.83 points.
Eight of Toronto's 14 sub-indices dipped, with consumer products, conglomerates, real estate, and banks leading the declines.
Advancing issues outnumbered declines 576 to 409, while 262 issues traded flat.
Abitibi-Price Inc. and Stone-Consolidated Corp. announced a merger in a stock swap deal.

Toronto stocks ended higher on Thursday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 33.27 points to 6009.90.
Trading volume was 95.3 million shares worth C$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion).
Canada's largest market increased by more than 2.5 percent in the past three sessions.
Banks led 12 of Toronto's 14 sub-indices to higher ground, rising almost 1.8 percent.
Investors were less concerned about a potential Canadian interest rate hike.
Investment advisor Ira Katzin with RBC Dominion Securities commented on financial services benefiting from stable interest rate expectations.
Market watchers were anticipating U.S. employment data to assess inflation trends.
Toronto's stronger sub-sectors included media, pipelines, and real estate.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners 500 to 447, with 301 issues remaining flat.

Mosaid Technologies Inc is a chip designer.
George Cwynar is the Chief Executive of Mosaid Technologies Inc.
Cwynar stated that Mosaid's earnings will bounce back in fiscal 1998.
Cwynar predicted profit and revenue growth of about 20 percent in fiscal 1998.
Mosaid's profit growth was about two percent in fiscal 1997, which ended on April 30.
Mosaid reported earnings per share of C$0.06 for the third quarter ended January 31.
Mosaid's earnings per share fell from C$0.32 in the previous year.
The decline in earnings was attributed to the collapse in memory chip prices and delayed orders.
Mosaid is based in Carp, a town about 35 km west of Ottawa.
Mosaid posted revenues of C$37 million in fiscal 1996.

China has decided to resume corn exports.
The resumption of corn exports could pressure the United States and other producers to discount their grain.
A U.S. trader stated that a price war is expected.
Traders reported that U.S. replacement corn is being discounted by US$3-$4 a tonne.
China banned overseas sales of corn in December 1994 to rebuild central stocks.
Total sales of Chinese corn to Southeast Asia could reach 300,000 tonnes by the end of this week.
Some traders believe the sales do not indicate a full lifting of the export ban.
Other traders suggest the sales could signal the beginning of increased Chinese corn exports.
Traders estimate that Chinese corn sales this year could reach one million tonnes.
At least 76,000 tonnes of corn have been confirmed sold to South Korea for April/May arrival.

Copper and zinc were the main focus of attention for Far East metal traders on Monday.
China has closed down to celebrate the arrival of the Year of the Ox.
Most Chinese markets will be closed until February 17.
Trading activity is expected to pick up mid-week.
There was a slight fundamental tightness in copper supply in the region.
A trader in Singapore reported difficulties in obtaining metal in mainland China.
The high cash price of copper is a deterrent for buyers.
Three months copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) ended at $2,239 a tonne.
Physical demand for copper in China for 1997 is expected to exceed supply by around 100,000 tonnes.
Chinese media reported that China's 1997 copper demand should rise five percent to 1.05 million tonnes.

Ford Motor Co plans to increase its stake in Jiangling Motors Corp.
Ford announced an investment of $54.5 million in Jiangling Motors Corp.
Ford's equity share in Jiangling will increase from 20 percent to about 30 percent.
The agreement is subject to approval from Jiangling's shareholders and China's regulatory authorities.
Ford and Jiangling are developing a light commercial vehicle that will include a nine- and a 12-seater bus.
A van and a chassis cab, or pick-up truck, will also be produced at Jiangling's plant in Nanchang.
Jiangling's share of China's top-end light truck market has fallen to 15-18 percent.
Qingling Motors, a major competitor, has increased its market share to about 21 percent.
Qingling's use of Japanese technology through Isuzu gives it a competitive advantage.
Jiangling expected to sell 17,000 vehicles in 1996, down from 20,500 in 1995.

Norilsk Nickel plant is facing financial difficulties and aims to maintain steady output.
Company officials stated that efforts to improve competitiveness have altered long-term profitability plans.
Valery Alfimenko reported that January output was slightly above planned levels but not at full capacity.
Alfimenko emphasized the importance of not producing less than the previous year.
Production levels will depend on market prices, according to Alfimenko.
The financial crisis has not impacted mining operations, but material supplies may be affected.
Norilsk is the largest producer of nickel, copper, and cobalt in Russia and a significant global producer of platinum and palladium.
Workers have set a deadline of February 20 for management to address three months of unpaid salaries.
Leonid Binder mentioned that output remains steady but did not provide specific figures.
Workers expressed no confidence in management due to wage arrears and demanded higher salaries.

Russia admitted it missed its chance to lead in Caspian oil projects.
Russia expressed ambitions in the Mideast Gulf after signing deals with Iraq.
Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov stated Iraq was a natural choice for investment.
Rodionov acknowledged that Russia missed many investment opportunities in the Caspian region.
Russian companies have a minor role in multi-billion dollar oil deals in Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan.
Russia and Iraq signed a 23-year deal to develop oil reserves in the Qurana oilfield.
The deal with Iraq is contingent on the lifting of U.N. sanctions imposed after Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The deal is expected to generate $70 billion in revenue for Baghdad.
Russia's largest oil company LUKoil holds a 52.5 percent stake in the Qurana oilfield.
Rodionov stated that Russia will only conduct preparatory work that complies with U.N. sanctions.

Russia's Gazprom is the world's largest gas company.
Gazprom has not experienced significant economic troubles at home that affect its ability to raise money abroad.
Energy analysts stated that Gazprom would declare an end to its conflict with the government at its annual shareholders' meeting.
Analyst Yuri Butayev noted that nonpayment issues affect Gazprom's collection rate and profitability.
Butayev described Gazprom as attractive due to its large reserves and exports to Europe.
Gazprom is emerging from a nonpayment crisis that has impacted many Russian enterprises.
The company has plans for major capital raising and has resolved its tax issues.
Gazprom faces challenges in collecting payments from domestic customers.
Analyst Ivan Mazalov stated that Gazprom has raised more capital abroad than any other Russian company.
Gazprom accounted for 26 percent of Russia's tax revenues in 1996.

The French government plans to sell the loss-making SFP film studios to Generale des Eaux and Havas.
The sale requires approval from the independent Privatisation Commission.
A state capital injection of up to 1.2 billion francs ($229 million) will precede the sale.
The Societe Francaise de Production et de Creation Audiovisuelle (SFP) will receive 350 million francs before the end of 1996.
Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy met European Commissioner Karel van Miert to discuss the planned capital injection.
Van Miert accepted the principle of a quick examination procedure for the European Commission's approval of the state's financial effort.
The cash injection is needed due to the financial situation of the SFP and will help future shareholders manage operating risks.
There were four offers for SFP, including bids from Global Studios, Little Big One, Jean Cressant, and Havas/Generale des Eaux.
The Havas/Generale des Eaux plan included 480 job cuts out of 1,010 SFP staff.
The SFP studios were created on the grounds of the Buttes Chaumont villa of Leon Gaumont and have faced difficulties due to competition from smaller production companies.

The French government called off the sale of electronics group Thomson SA.
This decision was made after weeks of defending the choice of buyer.
It was the second privatisation to be halted in less than a month.
The first privatisation halted was the sale of state-owned bank CIC.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe is at a record low in opinion polls.
The Finance Ministry stated the suspension was due to objections to the sale of Thomson's consumer electronics unit to Daewoo Electronics.
Several thousand workers of Thomson Multimedia protested against the sale on November 20.
Workers feared for their jobs and working conditions due to the sale to Daewoo Electronics.
Socialist opposition leaders criticized the government for choosing Lagardere over Alcatel Alsthom.
The Privatisation Commission informed the government it could not agree with the sale of Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo.

Two million severely handicapped people in Europe could communicate over the global Internet using eye-movement control.
A French team of researchers demonstrated a prototype of an Apple Macintosh computer that reacts to eye movements.
The system was evaluated in a clinical test with 30 people in France using an eye movement-controlled word processor.
The system allows handicapped individuals to access multimedia, including electronic books, compact discs, and computer games.
Bernard de Groc from Delta 7 stated that severely handicapped individuals are primarily young people aged 15 to 31 who have had road accidents.
These individuals retain their intellectual faculties and have a long life expectancy.
Doctor Philippe Thoumie coordinated clinical tests in three hospitals in France and reported that 22 out of 30 participants successfully used the system.
The system is designed to be lightweight and not make users feel uncomfortable or robotic.
